sections.en: In Prayer, the Primary Essence Is the Inner Longing and Passionate Desire to Pray…

p: [מב] בִּתְפִלָּה הוּא הָעִיקָּר הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָרָצוֹן לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וּלְהִתְחַנֵּן,
In prayer, the primary essence is the inner longing and passionate desire to pray and plead,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "אַל תַּעַשׂ תְּפִלָּתְךָ קֶבַע אֶלָּא רַחֲמִים וְכוּלֵי",
as they said: "Do not make your prayer a fixed routine, but supplications for mercy, etc." (Avot 2:13),
שֶׁהוּא עַצְמוֹ מַאֲמָרָם שִׁילְהֵי מְנָחוֹת בְּקָרְבָּנוֹת [שֶׁהַתְּפִלָּה דּוּגְמָתָן]:
which is identical to their teaching at the end of Menachot (110a) regarding sacrificial offerings [which prayer mirrors]:
"שֶׁלֹּא תֹאמַר אֶעֱשֶׂה רְצוֹנוֹ וְכוּלֵי, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: 'לִרְצֹנְכֶם תִּזְבָּחוּהוּ'",
"Lest you say: 'I will perform His will, etc.,' Scripture states: 'You shall slaughter it of your own free will (to your desire)'" (Leviticus 19:5),
דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כִּי אֵין הַקָּרְבָּן מִצְוָה,
meaning that the sacrificial offering is not a typical commanded obligation,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְלֹא צִוִּיתִים וְגוֹמֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי עוֹלָה וָזָבַח", וְכֵן בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת.
as it is written: "I spoke not unto your fathers... concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices" (Jeremiah 7:22), and likewise in numerous passages.
וְעַיֵּין בְּמוֹרֶה נְבוּכִים בְּטַעַם הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת.
And see the Guide for the Perplexed (3:32) regarding the rationale of sacrifices.
וְנוֹדַע מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב מַהֲרַ"ם אַלְשַׁקַר סִימָן קי"ז דְּכֵן הוּא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ, וְכָתַב מָשָׁל וְכוּלֵי עַיֵּין שָׁם,
And it is known what Maharam Alashkar wrote in Responsum 117 that this is found in the Midrash, citing a parable, see there:
דְּעִנְיַן הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת הוּא שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל הַתִּקְרֹבֶת נֶהֱנֶה מִמֶּנּוּ,
that the concept of sacrifices is that the recipient of an offering derives gratification from it,
וְכָל הָעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה – אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ נֶהֱנֶה וּמִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יְדֵי אוֹתוֹ קָרְבָּן כְּמוֹ אָדָם עַל יְדֵי מַאֲכָל;
and in all idolatry, that celestial force derives pleasure and gains strength through that sacrifice just as a person does through food;
וּמִתּוֹךְ שֶׁיָּדְעוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כֵּן, הָיָה חֶשְׁקָם וְכָסְפָּם שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהַהֲנוֹת כִּבְיָכוֹל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and because they recognized this regarding idolatry, they harbored an intense yearning and desire to likewise bestow pleasure, as it were, upon the Blessed Name;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ תִכְסֹף", כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תְּצַוֶּה ב),
and concerning this it is stated: "You will yearn for the work of Your hands" (Job 14:15), as our Sages expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Tetzaveh 2),
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִרְשָׁם בְּכָךְ שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כִּמְהַנִּים אוֹתוֹ.
and the Blessed Name permitted them to do so, that they might be considered as granting Him satisfaction.
רַק מִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְכָךְ בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא נֶהֱנֶה בְּכָךְ, אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין צָרִיךְ לְכָךְ,
Only one who truly needs it benefits from it, but the Blessed Name has no need for it;
וְלֹא תֹאמַר אֶעֱשֶׂה רְצוֹנוֹ וְכוּלֵי כִּבְכָל הַמִּצְווֹת,
so you must not say "I am doing His will, etc." as with all other commandments,
רַק "לִרְצוֹנְכֶם" – כְּפִי הָרָצוֹן וְהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּכֶם, כָּךְ הוּא הַקָּרְבָּן.
but rather "to your desire"—in accordance with your own inner will and longing, so is the quality of the sacrifice.
רַק דְּמִזֶּה הוּא הַהֲנָאָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: מֵהָרָצוֹן וְהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּהֶם לְהַהֲנוֹתוֹ.
The only gratification to the Blessed Name arises directly from this: from their heartfelt desire and longing to please Him.
וְכֵן הַתְּפִלָּה בִּמְקוֹם הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת,
So too is prayer, which stands in the place of the sacrifices:
שֶׁאֵין רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִבְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁיִּתְפַּלְּלוּ לְפָנָיו וִישַׁנּוּהוּ,
it is not the desire of the Blessed Name that human beings pray before Him to change His mind,
רַק הָרָצוֹן שֶׁלָּהֶם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל – זֶהוּ רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהָבֵן זֶה:
rather their very desire to pray—that itself is His blessed will; and understand this well.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avot 2:13: ‘Rabbi Shimon says: Be careful about reciting the Shema and praying. And do not regard yourself as wicked.’

paragraphs.text: The commanded act has a purpose: the refinement and divine will expressed through it.

rich.text: The commanded act has a purpose: the refinement and divine will expressed through it.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:22:1: “A person should not set his final purpose and intention on a particular thing, such as restraining desires, studying Torah, engaging in service, or the like. Concerning this the prophet repeatedly cries out that sacrifices were not requested. The commentators ask: were they not in fact commanded? The meaning is that they made this alone the final purpose—to bring sacrifices and perform mitzvot—as it is written, ‘Their fear of Me became a commandment of people learned by rote’ (Isaiah 29:13); this was not commanded. As the Midrash says (Tanchuma, Shemini 8; Bereshit Rabbah 44:1): what difference does it make to the Holy One, blessed be He, whether one slaughters from the neck, and so forth? Rather, the purpose is to refine. The bare physical act is not the final purpose of the command; its purpose is what each mitzvah signifies and intends, in order to refine.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah directly addresses the apparent contradiction behind the siman's sacrificial analogy: the prophets speak of offerings as unrequested although the Torah commands them. The criticism concerns making the external act an isolated final purpose. Its intended refinement and relation to Hashem's will give the act its meaning. This clarifies the siman's emphasis on the desire to pray while preserving the distinction between that purpose and the existence of a commandment.

sections.en: At Times a Person Faces a Spiritual Test of Such Overwhelming Magnitude That It…

p: [מג] פְּעָמִים יֵשׁ אָדָם עוֹמֵד בְּנִסָּיוֹן גָּדוֹל כָּל כָּךְ, עַד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא,
At times a person faces a spiritual test of such overwhelming magnitude that it is virtually impossible for him not to sin,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת לב.): "מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה הַבֵּן וְכוּלֵי",
in the spirit of the Sages' words (Berakhot 32a): "What can the son do and not sin, etc.?",
וּבָזֶה הוּא נֶחְשָׁב אֹנֶס גָּמוּר דְּרַחֲמָנָא פַּטְרֵיהּ.
and in such a state it is legally deemed absolute duress (ones gamur), from which the Merciful One exempts him.
וְגַם בְּהַסָּתַת הַיֵּצֶר בְּתוֹקֶף עָצוּם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַצְּחוֹ, שַׁיָּיךְ אֹנֶס
And even under the incitement of the evil inclination of such immense ferocity that it cannot be conquered, duress applies
[וְאִם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵסֵיב אֶת לִבּוֹ, הֲרֵי אֵין חֵטְא זֶה חֵטְא כְּלָל, רַק שֶׁרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה כָּךְ].
[and if the Blessed Name turned his heart, then this sin is not a sin at all, but rather the will of the Blessed Name unfolded thus].
וְעַיֵּין מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (נא:) גַּבֵּי תְּחִלָּתוֹ בְּאֹנֶס:
And examine Ketubot (51b) regarding a violation that began under duress:
אֲפִילּוּ צוֹוַחַת לְבַסּוֹף שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא מַנִּיחָהּ הִיא שׂוֹכַרְתּוֹ, מוּתֶּרֶת לְבַעְלָהּ;
even if she cries out at the end that were he to let her go she would hire him, she remains permitted to her husband;
מַאי טַעְמָא? יֵצֶר אַלְבְּשַׁהּ;
what is the reason? Passion enclothed her;
הֲרֵי דְּזֶה מִתְחַשֵּׁב אֹנֶס גָּמוּר,
which proves that this is deemed complete duress,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מֵרְצוֹנָהּ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵצֶר גָּדוֹל כָּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בָּאָדָם לְכָפְיוֹ, וְהוּא אֹנֶס גָּמוּר,
for even though it ended with her consent, an inclination of such ferocity is beyond human capacity to suppress, and constitutes total duress,
וְאֵין בָּזֶה עוֹנֶשׁ אַף דְּעָשָׂה אִיסּוּר, כֵּיוָן דְּהָיָה אָנוּס.
and bears no punishment even though a prohibition was transgressed, since one was under duress.
אֲבָל הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהָעִיד עַל עַצְמוֹ בָּזֶה, כִּי אוּלַי עֲדַיִן הָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ לִכְפּוֹת הַיֵּצֶר
However, a person cannot testify about himself in this regard, for perhaps he still possessed sufficient strength to master the inclination
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בָּזֶה מֵעִנְיַן זִמְרִי שֶׁטָּעָה בָּזֶה]:
[as I heard concerning the episode of Zimri who erred in this very self-assessment].

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vayetzei 2:2: “In the Gemara, Sukkah, before the statement “Draw it to the house of study,” it says that a person’s inclination overpowers him each day, and that without the Holy One’s help he cannot overcome it. This appears to show that even through Torah there is no remedy against the evil inclination without Hashem’s help. It concerns what the evil inclination provokes on its own, beyond what it was assigned. For this it is called wicked, as they derive from “The wicked watches the righteous”: in its wickedness it seeks to cause the person to stumble. Concerning the inclination implanted at creation, according to the measure of each individual soul, it says, “I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its remedy.” But against what the evil inclination adds on its own, a person has no strength to stand. The Holy One does not act unfairly, and “Hashem will not abandon him into its hand”—He helps him. Yet the Holy One does not help everyone in this way, but the one who looks to Him for it. This is through prayer, casting one’s burden upon Hashem.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 1:34:1: “‘Their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot listen’ (Jeremiah 6:10)—even if they wish to, so that they are like people under compulsion; for ‘Hashem's word has become a reproach to them; they do not desire it’ (there). This is like ‘its beginning was under compulsion and its end with willingness’ (Ketubot 51b): according to Shmuel's father, ‘the inclination clothed her.’ So too with the inclination to idolatry then, as Menashe said (Sanhedrin 102b): at the end, even the willingness is compulsion; the essential matter is the beginning. Or it may be understood according to the saying (Yerushalmi Chagigah 1:7), ‘Would that they abandoned Me but kept My Torah: its light would return them to the good,’ and as stated (Kiddushin 30b), ‘I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its remedy.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah examines the same Talmudic case of initial compulsion followed by apparent willingness. It directs attention back to the beginning, then offers Torah's restoring light as another reading of the prophetic passage. This illuminates why the siman combines recognition of genuine compulsion with its explicit refusal to let a person certify that condition for himself. The parallel supplies a distinction to examine, rather than a ruling about any particular case.

sections.en: A Person Possessed of Intense Longing for Physical Pleasures Must Not Be Saddened By…

p: [מד] מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּשׁוּקָה גְּדוֹלָה לְתַאֲווֹת הַגּוּף, אַל יִתְעַצֵּב בָּזֶה לַחְשׁוֹב כַּמָּה פָּגוּם הוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּשׁוּקָה כָּל כָּךְ.
A person possessed of intense longing for physical pleasures must not be saddened by this, thinking how blemished he must be to harbor such desires.
כִּי אַדְּרַבָּא, הוּא כְּלִי מוּכָן לְתוֹקֶף אַהֲבַת וּתְשׁוּקַת דְּרִישַׁת הָאֱמֶת.
For on the contrary, he is a vessel ideally prepared for the intense love and passionate pursuit of the Truth.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּחֲמוֹ הַהוּא סָבָא
Just as that elder comforted
[אֲשֶׁר הוּא אֵלִיָּהוּ לְדַעַת יֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים בְּתוֹסָפוֹת פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּחֻלִּין (ו.), וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּכֵן הוּא הָאֱמֶת, וּדְקוּשְׁיַת תּוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם אֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]
[who is Eliyahu, according to the view 'some explain' in Tosafot, first chapter of Chullin (6a); and I heard that this is the truth, and Tosafot's question there is not for this place]
לְאַבַּיֵּי (בְּסֻכָּה נב.).
Abaye (Sukkah 52a).
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא צַדִּיקִים נִדְמֶה לָהֶם יֵצֶר הָרָע כְּהַר וּרְשָׁעִים כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה,
And concerning this they said that in the World to Come the evil inclination appears to the righteous like a high mountain and to the wicked like a strand of hair;
וְאֵינוֹ שֶׁקֶר, רַק שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת,
and this is not a contradiction, rather both are true:
כִּי לָאֵלּוּ תְּשׁוּקָתָם וְתַאֲוָתָם עֲצוּמָה בְּיוֹתֵר:
for in these [the righteous], the longing and desire are far stronger.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 248:1: “The essence of a person is the desire in the heart, through which he has an advantage over the angels. This is called inclination: the good inclination and the evil inclination. When he strengthens his desire toward good, it is good; otherwise, the reverse. Our Sages said: Whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater inclination. For one person’s greatness over another is only according to the greatness of his desire for good, which is the power of inclination. The good inclination and the evil inclination stand opposite one another in the heart’s two chambers: according to the desire in his heart on the right for good, so it is on the left for evil. Therefore the evil inclination is also greater.”

sections.en: When a Person Has Sinned So Exceedingly That the Path of Repentance Seems Blocked

p: [מה] כְּשֶׁחָטָא הַרְבֵּה עַד שֶׁנִּסְתַּם הַתְּשׁוּבָה, כִּי כְּבָר סוּגְּרוּ דַּלְתֵי לִבּוֹ,
When a person has sinned so exceedingly that the path of repentance seems blocked, because the gates of his heart have slammed shut,
עַל זֶה אָמַר: "בּוֹרֵא נִיב שְׂפָתָיִם שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם",
concerning this Scripture proclaims: "He creates the utterance of the lips: Peace, peace" (Isaiah 57:19),
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בּוֹרֵא יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁל "שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם",
meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, creates something from nothing the speech of "Peace, peace,"
שֶׁהוּא קַבָּלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה, הֵיפֶךְ הַנֶּאֱמָר: "לָרְשָׁעִים אֵין שָׁלוֹם".
which is the acceptance of repentance, the absolute antithesis of that which is said: "There is no peace to the wicked" (ibid. 57:21).
וּתְחִלַּת אוֹתָהּ פָּרָשָׁה (יְשַׁעְיָה נז) בַּפָּסוּק "הַנֵּחָמִים בָּאֵלִים וְגוֹמֵר",
And the beginning of that passage (Isaiah 57) opens with the verse: "You who inflame yourselves among the terebinths, etc.,"
שֶׁדְּרָשׁוּהוּ (נִדָּה יג.) עַל הַמּוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
which our Sages expounded (Niddah 13a) regarding wasting seed,

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 108:1: “Concerning wasting seed, the Zohar says that repentance does not avail. This is because the drops of seed are drawn from the brain, and the person has damaged the drops of his brain. Repentance is in the heart, as it is written, “His heart will understand and he will return”; therefore it cannot repair wisdom, which is above it. Rather, Torah is needed, for it is the fallen fruit of the wisdom above, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah 17, and it too is in the brain. [It is called “being,” as is known; its numerical value equals that of keri, as I have written elsewhere.] A broken heart, becoming truly as nothing, belongs to keter, which, as is known, is higher still, and this avails. As it is written: “The face of Hashem is against evildoers”—this is that sin, which is called evil—“to cut off from the earth,” and so forth; as it says, “Your people are all righteous,” for inheritance of the land belongs only to the righteous, meaning the one who guards the covenant. It says, “They cried out,” and so forth: prayer is a remedy against being cut off from the earth. [Prayer is rooted in malkhut, the supernal land. His damage reached it, in the manner of “Hashem is your shadow”: exactly like a shadow, it does what he does, whether for good or, Heaven forbid, the reverse.] But to draw near to Hashem, the remedy is a broken heart: “And the crushed in spirit,” and so forth. Likewise, in the psalm “when he had come to Bathsheba,” which was composed concerning a breach of the covenant [which is present from birth, as it says, “For the inclination … from his youth”; therefore he asked, “Create in me a pure heart,” and creation is something new that now springs forth, being from nothing], it says, “For You do not desire a sacrifice,” and so forth [meaning repentance, in the sense of “Whoever sacrifices his inclination and confesses,” Sanhedrin 43b]: “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit,” and so forth.”

paragraphs.text: Context: This complete parallel explains why the severe Zohar formulation does not mean that return is impossible. Rav Tzadok describes Torah, prayer, and a broken heart, and ends with David’s request for the creation of a pure heart. These are the same themes of humility, creation anew, and healing developed in the present ois.

sections.en: And Unto the Wicked God Said

p: [מו] "וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חֻקָּי".
"And unto the wicked God said: What right have you to recount My statutes?" (Psalms 50:16).
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה יִדְווּ וְכוּלֵי,
And over this matter hearts faint,
כִּי הָעוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים נִקְרָא רָשָׁע כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת כ.).
for one who transgresses the words of the Scribes is termed wicked, as stated (Yevamot 20a).
אֲבָל עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים מַאֲמַר חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים פו:):
Yet concerning this, the early masters applied the statement of our Sages (Pesachim 86b):
כָּל מַה שֶּׁיֹּאמַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת עֲשֵׂה – חוּץ מִצֵּא.
"Whatever the host tells you, do—except: 'leave.'"
וְלֹא לְחִנָּם כָּתְבָה תּוֹרָה עִנְיַן הַמַּעְפִּילִים בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁלַח,
And not in vain did the Torah record the episode of the Ma'apilim (those who presumed to ascend) in Parashat Shelach,
אֲשֶׁר כְּבָר הֶאֱמִינוּ בְּדִבְרֵי מֹשֶׁה, וְלָמָּה לֹא שָׁמְעוּ לוֹ בָּזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם "אַל תַּעֲלוּ וְגוֹמֵר"?
who already believed the words of Moses; why then did they disobey him when he instructed them "Do not go up, etc."?
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם חָשְׁבוּ שֶׁזֶּה בִּכְלַל "חוּץ מִצֵּא".
Rather, they reasoned that this fell under the rubric of "except: 'leave.'"
וְעַיֵּין בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, קס עַמּוּד א) הִמְלִיץ כָּל עִנְיַן מְרַגְּלִים עַל הַתּוֹרָה,
And see the Zohar (Part III, 160a) which allegorizes the entire episode of the Spies to the Torah,
וְהָיָה הָעוֹנֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יַשִּׂיגוּהָ,
where the punishment was that they would not attain it,
וְעַל זֶה הֶעְפִּילוּ לַעֲלוֹת אַף נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and regarding this they dared to ascend even counter to the apparent will of the Blessed Name,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה.): "חוּצְפָּתָא – מַלְכוּתָא בְּלָא תָּגָא"
as in the dictum of our Sages (Sanhedrin 105a): "Audacity is kingship without a crown"
[וּלְמָדוּהָ מִבִּלְעָם שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ הִסְכִּים הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי בִּלְעָם נִסְתַּכֵּל עַד עִקְבְּתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא וּלְכָךְ יָדַע סוֹד זֶה].
[which they derived from Balaam, where afterward the Blessed Name consented; for Balaam gazed unto the footsteps of the Messiah, and therefore grasped this secret].
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּידוּעַ "מַלְכוּת" הוּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְ"כֶתֶר" הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
The explanation is: as is known, Malchut (Kingship) is the Congregation of Israel, while Keter (Crown) is the primordial root of Hashem's will,
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר: מֶמְשָׁלָה מֵעַצְמוֹ בְּלִי רְצוֹן הָרוֹצִים, וְהִתְקָרְבוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעַצְמָם.
meaning sovereign initiative from oneself without dependent will, and the spontaneous drawing near of the Congregation of Israel on their own.
וְהֵם לֹא הִצְלִיחוּ בָּזֶה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֲכָלוּהָ פַּגָּה,
But the Ma'apilim did not succeed in this because they ate it unripe,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה מט:): "בְּעִקְּבוֹתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא חוּצְפָּא יִסְגֵּא", שֶׁאָז הוּא הָעֵת לָזֶה
as our Sages stated (Sotah 49b): "In the footsteps of the Messiah audacity will increase," for only then is the proper hour for this
[וּלְעָתִיד: "נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר", וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
[and in the future: "A woman shall court a man" (Jeremiah 31:21), and this is not the place to elaborate].
וּלְכָךְ אָמַר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה: "וְהִוא לֹא תִצְלָח",
And therefore Moses said to them: "And it shall not prosper" (Numbers 14:41)—
נִרְאֶה שֶׁעֵצָה הוּא אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא תִצְלַח;
indicating that it is a valid concept, only that it would not prosper at that time;
וְדָיֵיק "וְהִוא" – שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "הִיא" וְלֹא אַחֶרֶת,
and he was precise in saying "and it" (ve-hi)—for everywhere our Sages expound: "it, but not another,"
שֶׁיֵּשׁ זְמַן אַחֵר שֶׁמַּצְלִיחַ,
teaching that there is another future time when it does prosper,
וְהוּא זְמַנֵּנוּ זֶה שֶׁהוּא עִקְבֵי מָשִׁיחַ:
and that is this present era of ours, which represents the footsteps of the Messiah.

paragraphs.text: Yevamot 20a:15: “‘A prohibition of holiness’ means the secondary forbidden relationships established by the Sages. Why does he call it ‘a prohibition of holiness’? Abaye said: ‘Whoever upholds the words of the Sages is called holy.’ Rava said to him: ‘And someone who does not uphold the words of the Sages is merely not called holy? Is he not also called wicked?’ Rather, Rava said: ‘Sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you.’”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Miketz 2:1: “As we heard from our holy master, of blessed memory, on the verse, “The Rock of Israel spoke to me: a righteous one rules over man, ruling through the fear of God”: “Rock” denotes firmness. Hashem gives firmness to the penitent’s heart, as though He had spoken to him personally, enabling him to rule over a righteous man. This means that even concerning matters of which Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said in the holy Zohar that repentance is ineffective, Heaven forbid, the penitent has the power to annul that judgment and repair them. “Ruling through the fear of God” also includes what was spoken by the Holy One, blessed be He, as when a heavenly voice declared, “Return, wayward children, except Acher.” Nevertheless, he could have repaired himself through repentance, because this is Hashem’s will. As the Shelah and Reishit Chokhmah wrote, this is what the Sages hinted at: “Do everything the master of the house tells you, except ‘Leave.’””

paragraphs.text: Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:26: “The rule is that there is nothing that cannot be repaired through repentance. When the Zohar explains that it does not depend on repentance, this means that its repentance is difficult. Being shown that it does not depend on repentance is itself part of that difficulty. Nothing stands in the way of repentance. Even if you hear, “Return, wayward children, except so-and-so,” as in the case of Elisha Acher, pay no heed. After all, Elisha Acher was ultimately accepted even though he did not repent; all the more so, had he repented, it would have helped him still more. Rather, they closed the doors of repentance before him, and he needed to persist until the entrance opened. This is what the Sages meant: “Do whatever the householder tells you, except ‘Leave.’” The householder is the Holy One, blessed be He. Whatever He tells you to do of the mitzvot, do—except “Leave.” If He says to you, “Leave My house and do not enter,” as in Elisha Acher’s case, do not listen to Him; instead, enter through repentance. For this is the householder’s desire, but He is misleading you.”

paragraphs.text: Context: This is the original interpretation behind “except ‘Leave.’” The apparent rejection is itself a test of persistence: the passage expressly distinguishes difficult repentance from impossible repentance.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Sh'lach 9:59-10:67: ‘‘But the people are strong’ (Numbers 13:28): one must be strong enough to take no account at all of worldly affairs, because one must have abundant wealth in order to devote oneself to Torah. Who can attain it? Indeed, ‘But the people who dwell in the land are strong’: anyone who wishes to attain it must be powerful in wealth, as it says: ‘A rich man answers harshly’ (Proverbs 18:23). ‘And the cities are great and fortified’: houses filled with every good thing, lacking nothing. Even with all this, ‘We also saw the descendants of the giant there’: a strong body is needed, mighty as a lion (being found there continually), because it exhausts a person’s strength to labor over what is forbidden and permitted, impure and pure, valid and invalid. Who can attain it? Furthermore, ‘Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev’ (Numbers 13:29). If a person says that despite all this he will attain it, ‘Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev’: this is the evil inclination, the prosecutor who accuses a person and is constantly present in the body. ‘And the Hittite and the Amorite,’ and so forth: how many accusers are there, so that a person cannot enter that world at all! Who can merit it, and who can enter it? With these words, ‘They discouraged the hearts of the children of Israel’ (Numbers 32:9), for they brought out a bad reputation concerning it, as it says: ‘They brought out a slanderous report of the land.’’

paragraphs.text: Context: The Zohar interprets the spies’ journey as an encounter with Torah. Calling Hebron “Torah” makes the allegorical setting explicit; Rav Tzadok then applies the spies’ discouragement and the response to it to spiritual effort.

From this source, the particular light and vitality appropriate to each one is drawn forth, dwelling and clothing itself within them to give them life. All of them come only from the extension of vitality and light from this source called Shekhinah, like the extension of light from the sun.”

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, On Book of Joshua 28: “Boldness means audacity: kingship without a crown, even though it is effective even toward Heaven. “Toward” means “against” in the holy tongue—that is, opposition; one who opposes the will of the blessed God can also accomplish something. Therefore Yosef too attained kingship through the intensity of his desire for it, as his brothers said to him, “Will you indeed reign over us?” His dreams likewise arose from his thoughts during the day. He attained it by the strength of his righteousness, and this is “kingship without a crown.” “Crown” means the beginning and hidden root of every complete structure of ten sefirot, as is known. It means an extension of kingship that has no root in its upper source, from whose power comes enduring existence. It exists only in the extension of the nine attributes revealed in this world, through the force of his righteousness, good deeds, and intense desire for it.”

sections.en: Regarding All the Innate Faculties Planted within Every Soul of Israel

p: [מז] כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת הַנְּטוּעוֹת בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אֵין לַחְשׁוֹב שֶׁהוּא רַע גָּמוּר וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת הֶפְכּוֹ,
Regarding all the innate faculties planted within every soul of Israel, one must not imagine that any of them is pure evil requiring absolute eradication to its opposite;
כִּי אֵין לְךָ שׁוּם מִדָּה וְכֹחַ שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ צַד טוֹב גַּם כֵּן,
for you have no character trait or faculty that does not also possess a dimension of good,
רַק צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ כְּפִי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
one only needs to utilize it in accordance with the will of the Blessed Name.
וְאִם אֵינוֹ כְּפִי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, גַּם הַמִּדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת רָעוֹת,
And if it is not aligned with the will of the Blessed Name, even good traits become evil,
כְּמוֹ שָׁאוּל שֶׁנֶּעֱנַשׁ בַּעֲבוּר הָרַחְמָנוּת,
as with King Saul who was punished on account of misplaced mercy,
וּבְגִטִּין (נו.): עַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן אַבְקוּלַס הֶחֱרִיבָה וְכוּלֵי.
and in Gittin (56a): "The excessive humility of Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas destroyed our Temple, etc."
וּלְהֵיפֶךְ אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת סג.):
And conversely, our Sages stated (Shabbat 63a):
אִם רָאִיתָ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם נוֹקֵם וְנוֹטֵר כְּנָחָשׁ – חָגְרֵהוּ וְכוּלֵי,
"If you see a Torah scholar who avenges and bears a grudge like a serpent—gird him upon your loins, etc.,"
וְנָחָשׁ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע בְּכַעַס.
though a serpent is the root of evil in anger.
וּבְתַלְמִיד חָכָם – רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר אֲשֶׁר כָּל מְגַמּוֹתָיו רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – אַדְּרַבָּה הוּא טוֹב מְאֹד,
But in a Torah scholar—meaning one whose entire aim is the will of the Blessed Name—on the contrary, it is "very good,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט): "טוֹב מְאֹד" – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע.
along the lines of what our Sages said (Bereishit Rabbah 9): "'Very good'—this is the evil inclination."
וְכֵן בְּגַאֲוָה (בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּסוֹטָה ה.): בְּשַׁמְתָּא מַאן דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ.
And likewise regarding pride (in the first chapter of Sotah 5a): "Under a ban of excommunication is one who possesses none of it."
וְלָכֵן הַנְּבִיאִים הָיוּ מְיַלְּלִים עַל אָבְדַן הָאֻמּוֹת: "לִבִּי לְמוֹאָב וְגוֹמֵר" וְכַיּוֹצֵא,
And therefore the Prophets wailed over the destruction of the nations: "My heart cries out for Moab, etc." (Isaiah 15:5) and the like,
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שִׁבְּחוּם עַל זֶה בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק).
and our Sages praised them for this in Midrash Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Balak).
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא חָסוּ עַל אִיבּוּד גּוּפָם, כִּי "בַּאֲבֹד רְשָׁעִים רִנָּה"
And surely they did not mourn over the destruction of their physical bodies, for "when the wicked perish there is singing" (Proverbs 11:10)

[וְאוּלַי יִהְיֶה "לִבִּי" עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ה, ב): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה י:): הוּא אֵינוֹ שָׂשׂ],

[and perhaps "my heart" is along the lines of the Sages' teaching (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): the Holy One is the heart of Israel, as stated: 'God is the rock of my heart' (Psalms 73:26); and the Sages stated (Megillah 10b): He Himself does not rejoice];
רַק יָדוּעַ: כָּל אֻמָּה הוּא כֹּחַ מְיוּחָד, ע' אֻמּוֹת וְע' כֹּחוֹת בַּנֶּפֶשׁ.
rather it is known: each nation represents a unique spiritual faculty, seventy nations corresponding to seventy faculties within the soul.
וּבַיּוֹם הַהוּא יִגְדַּל הַמִּסְפֵּד בְּאָבְדַן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב.),
And on that day the great lamentation will encompass the destruction of the evil inclination as well, as stated (Sukkah 52a),
כִּי "יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִכָּל חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא", וְאָז יִהְיֶה בִּכְלָל.
for "better is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come" (Avot 4:17), and then it will be included.
וְאָבְדַן אֻמָּה פְּרָטִית הוּא אִבּוּד מֶמְשֶׁלֶת אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ פְּרָטִי
And the destruction of an individual nation represents the eradication of the dominion of that particular faculty
[עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנִּתְאוֹנֵן קֹהֶלֶת וְכֵן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שִׁילְהֵי שַׁבָּת עַל הַיַּלְדוּת,
[analogous to Ecclesiastes and our Sages at the end of Shabbat lamenting the passing of youth,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: זִקְנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים וְכוּלֵי דַּעְתָּן מִתְיַשֶּׁבֶת וְכוּלֵי,
even though we learned that elderly scholars become more settled in mind,
וּבִשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ה) מֵחֲשִׁיבוּת הַזְּקֵנִים, וְכֵן בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת –
and in Shemot Rabbah (end of Parashah 5) regarding the dignity of the elderly, and in several places—
אֶלָּא שֶׁפָּסַק הַחֶמְדָּה וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע].
merely because the youthful passion and drive of the inclination have ceased].
וְכֹחַ בִּלְעָם בַּחֲצִיפוּת שֶׁלָּמְדוּ מִמֶּנּוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה.),
And the trait of Balaam lay in audacity, which our Sages derived from him (Sanhedrin 105a);
וְהוּא הָיָה רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם, דּוּגְמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קצג עַמּוּד ב),
and he was the foremost among the nations, the pagan counterpart to Moses our teacher in Israel, as taught in Zohar (Part III, 193b);
לְכָךְ הַכֹּחַ שֶׁהִשִּׂיג יְתוּקַּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים,
therefore, the faculty that he attained will be refined and rectified within Israel in the End of Days,
וּבְעִקְבֵי מָשִׁיחַ אָז "חוּצְפָּא יִסְגֵּא" – יִתְגַּדֵּל וְיִהְיֶה בְּמַעֲלָה:
and in the footsteps of the Messiah, then "audacity will increase"—it will become elevated and transformed into a supreme holy virtue.

paragraphs.text: Kohelet Rabbah 7:16:1: ““Do not be excessively righteous, and do not be overly wise”: Do not be more righteous than your Creator. This speaks of Shaul, as it is written, “Shaul came to the city of Amalek.” Rabbi Huna and Rabbi Benaya say: He began arguing against his Creator, saying: The Holy One, blessed be He, said, “Go and strike Amalek.” If the men sinned, what did the women sin? What did the children sin? What did the cattle, ox, and donkey sin? A heavenly voice went forth and said, “Do not be excessively righteous”—more than your Creator. The Sages say: He began arguing from the heifer whose neck is broken, saying: Scripture says, “They shall break the heifer’s neck there in the wadi.” He kills, yet she has her neck broken! If a human being sinned, what did the animal sin? A heavenly voice went forth and said, “Do not be excessively righteous.” Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: Whoever becomes compassionate where severity is called for will ultimately become cruel where compassion is called for. From where do we know that he became cruel where compassion was called for? It is stated, “He struck Nob, the city of the priests, by the sword.” Should Nob not have been treated at least like the offspring of Amalek? The Sages say: Whoever becomes compassionate where severity is called for will ultimately be struck by the attribute of judgment, as it is stated, “Shaul and his three sons died.””

sections.en: One Must Not Join with the Wicked

p: [מח] לֹא יִתְחַבֵּר עִם רְשָׁעִים, וַאֲפִילּוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה,
One must not join with the wicked, even to perform a mitzvah;
וְכֵן הוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּמְּכִילְתָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּהִתְחַבֶּרְךָ עִם אֲחַזְיָהוּ פָּרַץ ה' אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב כ, לז),
and this is explicitly taught in the Mekhilta, as written: "Because you have joined with Ahaziah, Hashem has destroyed your works" (II Chronicles 20:37),
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְחַבֵּר עִמּוֹ לִלְחוֹם נֶגֶד אֲרָם.
even though he joined with him to wage war against Aram.
וְנֶאֱמַר: "בְּנִי, אַל תֵּלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ אִתָּם" (מִשְׁלֵי א, טו),
And Scripture warns: "My son, walk not in the way with them" (Proverbs 1:15),
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם "דֶּרֶךְ" בְּסֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דֶּרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְווֹת.
and everywhere the word "way" (derekh) in Proverbs signifies the path of Torah and commandments.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא לה:) גַּבֵּי יוֹסֵף: "לִהְיוֹת עִמָּהּ" – לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And our Sages stated (Yoma 35b) concerning Joseph: "'to be with her'—in the World to Come,"
וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא רַק קִבּוּל שָׂכָר וְלֹא עוֹנֶשׁ, דְּזֶה אֵין נִקְרָא עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
and the World to Come is exclusively the reception of reward and not punishment, for punishment is not called the World to Come.
רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת יוֹסֵף נָשָׂא בִּתָּהּ וּמֵהֶם יָצָא שֵׁבֶט בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף.
Only that in truth Joseph married her daughter [Osnat], and from them emerged a tribe in Israel and the Messiah son of Joseph.
וְיוֹסֵף רָאָה גַּם כֵּן זֶה שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה יֵצֵא שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת גְּדוֹלָה כָּזוֹ,
And Joseph likewise foresaw that such an illustrious dynasty was destined to emerge from her;
רַק לֹא רָצָה לִהְיוֹת עִמָּהּ אֲפִילּוּ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
nevertheless, he refused to associate with her even for the sake of the World to Come.
דְּגַם שֶׁיְּהוּדָה זָנָה וְיָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ מְלָכִים וּנְבִיאִים, וְהָיָה זְנוּתוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For although Judah cohabited and from him came kings and prophets, and that encounter was the ultimate will of the Blessed Name,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה י:): יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל "מִמֶּנִּי וְכוּלֵי", וּלְמִצְוָה יֵחָשֵׁב
— as our Sages expounded (Sotah 10b): a Heavenly voice declared "From Me did these secrets emerge," and it was accounted as a mitzvah—
אֲבָל תָּמָר הָיְתָה צַדֶּקֶת וְזוֹ רְשַׁעַת, לֹא רָצָה לִהְיוֹת עִמָּהּ בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא:
yet Tamar was a righteous woman whereas this one [Potiphar's wife] was wicked, and Joseph refused to be associated with her in the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 7: “So too with King David, who went with Achish king of Gat (I Samuel 29–30) and did not wish to benefit from the spoil, for this too was contrary to proper judgment. Although he did not share their intention—his intention was for Heaven—it nevertheless says, ‘Do not walk in the way with them’ (Proverbs 1:15). That is: even when you are not inwardly going with them, refrain from them in such a way that others cannot mistakenly think you are going with them.”

rich.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 7

: “So too with King David, who went with Achish king of Gat (I Samuel 29–30) and did not wish to benefit from the spoil, for this too was contrary to proper judgment. Although he did not share their intention—his intention was for Heaven—it nevertheless says, ‘Do not walk in the way with them’ (Proverbs 1:15). That is: even when you are not inwardly going with them, refrain from them in such a way that others cannot mistakenly think you are going with them.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach applies ‘Do not walk in the way with them’ to David's association with Achish. Even an inward intention for Heaven does not remove the need to prevent others from reasonably reading the association as participation in their purpose. This adds a distinct outward dimension to the siman's warning about joining a wicked partner for an apparently good end. The full source also examines removing personal benefit, rather than treating intention alone as sufficient clarification.

sections.en: Each Person Must Know That in Whatever Realm His Inclination Attacks Him Most Fiercely

p: [מט] כָּל אֶחָד יֵדַע שֶׁבַּמֶּה שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ תּוֹקְפוֹ בְּיוֹתֵר, הוּא כְּלִי מוּכָן לְאוֹתָם דְּבָרִים בְּיוֹתֵר לִהְיוֹת נְקִיִּים וְזַכִּים אֶצְלוֹ.
Each person must know that in whatever realm his inclination attacks him most fiercely, he is a vessel specially prepared for those very matters to become exceptionally pure and refined within him.
וּבִדְבָרִים שֶׁהִרְבָּה לִפְשׁוֹעַ בָּהֶם, יֵדַע שֶׁהוּא כְּלִי מוּכָן לִהְיוֹת דַּיְיקָא בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר נָקִי וּבַר לֵבָב.
And in matters wherein he has sinned abundantly, he should know that he is a vessel prepared to become, precisely in that very thing, clean and pure of heart.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כא) שֶׁבְּאֵבֶר שֶׁבּוֹ חָטָא, בּוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה מִצְווֹת;
And therefore they stated in Vayikra Rabbah (21:5) that with the very limb wherewith one sinned, with it he should perform mitzvot;
וְאֵין זֶה רַק תִּיקּוּן לָעֲבֵירָה הַקּוֹדֶמֶת מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, אֲבָל הוּא גַּם תִּיקּוּן נַפְשׁוֹ בִּפְרָט,
and this is not merely a rectification for the prior transgression measure for measure, but it is also the individual rectification of his particular soul,
כִּי כָּל אֶחָד נִבְרָא לְתִיקּוּן אֵיזֶה דָּבָר פְּרָטִי אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ נִתְיַיחֲדָה נַפְשׁוֹ בִּפְרָט וְאֵין לָהּ חָבֵר
for each person was created to rectify a specific matter wherein his soul is uniquely distinguished, having no counterpart
[כְּמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא פַּרְצוּפִים שָׁוִים, וּפַרְצוּף פָּנִים רוֹמֵז עַל צֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים דְּנֶפֶשׁ],
[just as no two faces are identical, and the facial visage reflects the Divine image of the soul],
כְּנוֹדָע מַאֲמַר הַקַּדְמוֹנִים עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת קיח:): "אֲבוּךְ בְּמַאי זָהִיר טְפֵי?".
as is known from the teachings of the early masters on the Talmudic query (Shabbat 118b): "In what matter was your father especially vigilant?"
וְעַל כָּזֶה אָמְרוּ (גִּטִּין מג.): אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל,
And concerning this they said (Gittin 43a): "A person does not truly master words of Torah unless he has stumbled [in them],"
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַמַּכְשֵׁלָה הוּא מֵבִין שֶׁלְּכָךְ נוֹצַר – לְתַקֵּן אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.
meaning that through the stumbling he understands that for this purpose was he created: to rectify that specific thing.

הֲלֹא תִרְאֶה: אָחָז חָתַם הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קג:) וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מב) שֶׁמָּנַע תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן, אָמַר: אִם אֵין גְּדָיִים וְכוּלֵי,

Behold, consider: King Ahaz sealed the Torah, as they said in Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 103b) and in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 42) that he locked school children out of Torah study, saying: "If there are no kids, there are no goats, etc.,"
לְפִי שֶׁהוּא הָיָה כְּלִי מוּכָן לְהוֹלִיד חִזְקִיָּה שֶׁהָיָה מַרְבִּיץ תּוֹרָה בְּיוֹתֵר,
because he was the vessel prepared to father Hezekiah, who disseminated Torah to the utmost degree,
כִּדְאִיתָא סוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא קַמָּא וּפֶרֶק ב דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כ.), וְעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא עַם הָאָרֶץ בְּיָמָיו כִּדְאִיתָא בְּחֵלֶק (צד:) עַיֵּין שָׁם – מַמָּשׁ הַהִיפּוּךְ:

as stated at the end of the first chapter of Bava Kamma and in Sanhedrin (20a), to the extent that not an ignorant person could be found in his days, as brought in Sanhedrin (94b), see there—literally the complete opposite!

paragraphs.text: Shevet Musar 1:4: “Just as, from the subject a person most desires to study, he can understand that he has been reincarnated to complete that matter, so a person must know the root of his soul, from where it is drawn, and what he has come to repair and complete, as the Zohar on Song of Songs says concerning “Tell me, you whom my soul loves,” and so forth. To understand this, he should see which mitzvah his inclination most forcefully urges him to neglect, and strengthen himself to fulfill it. Certainly he has been reincarnated for that mitzvah. To prevent him from completing his task, his inclination opposes him and urges him to neglect it, so as to take him from the world empty-handed. Thus you find among the accomplished sages of the Talmud that, through their great wisdom, they perceived which mitzvah they had been reincarnated to fulfill, and held firmly to it more than to the other mitzvot. As it is said in Shabbat 118b, Rav Yosef asked Rav Yosef son of Rabba: In which mitzvah was your father especially careful? He answered: In the mitzvah of tzitzit, and so forth. Others were careful in other mitzvot, because through their wisdom they recognized what they had come to complete.”

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 21:5: ‘‘With this Aaron shall enter.’ This is what Scripture says: ‘For with strategies you shall wage war’ (Proverbs 24:6). Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Acha said in Rabbi Simon’s name: If you have made bundles of transgressions, make corresponding bundles of mitzvot. Against ‘haughty eyes’ (Proverbs 6:17), set ‘They shall be frontlets between your eyes’ (Deuteronomy 6:8). Against ‘a lying tongue’ (Proverbs 6:17), set ‘You shall teach them to your children’ (Deuteronomy 11:19). Against ‘hands that shed innocent blood’ (Proverbs 6:17), set ‘Bind them as a sign upon your hand’ (Deuteronomy 6:8). Against ‘a heart devising wicked thoughts’ (Proverbs 6:18), set ‘These words shall be’ (Deuteronomy 6:6). Against ‘feet that hurry to run to evil’ (Proverbs 6:18), run after the mitzvah of circumcision, which is between the knees. Against ‘a false witness who breathes lies’ (Proverbs 6:19), set ‘You are My witnesses, declares Hashem’ (Isaiah 43:12). Against ‘one who spreads strife among brothers’ (Proverbs 6:19), set ‘Seek peace and pursue it’ (Psalms 34:15). Rabbi Yochanan interpreted the verse in terms of helmsmen, for Rabbi Yochanan said: A person should always make himself a helmsman, planning how he can perform a mitzvah. Rabbi Benaah interpreted the verse in terms of Mishnah study, for Rabbi Benaah said: A person should always immerse himself in Mishnah study, so that if he becomes blocked, the Mishnayot will open a way for him—into Talmud if he seeks Talmud, or into aggadah if he seeks aggadah. Rabbi Elazar said in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name: Mishnah is an iron pillar.’

paragraphs.text: Sefer Etz Chaim 49:5:1: “Therefore, according to the spark of a person’s soul, he is especially bound to fulfill the mitzvot of that part. For one who belongs to the aspect from the loins upward does not have the mitzvah of removing forbidden fat [as his particular task of rectification], since he does not need it. But if he eats it, he will certainly cause damage; nevertheless, he will not initially be reincarnated for this. Therefore the early masters, who knew where their spark depended, attached themselves to certain mitzvot more than to others. One who understands will understand. [Gloss—Tzemach: This is the meaning of their question: In what was your father especially careful?]”

paragraphs.text: Gittin 43a: ‘Rabbah bar Rav Huna then had a spokesman stand beside him and expounded: ‘And this stumbling block is under your hand’—a person does not arrive at an understanding of words of Torah unless he has first stumbled over them. Although they said that one who betroths half a woman has not effected a betrothal, the betrothal of a woman who is half a slave and half free is valid. Why? In the former case he left part out of his acquisition; in the latter he left nothing out of his acquisition.’

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 16:5: “The moment of the inclination’s enticement between one spiritual level and another is the descent that the righteous undergo for the sake of ascent, as is known concerning “A righteous person falls seven times and rises.” This was the meaning of Rephidim after the splitting of the sea, when they were proceeding to the giving of the Torah, a higher level. When a person succeeds in overcoming it immediately, the descent is scarcely felt at all: he falls for only a moment and rises at once. There is only a momentary slackening; he immediately remembers, takes it to heart, and strengthens himself like a lion for Hashem’s service. The greater the subsequent ascent, however, the greater the preceding descent. For a great ascent the inclination grows stronger, one corresponding to the other, and the power that overcomes it is correspondingly greater.”

paragraphs.text: What the stumbling can restore
The return after failure can bring Torah into the heart with a stronger desire than before.

rich.text: The return after failure can bring Torah into the heart with a stronger desire than before.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 6: “The Holy One, blessed be He, then showed him the clarifications and suffering he would still need to undergo, and promised him concerning them, ‘I will guard you wherever you go and return you to this land.’ ‘I will return you’ is an expression of restoring a lost thing. For a person does not truly grasp words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them (Gittin 43a): through the stumbling that happens to a person, the words of Torah enter his heart with a greater desire than before. This is ‘I will return you’—an expression of teshuvah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach reads Hashem's promise to return Yaakov as both the restoration of something lost and teshuvah. The same statement about learning through stumbling is explained through an increased desire that brings the Torah into the heart. This identifies a positive result of the repair described here: a deeper attachment to the very Torah in which one stumbled. The subject is the return from a stumbling that occurred, not an instruction to seek one.

sections.en: Concerning All Manner of Salvations Granted by the Blessed Name to Man

p: [נ] עַל כָּל מִינֵי יְשׁוּעוֹת שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָאָדָם יֵשׁ "בְּעִתָּהּ" וַ"אֲחִישֶׁנָּה": זָכוּ – "אֲחִישֶׁנָּה", לֹא זָכוּ – "בְּעִתָּהּ" (סַנְהֶדְרִין צח.).

Concerning all manner of salvations granted by the Blessed Name to man, there exists "in its time" (be'itah) and "I will hasten it" (achishenah) (Isaiah 60:22): if they merit—"I will hasten it"; if they do not merit—"in its time" (Sanhedrin 98a).
וּ"בְעִתָּהּ" הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁכְּבָר חָסֵר לוֹ הַדָּבָר וְהוּא צָמֵא וּמִשְׁתּוֹקֵק וְנִצְרָךְ לָהּ
And "in its time" means when the matter is already acutely lacking to him and he is thirsty, yearning, and in desperate need of it

[וְכֵן הוּא "בְּעִתָּהּ" לְעִנְיַן בִּיאַת מָשִׁיחַ, כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ הַכֹּל צְמֵאִים לִישׁוּעָתוֹ וְלֹא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם עֵצָה אַחֶרֶת לִישׁוּעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמוּבָן לַמַּשְׂכִּיל כַּמָּה מַאֲמָרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בָּזֶה].

[and likewise is "in its time" regarding the advent of the Messiah, when all will be thirsting for his salvation and no other remedy remains for Israel's deliverance, as understood to the wise from numerous rabbinic teachings].
וַ"אֲחִישֶׁנָּה" הַיְינוּ "טֶרֶם יִקְרָאוּ", שֶׁמַּקְדִּים רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה.
Whereas "I will hasten it" corresponds to "Before they call I will answer" (Isaiah 65:24), wherein He prepares the cure prior to the blow.
וְזֶה שֶׁרָמַז רָבָא לְרַב עִילִישׁ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קלג:) בַּמֶּה שֶׁקָּרָא עָלָיו "בְּעִתָּהּ אֲחִישֶׁנָּה",
And this is what Rava hinted to Rav Ilish (Bava Batra 133b) when applying the verse "in its time I will hasten it" to him,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לַ"אֲחִישֶׁנָּה",
meaning that he did not merit "I will hasten it,"
אֲבָל עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְ"בְעִתָּהּ" – לָזֶה זוֹכֶה כָּל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אַף הַלֹּא זָכָה,
but at any rate to "in its time"—to this every soul among Israel merits, even one who has not otherwise merited;
שֶׁ"בְּעִתָּהּ" מַזְמִין לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַיְשׁוּעָה.
for "in its time" the Blessed Name unfailingly provides the salvation.
וְאִם יִרְאֶה שֶׁאֵין מַזְמִין, זֶה לְאוֹת שֶׁעֲדַיִן אֵין צָרִיךְ לָהּ וְיוּכַל לִהְיוֹת זוּלָתָהּ:
And if one perceives that He does not provide it, this serves as a sign that he does not truly need it yet, and is capable of enduring without it.

paragraphs.text: The answer already being prepared
Yitzchak's prayer and Rivkah's arrival illustrate help arranged before the request reaches expression.

rich.text: Yitzchak's prayer and Rivkah's arrival illustrate help arranged before the request reaches expression.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Chayei Sarah 4: “‘Yitzchak had come from coming,’ and so forth; ‘Yitzchak went out to converse,’ and so forth; ‘he saw, and behold,’ and so forth. Yitzchak was the root of all forms of fear in the world, even in refraining from action, as it is written, ‘He dwelt in the land of the Negev’—dried of every craving. Avraham our father recognized this quality in Yitzchak's soul and knew his great fear of taking any positive action, so he sent his servant to arrange a match for him. In truth, this was from Hashem, for the time had come for Yitzchak our father to marry. Yitzchak too began to awaken inwardly to ‘He did not create it for emptiness,’ and so forth. Yet because he feared taking practical action, he went out to converse in the field and pray that Hashem help him and bring him his match, for there is a person whose match comes to him (Moed Katan 18b). He was answered immediately in his prayer: ‘He raised his eyes,’ and so forth, for ‘Before they call, I answer.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach applies ‘Before they call, I answer’ to Yitzchak: Avraham has already sent his servant while Yitzchak is only now becoming inwardly ready to ask. His prayer and the arrival of the answer meet. This illustrates the siman's account of anticipatory help through an actual biblical narrative. The passage does not make the timing of an immediate answer a test of another petitioner's worth.

sections.en: All of Man's Self-effort in Breaking the Inclination Regarding Bodily Desires Is Called Mere…

p: [נא] כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם בִּשְׁבִירַת הַיֵּצֶר בַּתַּאֲווֹת נִקְרָא חֵן וְיוֹפִי לְבַד, שֶׁהוּא שֶׁקֶר וָהֶבֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ קִיּוּם לָעַד,
All of man's self-effort in breaking the inclination regarding bodily desires is called mere grace and beauty, which is deceitful and vain, possessing no eternal endurance;
כִּי הַיֵּצֶר מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל יוֹם, וְאוּלַי מָחָר לֹא יְנַצְּחֶנּוּ.
for the evil inclination renews its strength every day, and perhaps tomorrow he will not overcome it.
רַק הָעִיקָּר לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּעֶזְרוֹ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִבְטָח נֶאֱמָן, כִּי גוֹאֲלוֹ חָי.
Rather, the essential foundation is to plead before the Blessed Name to be his assistance, which constitutes a steadfast refuge, for his Redeemer lives (cf. Job 19:25).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ.): "שֶׁקֶר הַחֵן" – זֶה יוֹסֵף
And this is what they said (Sanhedrin 20a): "'Grace is deceitful' (Proverbs 31:30)—this refers to Joseph"
[אֵינוֹ יוֹפִי גָּמוּר, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה לו:) שֶׁיָּצְאוּ טִפִּין, לָכֵן נִקְרָא שֶׁקֶר],
[for it was not an absolute flawlessness, as our Sages stated in Sotah 36b that drops of seed emerged from his fingernails; therefore it was termed deceitful],
"וְהֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי" – זֶה בֹּעַז, שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם גַּם כֵּן שֶׁנִּתְקַשָּׁה וְהָיָה לוֹ תַּאֲוָה וְיֵצֶר, רַק הִתְאַמֵּץ נֶגְדּוֹ, וּלְכָךְ הָיָה רַק שָׁעָה אַחַת.

"'and beauty is vain'—this refers to Boaz," for they said there as well that his bodily nature hardened and he experienced desire and temptation, only that he braced himself against it, and therefore it lasted only an hour.
אֲבָל "אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה' הִיא תִתְהַלָּל" – זֶה פַּלְטִי, שֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ וּבוֹכֶה עַל מִצְוָה דַּאֲזָלָה מִינֵיהּ,
But "'a woman that fears Hashem, she shall be praised'—this refers to Palti," who went weeping over a mitzvah that had departed from him,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יוֹסֵף וּבֹעַז וַדַּאי הָיוּ רוֹצִים יוֹתֵר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ נִסָּיוֹן;
unlike Joseph and Boaz who surely would have preferred not to have faced that trial;
כִּי הוּא נִקְרָא פַּלְטִיאֵל, שֶׁפְּלָטוֹ וְכוּלֵי, זָכָה לְסִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא וְלֹא מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ:
for he was named Paltiel because God delivered him (pelato), meriting miraculous Heavenly assistance and not merely relying on his own effort.

paragraphs.text: Prayer turns dependence on divine help into an act of avodah

rich.text: Prayer turns dependence on divine help into an act of avodah

paragraphs.text: Yesterday’s success cannot secure tomorrow’s struggle. Asking Hashem for help expresses the dependence that makes lasting refuge possible.

rich.text: Yesterday’s success cannot secure tomorrow’s struggle. Asking Hashem for help expresses the dependence that makes lasting refuge possible.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 7:3: “Nevertheless, God grants His help only to those who seek His help in prayer, as it is said, “The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth.” It resembles the community of Israel’s request, “Return us, Lord, to You,” and afterwards, “we shall return.””

rich.text: : “Nevertheless, God grants His help only to those who seek His help in prayer, as it is said, “The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth.” It resembles the community of Israel’s request, “Return us, Lord, to You,” and afterwards, “we shall return.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The Kislev passage supplies the practical content of the siman’s instruction to seek Hashem’s assistance: one asks for it in prayer. Its ordering of ‘Return us’ before ‘we shall return’ explains why Rav Tzadok distinguishes enduring reliance from an isolated act of self-mastery. The person still seeks and returns, but does not treat the strength needed for the next struggle as an acquired possession.

sections.en: A Person Must Not Be Astonished If He Sees the Wicked Multiplying in The…

p: [נב] אַל יִתְמַהּ הָאָדָם אִם יִרְאֶה רְשָׁעִים מִתְרַבִּים בָּעוֹלָם וְהוֹלְכִים וּמִתְגַּדְּלִים בְּכָל יוֹם,
A person must not be astonished if he sees the wicked multiplying in the world and constantly growing in prominence every day,
כִּי יֵדַע שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בַּעַל הַכֶּרֶם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פג:), וְיוֹדֵעַ טִיבוֹ שֶׁל כֶּרֶם יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ, וּמְתַקֵּן צְרָכָיו בְּכָל עֵת וָרֶגַע.

for he should know that the Blessed Name is the Owner of the vineyard (Bava Metzia 83b), and He understands the nature of His vineyard far better than man, rectifying its needs at every single moment.
וְהִנֵּה רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צח.) אָמְרוּ שֶׁבֶּן דָּוִד אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיָּבוֹא בְּדוֹר שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ חַיָּיב, דְּיַעֲמִיד מֶלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה.

And behold, our Sages of blessed memory stated (Sanhedrin 98a) that the Son of David may arrive in a generation that is entirely guilty, wherein He will set up a monarch harsh as Haman so that they return in repentance.
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: אֵיזֶה דּוֹר חָבִיב מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת? זֶה דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁזָּכוּ לְקַבָּלַת תּוֹרָה;
And behold, our Sages asked: Which generation is most beloved of all generations? It is the Generation of the Wilderness, because they merited receiving the Torah;
וְכֵן עַל דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמְרוּ (מוֹעֵד קָטָן ט.) שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׂרוּ לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁזָּכוּ לְבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ;

and likewise regarding the generation of King Solomon, peace be upon him, they said (Moed Katan 9a) that they were assured life in the World to Come because they merited the construction of the Holy Temple;
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ וַדַּאי יִהְיֶה חָבִיב,
and it goes without saying that the generation of the Messiah will certainly be beloved,
וְאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֻּלּוֹ חַיָּיב וְיִתְהַפְּכוּ לְדוֹר חָבִיב עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְבִיאֵם לִתְשׁוּבָה,
yet it is possible that it will be entirely guilty and subsequently be transformed into a beloved generation through the Blessed Name bringing them to repentance;
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתָם מִמָּקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת.
and perforce the primordial root of their souls stems from a loftier source than all other generations.
דְּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָם בְּעֶצֶם,
For in truth, all sins of Israel are not part of their essential nature,
רַק הִמְשִׁילוּם רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.) לְאָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי חִילְפֵי,
but our Sages compared them (Sanhedrin 44a) to a myrtle standing among briers,
וְלָכֵן הֵם הַיִּסּוּרִים עַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא שֶׁהַחוֹחַ עוֹקְצָהּ;
and therefore the suffering brought on by sin is simply the thorn pricking it;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיִּשָּׂרְפוּ הַחוֹחִים שֶׁסְּבִיבוֹת, תִּשָּׁאֵר הַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה בִּשְׁלֵימוּתָהּ,
but when the encircling thorns are burned away, the rose will remain in its full perfection,
וְאַדְּרַבָּה, שׁוֹשַׁנָּה שֶׁבֵּין הַחוֹחִים חֲשׁוּבָה יוֹתֵר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קפט עַמּוּד ב)
and on the contrary, a rose nurtured among thorns is far more precious, as written in Zohar II:189b
[וַאֲתָאן לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עֲדִיפֵי].
[and we arrive at the opinion that penitents are greater].
וּתְשׁוּבָה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּרֶגַע אֶחָד כִּדְמוּכָח בְּפֶרֶק ב דְּקִדּוּשִׁין (מט:),
And repentance can take place in a single split second, as demonstrated in Kiddushin 49b;
וְאָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְגוֹמֵר", רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צוֹוֵחַ "שׁוּבוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה סוֹף אֵיכָה),

and we plead "Bring us back, Hashem, to You, and we shall return" (Lamentations 5:21), while the Blessed Name cries out "Return unto Me and I will return unto you" (Zechariah 1:3; Malachi 3:7) (Midrash Rabbah, end of Eichah),
וּמִסְּתָמָא בְּדוֹר שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אָז "דִּידַן נָצַח",
and presumably in a generation entirely guilty, perforce the verdict "our side has triumphed" will prevail;

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 9:1: “The essence of repentance is a resolve in the heart alone, for through this one is called completely righteous even if previously completely wicked, as explained in Kiddushin 49b. Even verbal confession, although it is a positive commandment of the Torah, “They shall confess,” is a separate mitzvah and does not prevent the repentance itself, whose essence is in the heart alone: regretting the past and resolving in one’s heart not to return to folly and not to sin again. Although this is not revealed to anyone—not even to the ministering angels, who do not know what is in the heart—it is revealed before Heaven, and the person is truly called completely righteous. This applies even if his sins have mounted exceedingly high: the statement there applies to every completely wicked person, even one who has transgressed the whole Torah. Beit Shmuel and Ḥelkat Meḥokek, in Even HaEzer [38], write that even if he stole and has not returned the stolen property, sincerely accepting in his heart that he will return it is effective.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 13:7: “At the close of Yom Kippur we likewise say seven times, “YHVH is God.” After Israel has repented and the gate of freedom—Binah, the world to come—has been revealed, this unity is mentioned seven times; seven is the number of completeness. This follows “Then you will understand ... and find knowledge of God”: one attains the inward knowledge through which this particular unity is attained, as in “Know today.” Every year Chanukah is a time when anyone can merit to repair his deeds so that they are reckoned as merits. paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah distinguishes the person’s tiny opening from the complete repentance that Hashem helps bring about. This clarifies how the present siman can join a change occurring in one instant with a generation’s eventual transformation. The initial turn is real and should not be postponed; its completion is received through continued return and divine assistance, culminating in the transformation of deliberate sins into merits.

p: [נג] דִּבּוּר שֶׁל חוֹל הַמּוּרְגָּל בְּפִי הָאָדָם וּמַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵיהּ, הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַמָּשׁ אֲפִילּוּ אֵצֶל אִישׁ הַהֲמוֹנִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
A mundane spoken phrase that is habitual in a person's mouth and constantly on his tongue is actual Torah, even for an ordinary, simple Jew;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּרְאֶה הַרְבֵּה בַּתַּלְמוּד מֵבִיא: "דְּאָמְרֵי אֱינָשֵׁי", וְהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
as we often see the Talmud bring "as people say," and it is words of Torah;
וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ז.) הַרְבֵּה: "הַהוּא דַּהֲוָה קָאָמַר וְאָזֵיל וְכוּלֵי, וַאֲמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: קְרָא כְּתִיב".
and in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (7a) multiple instances appear: "There was a certain man who used to say, etc., and Samuel remarked: It is explicitly written in Scripture."
כִּי כָּל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ אֲחִיזָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מְיוּחֶדֶת כַּנּוֹדָע,
For every soul of Israel has a unique grasp in a specific portion of Torah, as is known,
וּבְדִבּוּר שֶׁמַּרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵיהּ זֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ
and in the phrase habitual on his tongue lies the root of his soul

[כִּי הַדִּבּוּר הוּא יְסוֹד הַנֶּפֶשׁ, תַּרְגּוּם "נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" – "רוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסִיקְתָּא: אֵין בֵּין צַדִּיקִים הַחַיִּים לַמֵּתִים אֶלָּא הַדִּבּוּר, זֶהוּ יְסוֹד הַחַיּוּת].

[for speech is the foundation of the soul, the Targum of 'a living soul' being 'a speaking spirit'; and as they said in the Pesikta: between the living righteous and the deceased there is only speech, which is the bedrock of vitality].
וּמִזֶּה יוּכַל הָאָדָם לַעֲמוֹד עַל שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ לָדַעַת מַה עִנְיָנוֹ בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם.
And from this a person can comprehend the root of his soul to discern his specific purpose in this world.
וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא בְּרֵישׁ פְּסָחִים: הַהוּא דַּהֲוָה אָמַר וְכוּלֵי, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדָּן קָאָתֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם:
And similarly at the beginning of Pesachim (4a): "There was a certain man who used to say, etc., they said: infer from this that he descends from Dan," see there.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 23:1: “The eighth day of Chanukah is called “Zot Chanukah.” Although this name is not mentioned among the early authorities, since it is used by most of Israel, it certainly has a place in words of Torah. We find something even greater: the Gemara cites “This is what people say,” and this becomes words of Torah in the Talmud. The root of the name is the passage read on that day, “This was the dedication of the altar”; presumably this has a connection to the holiness of the day.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Rav Tzadok applies the principle here to a name used by the Jewish people, even though that name is not recorded among the early authorities. He connects ‘Zot Chanukah’ to the day’s Torah reading and holiness. The example helps explain what it means to look for a soul’s Torah-root within habitual speech: one seeks the particular scriptural and spiritual content expressed by it, rather than dismissing it as merely commonplace.

paragraphs.text: Poked Akarim 6:8: “All Israel also has a share in the Oral Torah, for even every unlearned Israelite possesses some matter of wisdom related to the Oral Torah, though it is completely concealed within him. Of the future it is said, “For they will all know,” meaning that their knowledge will emerge from concealment into revelation. Therefore the Zohar says that even an ordinary person’s words have substance, and sometimes a pearl is found in a poor person’s basket. In many places the Gemara says, “This is what people say,” and those words are Torah. At the beginning of Sanhedrin it records “A certain person used to say,” and these are words of Torah, as in many other places. Concerning this it says, “Who is wise? One who learns from every person,” for every person has some new matter of wisdom belonging specifically to the root of his soul, which can be learned from him. “You are called adam, but the nations of the world are not called adam”: only in each Israelite is there a particular matter of Oral Torah belonging to the root of his soul. An understanding person can learn it from him even if he himself knows nothing. But “those who seek the Lord understand everything”: from his conversations and speech about worldly matters they can grasp a matter of wisdom at the root of his soul that is concealed within it.”

p: [נד] (מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ)

(From his holy handwriting.) [This section was left out of the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902). The Lublin printing of 1913 restored it from manuscript under the heading "Section 54 is absent in some printings and added here from manuscript."]
עִיקַּר הַיַּהֲדוּת – בִּקְרִיאַת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל.
The core essence of Jewish identity consists in bearing the name of Israel.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "זֶה יֹאמַר לַה' אָנִי, וְזֶה יִקְרָא בְשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב, וְזֶה יִכְתֹּב יָדוֹ לַה', וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֶּה" (יְשַׁעְיָה מד, ה).

As it is said: "One shall say: 'I am the Lord's'; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel" (Isaiah 44:5).
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ רַק מַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁמְּכֻנֶּה בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל – דַּי.
Even if he possesses no virtue other than being titled by the name of Israel—it is sufficient.
וּמָצִינוּ בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כְּלָל גָּדוֹל (שַׁבָּת סח:) גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר בֵּין הָאֻמּוֹת, וּמֵבִיא חַטָּאת עַל הַחֵלֶב וְהַדָּם וְהַשַּׁבָּת וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,

And we find at the beginning of the chapter Klal Gadol (Shabbat 68b) concerning a convert who converted while living among the gentiles, and brings a sin-offering for consuming fat, blood, desecrating Shabbat, and idolatry;
עַיֵּין שָׁם דְּלֹא יָדַע כְּלָל שֶׁזֶּה אֲסוּרָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְשַׁבָּת.
see there, for he did not even know that these were forbidden, including idolatry and Shabbat.
וְנִמְצָא שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע כְּלָל מִכָּל הַתּוֹרָה, וּבַמֶּה הוּא גֵּר לְהִתְחַיֵּיב חַטָּאת? רַק בִּקְרִיאַת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּי.

Thus it turns out he knew nothing of the entire Torah, yet through what was he an authentic convert to be liable for a sin-offering? Solely through calling himself by the name of Israel is it sufficient.
וּבָזֶה יוּבַן מַה דְּיֵהָרֵג וְאַל יַעֲבֹר עַל הֲמָרַת דָּת לִהְיוֹת יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
And through this one can understand why it is ruled that one must be killed rather than transgress by converting to Islam,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם אֵין עוֹבְדִים עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּשִׁיתּוּף כַּנּוֹדָע, וְכֵן נִזְהָרִים עַל גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים,
even though they do not practice idolatry even in associative form (shituf), and likewise avoid forbidden sexual unions and bloodshed,
וְאֵין כּוֹפִין כְּלָל עַל אוֹתָן שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת דְּיֵהָרֵג וְאַל יַעֲבֹר.
so that they do not coerce him at all regarding the classical three cardinal sins of martyrdom.
אֲבָל הֲמָרַת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד, זֶה שָׁקוּל כְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ וּכְנֶגֶד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, וְעַיֵּין בָּרַדְבַּ"ז מִזֶּה.
Yet the renunciation of the name of Israel alone is equivalent to the entire Torah and balances against idolatry, sexual immorality, and murder; and see the Radbaz on this.

וְלָכֵן גַּם אֵצֶל הַהֲמוֹן הוּא פְּסוּל מִשְׁפָּחָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ מוּמָר בַּמִּשְׁפָּחָה, וְאֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ רָשָׁע גָּמוּר הָעוֹבֵר עַל כָּל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הֵמִיר.

Therefore among the common people it is considered a genealogical flaw to have an apostate in the family, while they are not concerned if there is a wicked sinner violating all biblical prohibitions so long as he has not converted.
וְכֵן דּוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ עוֹבְדִים עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא הֵמִירוּ,
And so the early biblical generations practiced idolatry, yet they never exchanged the name of Israel;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "חֲבוּר עֲצַבִּים אֶפְרָיִם, הַנַּח לוֹ" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ד, יז),
and concerning this it was stated: "Ephraim is joined to idols; let him alone" (Hosea 4:17),
שֶׁהֵם בְּחִיבּוּר אֻמָּה אַחַת וְלֹא נִתְפָּרְדוּ לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִם הַגּוֹיִם וְלִהְיוֹת בִּכְלָלָם:
because they remained bound as one single nation, never separating to merge with the gentiles and be counted among them.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 6:11: “The difference was only in the point within the heart. As the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 32:5), they were redeemed on account of four things. The intent of all four is that they distinguished themselves as a people of their own and called themselves ‘Israel.’ Even though no other distinguishing sign was visible, merely bearing the name and being set apart from the peoples by that name alone sufficed. [Therefore the book begins, ‘These are the names of the children of Israel’: this distinction of the name ‘children of Israel’ alone is the foundation of the Torah.] As the Sages stated at the beginning of the chapter Kelal Gadol (Shabbat 68b), even a child taken captive among the nations and a convert who converted among the nations is called someone who knew the fundamental principle of Shabbat and forgot it. So too with all Israel in Egypt then: because they were distinguished as a people of their own, although in practice ‘these worship idols,’ and so forth, they were considered to know the fundamental principle of Torah in the point within the heart. Knowledge of Torah lay hidden within them; it was merely forgotten and needed to be recalled.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik develops the same name-of-Israel argument through the generation in Egypt and the same case of a captive child or convert. Its concluding description is significant: Torah knowledge is hidden in the heart, forgotten, and needs to be recalled. This helps explain what the siman means by the sufficiency of the name as a foundation of belonging, while the cited case itself continues to recognize obligations and the need to learn them.

sections.en: The Root of Sins Arises from Forgetfulness

p: [נה] עִיקַּר הָעֲבֵירוֹת בָּאִים מֵחֲמַת הַשִּׁכְחָה, שֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב כִּדְאִיתָא בִּמְגִילָּה (יח.),
The root of sins arises from forgetfulness, which resides in the heart (Megillah 18a),
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ זוֹכֵר בַּמּוֹחַ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר בַּלֵּב;
for even if one remembers in the brain, he fails to remember in the heart;
כִּי אִלּוּ הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת זוֹכֵר בְּהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה עַל זֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כֵּן, אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל שֶׁהָיָה עוֹשֶׂה,
for had he truly remembered with heartfelt feeling that the Blessed Name commanded not to do this, it would be impossible for him to do it,
רַק שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר מַעֲלִימוֹ מִלִּבּוֹ, כְּעִנְיַן "שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ וְגוֹמֵר".
only that the inclination conceals it from his heart, as in "you grew fat, you grew thick, etc." (Deuteronomy 32:15).
תֵּדַע, שֶׁמִּצְוַת צִיצִית הוּא לִזְכּוֹר עַל יָדוֹ מִצְוֹת ה',
You may know this, for the mitzvah of tzitzit is specifically to remember through it the commandments of Hashem,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְנָחוֹת מד.) בְּמַעֲשֶׂה דְּתַלְמִיד שֶׁזָּכַר עַל יְדֵי הַצִּיצִית,
and our Sages stated (Menachot 44a) in the narrative of the student who remembered by virtue of his tzitzit;
וְשָׁם הָיָה מֵזִיד וְיוֹדֵעַ, רַק שֶׁעָמְדוּ הַצִּיצִית נֶגְדּוֹ, שֶׁנִּתְחַדֵּשׁ לוֹ הַזְּכִירָה רַק מִן הַמּוֹחַ לַלֵּב.
and there he was willful and knowledgeable, only that the tzitzit rose up against him so that remembrance was renewed from the brain into the heart.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים דְּלָכֵן נִסְמַךְ פָּרָשַׁת צִיצִית לַמְקוֹשֵׁשׁ, שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע עוֹד כָּזֶה לִשְׁכּוֹחַ שֶׁהוּא שַׁבָּת, וַהֲרֵי מְקוֹשֵׁשׁ מֵזִיד הָיָה.

And so the early masters said that for this reason the passage of tzitzit was juxtaposed to the wood-gatherer, so that such an event of forgetting that it is Shabbat would not recur, even though the gatherer acted willfully.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּנְדָרִים (ח.): נִשְׁבָּעִים לְקַיֵּים הַמִּצְווֹת,
And therefore they said in Nedarim 8a: one may swear to fulfill a mitzvah,
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמוּשְׁבָּע וְעוֹמֵד מֵהַר סִינַי – לְזָרוֹזֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ;
and even though he is already adjured from Mount Sinai—it serves to invigorate himself;
וּמַה זֵּירוּז הוּא? אֲבָל הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ:
And what is this urging? It is as we have said.

With the mouth.”

paragraphs.text: Context: The distinction is between accepting the truth intellectually and having it firmly present in the heart so that it governs action. This supplies Rav Tzadok’s fuller explanation of remembering in the mind while forgetting in the heart.

paragraphs.text: Tzitzit bring a concealed connection into conscious service and choice.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Korach 2: “The mitzvah of tzitzit points to this, as stated in Tanna Devei Eliyahu: tzitzit was given after the sin of the wood gatherer. Its words are: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe, ‘Why did this man profane Shabbat?’ Moshe said before Him, ‘Master of the world, I do not know.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, said, ‘I will tell you. Throughout the six weekdays an Israelite has tefillin on his head and arm; he sees them and turns back from his deeds. But on Shabbat, when he has no tefillin, he therefore profaned Shabbat.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, said, ‘Go and choose for them a mitzvah practiced also on Shabbat and festivals’—this is tzitzit, and so forth. This indicates why Hashem gave Israel tzitzit: it is true that at their root they are encompassed by His light. But because Hashem desires human service, He established the possibility of a person stepping outward and experiencing a concealed place. Through tzitzit one brings forth the precious from the worthless: the person serving Hashem brings it out of concealment and returns before Hashem. He then has a share in the service, and the service is called by his name.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef places the same Midrash about the wood gatherer within the dispute with Korach. Israel's connection to divine light at its root does not dispense with practical reminders: concealment makes conscious return through a mitzvah necessary. This develops the siman's distinction between already knowing the command in the mind and remembering it actively in the heart. The reminder awakens a present response, rather than supplying a previously unknown prohibition.

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Numbers 30:3:1: “Oaths, however, serve only to prohibit what is otherwise permitted. They do not apply at all to a matter already commanded: neither to violating a negative commandment nor to keeping it, nor to neglecting a positive commandment, such as “I swear that I will not make a sukkah” or “I will not put on tefillin.” They do not take effect even for fulfilling a positive commandment. If someone swears to fulfill the mitzvah and does not fulfill it, he incurs no liability on account of the oath—neither lashes nor an offering. It is simply permitted to stir oneself to action, as it is written, “I have sworn and shall uphold it, to keep Your righteous ordinances.””
