sections.en: The Blessed Name Gave the Torah Against the Will of Israel

p: [נו] הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נָתַן הַתּוֹרָה בְּעַל כָּרְחָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
The Blessed Name gave the Torah against the will of Israel, as our Sages expounded in Shabbat 88a,
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּיָד חֲזָקָה... אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם"
and so in the future, as it is written: "With a mighty hand [… and with fury poured out] will I rule over you" (Ezekiel 20:33)
[וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה.) קְרָאוּהוּ "רִתְחָא",
[and our Sages in Sanhedrin 105a termed this "wrathful fervor";
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי אַתָּה אָבִינוּ" שֶׁיִּצְחָק הוּא הַגּוֹאֵל עַל יְדֵי מִדָּתוֹ].
and therefore they stated in Shabbat 89b on the verse "For You are our Father" that Isaac is the redeemer through his attribute of Gevurah].
וְכֵן אֵצֶל כָּל פְּרָט, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹלֵחַ לוֹ הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת שֶׁל קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא מֵרְצוֹנוֹ.
And likewise for each individual, the Blessed Name sends him stirrings of repentance and thoughts of accepting the yoke of Heaven against his will.
רַק גַּם לָזֶה צָרִיךְ הַכָנָה וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא קְצָת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם הַכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, וְגָלוּתֵינוּ לְבִיאַת מָשִׁיחַ.
Only for this too some preparation and an awakening from below are required, just as the Egyptian exile prepared for the Giving of the Torah, and our exile prepares for the coming of the Messiah.
שֶׁלָּזֶה שֶׁל מְלוּכָה בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ, הַהַכָנָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא יִסּוּרִין שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ.
For this forced dominion, the preparation likewise stems from the Blessed Name, namely the afflictions He sends.
וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ כָּל אֶחָד לְיִסּוּרִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵרָכִין (טז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב).
And therefore everyone requires afflictions, as stated in Arachin 16b.
וְהַיִּסּוּרִים הֵם גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד הָרִתְחָא מִמִּדַּת גְּבוּרָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And afflictions likewise emerge from the fervor of His attribute of Gevurah.
וְיֵשׁ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא הַמּוֹעִיל לָזֶה, וְהוּא הַיִּרְאָה, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִמִּדָּה זוֹ,
And there is an awakening from below that aids this, which is fear/awe, also deriving from this attribute,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְעוֹרֵר לְמַעְלָה לִמְשׁוֹל עָלָיו בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ כְּמוֹ אָדוֹן עַל עֶבֶד.
through which he arouses Above to rule over him against his will like a master over a servant.
וְזֶהוּ "מָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה", וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַדְרִיכְךָ בַּתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת בְּעַל כָּרְחֲךָ.
And this is "What does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear" (Deuteronomy 10:12), and subsequently the Blessed Name will guide you in Torah and commandments against your will.
וְזֶהוּ מִצְוַת צִיצִית עַל זֶה, שֶׁהִיא לְיִרְאָה כַּנּוֹדָע, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר סוֹף שְׁלַח דִּתְכֵלֶת הִיא יִרְאָה,
And this is the purpose of the mitzvah of tzitzit, which promotes fear, as written in the Zohar (end of Shelach) that techelet represents fear,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא זְכִירַת כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת אַף בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ, כְּעוֹבָדָא דִּמְנָחוֹת:
and through this comes the remembrance of all commandments even against one's will, like the episode in Menachot.

sections.en: The Anguish of Soul That a Person Endures Over the Sins He Committed Is…

p: [נז] הָעָגְמַת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם עַל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁעָשָׂה, הֵם מַמָּשׁ יִסּוּרֵי גֵיהִנָּם עַל אוֹתָהּ עֲבֵירָה,
The anguish of soul that a person endures over the sins he committed is literally the torment of Gehenna for that transgression;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (יב:) דְּהַמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ בָּהּ מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ, כִּי כְּבָר סָבַל עוֹנֶשׁ גֵּיהִנָּם.
and therefore they stated at the end of the first chapter of Berakhot (12b) that whoever feels shame over a sin is forgiven, because he has already endured the retribution of Gehenna.
וּמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה, מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם מַזְכִּירִים לוֹ בְּכָל עֵת עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁעָשָׂה, וּמִתְמַרְמֵר עֲלֵיהֶם עַד שֶׁסּוֹבֵל שִׁיעוּר גֵּיהִנָּם הַמַּגִּיעַ לוֹ עַל זֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And he who is worthy has his transgressions brought to mind from Heaven at all times, grieving bitterly over them until he endures the measure of Gehenna due to him in this world;
וְזֶהוּ הַפֵּרָעוֹן מִן הָעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁנִּפְרָעִים מִן הַצַּדִּיקִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
and this is the exacting of payment for sins that is collected from the righteous in this world;

כִּי בְּעָנְשֵׁי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַמָּשׁ יֵשׁ מִשְׁפָּטִים אֲחֵרִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כח.): חַיֵּי, בָּנֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי לָא בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָא מִלְּתָא אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא.
for concerning literal worldly afflictions other rules apply, as our Sages stated (Moed Katan 28a): life, children and sustenance depend not on merit but on mazal.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
And this is what King David said: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalms 23:4);
וַדַּאי לֹא חָשַׁב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּגֵיהִנָּם לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ד.) דְּקָרֵי לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ חָסִיד עַיֵּין שָׁם,
surely he did not anticipate being in Gehenna in the World to Come, since he referred to himself as pious (Berakhot 4a);
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים לֹא הָיָה פּוֹתֵחַ פִּיו לַשָּׂטָן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אִם חָשַׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא יִגְרוֹם הַחֵטְא.
and at any rate he would not open his mouth to the prosecutor had he worried that sin might cause it.
רַק רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּשֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ בְּגֵיהִנָּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּשֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ בְּעַצְבוּת וּמָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה עַל חֲטָאָיו,
Rather, he meant when walking through Gehenna in this world, walking in sorrow and dejection over his sins;
וְעַל יְדֵי עַצְבוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת וְיוּכַל לָבוֹא לִידֵי רַע כַּנּוֹדָע,
and through sadness the Shechinah departs and one can stumble into evil, as is known;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
and concerning this he said: "I will fear no evil, for You are with me."
"אַתָּה" אֵינוֹ מַדְרֵגַת הַשְּׁכִינָה הַנִּקְרָא "אֲנִי" כַּנּוֹדָע שֶׁמִּסְתַּלֶּקֶת בְּעַצְבוּת,
"You" (Attah) is not the rung of the Shechinah called "I" (Ani) which departs during sadness,
רַק מַדְרֵגַת קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הַנִּקְרָא "אַתָּה", זֶהוּ עִמָּדִי גַּם בְּעֵת הָעַצְבוּת, שֶׁמִּצִּדּוֹ הוּא הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְכָךְ:
but the level of the Holy One called "You," which remains with me even in sorrow, for from His side comes the awakening to feel this remorse.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 247:1: “Since the Temple was destroyed, we have only the lower level of the illumination of the face—that is, the radiance of the face. This is the Divine Presence that went into exile with them, the level of “I.” This means that He dwells within one’s heart: the very apprehension is itself what is apprehended, for the person apprehends that no place is empty of Him and that the whole earth is full of His glory. Glory is the radiance: the recognition that emerges from His lordship and the attribute of His kingship, which rules over all. Just as someone who has not seen a king knows him through his rule, so a person knows Hashem through the whole creation. Avraham our father saw a palace aflame, and so forth; our Sages said that no one called Him Master until Avraham came. The name of lordship indicates the glory and radiance, as is known. I also heard concerning “The owner of the palace looked out upon him”: “upon him” means that He told him, You yourself are also included in the owner of the palace. For the whole world sees this and their hearts are not stirred at all to apprehend that there is an owner of the palace and seek Him. Your very seeking also comes from Me, and your heart is the place of My Presence. This is the meaning of “I.” But seeing the King Himself is the apprehension of “You.” This is prayer, like standing before the King, which takes the place of the Temple sacrifices. Therefore our Sages said that one should direct one’s heart toward the Holy of Holies, where there is actual seeing of the face. This belongs to the one who has prevailed in battle through the two-edged sword of the Shema, which is complete unity now as before the world was created. Through it every evil thing and foreign thought is nullified, and then the person recognizes the One addressed as “You,” beyond recognition through creation and created beings.”

sections.en: In a Matter Wherein a Person Is Completely Pure and Harbors No Selfish Interest…

p: [נח] בְּדָבָר שֶׁהָאָדָם נָקִי מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם נְגִיעָה וְתַאֲוָה, נִקְרָא צַדִּיק לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר
In a matter wherein a person is completely pure and harbors no selfish interest or lust, he is termed righteous regarding that specific thing
[וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַשְׁבָּ"א בְּנִדָּה (יד.) לְעִנְיַן גַּמָּלִין כֻּלָּם רְשָׁעִים, וּבְסוֹף קִדּוּשִׁין (פב.) אִיתָא רוּבָּם כְּשֵׁרִים, דִּלְגַבֵּי זֶה רְשָׁעִים וּלְגַבֵּי זֶה כְּשֵׁרִים]

[as the Rashba explained in Niddah 14a that camel drivers are called wicked, while in Kiddushin 82a they are termed fit, meaning relative to one trait they are wicked and relative to another they are fit]
לְעִנְיַן שֶׁעָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר: "לֹא יְאֻנֶּה לַצַּדִּיק כָּל אָוֶן" (מִשְׁלֵי יב, כא) בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.
in the sense that concerning him Scripture states: "No harm shall befall the righteous" regarding that specific area.
וּלְכָךְ הַשּׁוֹגֵג נִקְרָא חוֹטֵא וְצָרִיךְ כַּפָּרָה, שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁהָאֱלֹהִים אִנָּה לְיָדוֹ, הוּא לְאוֹת כִּי עֲדַיִן אֵינֶנּוּ נָקִי.

And therefore an inadvertent transgressor (shogeg) is termed a sinner and requires atonement, for since God caused it to happen through his hands, it indicates he is not yet entirely pure in that domain.
וּבְסוֹטָה (כח.): בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין הָאִישׁ מְנוּקֶּה מֵעָוֹן, אֵין הַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִים אִשְׁתּוֹ
And in Sotah 28a: when the husband is not free from guilt, the bitter waters do not test his wife
[וְלָכֵן תָּנֵי נָזִיר וְאַחַר כָּךְ סוֹטָה, עַיֵּין רֵישׁ סוֹטָה, כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא תְּחִלָּה מְנוּקֶּה מֵעָוֹן],
[which is why the Mishnah places Nazir before Sotah, to teach that he must first be free from iniquity],
כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּבוֹא לוֹ בֵּירוּר מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם לְשָׁמְרוֹ מֵעֲבֵירָה.
so that clarity from Heaven may come to preserve him from sin.
וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "כִּי כָשַׁלְתָּ בַּעֲוֹנֶךָ" – בָּאוּ לְךָ מִכְשׁוֹלִים בַּעֲוֹנֶךָ;
And so our Sages expounded: "'For you have stumbled in your iniquity' (Hosea 14:2)—obstacles have come upon you on account of your iniquity";
וּמִן הַמִּכְשׁוֹלִים שֶׁאֵירַע לָאָדָם, יוּכַל לָדַעַת דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵינֶנּוּ נָקִי מֵהֶם עֲדַיִן בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ.
and from the mishaps that occur to a person, he can recognize the matters from which he is not yet cleansed in the recesses of his heart.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מא) עַל לוֹט: מִי שֶׁלָּהוּט וְכוּלֵי סוֹף וְכוּלֵי.

paragraphs.text: Examination after a mishap and the final clarification

rich.text: Examination after a mishap and the final clarification

paragraphs.text: A mishap can demand renewed clarification without proving that all earlier sincere service was severed from Hashem.

rich.text: A mishap can demand renewed clarification without proving that all earlier sincere service was severed from Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Pesachim 4: “These clarifications are very difficult and weighty for a person to undergo. They become ‘light’ in the World to Come, when Hashem will clarify all Israel's actions and illuminate them, showing that their actions had not been separated from His will, since in the depth of their hearts they intended them for Heaven. Even a person's good desire will not be lost; Hashem will join it to an act, as stated in Kiddushin 40a: if someone intended to perform a mitzvah and was prevented by circumstances beyond his control, Scripture credits him as though he performed it. Then it will become clear that even the obstruction occurred by His will. Since the person's whole aim, desire, and will were solely to fulfill His will, and God brought about the event preventing him, it follows that this too was for his benefit, refining him again and again. As the Midrash says (Tanchuma, Shemini): what difference does it make to the Holy One, blessed be He, whether one slaughters from the back of the neck or from the neck? Rather, it is to refine His creatures, as it is written, ‘Every word of Hashem is refined.’ All the concealments a person experienced—first thinking one order of service was good for him and afterward another—were only to refine him; he had never, Heaven forbid, been separated from His will.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef examines the nazir who is unexpectedly defiled and begins to fear that his whole original undertaking was mistaken. It distinguishes that painful present examination from Hashem's final clarification, when the sincere intention and even its obstruction are shown as part of refinement. This adds a necessary distinction to the siman's inward examination after a stumbling: the demand to repair is real, while a person cannot turn his present misgivings into a complete verdict about the whole history of his service.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 41:7: ““Lot raised his eyes and saw the entire plain of the Jordan, that it was all watered, before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt, as you come to Tzoar” (Genesis 13:10). “Lot raised his eyes and saw the entire plain of the Jordan” – Rabbi Naḥman bar Ḥanin said: Anyone who has a voracious appetite for sexual immorality will ultimately be fed from his own flesh and blood. Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: This entire verse is comprised of expressions of sexual immorality. [“Lot raised his eyes”] – just as it says: “His master's wife raised her eyes [toward Joseph and she said: Lie with me]” (Genesis 39:7). “And saw the entire plain [kikar] of the Jordan, that it was all watered” – just as it says: “For due to a licentious woman, one is brought to a loaf [kikar] of bread” (Proverbs 6:26). “That it was all watered [mashke]” – just as it says: “He shall give the woman to drink [hishka] the bitter water that causes a curse” (Numbers 5:24). “Before the Lord destroyed [shaḥet]” – just as it says: “It was when he consorted with his brother's wife, he would spill [veshiḥet] on to the ground” (Genesis 38:9). “Like the garden of the Lord” – for trees; “like the land of Egypt” – for seeds. “Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan, and Lot journeyed from the east, and each parted from his brother” (Genesis 13:11). “Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent as far as Sodom” (Genesis 13:12). “And the men of Sodom were extremely wicked and sinful to the Lord” (Genesis 13:13). “Lot chose for himself” – Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra said: Like a person selecting his mother’s marriage contract. “Lot journeyed from the east [mikedem]” – he moved himself away from the One who preceded [kadmono] the world. He said: ‘I desire neither Abram nor his God.’ “Each parted from his brother. Abram lived [in the land of Canaan]” – Rabbi Meir says: You do not have among the cities any as evil as Sodom, as when a person is wicked, they refer to him as a person of Sodom. You do not have any among the peoples as tough as the Emorites, as when a person is tough, they refer to him as an Emorite. Rabbi Yosei said: You do not have among the cities any as beautiful as Sodom, as Lot circulated among all the cities of the plain and did not find a place as fine as Sodom, and these [the people of Sodom] were the most distinguished among them – “and the men of Sodom were extremely wicked and sinful to the Lord” (Genesis 13:13). “Wicked” – towards one another; “sinful” – through sexual immorality; “to the Lord” – through idolatry; “extremely” – through bloodshed.”

sections.en: Torah Is Called an Expression of Guiding the Way (moreh Derekh)

p: [נט] תּוֹרָה נִקְרָא לְשׁוֹן מוֹרֶה דֶּרֶךְ, שֶׁהִיא מוֹרָה וּמְלַמֶּדֶת לָאָדָם.
Torah is called an expression of guiding the way (moreh derekh), for it instructs and teaches man.
וְאֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בַּמֶּה שֶׁמְּלַמֶּדֶת הַחֻקִּים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים, שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם כְּשֶׁלּוֹמֵד סֵדֶר קָדָשִׁים נִקְרָא עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה;
And it does not merely mean that it teaches statutes and laws, for even when studying sacrificial orders (Kodashim) one is engaged in Torah;
רַק כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּמִּדְרָשׁ אֵיכָה (פְּתִיחָה ב): "הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ מַחֲזִירוֹ לְמוּטָב".
but as our Sages stated in the Midrash on Eichah (Petichta 2): "The illumination within it returns him to good."
וְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה
And the illumination of the Torah
[הוּא אַגּוֹנֵי וּמַצּוֹלֵי מִן הַחֵטְא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (כא.), וְזֶהוּ מַחֲזִיר לְמוּטָב]
[it shields and saves from sin, as they said in Sotah (21a), and this is 'returns him to good']
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי מַיְמִינִים בָּהּ, שֶׁהוּא סַמָּא דְחַיֵּי, וְחַיִּים וְאוֹר הַכֹּל אֶחָד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי עִמְּךָ מְקוֹר חַיִּים, בְּאוֹרְךָ נִרְאֶה אוֹר".

is achieved only by those who engage it on the right side, for it is an elixir of life, and life and light are one, as written: "For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light do we see light" (Psalms 36:10).
אֲבָל שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ אֵינוֹ מַשִּׂיג הָאוֹר, וּמִמֵּילָא אֵינָהּ מוֹרָה לוֹ וּמַחֲזִירָתוֹ לְמוּטָב, וְאֵין עַל זֶה שֵׁם תּוֹרָה,
But when studying not for its own sake, he does not attain the light, and consequently it does not guide him or return him to good, nor does the true title of Torah apply to it,
רַק הוּא בִּכְלַל "פִּטְטַיָּא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא" דְּאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (סוֹף בְּרָכוֹת) דְּטָבִין.
but rather it belongs to "idle chatter of the Torah" which the Yerushalmi (end of Berakhot) praises as beneficial.
וּלְכָךְ אָנוּ מְבָרְכִין "לַעֲסוֹק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה" וְלֹא "בַּתּוֹרָה", דְּמַאן סָפֵין וּמַאן רָקֵיעַ לִהְיוֹת בָּטוּחַ שֶׁיַּעֲסוֹק בָּהּ;
And therefore we formulate the blessing "to engage in the words of Torah" and not "in Torah," for who is worthy to be confident that he will truly engage in its essence;
רַק עַל כָּל פָּנִים הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּפִטְטַיָּא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, שֶׁאוֹתָם הַדִּבּוּרִים הֵם תּוֹרָה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
rather at any rate they are words of Torah and conversational Torah talk, those very words being Torah elsewhere.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצְוָה, וּמְבָרֵךְ "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ", שֶׁמַּכְנִיס קְדוּשָּׁה בַּלֵּב כְּכָל הַמִּצְווֹת.
And this is likewise a mitzvah over which one recites "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us," instilling holiness into the heart like all commandments.
וְהוּא נִלְמָד מִצִּיוּוּי "וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם", שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּיוֹמָא (יט:): וְלֹא בִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים;
And it is derived from the command "and you shall speak of them," which our Sages expounded in Yoma 19b: "and not of idle matters";
וַהֲרֵי זֶה מִצְוָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ לְדַבֵּר דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, רַק רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר אֲפִילּוּ דִּבּוּרִים שֶׁאֵינָם אֶלָּא לְאַפּוֹקֵי דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים.
and this is a mitzvah in its own right to speak words of Torah, meaning even speech aimed merely at avoiding idle chatter.
וּלְכָךְ אוֹמְרִים אַחַר כָּךְ "וְהַעֲרֶב נָא וְגוֹמֵר", מְבַקְּשִׁים עַל עֵסֶק לִשְׁמָהּ עַל יְדֵי הַהַעֲרָבָה וּמִיתּוּק שֶׁל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָתְךָ בְּפִינוּ,
And therefore we pray immediately afterward "And make sweet, etc.," beseeching to attain study for its own sake through the sweetness and pleasantness of the words of Your Torah in our mouth,
וְיִתְגַּבֵּר הַחֵשֶׁק עַד שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַגִּיעַ אַחַר כָּךְ לְמַדְרֵגַת לוֹמְדֵי "תוֹרָתְךָ" [וְלֹא "דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָתְךָ"],
so that our desire will intensify until we subsequently attain the rank of those who study "Your Torah" [and not merely "the words of Your Torah"],
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים נ:) שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ בָּא לִשְׁמָהּ:
as stated (Pesachim 50b) that from learning not for its own sake one comes to learn for its own sake.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 1: “This is also the meaning of the Gemara (Bava Metzia 44a): in his youth Rabbi taught his son Rabbi Shimon, ‘Silver acquires gold,’ and in his old age, ‘Gold acquires silver.’ In a person's youth there is great desire and longing for words of Torah, through which he acquires the gold: true words of Torah are called gold, while silver signifies desire and longing. In old age, however, a person must ask that his desire for words of Torah not depart, for all his powers of desire weaken. He therefore changed it to ‘Gold acquires silver’: this is a prayer to Hashem that words of Torah bring into his heart the desire for still more Torah. It is like a person already satisfied with food, who nevertheless desires to eat more when a good dish is brought before him. So it is with words of Torah. This is our daily prayer, ‘Hashem our God, please make the words of Your Torah sweet in our mouths’: that the Torah become sweet to us, so that we continually desire it more. This explains ‘You shall eat, eating and being satisfied’ (Joel 2:26): the doubled expression teaches that eating itself brings further desire. It is a parable for words of Torah, as explained.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach explains the very prayer cited here through a reciprocal movement: desire acquires Torah, and Torah in turn renews desire. Its interpretation of silver and gold distinguishes the energy of beginning from the need to keep that energy alive after acquiring knowledge. This explains why the siman's prayer for sweetness is part of the transition toward learning for its own sake, rather than a request for pleasantness detached from further service.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 3:2: “Nevertheless, the counsel is, “Feed him,” for “you are heaping coals upon his head”: ultimately the words of Torah will benefit the person. Although the evil inclination supposes that it will draw nourishment from Torah studied for ulterior motives, a person should still always engage in it, for from study for ulterior motives one comes to study for its own sake. The Midrash says, “If only they had abandoned Me but kept My Torah, for through occupying themselves with it, the light within it would have brought them back to the good”—that is, they would come to study for its own sake, as explained concerning Rosh Chodesh Kislev. This is as we explained concerning the statements, “Bring water to meet the thirsty” and “Let everyone who is thirsty go to the water”: when the student is worthy, the teacher should go to him; otherwise, “Let everyone who is thirsty go to the water.” Although a teacher is not obliged to teach an unworthy student, Scripture counsels the student himself to go to the water, for from study for ulterior motives he will come to study for its own sake, and the light within it brings him back to the good.”

וְכֵן אֲפִילּוּ מוֹכִיחוֹ וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִצְטַעֵר, הוּא הָרְצוּעָה מַרְדּוּת לוֹ עַל עֲוֹנוֹ
and likewise even if one rebukes him and he feels pain from it, that person serves as the chastising rod for his sin
[כִּי גַּם הַבּוּשָׁה וְהַצַּעַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם בַּעֲוֹנוֹ כְּשֶׁמּוֹכִיחִין אוֹתוֹ, גַּם זֶה הוּא לְיִסּוּרִין עַל עֲוֹנוֹ].
[for the shame and sorrow a person feels over his sin when rebuked also counts toward suffering for his iniquity].
וְלָכֵן יֵשׁ לָאָדָם לִיזָּהֵר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא נָקִי בָּזֶה,
Therefore, a person must be vigilant that he himself remains completely clear in this,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּפָקַדְתִּי אֶת דְּמֵי יִזְרְעֶאל עַל בֵּית יֵהוּא", וְכֵן נֶאֱמַר גַּבֵּי בַּעְשָׁא, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִּׁ"י;
as it is written: "And I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu" (Hosea 1:4), and likewise regarding Baasha, see Rashi there;
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר: "הִתְקוֹשְׁשׁוּ וָקוֹשּׁוּ" – קְשׁוֹט עַצְמְךָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ קְשׁוֹט אֲחֵרִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בָּבָא מְצִיעָא קז:), דִּבְלָאו הָכִי נֶעֱנָשׁ עַל כָּךְ.
and therefore it is said: "Gather yourselves together and assemble" (Zephaniah 2:1)—first adorn yourself and only then adorn others (Bava Metzia 107b), for otherwise one is punished for doing so.
וְיִסּוּרִין הַבָּאִים לְאַחֵר עַל יָדוֹ שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ, אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְבִיאָם אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי מִי שֶׁנָּקִי בַּדָּבָר,
And suffering brought upon another unintentionally is brought by the Holy One only through someone who is personally pure in that matter,
כִּי אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹצֶה לְהָבִיא תַּקָּלָה לְאִישׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
for the Holy One does not desire to bring a stumbling block to any Jew

[אִם לֹא שֶׁגַּם לוֹ יֵשׁ מִשְׁפָּט בָּזֶה שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל הָעוֹנֶשׁ עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּעֱנַשׁ זֶה עַל יָדוֹ, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַכּוֹת (י:): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַזְמִינָם לְפוּנְדָּק זֶה וְכוּלֵי וְזֶה וְכוּלֵי].
[unless he too faces a heavenly judgment to receive punishment for causing the other's penalty, as they said in Makkot 10b: the Holy One arranges them at the same inn, etc.]
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה: כְּשֶׁאֵין הָאִישׁ מְנוּקֶּה מֵעָוֹן, אֵין הַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִים אִשְׁתּוֹ:
And therefore they stated in Sotah: when the husband is not free from iniquity, the testing waters do not check his wife.

paragraphs.text: Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:219: “It is possible to explain “Do not be a witness against your fellow without cause” as referring to testifying against him about transgressions in which you too are afflicted like him; for that reason he is called your fellow. The next words support this: “Do not say, As he has done to me, so I will do to him.” Although it is a mitzvah to expose those who sin against their souls and the hypocrites, a sinner must not publicize someone whose wickedness is like his own. For his intention in revealing the other’s secrets is not good, but to rejoice in his misfortune. Secondly, how can he fail to be ashamed to mention the disgrace of those deeds in another when he himself still holds to them? It is said, “I will visit the blood of Yizreel upon the house of Yehu.” Thus, although Yehu performed a mitzvah by destroying the house of Achav, he bore his guilt, because he too was greatly sinful.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef extends the parapet beyond physical construction to responsibility for the effects of one's avodah on another person. This sharpens Rav Tzadok's demand to correct oneself before correcting others: even an act presented as religious service needs a safeguard against causing another person's fall. The other's need for correction does not by itself justify the manner of rebuke.

sections.en: The Priests Are Termed "Holy"

p: [סא] הַכֹּהֲנִים נִקְרְאוּ קְדוֹשִׁים,
The priests are termed "holy,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיִּבָּדֵל אַהֲרֹן לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כג, יג),
as it is written: "And Aaron was set apart, that he should be sanctified" (I Chronicles 23:13),
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְאֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהִקְרִיב אֵלָיו" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טז, ה).
and it is said: "even him whom He has chosen will He cause to come near unto Him" (Numbers 16:5).
וּבְכָל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ,
And throughout all of his descendants after him this spiritual level exists,
רַק שֶׁחֲלוּקִים בֵּין מְעַט וְרַב, עַד אַהֲרֹן שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית מַדְרֵגַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה.
differing only in degree between less and more, culminating in Aaron who represents the ultimate peak of the level of holiness.
וְלָכֵן הָעֲבוֹדָה לַכֹּהֲנִים,
Therefore the Temple service is entrusted to the priests,
וְכֵן רִבָּה בָּהֶן הַכָּתוּב מִצְווֹת יְתֵירוֹת,
and likewise Scripture multiplied for them additional, specific commandments,
כִּי הַמִּצְווֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת הֵם הַנּוֹתְנִים קְדוּשָּׁה בָּאָדָם,
for practical commandments of action are what infuse holiness into a person,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין: "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ",
as we say in the blessing: "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us,"
וְנֶאֱמַר: "קַדְּשֵׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ",
and as we say: "Sanctify us with Your commandments,"
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת כָּל מִצְוֹתָי וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טו, מ).
and as it is written: "and do all My commandments, and be holy unto your God" (Numbers 15:40).
וּלְכָךְ: כֹּהֲנִים זְרִיזִים בְּמַעֲשֶׂה – הִכְנִיס הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּהֶם מִדָּה זוֹ שֶׁל זְרִיזוּת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה כְּדֵי לְהַכְנִיס קְדוּשָּׁה בַּלֵּב.

And for this reason, priests are zealous in physical deed (Shabbat 20a)—the Blessed Name instilled within them this character trait of energetic alacrity in action in order to implant holiness deep in the heart.
וְעִנְיַן הַקְּדוּשָּׁה הוּא הַבְדָּלָה מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק לִהְיוֹת עוֹבֵד ה'.
And the true nature of holiness (kedushah) is separation and detachment from all worldly pursuits and lusts, existing exclusively to be a servant of Hashem.
וְנֶאֱמַר בַּכֹּהֲנִים: "לִי" (שְׁמוֹת כח, מא), שֶׁהוּא קַיָּים לְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב);
And concerning the priests Scripture states: "unto Me" (Li), which denotes an enduring covenant for all eternity, as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Vayikra Rabbah 2:2);
וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּכֹהֵן הַיּוֹתֵר פָּחוּת בְּמַעֲלָה, כָּל שֶׁהוּא מִזֶּרַע אַהֲרֹן,
and even regarding the cohen of the lowliest spiritual stature, so long as he descends from Aaron's seed,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין נִיכָּר בּוֹ שֶׁמֶץ קְדוּשָּׁה
— even though not a trace of holiness appears visible upon him—
"הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם וַה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב" (שְׁמוּאֵל א טז, ז),
"for man looks on the outward appearance, but Hashem looks on the heart" (I Samuel 16:7),

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Yisrael Kedoshim 5:4: “for Aharon, peace be upon him, was separated from Israel "to sanctify him as most holy" (I Divrei HaYamim 23:13); within whom resided the ultimate manifestation of holiness and separation achievable in this world; wherefore he alone entered the Holy of Holies, the place concerning which it is written: "And there shall be no man in the tent of meeting when he goes in to make atonement" (Vayikra 16:17); which the Sages expounded in the Jerusalem Talmud (Yoma 1:5): "even the angels whose faces have the likeness of a man"; for there exists a holiness transcending the angels which they cannot reach, reserved for the righteous whose partition is set inside the ministering angels. And Israel is "one nation in the earth" (II Shmuel 7:23), all forming a single complete corporate stature; except that just as within the human body there are primary vital organs containing greater life-force, like the heart which is the wellspring of vitality; and so other organs exist in descending rungs: organs upon which life directly depends, like the brain and lungs; and organs upon which less vitality depends, like the liver, whose perforation does not render the animal a tereifah; removal does so if an olive-sized portion does not remain both at the gallbladder and at the place of the liver’s vital attachment (Chullin 46a); and organs whose complete removal does not impair life, but whose diseased condition does, such as the kidneys (Chullin 54a); and parts that do not touch vitality at all, yet their injury causes severe bodily pain and illness; and parts where injury causes only minor and brief pain, like bruises on the external surface of the body; and parts that feel no pain whatsoever, being like superfluities, such as fingernails and hair, possessing various descending rungs; yet all are an integral part of the complete stature, the fingernail being called a human fingernail, part of the person's body; all receiving vitality from the heart, whence flow the issues of life (Mishlei 4:23); and according to the vitality channeled from the heart, so is the life of all organs and the collective stature!”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim develops the comparison to a single body: Aharon's concentrated holiness serves a people whose different members receive life in different measures. This explains why the siman can affirm a real priestly root even where its outward expression is slight. Difference of function and degree need not mean a separate source of life.

paragraphs.text: Kad HaKemach, Fringes 1:1: “It is well known that Israel’s holiness depends on the mitzvot. This is what the Sifrei says: “You shall sanctify yourselves”—this is the holiness of a mitzvah. The mitzvot through which we were commanded to sanctify ourselves are the commandments received through revelation, for these are the essence of holiness. It is concerning them that our Sages, the sages of truth, instituted the blessing, “Who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us.” Because of these revealed commandments, Israel were called a holy nation at Sinai, as it is stated, “You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.” A people is not called a holy nation through fulfilling the rational commandments, for even the idolaters, who are “a nation bereft of counsel, with no understanding,” occupy themselves with some of the rational commandments. Nor did the Sages institute a blessing over the rational commandments, for the essential blessing and holiness belong to the revealed commandments.”

sections.en: There Are Many Spiritual Virtues

p: [סב] מַעֲלוֹת הַרְבֵּה יֵשׁ, וְכֻלָּם זָכוּ כְּבָר גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת וּנְטָלוּם וְזָכוּ לִבְנֵיהֶם אַחֲרֵיהֶם.
There are many spiritual virtues, and the giants of the early generations already merited and acquired them all, bequeathing them unto their descendants after them.
כְּמוֹ מַעֲלַת שֵׁם "יִשְׂרָאֵל" זָכָה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ וּנְטָלָהּ וְזָכָה לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו
Just as our father Jacob merited the title and stature of "Israel," acquired it, and transmitted it to his seed after him

[וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן כַּמָּה מַדְרֵגוֹת בִּלְתִּי סָפֵק כְּמוֹ בְּכָל הַמַּעֲלוֹת, מִן הַפָּחוּת שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַד תַּכְלִית הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר עֶלְיוֹנָה בְּמַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁהוּא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם];

[and within this title there are undoubtedly various gradations, as in all virtues, from the lowliest person in Israel up to the ultimate supreme peak of this virtue, which is our father Jacob, peace be upon him];
אֲבָל הַגֵּרִים אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לִזְכּוֹת לְמַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב,
but converts cannot attain the virtue of [the name] Israel since they do not descend from Jacob's seed,
רַק כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן פֶּרֶק לו) עַל פָּסוּק "וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֶּה" – אֵלּוּ גֵּרֵי הַצֶּדֶק,
rather as our Sages expounded (Avot DeRabbi Natan 36) on the verse "and surname himself by the name of Israel" (Isaiah 44:5)—these are righteous converts,
שֶׁהוּא רַק כְּמוֹ כִּנּוּי וְלֹא עֶצֶם הַשֵּׁם.
meaning that it is merely an adopted surname and appellation, and not the intrinsic, inherited name itself.
וּמַעֲלַת שֵׁם "צַדִּיק" זָכָה יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק וּנְטָלוֹ וְזָכָה לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו,
And the virtue of the title "Tzadik" (Righteous) Joseph the Righteous merited, acquired, and endowed unto his seed after him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בֵּיאוּר מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג:): "אֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף",
as I explained elsewhere regarding the teaching of our Sages (Bava Batra 123b): "Amalek falls only at the hand of Joseph's descendants,"
וּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת כ.): "בְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף לָא שָׁלְטָא עֵינָא בִישָׁא",
and the teaching (Berakhot 20a): "The evil eye has no power over the offspring of Joseph";
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים", מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקָּרוֹ בְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף.
and even though it is written "and your people are all righteous" (Isaiah 60:21), its primary root is anchored in the seed of Joseph.
וְשֵׁם "חָסִיד" זָכָה דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּנְטָלוֹ, וְכֵן זַרְעָא דְּדָוִד אַחֲרָיו, בֵּית דָּוִד לְבַד.
And the title "Chasid" (Pious) King David, peace be upon him, merited and acquired, and likewise the seed of David after him—the House of David exclusively.
וְלֵוִי זָכָה לְשֵׁם "טָהוֹר" וְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו.
And Levi merited the title "Tahor" (Pure), bequeathing it to his seed after him.
וְאַהֲרֹן וְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו – לְשֵׁם "קָדוֹשׁ", עַיֵּין בַּזֹּהַר רֵישׁ קֹרַח.
And Aaron and his seed after him merited the title "Kadosh" (Holy), see the Zohar at the beginning of Parashat Korach.
וְכֵן שְׁאָר מַעֲלוֹת.
And so it is with the remaining virtues.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה לְמַעֲלַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַחָכְמָה וּלְשֵׁם "תַּלְמִיד חָכָם", וְלֹא זָכָה לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו,

But Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, merited the supreme virtue of Torah and Wisdom and the title of "Talmid Chacham" (Torah Scholar), yet did not transmit it as a bodily inheritance to his seed after him,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא) שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ שֶׁיִּנָּתֵן גְּדוּלָּתוֹ לְזַרְעוֹ וְלֹא נִתְּנוּ,
as our Sages noted (Bemidbar Rabbah 21:14) that he requested his mantle of leadership be given to his sons, but it was not granted;
כִּי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין מְצוּיִים לִהְיוֹת בְּנֵיהֶם תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (פא.),
for with Torah scholars it is uncommon that their children naturally become scholars, as stated in Nedarim 81a;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא עב:): כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה מוּנָּח לַכֹּל.
and therefore they said (Yoma 72b): "the Crown of Torah lies open and accessible to all."
וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא מֹשֶׁה "אָב בַּתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי" (מְגִילָּה יג.),
Therefore Moses is termed "a father in Torah, etc." (Megillah 13a),
כִּי תּוֹאַר "אָב" אַף לְשֶׁאֵין בָּנָיו, עַיֵּין בְּפֶרֶק ב דִּבְרָכוֹת (טז:) "אֵין קוֹרִין אָבוֹת וְכוּלֵי, אִי מֵרָחֵל וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
for the designation of "father" applies even to one who has no biological sons in that matter—see Berakhot 16b, "we do not refer to any as Patriarchs, etc."—
רַק הוּא אֲבִי כָּל הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
but rather he is the spiritual father of all Torah scholars throughout Israel.
וַחֲלוּקַּת מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה הוּא כְּפִי חֲלוּקַּת הַמַּעֲלוֹת שֶׁזָּכָה כָּל אַב מִשְׁפָּחָה וּמִשְׁפָּחָה וּנְטָלָהּ לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו.
And the demarcation of the tribal families in the Torah corresponds directly to the distribution of virtues which each patriarch of a family acquired and bequeathed to his offspring after him.
וּמִזֶּה הֵם חֲלוּקַּת הַכִּתּוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: אֵלּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מִדָּה זוֹ וְאֵלּוּ חֲפֵצִים בָּזוֹ,
And from this stems the divergence of pathways within Israel: these master this spiritual quality, and those desire that one;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ עַל כָּל הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים":
and therefore they proclaimed concerning all legitimate halakhic disputes in Israel: "Both these and those are the words of the living God."

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 47:1: “Avraham our father’s faith was manifest in his heart through the intensity of his own effort; that is why he is called the first of the converts. Nevertheless, our Sages said at the beginning of Bereshit Rabbah, Toldot, that Avraham was called Israel: he merited becoming like a native-born Israelite, whose quality is present from birth. This was after the birth of Yitzchak, through whom “your offspring shall be called,” and who was circumcised at eight days. That is, he was good from birth and circumcised for the blessed God before he possessed any understanding at all; this came from Avraham’s power within him. It therefore became clear that, through his own effort, Avraham our father had changed at his root to be this way, as though he were so from birth. For offspring resemble what their parent is in essence and at the root.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 1:10: “for even converts joined to Israel are designated by Scripture: "and surname himself by the name of Israel" (Isaiah 44:5), expounded by our Sages as referring to sincere converts. And since the Holy Spirit declared "shall surname himself by the name of Israel," he is truly so designated, though not by natural biological lineage but through an acquired title earned through righteous actions. Nonetheless he is designated thus, and Ezekiel (47:23) foretells that the convert shall receive an inheritance within the tribe where he sojourns, subsumed within the tribe; and this is not its place.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Dover Tzedek addresses the same expression, ‘by the name of Israel,’ and insists that Scripture's naming of converts is true; he also invokes their inclusion in a tribe's inheritance. This guards the present siman's terminology from being mistaken for a denial of the convert's actual inclusion in Israel. His distinction concerns the manner in which the name is received, through birth or subsequent attachment.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:30: “But Israel’s obstinacy proceeds from wisdom, through knowledge that connects wisdom with what is below it and with the powers of action. A person is obstinate only for the honor of Heaven; on the contrary, this becomes the channel through which precious souls emerge from Israel. Therefore “Amalek falls only into the hands of Yosef’s descendants.” Amalek is the root of obstinacy, and the main object of his accusation is Israel’s desires, as the Sages said on the verse “who encountered you.” But his obstinacy opposes the will of the blessed God, while the obstinacy of Yosef’s descendants accords with the will of the blessed God.”

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 20a: ‘Rabbi Yochanan would regularly go and sit at the entrances to the place of immersion. He said: When the daughters of Israel come up from immersion, they will look at me and have children as handsome as I am. The Sages asked him: Is the master not afraid of the evil eye? He answered: I come from Joseph’s descendants, over whom the evil eye has no power, as it is written: ‘Joseph is a fruitful son, a fruitful son by a spring (alei ayin).’ Rabbi Abbahu said: Do not read ‘alei ayin,’ but ‘olei ayin’—rising above the eye.’

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:86: “From the aspect of the Oral Torah, a person bequeaths his power to his children, because the child derives from the father’s essence. Just as the offspring of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov are, from birth, from the womb, and from conception, offspring blessed by Hashem and holy offspring, so it should be with Torah: one who is the very essence of Torah, whose powers are all of this character, should be able to bequeath it to his children. Yet Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, was the very essence of the Torah, which is called by his name, and he did not leave his crown to his children; rather, the crown of Torah lies available to everyone. For from the aspect of the Written Torah, which is Hashem’s Torah, he has no relationship with it that would make it exclusively his, so that he could bequeath it to his children. Only from the aspect of the Oral Torah, which is “his Torah,” would it be fitting for him to bequeath it; yet it is still not completely acquired, for “at first,” and so forth [it is called Hashem’s Torah]. Throughout a person’s life, the same beginning and end remain: at every level where he stands, he is at the end of what preceded it and at the beginning of what follows it. He always still needs labor and effort. With every teaching of Torah, he does not bless over the Torah at the beginning; only at the end does he recognize this, and it is then called “his Torah” retroactively.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 48:2: “Concerning a disagreement for the sake of Heaven, our Sages said: “Both these and those are the words of the living God.” Both are called “the city of our God” and the counsel of Hashem, for the blessed God created different views. Yet from this also emerged the disagreement of Korach and his congregation. The Zohar says that Korach was the beginning of disagreement in the manner of anger. The meaning is as follows: As is known, “the world is built through lovingkindness.” The beginning of creation comes from the attribute of lovingkindness associated with Avraham. This is God’s kindness in drawing forth abundance so that a creature should exist; from this aspect, the flow extends to every creature with the greatest possible perfection. If so, there could be no division into different creatures, for such division necessarily involves one lacking a quality that another has. Therefore, on the second day, the attribute of restriction was created: the left hand that pushes away, opposite the right hand that draws near. This produced distinctions: this creature’s attainment reaches this far, and that creature’s this far. From this came the attainment of Yitzchak our father, who followed Avraham, the first to attain knowledge that there is a Creator of the world. He was not satisfied with his father’s attainment, but sought an additional, distinct attainment. As is known, that is why “God of” is said separately concerning each of the forefathers: each attained something particular and distinct. Yitzchak introduced this recognition: there are different attainments and different paths to reaching God’s truth. Otherwise, one creature and one day of creation would have sufficed. Since God distinguished and formed different creatures, there must be different and distinct ways of praising Him, each true in itself and in its own place. This is the quality of the forefathers, among whom there is no actual disagreement: Avraham’s and Yitzchak’s qualities—love and fear—are both true together, and one must serve God through both. Each is true in itself and according to its level, like the upper and lower waters and the firmament separating them, each fully existing in its own place. But in the children afterward—that is, as these qualities spread—each already contained both qualities, though one quality predominated in one and the other in another. From this came disagreement: concerning the very same matter, one says this and another says that. For they are all also joined and united through their mutual inclusion; therefore they judge the same matter differently.”

p: [סג] הַבָּנִים דּוֹמִים לָאֵם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (מט.): יִשָּׂא בַּת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאִם וְכוּלֵי בָּנָיו תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים;
Sons resemble the mother, as stated in Pesachim 49a: let a man marry the daughter of a Torah scholar, for if [he dies or is exiled], his sons will be Torah scholars;
וְאִילּוּ אִם הוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אֵין בָּנָיו תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (פא.),
whereas if he alone is a Torah scholar, his sons are not guaranteed to be scholars, as stated in Nedarim 81a,
וְנֶאֱמַר: "בֵּן כְּסִיל תּוּגַת אִמּוֹ" (מִשְׁלֵי י, א), וְלֹא אָבִיו.
and it is written: "a foolish son is the grief of his mother" (Proverbs 10:1), and not his father.
וְזֶהוּ בִּזְכָרִים, אֲבָל הַנְּקֵבוֹת דּוֹמוֹת לָאָב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַעֲלַת בַּת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם,
And this rule applies to male offspring; female offspring, however, resemble the father, which is the exact spiritual virtue of the daughter of a Torah scholar;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנִדָּה (לא.): תָּלָה הַכָּתוּב הַזְּכָרִים בִּנְקֵבוֹת וּנְקֵבוֹת בִּזְכָרִים.
and as stated in Niddah 31a: Scripture attributed male offspring to the female, and female offspring to the male.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, מִצַּד הָרְגִילוּת הַבַּת אֵצֶל אִמָּהּ, הִיא דּוֹמָה גַּם כֵּן לְאִמָּהּ מִצַּד הַהֶרְגֵּל וְלֹא מִצַּד הַתּוֹלָדָה,
Nonetheless, by virtue of constant habituation where a daughter is raised alongside her mother, she also resembles her mother through habit, not through birth,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (כְּתוּבּוֹת סג.): "רְחֵילָא בָּתַר רְחֵילָא וְכוּלֵי",
as stated in Ketubot 63a: "a ewe follows a ewe, etc.";
לְכָךְ הַנּוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה יִבְדּוֹק בְּאַחֶיהָ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קי.).
therefore one who marries a woman should examine her brothers (Bava Batra 110a).
וּלְעוֹלָם הָאָבוֹת נִיכָּרִים בִּבְנֵיהֶם,
And fathers are forever recognized within their children,
כִּי מַה שֶּׁהוּא סָתוּם בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב שֶׁל הָאָבוֹת, מִתְגַּלֶּה לַפּוֹעַל בַּבָּנִים,
for that which is concealed in the innermost depths of the fathers' hearts breaks forth into tangible actuality within the sons,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי מִזֶּה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
as I have written concerning this elsewhere;
וְכָךְ קִבַּלְתִּי: כִּי הַבָּנִים – מַעֲמַקֵּי לֵב הָאָבוֹת:
and thus I received as a tradition: children are the externalized depths of their fathers' hearts.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Kedoshim 3:1: “The matter is explained by what is said in Eduyot: A father confers upon his son, among other things, wisdom; the influence of wisdom comes to the son from the father. The mother, who is not obligated in Torah study and is not obligated to teach her son Torah, brings fear of Hashem into the son, for she is called “a woman who fears Hashem.” This is what Scripture says: “A wise son gladdens his father, but a foolish son is his mother’s grief.” The son’s wisdom comes principally from the father, and the father rejoices. A foolish son means one who lacks fear of Heaven, as the Sages expounded: “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?”—those who engage in Torah but have no fear of Heaven. Because he lacks fear of Heaven, even though he studies Torah, he is nevertheless called a fool; for the essence of Torah is that it shows a person the way of Hashem. Since he lacks fear of Heaven, it is “a price in the hand of a fool.” Therefore it is written, “A foolish son”—who has no fear of Heaven—“is his mother’s grief,” because she did not instill fear of Heaven in him.”

paragraphs.text: Family resemblance and acquired habits are different influences, each requiring direction in divine service.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:30:1: “On ‘Go forth from your land’ (Genesis 12:1): the Midrash teaches (Kohelet Rabbah on 7:1; Tanchuma, Vayakhel 1) that a person has three names. The first is the name others call him, meaning the character a person learns from others. This is ‘from your land’; corresponding to it is ‘I will make you a great nation’ (Genesis 12:2)—an entire nation from whom to learn, so that learning from others will itself be good and need not be abandoned. The second is the name his father calls him, as the Sages taught, ‘A father endows his son’ [Eduyot 2:9], and ‘a ewe follows a ewe’ (Ketubot 63a). This is ‘from your father's house’; corresponding to it is ‘I will make your name great,’ from Avram to Avraham, ‘a father of a multitude of nations’ (Genesis 17:5), so that he becomes a father to the whole world and the ancestral house is also good. The third is the name recorded at his birth: his inborn disposition, as in ‘one born under Mars’ (Shabbat 156a). This is ‘from your birthplace’; corresponding to it is ‘I will bless you’ within your inborn nature. One must depart from these influences, but the departure is not to the opposite extreme. Rather, it is ‘to the land that I will show you,’ to the place toward which the spirit of Hashem directs him. Sometimes Hashem's will is precisely in the quality that appears deficient, as is known.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah distinguishes the character learned from other people, what is received through one's family, and the disposition present at birth. This gives a fuller account of the siman's distinction between resemblance through upbringing and resemblance through origin. Its conclusion also qualifies the implications: departing from these influences does not mean mechanically choosing their opposite; their proper use depends on the direction Hashem shows a person. Citation correction: “A father endows his son” is in Mishnah Eduyot 2:9. The accompanying reference to Avot in the supplied Hebrew is mistaken; the corrected reference is shown in square brackets in the translation.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 6:65: “But it is known that the children clarify the fathers. As I heard, the depths of the fathers’ hearts and what is hidden within them are revealed in the children. It is also known that every clarification must come through its opposite. Therefore Avraham fathered Yitzchak: his desire was to clarify that Avraham’s lovingkindness was only for the sake of Heaven. The dross of Yishmael, who came from him, was not called his offspring; this was clarified when he fathered Yitzchak, who is called his offspring and in whom the depths of his heart are revealed. Yitzchak’s quality, on the contrary, was restriction and fear for the sake of Heaven. This clarified that the lovingkindness manifest in Avraham our father was also only for the sake of Heaven. He was not like the nations of the world, who are immersed in one quality and cannot change it; in his depths he also possessed the opposite quality, and if it were needed for the sake of Heaven, he would use it as well, as happened at the binding of Yitzchak.”

sections.en: At Times a Person Clearly Sees That the Blessed Name Assists Him and Agrees…

p: [סד] פְּעָמִים שֶׁרוֹאֶה בְּבֵירוּר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְסַיְּיעוֹ וּמַסְכִּים עִם מַעֲשָׂיו, עִם כָּל זֶה אֵינוֹ רְאָיָה כִּי מַעֲשָׂיו יְשָׁרִים בֶּאֱמֶת,
At times a person clearly sees that the Blessed Name assists him and agrees with his actions; yet despite this, it is no definitive proof that his deeds are truly righteous in objective truth;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "מַדְרִיכֲךָ בְּדֶרֶךְ תֵּלֵךְ" (יְשַׁעְיָה מח, יז),
and regarding this it is stated: "Who leads you by the way that you should go" (Isaiah 48:17),
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַכּוֹת י:): בְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ – מוֹלִיכִין אוֹתוֹ
which our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Makkot 10b): "In the path that a man desires to go, along that path they lead him"
[וְאָמַר "בְּדֶרֶךְ", דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בְּסֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי דֶּרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת מ"ח,
[and Scripture uses the word "way" (derekh), which in Proverbs denotes the way of Torah, as I wrote above in Section 48,
כִּי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְסַיֵּיעַ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי דַעְתּוֹ הוֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה;
for the Blessed Name grants assistance only when the person genuinely believes in his own mind that he is walking in the way of the Torah;
וּמַה שֶּׁלָּמְדוּ מִבִּלְעָם, גַּם לְפִי דַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בִּלְעָם, כְּפִי סִטְרָא דִילֵיהּ, הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ זֶה יָשָׁר לוֹ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא, וּמוּבָן].
and what they derived from Balaam was because even in Balaam's own view, according to his side, this path was straight for him, as he was, which is understood].
הֲלֹא תִרְאֶה בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קיג.) שֶׁהָיָה קָשֶׁה לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲצִירַת הַגְּשָׁמִים,
Behold, consider Elijah, concerning whom our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 113a) that the withholding of the rain was grievous before the Blessed Name;
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן אָמַר לוֹ לְאֵלִיָּהוּ: "לֵךְ... וְנִסְתַּרְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר", וְעֲזָרוֹ לְהִסָּתֵר מִפְּנֵי אַחְאָב בְּדֶרֶךְ נֵס,
and nonetheless He commanded Elijah: "Go... and hide yourself, etc." (I Kings 17:3), miraculously assisting him to hide from Ahab through an overt miracle,
וְאִלּוּ הָיָה אַחְאָב מוֹצְאוֹ, הָיָה מַכְרִיחוֹ לְבַטֵּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה יְהוֹרָם לֶאֱלִישָׁע.
whereas had Ahab found him, he would have forced him to revoke the decree, as happened later and as Jehoram did to Elisha.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא" (דְּבָרִים ל, יב),
And concerning this it is stated: "It is not in heaven" (Deuteronomy 30:12);
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעֲזָרוּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּדֶרֶךְ נֵס לְהַרְאוֹת שֶׁהַדִּין עִמּוֹ, לֹא סָמְכוּ עַל זֶה (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נט:),
and even though they assisted Rabbi Eliezer through supernatural miracles to show the law was according to him, the Sages did not rely upon it (Bava Metzia 59b),
שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה.
for they reasoned that the miracle occurred merely because he desired to walk in that path.
וְזֶה הָיְתָה גַּם כֵּן תְּלוּנַּת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: "אַתֶּם הֲמִתֶּם אֶת עַם ה'" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יז, ו),
And this was likewise the complaint of the children of Israel: "You have killed the people of Hashem" (Numbers 17:6);
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרָאוּ הַפְלָגַת הַנֵּס בְּאָבְדָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם חָשְׁבוּ עַל זֶה כִּי "לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא",
for even though they witnessed the staggering miracle in their destruction, they nonetheless argued that "it is not in heaven,"
וְאֵין לִסְמוֹךְ עַל זֶה שֶׁהַדִּין עִם מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נֶגֶד קֹרַח וַעֲדָתוֹ,
and one cannot prove from miraculous occurrences that the halakhah stood with Moses and Aaron against Korah and his assembly,
רַק: אַתֶּם רְצִיתֶם לֵילֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה וּזְכוּתְכֶם גָּדוֹל, וּלְכָךְ הֲמִתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר:
but rather: you desired to walk in this path, and your personal merit was vast, and therefore you brought about their death.

paragraphs.text: An experience of assistance cannot replace the work of bringing one’s desires and actions under Torah’s direction.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 10:8: “But one must not think, God forbid, that because everything comes from the blessed God, one may follow the way of one’s heart without any effort and rely on the blessed God’s help, as in “For You are with me.” Against this, the Tanchuma concludes: “The utterance of the Lord is refined; He is a shield for all who take refuge in Him.” This refers to someone who exerts and strengthens himself, on his own side, to subdue his inclination with all his power; desires to take refuge beneath His blessed wings; looks to God; and prays and pleads before the Holy One, blessed be He. He is then assured that God will not leave him in the inclination’s hand. “He is a shield for all who take refuge in Him”: the evil inclination will have no power over him at all. A shield means that He conceals him from his enemy so that it cannot approach him at all.”

A shield means that He conceals him from his enemy so that it cannot approach him at all.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Lech Lecha explicitly rejects the inference that divine agency permits someone to follow whatever his heart desires. It describes reliance through resisting the inclination, seeking refuge in Hashem, and praying. Read alongside this siman’s warning about apparently confirming miracles, it directs attention back to the character of the person’s choice. Assistance and success are not substitutes for that examination; ‘It is not in heaven’ remains decisive in the siman’s halakhic example.

paragraphs.text: Eliyahu's crisis redirects his prayer
The widow's loss calls Eliyahu toward intercession for the generation, even amid the miracles sustaining him.

rich.text: The widow's loss calls Eliyahu toward intercession for the generation, even amid the miracles sustaining him.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Taanit 3: “When Eliyahu saw the death of the widow of Tzarfat's son, it touched his very life. The child's mother argued that Eliyahu was responsible: because he had come to lodge with her, the Holy One, blessed be He, compared her deeds with Eliyahu's, recalled her sin, and she was punished. This event therefore touched Eliyahu's very life. He understood from Hashem's bringing about such an event that His will was for him to pray that the whole generation repent, so that rain should come after the famine had become so severe. Hashem desired Eliyahu to pray for the whole generation's repentance, for He does not desire the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live. This is the Yerushalmi's meaning: when he revived the widow's son, the vow concerning dew and rain was released.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef follows the same drought narrative into the death of the widow's son. It reads Eliyahu's distress as a summons to pray for the generation's repentance and the return of rain. This supplies a particular corrective within the siman's example: the miraculous assistance that sustained Eliyahu did not end the need to discern what Hashem desired next. The source directs his strength toward the life and return of the people.

paragraphs.text: Tosafot HaRosh on Berakhot 52a:1: ““It follows Rabbi Yehoshua, who says that we do not heed a heavenly voice.” This is difficult: Rabbi Yehoshua said this concerning the disagreement between Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages, and we too do not follow Rabbi Eliezer or the heavenly voice there. But here, concerning Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, we follow the heavenly voice; perhaps Rabbi Yehoshua agrees in this case as well. The answer is that Rabbi Yehoshua’s formulation—“We do not heed a heavenly voice,” because “It is not in heaven”—implies that a heavenly voice should be disregarded in every case. We, however, follow the heavenly voice in favor of Beit Hillel because Beit Hillel were the majority; a heavenly voice was needed because Beit Shammai were sharper. But the heavenly voice for Rabbi Eliezer came only in Rabbi Eliezer’s honor, and [following it] would contradict the verse “Incline after the majority.””

paragraphs.text: Rav Nissim Gaon on Berakhot 19b:1: “Concerning the statement that a heavenly voice went forth and said, “What have you against Rabbi Eliezer, whose view the law follows everywhere?” I have seen two answers. The first is that the heavenly voice did not say that the law followed him in this matter; it said “everywhere” without specification. It is possible that it meant everywhere except this case, or similar cases in which the law does not follow Rabbi Eliezer. Thus the words of the heavenly voice would remain correct and valid. The second is that its purpose was only to test the Sages: would they abandon the tradition in their possession and the teaching in their mouths because of a heavenly voice, or not? This resembles what is written, “For Hashem your God is testing you.” Through all this, the soundness of their tradition became known. This is what Rabbi Yehoshua said: “It is not in heaven.” That is, Hashem’s Torah is perfect and has already been given to us at Sinai; He made known that He does not replace a single word of it. Our Torah contains no deficiency or uncertainty that would require proof from heaven.”

sections.en: A Person Must Surrender His Very Soul to the Blessed Name

p: [סה] הָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לִמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁאִם אֵינוֹ כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – אָז מוּסְכָּם לֵילֵךְ מִן הָעוֹלָם,
A person must surrender his very soul to the Blessed Name, resolving that if his life does not conform to the will of the Blessed Name, he wholeheartedly accepts to depart from this world,
כְּדִכְתִיב: "וּרְאֵה אִם דֶּרֶךְ עֹצֶב בִּי, וּנְחֵנִי בְּדֶרֶךְ עוֹלָם" (תְּהִלִּים קלט, כד),
as it is written: "And see if there be any grievous way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting" (Psalms 139:24),
וּכְעִנְיָן זֶה אָמַר יוֹנָה: "טוֹב מוֹתִי מֵחַיָּי" (יוֹנָה ד, ג).
and in this vein Jonah proclaimed: "it is better for me to die than to live" (Jonah 4:3).
וְזֶה עִנְיַן נְפִילַת אַפַּיִם אַחַר כָּל תְּפִלָּה,
And this is the inner meaning of falling upon one's face (nefilat apayim / Tachanun) following each prayer,
וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר רֵישׁ קֹרַח כִּי נְפִילַת אַפַּיִם הוּא מְסִירַת עַצְמוֹ לְמִיתָה,
for the Zohar states at the beginning of Parashat Korach that falling on one's face represents the surrender of oneself unto death,
וְגַם בַּפָּשׁוּט יִרְמוֹז לָזֶה.
and even in its literal posture it hints at this.
וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָפְלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים שָׁם בְּפָרָשַׁת קֹרַח.
And Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces twice there in Parashat Korach.
כִּי רָמַ"ח אִישׁ "חָטְאוּ בְּנַפְשֹׁתָם" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יז, ג),
For the two hundred and fifty men "sinned at the cost of their souls" (Numbers 17:3);
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ: קֹרַח שֶׁפִּקֵּחַ הָיָה וְכוּלֵי;
and our Sages remarked: "Korah, who was astute, what did he see?";
וְהִנֵּה גַּם הָרָמַ"ח אִישׁ לֹא שׁוֹטִים הָיוּ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁהָיוּ רָאשֵׁי סַנְהֶדְרָאוֹת,
and behold, those two hundred and fifty men were likewise no fools, for our Sages noted that they were heads of Sanhedrin courts,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה) שֶׁהָיוּ בִּכְלָלָם הַשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר נְשִׂיאִים,
and the Midrash relates that among them were the twelve tribal princes;
וְכֵן מוֹרֶה לְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: "אַתֶּם הֲמִתֶּם אֶת עַם ה'", וְהֵם רַק יְחִידִים, וּקְרָאוּם "עַם ה'" לְפִי שֶׁשְּׁקוּלִים כְּנֶגֶד כָּל הָעָם;

and so the scriptural phrase demonstrates: "You have killed the people of Hashem"—though they were few individuals, they called them "the people of Hashem" because they weighed equally against the entire nation;
וְהֶאֱמִינוּ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַעֲנִישָׁם,
and they fully believed Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, that he possessed the power to punish them,
אֲבָל הֵם חָטְאוּ בְּנַפְשׁוֹתָם, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנָזִיר: "חָטָא עַל הַנָּפֶשׁ" – פֵּירוּשׁ מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ.
but they sinned at the hazard of their souls, just as the Sages said concerning a Nazirite: "he sinned against the soul"—meaning he staked his very life.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּדְעוּ כִּי לֶעָתִיד לֹא יְלַמְּדוּ אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ, וְיִהְיֶה מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁ"כָּל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים",
This means that they knew that in the ultimate future "no man will teach his neighbor" (Jeremiah 31:33), and the state where "all the congregation are holy" will be attained;
וְחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁכְּבָר הִגִּיעוּ לְכָךְ
and they presumed that they had already reached that elevated stature
[כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת לוּלֵי שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא הָיוּ עַל מַדְרֵגַת לֶעָתִיד, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה.)],
[for in truth, had not sin intervened, they would indeed have stood at that future messianic level, as our Sages taught (Avodah Zarah 5a)];
וּמֵרוֹב הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּתָם לָזֶה, עַד שֶׁנִּתְרַצּוּ בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁאִם בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינָם בְּמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ – אָז טוֹב מוֹתָם מֵחַיֵּיהֶם, וּמוּסְכָּמִים לָמוּת בֶּאֱמֶת
and out of their overwhelming yearning for this, they consented in truth that if they were not genuinely at that level, then death was preferable to life, and they truly accepted death

[וְזֶהוּ: קֹרַח שֶׁפִּקֵּחַ הָיָה – פֵּירוּשׁ, "פִּקֵּחַ" בְּכָל מָקוֹם בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עָרוּם, כְּמוֹ "אִי פִּקֵּחַ הוּא וְכוּלֵי" (כְּתוּבּוֹת פח.), שֶׁטָּעַם מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ עוֹד].

[and this is: 'Korah, who was astute'—where 'astute' throughout the Sages' words means shrewdly cunning, like 'if he is astute, etc.' (Ketubot 88a), having tasted of the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, and this is not the place to elaborate further].
וּלְכָךְ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ חוֹטְאִים בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה בְּנַפְשׁוֹתָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַעֲלָה גְּדוֹלָה הוּא,
And therefore, even though they were termed sinners on this account at the cost of their souls, it was nonetheless an immense spiritual level,
וּלְכָךְ זָכוּ שֶׁהַמַּחְתּוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם נַעֲשׂוּ צִפּוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
and therefore they merited that their fire-pans were hammered into a sacred plating for the Altar.
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר לְמֹשֶׁה וּלְאַהֲרֹן: "הִבָּדְלוּ וְגוֹמֵר", וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ: "הֵרֹמּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
And therefore God commanded Moses and Aaron: "Separate yourselves, etc." (Numbers 16:21), and subsequently: "Get you up, etc." (ibid. 17:10);
וְהִקְשָׁה הָרַמְבַּ"ן: וְכִי אֵין בְּיַד ה' לְהַצִּילָם וְהֵם תּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה?
and the Ramban challenged: Is it not in Hashem's power to save them while remaining in the midst of the congregation?
אֲבָל לְפִי שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ בְּדָבָר זֶה גְּדוֹלִים בְּעִנְיַן הַמְּסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ, לְכָךְ הֻוצְרְכוּ לְהִבָּדֵל לְבַל יִלְקוּ עִמָּהֶם.
But because Korah's men were towering in this specific virtue of self-sacrifice, Moses and Aaron had to withdraw lest they be struck down along with them.
וּלְכָךְ תֵּיכֶף לְמַאֲמַר "הִבָּדְלוּ" וְ"הֵרֹמּוּ" הִרְגִּישׁוּ בָּזֶה, "וַיִּפְּלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם",
And therefore immediately upon the commands "Separate yourselves" and "Get you up," Moses and Aaron sensed this, "and they fell upon their faces,"
וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר דִּמְסַרוּ גַּרְמַיְיהוּ לְמִיתָה
— and the Zohar states that they surrendered their own lives unto death—
רָצוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּזֶה כְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם:
seeking through this act to match their standard of self-sacrifice.

paragraphs.text: Surrender within the request itself
Prayer can seek a benefit while yielding the decision about whether that benefit serves Hashem's will.

rich.text: Prayer can seek a benefit while yielding the decision about whether that benefit serves Hashem's will.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayera 39:2: “True clarification in prayer is as we find with King David, peace be upon him, when he said (Psalms 139:23–24): ‘Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my thoughts. See whether there is a grievous way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.’ This means: if my prayer is pure, and the good for which I pray will help me increase the honor of Heaven, then I entreat You to answer me and grant my request. But if it is revealed before You that the good for which I pray will turn me away from fearing You and from Your will, then I too do not desire the good You would bestow on me. This is like what the Gemara teaches (Ketubot 83a): a person may stipulate that he will not inherit an inheritance coming to him from another source. Hashem showed Avraham our father, peace be upon him, that He deals with him measure for measure: just as Avraham desires only such good as will increase the honor of Heaven, so Hashem desires the very life of Avraham our father, peace be upon him.”

Hashem showed Avraham our father, peace be upon him, that He deals with him measure for measure: just as Avraham desires only such good as will increase the honor of Heaven, so Hashem desires the very life of Avraham our father, peace be upon him.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov develops the very Psalm cited here into a condition within prayer: the petitioner asks for the desired benefit insofar as it will increase the honor of Heaven, and relinquishes it if it would lead away from Hashem. This illuminates the inward submission expressed by nefilat apayim after articulated prayer. The surrender reaches one's own preferred outcome while preserving the reality of prayer and the preciousness of life, as the paragraph's conclusion about Avraham makes explicit.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 18:3: “When Moshe said, “They shall put a thread of tekhelet on the corner fringe,” Korach immediately ordered two hundred and fifty garments of tekhelet to be made. The two hundred and fifty heads of Sanhedrin who rose against Moshe wrapped themselves in them, as it is stated, “They rose before Moshe, two hundred and fifty men from the children of Israel, leaders of the congregation, those summoned to assembly.” Korach arose and made them a feast, and they wrapped themselves in garments of tekhelet. Aharon’s sons came to take their priestly gifts, the breast and the thigh. They opposed them and said: Who commanded you to take this? Was it not Moshe? We will give nothing; God did not say this. They came and told Moshe. He went to appease them, and they immediately rose against him to confront him before Moshe. “Two hundred and fifty men from the children of Israel”—who were they? Elitzur son of Shedeur and his companions, “these men who were designated by name.” Although Scripture did not identify them openly, it gave their distinguishing signs, and from the verses you can recognize them. To what may this be compared? To a well-born man found stealing objects from a bathhouse. The owner did not want to expose him, so he began giving his distinguishing signs. When asked who had stolen his objects, he said: That well-born man, tall, with fine teeth, black hair, and a handsome nose. Once he gave the signs, they knew who he was. Here too, although Scripture left their identities unstated, it gave their signs, and you know who they were. Elsewhere it says, “These were those summoned from the congregation, the leaders of their ancestral tribes, heads of Israel’s thousands,” and “Moshe and Aharon took these men who were designated by name.” Here it says, “Leaders of the congregation, those summoned to assembly, men of renown,” and “They assembled against Moshe and Aharon.””

paragraphs.text: Taanit 11a:14-17: “Shmuel said: Anyone who observes a fast is called a sinner. He follows this tanna, as it was taught: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the Great says: What does “He shall atone for him for having sinned against the soul” teach? Against what soul did this person sin? Rather, he afflicted himself by abstaining from wine. Is this not an argument from the lesser to the greater? If one who afflicted himself only by abstaining from wine is called a sinner, all the more so one who afflicts himself by abstaining from every kind of enjoyment. Rabbi Elazar says: He is called holy, as it is stated, “He shall be holy; he shall let the locks of his head grow.” If one who afflicted himself in only one respect is called holy, all the more so one who afflicts himself in every respect. But according to Shmuel, is he not called holy? That refers to the growth of his hair. And according to Rabbi Elazar, is he not called a sinner? That concerns one who rendered himself impure.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Korach 1:2: “This was Korach’s error: at the giving of the Torah, it was indeed fitting that the true rectification should come about as it will in the future. This was his claim: “The entire congregation is holy”—they all heard at Sinai, “I am Hashem your God”—“and Hashem is among them.” That is, as it will be in the future, when the Holy One, blessed be He, sits among them and they surround Him in a circle. In a circle there are no differences of level; thus, “Why do you exalt yourselves above the congregation of Hashem?” This is indeed so when the attribute of Atika is revealed, as at the giving of the Torah, when “Hashem spoke with you face to face.” Likewise, the revelation at the splitting of the sea came from Atika, as the Zohar says, “It depends on Atika.” The Mekhilta and the Zohar say that a maidservant at the sea saw what Yechezkel did not see: she saw as did the greatest person in Israel. All were equal, for when the revelation depends on Atika, there are no differences of level. So too at the giving of the Torah: “Israel encamped there,” which Rashi explains as one person with one heart; there were no differences of level, as it is stated, “Hashem spoke with you face to face.” But afterward this level was lost, and this revelation will not come until the future, when the true rectification arrives.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Korach 2:1: “This is what the Midrash Rabbah intimates: “Were they fools? Rather, they sinned against their own souls.” They thought and accepted upon themselves, in surrender of their souls, that if the incense should make clear that despite all this their souls were still not completely purified, then what need had they for life in this world? “And Korach, who was astute”—he was a great scholar in the wisdom of Torah and should have known that “there is no righteous person on earth” and that there are higher levels above higher levels in the chambers of Torah. “But his eye misled him,” because he possessed the holy spirit and saw a great lineage, and so it seemed to him that he would be the chosen one. This was clarified by “They descended alive to the underworld”: even in the underworld they remain in the fullness of their life in holiness. This resembles what was said of Adam: “Lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the Tree of Life, and eat and live forever.” As the Midrash Rabbah says, they remain alive and in existence until now; at that very moment it became clear to them that Moshe is true and his Torah is true. In the future they too are destined to ascend, as it is stated, “Hashem puts to death and brings to life; He brings down to the underworld and raises up.””

Rather, they sinned against their own souls.” They thought and accepted upon themselves, in surrender of their souls, that if the incense should make clear that despite all this their souls were still not completely purified, then what need had they for life in this world? “And Korach, who was astute”—he was a great scholar in the wisdom of Torah and should have known that “there is no righteous person on earth” and that there are higher levels above higher levels in the chambers of Torah. “But his eye misled him,” because he possessed the holy spirit and saw a great lineage, and so it seemed to him that he would be the chosen one. This was clarified by “They descended alive to the underworld”: even in the underworld they remain in the fullness of their life in holiness. This resembles what was said of Adam: “Lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the Tree of Life, and eat and live forever.” As the Midrash Rabbah says, they remain alive and in existence until now; at that very moment it became clear to them that Moshe is true and his Torah is true. In the future they too are destined to ascend, as it is stated, “Hashem puts to death and brings to life; He brings down to the underworld and raises up.””

paragraphs.text: Context: Rav Tzadok’s parallel supplies the interpretation of their willingness to risk their lives, while retaining the error in their self-assessment and the distinction between Korach’s vision and its fulfillment.

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Numbers 17:10:1: ““Remove yourselves from this congregation”—I do not understand the reason for this verse and its counterpart above, “Separate yourselves from this congregation.” God has the power to kill many by plague around one righteous person, leaving that person alone alive, as occurred among the firstborn of Egypt. So too in every plague: three people sleep beneath one blanket, two die, and the one in the middle escapes. It appears that the wrath was going forth to kill the entire congregation as these sinners were killed, because they had followed them—through the opening of the earth’s mouth or the fire that came forth. These are encompassing blows, capable of killing everyone standing there together, unless a second miracle is performed for those who escape. Alternatively, the Holy One, blessed be He, said this in honor of the righteous: as long as they remained among them, He would not strike them. The purpose of these and similar statements is to make known that they need a plea for mercy and atonement, and Moshe is the one who hastens to do this immediately.”
