sections.en: Prayer Is Required for Every Matter

p: [סו] תְּפִלָּה צָרִיךְ לְכָל דָּבָר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּגְזַר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
Prayer is required for every matter, even when it has already been decreed by the Blessed Name.
הֲלֹא תִרְאֶה בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ ה': "הֵרָאֵה אֶל אַחְאָב וְאֶתְּנָה מָטָר" (מְלָכִים א יח, א),
Behold, consider Elijah, to whom Hashem explicitly promised: "Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain" (I Kings 18:1);
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נֶאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁעָלָה לְרֹאשׁ הַכַּרְמֶל "וַיִּגְהַר וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁהִרְבָּה בִּתְפִלָּה עַד שֶׁבָּא גֶּשֶׁם.
and nonetheless it is related afterward that he ascended to the top of Carmel, "and bowed himself down, etc." (ibid. 18:42), praying intensely until the rain arrived.
וַחֲכָמִים דְּאָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (טז.) דִּגְזַר דִּין הוּא בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, לֹא פְּלִיגֵי אַאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ סֵדֶר תְּפִלּוֹת בְּכָל יוֹם.

And the Sages who stated in Rosh Hashanah 16a that the final decree is sealed on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur do not dispute the Men of the Great Assembly who instituted the order of prayer every day.
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא: "כְּמַאן מְצַלֵּינַן הָאִידְנָא אַקְצִירֵי וּמָרִיעֵי? כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי" (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז.),
And that which the Gemara asks: "In accordance with whom do we pray today for the sick and the afflicted? In accordance with Rabbi Yosi" (Rosh Hashanah 16a),
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁהֵם הָיוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִים וּמַרְבִּים בִּתְפִלָּה לִקְרוֹעַ גְּזַר דִּין – זֶהוּ אֱלִיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
means that their intense praying to tear up a sealed decree follows the view of Rabbi Yosi.
וְהוּא מַאֲמָר יְגִיעִיִי, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁאָמְרוּ כֵּן לַהֲלָכָה בִּמְכֻוָּון,
And this was an intentionally formulated halakhic decree, meaning that they deliberately established the ruling thus,
שֶׁרְצוֹנָם הָיָה כָּךְ שֶׁתְּפִלָּתֵנוּ הָאִידְנָא יִהְיֶה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, שֶׁיּוֹעִילוּ אַף לִקְרוֹעַ גְּזַר דִּין דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה:
for their will was that our prayers today should follow Rabbi Yosi, possessing the power even to tear up the sealed decree of Rosh Hashanah.

This illuminates why the promise cited here does not make Elijah's prayer redundant: the prayer itself belongs to the path by which the promised mercy is received.

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 16a:13:1: ““According to whom do we now pray for the sick and the weak? According to Rabbi Yosei.” If you ask: Even according to the Rabbis, do we not pray “Heal us” and the blessing over the years? Moreover, Rabbi Yehudah, who says here that a person is judged on Rosh Hashanah and that his decree is sealed on Yom Kippur, says in the first chapter of Shabbat that one visiting the sick says, “May the Omnipresent have mercy on you and on the sick of His people Israel.” Rabbeinu Tam answers that prayer that someone not become ill is indeed according to Rabbi Yosei alone, but prayer that someone recover is according to everyone: when people will become ill was decreed; when they will recover was not decreed. At the beginning of the chapter “One who vows from cooked food,” it explains Rav Yosef’s statement: “the sick” means those actually ill, while “the weak” means the scholars. Thus we pray that the sick recover, and that the weak—the scholars—not become ill. The prayer in the blessing over the years is as explained later in this chapter: if little rain was decreed, the Omnipresent should send it at the proper times. Another answer is that communal prayer is different, for the community’s decree can be torn up, as stated later. Rabbi Yehudah’s statement in Shabbat can likewise be explained this way, for it resembles communal prayer: together with the individual, one prays for all the sick.”

sections.en: At Every Higher Spiritual Level to Which a Person Ascends

p: [סז] בְּכָל מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלֶה, יֵשׁ לוֹ לַחֲזוֹר וְלָשׁוּב עַל חֲטָאָיו,
At every higher spiritual level to which a person ascends, he must return and repent anew for his past sins;
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן "וְחַטָּאתִי נֶגְדִּי תָמִיד" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ה),
and this is the meaning of "and my sin is ever before me" (Psalms 51:5),
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶאֱמִין שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ,
even though he firmly believed that his repentance had already been accepted;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא לֹא הָיָה עוֹמֵד, וּבְכָל יוֹם הָיָה עוֹלֶה מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה.
nevertheless, because he was not spiritually stagnant, but was ascending each day from level to level.

וְנוֹדַע דִּבְרֵי הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל כִּי בְּגַן עֵדֶן, כָּל עֵת שֶׁמַּעֲלִין לְמַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה, מוֹסִיפִין לְדַקְדֵּק עָלָיו בַּחֲטָאָיו וּלְהַעֲנִישׁוֹ עַל כָּל חֵטְא קָטָן, וְכֵן הוּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.

And the teaching of the holy Ari of blessed memory is known: that in Gan Eden, whenever a soul is elevated to a loftier rung, they judge him with greater precision regarding his past sins, chastising him over every minute flaw, and so it is in this world.
וְזֶהוּ טַעַם "יְרִידָה לְצוֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה" הַמְּבוֹאָר בַּסְּפָרִים,
And this is the rationale for "descent for the sake of ascent" expounded in holy works:
שֶׁעֵת שֶׁמְּדַקְדְּקִים בּוֹ הוּא עֵת הַיְּרִידָה,
the period when they scrutinize him with exacting judgment is the time of descent,
וְאָז צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה,
and then he requires renewed repentance,
וְעָגְמַת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מֵחֲטָאָיו הוּא הָעוֹנֶשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת נ"ז,
and the anguish of soul he experiences over his sins constitutes the punishment, as I wrote above in Section 57,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכֶּה לַעֲלִיָּה:
and through this he merits the higher ascent.

paragraphs.text: Accepted repentance and continuing recognition
Divine forgiveness and the person's renewed awareness of deficiency belong to different sides of repentance.

rich.text: Divine forgiveness and the person's renewed awareness of deficiency belong to different sides of repentance.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, On Book of Joshua 23: “This is why Hashem is called ‘the One who abundantly forgives’: forgiveness comes from His side, whereas from the human side there must be recognition of the sin and deficiency, as it says, ‘My sin is before me always’ (Psalms 51:5). Even though one confessed on this Yom Kippur, one confesses again on the next (Yoma 86b). For if a person decides for himself that there was no stumbling, but that everything was his own achievement, as do the nations around him, that itself is truly a stumbling. From the human side, one must recognize that a person has no independent power. The days when he walked in darkness, unaware that Hashem gives him the strength to act (Deuteronomy 8:18), were therefore sin and stumbling; then Hashem says that it was not a stumbling, as explained above.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Likkutei Maamarim keeps together two statements that might appear to conflict: Hashem abundantly forgives, while the person continues to recognize his own failure. The distinction illuminates why a higher level can call forth renewed repentance without proving that the earlier repentance was rejected. The acknowledgment becomes more searching as the person's knowledge grows; the declaration that the past has been repaired remains a gift from Hashem rather than the person's self-exemption.

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar HaGilgulim 22:1: “After departing this world, the righteous person is prepared to rise through great levels in the World to Come, but not all at once. Immediately after his departure, he is punished to cleanse the more serious transgressions that he has, and then he is brought into one higher sphere. sections.en: All Forms of Divine Service Performed Through the Bodily Limbs and Their Commandments Exist…

p: [סח] כָּל הָעֲבוֹדוֹת שֶׁבְּאֵבְרֵי הַגּוּף וְהַמִּצְווֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם הֵם רַק לְהַיְשִׁיר הַלֵּב,
All forms of divine service performed through the bodily limbs and their commandments exist solely to rectify and align the heart;
וְהָעִיקָּר הוּא הַלֵּב שֶׁשָּׁם מְעוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and the principal core is the heart, which is the dwelling place of the Blessed Name,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי וְגוֹמֵר".
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): "The Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as it is stated: 'God is the rock of my heart, etc.'" (Psalms 73:26).
וּלְכָךְ לֹא יִהְיֶה זֶה הַמְּכֻוָּון מִן הָאָדָם, רַק כָּל אֵלֶּה דְּבָרִים הַמְּבִיאִים אֶל הַמְּכֻוָּון,
Therefore the physical act itself should not be man's ultimate objective, but rather all these deeds are instruments leading to the ultimate goal,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, פב עַמּוּד ב) עַל תַּרְיַ"ג מִצְווֹת – תַּרְיַ"ג עֵיטִין.
as written in the Zohar (Part II, 82b) concerning the 613 commandments: they are 613 counsels of holy advice.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "וְאַחַר הָרוּחַ רַעַשׁ – לֹא בָרַעַשׁ ה', וְאַחַר הָרַעַשׁ אֵשׁ וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א יט, יא–יב),
And regarding this Scripture states: "and after the wind an earthquake, but Hashem was not in the earthquake; and after the earthquake a fire, etc." (I Kings 19:11–12),
כִּי כְּבוֹד ה' אֵינוֹ בְּדָבָר הַנִּרְגָּשׁ וּמַרְעִישׁ, רַק "בְּקוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה",
for the glory of Hashem is not found in sensational, noisy display, but in "a still small voice,"
וְהוּא הַלֵּב שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְגָּשׁ לְשׁוּם בְּרִיָּה.
which is the inward heart, unfelt and unseen by any created being.
וְלָמְדוּ מִזֶּה בִּבְרָכוֹת (נח.) לְמַלְכוּתָא דְאַרְעָא,
And from this they derived in Berakhot 58a regarding earthly monarchy;
וּמַאן מַלְכֵי? רַבָּנָן, שֶׁהֵם הַמּוֹלְכִים עַל עַצְמָם, הַמּוֹשְׁלִים בְּיִצְרָם, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (עח:),
and who are kings? The Rabbis, who reign sovereignly over themselves and master their inclinations (Bava Batra 78b);
גַּם הַמְּלוּכָה בַּיֵּצֶר לֹא בְּרַעַשׁ, רַק קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה.
and mastery over the inclination is likewise not achieved through noisy tumult, but through a still small voice.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, "גּוּנְדָּא קַמַּיְיתָא חָלֵיף כִּי קָא אָוְושָׁא",
However, "the first troop passes with noisy clamor,"
כִּי לוּלֵי זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר, רַק מִקּוֹדֶם צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּרַעַשׁ וְתוֹקֶף נֶגְדּוֹ,
for without that preliminary stage it is impossible, and initially one must confront the inclination with forceful tumult,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה.): לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז אָדָם וְכוּלֵי.
as our Sages stated (Berakhot 5a): "A person should always stir up his good inclination against the evil inclination."
אֲבָל אֵין זֶה הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה הַגְּמוּרָה עֲדַיִן,
Yet that noisy struggle is not yet the complete dominion;
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בְּלִי רַעַשׁ,
rather, full dominion occurs when it operates without noise,
רַק כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "וְלִבִּי חָלַל בְּקִרְבִּי" (תְּהִלִּים קט, כב),
along the lines of what King David, peace be upon him, stated: "and my heart is slain within me" (Psalms 109:22),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ט הֲלָכָה ה) שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע בְּתַעֲנִית
and our Sages expounded (Yerushalmi Berakhot 9:5) that he slew his evil inclination through fasting
[שֶׁהוּא הָרַעַשׁ נֶגֶד הַתַּאֲוָה],
[which represented the tempestuous tumult waged against physical desire],
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה:
and through that quiet slaying is ultimate, absolute dominion attained.

If the heart is whole with the blessed God, everything is at peace; if the heart is deficient toward Him, everything is deficient. Our Sages expounded: “The Merciful One desires the heart.” They said in the Midrash: “My son, give Me your heart”—if you give Me your heart and your eyes, I know that you are Mine; if not, you are not Mine.”

One cannot simply say that they are counsels toward love of Hashem, for love of Hashem is itself one of the 613 commandments. Fear of Hashem is likewise one of the 613 commandments. Rather, they are counsels by which a person's body is drawn after Hashem's will, so that there should be no inclination in his heart, Heaven forbid, contrary to Hashem's will.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef asks why all 613 commandments are called counsels: love and awe themselves are already included among the commandments, so neither alone explains what the complete set counsels a person toward. His answer is the alignment of the body and the will with Hashem's will. This deepens the siman's opening claim that bodily acts straighten the heart, and explains why the quiet inward attainment is the aim of their disciplined preparation.

sections.en: When the Nations of the World Receive and Learn Any Good Character Trait Or…

p: [סט] (מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ)

(From his holy handwriting.) [This section was left out of the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902). R' Michael Mokotowski, a chasid of Rav Tzadok, copied it from the author's own manuscript into his copy of the book, and it was first printed in Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMalei (Jerusalem, 1968), edited by his son R' Avraham Eliyahu Kitov.]
כַּאֲשֶׁר אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מְקַבְּלִים וּלְמֵידִים אֵיזֶה מִדָּה טוֹבָה וְדָבָר טוֹב מִיְּהוּדִים,
When the nations of the world receive and learn any good character trait or good matter from Jews,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלִים הַיְּהוּדִים לְנַצְּחָם,
through this, the Jews are able to overcome and defeat them,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלָה הַכִּבְשָׂה לְהִתְקַיֵּם בֵּין הַזְּאֵבִים,
and through this, the sheep is able to endure and survive among the wolves,
עַל יְדֵי רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּיְקָא הַמִּתְחַבְּרִים לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
specifically through the sinners of Israel who associate with the nations of the world,
וּמֵהֶם לְמֵדִים אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב.
and from whom the nations of the world learn some good thing.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 57:1: “The congregation of Israel likewise has this power to influence others; those outside the congregation of Israel are the nations of the world. This is like the seventy bulls offered on the festival corresponding to the seventy nations. It is also as will happen in the future, when Mashiach comes to give certain commandments and teach Torah to the nations of the world as well, as stated in Bereshit Rabbah 98: “Many peoples shall stream toward him,” and “Then I will turn to the peoples a pure language.” These are the feet that descend to death, to the place of the husks and evil—the powers of the nations—in order to draw out the holy sparks within them as well and return them to holiness. Through this power within the congregation of Israel, which seeks to return even the nations’ powers to holiness, the corresponding power in evil—for “God has made one opposite the other”—arouses in the nations the power and desire to decree forced apostasy, God forbid, upon Israel, to bring the congregation of Israel, God forbid, over to them instead. As long as the congregation of Israel is whole—that is, its intention in associating with the nations is solely for the sake of Heaven, to draw out the holy sparks in them, so that the thighs remain connected to the body—then, although “the wicked watches for the righteous,” and so forth, “the Lord will not abandon him into his hand.” But it is written, “Because you associated with Ahaziah,” and so forth. Even though his intention was initially for the sake of Heaven, one who works with something filthy becomes soiled, like someone clearing drains whose body cannot avoid becoming dirty with mud and excrement. This requires great alertness and strength to prevent any filth from adhering to him, and not everyone attains this.”

Against that background, the ois describes providence making even compromised association a means through which some good is transmitted.

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָמַר "אָחִי הוּא",
And afterward, because Ahab said of Ben-Hadad 'he is my brother,'
נִתְקַלְקְלָה הַמְּצוּדָה עַל יְדֵי הָאַחֲוָה שֶׁעָשָׂה אוֹתוֹ עִמּוֹ,
the snare was ruined through the fraternity that he established with him,
מִמֵּילָא לֹא הָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁיְּנַצְּחוּ, וּבַמִּשְׁפָּט נִיצַּל].
and consequently it was no longer justified by judgment that they should prevail, and by judgment Ben-Hadad was spared].
וּמָרְדֳּכַי שֶׁנִּצַּח לְהָמָן,
And likewise Mordechai, who triumphed over Haman,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה:
as our Sages of blessed memory taught:
"אֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעָהּ שֶׁל רָחֵל",
'Amalek falls only at the hand of the offspring of Rachel,'
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר אָמְרוּ:
and elsewhere they taught:
זֶה נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים",
regarding this one (Amalek) it is stated: 'and he did not fear God,'
וְזֶה נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא",
while regarding this one (Joseph) it is stated: 'I fear God';
וְלָאו דַּוְקָא יוֹסֵף,
and this does not refer strictly to Joseph himself,
אֶלָּא כָּל זַרְעֵיהּ מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה גּוֹבֵר בָּהֶם,
rather, among all of Rachel's descendants the attribute of divine awe/fear is dominant,
וּלְכָךְ "וְרַבִּים מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִתְיַהֲדִים כִּי נָפַל פַּחַד מָרְדֳּכַי עֲלֵיהֶם",
and therefore Scripture states: 'And many of the peoples of the land became Jews, for the fear of Mordechai fell upon them,'
וְקִבְּלוּ יִרְאָה מִמֶּנּוּ,
meaning they received awe/fear from him,
וּמִצַּד זֶה הִגִּיעַ מִשְׁפַּט נִצּוּחוֹ.
and from that vantage point, the heavenly judgment of his victory arrived.

p: [ע] בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁבּוֹ הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁל אָדָם, בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר וְעַל יָדָהּ עַצְמוֹ הוּא מַעֲלָתוֹ,
In that very matter in which a person's deficiency lies, in that exact thing and through it itself is his true spiritual virtue,
כְּעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין ע.) עַל "וַיִּתְפְּרוּ עֲלֵה תְאֵנָה": בַּדָּבָר שֶׁקִּלְקְלוּ בּוֹ נִתְקָנוּ.
in the spirit of what our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Sanhedrin 70a–b) on "and they sewed fig leaves": through the very medium in which they corrupted were they rectified.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ב סוֹף הֲלָכָה ד): בַּיּוֹם שֶׁנֶּחְרַב הַבַּיִת נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ.
And along these lines is likewise what our Sages of blessed memory stated (Yerushalmi Berakhot 2:4): On the very day the Temple was destroyed, the Messiah was born.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צא:): מִנַּיִן לִתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה
And our Sages said (Sanhedrin 91b): From where is the resurrection of the dead derived from the Torah
[רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל דָּבָר שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם יֵשׁ לוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דְּבֵיקוּת בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים שֶׁהוּא אֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ].
[meaning that every matter in the world possesses a root in the Torah, signifying cleaving unto the Source of Life which is the absolute truth of the will of the Blessed Name].
וְזֶהוּ פָּרָה אֲדֻמָּה לְטַהֵר מִטֻּמְאַת מֵת,
And this is the red heifer (Parah Adumah) designed to purify from the defilement of death,

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Parashat Parah 1: “Therefore, when one draws from the mystery of wisdom, where no absence applies, he too recognizes that Israel's life cannot be utterly absent. This is why the purification of the red heifer is written before impurity from the dead. The meaning of its purification through ash follows the distinction explained in the holy Zohar between earth and ash: earth supports growth and produces fruit in the world, while ash produces no fruit. The ash's purification of the impure thus teaches that Israel's life cannot be utterly absent; rather, one stands and praises Hashem like the living.”

sections.en: One Must Not Seek or Pray to See the Harm of Any Person

p: [עא] אֵין לְבַקֵּשׁ לִרְאוֹת רָעַת אָדָם וַאֲפִילּוּ רָשָׁע,
One must not seek or pray to see the harm of any person, even a wicked one,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת י.): "יִתַּמּוּ חוֹטְאִים" – אֵין כְּתִיב אֶלָּא חַטָּאִים.
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Berakhot 10a): "'Let sins cease' is written, not 'let sinners cease'."
וְזֶהוּ בְּרַע לַשָּׁמַיִם, אֲבָל רַע לַבְּרִיּוֹת עָנְשׁוֹ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, שֶׁמּוּתָּר לְבַקֵּשׁ רָעָתוֹ גַּם כֵּן;
And this applies to one who is wicked toward Heaven; but one who does evil unto created beings, his retribution is measure for measure, such that it is permissible to pray for his downfall as well;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בֶּאֱלִישָׁע שֶׁקִּלֵּל לַנְּעָרִים מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם זִלְזְלוּהוּ לְפִי שֶׁרִפָּא לַמַּיִם וְעָשָׂה טוֹבָה לַבְּרִיּוֹת, וְהֵם חֲפֵצִים יוֹתֵר בְּרָעָתָם, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה מו: וְרַשִּׁ"י שָׁם), לָכֵן הָיָה רַשַּׁאי לְקַלְּלָם.

and as we find regarding Elisha who cursed the youths because they mocked him for having healed the waters and brought benefit to the townspeople, whereas they preferred the town's plight (Sotah 46b and Rashi there), therefore he was permitted to curse them.
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁקִּלֵּל אוֹיְבָיו בְּמִזְמוֹר ק"ט, פֵּירֵשׁ שָׁם בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁהָיוּ מְרֵיעִים לוֹ,
And likewise King David, peace be upon him, who cursed his adversaries in Psalm 109, explained there that it was because they actively harmed him,
וְאָמַר: "וַיֶּאֱהַב קְלָלָה וַתְּבוֹאֵהוּ" – מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָהַב זֶה.
stating: "He loved cursing, and it came unto him" (Psalms 109:17)—measure for measure, because he loved cursing.
וְכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר: "וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ אָאֹר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יב, ג), אֲבָל בְּלָאו הָכִי אֵין מְקַלֵּל לְאָדָם.
And likewise the Blessed Name proclaimed: "And him who curses you will I curse" (Genesis 12:3); but otherwise, one must not curse another person.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, גַּם בָּזֶה מָצִינוּ דֶּאֱלִישָׁע נֶעֱנַשׁ עַל זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (מז.) וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (קז:);
Nonetheless, even in this we find that Elisha was punished for it, as stated in Sotah 47a and Sanhedrin 107b;
וּמִלְּבַד זֶה גַּם כֵּן לֹא לְכָל אָדָם הוּתַּר, שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בֶּאֱלִישָׁע (סוֹטָה שָׁם): "וַיַּרְאֵם" – רָאָה שֶׁאֵין וְכוּלֵי,
and furthermore, it is not permitted to every individual, for our Sages expounded regarding Elisha (Sotah ibid.): "'And he looked upon them'—he saw that there was no good seed in them, etc.";
וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּעַל רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁהַנְּגִיעָה מְעַוֶּורְתּוֹ.
and one who does not possess the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh) might be blinded by personal bias and resentment.

וּלְכָךְ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאוֹתוֹ מִזְמוֹר אָמַר פָּסוּק "וְלִבִּי חָלַל בְּקִרְבִּי" (תְּהִלִּים קט, כב), שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מִזֶּה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע,

And therefore King David, peace be upon him, in that very psalm uttered the verse "and my heart is slain within me" (Psalms 109:22), which our Sages expounded (Avodah Zarah 4b) to mean that he had completely slain his evil inclination,
שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לָחוּשׁ לְשׁוּם נְגִיעָה לְתַאֲוַת עַצְמוֹ, כִּי כְּבָר אֵין לוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע.
declaring that he had no concern of being blinded by self-interest or personal passion, for he no longer possessed an evil inclination.

וְקוֹדֶם מִזְמוֹר זֶה נֶאֱמַר מִזְמוֹר שֶׁבּוֹ פָּסוּק "לִי גִלְעָד וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים קח, ט), שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ דָּרְשׁוּ דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קד:) שֶׁכֻּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,

And prior to this psalm comes the psalm containing the verse "Gilead is mine, etc." (Psalms 108:9), from which the masters of esoteric traces expounded in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 104b) that all those biblical sinners have a share in the World to Come,
וְזֶהוּ כְּעֵין שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יג:) מִמִּדַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמַּקְדִּים רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה.
which mirrors what our Sages said (Megillah 13b) regarding the attribute of the Blessed Name, that He provides the cure before the blow.
וְצָרִיךְ לְהַקְדִּים בְּלִבּוֹ הַטּוֹבַת עַיִן אֲפִילּוּ לָהֶם,
And one must first precede in his heart with a benevolent eye toward them,
וְאִם אַחַר כָּךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם מְקַלְּלָם, אָז הוּא בְּמִשְׁפָּט:
and if he nonetheless curses them afterward, it is then done with balanced justice.

His wife Beruriah said to him: ‘What is your reasoning? Is it because it is written, ‘Let sins cease’? Is it written ‘sinners’—chote’im? It is written ‘sins’—chatta’im.’’

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 40a:8-9: “Rava said: Rav Idi explained to me: “Say of the righteous that he is good, for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.” Is there a righteous person who is good and one who is not good? Rather, one who is good toward Heaven and toward people is a good righteous person; one who is good toward Heaven but bad toward people is a righteous person who is not good. Similarly: “Woe to the wicked who is bad, for the recompense of his hands shall be done to him.” Is there a wicked person who is bad and one who is not bad? Rather, one who is bad toward Heaven and toward people is a bad wicked person; one who is bad toward Heaven but is not bad toward people is a wicked person who is not bad.”

rich.text: : “Rava said: Rav Idi explained to me: “Say of the righteous that he is good, for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.” Is there a righteous person who is good and one who is not good? Rather, one who is good toward Heaven and toward people is a good righteous person; one who is good toward Heaven but bad toward people is a righteous person who is not good. Similarly: “Woe to the wicked who is bad, for the recompense of his hands shall be done to him.” Is there a wicked person who is bad and one who is not bad? Rather, one who is bad toward Heaven and toward people is a bad wicked person; one who is bad toward Heaven but is not bad toward people is a wicked person who is not bad.”

paragraphs.text: Context: This is the Talmudic distinction between conduct toward Heaven and conduct toward other people. Rav Tzadok applies that distinction here, then expressly limits personal judgment by noting Elisha’s punishment and the danger of self-interest.

paragraphs.text: Seeking the surviving point of good

rich.text: Seeking the surviving point of good

paragraphs.text: The favorable judgment of the interpreters of the remnant develops a person's remaining good into a ground of advocacy.

rich.text: The favorable judgment of the interpreters of the remnant develops a person's remaining good into a ground of advocacy.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Taanit 6: “How far does the protection arising from the righteous person's service extend in this world? Even concerning those four individuals of whom the ruling states that they have no share in the world to come, the Gemara nevertheless teaches (Sanhedrin 104b) that the interpreters of the remnant said they do have a share. The interpreters of the remnant are the righteous who take hold of the point of Israel and extend it, advocating that none be utterly cast away. They are called interpreters of the remnant because they expound the remaining impression in the heart, until through their service they can protect even those four individuals and bring them to the life of the world to come. Thus the day of rain is greater, for it includes both righteous and wicked, whereas resurrection is for the righteous, since then evil is entirely annulled.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the very interpreters of the remnant invoked at the close of this siman. Their favorable reading is an active attempt to take hold of the surviving good and enlarge it, rather than a denial that a serious judgment was stated. This clarifies the order Rav Tzadok requires: the heart must first contain a real concern for the other's possible restoration before it can claim to speak only for justice.

sections.en: Perform Supernatural Miracles Through the Medium of Torah

p: [עב] אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹת מוֹפְתִים עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה,
It is possible to perform supernatural miracles through the medium of Torah;

וְכָךְ הָיוּ כָּל מוֹפֵת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁפָּתַח שַׁעַר חָדָשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְעַל פִּי אוֹתוֹ אוֹר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הָיָה נִמְשָׁךְ שְׁפִיעַת אוֹר בָּעוֹלָם לִפְעוֹל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.

and such was every miracle wrought by Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who unlocked a new gate in the words of Torah, and through that illumination in the words of Torah, an outpouring of light was drawn down into the cosmos to effect that physical phenomenon.
וְאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹת עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה.
And it is also possible to perform miracles through the power of prayer.
וּמָצִינוּ בַּנְּבִיאִים שֶׁסִּפֵּר הַכָּתוּב כָּל הַמּוֹפְתִים שֶׁעָשָׂה אֵלִיָּהוּ וְשֶׁעָשָׂה אֱלִישָׁע, וְזוּלַת מִשְּׁאָר הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא נִזְכַּר מוֹפְתֵיהֶם.
And we find among the Prophets that Scripture explicitly recorded all the miracles wrought by Elijah and by Elisha, whereas among the other prophets their wonders are not described.
וּכְבָר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יד.): נְבוּאָה שֶׁהֻוצְרְכָה לְדוֹרוֹת נִכְתְּבָה, וְשֶׁלֹּא הֻוצְרְכָה לֹא נִכְתְּבָה;
And our Sages already taught (Megillah 14a): A prophecy that was necessary for future generations was transcribed, while that which was not needed for posterity was not written down;
וְאִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחֲךָ אוֹתָם סִפּוּרֵי הַמּוֹפְתִים הֵם צְרִיכִים לְדוֹרוֹת, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיוּ רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה, הֵם פָּתְחוּ שְׁעָרִים בָּזֶה,
and if so, perforce those accounts of their miracles are eternally needed for future generations, and even though they were temporary, they opened eternal spiritual gateways in this realm,
כִּי כָּל מוֹפְתֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ הָיוּ עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וְעַל יָדָהּ
for all of Elijah's miracles were wrought through the authority and mechanism of Torah
[דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל יְרִידַת הָאֵשׁ עַל יְדֵי חִדּוּשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁחִדֵּשׁ לְהַתִּיר הַבָּמָה],
[for example, the descent of fire from heaven through the halakhic innovation he established to temporarily permit an isolated altar],
וְכָל מוֹפְתֵי אֱלִישָׁע עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (כז.): "וֶאֱלִישָׁע דַּעֲבַד בְּרַחֲמֵי",
while all of Elisha's miracles were achieved through prayer, as stated in Megillah 27a: "And Elisha acted through prayers for divine mercy,"
וְזָכָה לְפִי שְׁנַיִם מֵאֵלִיָּהוּ, כִּי יוֹתֵר יֵשׁ לִפְעוֹל עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה.
and he merited a double portion beyond Elijah, because greater direct intervention can be effected through prayer.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, מַה שֶּׁעַל פִּי תּוֹרָה גָּדוֹל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּשַׁבָּת (י.): "מַנִּיחִים חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְעוֹסְקִים בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה", וְהַמַּעֲמִיק יָבִין:

Yet nonetheless, that which is done through Torah is intrinsically greater, as stated in Shabbat 10a: "They set aside eternal life and engage in transient temporal life," and the discerning mind will understand.

paragraphs.text: What remains for later generations
A scriptural account can preserve a spiritual opening beyond the immediate event it describes.

rich.text: A scriptural account can preserve a spiritual opening beyond the immediate event it describes.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Megillah 3: “The matter is as my holy grandfather explained: there are two kinds of divine inspiration. One comes through a person's preparation: he prepares and disciplines himself for Hashem's will and thereby reaches divine inspiration. As the Midrash teaches, zeal leads to cleanliness, and so forth, and piety leads to divine inspiration. By preparing himself through all the stages enumerated by the Midrash, a person attains divine inspiration. This is called prophecy needed for the generations, for since it came through human preparation, it remains established for the whole world.”

rich.text: : “The matter is as my holy grandfather explained: there are two kinds of divine inspiration. One comes through a person's preparation: he prepares and disciplines himself for Hashem's will and thereby reaches divine inspiration. As the Midrash teaches, zeal leads to cleanliness, and so forth, and piety leads to divine inspiration. By preparing himself through all the stages enumerated by the Midrash, a person attains divine inspiration. This is called prophecy needed for the generations, for since it came through human preparation, it remains established for the whole world.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef distinguishes an isolated inspiration from a lasting path opened through human preparation. This helps explain the siman's question about recording miracles that served only a particular moment: what remains is not merely the report of a wonder, but an opening in avodas Hashem. The two discussions illuminate that lasting function without making every miracle identical with the prophecy discussed there.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Pinchas 7:1: “Jeremiah's prophecy was not heard in its own time, for he rebuked them for failing to listen, and calamity consequently came. Yet the Gemara teaches that the words of anyone who has fear of Heaven are heard. The explanation is that such a person becomes a vehicle for the attribute of kingship, which is fear, and ‘kingship is the mouth; we call it the Oral Torah.’ These are ‘My words which I have placed in your mouth’; then ‘it shall not return to Me empty,’ and his words are heard. This is why the Gemara cites ‘The end of the matter: everything is heard.’ Even if it was not heard at the time, in the end events will turn so that it is heard. As the Sages said, ‘A prophecy needed for generations was written,’ and a time will come when it is heard.”

This strengthens the siman's distinction between an event's short duration and the continuing gateway it opens. It explains the premise about what is preserved for generations, while the siman itself goes on to distinguish the particular powers of Torah and prayer.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:9: “Shabbat corresponds to David the king, peace be upon him, as is known, and it is the level of prayer, called “temporal life,” for it is only for a time. Nevertheless it is life: the holiness of Shabbat is a temporary taste of eternal life. This taste of eternal life within the body in this world comes through prayer, the service of the heart. One draws eternal life into temporal life, so that even its moment is called vitality. They said: “One hour of repentance and good deeds in this world is better than all the life of the World to Come.” This life of one hour of repentance and good deeds is David’s level, for he established the yoke of repentance, as our Sages said in Avodah Zarah. This is the aspect of the feminine, which is lacking: “Three things are never satisfied.” It has no satiety or contentment; its contentment and pleasure lie in longing—“your longing shall be for your husband”—in seeking completion. This is David’s level, as he said, “Seek His face always,” and many similar verses: one continually seeks and searches, for one never attains the satiety of finding. Rather, “Let the heart of those who seek Hashem rejoice”: there is joy in the seeking itself, and it is better for him than all the life of the World to Come. Then there will no longer be room for effort and petition, for “today is for performing them and tomorrow for receiving their reward.” That is the hour of contentment which is better than all the life of this world: one will have contentment and rest in exchange for having given pleasure to God in this world. This is through Torah, which “restores the soul”; its study contains pleasure and contentment. Therefore it is actual eternal life, for it is itself the vitality of the World to Come.”

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:8: “The first is the vitality clothed in the body, to which death applies when the body dies. These lives have a limit in the measure of one’s days: throughout one’s life, one has this vitality of the soul flowing into the body. This is the life of this world, in which there is the effort of mitzvot and good deeds. There is also the soul’s eternal vitality in itself, apart from its clothing in the body. In itself it lacks nothing that would require the service of prayer; rather, the voice of Torah is “eternal life that He planted within us,” which is the occupation of the righteous in this world. The World to Come was created with the letter yod, the essence of wisdom, as is known; this world with the letter heh, the lower heh that alludes to prayer. The principal thing is certainly Torah, as it is said: “They leave eternal life and occupy themselves with temporal life!” Nevertheless, the view stated there that words of Torah have their own time and words of prayer their own time is also true. For “the beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem,” and “if fear of Hashem is his treasure—yes.” The effort of temporal life prepares one to merit eternal life, as it is said: “Prepare yourself in the antechamber,” and “One who did not toil before Shabbat,” and so forth.”

sections.en: When a Person Rectifies the Flaw Wherein He Sinned

p: [עג] כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם מְתַקֵּן מַה שֶּׁחָטָא, אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ אוֹתוֹ פֶּרֶק וְאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּהְיֶה תְּשׁוּבַת הַמִּשְׁקָל;

When a person rectifies the flaw wherein he sinned, the Blessed Name arranges for him that exact situation and that exact circumstance so that it constitutes a commensurate, counterbalancing repentance (teshuvat hamishkal);
שֶׁהֲרֵי וַדַּאי יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָסוּר הָאָדָם לְהָבִיא עַצְמוֹ לִידֵי כָּךְ, כְּמוֹ בְּ"אוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה, בְּאוֹתוֹ וְכוּלֵי" יַעֲבוֹר עַל אִיסּוּר יִחוּד,

for certainly there are scenarios where it is strictly forbidden for a person to bring himself deliberately into temptation—such as intentionally putting oneself in seclusion with the same woman, which would violate the prohibition of yichud;
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ זֶה אוֹ עִנְיָן כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, וְאֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ זֶה אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשֵׁל עוֹד.
rather, the Blessed Name providential arranges this or a comparable situation for him, and the Blessed Name orchestrates this only when He foreknows that the person will not stumble again.
וּלְכָךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ, הוּא סִימָן שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַן וְנִתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ.
And therefore, when the Blessed Name orchestrates such an encounter, it is a sign that he has already been spiritually rectified and his repentance has been accepted.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כה.) בַּחֲזָרָתָן שֶׁל חָשׁוּד עַל טְרֵיפוֹת: שֶׁיַּחֲזִיר אֲבֵדָה וְכוּלֵי וְכַיּוֹצֵא עַיֵּין שָׁם;
And this is what our Sages said in Sanhedrin 25a regarding the repentance of one suspected of selling non-kosher meat: that he must return a valuable lost object, etc., see there;
וַהֲרֵי זֶה אֵין בְּיָדָם, אִם אֵין מוֹצְאִין אֲבֵדָה מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ?
and behold, finding a lost item is not in their power—if they do not find one, what can they do?
רַק שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר תְּשׁוּבָתָם אֱמֶת, הַסִּימָן שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לָהֶם כָּךְ, וּכְשֶׁנִּזְדַּמֵּן לָהֶם הוּא סִימָן שֶׁתְּשׁוּבָתָם אֱמֶת.

Rather, when their repentance is genuine truth, the sign is that the Blessed Name arranges this opportunity for them, and when it presents itself to them, it is a confirmation that their repentance is sincere.
וְכָךְ בְּגֵיחֲזִי, שֶׁחֶטְאוֹ הָיָה שֶׁחָמַד לְמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ:
And so it was with Gehazi, whose sin was coveting that which was not his:
הַתְחָלַת תִּיקּוּנוֹ הִזְמִין לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשׂוֹרַת בִּזַּת אֲרָם,
the initial stage of his rectification the Blessed Name arranged for him through the discovery of the spoils of the Aramean camp,

כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם קז:) דְּהַמְּצֹרָעִים הֵם גֵּיחֲזִי וּבָנָיו, וְלֹא חָמְדוּ לִשְׁתּוֹק וּלְהַרְבּוֹת בְּבִזָּה לְעַצְמָם כִּי חָשְׁשׁוּ לַחֵטְא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּמְצָאָנוּ עָוֹן" (מְלָכִים ב ז, ט).

as our Sages expounded (ibid. 107b) that the four lepers were Gehazi and his sons, and they did not covet to keep silent and hoard the vast spoils for themselves because they feared sin, as it is written: "and punishment will overtake us" (II Kings 7:9).
וְאָז הָיָה הַהַתְחָלָה, וְלֹא נִזְכַּר עֲדַיִן שְׁמוֹ בְּפֵירוּשׁ.
And that was the beginning, where his name was not yet explicitly mentioned.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ סִפֵּר מֵעִנְיַן הַחֲזָרַת נַחֲלָה לָאִשָּׁה עַל יָדוֹ, וְהוּא דָּבָר דְּמִמֵּילָא בָּא עַל יָדוֹ, הוּא סִימָן לִגְמַר תִּיקּוּנוֹ.

And afterward Scripture relates how the restoration of the Shunammite woman's estate occurred through his words (II Kings 8:5), which came about spontaneously through him, serving as a sign of his complete rectification.
וְאָז אַחַר כָּךְ הָלַךְ אֱלִישָׁע לַאֲרָם, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם): לְהַחֲזִיר גֵּיחֲזִי בִּתְשׁוּבָה;
And then subsequently Elisha went to Damascus, concerning which our Sages said (Sanhedrin ibid.): to bring Gehazi back in repentance;
זָכָה לְמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּמִדּוֹת (פֶּרֶק ב): "יִתֵּן בְּלִבָּם וִיקָרְבוּךָ", שֶׁאַף אַחַר כָּל הַתִּיקּוּן צָרִיךְ לְהִתְקָרְבוּת אֱלִישָׁע.

he merited that which our Sages stated in Middot (chapter 2): "May He place in their hearts that they draw you near," for even after all internal rectification, he still required the personal rapprochement of Elisha.
וְזָכָה שֶׁמִּי שֶׁהִרְחִיקוֹ הוּא עַצְמוֹ קֵירְבוֹ;
And he was privileged that the very master who had pushed him away personally came to draw him close;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מְנָאוּהוּ בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְאָמְרוּ שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לָשׁוּב,
and even though our Sages of blessed memory enumerated him among those who have no portion in the World to Come and stated that he refused to repent,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת וְכוּלֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ:
nonetheless the interpreters of esoteric traces maintained that he indeed has a portion in the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Sha'arei Teshuvah 1:49: “The nineteenth principle is abandoning his sin when it presents itself to him and his desire is at its strongest. Our Sages of blessed memory said: Who is a penitent whose repentance reaches the Throne of Glory? One who is tested and emerges innocent at the same stage, in the same place, and with the same woman. This means that the sin presented itself to him while his inclination and physical vigor were as strong as at the first time when he sinned, yet he subdued his inclination and escaped the transgression out of fear of the Lord and dread of His majesty. If such an occasion has not presented itself to him, he should increase the fear of the Lord within himself day by day, throughout his life. When he renews the strength of that fear sufficiently to subdue his inclination and the force of its rule at the height of desire, surely He who searches hearts understands, and He who guards his soul knows, that if he were to face a test and encounter the same situation as before, he would save himself from his inclination. He thus stands before the Lord on the highest level of repentance.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 9:1: “And the essence of teshuvah is in the contemplation of the heart alone — for by it one is called a “complete tzaddik,” even if he was, beforehand, wholly wicked, as is explained in Kiddushin 49b. And even the verbal confession — though it is a positive Torah commandment, “and they shall confess” (Bamidbar 5:7) — that is a mitzvah in its own right, and it does not hold up the teshuvah, whose essence is in the heart alone: that he regrets the past, and resolves in his heart not to return again to his folly, and not to sin again. And although it is not revealed to any person — nor even to the ministering angels, who do not know what is in the heart — “before Heaven it is revealed”; and he is truly called a “complete tzaddik,” even if he multiplied transgressions to the utmost — for they said it there of “any wholly wicked man,” even one who transgressed the entire Torah. And in the Beis Shmuel and Chelkas Mechokek Even HaEzer §38 they wrote that even one who stole and did not return the theft — only that he accepted in his heart to return it — it avails to make him a “tzaddik”; and so it is implied in Berachos 5b in the case of the four hundred jars of wine of Rav Huna, that this acceptance suffices. And what they said in Sanhedrin 25b regarding the “return” of penitents breaking their dice and the like is with respect to his credibility to the public — for we are concerned lest he has not truly repented and is deceiving people, and so people need to see from him an actual act of teshuvah. And the “fences in the permitted” that they mentioned there are good counsels for the penitent, that his inclination not overpower him again in the future; and therefore he must fence himself even in the permitted, so as to distance himself from the prohibition in which he already stumbled — for the inclination, having already made itself a “nest” in his heart and become “master of the house,” can easily trip him, and so he needs extra fences.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin separates genuine inward teshuvah from the actions by which other people can safely restore their trust. That distinction explains the evidentiary role of the opportunities described here. They can disclose a repaired will without making an engineered encounter with temptation a requirement of repentance. The present siman explicitly forbids bringing oneself into an otherwise prohibited situation.

This proves that at their root they have a remedy, as the interpreters of scriptural hints said about all six who descend from Yaakov: they have a share in the World to Come. For everyone descended from Yaakov is bound at the root to the blessed God: “Your people are all righteous.””

items.h:
Editorial Note on the Missing Section
The text of Section 74 is not present in the editions consulted. Har Bracha proceeds directly from Section 73 to Section 75, and the other printed editions likewise mark Section 74 as missing. Other passages of Tzidkas HaTzadik, including Section 75, were omitted from early printings and later restored from manuscript copies. Section 74 is also absent from both known manuscript copies of the omitted material, so Rav Tzadok most likely skipped the number himself while writing (Tzvi Leshem, National Library of Israel blog, 2018, following an observation by Dr. Eitan Abramovitch). Accordingly, no text is reconstructed here; the original numbering is preserved.
Sources: Har Bracha ed., pp. 28-29; Josh Rosenfeld, The Seforim Blog, May 31, 2016; Tzvi Leshem, "From Tzidkas HaTzaddik to HaMalei to HaShalem," National Library of Israel blog, February 28, 2018 (blog.nli.org.il/zadik).

sections.en: Transgressions within the Soul of an Israelite Are Not an Essential Acquisition

p: [עה] (מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ)

(From his holy handwriting.) [This section was left out of the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902). R' Michael Mokotowski, a chasid of Rav Tzadok, copied it from the author's own manuscript into his copy of the book, and it was first printed in Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMalei (Jerusalem, 1968), edited by his son R' Avraham Eliyahu Kitov.]
הָעֲבֵירוֹת בְּנֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי אֵינָם קִנְיַן עַצְמִי רַק מִקְרִי,
Transgressions within the soul of an Israelite are not an essential acquisition, but merely incidental,
וּלְכָךְ יֵשׁ לָהֶם פְּדִיָּה,
and therefore they are subject to redemption,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהוּא יִפְדֶּה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכֹּל עֲוֹנֹתָיו".
as it is stated: 'And He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities' (Psalms 130:8).
כְּמוֹ קְדוּשַׁת דָּמִים יֵשׁ לָהּ פִּדְיוֹן,
Just as monetary sanctity (kedushat damim) is subject to redemption,
שֶׁדָּבָר אַחֵר נִתְפָּס תְּמוּרָתוֹ וְחָלָה עָלָיו הַקְּדוּשָּׁה,
wherein another object is seized in its stead and the sanctity takes effect upon it,
כָּךְ הוּא מְחַלֵּל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּאֲחֵרִים,
so He redeems Israel onto others [as consecrated property is redeemed onto something else],
כְּעִנְיַן "וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
in the manner of: 'And I will give people in your place, etc.' (Isaiah 43:4),
וְחָל עֲלֵיהֶם הָעֲבֵירוֹת.
and the transgressions take effect upon them.
וּכְעִנְיַן "וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר עָלָיו אֶת עֲוֹנֹתָם",
And similar to: 'And the he-goat shall bear upon itself their iniquities' (Leviticus 16:22),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁנּוֹתֵן הָעֲווֹנוֹת עַל רֹאשׁ עֵשָׂו.
and as our Sages of blessed memory taught, that He places the sins upon the head of Esau.

p: אֲבָל הַמִּצְווֹת הֵם קְדוּשַׁת הַגּוּף וְאֵין לָהֶם פִּדְיוֹן.
However, the mitzvot possess bodily sanctity (kedushat haguf), and they are not subject to redemption.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אִם יִתֵּן אִישׁ אֶת כָּל הוֹן בֵּיתוֹ בָּאַהֲבָה בּוֹז יָבוּזוּ לוֹ".
And as it is written: 'If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, it would be utterly scorned' (Song of Songs 8:7).
וְעַיֵּין בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת רַב הַאי גָּאוֹן שֶׁהֵבִיא מַהֲרַ״ם אַלְשַׁקַּר בְּעִנְיַן אֶחָד שֶׁמָּכַר מִצְווֹתָיו דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And see the Responsa of Rav Hai Gaon cited by Maharam Alashkar regarding one who sold his mitzvot, that it is completely ineffective, see there.
[וְעִנְיַן מְכִירַת הַבְּכוֹרָה דְּעֵשָׂו לְהַקְרִיב קָרְבָּנוֹת, שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כִּמְכִירַת דָּבָר קְדוּשָׁה,
[And regarding the sale of the birthright by Esau to offer sacrifices, which appears like the sale of a sacred matter,
שָׁמַעְתִּי לְפִי שֶׁהוּא הָיָה בְּכוֹר בְּדִמְיוֹן וְלֹא בֶּאֱמֶת,
I heard: because he was a firstborn only in illusion and not in truth,
לְפִיכָךְ הוֹעִילָה מְכִירָה בְּדִמְיוֹן].
therefore a sale within the realm of illusion was effective].

paragraphs.text: The holiness described as intrinsic rests on a bond that changing outward actions cannot simply exchange.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayera 58:2: “The matter is that Hashem bound His love to Avraham our father in a place beyond the reach of human actions. As the holy Zohar teaches (Bereshit 22b), ‘He is One, without reckoning and without partnership’; this love endures forever. Of this love it is said, ‘Many waters cannot extinguish love’ (Song of Songs 8:7), for no action reaches that place so as to extinguish it. As the Midrash Tanchuma says (Tzav 8), ‘He chose Avraham’: after the Akeidah, the love and bond Hashem has with Avraham our father were revealed even apart from his good deeds, through the choice by which He chose him from birth, as it says, ‘Who chose Avram’ (Nehemiah 9:7).”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov develops the same verse about love that many waters cannot extinguish, locating the bond with Avraham in divine choice at a level beyond the reach of changing actions. This clarifies the root of the siman's analogy to intrinsic sanctity. The parallel explains the endurance of the bond; it does not cancel the siman's distinction between the person's true possession and the sins from which he still requires redemption.

paragraphs.text: Rav Hai Gaon, quoted in Responsa Maharam Alashkar 101: “Certainly, one who pays a teacher to teach what they need, and the teacher teaches them, receives great reward for this. The teacher himself sometimes receives reward and sometimes does not. Likewise, one who feeds a poor person or a sage so that he will bless him receives reward for this and benefits through that poor person’s or sage’s blessing. One who supports people fulfilling mitzvot so that they can fulfill them receives reward for this, as do they. Especially one who helps those occupied with Torah and mitzvot to free their hearts to engage in them receives reward; the reward he receives is for his own action. But one who persuades himself that he can acquire his fellow’s reward with money or as a gift deserves scorn and ridicule. No precious wealth or treasures enable a person to acquire his fellow’s reward. Thus it is written: “If a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, they would utterly scorn him.” The Sages asked: What is meant by “they would utterly scorn him”? Ulla said: Not like Shimon, the brother of Azaryah, nor like Rabbi Yochanan of the house of the Nasi, but like Hillel and Shevna. For when Rav Dimi came, he said: Hillel and Shevna were brothers. One engaged in business and the other in Torah. He said to him, “Share with me and I will share with you.” A heavenly voice went forth and said: “If a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, they would utterly scorn him.””

paragraphs.text: Esav's outward precedence could be transferred because it did not express the inward root of the birthright.

rich.text: Esav's outward precedence could be transferred because it did not express the inward root of the birthright.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Yisrael Kedoshim 7:11: “Yaakov was first in formation—that is, in the truth concealed in this world. But in the visible disclosure of this world, in birth, Esav appeared first, for the service is in deed and the power of action, and Esav is the root of the power of deeds. As long as Avraham our father himself was alive, clothed in a physical body in this world, there was also a physical garment of his level in Esav because of the mixture of good and evil in the bodily world. But at Avraham's passing, when his spiritual holiness remained without a physical garment in this world, Esav no longer had a connection with it, since all his power belongs to physical embodiment in this world. Through that embodiment he could extend his hooves and display himself as pure, for this world is a world of falsehood; this is not so from the standpoint of ‘truth to Yaakov’ (Micah 7:20). Only Yaakov therefore received the spiritual dimension, and then ‘Yaakov cooked a stew’ (Genesis 25:29).”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim expands the compressed exception about selling Esav's birthright. It distinguishes priority in visible birth from the inward priority of formation, and describes Esav's connection to Avraham as dependent on an outward bodily garment. This makes precise why the siman can treat that sale as effective without making intrinsic holiness generally saleable.

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 7:1: “He [Yitzchak] considered him [Esav] a vessel prepared for holiness, since he had been formed as a firstborn. Although the firstborn had not yet been sanctified, the forefathers fulfilled the whole Torah and he knew that the firstborn would be sanctified in the future. In truth, however, Yaakov took the birthright and the blessings from him, for everything truly belonged to Yaakov. The birthright came first, even though holiness follows blessing, because the birthright at that time was not holiness itself but a preparation for holiness. He had to take all this from Esav indirectly, because from the appearance of this world everything initially seemed to belong to Esav. For this is the order of the world: first darkness and then light, as they said at the beginning of Berakhot.”

sections.en: At the Moment of a Person's Stumbling

p: [עו] בְּעֵת כִּשְׁלוֹן הָאָדָם, יֵדַע שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת הוּא הֲכָנָה לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר לְטוֹב;
At the moment of a person's stumbling, he should know that this very time is a preparation for that exact matter toward the good;
וְאִם יִזְכֶּה בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, יוּכַל לַעֲלוֹת לְמַדְרֵגָה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד.
and if he merits at that crucial hour, he can ascend to an exceedingly exalted spiritual rung.
כְּפִי גּוֹדֶל הַחֵטְא שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר מְסִיתוֹ, כָּךְ הוּא גּוֹדֶל הַטּוֹבָה שֶׁיּוּכַל לִקְלוֹט אָז,
Commensurate with the magnitude of the sin to which the evil inclination incites him, such is the magnitude of the goodness he can absorb then,
אִם יַהֲפֹךְ תְּשׁוּקָה זוֹ וְחֶמְדָּה זוֹ לְטוֹב,
if he will invert this intense longing and desire toward the good,
וּמֵאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן מַמָּשׁ הוּא הַטּוֹבָה – הֵיפֶךְ הָרָעָה.
and from that very same essence springs the goodness, as the exact antithesis of the evil.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (פִּינְחָס רטז סוֹף עַמּוּד א), כִּי בְּעֵת הַמַּבּוּל הָיוּ רְאוּיִים לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה,
And as written in the Zohar (Pinchas 216a end), that at the time of the Deluge they were originally worthy to receive the Torah,
וְהָיָה אָז מֹשֶׁה כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֻלִּין קלט:) עַל "בְּשַׁגַּם", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and Moses was already latent then, as our Sages expounded (Chullin 139b) on the word beshagam (Genesis 6:3), see there.
וּמַיִם הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה, וְהֵם הֲפָכוּהוּ לַ"מַּיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים";
And water signifies Torah, yet they perverted it into "the raging waters" (Psalms 124:5);
וְהַתּוֹרָה הִיא תַּכְלִית קִיּוּם הָעוֹלָם וְשֶׁבִּשְׁבִילוֹ נִבְרָא, וְאִלְמָלֵא וְכוּלֵי, וְהֵם גָּרְמוּ אָבְדָנוֹ;
and the Torah is the ultimate purpose of the world's existence for whose sake it was created—and were it not for it, etc.—yet they caused the world's destruction;
וְאוֹתוֹ עֵת הָיָה מוּכָן, אִלּוּ זָכוּ, מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ, שֶׁהוּא יְרִידַת מֵימֵי הַתּוֹרָה לְקִיּוּם הָעוֹלָם.
whereas that exact hour was prepared, had they merited, for the absolute opposite: the descent of the waters of Torah for the enduring preservation of the cosmos.
וְכֵן בְּעֵת הַחוּרְבָּן נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ב דִּבְרָכוֹת הֲלָכָה ד),
And likewise, at the moment of the Temple's destruction the Messiah was born (Yerushalmi Berakhot 2:4),
כִּי אוֹתוֹ עֵת הָיָה מוּכָן, אִם זָכוּ, לְבִיאַת מָשִׁיחַ וּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הַנִּצְחִי וְקַיָּים לָעַד;
for that very hour was primed, had they merited, for the advent of the Messiah and the building of the eternal Holy Temple that endures forever;

and this was the tragic error of the people of Jerusalem and the false prophets who imagined that, on the contrary, Hashem would bestow great favor upon them, since they saw the hour primed for it had they only merited.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan:2: “It says, ‘The rain was upon the earth for forty days’: God brought it down in mercy, so that if they returned, it would be rain of blessing, as Rashi explains. This is Torah, for the Gemara says, ‘Water means Torah.’ But because they did not return and corrupted their ways, it became raging waters, and that generation was judged; afterward it says, ‘The Flood was forty days.’ In Tishrei, ‘There was light’ is Rosh Hashanah, as stated in Tikkunei Zohar; likewise the Midrash explains, ‘My light’ on Rosh Hashanah. The renewal in Torah begins then, for ‘Torah is light,’ and continues until Shemini Atzeret, the flowing wellspring of Torah. Then the light of Oral Torah and its innovations are established. From that time, forty days are given to receive this flow and renewal in Torah permanently. So too, concerning the rainy season, the first rain, yoreh, is in Mar Cheshvan. Yoreh ‘instructs’ people to plaster their roofs and so forth; it also alludes to instructing people to accept the yoke of Torah in truth.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The rain is first described as an act of mercy, capable of becoming blessing through return; only after the generation persists in corruption is it called a Flood. This gives the present siman’s ‘same matter’ a concrete meaning: the prepared influx is not itself evil, but its reception can turn toward destruction or Torah. Rav Tzadok then applies this to accepting the yoke of Torah in Mar Cheshvan. A promising spiritual moment calls for that response; its promise alone does not guarantee a good outcome.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 171:1: “There is a place prepared for distress, Heaven forbid, as our Sages say in chapter Chelek concerning Shechem: “A place,” and so forth. So too there is a time, as our Sages say there, “A time,” and as they say concerning an Israelite who has a lawsuit in Av. So too with a soul, as in what our Sages said about Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat and many other cases. But how can it be conceived that this was prepared for evil from the beginning of creation? Is it not written, “From the mouth of the Most High evils do not issue”? In truth, the Sages’ language brings healing: they said “prepared for punishment”—pur’anut, a term related to payment. But “the reward of a mitzvah is not in this world”; here there is only payment for transgressions, unless one merits tasting the fruit of his deeds in this world, or performs one of the mitzvot that bear fruit here. That time, place, and soul are prepared to receive payment for what has been earned. The reason that the reward of a mitzvah is not in this world is that the Holy One, blessed be He, gives His full measure, and this world cannot receive that great abundance of good at all. In that place, time, and soul where the blessed God’s payment and reward flow, the abundance of the flow becomes, Heaven forbid, harmful punishment—as is known concerning the mystery of the breaking of the vessels: their death comes through an excess of light. Thus our Sages said concerning “A person shall not see Me”: at the time of their death they do see. This is why our Sages said that the cherubim were found embracing, although Israel were not doing the Omnipresent’s will: the flow of light was then intensely abundant. That is why Yechezkel merited visions of God. One who truly merits receives the payment of good then; this is the meaning of Mashiach’s birth on the Ninth of Av.”

sections.en: Even Regarding an Exceptionally Great Person

p: [עז] אֲפִילּוּ אָדָם גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹתֵר, אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ פְּגָם בְּמִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ, אֵין לְהִתְדַּבֵּק בּוֹ,
Even regarding an exceptionally great person, if there is a flaw in his family lineage, one should not bind oneself to him in marriage;
כִּי אִם הוּא מִפְּנֵי גָּדְלוֹ אֵין זֶה מַזִּיק לוֹ – יַזִּיק לְזַרְעוֹ,
for even if on account of his personal greatness it causes no harm to him, it will harm his future offspring,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (מה.): אֲפִילּוּ נֶהֱוֵי כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן לָא יָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ בְּרַתָּא.
as stated in Yevamot (45a): "Even were he to be like Joshua son of Nun, I would not give him my daughter."
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם דִּקְדֵּק וְאָמַר "כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן" וְלֹא "כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם"
Nonetheless, he was precise in saying "like Joshua son of Nun" and not "like Moses our teacher, peace be upon him"
[וְהַפּוֹסְקִים הוֹכִיחוּ מִזֶּה דְּאָסוּר לוֹמַר "כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם", וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם טַעַם יֵשׁ בַּדָּבָר],
[and halakhic authorities deduced from this that it is forbidden to say 'like Moses our teacher,' yet there is an intrinsic rationale in the matter],
כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה, וּמִצַּד כֶּתֶר הַתּוֹרָה אֵין לָחוּשׁ לְמִשְׁפָּחוֹת,
for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is the root of Torah, and from the perspective of the Crown of Torah one is not concerned with ancestral lineage,
וְכֶתֶר תּוֹרָה מוּנָּח לַכֹּל, וְאָמְרוּ (הוֹרָיוֹת יג.): "מַמְזֵר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם קוֹדֵם וְכוּלֵי",
and the Crown of Torah lies open to all, and they taught (Horayot 13a): "A scholar born of illicit union precedes a high priest who is ignorant,"
וּלְכָךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קִבֵּל הָעֵרֶב רַב.
and therefore Moses our teacher accepted the Mixed Multitude (Erev Rav).

paragraphs.text: Turei Zahav on Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 242:20: ““Because of disrespect.” Beit Yosef wrote: It seems to me that this is why the Gemara says, “Even if Yehoshua son of Nun had said it, I would not obey him,” and does not say, “Even if Moshe had said it.” It appears that he understands the disrespect as directed toward Moshe our teacher: the speaker says, in effect, “If another person were like him,” which is impossible, for it is written, “There has not arisen one like Moshe.” In Maharshal’s work on chapter HaChovel, section 53, he cites the following: It is written in the responsa that if a person quarrels with his fellow and says, “I would not accept it from you even if you were like Moshe our teacher,” he is flogged because of the disrespect. [Maharshal continues:] This is a surprising ruling to me, for it is a customary expression and does not greatly disgrace Moshe our teacher. Moreover, ordinarily the speaker did not intend an insult, but merely expressed his refusal to accept forgiveness or appeasement in exaggerated terms. We therefore do not derive further rulings from such a novelty. Nevertheless, it is fitting to be stringent with him through a Monday–Thursday–Monday fast, so that he will take care with his speech. According to his explanation, someone who says “like Yehoshua” should likewise be flogged, for what difference would there be? But the explanation I gave in Beit Yosef’s name appears more correct, since he brings proof from the Gemara. So too in Yevamot: “Even if he were like Yehoshua son of Nun, I would not give him my daughter.””

paragraphs.text: The Torah's emergence through broken vessels is connected with the release of holiness from concealment.

rich.text: The Torah's emergence through broken vessels is connected with the release of holiness from concealment.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Ki Tavo 11:2: “It is taught in the name of the holy Ari that Moses our teacher was the root of the Written Torah, while Rabbi Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah. For this reason Rabbi Akiva came from Sisera and the wife of Heber the Kenite: within them were sparks belonging to the aspect of the Oral Torah, while Sisera was the husk surrounding this holiness.”

rich.text: : “It is taught in the name of the holy Ari that Moses our teacher was the root of the Written Torah, while Rabbi Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah. For this reason Rabbi Akiva came from Sisera and the wife of Heber the Kenite: within them were sparks belonging to the aspect of the Oral Torah, while Sisera was the husk surrounding this holiness.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: In Ki Tavo, Rav Tzadok treats the tradition about Rabbi Akiva's ancestry as the emergence of Oral Torah from a place where its holiness had been enclosed. This gives a mechanism for the present siman's striking example of Torah in ‘broken vessels’: the apparent distance of the vessel does not determine the depth of the Torah hidden within it. The passage concerns a spiritual root and does not erase the distinctions in the siman's opening discussion.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Yitro 23:11-13: “When they reached him [Rabbi Shimon], they found him sitting and studying Torah. He was saying: “A prayer of the poor person when he faints, and before Hashem he pours out his plea.” Every prayer of Israel is a prayer, but the poor person’s prayer is higher than them all. Why? Because it rises to the King’s throne of glory and becomes a crown upon His head. The Holy One, blessed be He, is indeed praised through that prayer. The poor person’s prayer is called “prayer.” “When he faints”: this wrapping is not the wrapping of a garment, for he has none. Rather, here it is written, “when he faints,” and elsewhere, “those who faint from hunger.” “Before Hashem he pours out his plea”—he complains before his Master, and this is pleasing before the Holy One, blessed be He, because through him the world is sustained when no other sustainers of the world are present. Woe to the one against whom that poor person complains to his Master, for the poor person is closer to the King than all others, as it is written, “When he cries to Me, I will hear, for I am gracious.” As for other people in the world, sometimes He hears and sometimes He does not. Why? Because the King dwells in these broken vessels, as it is written, “With the contrite and humble in spirit,” and “Hashem is close to the brokenhearted,” and “A broken and crushed heart, God, You will not despise.””

sections.en: Sometimes Even Through Wicked Children It Is Possible That Some Benefit Sprouts Forth For…

p: [עח] פְּעָמִים גַּם בָּנִים רְשָׁעִים אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִצְמָח אֵיזֶה טוֹבָה לָאָב,
Sometimes even through wicked children it is possible that some benefit sprouts forth for the father,
כְּעִנְיַן אַבְרָהָם שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ יִשְׁמָעֵאל וּבְנֵי קְטוּרָה, שֶׁיָּצָא הַפְּסֹלֶת עַל יְדֵיהֶם.
like Abraham from whom emerged Ishmael and the sons of Keturah, through whom the inner dross was purged.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּזֶה צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה הָאָב שֶׁיֻּפְקַע תּוֹרַת זַרְעוֹ מֵהֶם,
However, in this the father must merit that the legal status of his spiritual lineage be completely severed from them,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאַבְרָהָם: "כִּי בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע",
as written concerning Abraham: "for in Isaac shall seed be called to you" (Genesis 21:12),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים סוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּיבָמוֹת (יז.): לֹא זָזוּ מִשָּׁם עַד שֶׁעֲשָׂאוּם כְּגוֹיִם גְּמוּרִים,
and as stated regarding the Ten Tribes at the end of the first chapter of Yevamot (17a): they did not depart from there until they designated them as complete gentiles;
וְיָדוּעַ דִּבְרֵי רַמְבַּ"ן עַל פָּסוּק "שֹׁרֶשׁ פֹּרֶה רֹאשׁ", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and the words of the Ramban on the verse "a root bearing gall" (Deuteronomy 29:17) are well known, see there.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר לְחִזְקִיָּהוּ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (י.): בַּהֲדֵי כַּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא לְמָא לָךְ?
And concerning this [Isaiah] said to Hezekiah in the first chapter of Berakhot (10a): "Why do you meddle in the secrets of the Merciful One?";
וַהֲרֵי מְנַשֶּׁה מֵאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה נֶאֱבַד חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד וְכָל הַשַּׁלְשֶׁלֶת הַקְּדוֹשָׁה מִן הָעוֹלָם אִלּוּ לֹא נוֹלַד.

for behold, Manasseh was counted among those who have no share in the World to Come, yet nonetheless the Messiah son of David and the entire holy lineage would have been lost from the world, Heaven forbid, had he not been born.
וּמָצִינוּ "וַיִּקֹּד הָעָם וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ" בְּפָרָשַׁת בֹּא, וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י: שָׂמְחוּ עַל בְּשׂוֹרַת הַבָּנִים;
And we find "and the people bowed their heads and worshipped" in Parashat Bo (Exodus 12:27), where Rashi explains: they rejoiced over the tidings of future children;
וַהֲרֵי שָׁם הוּא בִּשְׁאֵלַת "מָה הָעֲבֹדָה הַזֹּאת לָכֶם", שֶׁהוּא שְׁאֵלַת בֵּן רָשָׁע כִּדְאִיתָא בַּהַגָּדָה: "וְאַף אַתָּה הַקְהֵה וְכוּלֵי",
yet there it is framed in the question "What is this service to you?", which is the question of the wicked son as brought in the Haggadah: "you too blunt his teeth, etc.",
וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי שָׂמְחוּ עַל בְּשׂוֹרַת לֵידָתוֹ.
and even so, they rejoiced over the tidings of his birth.
וּמִיהוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא תְּרוּמָה ט) מְפוֹרָשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ עַיֵּין שָׁם,
However, in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Terumah 9) it is explicitly stated to the contrary, see there:
דִּתְפִלַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאִם יְבַקֵּשׁ בֵּן וְהוּא יִהְיֶה רָשָׁע – לֹא יִתֵּן לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
that King Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed that if he should request a son who would turn out wicked, the Blessed Name should not grant him one.

paragraphs.text: Sifrei Devarim 312:1: “Thus, when Avraham our father came into the world, dross emerged from him: Yishmael and all the sons of Keturah. When Yitzchak came into the world, dross emerged from him: Esav and all the chiefs of Edom. They became worse than the earlier ones. When Yaakov came, no dross emerged from him; rather, all his sons were born worthy, as it is stated, “Yaakov was a wholehearted man, dwelling in tents.” Through whom does the Omnipresent recognize His portion? Through Yaakov, as it is stated, “For Hashem’s portion is His people; Yaakov is the allotment of His inheritance,” and, “For Yah has chosen Yaakov for Himself.””

paragraphs.text: Divrei Soferim 38:3: “But the descendants of Yaakov our father can no longer change their name and uproot themselves from the root of Jewish identity. Even if their sins reach the heavens, one remains an Israelite in every respect, and the name Israel is not uprooted from him. This is the root in holiness within all Yaakov’s descendants, for his offspring are complete: there is no dross in the root that comes from him within all his subsequent descendants. Therefore this root of the name Israel, coming from Yaakov our father, remains forever. Esav, however, although born in holiness, still had the choice to uproot himself from this holiness inherited from his forefathers. Although the patriarchs merited that the root of their holiness should be fixed in all their descendants—for through their effort they transformed all their powers to holiness, no evil remained in them at all, and only good can emerge from a good root—they had not yet merited complete offspring until Yaakov. This means that their very essence should be transformed entirely, leaving no possibility of evil, so that their existence should be different from that of other human beings and they could beget only what resembled themselves. Just as a human being is not born from an animal, or an animal from a human being, so a gentile cannot be born from an Israelite, or an Israelite from a gentile. This began with Yaakov, who merited the name Israel for himself and his descendants. Avraham and Yitzchak had not yet had their essence transformed entirely until Yaakov’s birth. Then the promise “Through Yitzchak your offspring shall be called”—but not all of Yitzchak—was fulfilled, and Yishmael and Esav were excluded from being called the offspring of Avraham and Yitzchak. Avraham and Yitzchak were then also completed, so that their offspring were complete, because from then on only Yaakov’s descendants were called and reckoned their offspring.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 6: “When Shem saw his disciple Avraham go to rescue Lot, he could not understand the act according to his own judgment. Seemingly he should not have helped him, since Ammon and Moab would emerge from him, troublesome neighbors of Jerusalem (Sanhedrin 96b), and Hashem had warned that they should not enter the congregation. Why, then, did Avraham risk his life to rescue him? But Shem knew Avraham as his disciple and recognized him as thoroughly righteous, so that surely no stumbling would come through him. He prayed to Hashem to illuminate his eyes and disclose the reason for Avraham's act. Thus it says, ‘He was a priest to God Most High’: when he brought out the bread and wine he was serving Hashem and praying that He illuminate his eyes to understand what lay beyond his own intellect and comprehension. Hashem then illuminated his eyes to show that nothing had been done through Avraham in vain. Although Ammon and Moab would emerge from Lot and were told not to enter (Lamentations 1:10), this restriction concerned the males; the females were permitted immediately. From them would emerge the kingship of David and Shlomo, the principal support of the kingship of the land of Israel and Jerusalem. Therefore he said, ‘Blessed is Avram to God Most High.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach describes Shem's difficulty with Avraham's rescue of Lot: Ammon and Moab seemed to make the rescue an obstacle to Jerusalem's future. The answer appears through the permitted female lines from which David and Shlomo emerge. This is a close structural parallel to the siman's Menashe example: a visible failure in one generation does not disclose the whole future of the line. The qualification concerning male and female descendants is retained in the quotation.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Poked Akarim 4:21: “And although in Parashat Bo it says, “The people bowed and prostrated themselves,” and Rashi explains that this was over the news of children, while the question there is the wicked son’s “What is this service to you?”—there it is Hashem’s unsolicited promise. Evil does not issue from the Most High, and surely a chain of good will ultimately come from them. So too with Chizkiyahu: “Why concern yourself with the Merciful One’s hidden matters?” Although his son was wicked, to the point of being counted among those without a share in the World to Come, a great chain of righteous people later descended from him, and Mashiach will also be of his descendants. Thus what Hashem gives on His own is certainly good. When a person prays for children, he should pray for worthy children and Torah scholars, through whom the glory of Heaven will be increased, sanctified, and multiplied.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Poked Akarim returns to precisely the examples that close this siman. It distinguishes Hashem's unsolicited promise, which can include a hidden future chain of good, from the content of a person's prayer, which should ask for worthy children and increased kavod Shamayim. This supplies the distinction left unresolved here between rejoicing at the promise in Bo and Shlomo's prayer that an ultimately harmful request not be granted.

sections.en: The Concept of a Spiritual Blemish Above Caused by Sins Operates Along the Lines…

p: [עט] עִנְיַן הַפְּגָם לְמַעְלָה עַל יְדֵי עֲווֹנוֹת הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָנוּ אוֹמְרִים שֶׁהַחַמָּה לוֹקָה;
The concept of a spiritual blemish Above caused by sins operates along the lines of what we say when the sun suffers an eclipse;
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַחַמָּה בְּעַצְמוּתָהּ וּמִצִּידָּהּ אֵינָהּ לוֹקָה כְּלָל, רַק הֶעְדֵּר אוֹרָהּ לָאָרֶץ – זֶה מִקְרֵי לַקּוּת לַחַמָּה,
for in truth, the sun in its own essence and from its own perspective suffers no eclipse whatsoever, only that the withholding of its light from reaching the earth is termed an eclipse of the sun,
שֶׁהֲרֵי עִנְיַן תַּכְלִיתָהּ שֶׁל חַמָּה לְהָאִיר לָאָרֶץ, וְזֶה לַקּוּת מִצִּידָּהּ.
seeing that the ultimate purpose of the sun is to illuminate the earth, and this constitutes a failure from its functional side.
וְכֵן בְּכָל לַיְלָה הוּא לַקּוּת הַחַמָּה, שֶׁגַּם זֶה הוּא מִצַּד מָסָךְ הַמַּבְדִּיל, דּוּגְמַת לַקּוּתָהּ בַּיּוֹם.
And so every night is functionally an eclipse of the sun, for this too stems from a separating barrier, analogous to its daytime eclipse.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, כְּשֶׁהַלְּבָנָה מְאִירָה, אֵינוֹ לַקּוּת גָּמוּר לַחַמָּה,
Nonetheless, when the moon shines, it is not an absolute eclipse of the sun,
כִּידוּעַ שֶׁאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה הוּא מֵאוֹר הַחַמָּה וּבְרַק אוֹרוֹ;
for it is known that the light of the moon derives from the light of the sun and the sparkle of its radiance;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָנוּ קוֹרִים אוֹתוֹ אוֹר לְבָנָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַמְּבִינִים יוֹדְעִים כִּי הִיא בֶּאֱמֶת אוֹר חַמָּה וְלֹא לָקְתָה לְגַמְרֵי.
and even though we call it moonlight, those who understand know that it is truly solar light, so that the sun has not suffered a total eclipse.
אֲבָל בְּסוֹף חֹדֶשׁ אוֹ בְּעֵת לִקּוּיָהּ, שֶׁגַּם הַלְּבָנָה אֵין מְאִירָה, אָז הוּא לִקּוּת הַגָּמוּר לַחַמָּה.
But at the end of the month or during a lunar eclipse, when the moon likewise ceases to shine, that is an absolute eclipse of the sun.
וְזֶה מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמָא שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים קיב.): יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁעֵגֶל וְכוּלֵי,
And this is an exact mirror of what transpires Above, as stated (Pesachim 112a): "More than the calf wishes to suckle, the cow wishes to nurse";
וְתַכְלִית הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הָאֲצִילוּת לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל;
and the ultimate purpose of the unfolding of divine Emanation is to channel spiritual influx unto Israel;
וּכְשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל חוֹטְאִים, שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִים אוֹר יְדִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל בּוּרְיוֹ,
and when Israel sins, failing to receive the light of the knowledge of the Blessed Name in its pristine clarity,
אָז נֶחְשָׁב כִּבְיָכוֹל תְּשִׁישׁוּת לְפַמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה;
then it is accounted, as it were, as a weakening of the Heavenly Host;
