paragraphs.text: Poked Akarim 4:2: “All the Oral Torah is hinted at in the Written Torah. Therefore whatever has already been revealed from the Oral Torah and is written down in the books of Israel’s sages has, for us, the character of Written Torah: these hints in the Written Torah have already been revealed and have become a fixed order of governance. The world’s entire governance according to Torah follows the Written Torah and its oral interpretation. Whatever is already revealed from the Oral Torah means that the governance too is already revealed in that form, just as the law is fixed and known to all. Every renewal in governance comes through the renewal of Oral Torah revealed to the hearts of Israel’s sages in that generation. According to those new insights are the renewals in governance, through the righteous person who rules in the fear of God—the true Torah scholar among Israel’s sages.”

sections.en: All Possessions of a Person Derive from the Sparks of His Vital Soul-force Distributed…

p: [צא] כָּל קִנְיָנֵי הָאָדָם הוּא מֵחֶלְקֵי חַיּוּתוֹ הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בַּבְּרוּאִים,
All possessions of a person derive from the sparks of his vital soul-force distributed throughout created beings,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "בְּרֵאשִׁית" – בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי;
as they said: "In the beginning"—for the sake of Israel, etc.;
וְאָמְרוּ: הַמְּחַדֵּשׁ בְּטוּבוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית,
and we declare in prayer: "Who in His goodness renews daily the work of Creation,"
וּבְכָל יוֹם הַחִדּוּשׁ הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל;
and each day's cosmic renewal unfolds for the sake of Israel;
וְכָל חֵלֶק מִן הָעוֹלָם שַׁיָּיךְ לְנֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁאוֹר חַיּוּתוֹ הוּא הַמְּקַיֵּים אוֹתָם הַנִּבְרָאִים.
and every segment of the universe belongs to an individual Jewish soul, meaning that the radiance of his vital force sustains those specific creations.
מִמַּעֲשִׂים הַטּוֹבִים מִתְקַיְּימִים בְּרוּאִים הַטּוֹבִים וְהַטְּהוֹרִים
From good deeds, good and pure creatures are sustained
[וּמִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת הֵם מַלְאָכִים וְרוּחָנִיִּים],
[and from holy thoughts and divine desires, angels and spiritual entities are formed],
וּמֵהָרָעִים נַעֲשִׂים הָרָעִים
while from evil deeds, destructive forces are generated
[וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֵירוּבִין (יח:) מִשִּׁכְבַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה: רוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין]
[along the lines of Eruvin 18b that from wasted seed demons and night-spirits are formed]:
הַחַיּוֹת הַמַּזִּיקוֹת, וְכֵן עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים הָרוֹצְחִים,
dangerous wild beasts, murderous gentiles,
וְכֵן בַּדּוֹמְמִים: אֶבֶן שֶׁנִּסְקַל בָּהּ וְעֵץ שֶׁנִּצְלַב בּוֹ
and likewise among inanimate objects: the stone with which one was stoned and the gallows on which one was hung

[וְזֶה סוֹד מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כד): מִן הַכֹּל עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהִפָּרַע, אֲפִילּוּ מִן אֶבֶן וְכוּלֵי.
[and this is the secret of what our Sages said in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu: from everything the Holy One will exact retribution, even from a stone, etc.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "חַטָּאִים תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְאָנֹכִי בָּרָאתִי מַשְׁחִית לְחַבֵּל",
And this is "evil pursues sinners" (Proverbs 13:21), and "I have created the waster to destroy" (Isaiah 54:16),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ו: אֵשׁ יוֹצְאָה מִגּוּפָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים וּמְלַהֶטֶת אוֹתָן],
and as stated in Bereishit Rabbah 6: fire issues from the bodies of the wicked and consumes them],
וּבַצּוֹמְחִים: סַם הַמֵּמִית רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
and among plants: lethal poison, may the Merciful One spare us, and the like.
וּכְפִי מֶרְחַק הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת אוֹרוֹ וְחַיּוּתוֹ בָּהֶם, כָּךְ הֵם עִנְיָנָם וְיַחְסָם לוֹ:
And in proportion to the closeness or distance of the extension of his light and vitality within them, such is their relationship to him:
מֵהֶם קִנְיָנִים לוֹ, וּמֵהֶם הָיוּ בְּיָדוֹ אֵיזֶה זְמַן וּמְכָרָם,
some remain his permanent possessions; some were in his possession for a time and he sold them;
וּמֵהֶם רַק בִּשְׁאֵלָה אוֹ שְׂכִירוּת זְמַן מוּעָט,
some are merely borrowed or rented for a brief interval;
וּמֵהֶם רָאָם אֵצֶל אֲחֵרִים אוֹ נִסְתַּכֵּל בָּהֶם מִדֵּי עָבְרוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה מָקוֹם,
some he merely saw in the possession of others or gazed upon as he passed by;
וּמֵהֶם שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה מִיָּמָיו רַק חָשַׁק בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ לָהֶם,
and some he never saw in his life, yet yearned for them in his private thoughts;
וְכַיּוֹצֵא יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת לְאֵין שִׁיעוּר.
and like this there are countless gradations without end.
וְהַמֵּבִין עַל דָּבָר יוּכַל לָדַעַת וּלְהִתְבּוֹנֵן לְתַקֵּן כָּל אֵלֶּה,
And he who discerns these matters can understand and reflect on how to rectify all of them,
וְהַתִּיקּוּן הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הַהֲשָׁבָה לַמָּקוֹר
— and this rectification is achieved solely by returning them to the Source:
שֶׁיֵּדַע שֶׁהַכֹּל הוּא מֵעֶצֶם חַיּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמְּחַיֵּיהוּ וּמְקַיְּימוֹ, זוּלַת זֶה הָיוּ כְּלֹא הָיָה
recognizing that everything exists exclusively through the essential vitality of the Blessed Name Who animates and preserves it, without which it would vanish into nothingness
[וְזֶה סוֹד מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עג שֶׁהָיָה לְיַעֲקֹב שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא עֶדְרֵי צֹאן,
[and this is the mystical secret of Bereishit Rabbah 73 that Jacob possessed 600,000 flocks of sheep,
כִּי נַפְשׁוֹ הָיְתָה כּוֹלֶלֶת שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נְפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הַכְּלוּלָה כָּל אֶחָד מִפְּרָטֵי דּוֹרוֹתֵיהֶם,
for his soul encompassed the 600,000 root souls of Israel, each comprising the individual souls of all generations,
וְנִתְפַּשְּׁטוּ אָז חֶלְקֵי אוֹרוֹת נַפְשׁוֹ בַּצֹּאן שֶׁהוּא בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה,
and the rays of his soul-lights were then extended into sheep, which are pure animals,
כִּי אָז עֲדַיִן נִקְרָא יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגַת עַם הָאָרֶץ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק אֵלּוּ מְצִיאוֹת,
for he was then still called Jacob—the level of simple folk, as noted at the end of chapter Elu Metziot—
וְגַם יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לְצֹאן, וְהָיָה קִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁנִּתְפַּרְנֵס מֵהֶם,
and Israel too are likened to sheep; and they were his property from which he derived livelihood,
כִּי מִמַּה שֶּׁהוּא פַּרְנָסַת הָאָדָם שָׁם גָּנוּז עִיקַּר חַיּוּתוֹ,
for within that which provides a person's sustenance lies the core of his vitality,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הַפַּרְנָסָה הִיא עִיקַּר קִיּוּם חַיּוּתוֹ,
since livelihood is the literal preservation of life;
שֶׁלָּכֵן אָמְרוּ (בָּבָא קַמָּא צב:): בֵּירָא דִּשְׁתֵית מִנֵּיהּ מַיָּא לָא תִּשְׁדֵּי בֵּיהּ קָלָא,
which is why they said (Bava Kamma 92b): 'Into a well from which you drank water, do not cast a stone,'
שֶׁאֵין לְבַזּוֹתוֹ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ]:
showing that one must not denigrate the vessel of his sustenance, and this is not the place to lengthen].

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 86:1: “Everything belonging to a person—his wife and children, his male and female servants, his ox and donkey, his tent, his silver and gold, and all that he has—comes from the root of his soul. For all inanimate things, plants, and animals are also rooted in the human soul, and the root of their life comes from it, as is known. What is acquired by him is that whose life is rooted in him. Ownerless possessions and all the beasts of the forest exist because he has not yet repaired the entire root of his life, for these certainly also relate to a person. Concerning the future it is said, “The wolf shall dwell with the lamb.” Likewise, before the sin the serpent served the human being. As the person is, so are his possessions, as it is stated concerning Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair’s donkey: the Holy One, blessed be He, does not bring a stumbling block through the animals of the righteous. Likewise, all the species in Noach’s ark, which he fed, presumably came from his root, as explained above. Therefore the Sages said that they had not corrupted their ways.”

paragraphs.text: The material means of livelihood carries life from its divine source.

rich.text: The material means of livelihood carries life from its divine source.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Rosh Hashanah 13: “The order of these teachings has this meaning. As my grandfather, of blessed memory, said: whenever a person gives an acquisition over to Hashem, Hashem gives that acquisition back to the person with greater strength. Thus, ‘Bring an omer before Me on Pesach’: in this world Hashem placed garments from which a person receives the strength of his life. In truth, the principal life-giving power is the utterance of Hashem’s mouth contained in that garment. If a person takes the garment without recognizing that this utterance is primary, imagining instead that the garment gives him life, he not only fails to receive the utterance; the garment conceals it from him still further. Hashem therefore counsels us to take more than the garment itself, always recognizing the utterance within it. ‘Bring an omer before Me on Pesach’ teaches that at the very beginning of receiving a benefit, when its inward meaning is not yet recognized, it is still called animal food. A benefit whose inward meaning a person does not recognize is animal food. He should return that power to Hashem; this is what the omer offering signifies. Hashem promises that the grain in the fields will be blessed: He will give the person recognition of the benefit, so that he recognizes its inward meaning. This is called the grain in the fields—human food.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains what returning a possession to its source can mean while a person still uses it. Food is a garment through which life is received; the error is to treat that garment as an independent giver of life. The omer models receiving and returning the power in recognition of its Giver. This develops the siman’s account of livelihood as a place where one’s life is lodged, rather than reducing the connection to ownership alone.

Once you have acknowledged His kingship over everything, no more is required: contemplation is not necessary, but rather accepting the yoke of Heaven’s kingship through faith, knowing that nothing is separate from Him or interposes before Him even after the world was created. But the commandment “You shall know,” and so forth, concerns contemplating this. This is the entire wisdom of the Work of Creation and the Work of the Chariot known to the masters of truth. The whole purpose of this wisdom is to demonstrate the truth of this unity: all creation, which appears separate from the Creator, has in truth no separation at all. This is the entire purpose of Torah and all the commandments: to purify the heart until it reaches this knowledge and apprehension through seeing and contemplation—that in every human activity, deed, and device, in everything whatsoever, nothing is separate from Him, blessed be He.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Shavuot 10:2: “This is what is then stated in Raaya Mehemna: the barley omer is animal food, and so forth, and of them it is said, “You are My flock, the flock of My pasture; you are human.” We find concerning Yaakov our father that he had six hundred thousand flocks of sheep, as the Midrash says: Reish Lakish says six hundred thousand; the Rabbis say one million two hundred thousand; they do not disagree, and so forth. The number six hundred thousand signifies the holiness of the congregation of Israel, which is six hundred thousand. Until the giving of the Torah, Israel were in the category of sheep—“the flock of My pasture.” They attained the holiness of the category of humanity—“you are called human”—only after the giving of the Torah, when they attained the beauty of Adam before the corruption. Although Yaakov himself truly possessed the very beauty of Adam, as stated in the holy Zohar, this concerned him personally: he was like Adam before the sin. But for his descendants he did not attain the level of “you are human” until after the giving of the Torah; before the giving of the Torah they were in the category of sheep. Although Yaakov our father said of himself, “The God who shepherds me,” considering himself also to be in the category of sheep—as the Midrash says, “There is no occupation more lowly than a shepherd,” and so forth—David said, “From the elders I gain understanding”: Yaakov called Him a shepherd, and so forth. The reason is that Yaakov considered himself to be in the category of sheep. In particular, the flocks that allude to his descendants really were in the category of sheep until the giving of the Torah, when they attained the level of “you are human.” For this reason we offer barley, animal food, in the omer. On Shavuot, the time when our Torah was given, when they had already merited being called human, with Adam’s beauty, the offering is “Eat of My bread”—the two loaves.”

sections.en: Sometimes Spiritual Levels Are Opened Unto a Person

p: [צב] לִפְעָמִים נִפְתָּח לָאָדָם מַדְרֵגוֹת, וְאִם הוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶעְלָם מִמֶּנּוּ וְהוּא חוֹזֵר לְסוּרוֹ לִהְיוֹת מְשׁוּקָּע בַּתַּאֲווֹת – יֵשׁ לוֹ לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן וְלִדְאוֹג פֶּן הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קח:) בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, שֶׁהִטְעִימָן מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא;

Sometimes spiritual levels are opened unto a person, and if it is only temporary and afterward vanishes from him so that he returns to his waywardness, becoming immersed in desires—he must reflect and worry lest he be, Heaven forbid, in the category of what our Sages said in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 108a) regarding the Generation of the Flood, that He gave them a foretaste of the World to Come;
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק הָיָה קוֹרֵא שֶׁהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם הֲנָאָה וְחֶמְדָּה מֵעִנְיְנֵי תַּאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק נֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה,
and behold, they said in the chapter Hayah Koreh (Berakhot 17a) that the World to Come contains no pleasure or lust of worldly matters, but only delighting in the radiance of the Shechinah,
וְאַחַר פְּתִיחַת אוֹר כָּזֶה הֲרֵי לֹא הָיוּ עוֹד בְּנֵי מַבּוּל, רַק עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁנִּפְתַּח לָהֶם לְשָׁעָה וְנֶעְלַם;
and after the opening of such an illumination they should no longer have been corrupt, so perforce it opened to them for a brief hour and then vanished;

וְהוּא אֶחָד עִם הַדָּבָר אַחֵר דְּשָׁם דְּקָאָמַר: "זְמַן קָטָן אַחַר זְמַן גָּדוֹל", שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה זְמַן אוּלַי יָשׁוּבוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁפָּתַח לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹר כָּזֶה, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן הֶעְדֵּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶעֱלִימוֹ כְּרֶגַע וְחָזְרוּ לְתַאֲוָתָם.

and this is synonymous with the alternative interpretation there that says: "a short time after a long time," meaning an interval wherein perhaps they would repent through the Blessed Name opening such light to them—which also removes the evil inclination—and afterward He concealed it in an instant and they returned to their lust.
וְאִידַךְ לִישָּׁנָא: שֶׁהֵם יְמֵי אֶבְלוֹ דִּמְתוּשֶׁלַח, וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִיתַת צַדִּיקִים מְכַפֶּרֶת כְּשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ (יוֹמָא מב.),
And the other Talmudic formulation holds that these were the days of mourning for Methuselah, which means that the death of the righteous atones like the scapegoat (Yoma 42a),

the only distinction being that the Blessed Name opens the portal to repentance and radiates His light through an awakening from Above (itaruta de-le'ela) first, as noted above;
וּלְכָךְ בְּאוֹתָם יְמֵי אֶבְלוֹ הָיָה כֵּן אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא מִקּוֹדֶם, אַחַר זְמַן גָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם לִהְיוֹת שׁוּבוּ וְכוּלֵי בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא:

and therefore during those days of his mourning there was such an awakening from Above first, after the long period that preceded it to bring about "return unto Me, etc." through an awakening from below.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 1:1: “Here, however, the expanded state came first. As the writings of the holy Ari teach, on this night the expanded consciousness preceded the constricted consciousness. The expanded state is like someone who understands a matter because he has a great intellect, without any labor at all. Yet, because it came without labor, he can easily forget it. This is unlike someone who understood a matter through labor: it becomes fixed in his heart so that he cannot forget it. Although this is called the constricted state, the matter is nevertheless fixed in his heart like a peg that will not move.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim distinguishes the intensity of a revelation from its permanence. A person may grasp something through an extraordinary gift and still lose it; work makes the understanding fixed in the heart. This clarifies why Rav Tzadok treats the Flood generation’s taste of the world to come as an opening to repentance whose purpose was not fulfilled merely by experiencing it.

paragraphs.text: Poked Akarim 3:1: “It is known what the Sages said concerning “Hashem is your shadow”: He is like the shadow that does what the body itself does. All His attributes are measure for measure; it is not without cause, but because they also turn their attention to Him. Yet the blessed God desires that awakening from below come first: “Return to Me and I shall return to you,” while we ask, “Bring us back to You, and we shall return.” For we have no strength to begin: You must first bring us back through awakening from above, and then we shall return. So it was in Egypt: through awakening from above, the blessed God sent them “I have surely taken notice,” and through this “they will listen to your voice”—they would immediately believe this declaration. By Moshe our teacher’s saying “I have surely taken notice,” he introduced into their hearts complete faith in the blessed God’s providence over them. They therefore listened specifically to his voice: through his voice he brought hearing into them, through that very voice and declaration of “I have surely taken notice,” which he placed within their hearts. As soon as this entered their hearts, they understood the truth that the blessed God was certainly taking notice of them. Once it was revealed in the depths of their hearts that He watches over them, and they believed this with complete faith, it was certainly fitting in judgment that He watch over them. The removal of providence and of God’s remembrance of a person occurs only when the person is also in concealment from God. But when a person remembers God and believes that God is with him and watches over all his affairs, God certainly remembers and watches over him too. In Egypt they had been utterly submerged in forgetfulness. They possessed this sign: the redeemer who spoke in the language of taking notice would introduce into their hearts the awareness and remembrance that there is a blessed Creator who directs, watches over, and can bring them out of Egypt. Through this, the corresponding attention above follows. There cannot be attention above without remembrance also entering their hearts. Sometimes the awakening above comes first, but afterward, in any event, there must be awakening below. This is the sign of the redeemer’s using the language of taking notice: they could immediately sense in their hearts whether that awareness arose within them too. So it was: “The people believed, and they heard that He had taken notice.” Through hearing that He had taken notice, faith entered their hearts.”

But when a person remembers God and believes that God is with him and watches over all his affairs, God certainly remembers and watches over him too. In Egypt they had been utterly submerged in forgetfulness. They possessed this sign: the redeemer who spoke in the language of taking notice would introduce into their hearts the awareness and remembrance that there is a blessed Creator who directs, watches over, and can bring them out of Egypt. Through this, the corresponding attention above follows. There cannot be attention above without remembrance also entering their hearts. Sometimes the awakening above comes first, but afterward, in any event, there must be awakening below. This is the sign of the redeemer’s using the language of taking notice: they could immediately sense in their hearts whether that awareness arose within them too. So it was: “The people believed, and they heard that He had taken notice.” Through hearing that He had taken notice, faith entered their hearts.”

sections.en: Initially, the Blessed Name Illuminates a Person, But the Person Is Not Yet Accustomed…

p: [צג] תְּחִלָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לָאָדָם, וְהָאָדָם אֵין רָגִיל בָּזֶה עֲדַיִן וְקָשֶׁה עָלָיו לְקַבְּלוֹ כְּיָתֵד קָבוּעַ בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן שֶׁלֹּא יִמּוֹט, וּמְאַבְּדוֹ;

Initially, the Blessed Name illuminates a person, but the person is not yet accustomed to this and finds it difficult to secure it as a nail driven into a firm place so that it will not give way, and he loses it;

וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָאָדָם נוֹהֶה אַחֲרָיו וּמְבַקְּשׁוֹ, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּפוֹתֵחַ לוֹ, כְּטַעֲנַת "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי", אִם לֹא בְּקֹשִׁי גָּדוֹל, כְּעִנְיַן "כְּשֶׁרָצִיתִי לֹא רָצִיתָ, עַכְשָׁו וְכוּלֵי" (בְּרָכוֹת ז.).

and afterward the person yearns after Him and seeks Him, but the Blessed Name does not readily reopen it to him, parallel to the plea of "Bring us back, etc.," unless with great difficulty, in the manner of: "When I desired, you did not desire; now, etc." (Berakhot 7a).
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, הָיָה בִּכְפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָדָר קִבְּלוּהָ בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ בְּרָצוֹן;
And this is the concept of the Giving of the Torah: it occurred through overturning the mountain like a vat (Shabbat 88a), and afterward they re-accepted it willingly in the days of Ahasuerus;
אֲבָל לֹא נַעֲשָׂה לָהֶם נֵס בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא כְּבִימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא כִּדְאִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (ד.), רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר חֵטְא הַקּוֹדֵם;
but a miracle was not performed for them in the days of Ezra as in the days of Joshua son of Nun, because sin caused it (Berakhot 4a), meaning the prior sin;
וְלֹא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי.
and the Shechinah did not dwell overtly in the Second Temple (Yoma 21b).

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אִיתָא בְּסוֹף סֵפֶר הֵיכָלוֹת שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְּנָה תּוֹרָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל מַעֲלוֹתֶיהָ, עַיֵּין שָׁם י"ז מַעֲלוֹת דְּחָשֵׁיב, לֹא הָיוּ עַד הַבַּיִת שֵׁנִי, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה בּוֹ שְׁכִינָה.

And nonetheless, it is stated at the end of Sefer Heikhalot that even though the Torah had been given, all its sublime virtues—see there seventeen virtues enumerated—did not exist until the Second Temple, despite the Shechinah not dwelling overtly therein.
וְעַיֵּין עוֹד שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחוּ אֶבֶן עַל אֶבֶן בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי עַד שֶׁכָּפוּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְגִלָּה לָהֶם רָזֵי כָּל דָּבָר, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
And see further there that they did not lay stone upon stone in the Second Temple until they coerced the Holy One, blessed be He, and He revealed to them the mysteries of every matter, see there;
וְ"כָפוּ" הוּא נֶגֶד כְּפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and "they coerced" stands corresponding to the coercion of the mountain like a vat at the Giving of the Torah

[וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דִּכְפִיָּה זוֹ הוּא בִּיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (סט:) שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁפֵּירְשׁוּ בְּפֶרֶק אֵין עוֹמְדִין (בְּרָכוֹת לב.) וּבְהֶחָלִיל (סֻכָּה נב:)].

[and one may say that this coercion represents the nullification of the evil inclination of idolatry (Yoma 69b), which was seemingly counter to the initial divine plan, as in "whom I have afflicted" (Micah 4:6), and as they explained in Perek Ein Omdin (Berakhot 32a) and in HaChalil (Sukkah 52b)].
וְהָעֵצָה בְּהֶעְלֵם הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ אֵיכָה): "הַלְוַאי אוֹתִי עָזָבוּ וְתוֹרָתִי שָׁמָרוּ";
And the remedy in times of spiritual concealment is words of Torah, as in: "Would that they had forsaken Me but kept My Torah" (Midrash Rabbah, introduction to Eichah);
וְכֵן בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי הֵחֵלּוּ חַכְמֵי הַמִּשְׁנָה, וְעַל זֶה אָמַר שֶׁכָּל מַעֲלוֹת הַתּוֹרָה הָיוּ שָׁם יוֹתֵר,
and so in the Second Temple the Sages of the Mishnah began, and concerning this it said that all virtues of Torah were greater there,
וְזֶה בֶּאֱמֶת גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יב.): "חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא":
and this is in truth greater, as stated in Bava Batra 12a: "A sage is superior to a prophet."

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 7:5: “Shabbat 13b says: ‘Who wrote Megillat Ta’anit? They said: Chananyah ben Chizkiyah and his circle, who cherished the troubles.’ Apparently it should have said that they cherished the miracles; what have they to do with the troubles? Yet through the troubles and decrees they merited Torah’s illumination. As it says, ‘Your rod and Your staff comfort me’: precisely through the disciplinary rod, the support came to them with greater force. Pirkei Heikhalot says that although the Divine Presence did not dwell in the Second Temple, Torah’s splendor, preciousness, honor, and greatness were not given until the Second Temple. The intention is the Hasmonean period, when the illumination of Oral Torah began.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah explains the otherwise surprising expression ‘cherished the troubles’: the troubles became the setting in which greater Torah illumination was acquired. It invokes the same contrast between the Second Temple’s concealed Shechinah and its expanded Torah. The parallel clarifies the present siman’s movement from a light first bestowed and then lost to wisdom patiently sought in concealment. The gain is the Torah received through the renewed search, not difficulty considered in isolation.

paragraphs.text: What remains after Torah study
The lasting effect of study is distinguished from drawing Torah into the heart at the outset.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Simchat Torah 7:1: “The meaning of a blessing after it is what remains permanently in a person’s heart after he engages in Torah. A blessing before it concerns the person’s drawing words of Torah into his heart. But the result of those words of Torah that he has drawn into himself should remain in his heart permanently, like a peg that will never move. That permanence is called the blessing after it.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The Ishbitz teaching defines permanence by what remains after the act of learning. That distinction illuminates the siman’s opening difficulty: receiving light does not yet make it a fixed possession. The comparison supplements the existing historical explanation of the Second Temple with a description of the inward result sought by the learner.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 21b:7: “But was there fire in the Second Temple? Rav Shmuel bar Inya said: What is meant by the verse, ‘I shall take pleasure in it and be honored,’ where ve’ekkaved is written but ve’ekkavedah is read? Why is the letter hei missing? These are the five things that distinguished the First Temple from the Second Temple: the Ark, its cover, and the cherubim; the fire; the Shechinah; ruach hakodesh; and the Urim and Tummim. They answered: Yes, the fire was there, but it did not assist in the burning.”

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Bahya, Bereshit 46:27:2: “From the day the Divine Presence rested upon Mount Sinai at the giving of the Torah, it did not depart from Israel until the First Temple was destroyed. From the destruction of the First Temple, the Divine Presence did not rest among Israel, for in the Second Temple the Divine Presence did not rest. The intention is not to say that the Divine Presence did not rest in the Second Temple at all, for we find that it rests among twenty thousand, from what is written, “Return, Hashem, to the myriads of the thousands of Israel,” and, “The chariots of God are myriads, thousands upon thousands; Hashem is among them.” It need hardly be said that the Divine Presence rests among forty thousand. Moreover, Scripture testifies, “I shall be pleased with it and be glorified”—meaning: I shall cause the Glory, which is the Divine Presence, to rest in it. Rather, it did not rest there constantly as in the First Temple, because there were not six hundred thousand there: only forty thousand came up from Babylonia, as it is written, “The entire congregation together was forty thousand.” This is what the Sages expounded concerning “I shall be pleased with it and be glorified”: the written form of “be glorified” lacks the letter heh because five things were missing there—the Ark, the anointing oil, fire, the Divine Presence, and the Urim and Tummim. For this reason it says “be glorified,” to explain that the Glory, which is the Divine Presence, was there, but not Tiferet; this is the force of “be glorified,” excluding Tiferet. The missing heh, the last letter of the Name, indicates the absence of the Divine Presence, for it is among the five things that were missing. How was it absent, when Scripture says “I shall be glorified”? Rather, it did not rest there constantly as in the First Temple, but hovered over it. In the future, however, Israel will be numerous beyond counting. This is what is written: “The number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea.” It does not say, “The seed of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea,” but “the number”—meaning that those counted from twenty years of age and upward will be like the sand of the sea. Then Tiferet and the Glory will return. So Yeshayahu promised: “Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of Hashem has shone upon you.” Understand this.”

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 17:11: “As is stated explicitly in Sefer Heikhalot, the principal radiance and splendor of Torah were in the Second Temple period, even though the Divine Presence did not rest there. See there the many expressions of praise concerning that time, and how, because they longed for the blessed Lord to reveal the secrets of Torah to them, He promised them this. This is revelation through the wisdom of Oral Torah. They longed for it, to attain still greater understandings, even though it comes through concealment. Through this came the departure of prophecy: through the intensity of their longing for the revelation of Torah insights far above the attainment of the prophets, and for the mysteries of Oral Torah within their hearts in a concealed way, which is the quality of night. Prophecy, which was drawn from the prophecy of Moses our teacher, of blessed memory, departed. Therefore the prophets’ words, too, appeared in writing, like Written Torah, whose quality is day—that is, clear revelation, without darkness or concealment.”

paragraphs.text: Context: This is Rav Tzadok’s parallel discussion in Machshavot Charutz. It confirms how he understands the Heikhalot tradition: the Second Temple period disclosed the splendor of Oral Torah despite the absence of overt revelation of the Divine Presence. The quotation is from Machshavot Charutz, not from Sefer Heikhalot itself, and does not enumerate the seventeen virtues mentioned in the reader.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 69b:6-10: ““They cried out to Hashem God with a great voice.” What did they say? Rav said, and some say Rabbi Yochanan: Woe, woe! This is the one that destroyed the Temple, burned its Sanctuary, killed all the righteous, exiled Israel from their land, and still dances among us. Did You give it to us for any reason other than that we should receive reward through it? We want neither it nor its reward! A note fell to them from heaven, on which “Truth” was written. Rav Chanina said: Learn from this that the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth. They observed a fast for three days and three nights, and it was handed over to them. It emerged like a fiery lion cub from the Holy of Holies. A prophet said to Israel: This is the inclination to idolatry, as it is stated, “He said: This is wickedness.” As they seized it, a hair slipped from its mane; it cried out, and its voice traveled four hundred parasangs. They said: What shall we do? Perhaps, Heaven forbid, they will have mercy on it from heaven. A prophet told them: Throw it into a lead pot and cover its mouth with lead, for lead absorbs sound, as it is stated, “He said: This is wickedness. He cast it into the ephah and cast the lead weight over its mouth.””

paragraphs.text: Derekh Hashem, Part Four, On Torah Study 6: “Torah study in relation to the influences it brings: The second condition is rectifying one’s conduct. One who wishes to draw down an influence must be worthy and prepared to draw it down. But if he defiles himself through guilt and transgression, distances himself from his Creator, and strays after the powers of impurity and evil, it will certainly be said of him: “To the wicked, God said: What right have you to recount My statutes?” Likewise the Sages said: Whoever teaches an unworthy student is as though he throws a stone to Markulis. Such a person’s Torah will certainly draw down none of the influence we have described. Nevertheless, the Sages revealed a great secret to us: had the wicked not abandoned Torah study, they would ultimately have returned to the good. Although they cannot draw down any influence from before Him, as explained, the words of Torah themselves remain holy in their own right. Through persistent engagement with them, they will bring the student, time after time, a little awakening, like the faintest glimmer of illumination, which will eventually prevail over him and bring him back to the good. This is what the Sages wrote: “If only they had abandoned Me but kept My Torah, for its light brings them back to the good.” It is clear, however, that this does not concern someone who engages with it as mockery or jest, or to give it interpretations contrary to halakhah. Rather, he must engage with it at least as someone engages with other fields of wisdom.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 52:7: “Through the wisdom of the Oral Torah, which brings human wisdom into Torah, Esav and also Amalek are overcome, for through this one is attached to Torah’s hidden root. As it is written in Bava Batra: “A sage is greater than a prophet”; see Ramban there, who explains that this is attainment through the holy spirit. This means a spirit from the higher holiness—higher wisdom—which influences lower wisdom. The fiftieth gate hidden from Moshe our teacher refers to his attainment through prophecy, which is like seeing with his own eyes. Concerning this, according to one opinion in Rosh Hashanah, they said: “Among prophets none arose, but among kings one arose.” This means attainment through the attribute of kingship, lower wisdom. Although this is a lesser mode of attainment, it has an advantage in being able to attain matters that are higher. As is known, the divine Rabbi Yitzchak [the Ari] revealed the place and root from which Moshe our teacher’s attainment came, and he revealed lofty secrets far above that root. But all his attainments were only through the holy spirit, which bears no comparison with prophetic vision—even the unclear mirror of the other prophets, and all the more so the prophecy of Moshe our teacher. Prophetic attainment is revealed attainment, and through revelation one can attain only what can be attained in this world. Concerning the attainment of the World to Come, “No eye has seen”—meaning the eyes of the prophets, who see with the eye. The sages’ attainment, by contrast, comes from concealment, and they can also attain the hidden root. Although it is said concerning this, “Do not investigate what is beyond you,” and so forth—for the root hidden from every creature’s eye is called “beyond,” the supreme wonder, where there is no permission to inquire at all—this means attaining it completely through wisdom. Nevertheless, they have a hold upon it because the root of their wisdom comes from there. Since it is the wisdom of their hearts that has become Torah, it is attached to its root.”

paragraphs.text: Chiddushei Ramban on Bava Batra 12a:1: “Regarding the statement, “From the day the Temple was destroyed, although prophecy was taken from the prophets, it was not taken from the sages”: Rashi explained, “Although it was taken from prophets who are not sages.” This can be challenged, for in tractate Nedarim we say that the Holy One, blessed be He, causes His Presence to rest only upon someone wise, strong, and wealthy. Some answered that He causes His Presence to rest without interruption only upon a sage, but a prophet sent on a mission is different, such as the prophecy of Yonah son of Amittai on the mission to Nineveh. I am not satisfied with this. Rather, it means: although the prophecy of the prophets, which is appearance and vision, was removed, the prophecy of the sages, which comes by way of wisdom, was not removed. They know the truth through the holy spirit within them. For on a temporary occasion He causes His Presence to rest even upon pious people who are not sages; there we say, “From where do we know this? From Moshe,” and Moshe’s prophecy did not cease. This is the force of the expression “causes His Presence to rest.” Although the proof concerning wealth is also brought from Yonah, he was a prophet without interruption, but was sent only to Nineveh.”

sections.en: Sometimes a Person Attains an Illumination

p: [צד] פְּעָמִים מַשִּׂיג הָאָדָם הֶאָרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַגִּיעַ לְיִרְאָה, וְהוּא פָּנִים שֶׁל זַעַם;
Sometimes a person attains an illumination, and through it reaches awe/fear, which is the aspect of a severe, wrathful countenance (panim shel za'am);
וּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ עַל יָדוֹ לְאַהֲבָה, הוּא פָּנִים שֶׁל רָצוֹן;
and when through it he ascends to love, it is a countenance of favor (panim shel ratzon);
וְעַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ, הוּא מְתַקֵּן הַזַּעַם שֶׁבַּפָּנִים וּמִתְהַפֵּךְ לְרָצוֹן, וּבָא אַחַר כָּךְ לְאַהֲבָה.
and through the awe he possesses, he rectifies the wrath of the countenance, transforming it into favor, subsequently arriving at love.
אֲבָל אִם מַדְחֶה אָז מִפָּנָיו עַל יְדֵי הוֹלֵלוּת וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת, אָז אֵין נִתְקַן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְאָז הוּא "וְנָתַתִּי פָנַי בָּאִישׁ הַהוּא וְגוֹמֵר", רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.

But if he banishes it from his face through frivolousness and extraneous thoughts, then it is not rectified, Heaven forbid, and it becomes: "And I will set My face against that man, etc." (Leviticus 20:5), may the Merciful One preserve us.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם "פָּנִים" הוּא פְּתִיחוּת אוֹרוֹ.
And in every place, "panim" (face/countenance) signifies the opening of His light.
כִּי לְעוֹלָם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹתֵחַ שַׁעַר לִתְשׁוּבָה, וּבִשְׁעַת מִיתָתוֹ אָדָם רוֹאֶה שְׁכִינָה, זֶה נִקְרָא פָּנִים שֶׁל זַעַם;
For the Holy One, blessed be He, forever opens a gate for repentance, and at the hour of his death a person beholds the Shechinah, which is termed a severe countenance;
כִּי לְעוֹלָם פָּנִים הוּא הֶאָרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר מַגִּיעַ לָאָדָם, כִּי כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן פָּנָיו בּוֹ וּמִסְתַּכֵּל אֵלָיו – הֲרֵי "בְּאוֹרְךָ נִרְאֶה אוֹר";
for "panim" is always an illumination when it reaches man, since when the Blessed Name turns His face toward him and gazes upon him, behold: "in Your light do we see light" (Psalms 36:10);
וְאָמַר: "פָּנַי יֵלֵכוּ וַהֲנִחֹתִי לָךְ", כִּי יִרְאָה אֵינֶנָּה נִיחָא כַּנּוֹדָע:
and Scripture says: "My presence (Panai) shall go with you, and I will give you rest" (Exodus 33:14), for awe is not restful composure, as is known.

paragraphs.text: Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 1:1: ““I have placed Hashem before me always” is a great principle of Torah and of the virtues of the righteous who walk before God. A person’s sitting, movements, and activities when he is alone in his house are not like his sitting, movements, and activities when he is before a great king. Nor are his speech and free expression when he is with his household and relatives like his speech in the king’s presence. All the more so when a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it is stated, “Can a man hide in hidden places and I not see him? says Hashem.” Immediately fear and submission will come upon him in awe of the blessed God, and shame before Him always. [Guide of the Perplexed, Part III, chapter 52.]”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Resisei Layla 36:1: “These three kinds of repentance proceed from below upward. First a person has compassion on himself; this is easy for anyone to awaken on his own. Afterward he begins to feel awe before Hashem and the splendor of His majesty, and through this he sighs over his sins. Afterward he comes to love of Hashem and weeps before Him over what has already passed and is no longer.”

Afterward he begins to feel awe before Hashem and the splendor of His majesty, and through this he sighs over his sins. Afterward he comes to love of Hashem and weeps before Him over what has already passed and is no longer.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Resisei Layla describes the movement that the siman compresses into a few lines: self-concern gives way to awe before Hashem, and awe can lead to love. The quoted sequence explains why the first alarming illumination is an opening that requires a response, rather than a condition in which the person is meant to remain.

paragraphs.text: Devarim Rabbah 2:12: “Another explanation of “like Hashem our God”: This is what Scripture says, “As for me, may my prayer to You, Hashem, be at a time of favor.” Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa asked Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman: What is the meaning of this verse? He answered: The gates of prayer are sometimes open and sometimes locked, but the gates of repentance are always open. He asked: From where is this known? For it is written, “With awesome deeds in righteousness You answer us, God of our salvation, the trust of all the ends of the earth and of the distant sea.” Just as a ritual pool is sometimes open and sometimes locked, so the gates of prayer are sometimes open and sometimes locked; but as the sea is always open, so the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, is always open to receive those who return. Rav Anan said: Even the gates of prayer are never locked, as it is written, “Like Hashem our God whenever we call to Him.” Calling means prayer, as it is stated, “Before they call, I shall answer.” Rabbi Chiya the Great said: It is written, “Hope to Hashem; be strong, and He will strengthen your heart; hope to Hashem.” Pray and pray again, for there is an hour when it will be granted to you. Another explanation of “As for me, may my prayer”: David said “a time of favor” because he was an individual. But the prayer of a congregation never returns empty. Thus: “Like Hashem our God whenever we call to Him.””

sections.en: In the Days of Youth

p: [צה] בִּימֵי הַנְּעוּרִים רְתִיחַת הַתַּאֲוָה מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת, וְאָז מַרְבֶּה חֲטָאִים מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן, וְהֵם חַטֹּאת נְעוּרִים;
In the days of youth, the boil of passion surges, and then one multiplies sins from the side of the evil inclination, may the Merciful One preserve us, which are the sins of youth;
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם: "כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו".
and this occurred in the Generation of the Flood, as written there: "for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Genesis 8:21).
וְגַם כֵּן מְסַגֵּל טוֹב הַרְבֵּה מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הַטּוֹב וְחַשְׁקוּת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְזֶה הָיָה דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְזָכַרְתִּי לָךְ חֶסֶד נְעוּרַיִךְ";

And likewise, one amasses much good from the side of the good inclination and burning passion for words of Torah, and this was the Generation of the Wilderness, as written: "I remember for you the kindness of your youth" (Jeremiah 2:2);

וְהֵם עַצְמָם אוֹתָם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר פִּינְחָס (רטז סוֹף עַמּוּד א, עַיֵּין שָׁם) דְּהָיוּ רְאוּיִים לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה בַּמַּבּוּל אִלּוּ זָכוּ, וְנִשְׁמַת מֹשֶׁה הָיְתָה שָׁם.
and they were identical souls, as written in the Zohar (Pinchas 216a end, see there) that they were fit to receive the Torah during the Flood had they merited, and the soul of Moses was there.
וְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ, אָז יִהְיֶה פַּעַם שְׁלִישִׁית אוֹתוֹ דּוֹר, בְּסוֹד מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "תִּתְחַדֵּשׁ כַּנֶּשֶׁר נְעוּרָיְכִי";
And the generation of the Messiah will be that same generation for a third time, in the mystery of: "your youth is renewed like the eagle" (Psalms 103:5);
וְאָז יִהְיֶה הַתִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר, שֶׁבָּאוֹת בְּעִרְבּוּבְיָא חַטֹּאת נְעוּרִים וְחֶסֶד נְעוּרִים, וְהַטּוֹב יִתְגַּבֵּר עַל הָרַע וִיהַפְּכוֹ לְטוֹב.
and then complete rectification will take place, when the sins of youth and the kindness of youth arrive intermingled, and the good will overpower the evil and transform it into good.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר נֹחַ (עב עַמּוּד ב) וּבַתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן יח): "כַּד תֶּחֱמֵי קַשְׁתָּא בְּאַנְפִּין נְהִירִין תְּצַפֵּי לְרַגְלֵי מְשִׁיחָא",
And this is what is stated in the Zohar (Noach 72b) and in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 18): "When you see the rainbow in radiant hues, anticipate the footsteps of the Messiah,"
שֶׁהַקֶּשֶׁת הוּא אוֹת הַבְּרִית נֶגֶד עוֹנְשֵׁי חַטֹּאת נְעוּרִים,
for the rainbow is the sign of the Covenant counter to the retributions of the sins of youth,
וּבְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ יִהְיֶה זֶה בְּאַנְפִּין נְהִירִין בְּהֶאָרַת פָּנִים, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר עֵינֵיהֶם לָדַעַת כִּי סָר עֲוֹנָם בָּזֶה,
and in the generation of the Messiah this will appear in radiant hues with a luminous countenance, where the Blessed Name enlightens their eyes to know that their iniquity has departed in this realm,
וְ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים וְגוֹמֵר", פֵּירוּשׁ שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית כַּנּוֹדָע:
and "your people are all righteous, etc." (Isaiah 60:21), meaning guardians of the Covenant, as is known.

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok also records the Flood, wilderness, and messianic sequence in a dream remembered from Izbica.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Chalomot 3:1: “I dreamed [while I was in Izbica] that certain matters concerning the root of my soul were being revealed to me. Among these matters, I was told that the generation of the Messiah would be the very same souls as the generation of the wilderness [and the Messiah is the soul of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, as mentioned in Raaya Mehemna, Zohar III, 246b]. They themselves are the same souls as the generation of the Flood [for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was there too, as stated in the Zohar, III, 216b, and as they said in Chullin 139b: beshagam has the numerical value of Moshe]. At that time they corrupted their way. This sin is called in the books “the sin of youth,” as it is said of them, “for the inclination … from his youth.” They repaired this in the generation of the wilderness, when it was called “the kindness of youth” [as is known concerning the inward meaning of “a person’s desire is his kindness”], as it is written, “I remember for you the kindness of your youth.” The generation of the Messiah will embody “your youth is renewed like the eagle’s”: the same generation of youthful kindness will be renewed a second time. This is the substance of what I still remember.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Divrei Chalomot records the same sequence as a remembered dream, explicitly identifying the souls across the three generations. Tzidkat HaTzadik supplies the analysis of their work: youthful intensity first becomes corruption, then longing for Torah, and finally a good that transforms the intermingled evil. The parallel helps the reader distinguish the reported visionary setting from this siman’s explanation of the spiritual process. Neither passage describes the final renewal as a mere return to youthful innocence.

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 10:4: “It is known that being called “evil” in the eyes of the blessed God concerns impairment of the covenant, as was said of Er: “Er, Yehudah’s firstborn, was evil in the eyes of Hashem, [and Hashem put him to death],” and of King David concerning that incident: “I have done what is evil in Your eyes.” This is the root of evil in creation: the creation of the foreskin that covers the holy covenant. It is named only after the nations, as it is said, “All the nations are uncircumcised,” as we learn in Nedarim; this is the root of the nations’ evil in creation. For this reason the commandment of circumcision was given to Israel, who can remove that evil present from birth, because for them it is not at the root, but like thorns surrounding the rose and thorns around a myrtle. Although evil also has a hold upon that limb in Israel—this is the touching of the hollow of Yaakov’s thigh, where Esav’s angel had the power to accuse, since there is some root there of the little folly present from birth, concerning which they said, “Full of iniquity—even the most pious of the pious intends only his own pleasure”—concerning this it is said, “I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.” The Sages expounded: “A heart to bring forth flesh.” This will occur only in the future, through the blessed God’s removal of the heart of stone by slaughtering the evil inclination. Although Yaakov our father merited this even in this world, as they said concerning “Give me my wife”—“It was said only to establish descendants”—and therefore it is stated that he did not die, nevertheless, on account of his descendants, who are not like this, the hollow of his thigh was touched. But all this is only temporary, in this world, which resembles night: it is the world of falsehood, which lasts “only for a moment.” As soon as the sun shone upon him, he was healed of his limp. For in truth even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised, since the foreskin is not at their root at all, and “what is destined to be cut is regarded as already cut.””

Although Yaakov our father merited this even in this world, as they said concerning “Give me my wife”—“It was said only to establish descendants”—and therefore it is stated that he did not die, nevertheless, on account of his descendants, who are not like this, the hollow of his thigh was touched. But all this is only temporary, in this world, which resembles night: it is the world of falsehood, which lasts “only for a moment.” As soon as the sun shone upon him, he was healed of his limp. For in truth even the uncircumcised of Israel are called circumcised, since the foreskin is not at their root at all, and “what is destined to be cut is regarded as already cut.””

paragraphs.text: Context: The parallel explains why an inclination present from youth is nevertheless open to repair. It preserves the difference between Yaakov’s individual attainment, his descendants’ present struggle, and the complete removal of the inclination in the future.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 196:1: “Love of Torah without the blessed God—that is, love of wisdom alone—is the generation of the Flood, concerning which the Zohar says that it was then fitting for the Torah to be given. For they loved Torah and wisdom greatly. This is the meaning of “the sons of God [came] to the daughters of man”: it is known that the feminine is desire and the masculine its fulfillment. Angels have wisdom and attainment, but they have no evil inclination or longing. As stated in Midrash HaNe’elam, even desire for words of Torah requires the evil inclination. A human being has desire but lacks attainment, and then they joined—this is not the place to explain it. But without the blessed God, sexual wrongdoing proceeds from this. The children of Israel, the seed of Avraham who loved Me, have love of the blessed God fixed within them from birth and from the womb. This is the root, corresponding to Keter, which is beyond human grasp. Chokhmah and Binah are love of Torah and of Israel, for Binah is the heart, and there lies the chief love of companions, as it is written, “So the human heart to another.” Every attribute is a complete structure; these are the first three within the attribute of Chesed, and afterward the lower seven are their extension into the powers. They are the powers of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah: the bond of Israel to one another is from nefesh; the bond to Torah is from ruach; and the bond to the blessed God is from neshamah, which is beneath the Throne of Glory. Therefore they said, “The soul You placed within me is pure,” for no corruption applies there, since it is a portion of the Divine. Love of the blessed God does not move away at all. Therefore they said, “If only they had abandoned Me but [kept] My Torah,” for the children of Israel cannot abandon Him, as it were, as in “With poured-out wrath I shall reign over you.” Even if a person greatly increases transgressions to provoke, the root of love of the blessed God, corresponding to Keter, the hidden root of thought, is not severed there at all, for “although he sinned, he is still Israel.” The First Temple’s destruction was for “their abandoning My Torah”; but through love of Torah, its light brings the hidden love of the blessed God into revelation.”

paragraphs.text: The promise becomes recognizable even amid fear and concealment.

rich.text: The promise becomes recognizable even amid fear and concealment.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Noach 5: “‘When I bring a cloud over the earth, the rainbow will appear in the cloud.’ A cloud means awe and concealment; a rainbow means strong confidence. Even amid the intensity of awe you will have great trust. This is what the Holy One promised Noach. Thus the holy Zohar says (Bereshit 72b): do not anticipate the footsteps of Mashiach until you see a rainbow in luminous colors. This means: when the assurance from Hashem is clear and explicit before your eyes, then anticipate the footsteps of Mashiach. This is why Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi (Ketubot 77b), ‘Was the rainbow seen in your days?’ He did not ask, ‘Did you see it?’ ‘Was seen’ implies sometimes, rather than constantly; for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the rainbow was constant. Israel’s rainbow and strength are the passage of Shema Yisrael, which gives strength to the hearts of those who hope for His kindness.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach reads the cloud as concealment and the rainbow as the strength to trust within it. Its explanation of the rainbow’s luminous colors therefore clarifies the siman’s closing point: messianic illumination makes the assurance of the covenant apparent. The source’s contrast between occasional and constant perception also explains why the language concerns a revealed sign rather than confidence inferred from outward calm.

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:16:1: ““And it shall be, when I bring a cloud”—a cloud of water, which was the principal element in the generation of the Flood; although there was a flood of fire and water, the principal element stated in Scripture is a flood of water. This is the Lord’s glory: when a person bends his nature and struggles for the sake of the Lord’s will. This is the appearance of the rainbow in the cloud.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Matot 8:1: “The rainbow is the aspect of a strong assurance, for the Holy One, blessed be He, made a covenant that all flesh would never again be cut off by the waters of the Flood. [From the author’s manuscript.] Certainly this is not without a reason, if judgment calls for annihilation, for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not waive judgment. Rather, the rainbow, which is the appearance of the likeness of Hashem’s glory, awakens repentance. Therefore Tikkunei Zohar says: “When you see the rainbow in bright colors, look for the footsteps of the Messiah,” for Israel are redeemed only through repentance. “In bright colors” means that the awakening from above toward repentance will shine within the heart. Thus far. This means that even after all the corruptions in the world, repentance will avail, for “the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth.” This corresponds to Binah, the heart, as it is said, “His heart will understand, and he will return, and be healed.””

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Noach 1:2-3: “Come and see: all Israel have a share in the World to Come. Why? Because they guard the covenant upon which the world endures, as it is said, “Were it not for My covenant day and night, I would not have established the laws of heaven and earth.” Therefore Israel, who guard the covenant and accepted it, have a share in the World to Come. Moreover, for this reason they are called righteous. From here we learn that everyone who guards this covenant, upon which the world endures, is called righteous. From where do we know this? From Yosef: because he guarded the covenant of the world, he merited being called righteous. Therefore: “Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.””

sections.en: One Who Guards the Covenant and Never Experienced a Nocturnal Emission in His Days…

p: [צו] מִי שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית וְלֹא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו, הוּא נִקְרָא "יְפֵה תֹאַר" בַּכָּתוּב, כְּעִנְיַן יוֹסֵף: "יְפֵה תֹאַר";
One who guards the Covenant and never experienced a nocturnal emission in his days is termed "fair of form" (yefeh to'ar) in Scripture, as in the case of Joseph: "fair of form" (Genesis 39:6);
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "שֶׁקֶר הַחֵן וְהֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי",
and regarding this it is said: "Grace is deceitful and beauty is vain" (Proverbs 31:30),
כִּי מָצִינוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁהָיוּ נְקִיִּים מִזֶּה, כְּמוֹ עוֹג שֶׁפָּלַט מִדּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, וּבְלֹא תֵּבָה כְּלָל;
for we find even among gentile nations those who were clean of this, such as Og who escaped from the Generation of the Flood, and that without an ark at all;
וַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה נִיסָא לְשִׁקְרָא, רַק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בֶּן מַבּוּל, דְּהַיְינוּ מַשְׁחִית זֶרַע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק כָּל הַיָּד (נִדָּה יג:),
surely a miracle would not occur for falsehood, but rather he was not subject to the Flood decree because he did not spill seed, as stated in Niddah 13b,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר אַגְּמָרָא דְּנִדָּה (סא.) שֶׁהָיָה בֶּן אֲחִיָּה בַּר שַׁמְחֲזַאי, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ
and as I wrote elsewhere on the Gemara in Niddah 61a that he was the son of Achiyah bar Shamchazai, and this is not the place to elaborate
[וּלְכָךְ נִיתְּנָה אַרְצוֹ לַחֲצִי מַטֵּה מְנַשֶּׁה מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף, שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית].
[and therefore his land was given to the half-tribe of Manasseh from the seed of Joseph, guardians of the Covenant].

וּלְכָךְ נִתְיָירֵא מֹשֶׁה מִמֶּנּוּ, כִּי מֹשֶׁה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֻלִּין קלט:): "בְּשַׁגַּם" – בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא מֹשֶׁה, וְנֶאֱמַר עָלָיו: "כִּי מִן הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ", שֶׁהָיָה אָז בַּמַּיִם.

And therefore Moses feared him, for Moses was likewise present in the Generation of the Flood, as our Sages expounded (Chullin 139b): beshagam shares the numerical value of Moshe, and it is said of him: "because I drew him out of the water" (Exodus 2:10), meaning he was then in the water.
וְגַם כָּל עִיקַּר עִנְיַן מֹשֶׁה הָיָה לְתַקֵּן דָּבָר זֶה הַנִּקְרָא שְׁטוּת, שֶׁלְּכָךְ הָיָה פָּרוּשׁ מִן הָאִשָּׁה וְקָבוּר מוּל בֵּית פְּעוֹר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר;
And furthermore, Moses's entire mission was to rectify this matter termed folly, which is why he separated from his wife and was buried opposite Beit Peor, as I wrote elsewhere;
וְרָאָה זֶה נָקִי כָּל כָּךְ, נִתְיָירֵא מִמֶּנּוּ, עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "אַל תִּירָא",
and seeing Og so pristine in this trait, Moses feared him, until the Holy One, blessed be He, told him: "Fear him not" (Numbers 21:34),

כִּי קַיְימָא לַן בִּנְדָרִים (לא:): הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הָעֲרֵלִים אָסוּר בְּמוּלֵי אֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמוּתָּר בְּעַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרָא אֶלָּא עַל שְׁמָם, אֲפִילּוּ הֵם מוּלִים וְשׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית.

for we establish in Nedarim 31b: one who vows against the uncircumcised is forbidden to circumcised gentiles and permitted to uncircumcised Jews, for "uncircumcision" is designated solely upon their name, even if they are physically circumcised and guard the covenant.
וְ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" וְשׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית, אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁקִּלְקְלוּ:
And "your people are all righteous" and guardians of the Covenant, even when they have stumbled.

Through being guarded against sexual transgression and fearing the Lord, the beauty associated with women extends also to men, for fear of the Lord belongs primarily to the feminine side, as is known.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 44:1: “It is known what is written about Og escaping the generation of the Flood: this certainly was not for nothing, but because he was free of the sins of the generation of the Flood—end of quotation. It is also known what is written in the Zohar, volume III, at the beginning of 216b: the giving of the Torah was fit to occur in the generation of the Flood, and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was present then too—beshagam has the numerical value of Moshe—had they merited it. Through their sin, however, the flow of Torah’s waters was changed into the waters of the Flood. Likewise, they said in Zevachim 116a that at the giving of the Torah the nations of the world gathered to Balaam. According to the statement in the chapter Chelek, Sanhedrin 106b, that Balaam was killed at the age of thirty-three, which was in the fortieth year after the Exodus, he was therefore born seven years after the giving of the Torah. We must say: just as the root of the soul of Moses our teacher is called “Moses,” as stated above concerning his presence in the generation of the Flood, and similarly the Talmud says, “Moses, you have spoken well,” addressing a Torah scholar of a generation who possesses some of Moses’ wisdom, so Balaam corresponds to the knowledge of the other side. The nations’ deliberation with their own understanding is called their gathering to Balaam. Similarly, they said in Sotah 11a that he was among Pharaoh’s advisers, according to which he lived for very many years; yet Sanhedrin 106b applies to him, “Men of blood and deceit shall not live out half their days.” Sefer HaYashar writes that Pharaoh’s adviser was a different Balaam, this one’s grandfather, but the Sages’ wording does not suggest this. The same applies to their exposition in Sanhedrin 106a of “He saw the Kenite”: “You were with me in that counsel.” Rather, the meaning is as I have written: the root of the knowledge of the other side is called “Balaam,” whether clothed in a particular soul or present in Pharaoh’s own understanding. “Perhaps the Holy One, blessed be He, is bringing a Flood”: in accordance with their own condition, they took the flow of Torah’s waters coming into the world to be the waters of a Flood. If so, Og, who was saved from the Flood, necessarily had some connection with Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Purim 13:3: “‘Gladness’ is circumcision, as it says, ‘I rejoice over Your utterance.’ Here too the matter is of this kind. Circumcision appears to a person as though he is repairing a lack that Hashem created in him. Yet did Hashem, Heaven forbid, create a lack? In truth, the holiness of circumcision is completely fixed in every soul of Israel even before he circumcises himself. As the Gemara says (Nedarim 31b): one who vows not to benefit from the uncircumcised may benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may not benefit from circumcised gentiles; one who vows not to benefit from the circumcised may not benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may benefit from circumcised gentiles. Uncircumcision is named only after the latter, as it says, ‘For all the nations are uncircumcised.’ Thus gentiles are called uncircumcised even when circumcised, and an Israelite is called circumcised even while uncircumcised. This proves that the holiness of circumcision is fixed and enduring in Israel even without their act of service. Yet a person cannot recognize that permanently present holiness except by first circumcising himself. Every person must therefore initially experience concealment, imagining that Hashem created a lack in him and that he repairs it through his service. Through this concealment every soul is obliged to circumcise himself. After he is circumcised, it is revealed retrospectively that the holiness of circumcision is permanently within him.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim develops the same vow-law proof while preserving a crucial qualification. Israel’s rooted relation to the covenant is not created by the physical act, yet the act remains necessary to disclose it. This helps explain the siman’s distinction between an outwardly unblemished appearance and belonging at the root of the covenant, without making the final assurance a reason to disregard the mitzvah.

p: [צז] תִּיקּוּן לְמוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה הוּא עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל:): בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע, בָּרָאתִי תוֹרָה תַּבְלִין;
The rectification for emitting seed in vain is engagement in Torah study, as stated (Kiddushin 30b): "I created the evil inclination, I created the Torah as its antidote";
וְאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קְרָאוֹ "רָע", וְהַיְינוּ בַּעֲוֹן דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל דְּהַיְינוּ מוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה
and they stated in Sukkah 52a: the Holy One, blessed be He, called it "evil," which refers to the sin of the Generation of the Flood, namely emitting seed in vain
[וְאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (יג.) דְּלֹא נִגְזַר עַל דָּגִים שֶׁבַּיָּם, הַיְינוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל פָּסוּק "וּרְדוּ בִּדְגַת הַיָּם"],
[and they said in Kiddushin 13a that the decree did not fall upon the fish of the sea, which represent Torah scholars, as I wrote elsewhere on "and have dominion over the fish of the sea"],
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר בְּרֵאשִׁית (נז עַמּוּד א) וּבְרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּל הַיָּד דְּנִקְרָא רַע, זֶה הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי";
and as written in Zohar I:57a and at the beginning of chapter Kol HaYad that it is called "evil," this evil inclination that the Holy One created, as written: "and whom I have afflicted";
וּלְכָךְ יִמָּצֵא זֶה גַּם בַּחֲלוֹם, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה נִיכָּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִפְּעֻלַּת אָדָם.
and therefore this occurs even in dreams, showing clearly that this is not from the voluntary action of man.

וְתַבְלִין הוּא לְמַתֵּק הַמַּאֲכָל, הַיְינוּ לַהֲפוֹךְ הָרַע לְטוֹב מְאֹד כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט): זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִמְתָּק.
And an antidote/spice (tavlin) sweetens food, meaning transforming the evil into "very good" (Bereishit Rabbah 9), which is the evil inclination sweetened through words of Torah.
וּבַזֹּהַר בְּרֵאשִׁית וְנֹחַ: דְּלֵית מְסָאָבָא כְּמוֹהוּ.
And in the Zohar (Bereishit and Noach): there is no defilement like it.
וְהִנֵּה אָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק ב דִּבְרָכוֹת (טז.) דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַעֲלִין מִטֻּמְאָה לְטָהֳרָה.
And behold, they said in the second chapter of Berakhot (16a) that words of Torah elevate from impurity to purity.

וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר נֹחַ (סב עַמּוּד א) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה, הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יח.): בְּזֶבַח אֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר, אֲבָל מִתְכַּפֵּר בַּתּוֹרָה; הָכָא נַמֵּי כֵּן;

And what is written in Zohar Noach (62a) that repentance does not avail, is along the lines of Rosh Hashanah 18a: through sacrifice it is not atoned, but it is atoned through Torah; here too it is so;
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שִׁילְהֵי חֲגִיגָה: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין אוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט בָּהֶם.
and as our Sages expounded at the end of Chagigah (27a): the fire of Gehenna has no dominion over Torah scholars.
גֵּיהִנָּם גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא "רָע", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת סא.) עַל פָּסוּק "לֹא יִנָּקֶה רָּע",
Gehenna is likewise called "evil," as stated in Berakhot 61a on "he shall not be unpunished of evil" (Proverbs 11:21),
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (יט.) שֶׁהַכֹּל יוֹרֵד לָהּ עַל עִסְקֵי חִנָּם, הַיְינוּ שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית;
which aligns with Eruvin 19a that all descend there on account of vain pursuits, which refers to the preservation of the Covenant;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ גַּם כֵּן: "בָּרָאתָ גֵּיהִנָּם", שֶׁגַּם כֵּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרָאוֹ כְּמוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע
and this is why they said: "You created Gehenna" (Bava Batra 16a), which the Blessed Name created just as He created the evil inclination

[וְאָמְרוּ שָׁם גַּם כֵּן: "בָּרָאתָ צַדִּיקִים", צַדִּיק בְּכָל מָקוֹם שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית, גַּם הוּא מִתְּחִלַּת בְּרִיאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בָּאוֹת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי זֶה, כִּי יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם בִּרְשָׁעִים וּבְאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים].

[and they said there: "You created the righteous," where "tzadik" everywhere denotes the guardian of the Covenant, which also exists from the inception of Creation, as I wrote in the preceding section, since it exists even among the wicked and the gentiles].
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
And regarding this it is stated: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalms 23:4).
"רָע" הוּא דַּרְגָּא הַנִּזְכָּר, וְ"אַתָּה" פֵּירוּשׁ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבָּרָאתָ:
"Evil" refers to this aforementioned level, and "You" means by virtue of the fact that You created it.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 21:6: “Why did the Sages say, “You might say their hope is lost …,” when nothing stands in the way of repentance? This initial possibility follows the holy Zohar’s statements that repentance for this blemish is difficult. It depends on the first blemish—the serpent’s instigation—being completely clarified, so that deliberate sins become merits. The death that the serpent brought into the world would then cease as a consequence. That clarification cannot occur in this world until the days of the Messiah, when we merit eternal life. This is the Messiah’s light: “He asked life of You; You gave him length of days forever and ever.” Then the Messiah will “smell and judge,” as Sanhedrin 93b says, because the quality of fragrance and purity will be completely perfected: “His sensing by scent is in the fear of the Lord.” Therefore they said, “Scripture says, ‘The mandrakes have given fragrance’: both these and those will in the future give fragrance.” Even one who has, Heaven forbid, blemished this always has hope and repair, by taking care to turn his heart and eyes away from evil thoughts and continually entering into the occupation of Torah. As Maimonides says at the end of the laws of forbidden intercourse, “Thoughts of forbidden relations grow strong only in a heart empty of wisdom.” Through occupation in Torah one merits holy sight, as it says, “Your eyes shall see your teachers.” The word Torah means that it instructs a person in the revelation of the glory of His blessed name. Through this one merits the fragrance of purity: “The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever.” Occupation in Torah is the consummation of repentance and the repair of the blemish mentioned above. The word yirah, fear, hints at repentance, as they expounded, “‘Happy is the man who fears the Lord’—happy is one who repents while still a man.” They likewise said, “The purpose of wisdom is repentance …,” for “The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord.” Through Torah study it is always possible for the blemish to be repaired even in this world, as it says, “Healing to all his flesh.” And “The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever” refers to Torah, as the holy Zohar explains: it remains with a person forever, purifying him and refining his soul so that he merits a spirit of purity.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The Chanukah passage directly addresses the apparent loss of hope raised by the Zohar’s severe language. It distinguishes the complete removal of the serpent’s damage from the real purification that Torah can accomplish now. This expands the present siman’s comparison to atonement through Torah: a limitation on another form of repair does not close this path. Its practical description also explains the metaphor of seasoning—Torah enters and redirects the life of the heart rather than leaving the inclination untouched.

paragraphs.text: The exclusion of offerings does not exclude Torah and acts of kindness.

rich.text: The exclusion of offerings does not exclude Torah and acts of kindness.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Rosh Hashanah 1: “Rava said: through sacrifice and meal offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through Torah. Abaye said: it is atoned through Torah and acts of kindness. Thus the Talmud says (Megillah 31b) that on Rosh Hashanah we read ‘Hashem remembered Sarah’ and take the haftarah from Channah. Earlier it is written (I Samuel 2:27), ‘A man of God came to Eli,’ continuing through ‘all the increase of your house.’ The Sifrei identifies this man as Elkanah, Shmuel’s father. What did Shmuel add in his prophecy, when his father had already delivered that prophecy? He added its concluding words: ‘The sin of Eli’s house shall not be atoned through sacrifice and meal offering.’ The inference is: through sacrifice and meal offering it is not atoned, but it is atoned through Torah and acts of kindness. Even a decree accompanied by an oath therefore has a repair. Elkanah’s earlier prophecy had supplied no repair; Shmuel added that there is nothing in the world for which there is no repair. This is why we take the haftarah from Channah: even a decree accompanied by an oath has a repair.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef spells out the inference Rav Tzadok invokes. The added words about sacrifice in the prophecy concerning Eli’s house identify a limit on one means of atonement while opening another. This is the logical comparison behind the siman’s reading of the Zohar’s severe language; it does not erase the need for the actual repair described by the source.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 15:15: “The earlier authorities already protested this, for nothing stands in the way of repentance. In the section Noach it says, “All a person’s sins … depend on repentance; but the sin of pouring out seed … your iniquity is stained … except through great repentance.” These three words, “except,” and so forth, are enclosed in brackets, because they are absent from older books and were added from another manuscript version. Reishit Chochmah, in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 17, writes that some manuscript versions read, “except through the power of mighty repentance.” This appears to contradict the wording in Vayechi, which closes the door to repentance altogether. But in Vayakhel too, after describing at length the damage done by impairing the covenant, it says, “These words apply when one has not performed complete repentance, repentance fit to cover all one’s deeds.” Yet we still need a reason for its treating repentance for this sin so stringently. As I have written, with regard to repentance it is less severe, according to all opinions, even than prohibitions punishable by lashes, and certainly than offenses carrying excision or judicial execution. We have already noted the teaching in Kiddushin 49b: there is no wicked person, whatever the transgression, who cannot be considered wholly righteous through a thought of repentance in the heart in a single moment. There it says simply “even a wholly wicked person,” implying every transgression in the world, with none excluded.”

sections.en: Every Verse of Torah Contains the Latent Power and Vitality of That Specific Matter…

p: [צח] כָּל פָּסוּק שֶׁל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ וְחַיּוּת שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ.
Every verse of Torah contains the latent power and vitality of that specific matter of which it speaks.
תֵּדַע בִּתְפִלִּין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָיָה לְאוֹת וְגוֹמֵר", וְלֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אֵיזֶה פָּרָשָׁה מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לְאוֹת,
You may know this from tefillin: Scripture states: "And it shall be for a sign, etc." (Exodus 13:9), yet it did not explicitly specify which passage of the Torah must serve as this sign,
וְהַהֲלָכָה לִכְתּוֹב אוֹתָם הַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם זֶה
— and the halakhic ruling is to write those exact passages in which this is stated—
מִסְּתָמָא אוֹתָהּ פָּרָשָׁה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ פָּסוּק "וְהָיָה לְאוֹת וְגוֹמֵר", יֵשׁ בָּהּ אוֹתָהּ עִנְיַן כֹּחַ וּסְגֻלָּה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה לְאוֹת.
presumably because that very passage contains the inherent power and spiritual virtue to serve as that sign.
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה יָדוּעַ הַרְבֵּה לְיוֹדְעֵי הַשֵּׁמוֹת וּבְקַבָּלָה מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת, כִּי מִכָּל פָּסוּק יוֹצֵא שֵׁם הַמּוֹעִיל לְאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן הַנִּזְכָּר בַּפָּסוּק.
And similar to this is widely known to masters of holy Names and practical Kabbalah, for from every verse emerges a Name effective for the specific theme mentioned in the verse.
וְכֵן פָּסוּק "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל", בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַקְּבִיעוּת הַשְּׁמִיעָה בַּלֵּב, וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ שֶׁיֹּאמַר גַּם תֵּיבַת "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל".
And likewise the verse "Shema Yisrael": within it lies the power to embed hearing into the heart, which is why one must articulate the words "Shema Yisrael."
וְזֶה סוֹד גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן" (מִשְׁלֵי י, לב),
And this is also the secret of what I heard on the verse "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable" (Proverbs 10:32):
כִּי הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל כָּתַב סְגֻלָּה לְמִי שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ מְסִיתוֹ לְאֵיזֶה עֲבֵירָה – לְדַבֵּר בְּפִיו כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים פָּסוּק הַלָּאו שֶׁל הָעֲבֵירָה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִשְׁתַּנֶּה הָרָצוֹן;

for the holy Ari wrote an efficacious remedy for one whose inclination incites him to a transgression: to utter verbally multiple times the biblical negative prohibition of that sin, whereby the desire will be transformed;
וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן מִצְוָה וְדָבָר טוֹב:
and likewise regarding a positive commandment and a good matter.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Poked Akarim 6:7: “All Israel’s miracles and deliverances are through the power of Torah. Miracles in Scripture are through the power of the very letters in which the miracle is written; those are the substance of Torah through which the miracle is drawn. This is also known concerning the operation of divine names: in the letters of the verse describing a miracle is alluded the name that effects that matter. As the Tikkunim say (Tikkun 69), the name ‘Hakhtav’ comes from the verse ‘The writing was the writing of God’ (Exodus 32:16), and ‘Hadoresh’ from ‘To know how to sustain the weary with a word’ (Isaiah 50:4), and similarly elsewhere. It is so at the plain level too, through the power of those words of Torah. Every word of Torah has pardes—plain meaning, allusion, exposition, and secret—as is known; through these four ways, too, those words of Torah have the power to effect the miracle. Miracles that were not given to be written occur through the power of Oral Torah. This began after the miracle of Esther.”

The correspondence is more than a useful reminder: the letters recording the event are described as Torah through which its power is drawn. The distinction between written and Oral Torah also keeps the account from being reduced to a single technique involving written divine names.
