paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Writings, Proverbs 10:1: ““The lips of the righteous know what is pleasing.” This follows what the Sages said: “They compel him until he says, ‘I am willing.’” Through his speech he introduces willingness into his heart as well. This is “the lips of the righteous”: what he says only with his lips, because his heart is not yet clarified, helps him clarify his heart so that he wills it wholeheartedly. For example, when anger toward his fellow arises in his heart and he recognizes this as a failing, his first counsel is to speak kindly to his fellow. Even though this is not yet wholehearted, through it he works upon himself little by little, until he brings love into his heart in place of hatred. This is “know what is pleasing”: “know” means arranging. Through speech he arranges his will until he establishes it wholeheartedly in his heart. Similarly, “The sun knows its setting” means that it has order and regularity in its course, unlike the moon, whose path is sometimes longer, as stated in Rosh Hashanah.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Yisrael Kedoshim 7:28: “In Israel, even this is good, as they said: “They enticed Him with their mouths, and lied to Him with their tongues; their hearts were not firm with Him—but He, being merciful, forgives iniquity.” The Rambam’s explanation of “we compel him until he says, ‘I am willing’” is known: his heart’s refusal comes only from the evil inclination. Of this it says, “The lips of the righteous know favor.” I received the explanation that even when one sees that his heart does not yet want it, good speech with the mouth, called “the lips of the righteous,” helps teach and draw willingness into the heart as well. Yitzchak thought the same was true of Esav: since he saw him at least offering enticement with his mouth, he loved him in order to draw him toward his holy source.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim explicitly interprets the same verse, “The lips of the righteous know favor,” as speech that draws a good will into the heart. This makes the present siman’s counsel more intelligible: repeating a relevant verse is not merely reporting an intention already present. The words can help form the intention, while the distinction between Israel and Esav in the source prevents equating every outward profession with genuine inner repair.

sections.en: A Sign of Complete Repentance Is When One No Longer Remembers the Sin At…

p: [צט] סִימָן לִתְשׁוּבָה גְּמוּרָה – כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר כְּלָל הַחֵטְא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (נח:) שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה: "זְכוֹר וְכוּלֵי";
A sign of complete repentance is when one no longer remembers the sin at all, as stated in Bava Metzia 58b that one must not say to a penitent: "Remember your former deeds, etc.";
וְכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין מַזְכִּיר לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה הַגָּמוּר, וּמִמֵּילָא אֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר.
and so the Blessed Name does not bring it to mind for the complete penitent, and consequently he does not remember it.
כִּי כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָאָדָם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "מִי שָׂם פֶּה וְגוֹמֵר", וְכֵן כֹּחוֹת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְהַזְּכִירָה, וְאִם אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹפֵעַ לוֹ וּמַזְכִּיר לוֹ – אֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר.

For all human faculties derive from the Blessed Name—"Who makes man's mouth, etc." (Exodus 4:11)—and likewise the faculties of thought and memory; if the Blessed Name does not bestow it and remind him, he cannot remember.
וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק א: שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לוֹמַר: אֵינִי זוֹכֵר עֲווֹנוֹתָיו וְאֵין עוֹלִין עַל לִבִּי;
And in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 1: the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to say: "I do not remember his iniquities and they do not arise in My heart";
וּכְבָר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי וְגוֹמֵר",
and our Sages already taught (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): the Holy One is the heart of Israel, as stated: "God is the rock of my heart, etc." (Psalms 73:26),
מִמֵּילָא גַּם עַל לִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה, וְזֶהוּ מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
so naturally it does not arise in the human heart either, which is a foretaste of the World to Come.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ אָדָם לְעֹמֶק הַתְּשׁוּבָה כָּזֶה, שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַכַּפָּרָה, אֵינוֹ בְּנִיחָא;
And as long as a person has not reached such profound depth of repentance, which is the ultimate perfection of atonement, he is not at restful ease;

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 7:1: ““All Israel have a portion in the world to come”: this means the hidden depths of their hearts, which are not disclosed even to the person himself. This is the root of their soul, a portion of God above, concerning which it was said that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel. This is the mystery of the world to come, corresponding to the heart, as is known. It is the portion in the world to come that all Israel possess, even sinners, for all sins arise from the material aspect and its manifestation in this world, and not from the depth of the pure soul, hidden in this world and revealed in the future. Then “the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun”: the light of the Congregation of Israel will shine and radiate like “the Lord is a sun and shield,” as it were. This follows what they said: “In the future Israel will be called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He”—that is, they will be included in their source. Concerning this they said at the end of the chapter Elu Ovrin that the divine name will be read as it is written: the inward light will be revealed without a concealing and covering garment. That garment is the source of the root of the Congregation of Israel in this world, in which there is concealment, and their cleaving to the living God is not fully revealed until the future, when the Holy One, blessed be He, renews His world. It will be that same world, yet entirely renewed. In this world it is sufficient to know that there is a world to come, and through this they have a portion, as stated at the beginning of the chapter Chelek: one who denies it has no portion.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov explicitly places the two directions together: the person keeps the sin before him, while Hashem puts it aside. This comparison helps read the siman’s final sentence alongside its description of completed forgiveness. Rav Tzadok describes the peace of complete repair, while the person’s chosen task remains honest remembrance and return; ordinary loss of memory is not itself the spiritual attainment described here.

paragraphs.text: Sha'arei Teshuvah 4:21: “Concerning “My sin is always before me,” the Midrash explains that the sins should be before his eyes and remembered in his heart, but he should not mention them with his mouth. The Jerusalem Talmud gives a further explanation: they should not be in your eyes as though you had not done them, but as though you had done them and they had been forgiven. We have already mentioned this among the principles of repentance. Nevertheless, he should ask for mercy all his life for the forgiveness of his earlier and later sins, and fear lest he has not fulfilled the requirements of repentance. … But he should not recount the earlier sins individually after repenting of them and confessing them on Yom Kippur, for he has already fulfilled the command of confession concerning them. He should trust that his confession has been accepted to the extent that confession is fit to atone. Still, he should pray all his days for the forgiveness of his sins, as we said. Specifying the sins is an obligation of confession, not of prayer.”

sections.en: Teshuvah Means That One Returns (meshiv) That Matter Unto the Blessed Name

p: [ק] תְּשׁוּבָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁמֵּשִׁיב אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר אֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁהַכֹּל פּוֹעֵל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכֹחוֹ,
Teshuvah means that one returns (meshiv) that matter unto the Blessed Name, recognizing that everything is the operation and power of the Blessed Name,
אֲפִילּוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה טֶרֶם נוֹצְרָה בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט).
even the thought before it is formed within the heart of man (Bereishit Rabbah 9).
נִמְצָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נָתַן לוֹ כֹּחַ אָז גַּם בְּהָעֲבֵירָה,
Thus it turns out that the Blessed Name granted him the strength then even in the sin,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה, אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַגְּמוּרָה, הוּא זוֹכֶה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשִׂין זְכִיּוֹת, כִּי גַּם זֶה הָיָה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּךְ,
and through this, after complete repentance, he merits that willful transgressions become merits, for this too was the will of the Blessed Name,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פט:): "אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים וְכוּלֵי",
as stated in Shabbat 89b on "if your sins be as scarlet, etc." (Isaiah 1:18),
וּכְעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וַיֵּשֶׁב ד) עַל פָּסוּק "נוֹרָא עֲלִילָה עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם",
and in the spirit of Midrash Tanchuma (Vayeishev 4) on "awesome in deed toward the children of men" (Psalms 66:5),
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "לְמַעַן תִּצְדַּק בְּדָבְרֶךָ", רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר לְכָךְ נִטְּלָה מִמֶּנּוּ הַסַּיַּעְתָּא,
and in King David's words: "that You may be justified when You speak" (Psalms 51:6), meaning that Heavenly assistance was withdrawn from him for this very purpose,
וְאִם כֵּן הוּא מַמָּשׁ כִּזְכִיּוֹת מֵאַחַר שֶׁגַּם זֶה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and if so, it is literally like merits, since this too was the will of the Blessed Name.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַחֲסִידֶיךָ יְרַנֵּנוּ", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי יְשַׁעְיָה רֶמֶז רצו): אֵלּוּ רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי,
And this is "and let Your pious ones sing for joy" (Psalms 132:9), expounded (Yalkut Shimoni, Isaiah 296) as referring to the wicked of Israel;
וְכֵן עַל פָּסוּק "אִסְפוּ לִי חֲסִידָי וְגוֹמֵר" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם).
and likewise on "Gather My pious ones unto Me, etc." (Psalms 50:5).
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי "חָסִיד" הוּא הַנּוֹטֶה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין לְהִתְחַסֵּד, וְכֵן רָשָׁע נוֹטֶה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין לְהַרְשִׁיעַ;
For a "chasid" (pious one) deviates from strict justice to act with piety, and a wicked one deviates from strict justice to do wrong;
וּכְשֶׁיִּפְתַּח הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֶעָתִיד אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַגְּמוּרָה, וְיַכִּירוּ הַכֹּל כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתוֹ,
and when the Blessed Name reveals in the future after complete repentance, and all recognize the power of His sovereignty,
נִמְצָא הַזְּדוֹנוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ נְטִיָּה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין – הָיוּ חֲסִידוּת, כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ נוֹטִים מֵאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
it will turn out that the willful sins which deviated from strict justice were acts of chasidut, since they did not deviate from the absolute will of the Blessed Name.
וְדָיֵיק "חֲסִידָי" וַ"חֲסִידֶיךָ", וְלֹא "חֲסִידִים", רַק שֶׁאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם קְרוּיִים חֲסִידִים, וְלֹא לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם.

And Scripture is precise in saying "My pious ones" and "Your pious ones," not simply "pious ones," because in the eyes of the Blessed Name they are called pious, though not in the eyes of human beings.
וְצַדִּיק וְחָסִיד הֵם שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת בָּאָדָם בְּתוֹלָדָה, וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז.): "בָּרָאתָ צַדִּיקִים, בָּרָאתָ רְשָׁעִים",
And "tzadik" and "chasid" are two innate levels in man, regarding which they said (Bava Batra 16a): "You created the righteous, You created the wicked,"
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִילּוּ "צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע" לָא קָאָמַר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנִדָּה (טז:);
even though the angel does not decree whether one will be righteous or wicked (Niddah 16b);
רַק אֵלּוּ הֵם שְׁנֵי כֹּחוֹת בְּעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים, רַק תְּמוּר "רָשָׁע" הוּא שֵׁם "חָסִיד" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
but these are two primal forces in supernal worlds, where the holy counterpart of "wicked" is the title "chasid,"
וּשְׁנֵי הַכֹּחוֹת מְעוֹרָבִים בְּכָל אֶחָד, רַק אֵינָם שָׁוִים, בְּאֶחָד זֶה גּוֹבֵר, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ:
and both forces are intermingled in each person, differing only in which one dominates, and this is not the place to elaborate.

paragraphs.text: Akeidat Yitzchak 28:1:4: “Therefore God gives the gentle warning, “Go and see the works of God”: direct your hearts toward the sacred, and do not err in this. His attributing these events to human actions is a matter of a pretext, for those divine purposes will in any case come to pass and will not turn aside, without thereby compelling people in the details of their individual actions. Similarly, the woman was not compelled to mix her husband’s cup with lukewarm or cold water because he intended to divorce her. Her mixing it lukewarm was only a pretext on his part: had that not occurred, another reason—or many others—would not have been lacking, and all those actions remained possible for her, as we explained.”

paragraphs.text: The light of Mashiach ben David develops the siman’s distinction between righteousness from the outset and a past transformed through complete repentance.

rich.text: The light of Mashiach ben David develops the siman’s distinction between righteousness from the outset and a past transformed through complete repentance.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 6:4: “King David, however, is ‘the man raised on high,’ who established the yoke of repentance: even the prior damage can be repaired so that the transgressions become merits. It will be clarified that this too was under God’s providence beforehand, as in ‘If your sins are like years’—like these years ordered and coming from the six days of Creation. It will become known that this was arranged before Him. This is turning darkness into light. This is the root of the light of Messiah son of David, which is eternal life: it will be clarified that all the damages were under God’s providence, and they will be repaired with greater force to become ‘very good,’ beyond someone righteous from the outset. The latter is the aspect of Messiah son of Joseph, who will not endure. This is ‘In the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous do not stand.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah explains David’s ‘yoke of repentance’ as the power to repair prior damage and turn darkness itself into light. This illuminates why the present siman calls the restored sinners ‘Your pious ones’: their standing is disclosed through Hashem’s completed work of repentance, beyond how the deeds first appeared to human judgment. The comparison depends on complete repentance and retrospective clarification, both stated in this siman; it does not identify the unrepented deed with an act of piety.

paragraphs.text: Why the returning sinner is called Hashem’s chasid

rich.text: Why the returning sinner is called Hashem’s chasid

paragraphs.text: The designation follows a stronger conquest of the inclination through real return.

rich.text: The designation follows a stronger conquest of the inclination through real return.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 9:4: “Therefore they said in the Letters of Rabbi Akiva concerning the verse ‘Your pious ones shall sing’: these are the sinners of Israel who are destined to return. A sinner needs greater force of strength in conquering the inclination when he returns; therefore he is called ‘Your pious ones,’ meaning Hashem’s pious ones—those of exceptional piety. It is like ‘the trees of Hashem’ and ‘the cedars of Hashem’: wherever something is joined to Hashem’s name, it indicates its exceptional degree. Someone before whom an occasion for sin comes and who escapes it is called ‘mighty in strength’ (Kiddushin 40a). Through this he is assured of being guarded from then on, until he acquires through it the fixed name of a baal teshuvah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains the same possessive expression through the returning sinner’s greater effort. Its context distinguishes a moment of sincere return from repentance that has become a settled identity. Read beside the siman, this keeps ‘Your pious ones’ tied to actual transformation after repentance, rather than treating the old sin as meritorious while it remains unrepaired.

sections.en: In Practical Deed, It Is Impossible for a Person Not to Deviate Slightly From…

p: [קא] בְּמַעֲשֶׂה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא מְעַט מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אֵין אָדָם צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כ);

In practical deed, it is impossible for a person not to deviate slightly from strict justice, as written: "For there is not a righteous man upon earth, that does good, and sins not" (Ecclesiastes 7:20);
וְצַדִּיק הַיְינוּ הַנִּזְהָר שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין
and a "tzadik" is one who takes meticulous care not to deviate from strict justice
[וְכַנּוֹדָע שֶׁבְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה רִבּוּי הַקְּלִיפּוֹת בְּכָל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
[and as known, in the World of Action shells and husks abound across all levels, which is not to be elaborated here],
אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, רַק בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה וּרְצוֹן הַלֵּב שֶׁגּוֹמֵר בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁיִּתְנַהֵג כָּךְ וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא, שָׁם יוּכַל לִרְצוֹת וְלַחְשׁוֹק כָּךְ.

which is impossible in physical deed, but achievable only in thought and the desire of the heart, where he resolves to conduct himself thus without sinning, being capable there of purely longing for it.

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת, כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְמַחֲשָׁבָה וְרָצוֹן שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה בָּעוֹלָמוֹת הָהֵם, שֶׁגַּם מַעֲשֵׂה הַחֵטְא הַהוּא הוּא מִן הַסֵּדֶר וְאֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה כְּלָל מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, וְהַכֹּל בַּדִּין.

For in truth, when one ascends to the realm of thought and supernal will, even that sinful deed is seen as part of the cosmic order, never having deviated from strict justice, all being governed by law.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: בַּתְּחִלָּה עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה לִבְרוֹא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁבְּמַעֲשֶׂה הוּא יְצִיאָה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, אֲבָל בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה הוּא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין וְאֵין כָּאן יְצִיאָה.

And this is: "Initially it arose in Thought to create the world with the attribute of strict Judgment, etc.," for in practical deed there is a departure from strict justice, but in Thought it remains within strict Judgment without departure.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "צַדִּיק ה' בְּכָל דְּרָכָיו" (תְּהִלִּים קמה, יז) – פֵּירוּשׁ, "דְּרָכָיו" הֵם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ קִדּוּשִׁין, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יוֹדִיעַ דְּרָכָיו לְמֹשֶׁה", וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן מִתְנַהֵג עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה;

And as written: "Hashem is righteous in all His ways" (Psalms 145:17)—meaning His "ways" are words of Torah (Kiddushin 2b), and as written: "He made known His ways unto Moses" (Psalms 103:7), and the Blessed Name conducts Himself according to the Torah;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְמַעֲשֶׂה הוּא "חָסִיד", דְּהַיְינוּ לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין כִּדְאִיתָא בְּשַׁבָּת (קכ. וּבְרַשִּׁ"י),
but when it reaches practical deed He is "pious" (chasid), that is, beyond the letter of the law (Shabbat 120a and Rashi),
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְחַנֹּתִי אֶת אֲשֶׁר אָחֹן" וְגוֹמֵר.
matching: "and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, etc." (Exodus 33:19).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם זֶה פָּסוּק בַּתּוֹרָה וְאֶחָד מִדְּרָכָיו שֶׁנּוֹדַע,
And nonetheless, this too is a scriptural verse in the Torah and one of His known ways,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה' הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ" הוּא גַּם כֵּן הֲלָכָה קְבוּעָה;
parallel to: "It is time to work for Hashem; they have made void Your Torah" (Psalms 119:126), which is itself an established halakhah;
וְזֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי: כְּשֶׁחוֹזֵר לְמַחֲשָׁבָה, גַּם זֶה מִן הַסֵּדֶר וְהַשּׁוּרָה הָרְאוּיָה:
and this is as I wrote: when returning to Thought, even this belongs to the proper order and appropriate measure.

paragraphs.text: The relation of Hillel and Shammai illustrates the distinction between the world as first conceived in judgment and its practical existence with mercy.

rich.text: The relation of Hillel and Shammai illustrates the distinction between the world as first conceived in judgment and its practical existence with mercy.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 8:1: “Hillel was from the side of mercy, Abraham’s level, and Shammai from the side of judgment and might, Isaac’s level, as stated in Ra‘aya Mehemna. The Arizal likewise wrote that in the future the halakhah will follow Beit Shammai. This follows the Sages’ teaching that initially God intended to create the world with the attribute of judgment, and afterwards joined the attribute of mercy to judgment, as it says, “On the day the Lord God made.” There it also says “when they were created,” which is expounded as “through Abraham.” This is “The world is built through kindness.””

rich.text: : “Hillel was from the side of mercy, Abraham’s level, and Shammai from the side of judgment and might, Isaac’s level, as stated in Ra‘aya Mehemna. The Arizal likewise wrote that in the future the halakhah will follow Beit Shammai. This follows the Sages’ teaching that initially God intended to create the world with the attribute of judgment, and afterwards joined the attribute of mercy to judgment, as it says, “On the day the Lord God made.” There it also says “when they were created,” which is expounded as “through Abraham.” This is “The world is built through kindness.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah applies the same teaching about creation first arising in judgment to the schools of Hillel and Shammai. Mercy is joined to judgment so that the world can exist. This helps explain why the present siman does not treat practical kindness as a departure outside Torah: mercy itself belongs to Hashem’s revealed ways, even when practical life cannot sustain the original measure of strict judgment. The comparison concerns the structure Rav Tzadok describes; the quoted future teaching does not alter present halakhic rulings.

paragraphs.text: Sefer Etz Chaim 43:1:2: “The difference is that in Beriah the shell is less than the holiness, separate from it, and does not adhere to it. In Yetzirah the shell and holiness are evenly balanced and do not intermingle. paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 7: “‘I have raised my hand to Hashem.’ Avraham did not want to benefit from the king of Sodom, although we find that he accepted from Pharaoh and Avimelech, because his going to rescue Lot required clarification. A good power was present in Lot, since Naamah the Ammonite and Ruth the Moabite descended from him; the remainder was evil, since Ammon and Moab descended from him, as explained. Avraham had to clarify that, in its depth, his intention was only to rescue those two good offspring (Bava Kamma 38b). Wherever a person needs clarification, the counsel is first to remove all his interests in personal benefit. Then Hashem will clarify that even what he did contrary to the rule was good, for ‘It is a time to act for Hashem; they have annulled Your Torah’ (Psalms 119:126).”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach applies the same verse about a time to act for Hashem to Avraham's refusal of benefit from Sodom. This gives a concrete discipline beside Rav Tzadok's concluding claim that the apparent exception belongs to Torah's order; the claim does not establish the purity of a person's own motives.

p: [קב] מִי שֶׁמִּתְנַהֵג אֲפִילּוּ בְּכָל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת וְצָרְכֵי גּוּפָנִיִּים בִּקְדוּשָׁה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וּמַכְנִיס בָּהֶם עַבְדוּת וּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בֵּיצָה טז.) בְּהִלֵּל וְשַׁמַּאי – זֶהוּ נִקְרָא "חָסִיד",

One who conducts himself with holiness even in all permitted mundane matters and bodily necessities—meaning all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven, infusing into them servitude and the will of the Blessed Name in the manner of Hillel and Shammai (Beitzah 16a)—is termed a "chasid,"
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלָּאו דַּוְקָא מְדַקְדֵּק עַל פִּי שׁוּרַת הַדִּין.
meaning he does not restrict himself strictly to the baseline letter of the law.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" – בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי,
And this is termed "with all your heart"—with both your inclinations (Berakhot 54a),
שֶׁצַּדִּיק הוּא הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ, אֲבָל זֶה מַכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה גַּם בְּכָל חֶמְדּוֹת הַיֵּצֶר;
for a "tzadik" subdues his inclination, whereas this person introduces holiness even into the desires of the inclination;
וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה נוֹתֵן קְדוּשָׁה בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה, וְזוֹכֶה לְהוֹצִיא קְדוּשָׁה הַרְבֵּה מִן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע דַּיְיקָא;
and then the Blessed Name, measure for measure, instills holiness into all that he does, and he merits to extract vast holiness specifically out of the evil inclination;
וְאָז נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד", שֶׁהוּא יוֹתֵר מִטּוֹב סְתָם;
and then he is termed "very good," which is superior to ordinary good;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים וְכוּלֵי.
and regarding this it was said: "In the place where penitents stand, the wholly righteous cannot stand, etc." (Berakhot 34b).
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ תַּקָּלוֹת וּמִכְשׁוֹלִים, וְהוּא צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה וְכַפָּרָה עַל זֶה דְּנִקְרָא חֵטְא, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל.
And the Blessed Name orchestrates mishaps and obstacles for him, requiring repentance and atonement for what is deemed a sin, and through this he extracts the precious from the vile.
(מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ) וּמִדָּה זוֹ נוֹהֶגֶת בִּגְדוֹלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,

(From his holy handwriting.) [This passage was cut from the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902) without notice. It is restored here from R' Michael Mokotowski's copy of the author's manuscript, first printed in Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMalei (Jerusalem, 1968).] And this pattern holds among the great ones of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל הַפָּסוּק "אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא" –
as our Sages of blessed memory said on the verse "When a ruler sins" (Leviticus 4:22):
אַשְׁרֵי הַדּוֹר שֶׁהַנָּשִׂיא חוֹטֵא וְכוּלֵי.
"Fortunate is the generation whose ruler sins, etc." (Horayot 10b).
וְזוֹ מַדְרֵגַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this is the level of King David, peace be upon him,
הַגֶּבֶר שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה,
the man who raised up the yoke of repentance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה.) וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
as is stated (Avodah Zarah 5a), and as is stated elsewhere.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת קיב:) עַל זֶה:
And our Sages of blessed memory said about this (Shabbat 112b):
אִם הָרִאשׁוֹנִים כְּמַלְאָכִים אָנוּ כִּבְנֵי אָדָם,
"If the early ones were like angels, we are like human beings,"
וְנוֹדַע דִּבְנֵי אָדָם גְּדוֹלִים מִמַּלְאָכִים.
and it is known that human beings are greater than angels.
[וְאָמְרוּ גַּם כֵּן אַחַר כָּךְ:
[And they also said right afterward:
אִם הָרִאשׁוֹנִים כִּבְנֵי אָדָם אֲנַחְנוּ כַּחֲמוֹרִים,
"If the early ones were like human beings, we are like donkeys,"
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת;
and both are true:
שֶׁמִּצַּד הָרִאשׁוֹנִים כְּמַלְאָכִים, דְּהַיְינוּ בְּעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים,
for in the respect in which the early ones were like angels, that is, in the upper worlds,
זֶה גָּדוֹל לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
this is great before Hashem, blessed be He;
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
but in this world,
שֶׁהָיוּ הָרִאשׁוֹנִים כִּבְנֵי אָדָם אָנוּ כַּחֲמוֹרִים,
where the early ones were like human beings and we are like donkeys,
דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה וְהַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
that is, from the aspect of the World of Asiyah and of deed,
הֲרֵי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה זֶה קָטָן] (עַד כָּאן מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ)
in deed this is small.] (End of his holy handwriting.)
אֲבָל צַדִּיק שֶׁאֵין יוֹצֵא מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְנַהֵג עִמּוֹ כֵּן, וְ"לֹא יְאֻנֶּה לַצַּדִּיק" דַּיְיקָא "כָּל אָוֶן".
But with a "tzadik" who never departs from strict law, the Blessed Name conducts Himself likewise, and "no iniquity shall befall the righteous" (Proverbs 12:21) specifically.
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קכז:) בְּמַעֲשֶׂה דְּרָאָה קֶרִי "אוֹתוֹ חָסִיד"
And therefore they stated in Shabbat 127b in the episode of the nocturnal emission: "that chasid"
[וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִּׁ"י, וּבְבִרְכַּת הַזֶּבַח בִּתְמוּרָה דִּיקְדֵּק לָמָּה פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שָׁם וְלֹא בִּבְרָכוֹת;
[and see Rashi there, and Birkat HaZevach on Temurah examined why Rashi explained it there and not in Berakhot;
אַךְ כַּוָּונַת רַשִּׁ"י לְהוֹדִיעַ מִי הָיָה, דְּאָדָם גָּדוֹל הוּא, כְּדֵי לְהָסִיר מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה מִמִּי שֶׁאֵירַע לוֹ רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן],

but Rashi's intent was to identify who he was, since he was a great man [Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava or Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai], to remove depression from anyone to whom this occurred, may the Merciful One preserve us],
וְלֹא בְּחִנָּם נִקְרָא שָׁם בְּשֵׁם "אוֹתוֹ חָסִיד"
and not in vain was he specifically named "that chasid"
[וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּקְרָא כֵּן יֵשׁ טַעַם בַּדָּבָר].
[and likewise in every place where someone is so designated, there is an inner rationale].
וְגַם בְּעֵירוּבִין (יח:): אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן חָסִיד גָּדוֹל הָיָה וְכוּלֵי, בְּשִׁכְבַת זֶרַע דַּחֲזָא לְאוֹנְסוֹ.
And also in Eruvin 18b: "Adam the First was a great chasid, etc.," regarding emission experienced involuntarily.
דְּדַיְיקָא לְחָסִיד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין זֶה לְהוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל
For specifically to a "chasid" does the Blessed Name orchestrate this to extract the precious from the vile
[יָקָר אוֹתִיּוֹת קְרִי],
[yakar (precious) shares the letters of keri (emission)],
כִּידוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל כִּי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּטִפֵּי קֶרִי הֵם יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלוֹת מֵהַיּוֹצְאִים מִזִּוּוּג,
as is known from the holy Ari that the souls from involuntary emissions are greater than those emerging from marital union,
וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ יוֹתֵר כָּעֵת:
and this is not the place to elaborate further at present.

paragraphs.text: Beitzah 16a: ‘Hillel the Elder, however, had a different practice, for all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven, as it says: ‘Blessed is Hashem, day by day.’ It was likewise taught: Beit Shammai say: From the first day of your week, prepare for your Shabbat. Beit Hillel say: ‘Blessed is Hashem, day by day.’’

paragraphs.text: Beitzah 16a:4: “It was taught: They said of Shammai the Elder that all his days he ate in honor of Shabbat. If he found a fine animal, he would say, “This is for Shabbat.” If he found another finer than it, he would set aside the second and eat the first.”

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 5:1: “This is also what they said in Beitzah: “But Hillel the Elder had a different quality, for all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven.” This means that he did not set pleasure aside for Shabbat as Shammai did, because even on weekdays he ate in sacred purity: all his eating was in holiness and in the food’s spirituality, as on Shabbat. This is called “all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven.” As I wrote above, one who is like this does not need abstinence, because all his pleasures too are for the sake of Heaven and not for himself. This is “all his deeds”: even what appeared to be an act for his own pleasure was truly for the sake of Heaven. For one who is like this, all his permitted activities are holy, and he has no distinction between weekday and Shabbat.”

paragraphs.text: Serving with both inclinations means making one heart for good

paragraphs.text: The mitzvah of a cup of wine illustrates how a bodily capacity can enter divine service after its direction has been straightened.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 3:14: “Therefore the commandment is to bless over a cup of wine to gladden the heart, so that there is “joy for the upright of heart”: when one merits to empty evil from the fool’s heart and straighten the heart. The Talmud says: “What service is performed with joy and gladness of heart? This is song.” They said that song is recited only over wine, and so forth. “With gladness of heart” means the two hearts, as they expounded, “‘With all your heart’—with both your inclinations, the evil inclination and the good inclination.” This is a good heart: when one merits to straighten the heart so that it is one heart for good.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Lech Lecha explains ‘both inclinations’ through joy in a mitzvah: the heart’s powers become united toward good. This gives a concrete example of the present siman’s distinction between subduing a desire and bringing holiness into permitted bodily life. The example begins with removing evil and straightening the heart. It therefore does not erase the siman’s express requirement of repentance and atonement for what remains a sin; the desired end is a heart directed toward Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Upon Completion of Talmud 13: “It is known that there are two kinds of service: subduing and transforming. The first is the level of Yosef the righteous; the second is “the place where penitents stand,” where the bitter has been transformed into sweetness. The completely righteous cannot stand there, because they lack the power to transform it and stumble in it. “The place where penitents stand” means the very place of the sin that has been transformed into merit; for the completely righteous it is sin and deficiency. The Sefer HaYashar attributed to Rabbeinu Tam aptly writes that the completely righteous cannot stand there because it is evil; see there. In truth, the Gemara explicitly presents this as the penitents’ advantage. But both are true: the completely righteous cannot stand there because it is evil for them, while the penitents’ advantage is great because the bitter has been transformed into sweetness.”

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar HaGilgulim 39:33: “There is a distinction between these fifty or more drops mentioned above, from the five unions mentioned above, and all other souls. They possess a very great advantage over the others. All other souls come without an emission, through a union arising from the female’s awakening: she awakens toward the union and desires it, and afterward he too awakens. Since the male had no awakening of his own will but was awakened by her, the drops of the kindnesses and severities drawn forth in that union are not drawn from his faculty of knowledge itself, but from the kindnesses and severities that spread below into his six extremities, after becoming clothed and remaining there below. But the drops mentioned above are drawn forth without the female’s awakening, for they are drops of emission, as stated; they certainly emerge from the male’s awakening alone. The male desired to unite with his female counterpart but did not find her, because she was below in Beriah or a similar place, and then they emerged in vain. Since they come from the male’s awakening, they are certainly very great, drawn only from the faculty of knowledge itself, from the kindnesses and severities above, for that is the place where desire awakens. When they emerge from the foundation, they have not first descended and become clothed in the male’s six extremities; they merely passed through there and emerged from the foundation. Therefore the level of these souls is immeasurably greater than that of the other souls.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 243:1: “He concluded, “He redeems,” because this can contain redemption and deliverance from death, as is known, and as our Sages said in Berakhot: it is a favorable sign for a sick person. This applies after the fact: when he has already experienced an emission, he should trust that it is certainly for the good. But beforehand he should ask that he not need this redemption. “You have already redeemed me … God of truth” means through the attribute of truth to which I was attached during the day. For desire is called falsehood, and this is called redemption through falsehood; there is also redemption through truth and words of Torah. Redemption occurs by giving a substitute, and this is like the principle that a part of the life is equivalent to the whole life.”

And presumably there is some inner significance that warrants this association of terminology,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעַצְמוּתָם מַמָּשׁ הַהֵיפֶךְ.
even though their very nature is the complete opposite.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 47b: “So too below: if folly were not present in the world, wisdom would not be present in the world. This is why, when the companions learned the mysteries of wisdom from Rav Hamnuna the Elder, he would arrange before them a chapter of foolish matters so that wisdom would benefit through it. This is what is written: “More precious than wisdom and honor is a little folly”—because it is the perfection of wisdom and the honor of wisdom. Therefore it is written: “My heart guiding with wisdom, and grasping folly.” Rabbi Yosi said: “Precious through wisdom and honor”—that is, the preciousness and beauty of wisdom and the preciousness of the glory above: what is it? “A little folly.” A little folly shows and reveals the preciousness of wisdom and the glory above more than all the ways of the world.”

paragraphs.text: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 29:17-18: “Eliyahu arose, fled from the Land of Israel, and escaped, as it is said: “He arose, ate, and drank.” There the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to him and said: “What are you doing here, Eliyahu?” “I have been very zealous.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: “You are always zealous. You were zealous at Shittim over forbidden relations, as it is said, ‘Pinchas son of Elazar son of Aharon the priest.’ And here you are zealous? By your life, Israel shall not perform a circumcision until you see it with your own eyes.” From here the Sages instituted that a seat of honor should be made for the angel of the covenant—Eliyahu of blessed memory being called the angel of the covenant—as it is said: “The angel of the covenant whom you desire, behold, he comes.” May the God of Israel hasten to bring the Messiah in our lifetime, to comfort us and renew our hearts, as it is said: “He shall turn the heart of the fathers toward the children.””

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 93a: “Rabbi Abba opened and said: “Your people are all righteous.” The companions have explained this matter. Why is it written, “Your people are all righteous”? Are all Israel righteous? There are many guilty people among Israel, many sinners and wicked people who transgress the Torah’s commandments. Rather, the mystery of our teaching is this: Fortunate are Israel, who make a willing offering to the Holy One, blessed be He, offering their sons at eight days. When they are circumcised, they enter this good portion of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, “The righteous one is the foundation of the world.” Since they enter this portion of the righteous one, they are called righteous—certainly, all of them righteous. Therefore, “They shall inherit the land forever,” as it is written, “Open for me the gates of righteousness; I will enter them,” and, “This is the gate of Hashem; the righteous shall enter it”—those who have been circumcised and are called righteous.”

paragraphs.text: Context: The Zohar explicitly acknowledges wrongdoing before explaining “righteous” as a designation connected with entering the covenant. Its later discussion conditions the covenant’s protection on keeping it properly. This note explains the designation without equating it with the absence of every sin.

p: וְאֵין נִיכָּר בֵּינֵיהֶם אִם הוּא מִמַּדְרֵגַת גִּלּוּי אֵלִיָּהוּ אוֹ מִמַּדְרֵגַת יוֹסֵף שֵׁידָא,
And it is indistinguishable between them whether it originates from the level of Elijah's revelation or from the level of Yosef Sheida,
אֲפִילּוּ לְהָאַמוֹרָאִים בַּעֲלֵי הַתַּלְמוּד, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
even to the Amoraim, the masters of the Talmud, see there.
וְהוּא מִשֵּׁידִין יְהוּדָאִין הַנִּזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר,
And he is of the 'Jewish demons' mentioned in the Zohar,
דְּסוֹף אוֹתָן רוּחוֹת לִיתָקֵן לִהְיוֹת נְפָשׁוֹת יְקָרוֹת,
for the ultimate destiny of those spirits is to be rectified and become precious souls;
עַיֵּין לְקַמָּן אוֹת קי״ג.
see below, Ot 113.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vayeshev 5:1: “As it is taught in Netzach Yisrael by the Maharal of Prague concerning the statement in Eruvin 43a: “Those seven teachings that were said on Shabbat morning … was it not Elijah who said them? … Perhaps Joseph the demon said them.” If there had been an actual revelation of Elijah, visibly appearing to them, how could the Gemara have been uncertain through whom it came? Rather, the very appearance in the heart of a new understanding of Torah is an aspect of the revelation of Elijah. Discernment is needed here, however, because sometimes it comes from the opposite side, Joseph the demon.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 253a: “Likewise, the King’s riders are the masters of Mishnah, who are like angels. Jewish demons serve them, marked with the sign of Shaddai—another reading: with the letter yod. There are also demons and harmful spirits from the side of impurity, called gentile demons. “God made this corresponding to that.” Therefore the masters of Mishnah said that there are three kinds of them: one kind is like the ministering angels, a second kind like human beings, and a third kind like animals. Among them are those learned in the Written and Oral Torah. He is called “Yosef the demon” because a demon fathered him. It was not for nothing that the masters of Mishnah said: “If the teacher resembles an angel of Hashem of hosts, seek Torah from his mouth.””

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Sichat Shedim 1:14: “Therefore the Peri Etz Chayim writes (Gate of the Festival of Matzot, chapter 1) that these spirits, demons, and lilin of Adam were the souls of the Egyptian exile, for they are truly aspects of Adam's soul, spirit, and higher soul. Similarly, he writes that the ten drops that came from Yosef were the souls of the ten martyrs. They certainly had previously been some power of spirits, demons, and lilin, but these were so holy that such holy souls were subsequently created from them. This appears to be the meaning of the foreign and Jewish spirits mentioned in the Raaya Mehemna (Pinchas 253a; Ki Tetzei 277a). From the drops of Israelites come Jewish spirits, and from those of gentiles, foreign ones. Even when that power is called spirits, demons, and lilin, there is within it a power of Jewish belonging and a holy spark that later enters a soul of Israel; through this it is repaired.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sichat Shedim provides the fuller mystical account behind the siman's final sentence. The power described as a spirit still contains a spark that can later come into a soul of Israel and be repaired there. This explains why Rav Tzadok refuses to regard its existence as purposeless; it does not change his explicit distinction between an involuntary event and a deliberate act.

sections.en: Within Every Human Being There Exists Congenital Dross Stemming from the Counsel of The…

p: [קד] בְּכָל אָדָם יֵשׁ פְּסֹלֶת בַּתּוֹלָדָה מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ – עִרְבּוּבְיָא דְּטוֹב וָרָע,
Within every human being there exists congenital dross stemming from the counsel of the primordial Serpent—an entanglement of good and evil;
וּמִזֶּה הוּא מִקְרֵה לַיְלָה,
and from this arises nocturnal emission,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמַר: "לֹא תְאֻנֶּה אֵלֶיךָ רָעָה" (תְּהִלִּים צא, י),
concerning which Scripture promises: "There shall no evil befall you" (Psalms 91:10),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קג.): חֲלוֹמוֹת רָעִים וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים,
which our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Sanhedrin 103a as referring to distressing dreams and unchaste thoughts,
הַיְינוּ כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע" – שֶׁלֹּא וְכוּלֵי,

which aligns with the teaching of our Sages (Avodah Zarah 20b) on the verse "And you shall keep yourself from every evil thing" (Deuteronomy 23:10)—that one should not indulge in thoughts by day, etc.,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "חֲלוֹמוֹת רָעִים", דְּמוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה נִקְרָא "רַע" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנִדָּה (יג:).
and this is designated as "evil dreams," since emitting seed in vain is termed "evil," as stated in Niddah 13b.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר: "וְנֶגַע לֹא יִקְרַב בְּאָהֳלֶךָ",
And following this Scripture states: "neither shall any plague come near your tent,"
וְדָרְשׁוּ שָׁם: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּן אוֹ תַלְמִיד וְכוּלֵי,
which they expounded there: that you shall have no son or disciple, etc. [who spoils his dish in public];
שֶׁמִּי שֶׁלֹּא יְאֻנֶּה וְכוּלֵי, צָרִיךְ רַחֲמִים בָּזֶה שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא הַפְּסֹלֶת בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה.
for one who is spared from physical emission requires divine mercy so that the internal dross does not emerge instead through wayward offspring or disciples.
וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (יז:): "וְלֹא כֶאֱלִישָׁע שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ וְכוּלֵי",
And they stated in Berakhot 17b: "and not like Elisha, from whom emerged Gehazi, etc.";
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי אֱלִישָׁע לֹא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם (י:),
that is, because Elisha never experienced a seminal emission in his life, as brought there (Berakhot 10b),
וְעַד כָּאן בֵּרְכוֹ אָבִיו, שֶׁבָּזֶה אֵין מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה;
and "up to here his father blessed him" [Sanhedrin 103a: David's blessing to Solomon ends here], for in this his "bed" is not complete;
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, וְלֹא רָאָה קֶרִי, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק "רֵאשִׁית אוֹנִי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה).

whereas our father Jacob, peace be upon him, had a bed that was entirely whole, and yet he never experienced a seminal emission, as our Sages expounded on the verse "the first-fruits of my strength" (Bereishit Rabbah 98:4).
אֲבָל נִקְיוֹנוֹ הָיָה עַל יְדֵי גָּלוּת וְיִסּוּרִים,
But Jacob's purging of dross was accomplished through exile and tribulations;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "כִּי מַלְאָכָיו יְצַוֶּה לָּךְ וְגוֹמֵר",
and concerning this Scripture says: "For He will give His angels charge over you, etc." (Psalms 91:11),
וְהַסִּיּוּם: "כִּי יָדַע שְׁמִי" (שָׁם, יד)
— and the psalm concludes: "because he has known My Name" (ibid. 91:14)—
הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁנִּקְרָא שֵׁם ה',
which refers to words of Torah, which are termed the Name of Hashem;
בְּפֶרֶק מִי שֶׁמֵּתוּ (בְּרָכוֹת כא.) יָלֵיף בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפָנֶיהָ מִקְּרָא דְּ"שֵׁם ה'", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
as in the chapter Mi SheMeito (Berakhot 21a), where the blessing over Torah study is derived from the verse "When I proclaim the Name of Hashem" (Deuteronomy 32:3), see there,
כִּי כֻּלָּהּ שְׁמוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
for the entire Torah consists of mystical Names of the Holy One, blessed be He;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָעֵצָה לְגָלוּת וְיִסּוּרִין: "הֱוֵי גוֹלֶה לִמְקוֹם תּוֹרָה" (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד),
and this is the spiritual counsel for exile and suffering: "Exile yourself to a place of Torah" (Avot 4:14);
וְהַתּוֹרָה נִקְרָא "מוּסַר הַשְׂכֵּל",
and the Torah is called "the discipline of wisdom,"
שֶׁהַמִּצְווֹת גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא "עוֹל" בִּבְרָכוֹת (יז.) דּוּגְמַת יִסּוּרִין, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
for the commandments are likewise termed a "yoke" in Berakhot 17a, functioning like refining tribulations, see there.
וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה וְנִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ "יִשְׂרָאֵל",
And thus our father Jacob, peace be upon him, merited and his name was called "Israel,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק אֵלּוּ מְצִיאוֹת, דְּשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְעַם הָאָרֶץ וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם:
as stated at the end of the chapter Elu Metziot (Bava Metzia 33b), that the name "Jacob" is the root for simple folk, whereas the name "Israel" is the root for a Torah scholar.

paragraphs.text: The soul’s holiness and its attainment in the body

rich.text: The soul’s holiness and its attainment in the body

paragraphs.text: What begins as inward holiness becomes established in the embodied person through successive work.

rich.text: What begins as inward holiness becomes established in the embodied person through successive work.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Yisrael Kedoshim 1:5: “All the positive and negative commandments are helps and counsels from the One great in counsel, blessed be His name, to bring holiness upon a person from above. Therefore Avodah Zarah 20b says: ‘Guard yourself from every evil thing’ (Deuteronomy 23:10)—a person should not entertain sexual thoughts by day and thereby come to an emission at night. From here Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair said: Torah brings to watchfulness, watchfulness to diligence, and so on, until holiness. In our text holiness is last, although the passage concludes that piety is greater than them all. There is no contradiction: ‘greater’ concerns the soul's rank. With respect to a person's attainment while clothed in the body, holiness comes after all of them, because it is difficult for the body unless it has first been refined through the preceding stages. Although the principal vision proceeds from piety, it comes later in time, after the body too has been refined and reaches holiness. He learned this from ‘Guard yourself’: by guarding Torah's boundaries and sanctifying oneself from below, one is guarded from above against impurities during sleep, when the matter is outside one's control. This is the culmination of holiness: to be a holy person, beginning with Torah and being brought from stage to stage to holiness and holy inspiration.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim distinguishes a high quality of the soul from holiness becoming settled in the body. The latter is described as the result of the preceding disciplines, reaching even the state of sleep where direct control is absent. This develops the siman's contrast between an isolated appearance of purity and Yaakov's complete purification through a life of discipline.

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Genesis, Foreword 14-15: “We also possess a true tradition that the entire Torah consists of the names of the Holy One, blessed be He, its words being divided into names in another manner. For example, you might consider the opening verse as divided into different words, such as “berosh yitbara Elohim,” and so throughout the Torah, apart from the permutations and numerical values of the names. Rabbi Shlomo has already written in his Talmudic commentary how the great name of seventy-two is formed from the three verses beginning “Vayissa,” “Vayavo,” and “Vayet.” For this reason, a Torah scroll with an error of one letter, whether added or missing, is invalid. This requires us to invalidate a Torah scroll that lacks one vav from the words “otam,” of which thirty-nine are written in full in the Torah, or that writes a vav in one of the other occurrences written defectively, and similarly in other cases, even though one might think it makes no difference. This led the great masters of Scripture to count every full and defective spelling throughout the Torah and Scripture and to compose books of the tradition, back to Ezra the scribe and prophet who worked on this, as they expounded from “They read in the book, in the Torah of God, distinctly, giving understanding, and they understood the reading.” It appears that the Torah written in black fire upon white fire was in the manner we have mentioned: the writing was continuous, without breaks between words. It could be read by the way of the names, and it could be read as we read it, concerning Torah and commandments. It was given to Moshe our teacher in the reading of the commandments, while its reading as names was transmitted to him orally. Likewise, the great name mentioned above is written continuously and divided into words of three letters and into many other divisions, according to the use made by those who possess the tradition.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Shavuot 24:1: “The matter is that we find “the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven,” followed by accepting “the yoke of mitzvot,” and likewise, “Our leaders are laden”: our leaders in Torah and laden with mitzvot. This shows that Torah and mitzvot are called a yoke and a burden upon a person. The difference, however, is that one bears the yoke of a human king only through compulsion and constraint, would wish to escape it, and cannot be happy in it. But among Israel, accepting the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven and the yoke of Torah, although also called a yoke, is nevertheless done with joy, as we say, “They shall rejoice in Your kingship,” and as it is written, “Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.” Likewise, it is written, “The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart.” In its plain meaning this refers to mitzvot, while the Gemara expounds it concerning words of Torah. That is, although Torah and mitzvot are called a yoke, they gladden the human heart.”

p: [קה] (מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ)

(From his holy handwriting.) [This section was left out of the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902). R' Michael Mokotowski, a chasid of Rav Tzadok, copied it from the author's own manuscript into his copy of the book, and it was first printed in Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMalei (Jerusalem, 1968), edited by his son R' Avraham Eliyahu Kitov.]
עִנְיַן הַמִּקְרֶה רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן פְּעָמִים הוּא לְהַצָּלָה מִמָּוֶת כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעֵת חָלְיוֹ,
The phenomenon of nocturnal emission, may the Merciful One preserve us, is at times for rescue from death when it occurs during the time of one's illness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת (נז, ב) מִקְּרָא דְּ"יִרְאֶה זֶרַע יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים".
as brought in Berakhot (57b) from the verse: 'He shall see seed, he shall prolong days' (Isaiah 53:10).
וְכֵן בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
And likewise on the Day of Atonement,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא שִׁילְהֵי יוֹמָא,
as brought at the end of tractate Yoma (88a),
שֶׁהוּא זְמַן גְּמַר דִּין דְּחַיִּים וָמָוֶת לַבֵּינוֹנִים,
for it is the time of the final seal of judgment concerning life and death for the intermediate individuals (beinonim),
וְהוּא כְּעִנְיַן מִקְצָת נֶפֶשׁ כְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ.
and it is akin to the concept that 'a portion of a life is accounted as the whole life.'

paragraphs.text: Kohelet Rabbah 7:27:1: ““One by one, to find an account”: Rabbi Yitzchak said: Ordinarily, a person stumbles in a transgression for which he is liable to death at the hands of Heaven. Through what is atonement made for him? His ox dies, his hen is lost, his flask breaks, or he stumbles and injures his little finger, from which a drop of blood comes out. A part of the life is like the whole life, as it is said, “One by one, to find an account”: one offsets another, and the account is brought to its full reckoning. How exact is the reckoning? Rabbi Pinchas said: Down to one.”

p: וּפְעָמִים הוּא לִמְחִילַת עֲווֹנוֹת, כִּדְאִיתָא (יוֹמָא פח, א) בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁהוּא זְמַנּוֹ.
And at times it serves for the forgiveness of sins, as brought in Yoma (88a) regarding Yom Kippur, which is its appointed season.
וּפְעָמִים לְהַבְטִיחוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם גַּם כֵּן,
And at times it is to assure him of the World to Come, as also brought there,
דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא עָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי כַּנּוֹדָע.
for the Day of Atonement is of the aspect of the World to Come, as is known.
וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים עִקָּרוֹ לְכַפָּרַת פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
And the essence of Yom Kippur is for the atonement of the blemish of the covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּיוֹמָא ס"ז לְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עוּזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל,
as brought in Yoma (67b) that the scapegoat comes to atone for the deeds of Uzza and Azael,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם): "מֻבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא",
and this is why they stated (there): 'he is assured that he is a son of the World to Come,'
וּבֶן עוֹלָם הַבָּא נִקְרָא צַדִּיק בַּמִּשְׁנָה דְּרֵישׁ חֵלֶק,
and a possessor of the World to Come is termed righteous (tzaddik) in the Mishnah at the beginning of Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a),
וְהַיְינוּ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית.
which signifies one who guards the covenant.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 15:50: “This is the meaning of Yom Kippur: ‘On this day He will atone for you, to purify you’ (Leviticus 16:30). Then there is an awakening of the understanding in the heart, which is the world to come, where there is neither eating nor drinking; then Israel's sin will be sought and not found. Then all Israel have a share in the world to come, as it says, ‘Your people are all righteous’ (Isaiah 60:21), as the Mishnah teaches at the beginning of Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a). ‘Righteous’ means one who guards the covenant. Those who transgressed in damaging the covenant were not excluded there from a share in the world to come, for in truth, from the depth of the heart that will then be revealed, they are all so. This revelation occurs on Yom Kippur as well: ‘The goat shall bear their iniquities with it to an isolated land’ (Leviticus 16:22), to Azazel.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains the siman's link between Yom Kippur, the world to come, and the designation ‘righteous’ as guarding the covenant. Its claim concerns what is disclosed from the depth of the heart. It should therefore be read alongside, rather than in place of, the siman's repeated qualification ‘sometimes’ and its instruction that the person remain concerned during the year.

Zohar, Vayeshev 16:161-162: “It is written: “He created it not a waste, he formed it to be inhabited” (Is. 45, 18), that is, God made man for this purpose, and so dealt kindly with the world. Observe the Scriptural text: “And Abraham took another wife, and her name was Keturah” (Gen. 25, 1). Herein is an allusion to the soul which after death comes to earth to be built up as before.

Observe that of the body it is written: “And it pleased the Lord to crush him by disease; to see if his soul would offer itself in restitution, that he might see his seed, and prolong his days, and that the purpose of the Lord might prosper by his hand.” (Is. 53, 10). That is to say, if the soul desires to be rehabilitated then he must see seed, for the soul hovers round about and is ready to enter the seed of procreation, and thus “he will prolong his days, and the purpose of the Lord”, namely the Torah, “will prosper in his hand”.”

sections.en: "A Person Does Not Master Words of Torah Unless He Has Stumbled in Them"…

p: [קו] "אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל" (גִּטִּין מג.),
"A person does not master words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them" (Gittin 43a),
וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָה דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מְבִיאָה לִידֵי קֶרִי רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן,
and an intellectual stumbling in words of Torah brings about nocturnal emission, may the Merciful One preserve us,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי מִן הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ע"ו מֵעִנְיַן דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל,
as I wrote elsewhere on the verse "because I drew him out of the water" (Exodus 2:10), and as I wrote above in Section 76 regarding the Generation of the Flood,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יד.): "וְשָׂבֵעַ יָלִין בַּל יִפָּקֶד רָע" – הַמַּשְׂבִּיעַ עַצְמוֹ מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, וּמִינַּהּ לְהֵיפֶךְ.
and as stated in Berakhot 14a: "'and he that has it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil'—whoever sates himself with words of Torah, etc.," and infer the opposite from it.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה "חֵפֶץ ה' בְּיָדוֹ יִצְלָח", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, וְעוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And afterward through this, "the purpose of Hashem shall prosper in his hand" (Isaiah 53:10), as I wrote above, and he masters words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר מֵעִנְיַן יוֹסֵף שֵׁידָא,
as I wrote elsewhere regarding Yosef Sheida [see Section 103 above and Eruvin 43a],
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ דַּעֲווֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ זְכִיּוֹת,
and as they said [Yoma 86b] that willful sins become merits,
וּמִמַּיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים נֶהְפַּךְ לְמֵי הַדַּעַת, וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ הָעֲשׁוּקָה נִכְנְסָה לִקְדוּשָׁה וְנַעֲשָׂה מִמֶּנּוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;
and from the raging waters it is transformed into waters of divine knowledge, and the oppressed soul enters into holiness and becomes words of Torah;
כִּידוּעַ שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֵם עַצְמָן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא הוֹלָדַת נְפָשׁוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת.
for it is known that the souls of Israel are themselves words of Torah, and the innovation of words of Torah is the birth of holy souls.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קכז:): שָׁנָה לְתַלְמִידָיו – הוּא מַה שֶּׁנִּתְחַדֵּשׁ לוֹ דַּיְיקָא אַחַר שֶׁטָּבַל מִקּוֹדֶם, שֶׁהוּא הַתְּשׁוּבָה וְהַתִּיקּוּן.

And therefore they stated in Shabbat 127b: "he taught his disciples"—this was what was specifically revealed to him anew after he had first immersed in a ritual bath, which is repentance and rectification.
וְנִרְאֶה שֶׁזֶּה עַצְמוֹ הָיָה מַה שֶּׁאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ מֵעִנְיַן לָדוּן לְכַף זְכוּת, אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֹפֶן זֶה שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה לִכְאוֹרָה מוֹרֶה בְּבֵירוּר לְחוֹב, וְלֹא יָדַע זֶה מִקּוֹדֶם,

And it appears that this itself was what he said to them afterward regarding judging favorably, even in a case where the outward action seemingly points clearly to guilt, and he did not know this beforehand,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר שָׁם בְּתַלְמִיד שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּדוּק וְדִבְּרָה תּוֹרָה לָשׁוֹן נְקִיָּה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה חָשׁוּד אֶצְלוֹ עַל זְנוּת;
as he said there regarding "a student who was not vetted," where the Torah employed clean language, meaning that he was suspected by him of licentiousness;
וּמִדְּאָמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּדוּק מַשְׁמָע דְּבֶאֱמֶת כָּשֵׁר הָיָה, רַק שֶׁהוּא לֹא דָּנוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת, וְהָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט עֲבוּר זֶה רְאִיַּת הַקֶּרִי.
and from the phrasing "not vetted," it implies that in truth he was worthy, only that the master had not judged him favorably, and the resulting judgment for this was the nocturnal emission.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵירְעוֹ מִפְּנֵי טֹרַח הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁהָיָה דְּבַר מִצְוָה, וַהֲרֵי "שׁוֹמֵר מִצְוָה לֹא יֵדַע דָּבָר רָע", וְזֶה נִקְרָא "רָע" כַּנּוֹדָע.

Nonetheless, it occurred to him on account of the toil of the journey which was for a mitzvah; and behold, "he who keeps a commandment shall know no evil thing" (Ecclesiastes 8:5), and this is termed "evil," as is known.
רַק שֶׁכָּל דָּבָר נִידּוֹן עַל שֵׁם סוֹפוֹ, וְאָז נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד";
Rather, every matter is judged according to its ultimate outcome, and then it is termed "very good";
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲמוֹד עַל יְדֵי זֶה עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, זָכָה לָזֶה רַק עַל יְדֵי טֹרַח אוֹתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ לְפִדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִים,
and since it occurred so that through it he would master words of Torah, he merited this solely through the toil of that journey for the redemption of captives,
דְּאוֹתָהּ רִיבָה הִתְנַהֲגָה בְּדַרְכֵי גוֹיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן סוֹף פֶּרֶק ח,
for that maiden conducted herself in the ways of gentiles, as they said in Avot DeRabbi Natan (end of chapter 8),
וְהוּא מִדַּת חֲסִידוּת לְבַקֵּשׁ זְכוּת גַּם לָרְשָׁעִים,
and it is a measure of pious devotion (chasidut) to seek merits even for the wicked,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קי:): שְׁבָקֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לַחֲסִידוּתֵיהּ, מַאי חֲסִידוּתֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as stated in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 110b): "Rabbi Akiva abandoned his chasidut; what was his chasidut? etc.", see there.
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא בְּאוֹתוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה "חָסִיד אֶחָד"
And therefore he was called in that narrative "a certain chasid"
[וִיעֻיַּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"ב],
[and examine what I wrote above in Section 102],
שֶׁזֶּה לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין וְאֵין רוֹאֶה לַעֵינַיִם, כִּי גַּם בְּכָל רַע גָּנוּז טוֹב.
for this goes beyond the strict letter of the law and does not look merely to outward appearances, since within every evil goodness is concealed.
וּלְכָךְ זָכָה אָז לַעֲמוֹד עַל דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה לָדוּן לְכַף זְכוּת, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן גְּנִיזַת הַטּוֹב בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הָרָע לָעַיִן,
And therefore he merited then to master this principle of Torah—to judge favorably—which likewise represents the concealment of good within a deed that appears evil to the eye;
וְהִזְמִין לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹתוֹ מִכְשׁוֹל
and the Blessed Name orchestrated for him that very stumbling
[שֶׁהוּא לֵידַת נֶפֶשׁ בְּלֹא רְצוֹנוֹ וְדַעְתּוֹ, וְכֵן עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּמִי שֶׁעוֹמֵד מְזוּמָן עַל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר בְּלִי דַעְתּוֹ וְהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ;
[which is the birth of a soul without his conscious will and knowledge; and likewise "mastering words of Torah" means standing prepared upon that matter without his prior knowledge or effort;
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁחִדֵּשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, הוֹצִיא הַנֶּפֶשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל]
and through innovating the words of Torah afterward, he elevated that soul, as I wrote above]
לַעֲמוֹד מִתּוֹכוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה:
in order to master words of Torah through it.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 6:1: “For a name everywhere denotes the essential inner purpose of that entity, and the essence of Moses is the Torah—termed "the gift of his portion," indicating the portion uniquely appertaining to him. And it is known from the teaching of the Arizal on the Talmudic idiom (Shabbat 101b), "Moses, you have spoken well," that Moses is the root of Da'at within every Torah scholar across all generations of Israel; for the soul of Moses comprehensively incorporates the entire reality of the Torah. And the Sages stated (Gittin 43a): "A person does not truly comprehend words of Torah unless he first stumbles over them," which is the mystery of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, falling into the Nile and being drawn out of it. And the explanation of this is known from the masters of esoteric truth, the early kabbalists: that the Torah descended into the exile of Egypt, and the Children of Israel were required to be exiled thither to redeem and extract it from there; see there at length.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Ohr Zarua places the teaching about stumbling before attainment within the story of Moshe being drawn from the Nile. Since Moshe embodies the root of Torah, the rescue becomes a model of Torah recovered from exile. This illuminates the siman’s movement from a fall to a newly recovered insight. The sequence describes the repair of a failure; it supplies no instruction to manufacture one.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 76:1: “At the time of a person’s failure, he should know that at that same time a preparation for the good in that matter is present. If he merits it at that moment, he can rise to a very great level. The greatness of the sin toward which the inclination incites him corresponds to the greatness of the good he can then receive, if he turns this desire and longing toward the good. The good comes from that very matter, as the opposite of the evil. As the Zohar says in Pinchas, at the end of page 216a, at the time of the Flood they were fit to receive the Torah. Moshe was then present, as our Sages interpreted the word “beshegam” in Chullin 139b; see there. Water means Torah, but they turned it into “the raging waters.” Torah is the ultimate foundation of the world and the purpose for which it was created—“were it not,” and so forth—whereas they brought about its destruction. That same time was prepared, had they merited it, for precisely the opposite: the descent of the waters of Torah to sustain the world.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 10: “‘You intended evil against me; God intended it for good.’ Here Hashem showed how the tribes could be brought into Egyptian exile. The principal cause was their beginning to separate, for when Israel are united nothing can rule over them. Yosef separated from the tribes in this way. While Yaakov was alive it was not clear who was greatest among the tribes: sometimes he drew one closer and sometimes another, according to what was right in his eyes then. Before his death, however, when he blessed them and told Yehudah, ‘Your father's sons will bow to you,’ everyone recognized Yehudah's superiority. Yosef therefore did not know how to act. If he seated Yehudah at the head, he himself was king, and a king may not be slighted. If he sat at the head himself, he knew that Yehudah was the head. He therefore sat apart. The brothers judged that he did so from hatred, and were punished with exile because they should have judged him favorably. Yosef too was held at fault for leaving them room to err: he should actually have sat at the head, since he was king then, while knowing in his heart that Yehudah was greater. Since the brothers erred about him, some trace of the matter was present in human eyes. A person should therefore always pray not to judge his fellow adversely, and that his fellow not judge him adversely. The brothers were punished for failing to judge him favorably.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach supplies a concrete case of the good hidden beneath an apparently adverse act: Yosef sits apart because of a genuine conflict about precedence, and the brothers read it as hatred. The source holds both sides to a standard—the brothers should judge favorably, and Yosef should avoid leaving them room to err. This develops the siman's lesson without making hidden good intentions a reason to disregard the effect of one's conduct on others.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 102:1: “One who conducts himself with holiness even in all permitted matters and bodily needs—that is, whose deeds are all for the sake of Heaven, and who brings service and the will of the blessed God into them, in the manner the Sages described concerning Hillel and Shammai in Beitzah 16a—is called a chasid. This means that he does not merely take care to follow the strict line of the law. This is called “with all your heart”—with both your inclinations, and so forth. A righteous person subdues his inclination, but this person brings holiness into all the inclination’s desires as well. Then, measure for measure, the blessed God gives holiness to all that he does, and he merits bringing forth great holiness specifically from the evil inclination. It is then called “very good,” which is greater than simply good. Concerning this it is said: “In the place where penitents stand, completely righteous people cannot,” and so forth. The blessed God brings mishaps and stumbling blocks before him, and he needs repentance and atonement for this, for it is called sin; through this he brings the precious out of the worthless. But a righteous person who does not go beyond the line of the law is treated correspondingly by the blessed God, and “no iniquity will befall the righteous”—specifically the righteous. Therefore, in the account in Shabbat 127b of one who experienced an emission, they said “that chasid.””

sections.en: The Rectification for Nocturnal Emission Is Immersion in a Ritual Bath

p: [קז] תִּיקּוּן לַמִּקְרֶה הוּא הַטְּבִילָה,
The rectification for nocturnal emission is immersion in a ritual bath,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה מַגִּיעַ עוֹנֶשׁ הַמַּבּוּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנִדָּה (יג:),
for through wasted seed comes the retribution of the Deluge, as stated in Niddah 13b,
וּמְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן דּוּגְמַת מַבּוּל כְּרֶגַע וְתֵיכֶף יוֹצֵא,
and by immersing he accepts upon himself a semblance of the Flood for an instant and immediately emerges;
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר: "לֹא אֹסִף וְגוֹמֵר, כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו",
for the Blessed Name declared: "I will not again curse the ground... for the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Genesis 8:21),
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר עוֹד טֶרֶם יֵדַע הַנַּעַר וְכוּלֵי, וּבְלֹא דַעְתּוֹ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִתְגַּבֵּר, וְכֵן בִּשְׁנָתוֹ
meaning before the youth knows, etc., and without his conscious awareness the evil inclination surges, and so too in his sleep
[זֶה נִקְרָא בְּלֹא דַעְתּוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "גַּם בְּלֹא דַעַת נֶפֶשׁ לֹא טוֹב",
[which is called 'without his knowledge,' as written: 'Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good' (Proverbs 19:2),
וּמָצִינוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קמט:): אֵין "לֹא טוֹב" אֶלָּא רָע, וְזֶה נִקְרָא רָע.
and we find in Shabbat 149b: 'not good' means evil, and this is termed evil.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (ג.): אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת,
And they said in Sotah 3a: A person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly enters him,
וְהַיְינוּ אֵל אַחֵר שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קג עַמּוּד א): אִסְתָּרַס וְלָא עָבִיד פֵּירִין,
which is the 'other god' of whom the Zohar states (Part II, 103a): it is castrated and produces no fruit,
וּפֵירֵשׁ הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דַּעַת כַּנּוֹדָע.
and the holy Ari explained that it lacks Da'at (conscious divine awareness), as is known.
וּלְכָךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא סוֹד הַדַּעַת תִּיקּוּנוֹ,
And therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who embodies the mystical secret of Da'at, is its rectification,

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 15:42: “The reason for immersion before words of Torah is explained in Berakhot there: one must learn with awe, fear, trembling, and perspiration. See Rashi there, under ‘From here,’ who says that the condition of a baal keri comes only from levity and an unrestrained state of mind. If immersion is required even for an involuntary event, that too must in some sense belong to this category. Yet Heaven forbid that the supremely holy should have even a moment of levity or an unrestrained mind while awake. Nevertheless, so long as they have not been completely freed from the serpent's effect, to become a heart of flesh as in the future and as Yaakov was, even an involuntary event in sleep was not free of bodily pleasure at that moment. This too is counted in that category and gives rise to powers of impurity, Heaven forbid. For this the Sages instituted immersion or washing with nine kav of water: through this one is purified from that spirit of impurity and unrestrained state of mind that proceeds from it, and can cleave to the light and holiness of Torah, which is a tree of life.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains the siman's pairing of water with awe in study. It explicitly discusses an involuntary event and rejects attributing frivolity to the holy person's waking conduct; its concern is the remaining bodily state and readiness for attachment to Torah. This preserves the difference between the account of purification and an accusation of a chosen offense.

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Kiddushin 29b:15:1: ““This is for us, and that is for them”: Rashi explains that the people of Babylonia would go to the Land of Israel to study the mishnayot of the Tannaim. Since they studied away from home, household needs did not rest upon them. A person should therefore marry, so that he would be without improper thoughts, and then study Torah. “That is for them” refers to the people of the Land of Israel, who studied in their own locality: if one married, all the needs of the household would fall upon him and interrupt his study. Rabbeinu Tam finds this difficult. It implies that Shmuel says to marry first in order to be without improper thoughts, and applies this to the people of Babylonia; but improper thoughts would still be present when they went away from home to study. Furthermore, how could he leave home to study after marrying, when he must provide sustenance for his wife and children? In the first chapter of Gittin, page 6b, Rabbi Evyatar sent the message that people coming from there to here fulfilled concerning themselves, “They gave the boy for a prostitute and sold the girl for wine”—meaning that their sons and daughters had to be pledged for their support. This indicates that they were not acting properly by going away from home to study. Rabbeinu Tam therefore explains the reverse: Rabbi Yochanan, who said, “With a millstone around his neck, shall he engage in Torah?” spoke about the people of Babylonia, who could not leave their wives and go to study Torah, and who were also poor. Shmuel, who said to marry first, spoke about the people of the Land of Israel, who could study in their own locality and who were also wealthy; it was preferable for such a person to marry and study Torah in purity. Sometimes people of the Land of Israel also went away to Babylonia to study, but most studied in their own locality.”

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 22a:16-18: “The Sages taught: A person who has had a seminal emission and has had nine kav of water poured over him is pure. Nachum of Gam Zo whispered this to Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Akiva whispered it to Ben Azzai, and Ben Azzai went out and taught it to his students in the marketplace. Two amoraim in the West disagreed about this: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin and Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida. One transmitted “he taught it,” and one transmitted “he whispered it.” The one who transmitted “he taught it” explained that this was to prevent the interruption of Torah study and of procreation. The one who transmitted “he whispered it” explained that it was so that Torah scholars should not be constantly with their wives like roosters. Rabbi Yannai said: I have heard that they are lenient about it, and I have heard that they are stringent about it. Whoever is stringent about it for himself has his days and years prolonged.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 174:1: “We say in Shabbat 77b that this is the order of the world’s creation: first darkness and afterward light. Since the blessed God established this order in natural matters, it is certainly the fundamental divine will, as it is written, “In the place where penitents stand,” and so forth. Although, Heaven forbid, one may not say, “I shall sin and repent,” and choose to act that way—because he is not enabled to repent—nevertheless, this order comes about of itself, for “there is no righteous person on earth,” and so forth. Even concerning Yosef the righteous, the Sages said in Sotah 36b that ten drops emerged, expounding “His arms were made supple,” and so forth. Even concerning Yishai, David’s father, who died through the serpent’s agency, the Sages said at the beginning of Vayikra Rabbah on Tazria, “He was filled with iniquity,” and so forth. Likewise, the foundation of the house of David and the Messiah in Peretz was preceded by Er and Onan—darkness. This is the order: “The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light,” greater than the light seen by one who does not walk in darkness. Wherever “darkness” is written, it means the obscuring of Torah’s light, and not merely this world’s troubles. Likewise, “A person does not grasp words of Torah unless he has stumbled” comes through this darkness, which is the serpent’s agency in the wicked Esav, who struck Yaakov’s thigh, as is known. As soon as a person has reached such a state, Heaven forbid, and returns and is healed, he rises to light—like the person upon whose head a spray of water fell, who said, and so forth: “He raises the needy from the refuse heap,” in Yoma 87a.”
