sections.en: Emitting Seed in Vain

p: [קח] הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר נֹחַ (סב עַמּוּד א) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה,
Emitting seed in vain, the Zohar states in Parashat Noach (62a), is a sin for which ordinary repentance does not avail;
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי טִפֵּי זֶרַע נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַמּוֹחַ, וּפָגַם בְּטִפֵּי מוֹחוֹ.
and that is because drops of seminal fluid are drawn from the brain, and he blemished the spiritual drops of his intellect.
וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא בַּלֵּב כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב",
And standard repentance resides in the heart, as it is written: "and his heart understand, and he return and be healed" (Isaiah 6:10),
וּלְכָךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן עַל יָדָהּ הַחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמֶּנָּה.
and therefore it is impossible through the heart to rectify Wisdom (Chokhmah), which transcends it.
רַק צָרִיךְ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יז),
Rather, one requires Torah study, which is the unripe fruit of Supernal Wisdom, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (17:5),
וְהִיא גַּם כֵּן בַּמּוֹחַ
and Torah likewise resides in the brain
[וְנִקְרָא "יֵשׁ" כַּנּוֹדָע, בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "קֶרִי", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בָּזֶה].
[and wisdom is called Yesh (substance), which shares the numerical value of keri (310), and as I wrote elsewhere on this].
וְלֵב נִשְׁבָּר – לִהְיוֹת מַמָּשׁ כְּאַיִן, שֶׁהוּא בַּכֶּתֶר כַּנּוֹדָע שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה עוֹד,
And a broken heart: to become truly as nothing (Ayin), which reaches into Keter (the Crown) that transcends even Chokhmah,
וְזֶה מוֹעִיל,
and this is effective;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פְּנֵי ה' בְּעֹשֵׂי רָע", הוּא עָוֹן זֶה שֶׁנִּקְרָא כֵּן, "לְהַכְרִית מֵאֶרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר",

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 16:1: “Afterward it says, “Those who hate the righteous will be held guilty.” This refers specifically to someone who hates the aspect called “righteous”—one who does not take it to heart to regret this. But someone whose heart is broken within him over it, and who wishes to guard himself from now on, even though his heart is not yet refined, is described by “Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon those who fear Him, upon those who hope for His kindness.” One who fears and trembles over this, and hopes for God’s kindness that Heaven will help him improve his deeds from now on, has God’s eye upon him and will merit to repair the past. It is like what is said to Daniel: “From the first day that you set your heart to understand and to afflict yourself before your God, your words were heard.” Of this it says, “The Lord redeems the soul of His servants.” A servant is one who serves from fear, as in “If I am a master, where is My fear?” One who fears God and accepts from now on to become a servant of the King is described by “The Lord redeems,” even though he needs redemption, “and they shall not be held guilty.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah explains that the person’s heart need not already be purified for Hashem to attend to his return. Brokenness is joined there to wanting to guard oneself from now on, accepting service, and asking for assistance. This gives the present siman’s ‘broken heart’ a practical shape and explains why it can restore closeness beyond the limitation assigned to an ordinary form of repentance. The beginning is heard while the work of refining the heart is still ahead.

paragraphs.text: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 3:17: ““Those who taste it merit life” [the Shabbat prayer]—eternal life, as we have explained. These are the many worlds of each righteous person. “Righteous” means one who restrains himself from false desires and cleaves to truth, as with Yosef the righteous, because he restrained himself from desires. This is what the name “righteous” indicates everywhere in the holy tongue. He is the one who inherits yesh, for yesh means something substantial and existent, rather than false imagination, which is emptiness and nothingness. For the wicked person, the world of thought is a false imagining and does not qualify as yesh. This is clear, for keri is attachment to the world and its false, imagined desires, which is the opposite of substantial existence.]”

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 12:12: “The hidden levels are the first three, corresponding to the two days of Rosh Hashanah. These form the stature of the head: Chokhmah in the mind, and Keter above the head, the depth of the beginning of thought, hidden from the person himself—the place where thought is born. Therefore it is called “being from nothingness,” and “Wisdom is found from nothingness,” as is known. The two days have one sanctity and are one long day, because nothingness cannot be grasped except through the being drawn from it. Yom Kippur corresponds to Binah in the heart: “His heart will understand, and he will return and be healed,” as is known. These repair the hidden matters: the beginning on Rosh Hashanah is repentance from fear, and the completion on Yom Kippur is repentance from love—higher repentance, repentance fit to cover all one’s deeds. The seven intervening days repair what is revealed in character traits and actions.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Shvat 1:1: “Repair also comes through crying out and prayer, as it says, “Hashem’s face is against those who do evil,” alluding to this blemish, which is called evil, as is known. And it is written, “They cried out, and Hashem heard”: crying out is effective. As the holy Zohar, volume II, 20a, states: “Crying out is greater than them all, for crying out is in the heart,” as it is written, “Their heart cried out,” and so forth. See there, where it concludes that it never returns empty. It therefore helps even for this blemish, from which repentance was withheld in the holy Zohar, volume I, 219b.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The Shvat passage follows the same verses from Tehillim as this siman and cites the Zohar’s distinction of a cry arising in the heart. This clarifies why the siman places heartfelt brokenness alongside prayer when discussing a blemish described so severely elsewhere. The connection is more specific than the general importance of prayer: both passages locate an available path of return in the heart’s own cry, even where the ordinary route appears blocked.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 135:1: “For one who feels no desire in heart or mind for the service of Hashem, the counsel is: “Cast your burden upon Hashem.” Through his lowliness of mind in recognizing his lack, he awakens heavenly mercy, as it is written, “You have heard the desire of the humble, Hashem; You prepare their heart,” and so forth. This is the desire of the humble who recognize their lowliness and that they have no heart: the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares their heart. As is known, “Hashem is your shadow”: when a person is on the level of nothingness, he apprehends the blessed God likewise on the level of nothingness, and can draw forth and bring into being something from nothing, in the manner of “Create a pure heart.” This is wisdom in the mind; afterward comes something from something—will and desire in the heart. This means that the blessed God illuminates for him that there is nothing besides Him now, just as before the world was created; the whole earth is full of His glory. When this becomes clear before a person’s eyes, desires are immediately born in mind and heart. But first there must be “The nations have perished from His land”—meaning repentance for transgressions in deed, concerning which it is said, “Nations have entered Your inheritance.” For land, as is known, alludes to the body and the powers of action, while the nations are powers opposed to the will of the blessed God. Their removal comes through at least lower repentance, through which intentional sins become like inadvertent ones. Then the person attaches himself to the lowest of the ten levels of holiness taught in the first chapter of Kelim, the holiness of the land. It is known that everywhere the end is embedded in the beginning. Through this he can come to humility and the level of nothingness, the holiness of the Holy of Holies, as stated in Zohar II, page 121a. From there light goes forth into the world: “You prepare their heart,” in the sense that its light brings a person back to the good.”

sections.en: And in the Footsteps of the Messiah

p: [קט] וּבְעִקְּבֵי מָשִׁיחַ מִתְגַּבֵּר מְאֹד עָוֹן זֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה כִּי כִּמְעַט אֵין אָדָם בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל.
And in the footsteps of the Messiah, this sin intensifies exceedingly, and as written in Sefer Reishit Chokhmah that virtually no person in his generation was spared from it.

כִּי כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁיָּצְאוּ עַד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נוֹטְעוּ בְּזַרְעוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת סג.) עַל פָּסוּק "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כָּל גּוֹיֵי הָאָרֶץ" – לְשׁוֹן הַבְרָכָה

For all souls that emerged prior to our father Abraham, peace be upon him, were subsequently replanted into his seed, as our Sages expounded (Yevamot 63a) on the verse "and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed (venivrekhu)"—an expression of grafting (havrakhah)
[וְזֶה נֶאֱמַר לְטַעַם עַל הַהוֹדָעָה מִסְּדוֹם שֶׁגַּם הֵם נִבְרְכוּ בוֹ וְהָיוּ צְרִיכִים הֲכָנָה יְתֵירָה לְשֶׁיְּתוּקְנוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם.

[and this was stated as the rationale for informing Abraham regarding the destruction of Sodom, for they too were grafted through him and required intense preparation to be rectified, as the Ari wrote that they were the generation of the Exodus.
וְנוֹדַע דְּרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כג) עַל פָּסוּק "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי".
And the rabbinic exposition (Vayikra Rabbah 23) on the verse "a nation from the midst of a nation" is well known.
וְגַם יָדוּעַ דְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה בַּעֲבוּר אַבְרָהָם, לְכָךְ הוּא הִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְקְנוּ בֶּעָתִיד].
And it is also known that the Egyptian exile occurred on account of Abraham; therefore he prayed for them, and through this they were rectified in the future].
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם" – אַב מַמָּשׁ לְכָל הַגּוֹיִם.
And therefore he was called "the father of a multitude of nations"—a literal father to all nations.

וְהַיְינוּ כִּי ב' אֲלָפִים הוּא סִבּוּב שָׁלֵם בַּבְּרִיאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: בְּבֵי"ת נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה דְּתוֹרָה קָדְמָה ב' אֲלָפִים שָׁנָה לָעוֹלָם.

That is, because two thousand years constitute a complete cosmic cycle in Creation, as they said [Bereishit Rabbah 1:10]: with the letter Beit (equaling two) the world was created, and as I wrote elsewhere on the rabbinic dictum that the Torah preceded the world by two thousand years.
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צז.): ב' אֲלָפִים תֹּהוּ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁבְּכָל חֵלֶק הָיוּ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הָרְאוּיוֹת לָצֵאת:
And therefore our Sages said (Sanhedrin 97a): two thousand years of Desolation, two thousand of Torah, etc., wherein in each epoch all the souls destined to emerge came forth:
דְּתֹהוּ – עַד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
Desolation—extending until our father Abraham, peace be upon him;
וּדְתוֹרָה – בְּזַרְעוֹ עַד מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁיִּכְלוּ כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּגּוּף כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (סב.);
and Torah—among his seed until the Messiah, until all souls in the Heavenly reservoir (Guf) are exhausted, as stated in Yevamot 62a;
וְיִהְיֶה פַּעַם שְׁלִישִׁית בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ הַמַּתְחִיל בִּב' אֲלָפִים הַשְּׁלִישִׁיִּים.
and it will recur a third time in ultimate perfection in the generation of the Messiah, which commences in the third epoch of two thousand years.
וְהִנֵּה ג' דּוֹרוֹת שֶׁקָּדְמוּ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מָנוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And behold, the three corrupt generations that preceded our father Abraham were enumerated in chapter Chelek as having no share in the World to Come,
וְהַיְינוּ לְתוֹקֶף הָרַע שֶׁנִּתְגַּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם, וְזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה כַּאֲשֶׁר יְתוּקְנוּ הֵם גַּם כֵּן בְּתוֹקֶף גָּדוֹל.
and that was due to the overwhelming power of evil that overpowered them; and corresponding to this, when they are rectified, it unfolds likewise with tremendous power.
וּסְדוֹם הֵם דּוֹר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
And Sodom corresponds to the generation of the Exodus from Egypt, as noted above;
וְדוֹר הַפְלָגָה הֵם דּוֹר עוֹלֵי גוֹלָה גַּם כֵּן מֵאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ד.) שֶׁהָיוּ גַּם כֵּן רְאוּיִים לְנֵס כְּבִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה;

and the Generation of the Dispersion corresponds to the generation that returned from the Babylonian Exile, who also came from the land of Shinar, concerning whom our Sages stated (Berakhot 4a) that they were worthy of an overt miracle like the first entry into the Land;
וְדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל הֵם דּוֹר מָשִׁיחַ, בַּעֲלֵי בִּיאָה שְׁלִישִׁית, וּלְכָךְ מִתְגַּבֵּר עָוֹן דִּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל בְּיוֹתֵר
and the Generation of the Flood corresponds to the generation of the Messiah, the bearers of the third arrival, which is why the sin of the Generation of the Flood surges with supreme intensity
[וְג' אֵלּוּ הֵם גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד כְּלַל ג' סִדְרֵי ב' אֲלָפִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ]:
[and these three generations also correspond to the overarching three epochs of two thousand years mentioned above, and this is not the place to lengthen].

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 22:1: “‘All the families of the earth shall be blessed through you’ (Genesis 12:3). ‘Venivrekhu’ is an expression like the Talmud's layering of a tree. This accords with the holy Ari (Gate of Verses, Shemot, under ‘A new king arose’): the generation of the dispersion was reincarnated in the generation of the wilderness, those who left Egypt. Because the dispersion generation sinned by building the tower with mortar and bricks, the Egyptians enslaved Israel with mortar and bricks in crushing labor. Thus ‘All the families of the earth shall be blessed through you’ means that they themselves will be layered and planted into your holiness.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov makes the siman's botanical interpretation of ‘venivrekhu’ explicit: souls are planted into Avraham's holiness. The historical allocation differs, however. This passage links the generation of the dispersion to the Egyptian exile and its bricks, whereas Rav Tzadok here associates Sodom with the Exodus and the dispersion with the later return from Shinar. The comparison supports the meaning of grafting while preserving the distinct schemes of repair.

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar HaPesukim, Parashat Shemot 47-50: “The matter is this: Although the generation of the wilderness was being repaired and separated as good from evil, as mentioned, its original impurity did not entirely cease until they stood at Mount Sinai, as the Sages said. The secret is that the transgressions of Adam, and their own transgressions when reincarnated as the generation of the Flood, the generation of the Dispersion, and the people of Sodom, had not yet been repaired. Although they received their punishment in the Egyptian exile, they needed actively to return and fulfill the commandments they had transgressed. They therefore had to repair and fulfill them before the Torah was given at Mount Sinai. This is their meaning: Corresponding to the sin of the generation of the Dispersion, who denied the fundamental principle and worshipped idols as Adam also did, He gave them Shabbat and its laws at Marah, thereby repairing the sin of idolatry. This is the secret of the verse, “Happy is the person who does this, who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” The Sages expounded that even an idolater like Enosh, who was in the generation of the Flood, is forgiven all his sins if he keeps Shabbat. For one who acknowledges idolatry is as though he denies the whole Torah; one who rejects idolatry is as though he acknowledges the whole Torah; and one who keeps Shabbat according to its laws is as though he fulfills the whole Torah. The denial of the fundamental principle is also repaired, because one who acknowledges Shabbat acknowledges the divine source above, who created the world in six days and rested on the seventh. Corresponding to the Flood generation’s sin of robbery, like Adam’s, He gave them the section Mishpatim, where all the laws of robbery and theft are written. Moreover, its first law, “When you acquire a Hebrew servant,” concerns a person sold by the court for his theft, who is not repaired until he is sold and afterward goes free. Accordingly, “Yosef was sold as a servant,” and all the Israelites were slaves to Egypt, to repair the sin of robbery; then they went free. Once they accepted this law of the Hebrew servant, it was counted as though it had been fulfilled through them, and their sin of robbery was forgiven. The emission of seed in vain had already been repaired by their being thrown into the Nile, as mentioned, and they were separated from evil. Corresponding to the people of Sodom’s sin of denying the laws of justice, like Adam’s, they were given the section “You shall discern from among all the people,” and the appointment of judges.”

Rav Tzadok’s later distribution among the Exodus, Ezra’s return, and the messianic generation is a further arrangement in this ois, rather than the exact distribution stated by this source.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 8:2: “For Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Torah preceded the creation of the world by two thousand years. This is what is written: “I was beside Him as an amon,” and so forth. A day of the Holy One, blessed be He, is a thousand years, as it is written, “For a thousand years in Your eyes are like yesterday.” Thus, “Do you know this from of old,” and so forth: Torah knows what preceded the world’s creation. But you have no business expounding beyond “since a human was placed upon the earth.” Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Ben Sira: Do not expound what is greater than you; do not investigate what is stronger than you; do not seek to know what is beyond you; do not inquire into what is concealed from you. Contemplate what you have been permitted; you have no business with hidden matters.”

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And behold, the three corrupt generations that preceded our father Abraham were enumerated in chapter Chelek as having no share in the World to Come,

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:3: “The generation of the Flood has no share in the World to Come and does not stand in judgment, as it is stated, “My spirit shall not judge the human forever”: neither judgment nor spirit. The generation of the Dispersion has no share in the World to Come, as it is stated, “Hashem scattered them from there over the face of all the earth”: “Hashem scattered them”—in this world; “and from there Hashem scattered them”—in the World to Come. The people of Sodom have no share in the World to Come, as it is stated, “The people of Sodom were evil and sinful against Hashem exceedingly”: “evil”—in this world; “sinful”—in the World to Come. But they do stand in judgment. Rabbi Nechemyah says: Neither these nor those stand in judgment, as it is stated, “Therefore the wicked shall not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.” “The wicked shall not rise in judgment”—this is the generation of the Flood; “nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous”—these are the people of Sodom. They said to him: They do not stand in the congregation of the righteous, but they do stand in the congregation of the wicked.”

sections.en: All Offspring of a Person Derive from the Blessed Name

p: [קי] כָּל תּוֹלְדוֹת הָאָדָם הוּא מִן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
All offspring of a person derive from the Blessed Name
[שֶׁעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ תַּעֲנִית (ב.) דְּמַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל עֲקָרוּת רַק בְּיָדוֹ],
[which is why they stated at the beginning of Ta'anit 2a that the key of barrenness is in His hand alone],
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מִמֶּנִּי פֶּרְיְךָ נִמְצָא" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, ט);
as it is written: "From Me is your fruit found" (Hosea 14:9);
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֵל אַחֵר "אִסְתָּרַס וְלָא עָבִיד פֵּירִין" כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר, וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (מ.): עֲבֵירָה אֵין לָהּ פֵּירוֹת.
in contrast to the 'other god' who is castrated and produces no fruit, as brought in the Zohar, and likewise in Kiddushin 40a: a sin bears no lasting fruit.

וְהִנֵּה גַּם רוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין שֶׁנּוֹלָדִים מֵהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, הֵם נִקְרָאִים תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, נד עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "נִגְעֵי בְנֵי אָדָם".

And behold, even the spirits, demons, and night-spirits born of wasted seed are called his offspring, as written in the Zohar (Part I, 54b) on the verse "the stripes of the children of men" (II Samuel 7:14).
וְיָדוּעַ: "מִפִּי עֶלְיוֹן לֹא תֵצֵא הָרָעוֹת" (אֵיכָה ג, לח), וְנֶאֱמַר: "לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע" (תְּהִלִּים ה, ה), וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּמַה שֶּׁנִּקְרָא "רָע" יִהְיֶה מִמֶּנּוּ.

And it is known: "Out of the mouth of the Most High proceeds not evil" (Lamentations 3:38), and it is stated: "evil shall not dwell with You" (Psalms 5:5), so it is impossible that that which is termed evil should originate directly from Him.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
And concerning this it is said: "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalms 23:4),
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת דְּהַיְינוּ גֵּיהִנָּם,
and even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, which is Gehenna,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (יח:) וּבְסוֹטָה (ד:) דְּעַל פְּגַם הַבְּרִית לֹא יִנָּקֶה מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם.
and as stated in Eruvin 18b and Sotah 4b that for a blemish of the Covenant one is not absolved from the judgment of Gehenna.
עַל זֶה אָמַר: "כִּי בָאֵשׁ ה' נִשְׁפָּט" (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, טז),
Concerning this Scripture states: "For by fire will Hashem enter into judgment" (Isaiah 66:16),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים א, יח): תֵּרֵד כָּל אוּמָּה וֵאלֹהֶיהָ וְכוּלֵי, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר הַנּוֹתֵן לָהּ כֹּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת חַיִל.
and our Sages expounded (Midrash Tehillim 1:18): every nation and its deity shall descend, etc., meaning that which granted it the strength to wield power.
וְעָלֵינוּ נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי הוּא הַנֹּתֵן לְךָ כֹּחַ" (דְּבָרִים ח, יח), וְנֶאֱמַר: "כִּי גַם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, יב).
And concerning us it is said: "for it is He that gives you power" (Deuteronomy 8:18), and: "for You also have wrought all our works in us" (Isaiah 26:12).
זֶהוּ "אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי שָׁם),
This is "You are with me,"
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַגֵּיהִנָּם שֶׁהוּא שֶׁל אֵשׁ, דְּהַיְינוּ מַדְרֵגַת הַיִּרְאָה,
and through this, Gehenna which is of fire—representing the level of fear/awe—
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּחֲגִיגָה (יג:): נְהַר דִּינוּר מִזֵּיעָתָן שֶׁל חַיּוֹת יוֹרֵד עַל רֹאשׁ רְשָׁעִים בְּגֵיהִנָּם.
as stated in Chagigah 13b: the river of fire (nehar dinur) issuing from the sweat of the holy Chayot descends upon the heads of the wicked in Gehenna.
וְאִית יִרְאָה רָעָה שֶׁהִיא רְצוּעָה לְאַלְקָאָה בִישַׁיָּא;
And there is an evil, morbid fear which acts as a scourge to lash the wicked;
וְעַל יְדֵי "כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" נִתְהַפֵּךְ לְיִרְאַת ה' וְיִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת הַמְּבִיאָה אַדְּרַבָּה לְשִׂמְחָה,
and through "for You are with me" it is transformed into the fear of Hashem and awe of His exalted majesty which leads, on the contrary, to holy joy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה" (תְּהִלִּים ב, יא);
as stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 3) and: "and rejoice with trembling" (Psalms 2:11);
וְאָז כְּבָר נִיתְקַן וְקִבֵּל עָנְשׁוֹ בָּזֶה, כִּי זֶה מֵסִיר הַיִּרְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב.).
and then he has already been rectified and has received his retribution through this, for this removes the debilitating fear, as stated in Berakhot 22a.
וְכֵן הַיִּרְאָה מֵסִיר עָוֹן זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יְרָא אֶת ה' וְסוּר מֵרָע" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, ז),
And likewise holy fear eliminates this sin, as written: "Fear Hashem, and depart from evil" (Proverbs 3:7),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק ג דִּנְדָרִים (כ.) עַל פָּסוּק "וּבַעֲבוּר תִּהְיֶה יִרְאָתוֹ עַל פְּנֵיכֶם לְבִלְתִּי תֶחֱטָאוּ":
and as stated in the third chapter of Nedarim 20a on the verse: "and that His fear may be before your faces, that you sin not" (Exodus 20:17).

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Taanit 2a:12:1: ““Three keys were not entrusted to an agent”: One may ask: Do we not say in Sanhedrin, page 113, that the key to rain was entrusted to Eliyahu, and likewise the key to the resurrection of the dead, and likewise to Elisha, as it is written concerning Eliyahu, “As Hashem lives,” and so forth? It is also said in the later chapter, Taanit 23. The answer is that “they were not entrusted to an agent” does not mean that they were never entrusted, for the keys to resurrection and rain were indeed entrusted. Rather, they were not entrusted to an agent to be permanently appointed over them.”

paragraphs.text: Maharal, Chiddushei Aggadot, Kiddushin 40a (vol. II, p. 141): “Fruit is what necessarily follows and proceeds from an existing thing, just as fruit comes from a tree. A transgression, which has no existence in its own right, cannot be said to produce fruit—unless the transgression itself produces fruit, as with desecrating the Name and similar cases in which others learn from the sinner and he has disciples who are his fruit. This is certainly a transgression that produces fruit, and this transgression does have fruit. A mitzvah, however, has fruit, for the mitzvah’s exalted rank and level are in the World to Come, and this world is the fruit of the World to Come. Therefore a mitzvah has fruit, whereas a transgression does not.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Maharal explains the distinction between a mitzvah’s enduring source and the lack that constitutes transgression. He explicitly retains the exception for a sin that produces further wrongdoing through its example or disciples, including desecration of the divine Name. The existing Gemara note remains unchanged.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 97:1: “The repair for one who emits seed in vain is engagement with Torah, as it is stated in Kiddushin 30b: “I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its seasoning.” In Sukkah 52a they said that the Holy One, blessed be He, called it “evil,” meaning the sin of the Flood generation, the emission of seed in vain. [In Kiddushin 13a they said that the decree did not apply to the fish in the sea—meaning Torah scholars, as I have written elsewhere on the verse “Rule over the fish of the sea.”] As stated in Zohar, Bereshit, page 57a, and at the beginning of the chapter Kol HaYad, it is called evil. The Holy One, blessed be He, created this evil inclination, as it is written, “And whom I caused to suffer.” Therefore this can also occur in a dream, when it is evident that it is not a person’s action. A seasoning sweetens the food: that is, it turns the evil into “very good,” as our Sages said in Bereshit Rabbah, section 9, “This is the evil inclination,” which is sweetened through words of Torah. Zohar, Bereshit and Noach, says that there is no impurity like it. Yet in the second chapter of Berakhot, page 16a, they said that words of Torah raise a person from impurity to purity. The statement in Zohar, Noach, page 62a, that repentance does not avail is like what they said in Rosh Hashanah 18a: sacrifice does not atone, but Torah does atone. The same applies here. As our Sages said at the end of Chagigah, the fire of Gehinnom does not rule over Torah scholars. Gehinnom too is called “evil,” as stated in Berakhot 61a on the verse “Evil shall not go unpunished.” This is like what is said in Eruvin 19a, that everyone goes down there for matters of “chinnam,” meaning guarding the covenant. This too is the meaning of “You created Gehinnom”: the blessed God created it, just as He created the evil inclination. [There they also say, “You created righteous people.” A righteous person everywhere means one who guards the covenant; he too is so from the beginning of creation, as I wrote in the preceding ois, for this can also be found among the wicked and among the idol-worshipping nations.] Concerning this it is said, “Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for You are with me.” “Evil” is the level just described, and “You” means that You created it.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Introduction 21:2-6: “Fear is divided into three kinds. Two of them do not have the proper foundation, and one is the foundation of fear. A person may fear the Holy One, blessed be He, so that his children will live and not die, or because he fears punishment affecting his body or possessions, and therefore fears Him continually. It follows that he does not make the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, the primary matter. Another person fears the Holy One, blessed be He, because he fears punishment in that world and the punishment of Gehinnom. These two are not the foundation and root of fear. The fear that is fundamental is for a person to fear his Master because He is great and sovereign, the source and root of all worlds, and all are considered as nothing before Him, as it is stated, “All the inhabitants of the earth are considered as nothing.” He should place his will in that place called fear. Rabbi Shimon wept and said: Woe if I speak, and woe if I do not speak. If I speak, the wicked will know how to serve their Master. If I do not speak, the companions will lose this teaching. In the place where holy fear rests, below it there is an evil fear that lashes, strikes, and accuses; it is a strap for striking the wicked. Whoever fears because of the punishment of lashes and accusation, as described, does not have that fear of Hashem resting upon him which is called “the fear of Hashem leads to life.” What rests upon him instead? That evil fear. It follows that the strap, evil fear, rests upon him, and not the fear of Hashem. Therefore the place called fear of Hashem is called “the beginning of knowledge.” This commandment is included here; it is the root and foundation of all the other commandments of Torah. One who guards this fear guards everything; one who does not guard fear does not guard the commandments of Torah, for this is the gateway to everything.”

paragraphs.text: Mesillat Yesharim 24:6-13: “The second kind is awe of exaltation: a person keeps away from sins and does not commit them because of the great honor of His blessed Name. How could lowly and despicable flesh and blood begin, or dare in its heart, to do something against the will of the Creator, blessed and exalted be His Name? This fear is not so easy to acquire. It is born only through knowledge and understanding, by contemplating His exaltation and the human being’s lowliness—matters that arise from an understanding and discerning mind. This is the fear we placed as the second part of one of the divisions of piety described earlier. Through it a person feels shame and trembles when standing before his Creator to pray or perform any service. This is the praiseworthy fear for which the pious of all generations were praised, and of which Moshe says, “To fear this honored and awesome Name, Hashem your God.” The fear we are now explaining, fear of sin, is a part of that awe of exaltation and also a kind in its own right. It means that a person is continually fearful and concerned about his deeds, lest some trace of sin be mixed into them, or something small or great be present that does not accord with the greatness of His honor and the exaltation of His Name. You can see the close relationship between this fear and the awe of exaltation: the aim of both is to do nothing against His exalted honor. The difference, through which it is considered a distinct kind and called by a different name, is that awe of exaltation occurs at the time of an act, service, or encounter with a transgression. When a person stands praying or serving, he feels shame and humiliation, quakes and trembles before His exalted honor; or when a transgression presents itself and he knows it is a transgression, he refrains from it so as not to act defiantly before His glory, Heaven forbid. Fear of sin, however, is at every time and every hour: at every moment he fears lest he stumble and do something, however slight, against the honor of His blessed Name. It is therefore called fear of sin, for its essence is fear that sin may enter and become mixed into his deeds through negligence, laxity, or unawareness, in whatever way. Concerning this it is stated, “Happy is the person who fears always,” which the Sages interpreted as referring to words of Torah. Even when he sees no stumbling block before his eyes, his heart must be anxious lest one be hidden at his feet and he fail to guard against it.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah explicitly defines the perfection of love by its union with awe and quotes the same tradition about rejoicing through fear. This clarifies the siman's transformation: recognizing ‘You are with me’ redirects the fear toward Hashem and His greatness, allowing awe and joy to coexist. The outcome remains reverence that restrains sin, as the siman's last verse states.

sections.en: In the Footsteps of the Messiah

p: [קיא] בְּעִקְּבָתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא הָעִיקָּר הוּא רַק לְהוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל,
In the footsteps of the Messiah, the central task is exclusively to extract the precious from the vile (Jeremiah 15:19),
וְרַק בִּמְקוֹם יֵצֶר הָרָע וְתִגְבֹּורֶת עֲווֹנוֹת מִשָּׁם יִקָּחֲךָ דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה,
and specifically from the place of the evil inclination and the raging surge of sins will He take you, expressly through repentance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (צח.): בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא בְּדוֹר שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ חַיָּיב.
as stated in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 98a): the Son of David comes in a generation that is entirely guilty.
וְנֶפֶשׁ כָּזֶה הוּא מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
And such a soul belongs to the spiritual allotment of the Messiah,
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִקְרָא שֶׁהֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה.
and likewise King David, peace be upon him, is described as having established the yoke of repentance (Moed Katan 16b).
כִּידוּעַ דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל "רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת וְכוּלֵי" רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן;
For as is known, concerning the Congregation of Israel in exile it is written: "Her feet go down to death, etc." (Proverbs 5:5), may the Merciful One preserve us;
וּבְעִקְבֵי מָשִׁיחַ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִן הָרַגְלִין, וְשָׁם תִּגְבֹּורֶת הָרָע וְהַיֵּצֶר.
and in the footsteps of the Messiah, souls originate from the feet (raglin), where the surge of evil and passion is greatest.
וּלְכָךְ דּוֹר שֶׁל נְפָשׁוֹת כָּאֵלּוּ דַּיְיקָא יִזְכּוּ לְמָשִׁיחַ,
And therefore, precisely a generation comprised of such souls will merit the Messiah,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט): "טוֹב מְאֹד" – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע.
as in the rabbinic dictum (Bereishit Rabbah 9): "'Very good'—this is the evil inclination."
וְכֵן מָשִׁיחַ עַצְמוֹ נוֹלַד מִמָּקוֹם כָּזֶה,
And so the Messiah himself was born out of such a lineage,
כִּידוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם וַיֵּרָא עַל בְּנוֹת לוֹט וְלוֹט, שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וּמִשָּׁם נִצְמַח שׁוֹרֶשׁ בֶּן דָּוִד.
as is known from Midrash HaNe'elam (Vayeira) regarding Lot and his daughters, who represent the root of the power of passion, and from there sprouted the root of the Son of David.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אָז: שֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע לְטוֹב, שֶׁזֶּה שְׁחִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.).

That is, because this represents the ultimate perfection that will unfold then: that the very root of evil will be transformed into good, which is the slaughter of the evil inclination described in Sukkah 52a.
וְהוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבַּגּוּף, וְהַיּוֹתֵר סָמוּךְ לָרַע בְּכָל מִינֵי תֹּקֶף.
And he is the final soul in the reservoir of the Guf, and the one closest to evil in all manner of fierce intensity.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַדּוֹרוֹת הוֹלְכִים וּמִתְקַטְּנִים,
And in this physical world the generations steadily diminish in stature;
אֲבָל אָז כְּשֶׁיְּתוּקַּן, יִהְיֶה בְּטוֹב "סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה",
but then, when rectified, it will become good according to "the end of action is conceived in the initial thought,"
בְּסוֹד הַחַיּוֹת: "רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק",
in the mystical secret of the holy Chayot: "running and returning like the appearance of a flash of lightning" (Ezekiel 1:14),
שֶׁמִּמָּקוֹם שֶׁפּוֹסֵק, מִשָּׁם חוֹזֵר וּמַתְחִיל לְהָאִיר,
so that from the very place where it ceases, from there it returns and begins to radiate,
וְנַעֲשָׂה זֶה רֹאשׁ, וְנִתְהַפְּכוּ תַּחְתּוֹנִים לְמַעְלָה,
and this lowest point becomes the head, and the lower elements are inverted to the top,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים נ.): "עוֹלָם הָפוּךְ רָאִיתִי":
as our Sages expounded (Pesachim 50a): "I saw an inverted world—the upper below and the lower above."

paragraphs.text: The final repair restores created powers to their source

paragraphs.text: Sichat Shedim explains why the last stage of repair can transform a power that previously appeared only as an obstacle.

rich.text: Sichat Shedim explains why the last stage of repair can transform a power that previously appeared only as an obstacle.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Sichat Shedim 1:6: “At the completion of action, there is in truth no evil here, for the end of everything is for good, and He “devises means so that no banished one is banished from Him” (II Samuel 14:14). There is therefore no truly evil body at all. This is the secret of the saying, “Falsehood has no legs” (Shabbat 104a), and of the statements in Berakhot 6a and in HaNizakin (Gittin 68b) that the feet of demons are like those of roosters; this is not the place to elaborate. This came about through Shabbat, which is the repair of Adam. As our Sages said, Adam recited the psalm for Shabbat, when his repentance was accepted. So too, at the end of everything, repair will return to its source. The Holy One, blessed be He, does not allow evil to reach completion; therefore no creature is wholly evil, but everything is a mixture of good and evil. As stated in Shabbat 77b, everything has some benefit. Likewise, in the future everything will be repaired, and no creature will be missing from the world: “The wolf will dwell with the lamb” (Isaiah 11:6), and “The serpent—dust shall be its food” (Isaiah 65:25).”

This illuminates the present siman’s ‘inverted world’: the lowest point can become the beginning of a renewed ascent because its created power is recovered for good. Both accounts place the complete transformation at the end of repair. Tzidkat HaTzadik explicitly names repentance as the way of extracting the precious from the vile.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 21: “There the soul of King David, peace be upon him, was hidden, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah: “I found David My servant”—where did I find him? In Sodom. For “one opposite the other”: in one power’s rule over another, the strength of the surrounding shell corresponds to the strength of the holiness. Therefore, “Whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater inclination.” The holy spark of King David’s soul—he who is the principal victorious warrior, of whom “My heart is hollow within me” is interpreted to mean that he killed the evil inclination, and who will also slaughter it in the future—was submerged in the depths of evil, where the inclination was at its greatest strength. No person would have imagined that any holy spark or any holiness could be present there, amid the utmost defilement of bodily desire. It is therefore described as a “finding,” like a discovery that comes unexpectedly. Before Sodom was overturned through the side of might and the fire of Isaac that had begun to be revealed in the world, it was impossible for this to be revealed: that even in a place of such intense desire, holiness is present. Only after that strength of evil was overturned and weakened did a little holiness begin to appear in the intention of Lot’s daughters for the sake of Heaven. Even this was not yet without defilement; nevertheless, some intention to preserve the human species was revealed in her words, “There is no man in the land to come to us,” an intention for the sake of Heaven. This was the beginning of the revelation of King David’s holy light, which illuminates this truth: “Even darkness does not darken for You,” and “Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil, for You are with me.” His sovereignty rules over all, holiness is present everywhere, and the soul of an Israelite is attached to that holy spark—“You who cleave to the Lord your God”—and cannot become separated from it.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayera 21:314-316: “Midrash HaNe’elam: “Lot went up from Tzoar.” Rabbi Abbahu said: Come and see what is written about the evil inclination. Know that it is never abolished from human beings until the time of which it is written, “I will remove the heart of stone.” Although it sees people judged in Gehinnom, it returns to human beings. This is “Lot went up from Tzoar”: from the suffering of Gehinnom it rises to entice people. Rabbi Yehudah said: There are three governing faculties in a person: the governance of intellect and wisdom, which is the power of the holy soul; the governance of desire, which desires every kind of evil desire; and the governance that directs human beings and sustains the body, called the bodily soul. Rav Dimi said: This is the sustaining power. Rabbi Yehudah said: Come and see: the evil inclination rules only over the latter two powers. The desiring soul continually pursues the evil inclination, as implied by “The elder said to the younger: Our father is old.” The desiring soul stirs the other and entices it, together with the body, to cleave to the evil inclination. It says, “Come, let us give our father wine to drink and lie with him”: what do we have in the world to come? Let us pursue the evil inclination and the longing for this world’s pleasures. What do they do? Both agree to cleave to it. Thus it is written, “They gave their father wine to drink”: they fatten themselves with eating and drinking to stir the evil inclination.”

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 26:1: “The meaning is as known in the mystery of “running and returning like the appearance of lightning,” seen by those who behold the Chariot: where they go, there they return. At the place where the light ends, it returns, and the end becomes a beginning, turning back again, so that the last of all the levels attaches to the beginning and the deepest origin and is called the head of all the levels. For the beginning of everything is the blessed God, and complete cleaving to Him is the deepest origin of the unfolding of created beings.”

sections.en: A Person's Passionate Lust Derives from the Intensity of the Desire of His Father…

p: [קיב] תַּאֲוַת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁל הָאָדָם הוּא מִתֹּקֶף הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁל אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ בְּעֵת הֶרְיוֹנוֹ,
A person's passionate lust derives from the intensity of the desire of his father and mother at the time of his conception,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּמִּזְמוֹר כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּא וְכוּלֵי: "הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ז),
as King David, peace be upon him, expressed in the psalm composed when Nathan came to him: "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, etc." (Psalms 51:7),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם וַיֵּרָא (קיב עַמּוּד א) שֶׁהַמְּקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁעַת תַּשְׁמִישׁ לָא מִסְתָּפוּ בָּנָיו מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
and as written in Midrash HaNe'elam (Vayeira 112a) that whoever sanctifies himself at the time of marital intimacy, his children do not fear the evil inclination.
וּלְכָךְ בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁזִּנְתָה – "אֶת אָבִיהָ הִיא מְחַלֶּלֶת" (וַיִּקְרָא כא, ט), וַאֲפִילּוּ הוּא בְּגַן עֵדֶן דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ עַל דָּבָר זֶה.
And therefore, regarding a priest's daughter who commits adultery Scripture states: "she profanes her father" (Leviticus 21:9), and even if he is in Gan Eden, he is judged for this matter.
וּלְכָךְ נִרְאָה לְיוֹסֵף דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא.
And therefore the image of his father appeared to Joseph so that he would not sin (Sotah 36b).
וּכְשֶׁהָאָב קִבֵּל עָנְשׁוֹ וְנִתְקַן שָׁם, אָז הַבֵּן מִתְעוֹרֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
And when the father has received his retribution and is rectified there, then the son is awakened to repentance in this world;
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבַת הַבֵּן וְתִיקּוּנוֹ לְיִצְרָא דַּעֲבֵירָה, מַנִּיחִים לְאָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן.
and likewise conversely: through the son's repentance and his conquering of the impulse to sin, relief is granted to his father and mother in Gan Eden.
וּלְכָךְ בְּעֵת הַמִּילָה שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן הַבְּרִית וְהַתַּאֲוָה, אוֹמְרִים: "יִשְׂמַח אָבִיךָ וְאִמֶּךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי כג, כה).
And therefore at the circumcision ceremony, which is the rectification of the Covenant and passion, we recite: "Let your father and your mother be glad, etc." (Proverbs 23:25).
וְזֶה בִּכְלַל "הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ בְּחָכְמָה",
And this falls under "a father endows his son with wisdom" (Eduyot 2:9),
כִּי אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת:
for a person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly enters him (Sotah 3a).

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 52:10: “Therefore, although a person has sins that come from birth, as it is written (Psalms 51:7), ‘In sin my mother conceived me,’ and a person cannot clarify himself of those sins, Hashem in His abundant kindness and goodness suspends judgment concerning a person’s sin and judges him as he is now, in the present. As long as it is possible to turn the matter toward a person’s merit, that he did not act defiantly, He suspends judgment concerning his sins. Likewise, we see how many precious words of Torah come into being from this imaginary and temporal world; those words of Torah are eternal, standing at the height of the world forever.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov invokes the same verse about conception while distinguishing an inherited deficiency from a defiant act committed in the present. This qualification helps read the siman’s parent-and-child account as a description of transmitted conditions and shared repair, without making ancestry a substitute for judging the person’s present action.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 21:1: “As it is written, “The wise inherit honor”—like an inheritance that does not cease, as our Sages said in Bava Metzia 85a: wherever a person is a Torah scholar, and his son, and so forth, it does not cease. “He, his son, and his grandson” means that his wisdom is complete, for a father endows his son with wisdom, as taught at the end of the second chapter of Eduyot, because the son is drawn from the drops of his father’s mind. When wisdom is merely outward speech and is not truly in his depths—when he is wise only in appearance—his wisdom is incomplete, and his son is not a Torah scholar. This is the meaning of their not having recited the blessing over Torah first, as taught in Nedarim 81a: the blessing before Torah is the recognition that wisdom comes from the blessed Lord. Without this, it is merely an illusion and apparent wisdom, not true wisdom. There are two depths in “from the depths,” the hidden mind and heart; the second depth is revealed in the grandson. When wisdom is complete in all its depths, it no longer ceases, and honor is his inheritance.”

p: [קיג] "פְּרִי צַדִּיק – עֵץ חַיִּים" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ל),
"The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life" (Proverbs 11:30),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פה.) גַּבֵּי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אַף שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה לֹא כֵן.
as stated in Bava Metzia 85a regarding the son of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, even though initially he appeared quite the opposite.
דִּבְוַדַּאי הַצַּדִּיק מוֹלִיד נְפָשׁוֹת יְקָרוֹת
For certainly the righteous person engenders precious souls
[וְעֵץ חַיִּים הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד עִם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת].
[and the 'tree of life' is Torah, which is one with these holy souls].
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל: דְּרוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין שֶׁהוֹלִיד אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הָיוּ דּוֹר שִׁעְבּוּד מִצְרַיִם.
And along these lines is likewise what the holy Ari wrote: that the spirits and demons generated by Adam the First became the generation subjugated in Egypt.
וְכֵן י' טִפִּין שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִיּוֹסֵף הֵם עֲשָׂרָה הֲרוּגֵי מַלְכוּת.
And likewise the ten drops that issued from Joseph became the Ten Martyrs of the Kingdom.
רַק שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָזֶה "וְלֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת חָכָם" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ל), דִּבְחָכְמָה אִתְבְּרִירוּ וְלוֹקְחָם מִן הָרָע.
Only that for this is required "and he that wins souls is wise" (Proverbs 11:30), for through wisdom they are refined and extracted from evil.
וְלִפְעָמִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם בַּדּוֹר, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל מִפֶּרֶק הַפּוֹעֲלִים בִּבְנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
And sometimes this is achieved through a specific Torah scholar in the generation, as mentioned above from chapter HaPo'alim regarding the son of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
וְלִפְעָמִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ, שֶׁנִּקְרָא גַּם כֵּן לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת בְּמִשְׁפָּט בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאָבֵל.
And sometimes it is accomplished by the Holy One Himself, Who is likewise termed "He Who takes souls in judgment" in the Grace after Meals for mourners.
וְעַל יְדֵי מִיתַת הָאָב שֶׁנִּקְרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת, הוּא גַּם כֵּן "לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת" – נֶפֶשׁ בְּנוֹ
And through the father's death, wherein the Blessed Name is termed the Taker of souls, He is likewise the one who "takes souls"—the soul of his son
[וְכֵן נְפָשׁוֹת הָעֲשׁוּקוֹת רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן]
[and likewise the oppressed, captive souls, may the Merciful One preserve us]
וְעוֹשֶׂה מִמֶּנָּה עֵץ חַיִּים
and transforms it into a tree of life
[וְלִפְעָמִים הוּא עַל אוֹתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ דִּבְגְמָרָא שָׁם דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ "רַבִּי",
[and sometimes it occurs in the manner described in the Gemara there, where they addressed him prematurely as "Rabbi,"
וְנוֹתֵן בְּלֵב בְּנֵי אָדָם לְהַסְמִיכוֹ בְּרַבִּי וּלְהַגְדִּילוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְגַּדֵּל אַחַר כָּךְ בֶּאֱמֶת.
inspiring people's hearts to ordain him as Rabbi and honor him, whereby he subsequently becomes genuinely great.
וְאָז גַּם "רַבִּי" שֶׁקָּרְאוּ לוֹ אָז, וַדַּאי לֹא לַשָּׁוְא הָיָה,
And then, even the title "Rabbi" they applied to him back then was certainly not in vain;
כִּי כְּשֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה הָאֱמֶת, אָז נִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם תְּחִלָּה הָיָה כֵן רַק שֶׁהָיָה בְּהֶעְלֵם,
for when the truth is revealed, it becomes evident that even initially it was so, only that it lay in deep concealment,
כִּי "מֵאַרְיָא בִּישָׁא גּוּרְיָא טָבָא לָא נָפֵיק".
for 'from a bad lion a good cub does not come out.'
וְתֵדַע, דְּאָמְרוּ שָׁם: "לֹא שֶׁזֶּה גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה וְכוּלֵי",
And you may know this, for they said there: "Not that this one is greater than that one, etc.,"
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה רוֹעֶה זוֹנוֹת תְּחִלָּה,
and even though he was initially an associate of harlots,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא תִזָּכַרְנָה רִאשׁוֹנוֹת,
nonetheless his former deeds are not mentioned,
רַק הָיָה גַּם בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ טוֹב וְגָדוֹל כְּמוֹ בַּסּוֹף,
but he was inherently good and great in his beginning just as at his end,
וְעַל כֵּן נִזְכַּר זֶה בַּגְּמָרָא]:
and therefore was this recorded in the Gemara].

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar HaPesukim, Parashat Shemot 6: “It follows that all those demons and spirits created during the 130 years when Adam separated from Eve, as is known, were all exalted holy souls from the aspect of daat. They became mixed among the shells and required many reincarnations to refine and purify them until their impurity was removed. Therefore you find that the nation of Israel did not come into being until Jacob and afterward: most of the souls were mixed among the shells and were progressively refined, reincarnating from generation to generation. Their repair did not begin until Jacob, the chosen of the patriarchs, who repaired Adam. Then the repair of his children—the aforementioned souls—also began, and they continued to be refined in the Egyptian exile until Israel left Egypt.”

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 85a:12-13: “When he died, they brought him to his father’s cave. A snake was coiled around the cave. They said to it: “Snake, snake, open your mouth, and let a son enter beside his father.” It did not open for them. The people thought that this meant one was greater than the other. sections.en: Whoever Is a Torah Scholar Gathers Souls and Collects Holy Sparks from Sacred Souls…

p: [קיד] מִי שֶׁהוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, הוּא לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת וּמְלַקֵּט נִיצוֹצוֹת מִנְּפָשׁוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁנִּתְפַּזְּרוּ בְּעִמְקֵי תְּהוֹם רַבָּה.
Whoever is a Torah scholar gathers souls and collects holy sparks from sacred souls that have been scattered into the depths of the great abyss.
עַל יְדֵי לִמּוּד תּוֹרָתוֹ, כָּל דִּבּוּר שֶׁל תּוֹרָה מוֹצִיא אוֹתָם הַשַּׁיָּיכִים לוֹ,
Through his Torah study, every spoken word of Torah extracts those souls affiliated with him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְלֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת חָכָם" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ל).
as it is written: "and he that wins souls is wise" (Proverbs 11:30).
וְגַם נַפְשׁוֹ עַצְמוֹ,
And he also extracts his own soul,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פְּתִיחַת אֵיכָה): "הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ מַחֲזִירוֹ לְמוּטָב".
as stated (Midrash Rabbah, introduction to Eichah): "the illumination within it returns him to good."
אֲבָל בָּזֶה יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת, שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים כְּשֶׁהִיא בְּעֹמֶק רַע רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁנֶּחְבְּשָׁה וְנִשְׁקְעָה שָׁם,
However, in this there are gradations, for sometimes when a soul is in the depth of evil, may the Merciful One preserve us, so sunken and imprisoned there,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: "אֵין חָבוּשׁ מַתִּיר עַצְמוֹ" (בְּרָכוֹת ה:),
concerning which they said: "A prisoner cannot free himself from prison" (Berakhot 5b),
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חֻקָּי",
and regarding this it was stated: "And unto the wicked God says: What right have you to recount My statutes?" (Psalms 50:16);
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא עב:): לֹא זָכָה – נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
and likewise they said (Yoma 72b): if he did not merit, it becomes a deadly potion to him,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת וּמַכְנִיסָם גַּם כֵּן בְּעֹמֶק רַע רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.
such that through his words of Torah he gathers souls and drags them likewise into the depth of evil, may the Merciful One preserve us.
אַף דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לַסּוֹף כְּשֶׁיְּתַקֵּן הוּא מַרְוִיחַ, דְּעוֹלֶה וְעוֹלִים עִמּוֹ;
Even though ultimately when he rectifies he gains, for he ascends and they ascend with him;
אַךְ לְפִי שָׁעָה נֶאֱמַר עַל זֶה: "וּפֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, י) דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָרַע מִתְגַּבֵּר.
yet for the immediate present it is proclaimed: "and transgressors shall stumble in them" (Hosea 14:10), whereby through this evil is temporarily intensified.
רַק לִפְעָמִים גַּם לָזֶה יוֹעִיל תּוֹרָתוֹ, כְּשֶׁמַּצִּיל עַל יְדֵי כֵן אֵיזֶה נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא בַּחַיִּים,
However, sometimes even for this his Torah avails, when he thereby saves some soul that is alive in this world,
וְאוֹתוֹ נֶפֶשׁ מִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ וְיוּכַל לְהַצִּילוֹ,
and that soul overcomes its inclination and is empowered to save him,
וּכְמַעֲשֶׂה דְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא (סוֹף פֶּרֶק כב) שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּתוֹרָתוֹ, רַק הִצִּיל נֶפֶשׁ הָאִשָּׁה
as in the episode of a certain disciple in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta (end of chapter 22) who could not save himself through his own Torah, yet saved the soul of the woman
[שֶׁהָיְתָה גַּם כֵּן נֶפֶשׁ גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהָיְתָה יְכוֹלָה לְהָבִין כְּשֶׁרָאֲתָה אוֹתוֹ לוֹמֵד שֶׁהוּא כְּמַלְאָךְ,
[who was likewise a lofty soul, capable of discerning when she saw him learning that he was like an angel,
וּמִסְּתָמָא הָאֱמֶת כֵּן מִדְּנִזְכַּר בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֱלִיָּהוּ, אִם כֵּן יָדְעָה בְּטִיבָן שֶׁל מַלְאָכִים]
and presumably that was the truth since it was recorded in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu, showing she was versed in the nature of angels]
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִיא הִצִּילַתּוּ.
and afterward she saved him.
וְעִמְקֵי רַע נִקְרָא רַע בְּתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת, וְכָל סֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי מָלֵא מִזֶּה, וְנֶאֱמַר: "שׁוּחָה עֲמֻקָּה זוֹנָה" (מִשְׁלֵי כג, כז).
And the "depths of evil" denotes the immersion in wicked lusts, with which the Book of Proverbs is replete, as stated: "For a harlot is a deep pit" (Proverbs 23:27).
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (יח:): אֲפִילּוּ דּוֹמֶה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁקִּבֵּל תּוֹרָה מֵהַר סִינַי, לֹא יִנָּקֶה מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם;
And therefore they stated in Eruvin 18b: even if one resembles Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who received the Torah from Mount Sinai, he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehenna;
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְהַתִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָתוֹ,
meaning that he cannot liberate himself from prison through his own Torah,
אֲבָל יָכוֹל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים הַבָּאִים מִגִּירָא דִילֵיהּ.
but he can be freed through others who originate as arrows from his quiver.
וְכֵן אַחֵר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ "וְלָרָשָׁע וְגוֹמֵר", נִיצּוֹל עַל יְדֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁלָּמַד תּוֹרָה מִמֶּנּוּ, וְהוּא תִּיקֵּן וְהִצִּיל נַפְשׁוֹ מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם:

And so Acher [Elisha ben Avuyah], to whom it was said "And unto the wicked God says, etc.," was saved through Rabbi Meir who studied Torah from him, who rectified and delivered his soul from the judgment of Gehenna (Chagigah 15b).

paragraphs.text: Or HaChaim on Leviticus 7:37:2: “They said that the purpose of engaging in Torah is to refine the sparks of holiness that fell or were forcibly taken from holiness, and to restore them in complete unity to their former state. These are of two kinds. The first consists of the sparks of holiness that descended in the world of chaos, for a reason known to Him; what is understood by those who possess knowledge suffices as a sound explanation. The second consists of the oppressed souls that the man of wickedness seized from Adam through his sin, when he took great spoil, as is known concerning the vast number of souls he seized. Nothing commands him to disgorge what he swallowed except engagement in Torah. Through it one accomplishes the essential work: raising the holy sparks that fell before the world of repair, making Samael disgorge what he swallowed, and shattering and dissolving his power until he vomits out the wealth he swallowed. This is what the Sages said: “If [the evil inclination] encounters you”—if it is stone, it dissolves, and if it is iron, it shatters.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Or HaChaim explicitly distinguishes the fallen sparks of the world of chaos from the souls seized through Adam’s sin, and identifies Torah study as the means of recovering both. This supplies the fuller original account behind Rav Tzadok’s description of each Torah utterance bringing out the souls associated with its speaker.

paragraphs.text: Context: Ramchal distinguishes the immediate divine influence that requires worthy conduct from Torah’s intrinsic holiness, which can gradually awaken repentance even in a sinner. He expressly limits this latter claim to serious study, excluding mockery and deliberate distortion. This clarifies the distinction between Torah’s restorative power and the impediments Rav Tzadok describes here.

paragraphs.text: When wisdom supplies power to a wrong direction

rich.text: When wisdom supplies power to a wrong direction

paragraphs.text: The initial purity of wisdom does not prevent its misuse by the heart and body.

rich.text: The initial purity of wisdom does not prevent its misuse by the heart and body.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 4:8: “Nevertheless, the body’s and heart’s power to sin comes through the wisdom within them. As it says (Hosea 14:10), ‘Transgressors stumble through them,’ and the Sages said (Shabbat 88b) that for those who turn it to the left, it becomes a potion of death. Through wisdom itself a person stumbles and dies, for without it the body could not sin so greatly. One cannot speak falsehood unless one says something true at the beginning. That is, something wholly imaginary is nothing, just as an animal has no sin because it has no wisdom and is entirely imagination. What is wholly imagination has no place for sin; only someone who first has a foundation of truth can afterward say something false. This is clear to one who understands.”

rich.text: : “Nevertheless, the body’s and heart’s power to sin comes through the wisdom within them. As it says (Hosea 14:10), ‘Transgressors stumble through them,’ and the Sages said (Shabbat 88b) that for those who turn it to the left, it becomes a potion of death. Through wisdom itself a person stumbles and dies, for without it the body could not sin so greatly. One cannot speak falsehood unless one says something true at the beginning. That is, something wholly imaginary is nothing, just as an animal has no sin because it has no wisdom and is entirely imagination. What is wholly imagination has no place for sin; only someone who first has a foundation of truth can afterward say something false. This is clear to one who understands.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet explains why Torah’s power does not guarantee a good immediate result. Wisdom can give the heart and body greater power to pursue a wrong direction; falsehood itself can become persuasive through the truth it initially borrows. This clarifies the siman’s warning that a learner’s unresolved captivity can draw other souls downward, even though eventual repair remains possible.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 39:19-20: “When one studies truly not for its own sake, with some ulterior motive for one’s own honor—for example, to become a Torah scholar and the like—that motive, which comes from kelipat nogah, clothes itself in one’s Torah. The Torah is then temporarily in exile within the shell, until one repents, bringing healing to the world. When one returns to the Lord, one’s Torah returns together with oneself. Therefore our Sages said, “A person should always occupy himself [with Torah and commandments], for from doing so not for its own sake he comes to do so for its own sake”—certainly so, for he will certainly eventually repent, whether in this incarnation or another, since “no banished one shall remain banished from Him.””

paragraphs.text: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta 22: “There was a student of Rabbi Akiva who sat at the head of twenty-four thousand students. Once he went to the prostitutes’ market, saw a prostitute, and loved her. He kept sending a messenger between himself and her until evening. At evening she went up to the roof and saw that student sitting at the head of the students like an army commander, with Gabriel standing at his right. She immediately said to herself: “Woe to that woman, against whom all the punishments of Gehinnom will gather! Will this woman afflict a great man like this, who resembles an angel? When she dies and departs from this world, she will inherit Gehinnom. But if she does not receive him, she saves both him and herself from the judgment of Gehinnom.” When he came to her, she said: “My son, why are you losing the life of the world to come for an hour’s pleasure in this world?” His desire did not cool. She said: “My son, the place you desire is more filthy and unclean than all the other parts of the body, and no creature can bear its smell.” His desire still did not cool until she took hold of his nose and placed it at that place. When he smelled it, it became repulsive to him, and he never married. A heavenly voice went forth and said: “That woman and that man are destined for life in the world to come.””

paragraphs.text: Context: This is the complete rescue episode cited here. The woman’s recognition of the student’s spiritual stature turns her toward saving them both; her subsequent intervention then saves him from the intended sin. The narrative includes Gabriel’s presence, her repeated efforts, and the final heavenly declaration, preserving the sequence on which Rav Tzadok’s interpretation rests.

sections.en: When a Person Innovates an Insight in the Torah

p: [קטו] כְּשֶׁמְּחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר בַּתּוֹרָה, צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מִצַּד שׁוּם נְגִיעָה בַּלֵּב שֶׁרוֹצֶה כָּךְ, אוֹ לְהִתְפָּאֲרוּת, אוֹ לַחְלוֹק עַל דִּבְרֵי זוּלָתוֹ וְכַיּוֹצֵא,

When a person innovates an insight in the Torah, it must not stem from any personal bias in the heart that desires it to be so, nor for self-aggrandizement, nor to dispute the words of another, or the like;
רַק מִצַּד הַתְּשׁוּקָה לֵידַע הָאֱמֶת,
but solely from the pure yearning to know the Truth.
וְאָז אֲפִילּוּ טוֹעֶה נִקְרָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְדִבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים,
And then, even if he errs, it is termed words of Torah and the words of the living God,
שֶׁהֲרֵי נִזְכַּר בַּתַּלְמוּד דִּבְרֵי הַטּוֹעִים וְשֶׁנִּדְחוּ מֵהֲלָכָה, שֶׁגַּם הַהֲוָא אָמֵינָא הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,

for behold, the Talmud explicitly records the words of those who erred and opinions that were rejected from practical halakhah, showing that even the initial hypothesis (hava amina) is words of Torah;
שֶׁכָּךְ יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: מוּשְׂכָּל רִאשׁוֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַגָּעָה לָאֱמֶת, וְגַם הַמּוּשְׂכָּל רִאשׁוֹן הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְדִבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים.

for thus the Blessed Name established the process: first an initial conception, and only subsequently arriving at the truth; and that initial conception is likewise from the Blessed Name and constitutes the words of the living God.
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַנְּגִיעָה, אָז אֵינוֹ נִקְרָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּלָל,
But when it stems from personal bias, then it is not termed words of Torah at all;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיָרָבְעָם: "הַחֹדֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּדָא מִלִּבּוֹ" (מְלָכִים א יב, לג),
as written concerning Jeroboam: "the month which he had devised of his own heart" (I Kings 12:33),
וּבְוַדַּאי הוּא דָּרַשׁ לָהֶם אֵיזֶה דְּרָשׁ וְלִמּוּד שֶׁחַג הָאָסִיף הוּא בְּחֶשְׁוָן,
and certainly he expounded to them some textual exegesis and derivation that the Harvest Festival falls in Marcheshvan;
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד הַנְּגִיעָה לַעֲשׂוֹת נֶגֶד בֵּית דִּין שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, נִקְרָא "אֲשֶׁר בָּדָא מִלִּבּוֹ", וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר בָּזֶה "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים".

yet because it stemmed from personal bias to undermine the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem, it was branded "which he had devised of his own heart," and concerning this it was not said: "both these and those are the words of the living God."
וְכֵן דּוֹאֵג עָשָׂה הַכֹּל עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה בְּדַעְתּוֹ, כִּי רֹאשׁ הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין הָיָה,
And likewise Doeg acted completely in accordance with the Torah in his own mind, for he was the head of the Sanhedrin,
וְהוּא הוֹרָה "עַמּוֹנִי – וְאֲפִילּוּ עַמּוֹנִית" עַל פִּי הֲלָכָה שֶׁבְּדַעְתּוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי אִשְׁתִּיתוּ נֶגְדּוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יְבָמוֹת עז.),
and he ruled: "'an Ammonite'—even a female Ammonite" based on the halakhah as he construed it, seeing that the scholars initially fell silent before him (Yevamot 77a),
וּמִמֵּילָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ וְהוּא מִפְּסוּלֵי קָהָל, וְדָנוֹ לְמוֹרֵד בַּמַּלְכוּת, וְכֵן לַאֲחִימֶלֶךְ.
and consequently it was impossible for David to be king, being disqualified from the congregation, and so he judged David as a rebel against the monarchy, and likewise Ahimelech.
וְשָׁאוּל, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה סָבוּר גַּם כֵּן כֵּן, הוּא הָיָה בְּטָעוּת וְנִקְרָא בֶּאֱמֶת בְּחִיר ה'.
And Saul, even though he likewise held this view, was merely in honest error, and was in truth titled the chosen one of Hashem.
אֲבָל דּוֹאֵג, דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵלּוּ נָבְעוּ מִלִּבּוֹ מִצַּד הַקִּנְאָה, וְאִלּוּלֵי נְגִיעָה זוֹ לֹא הָיָה טוֹעֶה.
But with Doeg, these words of Torah welled up from his heart out of jealousy, and were it not for this personal bias, he would not have made this error.
בְּאֹפֶן זֶה נַעֲשִׂים דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה סַם הַמָּוֶת רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן, שֶׁנֶּאֶבְדוּ מִן הָעוֹלָם,
In this manner, words of Torah become a potion of death, may the Merciful One preserve us, causing one to be lost from the world,
כִּי אֵין זֶה נִקְרָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל, רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
for this is not truly termed words of Torah at all, but only so to outward appearance
[וְאֵין בְּכֹחַ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כָּאֵלּוּ לְהוֹצִיא נְפָשׁוֹת כְּלָל, כְּעִנְיַן "אֵל אַחֵר אִסְתָּרַס וְלָא עָבִיד פֵּירִין".
[and such words of Torah have no power to extract and redeem holy souls at all, in the manner of 'the other god is castrated and bears no fruit.'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה טו:) וּבְפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:): מִי זוּטַר וְכוּלֵי, אֶלָּא רַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי,
And this aligns with Chagigah 15b and Sanhedrin 106b: 'Is this a small matter, etc.? Rather, the Merciful One desires the heart.'
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁהַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ יִהְיֶה מְחֻבֶּרֶת עִם הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב יַחַד, וְהַחָכְמָה יִהְיֶה יוֹצֵאת מִן הַלֵּב,
Which means that the wisdom in the brain must be bound together with the understanding in the heart, wisdom emerging directly from the heart,
וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי הַדַּעַת הַמְּחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה,
and this occurs through Da'at (awareness) which unites Chokhmah and Binah;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֵל אַחֵר אֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"ז,
whereas the 'other god' lacks Da'at as I wrote above in Section 107,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה א): תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה וְכוּלֵי]:
and concerning this they taught (Vayikra Rabbah 1:15 end): 'A Torah scholar who lacks Da'at, etc.']

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Shabbat Chol HaMoed Sukkot 19:1: “Concerning words of Torah, however, the Midrash concludes: lest you say that after a person gives his learning to another it no longer returns to him, Scripture says, ‘There they return to go.’ At the completion of every transmission there must be a little forgetting in the giver. This forgetting is the completion through which a new birth occurs, for every birth must first have forgetting before the birth can come from it. So too in transmitting Torah, when it moves from thought into speech, a person cannot always maintain a clearly illuminated awareness that he is only a conduit. Because he then forgets that he is only a conduit, he acquires a personal interest and wants to maintain his own statement, as the Talmud says, a person is inclined to maintain his statement. Thus the Midrash says: after a person gives his learning to another, when a little forgetting at the completion of transmission is unavoidable, lest you think those words of Torah are lost from him and remain in the isolated detail, Scripture says, ‘There they return to go.’ Since a person cannot avoid that little forgetting at the completion, they return to him; they do not, Heaven forbid, remain in the isolated detail.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim describes a subtler form of attachment to one’s teaching: forgetting for a moment that one is a conduit and therefore wanting to defend one’s own words. It also describes the teaching returning rather than remaining trapped in that private claim. This is a qualified comparison with Rav Tzadok’s distinction: a passing lapse during transmission is not identified with deliberately deriving an argument from envy or personal interest, but it too requires the teacher to relinquish ownership of the truth.

paragraphs.text: Derekh Hashem, Part Four, On Torah Study 5: “The conditions that must accompany study are reverence during the study itself and the correction of conduct at all times. For all the power of Torah lies in His having attached His precious influence to it, so that speaking its words and understanding them draw down that great influence. Without this, speaking of it would be like speaking of other matters or books of learning, and understanding it would be like understanding other subjects of the natural world. These provide only knowledge of the particular subject; they impart no intrinsic excellence or elevation to the soul of the reader, speaker, or thinker, and no repair to creation as a whole. This influence, however, is divine, and is the highest and most exalted of the influences that reach created beings from Him. A person should therefore fear and tremble when engaged in such a matter: he approaches his God and occupies himself with drawing that great light from Him. He must be humbled by his human lowliness and tremble before His exaltedness. He should rejoice greatly in the good portion he has merited, but with trembling. This includes not sitting frivolously or treating either its words or its books disrespectfully, and knowing before Whom one stands and works. When one does this, one’s study truly becomes what it should be: the influence described is drawn down through it, divine excellence becomes rooted within oneself, and repair and illumination extend to all creation. But if this condition is absent, the illumination is not drawn down through one’s study. One’s words are merely like other human speech, one’s reading like reading a letter, and one’s thoughts like thoughts about worldly affairs. Indeed, one incurs guilt for approaching the holy without reverence and behaving frivolously before one’s Creator while speaking before Him and engaging with His holiness. The excellence of the study and the degree of influence it draws down correspond to the degree of reverence, honor, and care invested in it.”

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 1:15: ‘Another interpretation: ‘He called to Moses, and Hashem spoke.’ From here they said: A Torah scholar who lacks judgment—a carcass is better than he is. Know that this is so: go and learn from Moses, the father of wisdom and the father of the prophets, who brought Israel out of Egypt. Through him many miracles were performed in Egypt and awesome deeds at the Sea of Reeds. He ascended to the highest heavens, brought Torah down from heaven, and worked on the construction of the Mishkan. Yet he did not enter the innermost place until He called him, as it is said, ‘He called to Moses, and He spoke’ (Leviticus 1:1). Elsewhere it says, ‘Hashem saw that he turned aside to see,’ and so forth (Exodus 3:4). At the bush, there was a separation between His calling to him and His speaking; in the Tent of Meeting there is no separation here. What is the case at the bush like? It is like a king of flesh and blood who became angry with his servant and ordered him imprisoned. When he gives instructions to the messenger, he gives them only from outside. But in the Tent of Meeting, when he is pleased with his children and his household is happy, he gives instructions to the messenger only from within, as if seating him between his knees, with a hand like a father’s upon his son. Therefore it says, ‘He called to Moses.’’
