sections.en: Through Errors Occurring in Words of Torah Wherein One Stumbles and Subsequently Masters The…

p: [קטז] עַל יְדֵי הַטָּעֻיּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁטּוֹעֶה וְאַחַר כָּךְ עוֹמֵד עַל הָאֱמֶת, שֶׁזֶּה קָרָא יְשַׁעְיָה "מַכְשֵׁלָה" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּחֲגִיגָה (יד.) דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,

Through errors occurring in words of Torah wherein one stumbles and subsequently masters the truth—which Isaiah designated as a "ruin/obstacle" (makhshelah, Isaiah 3:6), explained in Chagigah 14a as referring to words of Torah—
עַל יְדֵי זֶה לוֹקֵחַ אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה שֶׁבָּאִים מִצַּד יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ יְשַׁעְיָה "מִכְשׁוֹל" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.),
one gathers those captive souls generated by emitting seed in vain that stem from the evil inclination, which Isaiah titled a "stumbling block" (mikhshol, Isaiah 57:14; Sukkah 52a),
וְהוּא בְּפָרָשַׁת "הַצַּדִּיק אָבָד" שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ עַל עָוֹן זֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת מ"ה.
located in the passage "The righteous perishes" which is expounded upon this very sin, as I wrote above in Section 45.
וּמִכְשׁוֹל הַיְינוּ "לִפְנֵי עִוֵּר" בְּאֵין רוֹאֶה, וְכֵן זֶה בַּחֲלוֹם לַיְלָה
And a stumbling block means "before the blind" where none sees, and likewise this emission occurs in the nocturnal slumber of the night

[וּ"מִדֶּרֶךְ עַמִּי", וְ"דֶרֶךְ" בְּכָל מָקוֹם רוֹמֵז עַל "דֶּרֶךְ גֶּבֶר בְּעַלְמָה", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (יא.) "מִבְּלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ", וְכֵן עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ קִדּוּשִׁין].

[and 'out of the way of My people,' where 'way' everywhere alludes to 'the way of a man with a maid' (Proverbs 30:19), as in Berakhot 11a, and likewise to words of Torah, as at the start of Kiddushin].
וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹבֵר עַל לָאו דְּ"לִפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל"
And certainly the Blessed Name does not violate the prohibition "you shall not put a stumbling block before the blind"

[וְעַיֵּין בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (כט.) פְּלוּגְתָּא אִי נִתְקָל פּוֹשֵׁעַ, וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר בֵּאַרְנוּ דְּכָל אֶחָד דִּבֵּר כְּפִי שָׁרְשׁוֹ, רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְשִׁיטָתוֹ בְּגִטִּין נב. וְהוֹרָיוֹת יג: דְּדִבְרֵי חֲלוֹמוֹת לֹא מַעֲלִין וְלֹא מוֹרִידִין, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],

[and see Bava Kamma 29a regarding the dispute whether one who trips is negligent, which we explained elsewhere as reflecting each sage's soul-root, Rabbi Meir following his view in Gittin 52a and Horayot 13b that dreams are meaningless, and this is not the place to lengthen],
רַק הוּא כְּדֵי לַעֲמוֹד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְהוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל.
but rather it occurs so that one subsequently masters words of Torah to extract the precious from the vile.
וְאָז דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "מַכְשֵׁלָה" – נוּקְבָא לְגַבֵּי "מִכְשׁוֹל" דְּכַר, וּמְקַבֶּלֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הָעֲשׁוּקָה הַהוּא שֶׁהוּא הַמִּכְשׁוֹל, וּמוֹצִיאָתוֹ לָאוֹר וְלִקְדוּשָׁה,

And then words of Torah are called a makhshelah (feminine noun) relative to the masculine mikhshol, receiving that oppressed captive soul which was the stumbling block and delivering it into light and holiness,
שֶׁגַּם בָּהּ נֶאֱרַע מַכְשֵׁלָה וְהַעֲמָדָה עַל הָאֱמֶת אַחַר כָּךְ דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה, כִּי אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵי בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר, עַל יְדֵי זֶה הֶעֱלָה הַמִּכְשׁוֹל.

for in the Torah study there likewise occurred an initial stumbling and an arrival at the truth specifically through it—since a person does not master Torah in any other way—and through this he elevates the stumbling block.
וְדַיְיקָא יְשַׁעְיָה קְרָאוֹ כֵן וְנִתְנַבֵּא "הָרִימוּ מִכְשׁוֹל וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁהוּא עָמַד עַל זֶה,
And specifically Isaiah termed it thus and prophesied "take up the stumbling block, etc.," for he grasped this deeply,
כַּנּוֹדָע דִּבְרִית הַלָּשׁוֹן וּבְרִית הַמָּעוֹר מְכֻוָּונוֹת, דִּלְכָךְ בַּתּוֹרָה מְתַקְּנִים חֵטְא הַמָּעוֹר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת צ"ז וְק"ז;
as is known that the Covenant of the Tongue and the Covenant of Circumcision run parallel, which is why through Torah one rectifies the sin of the organ, as I wrote above in Sections 97 and 107;
וְכֵן לְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם: "פִּיו הִכְשִׁילוֹ",
and so is the common idiom of our Sages: "his mouth caused him to stumble,"
וּבְגִטִּין (נז.): אַכְשְׁלֵיהּ פּוּמֵיהּ לְבַר דְּרוֹמָא,
and in Gittin 57a: his mouth caused Bar Droma to stumble,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה מֵזִיד, קְרָאוּהוּ
even though he acted deliberately, they called it
[וְכֵן בְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, הוּא מְהַרְהֵר וְרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא לִידֵי הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה]
[and likewise with wasted seed: he thinks about it yet wants not to come to it]
"מִכְשׁוֹל", כִּי הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּמֵה' מַעֲנֵה לָשׁוֹן" (מִשְׁלֵי טז, א), וּמִזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ בַּפֶּה מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לְדַבֵּר כְּלָל כַּנּוֹדָע בְּכָל מָקוֹם.

a "stumbling block," because it is ordained from the Blessed Name, as written: "and the answer of the tongue is from Hashem" (Proverbs 16:1), bringing to his lips what he never intended to articulate, as known in multiple sources.
וּבָזֶה נִכְשַׁל יְשַׁעְיָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי אִישׁ טְמֵא שְׂפָתַיִם אָנֹכִי" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, ה),
And in this Isaiah stumbled, as it is written: "because I am a man of unclean lips" (Isaiah 6:5),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (מט:): כִּי מְטָא לַהֲדֵי פּוּמָא וְכוּלֵי, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁדִּבֵּר רַע עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and as stated in Yevamot 49b: when the saw reached his mouth he perished, because he spoke critically of the children of Israel;
וְנַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם עֶצֶם הַתּוֹרָה, נִמְצָא הוּא טָעוּת בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
and the souls of Israel are the very essence of the Torah, so that speaking against them constituted an error in words of Torah.
וְאָמְנָם בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לֹא נִכְשַׁל רַק לְשָׁעָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְבְּעוּ דְּבָרָיו בַּסֵּפֶר וְהֵם דִּבְרֵי נְבוּאָה מִפִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
However, in truth, Heaven forbid that he stumbled permanently, but only for an instant, for his words were nonetheless established in the canon as prophetic words from the mouth of the Blessed Name;
רַק טָעוּת לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן, לְכָךְ הָיָה עָנְשׁוֹ עַל יְדֵי מְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁטָּעַן נֶגְדּוֹ שֶׁנִּכְשַׁל בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא נִכְשַׁל:

it was merely a seeming error to outward appearance, which is why his punishment came through Manasseh who alleged against him that he contradicted the Torah of Moses (Yevamot 49b), even though in truth he had not stumbled.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52a: ‘Isaiah called it a ‘stumbling block,’ as it is said: ‘Build up, build up; clear a way; remove the stumbling block from My people’s path.’ Ezekiel called it a ‘stone,’ as it is said: ‘I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.’ Joel called it the ‘northern one’—tzefoni—as it is said: ‘I will remove the northern one far from you.’ The Sages taught: ‘I will remove the northern one far from you’ refers to the evil inclination, which lies hidden—tzafun—in a person’s heart.’

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Pekudei 4:1: “That is, what he said, “And I dwell among a people of unclean lips,” was spoken by the mouth of Hashem, for these words were according to His will. This is the meaning of “Your iniquity has departed.” Although Isaiah’s intention was to describe Israel as unclean of lips, and this was like speaking maliciously of Israel, the words written among the Prophets are words of Torah, truly spoken by the mouth of Hashem. They teach merit concerning Israel: their sin is only from the lips outward, like the statement, “Doeg’s Torah was only from the lips outward.” This was a merit for Israel, that their impurity and sin were only from the lips outward. Similarly, the Midrash says that in two places Israel acted toward the Holy One, blessed be He: at Sinai they acted with their mouths and not their hearts, as it is said, “They enticed Him with their mouths.” Since they went wrong shortly after saying, “We shall do and we shall hear,” their statement was only outward, in their mouths and not their hearts. In Babylonia they acted with their hearts and not their mouths: their sin there was only from the lips outward, while their hearts were bound to Hashem. This is the meaning of “They acted only outwardly.” Here too, the words taught merit concerning Israel: they were merely a people of unclean lips, outwardly, while their hearts were pure and bound at their root to Hashem. This was the intention from Hashem’s side. But Isaiah, for his part, intended to accuse Israel with these words. This resembles one who intended to take pork but actually took lamb, who still requires atonement and forgiveness. Concerning this it says, “Your sin shall be atoned.” See also Yevamot 49b.”

paragraphs.text: Yevamot 49b:10-50a:3: ““I saw Hashem”: As it was taught, all the prophets looked through a dim glass, while Moshe our teacher looked through a clear glass. “Seek Hashem when He may be found”: One statement concerns an individual, the other a community. When can an individual find Him? Rav Nachman said in Rabbah bar Avuhah’s name: These are the ten days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. “I shall fulfill the number of your days”: This is a dispute among the tannaim. It was taught: “I shall fulfill the number of your days”—these are the years allotted to a generation. If one merits, they complete them for him; if he does not merit, they deduct from them. These are Rabbi Akiva’s words. The Sages say: If he merits, they add to them; if he does not merit, they deduct from them. They said to Rabbi Akiva: But it says, “I shall add fifteen years to your days”! He replied: They added years that were already his. Know this, for a prophet had already prophesied, “A son shall be born to the house of David, Yoshiyahu by name,” when Menashe had not yet been born. And the Rabbis? Does it say “from Chizkiyahu”? It says “to the house of David”: he might be born from Chizkiyahu or from someone else.”

sections.en: Whoever Is Pristine and Free from Sins of Passion Requires Extraordinary Vigilance Regarding Anger…

p: [קיז] כָּל מִי שֶׁנָּקִי מֵחֲטָאֵי הַתַּאֲוָה, צָרִיךְ שְׁמִירָה יְתֵירָה בְּעִנְיְנֵי כַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה שֶׁהוּא עָלוּל לָהֶם,
Whoever is pristine and free from sins of passion requires extraordinary vigilance regarding anger and bloodshed to which he is susceptible;
וְכִידוּעַ דְּ"לֹא תִרְצַח" וְ"לֹא תִנְאָף" הֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים, וְהֵם יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל בָּרָע
for as is known, "You shall not murder" and "You shall not commit adultery" are two opposites, representing the right and left sides within evil
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל יָרָבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט שֶׁנִּקְרָא אֶפְרָתִי – דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו, וְשֵׁם אִמּוֹ צְרוּעָה – הַיְסוֹד שֶׁלּוֹ כַּעַס].

[and as I heard regarding Jeroboam son of Nebat who was called an Ephraimite (Efrati)—meaning he never experienced a nocturnal emission in his days, while his mother's name was Tzeruah (afflicted with tzara'at), showing his flaw lay in anger].
וְכָל זַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף הֵם שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית כַּנּוֹדָע, וּרְצִיחָה שְׁכִיחָה שָׁם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַכּוֹת (י.): בְּגִלְעָד שְׁכִיחֵי רוֹצְחִים, בִּשְׁכֶם שְׁכִיחָא רוֹצְחִים.

And all the seed of Joseph are guardians of the Covenant as is known, and murder was prevalent in their territories, as stated in Makkot 10a: in Gilead murderers were common, in Shechem murderers were common.
וּבְבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פד.) שֶׁסִּפְּרוּ מִשּׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְיָדוּעַ שׁוּפְרֵיהּ וְיוֹפִי הַתֹּאַר בְּכָל מָקוֹם הוּא עַל שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת צ"ו,
And in Bava Metzia 84a they recounted the exquisite beauty of Rabbi Yochanan, and it is known that beauty of form everywhere denotes guardianship of the Covenant as I wrote above in Section 96,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר עָלָיו דְּאָתֵי מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף,
and immediately thereafter it is stated of him that he descended from the seed of Joseph;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָעִנְיָן שֶׁאֵירַע לוֹ מֵרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
and following this comes the painful episode that occurred between him and Reish Lakish

[כְּמִנְהַג רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּגְּמָרָא בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת, מִתּוֹךְ שִׁבְחוֹ וּבִמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ שָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה קְצָת הֵיפֶךְ, כִּי תוֹרָה הִיא וְלִלְמוֹד צָרִיךְ, וּכְמוֹ כֵן גַּם בַּתַּנַּ"ךְ],

[as is the custom of our Sages in several places in the Talmud, out of a sage's praise and in the very place of his greatness you find that which appears somewhat opposite, for it is Torah and we must study it, and likewise throughout Scripture],
שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הָרִתְחָא דְּרַבָּנָן שֶׁהָיְתָה גּוֹבֶרֶת בּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לִמְחוֹל.
which arose from the righteous scholarly indignation (ritcha de-rabbanan) surging within him, such that he refused to forgive.

וְגַם גּוּף הַהַעֲנָשָׁה שֶׁהָיָה רָגִיל בָּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (קיז.) עִם רַב כַּהֲנָא, דָּבָר זֶה הוּא גַּם כֵּן לְמִי שֶׁהוּא בַּטֶּבַע כֵּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁילְהֵי שַׁבָּת (קנו.): מָר נַמֵּי עָנֵישׁ וְקָטֵיל.

And the severe penal power that Rabbi Yochanan wielded, as recorded in Bava Kamma 117a with Rav Kahana, belongs naturally to one of such temperament, as stated at the end of Shabbat 156a: "The master also punishes and slays."
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּרִתְחָא דְּרַבָּנָן הוּא טָב בְּכָל סִטְרִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קפב עַמּוּד ב) וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּתַעֲנִית (ד.) דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מְרַתְּחָא לֵיהּ,
And although scholarly indignation is praiseworthy from all angles as written in Zohar II:182b, and in Ta'anit 4a that it is the fiery Torah that boils within him,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה דְּשָׁם לֹא הִצְלִיחַ רִתְחֵיהּ, וּמַאי סְלֵיק בֵּיהּ.
nonetheless it is evident that in that instance his wrath did not succeed, and consider what tragic end came of it!
וּלְפִי שֶׁקָּרָא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ "לִסְטָאָה", דְּהַיְינוּ רוֹצֵחַ, וּלְפִי שֶׁאָסוּר לְהַזְכִּיר לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה מַעֲשָׂיו הָרִאשׁוֹנִים,
And because he called Reish Lakish a "bandit"—which denotes a killer—and because it is forbidden to remind a penitent of his past deeds (Bava Metzia 58b),
לְכָךְ הוּא גַּם כֵּן נִזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ עִנְיָן כָּזֶה עַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁחֲבֵירוֹ נֶעֱנַשׁ עַל יָדוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא מִזֶּה הַגְּרָם מִיתָה לְעַצְמוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁגָּרַם לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
therefore he too was met with this exact dynamic: through his colleague being punished on his account, and through this he brought about his own death, just as he had caused that of Reish Lakish

[וְנִרְאֶה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָצָה לִמְחוֹל, כִּי הִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁקָּרַב קִצּוֹ וְחָשַׁב דְּנִדְחֶה מִפְּנֵי גַּבְרָא, וּבְוַדַּאי רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ יִמְלוֹךְ תַּחְתָּיו, וְסָבַר חַיָּיו קוֹדְמִין, וּבָזֶה אֵין צָרִיךְ לִמְחוֹל כִּדְאַשְׁכְּחַן בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּיוֹמָא פז:,

[and it appears that the reason he refused to forgive was that he sensed his end approaching, suspecting he was being pushed aside in favor of another, since Reish Lakish would certainly preside in his place, and he held that his own life took precedence, in which case one is not obligated to forgive, as we find with Rabbi Chanina in Yoma 87b;

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: Whoever is pristine and free from sins of passion requires extraordinary vigilance regarding anger and bloodshed to which he is susceptible;

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 6:84: “Even if someone is found completely pure from his childhood—which must mean that by the nature of his birth he has no deficiency of desire—opposite it he has a deficiency in anger, for these are the two opposing inclinations in a person. This is “the flame of the turning sword,” of which the Zohar and the Tikkunim say that it turns “at times to life, at times to death.” That is, one who is entirely free of desires cannot lack a root of anger. There is, however, “the anger of the scholars,” which is good in all its aspects, as the Zohar states. Similarly, our Sages said that “Torah makes him seethe,” for “My words are like fire”; these are words of the living God, and there is life and added vitality in this. Nevertheless, one free of desires cannot escape every deficiency of anger, for otherwise he would live forever. Hashem did not desire this until the end, when death will be swallowed forever, and He created the evil inclination “to guard the way to the Tree of Life.” Moshe our teacher, the teacher of Israel, demonstrates this: he was buried opposite Peor, which alludes to desires, and he stood entirely against them. Nevertheless, our Sages said, “He too died for his sin”: saying “Listen, rebels” and striking the rock belonged to anger and indignation that did not accord with Hashem’s revealed will.”

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Deuteronomy, Shoftim 15: “As we find concerning Achiyah the Shilonite anointing Yeravam as king: Achiyah was from Shiloh, from the tribe of Yosef, and Yeravam too is described as an Ephraimite, for he was especially refined and careful concerning “You shall not commit adultery,” which is Yosef’s inheritance. Hashem then showed him that this love had been directed only toward Aviyah son of Yeravam, in whom something good was found. Therefore, from the time he anointed Yeravam until the statement that “the child died” by Hashem’s word, Achiyah is not called a prophet or a Shilonite, but simply Achiyah. In that statement it says, “According to the word of Hashem by the hand of Achiyah the Shilonite, the prophet,” for Hashem set matters right through this. Understand.”

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 84a:12-16: “One day Rabbi Yochanan was bathing in the Jordan. Reish Lakish saw him and jumped into the Jordan after him. Rabbi Yochanan said: “Your strength should be for Torah.” Reish Lakish replied: “Your beauty should be for women.” Rabbi Yochanan said: “If you repent, I shall give you my sister, who is more beautiful than I.” He accepted. He wished to return to fetch his clothes but could not return. Rabbi Yochanan taught him Scripture and Mishnah and made him a great man. One day they disagreed in the study hall: from when do a sword, knife, dagger, spear, hand sickle, and harvesting sickle become susceptible to impurity? From the completion of their manufacture. When is their manufacture complete? Rabbi Yochanan says: when one tempers them in the furnace. Reish Lakish says: when one polishes them in water. Rabbi Yochanan said to him: “A robber knows his robbery.” He replied: “What have you benefited me? There they called me master, and here they call me master!” Rabbi Yochanan said: “I benefited you by bringing you under the wings of the Divine Presence.” Rabbi Yochanan was distressed, and Reish Lakish became ill. His sister came weeping and said: “Act for the sake of my children!” He replied: “Leave your orphans; I shall keep them alive.” “Act for the sake of my widowhood!” He replied: “And let your widows trust in Me.” Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish died, and Rabbi Yochanan grieved greatly after him. The Rabbis said: “Who should go to console him? Let Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat go, for his teachings are sharp.””

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Bereshit 9: “I will make him a help meet for him. He explained the matter: for such is the will of the Creator, blessed be He, that help and support should flourish for a person from that which opposes him, namely like a disciple to his master, as we find (Bava Metzia 84a) regarding Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish facing Rabbi Yochanan, who would raise twenty-four difficulties against him and he would resolve them with twenty-four solutions, and the teaching was consequently broadened and clarified, and not like Rabbi Elazar who merely told him: 'there is a Baraita that supports you'; for through a person seeing the challenges raised against him, he then fortifies his words with further proofs and his positions emerge thoroughly to light.”

: “I will make him a help meet for him. He explained the matter: for such is the will of the Creator, blessed be He, that help and support should flourish for a person from that which opposes him, namely like a disciple to his master, as we find (Bava Metzia 84a) regarding Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish facing Rabbi Yochanan, who would raise twenty-four difficulties against him and he would resolve them with twenty-four solutions, and the teaching was consequently broadened and clarified, and not like Rabbi Elazar who merely told him: 'there is a Baraita that supports you'; for through a person seeing the challenges raised against him, he then fortifies his words with further proofs and his positions emerge thoroughly to light.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach reads Reish Lakish’s objections to Rabbi Yochanan as the model of “a help opposite him”: the challenge made the teaching clearer in a way that simple agreement could not. This supplies the positive side of Rav Tzadok’s warning about their quarrel. The person who seems to obstruct one’s Torah may be contributing precisely the scrutiny it needs, so personal anger can destroy an indispensable form of help.

sections.en: One Who Is a Torah Scholar Whose Very Casual Conversation Requires Study (Sukkah 21b)

p: [קיח] מִי שֶׁהוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ שִׂיחַת חוּלִין שֶׁלּוֹ צְרִיכָה לִמּוּד כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:),
One who is a Torah scholar whose very casual conversation requires study (Sukkah 21b),
אָז יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ גַּם בְּשִׂיחַת חוּלִין לְתַקֵּן נְפָשׁוֹת, שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
possesses the power through mundane conversation to rectify souls, for it is literally Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין נד:) שֶׁכָּל שִׂיחָתָן תּוֹרָה;
as our Sages stated (Eruvin 54b) that all of their conversation is Torah;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁתִּמְצָא בַּתּוֹרָה כַּמָּה סִפּוּרֵי מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת, וְכֵן בַּתַּלְמוּד כַּמָּה דְּבָרִים נִרְאִים כְּסִפּוּרֵי חוֹל, וְהֵם תּוֹרָה מַמָּשׁ כְּכָל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
and just as you find in the Torah numerous historical narratives, and in the Talmud many passages appearing as secular accounts which are in truth actual Torah like all sacred words.
וְכָל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ, שִׂיחַת חוּלִין שֶׁלּוֹ גְּדוֹלָה מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ,
And whoever is greater than his fellow, his casual conversation is greater than the formal Torah study of his peer,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס): יָפָה שִׂיחָתָן שֶׁל עַבְדֵי אָבוֹת מִתּוֹרָתָן שֶׁל בָּנִים
as stated in Bereishit Rabbah 60:8: "More beautiful is the casual speech of the servants of the Patriarchs than the Torah of their children"

[וְלֹא הָיְתָה מַעֲלַת אֱלִיעֶזֶר רַק מַעֲלַת אַבְרָהָם, לְכָךְ קְרָאוֹ עַבְדֵי אָבוֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא כח:): דַּמֶּשֶׂק – דּוֹלֶה וּמַשְׁקֶה מִתּוֹרַת רַבּוֹ, כִּי מַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עֶבֶד קָנָה רַבּוֹ, וְכָל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ הַכֹּל נִקְרָא תּוֹרַת רַבּוֹ].

[and this was not Eliezer's independent virtue but Abraham's, which is why they were termed 'servants of the Patriarchs,' and in Yoma 28b: Dammasek—he draws and gives drink from the Torah of his master, for what a servant acquires his master acquires, and all Torah he possessed was termed his master's Torah].
וְאָמְרוּ זֶה בְּסֻכָּה (שָׁם) בְּשִׂיחַת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּסֻכָּתוֹ,
And they stated this in Sukkah 21b concerning the conversation of Rabban Gamliel in his sukkah;
וְנִרְאֶה מִזֶּה דִּבְסֻכָּה, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵם בְּצִלָּא דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא, זוֹכִים לִהְיוֹת כֵּן;
and it appears from this that in the sukkah, because they dwell in the Shade of Faith, they merit this elevation;
וְשָׁם קְרָאוּ לְשִׂיחַת חוּלִין "עָלֵהוּ", וּמָצִינוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק.): "וְעָלֵהוּ לִתְרוּפָה" – לְהַתִּיר פֶּה עֲקָרוֹת,
and there they compared casual conversation to the leaves of the tree ("its leaf does not wither"), and we find in Sanhedrin 100a: "'and its leaf for healing'—to open the mouth of the barren,"

meaning the begetting of new souls occurs through the Torah novelties embedded within their casual conversations;

paragraphs.text: Divrei Soferim 36:1: “One whose concerns, thoughts, and reflections are all immersed in words of Torah merits that all his conversation is Torah. As it is said, “Converse”—these are the masters of Talmud, whose entire conversation is words of Torah. The masters of Talmud are those entirely immersed in Torah. Of them the Tanchuma says that there is great distress and loss of sleep, and it is compared to darkness, as it is said, “The people walking in darkness saw a great light”—these are the masters of Talmud; see there. Similarly, Sanhedrin says, “He has seated me in dark places”—this is the Babylonian Talmud. For Talmud is the examination of the depths of Torah, which is “deep; who can find it?” Rashi likewise explains that this was said because of its depth. Since one must deepen his thoughts in it, all his conversation thereby becomes words of Torah, for a person is wherever his thought is engaged and attached, as is known. “Conversation” means a light utterance that leaves his mouth without deliberate intention, as Chagigah says concerning “what is his conversation”: Rav said, even the extra conversation between husband and wife.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 7:5: “Afterward the holy Zohar (132a) says: come and see how many hidden supernal secrets there are in Torah. When David looked and knew how many wonders issue from Torah, he began, ‘Uncover my eyes, that I may behold wonders from Your Torah.’ The Zohar gives this introduction to Eliezer’s mission to bring Rivkah because it prepared the birth of Yaakov’s soul, the attribute of Torah. The principal wonder—‘wonders from Your Torah’—is that through this we merit ‘He will open our heart in His Torah.’ It says that this passage contains supernal secrets, as the Midrash says (Bereishit Rabbah 60:8), ‘The conversation of the servants of the patriarchal households is more beautiful than the Torah of their children.’ Certainly no letter in Torah is superfluous, Heaven forbid. Rather, in this passage of Eliezer’s conversation are secrets and many hidden treasures, to bring Yaakov’s soul out from the forces of Lavan and Betuel; through these words of Torah we merit the opening of the heart to Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Peri Tzadik explains why Eliezer’s ordinary account can be treated as Torah with power to draw forth a soul. His mission prepares the birth of Yaakov, the attribute of Torah, by taking Rivkah from the surrounding forces of Lavan and Betuel. Reading that narrative is then connected with the learner’s own heart opening to Torah. This develops the siman’s transition from a story to the repair and birth of souls.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Sukkot 9:1: “Returning to the matter: this is what the Zohar alludes to by “one who is from the stock and root of Israel.” That is, one who is assured that the root of his birth is in holiness dwells in the shade of faith without fear at all. He can trust and take refuge in Him through faith beyond understanding, because he is attached to the root. Therefore he need fear no evil, and he inherits freedom for himself and his children forever. Israel as a whole are called the children of Israel: they are attached by their birth to the root, in the inner point of their hearts, beyond understanding. From it joy flows to us during this festival, the season of our rejoicing, as we explained concerning “Avraham made a great feast.””

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 103a: “Therefore it is written, “Every native among Israel shall dwell in sukkot”: everyone who comes from Israel’s holy root and stock shall dwell in sukkot beneath the shade of faith. One who is not from Israel’s holy stock and root does not sit in them and removes himself from beneath the shade of faith. It is written, “Canaan, in whose hand are deceitful scales”—this is Eliezer, Avraham’s servant. Come and see: it is written, “Cursed is Canaan.” Because this Canaan merited serving Avraham, once he served him he dwelled beneath the shade of faith and merited leaving that curse. Moreover, blessing is written of him: “He said: Come, blessed of Hashem.” What does this teach? Whoever dwells beneath the shade of faith inherits freedom for himself and his children forever and is blessed with a supernal blessing. Whoever removes himself from the shade of faith inherits exile for himself and his children, as it is written, “He fought against Israel and took captives from them.””

Whoever removes himself from the shade of faith inherits exile for himself and his children, as it is written, “He fought against Israel and took captives from them.””

sections.en: All the Narratives in the Torah and the Talmud Recounting Wondrous Miracles Performed Contain…

p: [קיט] כָּל הַסִּפּוּרִים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה וּבַגְּמָרָא מִדְּבָרִים מוּפְלָאִים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ, שָׁם עַצְמוֹ יֵשׁ הַכֹּחַ לַעֲשִׂיָּה הַהוּא,
All the narratives in the Torah and the Talmud recounting wondrous miracles performed contain within themselves the active power to execute that deed,
כִּי כָּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה חַיִּים וְקַיָּימִים וְשָׁם יֵשׁ הַחַיּוּת לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר,
for all words of Torah are alive and enduring, and within them resides the vital energy for that specific occurrence;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּיקּוּנִים סוֹף תִּיקּוּן נ"ה: כִּי מִפָּסוּק "וְהַמִּכְתָּב מִכְתַּב אֱלֹהִים הוּא" יָצָא שֵׁם הַכּוֹתֵב,
as written in Tikkunei Zohar (end of Tikkun 55): from the verse "and the writing was the writing of God" (Exodus 32:16) issues the mystical Name that causes writing to appear;
וּמִפָּסוּק "ה' אֱלֹהִים נָתַן לִי לְשׁוֹן לִמּוּדִים וְגוֹמֵר" – שֵׁם הַדּוֹרֵשׁ.
and from the verse "The Lord God has given me the tongue of the learned, etc." (Isaiah 50:4) issues the Name of the preacher.
וּבְסֵפֶר עֲבוֹדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל פָּרָשַׁת חַיֵּי מִפָּסוּק "וָאָבֹא הַיּוֹם אֶל הָעָיִן", שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י: הַיּוֹם יָצָאתִי וְהַיּוֹם בָּאתִי, יוֹצֵא שֵׁם לִקְפִיצַת הָאָרֶץ.

And in Sefer Avodat Yisrael (Parashat Chayei Sarah): from the verse "And I came this day unto the fountain" (Genesis 24:42), where Rashi explains: today I departed and today I arrived, issues the Name for miraculous contraction of the road (kefitzat haderekh).
וְכֵן יָדוּעַ מִפָּסוּק שֶׁל הַכָּאַת סַנְוֵרִים יוֹצֵא שֵׁם לִפְעוֹל כֵּן.
And likewise it is known that from the verse of smiting with blindness (Genesis 19:11) issues a Name to effect the same.
וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה:): "יְהַב לֵיהּ יְדָא וְאוֹקְמֵיהּ", דְּרָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת יְ'הַב לֵ'יהּ יְ'דָא הוּא שֵׁם הַפּוֹעֵל כֵּן.
And in the words of our Sages (Berakhot 5b): "He gave him his hand and raised him up," the initial letters of Yehav Lei Yada
(י-ל-י)
form a Name that performs this healing.
וְכֵן הַרְבֵּה בְּסֵפֶר שִׁמּוּשׁ תְּהִלִּים וּשְׁאָרֵי, כִּי כָּל שֵׁם הוּא כְּמוֹ מַפְתֵּחַ לְאוֹתוֹ חֶדֶר.
And likewise many examples in Sefer Shimush Tehillim and others, for every holy Name is like a key to that specific chamber.
וְהָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁפָּעַל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר, הוּא שֶׁמָּצָא וְעָמַד עַל אוֹתוֹ מַפְתֵּחַ וּמְסָרוֹ לָרַבִּים שֶׁנָּהַג בּוֹ טוֹבַת עַיִן,
And the first master who achieved that miracle was the one who discovered that key and transmitted it to the public with a generous eye,
וְהֵם גְּנִיזִין בַּתּוֹרָה וּבִלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים, שֶׁכָּל חֶמְדִּין טָבִין גְּנִיזִין שָׁם.
and they are concealed within the Torah and the language of the Sages, wherein all precious treasures are hidden.
וְ"אִם רֵיק הוּא – מִכֶּם", לָמָּה? שֶׁאֵין אַתֶּם יְגֵיעִים וְכוּלֵי
And "if it is empty—it is from you" (Yerushalmi Peah 1:1); why? Because you do not exert yourselves
[וְכָל שֵׁמוֹת הָאֲמוּרִים לְעִנְיַן לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הוּא מִצַּד עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הָעִיקָּר הָרְמִיזוֹת בּוֹ בַּעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וְלֵב כַּנּוֹדָע]:
[and all Names mentioned regarding physical actions belong to the World of Action, but in truth the essential allusions pertain to interior service in the mind and heart, as is known].

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 27:1: “A person must know, in all his activities and deeds, that he is not the one who acts. Everything occurs through a higher power, and all his activities come from Hashem, as in “You have also performed all our deeds for us.” Without this he has no power to do anything; it is only through Hashem’s active power, drawn into him from the ten utterances of Creation. These stand living and enduring forever, supplying the powers of activity, each thing on its day, according to the activity of the things during the days of Creation.”

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar Maamarei Razal, Berakhot 5b: “I have already informed you, concerning “The ox knows its owner,” that by the name Y-L-Y, the second name of the seventy-twofold name, Moshe our teacher raised Yosef’s coffin; its reason was explained there. This name also has the property of raising a sick person from his illness. It is therefore alluded to in the initial letters of “He gave him his hand,” whose initials are Y-L-Y, and thereby “he raised him.” Therefore he should say to the sick person, “Give me your hand.” The sick person then gives his hand, and the person raising him says, “He gave him his hand and raised him,” intending the name indicated by these initial letters.”

paragraphs.text: Sha'arei Orah, Introduction 8-10: “The true boundary and the tradition of the covenant are these: one who wishes to attain his needs through the names of the Holy One, blessed be He, should exert all his strength in Torah to understand the meaning of each of the holy names mentioned in Torah, such as Ehyeh, Yah, the four-letter name, Adonai, El, Eloah, Elohim, Shaddai, and Tzevaot. A person should know and understand that each of these names is like a key to every matter that a person needs in any respect in the world. When he contemplates these names, he will find all Torah and mitzvot dependent upon them. When he knows the meaning of each name, he will recognize the greatness of the One who spoke and the world came into being. He will fear and revere Him, and long, yearn, and desire to cleave to Him through knowing His names. Then he will be close to Hashem and his prayer will be accepted. Concerning this it is said, “I shall raise him high because he knows My name; he will call to Me and I shall answer him.” Scripture does not say, “because he mentions My name,” but “because he knows My name.” Knowledge is the essential thing, followed by “he will call to Me and I shall answer him”: when he needs something and directs his intention toward the name upon which that need depends, then “I shall answer him.””

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 38a:4-6: “Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Chanina said: Torah was given only to Moshe and his descendants, as it is said, “Write for yourself” and “Carve for yourself”: just as the discarded stone is yours, so the writing is yours. Moshe acted generously with it and gave it to Israel. Of him Scripture says, “One with a generous eye shall be blessed.” Rav Chisda objected: “Hashem commanded me at that time to teach you”! He commanded me, and I taught you. “See, I have taught you statutes and laws as Hashem my God commanded me”! He commanded me, and I taught you. “Now write this song for yourselves”! sections.en: One Who Brings Merit to the Guilty Cannot Avoid Having Some Slight Trace Cling…

p: [קכ] מִי שֶׁמְּזַכֶּה לְחַיָּיבַיָּא, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִדְבַּק בּוֹ מְאוּמָה.
One who brings merit to the guilty cannot avoid having some slight trace cling to him.
וְכִידוּעַ הַמָּשָׁל עַל זֶה מִמִּי שֶׁגּוֹרֵף בִּיבִין
And known is the parable of one who cleans out sewers
[וּבָזֶה יוּבַן צַחוּת לְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וָאֵרָא): נוֹחַ הָיָה לִשְׁלֹמֹה לִהְיוֹת גּוֹרֵף בִּיבִין וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
[and through this one understands the phrasing in Shemot Rabbah (beginning of Va'era): "Better had it been for Solomon to clean sewers, etc.,"
[אֲבָל בַּגְּמָרָא דְּשַׁבָּת נ"ו עַמּוּד ב' אִיתָא שַׁמָּשׁ לְדָבָר אַחֵר, וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
[but in the Gemara, Shabbat 56b, it reads "an attendant to 'something else'" (that is, to idolatry); it is all one, and this is not the place to elaborate],
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא לֹא רָצָה לְהוֹכִיחָן וְלִהְיוֹת גּוֹרֵף בִּיבִין שֶׁלֹּא יִדְבַּק בּוֹ מְאוּמָה,
meaning that Solomon did not wish to rebuke them and clean out sewers lest anything cling to him;
וּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ לִמְחוֹת וְכוּלֵי, וְנִדְבַּק בּוֹ הַכֹּל].
but in truth, whoever has the power to protest and does not, bears the guilt, and all clung to him].
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לִרְאִיַּת קֶרִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קכז:) בְּאוֹתוֹ חָסִיד מִפְּנֵי טֹרַח הַדֶּרֶךְ לִפְדּוֹת אוֹתָהּ רִיבָה,
And through this he came to experience a nocturnal emission, as stated in Shabbat 127b regarding that pious man who toiled on the road to redeem that captive maiden,
דְּאִיתָא בְּאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן (פֶּרֶק ח) שֶׁהִטְבִּיל לָרִיבָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָכְלָה אִיסּוּרִים, וְהָיָה מְזַכֶּה לְחַיָּיבַיָּא;
for it is stated in Avot DeRabbi Natan (chapter 8) that he immersed the maiden because she had eaten forbidden foods, thus bringing merit to the guilty;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֱלִישָׁע, שֶׁאָמְרוּ עָלָיו סַנְהֶדְרִין (קז:) שֶׁהָיָה מַדְחֶה בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדַיִם, נֶאֱמַר עָלָיו בִּבְרָכוֹת (י:) שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו.
unlike Elisha, concerning whom they said in Sanhedrin 107b that he pushed away Gehazi with both hands, regarding whom it is stated in Berakhot 10b that he never saw a seminal emission in his days.
וְאָמְרוּ שָׁם בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין דְּאֵין לִהְיוֹת כֶּאֱלִישָׁע, רַק הַקֵּירוּב יוֹתֵר בְּחֹזֶק מִן הַדִּחוּי, שֶׁהוּא בַּיָּמִין.
And they said there in Sanhedrin that one should not act like Elisha, but drawing near must be stronger than pushing away, operating with the right hand.
וְאָמְרוּ תֵּיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ שָׁם דְּגַם הַיֵּצֶר כֵּן יִהְיֶה: שְׂמֹאל דּוֹחָה וְיָמִין מְקָרֶבֶת,
And immediately afterward they said there that with the inclination it should be likewise: the left pushes away and the right draws close,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בֶּאֱלִישָׁע הָיָה גַּם יָמִין דּוֹחָה.
whereas with Elisha the right pushed away as well.
וְאַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ט): "טוֹב מְאֹד" – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע,
And even though they said in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 9): "'Very good'—this is the evil inclination,"
יָדוּעַ דְּהַכֹּל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם, וְיֵשׁ מִדָּתוֹ לְאַכְפַּיָּא וְלִהְיוֹת דּוֹחֶה לְגַמְרֵי, וְיֵשׁ מִדָּתוֹ לְאַהְפָּכָא:

it is known that all depends on each person's unique spiritual path: there is one whose task is to suppress (le-akpaya) and reject completely, and there is one whose task is to transform (le-ahpakha).

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 57:1: “As long as the community of Israel is whole—that is, their intention in joining with the nations is solely for the sake of Heaven, to bring out the holy sparks within them, so that the thighs remain joined to the body—then although “the wicked watches for the righteous,” “Hashem will not abandon him into his hand.” Yet it is indeed said, “Because you joined with Achazyahu…” Although his intention at the outset was for the sake of Heaven, one who deals with something filthy becomes soiled, like someone who cleans sewers, whose body cannot avoid becoming dirty with mud and excrement. This requires great vigilance and strength, so as not to allow any filth to adhere to him, and not everyone merits it.”

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 6:1: “Of Shlomo, who contemplated nullifying a letter of Torah, what is written? “The words of Agur son of Yakeh”: he gathered words of Torah and then cast them up. “The utterance of the man to Itiel”: this command of the Holy One, blessed be He, “He shall not multiply wives,” was given only because “his heart shall not turn away.” “To Itiel”: he said, “God is with me, and I am able.” What is written of him? “When Shlomo grew old, his wives turned his heart.” Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: It would have been better for Shlomo to clean sewers than to have this verse written about him. Therefore Shlomo said of himself, “I turned to consider wisdom and knowledge, madness and folly.” Shlomo said: What I thought was being wiser than the words of Torah, imagining that I understood Torah’s reasoning—that understanding and that knowledge were madness and folly.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Dover Tzedek interprets the two hands as a coordinated response rather than competing alternatives: the right draws near so that the left can effectively restrain. Its image of a little leaven being beneficial helps explain why Rav Tzadok distinguishes complete subduing from transformation and relates the appropriate response to the person’s level. The source does not dispense with the need for restraint.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 27:8-10: “There are two kinds of gratification before Him, blessed be He, on high. One comes from the complete elimination of the other side and the transformation of bitterness into sweetness and darkness into light, through the righteous. The second comes when the other side is subdued while it is still strong and powerful, raising itself like an eagle, and from there the Lord brings it down through the awakening from below brought about by the intermediate person. This is what Scripture says, “Make me delicacies, such as I love.” “Delicacies” is plural: two kinds of gratification. It is the Shekhinah speaking to her children, the collective Israel, as explained in the Tikkunim. By analogy, among physical delicacies there are two kinds: one consists of pleasant, sweet foods; the other of pungent or sour things that have been seasoned and prepared so well that they become delicacies that restore the soul. sections.en: Throughout the Entire Torah the Sin of Emitting Seed in Vain Is Not Explicitly…

p: [קכא] בְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ לֹא נִזְכַּר בְּפֵירוּשׁ עָוֹן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, רַק נִזְכַּר שֶׁנֶּעֶנְשׁוּ דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל וְעֵר וְאוֹנָן

Throughout the entire Torah the sin of emitting seed in vain is not explicitly stated as a direct commandment, but it is merely recorded that the Generation of the Flood, and Er and Onan, were punished for it
[וְיָדוּעַ דְּעֵר הוּא נִיצוֹץ מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁיָּרַד פַּעַם רִאשׁוֹן לָעוֹלָם וּבָא לְתַקֵּן עָוֹן דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, עַיֵּין מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"ט וְקי"א],
[and it is known that Er was a spark of the Messiah who descended for the first time into the world to rectify the sin of the Generation of the Flood; see what I wrote above in Sections 109 and 111],

כִּי לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לִכְתּוֹב הָאִיסּוּר בְּפֵירוּשׁ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִסַּד בְּטֶבַע הָעוֹלָם שֶׁיֶּאֱרַע זֶה גַּם כֵּן לָאָדָם בְּאֹנֶס, וְיִהְיֶה צְעָקָה גְּדוֹלָה: עַל מֶה עָשָׂה ה' כָּכָה לָנוּ לְהַכְשִׁילֵנוּ.

for it was impossible to write the prohibition explicitly, seeing that the Blessed Name established in the nature of the world that this also occurs to a person involuntarily, which would have prompted an outcry: "Why has Hashem done this to us to cause us to stumble?"
רַק הִנִּיחָה תּוֹרָה דָּבָר זֶה לִלְמוֹד דָּבָר זֶה מִמִּצְוֹת בְּנֵי נֹחַ דְּ"וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ", כְּמוֹ דְּמִיעֲטֵיהּ אֵשֶׁת חֲבֵירוֹ, הָכָא נַמֵּי כָּל שֶׁלֹּא בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ.

Rather, the Torah left this to be derived from the Noahide commandment "and he shall cleave unto his wife" (Genesis 2:24): just as this excludes the wife of his fellow, so too it excludes any discharge not within his wife.

וְכָל מִצְווֹת בְּנֵי נֹחַ הוּא מִכְּלַל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדְמוּ לַתּוֹרָה, וְכֵן דָּבָר זֶה גַּם כֵּן מִדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, דְּיֵשׁ לֵידַע מֵעַצְמוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן, וְכָל הַבַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵין עוֹשִׂים כֵּן וְאֵין לָצֵאת מִיִּשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם

And all Noahide laws are part of natural decency (derekh eretz) that preceded the Torah, and likewise this matter is part of derekh eretz, for one should understand intuitively that it violates decency to act thus, as no animals act thus, and one should not depart from the civilized order
[וּבָזֶה יוּבַן מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק מִי שֶׁמֵּתוּ (בְּרָכוֹת כב.) דְּבַעַל קֶרִי שׁוֹנֶה בְּהִלְכוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
[and through this one understands Berakhot 22a, that one who experienced an emission may study the laws of derekh eretz, and this is not the place to elaborate].
וְהִנֵּה דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ קָדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה, וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק א נִקְרָא דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ "דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים" עַיֵּין שָׁם
And behold, derekh eretz preceded the Torah, and in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 1) derekh eretz is called "the way to the Tree of Life," see there
[וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "פְּרִי צַדִּיק" דַּיְיקָא "עֵץ חַיִּים"]
[and therefore 'the fruit of the righteous' specifically is called 'a tree of life'].
וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ.
And one who lacks derekh eretz cannot reach it [the Tree of Life].
(מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ) אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שָׂם שׁוֹמְרִים לִשְׁמוֹר

(From his holy handwriting.) [This passage was cut from the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902) without notice. It is restored here from R' Michael Mokotowski's copy of the author's manuscript, first printed in Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMalei (Jerusalem, 1968).] But Hashem, blessed be He, has set guards to keep watch
שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעוּ בֶּאֱמֶת לָזֶה עַד בִּיאַת מָשִׁיחַ,
so that they not truly attain this until the coming of the Messiah,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ "חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לּוֹ".
of whom it is said: "He asked life of You; You gave it to him" (Psalms 21:5).
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דְּתֵיכֶף אַחַר חֵטְא דְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
And as is known, immediately after the sin of Adam, the first man,
הִתְחִילוּ הַטִּיפֵּי קֶרִי דַּחֲזָא לְאוֹנְסוֹ לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ,
the drops of emission that came upon him involuntarily began to issue from him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל.
as the Ari of blessed memory wrote.
וּמִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו,
And one who has never seen an emission in his life—
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הָוֵי יָמִין דּוֹחָה לַיֵּצֶר,
perforce the right hand is pushing the inclination away,
וְגַם זֶה אֵינוֹ מִיִּשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם,
and this too is not in keeping with the settlement of the world,

paragraphs.text: Ordinary decent conduct can disclose a Torah inheritance before formal learning is visible.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Simchat Torah 39:2: “Since Torah was apportioned to the whole congregation of Yaakov, even the lowest soul, a true Torah scholar must recognize from the garment of derekh eretz he sees in an unlearned person the precious depth of the Torah point within him. This is why the man seized Rabbi Yannai and said, ‘My inheritance is with you’: it is not written ‘the congregation of Yannai,’ but ‘the congregation of Yaakov.’ Hashem apportioned Torah to all the souls of Israel, so that even the lowest soul of Israel is not completely devoid of Torah, Heaven forbid. In the Torah point within each one, he is distinguished and elevated above all Israel. Thus the man seized Rabbi Yannai and said, ‘My inheritance is with you.’ That is: although I myself do not recognize the words of Torah in the depth of my heart because I am unlearned, you, Rabbi Yannai, are a Torah scholar. You should have discerned from my derekh eretz the precious Torah point within me from which all that conduct branches. These true words awakened Rabbi Yannai; he immediately acknowledged them, regretted his act, and said, ‘You have all this derekh eretz, and I called you a dog.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim explains why derekh eretz can stand before Torah without being detached from it. In the story of Rabbi Yannai, the guest's conduct expresses a Torah point he cannot yet identify through formal learning. The scholar is challenged to recognize it. This develops the siman's image of a path toward the tree of life: preparation can already carry the inward relation to what it prepares one to receive.

sections.en: We Establish in Shabbat 71a That a Sin-offering Brought to Atone for a Sin…

p: [קכב] קַיְימָא לַן בְּשַׁבָּת (עא.) שֶׁהַחַטָּאת הַבָּא לְכַפֵּר הַחֵטְא גּוֹרֵר אוֹתוֹ חֵטְא גַּם פַּעַם אַחֵר שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם.
We establish in Shabbat 71a that a sin-offering brought to atone for a sin drags along and atones for that same sin performed another time, see there.
וְנִלְמַד גַּם כֵּן מִזֶּה בִּתְשׁוּבָה, שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְכַפָּרָה נִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ גַּם פְּעָמִים אֲחֵרִים שֶׁעָשָׂה דָּבָר זֶה, כִּי חֵטְא גּוֹרֵר חֵטְא.
And we likewise learn from this regarding repentance: when one merits atonement, other instances in which he committed that same act are also forgiven, for one sin drags along another.
וְשָׁם אִיתָא בְּלֹא יוֹדֵעַ דְּחַיָּיב אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְכַּפֵּר בְּחַטָּאת עַל זֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן (פֶּרֶק ל),

And there it is stated that if he does not know, he is liable for a provisional guilt-offering (asham talui), meaning he cannot attain atonement through a sin-offering, as in Avot DeRabbi Natan (chapter 30);

וְנִזְכַּר הָעִנְיָן גַּם כֵּן בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת, כִּי הֶחְמִירָה תּוֹרָה בְּסָפֵק דְּאָשָׁם תָּלוּי חָמִיר מֵחַטָּאת, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה הַטַּעַם: כִּי הַיְּדִיעָה שֶׁנּוֹדַע לוֹ מְכַפֶּרֶת מִקְצָת מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא מִתְחָרֵט, עַיֵּין שָׁם.

and this concept is also cited by Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah in the first chapter of Berakhot, for the Torah was more stringent regarding doubt—an asham talui being more demanding than a chatat—the reason being that the definite knowledge of the sin provides partial atonement because through it he experiences genuine remorse, see there.
וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכֵי בִּגְרִירָה נִתְכַּפְּרָה, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְכָל כַּפָּרַת חֲטָאִים בִּתְשׁוּבָה.
And even so, through the principle of dragging (grirah) it is atoned, and the same applies to all atonement of sins through repentance.

וּלְכָךְ הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב), אִם שָׁב עַל עֲוֹן קֶרִי וּמִתְכַּפֵּר וּמוֹצִיא אוֹתָן טִפִּין הָעֲשׁוּקִים, מִמֵּילָא בִּגְרִירָה מוֹצִיא גַּם כֵּן טִפֵּי דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה בְּהָקִיץ.

Therefore, regarding emitting seed in vain where ordinary repentance does not avail (Zohar I:219b): if one repents over an involuntary emission and is forgiven, extracting those oppressed captive sparks, automatically by dragging he likewise redeems the drops emitted willfully while awake.
וְעַל כָּךְ גַּם כֵּן יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִנְיַן הַקֶּרִי בַּטֶּבַע, כִּי הוּא "חֹשֵׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת לְבִלְתִּי יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יד, יד), וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְתוּקַּן;

And for this reason too the Blessed Name established the phenomenon of nocturnal emission in nature, for "He devises means that the banished not be cast out from Him" (II Samuel 14:14), and through this it is rectified;
וּמִי שֶׁחָטָא בְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִקְרִים כְּדֵי לָשׁוּב עֲלֵיהֶם
and for one who sinned through wasting seed, the Blessed Name orchestrates nocturnal occurrences so that he may repent over them

[וְזֶה סוֹד גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא פו:): עָבַר וְשָׁנָה הֻתְּרָה לוֹ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ? אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵי. וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁשָּׁב עַל הַהֶיתֵּרִים דְּאַחַר כָּךְ, מִמֵּילָא נִתְכַּפְּרוּ הָרִאשׁוֹנִים, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ],

[and this is also the secret of Yoma 86b: 'If one transgressed and repeated it, it became permitted to him—could you think so? Rather, it seems to him as permitted'; and through repenting over those later instances that appeared permitted, the earlier willful ones are automatically forgiven, and this is not the place to lengthen].
וְאַף מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא בְּזָדוֹן בְּהָקִיץ, הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַזְמִין לוֹ בְּאֹנֶס גָּמוּר לְתַקֵּן אוֹתוֹ הַבָּא עַל יְדֵי הִרְהוּר בַּיּוֹם,
And even for one who never sinned willfully while awake, the Holy One brings upon him an entirely involuntary occurrence in order to rectify any stray unchaste thought by day,
וְכֵן לְתַקֵּן אֲחֵרִים הַחוֹטְאִים, דִּיחִיד שֶׁשָּׁב מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ וּלְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם):
and likewise to rectify other sinners, for when a single individual repents, forgiveness is granted to him and to the entire world (Yoma 86b).

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 21:1: “This was the meaning of the scapegoat, which the Zohar describes as a collective asham talui. An asham talui comes for what is not known, to protect the person from suffering until he knows and brings a sin offering. Likewise, acts that can be clarified only from Hashem's side, because their repair is wholly outside human understanding, require an asham talui; this was the scapegoat. It therefore had to remain alive until the blood of its fellow was applied. As long as it was possible to clarify from it actions that could be included in the goat whose lot was for Hashem, transforming deliberate sins into merits, they did not send it away. They delayed sending it into the wilderness until no more could be gathered from it and turned into merits through service. Then they sent it to Azazel, into the wilderness.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim gives a conceptual account of the uncertainty that Rav Tzadok mentions through the asham talui. Some actions can still be clarified through human service; other matters remain beyond a person's present understanding. The scapegoat waits while the first kind of work is still possible. This clarifies why lack of knowledge need not mean abandonment of repair, while keeping this explanation distinct from the siman's particular inference about one atonement drawing others with it.

Rav Tzadok takes the severity of this statement seriously and then explains the exceptional depth of repair through which even this failure can be addressed. He no longer feels distant from it, as though he were not commanded concerning it at all, and has “bread in his basket.” Through this, perhaps the desire will not intensify so much, and it will become possible for him not to stumble over that matter again. paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 159:1: “When one individual repents, he and the whole world are forgiven, as our Sages teach in Yoma 86b. How is forgiveness possible? Only because he also awakens thoughts of repentance in their hearts. Not everyone who wishes to make himself that individual can do so, for this has not yet occurred; only Mashiach son of David will be such a person. His soul must include all souls, for otherwise his thoughts of repentance cannot give rise to thoughts of repentance in those whose souls have no connection with his. His thoughts of repentance must also encompass every part of his soul. One who encompasses the whole world possesses all the kinds of powers found in the whole world; if he repents in only one power, he awakens repentance only in those connected with that power.”

sections.en: And Through the Study of Torah with Diligent, Exhausting Toil

p: [קכג] וְעַל יְדֵי לִמּוּד תּוֹרָה בִּיגִיעָה נִתְקָן עָוֹן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
And through the study of Torah with diligent, exhausting toil, the sin of emitting seed in vain is rectified,
כִּי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּנִדָּה (יג.) דְּחַיָּיב מִיתָה;
for our Sages of blessed memory stated in Niddah 13a that one who does so is liable to the death penalty;
וּבְוַדַּאי כָּל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים לְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת וּלְהַמְשִׁיךְ טוֹבָה וְחַיִּים לָעוֹלָם.
and certainly all words of the Sages are intended to arouse mercy upon created beings and to draw down goodness and life unto the world.
וְכַוָּנָתָם בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאָמְרוּ חִיּוּב עוֹנֶשׁ עַל הָאָדָם, הַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּעוֹנֶשׁ זֶה מִתְכַּפֵּר,
And their underlying intent in any place where they articulated a liability of punishment upon a person is that through this very punishment he attains atonement,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מז:) בְּחַיָּיבֵי מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין דְּמִיתָתָם כַּפָּרָתָם;
as stated in Sanhedrin 47b regarding those liable to court-imposed capital execution, that their death constitutes their atonement;
כִּי רָאוּ שֶׁקָּשֶׁה לִמְצוֹא כַּפָּרָה [וּכְמוֹ בְּעָוֹן זֶה רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן],
for the Sages recognized that it was exceedingly difficult to find atonement [as with this sin, may the Merciful One preserve us],
וּמָצְאוּ לוֹ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁמְּחַיֵּיב עוֹנֶשׁ כָּךְ,
and they discovered for it a scriptural verse from the Torah mandating such a penalty,
וּמִמֵּילָא עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁבְּעוֹנֶשׁ זֶה מִתְכַּפֵּר, כִּי אִם לֹא כֵן לָמָּה יֵעָנֵשׁ,
and consequently perforce through this punishment he is atoned, for were it not so, why should he be punished?
כַּנּוֹדָע שֶׁהָעוֹנֶשׁ הוּא כְּדֵי לְהִתְכַּפֵּר.
seeing that retribution exists entirely in order to achieve spiritual purification and atonement.

וּלְכָךְ פְּעָמִים נִגְזַר עַל הָאָדָם בִּשְׁבִיל הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ בָּנִים וְכַיּוֹצֵא, שֶׁהוּא מֵאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּקְרָא מִיתָה בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ה.).

And therefore it is sometimes decreed upon a person on account of wasted seed that he have no children, or the like, which is one of the four conditions termed "death" in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (5a).

וְעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁמֵּמִית עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן מִיתָה כִּדְרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת סג:) עַל פָּסוּק "אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל",

And through words of Torah, wherein a person slays himself over words of Torah—which is likewise termed death, as our Sages expounded (Berakhot 63b) on the verse "when a man dies in a tent" (Numbers 19:14)—
וְאָז נִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ בָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן דּוּגְמַת מִיתָה
he is thereby atoned through this form of spiritual death
[וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (תָּמִיד לב.): מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְיִחְיֶה? יָמִית עַצְמוֹ].
[and therefore they stated in Tamid 32a: "What shall a man do to live? Let him slay himself"].
וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "עֵץ הַחַיִּים" כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה),
And words of Torah are designated as the "Tree of Life," as our Sages stated (beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah),
וּמִיתָה נִקְרָא "דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אָנֹכִי הֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ כָּל הָאָרֶץ" (מְלָכִים א ב, ב);
and physical death is termed the "way of the earth" (derekh eretz), as written: "I go the way of all the earth" (I Kings 2:2);
וּלְכָךְ מִיתָה הוּא דֶּרֶךְ לְהַגִּיעַ לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הוּא דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת קכ"א.
and therefore death serves as the path to attain eternal life, for derekh eretz is the path leading unto the Tree of Life, as I wrote above in Section 121.
וְכֵן מִי שֶׁמֵּמִית עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, זֶהוּ הַדֶּרֶךְ לְעֵץ הַחַיִּים דְּהַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּמְתַקֵּן בָּזֶה מַה שֶּׁפָּגַם בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
And likewise, one who slays himself over words of Torah follows the path to the Tree of Life—namely Torah—and rectifies through this that which he blemished in the realm of derekh eretz
[וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ב): טוֹב תּוֹרָה עִם דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
[and our Sages stated (Avot 2:2): "Excellent is Torah study combined with derekh eretz,"
וּבִבְרָכוֹת (לה:): הַנְהֵג בָּהֶן מִנְהַג דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְכוּלֵי, וְאִם לָאו אֵין מִתְקַיֵּים;
and in Berakhot 35b: "Conduct yourself with them in the manner of derekh eretz, etc., for if not, it will not endure";
אַךְ הָעֵצָה עַל זֶה: לְהָמִית עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
yet the sublime counsel for this is to slay oneself over words of Torah.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא נָהַג בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ בִּפְרִישׁוּת מִן הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁגַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not conduct himself according to standard derekh eretz regarding marital intimacy, which is likewise termed derekh eretz,
וּלְכָךְ דִּבְּרוּ עָלָיו לָשׁוֹן הָרָע עַל זֶה שֶׁחֲשָׁבוּהוּ לִמְבַטֵּל מִצְוָה, כֵּיוָן דְּאִשְׁתּוֹ לֹא מָחֲלָה;
and therefore Aaron and Miriam spoke against him on this account, considering him to have neglected a mitzvah since his wife had not explicitly waived her marital rights;
וּבְוַדַּאי כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה, יֵשׁ מַמָּשׁ בְּדִבּוּרָם גַּם כֵּן.
and certainly, since it was recorded in the Torah, their words contained some substance as well.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם נֶעֶנְשׁוּ וְנֶאֱמַר: "אֲשֶׁר נוֹאַלְנוּ וַאֲשֶׁר חָטָאנוּ", דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הִסְכִּים עַל יָדוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שַׁבָּת פז.),

However, they were nonetheless punished, Aaron declaring: "wherein we have done foolishly, and wherein we have sinned" (Numbers 12:11), because the Holy One, blessed be He, retroactively consented with Moses's choice (Shabbat 87a),
וְהוּא כְּעֵין עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ דְּהִיא גְּדוֹלָה גַּם כֵּן.
and it functioned like a transgression performed purely for Heaven's sake (aveirah lishmah), which is likewise immensely great.
וְחָשֵׁיב שָׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים, וְדִמָּה זֶה לִשְׁבִירַת לוּחוֹת דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ.
And the Talmud enumerates there three things Moses did on his own initiative, comparing his marital separation to the breaking of the Tablets, which was likewise an aveirah lishmah.
וְלִפְעָמִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל גַּם כֵּן לְתַקֵּן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "רְאֵה חַיִּים עִם אִשָּׁה", וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:
And sometimes through this one can likewise rectify, as written: "Enjoy life with the wife whom you love" (Ecclesiastes 9:9), and this is not the place to elaborate].

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Yisrael Kedoshim 8:15: “Afterward comes the portion of Parah, to purify the impure through an awakening of holiness from the person's own side and effort. Through this, the impurity of death is purified by the dew of Torah that gives him life (Ketubot 111b), through his “putting himself to death” over words of Torah. For it is written, ‘A person who dies in a tent’ (Numbers 19:14; Berakhot 63b; Shabbat 83b), and Scripture compares tents to streams (Numbers 24:6; Berakhot 16a), which likewise raise a person from impurity to purity.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim places the figurative dying in Torah within an expressly life-giving sequence. Personal effort in Torah is described as the dew that revives and the water that purifies. This supplies the positive mechanism of the siman’s image: the exertion of study becomes the path to renewed life and purity.

For it is written, “Blessed above women shall be Yael, wife of Chever the Kenite; above women in the tent shall she be blessed.” Who are the women in the tent? Sarah, Rivkah, Rachel, and Leah.”

sections.en: The Prohibition Against Emitting Seed in Vain Is Subsumed within the Positive Commandment Of…

p: [קכד] אִיסּוּר דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה הוּא בִּכְלַל מִצְוָה דִּפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה,
The prohibition against emitting seed in vain is subsumed within the positive commandment of procreation (peru u'revu),
כַּנִּרְאֶה מִדִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹסָפוֹת סַנְהֶדְרִין (נט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּחִדּוּשַׁי;
as is evident from the words of Tosafot in Sanhedrin 59b and as I wrote in my novellae;
וְלָכֵן עַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה בְּכַוָּנָה הָרְאוּיָה לְשֵׁם ה', יוּכַל גַּם כֵּן לְתַקֵּן מַה שֶּׁחָטָא בְּאִיסּוּר זֶה וְלִקְלוֹט אוֹתָן טִפִּין לִקְדוּשָׁה,

and therefore through the mitzvah of procreation fulfilled with holy intention for the sake of Hashem, one can likewise rectify that wherein he sinned regarding this prohibition, drawing those captive drops back into holiness,
כִּי כָּל לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה – הָעֲשֵׂה הוּא תִּיקּוּן הַלָּאו.
for in every negative prohibition derived implicitly from a positive commandment, the positive performance serves as the rectification of the prohibition.
וְגַם בְּלָאו הָכִי אָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כא): כִּי בָּאֵבֶר שֶׁעָשָׂה בּוֹ חֲבִילוֹת עֲבֵירוֹת – יַעֲשֶׂה בּוֹ חֲבִילוֹת שֶׁל מִצְווֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
And even without this, they stated in Vayikra Rabbah (21:5): with the very limb wherewith one performed bundles of transgressions, let him perform bundles of mitzvot, see there;
וְכֵן כָּאן, בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר חֲבִילוֹת מִצְווֹת הַיְינוּ פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וּמִצְוַת עוֹנָה
and so here, with that same physical organ the "bundles of mitzvot" are procreation and marital intimacy
[וּמִיהוּ יֵשׁ לוֹמַר נַמֵּי "יָשַׁב וְלֹא עָבַר עֲבֵירָה" כִּדְרַב חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפָּא שֶׁנִּזְדַּמְּנָה לְיָדוֹ, מִקְרֵי גַּם כֵּן מִצְוָה כִּדְאִיתָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (לט:)].

[though one may also say that passive restraint—"he sat and did not commit a sin" when an opportunity presented itself, like Rav Chanina bar Pappa—is likewise credited as a mitzvah, as brought in Kiddushin 39b].
וְאֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר חֲבִילוֹת בְּרִבּוּי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה,
And "bundles" does not mean excessive physical frequency,
דְּעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב.): שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מְצוּיִין וְכוּלֵי, וְאָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת: "אַל תַּרְבֶּה שִׂיחָה" כַּנּוֹדָע;

for regarding this they taught in Berakhot 22a: so that Torah scholars should not be constantly engaged in marital intimacy like roosters, and in Avot: "Do not converse excessively with a woman," as is known;
רַק אֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בְּכַמּוּת אֶלָּא בְּאֵיכוּת, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה,
rather "bundles" refers not to quantity but to spiritual quality: that it be conducted in profound holiness and purity,
דִּבְלָאו הָכִי מִקְרֵי בְּעִילַת זְנוּת וּכִבְהֵמוֹת כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים.
for otherwise it is considered an act of licentiousness and animalistic behavior, as stated repeatedly in the Zohar.
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בִּקְדוּשָׁה כְּפִי אֶפְשָׁרוּת הָאָדָם
Only when it is carried out in holiness according to human capacity

[דְּאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא, וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "בֶּעָווֹן מָלֵא" – דַּאֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ)],

[for the Holy One does not act tyrannically, and our Sages noted: "in total iniquity"—meaning even the most pious of the pious cannot entirely avoid some subtle base element (Midrash Rabbah, Tazria 14:5)],
אָז "ה' צִלְּךָ", גַּם כֵּן דּוּגְמָתוֹ שׁוֹפֵעַ לָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
then "Hashem is your shadow" (Psalms 121:5): a corresponding holy influx is poured out unto the Supernal Earth (Malchut),
אֲשֶׁר הָיְתָה חֲרֵיבָה וִיבֵשָׁה עַל יְדֵי חֲטָאָיו כַּנּוֹדָע כִּדְאִיתָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים, וְנִתְקַן הַכֹּל.
which had been made barren and parched through his past sins, as brought in the Tikkunim, and everything is healed.
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁיּוֹרְדִים טִפֵּי גְּשָׁמִים מִלְּמַעְלָה עַל הָאָרֶץ, הִיא נוֹתֶנֶת יְבוּלָהּ,
And through the descent of supernal rain-drops from Above upon the Earth, she yields her produce,
שֶׁהִיא רוּחַ קְדוּשָׁה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם תַּחַת רוּחַ הַטֻּמְאָה שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ מִקּוֹדֶם,
which is a spirit of holiness within the human heart replacing the spirit of impurity that resided there previously,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאוֹתוֹ מִזְמוֹר: "וְרוּחַ קָדְשְׁךָ אַל תִּקַּח מִמֶּנִּי, הָשִׁיבָה לִּי וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, יג–יד):
as King David, peace be upon him, pleaded in that psalm: "and take not Your holy spirit from me; restore unto me the joy of Your salvation, etc." (Psalms 51:13–14).

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Et HaOchel 10:1: “The mitzvah of eating matzah gives holiness to eating. Every mitzvah, particularly one over which we bless ‘Who sanctified us through His commandments and commanded us,’ adds holiness to a person, especially to the organ and power through which it is performed. As the Sages said in Vayikra Rabbah (21:5): ‘If you have made bundles of transgressions, make corresponding bundles of mitzvot,’ continuing with the example of the hands and the other faculties.”

sections.en: Giving Charity to the Poor Is Likewise Effective to Rectify the Sin of Wasted…

p: [קכה] צְדָקָה לַעֲנִיִּים גַּם כֵּן מוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן עָוֹן הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
Giving charity to the poor is likewise effective to rectify the sin of wasted seed,

וּבִכְלָל לְכָל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה חַיָּיב מִיתָה מוֹעִיל צְדָקָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב דְּ"תַּצִּיל מִמָּוֶת" (מִשְׁלֵי י, ב), וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יא.).
and generally for anything regarding which our Sages said one is liable to death, charity avails, as written: "and righteousness delivers from death" (Proverbs 10:2; Bava Batra 11a).

וּלְעָוֹן זֶה בְּיִחוּד, דְּעַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּחַיֶּה נְפָשׁוֹת, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שָׁם: כָּל הַמְּקַיֵּים נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כְּאִלּוּ קִיֵּים עוֹלָם מָלֵא, וּבִכְלַל הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת עֲשׁוּקוֹת – מֵחַיִּים מַמָּשׁ.

And for this sin in particular: because through sustaining living souls—our Sages stating there that whoever preserves a single Jewish soul is as though he preserved an entire world—he literally sustains from death the entire universe, including those captive, oppressed souls.
וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְעָנִי הָגוּן, דִּבְלָאו הָכִי אֵין מוֹעִיל,
Provided that the charity is given to a worthy, upright poor person, for otherwise it does not avail,
דְּהוּא קְצָת מֵעֵין דּוּגְמָא דְּחֶטְאוֹ שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ חַיִּים לְמִי שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי,
as giving to an unworthy recipient somewhat mirrors the nature of his original sin, channeling life unto that which is undeserving;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיִרְמְיָה שֶׁקִּלֵּל לְאַנְשֵׁי עֲנָתוֹת: "וְיִהְיוּ מֻכְשָׁלִים לְפָנֶיךָ, בְּעֵת אַפְּךָ עֲשֵׂה בָהֶם" (יִרְמְיָה יח, כג) – הַכְשִׁילֵם בִּבְנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאֵינָם מְהֻגָּנִים, כִּדְאִיתָא סוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא קַמָּא (טז:).

and as written concerning Jeremiah who cursed the men of Anathoth: "and let them be overthrown before You; deal with them in the time of Your anger" (Jeremiah 18:23)—cause them to stumble through unworthy recipients, as brought in Bava Kamma 16b.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הֵם הֶחֱטִיאוּ לְיִרְמְיָה בְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה כַּנּוֹדָע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּאֶבֶן הָעֵזֶר סִימָן א בְּחֶלְקַת מְחוֹקֵק סָעִיף קָטָן ח)
That is, because they forced Jeremiah into a situation resulting in wasted seed, as noted in Chelkat Mechokek on Even HaEzer 1, note 8
[וְאוּלַי זֶה גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל "כִּי כָרוּ שׁוּחָה וְגוֹמֵר", עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּבָבָא קַמָּא.
[and perhaps this is likewise alluded to in "for they have digged a pit to take me," see Bava Kamma there.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָשַׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת לְבִלְתִּי יִהְיֶה לְבַטָּלָה, וְנוֹלַד מִזֶּה בֶּן סִירָא כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם,
However, the Blessed Name devised means that it not be in vain, and from that conception was born Ben Sira, as brought there;
וּלְכָךְ בֶּן סִירָא הָיָה כָּלוּל טוֹב וָרָע כִּדְאִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק:) דְּהוּא מִסְּפָרִים חִיצוֹנִים, וּמִילְּתָא מַעֲלָיוּתָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ דָּרְשִׁינַן עַיֵּין שָׁם,
and therefore Ben Sira embodied an intermingling of good and evil, being enumerated in Sanhedrin 100b among external apocryphal books, yet whose sublime teachings we cite and expound, see there,
וְכֵן בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (צב:) קְרָאוּהוּ "כְּתוּבִים",
and in Bava Kamma 92b they even referred to his proverbs as "Scriptures,"
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיְתָה נֶפֶשׁ יְקָרָה, רַק דְּיָצְאָה לַחִיצוֹנִים וּמִשָּׁם נִלְקְחָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
for in truth his soul was immensely precious, only that it emerged through the external realm and was rescued from there, and this is not the place to elaborate],
וְקִלְּלָהּ שֶׁיִּכָּשְׁלוּ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, דְּלֹא רָצָה לְקַלְּלָם שֶׁיִּכָּשְׁלוּ בְּחֶטְאוֹ, דְּזֶה גּוֹרֵם רָעָה לַכֹּל כַּנּוֹדָע בַּזֹּהַר, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בָּזֶה.

and Jeremiah cursed them that they stumble measure for measure, refusing to curse them to stumble in actual wasted seed, which inflicts universal spiritual damage throughout creation as known in the Zohar, unlike stumbling in unworthy charity.

וְהִנֵּה דָּבָר זֶה אֵין בְּיַד הָאָדָם לֵידַע כְּלָל, עַיֵּין בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (סח.) וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּסֻכָּה (מט:): שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר כָּל הַבָּא לִקְפּוֹץ קוֹפֵץ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: "מַה יָּקָר חַסְדְּךָ" (תְּהִלִּים לו, ח).

And behold, discerning who is a worthy recipient is not within mortal power to know, see Ketubot 68a and Sukkah 49b: "Lest you say: whoever wishes to give charity may simply jump and give? Scripture states: 'How precious is Your lovingkindness, O God!'"
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה סא) דָּרְשׁוּ פָּסוּק "וְלָעֶרֶב אַל תַּנַּח יָדֶךָ, כִּי אֵינְךָ יוֹדֵעַ אֵי זֶה יִכְשָׁר" (קֹהֶלֶת יא, ו) עַל נְתִינַת צְדָקָה, שֶׁאֵין יוֹדֵעַ אֵיזֶה יִכְשָׁר;

And in Bereishit Rabbah (61:3) they expounded the verse "and in the evening withhold not your hand, for you know not which shall prosper" (Ecclesiastes 11:6) regarding the distribution of charity, for man knows not which recipient is truly worthy;
רַק מִי שֶׁשָּׁב כָּרָאוּי וּמְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם שֶׁיְּתוּקַּן חֶטְאוֹ מִכֹּל וָכֹל, אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ כָּרָאוּי:
only one who repents properly and pleads for Heavenly mercy that his sin be utterly rectified, does the Blessed Name providential arrange for him truly worthy recipients.

paragraphs.text: Moed LeKol Chai 28, rectification 43: “There he also wrote, on folio 121a, another rectification: the wealthy person should increase his charity to forty small coins, and the poor person should give no fewer than four small coins to the four corners of the city, beginning at the southeast corner, in accordance with the rule governing the direction in which one turns. This is the attribute of kindness associated with Avraham. Corresponding to his own conduct, he becomes a wanderer, moves about, and exerts himself in the sweat of a mitzvah by going from place to place through the four corners and directions of the city, as much as he can bear. These correspond to the four exiles into which Israel was exiled. His intention in walking in the city’s four directions should be to gather Israel’s dispersed and bring into holiness his holy sparks that descended into the kelipot through wasted seed. The charity must be given secretly, like a mikveh of forty seah whose contents are unseen, and he should give it to those who labor in Torah. Of him it is said, “He removes the first offense first,” for this rectifies the blemish of the covenant for everything he blemished that week. He will not need another rectification or fasts, for this order is a wondrous and complete rectification.”

paragraphs.text: The life one sustains through charity should become a vehicle for good, but its future use is not fully visible.

rich.text: The life one sustains through charity should become a vehicle for good, but its future use is not fully visible.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 5:2: “For sometimes a person fulfills the commandment of charity, giving a gift from his hand to a poor person. If the poor person uses this strength to fulfill the will of Hashem, blessed be He, the commandment will then be vindicated, and “the work of charity shall be peace.” But if, Heaven forbid, he gives to an unworthy poor person, who uses that strength to act contrary to the will of Hashem, blessed be He, he will thereby be helping those who transgress His will. This is termed “burial,” for the matter is hidden and stored away in concealment, and its ultimate outcome is unknown. For this, every devout person should pray to Hashem, blessed be He, to help him perform the commandment, so that he encounters a worthy poor person and can fulfill His commandments completely. For through his own grasp, a person cannot clarify his conduct in this matter, because this world is full of uncertainty.”

If the poor person uses this strength to fulfill the will of Hashem, blessed be He, the commandment will then be vindicated, and “the work of charity shall be peace.” But if, Heaven forbid, he gives to an unworthy poor person, who uses that strength to act contrary to the will of Hashem, blessed be He, he will thereby be helping those who transgress His will. This is termed “burial,” for the matter is hidden and stored away in concealment, and its ultimate outcome is unknown. For this, every devout person should pray to Hashem, blessed be He, to help him perform the commandment, so that he encounters a worthy poor person and can fulfill His commandments completely. For through his own grasp, a person cannot clarify his conduct in this matter, because this world is full of uncertainty.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov poses the exact difficulty that concludes this siman: the giver cannot know completely how the recipient will use the strength provided. He therefore joins the mitzvah to prayer for a fitting recipient and a good outcome. This deepens the siman’s appeal to divine help without turning uncertainty into a reason to abandon charity.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 11a:2: “It was taught: They said of Binyamin the Righteous that he was in charge of a charity fund. Once, during years of drought, a woman came before him and said to him: ‘Rabbi, provide for me!’ He said to her: ‘By the Temple service, the charity fund has nothing!’ She said to him: ‘Rabbi, if you do not provide for me, a woman and her seven sons will die!’ He arose and provided for her from his own funds. paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 10a:16-10b:2: “Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said: Rabbi Yochanan raised a contradiction. It is written, “Wealth will not avail on a day of wrath, but charity saves from death,” and it is written, “Treasures of wickedness will not avail, but charity saves from death.” Why these two statements about charity? One saves a person from an unusual death, and one saves him from the judgment of Gehinnom. Which saves him from the judgment of Gehinnom? The verse in which “wrath” is written, for it is written, “That day is a day of wrath.” Which saves him from an unusual death? He gives it without knowing to whom he gives it, and the recipient receives it without knowing from whom he receives it. Giving without knowing to whom excludes the practice of Mar Ukva; receiving without knowing from whom excludes the practice of Rabbi Abba. What, then, should he do? Give to the charity fund. An objection was raised: What should a person do so that he will have male children? Rabbi Eliezer says: He should distribute his money to the poor. Rabbi Yehoshua says: He should gladden his wife for the marital mitzvah. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: A person should not give a coin to a charity purse unless someone like Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon is appointed over it. When we said to give to the fund, we meant one over which someone like Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon is appointed.”
