sections.en: Whoever Brings Merit to the Guilty Is Likewise Empowered to Rectify This Sin

p: [קכו] מַאן דִּמְזַכֵּי לְחַיָּיבַיָּא מוֹעִיל גַּם כֵּן לְתַקֵּן זֶה,
Whoever brings merit to the guilty is likewise empowered to rectify this sin,

שֶׁהוּא נִקְרָא "לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת", וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק "וְאֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יב, ה) שֶׁהוּא כְּאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאָם, וְנֶפֶשׁ מֵשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ

for he is titled "he that wins souls" (Proverbs 11:30), as our Sages expounded on the verse "and the souls that they had gotten in Haran" (Genesis 12:5), that it is as though he created them, and soul restores soul
[וּמֵעָוֹן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, כְּשֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ מִזְּדוֹנוֹת זְכִיּוֹת וְאוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת נִלְקָחִים לִקְדוּשָׁה, מוֹסִיף שֶׁפַע גָּדוֹל,
[and regarding the sin of wasted seed, when willful sins are converted into merits and those souls are redeemed into holiness, vast divine influx is added,
וְנִמְצָא דְּהָיָה מְזַכֶּה לְחַיָּיבַיָּא בָּזֶה, וְחֶטְאוֹ מַמָּשׁ מֵעֵין דּוּגְמָא דְּתִיקּוּנוֹ,
and it turns out that he brought merit to the guilty through this, his sin mirroring the very pattern of his rectification,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ע:): בַּדָּבָר שֶׁקִּלְקְלוּ בּוֹ נִתְקָנוּ;
and concerning this they said (Sanhedrin 70b): in the very matter wherein they corrupted are they rectified;
וְעַיֵּין לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"כ דְּעַל זֶה מַגִּיעַ עוֹנֶשׁ זֶה, וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלְגֵּל חוֹבָה עַל יְדֵי זַכַּאי רַק זְכוּת,
and see above Section 120 that on this account this penalty arrives, and certainly the Blessed Name does not bring about liability through a meritorious person, only merit;
רַק הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כְּעִנְיַן "שְׂכַר מִצְוָה – מִצְוָה", דְּגַם בָּזֶה הוּא מְזַכֶּה לְחַיָּיבַיָּא עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
rather it is truly in the manner of "the reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah," wherein through repentance he brings merit to the guilty.
וּדְכַוָּותֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי מַכְשֵׁלָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה בָּא קֶרִי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"ו, וְעַל יָדוֹ הַתִּיקּוּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת קט"ז].
And parallel to this, through a stumbling in Torah study nocturnal emission occurs as I wrote above in Section 106, and through it comes rectification as I wrote above in Section 116].
וְלָכֵן אָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאוֹתוֹ מִזְמוֹר: "אֲלַמְּדָה פֹשְׁעִים דְּרָכֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, טו),
And therefore King David, peace be upon him, proclaimed in that psalm: "I will teach transgressors Your ways, etc." (Psalms 51:15),
רַק הִקְדִּים: "הָשִׁיבָה לִּי שְׂשׂוֹן יִשְׁעֶךָ",
only he preceded with: "Restore unto me the joy of Your salvation,"
כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְחַיָּיב לְזַכּוֹת אֶת הַחַיָּיב, וְאָמְרוּ: "יָבוֹא טָהוֹר וִיכַפֵּר עַל הַטָּהוֹר", וְאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת לב.): "מְגַלְגְּלִין זְכוּת עַל יְדֵי זַכַּאי".

for it is impossible for a debtor to absolve another debtor, and they taught: "let the pure come and atone for the pure" (Yoma 43b), and: "merit is brought about through the meritorious" (Shabbat 32a).
רַק צָרִיךְ מִקּוֹדֶם תְּשׁוּבָה וְרַחֲמִים שֶׁיָּשִׁיב לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוּחַ קְדוּשָׁה שֶׁבְּנֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי,
Rather, one first requires repentance and mercy so that the Blessed Name restores to him the holy spirit intrinsic to the Jewish soul,
וְאָז אַחַר כָּךְ, לְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם וּלְהוֹצִיא נְפָשׁוֹת עֲשׁוּקוֹת, יוּכַל עַל יְדֵי זֶה דַּ"אֲלַמְּדָה וְגוֹמֵר"
and then afterward, to rectify the past and redeem captive souls, he is empowered through "I will teach transgressors Your ways, etc."
[וּפְעָמִים אוֹתָן חַיָּיבַיָּא הֵם אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת עַצְמָן, וּלְכָךְ נִזְדַּמְּנוּ לְיָדוֹ דַּיְיקָא לְתַקְּנָם.
[and sometimes those very sinners are those captive souls themselves, which is why they were orchestrated into his hands specifically so that he rectify them.
וְעַיֵּין רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּל הַיָּד: הַמְשַׂחֲקִין בַּתִּינוֹקוֹת וּמְקַבְּלֵי גֵּרִים, זֶה בָּא מִזֶּה, כִּי הֵם גַּם כֵּן אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:

And examine Niddah 13b regarding those who delay the Messiah through playing with children and receiving converts, the one stemming from the other, for they are likewise those very souls as is known, and this is not the place to elaborate].

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Yonah on Pirkei Avot 4:2:3: ““The reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah”: This is another reason, beyond the natural explanation. It means that the Holy One, blessed be He, has not placed good and evil in a person’s hands, but only the choice, as it is said, “Choose life.” After he chooses one path, if he walks in the good, Hashem is with him. When he performs one mitzvah, it assists him to perform another, for by himself he does not even have the power to do good. Concerning this it says, “The reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah, and the reward of a transgression is a transgression.” Heaven forbid that this is its entire reward; if so, what reward would he have? That is not so, for its reward remains for the World to Come. Rather, it means that the fruit of a mitzvah is a mitzvah: he enjoys its fruits in this world when it helps him perform other mitzvot. Thus the principal grows and remains for the World to Come. This is “Say of the righteous that it is good, for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.””

The actual contrast is zakkai and chayyav, “acquitted” and “liable”; Rav Tzadok’s wording, “the pure … for the pure,” gives the sense; the Gemara’s own words are “let one who is acquitted come and atone for one who is liable.”

paragraphs.text: Pardes Rimmonim 31:9:4: “So too, relations with a pregnant or nursing wife are permitted and are not called wasted seed, Heaven forbid. Although they do not serve physical generation, they serve spiritual generation: through the couple’s good intention, the supernal Bridegroom and Bride are united, as through other acts of mitzvot. This is the secret of Avraham and Sarah generating souls for converts, as our Sages explained. Through their intention, the Bridegroom and Bride were united and generated holy souls for those converts, in the mystery of the supernal generation explained in the Gate of Essence and Governance. This is “The souls that they made in Charan.””

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Yevamot 109b:3:1: ““Evil after evil will come upon those who receive converts”: Ri says that this applies where they persuade them to convert or receive them immediately. But if they make an earnest effort to convert, we must accept them. We find that Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov were punished for not receiving Timna when she came to convert; she went and became the concubine of Eliphaz son of Esav, and Amalek, who afflicted Israel, descended from her, as is stated in the aggadah of Chelek. Yehoshua also accepted Rachav the harlot, and Naamah and Rut the Moabite were accepted. At the beginning of “With What May One Kindle,” Hillel converted the man who said, “Convert me on condition that you make me High Priest,” and the one who said, “On condition that you teach me the entire Torah.” Although they were not making an earnest effort to convert, Hillel knew that in the end they would become genuine converts, as indeed happened.”

sections.en: A Definitive Sign of Complete Repentance and That His Repentance Over This Sin Of…

p: [קכז] סִימָן לִתְשׁוּבָה גְּמוּרָה וְשֶׁנִּתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ עַל עָוֹן זֶה דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה וּבִכְלָל קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית, הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר נִפְתְּחוּ לְפָנָיו מַרְאוֹת הָאֱלֹהִים;
A definitive sign of complete repentance and that his repentance over this sin of wasted seed and blemishes of the Covenant has been accepted, is when the visions of God open before him;
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁרוֹאֶה וּמַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִכְחוֹ, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה נִקְרָא אֵצֶל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם "רוּחַ קָדְשְׁךָ" וּ"שְׂשׂוֹן יִשְׁעֶךָ";
meaning that he perceives and recognizes that the Blessed Name is directly before him, which King David, peace be upon him, titled "Your holy spirit" and "the joy of Your salvation";
כִּי אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא עַל פָּסוּק "מִבְּשָׂרִי אֶחֱזֶה אֱלוֹהַּ" (אִיּוֹב יט, כו), דִּלִשְׁמִירַת בְּרִית בָּשָׂר תֵּיכֶף מַגִּיעַ מַחֲזֶה: "וַיֵּרָא וְגוֹמֵר".

for they stated in Bereishit Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Vayeira) on the verse "from my flesh shall I see God" (Job 19:26), that for guarding the covenant of the flesh there immediately follows divine vision: "And Hashem appeared unto him, etc." (Genesis 18:1).
וְהִנֵּה בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה, אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר חַיֵּי שָׂרָה (קכט סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דִּבְשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא זוֹכֶה לְכָל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת
And behold, regarding a penitent (ba'al teshuvah), the Zohar states (Chayei Sarah 129a end) that in one hour, in a single instant, he merits to ascend to all spiritual rungs
[וְשָׁמַעְתִּי בְּשֵׁם הָרַבִּי רַבִּי בּוּנִם זַ"ל כִּי דָּבָר זֶה מִיגִיעַת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחַאי עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם],
[and I heard in the name of the Rebbe, Reb Bunim (of Peshischa), of blessed memory, that this was attained through the toil of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him],
וְדָבָר זֶה עִיקָּרוֹ עַל בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה מֵעָוֹן קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית כִּדְאִיתָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יז.) עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹרְדְּיָא;
and this concept applies primarily to a penitent repenting from the sin of blemishing the Covenant, as brought in Avodah Zarah 17a concerning Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya;
וּבְלָאו הָכִי סְתָם תְּשׁוּבָה בְּעָוֹן זֶה כִּדְמַשְׁמָע בְּפֶרֶק יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים (יוֹמָא פו:): הֵיכִי דָּמֵי בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה? מַחֲוֵי וְכוּלֵי בְּאוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה.
and even generally, standard repentance is framed around this sin, as implied in Yoma 86b: "Who is a true penitent? One to whom the same woman presents herself in the same situation, etc."
וּכְשֶׁמְּתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה הָרְאוּיָה
And when one rectifies through proper repentance

[שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם לֹא יַחֲזוֹר לְדָבָר זֶה אֲפִילּוּ יַעֲבוֹר עָלָיו מָה, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּעִיד עָלָיו יוֹצֵר בְּרֵאשִׁית עַל כָּךְ כִּלְשׁוֹן הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁהִגִּיעַ תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ לְכָךְ],

[which means that he will never return to this, whatever befalls him; that is, the Creator of the universe can testify about him, in the words of Maimonides in Hilkhot Teshuvah (2:2), that his repentance has reached this level],
אָז תֵּיכֶף מַגִּיעַ לוֹ הָרְאִיָּה הָרְאוּיָה לְשׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
then there immediately reaches him the divine vision appropriate to the guardian of the Covenant as noted above

[וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹרְדְּיָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שָׁם שֶׁמֵּת תֵּיכֶף, הָא אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק לד) עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי לֹא יִרְאַנִי וְגוֹמֵר": הָא בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתוֹ רוֹאֶה,

[and regarding Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya in Avodah Zarah who died immediately, our Sages stated (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 34) on the verse "for man shall not see Me and live" (Exodus 33:20): behold, at the hour of his death he sees,
וְהִיא הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁזָּכָה לָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת כִּי הָיָה מְחוּיָּב מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין,
which was the divine vision he merited, and afterward he died because he was liable to court-imposed capital punishment,
וְדִין אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת לֹא בָּטְלוּ, כִּי מִמִּיתַת בֵּית דִּין לָא מַהֲנֵי כֹּפֶר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "לֹא תִקְחוּ כֹפֶר וְגוֹמֵר",
and the dynamic of the four capital penalties was never abolished, seeing that for court execution no ransom avails, as written: "You shall take no ransom, etc.",
וְאֵין שׁוּם פִּדְיוֹן וְתִיקּוּן מוֹעִיל מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְמִיתָה בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם.
and no monetary redemption or ritual substitution avails, unlike death at the hands of Heaven.
וְאָמְנָם חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הִמְצִיאוּ כַּמָּה עֵצוֹת וְהַצָּלוֹת גַּם לְהַמִּיתַת בֵּית דִּין, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
Truly, our Sages devised numerous spiritual counsels and deliverances even for court execution, which is not to be elaborated here.
וְאָמְרוּ שָׁם: בָּכָה רַבִּי: יֵשׁ קוֹנֶה וְכוּלֵי,
And they said there: Rebbe wept and said: "There is one who acquires his world in a single hour, etc.",
כִּי אָמְרוּ: "יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים וְכוּלֵי",
for they taught: "Better is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come,"
וְגַם זֶה הוּא לְעוֹנֶשׁ מַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עוֹלָמוֹ בְּשָׁעָה אַחַת וְהֻוצְרַךְ תֵּיכֶף לֵילֵךְ לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא, גַּם זֶה מִכְּלַל עוֹנְשָׁיו]:
and that he acquired his world in one hour and was compelled to depart immediately to the World to Come was likewise part of his punishment, depriving him of further years of Torah and mitzvot].

paragraphs.text: An occasional revelation and an enduring dwelling

rich.text: An occasional revelation and an enduring dwelling

paragraphs.text: Recognition of Hashem before oneself concerns a changed readiness, not merely an isolated experience.

rich.text: Recognition of Hashem before oneself concerns a changed readiness, not merely an isolated experience.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Vayera 1:3: “The principal difference appears to be that the earlier revelation was for speech; this does not require circumcision, and there were prophets among the nations as well. Here it says ‘He appeared’ without recording any speech afterward to explain its purpose. The Sages therefore explained it as visiting the sick. But the plain meaning appears to be that, until then, revelation had occurred only for a prophetic message, occasionally, when Avraham prepared himself. Now he had become whole, his body always ready for it. ‘He appeared to him’ means that He now appeared to be with him continually. Thus, at the last speech before circumcision at the end of Lech Lecha, it says, ‘He finished speaking with him, and God ascended from Avraham’ (Genesis 17:22). This is a model for all the earlier speeches: the revelation was only during the speech and departed immediately afterward. Scripture states it here to explain the difference between seeing before circumcision and seeing afterward. The latter was not for a speech or another particular purpose and did not depart at all, for his body had already been sanctified to be a dwelling for the Shekhinah in his heart continually, as with Israel. Concerning ‘My heart is awake,’ Shir HaShirim Rabbah asks: from where is it known that the Holy One is the heart of Israel? From ‘The Rock of my heart.’”

rich.text: : “The principal difference appears to be that the earlier revelation was for speech; this does not require circumcision, and there were prophets among the nations as well. Here it says ‘He appeared’ without recording any speech afterward to explain its purpose. The Sages therefore explained it as visiting the sick. But the plain meaning appears to be that, until then, revelation had occurred only for a prophetic message, occasionally, when Avraham prepared himself. Now he had become whole, his body always ready for it. ‘He appeared to him’ means that He now appeared to be with him continually. Thus, at the last speech before circumcision at the end of Lech Lecha, it says, ‘He finished speaking with him, and God ascended from Avraham’ (Genesis 17:22). This is a model for all the earlier speeches: the revelation was only during the speech and departed immediately afterward. Scripture states it here to explain the difference between seeing before circumcision and seeing afterward. The latter was not for a speech or another particular purpose and did not depart at all, for his body had already been sanctified to be a dwelling for the Shekhinah in his heart continually, as with Israel. Concerning ‘My heart is awake,’ Shir HaShirim Rabbah asks: from where is it known that the Holy One is the heart of Israel? From ‘The Rock of my heart.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Peri Tzadik asks why circumcision is said to make revelation possible when Avraham had already received revelations before it. Its answer distinguishes an appearance for a particular prophetic message from the body becoming an enduring dwelling for the Shekhinah. This develops the siman's own definition of seeing as recognizing Hashem before oneself, read with its requirement of a lasting return.

sections.en: When a Person Commits a Transgression Under the Principle of "It Is Time To…"

p: [קכח] כְּשֶׁאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה עֲבֵירָה כְּעִנְיַן "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, קכו) וּ"בְּכָל דְּרָכֶיךָ דָעֵהוּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, ו), מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ כַּפָּרָה עַל הָעֲבֵירָה שֶׁעָשָׂה,

When a person commits a transgression under the principle of "It is time to work for Hashem; they have made void Your Torah" (Psalms 119:126) or "In all your ways acknowledge Him" (Proverbs 3:6), he nonetheless requires atonement for the transgression he committed,
וּכְאוֹתָהּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת לא:): דְּמִתְעַנִּין תַּעֲנִית חֲלוֹם בְּשַׁבָּת וְצָרִיךְ לְמֵיתַב תַּעֲנִיתָא לְתַעֲנִיתֵיהּ;
as in that which they taught (Berakhot 31b): one who fasts a dream-fast on Shabbat must fast again to atone for that fast;
וְכֵן בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כו:): סָבְרִי מִצְוָה קָעָבְדִי, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם צְרִיכָה כַּפָּרָה;
and likewise in Sanhedrin 26b: they reasoned they were performing a mitzvah, yet it nonetheless required atonement;
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּשְׁבִירַת הַלּוּחוֹת, וְגָרַם עַל יְדֵי זֶה שִׁכְחַת הַתּוֹרָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין נד.): אִלְמָלֵא וְכוּלֵי,
and so with Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, regarding the breaking of the Tablets, which caused the forgetfulness of Torah (Eruvin 54a): "Had not the first tablets been broken, etc.,"
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִקְרֵי עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ,
even though the Holy One consented with his action, it was nonetheless titled an aveirah lishmah,

וּלְכָךְ סָבַל גַּם הוּא כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת וָאֶתְחַנַּן) שֶׁנִּיטְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מָסוֹרוֹת הַחָכְמָה וְהָיָה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ יוֹשֵׁב וְדוֹרֵשׁ וְכוּלֵי.
and therefore he too suffered, as our Sages stated (Midrash Tanchuma, end of Va'etchanan) that the traditions of wisdom were sealed from him and Joshua sat and expounded in his presence.
וְכֵן אֶסְתֵּר, דְּנִיטְּלָה מִמֶּנָּה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעָה לְבֵית הַצְּלָמִים (מְגִילָּה טו:), הוּא לְעוֹנֶשׁ אַעֲבֵירָה אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִצְוָה רַבָּה קָעָבְדָא

And likewise Esther, from whom the Holy Spirit departed when she reached the chamber of idols (Megillah 15b), which was a punishment for the transgression, even though she was performing a momentous mitzvah
[וְזֶה סוֹד שֶׁאָמְרָה: שֶׁמָּא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁקְּרָאתִיו "כֶּלֶב", וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
[and this is the mystical secret of why she asked: perhaps it is because I called him a 'dog', and this is not the place to elaborate].
וּלְכָךְ בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה, אַף דִּזְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ זְכִיּוֹת, מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ סִגּוּפִים וְתַעֲנִיּוֹת לְכַפָּרָה, מִשּׁוּם דְּעַל כָּל פָּנִים לֹא עֲדִיפֵי מֵעֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ.

And therefore a penitent, even though willful transgressions are transformed into merits, nonetheless requires self-afflictions and fasts for atonement, since at the very least his past sins are no superior to an aveirah lishmah.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (נ.): כָּל הָאוֹמֵר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וַתְּרָן וְכוּלֵי,
And concerning this they said in Bava Kamma 50a: "Whoever says that the Holy One is indulgent, let his life be yielded,"
דְּעַל כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁעָשָׂה מִיָּמָיו נִפְרָעִים בְּעוֹנֶשׁ הַקָּצוּב וְרָאוּי לְכָךְ;
for regarding every deed a person ever committed, payment is exacted through the designated punishment fitting for it;

אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָזֶה עֵצוֹת רַבּוֹת בְּרַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יז:) בִּגְזַר דִּין דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בִּירִידַת גְּשָׁמִים: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ וְכוּלֵי.

save that there exist many mitigating counsels through Heavenly mercy, along the lines of what our Sages taught (Rosh Hashanah 17b) regarding the decree of rainfall on Rosh Hashanah: behold, if they were initially sentenced to scarce rain, etc.
וְכֵן כָּאן, לִפְעָמִים נוֹתֵן לוֹ הַיִּסּוּרִין בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת שֶׁהוּא טוֹבָה לוֹ,
And so here: sometimes He sends the afflictions at a time when it turns out to his benefit,
וְגַם יֵשׁ חִלּוּפִין בִּדְבָרִים הַדּוֹמִים זֶה לָזֶה, וְעַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית יִסּוּרִין שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּעֵרָכִין (טז:).

and there are substitutions made through analogous tribulations, down to the minimal definition of suffering stated in Arachin 16b (such as reaching into one's pocket for a coin and pulling out the wrong denomination).
וְגַם פְּעָמִים הוּא שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק ג) דְּנִפְרָעִין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ
And sometimes retribution is exacted unconsciously, as stated in Avot (3:16) that payment is collected without his awareness
[וְכָל שֶׁלֹּא בְּהַרְגָּשָׁתוֹ מִשּׁוּם עוֹנֶשׁ מִקְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ, שֶׁפְּעָמִים אָדָם שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וּמְדַמֶּה שֶׁטּוֹב לוֹ מְאֹד וַאֲחֵרִים מְבִינִים שֶׁאֵין טוֹב].
[and whenever he does not feel it as a punitive blow, it is termed 'without his knowledge,' for sometimes a man rejoices in his lot imagining all is wonderful, while others perceive his misfortune].
וְגַם עַל יְדֵי הַמְּרִירוּת בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ – זֶה מַמָּשׁ עוֹנְשֵׁי גֵיהִנָּם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר:
And likewise, through the bitter remorse experienced in his repentance—that is literally the retribution of Gehenna, as I wrote elsewhere.

paragraphs.text: Knowing Hashem after a failure
The availability of teshuvah preserves responsibility and prevents despair.

rich.text: The availability of teshuvah preserves responsibility and prevents despair.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Berakhot 7: “So the holy Zohar says (Shemini 35b): when the Holy One wished to create the world, Torah said before Him, ‘This person whom You are about to create is destined to sin before You.’ The Holy One replied, ‘Was I called long-suffering for nothing?’ The Midrash (Devarim Rabbah, Vaetchanan 2) compares prayer to a mikveh and repentance to the sea. A mikveh is sometimes open and sometimes closed; so too prayer is sometimes open and sometimes closed. Repentance is like the sea: just as the sea is always open, the Holy One's hand is always open to receive those who return. All this teaches that even if a person, Heaven forbid, has stumbled in a bad act, repentance is not withheld from him. This is the meaning of ‘Know Him in all your ways,’ upon which the substance of Torah depends. As Rava concludes, ‘Even in a matter of transgression’: the person should not despair after stumbling in sin, because repentance is always available. This is the general principle of the substance of Torah.”

A mikveh is sometimes open and sometimes closed; so too prayer is sometimes open and sometimes closed. Repentance is like the sea: just as the sea is always open, the Holy One's hand is always open to receive those who return. All this teaches that even if a person, Heaven forbid, has stumbled in a bad act, repentance is not withheld from him. This is the meaning of ‘Know Him in all your ways,’ upon which the substance of Torah depends. As Rava concludes, ‘Even in a matter of transgression’: the person should not despair after stumbling in sin, because repentance is always available. This is the general principle of the substance of Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef gives an explicit reading of the same rabbinic phrase, ‘even in a matter of transgression’: a person must not despair after stumbling, because return remains open. It is a useful qualification beside the siman's insistence that a higher purpose does not remove the need for repair. The possibility of continuing mitzvot before complete purification supplies a route back, rather than a justification for repeating the failure.

sections.en: The Moment a Person Desires to Repent

p: [קכט] מִיָּד שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב, הֲרֵי הוּא "בָּא לִטָּהֵר", וְהַמִּשְׁפָּט לְסַיֵּיעַ אוֹתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (לח:);
The moment a person desires to repent, behold he is "coming to purify himself," and the heavenly rule is to assist him, as stated in Yoma 38b;
וּכְשֶׁמְּסַיְּיעִין, אָז מִמֵּילָא נִיתּוֹסַף בּוֹ רוּחַ טָהֳרָה וְהוּא מוֹסִיף לָבוֹא לִטָּהֵר,
and when they assist him, there is automatically added within him a spirit of purity, prompting him to strive further to purify himself;
וְאָז חוֹזֵר הַסִּיּוּעַ מִלְּמַעְלָה בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת, וּמִמֵּילָא מוֹסִיף לְמַטָּה לָבוֹא לִטָּהֵר,
and then assistance from Above returns with even greater intensity, leading him below to strive further to purify himself;
וְכָךְ חוֹזֵר חָלִילָה, עַד שֶׁמִּפֶּתַח כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט נַעֲשָׂה כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב).
and so it cycles repeatedly, until from an opening as narrow as the eye of a needle it expands into the portal of the Temple Hall (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2).
וּמֵאַיִן בָּא שֶׁפְּעָמִים אָדָם רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב וְאֵין נִגְמָר, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִין חֲרָטוֹת רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן?
Whence then comes it that sometimes a person desires to repent yet it never comes to fruition, in the manner of: "transgressors in Israel are full of regrets," may the Merciful One preserve us?
הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית, כִּי בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב, אָז הוּא הַקִּטְרוּג הַגָּדוֹל מִיֵּצֶר;
This is as written in Midrash HaNe'elam in Zohar Chadash (end of Bereishit), for at the very moment a person desires to repent, then arises the fiercest accusation from the evil inclination;
וּלְכָךְ זְמַן הַקִּטְרוּג בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה [שֶׁנִּקְרָא "בְּהִמָּצְאוֹ" וְעֵת רָצוֹן], עַיֵּין שָׁם.
which is why the time of accusation peaks on Rosh Hashanah [which is called "while He may be found" and an acceptable time], see there.
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בְּקִטְרוּג – הַיְינוּ אִם מַגִּיעוֹ עַל פִּי מִשְׁפָּט לְסַיְּיעוֹ, בְּטַעֲנוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ.
And by "accusation" it means challenging whether according to strict justice he is deserving of divine assistance, through various claims the accuser levels.
וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם בְּעֵת שֶׁבָּא לִיטָּהֵר עַל הַסִּיּוּעַ.
Therefore, when coming to purify oneself, one must intensely plead for Heavenly mercy to receive that assistance.
וְהָעֵצָה נֶגְדּוֹ הוּא הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהַבְּטִיחוּת בַּלֵּב, שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב רַחֲמָיו וַחֲסָדָיו יְקַבְּלוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה לְפָנָיו;

And the spiritual remedy against this obstacle is heartfelt joy and steadfast confidence that certainly the Blessed Name in His abundant mercy and kindness will accept him in complete repentance before Him;
וְתוֹכוֹ רָצוּף הַמְּרִירוּת הַגָּדוֹל עַל חֶטְאוֹ,
while his interior is simultaneously lined with profound bitterness over his sin,
שֶׁזֶּה מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמַת תַּשְׁרַ"ת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כַּיָּדוּעַ,
which is an exact reflection of the Tashrat shofar order performed on Rosh Hashanah:
דְּהַתְּקִיעוֹת הֵם לְשִׂמְחָה, וּשְׁבָרִים-תְּרוּעָה הַיְינוּ גְּנוֹחֵי גָּנַח וִילּוֹלֵי יִילֵיל כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה,
for the clear blasts (tekiah) denote joy, while the broken sobs (shevarim-teruah) denote groaning and wailing,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְעַרְבֵּב הַשָּׂטָן.
and through this integration the Satan is confounded.
וּלְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: "מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד בְּבוֹא אֵלָיו נָתָן וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, א–ב),
And therefore it is stated: "A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, etc." (Psalms 51:1–2),
שֶׁהוּא הַפְּשׁוּטָה שֶׁלְּפָנֶיהָ בְּשִׂמְחָה וְזִמְרָה, בָּטוּחַ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַעֲנֶנּוּ
which opens with a mizmor (song), functioning as the simple straight blast (peshutah) that precedes, in joy and song, confident that the Blessed Name will answer him
[וּבְכָל מִזְמוֹר שֶׁל בַּקָּשָׁה שֶׁבִּתְהִלִּים, סוֹפוֹ לְעוֹלָם בִּישׁוּעָה וְנֶחָמָה כְּעִנְיַן פְּשׁוּטָה לְאַחֲרֶיהָ.
[and in every supplication psalm in the Psalter, its conclusion is invariably in salvation and consolation, like the simple blast that follows.
וְגַם כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה, אָז מַשִּׂיג תֵּיכֶף בְּשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא הָאוֹר וְהַגִּלּוּי, וְזֶהוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁלְּאַחֲרֶיהָ,
And also because in true repentance, one immediately attains in one hour, in a single instant, supernal light and revelation, which is the joy that follows,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּדִמְעָתִי עַרְשִׂי וְגוֹמֵר", וְתֵיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ: "כִּי שָׁמַע ה' קוֹל בִּכְיִי וְגוֹמֵר", וְכֵן בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת.
as in: "I water my couch with my tears, etc." (Psalms 6:7), followed immediately by: "for Hashem has heard the voice of my weeping, etc." (ibid. 6:9), and so in many places.
וְשֶׁלְּפָנֶיהָ הוּא כְּעִנְיַן "טֶרֶם יִקְרָאוּ וַאֲנִי אֶעֱנֶה",
And that which precedes reflects "before they call, I will answer" (Isaiah 65:24);
וּבְוַדַּאי כְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹנֶה, הוּא בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת, וּמַרְגִּישׁ תֵּיכֶף לֵב הָאָדָם גַּם קוֹדֶם הַקְּרִיאָה קְצָת שִׂמְחָה וּבְטִיחוּת.
and certainly when the Holy One answers, it reverberates through all worlds, and the human heart immediately senses even before calling a measure of joy and confidence.
וּכְשֶׁהָאָדָם מִתְאַמֵּץ לְבָבוֹ לִהְיוֹת כֵּן, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ כֵן מֵעַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי הָעֲנִיָּה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And when a person braces his heart to cultivate this trust, even if it does not arise spontaneously through Hashem's response,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי פְּעֻלַּת לִבּוֹ עוֹשֶׂה רֹשֶׁם לְמַעְלָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן, כְּעִנְיַן "ה' צִלְּךָ" כַּנּוֹדָע]:
nonetheless through the deliberate stirrings of his heart he creates an impression Above to make it so, in the manner of "Hashem is your shadow," as is known].

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 5:6: “Different is Israel: Hashem bestows upon them little by little as they are able to bear, so that they recognize and know Who is the One giving them wealth and strength, and at every hour and moment they return anew before the Master, Hashem God of Israel, that He channel unto them a renewed influx, and "before they call, Hashem will answer" (Isaiah 65:24); and this influx endures for all eternity, and unto them too it is accounted as an active share and acquisition, as written of them: "For Hashem's portion is His people", because Hashem bestows upon them with an exceedingly generous eye, so that it be credited to them that through the labor of their hands—namely through their prayer—they acquired this.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov describes help given gradually, in a measure the recipient can bear, so that the person repeatedly recognizes its Giver and turns to Him anew. This clarifies the ascending movement described here: assistance does not end human participation, but creates the capacity for a further movement toward Hashem. The resulting attainment can still be credited to the person’s prayer and effort.

sections.en: Even Though Free Choice Is Granted Unto Man

p: [קל] אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבְּחִירָה נְתוּנָה לָאָדָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין אָדָם יָכוֹל לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ וְעִיקָּרוֹ,
Even though free choice is granted unto man, nonetheless a person cannot alter his essential root and core;
וּכְאוֹתָהּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מד.): "אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא", מִשּׁוּם דְּהוּא מִשָּׁרְשָׁא וְגִזְעָא קַדִּישָׁא;
as in that which they stated in Sanhedrin 44a: "Even though he sinned, he remains Israel," because he derives from a holy root and stock;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת (כט.): טָבָא לָא הָוֵי בִּישָׁא, אִם לֹא בְּרַע מֵעִיקָּרוֹ;
and so it is stated in Berakhot 29a: one who is fundamentally good does not turn bad, unless he was corrupt from his very root;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּחֲגִיגָה (טו:): טִינָא הָיְתָה בְּלִבָּם;
and in Chagigah 15b: there was muddy slime in their hearts from the start;
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: בִּישָׁא לָא הָוֵי טָבָא,
and likewise conversely: one fundamentally evil does not become good;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה לְגַלּוֹת זֶה הַגְּמִירָא בְּפֵירוּשׁ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם גִּלּוּהוּ בְּסוֹד בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת לַמְּבִינִים,
and although our Sages did not wish to disclose this tradition explicitly, they revealed it in esoteric allusions in many places for the discerning,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת מח.): בּוּצִינָא מִקַּטְפֵיהּ יְדִיעַ.
and concerning this they said (Berakhot 48a): a pumpkin is known from its very blossom.
רַק הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַזֶּה נֶעְלָם מִכָּל הַבְּרוּאִים
Only that this primordial root is concealed from all created beings
[דְּזֶהוּ בְּסוֹד הַיְדִיעָה וְהַבְּחִירָה שֶׁנִּתְקַשּׁוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים],
[which touches upon the mystery of divine Foreknowledge and human Free Choice with which the early masters struggled],
כִּי לִבָּא לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא.
for the heart does not reveal its secrets to the mouth.
וּלְכָךְ מָצִינוּ גַּם כֵּן חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And therefore we also find transgressors concerning whom our Sages stated that they have no share in the World to Come;
וְ"אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא" הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָעִיקָּר חָסֵר מִן הַסֵּפֶר וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ רַע
and having no portion in the World to Come means that the foundation is lacking from the ledger and his root was evil
[וּלְכָךְ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְנַשֶּׁה אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, לֹא הוֹעִילָה לוֹ תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ, כִּי מֵאַחַר דְּעִיקָּרוֹ בִּישָׁא,
[and therefore according to the opinion that Manasseh has no portion in the World to Come, his repentance was not accepted because his essential root was corrupt,
וְלָכֵן אָמַר אִידָךְ דִּמְרַפֶּה יְדֵי בַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה, וְלָכֵן לֹא גִּלּוּ זֶה רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ,
which is why the opposing sage challenged that this weakens the hands of penitents, and why our Sages did not disclose this openly;
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין זֶה רִפּוּי כְּלָל, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ],
yet in truth it is no discouragement at all, and this is not the place to lengthen],
וְהוּא נַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי פְּעֻלָּתוֹ וּבְחִירָתוֹ לְרַע;
which becomes manifest through his active deeds and choices for evil;
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים יָכוֹל לְהִתְקָרֵב, וַאֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה הֲרֵי הוּא כְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג.),
and likewise conversely: through repentance and good deeds one can draw near, and even a gentile who engages in Torah study is comparable to the High Priest (Avodah Zarah 3a),
וְכָל הַתּוֹרָה מָלֵא מִזֶּה, וְנֶאֱמַר: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא וְגוֹמֵר", וּבְרִיאָה הוּא יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן,
and the entire Torah is replete with this, and it is stated: "Create in me a clean heart, etc." (Psalms 51:12), where creation is something from nothing,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁזֶּה בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, מוֹעִיל רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם
meaning that since this is in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, Heavenly mercy is efficacious
[וּלִכְשֶׁיִּזְכֶּה בְּרַחֲמִים אוֹ לְהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אָז יִהְיֶה בֶּאֱמֶת לְמַפְרֵעַ שָׁרְשׁוֹ כָּךְ,
[and when he merits through mercy, or the reverse, Heaven forbid, then in ultimate retroactive truth his root becomes defined as such,
וְאֵין שִׁינּוּי בַּיְדִיעָה, כִּי יְדִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין נוֹפֵל תַּחַת הַזְּמַן דְּעָבָר וְעָתִיד, רַק אָנוּ תַּחַת הַזְּמַן, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ בֵּיאוּרוֹ].
and there is no alteration in Foreknowledge, for the knowledge of the Blessed Name does not fall under time of past and future, only we are under time, and this is not the place to explain it].
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי יְחֶזְקֵאל שנח): שָׁאֲלוּ לַחָכְמָה וְכוּלֵי, לַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, לַנְּבוּאָה וְכוּלֵי, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר: יַעֲשׂוּ תְּשׁוּבָה;
And therefore they taught (Yalkut Shimoni, Ezekiel 358): they asked Wisdom, Torah, and Prophecy what the sinner's fate should be, and the Holy One alone responded: "Let them repent";
אֲבָל מִצַּד כֻּלָּם בִּישָׁא לָא הָוֵי טָבָא.
for from the perspective of all of them, what is corrupt cannot become good.
וְזֶה הָיָה טַעֲנַת הָעָם בִּיחֶזְקֵאל בְּפָרָשַׁת "וּבְשׁוּב צַדִּיק וְגוֹמֵר וּבְשׁוּב רָשָׁע וְגוֹמֵר": "וַאֲמַרְתֶּם לֹא יִתָּכֵן דֶּרֶךְ ה'" (יְחֶזְקֵאל יח, כה);

And this was the objection of the people in Ezekiel in the passage "When the righteous turns away, etc., and when the wicked turns away, etc.": "Yet you say: The way of the Lord is not equal" (Ezekiel 18:25);
וּבְוַדַּאי דַּעַת שׁוֹטִים לֹא נִזְכַּר בַּכָּתוּב, רַק הֵם אַטָּבָא וּבִישָׁא מֵעִיקָּרוֹ אָמְרוּ, וְהֵם חָשְׁבוּ שֶׁגַּם הֵם מְבִינִים;

and certainly a foolish argument would not be memorialized in Scripture, but they were arguing based on the principle of what is fundamentally good or evil from its root, imagining that they understood this;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר לָהֶם: "דַּרְכֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁאַתֶּם אֵין יוֹדְעִים כְּלָל בָּזֶה;
and concerning this the prophet answered: "are not your ways unequal?", meaning that you do not understand this at all;
וּכְשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַבְּלוֹ, אָז מִתְגַּלֶּה לְמַפְרֵעַ דְּעִיקָּרוֹ כָּךְ:
and when the Blessed Name accepts him, it is revealed retroactively that such was his true root from the beginning.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 19:1: “Although it is true that every soul of Israel has a bond and connection in the divine root above the reach of its service, without repentance and service it is impossible to reach that higher root: the person's capacity would be annulled before arriving there. My holy grandfather compared this to a very wealthy person traveling in the wilderness far from home. Though he has great wealth and property at home, if he lacks food on the road he certainly will not reach his home, for he will die of hunger first. Through repentance and service, however, one can reach the illumination of the higher union that no sin or iniquity touches. When a person gives his entire understanding over to Hashem's will on this day, even what occurred with him earlier without awareness is clarified retrospectively as having been His will as well.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim places the higher connection and the required human path in the same complete thought. The wealthy traveler may own abundant resources at home, yet without provisions he will not reach them. So the deeper root and its retrospective clarification do not exempt a person from repentance and service. This develops the siman's insistence on chosen return alongside divine knowledge beyond time.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 4:9: “This is the convert's claim in Shabbat's chapter Bameh Madlikin (31a), and Shammai's strictness in distancing him. Shammai is the level of awe, from which come strength and strictness, the level of Yitzchak, with whom Israel begins as explained above; therefore he distanced the converts there. From the side of awe, its complete attainment is the opposite of that request, as explained above. Hillel's humility brought them near, like Moshe, who was exceedingly humble (Numbers 12:3) and therefore brought near the mixed multitude and argued concerning Michah, as explained above. Avraham too was humble, as Berakhot 6b teaches that the humble person is Avraham's disciple; therefore he is the father of converts, as taught in Bikkurim [Jerusalem Talmud 1:4:5]. Humility is measuring one's deficiency against Hashem's greatness, leaving no place for superiority over the convert who comes with his staff and bag. The One who said [that oil should burn] can say that vinegar should burn as well (Taanit 25a), and can place light in vinegar too, like ‘Create a pure heart for me, God’ (Psalms 51:12). Creation is something from nothing; this is not the place to explain further.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik applies the same new-heart principle to Hillel's receiving converts. Humility measures one's own deficiency against Hashem's greatness and leaves no basis for contempt toward the person arriving from outside. This gives a practical consequence to the siman's warning that the root is hidden from every creature: the human task remains welcome, prayer, repentance and good deeds, rather than a verdict about an allegedly fixed inner nature. Citation clarification: the teaching that Avraham is father of converts is Rabbi Yehudah’s teaching in Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 1:4:5, adopted there in practice. Mishnah Bikkurim 1:4 gives the initial contrary position. The square brackets distinguish the corrected location from the wording of the supplied Hebrew.

sections.en: The Root of the Souls of All Israel Is Derived Directly from the Source…

p: [קלא] שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים,
The root of the souls of all Israel is derived directly from the Source of Life,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ.)
as they said: "All Israel have a portion in the World to Come" (Sanhedrin 90a)
[וַאֲפִילּוּ אוֹתָם שֶׁמָּנוּ שָׁם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם תִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קד:)].
[and even those from Israel enumerated there as excluded possess rectification according to the interpreters of esoteric traces, see Sanhedrin 104b].
וְדָבָר זֶה נִתְגַּלָּה לָרִאשׁוֹנָה בְּבֵיאוּר גָּמוּר עַל יְדֵי בִּלְעָם, שֶׁכָּל פָּרָשָׁתוֹ הוּא עַל עִנְיַן מַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
And this principle was first revealed with absolute clarity through Balaam, whose entire biblical narrative centers on this supreme virtue of Israel:
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יַגְדִּילוּ חֲטָאִים זוֹ עַל זוֹ, אֵין אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִיתֶּקֶת מֵהֶם כִּמְלֹא נִימָא
that even if their sins multiply and pile one upon another, the love of the Blessed Name is never severed from them by even a hairsbreadth
[וְהוּא הָיָה מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק דְּאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
[and Balaam stood as the absolute antithesis of this, as stated in chapter Chelek that he has no portion in the World to Come;
וְעִם כָּל מַעֲלָתוֹ שֶׁהָיָה נְבִיא אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְדוּגְמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
and despite all his virtue as prophet of the gentiles mirroring Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
וַאֲפִילּוּ יוֹסִיף מַעֲלוֹת זֶה עַל גַּבֵּי זֶה, וְכֵן אָמַר: "אֶת שִׁבְעַת הַמִּזְבְּחֹת עָרַכְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר" בַּעֲבוֹדָה –
and even if he piled virtues one upon another, professing in worship: 'I have prepared the seven altars, etc.'—
אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם וְאַחֲרִיתוֹ עֲדֵי אֹבֵד.
it amounts to nothing, and his end is unto destruction.
וְדַיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי הַהֵיפֶךְ מִתְגַּלֶּה מַעֲלָה זוֹ, כְּעִנְיַן: אֵין שְׁבָחָהּ שֶׁל מַטְרוֹנִיתָא וְכוּלֵי (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת עֵקֶב)].
And precisely through the opposite is this virtue revealed, in the spirit of: 'The praise of the matron is not recognized, etc.' (Midrash Rabbah, Eikev)].
וּקְרָאוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בִּדְבָרִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א): "מַחֲלִיק לָשׁוֹן", שֶׁהֶחֱלִיק וְכוּלֵי וְנָפְלוּ עַל יָדוֹ;
And our Sages of blessed memory called him (Devarim Rabbah 1) a "flatterer" who smoothed his tongue, causing them to stumble through his seductive words;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה:): מִבִּרְכָתוֹ אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ מַה הָיָה בְּלִבּוֹ, וְנֶאֱמַר: "וַיַּהֲפֹךְ ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְּךָ אֶת הַקְּלָלָה לִבְרָכָה";
and so they said (Sanhedrin 105b): "From his blessing you may discern what was in his heart," as it is written: "and Hashem your God turned the curse into a blessing for you" (Deuteronomy 23:6);
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, סג עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְהַכְנִיס עַיִן הָרָע.
and our Sages stated in the Zohar (Part III, 63b) that he sought to cast an evil eye upon them.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי יָדַע שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַמַּעֲשִׂים יוּכַל לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
That is, because he knew that through practical deeds even the spiritual root can potentially be altered,
וְהוּא לֹא הוֹדִיעָם זֶה, רַק הֶחֱלִיק לָשׁוֹן כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּבְטְחוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה וְיֶחֶטְאוּ וְיִשְׁתַּנֶּה הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
yet he did not inform them of this, but flattered them with smooth speech so that they would become complacent, sin, and thereby have their root altered;
וְזֶה שֶׁהָיָה בְּלִבּוֹ: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ
and this is what was hidden in his heart: that they should become the absolute opposite
[וְגַם כִּי כָּל הַשָּׂגוֹת אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא דּוּגְמַת מַשִּׂיג בַּחֲלוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּשׁוּב ה' וְגוֹמֵר",
[and also because all of a person's perceptions in this world of the World to Come resemble a dream, as written: 'When Hashem brings back, etc., we were like dreamers,'
וְהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִקְרָא שׁוֹרֶשׁ וְיָכוֹל לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
and the World to Come is termed 'root' and can be altered as noted above;
וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נה.): חֶלְמָא טָבָא חֶדְוָותֵיהּ מִסְתַּיֵּיהּ, וְכָל יָמָיו שֶׁל דָּוִד לֹא רָאָה חֲלוֹם טוֹב,
and they said (Berakhot 55a): 'For a good dream, the joy it brings suffices,' and throughout David's days he never saw a good dream,
וּלְכָךְ בִּקֵּשׁ הוּא דִּיהֵא חֶדְוָותֵיהּ מִסְתַּיֵּיהּ,
which is why he [Balaam] sought that 'its joy suffice',
וּלְכָךְ מַזְכִּירִים בַּהֲטָבַת חֲלוֹם הֲפוֹךְ קִלְלַת בִּלְעָם] –
and why in the prayer for transforming bad dreams we mention the inversion of Balaam's curse] –
וְהַיְינוּ עַיִן הָרָע וּמַחֲלִיק.
and this was his evil eye and flattery.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָפַךְ, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן: שֶׁגַּם שֶׁיֶּחֶטְאוּ לֹא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּלָל;
And the Blessed Name inverted it, ensuring that in ultimate truth it remains thus: even when they sin, their essential root is never altered at all;
וּלְכָךְ נִקְבְּעוּ דְּבָרָיו בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן.
and therefore his words were canonized within the Torah, because this is absolute divine truth.
וְנִמְצָא נֶהֶפְכוּ דְּבָרָיו לִבְרָכָה מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַכֹּל בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן.
And it turns out that his words were converted into blessing, since everything is in truth so
[וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הָיָה אָדָם שֶׁיָּדַע אֲמִיתַּת דָּבָר זֶה כָּמוֹהוּ,
[and concerning King Solomon, peace be upon him, no man knew the truth of this like him,
וּלְכָךְ בָּטַח לַעֲבוֹר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַל פִּי דַעְתּוֹ,
and therefore he relied upon it to transgress biblical restrictions based on his own reasoning,
וּלְכָךְ בִּקְשׁוּ לְדוּנוֹ לְאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֲבָל לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָם,
leading the Sages to seek to exclude him from the World to Come, yet they could not,
וְלָכֵן נִיתַּן בִּלְעָם תְּמוּרָתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר]:
and therefore Balaam was substituted in his stead, as I wrote elsewhere].

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Achrei Mot 20:124-21:130: ‘There is a person through whom curses are destined to be fulfilled: wherever he directs his gaze, he brings curses, blight, and terror. Such was Balaam, who was called ‘evil-eyed’: he was suited to every evil and was not suited to good. Even when he blessed, his blessing was no blessing and did not endure. When he cursed, however, his curse against anyone was fulfilled, even in a single moment. Therefore it is written: ‘Open of eye’ (Numbers 24:3). Wherever his eye held sway became cursed. Come and see what is written: ‘He turned his face toward the wilderness’ (Numbers 24:1), so that he might arouse from that side the power ruling there, and it would bring an accusation against Israel. What is written of the priests? ‘One with a good eye shall be blessed’ (Proverbs 22:9), for he is suited to this, and blessing rests in his gaze. Therefore we learned: A person should turn aside even from a hundred roads rather than encounter someone who has an evil eye.’

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Masei 11:3: “This is the meaning of the exposition, “Do not trust in an intimate companion”: If the evil inclination tells you, “Sin, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will forgive you,” do not believe it. “An intimate companion” means the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, “You are the intimate companion of my youth.” Why is the blessed God called an aluf here? The evil inclination tempts a person by saying that God will afterward clarify that the person’s deed was bound at its root to God and that deliberate sins will become merits. Even when He was an aluf—a king without a crown—He was nevertheless “the intimate companion of my youth.” This is how Bilaam magnified Israel on this basis. Thus the Midrash expounds: “One who smooths his tongue”—this is Bilaam, who flattered them through his prophecies, so that their hearts became proud and they fell at Shittim. He made it seem easy to them by saying that God would clarify all Israel’s deeds for the good, and through this they fell at Shittim. Concerning this it says, “Do not believe in a friend”—the evil inclination—and “Do not trust in an intimate companion,” that God will clarify Israel’s deed. That applies only after the deed, when one repents out of love, so that it becomes a merit. But one who relies on this, Heaven forbid—one who says, “I will sin and repent”—is not given assistance to repent.”

sections.en: In This World, the Primary Foundation Is the Purity of the Heart, as Stated

p: [קלב] בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָעִיקָּר הוּא טָהֳרַת הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:): רַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי.
In this world, the primary foundation is the purity of the heart, as they said (Sanhedrin 106b): the Merciful One desires the heart.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי שָׁם מִשְׁכַּן הַיֵּצֶר וְשָׁם הוּא הַיְגִיעָה.
And that is because there lies the dwelling place of the evil inclination, and there unfolds the spiritual labor.
אֲבָל הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַנִּיחָא, שָׁם הָעִיקָּר הוּא בַּחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
But in the World to Come, which is the realm of tranquil rest, the primary foundation is in the wisdom residing within the mind,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ (מְנָחוֹת כט:): "כִּי בְּיָהּ ה' צוּר עוֹלָמִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, ד) – בְּיוֹ"ד נִבְרָא עוֹלָם הַבָּא וּבְהֵ"א עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
as they expounded: "for in Yah Hashem is an everlasting rock" (Isaiah 26:4)—with the letter Yud the World to Come was created, and with the letter Hei this world was created (Menachot 29b).
וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁהַיּוֹ"ד רוֹמֵז לַחָכְמָה, וְהַהֵ"א לַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And it is known that the Yud alludes to Chokhmah (Wisdom), and the Hei to Binah (Understanding) in the heart
[וְאָמְרוּ: הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כִּפְרוֹזְדּוֹר, וּמִי שֶׁלֹּא הִתְקִין עַצְמוֹ בּוֹ אֵין יָכוֹל לִכְנוֹס לִטְרַקְלִין,
[and they said: 'This world is like an antechamber, and he who does not prepare himself in it cannot enter the banquet hall' (Avot 4:16),
הוּא כְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת לא:): מָשָׁל לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ מַפְתְּחוֹת הַפְּנִימִיּוֹת וְהַחִיצוֹנוֹת לֹא מָסְרוּ לוֹ, בְּהֵי עָיֵיל?
matching Shabbat 31b: 'a parable of one who holds the inner keys while the outer keys were not delivered to him—how can he enter?';
עַיֵּין יוֹמָא (עב:) שֶׁלָּמְדוּ זֶה מִפָּסוּק "וְלֵב אָיִן"].
see Yoma 72b where they derived this from 'and he has no heart'].
וּלְכָךְ שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נז:),
Therefore Shabbat, which is a foretaste of the World to Come (Berakhot 57b):
מִי שֶׁזָּכָה לִטְעוֹם מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו זוֹכֶה לְהַשִּׂיג אָז חָכְמָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
whoever has merited to taste from the fruit of his labors merits to apprehend then divine wisdom from the Blessed Name, reflecting the World to Come.
וּבַלֵּב יֵשׁ שׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו", רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ, וְהַיְינוּ בַּעֲוֹן דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל,

And within the heart there exists an inclination toward evil, as written: "for the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Genesis 8:21)—meaning from his very root, identified with the sin of the Generation of the Flood;
וּלְכָךְ אֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה לָזֶה, דִּלְשׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע אֵין מוֹעִיל, דְּבִישָׁא לָא הָוֵי טָבָא.
and therefore ordinary repentance does not avail for this, for against a corrupted root it is ineffective, since what is inherently evil does not become good.
וְהַיְינוּ תְּשׁוּבָה תַּתָּאָה;
This applies to lower repentance (teshuvah tata'ah);
רַק צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה עִלָּאָה מֵעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי הַמִּתְעוֹרֵר מִן הַחָכְמָה, שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
rather, one requires higher repentance (teshuvah ila'ah) drawn from the World to Come, awakened from Chokhmah, which is the root of roots,
וְשָׁם אֵין רַע כְּלָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה",
and there no evil exists whatsoever within Israel, as we say: "the soul which You gave within me is pure,"
כִּי גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע שָׁרְשׁוֹ "טוֹב מְאֹד" כַּנּוֹדָע
for even the root of evil has its ultimate supernal root in "very good," as is known
[וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קח:) בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל שֶׁהִטְעִימָן מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, הַיְינוּ כְּדֵי לְתַקְּנָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הוֹעִיל]:
[and therefore they stated in Sanhedrin 108b that He gave the Generation of the Flood a taste of the World to Come in order to rectify them, though it did not avail].

paragraphs.text: The preparation that makes lasting wisdom accessible

rich.text: The preparation that makes lasting wisdom accessible

paragraphs.text: The work of the heart in this world prepares a person to receive a more enduring life of wisdom.

rich.text: The work of the heart in this world prepares a person to receive a more enduring life of wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:8: “And the primary focus is certainly Torah, as rebuked in Shabbat (10a): "They abandon eternal life to engage in transient life!"; yet the statement there is also true: there is a time for Torah, and there is a time for prayer; for in truth: "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem" Psalms 111:10, and "if the fear of Hashem is his treasure, yes" (Shabbat 31b), the labor of transient prayer serving as the essential preparation to merit eternal life, as in Avot (4:16): "Prepare yourself in the vestibule," and "he who did not toil on Friday, what shall he eat on the Sabbath?"”

rich.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:8

: “And the primary focus is certainly Torah, as rebuked in Shabbat (10a): "They abandon eternal life to engage in transient life!"; yet the statement there is also true: there is a time for Torah, and there is a time for prayer; for in truth: "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem" Psalms 111:10, and "if the fear of Hashem is his treasure, yes" (Shabbat 31b), the labor of transient prayer serving as the essential preparation to merit eternal life, as in Avot (4:16): "Prepare yourself in the vestibule," and "he who did not toil on Friday, what shall he eat on the Sabbath?"”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Likkutei Maamarim preserves both sides of the relationship: Torah is eternal life, yet the effort of prayer and yirah remains its necessary preparation. Its reference to preparing in the antechamber explains the siman’s image of the missing outer key. Intellectual attainment alone does not perform the heart’s work of preparing to enter.

paragraphs.text: Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:19-21: “Although this teaching says without qualification that there is no repentance for it, we must explain this matter, for we hold that there is nothing for which repentance is unavailable: the Holy One, blessed be He, accepted even Menashe. Why, then, should this transgression differ from the others? It seems to me that the meaning is that the matter does not depend on lower repentance, as with other people who cause a blemish, whose initial return is through lower repentance—turning away from evil—and who are immediately accepted. This also follows from the adjacent wording: “There is no sinner who does not behold the face of the Divine Presence except this one.” The reason is that this sin affects both the Tzaddik and the Divine Presence, as explained; because the Divine Presence is his accuser, he is not accepted through that repentance. In this way we understand the verse, “The face of Hashem is against evildoers, to cut off their remembrance from the earth. They cried out, and Hashem heard.” The evildoers are those who emit seed in vain, who are cut off from the land of life because the blemish affects it. But they cried out and returned in repentance, and Hashem heard and saved them from all their troubles. The Zohar explains: Rabbi Yehudah said, Great is crying out, for it tears up a person’s decree for all his days. Rabbi Yitzchak says, Great is crying out, for it has power over the supernal attribute of judgment. Rabbi Yosei says, Great is crying out, for it has power in this world and the World to Come; through crying out one inherits this world and the World to Come, as it is written, “They cried out to Hashem in their trouble; He delivered them from their distress.” Thus crying out is above lower repentance according to all these explanations, and therefore “Hashem heard.” The meaning is that his repentance is difficult, until he reaches higher repentance.”

paragraphs.text: Tomer Devorah 4:1-2: “It is to return in repentance, for nothing is as important as repentance, since it repairs every blemish. Just as Binah sweetens all judgments and removes their bitterness, so a person should repent and repair every blemish. One who thinks of repentance throughout his days causes Binah to illuminate all his days; all his days are thus in repentance, that is, he includes himself in Binah, which is repentance, and his lifetime is crowned with the mystery of higher repentance. See that repentance contains the root of all things that exist, in the mystery of the Jubilee. The root of the external forces—the river of fire, included in holiness through the powers of judgment—is rooted there. From there it spreads and is called the spreading of fierce anger. Through the mystery of “Hashem smelled the pleasing aroma,” that expansion returns to its source, judgments are sweetened, anger is quieted, and Hashem relents concerning the calamity. A person likewise effects this mystery through repentance. Repentance also benefits evil: Do not say that repentance benefits only the holy part of a person: the evil part within him is also sweetened, in the likeness of this attribute. Know this, for Kayin was evil and came from the serpent, yet it was said to him, “If you do well, will you not be lifted up?” Do not think that because you come from the side of evil there is no repair for you; that is false. If you do well and root yourself in repentance, you can ascend there through the good rooted there, for every supernal bitterness has a sweet root, and one can enter through that root and make oneself good.”

sections.en: The Torah Operates Directly Upon the Heart of Man

p: [קלג] הַתּוֹרָה הִיא פּוֹעֶלֶת בְּלֵב הָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי, פְּתִיחְתָּא ב): הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ מַחֲזִירוֹ לְמוּטָב, וְעַל שֵׁם כָּךְ נִקְרָא תּוֹרָה.
The Torah operates directly upon the heart of man, as they said (Eichah Rabbah, Petichta 2): the illumination within it returns him to good, and for this reason it is termed Torah (instruction).
אֲבָל יֵשׁ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהֵם מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (קו:) עַל דּוֹאֵג,
But there are words of Torah which remain merely from the lips outward, as stated in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 106b) concerning Doeg,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לָמָּה זֶּה מְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה וְלֶב אָיִן" (מִשְׁלֵי יז, טז),
and regarding this Scripture states: "Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?" (Proverbs 17:16),

וְזֶה נִקְרָא "פִּטְטַיָּא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא", דְּגַם כֵּן טָבִין לְהָבִיא הָאָדָם לִידֵי תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים נ:) שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי [כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת נ"ט], אִם אֵין הַחֵטְא גּוֹרֵם כִּבְדוֹאֵג.

and this is called "idle chatter of the Torah," which is nonetheless good to bring a person to authentic Torah, as they said (Pesachim 50b): from not for its own sake one comes to its own sake [as I wrote above in Section 59], provided sin does not intervene as with Doeg.
אֲבָל הָעִיקָּר הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּכְנָס לַלֵּב;
However, the ultimate core consists of words of Torah that penetrate the heart;
וְאֵיזֶה נִכְנָס לַלֵּב? כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא צָמֵא וּמִשְׁתּוֹקֵק מְאֹד,
and which words penetrate the heart? When a person is deeply thirsty and intensely yearns,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וָאֹכְלָה וַתְּהִי בְפִי כִּדְבַשׁ לְמָתוֹק" (יְחֶזְקֵאל ג, ג), שֶׁהוּא כְּעִנְיַן: "וְתוֹרָתְךָ בְּתוֹךְ מֵעָי" (תְּהִלִּים מ, ט), פֵּירוּשׁ נִבְלָעָה בְּכָל הָאֵבָרִים.

matching: "and I ate it, and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness" (Ezekiel 3:3), which is as: "and Your Torah is within my inward parts" (Psalms 40:9), meaning absorbed throughout all the limbs.
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא (פֶּרֶק יד): אֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִבְלָעִים בְּלֵב הָאָדָם אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁהוּא עָיֵיף לָהֶם.
And so it is stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta (chapter 14): words of Torah are not absorbed into the heart of man unless he is weary for them.
וְהָעֲיֵיפוּת וְהַצִּמָּאוֹן הוּא מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ שֶׁחָסֵר בַּדָּבָר וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְהַשְׁלִימוֹ.
And weariness and thirst emerge from the perception of lack, feeling deficient in a matter and recognizing that words of Torah are needed to complete him.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת לא.): אִי יִרְאַת ה' הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ – אִין, וְאִי לָא – לָא;
And concerning this they said (Shabbat 31a): "If the fear of Hashem is his storehouse, yes; and if not, no";
פֵּירוּשׁ, הַיִּרְאָה הוּא הַרְגָּשַׁת הַחִסָּרוֹן, שֶׁמִּזֶּה יַגִּיעַ הַיִּרְאָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עֵקֶב עֲנָוָה יִרְאַת ה'" (מִשְׁלֵי כב, ד), וְהִיא הָאוֹצָר לְקַבֵּל בָּהּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.

for fear is the awareness of deficiency from which true awe arrives, as written: "The reward of humility is the fear of Hashem" (Proverbs 22:4), and this humility serves as the treasury to receive words of Torah.
וְהַצִּמָּאוֹן הוּא בַּלֵּב מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (תּוֹלְדוֹת קלח עַמּוּד א) דְּאִלְמָלֵא יֵצֶר הָרָע חֶדְוָותָא דִּשְׁמַעְתָּא לָא לֶהֱוֵי.
And thirst resides in the heart from the side of the inclination, as written in Midrash HaNe'elam (Toldot 138a) that were it not for the evil inclination, the joy of legal learning would not exist.

וּכְשֶׁמִּתְמַלֵּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ שֶׁנִּבְלָעִין בַּלֵּב, אָז הוּא תִּיקּוּן חַטֹּאת יִצְרָא דַּעֲבֵירָה, שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים:

And when the heart is replenished through words of Torah originating in the mind and absorbed into the heart, that constitutes the rectification for the sins of the inclination to transgress, achieved through Torah as I wrote above many times.

paragraphs.text: The heart receives Torah when the learner seeks its inward content rather than resting in its outer form.

rich.text: The heart receives Torah when the learner seeks its inward content rather than resting in its outer form.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Ki Tavo 6: “My holy grandfather explained that a heart signifies inwardness. The principal thing in every matter is its inward content and the utterance of Hashem's mouth within it. Even the inward content of the 613 commandments is Torah, as the Zohar says (Shemini 35b), through Torah the Holy One created the world. The purpose of every matter is words of Torah. Thus the verse says (Proverbs 17:16), ‘Why is there a price in a fool's hand to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart?’ The fool does not want the inward content of the matter and is at rest with the garment itself. Israel, however, do not rest in any garment of this world; in every matter they want its inward content, and do not want things in which they do not see Heaven's honor. Even their intention in worldly benefit and pleasure is to be able to serve Hashem with that strength. Their whole aim is to fulfill His will. Hashem therefore says that all their worldly benefits are included in His will, since they serve Him with that strength.”

This clarifies the positive side of Rav Tzadok's thirst: the learner feels that outward possession alone has not yet given him what he needs, and seeks the divine life within what he learns.

paragraphs.text: Or HaChaim on Leviticus 18:2:8: “This is what David meant when he said, “I desire to do Your will, my God, and Your Torah is within my innards.” Through the abundance of his attachment to the Master of masters, blessed be His name forever, even the heart was transformed to act as the soul acts: desire and longing arose within it to do His will. He was not among those who desire things distant from holiness and must restrain them by refusing consent; rather, of himself he desired His will, rejecting those things that the heart naturally desires and longs for. This is why he precisely said “I desire,” for the sensory desire had ceased. Elsewhere he said, “My heart is slain within me.” “Your Torah is within my innards” means that his longing for holy service was so great that, when studying Hashem’s Torah, he felt as though he were eating and filling his innards with natural nourishment.”

paragraphs.text: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta 14:1: “The beginning and end of all matters are fear of Heaven and good deeds. A person should not read Scripture and study Mishnah while lacking fear of Heaven, as it is said, “The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem; good understanding belongs to all who practice them,” and, “The end of the matter, all having been heard: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.” Who makes himself poor? One who indulges excessively in eating, drinking, and sleeping, as it is said, “The drunkard and glutton will become poor, and drowsiness will clothe one in rags,” and, “Do not love sleep, lest you become poor; open your eyes and be satisfied with bread.” Bread and wine mean words of Torah, as it is said, “Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed,” and, “The Lord God has given me a learned tongue, to know how to sustain the weary with a word; morning by morning He awakens my ear to hear like the learned.” You have thus learned that words of Torah are absorbed into a person’s heart only in one who is weary for them.”

sections.en: Sometimes It Appears to a Person That He Has Already Repented and His Sins…

p: [קלד] פְּעָמִים נִדְמֶה לָאָדָם שֶׁכְּבָר שָׁב וְנִמְחֲלוּ חֲטָאָיו, וְאַחַר זְמַן חוֹזֵר וּמִתְעוֹרֵר לְהִתְמַרְמֵר עַל חֲטָאָיו וּמַרְגִּישׁ שֶׁשְּׁנֵי הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת אֵינָם דִּמְיוֹן.

Sometimes it appears to a person that he has already repented and his sins have been forgiven, yet after a time he is reawakened to feel bitter anguish over his sins, sensing that neither of these two thoughts is an illusion.
וּבֶאֱמֶת שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת, דְּקַיְימָא לַן (יוֹמָא פו:): עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁהִתְוַדָּה יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים זֶה, חוֹזֵר וּמִתְוַדֶּה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הַבָּא,
And in truth both are truth, for we establish (Yoma 86b): sins that one confessed on this Yom Kippur, he confesses again on the following Yom Kippur,
וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁהַהֲלָכָה דְּלֹא זָז מִשָּׁם עַד שֶׁמּוֹחֲלִין לוֹ, וַהֲרֵי גַּם זֶה אֱמֶת.
even regarding sins concerning which the halakhah states that one does not move from his place before he is forgiven, that too being absolute truth.
רַק כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֵין שִׁיעוּר לְכָל מַעֲלוֹת הָאָדָם בְּמַדְרֵגָתוֹ, כָּךְ אֵין שִׁיעוּר לְמַדְרֵגוֹת הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
Rather, just as there is no limit to the ascending spiritual virtues of man, so there is no limit to the rungs of repentance.
וּכְפִי מַעֲלַת הָאָדָם וְהַשָּׂגָתוֹ, כָּךְ הוּא תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ.
And commensurate with a person's stature and perception, such is his repentance.
כִּי כָּל עִנְיְנֵי הָאָדָם עַל יַחַס אֶחָד, וְהָאָדָם אֵינוֹ עוֹמֵד בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד,
For all affairs of man operate in dynamic proportion, and man never remains stagnant in one place;
כִּי עַל זֶה נִתְאוֹנֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קוֹדֶם פְּטִירָתוֹ: "לֹא אוּכַל עוֹד וְגוֹמֵר", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי", וְנִקְרָא "נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ",

concerning this Moses our teacher lamented prior to his passing: "I can no more go out and come in" (Deuteronomy 31:2), as written: "free among the dead" (Psalms 88:6), death being termed "his soul rested,"
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין נָח לְעוֹלָם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הוּא מַרְגִּישׁ.
whereas in this world a person never rests, even when he does not feel it.
וְכָל מִי שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ טוֹב דִּגְמִירֵי דְּלָא הָוֵי בִּישָׁא, הוּא הוֹלֵךְ מִמַּעֲלָה לְמַעֲלָה בְּטוֹבָה, וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ,
And whoever possesses a good root—concerning whom it is established that he does not turn bad—ascends from level to level in goodness, and conversely,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קנב.): זִקְנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים כָּל זְמַן שֶׁמַּזְקִינִין וְכוּלֵי, זִקְנֵי עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְכוּלֵי.
as they said: as elderly Torah scholars age, their wisdom settles, whereas as elderly boors age, their confusion increases (Shabbat 152a).
וּלְכָךְ כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ אֶל מַעֲלָה וּמַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה, אָז כְּפִי מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ לֹא הִתְחִיל לָשׁוּב עֲדַיִן, וְחַטָּאתוֹ נֶגְדּוֹ תָּמִיד מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא
And therefore, when he reaches a higher, more elevated rung, relative to this new level he has not even begun to repent, and his sin stands before him anew from level to level
[וּכְשֶׁהוּא בַּמַּדְרֵגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה כְּבָר תִּיקֵּן כְּפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ הַחֵטְא וְכֵן בְּכָל דַּרְגִּין וְעוֹלָמוֹת וְאֵין עוֹד רֹשֶׁם;
[and while on the lower rung he had already rectified the sin according to that level, with no remaining trace throughout those worlds;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּשֶׁמִּתְעַלֶּה, חוֹזֵר הַחֵטְא בְּכָל תָּקְפּוֹ, וְדָבָר זֶה עָמוֹק בַּחָכְמָה.
nevertheless when he ascends, the sin re-emerges in full force relative to the higher light, and this matter is profound in wisdom.
וּלְכָךְ כְּשֶׁעָלָה אַחֵר לַמַּדְרֵגוֹת, אָז נִתְגַּלָּה הַטִּינָא שֶׁהָיְתָה בְּלִבּוֹ בְּיַלְדוּת;
And therefore when Acher (Elisha ben Avuyah) ascended to higher rungs, the subtle stain present in his heart from youth was exposed;
וּבְוַדַּאי מִי שֶׁעָלָה לַפַּרְדֵּס וְהָיָה בְּמַעֲלָה גְּדוֹלָה כָּל כָּךְ, מִסְּתָמָא שָׁב עַל טִינָא שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ וְחַטֹּאת נַעֲרוּתוֹ.
and certainly one who entered the Pardes and stood at such exalted stature had previously repented for the flaws of his youth.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 7:4: “The quality of all the Patriarchs was exertion in the service of the blessed God, as stated in Sanhedrin 96a: “When I pay the reward of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who ran before Me like horses,” and so on. This was especially true of Abraham our father, whose occupation was the holiness of positive commandments, rooted in love and alacrity. As they said in Chullin 16a, “The verse teaches us Abraham’s alacrity.” He never became still or rested from exerting himself in action in the service of the blessed God. This is what was said to him: “Go for yourself”—to set your own level right, as stated in the holy Zohar. He was to keep moving from level to level in his quality of love. This corresponds to reaching the passage “You shall love.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Lech Lecha describes Avraham’s service as movement that does not become stationary, with each level calling for further action rooted in love. This supplies the positive setting for the renewed teshuvah described here. The return of an awareness of sin can reflect a higher measure of understanding, rather than prove that the earlier forgiveness was unreal. The present siman explicitly affirms both experiences as true; the parallel explains why growth itself generates a new task.

sections.en: One Who Feels That He Possesses No Desire in Heart or Mind for The…

p: [קלה] מִי שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם חֵשֶׁק בְּלֵב וּמוֹחַ לַעֲבוֹדַת ה', אָז הָעֵצָה: "הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה' יְהָבְךָ" (תְּהִלִּים נה, כג).
One who feels that he possesses no desire in heart or mind for the service of Hashem, the counsel for him is: "Cast your burden upon Hashem" (Psalms 55:23).
וּמִתּוֹךְ שִׁפְלוּת דַּעְתוֹ בְּהַכָּרַת חֶסְרוֹנוֹ מְעוֹרֵר רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם,
And through his lowliness of spirit in recognizing his profound deficiency, he awakens Heavenly mercy,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "תַּאֲוַת עֲנָוִים שָׁמַעְתָּ ה' תָּכִין לִבָּם וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם י, יז), שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה הוּא תַּאֲוַת הָעֲנָוִים וּמַכִּירִים שִׁפְלוּתָם שֶׁלֵּב אָיִן – הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵכִין לִבָּם;

as written: "You have heard the desire of the humble, Hashem; You will direct their heart, etc." (Psalms 10:17), for this very longing is the desire of the humble who recognize their lowliness and lack of heart—and the Holy One prepares their heart;
כִּידוּעַ "ה' צִלְּךָ", כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּמַדְרֵגַת "אַיִן", מַשִּׂיג מַעֲלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן בְּמַדְרֵגַת "אַיִן",
for as is known, "Hashem is your shadow": when a person is at the level of Ayin (Nothingness), he grasps the transcendence of the Blessed Name likewise at the level of Ayin,
וְיָכוֹל לְהַמְשִׁיךְ וּלְהוֹלִיד יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן [כְּעִנְיַן "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא"],
and is empowered to draw down and generate substance from nothingness (yesh me'ayin) [matching "Create in me a clean heart"],
וְהוּא חָכְמָה בַּמּוֹחַ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יֵשׁ מִיֵּשׁ – רָצוֹן וְחֵשֶׁק בַּלֵּב;
which is wisdom in the brain, followed by substance from substance (yesh mi-yesh)—will and desire in the heart;
פֵּירוּשׁ, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לוֹ שֶׁאֵין זוּלָתוֹ כְּלָל עַכְשָׁו כְּעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ,
meaning that the Blessed Name illuminates for him that there is none beside Him now just as before the world was created, the glory of Hashem filling the entire earth;
וּכְשֶׁדָּבָר זֶה מֵאִיר לְעֵינֵי הָאָדָם, אָז תֵּיכֶף נוֹלָדִים רְצוֹנוֹת בְּמוֹחַ וָלֵב.
and when this reality radiates before a person's eyes, holy desires are immediately born within mind and heart.
אֲבָל צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת מִקּוֹדֶם "אָבְדוּ גוֹיִם מֵאַרְצוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים י, טז)
— But prior to this there must be "the nations are perished out of His land" (Psalms 10:16)—
פֵּירוּשׁ, תְּשׁוּבָה עַל הָעֲבֵירוֹת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "בָּאוּ גוֹיִם בְּנַחֲלָתֶךָ" (שָׁם עט, א),
meaning repentance over transgressions in physical deed, concerning which it is said: "the nations are come into Your inheritance" (Psalms 79:1);
כִּידוּעַ שֶׁאֶרֶץ רוֹמֵז לַגּוּף וְכֹחוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, וְגוֹיִם הֵם כֹּחוֹת הַהָפְכִיִּים מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for "land" alludes to the physical body and faculties of action, and "nations" are the forces opposing the will of the Blessed Name,
וַאֲבִידָתָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה תַּתָּאָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים, שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ כִּשְׁגָגוֹת,
and their perishing is achieved through at least lower repentance (teshuvah tata'ah), wherein willful sins become like inadvertent errors,
וְאָז מִתְדַּבֵּק בַּמַּדְרֵגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה מִמַּדְרֵגַת עֶשֶׂר קְדוּשׁוֹת דִּתְנַן בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּכֵלִים, שֶׁהִיא קְדוּשַׁת הָאָרֶץ.
and then one attaches himself to the lowest of the ten sanctities enumerated in the first chapter of Kelim, which is the sanctity of the Land.
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי בְּכָל מָקוֹם נָעוּץ סוֹפָהּ בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ,
And it is known that everywhere its end is wedged in its beginning,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לָבוֹא לַעֲנָוָה וּמַדְרֵגַת "אַיִן", שֶׁהִיא קְדוּשַׁת הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קכא עַמּוּד א),
and through this one can attain humility and the level of Ayin, which corresponds to the sanctity of the Holy of Holies (Zohar II:121a),
וּמִשָּׁם אוֹרָה יוֹצְאָה לָעוֹלָם, שֶׁהוּא "תָּכִין לִבָּם", כְּעִנְיַן הַמָּאוֹר מַחֲזִירוֹ לְמוּטָב:
and from there light issues forth into the world, fulfilling "You will direct their heart," in the manner of the illumination returning one to good.

paragraphs.text: Receiving the vessel together with the gift

paragraphs.text: Prayer can ask for the heart’s capacity to receive, as well as the benefit itself.

rich.text: Prayer can ask for the heart’s capacity to receive, as well as the benefit itself.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 21:1: “‘Grant us, Hashem our God, the blessing of Your appointed times.’ Every festival has its particular blessing. On this festival the principal blessing is the receptive vessel that Hashem builds in Israel's heart to receive all good. Therefore we pray ‘Grant us’: that Hashem arrange within us this vessel to receive every good at its time, when He too is occupied in bestowing it upon us. This is like ‘Prepare their heart; incline Your ear’ (Psalms 10:17): Hashem gives the vessel together with the good. That is the principal matter of this festival. ‘As You desired and promised to bless us’ means that on the festival Hashem stands in great favor toward creation. ‘Sanctify us through Your commandments’ means that all the benefits should be for us only the joy of a mitzvah, through which it will be easier to serve Hashem. ‘Give us our portion in Your Torah’ means that He open the mitzvah's inward content, and it will shine like Torah, as in a mitzvah at its time, as the Gemara teaches (Kiddushin 33). ‘Purify our heart to serve You in truth’ means removing all the barriers from the heart's inner point, leaving only service of You in truth.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim makes explicit what the siman means by Hashem preparing the heart: He gives both the good and the vessel through which it can be received at its proper time. The rest of the passage identifies that vessel with joy in a mitzvah, inward Torah and a purified heart. This develops the prayer for desire while preserving Rav Tzadok's prior requirement to turn away from wrongful deeds.
