paragraphs.text: Mishnah Kelim 1:6-9: “There are ten degrees of holiness. The Land of Israel is holier than all other lands. What is its holiness? From it the omer offering, first fruits, and the two loaves are brought, whereas they are not brought from other lands. Walled towns are holier than it, for those afflicted with tzaraat are sent out of them, and a corpse may be carried around within them as long as desired; once it has gone out, it is not brought back. Within the wall of Jerusalem is holier than these, for offerings of lesser sanctity and the second tithe are eaten there. The Temple Mount is holier than it, for men and women with an abnormal discharge, menstruating women, and women after childbirth may not enter there. The Cheil is holier than it, for non-Jews and those impure through contact with the dead may not enter there. The Women’s Courtyard is holier than it, for one who has immersed that day but awaits sunset may not enter there, though entry does not incur a sin offering. The Israelites’ Courtyard is holier than it, for one who still lacks the offering that completes purification may not enter there, and entry in the relevant state of impurity incurs a sin offering. The Priests’ Courtyard is holier than it, for Israelites enter only when needed for laying hands on an offering, slaughtering, or waving. Between the Entrance Hall and the altar is holier than it, for priests with bodily blemishes or untrimmed hair may not enter there. The Sanctuary is holier than it, for one who has not washed his hands and feet may not enter there. The Holy of Holies is holier than these, for only the High Priest enters there, on Yom Kippur, at the time of the service. Rabbi Yosei said: In five respects the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar is equal to the Sanctuary: priests with blemishes, untrimmed hair, those who have drunk wine, and those who have not washed their hands and feet may not enter there, and people withdraw from between the Entrance Hall and the altar during the burning of incense.”

rich.text: : “There are ten degrees of holiness. The Land of Israel is holier than all other lands. What is its holiness? From it the omer offering, first fruits, and the two loaves are brought, whereas they are not brought from other lands. Walled towns are holier than it, for those afflicted with tzaraat are sent out of them, and a corpse may be carried around within them as long as desired; once it has gone out, it is not brought back. Within the wall of Jerusalem is holier than these, for offerings of lesser sanctity and the second tithe are eaten there. The Temple Mount is holier than it, for men and women with an abnormal discharge, menstruating women, and women after childbirth may not enter there. The Cheil is holier than it, for non-Jews and those impure through contact with the dead may not enter there. The Women’s Courtyard is holier than it, for one who has immersed that day but awaits sunset may not enter there, though entry does not incur a sin offering. The Israelites’ Courtyard is holier than it, for one who still lacks the offering that completes purification may not enter there, and entry in the relevant state of impurity incurs a sin offering. The Priests’ Courtyard is holier than it, for Israelites enter only when needed for laying hands on an offering, slaughtering, or waving. Between the Entrance Hall and the altar is holier than it, for priests with bodily blemishes or untrimmed hair may not enter there. The Sanctuary is holier than it, for one who has not washed his hands and feet may not enter there. The Holy of Holies is holier than these, for only the High Priest enters there, on Yom Kippur, at the time of the service. Rabbi Yosei said: In five respects the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar is equal to the Sanctuary: priests with blemishes, untrimmed hair, those who have drunk wine, and those who have not washed their hands and feet may not enter there, and people withdraw from between the Entrance Hall and the altar during the burning of incense.”

paragraphs.text: Context: The Mishnah supplies the ascending degrees from the holiness of the Land to the Holy of Holies. Its concrete distinctions and Rabbi Yosei’s qualification are retained; Rav Tzadok uses this hierarchy as an analogy for the movement from action to the highest root.

sections.en: When a Person Prospers and Fortune Smiles Upon Him

p: [קלו] כַּאֲשֶׁר הָאָדָם מַצְלִיחַ וְהַשָּׁעָה מְשַׂחֶקֶת לוֹ, הוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה מַחֲזִיקִין אוֹתוֹ לְצַדִּיק בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת;
When a person prospers and fortune smiles upon him, it is because at that moment he is accounted as righteous throughout all worlds;
שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ז:): וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁזּוֹכֶה בַּדִּין, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מָרוֹם מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ" (תְּהִלִּים י, ה),
for they said (Berakhot 7b): "and not only that, but he is vindicated in judgment," meaning in the Heavenly Court, as written: "Your judgments are on high" (Psalms 10:5),
וְשָׁם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִזְכּוֹת אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי מִצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לב.),
and there it is impossible to be vindicated except through mitzvot and good deeds (Shabbat 32a),
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁזּוֹכֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מִצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לְיָדוֹ אֵיזֶה מִצְוָה שֶׁעֲבוּרָהּ מַגִּיעַ לוֹ זֶה.
so perforce he merits because he possesses mitzvot and good deeds, and the Blessed Name provides some mitzvah through his hands for which this reward is due.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַסְתִּיר אוֹרוֹ לְמַעְלָה כְּרֶגַע, נִדְמֶה בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת שֶׁזֶּה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר.
And when the Blessed Name conceals His light Above for a moment, it appears throughout all worlds as though this person were completely righteous.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה סוֹף פֶּרֶק כ): שְׂכָרוֹ שֶׁל אַשּׁוּר שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ סַנְחֵרִיב;
And therefore they stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 20): the reward of Ashur was that Sennacherib issued from him;
וַהֲרֵי כְּבָר הָיָה אַשּׁוּר אָז בְּעוֹלַם הָאֱמֶת, וּמַה שָּׂכָר הוּא לוֹ טוֹבַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָיָה לְסַנְחֵרִיב, שֶׁיָּדַע שָׁם שֶׁזֶּה הֶבֶל וְשֶׁקֶר?
and behold, Ashur was already in the World of Truth, so what reward to him was the worldly prosperity of Sennacherib, knowing there that this is vanity and falsehood?

רַק כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כַּאֲשֶׁר הִצְלִיחַ סַנְחֵרִיב, הָיָה אָז כָּךְ בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת וְעַד מְקוֹם מַדְרֵגַת אַשּׁוּר בַּמָּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה, כִּי הוּא זַכַּאי וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דוֹר רְשָׁעִים.
Rather, when Sennacherib prospered, it was truly reflected thus across all worlds up to the station of Ashur Above, seeing him as meritorious while the generation of Israel were wicked.
וְהֵם בְּכַבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא אֵיךְ מִדַּת מִשְׁפָּטָיו, אֲבָל עַל כָּל פָּנִים הָיָה כָּךְ, כִּי לוּלֵי כֵן אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁהָיָה נַעֲשָׂה בָּעוֹלָם כֵּן.
And these are the secrets of the Merciful One regarding the nature of His judgments, yet at any rate it was so, for otherwise it could never have occurred in the world.
וְנִתְעַלָּה אַשּׁוּר לְפִי אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה גַּם בְּעוֹלַם הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהוּא בּוֹ.
And Ashur was elevated for that hour even within the World of Truth wherein he dwelled.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת שָׁם): "אַל תְּקַנֵּא בְּעֹשֵׂי עַוְלָה" (תְּהִלִּים לז, א) – לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹהֶם, וּמֵאַיִן יָבוֹא זֶה?
And concerning this they said (Berakhot 7b): "'Do not envy evildoers' (Psalms 37:1)—do not seek to be like them"; whence could such an inclination arise?
אֲבָל הַיְינוּ שֶׁיַּחְשׁוֹב שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הוּא כֵּן;
It means: lest one think that they are genuinely righteous;
וְלֹא דִּבֵּר בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁכְּבָר יָדוּעַ לְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי הוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה, רַק שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָם יֵשׁ כֵּן,
and this was not spoken of gentiles, which every Jew already knows is temporary, but within Israel itself this occurs:
כְּמוֹ דּוֹאֵג בְּעֵת הַצְלָחָתוֹ הָיָה מוּחְזָק בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְצַדִּיק גָּמוּר, וְגַם בְּעִנְיְנֵי עַבְדוּת ה' הָיָה מַצְלִיחַ בְּיָדוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַמִּשְׁפָּט לְהֵיטִיב לוֹ.
like Doeg, who during his prosperity was regarded by Israel as completely righteous, succeeding even in divine service so that the judgment mandated favoring him.
וְצָרִיךְ לָזֶה מְבִינוּת גְּדוֹלָה אֵיזֶה דָּבָר הוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִתְגַּלֶּה לְמַפְרֵעַ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כֵן כְּלָל
And this demands profound discernment to recognize what is merely temporary and later revealed retroactively never to have been truly so
[וְאַדְּרַבָּה, כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת הֵם הֵיפֶךְ עַל דֶּרֶךְ: בַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה מְהַפְּכִין וְכוּלֵי, וְכֵן רְשָׁעִים מְהַפְּכִין מִדַּת הָרַחֲמִים וְכוּלֵי,
[and on the contrary, mitzvot operate inversely, as in: penitents turn [willful sins into merits], etc., and the wicked turn the attribute of mercy [into judgment], etc.,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְחֶסֶד לְאֻמִּים חַטָּאת" (מִשְׁלֵי יד, לד), עַיֵּין בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (י:) דִּלְפִי שָׁעָה חַטָּאת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת לָהֶם],
and as written: 'the kindness of the nations is sin,' see Bava Batra 10b that temporarily it counts against Israel, but ultimately against them],
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמַּצְלִיחַ גַּם בְּתוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת לְפִי מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הָאָדָם:
even though he currently succeeds in Torah and mitzvot according to human sight.

But the judgment above concerns individual souls, and no soul is like another.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:34: “Even Avraham's statement (Genesis 17:18), ‘If only Yishmael would live before You,’ corresponds to ‘Do not bear false witness against your fellow.’ ‘Your fellow’ means the Holy One, as the Zohar teaches (Beshalach 55b). Hashem had promised him (Genesis 17:16), ‘I will bless her and also give you a son from her.’ Why then did he say, ‘If only Yishmael would live before You,’ which appears like false testimony? Hashem told him not to say so: rather, what I have counseled will stand, ‘Sarah your wife will bear you a son.’ Hashem illuminated this statement for him until he himself afterward sent Yishmael out of his house. Yet, because Yishmael was righteous at that time, Hashem showed him not to fix his gaze on what would occur with him later. ‘As he is there,’ he is righteous and must not be judged adversely, as taught in the Talmud (Rosh Hashanah 16b) and the Midrash.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov distinguishes Avraham's present view of Yishmael from the later outcome: Hashem directs attention to how he stands now. This is a qualified comparison with the siman's account of temporary success and final disclosure. It cautions against treating the visible present as proof of a permanent spiritual state, while also refusing to condemn a person now on the basis of a supposed knowledge of his future.

p: [קלז] כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם רוֹאֶה שֶׁכָּל הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת טוֹבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת טוֹבוֹת שֶׁנּוֹפְלִים בְּלִבּוֹ וּמוֹחוֹ הוּא רַק לְרֶגַע וּמִיָּד מִתְעַלְּמִים מִמֶּנּוּ, וְדוֹאֵג שֶׁמָּא הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כְּעִנְיַן פּוֹשְׁעִים מְלֵאִים חֲרָטוֹת

— When a person sees that all the good thoughts and noble aspirations entering his heart and mind last only a moment and vanish immediately, and he fears lest he be like transgressors full of regrets—
הָעֵצָה לָזֶה: "הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה' יְהָבְךָ וְהוּא יְכַלְכְּלֶךָ, לֹא יִתֵּן לְעוֹלָם מוֹט לַצַּדִּיק" (תְּהִלִּים נה, כג),
the counsel for this is: "Cast your burden upon Hashem, and He will sustain you; He will never suffer the righteous to be moved" (Psalms 55:23),
וְ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים", רַק שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּמִתְמוֹטֵט חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּעֵת הַהֶעְלֵם.
and "Your people are all righteous," only that one appears shaken, Heaven forbid, during the time of concealment.

וְ"הַשְׁלֵךְ וְכוּלֵי" הַיְינוּ שֶׁגַּם זֶה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְנִמְצָא כְּאִלּוּ הַמַּשָּׂא מוּטֶּלֶת עָלָיו, שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁאַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן, וּמִמֵּילָא הַמִּשְׁפָּט עַל זֶה דְּ"הוּא יְכַלְכְּלֶךָ".
And "Cast, etc." means that this concealment also comes from the Blessed Name, making the burden resting upon Him, so that since you do so, the judgment dictates that He will sustain you.
הַכִּלְכּוּל הוּא בְּלֶחֶם וָמַיִם, הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁבָּהֶם מֵאִיר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵיךְ הַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה וְאֵין זֶה הִתְמוֹטְטוּת.
Sustenance is through bread and water, meaning words of Torah, wherein the Blessed Name illuminates for him how all is for the good and not an actual collapse.
וְאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כו:): דְּלָא הֲווֹ יָדְעֵי רַבָּנָן מַאי "יְהָבְךָ",
And they said (Rosh Hashanah 26b) that the Rabbis did not know what yehavkha meant,

פֵּירוּשׁ דְּהוּא לְשׁוֹן יְהִיבָא, וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר מַה שֶּׁנִּיתַּן לָאָדָם דְּהַיְינוּ הָאוֹר וְהַטּוֹבָה יַכִּיר שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלֹא מִכֹּחוֹ, אוֹ מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם נוֹתֵן וְהַיְינוּ הַהֶעְלֵם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.

deriving from the Aramaic for giving: either that what was given to man—the light and goodness—he must recognize as coming from Hashem and not from his own strength; or what man yields, which is the concealment.
עַד שֶׁנּוֹדַע לָהֶם מִטַּיָּיעָא, כִּי כֵּן נִקְרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "מַדְרִיכֲךָ בְּדֶרֶךְ תֵּלֵךְ".
Until they learned it from an Arab traveler, for Hashem is called: "Who leads you by the way you should go" (Isaiah 48:17).
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה עַצְמוֹ שֶׁל "הַשְׁלֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר" אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם רַק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לוֹ לְהַשְׁלִיךְ,
This means that casting one's burden is impossible for a person without the Blessed Name illuminating for him to do so;
וְאִם כֵּן אֵין צָרִיךְ עוֹד לָדַעַת מַאי "יְהָבְךָ", דְּכָל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לוֹ לְהַשְׁלִיךְ, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשְׁלִיךְ כְּלָל.
and if so, one need not wonder what yehavkha is, for so long as Hashem does not enlighten him to cast it, he cannot cast it at all.
וּלְכָךְ מִתְּחִלָּה לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעֵי עַד שֶׁהֵאִיר לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְיָדְעוּ דְּהוּא הַמַּשָּׂא, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דָּבָר הַמַּכְבִּיד עַל הָאָדָם וּמֵצִיק לוֹ.
And therefore initially they did not know until the Blessed Name illuminated it for them, and they understood it to mean burden—that which weighs down upon a person and oppresses him.
וְזֶה כְּעִנְיַן: כָּל הַמְּשַׁתֵּף שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם [וְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם נִקְרָא "אַגַּמְלָאֵי" – גָּמָל שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ] בְּצַעֲרוֹ כּוֹפְלִין לוֹ וְכוּלֵי (בְּרָכוֹת סג.),

And this is in the spirit of: "Whoever associates the Name of Heaven [and the Name of Heaven is called agamla'i, 'on my camel': the camel of the Blessed Name] with his distress, his livelihood is doubled" (Berakhot 63a),
וְהַשִּׁתּוּף הַיְינוּ שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמַכְנִיס אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר, וּמִמֵּילָא הֵקֵל מִמֶּנּוּ:
and association means knowing that everything is from the Blessed Name, bringing Hashem into that distress, whereby it is automatically lightened.

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah develops the same casting-burden verse while requiring both natural action and prayer for success. This qualifies the siman's dependence on help from above: casting the burden concerns recognition of the source and relief of distress, while Torah, prayer and chosen effort remain the means through which the person responds.

sections.en: Sometimes a Person Sees That He Yearns and Longs for the Service of Hashem…

p: [קלח] פְּעָמִים הָאָדָם רוֹאֶה שֶׁהוּא חוֹשֵׁק וְכוֹסֵף לַעֲבוֹדַת ה' בְּמוֹחַ וָלֵב, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְמַעֲשֶׂה אֵינוֹ מַצְלִיחַ.
Sometimes a person sees that he yearns and longs for the service of Hashem in mind and heart, yet when he comes to physical action he does not succeed.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא: "אֱוִיל שְׂפָתַיִם יִלָּבֵט" (מִשְׁלֵי י, ח), כְּמוֹ שֶׁמַּשְׁמָע מִמַּה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּסוֹטָה (מז:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְעָם לֹא יָבִין יִלָּבֵט", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And this is designated: "a prating fool shall fall" (yillavet, Proverbs 10:8), as is implied by what our Sages said in Sotah 47b on "a people that does not understand shall fall," see there.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּלְשׁוֹן "יִלָּבֵט" – שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא הַפְּעֻלָּה מִן הַכֹּחַ אֶל הַפּוֹעַל.
For the term yillavet denotes being unable to bring the potential into physical realization.
וְדָבָר זֶה נִתְגַּלָּה לִשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְהוּא אָמַר פָּסוּק זֶה,
And this reality was revealed to King Solomon, peace be upon him, who uttered this verse;
אֲבָל עַל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נה:): לֹא רָאָה חֲלוֹם טוֹב;
but concerning King David, peace be upon him, they said (Berakhot 55b) that he never saw a good dream;

פֵּירוּשׁ, "חֲלוֹם" נִקְרָא עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּשׁוּב ה' אֶת שִׁיבַת צִיּוֹן הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים", וְהוּא עוֹלַם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין כב.): "הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם וְלֹא לְמָחָר וְכוּלֵי",

meaning that this world is termed a "dream," as written: "we were like dreamers" (Psalms 126:1), and it is the World of Action, as stated: "today to do them, and not tomorrow to do them" (Eruvin 22a),
וּבְדָבָר זֶה לֹא רָאָה מֵעוֹלָם דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם טוֹב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁחָשַׁק מְאֹד לִבְנוֹת הַבַּיִת וְנֶאֱמַר: "רַק אַתָּה לֹא תִבְנֶה וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א ח, יט).
and in this realm King David never saw manifest good, such as his passionate desire to build the Temple, concerning which it was told him: "Only you shall not build the house, etc." (I Kings 8:19).
וּבֶאֱמֶת דָּוִד הָיָה נֶגֶד הַמַּעֲשֶׂה כַּיָּדוּעַ,
And in truth David represented the dimension of action, as is known,
וְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁהָאָדָם מוּכָן לוֹ לְהַשְׁלִימוֹ, נִדְמֶה לוֹ תָּמִיד שֶׁהוּא חָסֵר בָּזֶה כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוֹסִיף חֵשֶׁק וְאֹמֶץ בָּזֶה,
and whatever a person is destined to complete appears to him as constantly lacking so that he intensifies desire and fortitude in it,
וְכָל אֲשֶׁר יוֹסִיף חֵשֶׁק לֹא יוֹעִיל לְהַשְׁקִיטוֹ כִּי יִרְאֶה הַכֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַצְלִיחַ.
and all the desire he adds does not serve to bring him peace, because he sees that he does not visibly succeed.
כִּי הַהַשְׁקָטָה הוּא שֶׁכְּבָר נִשְׁלַם, וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא רַק אַחַר דְּנָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ,
For tranquility exists only when something is fully completed, and this occurs only after the soul has rested,
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת ל.): בְּחַיֶּיךָ אֵינִי מוֹדִיעַ, בְּחַיֵּי שְׁלֹמֹה בִנְךָ אֲנִי מוֹדִיעַ;
as our Sages stated (Shabbat 30a): "During your lifetime I will not reveal it; during the lifetime of your son Solomon I will reveal it";
וְסוֹף שֶׁנִּקְרָא הַבַּיִת עַל שֵׁם דָּוִד כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יב),
and ultimately the Temple was called by the name of David (Bemidbar Rabbah 12),
וְנוֹדַע כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הוֹצִיא אֶל הַפּוֹעַל הַכֹּל, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הִצְלִיחוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו.
and it became known that in truth he actualized everything into reality, even though the Blessed Name did not grant him visible success in his actions during his lifetime.
וְנוֹדַע לִשְׁלֹמֹה כִּי רַק "אֱוִיל שְׂפָתַיִם", רַק שֶׁהַכֹּל מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ – יִלָּבֵט
And it became known to Solomon that only a "prating fool"—one whose service is from the lips outward—truly falls
[וְזֶה הָיָה דּוֹאֵג כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק,
[and this was Doeg as our Sages noted in chapter Chelek,
וְהוּא הָיָה לְפִי שָׁעָה נִרְאֶה כִּמְצַלִּיחַ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו, שֶׁעָלָיו אָמַר דָּוִד: "אַל תִּתְחַר בַּמַּצְלִיחַ דַּרְכּוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים לז, ז), וְיָדוּעַ "דַּרְכּוֹ" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דֶּרֶךְ ה'],
who temporarily appeared successful in his deeds, of whom David said: 'Do not fret because of him who prospers in his way' (Psalms 37:7), where 'his way' denotes the way of Hashem],
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוֹצִיא לַפּוֹעַל, אֵינוֹ כֵן בֶּאֱמֶת.
even though he brings it into physical action, it is not genuine truth.
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁחֶשְׁקוֹ יוֹצֵא מֵעֹמֶק שֶׁבַּלֵּב, הוּא אֵינוֹ נִלְבָּט, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה לָעַיִן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַצְלִיחַ בִּיצִיאָה לַפּוֹעַל:
But one whose desire issues from the depth of the heart never falls, even though to outward sight he seems not to succeed in tangible actualization.

paragraphs.text: David’s labor and the Temple’s enduring holiness

rich.text: David’s labor and the Temple’s enduring holiness

paragraphs.text: The inward work can establish what remains even when the visible result comes through another.

rich.text: The inward work can establish what remains even when the visible result comes through another.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Taanit 15: “This is the meaning of the Talmud's statement that He caused His Shekhinah to dwell in Shiloh and the other places. In Shiloh and Gilgal He caused His presence to dwell from His side without Israel's prior suffering; concerning this it says, ‘Zion said, He has forsaken me,’ and ‘Even these may be forgotten’—their holiness ceased. See Aggadat Bereishit, chapter 71, cited in Sidrei Taharot, Kelim 72. The eternal Temple is different: there His presence dwelled through David's suffering and labor, and he prayed for it with self-giving, until Hashem said to him (I Kings 8:19), ‘Your son who will come from your loins will build the house for My name.’ Concerning this the verse says, ‘I will not forget you.’ Through the suffering associated with that holiness it is fixed; all the prayers and offerings were there. Although sin concealed this light, He promises us that through our prayer that He return to dwell in Jerusalem, He will certainly rebuild Jerusalem and return His presence as before to the eternal Temple. This is what we say here: like a woman in her period who awaits her return to her former permitted state, Jerusalem too will have a repair.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef identifies David's suffering, effort and prayer as the basis for the Temple's enduring holiness. His son builds it, and later sin conceals its light, yet neither fact erases what David's work established. This develops Rav Tzadok's distinction between a visible lack of completion and an inward desire that truly brought the work into being.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 7:5: “The king Messiah is David himself, as is known. David, however, was the beginning of the endeavor from the side of the final deed, while the Messiah is the completion of the whole stature as it exists in the original thought. Reaching the root of that original thought itself is the World to Come. The days of the Messiah precede the World to Come: they are the end of this world, from which one reaches the World to Come, and the greatest perfection a person can attain in this world. “God made the human being upright.” Had Adam not sinned, he would himself have been David, the final deed of Creation; through his endeavor to reach the greatest perfection possible for him, he could afterward also have reached the level of the Messiah. As is known, he includes these two souls, hinted at by the initials of his name, Adam: Adam, David, Messiah.”

Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: What is the meaning of the verse, ‘Show me a sign for good, so that those who hate me may see and be ashamed’? David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: ‘Master of the universe, forgive me for that sin.’ He said to him: ‘You are forgiven.’ He said to Him: ‘Show me a sign during my lifetime.’ He answered: ‘During your lifetime I will not make it known; during the lifetime of Solomon your son I will make it known.’’

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 30a:7: “When Solomon built the Temple, he sought to bring the Ark into the Holy of Holies. The gates clung to one another. Solomon uttered twenty-four songs of prayer and was not answered. He began, “Lift up your heads, gates; be uplifted, everlasting entrances, and let the King of glory enter.” They ran after him to swallow him, saying, “Who is this King of glory?” He said to them, “Hashem, mighty and powerful.” He again said, “Lift up your heads, gates; lift yourselves, everlasting entrances, and let the King of glory enter. Who is this King of glory? Hashem of hosts—He is the King of glory, forever,” and was not answered. When he said, “Hashem God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed; remember the kindnesses of David Your servant,” he was immediately answered. At that moment the faces of all David’s enemies became black like the bottom of a pot, and all the people, all Israel, knew that the Holy One, blessed be He, had forgiven him that sin. Did Solomon not speak well when he said, “I praise the dead who have already died”?”

sections.en: All Actions and Spiritual Labors Are Recognized Only at the End

p: [קלט] כָּל הַפְּעֻלּוֹת וְהָעֲבוֹדוֹת נִיכָּרִים רַק בַּסּוֹף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קנג.): אֵיזֶהוּ בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא? "וְאָזְנֶיךָ תִּשְׁמַעְנָה דָבָר מֵאַחֲרֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי" (יְשַׁעְיָה ל, כא);
All actions and spiritual labors are recognized only at the end, as stated in Shabbat 153a: Who is destined for the World to Come? "And your ears shall hear a word behind you, etc." (Isaiah 30:21);
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר הָעֵסֶק, הוּא מְכֻסֶּה וְנֶעְלָם מֵעֵין הַכֹּל, וַאֲפִילּוּ מֵעֵין הָאָדָם,
and as long as the endeavor is not completed, it remains hidden from the sight of all, even from the person himself,
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּדְמֶה צַדִּיק וְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ "צַדִּיק אַתָּה" – הֱיֵה וְכוּלֵי (נִדָּה ל:),
such that even if he appears righteous and the entire world tells him "you are righteous," be [in your own eyes like a wicked person], etc. (Niddah 30b),
וְכֵן גַּם כֵּן לְהֵיפֶךְ, כִּי כָּל דָּבָר נִידּוֹן עַל שֵׁם סוֹפוֹ.
and likewise the reverse, for every matter is judged according to its ultimate outcome.
וְאִם בַּסּוֹף יֹאמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא הִצְלִיחַ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אָז כָּל מִקּוֹדֶם נִקְרָא שֶׁקֶר וְכָזָב, לְשׁוֹן הֶפְסֵק, כְּמוֹ "יְכַזְּבוּ מֵימָיו" (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יא).

And if at the end the Blessed Name declares that it did not succeed, Heaven forbid, then everything prior is deemed falsehood and deceit, in the sense of cessation, as in "whose waters fail not" (Isaiah 58:11).
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה – זְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ זְכִיּוֹת, וְגַם מִקּוֹדֶם הִצְלִיחַ.
And likewise conversely: for a penitent, willful sins become merits, and retroactively he succeeded even beforehand.
וְדָבָר זֶה יוֹצְרָן יוֹדֵעַ גַּם בְּעֵת הַהַתְחָלָה,
And this their Creator knows even at the very beginning:
לְהַכִּיר בְּכָל מִדָּה וּמַחֲשָׁבָה וּמַעֲשֶׂה טוֹב וָרָע אֵיזֶה הִיא בֶּאֱמֶת מֵעֵבֶר לְעֵבֶר, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁיַּצְלִיחַ בָּהּ עַד הַסּוֹף וְיַשְׁלִימֶהָ בְּטוֹב,
to discern within every trait, thought, and deed—good or evil—which one is genuine from end to end, destined to succeed to the conclusion and finish in goodness,
וְאֵיזֶה שֶׁקֶר וְאֵינָהּ רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִשְׁתַּנֶּה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה כֵּן.
and which is false, lasting only temporarily and destined to shift and dissolve.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים נד:): שִׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים מְכֻסִּים מִבְּנֵי אָדָם וְכוּלֵי;
And concerning this our Sages said (Pesachim 54b): Seven things are concealed from human beings, etc.;
וְיָדוּעַ מִסְפַּר שִׁבְעָה הֵם כְּלַל בִּנְיַן הָעוֹלָם וְכָל הַמִּדּוֹת הַנִּמְצָאִים בַּבְּרִיאָה וּבָאָדָם,
and it is known that the number seven represents the complete structure of the cosmos and all attributes found in creation and in man,
וְכֻלָּם מְכֻסִּים מִבְּנֵי אָדָם לְעִנְיַן הַמַּעֲמַקִּים שֶׁבָּהֶם וְסוֹפָם, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ בֵּיאוּר כֻּלָּם.
and all of them are hidden from mankind regarding their ultimate depths and final outcomes, and this is not the place to explain them all.
וְיָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "מְכֻסִּים מִבְּנֵי אָדָם" – הַיְינוּ אַף מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבִּבְנֵי אָדָם
And it is known that "concealed from human beings" includes even Moses our teacher, the greatest of men
[וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סִפְרֵי דְּבָרִים פִּסְקָא יז) בִּשְׁמוּאֵל: "אַל תַּבֵּט אֶל מַרְאֵהוּ", לְפִי שֶׁאָמַר: "אָנֹכִי הָרֹאֶה"],
[and as our Sages expounded in Sifrei Devarim regarding Samuel: 'Look not on his countenance' (I Samuel 16:7), because he had declared: 'I am the seer'],
וְאִם כֵּן אֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל מַלְאֲכֵי מַעְלָה וְעוֹלָמוֹת עֶלְיוֹנִים.
and if so, it goes without saying that it is hidden from all the angels on high and supernal worlds.
וּלְכָךְ יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת אָדָם בַּעַל מַדְרֵגָה מִן עוֹלָמוֹת, כִּי גַּם שָׁם נִדְמֶה שֶׁהוּא טוֹב וְהַסּוֹף עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ.
And therefore a person can attain a lofty spiritual reputation across worlds, because there too he appears good, while the final end is not yet known.

רַק הָעֵצָה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "וְקֹוֵי ה' הֵמָּה יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ" (תְּהִלִּים לז, ט), וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְהַחוֹסֶה בִי יִנְחַל אֶרֶץ" (יְשַׁעְיָה נז, יג), וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יב:): נַחֲלָה אֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק.

Rather, the remedy is what is written: "but those that wait for Hashem, they shall inherit the land" (Psalms 37:9), and: "he that puts his trust in Me shall possess the land" (Isaiah 57:13), concerning which our Sages taught (Rosh Hashanah 12b): an inheritance has no interruption.

וְהַיְינוּ תְּפִלָּה וְרַחֲמִים, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא קִיוּוּי לַה', כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "קַוֵּה אֶל ה' חֲזַק וְיַאֲמֵץ לִבֶּךָ וְקַוֵּה אֶל ה'" (תְּהִלִּים כז, יד), וְלָמְדוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת לב:): תְּפִלָּה צְרִיכָה חִזּוּק.

And this refers to prayer and pleas for mercy, which is termed hoping in Hashem, as written: "Hope in Hashem; be of good courage, and He shall strengthen your heart; hope, I say, in Hashem" (Psalms 27:14), from which our Sages derived (Berakhot 32b): prayer requires repeated strengthening.

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לְנַחֲלָה, וְאִם כֵּן דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁתָּלוּי בִּידִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל – אֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ בְּחִירָה? לְכָךְ לָמְדוּ דְּגַם זֶה צָרִיךְ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת:

That is, even though through this one attains an enduring inheritance—and since this depends on the foreknowledge of the Blessed Name, how can free choice apply?—they taught that even this requires persistent human exertion.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Ha'azinu and Shabbat Shuvah 6: “‘May my teaching drop like rain; may my utterance flow like dew.’ My holy grandfather explained ya'arof as related to the back of the neck: some words of Torah hold a person from behind his neck and do not let him turn from Hashem's will. If a person clearly recognized direct light from Hashem and stood face to face before Him, there would be no place for service; he would recognize explicitly that departing from His will by a hair's breadth is departing from life. Because Hashem desires to benefit His creatures, He concealed this light, and a person does not stand so directly face to face. He must break through the concealment, recognize Hashem's light explicitly, and stand face to face again. Thus, when receiving prophecy, the prophet said, ‘Thus says Hashem,’ standing face to face and recognizing His will explicitly. The Talmud says (Megillah 32a): from where is it known that one may make use of a heavenly echo? From ‘Your ears will hear a word from behind you’ (Isaiah 30:21). When the person is in concealment, he must recognize Hashem's light from behind: he must attend to the words of Torah that hold him within the concealment so he does not turn from His will. This is called a heavenly echo. Those words of Torah that hold him within concealment are called ‘May my teaching drop like rain.’ When he breaks through the concealment and stands face to face before Hashem's light, this signifies ‘May my utterance flow like dew.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Rav Tzadok emphasizes the end at which an action becomes known; Tiferet Yosef reads the same ‘word from behind you’ as Torah holding a person to Hashem's will while clarity is absent. The readings are complementary rather than identical. The second explains how to continue the effort and hope required by the siman without pretending to know the final verdict.

sections.en: As Long as a Person Has Not Reached Spiritual Perfection

p: [קמ] כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין הָאָדָם בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, כָּל מַה שֶּׁמְּדַמֶּה לוֹ, יֵדַע שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ, כְּעִנְיַן "הָאֹמְרִים לָרַע טוֹב וְלַטּוֹב רָע" (יְשַׁעְיָה ה, כ),

As long as a person has not reached spiritual perfection, whatever he imagines to himself, let him know that it is literally the reverse, in the manner of: "those who say of evil, it is good, and of good, it is evil" (Isaiah 5:20),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים נ.): "עוֹלָם הָפוּךְ רָאִיתִי", שֶׁשָּׁם בִּמְקוֹם הָאֱמֶת הוּא מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ מִבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
and as stated in Pesachim 50a: "I saw an inverted world," for there in the realm of Truth it is literally opposite to this world,
וּמַה שֶּׁנִּדְמֶה לוֹ לְטוֹב יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ, וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ.
and what seems to him good may have no substance at all, and likewise the reverse.
רַק מִי שֶׁהֵאִיר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֵינָיו בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ "אֱמֶת" כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ד:), עַל יָדָהּ יָכוֹל לָבוֹא עַל הָאֱמֶת,
Only one whose eyes the Blessed Name has enlightened through words of Torah—concerning which "Truth" is written (Avodah Zarah 4b)—can through it arrive at the Truth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים שָׁם): "וַאֲנַן", פֵּירוּשׁ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, "הֵיכִי הָתָם? כִּי הֵיכִי דַּאֲתֵינַן הָכָא וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה מְאִירָה בָּזֶה לָאָדָם לַעֲמוֹד עַל הָאֱמֶת.
as stated in Pesachim: "And as for us—meaning Torah scholars—how do we appear there? Just as we are held here," for the Torah illuminates for a person to master the Truth.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כו:): עֵצָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ דְּבַר ה' – הִיא תָקוּם.
And concerning this they said in Sanhedrin 26b: counsel that contains the word of Hashem shall endure.
אֲבָל בְּלָאו הָכִי, מַחֲשָׁבָה מוֹעֶלֶת לְבַטֵּל, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַסּוֹף מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ מִמַּה שֶּׁחָשַׁב.
But otherwise, human calculation is overturned, meaning that the end will be the exact opposite of what he calculated.
וְהַסּוֹף הוּא גִּלּוּי הָאֱמֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר, כִּי בַּהֹוֶה הַכֹּל אֶחָד, רַק בַּסּוֹף נִיכָּר,
And the end represents the disclosure of the truth within that matter, for in the present all appears uniform, but at the end it is recognized,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד" (מִשְׁלֵי יב, יט), וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קפח עַמּוּד ב): כּוֹנַנְתָּ לֹא כְּתִיב אֶלָּא "תִּכּוֹן".

as it is written: "The lip of truth shall be established forever" (Proverbs 12:19), and the Zohar states (Part II, 188b): it is not written 'is established' in the past, but 'shall be established' in the future.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נה.): חֶלְמָא טָבָא חֶדְוָותֵיהּ מִסְתַּיֵּיהּ, בִּישָׁא – עֲצִיבוּתָא מִסְתַּיֵּיהּ;
And concerning this they said (Berakhot 55a): for a good dream the joy it brings suffices, and for a bad dream the sorrow it brings suffices;
פֵּירוּשׁ, כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה עוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִקְרָא חֶלְמָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּשׁוּב ה' וְגוֹמֵר",
meaning that all affairs of this world are termed a dream, as written: "When Hashem brings back, etc. we were like dreamers";
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם נז:): חֲלוֹם אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בִּנְבוּאָה, וְכֵן שַׁבָּת אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
nonetheless our Sages stated (ibid. 57b): a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy, and Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come,

שֶׁקְּצָת טַעַם נִרְגָּשׁ גַּם כֵּן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּעִנְיַן אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַרְגָּשַׁת הַטַּעַם הַיּוֹתֵר מוּעָט, כִּי אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים וְאֶחָד אֵין טַעַם, וְהַתְחָלָתוֹ אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים.

so that a slight taste is experienced in this world, mirroring one-sixtieth which represents the minimal threshold of taste (for in one-sixty-first there is no taste, while its threshold begins at one-sixtieth).
כִּי הַמַּעֲשִׂים הֵם רוֹשְׁמִים מוּעָטִים לַאֲמִיתַּת הַנְּקוּדָּה שֶׁבַּלֵּב הַנֶּעְלָם.
For physical actions are faint impressions of the true concealed point within the heart.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם נה:): הַחֲלוֹמוֹת הוֹלְכִים אַחַר הַפֶּה
— And regarding this our Sages stated (ibid. 55b): dreams follow the mouth—
הַיְינוּ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה יָכוֹל לְבָרֵר כָּל מַעֲשִׂים שֶׁעָשָׂה יִהְיֶה לְטוֹב,
meaning through words of Torah, for through words of Torah one can clarify all deeds he has done so that they result in good;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיוּ אֵיךְ שֶׁהָיוּ, עַל יְדֵי הַפֶּה הוּא נַעֲשֶׂה טוֹב, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר עֵינָיו בָּזֶה,
and even though they were as they were, through the mouth they become good, as the Blessed Name enlightens his eyes in this,
וְאָז נִקְבָּע הַחֲלוֹם לֶאֱמֶת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דְּתוֹרָה הִיא אֱמֶת;
and then the dream is established as truth as noted above, for Torah is Truth;
וּמִי שֶׁדָּבוּק בַּתּוֹרָה הֲרֵי דָּבוּק בְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הָאֲמִתִּיִּים,
and one who cleaves to the Torah cleaves to true eternal life,
מִמֵּילָא כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים שֶׁלּוֹ עַל כָּרְחֲךָ כֵּן, כִּי בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהוּא הָאָדָם – שָׁם הוּא כֻּלּוֹ:
and consequently all of his actions are perforce so, for where a person is—there he is entirely.

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Human Dispositions 2:1: “Those whose bodies are ill taste the bitter as sweet and the sweet as bitter. Some of the sick desire and crave foods unfit to eat, such as earth and charcoal, and hate good foods such as bread and meat, all according to the severity of the illness. Similarly, people whose souls are ill desire and love bad character traits, hate the good way, and are sluggish about following it; it is very burdensome to them, according to their illness. Of such people Isaiah says, “Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make darkness into light and light into darkness, bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter.” Of them it says, “Those who abandon upright paths to walk in ways of darkness.” What is the remedy for those whose souls are ill? They should go to the sages, who are physicians of souls, and they will heal their illness through the character traits they teach them, until they bring them back to the good way. Of those who recognize their bad traits but do not go to the sages to heal them, Solomon says, “Fools despise wisdom and instruction.””

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Sanhedrin 26b:9:1-4: ““Thought”: Anxiety of the heart about a person’s livelihood. “Has an effect”: It causes him to forget his learning. “He frustrates the thoughts of the cunning”: He gives them sustenance and removes thoughts from their hearts that would not allow them to accomplish Torah wisdom. Another interpretation: Thought that a person thinks, “I shall do such and such; such and such will succeed for me,” has the effect of disrupting the matter, so that his plan is not fulfilled, even concerning Torah—for example, saying, “By a particular day I shall finish studying such and such tractates.” “He frustrates the thoughts of the cunning”: Their plans do not succeed, even concerning Torah wisdom.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Rashi records two readings: worry that impairs learning, and confident planning whose projected outcome is frustrated. Rav Tzadok’s explanation here follows the second; neither the first interpretation nor the Gemara’s existing qualification about study for its own sake is suppressed.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Ki Tisa 4:14: “If the verse had said, “The lip of truth has been established forever,” it would be as you say. But it says only “shall be established”: the lip of truth is destined to be established, unlike its present state. Now the lip of falsehood stands, while the lip of truth lies in the dust. When truth rises to its standing and springs from the earth, then “the lip of truth shall be established forever.””

Once I dreamed a dream and went to all of them. What one interpreted for me another did not, and all of their interpretations came true for me, fulfilling the saying, “All dreams follow the mouth.” Is “All dreams follow the mouth” a verse? paragraphs.text: A world likened to a dream is clarified by recognizing the divine utterance that sustains it.

rich.text: A world likened to a dream is clarified by recognizing the divine utterance that sustains it.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Miketz 6: “‘You hear a dream to interpret it.’ All the matters of this world are like a dream requiring interpretation, and as a person interprets it, so it is established with him. The person who understands in everything that all is only from Hashem and that all lives through the utterance of His mouth understands the meaning in every matter and reaches true life. With bread, for example, the principal life-giving element within it is the utterance of Hashem's mouth. Someone who eats simply like an animal receives from the bread only the life of this world. Someone who understands that Hashem's utterance gives life attains enduring life. For the letters of lechem, bread, are those of chalom, dream: it requires interpretation. So it is with all pleasures, for all the pleasures and benefits in the world are likened to bread.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach develops the siman's dream analogy through an ordinary act: eating bread. Receiving only the outward food gives temporal life, while recognizing Hashem's utterance within it connects the act to enduring life. This helps explain why Rav Tzadok locates the power of interpretation in Torah and in the person's attachment to truth, rather than in an arbitrary favorable statement about events.

sections.en: The Spiritual Concealment That Befalls a Person Seemingly Appears as Proof That the Yearning…

p: [קמא] הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לָאָדָם הוּא נִרְאֶה לִכְאוֹרָה רְאָיָה שֶׁגַּם הַחֵשֶׁק וְהַחַיּוּת שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ מִקּוֹדֶם הָיָה שֶׁקֶר, כִּי "שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד" (מִשְׁלֵי יב, יט).

The spiritual concealment that befalls a person seemingly appears as proof that the yearning and vitality he possessed previously were false, for "the lip of truth shall be established forever" (Proverbs 12:19).
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אַדְּרַבָּה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בּוֹנֶה שֶׁתִּכּוֹן לָעַד הַחֵשֶׁק;
Yet in truth, on the contrary, through this very concealment the Holy One, blessed be He, builds the foundation so that this yearning shall be established forever;
כַּאֲשֶׁר מַשִּׂיג בַּהֶעְלֵם שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶסְתֵּר פָּנִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמִתְחַנֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיָּאִיר לוֹ – הֲרֵי כְּבָר אֵינוֹ בַּהֶעְלֵם,
for when he recognizes in the midst of concealment that he is in a state of divine hiddenness, and pleads before the Blessed Name to illuminate him—behold, he is no longer truly in concealment,
שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "תַּכְלִית הַיְּדִיעָה שֶׁלֹּא נֵדַע".
concerning which it is said: "the pinnacle of knowledge is to know that we do not know."
וְדָבָר זֶה נִקְרָא "עֲנָוָה", וְהוּא מַדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה כַּנּוֹדָע,
And this state is termed "humility," which is the loftiest of all spiritual levels as is known,
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וַעֲנָוִים יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ" (תְּהִלִּים לז, יא) – פֵּירוּשׁ, יְרֻשָּׁה אֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכט:),
and it is stated: "But the humble shall inherit the land" (Psalms 37:11)—meaning an inheritance suffers no interruption (Bava Batra 129b),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה עָנָו מִכָּל הָאָדָם: "לֹא כָהֲתָה עֵינוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים לד, ז), שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לְמַעֲלוֹתָיו שׁוּם הֶפְסֵק,
and as written of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who was the humblest of all men: "his eye was not dim, etc." (Deuteronomy 34:7), showing that his virtues suffered no cessation,
וְדַיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה שֶׁתִּכּוֹן לָעַד.
and precisely through this humility was it effected that his spiritual standing endure forever.
וְנֶאֱמַר (הוֹשֵׁעַ ו, ד): "מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה לָּךְ וְגוֹמֵר, וְחַסְדְּכֶם כַּעֲנַן בֹּקֶר וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁפּוֹסֵק מִיָּד הַחֵשֶׁק,
And it is stated (Hosea 6:4): "What shall I do unto you, etc.? For your goodness is as a morning cloud, etc.," where the holy yearning immediately ceases;
"עַל כֵּן חָצַבְתִּי בַּנְּבִיאִים וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם, ה)
— "therefore have I hewed them by the prophets, etc." (ibid. 6:5)—
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִבְנֶה קוֹמַת הַנָּבִיא וַחֲכַם הַדּוֹר,
meaning that from the good thoughts and aspirations of Israel the stature of the prophet and the sage of the generation is constructed,
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (עֲרָכִין יז.): פַּרְנָס לְפִי הַדּוֹר;
and therefore they said (Arachin 17a): a leader is according to the generation;
וְאָמְרוּ: אֵיזֶה דוֹר חָבִיב וְכוּלֵי? דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, וְהָיָה אָז פַּרְנָס מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לֹא קָם וְגוֹמֵר".

and they said: which generation is most beloved? The Generation of the Wilderness, whose leader was Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, of whom it is said: "and there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses" (Deuteronomy 34:10).
וְכַאֲשֶׁר חַסְדָּם כַּעֲנַן בֹּקֶר, אָז מַגִּיעַ הַמִּשְׁפָּט: "חָצַבְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר";
And when their devotion is fleeting as a morning cloud, then arrives the judgment: "I have hewed them, etc.";
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּעֲנִית ה:): "בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם" לֹא נֶאֱמַר, אֶלָּא "בְּאִמְרֵי פִי" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ו, ה)
— and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Ta'anit 5b): it is not stated "by their deeds," but rather "by the words of My mouth" (Hosea 6:5)—
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נַחְשׁוֹב אִם כֵּן שֶׁהַתְחָלַת הַחֶסֶד הָיָה שֶׁקֶר וְכָךְ הַפַּרְנָס, וְאִם כֵּן זֶהוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם.
meaning lest we think that the initial devotion was false and likewise the leader, which would attribute it to their corrupt deeds.
לָזֶה אָמַר דְּהָאֱמֶת אֵינוֹ כֵן, רַק "בְּאִמְרֵי פִי", שֶׁגַּם זֶה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁרָצָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הֶעְלֵם;
To this the verse responds that the truth is not so, but rather "by the words of My mouth," for this concealment also derives from the Blessed Name Who willed that there be hiddenness;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה: "וּמִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ אוֹר יֵצֵא" (שָׁם)
— and through this: "and your judgments are as the light that goes forth" (ibid.)—
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הָאוֹר בְּמִשְׁפָּט, שֶׁכֻּלָּם יוֹדוּ וְיַעֲנוּ אָמֵן בְּעַל כָּרְחָם, כִּי מַגִּיעַ לָכֶם בְּמִשְׁפָּט אוֹרָה וְטוֹבָה:

so that the light shall emerge in rigorous justice, wherein all will concede and answer "Amen" even against their will, recognizing that light and goodness are rightfully due to you by divine justice.

paragraphs.text: A generation’s many spiritual powers are described as gathered in its leader.

rich.text: A generation’s many spiritual powers are described as gathered in its leader.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, On Book of Joshua 10: “It is known that the leader of a generation has a soul encompassing all the souls of that generation, as the Sages said (Arakhin 17a), a leader according to the generation, and a generation according to the leader. Every generation is a particular arrangement of the souls of that generation—that is, parts of Hashem's wisdom, as explained. The gathering of all those wisdoms is itself also one soul. Souls divide into details and further details according to the order Hashem arranged, and their totality is itself a distinct soul, different from the details taken alone. The father's soul includes the souls of all his children; Adam included the souls of all the generations, and their totality was Adam's distinct soul. Likewise, the leader's soul includes all the generation's souls, as a king is the whole nation. He can therefore lead them all, because his wisdom includes all their wisdom, and likewise his understanding and all his spiritual powers.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Likkutei Maamarim explains the siman's statement that the generation's thoughts and desires build the stature of its leader. Their gathering is itself described as a distinct soul, with the leader including their wisdom and powers. This makes the relation reciprocal rather than a claim about popularity, and clarifies why the siman discusses the generation's brief illumination and its leader together.

sections.en: Even Though in the Affairs of This World a Person Must Not Rely Upon…

p: [קמב] אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבְּעִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵין לָאָדָם לִסְמוֹךְ עַל נֵס כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת לב.), בְּעִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא יִסְמוֹךְ אַף עַל נֵס.

Even though in the affairs of this world a person must not rely upon a miracle, as our Sages stated (Shabbat 32a), in the spiritual matters of the World to Come one may indeed rely even upon a miracle.

רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר, אַף שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁכְּפִי דֶּרֶךְ הַתּוֹרִיִּי הַמְּסוּדָּר [שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא דֶּרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַבָּא] כִּמְעַט אָבְדָה תִּקְוָתוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מֵרוֹב חֲטָאָיו, וְשֶׁעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר "וְלָרָשָׁע וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁמַּדְחִים כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁלּוֹ

— That is to say, even if he sees that according to the standard ordered path of the Torah [which is termed the "natural order" of the World to Come] his hope is virtually lost, Heaven forbid, from the multitude of his sins, and that concerning him it is said "And unto the wicked God says, etc." (Psalms 50:16), seeing that all his good deeds are rejected—
עַל כָּל פָּנִים יִסְמוֹךְ עַל נֵס, כִּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵינוֹ בְּטֶבַע.
nonetheless let him rely upon a miracle, for the World to Come is not bound by nature.
וְנֵס יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת מֵאֲפֵילָה לְאוֹר גָּדוֹל [מֵאֲפֵילָה דַּיְיקָא],
And a miracle can transport one from darkness into great light [specifically out of deep darkness],
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "בְּטַח בַּה' וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים לז, ג), וְלֹא יָחוּשׁ שֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם הַמַּעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים לָרִיק;
and concerning this it is stated: "Trust in Hashem, and do good, etc." (Psalms 37:3), and let him not worry that his good deeds are in vain, Heaven forbid;

וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר (תּוֹלְדוֹת קמב עַמּוּד א) עַל פָּסוּק "עָז לוֹ בָךְ" (שָׁם פד, ו) – הַיְינוּ לְעִנְיָן זֶה, שֶׁ"מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם", שֶׁיַּעַזְרֶנּוּ וִיהַפֵּךְ לִבּוֹ לְטוֹב, עַל זֶה יוּכַל לִסְמוֹךְ וְלֹא כַּחֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.

and so it is stated in the Zohar (Toldot 142a) on the verse "whose strength is in You" (Psalms 84:6)—meaning in this regard, that "highways are in their heart," that He will assist him and overturn his heart to good; on this he may rely, and not as Chananiah, Mishael and Azariah, etc., see there.
וּ"מְסִלּוֹת" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ הַדֶּרֶךְ כְּבוּשָׁה, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת מְסִלָּה מִן הַצַּד בִּלְבָבָם לְטוֹבָה.
And "highways" (mesilot) denotes that it is not the paved public road, but the Blessed Name can forge a highway from the side within their hearts for the good.
וְיָדוּעַ: כָּל נֵס הוּא יֵשׁ מִיֵּשׁ וְלֹא בַּאֲתַר רֵיקַנְיָא, וְלָכֵן צָרִיךְ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא מִקּוֹדֶם.
And it is known: every miracle is substance from substance (yesh mi-yesh) and not in an empty place, which is why an awakening from below (itaruta de-letata) is required beforehand.
אֲבָל יֵשׁ עוֹד מַדְרֵגָה, כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית, דְּהַיְינוּ בְּרִיאָה יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן,
However, there is a yet higher level, for the Blessed Name renews daily the work of Creation, which is creation ex nihilo (yesh me'ayin),
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי וְגוֹמֵר", וּכִשְׁאֵלָתֵנוּ: "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְגוֹמֵר";
as in: "Create in me a clean heart, etc." (Psalms 51:12), and in our daily petition: "Restore us, etc.";
וְזֶהוּ הַנִּסִּים הַנֶּעְלָמִים בְּדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "וְעַל נִסֶּיךָ וְכוּלֵי",
and these are the hidden miracles enclothed in the natural order, as we say: "and for Your miracles, etc.,"
וְהוּא הַבַּת קוֹל שֶׁיּוֹצֵאת בְּכָל יוֹם: "שׁוּבוּ וְכוּלֵי", וְהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל.
and this is the Heavenly Voice that issues forth each day proclaiming "Return, etc.," which operates in profound concealment.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ: "גּוֹל עַל ה' וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים לז, ה) – אַחַר "וּבְטַח וְגוֹמֵר" יָבוֹא לְמַדְרֵגָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁ"הוּא יַעֲשֶׂה": הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה הַכֹּל

And concerning this Scripture states right afterward: "Commit your way unto Hashem, etc." (Psalms 37:5)—after "Trust in Hashem," one arrives at the second level where "He will bring it to pass": the Blessed Name Himself will do everything
[מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִקּוֹדֶם אָמַר: "וַעֲשֵׂה" – אַתָּה].
[unlike previously where it commanded: "and do"—referring to your own action].
וְעִנְיַן "גּוֹל" – דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְגַלְגֵּל, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא בְּרִחוּק,
And the meaning of "commit" (gol, roll) is something that one must roll from afar,
וּבְכָל הַהַרְחָקִים וְהֶסְתֵּרִים יְגַלְגֵּל דַּרְכּוֹ וְהַנְהָגָתוֹ אֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
meaning that throughout all distance and concealments he should roll his way and conduct unto the Blessed Name
[פֵּירוּשׁ "עַל" – בְּסָמוּךְ, גַּם "עַל" מַמָּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "כֶּתֶר יִתְּנוּ וְגוֹמֵר", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא): מִתְּפִלָּתָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל],
[interpreting "al" (upon) as adjacent to, or literally upon, as in 'they give a crown unto You,' which our Sages in Shemot Rabbah 21 explained: woven from the prayers of Israel],
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַכֹּל, וּמִמֵּילָא הוּא יַעֲשֶׂה, רַק צָרִיךְ מִקּוֹדֶם "בְּטַח וְגוֹמֵר" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
meaning that everything stems from Him, and consequently He will bring it to pass, only that one must first attain "Trust, etc." as noted above
[וְהוּא מַדְרֵגַת בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה בְּשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא דֶּרֶךְ נֵס, וְאַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁמִּתְהַפְּכִים לִזְכִיּוֹת נַעֲשָׂה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר, וְהוּא מַדְרֵגַת "גּוֹל וְגוֹמֵר";

[and this is the level of a penitent who turns in a single moment by way of a miracle, and subsequently when sins are transformed into merits he becomes a completely righteous person, which is the level of 'Commit, etc.';
וּפְלוּגְתָּא אֵיזֶה גָּדוֹל, וְיָדוּעַ דְּאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:
and it is a dispute which is greater, and it is known that 'both these and those are the words of the living God,' and this is not the place to lengthen].

paragraphs.text: Hope in a spiritual rescue can be patient while the path remains hidden.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Sukkot 13:1: “Emunah is related to ‘as a nurse carries the infant.’ As the Tikkunei Zohar explains (introduction, 2a), ‘the father of faith, which is understanding.’ One should not hasten the time or press the hour, but wait in faith. Then this kindness will be revealed, and he will recognize it within his understanding too. ‘Tend faith’ means to guard the matter until it is also revealed in one's understanding. The term faith applies only to what is not explicit in one's understanding: what is already explicit needs no faith. What is not explicit requires faith—guarding the matter well until it emerges into explicit revelation before human eyes.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim explains the same ‘trust in Hashem’ passage through a definition of faith: holding to what has not yet become clear without forcing its time. This qualifies the siman's permission to hope for an unexpected spiritual rescue. The hope accompanies its stated first response of doing good and prayer; it is not a timetable imposed on the rescue.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 7:17: “Therefore he does not succeed by entering through the lower opening, which is “the gate of the Lord through which the righteous enter,” merely restraining himself because the thing is forbidden. He must raise himself to a higher level, the upper opening: not doing anything that does not give satisfaction and fulfill the will of the blessed Lord. Even if it has become like something permitted to him, he nevertheless recognizes that it is at least not the fulfillment of the blessed Lord’s will. When he takes to heart whether it is the blessed Lord’s will, what desire the blessed Lord has in this, and that he does not wish to do anything that is not His will, he thereby escapes every kind of enticement by the inclination, even in the strongest trial. This accords with the well-known account of what happened to one of the outstanding holy men of the generation before ours. This is the gate through which penitents enter, which is a higher place. It is the lower opening in the first heh of the divine name, while in the final heh it is the upper opening; the lower opening is the gate open to the righteous.”

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Exodus 25:24:1: ““A border of gold around it”: A sign of the crown of kingship, for the table signifies wealth and greatness, as people speak of “the table of kings”—Rashi’s explanation. This is indeed so, for this is the secret of the table: since the world came into existence, the blessing of Hashem does not create something from nothing; the world follows its customary order, as it is written, “God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good.” But when the root of something is present, the blessing rests upon it and increases it. Thus Elisha said, “Tell me what you have in the house,” and the blessing rested on a small vessel of oil and filled all the vessels. With Eliyahu, “The jar of flour did not come to an end, and the flask of oil did not diminish.” Likewise, the blessing rests on the table through the showbread, and from it abundance comes to all Israel. Therefore they said that any priest who received a portion the size of a bean would eat and be satisfied.”

sections.en: When a Person Begins to Enter Into Torah Study and the Service of The…

p: [קמג] כְּשֶׁמַּתְחִיל הָאָדָם לִכְנוֹס לְתוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לוֹ מְאֹד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פֵּתַח דְּבָרֶיךָ יָאִיר מֵבִין פְּתָיִים" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, קל).

When a person begins to enter into Torah study and the service of the heart, the Blessed Name illuminates him immensely, as it is written: "The opening of Your words gives light; it gives understanding unto the simple" (Psalms 119:130).
וְכָל הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת לְתוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה נִקְרָא "דְּבָרֶיךָ", שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְדַבֵּר עִם הָאָדָם, וְאֵלּוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת נַעֲשִׂים מִזֶּה.
And all thoughts and desires for Torah and divine service are termed "Your words," for the Blessed Name speaks with the person, and these thoughts are generated from that divine communion.
וּבַפְּתִיחָה יָאִיר מְאֹד, שֶׁזֶּה "מֵבִין פְּתָיִים", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ג) דְּקוֹרִין לְיָנוֹקָא פַּתְיָא;
And at the opening He shines forth brightly, which "gives understanding unto the simple," as stated in Shemot Rabbah (chapter 3) that an infant is termed simple;
וּבְהַתְחָלַת הָעֲבוֹדָה נִקְרָא כָּל אֶחָד "נַעַר", וּלְהַהַתְחָלַת הֲבָנָה צָרִיךְ אוֹר גָּדוֹל,
and at the beginning of divine service everyone is considered a "youth," and for the inception of understanding one requires a great illumination,

וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִסְתַּלֵּק, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק זֶה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג): זֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: בְּרֵאשִׁית וְכוּלֵי וַיְהִי אוֹר, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: אוֹר שֶׁבָּרָא וְכוּלֵי גְּנָזוֹ;

and afterward it recedes, as our Sages of blessed memory expounded on this verse (Bereishit Rabbah 3): this is what is written, 'In the beginning, etc., and there was light,' and our Sages stated: the light that He created, He concealed;
וְהִנֵּה לָמָּה בְּרָאוֹ? עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הַצֹּרֶךְ כָּךְ: שֶׁיִּבָּרֵא וְיִגָּנֵז.
and behold, why did He create it? Perforce the necessity was thus: that it be created and then concealed.
וְכֵן בְּעֵת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה נֶאֱמַר: "אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו), שֶׁהָיָה אָז "פֵּתַח דְּבָרֶיךָ", וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִסְתַּלֵּק עַד לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר.

And so at the Giving of the Torah it was stated: "I said: You are godlike beings, etc." (Psalms 82:6), which was then "the opening of Your words," and afterward it departed until the ultimate future when it shall return.
וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה – תְּפִלָּה, כִּידוּעַ דְּהַתְחָלָה הוּא מַדְרֵגַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְהוּא "פֵּתַח דְּבָרֶיךָ",
And the spiritual remedy for this is prayer, for as is known, the beginning is the attribute of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, which is "the opening of Your words,"
וְהַסּוֹף שֶׁחוֹזֵר לְהָאִיר הוּא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמָשִׁיחַ, וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּתְפִלָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" (שָׁם קט, ד).
and the culmination when the light returns to shine is King David, peace be upon him, and the Messiah, which is the spiritual rung of prayer, as written: "and I am prayer" (Psalms 109:4).

וּלְכָךְ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּעֵת בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן "פֵּתַח דְּבָרֶיךָ" בְּאוֹר גָּדוֹל וְהִתְנַדְּבוּ בְּלֵב שָׁלֵם, פָּתַח בִּתְפִלָּה: "שָׁמְרָה זֹּאת לְעוֹלָם לְיֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבוֹת לְבַב עַמֶּךָ וְהָכֵן לְבָבָם אֵלֶיךָ" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, יח), שֶׁלֹּא יִסְתַּלֵּק וְיִגָּנֵז

And therefore King David, peace be upon him, during the preparations for building the Temple—which was likewise "the opening of Your words" with great light, when they donated with a whole heart—opened in prayer: "Keep this forever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct their heart unto You" (I Chronicles 29:18), praying that it not depart and be concealed
[דְּזָכָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִדְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְקִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָרַב בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ עוֹמֵד, כִּי קְדֻשָּׁה זוֹ נִשְׁאֲרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלָם]

[for he merited that the initial sanctity sanctified for its time and sanctified for the future, and even though destroyed it remains in its sanctity, for this holiness remained within Israel forever]
מֵעַתָּה, וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּילֵיהּ.
from that point onward, which is his unique spiritual rung.
וְלָכֵן אָנוּ אוֹמְרִים אַחַר הַתְּפִלָּה פָּסוּק זֶה, כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה נִכְנָסִים מוֹחִין וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת וְחֶשְׁקוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת בְּלֵב הָאָדָם
And therefore we recite this verse following prayer, for through prayer new mentalities, thoughts, desires, and holy yearnings enter the heart of man
[וּלְמִי שֶׁתְּפִלָּתוֹ מִצְוַת אֲנָשִׁים מְלֻמָּדָה, גַּם הָעֲנִיָּה כָּךְ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַרְגִּישׁ רַק בְּהֶרְגֵּל;
[and for one whose prayer is merely a perfunctory commandment learned by rote, the response is likewise such that he senses it only routinely;

אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין שׁוּם תְּפִלָּה מֵאִישׁ יִשְׂרְאֵלִי שֶׁלֹּא יֵעָנֶה, רַק עַל כָּל תְּפִלָּה יֵשׁ עֲנִיָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "קָרוֹב ה' לְכָל קֹרְאָיו לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָאֻהוּ בֶאֱמֶת", וְנֶאֱמַר: "תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב" – הַיְינוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל],

nonetheless there is no prayer of a Jewish person that is not answered, but over every prayer there is a divine response, as written: 'Hashem is near unto all who call upon Him in truth,' and 'You give truth to Jacob'—which encompasses all of Israel],
וּמְבַקְּשִׁים שֶׁלֹּא יִגָּנֵז:
and we plead that this illumination not be concealed.

paragraphs.text: The loss of felt illumination need not erase what labor has established in the heart.

rich.text: The loss of felt illumination need not erase what labor has established in the heart.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Taanit 15: “When Hashem gives a person illumination of understanding in the light of Torah, without the person having endured or labored for those words of Torah, then if he turns his attention away even for a moment, Scripture says (Proverbs 23:5), ‘Will you set your eyes upon it? It is gone.’ As the Jerusalem Talmud says at the end of Berakhot in the name of the Scroll of the Pious: if you leave it one day, it leaves you two. But Torah that comes through labor, for which the person has endured, becomes fixed in his heart and will not let him turn away. As it says (Deuteronomy 32:2), ‘May my teaching drop like rain’: my holy grandfather explained that Torah for which a person labors holds him from behind his neck and will not let him turn away, like someone holding his fellow so he cannot leave. If the person nevertheless turns away from Torah that came through labor, he can reawaken it through much prayer and regain his former illumination. Through the endurance and labor he devoted to it, it became fixed in his heart, and he can reawaken the Torah repeatedly through prayer.”

As it says (Deuteronomy 32:2), ‘May my teaching drop like rain’: my holy grandfather explained that Torah for which a person labors holds him from behind his neck and will not let him turn away, like someone holding his fellow so he cannot leave. If the person nevertheless turns away from Torah that came through labor, he can reawaken it through much prayer and regain his former illumination. Through the endurance and labor he devoted to it, it became fixed in his heart, and he can reawaken the Torah repeatedly through prayer.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef adds a distinction to the siman's account of first light and prayer. A gift can be lost when attention moves away; Torah acquired through effort becomes fixed enough to be awakened again through prayer. This explains a way in which the plea to preserve the first desire works together with the learner's subsequent labor.

sections.en: In the Place Where a Person's Thought Is

p: [קמד] בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהוּא הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁל אָדָם, שָׁם הוּא כָּל הָאָדָם;
In the place where a person's thought is, there is the entirety of the person;
כִּי עִיקַּר הָאָדָם אֵינוֹ הַגּוּף רַק הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֵינָהּ דָּבָר רַק כֹּחַ הַמְּחַשֵּׁב וּמְהַרְהֵר וְהָרוֹצֶה שֶׁבָּאָדָם.
for the core of man is not the physical body but the soul, and the soul is nothing other than the faculty of thinking, reflecting, and desiring within man.
וּמָקוֹם שֶׁמַּחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ אֲדוּקָה, כָּךְ הוּא כָּל צוּרַת הָאָדָם בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת.
And where his thought is bound fast, such is the entire form of the person at that moment.

תֵּדַע, שֶׁכֹּחַ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבָּאָדָם בְּעֵת הַזִּוּוּג פּוֹעֵל בַּוָּלָד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּכְּבָשִׂים דְּיַעֲקֹב, וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא נָשׂא ז) מִלֵּידַת בֵּן לָבָן לְכוּשִׁיִּים

You may know this, for the power of thought in a person during marital union shapes the offspring to be formed accordingly, as occurred with the sheep of Jacob, and as our Sages stated (Midrash Tanchuma, Nasso 7) regarding the birth of a white child to black parents
[וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (נִדָּה לא.): תָּלָה הַכָּתוּב הַזְּכָרִים וְכוּלֵי, כִּי הַכֹּל לְפִי הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל אוֹת ס"ג)].
[and this is what they said in Niddah 31a: Scripture attributed male offspring to the female, etc., for all follows the thought (as explained above in Section 63)].
וְיָדוּעַ דְּטִפַּת הַזֶּרַע הוּא תַּמְצִית כֹּחַ הָאָדָם, שֶׁהֲרֵי עַל יְדֵי זֶה נוֹלָד גַּם כֵּן דְּמוּת אָדָם, עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הִיא תַּמְצִית מִכָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו וְאֵבָרָיו,
And it is known that the seminal drop is the essence of a person's total power, seeing that through it an entire human form is born, so perforce it is the condensation of all his faculties and limbs;
וַהֲרֵי שֶׁכָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו וְאֵבָרָיו מְלֻבָּשִׁים כָּךְ, כִּי בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁמְּחַשֵּׁב נַעֲשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר צוּרַת כָּל הָאָדָם בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה.
behold, all his faculties and limbs are enclothed in that state, because in the place where he thinks, that very thing becomes the form of the entire person at that hour.
וּלְכָךְ הַמְּחַשֵּׁב בְּאַחְדוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל שָׁעָה נַעֲשֶׂה כֵּן,
Therefore, one who meditates on the unity of the Blessed Name at all times becomes transformed into that reality,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב): "תַּמָּתִי" – תְּאוֹמָתִי וְכוּלֵי,
and concerning this they said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): "'My undefiled one' (tamati)—my twin (te'omati), etc.,"
וְאָמְרוּ (שָׁם סוֹף פֶּרֶק ג): לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ וְכוּלֵי, וְאָמְרוּ: שְׁכִינָה מְדַבֶּרֶת מִתּוֹךְ גְּרוֹנוֹ.
and they stated (ibid., end of chapter 3): He did not cease cherishing her until He called her His mother, etc., and they said: the Shechinah speaks through his throat.
וְכֵן הַדָּבֵק בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁמְּחַשֵּׁב בָּהּ תָּמִיד, כָּל אֵבָרָיו כֵּן,
And likewise, one who cleaves to the Torah and contemplates it constantly, all his limbs become transformed into it,

כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹף חֲגִיגָה כז.): תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין אוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֶטֶת בָּהֶן, שֶׁכָּל גּוּפָן אֵשׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ" (יִרְמְיָה כג, כט).

as our Sages of blessed memory stated (end of Chagigah 27a): the fire of Gehenna has no dominion over Torah scholars, for their entire body is fire, as it is said: "Is not My word like as fire?" (Jeremiah 23:29).
וְכֵן בְּכָל מִדָּה וּמִדָּה.
And so it is with every single character trait.
וּלְכָךְ אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב, אֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם, זָכוּ לִבְנֵיהֶם אַחֲרֵיהֶם, שֶׁכָּל בְּנֵיהֶם גּוּפָן מְשׁוּנֶּה מִשְּׁאָר אֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים, וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.

And therefore Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the Patriarchs of the world, merited for their children after them that the very bodily constitution of all their descendants is fundamentally distinct from other nations; and likewise the reverse, Heaven forbid.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יח:): רְשָׁעִים בְּחַיֵּיהֶם קְרוּיִים מֵתִים, לְפִי שֶׁדְּבוּקָה מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם בְּמָקוֹם הַנִּקְרָא מִיתָה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין קַיָּים לָעַד.
And concerning this they said (Berakhot 18b): the wicked in their lifetime are called dead, because their thought is cleaving to the place termed death, meaning that which does not endure forever.
וְגַם בְּאוֹתוֹ שָׁעָה אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם חַיּוּת אֱלוֹהַּ שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא חַיִּים.
And also at that hour he possesses no divine vitality, which alone is termed life.

וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשִׁילְהֵי כְּתוּבּוֹת (קיא:): עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְכוּלֵי מָצָאתִי לָהֶם תַּקָּנָה וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁמִּצַּד הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה בְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם נַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם:

Therefore our Sages stated at the end of Ketubot 111b: for simple folk I have found a remedy through marrying their daughters to Torah scholars, for through thinking of and binding with a Torah scholar, one becomes like a scholar.

paragraphs.text: Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 1 1:4: “It is known to those of understanding that the human body is not the person himself as far as the body is concerned, for it is called the person’s flesh, as it is written, “You clothed me with skin and flesh, and covered me with bones and sinews.” It is also written, “It shall not be poured upon a person’s flesh.” The person is thus the inward being, while the body is a garment in which the intellectual soul, which is the person himself, is clothed while in this world. After death that garment is removed, and he is clothed in a pure, clean, spiritual garment, as it is written, “Remove the filthy garments,” and “Clothe you in fine garments.” This is called the garment of the sages.”

paragraphs.text: The thought that holds the heart’s life

paragraphs.text: A central attachment is distinguished from the outer passing garments of thought.

rich.text: A central attachment is distinguished from the outer passing garments of thought.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Machshavot Charutz 1:6: “A thought of this kind, upon which the heart's principal point of life depends, is the essence of the person—not the other outer thoughts, which are garments of the inward and principal thought. Almost no person is completely pure even in thought's outer garment, belonging to Hashem alone so that no other thought rises in his mind for even one moment throughout his life.”

rich.text: : “A thought of this kind, upon which the heart's principal point of life depends, is the essence of the person—not the other outer thoughts, which are garments of the inward and principal thought. Almost no person is completely pure even in thought's outer garment, belonging to Hashem alone so that no other thought rises in his mind for even one moment throughout his life.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Machshavot Charutz makes an explicit distinction relevant to ‘where his thought is attached.’ The thought carrying the heart's central life defines the person at depth; other thoughts can be outer garments. It also acknowledges how difficult it is to be entirely free of a momentary other thought. This helps read the siman's language of attachment with precision while preserving the task of directing thought toward Torah.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Nasso 7:1: “An Arab king asked Rabbi Akiva: I am black and my wife is black, but she bore me a white son. I will kill her, for she has been unfaithful to me. He asked him: Are the images in your house black or white? He answered: White. He said: When you were with her, she set her eyes on the white images and bore a child like them. If you wonder at this, learn from Jacob’s sheep, which conceived from the rods, as it is said, “The sheep conceived at the rods.” The Arab king acknowledged the explanation and praised Rabbi Akiva.”

paragraphs.text: Context: This is the Midrashic narrative Rav Tzadok invokes for the effect of the image held in mind at conception; it explicitly links its example to Jacob’s sheep. The relevant source is this story at the end of Nasso 7, rather than the preceding laws of the suspected adulteress.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:11:2: ““With the crown with which his mother crowned him”: Rabbi Yochanan said: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai asked Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosi, “Have you perhaps heard from your father the meaning of ‘With the crown with which his mother crowned him’?” He replied, “Yes.” He asked, “How?” He replied: “It is like a king who had an only daughter whom he loved exceedingly and called ‘my daughter.’ He did not cease loving her until he called her ‘my sister,’ and did not cease loving her until he called her ‘my mother.’ So the Holy One, blessed be He, loved Israel exceedingly and called them ‘My daughter,’ as it is written, ‘Hear, daughter, and see.’ He did not cease loving them until He called them ‘My sister,’ as it is said, ‘Open to Me, My sister, My companion.’ He did not cease loving them until He called them ‘My mother,’ as it is said, ‘Listen to Me, My people, and My nation, give ear to Me’—the written form can be read ‘My mother.’” Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai stood and kissed him on his head, saying, “Had I come only to hear this explanation from your mouth, it would have been enough.””

Therefore he said, “This is the word,” for his speech was the actual word of Hashem: “The Divine Presence speaks from his throat.” He spoke from his essential vitality, meaning the letters of his soul: the combinations of his soul at that time corresponded to the words he spoke. paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 15:62: “However, one can say that from the statement "they are not consumed" there is no difficulty: for that phrase "has no dominion," rather than stating "they do not enter at all," makes it clear that they enter, only that the fire does not dominate them; and so they stated in Menachos 100a that Topheth was prepared even for a king who is a Torah scholar; and if so, perforce it does not mean that the fire has no effect at all such that he feels no burning, for if so, for what purpose do they enter and why was it prepared for him? And they also related in Chagigah 15b regarding Acher, that Rabbi Meir caused smoke to ascend from his grave to judge him, showing that the fire held dominion over him even though he was a Torah scholar; and initially when the heavenly court ruled not to judge him on account of his Torah, that meant not to bring him into Gehinnom at all, for since they judged that he would have no share in the World to Come, they gave him the reward of his Torah—which the Holy One, blessed be He, does not withhold—that he should not be judged or suffer in the agony of Gehinnom; while Rabbi Meir said that he should be judged so that he might ultimately enter the World to Come; yet in any event we see that the fire dominated him even though his entire body was fire!”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin asks explicitly why a scholar whose body is fire can nevertheless undergo judgment, and uses Acher as the difficult example. This qualifies the siman’s account of thought shaping the whole person. Torah’s formative presence is not an automatic exemption from the consequences of misconduct; Rav Tzadok distinguishes entry into judgment from what judgment can ultimately destroy.
