paragraphs.text: There is no greater transgression for the sake of Heaven than Esther’s. Her statement about herself, “If I perish, I perish,” was written through the holy spirit. Presumably there is an actual designation of loss here, arising from such a transgression as intercourse with a gentile, which is the ultimate assimilation among the nations, described as being lost—as in “Those lost in the land of Assyria shall come,” referring to those who had become assimilated among the nations. Dinah had intercourse with a gentile: although it began under compulsion, because of its later stage—concerning which our Sages said that a woman who has had intercourse with a gentile finds it difficult to separate—she had to be reincarnated as a gentile woman, Cozbi daughter of Tzur, as is known.

paragraphs.text: Esther, however, whose entire intention was for the sake of Heaven and to save all Israel from the decree of destruction and annihilation, could not herself be lost, Heaven forbid. Rather, through this she rectified all Israel, who had sinned then through bowing to the image and enjoying the banquet of a non-Israelite. This constitutes mingling with the nations and assimilating among them so as to become like them, Heaven forbid. Through it they aroused that wicked man’s decree to write concerning the Jews that they should be destroyed. Yet they had acted only outwardly and under compulsion. Their sin was that they had not given up their lives for the sanctification of Hashem’s name, as Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah did.

paragraphs.text: She too sinned in this respect when she initially replied to Mordecai that she ought not put herself in danger in order to save all Israel, and did not wish to sacrifice her life as she was obligated to do. Concerning this he replied, “[You and your father’s house] shall perish”: the decree would be fulfilled in her, for her sin was greater than theirs. What is done under compulsion and only outwardly is not truly called idolatry at all, or assimilation among the nations; but she did not concern herself with saving all Israel from destruction when a certain decree stood before her. She immediately repented and sacrificed herself—not only risking her body, but also risking the loss of her soul through the imparting of defilement and the ultimate assimilation among the nations, although it was against her will. Through this she rectified herself and all Israel, by committing another such grave transgression as entering of her own will. Nevertheless, it was entirely contrary to her true will. It was a transgression for the sake of Heaven that, on the contrary, is considered a great mitzvah, as I have received: in this manner lies the ultimate rectification of every sin. This is not the place to elaborate.”

paragraphs.text: Context: This is the extended parallel behind “as I wrote elsewhere.” Rav Tzadok moves from Moses and the Tablets to Elijah, Yael, and Esther, while retaining repentance, punishment, and atonement as integral parts of the discussion. His argument distinguishes an act’s outward form from its true intention and from the retrospective disclosure of its role. Elijah’s exceptional act is explicitly commanded by Hashem, and Esther’s action is described as contrary to her true will and undertaken to save Israel. The paragraph itself states that even complete repentance out of love does not remove every need for atonement. The kabbalistic account of Dinah and Cozbi is quoted as Rav Tzadok’s interpretation.

The paragraph itself states that even complete repentance out of love does not remove every need for atonement. The kabbalistic account of Dinah and Cozbi is quoted as Rav Tzadok’s interpretation.

Is it good in your eyes that Hashem’s power be limited in their eyes? Let them and a hundred like them perish, but let My power not be limited before them even for a single moment.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Rashi on Numbers 11:22 preserves two readings of the meat request. Rabbi Akiva understands Moses’ words as questioning the provision, while Rabbi Shimon rejects that reading and understands Moses as protesting the sequence of feeding and then punishment. Rashi’s preservation of the disagreement matters: Rav Tzadok’s reference to a corresponding failure in Moses accords with the first approach, while his connection between the leader and the people is his larger interpretation. Numbers 20:12 supplies the explicitly named Meribah example.

sections.en: A Person's Honor in This World Corresponds to His Purity in Mundane, Permitted Pursuits

p: [קנה] הַכָּבוֹד שֶׁל הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא כְּפִי טָהֳרָתוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁלּוֹ, שֶׁהֵם הַלְּבוּשִׁין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְדִבְרֵי הַמִּצְוָה,
A person's honor in this world corresponds to his purity in mundane, permitted pursuits, which serve in this world as the outer garments for holy commandments,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (בְּשַׁלַּח סא עַמּוּד א) דְּנֶצַח וָהוֹד לְבוּשֵׁי מַלְכָּא, וְהֵם תְּרֵין בַּדֵּי עֲרָבָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא וּבַתִּיקּוּנִים,
as written in the Zohar (Beshalach 61a) that Netzach and Hod are the garments of the King, representing the two willow branches (aravah), as stated in the Ra'aya Mehemna and the Tikkunim,
שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר: עֲרָבָה לֹא טַעַם וְלֹא רֵיחַ, כָּךְ וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
concerning which our Sages stated in Vayikra Rabbah (Emor 30:12): the willow has neither taste nor fragrance, so are those who have neither Torah nor good deeds, see there.
וְכֵן הִמְשִׁילוּ בְּחֻלִּין (צב.) עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים לְעַלְיָא וְאִתְכַּלְיָא, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And so in Chullin 92a they compared simple folk and Torah scholars to the protective grape leaves (alya) and the clusters of grapes (itkalya), see there.
וְכֵן יֵשׁ בִּפְעֻלַּת כָּל אֶחָד בְּעַצְמוֹ: פְּעֻלּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה הֵם מַעֲשֵׂה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, וּפְעֻלּוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ נִקְרָא עַם הָאָרֶץ.
And so it is within the actions of each individual: spiritual Torah actions are the deeds of a scholar, while his worldly activities are called the am ha'aretz (the unlearned).

וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:) עַל "וְעָלֵהוּ לֹא יִבּוֹל" (תְּהִלִּים א, ג) – אֲפִילּוּ שִׂיחַת חוּלִין וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁהֵם עַלְיָא לְאִתְכַּלְיָא דְּהַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And so our Sages expounded (Sukkah 21b) on "and its leaf does not wither" (Psalms 1:3)—even the casual speech of scholars, which serves as the protective leaf for the cluster of Torah,
וְאִלְמָלֵא עַלְיָא וְכוּלֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (לה:): הַנְהֵג בָּהֶן וְכוּלֵי, בְּמָטוּתָא מִינַּיְיכוּ וְכוּלֵי, וְהַרְבֵּה וְכוּלֵי וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ, דְּאִלְמָלֵא וְכוּלֵי.

and were it not for the leaf, the cluster could not endure, as stated in Berakhot 35b: "Conduct yourself with them in the way of the world... I beg of you, etc., many did as Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and did not succeed, because without the leaf, etc."
וְאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קיג.): מָאנֵי מְכַבְּדוּתָא, (וְשָׁם קמה:): וּבְלָא מָתָא תּוֹתְבָאי.
And they stated in Shabbat 113a: clothes are that which honor a person; and on 145b: when out of town, my clothes establish my name.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּלְאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְגָּרֵשׁ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִגַּן עֵדֶן שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹמוֹ, עָשׂוּ לוֹ מַלְבּוּשִׁים, וּכְפִיהֶם הוּא הַכָּבוֹד.
That is, after Adam the First was expelled from Gan Eden which was his native home, garments were made for him, and according to them honor is bestowed.
וְזֶהוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁפְּעֻלּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת הוּא נִקְרָא גּוּף הָאָדָם וְהָרְשׁוּת הוּא מַלְבּוּשָׁיו;
And this applies to this world, wherein actions of Torah and mitzvot are termed the person's essential body, while permitted mundane acts are his outer garments;
אֲבָל בְּגַן עֵדֶן הַלְּבוּשׁ מִפְּעֻלַּת הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (וַיַּקְהֵל רי עַמּוּד א),
but in Gan Eden the soul's garment is woven from the deeds of Torah and mitzvot, as written in the Zohar (Vayakhel 210a),
וְהַיְינוּ דְּגוּף הָאָדָם שָׁם נִקְרָא רַק הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וָלֵב
meaning that the "body" of the person there consists strictly of the thoughts and desires within mind and heart
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּף נִקְרָא גּוּף הָאָדָם וְהַלְּבוּשׁ הוּא הַמַּלְבִּישׁ אֶת הַגּוּף, וּלְאַחַר מִיתָה אָז גּוּף הָאָדָם נִקְרָא הַנְּשָׁמָה וְהַגּוּף נִקְרָא רַק לְבוּשׁ.

[and just as in this world the physical body is called the person's body and clothes are the garments worn over the body, after death the soul is termed the body and the physical form is merely a garment.
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּרַשְׁבִּ"י בִּבְרָכוֹת שָׁם דְּלֵית לֵיהּ הַנְהֵג בָּהֶן מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
And this was the lofty level of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in Berakhot who rejected engaging in mundane labor,
כִּי הוּא זָכָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַמָּשׁ לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן, שֶׁהַגּוּף רַק לְבוּשׁ וְעַלְיָא לְאִתְכַּלְיָא, וְלֹא הַמִּדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
for in this physical world he literally merited to be as in Gan Eden, where the body is merely an outer robe and the leaf to the grape-cluster, and not the trait of derech eretz,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לג:) שֶׁהֶעֱנִישׁ לְהָעוֹסְקִים בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
as stated in Shabbat 33b that he struck down those who engaged in mundane plowing, and this is not the place to elaborate],
וְשָׁם הַכָּבוֹד כְּפִי הַפְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ בְּתוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת.
and there in Gan Eden honor corresponds to his practical deeds in Torah and mitzvot.
וְעוֹד לְמַעְלָה הַלְּבוּשׁ כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר (שָׁם עַמּוּד ב) מִן הַכַּוָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּלֵּב וּרְצוֹנוֹת לְתוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
And higher still in the celestial realms, the garments are woven from the intentions of the heart and holy longings for Torah and mitzvot (Zohar ibid. 210b), see there;
וְשָׁם הַכָּבוֹד לְכָל אֶחָד כְּפִי כַּוָּנָתוֹ הַטּוֹבָה, וַעֲדַיִן נִקְרָא "בְּלָא מָתַאי".
and there honor is bestowed according to his pure intention, yet even this is still termed being "away from home."
אֲבָל "בְּמָתַאי" – זֶה יִהְיֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהוּא שְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל (כַּנּוֹדָע בַּזֹּהַר):
But being "at home" will unfold in the World to Come, which is the Jubilee Year (as known in the Zohar):
"תָּשֻׁבוּ אִישׁ אֶל אֲחֻזָּתוֹ" (וַיִּקְרָא כה, יג), שָׁם יִהְיֶה שְׁמַאי – הַשֵּׁם מוֹרֶה עַל הָעֶצֶם, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּפִי עֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹר מַחְצַב הַנְּשָׁמוֹת.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 12:1: “Although “leaves” are everywhere expounded as what is not the principal object, as Sukkah expounds “its leaf does not wither” to include even ordinary conversation, and Chullin identifies leaves and grape clusters with ordinary people and Torah scholars, it also says that without the leaves the clusters could not endure: in grape clusters the leaves protect. This concerns what lies ahead. The principal thing is certainly Torah scholars and effort in Torah with intention for the sake of Heaven, while action is the leaves: ordinary people are those who perform mitzvot and good deeds. So too within the individual: when a person engages in mitzvot and good deeds, this sustains his wisdom, as Avot teaches, while the principal fruit is wisdom.”

The comparison helps keep the imagery relational: it describes what sustains or clothes what at a particular level, rather than assigning one fixed meaning to “leaf” throughout all the teachings.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Hoshana Rabba 13:1: “Every kind of suffering proceeds from the lack of a place, as the Talmud asks (Shabbat 145b): why are Babylonian Torah scholars distinguished by their clothing? Because they are not in their own place. As people say: in my own city, my name; outside it, my garment. Someone away from his place must distinguish himself through many boundaries, because opponents continually confront and press him, requiring extensive clarification. Concerning this Hashem promised, ‘I will establish a place for My people Israel.’ Israel's principal place is as the Midrash says: the Holy One is the place of the world, while His world is not His place. When He illuminates this recognition for Israel, that He is the world's place, they recognize that nowhere in the world is outside His protection.”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vaetchanan 8:1: “There is likewise a difference among the souls of Torah scholars. Some are consecrated from birth to belong entirely to God, like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his companions, whose Torah was their occupation. They were exempt from prayer, which is called temporal life, because all their occupation was with eternal life. They did not turn their attention at all to their livelihood, and a carob tree and a spring of water were created for them. Yet not everyone merits this, as they said: Many acted like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and did not succeed. We have already discussed the Gemara’s statement that when Israel do not fulfill God’s will, they perform their own work, as it says, “You shall gather your grain.” Maharsha asks: Surely this passage says, “If you diligently obey My commandments”; how can they be called people who do not fulfill God’s will? The explanation is that God’s original thought and will at Creation, when He made the human being upright, was that the person should be free for His service. This is called God’s will. But the Holy One, blessed be He, does not deal oppressively with His creatures, and therefore did not explicitly command this. Accordingly, when they left the cave, saw people plowing and harvesting, and punished them for leaving eternal life and occupying themselves with temporal life, a heavenly voice said, “Have you come out to destroy My world?”—because most of the public cannot maintain this way of life.”

sections.en: The Rectification for Nocturnal Emission

p: [קנו] תִּיקּוּן לְמִקְרֵה לַיְלָה
The rectification for nocturnal emission

[וְגַם בְּמֵזִיד נִקְרָא כֵּן בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (קו.) עַל פָּסוּק "וַתִּקְרֶאןָ" – רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ כֻּלָּם וְכוּלֵי]

[and even when committed willfully it is termed thus in Scripture and Chazal; and in Sanhedrin 106a on "and they called the people" (Numbers 25:2), Rabbi Yehoshua states that they all experienced emissions]
לְהַאֲמִין בֶּאֱמוּנָה שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם מִקְרֶה בָּעוֹלָם כְּלָל, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁיֶּאֱרַע לוֹ, יֵדַע שֶׁהַכֹּל בְּכַוָּנַת מְכַוֵּין יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.

is to believe with complete faith that there is no such thing as chance (mikreh) in the world at all, and whatever occurs to him, let him know that it is entirely through the deliberate design of the Designer, blessed be His Name.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת עִיקַּר הַכֹּל, וְכָל תַּרְיַ"ג מִצְווֹת הַתּוֹרָה הֵם רַק עֵיטִין לְהַגִּיעַ לִידִיעָה זוֹ שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And this realization is truly the core of everything, and all 613 commandments of the Torah are merely counsels of advice to arrive at this awareness: that everything is from the Blessed Name.
וְכָל הָעֲבֵירוֹת נִקְרָא בַּתּוֹכָחָה "אִם תֵּלְכוּ עִמִּי קֶרִי" (וַיִּקְרָא כו, כא) – לְשׁוֹן מִקְרֶה, כִּי הָעֲבֵירוֹת הֵם יְצִיאָה מִן הַסֵּדֶר וְאֵין לָהֶם סֵדֶר

And all sins are designated in the Reproof as "if you walk with Me in happenstance (keri)" (Leviticus 26:21)—an expression of chance (mikreh), for sins appear as a departure from cosmic order, having no divine structure
[וּבְשׁוּב ה' וְגוֹמֵר "כְּחֹלְמִים" (תְּהִלִּים קכו, א), כְּמוֹ בַּחֲלוֹם אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה כַּמָּה מַעֲשִׂים וּכְשֶׁהֵקִיץ אֵין כְּלוּם, כָּךְ כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת אָז;
[and when Hashem returns the captivity we shall be 'like dreamers' (Psalms 126:1), for just as in a dream a man performs deeds that vanish upon awakening, so will all sins be seen then;
זוּלַת הַקֶּרִי שֶׁזֶּה גַּם כְּשֶׁהֵקִיץ יֵשׁ פְּעֻלָּה, וְכֵן כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת נִקְרָא כֵּן, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
save for nocturnal emission where even upon awakening a physical result remains, and likewise all sins are so termed, and this is not the place to elaborate],
וְכֵן כָּל הָעֳנָשִׁים נִקְרָא שָׁם "חֲמַת קֶרִי" (וַיִּקְרָא כו, כח).
and likewise all the punishments are designated there as "the fury of happenstance (chamat keri)" (Leviticus 26:28).
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁמַּאֲמִין שֶׁאֵין מִקְרֶה, מַמְתִּיק כָּל הַדִּינִים וּמְתַקֵּן כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת,
And by believing that there is no chance, he sweetens all strict judgments and rectifies all sins;
כִּי אִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחֲךָ כֻּלָּם לֹא הָיוּ יוֹצְאִים מִן הַסֵּדֶר, וְהָיָה מְסוּדָּר כָּךְ וְלֹא בְּמִקְרֶה, וְאִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ עֲבֵירָה,
for if so, perforce none of them truly departed from divine order, but all was so orchestrated and not by chance, and if so, it was not an absolute rebellion,

paragraphs.text: Knowledge and choice each have their place

rich.text: Knowledge and choice each have their place

paragraphs.text: Rav Tzadok distinguishes the illumination reached in teshuvah from the standpoint of choosing an act.

rich.text: Rav Tzadok distinguishes the illumination reached in teshuvah from the standpoint of choosing an act.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Tzidkat HaTzadik 40:1: “The essence of repentance is that Hashem illuminate a person's eyes until deliberate sins become merits: he recognizes and understands that all he sinned was also within Hashem's will, as the Sages teach in Berakhot concerning three verses, including “You turned their hearts backward” and “whom I afflicted.” This is the matter of knowledge and choice explained by the Ari at the end of Four Hundred Shekels of Silver: both are true, each in its own place. Where choice operates there is no place for knowledge, and where knowledge operates there is in truth no place for choice. When a person attains this immense light, all his deliberate sins cease to be outside the depth of Hashem's knowledge, and He, His knowledge and His will are all one. Since Hashem willed it so, all is merit, and he attains the complete atonement of Yom Kippur. This is the secret of the scapegoat: if a person performed this act on his own, he would be committing outright idolatry, the prohibition “You shall have no other gods,” the foundation of all negative commandments and all departures from Hashem's will. But because sending the goat is Hashem's will and command, it becomes a mitzvah rather than a transgression. The Sages explain this in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, chapter 46; see Ramban on Acharei. We give a portion to Azazel, the evil, because Hashem commanded that it be given, and thus the transgression becomes a mitzvah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Siman 40 is an especially precise counterpart to the retrospective claim here. It states explicitly that knowledge and choice are both true in their respective places, then uses the scapegoat to distinguish a commanded act from the same act undertaken independently. Read together, these passages describe the illumination of teshuvah without making the human standpoint of choice disappear or converting an uncommanded act into a mitzvah by personal assertion.

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim distinguishes Israel's acknowledgment that everything is in Heaven's hands from taking that acknowledgment as encouragement to pursue one's desires. It places the latter fault at the root even when an outwardly fine garment hides it. This is an essential qualification when reading the siman's retrospective restoration of order. The same source later describes the great shofar bringing even those called lost back into recognition and repair.

p: [קנז] אִלּוּ הָיָה נִמְצָא אָדָם שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית כָּל יָמָיו בְּתַכְלִית שֶׁלֹּא נִתְכַּוֵּין מֵעוֹלָם בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר לַהֲנָאָתוֹ, הָיָה חַי לְעוֹלָם,
Had there existed a person who guarded the Covenant throughout all his days to such perfection that he never once intended in that organ for personal pleasure, he would live forever,
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כז): אִם יֹאמְרוּ לְךָ: אִלּוּ לֹא חָטָא אָדָם הָיָה חַי לְעוֹלָם? אֱמוֹר לָהֶם: הֲרֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ וְכוּלֵי.
as our Sages stated in Vayikra Rabbah (27:4): "If they say to you: Had Adam not sinned, would he have lived forever? Say to them: Behold, Elijah, etc."
וְאֵלִיָּהוּ נִקְרָא "מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית" כַּנּוֹדָע
And Elijah is designated the "Angel of the Covenant," as is known
[וּלְכָךְ אָמְרָה לוֹ אוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה: בָּאתָ אֵלַי בִּתְשַׁמִּישׁ הַמִּטָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק לג;
[and therefore that woman alleged to him: "You came to me in marital intimacy," as stated in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 33;
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי כָּל שֶׁקֶר שֶׁאוֹמְרִים עַל אָדָם הוּא מַה שֶּׁאוֹתוֹ אָדָם מְיוּחָד לְטוֹבָה בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר,
and it is known that every falsehood spoken against a person targets the very matter in which that person is uniquely sublime for good,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְמֹשֶׁה: "וּמַדּוּעַ תִּתְנַשְּׂאוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טז, ג), וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם יב, ג).
as they accused Moses: "Why do you lift yourselves up, etc." (Numbers 16:3), while Scripture testifies: "Now the man Moses was very humble, etc." (ibid. 12:3).
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יח): אוֹתוֹ תִּינוֹק – מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף;
And our Sages stated (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah 18): that child was Mashiach ben Yosef;
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי הוּא הַמְתַקֵּן אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר, דַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף,
and it is known that he is the one who rectifies that very trait, the rung of Joseph,
וּמִיתָתוֹ נִקְרָא: "וְהִבִּיטוּ אֵלַי אֵת אֲשֶׁר דָּקָרוּ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.),
and his death is referred to in: "and they shall look unto Me whom they have pierced" (Zechariah 12:10; Sukkah 52a);
וְחַד אָמַר: יֵצֶר הָרָע, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת, כִּי מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף דּוֹקֵר לְיֵצֶר הָרָע,
and one sage interprets this as the evil inclination, both being truth, for Mashiach ben Yosef pierces the evil inclination,
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין נְקִיִּים בָּזֶה, עַל יָדָם מַגִּיעַ מִיתָתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
and because the people of Israel are not pristine in this realm, his death is brought about through them as I wrote elsewhere;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרָה: "מַדּוּעַ בָּאתָ... לְהַזְכִּיר אֶת עֲוֹנִי", וְהוּא הֶחֱיָהוּ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
and therefore she challenged: "Have you come to call my sin to remembrance?" (I Kings 17:18), and he revived him, and this is not the place to elaborate].
וְיִשַׁי מֵת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ (שַׁבָּת נה:) וְנִקְרָא "נָחָשׁ" בַּכָּתוּב (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יז, כה), רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁרַק דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ,

And Jesse died solely through the counsel of the Serpent (Shabbat 55b) and was called "Nachash" (Serpent) in Scripture (II Samuel 17:25), meaning that only in this single trait was the root of the Serpent present in him,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עָלָיו (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ) עַל פָּסוּק "הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי",
as our Sages expounded concerning him (Midrash Rabbah, Tazria) on the verse "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity" (Psalms 51:7);
וְנִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן בִּישַׁעְיָה: "מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ יֵצֵא צֶפַע וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה יד, כט) עַל מָשִׁיחַ.
and it is likewise said in Isaiah: "out of the serpent's root shall come forth a basilisk, etc." (Isaiah 14:29), referring to the Messiah.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּבֶן דָּוִד יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה, וְהוּא יִזְכֶּה לְחַיִּים דַּיְיקָא וְלֹא מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף,
That is, the Son of David will likewise issue from this lineage, yet he specifically will merit eternal life and not Mashiach ben Yosef,
כִּי רַק עַל יְדֵי תִּיקּוּן הַקִּלְקוּל יִהְיֶה הַחַיִּים, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תָּמִיד לב.): מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְיִחְיֶה? יָמִית עַצְמוֹ.
for specifically through rectifying the damage will eternal life be attained, in the manner of: "What shall a man do to live? Let him slay himself" (Tamid 32a).
כִּידוּעַ דְּאִילָנָא דְּמוֹתָא נִקְרָא הָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר בַּמִּדְבָּר קיט עַמּוּד א, בְּהַעֲלוֹתְךָ קנה עַמּוּד ב,
For as is known, the "Tree of Death" denotes the Supernal Earth (Malchut), as written in Zohar III:119a and 155b,
וְתִיקּוּנָהּ לְחַבְּרָהּ בְּבַעְלָהּ, עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה מֵאִילָנָא דְּמוֹתָא – אִילָנָא דְּחַיֵּי, וְלֹא בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר.
and its rectification is to unite it with its Husband (Tiferet), through which the Tree of Death is transformed into the Tree of Life, and in no other way.
וְעַל יְדֵי קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית מַגִּיעַ הַקִּלְקוּל בָּזֶה כַּנּוֹדָע בְּטַעַם "ה' צִלְּךָ" (תְּהִלִּים קכא, ה),
And through blemishing the Covenant the rupture reaches this supernal union, as known regarding "Hashem is your shadow" (Psalms 121:5),
וּלְכָךְ אֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה, הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אִם יְכֻפַּר הֶעָוֹן הַזֶּה לָכֶם עַד תְּמֻתוּן" (יְשַׁעְיָה כב, יד) בְּג' חִלּוּקֵי כַּפָּרָה שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דּוֹרֵשׁ,

and therefore ordinary repentance does not avail, matching: "Surely this iniquity shall not be expiated by you till you die" (Isaiah 22:14) among the categories of atonement expounded by Rabbi Yishmael (Yoma 86a),
דִּשְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית נִקְרָא קִדּוּשׁ ה' בְּסוֹטָה (י:): יוֹסֵף שֶׁקִּדֵּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְכוּלֵי
for guarding the Covenant is termed sanctifying the Name of Hashem, as in Sotah 10b: "Joseph who sanctified the Name of Heaven, etc."
[כִּידוּעַ דְּשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם הוּא הֵ"א (שֶׁנִּיתּוֹסַף בְּיוֹסֵף) אַחֲרוֹנָה דְּשֵׁם שֶׁמּוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ לָשֵׁם, שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּאֶרֶץ הַנִּזְכָּר],
[for as is known, 'the Name of Heaven' is the final Hei of the Tetragrammaton added to Yehosef, wherein one surrenders himself unto that Name, which is the rung of the Supernal Earth],
וּבְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִדְרָשׁ מִכְּלַל הֵן – לָאו.
and in words of Torah, from the positive we infer the negative: violating it constitutes a desecration of the Name requiring death.
וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה בַּזֹּהַר סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בַּמִּדְבָּר (קכא עַמּוּד א): שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה בְּלֹא רַמִיָּה, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And the counsel for this is in the Zohar (end of Bemidbar 121a): that he surrender his soul unto death without deceit, see there.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית (ח:) מִקְּרָא דְּדָנִיֵּאל, דְּקַבָּלַת הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת הָוֵי כְּמַעֲשֶׂה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְחַיִּים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל

And that matches what is stated in Ta'anit 8b from the verse in Daniel, that the sincere acceptance of the heart is legally equivalent to action, and through this he merits eternal life as noted above
[אַךְ צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת, כִּי אִם יַחְשׁוֹב עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִזְכּוֹת בַּחַיִּים – אֵינוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת, וְאָז אַדְּרַבָּה סַכָּנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בַּזֹּהַר.
[yet it must be in total sincerity, for if he calculates through this to attain life, it is not genuine truth, and then on the contrary it invites mortal danger as written in the Zohar.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: אַל יִפְתַּח פִּיו לַשָּׂטָן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפָרָשַׁת בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ שָׁם גַּבֵּי מֹשֶׁה.
And that aligns with: 'A person should never open his mouth to the Satan,' and as written in Parashat Beha'alotekha regarding Moses.
וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁשָּׁם מֹשֶׁה לֹא רָצָה בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן, שֶׁהֲרֵי בִּקֵּשׁ אַדְּרַבָּה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:
For there Moses did not truly desire death, seeing that on the contrary he sought the welfare of Israel, and this is not the place to elaborate].

paragraphs.text: Radak on Malachi 3:1:4: ““The lord”—this is the King Messiah, and he is the angel of the covenant. Alternatively, “the angel of the covenant” refers to Elijah. Thus the aggadah says that Elijah was zealous for the covenant of circumcision, which the kingdom of Ephraim prevented them from observing, as it says: “I have been very zealous for the Lord, God of Israel, for the children of Israel have forsaken Your covenant.” He said to him: You were zealous at Shittim, and here you are zealous for circumcision. By your life, Israel will not perform circumcision without your seeing it with your own eyes. From this they established a seat of honor for Elijah, who is called the angel of the covenant, as it says: “The angel of the covenant whom you desire—behold, he comes, says the Lord of hosts.””

paragraphs.text: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 33:3: “"He and she" (indicate that it was) by the merit of Elijah that they had to eat. After (a period of) days, the son of the woman fell sick and died, as it is said, "And it came to pass after these things that the son of the woman fell sick" (1 Kings 17:17). The woman said to him (Elijah): Thou didst come unto me for coition, and thou wilt bring my sin to remembrance against me, and my son is dead. Now take away all that which thou hast brought to me, and give me my son. Elijah, may he be remembered for good, arose and prayed before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said before Him: Sovereign of all the worlds ! Is it not enough (to endure) all the evils which have befallen me, but also this woman; for I know that out of sorrow for her son has she spoken of a matter which has not occurred, which she has brought against me to vex me. Now let all the generations learn that there is a resurrection of the dead, and restore the soul of this lad within him; and He was entreated of him, as it is said, "And the Lord hearkened unto the voice of Elijah" (1 Kings 17:22). Another Scripture text says, "And Elijah || took the child… See, thy son liveth" (1 Kings 17:23).”

paragraphs.text: The two messianic roles and the removal of death

rich.text: The two messianic roles and the removal of death

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek explains the end of a particular opposing power and its renewal without rivalry.

rich.text: Dover Tzedek explains the end of a particular opposing power and its renewal without rivalry.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 2:4: “When the time comes for death to be swallowed up forever and the matter of killing to depart from the world, the corresponding holy power of killing in Yosef must also depart. Therefore he too will be killed and depart from the world. The sunlight of Yosef and his power of holy killing against Esav will then depart, for that matter will no longer exist in the world. Then the light of Mashiach ben David will shine, and he will revive Mashiach ben Yosef. “New faces have come here”: after resurrection he becomes a new creature, without the self-exaltation associated with his previously described level. Therefore he will no longer envy Yehudah and will acknowledge Mashiach ben David. Thus it says, “They shall look toward Me concerning the one whom they pierced”: the killing of Mashiach ben Yosef is attributed to Israel. All Israel's striving is to repair the serpent's counsel and have death swallowed up; through this the death reaches ben Yosef, like the death of the evil inclination mentioned there and above. In this way they have pierced him indirectly.”

In this way they have pierced him indirectly.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Dover Tzedek expands the very interpretation signaled here by “as I have written elsewhere.” Yosef's role in opposing a destructive force belongs to the period when that force is present. Its cessation and renewal under Mashiach ben David are therefore connected to the removal of death itself. This supplies context for the deliberately compressed association of the deaths of Mashiach ben Yosef and the evil inclination, rather than treating the two expressions as an unexplained verbal equivalence.

paragraphs.text: David’s return changes the direction of the past through an actual sanctification of the Name.

rich.text: David’s return changes the direction of the past through an actual sanctification of the Name.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 11:7: “Since Hashem's name was sanctified through King David's consequences and the greatness of his repentance, that act is truly considered a sanctification of Hashem, rather than a desecration. Nevertheless, he does not need death to complete the cleansing; on the contrary, through this he merits enduring life. In every passage of Torah one infers the affirmative from the negative: if desecration of the Name requires death for atonement, the good measure is greater, and sanctification of Hashem gives life.”

rich.text: : “Since Hashem's name was sanctified through King David's consequences and the greatness of his repentance, that act is truly considered a sanctification of Hashem, rather than a desecration. Nevertheless, he does not need death to complete the cleansing; on the contrary, through this he merits enduring life. In every passage of Torah one infers the affirmative from the negative: if desecration of the Name requires death for atonement, the good measure is greater, and sanctification of Hashem gives life.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains the positive counterpart of the siman's atonement language. Through David's repentance and its consequences, the Name is sanctified; the former desecration becomes part of that sanctification. The source therefore speaks of gaining enduring life. This clarifies why Rav Tzadok locates the life of the Davidic repair in transformed failure rather than in an untouched outward record alone.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Bamidbar 8:74-76: “A person should regard himself as though he has departed from the world, for he entrusts his soul to this place of death. Therefore it has no letter vav, for vav is the Tree of Life, while this is the Tree of Death. This teaches the mystery that there are sins not atoned for until a person departs from the world, as it is written, “This sin will not be atoned for you until you die.” This person truly gives himself over to death and hands his soul over to that place—not as a deposit, as at night, but as one who has truly departed from the world. This rectification requires the heart’s intention; then the Holy One, blessed be He, has compassion on him and atones for his sins. Fortunate is the person who knows how to seek His favor and serve his Master with desire and intention of heart. Woe to one who comes to seek his Master’s favor with a distant heart and without willingness, as it says, “They enticed Him with their mouths and lied to Him with their tongues, but their heart was not steadfast with Him.” He says, “To You, Lord, I lift my soul,” while all his words come from a distant heart. He brings upon himself departure from the world before his time when that tree awakens in the world to execute judgment. Therefore a person must attach his soul and will to his Master and not approach Him with a false intention, for it says, “One who speaks falsehood will not stand before My eyes.” What does “will not stand” mean? When he prepares himself for this while his heart is distant from the Holy One, blessed be He, a voice goes out and says, “He will not stand before My eyes.” This person seeks to set himself in order; “he will not stand”—I do not desire that he should do so. All the more if he comes to unify the holy name without unifying it properly.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef interprets the same Zohar passage through the responsibility to clarify oneself to the limit of one's ability. The surrounding discussion warns that believing one has done everything is not sufficient if further clarification remains possible. This explains why the siman rejects an acceptance secretly adopted merely as a device for obtaining life: the condition concerns the reality of the heart's service, rather than the wording of a declaration.

sections.en: Through the Surrender of One's Soul Unto Death in His Thought in Absolute Truth—wholeheartedly…

p: [קנח] עַל יְדֵי מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ לְמִיתָה בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת גָּמוּר, שֶׁמַּסְכִּים בְּלִבּוֹ אִם רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְטוֹב לוֹ יוֹתֵר לָמוּת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, הוּא רוֹצֶה כָּךְ בְּרָצוֹן טוֹב – הוּא נִיצוֹל מִגְּזֵירַת מִיתָה רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.

Through the surrender of one's soul unto death in his thought in absolute truth—wholeheartedly consenting that if it is the will of the Blessed Name and better for him to die, Heaven forbid, he desires it with goodwill—he is delivered from the decree of death, may the Merciful One preserve us.

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, שֶׁמַּחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וְקַבָּלָתוֹ עַל עַצְמוֹ כְּמַעֲשֶׂה, וְהוּא אַחַר כָּךְ כְּאִלּוּ בָּא בְּגִלְגּוּל שֵׁנִי לְזֶה הָעוֹלָם, וְהוּא יֵדַע מַה שֶּׁקִּלְקֵל בְּגִלְגּוּלוֹ הָרִאשׁוֹן וְיָכוֹל לְתַקְּנוֹ בְּגִלְגּוּל זֶה.

As I wrote above, his thought and heartfelt acceptance are accounted as action, and subsequently he is as though he returned in a second reincarnation (gilgul) into this world, knowing what he corrupted in his first lifetime and empowered to rectify it in this reincarnation.
וְאֵין לְךָ שׁוּם עֲבֵירָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה, כִּי הַמִּיתָה מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל הַכֹּל.
And you have no sin in the world that does not find rectification through this, for death atones for everything.
וְלָכֵן מִזְמוֹר דְּ"אֵלֶיךָ ה' נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא" (תְּהִלִּים כה, א) מְסַיֵּים בִּנְפִילַת אַפַּיִם: "וְהוּא יִפְדֶּה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכֹּל עֲוֹנֹתָיו" (שָׁם קל, ח)
And therefore the psalm "Unto You, Hashem, do I lift up my soul" (Psalms 25:1) concluding the Tachanun supplication ends: "and He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities" (Psalms 130:8)
[וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה דִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ לְמִיתָה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא כְּלֹא נֶחְשָׁב בְּעֵינֵי עַצְמוֹ, עַל יְדֵי זֶה דָּבוּק בְּאוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא "הוּא" כַּנּוֹדָע].
[and through this surrender unto death, viewing himself as absolute nothingness, he cleaves unto that supreme level termed 'Hu' (He), as is known].
וּלְכָךְ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, הַגֶּבֶר שֶׁהֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, אָמַר דָּבָר זֶה.
And therefore King David, peace be upon him, the man who established the yoke of repentance, articulated this.

כִּי רָאשֵׁי הַיְצָרִים הֵם שְׁנַיִם: דַּעֲבֵירָה וּדְעַבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (סט:) וּבְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה, וּמִשְּׁנֵיהֶם מִי שֶׁפּוֹרֵשׁ מֵת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יז.);
For the foremost inclinations are two: that of unchastity and that of idolatry (Yoma 69b; Shir HaShirim Rabbah), and from both of them one who separates dies, as stated in Avodah Zarah 17a;
וְזָכָה דָּוִד לְ"אֵלֶיךָ ה' וְגוֹמֵר", פִּדְיוֹן עַל הַמִּיתָה, וְ"חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לּוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים כא, ה).
and David merited "Unto You, Hashem, etc.," achieving redemption from death: "He asked life of You, You gave it to him" (Psalms 21:5).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי שְׁנֵי הַיְצָרִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים הֵם שְׁנֵי קְצוֹת שֶׁהֵם הָפְכִיִּים זֶה לָזֶה כַּנּוֹדָע, וְיוֹסֵף עָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן דַּעֲבֵירָה וְלֹא דָּוִד.
That is, because these two inclinations are two polar extremes opposing one another, and Joseph withstood the trial of unchastity while David did not.
וְהִנֵּה הַמִּשְׁפָּט מֵת בְּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף, וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ;
And behold, the judgment of death befalls Mashiach ben Yosef, while Mashiach ben David experiences the reverse;

רַק דְּמִיּוֹסֵף יָצָא יָרָבְעָם שֶׁהוּא יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם לְתַקֵּן רַק עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּלוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי עַל יְדֵי אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה בְּטַעֲנַת "לָא הוּא וְלָא אַגְרֵיהּ".

only that from Joseph issued Jeroboam who personified the inclination for idolatry, which was impossible for human effort to rectify except through its complete eradication by the Men of the Great Assembly claiming: "Neither it do we desire, nor its reward" (Yoma 69b).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִצְרָא דַּעֲבֵירָה צָרִיךְ בָּעוֹלָם כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם, וּלְכָךְ אֵין מַגִּיעַ הַמִּיתָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
In contrast, the inclination for unchastity is necessary for the world's survival, which is why actual death is not mandated, and this is not the place to elaborate.

וּלְכָךְ זָכָה דָּוִד לְדַרְגָּא דִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ לְמִיתָה בַּחַיִּים, שֶׁהוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּל יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶצְלוֹ לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם כֹּחַ זוּלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ כֻּלּוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ עוֹד

And therefore David merited the level of surrendering his soul unto death during physical life, achieved solely through utterly nullifying the inclination for idolatry within himself, recognizing no power other than Hashem and surrendering himself entirely to the Blessed Name, and this is not the place to elaborate further.
[וּפִינְחָס זֶה אֵלִיָּהוּ מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית, וּבָא מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁפִּטְפֵּט בְּיִצְרוֹ;
[And Phinehas is Elijah the Angel of the Covenant, descending from the seed of Joseph who curbed his inclination;
רַק שְׁבָטִים בִּזּוּהוּ: מִזַּרְעָא דְּיִתְרוֹ שֶׁפִּטֵּם וְכוּלֵי – יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
yet the tribes degraded him: descending from Jethro who fattened calves for idols—the inclination for idolatry as noted above;
רַק הוּא מָסַר נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה בְּזִמְרִי, שֶׁאִלְמָלֵי נֶהֱפַךְ זִמְרִי וַהֲרָגוֹ וְכוּלֵי כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין פב.),
yet he surrendered his life unto death against Zimri, for had Zimri turned and slain him, etc. (Sanhedrin 82a),
וְלָכֵן זָכָה לִבְרִית שָׁלוֹם בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ דְּחַי לְעוֹלָם]:
and therefore he merited the Covenant of Peace in Elijah who lives forever].

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Shabbat Chol HaMoed Sukkot 33:1: “Therefore, after the sin, Moshe was not at ease with the governance of an angel. An angel cannot recognize how a person's life from Hashem was not interrupted even during the sin. This resembles the teaching of the Zohar Chadash on Vayetzei: after a person surrenders all his life in Nefilas Apayim, Hashem returns his life through a narrow path hidden even from the heavenly host. So too after a person sins and repents, only Hashem Himself can show the repair: that this person's connection was never interrupted, even during the sin, as the Sages teach, “I am Hashem after a person sins and repents.” From the angel's standpoint, however, the connection is interrupted during the sin and no repair is available from that standpoint. Therefore Moshe was not at ease after the sin with the governance of an angel, and prayed, “See, You say to me…””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim makes the same prayer comparison and explains what lies behind the renewed life: a connection sustained by Hashem even where an angel cannot perceive its continuity through the sin. This adds a precise dimension to the siman's image of beginning again with knowledge of what requires repair. The cited passage is about the inward act of Nefilas Apayim and the divine restoration that makes teshuvah possible.

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:29: “This matter of the deepest origin of thought is not clarified in this world, as is known. That deepest origin is called “nothing,” whereas thought is called “something,” since a person’s thought—what he is thinking—is already a perceptible entity. It is something from nothing: from the deepest origin, hidden from the person’s eye and seemingly nonexistent. For this reason it is also called “He,” as is known. It is said, “On that day Israel’s iniquity will be sought and will be absent.” In this world there are sins, for one cannot become purified at that level; only “on that day,” meaning that there is a day [indicating clarification of a matter] called “that day,” when the hidden gate called “He,” which indicates the concealed, will open.”

paragraphs.text: Open prophecy withdrew when the struggle against idolatry was abolished.

rich.text: Open prophecy withdrew when the struggle against idolatry was abolished.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Sichat Malakhei HaSharet, From Yerushalmi 16: “Sin caused this to be hidden through the request of the Great Assembly. Seeing the greatness of the sins, they said, “We want neither it nor its reward,” and abolished the impulse to idolatry; the Midrash places this in the days of Mordechai and Esther. By subduing that impulse, the opposite of recognizing Hashem, they had attained revelation of the Shechinah. Even when they followed it, nature was disrupted against them measure for measure: saying “Hashem does not see,” they were shown that He sees all their acts. But when the impulse was abolished, prophecy and the Shechinah's open presence withdrew as well, because the setting through which they attained that revelation was gone. All was then concealed. Esther, at the end of the Babylonian exile, therefore marks the end of the open miracles given to be written; thereafter the miracles were hidden and were not given to be written.”

By subduing that impulse, the opposite of recognizing Hashem, they had attained revelation of the Shechinah. Even when they followed it, nature was disrupted against them measure for measure: saying “Hashem does not see,” they were shown that He sees all their acts. But when the impulse was abolished, prophecy and the Shechinah's open presence withdrew as well, because the setting through which they attained that revelation was gone. All was then concealed. Esther, at the end of the Babylonian exile, therefore marks the end of the open miracles given to be written; thereafter the miracles were hidden and were not given to be written.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet develops what was included in “neither it nor its reward.” Overcoming the impulse toward idolatry had been a setting for open recognition of the Shechinah; when the impulse was abolished, that form of prophecy and open miracle also receded. This makes the siman's contrast of the two impulses more precise: their histories and place in the world differ, so removing one cannot simply be made the model for removing the other.

sections.en: If a Single Individual Repents

p: [קנט] יָחִיד שֶׁשָּׁב מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ וּלְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא פו:);
If a single individual repents, forgiveness is granted to him and to the entire world, as our Sages stated (Yoma 86b);
וְאֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר מְחִילָה? רַק שֶׁמְּעוֹרֵר בְּלִבָּם גַּם כֵּן הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה.
and how is such universal forgiveness possible? It is because he awakens in the hearts of others thoughts of repentance as well.
וְלֹא כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת עַצְמוֹ יָחִיד בָּזֶה עוֹשֶׂה, כִּי לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן;
And not everyone who wishes to make himself that unique individual can do so, for such a figure has not yet arisen;
רַק מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד הוּא יִהְיֶה כֵּן, כִּי צָרִיךְ שֶׁתִּהְיֶה נַפְשׁוֹ כּוֹלֶלֶת מִכָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת,
only the Messiah son of David will be thus, for his soul must encompass all souls,
כִּי בְּלָאו הָכִי אֵין הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָתוֹ יְכוֹלִים לְהוֹלִיד הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה בְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְנַפְשׁוֹ.
since otherwise the stirrings of his repentance cannot generate repentance in those who have no affinity to his soul.
וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַהִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה כּוֹלְלִים כָּל חֶלְקֵי נַפְשׁוֹ.
And those thoughts of repentance must encompass all facets of his soul.
כִּי מִי שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ, אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ כָּל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ,
For whoever encompasses the entire world contains within himself all kinds of powers of the entire world,
וְאִם שָׁב רַק בְּכֹחַ אֶחָד לְבַד, אֵין מְעוֹרֵר תְּשׁוּבָה רַק לְמִי שֶׁנִּתְלִים בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ.
and if he repents only within one single faculty, he awakens repentance only in those attached to that faculty.
כְּמוֹ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת, שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא רֶגֶל ד' שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה, וְהֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה רַק בַּעֲוֹן תַּאֲוָה לְבַד.

Like King David, peace be upon him, who likewise encompassed all souls, being the fourth leg of the divine Chariot, yet who established the yoke of repentance specifically regarding the sin of passion alone.
וְלָכֵן יָרָבְעָם שֶׁהָיָה נָקִי בָּזֶה
And therefore Jeroboam, who was pristine in this regard

[כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁנִּקְרָא אֶפְרָתִי, שֶׁפֵּירוּשׁ שֵׁם זֶה: מִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו, וְלָכֵן מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילֹנִי שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּשִׁילֹה יֵשׁ לוֹ יַחַס עִם שֵׁבֶט אֶפְרָיִם],

[as I heard that he was called Efrati, meaning one who never experienced nocturnal emission, which is why he found favor in the eyes of Ahijah the Shilonite, Shiloh being connected to the tribe of Ephraim],
לֹא שָׁב וְנֶחְלַק עַל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד.
did not repent, and rebelled against the Davidic monarchy.
וְזוּלַת הָאָבוֹת וְדָוִד לֹא הָיָה מִי שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ
And apart from the Patriarchs and David, there was no one who encompassed the entire world
[כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כּוֹלֵל רַק הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁדּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר כֻּלּוֹ דּוֹר דֵּעָה וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים].
[for Moses our teacher encompasses solely Torah scholars, except that the Generation of the Wilderness was entirely a generation of knowledge and scholars].
וּשְׁאָר יְחִידִים שֶׁשָּׁבִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם יְכוֹלֶת לְהָשִׁיב רַק הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַתְּלוּיִים בָּהֶם [וּבְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ שֶׁשָּׁבִים],
And other individuals who repent are empowered to awaken only those souls dependent upon them, [and within that specific faculty in which they repent],
כְּאוֹתוֹ תַלְמִיד בִּמְנָחוֹת (מד.) שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ עוֹרֵר גַּם כֵּן הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה בְּאוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה שַׁיָּיכֶת לוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי נַעֲשֵׂית אַחַר כָּךְ אִשְׁתּוֹ.
like that student in Menachot 44a whose repentance awakened a stirring of repentance in that woman who was soul-tied to him, becoming subsequently his wife.
וּמִי שֶׁמְּחוּיָּב מִיתָה בַּחֲטָאָיו, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעוֹרְרוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה עַד שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגַת תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ, וְאָז יוּכַל לְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ תְּשׁוּבָה.

And one who is liable to death for his sins cannot be awakened to repentance until the tzadik surrenders his own life unto death as well, which matches his level of repentance, and only then can he stir repentance within him.
וּלְכָךְ פִּינְחָס עָצַר הַמַּגֵּפָה
Therefore Phinehas halted the plague
[שֶׁהוּא עוֹנֶשׁ הַמַּגִּיעַ לִזְנוּת – אַנְדְּרָלָמוּסְיָא, רַק שֶׁשָּׁבוּ]
[which is the retribution visiting unchastity—indiscriminate destruction, save that they repented]
עַל יְדֵי מְסִירַת נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה, וְעוֹרְרָם שֶׁשָּׁבוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ גַּבֵּי מִלְחֶמֶת מִדְיָן.
through surrendering his life unto death, awakening them to repent as the Sages said concerning the war with Midian.
וְכֵן בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סה) בְּעוּבָדָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה, שֶׁרַק כְּשֶׁהוֹלִיכוּהוּ לַצְּלָב, אָז עוֹרֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָה לְבֶן אֲחוֹתוֹ.
And so in Bereishit Rabbah (end of Parashah 65) regarding Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer of Tzreidah, that only when they led him to the gallows did he awaken his nephew Yakum to repentance.
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָפְלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם בְּעֵת מַחֲלוֹקֶת קֹרַח, שֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁנִּגְזַר עֲלֵיהֶם מִיתָה וּמָסְרוּ נַפְשָׁם לְמִיתָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר, וּכְדֵי לְהַעֲלוֹתָם בִּתְשׁוּבָה;

And so Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces during the rebellion of Korah, seeing death decreed upon them and surrendering their lives unto death, as written in the Zohar, in order to elevate them in repentance;
וְלֹא הוֹעִיל, לְפִי שֶׁהֵם נֶחְלְקוּ עָלָיו וְהִפְרִידוּ עַצְמָם מֵחִבּוּרָם בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, וּלְכָךְ לֹא פָּעַל הִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ בְּלִבָּם,
yet it did not avail because they rebelled against him and severed themselves from connection with his soul, so his spiritual awakening could not operate within their hearts,
כִּי בְּמִדָּה שֶׁאָדָם מוֹדֵד מוֹדְדִין לוֹ, וּבְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁרוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ מוֹלִיכִין אוֹתוֹ:
for with the measure a man metes out is it measured unto him, and in the way one desires to go, along that path they lead him.

paragraphs.text: The account of Yosi ben Yoezer shows what the present siman means by an awakening passing from one person to another.

rich.text: The account of Yosi ben Yoezer shows what the present siman means by an awakening passing from one person to another.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 6:2: “Nevertheless, Yosi ben Yoezer’s words entered his heart, and he carried out upon himself the four court-imposed deaths; within a short time he preceded Yosi to the Garden of Eden. So too Yosef Meshita: although he had previously rebelled and entered the Sanctuary, afterwards he would not consent to enter again, even at the cost of his life, and sanctified the divine Name. This is ‘the fragrance of his garments,’ expounded as ‘the fragrance of his betrayers,’ as in Sanhedrin 37a. From the fragrance of his previous betrayal he was elevated with still greater force, for the inner heart was revealed: at Israel’s root they are bound to holiness. This is the meaning of ‘It is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will; what prevents us is the leaven in the dough.’ This applies even to the most disreputable person, as they had been beforehand.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah retells the encounter cited in this siman and explains its inward result: beneath the previous betrayal, a heart bound to holiness was revealed. This gives content to the siman’s claim that the tzaddik awakens a connected soul rather than mechanically transferring forgiveness. The other person’s own will turns and becomes manifest. The limits of such influence remain explicit here: a particular person awakens the souls and faculties connected to his own return, and the universal completion is reserved for Mashiach.

sections.en: A Person's Soul Encompasses the Souls of All His Servants and Those Subordinate To…

p: [קס] הָאָדָם נַפְשׁוֹ כּוֹלֶלֶת מִכָּל נַפְשׁוֹת מְשָׁרְתָיו וְהַנִּכְנָעִים תַּחְתָּיו,
A person's soul encompasses the souls of all his servants and those subordinate to him,
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ: "מֹשֵׁל מַקְשִׁיב עַל דְּבַר שָׁקֶר, כָּל מְשָׁרְתָיו רְשָׁעִים" (מִשְׁלֵי כט, יב), וְאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין (ד:): הָא עַל דְּבַר אֱמֶת וְכוּלֵי.
which is why Scripture states: "If a ruler hearkens to falsehood, all his servants are wicked" (Proverbs 29:12), from which Chullin 4b infers: but if he hearkens to truth, his servants are righteous.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה עֹבַדְיָה גַּם כֵּן מִמְּשָׁרְתֵי אַחְאָב, לְפִי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קב:): אַחְאָב וַתְּרָן בְּמָמוֹנוֹ הָיָה, וּלְכָךְ עֹבַדְיָה עַל הַבַּיִת, שֶׁבָּזֶה הָיָה כִּשְׁרוֹנוֹ.
Nonetheless Obadiah was among the stewards of Ahab, because Sanhedrin 102b states: Ahab was generous with his money, and therefore Obadiah presided over his household, where his financial virtue lay.
וּמִצַּד הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ בְּוַתְּרָנוּת הָיָה עֹבַדְיָה.
And from the element of good within Ahab's generosity stemmed his connection to Obadiah.
וְכֵן כָּל אֶחָד שֶׁמּוּרְכָּב מִטּוֹב וָרָע, כֵּן מְשָׁרְתָיו: וְהַטּוֹב הוּא מְמוּנֶּה עַל הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ, וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ.
And so with every person composed of good and evil, so are his attendants: the good is appointed over his good traits, and the evil over his bad.
וְכֵן כָּל הַחֲפָצִים, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר הַמַּאֲכָלִים שֶׁל הָאָדָם, הוּא מֵהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחַ נַפְשׁוֹ וְחַיּוּתוֹ בָּהֶם, וּמִזֶּה הוּא חַיּוּתָם כַּיָּדוּעַ.

And so with all possessions, and it goes without saying a person's food, which derive from the extension of his soul-power and vitality within them, from which they receive their vitality as is known.
וּמִמָּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא טוֹב, כָּךְ כָּל כֵּלָיו הַמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִים מֵאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ, וְכֵן הַמַּאֲכָלִים שֶׁמֵּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ יֵשׁ בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה גְּדוֹלָה.
And from whatever source within him is good, so are all his utensils extending from that power, and likewise the food deriving from that power contains immense holiness.
וְזֶה טַעַם גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "עַל כֵּן לֹא יֹאכְלוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב, לג), שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁהַמַּלְאָךְ יָכֹל לוֹ שָׁם, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּיֵשׁ שָׁם חִסָּרוֹן בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ

And this is the inner reason of the sciatic nerve (gid hanasheh), concerning which it is said: "Therefore the children of Israel eat not, etc." (Genesis 32:33), for since the angel could prevail against Jacob there, infer that there existed a deficiency in the spiritual root
[וְהַיְינוּ בַּתַּאֲוָה דְּשָׁם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: אֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד וְכוּלֵי],
[namely in the bodily desire situated there, as I wrote elsewhere on the rabbinic dictum: 'even the most pious, etc.'];

וּלְכָךְ אֵין לֶאֱכוֹל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, דִּמְקוֹם חַיּוּתוֹ מִגִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה דְּאָדָם, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מד עַמּוּד ב): נֶפֶשׁ מְשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, כִּי יֵשׁ שָׁם חַיּוּת מֵאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר.

and therefore one must not eat the sciatic nerve, for the food's vitality would nourish the sciatic nerve of the human body, in line with Berakhot 44b: soul restores soul, drawing vitality into that organ.
[וְטַעַם דָּם – כִּי "הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ" (דְּבָרִים יב, כג), שֶׁעִיקַּר חֵטְא בַּנֶּפֶשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תֶחֱטָא" (וַיִּקְרָא ד, ב) כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
[And the prohibition of blood is because 'the blood is the life' (Deuteronomy 12:23), the root of sin lying in the animal soul, as in 'if a soul sins' (Leviticus 4:2), as I wrote elsewhere.

וְכֵן עִיקַּר הַחֵטְא כְּעִנְיַן "שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים לב, טו), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יָצָא מֵחֵלֶב עֵינֵמוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים עג, ז) וּבְכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת, וְלָכֵן אָסוּר חֵלֶב, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:

And likewise the essence of sin arises from indulgence, as in 'you grew fat, thick, etc.,' and 'their eyes stand out with fatness,' and so in many places, which is why forbidden animal fat (chelev) is prohibited, and this is not the place to elaborate].

paragraphs.text: The relation is a connection between corresponding levels, whose differences remain real.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:77:1: “Property belongs to a person: even when it is lost, it must be returned when he has an identifying mark or recognizes it, indicating a relation, recognition and testimony that it is his. Everything lives through Hashem's word, and the person's own life presumably has a relation to the life within the possession. There are four levels in the lower world—inanimate, plant, animal and speaking human—with the upper realms as a fifth. Likewise there are four elements—fire, air, water and earth—with heaven as a fifth substance. Likewise there are four soul levels: nefesh, ruach, neshamah and the soul of the soul, chayah, with yechidah as the fifth, as explained elsewhere. A person contains the inanimate, plant, animal and speaking levels; the inanimate power is the power of the nefesh, and so forth. There is certainly a difference between the inanimate power in an inanimate thing and the corresponding power within a person; nevertheless they have a bond and relation.”

It explicitly distinguishes an inanimate power in an object from the corresponding power in a human being. This clarifies the siman's extension of a person's faculties into possessions and food: relation and correspondence are intended, without making the levels identical.

paragraphs.text: Pri Tzaddik explains the spiritual value of the righteous person's possessions through their divine source.

rich.text: Pri Tzaddik explains the spiritual value of the righteous person's possessions through their divine source.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Vayishlach 10:1: ““Complete in his wealth” corresponds to “with all your might,” which Berakhot expounds as a person whose money is dearer to him than his body. How can there be someone whose money is dearer than his body to whom one says, “You shall love…”? In fact, Chullin says this of the righteous: their money is dearer to them than their bodies because they do not reach out to take what belongs to others. We likewise find concerning Abba Chilkiyah in Taanit that he said, “This heals, while this does not heal.” The reason is that their property is only what Hashem gives them, and they know that it belongs to the essential root of their life; therefore it is dear to them, as explained in teaching 6.”

It does not make every possession or every use of it holy automatically; the present siman explicitly differentiates the good and bad powers of a mixed person.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 216:1: “They established three meals for this, for food sustains life. Through eating in accordance with the blessed God’s will, these influences enter the heart: since God established food to sustain human life, it certainly contains a life-giving power. They said in the Mekhilta: Torah was given only to those who ate manna. That is the bread eaten by the ministering angels; it contains immense spiritual vitality, and through it one merits much Torah. Presumably all the Torah scholars who occupy themselves with Torah, to whom Torah is given, are eaters of manna, as it says: Whoever accepts the yoke of Torah has the yoke of government and ordinary work removed from him. His livelihood resembles manna and certainly contains that holiness, bringing vitality from the truth of the blessed God into his heart, through which he apprehends Torah from the truth of His wisdom.”

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Leviticus 4:2:1: ““When a soul sins inadvertently”: Because thought belongs to the soul, and it is the soul that errs, “soul” is mentioned here. The reason for offerings on behalf of the soul that errs is that all sins produce a disgrace in the soul and constitute a blemish in it. It cannot receive the presence of its Maker unless it is pure of every sin. Otherwise even the foolish among the nations would merit coming before Him. Therefore the soul that sins inadvertently brings an offering, so that it may merit drawing near to the God who gave it. For this reason too, “soul” is mentioned.”

sections.en: When a Person Experiences Suffering in a Particular Limb or in a Specific Faculty…

p: [קסא] כְּשֶׁאָדָם מִתְיַסֵּר בְּאֵיזֶה אֵבֶר אוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה כֹּחַ מִכֹּחוֹתָיו
When a person experiences suffering in a particular limb or in a specific faculty among his spiritual powers
[כִּי ע' כֹּחוֹת בַּנֶּפֶשׁ נֶגֶד ע' אֻמּוֹת בָּרָע כַּיָּדוּעַ],
[for there are seventy faculties in the soul corresponding to seventy nations in evil, as is known],
מִסְּתָמָא בּוֹ חָטָא,
presumably through it he sinned;
וּמִיָּד שֶׁלָּקָה, הֲרֵי הוּא כְּאָחִיךָ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַכּוֹת כג.)
and the moment he is afflicted with lashes, behold he is restored as your brother, as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Makkot 23a)
[וַאֲפִילּוּ רַק כְּפָתוּהוּ וְכוּלֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַכּוֹת (שָׁם),
[and even if they merely bound him to be lashed, etc., as stated in Makkot there,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קכא:) בְּנָחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחֲרָיו, כִּי בָּזֶה יָצָא יְדֵי עוֹנְשׁוֹ וְיִסּוּרִין שֶׁלּוֹ בַּפַּחַד שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁיִּשְּׁכֶנּוּ;
and as in Shabbat 121b regarding a snake that was pursuing a person, for through that alone he fulfilled his punishment and suffering via the mortal terror that it would bite him;
וְכֵן הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת דְּמִן הַשָּׁמַיִם נִזְדַּמְּנוּ וְכוּלֵי כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם,
and so it was in truth that from Heaven it was orchestrated, as brought there,
רַק שֶׁחָסוּ עָלָיו וּפְדָאוּהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נה.): חֶלְמָא בִּישָׁא וְכוּלֵי,
only that they showed compassion upon him and redeemed him through that terror, along the lines of Berakhot 55a regarding a distressing dream whose anguish suffices,
כִּי כְּשֶׁשָּׁב בֶּאֱמֶת, אָז כָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא כְּחוֹלְמִים (תְּהִלִּים קכו, א)];
for when one truly repents, all worldly experiences become like dreamers (Psalms 126:1)];
וְאָז אוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר וְכֹחַ מְתוּקָּן, וְנֶפֶשׁ מֵשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, שֶׁאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר יֵשׁ בּוֹ תִּיקּוּן, אֶלָּא שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהוֹסִיף וּלְחַזְּקוֹ.
and then that limb and faculty are spiritually rectified, and soul restores soul, seeing that within that limb rectification now resides, only that one must further strengthen and fortify it.
וְאָז "בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם בְּנֵי אֵל חָי" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ב, א) – דַּיְיקָא בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם הוּא מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ:

And then "in the place where it was said unto them: 'You are not My people,' there it shall be said unto them: 'You are the children of the living God'" (Hosea 2:1)—specifically in that exact spot is it transformed into the literal opposite.
(מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ) כְּגוֹן מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נַעֲשָׂה דַּיְיקָא עֲבוֹדַת ה',

(From his holy handwriting.) [This passage was cut from the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902) without notice. It is restored here from R' Michael Mokotowski's copy of the author's manuscript, first printed in Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMalei (Jerusalem, 1968).] For instance, out of idolatry specifically there comes the service of Hashem,
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (נב.)
and therefore they said in Avodah Zarah (52a)
דְּיָלְפִינַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל טְעוּנָה גְּנִיזָה מִמִּזְבֵּחַ, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
that we derive from the altar that the idol of a Jew requires interment, see there,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ עָבַד רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלֹא כֹּחַ אַחֵר.
for in very truth he served only Hashem, blessed be He, and no other power.
וְכֵן מִקִּלְקוּל הַבְּרִית נַעֲשָׂה שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית,
And likewise, out of the damage to the covenant comes the guarding of the covenant,
וְדַיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְשֵׁם צַדִּיק,
and specifically through this one merits the name "tzadik,"
שֶׁרוֹצֶה לוֹמַר הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
which means the one who directs his flow to the Congregation of Israel.
וּבְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה הִשְׁפִּיעַ לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן,
And in emitting seed in vain he directed his flow to another place, may the Merciful One save us;
וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם שָׁם יֵשׁ שְׁכִינָה בַּגָּלוּת,
yet in truth the Shechinah is in exile there too,
כַּנּוֹדָע עַל פָּסוּק "וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה",
as is known on the verse "and His kingdom rules over all" (Psalms 103:19),
וְעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה נַעֲשָׂה מֵאוֹתָם טִיפִּין גֵּרִים,
and through repentance converts are made from those drops,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְנוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
as we wrote elsewhere
אַגְּמָרָא (נִדָּה יג:) מְשַׂחֲקִים בְּתִינוֹקוֹת וּמְקַבְּלֵי גֵּרִים,
on the Gemara (Niddah 13b) about "those who play with children and those who accept converts,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁחוֹזְרִים אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת לִקְדוּשָּׁה.
meaning that those souls return to holiness.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּגֵרִים נִקְרָא תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה,
And it is known that converts are called "under the wings of the Shechinah,"
וְנִמְצָא הִשְׁפִּיעַ הַכֹּל לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
so it turns out that he directed all his flow to the Congregation of Israel and not to another place, Heaven forbid,
וְהוּא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר.
and he is a complete tzadik.
וְאִשָּׁה נִקְרָא גּוּף,
And a woman is called "body,"
וּלְכָךְ מְשַׂחֲקִין בְּתִינוֹקוֹת נַעֲשָׂה גּוּף גֵּר.
and therefore through those who play with children the body of a convert is formed.
וּבְלָאו הָכִי מוֹצִיא רַק רוּחָנִיּוּת הַחַיּוּת לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
Otherwise, he brings out only the spirituality of the life-force into holiness,
וּמְעַכֵּב הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא בָּא לְתַקֵּן זֶה,
and he delays the Messiah, who comes to rectify this,
וְצָרִיךְ לְלַקֵּט הַכֹּל,
and everything must be gathered up;
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁמְּשַׂחֲקִין וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁאֶצְלָם לִשְׂחוֹק,
and this is "when they play, etc."—that for them it is mere play;
כִּי גַּם בֶּאֱמֶת מִמֵּילָא נִתְקַן הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ,
for in truth everything is in any case rectified through the Messiah,
רַק שֶׁזֶּהוּ מְעַכְּבוֹ, שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהִשְׁתַּהוֹת לְתִיקּוּן גַּם זֶה.
only this is what delays him, for he must tarry to rectify this as well.
אֲבָל הַזּוֹכֶה לָשׁוּב בֶּאֱמֶת
But one who merits to repent in truth—
נַעֲשָׂה מֵהֶם נְפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ וְלֹא גֵּרִים,
from them actual Jewish souls are made, and not converts;
כִּי גֵּרִים נִקְרָא תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה,
for converts are called "under the wings of the Shechinah,"
וְנִקְרָא צַדִּיק שֶׁאֵינוֹ גָּמוּר,
and he is called a tzadik who is not complete,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ כֹּחַ לִגְמַר הָרָאוּי לְהוֹלָדַת נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
who lacks the strength for the completion (gemar) required to beget a Jewish soul,
רַק כְּעִנְיַן הַעֲרָאָה,
only something like ha'ara'ah, the initial stage of union;
וְעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה גְּמוּרָה נִקְרָא צַדִּיק גָּמוּר. (עַד כָּאן מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ)
but through complete repentance he is called a complete tzadik. (End of his holy handwriting.)

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 205:1: “In every evil power there is, in truth, also good. The seventy souls of the house of Israel correspond to the seventy nations: they comprise the good in the seventy powers of the soul, while the idolaters comprise the evil. By bringing out the words of Torah hidden within it and drawing what it has swallowed out of its mouth, the illusion is thereby nullified, and this is victory over that nation.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Rav Tzadok gives the correspondence between seventy nations and seventy powers of the soul. His distinction between the good and evil manifestations of a power explains why its correction need not mean its destruction.

paragraphs.text: Makkot 23a:19-23b:1: “Mishnah: All those liable to karet, the penalty of being cut off, who have received lashes are released from that liability, as it is said, ‘And your brother is degraded before your eyes’: once he has received lashes, he is again your brother. These are the words of Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel. Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel also said: If a person who commits one transgression loses his life on its account, how much more should a person who performs one mitzvah be granted his life! Rabbi Shimon says: This is learned from the very same passage, for it is said, ‘The souls that do these things shall be cut off,’ and so on, and ‘Which a person shall do and live by them.’ Thus, one who refrains from committing a transgression is given a reward like one who performs a mitzvah.”

paragraphs.text: Yosef turns the encounter toward his own repair

rich.text: Yosef turns the encounter toward his own repair

paragraphs.text: The frightening encounter becomes an occasion for examining the corresponding faults.

rich.text: The frightening encounter becomes an occasion for examining the corresponding faults.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 20:4: “When Yosef was thrown into the pit of snakes and scorpions and did not kill them, he knew that they had been brought before him to kill him and that a miracle had occurred. He then sensed that he needed clarification concerning two things: his report that his brothers looked at the daughters of the land, and that they were suspected of eating a limb from a living animal. For these matters the snakes and scorpions came before him. The snake is the root of damage to the covenant, the serpent's counsel that introduced the appetite for eating into Adam. It was therefore punished with “dust is the snake's bread,” losing the taste of that appetite. The scorpion certainly kills, as Berakhot 33a says, “For a scorpion he interrupts.” It corresponds to the damage of bloodshed extending through Kayin and to the fault of a limb from a living animal. The nations too guard against this because it is great cruelty, besides the prohibition commanded to the descendants of Noach. Nevuchadnezzar was therefore ashamed when he ate a live hare, as in Nedarim 65a. When the snakes and scorpions came before Yosef, he sensed his need for clarification concerning the evil report, and he certainly repented for these two faults.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah applies the same Shabbat passage to Yosef in the pit. It describes how the encounter awakened his own need to clarify the reports he had made about his brothers, followed by repentance. This provides a concrete example of the siman's movement from fear to the repair and strengthening of a particular faculty, rather than stopping at the fear itself.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 15:86: “But one can say that this matter depends upon the Tannaitic dispute between Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Meir in Kiddushin 36a: and then I merited to find in the Responsa of the Rashba Part I, §124 and §212 who likewise cited for this issue this dispute of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah, and that the halachah follows Rabbi Meir because his textual proofs are more precise, see there, and it brought me great joy; for Rabbi Meir holds that in all circumstances they are termed "children of the Living God" (Hoshea 2:1); but Rabbi Yehudah says: when they do not conduct themselves as children, they are not termed "children." And at the beginning of the formation of the Israelite nation, at the start of the mission to redeem them from Egypt, it is stated in Parashas Shemos: "Israel is My son, My firstborn; send forth My son that he may serve Me" (Shemos 4:22–23); it is clear that the collective of Israel are His children, blessed be He, and that for this reason He brought them forth to be His people and serve Him because they are His children;”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin locates that verse within the dispute concerning whether Israel remains called Hashem’s children when conduct is deficient, and records the support for Rabbi Meir’s view. This explains the depth of the siman’s concluding reversal: the recognition of repair can uncover an enduring relationship, rather than create a wholly unrelated identity after punishment.

paragraphs.text: Concern for Heaven's honor can itself open a path of return when a person feels no connection.

rich.text: Concern for Heaven's honor can itself open a path of return when a person feels no connection.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Bamidbar 1: “This was fixed here in the census of the wilderness generation. Through their service they illuminated that no unfolding in the world lies outside words of Torah. It was thereby established for all later generations that even in the greatest concealment, it cannot be that a person has no way to return to Hashem's light: a path back always remains, although he himself recognizes no connection. Nevertheless, Israel retains the cry, ‘What will You do for Your great name?’ On his own account he is ready to accept all the suffering; what he lacks is, ‘What will You do for Your great name?’ Since Hashem established in this world that Heaven's honor is, as it were, incomplete and Israel completes it through service, he therefore cries that Heaven's honor is incomplete. From this very cry he has a way to return to Hashem's light.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef develops the same verse in Hosea by distinguishing consciously asking Hashem to fill one's lack from concealment so deep that no connection is felt. Even there, the cry that Heaven's honor remains incomplete is itself a way back. This explains the siman's insistence that the very place called ‘not My people’ becomes the place of renewed sonship.

p: [קסב] (מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ)

(From his holy handwriting.) [This section was left out of the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902), and it was also missing from R' Michael Mokotowski's copy, so Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMalei (1968) lacks it. R' Yehoshua Mondshine first printed it in Sifsei Tzaddikim 4 (1992), pp. 27–29, from a manuscript of the passages omitted from the printing.]
מִכָּל עֲבֵירָה נַעֲשָׂה מַלְאָךְ רַע כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה,
From every transgression an evil angel is formed, as our Sages of blessed memory taught,
זֶהוּ לְטוֹבָה לִבְנֵי אָדָם,
and this is actually for the benefit of human beings;
שֶׁהַמַּלְאָךְ הוּא חַיּוּת רוּחָנִי, וְהוּא מַכִּיר בַּאֲמִתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְחָפֵץ שֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹב,
for the angel is spiritual vitality, and it recognizes the truth of Hashem, blessed be He, and yearns to be transformed into good,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר הָאָדָם לִתְשׁוּבָה.
and through this the person is aroused to repentance.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Tzidkat HaTzadik 242:1: “Repentance resembles a sage's release that uproots the matter retroactively, and the bad angel made by the transgression is entirely nullified. When repentance comes from love, sins become merits: the angel is not nullified but transformed to good. These are the levels of transformation and subduing. Fear establishes a boundary in the heart against evil; love turns the bitter—the person's impulse and desire—sweet, by drawing it to the study house and Torah. In this way the evil impulse becomes “very good,” since the desire for Torah comes through it. Torah seasons the impulse so that it becomes good.”

rich.text: : “Repentance resembles a sage's release that uproots the matter retroactively, and the bad angel made by the transgression is entirely nullified. When repentance comes from love, sins become merits: the angel is not nullified but transformed to good. These are the levels of transformation and subduing. Fear establishes a boundary in the heart against evil; love turns the bitter—the person's impulse and desire—sweet, by drawing it to the study house and Torah. In this way the evil impulse becomes “very good,” since the desire for Torah comes through it. Torah seasons the impulse so that it becomes good.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Siman 242 supplies the distinction implicit in this opening: repentance can nullify the angel, while return from love transforms the desire itself toward Torah. It later explains “repentance that covers all his deeds” as the general return from love. Together the passages describe an actual change in the person and the power produced by the act; the emergence of remorse is the beginning of that work, rather than its automatic completion.

and this is the very angel created through him
[וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ב:): "רָאָה וַיַּתֵּר גּוֹיִם" (חֲבַקּוּק ג, ו) – שֶׁהִתִּיר לָהֶם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוֹלְכִים לַאֲבַדּוֹן],
[and therefore they said (Avodah Zarah 2b): 'He saw and released the nations' (Habakkuk 3:6)—He released them (from the seven Noahide commandments), and through this they go to destruction],
וְאֵין לְךָ עֲבֵירָה שֶׁל אָדָם שֶׁלֹּא הִרְהֵר עָלֶיהָ בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
and there is no transgression committed by a man of Israel over which he did not reflect with repentance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים חֲרָטוֹת",
as our Sages of blessed memory said: 'The sinners of Israel are full of remorses,'
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הָעֲבֵירָה עַצְמָהּ.
and this remorse is generated through the agency of the transgression itself.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 241:1: “A person’s commandments and good deeds—and certainly words of Torah—bring good thoughts into his heart; transgressions bring the opposite, as our Sages say, “One commandment draws another, and a transgression, and so forth.” The meaning of this drawing is that an angel is created from every commandment: that is, a spiritual power. As the Zohar states, no deed or speech of a person, good or evil, is lost. Through this good angel, which belongs to him, was born of his action, and dwells near him—for the angel is spiritual, like human thought—a thought falls into his heart to perform other commandments.”
