p: וְעַל יְדֵי הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה מַרְבֶּה מַזִּיקִים רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ מִזֹּהַר,
And through wasting seed, a person multiplies harmful spirits, may the Merciful One preserve us, more than through all other transgressions, as is known from the Zohar;
לְכָךְ גַּם כֵּן הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה שֶׁנּוֹפְלִים בְּלִבּוֹ הֵם הַרְבֵּה.
therefore, the reflections of repentance that fall into his heart are likewise very numerous.
וְכָל עִיקַּר עִנְיַן הָעֲבֵירוֹת הוּא רַק לְעוֹרֵר הָאָדָם לִתְשׁוּבָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
And the fundamental underlying reason for the existence of transgressions is solely to awaken a person to repentance through them, as mentioned above;
[כִּי יֵשׁ אִימָּא עִילָּאָה וְאִימָּא תַּתָּאָה,
[for there exist Imma Ila'ah (Supernal Mother - Binah/Repentance) and Imma Tata'ah (Lower Mother - Malchut/Prayer),
הַיְינוּ תְּשׁוּבָה וּתְפִלָּה,
namely Repentance and Prayer,
שֶׁעַל יָדָם הוּא הַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵיךְ הוּא שׁוֹכֵן בְּקִרְבּוֹ,
through which one attains recognition of Hashem, blessed be He, how He dwells within him;
וּתְפִלָּה הִתְעוֹרְרוּתָהּ עַל יַד מִצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים,
and prayer's awakening occurs through mitzvot and good deeds,
וּתְשׁוּבָה עַל יְדֵי עֲבֵירָה.
whereas repentance is awakened specifically through transgression.
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה הוּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עַצְמוֹ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
However, Torah is the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself, and this is not the place to elaborate].

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 7:12-16: “But the vitality in drops of semen emitted in vain, although it descended and became included in the three impure shells, rises from there through proper repentance and intense intention in the bedtime Shema, as is known from the Ari. This is hinted at in the Gemara: “Whoever recites the Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a two-edged sword,” and so forth—to slay the bodies of the external forces that have become a garment for the vitality in the drops, so that the vitality rises from them, as is known to those versed in the hidden wisdom. Therefore the transgression of seed emitted in vain is not listed in the Torah among forbidden relations, although it is more severe than they are in the magnitude and abundance of the impurity and shells it generates and greatly multiplies. In forbidden relations, however, one adds strength and vitality to an especially impure shell, from which one cannot raise the vitality through repentance—[gloss: because it has been absorbed into the foundation of the female aspect of the shell, which receives and absorbs vitality from holiness; in seed emitted in vain there is no such female aspect, but only its powers and armies clothing the vitality in the drops, as is known to those versed in the hidden wisdom]—unless one repents with such great love that deliberate sins become merits. This explains our Sages’ statement, “What is a crooked thing that cannot be repaired? One who has relations with a forbidden partner and fathers a mamzer”: then, even if he performs repentance of that magnitude, he cannot raise that vitality to holiness, because it has already descended into this world and become clothed in a body of flesh and blood.”

Tanya differentiates their quantity from the way vitality becomes bound to them, and it specifies different conditions of repentance. The statement concerns the recovery of that vitality, not a denial of the person’s ability to repent.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Achrei Mot 50:299: “Because it is a precious supernal treasure—His very name—the whole Torah is hidden and revealed in the mystery of His name. Therefore Israel has two levels, hidden and revealed. For we learned: three levels are bound to one another—the Holy One, blessed be He, the Torah, and Israel. Each has level upon level, hidden and revealed. The Holy One, blessed be He, has level upon level, hidden and revealed; the Torah likewise has hidden and revealed; Israel likewise has level upon level. This is what is written: “He declares His words to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel.” There are two levels, Jacob and Israel: one revealed and one hidden.”

p: וְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה הוּא לִתְשׁוּבָה גְּדוֹלָה,
And the blemish of wasting seed is directed toward a great repentance,
"תְּשׁוּבָה דַּחַזְיָא לְחַפָּאָה עַל כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי",
a 'repentance that is fitting to cover and atone over all his deeds,'
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, ריד, ב),
as brought in the Zohar (Part II, 214b),
שֶׁבָּזֶה תִּיקּוּן הַמְכֻוָּן מִן הַחֵטְא הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
wherein lies the very rectification intended through the aforementioned sin.
וּלְכָךְ דַּיְיקָא:
And therefore Scripture states precisely:
"בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם, יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם בְּנֵי אֵל חָי",
'in the place where it was said to them: You are not My people, there it shall be said to them: Children of the living God' (Hosea 2:1),
עַל יְדֵי הָעֲבֵירוֹת וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי הַמִּצְווֹת,
meaning specifically through transgressions and not through mitzvot,
לְפִי שֶׁתְּשׁוּבָה גְּדוֹלָה מִתְּפִלָּה.
because repentance is greater than prayer.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 20: “Therefore the repair is through intention in the recitation of Shema: the unification in which one unifies the whole world and all it contains as Hashem's unity. Hashem is thereby recognized as the One who acts and the master of the deed, and the deed too is repaired. This is called in the Zohar “teshuvah fit to cover all his deeds”: it covers and overspreads all the acts he did, declaring that they are not his acts but Hashem's act. This is not like other teshuvah, which displaces a thought and makes the sins like inadvertent acts, merits, or a transgression for Heaven's sake. Rather, this covers and overspreads them all until they are not revealed at all, since they are unified in Hashem's unity.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Likkutei Maamarim quotes the same Zohar expression and explains the particular force of “covering.” In the surrounding argument, ordinary remorse displaces the earlier thought, while this further account addresses the deed through the unity proclaimed in Shema. This clarifies why the siman introduces “great teshuvah” at this exact point rather than using the phrase as a general adjective for strong remorse.

And this state is designated in several places as 'And it shall come to pass on that day,'
שֶׁעֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for this revelation is not yet fully completed in this world,
כִּי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִבְרָא בְּז' יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן שֶׁהֵם ז' הַתַּחְתּוֹנוֹת,
since this world was fashioned through the seven structural building days, which are the seven lower Sefirot;
וּמַדְרֵגַת חָסִיד, וְגִבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ, וְעָנָו, אוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וְנָבִיא וְחוֹזֶה וְצַדִּיק יָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,

and the spiritual rungs of a Chasid (Chesed), a mighty one conquering his urge (Gevurah), a humble one or Torah scholar (Tiferet), a prophet and seer (Netzach and Hod), and a Tzaddik (Yesod) can all be manifest in this world;
וְגַם מַדְרֵגַת מֶלֶךְ הָיָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בִּזְמַן הַבַּיִת,
and likewise the rung of King (Malchut) was present in this world during the era of the Temple,
וְכֵן "מַאן מַלְכֵי? רַבָּנָן".
as well as 'Who are kings? The Rabbis.'

p: אֲבָל שְׁלֵימוּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁהוּא הַכָּרַת הַחִסָּרוֹן,
However, the ultimate perfection of Malchut, which consists of the absolute recognition of human lack and deficiency,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לִתְשׁוּבָה שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל ז' יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן,
through this awareness one arrives at repentance (Binah), which transcends all seven structural building days;
וְכוּלָּם יוֹנְקִים מִמֶּנָּה,
and all lower sefirot draw their spiritual sustenance from it,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ צַדִּיק צָרִיךְ לָהּ,
such that even a righteous Tzaddik requires it,
וְהוּא בָּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרַת הַחִסָּרוֹן,
and it comes solely through the deep consciousness of deficiency;
וּשְׁלֵימוּתוֹ: "אָז יַכִּירוּ כֻּלָּם כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתֶךָ".
and its culmination will be: 'Then all shall recognize the power of Your sovereignty.'

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 9:6: “The essence of kingship is attained through exceptionally great awe, as they said: “Once the king bows, he does not straighten again”—because of the abundance of awe and fear. Through this he becomes a chariot for the attribute of kingship, of which it is said, “It is awe, and awe rests within it,” as the Zohar states. Then he recognizes his lowliness: that he has nothing from his own effort except what the blessed God has granted him, like Abraham, Moses, Aaron, and David. For the attribute of kingship signifies that it has nothing of its own. He then merits clarification in all the attributes up to the crown, as the passage Patach Eliyahu says, “The supernal crown is the crown of kingship”: by crowning the blessed God through his lowliness, he merits clarification in the attribute of the supernal crown.”

p: [קסג] (מִכְּתַב יַד קָדְשׁוֹ)

(From his holy handwriting.) [This section was left out of the first printed edition (Lublin, 1902). R' Michael Mokotowski, a chasid of Rav Tzadok, copied it from the author's own manuscript into his copy of the book, and it was first printed in Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMalei (Jerusalem, 1968), edited by his son R' Avraham Eliyahu Kitov.]
הַנְּפָשׁוֹת כֻּלָּם קֶשֶׁר אֶחָד, כְּעִנְיַן "יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ",
All souls are bound in one single knot, as in the concept of 'Jacob is the lot/rope of His inheritance' (Deuteronomy 32:9),
וְאִם אֶחָד מוֹשֵׁךְ לְמַעְלָה הַכֹּל נִמְשָׁךְ לְמַעְלָה, וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ,
and if one pulls upward, everything is drawn upward, and likewise the reverse,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ "וְחוֹטֶא אֶחָד יְאַבֵּד טוֹבָה הַרְבֵּה".
along the lines of 'and one sinner destroys much good' (Ecclesiastes 9:18).
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּקִדּוּשִׁין,
And that is when the entire world is balanced half and half, as brought at the end of the first chapter of Kiddushin (40b),
לְפִי שֶׁהָעוֹלָם מַמְשִׁיכִין בַּחֶבֶל, זֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ לְכָאן וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ לְכָאן וּמִי שֶׁכֹּחוֹ גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר מְנַצֵּחַ,
for the world is tugging on a rope—this one pulls here and that one pulls there, and whoever's strength is greater prevails,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: "הָעוֹלָם נִידּוֹן אַחַר רוּבּוֹ".
and as they stated there: 'the world is judged according to its majority.'

paragraphs.text: What the unbreakable bond preserves
The image of the rope distinguishes injury to Israel’s revealed condition from severance of its root.

rich.text: The image of the rope distinguishes injury to Israel’s revealed condition from severance of its root.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 15:79: “But regarding the sinners of Israel, "Let sins cease" is written (Tehillim 104:35), and not "sinners," as they expounded in Berachos 10a; for the root of all the souls of Israel is cleaved unto the Living God, for "the portion of Hashem is His people" (Devarim 32:9); and as they stated in Kiddushin 36a that even when they lack faith and worship idols, where it is said of them "you are not My people" (Hoshea 1:9), appearing outwardly as if they are not His people; in truth they remain the portion of Hashem, believers the descendants of believers, as they stated in Shabbos 97a; and the seed of Yaakov whose bed is complete have in their hearts nothing other than the One, as they stated in Pesachim 56a. For Hoshea designated them "not My people" because when told to prophesy he said: "Exchange them for another nation," as related in Pesachim 87a; because he presumed that it was possible to sever the name of Israel and the root of Judaism through the multitude of sins, God forbid; until the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "They are My children, the descendants of My beloved ones, Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov," commanding him to plead for mercy to annul the decrees brought about through him, as they related ibid. 87b; for when the leading tzaddik of the generation below consents to the prosecuting Attribute of Judgment, the pleas of the Attribute of Mercy are sealed and judgment is decreed, and from the perspective of strict justice it was indeed so; but through the awakening of the Attribute of Mercy he perceived that "in the place where it was said unto them: 'You are not My people,' it shall be said unto them: 'You are the sons of the living God'" (Hoshea 2:1); that when sins cease, the wicked are no more, and the holy root remains. For all their sins stem merely from the brambles and thorns that encircle the myrtle and the rose (Vayikra Rabbah 23:3);”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin reads the same verses in Hoshea as an apparent loss of relationship that cannot eradicate the soul’s root in Hashem. Its distinction between the sin and the sinner explains what the rope image preserves through stretching and division. It also directs the desired outcome toward the removal of sin and recovery of the good root, rather than treating the sin as a model to imitate.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 50:2: “All Jewish souls form one bond. When one Jewish soul becomes wholly bound to Him, all are consequently drawn with it, like someone pulling the end of a rope, which draws the whole rope along. “Jacob is the rope of His inheritance”: one end is bound above to the form of Jacob engraved upon the Throne of Glory, and its lower end consists of the souls of the lowest sinners of Israel. It continues thus from level to level. Yom Kippur awakens the individual who repents to enter “unto the Lord,” into the Holy of Holies; the whole rope is consequently drawn with him in an awakening of repentance and an ascent above, each according to his measure and level, and atonement is drawn to them too. Rabbi and the Sages disagree whether it atones even for those who do not repent: that concerns complete atonement, beyond what is fitting through the individual who repents. In the latter matter all agree that there is forgiveness for the whole world; but this depends on the strength of his repentance—that is, the strength with which he draws the rope upward.”

p: וְעַל יְדֵי הַמְּשִׁיכָה בַּחֶבֶל, הַחֶבֶל מִתְפַּקֵּעַ וּמִתְאָרֵךְ,
And through the pulling on the rope, the rope snaps open and lengthens,
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁנִּתְרַבּוּ נְפָשׁוֹת – וְלֹא שֶׁנִּתְרַבּוּ, רַק שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ אֶחָד לִשְׁנַיִם.
meaning that souls multiply—not that brand-new souls multiply, but that one divides into two.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (דַּף ה.):
And this is what they taught in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (5a):
"אִלְמָלֵא אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ אָנוּ לֹא בָּאנוּ לָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי",
'Had our ancestors not sinned, we would not have come into the world, etc.,'
אֶלָּא כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא בָּאנוּ לָעוֹלָם, שֶׁהָיוּ נִכְלָלִים בִּמְקוֹרָם.
meaning rather like one who had not entered the world, as they would have remained included in their unified source.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַחֲטָאִים מִתְרַבִּים נְפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
And through sins, souls of Israel multiply,
וּלְפִיכָךְ מַתְחִיל בְּהוֹשֵׁעַ תֵּיכֶף אַחַר הָאַרְבַּע שֵׁמוֹת רָעִים וּמְכוֹעָרִים שֶׁקָּרָא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
and therefore Scripture begins in Hosea (2:1), immediately after the four harsh and unsightly names applied to Israel,
פָּסוּק "וְהָיָה מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּחוֹל הַיָּם וְגוֹמֵר",
with the verse: 'And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, etc.,'
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְרַבָּה מִסְפָּרָם וְנִתְאָרֵךְ הַחֶבֶל לְאֵין חֵקֶר.
for through this their number multiplied and the rope lengthened beyond fathom.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Bamidbar 2: “Because Hashem's desire to benefit was present in the creation of every individual of Israel, He placed before each one a particular matter whose completion, as He presents it to us, requires that person's service. “There shall be a number” means that each has a particular task through which he must complete the revealed divine honor. From Hashem's own side nothing is lacking; the arrangement comes from His desire to benefit the creatures. The particular matter placed before this person must be completed by him and no other. Thus each soul is important to Hashem. But in the totality, “it shall not be measured or counted”: all particulars are included in His unity, and His honor is complete even without human service.”

rich.text: : “Because Hashem's desire to benefit was present in the creation of every individual of Israel, He placed before each one a particular matter whose completion, as He presents it to us, requires that person's service. “There shall be a number” means that each has a particular task through which he must complete the revealed divine honor. From Hashem's own side nothing is lacking; the arrangement comes from His desire to benefit the creatures. The particular matter placed before this person must be completed by him and no other. Thus each soul is important to Hashem. But in the totality, “it shall not be measured or counted”: all particulars are included in His unity, and His honor is complete even without human service.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the same Hosea verse by distinguishing the countless whole from the significance of each counted individual. Each has a particular service that another cannot perform in his place. This gives a complementary explanation of the siman's division of the one rope into particular souls: the common root and the importance of individual work coexist. Its eventual inclusion in unity does not cancel that work.

p: [קסד] בְּדַעַת בְּנֵי אָדָם אֵין הַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה כְּמוֹ הַצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר,
In human perception, a penitent (ba'al teshuvah) is not equal to a wholly righteous person (tzadik gamur),
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַחֲטָאִים שֶׁעָשָׂה כְּבָר חֲשׁוּבִים כִּזְכִיּוֹת,
and it goes without saying that the sins he committed previously would not be considered as merits,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמַּאֲמִין בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ כִּזְכִיּוֹת,
even though one believes in the words of our Sages that willful sins become like merits (Yoma 86b),
וְגַם אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת לד:): "בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי"
and they also said (Berakhot 34b): "In the place where penitents stand, the wholly righteous cannot stand"
[וּמַאן דִּפְלִיג, הַיְינוּ בְּעִנְיַן הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים, דְּמָר יָלֵיף מִקְּרָא דִּ"לָרָחוֹק וְלַקָּרוֹב" שֶׁהוּא בַּנְּבִיאִים, וּלְדַעְתּוֹ אֵינוֹ כֵן מִצַּד הַנְּבוּאָה.

[and the one who disputes this does so regarding the comprehension of the prophets, where one master derives from the verse 'to him that is far off and to him that is near' (Isaiah 57:19) which is among the prophets, and in his view it is not so from the side of prophecy.
דְּצַדִּיק גָּמוּר – "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה", שֶׁזֶּהוּ רַק מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
For concerning the wholly righteous it is said 'no eye has seen' (Isaiah 64:3), which is exclusively from the side of the Blessed Name.
אֲבָל תְּשׁוּבָה שַׁיָּיכוּת לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק הוּא כְּטַעַם: לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ אִמִּי, שֶׁגְּדוֹלָה מִמֶּנּוּ, וְעוֹד דְּבָרִים בְּגוֹ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמָם].

But repentance belongs to the Congregation of Israel, which mirrors: He did not cease cherishing her until He called her His mother, which is greater, and there are deeper matters within this, and this is not the place for them].
וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהַתְּשׁוּבָה נִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא, וְאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה לִבְנֵי אָדָם הַיְקָרוּת וְהַיּוֹפִי שֶׁבָּהּ.
And this is because repentance is termed the Concealed World (alma de-itkasya), and its inner preciousness and beauty are not visible to ordinary human beings.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ: "כִּי שְׂנוּאָה לֵאָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לא), וְעַיֵּין בַּזֹּהַר הַטַּעַם.
And of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who is the root of all Israel, it is stated: "that Leah was hated" (Genesis 29:31), and see the Zohar for the inner reason.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג.) שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: הַגְּדוֹלָה לַגָּדוֹל וְכוּלֵי,
That is, as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Bava Batra 123a) that people would say: the elder daughter is for the elder son, etc.;
הַיְינוּ לְפִי הַנִּגְלֶה שַׁיָּיכֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְחֵלֶק עֵשָׂו, וְהָיְתָה בּוֹכָה – זֶהוּ סוֹד הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
meaning according to outward appearance she seemed linked, Heaven forbid, to the portion of Esau, and she wept—and this weeping is the mystical secret of repentance.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רָחֵל: "יְפַת תֹּאַר וִיפַת מַרְאֶה", שֶׁהַכֹּל אוֹמְרִים: הַקְּטַנָּה לַקָּטָן, כִּי בְּעָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא יֵשׁ בָּהּ יֹפִי מַעֲשִׂים.

In contrast, Rachel was "beautiful of form and fair to look upon," where all said: the younger daughter is for the younger son, for in the Revealed World (alma de-itgalya) she possessed manifest beauty of deeds.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, עִיקַּר תּוֹלָדוֹת מִשֶּׁל לֵאָה, שֶׁעִיקַּר הַהוֹלָדָה, הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּנְפָשׁוֹת לִרְצוֹן ה', הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה.

Nevertheless, the primary offspring issued from Leah, for the essence of true spiritual generation—innovating words of Torah and birthing holy souls for the will of Hashem—is entirely through the spiritual rung of repentance.

וּבֶאֱמֶת הִיא אִמּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (זוּטָא פֶּרֶק ה) דְּאֵין לְךָ מִדָּה טוֹבָה וְדָבָר טוֹב בָּא לִבְנֵי אָדָם אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי עֲנִיּוּת – פֵּירוּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And in truth she is his mother, as stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta (chapter 5) that no worthy trait or good thing comes to human beings except through poverty—meaning poverty in words of Torah,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּגִטִּין (מג.) עַל פָּסוּק "וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָה וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁאֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵי,
as our Sages taught in Gittin 43a on the verse "and let this ruin be under your hand" (Isaiah 3:6), that a person does not master Torah unless he has stumbled in it,
וְעַל יְדֵי הָעֲבֵירָה וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה נוֹלָד הַחַיּוּת אַחַר כָּךְ.
and through the sin and the subsequent repentance, authentic spiritual vitality is born afterward.
אַךְ סָנֵי בַּר נָשׁ עֶרְיַין דְּאִמֵּיהּ, וּמִטֶּבַע הָאָדָם שֶׁשּׂוֹנֵא הַתְּשׁוּבָה עַל הָרַע;
However, a person naturally disdains his mother's nakedness, and by nature man dislikes repenting over evil;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקָּר שֶׁהֶעֱמִידוֹ עַל מַה שֶּׁהוּא, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין חָפֵץ לִדְבַּק בָּזֶה.
and even though this repentance is the very foundation that established him as what he is, he nevertheless has no desire to cleave to it.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין אִשָּׁה אֶלָּא לְבָנִים, וְהַתּוֹלָדוֹת רַק מִלֵּאָה
But in truth, a wife is chosen primarily for children, and the true progeny derived from Leah
[וְגָרַם עַד "וַתְּקַנֵּא רָחֵל וְגוֹמֵר", לְפִי שֶׁזֶּה עִיקָּר.
[and this reality led to "And Rachel envied her sister" (Genesis 30:1), because this fruitfulness was paramount.
וְכָל כָּךְ כֹּחַ הַקִּנְאָה שֶׁהוֹעִיל, שֶׁאָז עָמְדָה לֵאָה מִלֶּדֶת, דְּפָרָשַׁת "וַתְּקַנֵּא וְגוֹמֵר" נֶאֱמַר שָׁם עַיֵּין שָׁם,
And so potent was the force of this envy that Leah ceased bearing, for the passage of 'And Rachel envied' was recorded there, see there,
וְלֹא יָלְדָה עַד שֶׁאָמַר לָהּ רָחֵל: "לָכֵן יִשְׁכַּב וְגוֹמֵר", וְסִילְּקָה קִנְאָתָהּ.
and she did not bear again until Rachel told her: 'Therefore he shall lie with you tonight,' and removed her envy.

וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, נֶאֱמַר: "וְסָרָה קִנְאַת אֶפְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה יא, יג) – זַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל, וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּצַדִּיק כַּיָּדוּעַ,

And likewise King David, peace be upon him, who established the yoke of repentance, concerning him it is said: 'The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, etc.' (Isaiah 11:13)—Ephraim representing the seed of Rachel and the rung of the tzadik as is known,
וְהוֹעִיל לַחֲלוֹק מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד, שֶׁזֶּה חִסָּרוֹן בְּעֶצֶם מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד לְפִי שָׁעָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:
which had the effect of dividing the Davidic monarchy, an essential temporary blemish in the kingdom of the House of David, and this is not the place to lengthen].

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 7:2: “For a penitent merits this in one hour, in one instant, as they said in the Zohar, Chayei Sarah. Hence, “In the place where penitents stand, the wholly righteous cannot stand,” for they are closer to the King. It appears that this is what Bereshit Rabbah means: “‘Darkness’ is the deeds of the wicked … I do not know which He desires more,” and so forth. How could one suppose that He desires wicked deeds? The meaning concerns the created order, for “God made the human being upright.” Although He created the wicked and the evil inclination, He created Torah as its remedy, to be “a lamp for my feet, Your word, and a light for my path”; for “though I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light,” and “though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for You are with me.” Although in the end they become closer, because the penitent raises holy sparks from low places of life and turns darkness into light, one might suppose that the blessed God desires this more. Of this they said, “God saw the light, that it was good”: nevertheless, His principal desire and will is for the righteous person, “for it is good.””

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 7:3: “Although it is known that the attribute of kingship is the last, the eighth counted from understanding in the heart, and is the crown of the foundation when it is only a point—when it expands into a complete stature, the stature of the feminine, of this they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah that He cherishes her so much that He calls her “My daughter,” “My sister,” and “My mother.” The congregation of Israel, whose souls are a portion of God above—for one who breathes breathes from within himself—and are emanated from His holy emanation, which He emanated when He willed that there be room for the creation of worlds, is the last level of the emanated levels: the level capable of clothing itself in the bodily garment of this world, so that His Presence may dwell below, in this physical world. This is the purpose and end of the whole unfolding of emanation: He desired His light to be revealed also among those below, and this is the whole intention of creation. Therefore, although they are the end of all creation, they are also its beginning and principal purpose, for “the end of the deed is first in thought,” and Israel arose in thought. This is “You formed me behind and before”: once they reach their completion and the intention of all creation is fulfilled through the human being, he is before and at the head of everything, for this was the initial intention in creating the world. This is His calling her “My mother”: she is the source that gives birth to the unfolding of all six directions of emanation. For the depth of the end is itself the depth of the beginning, in the mystery of “their end is embedded in their beginning”; the whole unfolding of emanation was to attain the purpose, the building of the stature of the congregation of Israel and the dwelling of the Presence below, and this is the root of the unfolding’s beginning.”

rich.text: : “Although it is known that the attribute of kingship is the last, the eighth counted from understanding in the heart, and is the crown of the foundation when it is only a point—when it expands into a complete stature, the stature of the feminine, of this they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah that He cherishes her so much that He calls her “My daughter,” “My sister,” and “My mother.” The congregation of Israel, whose souls are a portion of God above—for one who breathes breathes from within himself—and are emanated from His holy emanation, which He emanated when He willed that there be room for the creation of worlds, is the last level of the emanated levels: the level capable of clothing itself in the bodily garment of this world, so that His Presence may dwell below, in this physical world. This is the purpose and end of the whole unfolding of emanation: He desired His light to be revealed also among those below, and this is the whole intention of creation. Therefore, although they are the end of all creation, they are also its beginning and principal purpose, for “the end of the deed is first in thought,” and Israel arose in thought. This is “You formed me behind and before”: once they reach their completion and the intention of all creation is fulfilled through the human being, he is before and at the head of everything, for this was the initial intention in creating the world. This is His calling her “My mother”: she is the source that gives birth to the unfolding of all six directions of emanation. For the depth of the end is itself the depth of the beginning, in the mystery of “their end is embedded in their beginning”; the whole unfolding of emanation was to attain the purpose, the building of the stature of the congregation of Israel and the dwelling of the Presence below, and this is the root of the unfolding’s beginning.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Rav Tzadok gives the mystical interpretation of the daughter-sister-mother parable. The final recipient is called “mother” when the completion of creation discloses that it was the initial purpose; the quotation retains the stages on which this reversal depends.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 6:7: “People said, “The elder for the elder,” because outwardly it seemed as though she resembled him, Heaven forbid. In truth, Esav's deeds were hateful to her. In this she rose above Rachel, whose children are Esav's accusers because they are good while he is evil. If a person sins, he can outwardly appear like Esav. But for Leah, the root of his deeds is hateful: hatred is the heart's rejection of the thing, even if outward action does not appear so. The root within the heart is different. Therefore “one who denies idolatry is called a Jew”: this is the root of Judah from Leah, whose heart has no belief in idolatry or any power opposed to Hashem.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin distinguishes the public claim “the elder for the elder” from Leah's inward rejection of Esav's ways. That distinction explains how the siman uses apparent ugliness and hidden fruitfulness: the inner relation of the returning heart is not fully legible from its outward position. The comparison develops this particular symbolism, rather than making visible failure itself a virtue.

sections.en: The Souls of Israel Each Constitute an Independent, Unique Spiritual Level

p: [קסה] הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כָּל אֶחָד מַדְרֵגָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
The souls of Israel each constitute an independent, unique spiritual level,
כִּי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים שָׁוִים מַמָּשׁ, דְּאִם כֵּן מַה צֹּרֶךְ לִשְׁנַיִם
for the Blessed Name never makes two things completely identical, since if so, what need would there be for two?
[וְעוֹד בְּרוּחָנִיִּים, בַּמֶּה יִתְחַלֵּק אֶחָד מִשְּׁנַיִם אִם לֹא בְּחִלּוּק מַדְרֵגָה?]
[Moreover, in spiritual entities, through what could one be distinguished from another if not through a difference in level?]
וְכָל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת קוֹמָה אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה, וְכֵן כָּל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִית קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה,
And all souls together form one complete cosmic stature, and likewise each individual soul is itself a complete stature;
נִמְצָא יֵשׁ לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ לַעֲלוֹת בְּמַדְרֵגוֹת כְּמִסְפַּר הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
consequently, every soul must ascend through levels corresponding to the total number of the souls of Israel.
וְעִיקַּר הַיְגִיעָה לְהַגִּיעַ עַד מַדְרֵגַת עַצְמוֹ,
And the primary toil is to reach the rung of oneself,
דְּהַיְינוּ מִמֶּנּוּ [מִמְּקוֹם נַפְשׁוֹ בַּקּוֹמָה הַכְּלָלִית] וּלְמַטָּה, מִסּוֹף הַכֹּל עַד מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁלּוֹ.
that is, from himself [from his soul's place in the collective stature] downward, from the very bottom up to his own level.
אֲבָל מִמֶּנּוּ וּלְמַעְלָה, שֶׁכְּבָר יָצְאוּ נְפָשׁוֹת שְׁלֵימוֹת מִמַּדְרֵגוֹת הָהֵם
But from his level upward, where perfected souls from those higher rungs have already emerged into the world
[כִּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הוֹלְכִים מִמַּעְלָה לְמַטָּה, וְאָנוּ הַיּוֹם בְּעִקְּבוֹת מָשִׁיחַ מִן הָעִקְבִיִּים,
[for the generational levels descend from above to below, and we today in the footsteps of the Messiah stem from the heels,
עִיקָּר בַּעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁאָדָם דָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבָיו וּשְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית, וְכֵן הַמִּצְווֹת וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לָצֵאת מִן הַהֶרְגֵּל],
where the primary struggle lies in sins a person treads upon with his heels and guarding the Covenant, as well as breaking habitual routine in mitzvot],
יֵשׁ לוֹ סַיַּעְתָּא גְּדוֹלָה מֵאוֹתָם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁכְּבָר יָצְאוּ,
he possesses immense Heavenly assistance from those souls who have already lived,
שֶׁכְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַמַּדְרֵגָה שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד [בַּקּוֹמָה הַכְּלָלִית], הוּא בָּא וּמְסַיְּיעוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בְּסוֹד הָעִבּוּר.
for when he reaches the level of each soul [in the collective stature], that soul comes and assists him, as I wrote elsewhere concerning the mystery of spiritual impregnation (ibbur).
כִּי אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁל מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ כְּבָר נִשְׁאַר בָּעוֹלָם
For that power of spiritual effort belonging to that level has already remained in the world
[עַל יְדֵי הַהֶבְלָא דְּגַרְמֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר],
[through the spiritual vapor of the bones, as I wrote elsewhere],
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ יְגִיעָה כָּל כָּךְ רַק עַד לוֹ
and one does not need such exhausting labor once he reaches his own level
[וְזֶה סוֹד מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טו.): לֹא עָלָה עֶזְרָא מִבָּבֶל עַד שֶׁיִּחֵס עַצְמוֹ].
[and this is the secret of Bava Batra 15a: Ezra did not ascend from Babylonia until he traced his lineage].
וְלָכֵן בְּדוֹרוֹת אֵלּוּ אֵין צָרִיךְ יְגִיעָה כָּל כָּךְ כִּבְדוֹרוֹת רִאשׁוֹנִים, וְנָקֵל לָבוֹא לְמַדְרֵגוֹת מִיָּד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת עַצְמוֹ.
Therefore in these latter generations one does not require as much exertion as in the early generations, and it is easy to attain higher levels the moment he reaches his own inherent level.
אֲבָל לְעֻמַּת זֶה הָיָה מַעֲלַת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים שֶׁהָיוּ מִמָּקוֹם יוֹתֵר גָּבוֹהַּ,
However, corresponding to this was the great virtue of the early generations who stemmed from a much loftier place,
וְכָל כָּךְ מַכְבִּיד עָלֵינוּ הַיֵּצֶר אוֹתָהּ יְגִיעָה מוּעֶטֶת בְּדוֹרֵנוּ כְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַמְּרֻבָּה שֶׁלָּהֶם:
and the evil inclination weighs down upon us regarding that small exertion in our generation just as heavily as it did upon their immense striving.

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Bamidbar 2: see note 2077.

Explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the individual number of each soul through the particular service assigned to that person, while the whole is included in divine unity beyond number. This gives content to the siman's claim that two souls are not interchangeable. The quotation supports that first claim; it is not offered as proof of the later, more specific account of assistance from earlier generations.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 2: “Every vessel apprehends according to what it is; likewise a person apprehends the blessed God according to what he is. It is known that the body’s organs are a garment for the soul’s organs. That is, just as we see the body divided into organs, so the soul that spreads through those organs and gives them life is also divided into organs; the soul’s vitality in the head is not like its vitality in the foot, for example. The soul therefore also has a division of levels, generally the three levels in the human stature: the head, the body, and the feet below the body. Through what does a person apprehend the blessed God? Through the soul. Apprehension is consequently divided into levels as well: the apprehension through the part of the soul called the head and brain is not like that through the part called the foot. Likewise, the whole congregation of Israel is one complete stature: there are souls who are the heads of the generation, eyes of the congregation, counterparts of the heart, counterparts of the feet, and similarly all the organs. One person’s apprehension is unlike another’s, according to his level and position in the stature of the whole congregation of Israel.”

paragraphs.text: What leaving a habit means
Torah must become active even in the body's ordinary responses.

rich.text: Torah must become active even in the body's ordinary responses.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 26:5: “In every generation a person must see himself as though he left Egypt. Anything in which he is so immersed that he thinks escape from the habit impossible is called Egyptian bondage. He must work so that no fixed natural habit rules him; to the extent he is freed from it, he finds enduring freedom in his heart. How can he bring himself out? By fixing in his heart that Torah stands above the things of this world. One who accepts Torah's yoke is freed from the yoke of government and ordinary worldly occupation. As Torah becomes fixed in him, he rises above worldly habits. This must be through action and speech, for speech completes the matter, so that it is settled even in the final garment, without deliberate awareness. As the Yerushalmi says, “I am grateful to my head: when I reach Modim, it bows of its own accord.” That is, the body follows His will even without conscious direction.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim gives concrete meaning to the siman's work of departing from habit. The habit that seems impossible to leave is a personal Egypt; Torah is impressed through speech and action until even bodily response follows it. This illuminates why a later generation's apparently small task can still require real effort. Its explanation of habit does not replace the siman's separate account of aid from earlier souls.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 15:9-11: “Through this one can understand the Gemara’s statement that “one who serves God” means someone who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times, while “one who has not served Him” means someone who reviews his chapter only one hundred times. This is because in their days it was customary to review every chapter one hundred times, as the Gemara there illustrates with the market of donkey drivers: they are hired for ten parasangs at one zuz, but for eleven parasangs at two zuz, because this exceeds their usual distance. Therefore this one hundred and first repetition, beyond the habit in which he was trained from his youth, is equal to all the others and surpasses them in excellence and strength, so that he is called “one who serves God.” For to change the nature of habit, he must awaken love of the Lord by contemplating the Lord’s greatness in his mind, in order to rule over the nature in the left chamber, filled with the blood of the animal soul that comes from kelippah, from which this nature derives. This is complete service for the intermediate person. Alternatively, he may awaken the hidden love in his heart in order to rule through it over the nature in the left chamber. This too is called service: to struggle with nature and the inclination by awakening the hidden love in his heart.”

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar HaGilgulim 1:12-13: “Through this you will also understand the matter well known in our Sages’ words: the spirits or souls of the righteous come and enter a person in the mystery called ibbur, to assist him in serving the blessed God. As written in the manuscript Midrash HaNe’elam concerning “one who comes to purify himself is assisted,” Rabbi Natan says: The souls of the righteous come and assist him. So too, in the Zohar’s introduction to Bereishit, Rav Hamnuna the Elder came to Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abba in the appearance of a donkey driver, and so forth. There is no doubt that the spirits and souls of the righteous are stored and bound in the bond of life, each at its fitting root with the Lord their God, and they do not descend from their place at all. Rather, those earlier spirits that remained below, at every aspect and level in Yetzirah, and did not ascend above as explained, descend and enter a person to assist him. The principal spirit, the highest of all that he acquired through his deeds, remains forever bound in the bond of life and does not move from there; likewise for the levels of neshamah, chayah, and yechidah.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 238:1: “As is known, every Jewish soul has a particular power in holiness, and the number of generations that have passed corresponds to the number of powers of holiness and words of Torah revealed in the world. Therefore in every generation holiness continues to be revealed more, although the generations diminish, as is known, because what was revealed to the earlier ones has already been revealed—as in the familiar parable of a dwarf upon a giant. In words of Torah this is through the books. Certainly, too, the holiness of all the Jewish souls that reached completion is already revealed in the world—that is, in the hearts of the children of Israel. What requires no exertion, so that one performs a good act or thinks a good thought without deliberate intention and effort, is due to that power of holiness having already been revealed in the world. Every deed, action, and thought comes from a particular power and a particular holiness, with divisions into thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads, as numerous as the souls.”

[This is the mystery of its root in the name Elohim, which is said throughout the work of creation: all creation is through the mystery of contraction, as is known, by which the physical can come into being from the spiritual. Only the soul itself rises above—that is, the mature consciousness from the upper realms and from the soul itself. The breath pertains only to the formation of the body and therefore always remains in the body, below in the world.”

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar HaGilgulim 38:154: “Once I asked my teacher of blessed memory how he could tell me that my soul was so elevated, as stated above, when even the least of the earlier generations was righteous and pious, and I do not reach his heel. He told me: Know that the greatness of the soul does not depend on a person’s deeds alone, but on the time and that generation. A very small deed in this generation is equivalent to several great commandments in other generations, because in these generations the shell grows exceedingly strong, without limit, unlike the earlier generations. Had I lived in the earlier generations, my deeds and wisdom would have been extraordinary compared with several of the earlier righteous ones. As our Sages said of Noah, “He was complete in his generations”: had he lived in generations of righteous people, he would have been more righteous. Therefore I should not grieve over this at all, for without doubt my soul has a great advantage over several of the earlier righteous ones from the time of the Tannaim and Amoraim.”

sections.en: When a Person Accepts Upon Himself the Yoke of Torah and Enters Under The…

p: [קסו] כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם מְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ עוֹל תּוֹרָה וְנִכְנָס תַּחַת עֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, צָרִיךְ קַבָּלָה בַּלֵּב וְהַסְכָּמָה גְּמוּרָה לַעֲזוֹב כָּל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמִּתְנַגְּדִים לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,

When a person accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah and enters under the service of the Blessed Name, he requires an internal acceptance in the heart and complete resolve to abandon all worldly desires that conflict with the will of the Blessed Name,
וְלֹא לֶאֱחוֹז בָּזֶה וְגַם מִזֶּה אַל יַנַּח יָדוֹ, שֶׁאָז זֶה וְזֶה לֹא עָלְתָה.
and not grasp onto this while also failing to withdraw his hand from that, for then neither the one nor the other will succeed.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (יוֹמָא עב:): לֹא זָכָה – נַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי, כִּי גַּם תּוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יְבָמוֹת קט:).
And concerning this it was stated (Yoma 72b): if he does not merit, it becomes a deadly potion, for he does not truly possess Torah either (Yevamot 109b).
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּעֵשָׂו: "וַיַּרְא עֵשָׂו כִּי רָעוֹת בְּנוֹת כְּנָעַן וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, ח–ט),
And just as was said regarding Esau: "And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father... and he took Mahalath, etc." (Genesis 28:8–9),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סז): כּוֹב עַל כּוֹב, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and our Sages expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (end of Parashah 67): adding misery upon misery, see there.

וְהַיְינוּ מֵאַחַר שֶׁלֹּא גֵּירַשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת, רַק כִּמְבַקֵּשׁ לָצֵאת יְדֵי יִצְחָק גַּם כֵּן וְלִקַּח גַּם שֶׁלֹּא מִבְּנוֹת כְּנַעַן, אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֶחֱזִיק גַּם הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת, לְכָךְ נֶהֶפְכָה לוֹ גַּם זֶה לְרֹעַ.

That is, since he did not divorce the first wives, but merely sought to satisfy Isaac by also taking a wife not from the daughters of Canaan while still retaining the former wives, this marriage likewise turned to wickedness for him.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נֶאֱמַר בַּתּוֹרָה "אָנֹכִי" קוֹדֵם לְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
Nevertheless, in the Torah "I am Hashem your God" precedes "You shall have no other gods,"
כִּי אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַדַּאי מֵ"אָנֹכִי" יָבוֹא לְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" וְסוֹפוֹ לְרַחֵק;
for among the children of Israel, from "I am" one will certainly arrive at "You shall have no," and he will ultimately distance all evil;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים נ:): לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק וְכוּלֵי שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי.
and as stated in Pesachim 50b: a person should always engage in Torah even not for its own sake, for from not for its own sake he will come to its own sake.
וְהַתּוֹסָפוֹת הִקְשָׁה מַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹסֵק שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ נוֹחַ לוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְשֶׁנֶּהֶפְכָה וְכוּלֵי, וְלֹא זָכָה נַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי.

And Tosafot challenged this from what we find elsewhere, that whoever engages in Torah not for its own sake, it would have been better for him had he not been created, and had his afterbirth been turned over on his face, and if he did not merit it becomes a potion of death.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת: וְכָל הָעוֹסֵק וְכוּלֵי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ דְּשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ נוֹחַ וְכוּלֵי וְנַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי,
But in truth both are truth: whoever engages in Torah, even though he knows that studying not for its own sake invites severe warnings,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ כָּל זֶה, כִּי חָשְׁקָה נַפְשׁוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה,
he nonetheless accepts all this upon himself because his soul passionately yearns for the Torah;
וּמַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אִם אֵין לִבּוֹ שָׁלֵם וּמְנוּקֶּה מִכָּל רַע וּפְנִיּוֹת וְחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה עֲדַיִן?
and what shall he do if his heart is not yet completely whole and cleansed of all base motives and worldly desires?
בְּאַהֲבָתָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה יִשְׁגֶּה, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ הַסַּכָּנָה וְהָרָע שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ,
In the love of Torah let him be enraptured (Proverbs 5:19), even though he knows the spiritual danger involved;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק וְכוּלֵי, וִיקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ כָּל זֶה, לְפִי שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי, וְאָז יָשׁוּב הַכֹּל לְטוֹב:
nonetheless, let him always engage in Torah and accept all this upon himself, because from not for its own sake he will come to its own sake, and then everything will be transformed to good.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Resisei Layla 6:2: “Words of Torah, moreover, intrinsically gladden the heart, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 7:19): "Wisdom strengthens the wise," imbuing him with strength and fortitude, and therefore they taught (Yoma 72b): "If he did not merit, it becomes a potion of death, etc.," because wisdom can engender levity and arrogance within him, and he is termed 'wise to do evil,' Heaven forbid. And this applies to that severe form of study not for its own sake of which our Sages of blessed memory said (Yerushalmi Berakhot 1:2): "'It would have been better for him had his afterbirth turned over, etc.';" whereas for standard learning not for its own sake, concerning which they said (Pesachim 50b): "'A person should always engage in Torah even not for its own sake...'", it certainly does not engender levity at any rate. However, when Torah study is conducted purely for Heaven's sake, the mark is quite the opposite: it brings forth reverence and meticulous care, as they stated (Kiddushin 40b): "Great is study, for it leads directly to action."”

And this applies to that severe form of study not for its own sake of which our Sages of blessed memory said (Yerushalmi Berakhot 1:2): "'It would have been better for him had his afterbirth turned over, etc.';" whereas for standard learning not for its own sake, concerning which they said (Pesachim 50b): "'A person should always engage in Torah even not for its own sake...'", it certainly does not engender levity at any rate. However, when Torah study is conducted purely for Heaven's sake, the mark is quite the opposite: it brings forth reverence and meticulous care, as they stated (Kiddushin 40b): "Great is study, for it leads directly to action."”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Resisei Layla distinguishes ordinary shelo lishmah from study that produces irreverence, and describes lishmah by its increase of yirah and care in action. This gives a criterion for the tension examined here: a person may begin while the heart is still mixed, but must not turn Torah’s strength into indifference toward serving Hashem. The direction of the learning matters as well as its starting motive.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 5: “In reason, a person ought not to attain the precious declaration ‘I am Hashem your God’ before his heart has been purified through ‘You shall have no other gods,’ for first one must turn from evil and afterward do good. But Hashem, in His great mercy, placed ‘I am’ before ‘You shall have no other gods.’ Otherwise no person in the world could attain the declaration ‘I am’: who can say that he has purified his heart in every prohibition? Of this King David said (Psalms 138:2), ‘You have magnified Your word above all Your name.’ An utterance here is a whisper: Hashem will afterward clarify that Israel's heart is clean. Therefore he says, ‘I will thank Your name’—the goodness and greatness You showed us by first giving us the declaration ‘I am,’ so that afterward He would clarify within our heart the declaration ‘You shall have no other gods.’”

sections.en: Regarding Words of Torah a Person Is Permitted to Feel Fear

p: [קסז] בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מוּתָּר אָדָם לִפְחוֹד, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת (ס.);
Regarding words of Torah a person is permitted to feel fear, as our Sages of blessed memory stated in Berakhot 60a;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּפְחַד שֶׁמָּא הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם סַם הַמָּוֶת, וְעַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד עַצְמוֹ מִתְמַתֵּק וְנַעֲשָׂה "מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ – לִשְׁמָהּ".
meaning that he should fear lest it become for him a potion of death, and through that very fear it is sweetened and transformed from "not for its own sake" into "for its own sake."
כִּי "הַאי מַאן דִּמְבַעִית – מַזָּלֵיהּ חָזֵי" (מְגִילָּה ג.),
For "one who is frightened, his guardian star (mazal) sees it" (Megillah 3a),
וְהוּא דּוּגְמַת חֲלוֹם דְּגַם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁמַּזָּלוֹ רוֹאֶה,
and this is analogous to a dream which also reflects what one's mazal sees,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נה.): חֶלְמָא בִּישָׁא – עֲצִיבוּתֵיהּ מִסְתַּיֵּיהּ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁבַּעֲצִיבוּת עַצְמוֹ דַּי.
and our Sages stated (Berakhot 55a): for a bad dream, the sorrow it causes suffices as its atonement.
וְכֵן בְּעִנְיַן תּוֹרָה: "שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי", וְדַי בָּזֶה מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְפַחֵד בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
And likewise regarding Torah: "if he did not merit, it becomes a potion of death," and it suffices that he experiences this reverent dread over words of Torah.
וּ"פִקּוּדֵי ה' יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב" (תְּהִלִּים יט, ט), וְ"הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יט), וְכֵן בִּשְׁאָר פְּסוּקִים שֶׁנּוֹתֶנֶת עֹז וְחֶדְוָה שֶׁהוּא הִפּוּךְ הַפַּחַד.

And "The statutes of Hashem are right, rejoicing the heart" (Psalms 19:9), and "Wisdom strengthens the wise" (Ecclesiastes 7:19), and so throughout verses testifying that Torah grants strength and joy, which is the antithesis of fear.
רַק רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ: "לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק אָדָם שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ וְכוּלֵי",
However, our Sages stated: "A person should always engage in Torah not for its own sake, etc.,"
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי דָּבָר זֶה הוּא "לְעוֹלָם", פֵּירוּשׁ בִּתְמִידוּת;
and that is because this condition is "always"—meaning in continuous daily routine;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַלִּשְׁמָהּ אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל לִהְיוֹת בִּתְמִידוּת, דְּלִשְׁמָהּ הַיְינוּ דְּבֵיקוּת,
whereas pure study for its own sake cannot possibly be continuous, since lishmah denotes absolute meditative cleaving (devekut),
וְשִׁעוּרוֹ כְּעוֹנַת תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת, שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לָבוֹא לִדְבֵיקוּת רַק בְּשַׁבָּת,
whose frequency is like the conjugal time of Torah scholars once a week, for one cannot reach such devekut except on Shabbat,
אוֹ הַטַּיָּילִין [פֵּירוּשׁ הַמְטַיְּילִים בַּפַּרְדֵּ"ס הַיָּדוּעַ] אֶחָד בַּיּוֹם לְכָל הַיּוֹתֵר.
or for spiritual wanderers [meaning those strolling in the mystical Orchard] once a day at most.

אֲבָל בִּתְמִידוּת הוּא שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, רַק שֶׁ"מִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי" – פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ עַצְמוֹ, מִתּוֹכוֹ וּפְנִימִיּוּתוֹ, הוּא בָּא לִהְיוֹת אוֹתוֹ לִמּוּד עַצְמוֹ לִשְׁמָהּ;
But continuous study is technically not for its own sake, except that "from within it he comes to its own sake"—meaning from within the interior of that study itself it comes to be for its own sake;
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד דִּמְפַכְּחָא לֵיהּ, שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: "אִי יִרְאַת ה' אוֹצָרוֹ – אִין וְכוּלֵי",
and that is through the reverent fear that sobers him, concerning which they said: "If the fear of Hashem is his storehouse, yes, etc.,"
וְזֶהוּ "אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם מְפַחֵד תָּמִיד" (מִשְׁלֵי כח, יד) – פֵּירוּשׁ עַל עִסְקוֹ הַתְּמִידוּת,
and this is "Praiseworthy is the man that fears always" (Proverbs 28:14)—meaning regarding his continuous study,
דְּוַדַּאי לִפְרָקִים מַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת הַדְּבֵיקוּת שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לִפְחוֹד כְּלָל.
for certainly at designated times he reaches the level of devekut where he does not need to fear at all.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ח.): "אַשְׁרֶיךָ" – בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דִּלְשׁוֹן אִישּׁוּר מַשְׁמָע מֵאֲחֵרִים [מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְשׁוֹן "וְטוֹב לָךְ"],
And our Sages stated (Berakhot 8a): "praiseworthy are you" refers to this world, for praise (ashrekha) implies acclaim recognized by others [unlike the phrase "and it shall be good with you"],
וְזֶהוּ רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דִּבְעוֹלָם הַבָּא כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹלָם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נב).
and this applies only in this world, for in the World to Come each individual possesses a world of his own (Shemot Rabbah 52).
וּבֶאֱמֶת לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ כְּלָל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, וְכִדְאָמְרוּ בִּזְבָחִים (ב:): סְתָמָא לִשְׁמָן קָיְימָא.
And in truth, Torah does not fundamentally admit "not for its own sake," as they stated in Zevachim 2b: by default offerings stand for their own sake.
רַק דִּלַאֲחֵרִים יֵשׁ טַעֲנוֹת, כִּי עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרִים בַּתּוֹרָה נִתְגַּבֵּר כֹּחַ הַדִּבּוּר בָּעוֹלָם,
Only that other observers raise accusations, for through words of Torah the power of speech is energized in the world,
וּלְפִי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם יֵשׁ דִּבּוּרִים דְּלָשׁוֹן הָרָע וְגַם כֵּן מִתְגַּבְּרִים, וְיוּכְלוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְדַבֵּר "חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם" עָלָיו
and since in the world evil speech exists and also gains strength, people might speak "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" against him
[שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן דָּוִד שֶׁהוּא סוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, הָיוּ דוֹרוֹ בַּעֲלֵי דִּלְטוֹרְיָא וְדִבְּרוּ לָשׁוֹן הָרָע עָלָיו],
[which was the situation of David who embodies the Oral Torah, whose generation contained slanderers speaking evil against him],
וּלְזֶה הָעֵצָה – פַּחַד, שֶׁהוּא הַצִּמְצוּם, וּמִצְטַמְצְמִים כֹּחוֹתָיו וְאֵין מִתְפַּשְּׁטִים לַחוּץ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְהָאִישּׁוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אָז:
and the remedy for this is holy fear, which constitutes constriction (tzimtzum), concentrating his faculties so they do not disperse outward, and then praise is affirmed in this world.

rich.text: Awe distinguishes holy intensity from the inclination’s fire

paragraphs.text: The concern accompanying Torah study directs its energy against the yetzer hara rather than allowing that energy to become self-assertion.

rich.text: The concern accompanying Torah study directs its energy against the yetzer hara rather than allowing that energy to become self-assertion.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 7:1: “The Gemara expounds “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool?” concerning those who engage in Torah but have no awe of Heaven. The anger of the sages is to stir against the evil inclination so that one will not be a fool. This comes through awe, Isaac’s fear, holy fire; its waste is Esau—anger, the evil inclination’s fire. This is according to the Geonim’s reading.”

rich.text: : “The Gemara expounds “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool?” concerning those who engage in Torah but have no awe of Heaven. The anger of the sages is to stir against the evil inclination so that one will not be a fool. This comes through awe, Isaac’s fear, holy fire; its waste is Esau—anger, the evil inclination’s fire. This is according to the Geonim’s reading.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kislev distinguishes the fire of holy awe from its waste, anger, even while discussing the intensity of the sages. This sharpens the present siman’s explanation of why fear can sweeten learning that is not yet wholly lishmah. Awe governs the direction of the energy released by Torah and gathers it toward service. It is therefore compatible with Torah’s strength and joy, while checking the misuse of those powers that the siman fears.

sections.en: A Person's Fears Arise from Sins

p: [קסח] הַפְּחָדִים שֶׁל הָאָדָם הוּא מִן הַחֲטָאִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ס.), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פָּחֲדוּ בְצִיּוֹן חַטָּאִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה לג, יד);
A person's fears arise from sins, as our Sages stated in Berakhot 60a, and as written: "The sinners in Zion are afraid" (Isaiah 33:14);
וְהַפְּחָדִים הֵם מַמָּשׁ יִסּוּרֵי גֵיהִנָּם, עַיֵּין רַאֲבַ"ד עַל סֵפֶר יְצִירָה בְּעִנְיַן יִסּוּרֵי גֵיהִנָּם.
and fears are literally the afflictions of Gehenna, see the Ra'avad on Sefer Yetzirah regarding the afflictions of Gehenna.

וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם ה. וְזֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קנג סוֹף עַמּוּד א): מַה מֶּלַח מְמַתֶּקֶת הַבָּשָׂר, אַף יִסּוּרִין מְמַתְּקִין הָעֲווֹנוֹת.
And this experience constitutes the sweetening of judgments, as our Sages stated (ibid. 5a; Zohar III:153a): just as salt sweetens meat, so suffering sweetens sins.
וְהַחֲטָאִים וְהַדִּינִים וְהַיִּסּוּרִים הַכֹּל דָּבָר אֶחָד, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז.): יוֹרֵד וּמַסִּית, עוֹלֶה וּמַקְטְרִיג, יוֹרֵד וְנוֹטֵל נְשָׁמָה.
And sins, strict judgments, and afflictions are all one single entity, as our Sages stated (Bava Batra 16a): he descends and incites, ascends and accuses, descends and takes the soul.
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נ): אֵין מַלְאָךְ אֶחָד עוֹשֶׂה שְׁתֵּי שְׁלִיחוּת, הַיְינוּ דְּהַמַּלְאָךְ נִקְרָא כֹּחַ אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר
And behold, our Sages stated (Bereishit Rabbah 50): a single angel does not perform two missions, meaning that the angel is the specific metaphysical power of that thing
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בְּמוֹרֶה נְבוּכִים, וְיַצִּיבָא מִילְּתָא גַּם מִטַּעַם חַכְמֵי הָאֱמֶת בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר],
[and as he wrote in the Moreh Nevukhim, and this is confirmed likewise by the Kabbalists as I wrote elsewhere],
וְכָל כֹּחַ וָכֹחַ מְיוּחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
and every force is distinct in its own right.
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּזֶה הַכֹּל עִנְיָן אֶחָד: וּבְעוֹלַם הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁשָּׁם מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא דִּין נִקְרָא "דִּינִים",
So perforce all of this is one unified dynamic: in the World of the Throne where the King sits upon the Throne of Judgment it is called "judgments,"
וּבְעוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים נִקְרָא "חֲטָאִים", כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה א, ו): מַתִּישׁ כֹּחַ פַּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה;
and in the World of Angels it is termed "sins," as our Sages stated (Midrash Rabbah, Eichah 1:6): it weakens the Heavenly Host;
וּלְמַטָּה – "יִסּוּרִים".
and down below in this world it is called "afflictions."
וְהַמְתָּקַת הַחֲטָאִים הוּא הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים.
And sweetening sins is identical to sweetening judgments.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, אָז נַעֲשֶׂה הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁם,
And through repentance, the sweetening of judgments occurs at their very root,
כִּי הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּל בַּלֵּב, וְעִיקַּר תְּשׁוּבָה בַּלֵּב – זֶה נִקְרָא הַמְתָּקָה בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ.
for the root of all is in the heart, and the essence of repentance is in the heart—which is termed sweetening at the root.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן הַפַּחַד בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה דְּשָׁרֵי, שֶׁמְּפַחֵד עַל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And this is likewise the permitted fear in words of Torah, where one fears having transgressed words of Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֶזְרָא שֶׁהָעָם רָעֲדוּ מְאֹד עַל הָעֲבֵירָה, וְלֹא שֶׁמְּפַחֵד מִפְּנֵי מִילֵּי דְּעָלְמָא – זֶהוּ "אַשְׁרֵי";
as written in Ezra (10:9) that the people trembled exceedingly over the transgression, and not that he fears worldly affairs—this is the 'Praiseworthy' (of Proverbs 28:14);
כִּי הוּא הַמְתָּקָה בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, דְּאִתְהֲפֵיךְ מְרִירוּ לְמָתוֹק, שֶׁהַפַּחַד עַצְמוֹ שִׂמְחָה,
for it is a sweetening at the root, transforming bitterness into sweetness, where the fear itself becomes joy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג): אֲנִי שָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי;
as stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 3): "I rejoiced out of my fear";
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק בְּיִרְאַת ה', אֲבָל בִּשְׁאָר יְרָאוֹת רַק מֵבִיא לִידֵי שִׂמְחָה אַחַר כָּךְ:
and this is possible only within the fear of Hashem, whereas with other fears it merely brings to joy afterward.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:46:1: “The scoffers say that this fear is foolishness and does not come from Avraham’s holy source, for fear born from love is true yirah; rather, they say it comes from Avimelech, who was also afraid. As it says, “I said: surely there is no fear of God”—implying that the truth was otherwise, as indeed it was, since he did not need to send them away. But it was a fear of melancholy, like “The sinners in Zion were afraid,” as the Sages said [Berakhot 60a]: “You are a sinner”; and, in explaining the verse that praises constant fear, “That refers to matters of Torah.” This is Yitzchak’s level, which is Torah, as I heard concerning the Sages’ expression “Moshe from the mouth of Gevurah”: the fear that comes from words of Torah is good.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah contrasts the fear associated with Avimelech with Yitzchak’s yirah, born from love and directed by Torah. This makes the distinction at the end of the siman more precise. The point is not to call every frightening feeling a spiritual attainment, but to identify the fear whose movement is toward Hashem and can itself be joined to joy. Citation correction: the quoted exchange is in Berakhot 60a. The reference to HaNizakin in the supplied Hebrew has been corrected here. The answer about Torah responds to the verse praising constant fear; it does not describe the student’s sinful fear as Torah study.

His soul desires and He performs” (Job 23:13) – it is taught: One angel does not perform two missions, and two angels do not perform one mission. Yet you say: “[The] two [angels came to Sodom]”? The explanation is that Mikhael gave his tidings and departed, Gavriel was dispatched to overturn Sodom, and Refael, to rescue Lot. “The two angels came to Sodom” – here it says “angels,” but elsewhere, it characterizes them as “people” (Genesis 18:2). The explanation is that there, when the Divine Presence was over them, they were characterized as “people.” Once the Divine Presence departed from over them, they assumed the manifestation of angels. Rabbi Tanḥuma said that Rabbi Levi said: To Abraham, whose power was great, they appeared in the image of men; to Lot, whose strength was inferior, they appeared in the image of angels. Rabbi Ḥanina said: Before they performed their mission, they are characterized as people; after performing their mission, as angels. Rabbi Tanḥuma said: This is analogous to one who assumed a position of local government from the king. Until he reached his seat of authority, he walked about as a commoner. Once he reached the seat of his authority, he walked about as a nobleman. So, until they performed their mission, they are characterized as people, after performing their mission, they are characterized as angels.”

sections.en: When Fear of Something Falls Upon a Person

p: [קסט] כַּאֲשֶׁר נוֹפֵל עַל אָדָם פַּחַד מֵאֵיזֶה דָבָר, אָז תֵּיכֶף יְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים לְהִנָּצֵל מִזֶּה,
When fear of something falls upon a person, let him immediately plead for mercy to be saved from it,
כִּי לְכָךְ עוֹרְרוּהוּ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בְּפַחַד זֶה,
for for this very purpose did Heaven awaken him through this fear,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד:): לְעוֹלָם יַקְדִּים אָדָם תְּפִלָּה לַצָּרָה;
as our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 44b): "A person should always anticipate distress with prayer";
וּמִנַּיִן יוֹדֵעַ קוֹדֶם מִן הַצָּרָה רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן? רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרֵר עַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד.
and whence does he know beforehand of the distress, may the Merciful One preserve us? The Blessed Name awakens him through fear.
כִּי יֵשׁ דִּינָא קַשְׁיָא רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַמְתִּיק אַחַר צֵאתוֹ לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם, רַק צָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּיקוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּעוֹדוֹ בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ.

For there exists harsh judgment (dina kashya), may the Merciful One preserve us, which cannot be sweetened after it emerges into the world, but must be sweetened at its root while still in its formative gestation.
דְּמַזָּל הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כַּיָּדוּעַ וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, וּמַזָּלֵיהּ חָזֵי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲדַיִן וּמִיבְעִית.
For one's mazal is the root as is known, and his mazal perceives what is still in the root, and he becomes frightened.
וּבִתְפִלָּה מַמְתִּיק בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא אַחַר כָּךְ טוֹב
And through prayer he sweetens it at the root until it subsequently emerges as good
[וְזֶה עִנְיַן יְמֵי אֱלוּל שֶׁהוּא ל' יוֹם לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, שׁוֹאֲלִין וְדוֹרְשִׁין בְּעִנְיָנוֹ, דְּל' יוֹם מִקּוֹדֶם הוּא זְמַן הַהֲכָנָה.
[and this is the significance of the days of Elul, thirty days before Rosh Hashanah when we inquire into its themes, for thirty days prior is the period of preparation.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִקְרָא "הַיּוֹם הֲרַת עוֹלָם", שֶׁהוּא הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁעָלָה לִבְרוֹא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין, דְּהַיְינוּ סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהוּא עֵת קֵץ וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And it is known that Rosh Hashanah is called 'the day of the world's conception,' which represents the initial Thought to create with strict Judgment—meaning the ultimate end, the World to Come,
שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה יִצְחָק רֹאשׁ הַהַנְהָגָה כַּנּוֹדָע, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל מִינֵי טוֹבָה בְּדִין, זֶה הָיָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה.
when Isaac will head the governance, when all goodness will be awarded by strict justice, which was in Thought first.

וּלְהַמְתִּיק גַּם הַדִּינִים דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה בְּשָׁרְשָׁם, שֶׁהוּא עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה [שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַנִּקְרָא מַזָּלָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר], מַקְדִּימִים בֶּאֱלוּל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל.
And to sweeten even the judgments of Thought at their root, the depth of Thought's inception [which is what is called mazala, as I wrote elsewhere], we anticipate in Elul with prayer.
וּלְהַמְתִּיק שָׁם בְּעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת אַף לְרֹשֶׁם רָע כְּלָל כַּיָּדוּעַ.
And sweetening there in the depth of inception leaves no room even for an impression of evil, as is known.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה דְּחֹדֶשׁ אֱלוּל בְּיוֹ"ד, כִּידוּעַ דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּמְנָחוֹת (כט:) עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי בְּיָהּ ה' וְגוֹמֵר": עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהֵ"א,
Therefore Sefer Yetzirah states that the month of Elul was created with the letter Yud, reflecting Menachot 29b: this world was created with Hei,
וּלְכָךְ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן שֶׁהוּא כְּפִי סוֹף הַבְּרִיאָה וּמַעֲשֵׂה עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהֵ"א, וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּיוֹ"ד, וְהָיָה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת כֵּן תִּשְׁרֵי.
so the month of Nisan which aligns with the physical world is with Hei, while the World to Come is with Yud, and so should Tishrei have been.

אֲבָל יָדוּעַ דְּהַזְּמַנִּים יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי לְהוּ, וְהֵם קִדְּשׁוּ לֶאֱלוּל בִּקְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ כִּי רָצוּ לְהַמְתִּיק בְּשָׁרְשָׁן, וּלְכָךְ אֱלוּל בְּיוֹ"ד, וְהוּא עַל שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
But Israel sanctifies the seasons, and they sanctified Elul with this holiness to sweeten at the root; thus Elul is associated with Yud, signifying Thought.
וְל' יוֹם קוֹדֶם הַיְינוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה לַחְשׁוֹב זוֹ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, שֶׁהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה דְּבוּקָה בְּשָׁרְשָׁהּ]:
And thirty days prior represents thinking this thought, where thought cleaves to its primordial root].

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Miketz 1: “That night Yosef's cry grew: “Return, Hashem—until when?” Immediately he attained deliverance. Concerning this it says, “Hashem, God of my deliverance… I cried at night before You.” Such is the Holy One's way: before He gives deliverance, He places a cry in the person's heart, so that it may be called “the labor of your hands.””

rich.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Miketz 1

: “That night Yosef's cry grew: “Return, Hashem—until when?” Immediately he attained deliverance. Concerning this it says, “Hashem, God of my deliverance… I cried at night before You.” Such is the Holy One's way: before He gives deliverance, He places a cry in the person's heart, so that it may be called “the labor of your hands.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach describes Yosef's cry intensifying immediately before his deliverance, and explains that Hashem places such a cry in the heart so the gift may become the fruit of the person's own work. This supplies a concrete counterpart to the siman's call to turn an awakening into prayer before the matter fully emerges. The comparison concerns the sequence of awakening and response; it does not replace the siman's distinct explanation of Elul.

paragraphs.text: Awakening prayer before trouble
Recognizing a need can awaken prayer before a crisis has to do so.

rich.text: Recognizing a need can awaken prayer before a crisis has to do so.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Resisei Layla 11:1: “Every distress that Hashem sends a person in this world, Heaven forbid, is for this: to awaken him to prayer. As the Sages said (Shemot Rabbah 21) concerning ‘Pharaoh drew near’: it is like a noblewoman whose voice the king wished to hear. They also said (Yevamot 64a), ‘Why were the patriarchs infertile? Because the Holy One desires the prayers of the righteous.’ Of this they said (Sanhedrin 44b), ‘A person should always precede [trouble with prayer], as it says, “Will your cry set you beyond distress?”’ He should awaken himself to prayer earlier and not need trouble to awaken him, Heaven forbid. All the exiles and sufferings serve this: to elevate all the affairs of this world to the world's heights through prayer, so that the night shines like day.”

rich.text: : “Every distress that Hashem sends a person in this world, Heaven forbid, is for this: to awaken him to prayer. As the Sages said (Shemot Rabbah 21) concerning ‘Pharaoh drew near’: it is like a noblewoman whose voice the king wished to hear. They also said (Yevamot 64a), ‘Why were the patriarchs infertile? Because the Holy One desires the prayers of the righteous.’ Of this they said (Sanhedrin 44b), ‘A person should always precede [trouble with prayer], as it says, “Will your cry set you beyond distress?”’ He should awaken himself to prayer earlier and not need trouble to awaken him, Heaven forbid. All the exiles and sufferings serve this: to elevate all the affairs of this world to the world's heights through prayer, so that the night shines like day.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Resisei Layla develops the same instruction to pray before trouble. Feeling the lack awakens the voice of prayer; praying earlier means that a crisis need not perform that awakening. This explains the siman's practical first step when fear arises, before its discussion of Elul and judgment at the root.

paragraphs.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Shofar 5: “We say on Rosh Hashanah, “Today is the world’s conception.” The Sages disagreed whether the world was created in Tishrei or in Nisan. How could they disagree over what occurred, and how could “These and those are the words of the living God” apply to such a disagreement? The answer is that there are conception and birth: one speaks of one thing and the other of another, and they do not disagree. Conception took place in Tishrei; the letters of Tishrei are also the letters of reishit, “beginning.” Birth took place in Nisan, since miracles are needed to emerge from the womb at birth. Nisan likewise suggests nes, “miracle,” and redemption occurred in it through a miracle. It is known that the entire exodus from Egypt is described in terms of birth: “I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood.” So too here it says, “Today is the world’s conception,” using the language of pregnancy, rather than saying, “The world was created,” for in Tishrei there was conception. Here it speaks of the human being, although the world itself was created on the twenty-fifth of Elul; from the human being the world may be understood.”
