sections.en: When the Holy One, Blessed Be He, Desires to Bestow Good Upon a Person…

p: [קע] כְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹצֶה לְהֵיטִיב לָאָדָם וְרוֹצֶה רַק שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל הָאָדָם עַל הַדָּבָר, אָז מַזְמִין לְפָנָיו צַעַר אוֹ פַּחַד מֵעֵין דָּבָר זֶה,
When the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to bestow good upon a person and desires only that the person pray for it, He orchestrates distress or fear akin to that matter,
וּכְדִשְׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת סד.): מִפְּנֵי מָה הָיוּ אִמָּהוֹת עֲקוּרוֹת וְכוּלֵי.
as our Sages stated (Yevamot 64a): Why were the Matriarchs barren? Because Hashem yearns for their prayers.
אוֹ רוֹאֶה אַחֵר מְעוּנֶּה בְּאוֹתוֹ דָבָר וּמְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עָלָיו כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא נַעֲנֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פַּחַד פָּחַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵנִי" (אִיּוֹב ג, כה).
Or he witnesses another afflicted in that very matter and pleads for mercy on his behalf so that he himself is answered, as written: "For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me" (Job 3:25).
כִּי כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה לְהָבִיא לָעוֹלָם אוֹ לָאָדָם, הִיא מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת לְכַמָּה גְּוָונִין, וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ הַהֵיפֶךְ גַּם כֵּן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
For every matter the Blessed Name seeks to bring into the world or unto man extends into various manifestations, containing its opposite as well, Heaven forbid,
כִּדְאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל וְזֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רטז עַמּוּד ב) בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל שֶׁהָיוּ מְעוּתָּדִים לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה אִלּוּ זָכוּ, וְכֵן בְּכָל דּוֹר וּבְכָל אָדָם.
as stated (Shemot Rabbah 30; Zohar III:216b) concerning the Generation of the Flood, that they were destined to receive the Torah had they merited, and so in every generation and within every person.
וּלְכָךְ כְּשֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר מִדָּה זוֹ לְטוֹבָה, מִתְעוֹרֵר גַּם כֵּן הַהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וּמַרְגִּישׁ פַּחַד וּמִתְפַּלֵּל וּבָא הַטּוֹב.
And therefore, when this attribute awakens toward the good, its opposite is likewise aroused, and he senses fear, prays, and the good arrives.
אֲבָל לְעוֹלָם הוּא בָּא הַדָּבָר שֶׁמִּתְפַּחֵד, רַק שֶׁבָּא הַהֵיפֶךְ, דְּהַיְינוּ כָּל מִינֵי טוֹבָה שֶׁבְּדָבָר זֶה.
Yet in reality the very thing he feared arrives, only that it arrives in its inverted form—namely all manner of goodness within that matter.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סו): צַדִּיקִים תְּחִלָּתָן יִסּוּרִין וְסוֹפָן שַׁלְוָה,
And this is what is stated (Bereishit Rabbah 66): the righteous experience afflictions at their outset and tranquility at their end,
פֵּירוּשׁ בְּכָל דָּבָר וְכָל מִדָּה טוֹבָה וְעִנְיָן טוֹב, תְּחִלַּת הַכְּנִיסָה בּוֹ הוּא בְּצַעַר, כְּטַעַם כָּל הַתְחָלוֹת קָשׁוֹת
meaning in every matter, good character trait, and worthy endeavor, the initial entry into it involves distress, because all beginnings are difficult
[עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (גִּטִּין מג.): אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן וְכוּלֵי],
[along the lines of Gittin 43a: a person does not master words of Torah unless he stumbles],
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (ה.): ג' מַתָּנוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְכוּלֵי, וּכִבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: בְּרֵישָׁא וְכוּלֵי (שַׁבָּת עז:).
and as in Berakhot 5a: three precious gifts were given through suffering, and matching creation: first darkness, then light (Shabbat 77b).

לְפִי שֶׁהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רוּבּוֹ רַע כַּיָּדוּעַ, וּלְכָךְ כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ, רוֹאֶה הוּא מִקּוֹדֶם כֹּחַ הָרָע שֶׁבּוֹ וּמִצְטַעֵר, וְעַל יְדֵי הַצַּעַר מַמְתִּיקוֹ וּמִיָּד סוֹפוֹ שַׁלְוָה.

Because this world is predominantly coarse and evil, whenever a matter awakens within him, he first perceives the power of evil within it and feels anguish, and through that anguish he sweetens it, and immediately its culmination is tranquility.

וּכְעִנְיַן תְּלָתָא דְּפוּרְעָנוּתָא וְשֶׁבַע דְּנֶחָמָתָא שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, שֶׁהֵם ג' רִאשׁוֹנוֹת וְז' תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת, שֶׁהַהַתְחָלָה חָלוּק לְג' וְהַסּוֹף לְז' כַּיָּדוּעַ.

And this mirrors the three Haftarot of rebuke and seven of consolation instituted by our Sages, corresponding to the three upper and seven lower sefirot, the beginning dividing into three and the end into seven.
וְהַתְחָלַת כָּל פְּעֻלָּה הוּא מִצַּד הֶכְרֵחַ הַפּוֹעֵל שֶׁחָסֵר לְאוֹתָהּ פְּעֻלָּה, אִם כֵּן הַהַתְחָלָה מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁהוּא חָסֵר וְדָחוּק לְכָךְ,
And the start of every action stems from the necessity felt by the actor who lacks that outcome; thus the beginning emerges from deficiency, being pressured toward it,
וּ"מִן הַמֵּצַר קָרָאתִי יָּהּ" (תְּהִלִּים קיח, ה), שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַצַּעַר זוֹעֵק לַה', וְעוֹנֵהוּ בַּמֶּרְחָב,
and "Out of the straits I called upon Yah" (Psalms 118:5), where out of distress he cries to Hashem, Who answers him with expansive relief,
שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא נֶחָמָה, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּתְנַחֵם עַל צַעַר הֶעָבָר, שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁאֵין צַעַר, כְּעִנְיַן "וְנַסְתֶּם וְאֵין רֹדֵף" (וַיִּקְרָא כו, יז).
which is termed consolation—being comforted over past distress, realizing that in truth there is no distress, in the manner of: "and you shall flee when none pursues you" (Leviticus 26:17).
כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה, בְּוַדַּאי לֹא קִלְּלָם, רַק בְּכָל קְלָלָה טָמוּן הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ לוֹ רַק עַל יְדֵי הַקְּלָלָה.
For Moses our teacher loved Israel and certainly did not curse them, but within every curse lay hidden the blessing that could not be attained except through that curse.
וּבְקִלְלַת הַנְּסִיסָה שָׁם הוּא הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵין רוֹדֵף כְּלָל.
And within the curse of fleeing lies the blessing that there is no pursuer at all.
וּכְשֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר הֶאָרָה זוֹ לְהַכִּיר שֶׁאֵין רוֹדֵף כְּלָל, מִתְעוֹרֵר גַּם כֵּן הַהֵיפוּךְ שֶׁהוּא הַנְּסִיסָה,
And when this illumination awakens to recognize that none pursues, its opposite—the sensation of fleeing—is likewise aroused,
וְעַל יְדֵי הַנְּסִיסָה מַכִּיר תֵּיכֶף אֲמִיתַּת יִחוּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַד שֶׁאֵין רוֹדֵף כְּלָל.
and through fleeing he instantly perceives the ultimate unity of the Blessed Name, realizing that there is truly no pursuer.
וְכֵן בְּקִלְלַת "וְלֹא תַאֲמִין בְּחַיֶּיךָ" (דְּבָרִים כח, סו), הוֹדִיעֲךָ שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בְּקַלְקָלָה הֵם קְרוּיִים חַיִּים, וְלֹא כִּרְשָׁעִים שֶׁבְּחַיֵּיהֶם קְרוּיִים מֵתִים.

And likewise with the curse "and you shall have no assurance of your life" (Deuteronomy 28:66), it informs you that even in their fallen state they are called "living," unlike the wicked who in their lifetime are called dead.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם מִגּוֹדֶל הַפַּחַד עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַאֲמִינוּ גַּם בְּכָךְ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חַיֵּי עוֹלָם בְּהַכִּירָם מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם.
Only that out of the magnitude of fear they do not believe that they possess eternal life when examining their deeds.
וּבְאוֹתוֹ פָּסוּק נִתְגַּלָּה זֶה שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חַיִּים, דְּאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים קְרוּיִים מֵתִים וְאֵין לָהֶם חַיִּים כְּלָל לְהַאֲמִין בָּהֶם.
And in that very verse it is revealed that all Israel have life, whereas the gentile nations are termed dead and have no true life to believe in.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 66:4: ““Peoples will serve you, and nations will prostrate themselves to you. Be a lord to your brethren, and your mother’s sons will prostrate themselves to you. Cursed be one who curses you, and blessed be one who blesses you” (Genesis 27:29). “Peoples will serve you” – these are the seventy nations. “And nations will prostrate themselves to you” – these are the descendants of Ishmael and the sons of Ketura, in whose regard it is written: “Ashurim, Letushim, and Leumim” (Genesis 25:3). “Be a lord to your brethren” – this is Esau and his chieftains. “And your mother’s sons will prostrate themselves to you” – here it says: “And your mother’s sons will prostrate themselves to you,” but elsewhere it says: “And your father’s sons will prostrate themselves to you” (Genesis 49:8). It is that Jacob, because he took four wives, Leah, Rachel, Zilpa, and Bilha, he says: “Your father’s sons.” Isaac took Rebecca, he said: “Your mother’s sons.” “Cursed be one who curses you…” – and elsewhere it says: “Those who bless you are blessed, and those who curse you are cursed” (Numbers 24:9). It is that Bilam, because he was a hater, began with a blessing and concluded with a curse. Yitzḥak, who was a lover, opened with a curse and concluded with a blessing. Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Rabbi Ḥiyya said: The wicked, because their beginning is tranquility and their end is suffering, they begin with blessing and end with curse. The righteous, because their beginning is suffering and their end is tranquility, they begin with curse and end with blessing: “Cursed be one who curses you, and blessed be one who blesses you.””

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 7:1-3: “However, the vital animal soul in Israel that comes from the kelippah and is clothed in human blood, as explained above; the souls of pure animals, beasts, birds, and fish permitted for eating; the existence and vitality of all inanimate things and plants permitted for eating; and the existence and vitality of every deed, speech, and thought in worldly affairs containing no forbidden aspect—not a root or branch of the 365 prohibitions and their biblical or rabbinic extensions—but performed without intent for Heaven, rather from bodily will, desire, and appetite, even when truly needed for the body’s existence and life, if the intention is not for Heaven in order to serve Hashem with one’s body: all these deeds, speech, and thoughts are no better than the vital animal soul itself. All alike flow and are drawn from the second level among the kelippot and the other side: the fourth kelippah, called kelippat nogah. In this world, called the World of Action, it is almost entirely evil, with only a little good mixed within it; from that good come the good qualities in Israel’s animal soul, as explained above. It is an intermediate level between the three entirely impure kelippot and the level and degree of holiness. Therefore it is sometimes included among the three impure kelippot, as written in Etz Chaim, Gate 49, at the beginning of chapter 4, in the Zohar’s name; and sometimes it is included and rises into the level and degree of holiness—that is, when the good mixed within it is separated from the evil, prevails, ascends, and is included in holiness.”

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Megillah 31b:1:1: “The reason is that we follow the Pesikta in reciting three haftarot of calamity before the Ninth of Av: “The words of Yirmeyahu,” “Hear the word of Hashem,” and “The vision of Yeshayahu.” After the Ninth of Av come seven of consolation and two of repentance: “Comfort, comfort,” “Zion said,” “Afflicted, storm-tossed” by itself, “I, I,” “Sing, barren one,” “Arise, shine,” “I will greatly rejoice,” “Seek,” and “Return.” Therefore we place “Afflicted, storm-tossed” before “Sing, barren one,” for consolations proceed by becoming ever greater.”

paragraphs.text: The limit creates room for a person's service and relation to Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The Seventh Day of Pesach 25:4: ““My strength and song is Yah”: strength indicates firmness, and song indicates limitation. Israel's strength comes from Hashem's limiting the greatness of His light. Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 21, page 63) says that with the name Yah He created the hidden worlds, and with Vav-He He created this world and the World to Come. Hashem limited His light and placed within this world a form in which completion requires Israel's service. Through this limitation there is a bond and unity with Israel. Concerning it the verse says, “From narrowness I called Yah; Yah answered me in breadth.” Through the limitation Israel sees its connection with Hashem, and there is no greater breadth than this. Therefore it says, “He became my deliverance”: all deliverances flow to Israel through this connection.”

Divine concealment gives Israel an actual part in the service; recognizing the connection made possible through that limitation is itself the breadth. This develops the siman's account of the good within a painful beginning without reducing its pattern to the outward pain alone.

sections.en: There Is a Place Prepared for Distress

p: [קעא] יֵשׁ מָקוֹם מוּכָן לְצַעַר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קב.): בִּשְׁכֶם מָקוֹם וְכוּלֵי;
There is a place prepared for distress, Heaven forbid, as our Sages stated in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 102a): in Shechem, a place prepared for calamity;
וְכֵן זְמַן, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם): עֵת וְכוּלֵי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית כט:): בַּר יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאִית לֵיהּ דִּינָא וְכוּלֵי בְּאָב וְכוּלֵי;
and likewise time, as our Sages said: a time prepared for calamity, and as stated (Ta'anit 29b): a Jew who has litigation with a gentile should avoid it in the month of Av;
וְכֵן בַּנֶּפֶשׁ, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם כה.) בְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פְּדָת וְטוּבָא.
and likewise in the soul, in the manner our Sages taught (ibid. 25a) regarding Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat, and many others.
וְאֵיךְ יְצוּיַּר זֶה שֶׁמּוּכָן מִתְּחִלַּת בְּרִיאָה לְרַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וַהֲלֹא "מִפִּי עֶלְיוֹן לֹא תֵצֵא הָרָעוֹת" (אֵיכָה ג, לח)?
And how can it be conceived that something was prepared from the inception of Creation for evil, Heaven forbid, seeing that "out of the mouth of the Most High proceeds not evil" (Lamentations 3:38)?
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת לְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים מַרְפֵּא, שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה "מוּכָן לְפֻרְעָנוּת" – לְשׁוֹן פֵּרָעוֹן;
But in truth the words of the Sages are healing, for they said "prepared for calamity (pur'anut)"—which is the language of payment and recompense (pera'on);

רַק דִּשְׂכַר מִצְוָה בְּהַאי עָלְמָא לֵיכָּא (קִדּוּשִׁין לט:), רַק פֵּירָעוֹן הָעֲבֵירוֹת, אִם לֹא שֶׁזָּכָה לִטְעוֹם מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אוֹ מֵאוֹתָן מִצְווֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם פֵּירוֹת.

only that reward for a mitzvah does not exist in this world (Kiddushin 39b), but only payment for transgressions, unless one merits to taste the fruit of his deeds in this world or from those mitzvot that bear terrestrial fruit.
וְאוֹתוֹ הַזְּמַן, מָקוֹם וְנֶפֶשׁ הוּא מוּכָן לְקַבֵּל פֵּירָעוֹן מַה שֶּׁנִּשְׂתַּכֵּר.
And that time, place, and soul are prepared to receive the recompense of what was earned.

וּמַה דִּשְׂכַר מִצְוָה בְּהַאי עָלְמָא לֵיכָּא, הַיְינוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן מְלֹא עָמְסוֹ וְכוּלֵי (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק.), וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְקַבֵּל רוֹב טוֹבָה הַהוּא כְּלָל.

And the reason reward for a mitzvah does not exist in this world is because the Holy One gives according to His full capacity (Sanhedrin 100a), and it is impossible in this physical world to receive that immense goodness at all.
וּבְאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם, זְמַן, נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁנִּשְׁפַּע הַפֵּירָעוֹן וּשְׂכָרוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מִצַּד רִבּוּי הַשֶּׁפַע נַעֲשָׂה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם פֻּרְעָנוּת לְרַע,
And in that place, time, and soul wherein the recompense and reward of the Blessed Name are poured out, out of the sheer abundance of the influx it becomes, Heaven forbid, pur'anut for apparent evil,
כִּידוּעַ בְּסוֹד שְׁבִירָתָן שֶׁל כֵּלִים זוֹהִי מִיתָתָן עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הָאוֹר;
as is known in the esoteric secret of the Shattering of the Vessels, which was their demise through the overwhelming abundance of light;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק לד) עַל פָּסוּק "לֹא יִרְאַנִי" – הָא בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתָן רוֹאֶה.
and so our Sages stated (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 34) on "man shall not see Me and live"—behold, at the hour of their death they see.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא נד:) שֶׁמָּצְאוּ כְּרוּבִים מְעוֹרִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם;
And therefore our Sages stated (Yoma 54b) that they found the cherubim intertwined in embrace, even though Israel was not performing the will of the Omnipresent;
כִּי אָז הָיָה תֹּקֶף רִבּוּי שֶׁפַע הָאוֹר, וּלְכָךְ זָכָה יְחֶזְקֵאל לְמַרְאוֹת אֱלֹהִים.
for then was the peak of the overwhelming abundance of the light's influx, and therefore Ezekiel merited the visions of God.
וּמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה בֶּאֱמֶת, מְקַבֵּל פֵּירָעוֹן הַטּוֹבָה אָז, שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן לֵידַת מָשִׁיחַ בְּטִשְׁעָה בְּאָב.
And whoever truly merits receives the payment of goodness then, which is the inner meaning of the birth of the Messiah on the Ninth of Av.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא): לַכֹּל נָתַתָּ בֶּן זוּג, שֶׁלְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ זוּג, דְּהַיְינוּ עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ, שֶׁיֵּשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ נֶגְדּוֹ וְזֶהוּ לְעֵזֶר לוֹ.

And our Sages stated (Bereishit Rabbah 11): unto all You gave a mate, for every entity has a counterpart, meaning a "helpmate opposite him," where something is literally opposite him and that serves as his help.

וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְלַאכְתּוֹ הוּא מִיּוֹם שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סח): לְזַוֵּוג זִוּוּגִים אֵלּוּ שֶׁל מָקוֹם וּזְמַן וְנֶפֶשׁ כָּל אֶחָד בְּהֶפְכָּן;
And the work of the Blessed Name since the day the world was created (Bereishit Rabbah 68) is to pair these unions of place, time, and soul, each with its opposite;
דְּיֵשׁ מָקוֹם מוּכָן לְהֵיפֶךְ מַמָּשׁ, שֶׁלֹּא לְקַבֵּל שׁוּם שְׂכַר מַעֲשִׂים, רַק לִבְטוֹחַ בְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁנֶּאֱמָן לְשַׁלֵּם שָׂכָר, וּבְזִוּוּגָם מִתְמַתְּקִים יַחַד.

for there is a place prepared for the exact opposite, not to receive any immediate reward for deeds, but to trust in the Master of the house Who is faithful to pay reward, and in their union they are sweetened together.
וְיָדוּעַ נֶגֶד כ"ב יָמִים שֶׁבֵּין הַמְּצָרִים הֵם מֵרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה עַד שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת
And it is known that facing the twenty-two days of Bein HaMetzarim (from 17 Tammuz to 9 Av) stand the twenty-two days from Rosh Hashanah through Shemini Atzeret
[וְשִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה הוּא נֶגֶד י' בְּאָב, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִלּוּ הֲוַאי הָתָם וְכוּלֵי (תַּעֲנִית כט.),
[and Simchat Torah corresponds to the Tenth of Av, concerning which Rabbi Yochanan said: Had I been there, I would have established the fast on the Tenth (Ta'anit 29a),
כִּי סְפֵיקָא דְיוֹמָא שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם טוֹב הוּא נֶגֶד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַדּוֹמָה לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁהֵם שְׁנֵי לוּחוֹת הַבְּרִית,
for the rabbinic second day of the diaspora (safeka deyoma) on every festival corresponds to the Oral Torah resembling the Written Torah, which are the two Tablets of the Covenant,
וְכֵן שְׁנֵי יָמִים יוֹם טוֹב אֶחָד דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְאֶחָד דְּרַבָּנָן, וְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה יוֹרֶדֶת לִשְׁנֵי הַיָּמִים;
and so two days of Yom Tov, one biblical and one rabbinic, where the holiness descends into both days;
וְכֵן הַשֶּׁפַע שֶׁיָּרַד לְט' בְּאָב שֶׁהָיָה מִלְּמַעְלָה שֶׁפַע גָּדוֹל וְעָצוּם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, נִתְחַלֵּק גַּם לְי' בְּאָב, וּלְמַטָּה נִתְהַפֵּךְ רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן].

and so the influx that descended upon the Ninth of Av, which from Above was an immense influx as noted above, was divided unto the Tenth of Av as well, though below it was inverted into tragedy, may the Merciful One preserve us].
וְיָדוּעַ דְּטַעַם סֻכָּה הוּא הַחִסָּיוֹן בַּה' וְהַבִּטָּחוֹן בּוֹ.
And it is known that the reason for the Sukkah is seeking refuge in Hashem and trusting in Him.

וְנֶגֶד ט' בְּאָב הוּא שְׁמִינִי עֲצֶרֶת, שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא פִּינְחָס טז): פַּר אֶחָד וְכוּלֵי, אֲנִי וְאַתֶּם, כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד "ה' בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְגוֹמֵר", מַמָּשׁ הֵיפֶךְ ט' בְּאָב.

And facing the Ninth of Av is Shemini Atzeret, concerning which our Sages stated (Midrash Tanchuma, Pinchas 16): one bull—I and you alone, like the future 'Hashem alone shall lead him' (Deuteronomy 32:12), the exact opposite of the Ninth of Av.
וְכ"ב יָמִים הֵם נֶגֶד כ"ב אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁפָּגְמוּ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּאֵיכָה רַבָּתִי,
And the twenty-two days correspond to the twenty-two letters of the Torah which they blemished, as our Sages expounded in Eichah Rabbah,
דִּלְכָךְ בְּי"ז בְּתַמּוּז נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ לוּחוֹת וְנִשְׂרְפָה הַתּוֹרָה, וְהוּא נֶגֶד אוֹת א' שֶׁמַּתְחִיל בּוֹ אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה,
which is why on the Seventeenth of Tammuz the Tablets were broken and the Torah was burned, corresponding to the letter Aleph which begins the letters of the Torah,
וּבְאוֹתוֹ זְמַן יוֹרֵד שֶׁפַע דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה, רַק שֶׁהוּא בִּרְאִיָּה כְּטַעַם מַרְאוֹת יְחֶזְקֵאל.
and during that period an abundant influx of words of Torah descends, only that it occurs in vision, matching the visions of Ezekiel.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נז:): הָרוֹאֶה יְחֶזְקֵאל יְצַפֶּה לְחָכְמָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ דּוּגְמַת פֶּסַח "רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵי",
And our Sages stated (Berakhot 57b): one who sees Ezekiel should anticipate wisdom, which mirrors Passover where "a maidservant saw at the Sea, etc.,"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁבוּעוֹת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה בְּקִנְיָן, וְצָרִיךְ מ"ט יְמֵי סְפִירָה בֵּינְתַיִם.
and afterward Shavuot brings the Giving of the Torah in permanent acquisition, requiring forty-nine days of the Omer count in between.
וְכֵן מִי' בְּאָב עַד רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הֵם מ"ט יְמֵי סְפִירַת נְקִיִּים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַתְחִיל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּקִנְיָן כְּפִי תֹּקֶף הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁבֵּין הַמְּצָרִים:

And so from the Tenth of Av until Rosh Hashanah are forty-nine clean days of counting, and afterward words of Torah commence in permanent acquisition commensurate with the intensity of the vision beheld during the Three Weeks of Bein HaMetzarim.

paragraphs.text: Taanit 25a:11-13: “Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat was in very straitened circumstances. He underwent bloodletting and had nothing to eat afterward. He took a clove of garlic and put it in his mouth; his heart grew faint and he fell asleep. The Sages came to inquire after him. They saw him weeping and laughing, and a flash of fire emerged from his forehead. When he awoke, they asked him, “Why were you weeping and laughing?” He told them: “The Holy One, blessed be He, was sitting with me, and I said to Him, ‘How long must I suffer in this world?’ He said to me, ‘Elazar, My son, would you like Me to overturn the world from its beginning? Perhaps you would then be born at a time of sustenance.’ I said before Him, ‘All that—and only perhaps?’ I asked Him, ‘Have I already lived longer than I have yet to live?’ He said to me, ‘You have already lived longer.’ I said before Him, ‘If so, I do not want it.’””

paragraphs.text: Chidushei Agadot on Bekhorot 8b:4: “Further, “They brought two eggs and said to him: Which is from the hen”—this follows what was said in our passage: a hen produces after twenty-one days, and its counterpart among trees is the almond. We say that Yirmeyahu alluded to this in “I see an almond rod”: the twenty-one days from the seventeenth of Tammuz to the Ninth of Av. They alluded to these days by a black hen, on account of exile. There are also twenty-one days of forgiveness and joy, from the first festival day of Rosh Hashanah to the twenty-first of Tishrei, Hoshana Rabbah, the day on which the sealing is completed, as found in the Midrashim. To these they alluded by a white hen, on account of the whitening of sins. Thus they said: The two eggs produced by the two hens are both white, and one cannot recognize which came from the black hen and which from the white. Likewise, you have no distinguishing sign, for one fate befalls them all: calamities and good things have equal numbers of days, twenty-one, and there is no ground for your hope. He answered by the corresponding example of black goats: these are the two goats Israel brought on Yom Kippur. The white one represents the goat for Hashem, and the black one the goat for Azazel. The cheese produced from both is white, for the goat sent to Azazel also whitened Israel’s sins, as it says, “The goat shall bear”; and as they said, they tied a crimson thread to the scapegoat, and when it reached the wilderness it turned white. So too with the two hens: both produced after twenty-one days, and both produced white eggs. These two periods of twenty-one days likewise have equal results in whitening: just as the twenty-one days from Rosh Hashanah to Hoshana Rabbah produce the whitening and atonement of sins, so the twenty-one days of calamity from the seventeenth of Tammuz to the Ninth of Av produced the whitening of sins, for troubles and sufferings atone, as they said, “Exile atones.””

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And it is known that the reason for the Sukkah is seeking refuge in Hashem and trusting in Him.

paragraphs.text: Sefat Emet, Deuteronomy, Sukkot 13:5: “The mitzvah of sukkah is the quality of trust in Hashem, blessed be He. As our Sages said, “Leave your permanent dwelling”: do not trust in wealth and possessions, but trust in Hashem. Therefore it is the time of our rejoicing, for there is no joy like the joy of one who truly trusts in Hashem, as explained in Chovot HaLevavot. Therefore prayers and Hoshanot were instituted on this festival: to know that all the blessings of the year depend only on Hashem’s help, and not to trust in gathering all the produce into one’s house. As it is written, “Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him.” The water libation alludes to this: pouring out the heart like water before Him, blessed be He. Surely this is implanted in the hearts of Israel: whenever they need deliverance, they trust in Him. Therefore Hashem shelters them during these days, as it is written, “One who trusts in Hashem—kindness will surround him.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Matot develops the same twenty-two-day and alphabet structure by pointing to the expansion of Oral Torah through the Tannaim and Amoraim after the destruction. This supplies a concrete counterpart to the siman's movement from a powerful vision toward acquired Torah. The comparison concerns the capacity to receive and develop the light within concealment; it does not make the destruction itself the desired final state.

p: [קעב] כְּמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּמָקוֹם "אֶבֶן שְׁתִיָּה" שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הֻשְׁתַּת הָעוֹלָם וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הָעוֹלָם,
Just as in space there exists the Foundation Stone (Even Shetiyah) from which the world was founded and which is the root of the entire universe,
וְכָךְ בְּנֶפֶשׁ יֵשׁ נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת שֶׁכּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל הַדּוֹר וְהוּא פַּרְנַס הַדּוֹר כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְכֵן הַכּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת כַּנּוֹדָע,
and so too in soul there exists one soul that encompasses the entire generation, namely the leader of the generation as is known, and likewise one that encompasses all generations as is known,
וְכֵן בִּזְמַן יֵשׁ זְמַן שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַיָּמִים וְהוּא יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
and so too in time there exists a time that encompasses all days, which is the Sabbath day
[וְכָל אֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ חָלוּק לִשְׁנַיִם: בְּמָקוֹם יֵשׁ מִזְבֵּחַ וְקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, וּבִזְמַן שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב, וּבִנְפָשׁוֹת מֶלֶךְ וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל;
[and each of these dimensions is subdivided into two: in space there are the Altar and the Holy of Holies; in time, Shabbat and the Festivals; and in soul, the king and the High Priest;
קְדֻשַּׁת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא, שֶׁנִּבְדַּל אַהֲרֹן לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ וְגוֹמֵר,
the sanctity of the High Priest is fixed and permanent, for Aaron was set apart to be sanctified, etc.,
וּקְדֻשַּׁת מֶלֶךְ עַל יְדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
while the sanctity of the king is established through Israel, as it is said: "you shall surely set a king over you, etc." (Deuteronomy 17:15),
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נְזוּפִים לֹא נִתְיַיחֵד וְכוּלֵי (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכא:)].
and all the years Israel were under censure, divine communication was not uniquely granted to Moses (Bava Batra 121b)].
וְהַמְתָּקַת כָּל דָּבָר הוּא בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ,
And the sweetening of every entity takes place at its root,
וּבְשַׁבָּת יָכוֹל לְהַמְתִּיק כָּל יְמֵי הַשָּׁבוּעַ לְהִתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹב, כִּי בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נָקֵל לְהַמְתִּיק כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּכָל דָּבָר.
and on Shabbat one is able to sweeten all the days of the week so that they transform into good, for at the root it is easy to sweeten, as is known in all matters.
וְהַמְתָּקַת הַמְּקוֹמוֹת הוּא עַל יְדֵי "וְהִתְפַּלְלוּ אֵלֶיךָ דֶּרֶךְ אַרְצָם" (מְלָכִים א ח, מח) וְדֶרֶךְ בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
And the sweetening of geographic places is achieved through "and they pray unto You toward their land" (I Kings 8:48) and toward the Holy Temple,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה אֵין מִתְדַּבְּקִים בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן מֵאֲוִיר אֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים הַמְטַמֵּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
and through this, the defilement of the air of the land of the nations does not cling to him, Heaven forbid.
וְהַמְתָּקַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ בְּכָל חֶסְרוֹנוֹת שֶׁבָּהּ בַּתּוֹלָדָה – עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּקָהּ לְפַרְנַס הַדּוֹר,
And the sweetening of the soul in all its congenital deficiencies is accomplished through its attachment to the leader of the generation,
וּכְדִשְׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ח.): כָּל זְמַן שֶׁשִּׁמְעִי בֶן גֵּרָא קַיָּים לֹא וְכוּלֵי,
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Berakhot 8a): so long as Shimei ben Gera was alive, Solomon did not marry the daughter of Pharaoh;
כִּי הָאָב וְהָרַב הֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְנֶפֶשׁ הַבֵּן וְהַתַּלְמִיד.
for the father and the teacher are the spiritual root for the soul of the son and the disciple.
וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּנֶפֶשׁ הָאָב: בְּיוֹסֵף, רָאָה דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו, וְזֶה מוֹנֵעַ מֵרַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
And as they stated regarding the soul of the father: with Joseph, he saw the visage of his father's countenance (Sotah 36b), and this restrains one from evil, Heaven forbid.
וְהַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל הוּא הָיָה נוֹשֵׂא עֲווֹנוֹת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And the High Priest would bear the iniquities of all Israel,
וּבְיוֹסִיפוֹן תִּרְאֶה שֶׁקְּרָאוּהוּ הַכֹּל "הַמְכַפֵּר בְּעַד כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל",
and in Josippon you will see that all titled him "the one who atones on behalf of all Israel,"
שֶׁמֵּסִיר כָּל מִינֵי כִּיעוּר וּמְיַפֶּה בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל מִינֵי יוֹפִי, כְּעִנְיַן אַהֲרֹן שׁוֹשְׁבִינָא דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא
removing every form of ugliness and adorning the children of Israel with every kind of beauty, in the manner of Aaron who is the bridesman of the Queen
[וְכֵן הוּא הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים וְשַׁבָּת].
[and likewise is the Holy of Holies and Shabbat].
אֲבָל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנִּקְרָא מֶלֶךְ, הוּא שׁוֹשְׁבִינָא דְּמַלְכָּא,
But Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is called king, is the groomsman of the King,
לְהַרְאוֹת לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹר פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ חַיִּים וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם.
to reveal unto the children of Israel the light of the countenance of the King of Life and eternal Sovereign.
וְזֶהוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַיָּמִים טוֹבִים,
And this is the sanctity of the Festivals;
וּבִפְרָט זֶה בְּהַשָּׂגוֹת אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הַהַמְשָׁכָה לְכָל הַשָּׁנָה הוּא מֵהָרְגָלִים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם: "יֵרָאֶה וְגוֹמֵר אֶת פְּנֵי וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת לד, כג):

and specifically in this—in the perceptions of the light of the Blessed Name—the continuous drawing down for the entire year derives from the pilgrimage festivals, concerning which it is stated: "all your males shall appear before the face of the Lord God, etc." (Exodus 34:23).

paragraphs.text: Yoma 54b:2-4: ““It was called Shetiyah.” It was taught: Because from it the world was founded. Our Mishnah follows the view that the world was created from Zion. For it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says: The world was created from its center, as it is said, “When the dust is poured into a solid mass and the clods cling together.” Rabbi Yehoshua says: The world was created from its sides, as it is said, “For to the snow He says: Become earth; and to the rain shower and the showers of His mighty rain.” Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said: The Holy One, blessed be He, cast a stone into the sea, and from it the world was founded, as it is said, “On what were its foundations sunk, or who cast its cornerstone?” The Sages say: It was created from Zion, as it is said, “A psalm of Asaf: God, God, Hashem,” and it says, “From Zion, the perfection of beauty”—from it the beauty of the world was perfected.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 8:6: “Moses and Aaron embody netzach and hod. Moses corresponds to netzach, on the right side, as Abraham made His divinity known so that He would be called God of the earth; Moses likewise brought the Divine Presence down to earth. He is the King’s attendant. Aaron embodies hod, on the left side, and is the Matron’s attendant: he atones for and adorns the Matron, the Congregation of Israel, so that she finds favor in God’s eyes. The entire sacrificial service and the holiness of Yom Kippur operate through Aaron the priest. Yet the Zohar also says that the priest comes from kindness. This follows “For the priest’s lips preserve knowledge”: knowledge joins right and left, wisdom and understanding, mind and heart.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah spells out the imagery used here: Moshe makes the divine presence known below, while Aharon atones for and adorns the congregation so that it can find favor. This makes the siman’s two functions intelligible rather than treating king and High Priest as interchangeable encompassing figures. Its closing qualification also matters: the priest’s knowledge joins right and left, so the roles remain distinct without becoming disconnected powers.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Metzora 7:23-24: “Come and see: What is the difference between Moshe and Aharon? Which of them is higher? Moshe is higher. Moshe is the attendant of the King; Aharon is the attendant of the Queen. It is like a king who had an exalted queen. What did he do? He gave her an attendant to prepare her and attend to the affairs of the household. Therefore, when this attendant enters before the king, he enters only with the queen. This is what is written: “With this shall Aharon enter.” Moshe is the attendant of the King; therefore he was invited as a guest, and afterward, “Hashem spoke to him.” Aharon is the attendant of the Queen, and all his affairs are to reconcile the King with the Queen, so that the King is reconciled with her. Therefore, because he is her attendant, he established his dwelling with her, to prepare the household and attend continually to its affairs. Accordingly he was appointed after the pattern above and called High Priest. From where do we know this? As it is written, “You are a priest forever, according to My word, Malki-Tzedek.””

sections.en: All Natural Phenomena Fulfill the Will of the Blessed Name

p: [קעג] כָּל הַדְּבָרִים הַטִּבְעִיִּים הֵם עוֹשִׂים רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כֹּל פָּעַל ה' לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ" (מִשְׁלֵי טז, ד) – לְקִילּוּסוֹ,
All natural phenomena fulfill the will of the Blessed Name, as it is written: "Hashem has made everything for His own purpose" (Proverbs 16:4)—meaning for His praise;
וְאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין (ז.): בְּגִינַאי נַהֲרָא, אֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנִי – מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּטִבְעוֹ כָּךְ
and they stated in Chullin 7a regarding the river Ginai: "I am going to perform the will of my Maker," which is simply its natural flowing
[וּלְפִיכָךְ גַּם הָאָדָם, כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשִׂים הַטִּבְעִיִּים שֶׁהוּא מֻכְרָח בָּהֶם מִצַּד טִבְעוֹ, נִקְרָא הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנוֹ וְיֵשׁ מִצְוָה בַּדָּבָר;

[and therefore a human being as well, when engaging in natural actions to which he is compelled by his physical nature, is considered going to perform the will of his Maker, and a mitzvah resides in the matter;
וּבִכְלָל גַּם כֵּן אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה וְזִוּוּג, שֶׁהוּא בְּטֶבַע כִּבְכָל בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים הַטִּבְעִיִּים שֶׁאֵינָם בְּחִירִיִּים;
and this includes eating, drinking, and marital intimacy, which are natural as in all animals that do not possess free choice;
וּבִלְבַד מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּהֶכְרֵחַ, כְּגוֹן אֲכִילָה לְרַעֲבוֹן,
provided it is done out of necessity, such as eating to satisfy hunger,
וְכֵן בְּזִוּוּג עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם כְּשֶׁמּוֹצֵא וְכוּלֵי, דְּהַטֶּבַע תּוֹבְעוֹ לְכָךְ,
and so too in intimacy, in line with what Maimonides wrote: when he senses, etc., that nature demands it of him,
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ בִּיהוּדָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פה) רֶמֶז לַמַּלְאָךְ הַמְמוּנֶּה וְכוּלֵי, וְעַיֵּין בְּמוֹרֶה נְבוּכִים (פֶּרֶק ו מֵחֵלֶק ב);

and similar to this with Judah, concerning whom our Sages expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 85:8) that it was a hint to the angel appointed over desire, etc., and see Guide for the Perplexed (Part II, chapter 6);
וְלִהְיוֹת מְכַוֵּין לְכָךְ רַק בִּשְׁבִיל רְצוֹן קוֹנוֹ שֶׁבְּרָאוֹ כֵּן,
and intending it solely for the sake of the will of his Maker Who created him thus,
זֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (כ:): דּוֹמֶה לְמִי שֶׁכְּפָאוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְזֶהוּ רְצוֹן קוֹנוֹ].
which is what they stated in Nedarim 20b: comparable to one compelled by a demon, and that is the will of his Maker].
וּבַזֹּהַר פִּינְחָס (רכב עַמּוּד ב) וּבְפֶרֶק שִׁירָה, דִּצְפַרְדֵּעַ אָמְרָה לְדָוִד שֶׁהִיא מְקַלֶּסֶת יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And in Zohar Pinchas (222b) and in Perek Shirah, the frog said to David that it sings praises day and night to the Blessed Name,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמַה שֶּׁצּוֹוַחַת בְּקוֹלָהּ, כֵּיוָן דְּהַכֹּל לְמַעֲנֵהוּ – לְקִילּוּסוֹ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים קמח), הֲרֵי פְּעֻלָּתָהּ תְּמִידִית לְקִילּוּס לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
meaning that its continuous croaking, since everything is for His purpose—for His praise (Shocher Tov, Psalm 148)—is an uninterrupted act of praising the Blessed Name.
וְצָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לִלְמוֹד מֵהֶם, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (נג:): דַּחֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה לָמְדוּ קַל וָחֹמֶר מִצְּפַרְדְּעִים;
And a person must learn from them, as they taught in Pesachim 53b: that Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah derived an a fortiori argument from the frogs;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם אֵינָם בַּעֲלֵי בְחִירָה, רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם לְמֵידִין שֶׁעֲשִׂיַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא גַּם בִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ וּבִטּוּל הַדָּבָר הַהוּא,
and even though animals lack free will, we nonetheless learn that fulfilling the will of the Blessed Name includes self-sacrifice (mesirut nefesh) and the nullification of that entity,
שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּךְ רָאִינוּ יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּצְפַרְדְּעֵי מִצְרַיִם: דִּכְשֶׁיֵּשׁ קִדּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם בַּדָּבָר, הֵם פּוֹעֲלִים פְּעֻלָּתָם בִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ.
for thus we saw the Blessed Name established in the frogs of Egypt: that when sanctification of the Name is at stake, they carry out their action through self-sacrifice.

הֲגַם דִּבְטֶבַע כָּל הַבְּרוּאִים לִבְרוֹחַ מִדָּבָר הַמַּזִּיקָם, וּמִזֶּה לְמֵידִין בִּבְחִירָה גַּם כֵּן לִשְׁמוֹר הַגּוּף וְלִשְׁבּוֹת מִפְּעֻלָּתוֹ גַּם בְּמִצְוֹת ה', דּוּגְמַת הֵם בִּפְעֻלָּתָם הַטִּבְעִית;

Although it is the instinct of all creatures to flee from what harms them, and from this we learn in free choice to preserve the body and cease activity even in Hashem's commandments, modeling their natural preservation;
אֲבָל בִּפְעֻלָּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ קִדּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם צָרִיךְ לִמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ כְּמוֹהֶם.
yet in an act that involves the sanctification of the Name, one must practice self-sacrifice like them.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מַלְּפֵנוּ מִבַּהֲמוֹת אָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר" (אִיּוֹב לה, יא), שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ בִּפְעֻלָּתֵנוּ הַבְּחִירִית לְמֵידִין מֵהֶם:
As it is written: "Who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, etc." (Job 35:11), meaning that we, in our choice-driven actions, learn from them.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Ha'azinu and Shabbat Shuvah 11: ““When the Most High apportioned nations… He set the boundaries of peoples according to the number of Israel, for Hashem's portion is His people.” Hashem grants great powers to the nations too, and precious powers are found in all kinds of creatures. The Gemara interprets “He teaches us from the beasts of the earth and makes us wise from the birds”: had Torah not been given, we would learn modesty from the cat, avoidance of theft from the ant, fidelity from the dove and proper conduct from the rooster. Great powers can likewise sometimes be found among the nations exceeding Israel's, for Israel is described as “the fewest of all peoples” (Deuteronomy 7:7); all the more are great powers found among the heavenly hosts. Yet the principal point is “Hashem's portion is His people; Yaakov is the rope of His inheritance”: the whole is directed toward Israel.”

paragraphs.text: Natural necessity and surplus desire
The same river comparison distinguishes the needs built into human nature from further desires.

rich.text: The same river comparison distinguishes the needs built into human nature from further desires.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:64: “After the giving of Torah they knew that Hashem's will includes what a person needs. As Chullin 7a says of the river Ginai, ‘I am going to fulfill my Creator's will’: the nature implanted in it is its Creator's will, like a mitzvah. Likewise, what a person naturally needs for eating and drinking is the Creator's will and a mitzvah. They knew this through Torah's gift, called a complete gift: this gift belongs to them from their hidden root. Such is Torah's way—bread with salt and measured water, only what is necessary. Through this their hidden root became known to them. They still remained uncertain concerning the expansion and surplus of desires. This applies only to the fruits of the land, through mitzvot: when a person performs a mitzvah with bread or food, Heaven's name rests upon that expansion itself, in the manner of the land of Israel. As I wrote elsewhere, this is the secret of the blessing over enjoyment that the Sages instituted before every enjoyment; this is not the place to explain it. Through this their hidden root became known to them in this too.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Lech Lecha describes a heart that learns service from what the eyes see and the ears hear, and cites the same teaching about learning from animals. This explains how the present siman moves from a creature’s natural action to a person’s chosen avodah. The creature is a lesson to be understood, not a replacement for judgment. This siman accordingly distinguishes ordinary preservation of the body from the particular circumstances of sanctifying Hashem’s Name.

sections.en: Through Corruption and Blemishing of the Covenant

p: [קעד] עַל יְדֵי קִלְקוּל וּפְגַם הַבְּרִית נֶעְלָם אוֹר תּוֹרָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אוֹר זָרֻעַ לַצַּדִּיק" (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא) דַּיְיקָא, וּכְתִיב: "כִּי נֵר מִצְוָה וְתוֹרָה אוֹר" (מִשְׁלֵי ו, כג).

Through corruption and blemishing of the Covenant, the light of Torah is concealed, Heaven forbid, as it is written: "Light is sown for the righteous (tzadik)" (Psalms 97:11) specifically, and it is written: "For the commandment is a lamp, and the Torah is light" (Proverbs 6:23).
וְכֵן מַכַּת חֹשֶׁךְ לְמִצְרַיִם הִיא מַכָּה הַתְּשִׁיעִית, כַּנּוֹדָע דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם מִסְפַּר עֶשֶׂר רוֹמֵז לְקוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה, וְהַתְּשִׁיעִית נֶגֶד אוֹת בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ.

And so the plague of darkness upon Egypt was the ninth plague, as is known that everywhere the number ten alludes to a complete stature, and the ninth corresponds to the sign of the holy Covenant (Yesod).
שֶׁבְּמִצְרַיִם – זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה: הֵם שְׁטוּפֵי זִמָּה, הָיָה לָהֶם חֹשֶׁךְ, וּלְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָם, דְּ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים".

For in Egypt, one stood facing the other: they were steeped in licentiousness, so they had darkness, while all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings, for "your people are all righteous."
וְגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה לְתַקֵּן קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל מַה שֶּׁנִּתְגַּלְגֵּל הַגָּלוּת עַל יְדֵי מְכִירַת יוֹסֵף;
And the Egyptian exile came to rectify the blemish of the Covenant, as I wrote elsewhere concerning why the exile was brought about through the selling of Joseph;
וּלְכָךְ אַחַר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁתִּיקְּנוּ הַבְּרִית בְּקֹשִׁי הַשִּׁעְבּוּד, זָכוּ לְאוֹר תּוֹרָה.
and therefore, after the Exodus from Egypt, having rectified the Covenant through the harshness of servitude, they merited the light of the Torah.
וּלְכָךְ פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שׁוֹבָבִי"ם, מִתְּחִלַּת גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם עַד אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, מְיוּחָד לְתִיקּוּן הַבְּרִית.
And therefore the Torah portions of Shovavim, from the inception of the Egyptian exile until after the Giving of the Torah, are designated for the rectification of the Covenant.
וְהוּא בְּחֹדֶשׁ שְׁבָט שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּאוֹת הַצַּדִּי"ק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה
And this falls in the month of Shevat, which was created through the letter Tzadik, as written in Sefer Yetzirah
[וְטֵי"ת מִתְחַלֵּף בְּצַדִּי"ק בַּאֲרַמִּי לָרוֹב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהַגָּהוֹת הֶעָרוּךְ, וְהוּא כְּטַעַם: אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב, דְּהַפּוֹגֵם נִקְרָא רַע כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר].

[and the letter Tet interchanges frequently with Tzadik in Aramaic, as written in the glosses of the Arukh, reflecting: "Say of the righteous (tzadik) that it shall be good (tov)," for one who blemishes is called evil, as brought in the Zohar].
וְאָמְרִינַן בְּשַׁבָּת (עז:): דְּכָךְ הוּא סֵדֶר בְּרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם – בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא;
And we say in Shabbat 77b: such is the order of the creation of the world—first darkness, and then light;
בְּוַדַּאי מֵאַחַר שֶׁבִּדְבָרִים הַטִּבְעִיִּים יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּךְ, וַדַּאי כָּךְ הוּא עִיקַּר הָרָצוֹן,
surely, since the Blessed Name established it so in natural things, this is certainly the primary divine will,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: מְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין וְכוּלֵי.
and as stated: the place where penitents stand, etc. (Berakhot 34b).
הֲגַם דְּחָלִילָה לוֹמַר "אֶחֱטָא וְאָשׁוּב" וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן בִּבְחִירָתוֹ, מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין מַסְפִּיקִין;
Although, Heaven forbid that one say "I will sin and repent" and do so by free choice, because he is not granted the opportunity;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מֵעַצְמוֹ נַעֲשָׂה כֵּן, דְּ"אֵין אָדָם צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כ),
nonetheless it transpires on its own, for "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not" (Ecclesiastes 7:20);
אֲפִילּוּ יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה לו:) דְּיָצְאוּ י' טִפִּין עַל פָּסוּק "וַיָּפֹזּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
even Joseph the Righteous, our Sages said (Sotah 36b) that ten drops emerged from him, based on "and the arms of his hands were made supple" (Genesis 49:24),
וַאֲפִילּוּ יִשַׁי אֲבִי דָוִד שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ, אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ) "בֶּעָווֹן מָלֵא וְכוּלֵי".
and even Jesse the father of David, who died solely through the counsel of the Serpent, our Sages expounded (Midrash Rabbah, Tazria) that he was conceived in full iniquity.
וְכֵן יְסוֹד בִּנְיַן בֵּית דָּוִד וּמָשִׁיחַ בְּפֶרֶץ, הָיָה מִקּוֹדֶם עֵר וְאוֹנָן – חֲשׁוֹכָא.
And likewise, the foundation of the House of David and the Messiah through Perez was preceded by Er and Onan—darkness.
וְכָךְ הוּא הַסֵּדֶר, וְ"הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל" (יְשַׁעְיָה ט, א), מֻפְלָג מִמִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ הוֹלֵךְ בַּחֹשֶׁךְ.
And such is the order: "The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light" (Isaiah 9:1), far more wondrous than one who does not walk in darkness.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם "חֹשֶׁךְ" דִּכְתִיב הַיְינוּ חַשְׁכוּת מֵאוֹר תּוֹרָה, וְלֹא בְּצָרוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבַד.
And everywhere "darkness" is written, it refers to darkness from the light of Torah, and not worldly troubles alone.
וְכֵן "אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל" – הוּא עַל יְדֵי חֹשֶׁךְ זֶה,
And so, "a person does not master words of Torah unless he stumbles" (Gittin 43a) occurs through this darkness,
שֶׁהוּא עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ דְּעֵשָׂו הָרָשָׁע שֶׁפָּגַע בְּכַף יֶרֶךְ יַעֲקֹב כַּנּוֹדָע.
which is the counsel of the Serpent of Esau the wicked, who struck the hollow of Jacob's thigh, as is known.
וְתֵיכֶף כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעַ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְכָךְ וְשָׁב, וְרָפָא, יָקוּם לָאוֹר,
And immediately when one reaches that point, Heaven forbid, and repents, and is healed, he arises unto light,
כְּהַהוּא דִּמְטָא זַרְזִיפָא דְּמַיָּא אַרֵישֵׁיהּ, אֲמַר וְכוּלֵי: "מֵאַשְׁפֹּת יָרִים אֶבְיוֹן" (יוֹמָא פז.):
like that individual upon whose head a flow of water fell, and he proclaimed: "He raises the needy out of the dunghill" (Psalms 113:7; Yoma 87a).

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar Ruach HaKodesh 43:2: “The matter of the well-known Shovavim: that is, there is an ancient custom throughout Israel to fast forty consecutive days, from the first day of the portion Shemot until the portion Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. They gave these days the sign “Return, wayward children”—the initials of Shemot, Vaera, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro, and Mishpatim. The main fasting during these forty days was instituted for the transgression of a seminal emission, and these days are more suited to fasting for this than all other days of the year. The reason becomes clear from what we explained concerning the exile in Egypt with mortar and bricks. There it was explained that those enslaved in the Egyptian exile were the sparks of souls that emerged from Adam during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through drops of seminal emission. All these were rectified in that Egyptian exile. Therefore, during the reading of these portions there is a special quality for accepting the repentance of one who fasts during them for this transgression. rich.text: : “The matter of the well-known Shovavim: that is, there is an ancient custom throughout Israel to fast forty consecutive days, from the first day of the portion Shemot until the portion Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. They gave these days the sign “Return, wayward children”—the initials of Shemot, Vaera, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro, and Mishpatim. The main fasting during these forty days was instituted for the transgression of a seminal emission, and these days are more suited to fasting for this than all other days of the year. The reason becomes clear from what we explained concerning the exile in Egypt with mortar and bricks. There it was explained that those enslaved in the Egyptian exile were the sparks of souls that emerged from Adam during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through drops of seminal emission. All these were rectified in that Egyptian exile. Therefore, during the reading of these portions there is a special quality for accepting the repentance of one who fasts during them for this transgression. They begin with Shemot because that portion begins the enslavement, and end with Mishpatim for the reason explained there concerning the proximity of “When you acquire a Hebrew slave” to the giving of the Torah: then those sparks completed their rectification in the matter of “When you acquire a Hebrew slave”; see there.”

paragraphs.text: Chanukah describes the recovered first light through Torah, righteousness, and purity, giving content to this siman’s promise of renewed illumination.

rich.text: Chanukah describes the recovered first light through Torah, righteousness, and purity, giving content to this siman’s promise of renewed illumination.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 2:10: “This is through the first light, which was hidden for the righteous, the light called good. It is attained through Torah’s light, as Israel merit to be ‘those occupied with Your Torah,’ for every Israelite has some occupation in Torah; and to be righteous, for ‘the righteous are destined for light,’ as it says, ‘Light is sown for the righteous’; and to be pure, for ‘The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever,’ and, ‘The fear of the Lord is wisdom.’ Of someone occupied in Torah without fear of Heaven, the Sages said, ‘Why is there a price in the fool’s hand …?’—those who occupy themselves with Torah but lack fear of Heaven. This is the root of the dedication established for the first light that Israel merit, as God illuminates for Israel: ‘The Lord is God, and He illuminated for us.’ For this we make a dedication.”

rich.text: : “This is through the first light, which was hidden for the righteous, the light called good. It is attained through Torah’s light, as Israel merit to be ‘those occupied with Your Torah,’ for every Israelite has some occupation in Torah; and to be righteous, for ‘the righteous are destined for light,’ as it says, ‘Light is sown for the righteous’; and to be pure, for ‘The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever,’ and, ‘The fear of the Lord is wisdom.’ Of someone occupied in Torah without fear of Heaven, the Sages said, ‘Why is there a price in the fool’s hand …?’—those who occupy themselves with Torah but lack fear of Heaven. This is the root of the dedication established for the first light that Israel merit, as God illuminates for Israel: ‘The Lord is God, and He illuminated for us.’ For this we make a dedication.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The present siman specifies that its darkness is a loss of Torah’s light, and that return leads back to that light. Chanukah develops the positive side: the concealed first light is received through Torah joined to fear of Heaven. This keeps the promised renewal connected to an actual form of service rather than to a change of feeling alone. The present siman’s rejection of choosing sin in order to repent remains essential to its account of darkness preceding light.

sections.en: One Must Take Heed Not to Cause Pain to Any Creature

p: [קעה] צָרִיךְ לִיזָּהֵר מִלִּגְרוֹם צַעַר לְשׁוּם בְּרִיָּה, אֲפִילּוּ לְצוֹרֶךְ מִצְוָה,
One must take heed not to cause pain to any creature, even for the purpose of a mitzvah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ח:) עַל "כָּל לֹחֲצָיו" – אֲפִילּוּ גַּבָּאֵי צְדָקָה.
as stated in Bava Batra 8b on "all that oppress them" (Jeremiah 30:20)—even charity collectors.
וַאֲדֹנִירָם עַל הַמַּס דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לַחְצוֹב אֲבָנִים לְבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, דְּאֵין לְךָ מִצְוָה גְּדוֹלָה מִזּוֹ,
And Adoniram who was over the levy for King Solomon, peace be upon him, to hew stones for the building of the Temple—than which there is no greater mitzvah—
נֶעֱנַשׁ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה: רָגְמוּ בוֹ אֶבֶן.
was punished measure for measure: they stoned him with stones (I Kings 12:18).
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמַס נִקְרָא מַה שֶּׁיּוֹתֵר לְפִי הַכֹּחַ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אָבִיךָ הִכְבִּיד וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם, ד),
That is, because a "levy" (mas) denotes what exceeds normal strength, as written: "Your father made our yoke grievous, etc." (ibid. 12:4),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (יא.) בַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ: הַכֹּל נַעֲשׂוּ רָשִׁים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיָּשֶׂם מַס";
and as stated in Megillah 11a concerning Ahasuerus: all became poor, as it is said: "and he laid a tribute";
וְהוּא מִקְרָא דְּ"שָׂרֵי מִסִּים לְמַעַן עַנֹּתוֹ" (שְׁמוֹת א, יא), דְּהוֹרָאַת מַס הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּהַכְבָּדָה לְעַנּוֹת נֶפֶשׁ.
and this is based on the verse "taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens" (Exodus 1:11), for the meaning of a levy is when it burdens so as to afflict the soul.
וְעַל זֶה נֶעֱנָשִׁים גַּם כְּשֶׁהוּא לְמִצְוָה.
And for this one is punished even when it is for the sake of a mitzvah.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כד): אֲפִילּוּ אֶבֶן שֶׁנִּסְקַל וְעֵץ שֶׁנִּצְלַב עָתִיד לִיתֵּן הַדִּין.
And our Sages stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 24): even the stone with which one was stoned and the tree upon which one was hanged are destined to give reckoning.
וְהַיְינוּ אֲפִילּוּ בִּמְחוּיָּבֵי מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין,
That is, even regarding those liable to capital execution by a court;
וּלְכָךְ הָיוּ הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין מִתְעַנִּין אוֹתוֹ יוֹם (סַנְהֶדְרִין סג.) לְכַפֵּר עַל נַפְשׁוֹתָם,
and therefore the Sanhedrin would fast on that day (Sanhedrin 63a) to atone for their souls,
וְסַנְהֶדְרִין הַהוֹרֶגֶת וְכוּלֵי נִקְרֵאת חָבְלָנִית (מַכּוֹת ז.),
and a Sanhedrin that executes once in seven years is called destructive (Makkot 7a),
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בְּדִין נֶעֱנָשׁ, דְּגַם "כָּל שֶׁחֲבֵירוֹ נֶעֱנָשׁ עַל יָדוֹ וְכוּלֵי" (שַׁבָּת קמט:);
even though the person was punished by law, for "whoever has his fellow punished on his account, etc." (Shabbat 149b);
וְהַהוֹרֵג שׁוֹגֵג חַיָּיב גָּלוּת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַלָּה מְחוּיָּב מִיתָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַכּוֹת י:) דִּמְגַלְגְּלִין וְכוּלֵי;
and an accidental killer is liable to exile, even though the victim was deserving of death, as our Sages stated (Makkot 10b) that liability is brought about, etc.;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה וּ"בִעַרְתָּ הָרָע", מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי גּוֹרֵם צַעַר לְמַעְלָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
and even though it is a mitzvah to "purge the evil from your midst" (Deuteronomy 17:7), it nonetheless causes sorrow Above, Heaven forbid,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה י:) שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שָׂמֵחַ בְּמַפַּלְתָּן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים,
as stated in Megillah 10b that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rejoice over the downfall of the wicked,
וְאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין מו.): שְׁכִינָה מָה אוֹמֶרֶת וְכוּלֵי.
and they said (Sanhedrin 46a): What does the Shechinah say? "My head is heavy, My arm is heavy."
וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בְּצַעֲרָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים, אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁהוּא כְּפִיָּה לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
And all the more so regarding the distress of the righteous, even when it is coercion for the sake of a mitzvah
[אַמְנָם מִדַּת מַלְכוּת הוּא דַּיְיקָא לְהֵיפֶךְ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: אַדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם – יָדֶיךָ חַדּוֹת וַחֲרוּצוֹת לִרְדּוֹת בָּהֶן עוֹלָמִי.
[however, the attribute of monarchy is specifically the reverse, as our Sages expounded concerning King David: your hands are sharp and decisive to rule My world with them.
וְנֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "אַדְמוֹנִי" כִּבְעֵשָׂו, רַק "עִם יְפֵה עֵינַיִם" – מִדַּעַת סַנְהֶדְרִין (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סג), לְכָךְ זָכָה לְמַלְכוּת.
And of him it was said "ruddy" as of Esau, only "with beautiful eyes"—meaning with the consent of the Sanhedrin (Bereishit Rabbah 63:8), which is why he merited kingship.
וְשָׁאוּל נִסְתַּלֵּק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה רַחְמָן עַל הָאַכְזָרִים כַּנּוֹדָע,
And Saul was removed because he showed mercy to the cruel, as is known,
דְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּת הִיא מִדַּת הַדִּין הַקָּשָׁה,
for the attribute of monarchy is the severe attribute of strict judgment,
וְנֶאֱמַר: "בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ", כִּי אוֹרַיְיתָא נָפְקָא מִגְּבוּרָה כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, פ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
and it is stated: "By me kings reign" (Proverbs 8:15), because Torah issues from Gevurah, as brought in the Zohar (Part III, 80b),
וְעַל יָדוֹ זָכָה מֹשֶׁה לְמַלְכוּת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה עָנָו מִכָּל הָאָדָם, אָמַר לוֹ קֹרַח: "מַדּוּעַ תִּתְנַשְּׂאוּ".
and through this Moses merited kingship; even though he was the humblest of all men, Korah said to him: "Why do you lift yourselves up?" (Numbers 16:3).
כִּי כָּל הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת מִצַּד דִּבְרֵי מֹשֶׁה מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה,
For all elevation stemmed from the words of Moses from the mouth of the Almighty (Gevurah),
וּבְקֹרַח עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן פָּגְעָה מִדַּת הַדִּין וְנִתְנַשֵּׂא יוֹתֵר.
and in Korah himself the attribute of judgment struck, and he became arrogant beyond measure.
וְכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְנַשֵּׂא כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה מִדַּת הַדִּין בָּרְשָׁעִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה]:
And so the Blessed Name is exalted when He executes the attribute of judgment upon the wicked, as our Sages stated].

paragraphs.text: Context: Rambam makes explicit that a donor’s shame-driven willingness does not permit collectors to press him beyond his means. This adds a concrete qualification to the existing Gemara and directly illustrates Rav Tzadok’s concern about causing pain in pursuit of a mitzvah.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 6:66: “For even the tree on which a person was hanged and the stone with which he was stoned will eventually be called to account, as they said in Tanna Devei Eliyahu. Therefore the Sanhedrin fasted that day to atone for themselves and to clarify that their intention was for the sake of Heaven. The clarification came through the condemned person’s confession, for one mitzvah leads to another, and every holy matter and deed done for the sake of Heaven gives birth to holiness in the world. If an opening of repentance arose within him so that he confessed, their action was truly for life—eternal life—and not for death. Through this it became clear that their action was solely for the sake of Heaven, without any hatred or worldly motive.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach interprets the same verse, “Through Me kings reign,” as self-rule preceding rule of others. The comparison describes a prerequisite of authority; self-confidence alone does not confer that office or its powers.

sections.en: When They Build or Establish a New Synagogue or House of Study in Any…

p: [קעו] כְּשֶׁבּוֹנִים אוֹ מְיַסְּדִים בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת אוֹ בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ חָדָשׁ בְּאֵיזֶה מָקוֹם, נַעֲשֶׂה מִקּוֹדֶם שָׁם מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם.
When they build or establish a new synagogue or house of study in any location, the blotting out of Amalek occurs beforehand in that place.
דְּתֵיכֶף אַחַר מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק בָּא קְדוּשַׁת הַמָּקוֹם,
For immediately after the blotting out of Amalek comes the sanctity of the place,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ:): ג' מִצְווֹת נִצְטַוּוּ בִּכְנִיסָתָן וְכוּלֵי: מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
as our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 20b): three commandments were commanded to them upon entering the Land: blotting out Amalek, and afterward building the Temple.
לָכֵן קָבְעוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֶּרֶק בְּנֵי הָעִיר מִקְּדוּשַׁת בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת וּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ בְּמַסֶּכֶת מְגִילָּה,
Therefore our Sages established the chapter Benei Ha'ir concerning the sanctity of the synagogue and study hall in Tractate Megillah,
כִּי תֵּיכֶף לְ"כָל קַרְנֵי רְשָׁעִים אֲגַדֵּעַ" – "תְּרוֹמַמְנָה קַרְנוֹת צַדִּיק" (תְּהִלִּים עה, יא).
for immediately following "All the horns of the wicked will I cut off" comes "the horns of the righteous shall be exalted" (Psalms 75:11).
וַחֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): וְהֵיכָן מִתְרוֹמֶמֶת קַרְנָם? בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם;
And our Sages stated (Megillah 17b): And where are their horns exalted? In Jerusalem;
הַיְינוּ דְּהַרָמַת קֶרֶן יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא מְצוּמְצֶמֶת בְּמָקוֹם מְקוּדָּשׁ לְבַד בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלֹא בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַגּוֹרֵם בִּיטּוּל.
meaning that the uplifting of the horn of Israel is concentrated within a sanctified place alone in the Land of Israel, and not in outward dispersion that causes nullification.
וּבָתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת הֵם קְדוּשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּמְגִילָּה (כט.): דַּעֲתִידִים שֶׁיִּקָּבְעוּ בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
And synagogues and study halls partake of the sanctity of the Land of Israel, as our Sages stated in Megillah 29a: they are destined to be established in the Land of Israel.
וְהַג' מִצְווֹת הֵם תְּכוּפוֹת יַחַד.
And the three commandments are closely intertwined.

וְגַם בְּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת וּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ חָדָשׁ, שֶׁהוּא נִקְרָא "מִקְדָּשׁ מְעַט" כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם), נִתְנַשֵּׂא גַּם כֵּן נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת נְשִׂיאוּת מְעַט עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַמְנָאַת מֶלֶךְ.

And also in the building of a new synagogue and study hall, which is called a "miniature sanctuary" (mikdash me'at, ibid.), a single soul is likewise elevated with a miniature leadership akin to appointing a king.
רַק בִּכְנִיסָה לָאָרֶץ הָיָה זֶה קוֹדֶם מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק.
Only that upon entering the Land, this appointment occurred prior to the blotting out of Amalek.
וּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא יִהְיֶה הַסֵּדֶר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים (ה.) לִג' רִאשׁוֹן, וְחָשֵׁיב שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ בַּסּוֹף,
And in the future to come, the order will be as stated in Pesachim 5a regarding the three things termed "first," enumerating the name of the Messiah at the end,
וְהוּא נֶגֶד רִאשׁוֹן דְּפֶסַח, דִּבְנִיסָן עֲתִידִין לִגָּאֵל.
which corresponds to the "first" of Passover, for in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed.
וְלוּלָב וְסֻכָּה הֵם יַחַד, כִּי לְעוֹלָם תְּכוּפִים יַחַד:
And the lulav and sukkah go together, for they are forever closely linked:
כְּרִיתַת זֶרַע עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד לוּלָב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ל) דְּמוֹרֶה עַל נִצּוּחַ,
the cutting off of the seed of Amalek corresponds to the lulav, as stated in Vayikra Rabbah (30:2) that it signifies victory;
וּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ דְּנִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן "סֻכַּת שָׁלֵם" (תְּהִלִּים עו, ג).
and the building of the Temple, which is likewise called "His tabernacle in Salem" (Psalms 76:3).
וּלְעוֹלָם מְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק קוֹדֶמֶת,
And the blotting out of Amalek always precedes,
וּלְכָךְ קְדוּשַׁת הַמָּקוֹם לֹא פָּסְקָה, דִּקְדֻשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִדְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְקִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵן שׁוֹמְמִין.
and therefore the sanctity of the place never ceased, for the first sanctification sanctified for its time and sanctified for all future time, even while desolate.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד פָּסְקָה לְפִי שָׁעָה, לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה אָז קוֹדֶמֶת לִמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק.
In contrast, the monarchy of the House of David ceased temporarily, because it originally preceded the total eradication of Amalek.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לֶעָתִיד, שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ אֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק, לְפִי שֶׁבָּא אַחַר כָּךְ.
Whereas in the future, the name of the Messiah will have no interruption, because it arrives afterward.

וְכֵן בְּהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת מְעַט דְּמִקְדָּשׁ מְעַט שֶׁבַּגּוֹלָה: כְּשֶׁהַמְּחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק, הַיְינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע, וְגַם קְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם קוֹדְמִים לְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת קְדוּשַׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ – אָז אֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק:

And so it is regarding the miniature elevation of a miniature sanctuary in the Diaspora: when the blotting out of Amalek—namely the root of evil—and the sanctity of the place precede the elevation of the soul's sanctity, then it suffers no interruption.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 1:8: “Shaul was the first king, and had he fulfilled the eradication of Amalek, the final repair would have occurred then. Concerning the Rosh Chodesh goat, the Zohar says that one goat draws the opposing power to its own place so that it separates from the moon; this is the eradication of Amalek commanded to Shaul. Although the principal kingship of David comes from Yehudah, Shaul was commanded concerning Amalek, who falls only through Rachel's descendants, as Bereshit Rabbah teaches. Amalek is the beginning of the impure shell, and the supernal crown is the crown of kingship; a king who embodies that quality can subdue it. “Mashiach” has the numerical value of “nachash,” as the holy books explain, and he will repair everything. Had Shaul fulfilled the command to erase Amalek's memory, he would have been Mashiach ben Yosef. As Rema MiPano wrote concerning Yonatan's words, “I shall be second to you,” he intended to be Mashiach ben Yosef; so too Shaul would have been Mashiach ben Yosef had he fulfilled Amalek's eradication. Shaul too is called “Hashem's anointed.””

sections.en: In Every Matter There Is PaRDeS (Four Levels of Understanding: Peshat, Remez, Derush, Sod)

p: [קעז] בְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ פַּרְדֵּ"ס.
In every matter there is PaRDeS (four levels of understanding: Peshat, Remez, Derush, Sod).
פְּשָׁט הוּא עֲשִׂיַּת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת בַּפּוֹעַל מַמָּשׁ.
Peshat (literal) is the performance of all Torah and mitzvot in tangible, physical action.
וְרֶמֶז הוּא הָרְמִיזוֹת שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁנַּעֲשִׂים מֵאוֹתָם הַפְּעֻלּוֹת,
And Remez (allusion) is the inner stirrings of the heart generated by those actions,
כְּעִנְיַן "חֵרֵשׁ רוֹמֵז וְנִרְמָז" (גִּטִּין נט.), שֶׁהָרֶמֶז הוּא רוֹמֵז עַל הַמְּכֻוָּון שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהוֹצִיאוֹ לַפּוֹעַל.
in the manner of "a deaf-mute communicates by hints and signs" (Gittin 59a), where a hint points to the intention within his heart which he cannot fully articulate in outward speech.
וְכֵן כָּל הָעֲבוֹדוֹת הֵם רְמִיזוֹת לְמַה שֶּׁבַּלֵּב,
And likewise, all outer forms of divine service are allusions to that which is in the heart:
דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל מִצְוַת צְדָקָה בַּפּוֹעַל, וּרְמִיזָתָהּ בַּלֵּב – לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק בְּמִדַּת רַחֲמָנוּת שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, לְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת וּלְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְזוּלָתוֹ.

for example, the mitzvah of charity in action, while its internal allusion in the heart is to cleave unto the attribute of mercy of the Blessed Name, having compassion upon creatures and bestowing unto others.
וּדְרוּשׁ הוּא הַכַּוָּנָה מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, לָדַעַת אֵיזֶה לִמּוּד מְחוּדָּשׁ דְּחָכְמָה וִידִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹלָד מֵעוֹבָדָא זוֹ בְּמוֹחוֹ.

And Derush (homiletical/intellectual inquiry) is the contemplation stemming from wisdom in the brain, to know what novel concept of wisdom and knowledge of the Blessed Name is born from this deed within one's intellect.
וְאַחַר שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ – כְּלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה גּוֹמְרִים, וְלֵב חוֹמֵד, וְעַיִן רוֹאֶה חָכְמַת הַדָּבָר – אָז זוֹכֶה לְסוֹד,
And after one attains these three—the instruments of action completing the deed, the heart desiring, and the eye seeing the wisdom of the matter—he then merits Sod (mystery),
שֶׁהוּא עִנְיַן מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין מ.): לְאָדָם טוֹב מַטְעִימִין לוֹ מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
which is the essence of what is stated (Kiddushin 40a): to a good person they grant a taste of the fruit of his deeds in this world.
הַטַּעַם עַל דֶּרֶךְ "טַעֲמוּ וּרְאוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים לד, ט) נִקְרָא סוֹד,
This "taste," in the spirit of "Taste and see that Hashem is good" (Psalms 34:9), is termed Sod,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַסְבִּיר לַחֲבֵירוֹ טַעַם שֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ בְּחִכּוֹ,
for it is impossible to explain to one's fellow a taste that one feels upon his palate,
כְּעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן פֶּרֶק לז): שְׁנַיִם אוֹכְלִין מִקְּעָרָה אַחַת, כָּל אֶחָד טוֹעֵם לְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו.
in the manner of what they said (Avot DeRabbi Natan 37): two people eat from one bowl, yet each tastes according to his deeds.
כִּי הַטַּעַם אֵין שָׁוֶה בְּכָל אֶחָד, וְזֶה נִקְרָא סוֹד כַּיָּדוּעַ, שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיד כְּלָל.
For the taste is not identical in each person, and this is termed Sod as is known, which is that which cannot be communicated at all.

כִּי מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיד, הֲרֵי אַחַר שֶׁהִגִּיד שׁוּב נוֹדַע גַּם לְהָאַחֵר, וְאֵיךְ הוּא סוֹד וָסֵתֶר, וְשֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "סוֹד ה' לִירֵאָיו" (תְּהִלִּים כה, יד) אוֹ "לִישָׁרִים סוֹדוֹ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, לב)?

For that which can be expressed, once spoken is known to the other as well, so how could it be a hidden secret, concerning which it is said: "The secret of Hashem is to them that fear Him" (Psalms 25:14) or "His secret is with the upright" (Proverbs 3:32)?
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר שֶׁגָּלוּי לְמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְבַד, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹתוֹ כְּלָל.
So perforce it is something revealed solely to the one who merits it, and it is impossible to transmit it outwardly at all.
וְזֶהוּ הַטְּעִימָה שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד טוֹעֵם לְפִי חֶלְקוֹ.
And this is the experiential tasting that each individual tastes according to his allotted portion.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מט) וּבְתַנְחוּמָא (וַיֵּרָא ו): דִּבְסוֹף לִנְבִיאִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי אִם גָּלָה סוֹדוֹ אֶל עֲבָדָיו הַנְּבִיאִים" (עָמוֹס ג, ז);

And our Sages stated in Bereishit Rabbah (49:2) and in Tanchuma (Vayeira 6): ultimately this secret is granted to the prophets, as it is said: "for He reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets" (Amos 3:7);
כִּי יִרְאָה הַיְינוּ בַּלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן".
for fear resides in the heart, as stated in Yoma 72b on the verse "and he has no heart."
וְזֶהוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה – עִיקָּר רַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי, וּמִשֶּׁנִּתְּנָה תּוֹרָה נִתְחַדְּשׁוּ מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְווֹת.
And this was before the Torah was given—primarily the Merciful One desired the heart; and once the Torah was given, the physical deeds of the commandments were instituted.
וְיָשָׁר הַיְינוּ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, וְזֶהוּ אַבְרָהָם וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ
And "upright" (yashar) pertains to practical action, and this is exemplified by Abraham and Joshua
[זַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁהֵם כְּשׁוֹר לָעוֹל בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְווֹת] דְּמַיְיתֵי שָׁם.
[the seed of Joseph, who are like an ox to the yoke in the physical performance of mitzvot], whom the Midrash cites there.

אֲבָל בַּסּוֹף לִנְבִיאִים, דְּהַיְינוּ הַכּוֹלְלִים כָּל הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת צב.): אֵין הַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה אֶלָּא עַל חָכָם בַּמּוֹחַ, גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ בַּלֵּב, וְעָשִׁיר בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְווֹת

But ultimately to the prophets, who encompass all three dimensions, as stated in Shabbat 92a: the Shechinah rests only upon one who is wise in the brain, mighty in conquering his inclination in the heart, and rich in the physical deeds of the mitzvot
[וְהֵם גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה: קִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד; עָשִׁיר הַשָּׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְאֵינוֹ מְקַנֵּא, וְגִבּוֹר נֶגֶד הַתַּאֲוָה, וְכָבוֹד – חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ]:

[and these also correspond to the three traits: envy, lust, and honor; rich is he who rejoices in his portion and does not envy, mighty is against lust, and honor belongs to the wise: "The wise shall inherit honor"].

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Chalomot 12:1: “What the Sages said (Yoma 75a), that the manna changed into every taste, refers to the actual manna that Israel ate. But when the Sages said (Mekhilta, Beshalach, Vayassa 5) that goats and gazelles ate from it and the nations of the world tasted manna in their flesh, what was perceptible there was only the essential taste of manna described in the Torah: “like a wafer with honey” (Exodus 16:31), and nothing more. The taste absorbed into their flesh no longer changed, and therefore the nations of the world could taste it too. This also resolves the statement that the mixed multitude could not taste the manna [meaning its changing tastes. This is the principal difference between manna and all other foods, revealing that it is bread from heaven rather than from earth, with no earthly counterpart at all. This belongs only to Israel, who could eat such bread. The mixed multitude, however, presumably were also nourished by manna in the wilderness; they were the ones who said, “Our soul loathes this insubstantial bread” (Numbers 21:5), since at least the beginning of all the complaints came from them, and most or all of them did. Because they sensed in it only one ordinary taste, they became weary of its sameness. See the holy Zohar, Ki Tissa 191b: Scripture proclaims, “The children of Israel ate the manna” (Exodus 16:35), excluding the mixed multitude. Nevertheless, it says there that they ate from its residue and from what Israel gave them; see there. This too can be explained as I have written].”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Divrei Chalomot distinguishes the manna’s ordinary taste, which could be encountered indirectly, from its changing tastes experienced by Israel. This develops the present siman’s definition of sod as a taste that cannot simply be conveyed by description. The outward object may be shared while the inward reception differs. Tzidkat HaTzadik places that reception after action, desire of the heart, and understanding; the illustration therefore clarifies the meaning of taste without replacing those stages of avodah.

paragraphs.text: Yosher Divrei Emet, First Kuntres 22:1: “This is called the hidden wisdom. I heard from the holy mouth of our teacher Rabbi Menachem Mendel, of blessed memory, that “hidden” means something a person cannot convey to another. It is like the taste of food: one cannot describe it to a person who has never tasted that flavor; one cannot explain in words how and what it is. This is called a hidden matter. So too with love and fear of the Creator, blessed be His name: one cannot explain to another what the love in the heart is like. This is called “hidden.” But as for what people call hidden—the wisdom of Kabbalah—how is it hidden? The book lies before anyone who wishes to study it. If he does not understand, he is unlearned, and for such a person Gemara and Tosafot are also called hidden. Rather, the hidden matters throughout the Zohar and the writings of the Ari are all founded on cleaving to the Creator, for one who merits to cleave to Him and behold the supernal Chariot, like the Ari, of blessed memory, to whom the paths of heaven were clear, and who constantly walked in them with the eyes of his intellect, like the four Sages who entered the pardes, as explained in Tosafot to Chagigah and in Hagahot Maimoniyot at the beginning of Sefer HaMadda, at the end of chapter four; see there.”

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Vayera 6:9: “Another explanation of Then he openeth the ears of men: This alludes to Abraham, for it is said: And God said: Shall I hide from Abraham?, and By their chastisement sealeth the decree (Job 33:16) refers to the Sodomites, against whom He sealed the decree when a single righteous man could not be found amongst them. Another comment on And the Lord said: Shall I hide from Abraham? Scripture states elsewhere in allusion to this verse: For the Lord will do nothing, but He revealeth His counsel unto His servants, the prophets (Amos 3:7). In the beginning the Holy One, blessed be He, used to reveal His secrets to those who feared Him, as it is said: The counsel of the Lord is with them that fear Him (Ps. 25:14). Then He made His secrets known to the righteous, as is said: In the council of the upright and in the congregation (Ps. 111:1); and finally He revealed it only to the prophets, as it is said: But He revealeth His counsel unto His servants, the prophets. After Israel transgressed at the time of Achan, the Holy One, blessed be He, informed Joshua, as it is said: Israel hath sinned (Josh. 7:11). When Eli’s sons sinned, the Holy One, blessed be He, disclosed it to Samuel, as is said: And the Lord called Samuel (I Sam. 3:4). When the Sodomites sinned, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed it to Abraham, as is said: Shall I hide from Abraham?”

paragraphs.text: Eight Chapters 7:3: “Know that no prophet prophesied until he possessed all the intellectual virtues and most of the moral virtues, including the strongest of them. This is their statement: “Prophecy rests only upon one who is wise, mighty, and wealthy.” “Wise” unquestionably includes all the intellectual virtues. “Wealthy” is one of the moral virtues, meaning contentment, for they call the contented person wealthy. Thus they define the wealthy person: “Who is wealthy? One who rejoices in his portion”—meaning that what his circumstances have provided suffices for him, and he does not grieve over what they have not provided. “Mighty” is likewise one of the moral virtues, meaning that he directs his powers according to understanding and counsel, as we explained in chapter five. This is their statement: “Who is mighty? One who masters his inclination.””
