items.h: After the teacher’s death: faith and fellowship

p: וְאַחַר פְּטִירַת הָרַב, וְאָבְדוּ עֶשְׁתּוֹנוֹתָיו כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אַל תִּבְטְחוּ בִנְדִיבִים וְגוֹמֵר, בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא אָבְדוּ עֶשְׁתֹּנֹתָיו" (תְּהִלִּים קמו, ג–ד) [וְקָאֵי אַעֶשְׁתּוֹנוֹת הַבּוֹטֵחַ],

And after the master passes away, when his plans seem lost—as in "Put not your trust in princes... in that very day his thoughts perish" (Psalms 146:3–4), [referring to the thoughts of the one who placed his trust]—

וּמַתְחִיל לְהַכִּיר כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְ"אַשְׁרֵי... שִׁבְרוֹ עַל ה' אֱלֹהָיו" (שָׁם, ה) – הַכָּרָה זוֹ נִקְרָא יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, וְאָז "נִדְבְּרוּ וְגוֹמֵר",

he begins to recognize that Hashem truly teaches Torah to His people Israel, and "Happy is he... whose hope is in Hashem his God" (ibid. 146:5); this recognition is fear of Heaven, and then "they spoke, etc.,"

וּמְבַקֵּשׁ לִקְנוֹת חֲבֵירִים כְּעִנְיַן שֶׁחֲבֵירֶיךָ יְקַיְּמוּהָ בְּיָדְךָ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד, יד), שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד יִרְאָה שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁכַּח חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כְּדֶרֶךְ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ (שַׁבָּת קמז:), וְזֶהוּ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.

and he seeks to acquire colleagues so that "your colleagues may establish it in your hand" (Avot 4:14), out of fear lest he forget, like Rabbi Elazar ben Arach (Shabbat 147b), which is fear of Heaven.
וְהוּא בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה תְּחִלָּה שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְבָנִים תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי כֵן יְבֹרַךְ גֶּבֶר יְרֵא ה' וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים קכח, ד).
And this fulfills blessing the Torah first, through which one merits scholar sons, as written: "for surely thus shall the man be blessed that fears Hashem, etc." (Psalms 128:4).
וְדָבָר זֶה נִקְרָא "לְאוֹקְמֵי גִּירְסָא" שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (ו:) דְּהוּא סַיַּעְתָּא מִן שְׁמַיָּא
And this is called "retaining one's learning" (le'okmei girsa), which Megillah 6b states requires Heavenly assistance
[וְזֶהוּ גִּירְסָא דְּהַיְינוּ דִּבּוּר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת קפ"ג].
[and girsa is vocal speech, as noted in Section 183].

וְלָכֵן אָמַר: "אַשְׁרֵי וְגוֹמֵר שִׁבְרוֹ וְגוֹמֵר", וְלֹא אָמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיוּוּי כְּמוֹ שֶׁפָּתַח: "אַל תִּבְטְחוּ וְגוֹמֵר", רַק: בִּטְחוּ בַּה', רַק דְּזֶהוּ סַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא וְאֵינוֹ בִּידֵי אָדָם;
Therefore Scripture says: "Happy is he... whose hope is, etc.," rather than phrasing it as a direct command to trust in Hashem, because this is Heavenly assistance beyond mortal hands;
וְלָכֵן אָמַר "אָז נִדְבְּרוּ" וְלֹא "דִּבְּרוּ", רַק "נִדְבְּרוּ" – שֶׁאֵירַע כָּךְ.
and therefore it says nidberu (they were conversing) rather than dibru (they spoke), indicating that it simply came about so.

וְזֶהוּ "מִכְתְּבַן מִילַּיְיהוּ", פֵּירוּשׁ סֵפֶר הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת הֵם נַפְשׁוֹתָן כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּירְשׁוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים עַל סִפְרָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים וְשֶׁל רְשָׁעִים דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, וּ"מִכְתְּבַן" הַיְינוּ שֶׁנֶּחְקַק לְזִכָּרוֹן וּלְאוֹקְמֵי גִּירְסָא שֶׁלֹּא יֵעָתֵק מֵהֶם עוֹד;

And this is "their words were written"—the book of remembrance being their souls, as early masters explained regarding the books of the righteous and wicked on Rosh Hashanah; "written" meaning etched into memory to retain learning so it never departs;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּיָחִיד שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית (ז.) דְּמִטַּפְּשָׁן.
unlike an isolated learner, of whom Ta'anit 7a says he grows foolish.

וְהֲגַם דְּדָבָר זֶה סַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא, הַתַּנָּא דְּאָבוֹת אָמַר בְּצִיוּוּי "וּקְנֵה", שֶׁהוּא בְּיָדוֹ וַדַּאי לִקְנוֹת חָבֵר, רַק שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מֵאוֹתָם שֶׁחֲבֵירֶיךָ יְקַיְּמוּהוּ בְּיָדְךָ – זֶהוּ סַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא,

And although this is Heavenly assistance, the Tanna of Avot commanded "acquire," for acquiring a colleague is in one's hands, though having colleagues who establish Torah in your hand is Heavenly assistance,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים בְּסֻכָּה (מט:): "מַה יָּקָר וְגוֹמֵר", וְהַיְינוּ מִשּׁוּם שֶׁאָמַר בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (טז:): הַכְשִׁילֵם בְּשֶׁאֵינָם מְהֻגָּנִים.
as with acts of kindness in Sukkah 49b: "How precious is Your lovingkindness," parallel to Bava Kamma 16b: cause them to stumble with unworthy recipients.

וְנִרְאֶה דִּלְכָךְ סִיֵּים רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָה: "וֶהֱוֵי דָן וְכוּלֵי", דְּאֵין לוֹ לָחוּשׁ לְכָךְ, דְּהֲגַם דִּבְרַב נֶאֱמַר "עֲשֵׂה" אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם שָׁם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים (פה עַמּוּד ב) דְּאִית לְמֵילַף מִכָּל בַּר נָשׁ וְכוּלֵי,

And it appears that Yehoshua ben Perachyah concluded "judge favorably" to show one should not worry; for regarding a master it says "make" even if he is imperfect, as Maimonides wrote and as the Zohar states (Kedoshim 85b) that one can learn from anyone,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּחָבֵר צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הָגוּן, מִכָּל מָקוֹם "הֱוֵי דָן וְכוּלֵי", וְאַל תְּדַקְדֵּק בּוֹ יוֹתֵר, וּבְטַח בַּה' שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי יִהְיֶה בְּעֶזְרְךָ.
whereas a colleague must be worthy; nonetheless judge favorably, do not over-scrutinize, and trust that Hashem will assist you.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8:2: “Just as, when a person engages in Torah through speech, the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in it opposite him, as the Sages say in Tanna de-Vei Eliyahu Rabbah 18, so when he writes words of Torah, the Holy One writes them as well. God’s writing means the coming into being of souls—for example, the Written Torah, whose letters are the roots of the souls of Israel, as is known. So too all writing of the Oral Torah reveals what is concealed in the Written Torah. All souls consist of letters, and a person’s deeds, in commandments and transgressions, change their combination, as explained in Raavad’s commentary to Sefer Yetzirah at the beginning of chapter 3, concerning the three books of the wholly righteous and the others; see there. Through those letters written by the hand of the Holy One, souls are formed.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Rosh Hashanah 5: “The explanation is that it is written (Numbers 10:9), ‘You shall be remembered before Hashem your God.’ What can remembrance mean for Hashem? For a person, who sometimes forgets, remembrance has a place. But before Hashem there is no forgetting before the throne of His glory, and nothing is hidden from His sight: what does remembrance mean? All this remembrance is on the human side. Where a person establishes continual remembrance of Hashem, Hashem fixes it within him permanently, so that he does not forget Hashem for even a moment. This is called remembrance with Hashem. As it says (Malachi 3:16), ‘Then those who fear Hashem spoke to one another; Hashem attended and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him.’ My holy grandfather explained in Mei HaShiloach that Hashem's book of remembrance means His establishing words of Torah permanently within the person.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef asks how remembrance can apply to Hashem, before Whom nothing is forgotten. It explicitly interprets the same book of remembrance as Hashem establishing Torah permanently within the person. This directly explains the siman's account of the writing as an engraving in the souls that preserves their learning.

sections.en: The Essence of Fellowship Is with the God-fearing

p: [קפו] עִיקַּר הַהִתְחַבְּרוּת הוּא לִירֵאִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "חָבֵר אָנִי לְכָל אֲשֶׁר יְרֵאוּךָ" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, סג), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אָז נִדְבְּרוּ יִרְאֵי ה' אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ" (מַלְאָכִי ג, טז).

The essence of fellowship is with the God-fearing, as written: "I am a companion of all them that fear You" (Psalms 119:63), and: "Then they that feared Hashem spoke often one to another" (Malachi 3:16).
כִּי שָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת חָכְמָה, בִּינָה, דַּעַת: חָכְמָה – מַה שֶּׁמְּקַבֵּל מֵאֲחֵרִים, זֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁקִּבֵּל מֵרַבּוֹ;
For the three cognitive faculties are Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at: Chokhmah is what one receives from others, namely from his master;
וּלְהָבִין דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר – זֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הִתְחַבְּרוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית ז.): "בַּרְזֶל בְּבַרְזֶל יַחַד וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי כז, יז).
and discerning one matter from another (Binah) is achieved through fellowship, as stated: "Iron sharpens iron, etc." (Proverbs 27:17; Ta'anit 7a).
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַחֶבְרָה: לְחַדֵּד זֶה אֶת זֶה שֶׁיִּתְחַדְּשׁוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַל יָדָם, דִּלְכָךְ מִצְטָרְפִין לְזִמּוּן כִּדְאִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת (מז:) וְלֹא פָּרִיךְ "וְחִידּוּד גַּבְרָא",

And this is the purpose of companionship: sharpening one another so that Torah insights are innovated through them; which is why [two scholars who sharpen each other] combine for a zimun (Berakhot 47b), and the Gemara does not object, "Is sharpening a person?",

דְּמַה שֶּׁצָּרִיךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה הַיְינוּ דְּאֵין חַבְרוּתָא בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (טז:) לְעִנְיַן שַׁיָּירָא, וּבְסֻכָּה (יג.) לְעִנְיַן אֲגֻדָּה וַחֲבִילָה עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת, וְכֵן בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סח) עַל פָּסוּק "יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ" – אֵין הַחֶבֶל נִפְקָע בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה.

for a fellowship requires at least three, as in Eruvin 16b regarding a caravan, Sukkah 13a regarding a bundle, and Bereishit Rabbah 68 on "Jacob is the lot (chevel, rope) of His inheritance"—a threefold cord is not easily broken.
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַחִידּוּד הוּא חַבְרוּתָא גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁנַיִם, כִּי הַחִידּוּד מְחַבְּרָם, וְזֶה לְשׁוֹן "חִידּוּד" – מִן חַד נַעֲשָׂה אֶחָד וּמְחֻבָּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְפָּרֵד.

But through intellectual sharpening, a fellowship exists even between two, for sharpening binds them together; and this is the root of chidud (sharpening)—from distinct ones (chad) they become unified (echad) and inseparable.

וְהַיְינוּ כִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה הוּא חִבּוּר שְׁנֵי קְצוֹת וְאֶמְצָעִי הַמְחַבֵּר, וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מה:): אִיכָּא דֵּעוֹת, דְּהָעִיקָּר שָׁלֹשׁ דֵּעוֹת הַנִּפְרָדוֹת שֶׁמִּתְחַבְּרִים יַחַד עַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילָה יַחַד, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין (ד:): אֵין הֲסָתָה בְּלֹא אֲכִילָה וְכוּלֵי.

And that is because three represents two extremes and the middle harmonizer; as they said in Berakhot 45b: there are distinct minds, where three separate minds unite through eating together, as in Chullin 4b: there is no seduction without dining, etc.
וְכֵן פִּתָּן וְיֵינָן מִשּׁוּם בְּנוֹתֵיהֶם, שֶׁעִיקַּר הִתְחַבְּרוּת עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה.
And so their bread and wine were banned on account of their daughters (Avodah Zarah 36b), for connection occurs through eating and drinking.

וְזֶהוּ הַזִּמּוּן דִּבְרָכָה לְפָנֶיהָ כְּשֶׁרָעֵב דּוּגְמַת שָׁבוּעוֹת [וּפֶסַח בְּחֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב], וּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ כְּשֶׁהוּא שָׂבֵעַ דּוּגְמַת סֻכּוֹת חַג הָאָסִיף שֶׁהוּא זְמַן שִׂמְחָתֵנוּ

And this is the zimun: a blessing beforehand when hungry mirrors Shavuot [and Passover in the month of Aviv], while Grace after Meals when sated mirrors Sukkot the Feast of Ingathering, the season of our rejoicing
[וּבְמוֹעֵד קָטָן (ט.): אֵין שִׂמְחָה בְּלֹא אֲכִילָה וְכוּלֵי],
[and in Moed Katan 9a: there is no joy without eating, etc.],
וּמִשָּׁם שׁוֹאֲבִין רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דְּהֶחָלִיל (סֻכָּה פֶּרֶק ה הֲלָכָה א), דְּדַעַת הַיְינוּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כִּדְפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא.
and from there they drew the Holy Spirit (Yerushalmi Sukkah 5:1), for Da'at is the Holy Spirit as Rashi explains on Ki Tisa.
וְזֶהוּ אַחַר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה, דְּדַעַת הַמְחַבֵּר כַּנּוֹדָע, וְכֵן חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת הַשְּׁלִישִׁי לָרְגָלִים.
And this follows Chokhmah and Binah, for Da'at unites them, just as Sukkot is the third pilgrimage festival.

וּלְכָךְ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה אָז צָרִיךְ זִמּוּן, דִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מה.) דְּהַיְינוּ "גַּדְּלוּ לַה' אִתִּי וּנְרוֹמְמָה שְׁמוֹ יַחְדָּו" (תְּהִלִּים לד, ד), שֶׁלָּזֶה צָרִיךְ הֲכָנָה וְזִמּוּן לְהִתְכַּלֵּל יַחַד הַנְּפָשׁוֹת.
Therefore with three a zimun is required, as Berakhot 45a derives from "O magnify Hashem with me, and let us exalt His name together" (Psalms 34:4), which demands preparation to unite souls together.

וְכֵן בִּזְמַן, שׁוֹפָר דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁקּוֹדֶם סֻכּוֹת הוּא הַזִּמּוּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים דְּרוֹמֵז: עוּרוּ יְשֵׁנִים וְכוּלֵי, וַהֲכָנָה לְחִבּוּר וְיִחוּד הַקְּצוֹת עַל יְדֵי חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת.
And in time, the shofar of Rosh Hashanah before Sukkot is the zimun, as early masters wrote: "Awake, sleepers," preparing the union of extremes through Sukkot.

וְכֵן הַחִידּוּד מְחַבֵּר דּוּגְמַת הָעֲקֵידָה, דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קיט עַמּוּד ב) דְּאָז נִתְכַּלְּלוּ יַחַד אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כב, יב);
And sharpening unites like the Binding of Isaac, where Zohar I:119b states Abraham and Isaac integrated, as written: "now I know that you fear God" (Genesis 22:12);

וְהַיְינוּ דְּמַחֲוֵי רַב חִסְדָּא כְּגוֹן אֲנָא וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת וְכוּלֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (סז.), דְּהֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים: רַב חִסְדָּא חָרִיף וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת סִינַי, וְכָל חַד מְרַתֵּת מֵחַבְרֵיהּ – זֶהוּ הַיִּרְאָה,
which matches Rav Chisda saying: like me and Rav Sheshet (Eruvin 67a), who were opposites—one sharp and one erudite (Sinai)—each trembling before the other, which is awe;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַחִידּוּד "נִדְבְּרוּ יִרְאֵי ה'" וְנִתְחַבְּרוּ וְנִתְכַּלְּלוּ שְׁנֵי הַקְּצוֹת, וּלְכָךְ מְזַמְּנִין, וְהוּא בִּכְלַל שַׁבָּת הַקּוֹדֵם בַּגְּמָרָא

and through sharpening, "they that feared Hashem spoke" and united two extremes, and therefore they invite for zimun, and this is included in the statement about Shabbat that comes just before it in the Gemara
[וּכְמוֹ בַּמֵּימְרוֹת שֶׁלִּפְנֵיהֶם שָׁם: עַל יְדֵי הָאָרוֹן נִרְאִין כַּעֲשָׂרָה, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם, דִּבְלָאו הָכִי תָּמוּהַּ].
[and as in the sayings there: through the Ark they appear as ten, see there, which otherwise is puzzling].

וְהַיְינוּ דִּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ יִרְאָה, וְכִידוּעַ דְּבִינָה מִינַּהּ דִּינִין מִתְעָרִין, כִּי כָּל חִדּוּשׁ יֵשׁ יִרְאָה שֶׁמָּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הוּא שָׁוְא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהַקְדָּמַת הַזֹּהַר (ה עַמּוּד א) דְּלָכֵן אֵין לְחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא שָׁמַע מֵרַבּוֹ.

And for this awe is needed, for judgments awaken from Binah, since with every novel insight there is fear lest it be vain, as stated in the Zohar's introduction (5a) not to innovate what was not received from a master.
וּלְכִי הִתְנוּ (שַׁבָּת סג.) בִּמְחַדְּדִין שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִשְׁמָהּ וּבַעֲנָוָה, אָז מַצְלִיחִין, דְּגַם בְּמַחֲלוֹקְתָּן אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים.
And when they stipulated (Shabbat 63a) that scholars who sharpen each other act for Heaven's sake and with humility, they prosper, and in their dispute both are words of the living God.
וְהוּא יִחוּד כְּמַחֲלוֹקֶת שַׁמַּאי וְהִלֵּל סוֹפָהּ לְהִתְקַיֵּים, שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּזָב וְדָבָר הַפּוֹסֵק כְּכָל רִיב וּמְדָנִים יַפְרִיד אַחִים.
And this is a union like the dispute of Shammai and Hillel that endures, which does not fail and come to an end like every strife and contention that separates brothers.
וּלְכָךְ "בִּינָה לִבָּא" שֶׁשָּׁם הַיִּרְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן", וְעוֹשֶׂה חֲדָשׁוֹת בַּעַל מִלְחָמוֹת כַּנּוֹדָע.
Therefore Binah is the heart where awe resides (Yoma 72b), making new things and waging holy battles.

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שַׁבָּת הוּא מְנוּחָה, דְּזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁעוֹשִׂין לִשְׁמָהּ אָז "אֶת וָהֵב בְּסוּפָה" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כא, יד), וּמִתְיַיחֲדִין יַחַד וּמְזַמְּנִין, וְאָז עוֹלִין לִגְדוּלָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת שָׁם), דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁזּוֹכִין לְתַלְמִידִים שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגַת הַדַּעַת הַמְחַבֵּר, כְּמוֹ יִצְחָק עַל יְדֵי הָעֲקֵידָה נִזְדַּמְּנָה לוֹ רִבְקָה לְהוֹלִיד יַעֲקֹב הַמְחַבֵּר

In contrast, Shabbat is rest; when done for Heaven's sake, love comes at the end (et vahev be-sufah), they unite and invite, rising to greatness (Shabbat ibid.)—meriting disciples, the level of unifying Da'at, just as through the Akedah Rebecca was prepared for Isaac to bear Jacob the harmonizer
[עַיֵּין זֹהַר שְׁמוֹת יד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב דַּאֲבוֹת הֵם חָכְמָה, בִּינָה, דַּעַת]:
[see Zohar Shemot 14b end that the Patriarchs embody Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at].

paragraphs.text: The Chanukah lamp, mezuzah, and tzitzit provide a ritual image of the threefold cord described in the siman’s account of fellowship.

rich.text: The Chanukah lamp, mezuzah, and tzitzit provide a ritual image of the threefold cord described in the siman’s account of fellowship.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 11:1: “Therefore the Maharil explains that the intention concerns the tzitzit thread in the middle. A thread of tzitzit serves to recall all the mitzvot, and joining the two mitzvot of Chanukah and mezuzah helps that thread become strengthened like the threefold cord. Through this it becomes “Jacob, the rope of His inheritance,” tripled from the holiness of all three patriarchs, like a rope that is not plaited from fewer than three strands, as Bereishit Rabbah says. Through the Chanukah lamp this power was established and completed within the totality of Israel’s souls.”

rich.text: : “Therefore the Maharil explains that the intention concerns the tzitzit thread in the middle. A thread of tzitzit serves to recall all the mitzvot, and joining the two mitzvot of Chanukah and mezuzah helps that thread become strengthened like the threefold cord. Through this it becomes “Jacob, the rope of His inheritance,” tripled from the holiness of all three patriarchs, like a rope that is not plaited from fewer than three strands, as Bereishit Rabbah says. Through the Chanukah lamp this power was established and completed within the totality of Israel’s souls.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah applies the threefold cord to mitzvot joined at the doorway and to Yaakov’s inheritance from the three Avos. This gives a concrete image for the present siman’s distinction between separate minds and a bond that can hold them together. Here the third, connecting dimension is da’at: fellowship reaches beyond the mere presence of several people when their distinct powers are brought into a shared service of Hashem.

p: [קפז] הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הֵם עֹז לָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְהַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז [לֶחָכָם]" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יט), וְ"אֵיזֶהוּ גִבּוֹר? הַכּוֹבֵשׁ [אֶת יִצְרוֹ]" (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד, א), שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל:): מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע, בָּרָאתִי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי;

Words of Torah are strength to man, as written: "Wisdom strengthens the wise" (Ecclesiastes 7:19), and: "Who is mighty? He who subdues his inclination" (Avot 4:1), through which one overcomes his inclination (Kiddushin 30b): "drag him to the house of study," and: "I created the evil inclination, I created the Torah as an antidote";
שֶׁזֶּהוּ "אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי" (סֻכָּה נב:), וְהָעֵזֶר וְהַסַּיַּעְתָּא הוּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁמֵּאִיר לוֹ.
for this is "were not the Holy One to help him, he could not withstand it" (Sukkah 52b), the divine assistance being the words of Torah that illuminate him.
וְהַסַּיַּעְתָּא לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא רַב וַחֲבֵירִים וְתַלְמִידִים.
And assistance in Torah comes through a master, colleagues, and disciples.
וְאָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים: "וְחָנֵּנוּ מֵאִתְּךָ חָכְמָה בִּינָה וָדָעַת", שֶׁהֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה הַנִּזְכָּרִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת קפ"ו – יְהֵא מֵאִתְּךָ בְּלֹא סִיּוּעַ בְּנֵי אָדָם,
And we pray: "Graciously bestow upon us from Yourself wisdom, understanding, and knowledge," which are the three mentioned in Section 186—that it come directly from You without human mediation,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא) בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: רַב לֹא הָיָה לוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי ה' יִתֵּן חָכְמָה, מִפִּיו דַּעַת וּתְבוּנָה" (מִשְׁלֵי ב, ו).
as stated in Bereishit Rabbah 61 regarding Abraham: he had no master, etc., and as written: "For Hashem gives wisdom; out of His mouth come knowledge and understanding" (Proverbs 2:6).
וְעַל זֶה נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהִיא תִּהְיֶה הָרַב וְהֶחָבֵר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י אָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק א מִשְׁנָה ו) עַל "קְנֵה לְךָ חָבֵר": יֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים סְפָרִים.
And for this the Torah was given to Israel, that it serve as master and colleague, as Rashi comments on "acquire for yourself a colleague" (Avot 1:6): some say books.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַסְּפָרִים הֵם רַבּוֹתָיו, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁבוּת יַעֲקֹב (חֵלֶק ב) מֵהַאי טַעְמָא לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹרֶה בִּפְנֵי רַבּוֹ כְּשֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהִסְתַּכֵּל בַּסֵּפֶר.
And in truth, sacred books are one's teachers, as written in Shevut Yaakov (Part II) that ruling halakhah while able to consult a book is like ruling in the presence of one's master.
רַק זֶהוּ בַּהַתְחָלָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁמְּחַדֵּשׁ חִדּוּשִׁין עַל יָדָם נַעֲשׂוּ מַדְרֵגַת חָבֵר.
Only that this applies at the start, and afterward when one innovates insights through them, they assume the status of a colleague.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ג): לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ "בִּתִּי" וְכוּלֵי, "אֲחוֹתִי" וְכוּלֵי, "אִמִּי" וְכוּלֵי;
And this is what Shir HaShirim Rabbah (end of chapter 3) expounds: He did not cease cherishing her until He called her "My daughter," "My sister," "My mother";

וְ"אִמִּי" הַיְינוּ מַדְרֵגַת תַּלְמִיד, וְהַיְינוּ דִּלְבַסּוֹף נַעֲשֵׂית תּוֹרָתוֹ, וּכְאִלּוּ הוּא הַמּוֹלִיד הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי, כִּי מַמָּשׁ פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת בָּאוּ לְכָאן.

and "My mother" is the stage of disciples, meaning ultimately it becomes his own Torah, as though he gives birth to the very Torah given to Moses at Sinai, for a brand-new countenance has truly arrived here.

כְּמוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל, עַל יְדֵי פֵּירוּשׁ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּכְּתוּבִים, וַדַּאי הֵם נִקְרָאִים בּוֹנֶיהָ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי סְפָרִים שֶׁחִבְּרוּ הֵם לְלַמֵּד חֲדָשׁוֹת לַאֲחֵרִים;
For example, through our Sages' expositions of Scripture, they are called the builders of Torah, through the books they composed to teach new insights to others;
וְאוֹרַיְיתָא וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חַד, לְכָךְ לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ "אִמִּי", שֶׁהֵם הוֹלִידוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה וְהַחָכְמָה בָּעוֹלָם.
and the Torah and the Holy One are One, which is why He did not cease until He called her "My mother," for they birthed the root of Torah and Wisdom in the world.
וְהַיְינוּ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בְּחֵשֶׁק עָצוּם הַקּוֹדֵם, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בַּתְּחִלָּה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת קפ"ד – נִקְרָא "בִּתִּי".
And through the awakening from below in immense desire at the beginning, as noted in Section 184, she is called "My daughter."

וְאַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁבָּא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא לְסִיּוּעַ וְנִתְחַדֵּשׁ לוֹ חִדּוּשִׁין וְנוֹלַד הַיִּרְאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, אָז נִקְרָא "אֲחוֹתִי", וְאָז הֵם מִתְיַיחֲדִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר עַל פָּסוּק "אָמְנָה אֲחֹתִי וְגוֹמֵר וַתְּהִי לִי לְאִשָּׁה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ, יב).

And afterward when the awakening from Above arrives to assist and insights are innovated and awe is born, she is called "My sister," and then they unite, as in the Zohar on: "she is indeed my sister... and she became my wife" (Genesis 20:12).

וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַחִדּוּשִׁין הֵם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֲנָוָה וְלִשְׁמָהּ, שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מִגַּרְמֵיהּ כְּלוּם, אָז מַצְלִיחִין וְעוֹלֶה לִגְדוּלָּה לִהְיוֹת נִקְרָא "אִמִּי",

And through recognizing that the innovations are from the Blessed Name—which is humility and Torah study for its own sake, realizing he has nothing of his own—they prosper and rise to greatness to be called "My mother,"

כְּמִשְׁפַּט אַחַר הַבְּרָכָה וְהַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹמֵר שֶׁהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ, גַּם הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא הוּא מִשֶּׁלּוֹ, כְּטַעַם: תְּנוּ עֹז [הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל] לֵאלֹהִים (תְּהִלִּים סח, לה), כִּי עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא שֶׁנּוֹלַד זֶה:

for after the blessing and the recognition that all is from Hashem, Hashem declares that all is the person's, even the supernal awakening, in the spirit of: "Ascribe strength [that is, words of Torah, as above] unto God" (Psalms 68:35), for through his awakening from below this was born.

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 30b:4: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its seasoning. If you occupy yourselves with Torah, you are not handed over into its power.”

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 30b:8: “The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: My son, if this wretched one encounters you, draw him to the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter.”

rich.text: : “The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: My son, if this wretched one encounters you, draw him to the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter.”

paragraphs.text: Context: These are two adjoining formulations of Torah’s power against the evil inclination. The first is the “seasoning” formulation explicitly used by Rav Tzadok; the second describes bringing the struggle into the study hall.

paragraphs.text: Even a great teacher needs fresh assistance; past achievement does not make the next struggle automatic.

rich.text: Even a great teacher needs fresh assistance; past achievement does not make the next struggle automatic.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 9:5: “There is Amalek, the evil inclination, the accusing prosecutor continually present within a person, as the holy Zohar says. It is written, “Who cooled you on the way”: Amalek, the first of the nations, occupies himself with cooling a person and casting laziness and sadness upon him. This rules even among the great. Jabez spread Torah in Israel and restored through his reasoning the laws forgotten during the mourning for Moses. Nevertheless he asked, “That it not sadden me”—that the evil inclination not overpower him and prevent him from studying. A person cannot escape this shell through choice alone. Of this they said, “Were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not overcome it,” and “The greater a person is than his fellow, the greater his inclination.” This is “Your miracles that are with us every day”: God’s help is a miracle beyond the regular order of governance through choice. It occurs every day, because the inclination grows stronger and renews itself every day. “The greater a person is than his fellow, the greater his inclination”—this explains its daily renewal.”

Nevertheless he asked, “That it not sadden me”—that the evil inclination not overpower him and prevent him from studying. A person cannot escape this shell through choice alone. Of this they said, “Were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not overcome it,” and “The greater a person is than his fellow, the greater his inclination.” This is “Your miracles that are with us every day”: God’s help is a miracle beyond the regular order of governance through choice. It occurs every day, because the inclination grows stronger and renews itself every day. “The greater a person is than his fellow, the greater his inclination”—this explains its daily renewal.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah develops the daily renewal of the inclination through Yaavetz, whose great work in restoring Torah did not remove his need to ask for protection from discouragement and interruption of study. This gives the present siman’s ‘help’ a continuing character. Torah’s illuminating strength is not simply an achievement stored from an earlier victory; it is the form in which Hashem sustains the learner through the renewed struggle.

paragraphs.text: Torah gives strength against the inclination, and its innovations arise through human longing and assistance from above. Recognizing that source makes it possible for what is received to become the person’s own Torah.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 8:8: “At first, the five occurrences of “light” in the utterance “Let there be light” corresponded to the five books of the Torah, as is taught in Bereishit Rabbah. Afterward the first light was hidden away for those who labor in Oral Torah, as is taught in the Tanchuma in Noach. Concerning Oral Torah it is said, “May my utterance flow like dew.” As we have explained, Oral Torah is compared to dew: when dew descends, its descent from heaven is not visible; one understands that it fell only upon seeing the earth wet. Similarly, it appears to the sages that they are originating insights in their hearts, but in truth these are the word of God—“My words that I have placed in your mouth”—and they come from the dew of Atika. Abraham our father attained this: his two kidneys poured forth wisdom that God had prepared for him, as is taught in Bereishit Rabbah. This is what was said to him, “Yours is the dew of your youth.” Shabbat too is the seventh quality, Malkhut: “the mouth, which we call Oral Torah.” It is the time to merit Torah, particularly at the meal of Atika.”

The image clarifies the recognition on which Tzidkat HaTzadik makes the scholar’s subsequent attainment depend.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 10:2: “The Chanukah lamp alludes to the illumination of Oral Torah. This is the menorah’s meaning when the Midrash relates that the Holy One, blessed be He, says, “Come and give Me light.” It is the light of Oral Torah, what the sages discover anew; “It is not in Heaven.” Thus the Talmud relates that God said, “My children have defeated Me.” It also says that He was repeating teachings from the mouths of all the sages, but not from Rabbi Meir, and then, “Now He says: My son Meir says,” and so forth.”

rich.text: : “The Chanukah lamp alludes to the illumination of Oral Torah. This is the menorah’s meaning when the Midrash relates that the Holy One, blessed be He, says, “Come and give Me light.” It is the light of Oral Torah, what the sages discover anew; “It is not in Heaven.” Thus the Talmud relates that God said, “My children have defeated Me.” It also says that He was repeating teachings from the mouths of all the sages, but not from Rabbi Meir, and then, “Now He says: My son Meir says,” and so forth.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah joins the menorah’s light with the sages’ innovations and ‘It is not in heaven.’ This illuminates the culmination of the present siman: the learner recognizes that the illumination comes from Hashem, yet Hashem attributes the resulting Torah to the learner. Humility and the standing of one’s own Torah therefore support each other. The gift becomes a real contribution precisely through the learner’s awakening, labor, and faithful reception.

sections.en: There Are Four Levels Among Colleagues

p: [קפח] אַרְבַּע מַדְרֵגוֹת בַּחֲבֵרִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת סג.): מְחַדְּדִים, וְנוֹחִים, וּמַקְשִׁיבִים, וּמַדְגִּילִים;
There are four levels among colleagues, as stated in Shabbat 63a: those who sharpen each other, those who are gentle, those who listen, and those who assemble in groups (madgilim);
וְהִיא הַפְּחוּתָה, כִּדְמַסַּיֵּים עֲלַהּ: וְהוּא דְּיָדְעֵי, וְהוּא דְּלֵית לְהוּ וְכוּלֵי.
and the last is the lowest, as the Talmud concludes: provided they know the general form, and provided they have no master in town, etc.
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "מַדְגִּילִים" לְפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י, שֶׁאֵין בְּיָדָם אֶלָּא הָאֲסִיפָה לְבַד,
And therefore they are called madgilim according to Rashi, having in their power merely assembling together,
כְּעִנְיַן "אֲגָרָא דְּפִרְקָא – רִיהֲטָא, וּדְכַלָּה – דּוּחְקָא", שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו:) לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מְבִינִים, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
like "the reward of the public discourse is the running, and of the Kallah gathering is the crowding," which Rashi explains in Berakhot 6b is because many do not understand, see there.
וְכֵן בְּכַלָּה, מִפְּנֵי רִבּוּי הָעָם אֵין עוֹמְדִים עַל בּוּרְיוֹ, וְלֹא קַשְׁיָא קֻשְׁיַת תּוֹסָפוֹת דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (כב:) עַיֵּין שָׁם,
And so at the Kallah, due to the crowd they do not grasp the depth, resolving the query of Tosafot in Avodah Zarah 22b,
דְּרַק בִּשְׁבִיל הָאֲסִיפָה לְבַד גַּם כֵּן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹהֲבָן, הוֹאִיל וְלֵית לְהוּ רַב וְיוֹדְעִים עַל כָּל פָּנִים צוּרְתָא דִּשְׁמַעְתָּא;
for solely for gathering together the Holy One loves them, since they have no master and know at least the basic outline of the teaching;
פֵּירוּשׁ, "צוּרָה" הוּא הַחֲשִׁיבוּת, כְּמוֹ "אֲנָשִׁים הַלָּלוּ בַּעֲלֵי צוּרָה" בְּמוֹעֵד קָטָן (ט.),
for "form" (tzurah) denotes dignity and core essence, like "these men are men of form" in Moed Katan 9a,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי יְדִיעַת שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַדָּבָר כְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י, שֶׁזֶּהוּ כְּמוֹ צוּרָה לַחֹמֶר שֶׁהוּא הַיְדִיעָה בִּפְרָטוּת.
which is knowing the root of the matter as Rashi explains, serving as form to the matter of detailed knowledge.

וּבְאֵלּוּ לֹא אָמַר "אִם אֵין עוֹשִׂין כֵּן וְכוּלֵי" שֶׁיֵּעָנְשׁוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין יוֹדְעִין כָּל כָּךְ, רַק אֲסִיפָתָן הוּא נְדִיבוּת יוֹתֵר מִן הָרָאוּי, וְזֶה מוֹלִיד אַהֲבָה [כַּמַּיִם הַפָּנִים וְגוֹמֵר].

And regarding these it does not say "if they do not do so, they incur penalty," since they do not know as much, their gathering being generous beyond expectation, which begets love ["as in water face reflects face, etc."].
וּ"מַקְשִׁיבִים" הַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יוֹדֵעַ חָכְמָה וַחֲבֵירוֹ מְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ מַה שֶּׁהוּא יוֹדֵעַ, דְּהַקְשָׁבָה פֵּירוּשׁ קַבָּלָה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שְׁמִיעָה.
And "those who listen" (makshivim) means each possesses wisdom and his fellow receives what he knows, for listening denotes receptive acceptance, unlike mere hearing.

אֲבָל אֵין חִדּוּשִׁין, דְּהַיְינוּ בִּינָה, נוֹלָד בֵּינֵיהֶם, רַק עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פה:): עָבֵידְנָא דְּלָא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יִגְמוֹר לַחֲבֵירוֹ סִדְרוֹ;
But no novel insights (Binah) are born between them, functioning like Rabbi Chiya in Bava Metzia 85b: "I act so that Torah is not forgotten," teaching each other their orders;
וְזֶהוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹמֵעַ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁמִּתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדֵיהֶם, שֶׁזֶּה פֵּירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְקוֹלָן.
and this is "the Holy One listens, etc.," that it endures in their hand, which is the meaning of God listening to their voice.
כִּי אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ זְמַן לוֹמַר שֶׁאָז שָׁמַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִסְתַּלְּקָה הַשְּׁמִיעָה, רַק שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹמֵעַ לְעוֹלָם;
For with the Blessed Name time does not apply, to say He heard then and ceased hearing later, but He hears eternally;
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי קוֹלָן קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, קסח עַמּוּד ב) דְּקָלִין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וּצְלוֹתָא לָא אִתְאֲבִידוּ לְעָלְמִין, וְהַיְינוּ דְּלָא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח.
meaning their voice is permanently established, as written in Zohar III:168b that voices of Torah and prayer are never lost, ensuring Torah is not forgotten.

וּבְאֵלּוּ "אִם אֵין עוֹשִׂין וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁמְּחוּיָּיבִין בְּכָךְ מֵאַחַר שֶׁבְּיָדָן לְקַיֵּים הַשְּׁכִינָה, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח אוֹתוֹ קוֹל שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹמְעוֹ תָּמִיד, וְחַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְהֵיפֶךְ גּוֹרֵם וְכוּלֵי.

And regarding these: "if they do not do so, etc.," they are held accountable, since it is in their power to sustain the Shechinah so that voice is never forgotten, while neglecting it causes the reverse.
וְכָל זֶה עֲדַיִן מַדְרֵגַת "בִּתִּי", שֶׁאֵין חִדּוּשִׁין בֵּינֵיהֶם, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְיִרְאָה רַק לְאַהֲבָה, וְכֵן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹהֲבָן וְשׁוֹמְעָן.
And all this remains the level of "My daughter," where there are no innovations between them, requiring love rather than fear, and so the Holy One loves them and listens to them.

וּשְׁנֵי הָאֲחֵרִים הֵם כְּשֶׁמְּחַדְּשִׁין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְאָז נִקְרָא "יִרְאֵי ה'", וְהֵם שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת דְּנֹעַם וְחוֹבְלִים הַנִּדְרָשׁ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כד.) עַל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבָבֶל.

The other two levels apply when they innovate insights, termed "they that fear Hashem," reflecting the two rungs of "Graciousness" (No'am) and "Binders" (Chovlim) expounded in Sanhedrin 24a concerning scholars of the Land of Israel and Babylonia.
וְהַנּוֹחִין זֶה נֹעַם, וְאֵלּוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם נִקְרְאוּ יִרְאֵי ה' שֶׁאֵינָם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַקְשִׁיב – פֵּירוּשׁ מְקַבֵּל מַה שֶּׁהֵם גּוֹזְרִים,
And the gentle ones embody Graciousness, both called those who fear Hashem, not being sharp opposites, and the Holy One hearkens (makshiv)—meaning He accepts what they decree,
דְּזֶה נִקְרָא "אֲחוֹתִי", שֶׁחִדּוּשִׁים שֶׁלָּהֶם מְקוּבָּלִים וּמוּסְכָּמִים לְמַעְלָה, וּבִתְנַאי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם יִרְאֵי ה'.
which is termed "My sister," where their insights are accepted and consented to Above, provided both fear Hashem.

וְעִיקַּר הַרְבָּצַת תּוֹרָה הָיְתָה בְּבָבֶל כִּדְאִיתָא בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (קו.), כִּי רִבּוּי הַתַּלְמִידִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַפִּלְפּוּל וְהַחִידּוּד שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת וְהַהֲפָכִין, וְזֶהוּ הַמְּחַדְּדִין, עַל יְדֵי זֶה עוֹלִין לִגְדוּלָּה דְּהַיְינוּ הַעֲמָדַת תַּלְמִידִים.

And the primary dissemination of Torah took place in Babylonia (Ketubot 106a), for multiplying students occurs through dialectic (pilpul) and sharpening born of dispute and opposing views, and this is "those who sharpen," through which they rise to greatness by raising students.

כִּי שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים עַל כָּרְחֲךָ צְרִיכִין לְאֶמְצָעִי וְדַעַת הַמְחַבֵּר, וְזֶה נִקְרָא "וַהֲדָרְךָ", וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קמה:) שֶׁתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל עוֹשִׂין צִיצִין וּפְרָחִים לַתּוֹרָה.
For two opposites perforce require a harmonizing middle and uniting Da'at, termed "your majesty" (hadarekha), as in Shabbat 145b that scholars in Babylonia craft ornaments and blossoms for the Torah.

וּבַזֹּהַר נִקְרָא פִּלְפּוּל הַתַּלְמוּד קִשּׁוּטֵי כַּלָּה שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַהֶדֶר בֶּאֱמֶת, וּלְכָךְ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּבָבֶל מְצוּיָּינִין כִּדְאִיתָא (שָׁם), וּפֵירוּשׁ שֶׁאֵינָן בְּנֵי מְקוֹמָן, שֶׁהַחִידּוּד מוֹצִיאוֹ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ.

And in the Zohar Talmudic pilpul is called the bridal adornments, which is true majesty, which is why Babylonian scholars were distinguished (metzuyanim, ibid.), meaning not remaining confined to their place, for sharpening moves one beyond his initial boundary.
כִּי נוֹחִין בְּיִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת הֲרֵי זֶה עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה יב:): "שַׁאֲנַן מוֹאָב וְגוֹמֵר" (יִרְמְיָה מח, יא), וּבַגּוֹלָה וְגוֹמֵר דְּיָתְבֵי בְּדוּכְתַּיְיהוּ;
For being gentle in settled composure reflects Megillah 12b: "Moab has been at ease from his youth" (Jeremiah 48:11), "…nor has he gone into exile" (ibid.), for they stayed in their place;
אֲבָל הַחִידּוּד מַרְחִיב הַדְּרוּשׁ וּמַרְחִיקוֹ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְצוּיָּינִין,
but sharpening broadens exposition and propels it far from its origin, making them distinguished,
וְזֶה גּוֹרֵם לְגַסּוּת הָרוּחַ וּלְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, דְּהַיְינוּ עַל מְנָת שֶׁיִּקְרָאוּהוּ רַבִּי כִּדְאִיתָא בִּנְדָרִים (סב.),
which risks haughtiness and learning not for its own sake—in order to be called Rabbi (Nedarim 62a)—
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (מט:) דְּגַסּוּת לְבָבֶל נָחִית, לָכֵן הִתְנוּ בָּזֶה "עַל דְּבַר אֱמֶת וְעַנְוָה צֶדֶק" (תְּהִלִּים מה, ה).
which is why Kiddushin 49b states that arrogance descended to Babylonia, leading the verse to condition: "in behalf of truth, humility, and righteousness" (Psalms 45:5).
וְאָז זוֹכִין לִימִין הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה וְתַכְלִית הַתּוֹרָה עַד שֶׁעוֹלֶה לִגְדוּלָּה.
And then they merit the right hand of Torah, the ultimate pinnacle of Torah study until one rises to greatness.
וְכָל אֵלּוּ אַרְבַּע מַדְרֵגוֹת הֵם בְּכָל תַּלְמִיד מִן עֵת דְּלֵית לֵיהּ רַבָּה בְּמָתָא, שֶׁנִּפְטַר הָרַב וּמִתְחַבֵּר לַחֲבֵירִים, עַד שֶׁעוֹלֶה לִגְדוּלָּה:
And all these four levels unfold for every disciple from the time he has no master in town—the master having passed away and he bonds with colleagues—until he ascends to greatness.

paragraphs.text: Why the effort to gather has value of its own

rich.text: Why the effort to gather has value of its own

paragraphs.text: Limited attainment does not cancel the value of longing and making an effort to come to Torah.

rich.text: Limited attainment does not cancel the value of longing and making an effort to come to Torah.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 1:31: “The matter is that Avraham's level was like the Sages' teaching: ‘The reward of the gathering is for the crowding; the reward of the discourse is for hurrying.’ What is chiefly precious in this world is longing and willingness to serve Hashem. It is precious beyond the action itself, even when the action is small. As King Shlomo said, ‘Vanity of vanities, Kohelet said’; yet this breath sustains and establishes the world. The Zohar says that this book was established upon seven breaths, and the world stands upon them. Hashem's principal concern with created beings in this world is their longing, willingness, and effort.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov uses the same sayings about the reward for hurrying and crowding to learn. It locates their preciousness in the longing and effort of the person, even when the immediate attainment is small. This explains why the siman's least advanced gathering is still beloved, while leaving intact its distinctions among the understanding, responsibilities, and creative work of the four kinds of companions.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 25:5: “Homiletically, the passage is expounded as referring to the Oral Torah. These are “the wars of Hashem” conducted through a book of Torah. As the Sages said (Kiddushin 30b), even a father and son, or a teacher and student, studying Torah at one gate become enemies of one another, yet they do not leave until they love one another, as it says, “Et Vahev in Suphah,” and so forth. Afterward they sang concerning the well, which alludes to the Oral Torah.”

rich.text: : “Homiletically, the passage is expounded as referring to the Oral Torah. These are “the wars of Hashem” conducted through a book of Torah. As the Sages said (Kiddushin 30b), even a father and son, or a teacher and student, studying Torah at one gate become enemies of one another, yet they do not leave until they love one another, as it says, “Et Vahev in Suphah,” and so forth. Afterward they sang concerning the well, which alludes to the Oral Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah describes father and son, or rebbe and talmid, becoming opponents in Torah and remaining together until love emerges. This clarifies the connecting da’at required in the present siman’s account of sharpened disagreement. The disagreement can move each beyond his original limit, but its fruit is not the perpetuation of hostility. The siman’s requirements of truth, humility, and righteousness preserve the conditions in which such a dispute builds Torah and raises students.

sections.en: There Are Two Distinct Modes of Divine Perception

p: [קפט] שְׁנֵי מִינֵי הַשָּׂגוֹת אֱלֹהוּת יֵשׁ:
There are two distinct modes of divine perception:
א' – מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה מַכִּיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא, וְזֶה נִקְרָא "מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית";
First, through Creation one recognizes that there is a Creator, which is termed the "Work of Creation" (Ma'aseh Bereishit);
ב' – מִצַּד הַהַנְהָגָה, וְזֶה נִקְרָא "מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה" – אֵיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹכֵב עַל הַבְּרוּאִים.
Second, through Providential Governance, which is termed the "Work of the Chariot" (Ma'aseh Merkavah)—how the Blessed Name rides upon and directs all created beings.
וְהֵם שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת דִּרְאִיָּה וִידִיעָה שֶׁל אָבוֹת וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַנִּזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר וָאֵרָא (כג עַמּוּד א, עַיֵּין שָׁם),
And these reflect the two spiritual rungs of "Vision" and "Knowing" pertaining to the Patriarchs and to Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, mentioned in Zohar Va'era (23a, see there):

שֶׁהָאָבוֹת הִשִּׂיגוּ מִצַּד הַבְּרוּאִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה לט) בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: רָאָה בִּירָה דּוֹלֶקֶת וְכוּלֵי,

for the Patriarchs perceived through the medium of creations, as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishit Rabbah 39:1) concerning our father Abraham, peace be upon him: he saw a palace lit up, etc.,
וְהִיא נִקְרֵאת רְאִיָּה דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא;
and this is called a manifest, revealed vision (re'iyah de-itgalya);
וְלָכֵן נִזְכַּר אוֹתוֹ שֵׁם אֶצְלָם שָׁם בַּכָּתוּב, הַמּוֹרֶה שֶׁאָמַר לְעוֹלָמוֹ "דַּי" כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה יב.),
and therefore that specific divine Name (El Shaddai) is mentioned regarding them in Scripture, which indicates that He said to His world "Enough" (Dai), as our Sages taught (Chagigah 12a),
וּפֵירֵשׁ הָרַבִּי רַבִּי בּוּנִים זְצוֹקַ"ל: שֶׁיֵּשׁ דַּי בִּבְרִיאָה זוֹ לְהַכִּיר אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יָדוֹ
and the Rebbe Reb Bunim of blessed memory explained: that there is enough within this physical Creation to recognize His Godliness through it
[וְאוֹתוֹ שֵׁם מוֹעִיל גַּם כֵּן לְבָנִים כַּנּוֹדָע, כִּי זֶה מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה, כִּי לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ.
[and that Name is likewise efficacious for children, for this belongs to Creation, seeing that He did not create the world in vain.
וְכֵן תּוֹאַר "אָב" הוּא שֵׁם טָפֵל לְבֵן, וְזוֹ הַשָּׂגַת אֲבוֹת הָעוֹלָם;
And likewise the title "Father" is an appellation relative to a son, and this was the comprehension of the Patriarchs of the world;
אֲבָל תּוֹאַר "רַב" טָפֵל לְתַלְמִיד, וְזֶהוּ הַשָּׂגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל].
but the title "Master/Teacher" is relative to a disciple, and this was the comprehension of Moses, the teacher of Israel].
וִידִיעָה הוּא בַּהַנְהָגָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הוֹדִעֵנִי נָא אֶת דְּרָכֶךָ" (שְׁמוֹת לג, יג), וְלֹא אִתְגַּלְיָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְחַנֹּתִי אֶת אֲשֶׁר אָחֹן" וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם, יט),

And "Knowing" pertains to Providential Governance, as written: "Show me now Your way" (Exodus 33:13), which is unrevealed, as written: "and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, etc." (ibid. 33:19),
וְלֹא הוֹדִיעוֹ, רַק יָדַע דִּשְׁמוֹ הֲוָיָ"ה – הוֹוֶה וּמְהַוֶּוה הַכֹּל, וְהָיָה הוֹוֶה וְיִהְיֶה,
wherein He did not disclose the precise reason, yet Moses knew that His Name Havayah denotes that He was, is, will be, and continuously brings everything into being,
דְּהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם כֵּן עַכְשָׁו, דְּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת מַחֲשָׁבָה תְּפִיסָה;
which means that just as before the world was created, so is He now—which no mortal thought can grasp;
וְזֶהוּ הַדַּעַת מַדְרֵגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁהוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
and this is Da'at, the level of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who encompasses all souls of Torah scholars in Israel, and this perception is accessible only to a Torah scholar.
אֲבָל הַשָּׂגַת הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁל הָאָבוֹת, שֶׁהֵם כּוֹלְלִים כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת כֻּלָּם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, זֶה אֶפְשָׁר לְכָל אֶחָד, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, לְהַשִּׂיג,
However, the perception of Vision of the Patriarchs, who encompass all souls of Israel without exception, can be attained by anyone, even one who is not a scholar,
שֶׁהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ מוּטְבַּעַת בּוֹ מֵאֲבוֹתָיו מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב
for this comprehension is ingrained in him from his forefathers because he descends from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
[וְדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר שֶׁנִּקְרָא דּוֹר דֵּעָה: "רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה יְחֶזְקֵאל",
[and the Generation of the Wilderness, termed a generation of knowledge: "a maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see,"
דְּהַיְינוּ מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה, שֶׁהָיוּ כֻּלָּם מוּכָנִים לְדֵעָה וּלְמַדְרֵגַת הַדַּעַת דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַפַּרְנָס הַכּוֹלְלָן].
meaning the Work of the Chariot, because they were all primed for Da'at and the stature of Moses, the leader who encompassed them].
וְגַם לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם בְּעִתּוֹת הַהֶעְלֵם יוּכַל לְהִתְחַזֵּק עַל כָּל פָּנִים בְּהַשָּׂגָה זוֹ שֶׁמּוֹרָשָׁה לוֹ מֵהָאָבוֹת,
And a Torah scholar as well, in times of spiritual concealment, can at least fortify himself with this baseline perception inherited from the Patriarchs,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהִלְכוֹת יְסוֹדֵי הַתּוֹרָה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ב): כֵּיצַד הִיא הַדֶּרֶךְ לְאַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה? כְּשֶׁיָּשִׂים הָאָדָם אֶל לִבּוֹ וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם:
in line with Maimonides in Hilkhot Yesodei HaTorah (2:2): What is the path to love and fear Him? When a person contemplates His wondrous creations, etc., see there.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 1: “"And Hashem said to Avram: Go for yourself from your land, etc." (Genesis 12:1). It is written (Isaiah 44:3): "For I will pour water upon the thirsty, and streams upon the dry land"; when Avraham our Father, peace be upon him, began to seek and search after the root of his true life, after he understood that all delights of this world cannot be termed authentic life, for all worldly delight serves merely to remove afflictions and impediments; and after all anxieties are eliminated, what is the very substance of life for which the world was created? Concerning this Hashem, blessed be He, said to him: "Go for yourself"—meaning, unto your very self, for in truth, all mundane matters of this world cannot be termed life, and the core of life you will find within yourself: (Isaiah 41:16) "And you shall rejoice in Hashem, and shall glory in the Holy One of Israel"—this is the essence of life.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach describes Avraham discovering the insufficiency of worldly satisfactions and then receiving the personal call “Go to yourself.” This gives a concrete movement between the two kinds of recognition discussed here: the question arises within reflection on the world, while the answer directs a particular person toward the life Hashem asks of him.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 39:1: ‘‘Hashem said to Avram: Go forth from your land,’ and so forth (Genesis 12:1). Rabbi Yitzchak opened: ‘Listen, daughter, and see; incline your ear, and forget your people and your father’s house’ (Psalms 45:11). Rabbi Yitzchak said: This is a parable of someone traveling from place to place who saw a palace alight. He said: ‘Can it be that this palace has no one directing it?’ The owner of the palace looked out at him and said: ‘I am the owner of the palace.’ So, because our father Abraham was saying, ‘Can it be that this world has no one directing it?’ the Holy One, blessed be He, looked out at him and said: ‘I am the owner of the world.’ ‘The king will desire your beauty, for he is your master’ (Psalms 45:12). ‘The king will desire your beauty’—to make you beautiful in the world. ‘Bow down to him’ (Psalms 45:12). Thus: ‘Hashem said to Avram.’’

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 12a:15: “Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: When the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, it kept expanding like two balls of warp thread unwinding, until the Holy One, blessed be He, rebuked it and brought it to a halt, as it is said: ‘The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke.’ This is what Reish Lakish said: What is the meaning of the verse, ‘I am El Shaddai’? I am the One who said to the world: ‘Enough’—dai. Reish Lakish said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, created the sea, it kept expanding until the Holy One, blessed be He, rebuked it and dried it up, as it is said: ‘He rebukes the sea and dries it up, and He makes all the rivers dry.’”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vaera 3:1: “It is said in the name of our master Rabbi Bunim, of blessed memory, that he explained “He said to His world: Enough” to mean that this would suffice for the creature to recognize His blessed kingship. The intended purpose of creation is that a person should recognize His kingship, and one can learn from everything that was created. As stated in Eruvin 100b: Had Torah not been given, we would have learned modesty from the cat, the avoidance of theft from the ant, and sexual fidelity from the dove, and so forth. The world continued expanding so that people could recognize His kingship more fully, until the Holy One, blessed be He, told it that no further expansion was needed: the creation already made was sufficient to recognize the glory of His blessed kingship.”

sections.en: The Eye and the Heart Are the Brokers of Sin

p: [קצ] הָעַיִן וְהַלֵּב הֵם סַרְסוּרֵי הָעֲבֵירָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּבְרָכוֹת (פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה ה), וְכֵן סַרְסוּרִים לְטוֹב,
The eye and the heart are the brokers of sin, as stated in the Yerushalmi (Berakhot 1:5), and they are likewise brokers for good,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: אִם אַתְּ יָהֵיב עֵינָא וְלִבָּא לִי, אֲנָא וְכוּלֵי.
as stated there: If you give your eye and your heart to Me, I know that you are Mine.
וְהֵם שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת דִּרְאִיָּה וִידִיעָה הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל אוֹת קפ"ט.
And they correspond to the two rungs of Vision and Knowing mentioned above in Section 189.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "שְׁלַח אוֹרְךָ וַאֲמִתְּךָ הֵמָּה יַנְחוּנִי" (תְּהִלִּים מג, ג), דְּעִיקַּר הָרְאִיָּה הוּא הָאוֹר.
And concerning this Scripture says: "Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me" (Psalms 43:3), for the core of vision is light.
וְהֵם מַדְרֵגַת יַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף: "תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב" (מִיכָה ז, כ), וְ"אוֹר זָרֻעַ לַצַּדִּיק" (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא);
And these are the rungs of Jacob and Joseph: "You give truth to Jacob" (Micah 7:20), and "Light is sown for the righteous (tzadik / Joseph)" (Psalms 97:11);
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ בְּיוֹסֵף (בְּרָכוֹת כ.): עַיִן שֶׁלֹּא וְכוּלֵי, אֵין עַיִן הָרָע וְכוּלֵי.
which is why they said of Joseph (Berakhot 20a): the eye that refused to gaze upon what is not his, the evil eye has no dominion over it.
וְהוּא אָמַר בַּשְּׁבָטִים "נוֹתְנִין עֵינֵיהֶם וְכוּלֵי", וְסָבוּר דְּשׁוּרְיָינָא דְּעֵינָא בְּלִבָּא תַּלְיָא כִּדְאִיתָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כח:),
And Joseph suspected of his brothers that they cast their eyes on pagan women, reasoning that the sinews of the eye depend on the heart (Avodah Zarah 28b),
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית כד.): כַּלָּה שֶׁעֵינֶיהָ וְכוּלֵי כָּל גּוּפָהּ וְכוּלֵי.
and as they said (Ta'anit 24a): a bride whose eyes are beautiful, her entire body requires no examination.
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת הָעִיקָּר הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מִכָּל מִשְׁמָר נְצֹר לִבֶּךָ כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כג), שֶׁבּוֹ עִיקַּר הַחַיּוּת וְהַדְּבֵיקוּת בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים,

Yet in truth the heart is paramount, as written: "Above all that you guard, protect your heart, for out of it are the issues of life" (Proverbs 4:23), for in it resides the vital core of cleaving unto the living God,
וּבָזֶה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה וְכֻלּוֹ זֶרַע אֱמֶת.
and in this our father Jacob, peace be upon him, had a bed that was whole and entirely seed of truth.
וּבִלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים: "עַיִן יָפָה" וְ"עַיִן טוֹבָה" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר נְדִיבוּת הַלֵּב וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַנֵּא,
And in the language of the Sages, a "generous eye" and a "good eye" denote benevolence of the heart and freedom from envy,
וְכֵן בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: "טוֹב עַיִן הוּא יְבֹרָךְ כִּי נָתַן מִלַּחְמוֹ לַדָּל" (מִשְׁלֵי כב, ט).
and so in Scripture: "He that has a bountiful eye shall be blessed, for he gives of his bread to the poor" (Proverbs 22:9).
וְהַהִיפּוּךְ: עַיִן רָעָה, וּבִלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "רַע עַיִן" (שָׁם כג, ו).
And the opposite is an evil eye, termed in Scripture "evil of eye" (ibid. 23:6).
וְזֶה הַחִסָּרוֹן הוּא בְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף דַּיְיקָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אֶפְרַיִם לֹא יְקַנֵּא אֶת יְהוּדָה" (יְשַׁעְיָה יא, יג),
And this failing is found specifically in the seed of Joseph, as written: "Ephraim shall not envy Judah" (Isaiah 11:13),

כִּי שׁוֹרֶשׁ יוֹסֵף יְרֵא חֵטְא, שֶׁזֶּהוּ שְׁמִירַת הָעַיִן, וְהוּא אוֹתִיּוֹת רְאִיָּ"ה, כְּטַעַם: מַחֲוֵי לְהוּ יִצְחָק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ (שַׁבָּת פט:), שֶׁזֶּה מִכֹּחַ יִצְחָק וּמִמִּדָּתוֹ.

for the root of Joseph is fear of sin, which is guarding the eye, sharing the letters of re'iyah (vision), reflecting: Isaac points out the Holy One to their eyes (Shabbat 89b), stemming from Isaac's power of Gevurah.
וְהַנְּדִיבוּת הוּא מִמִּדַּת הָאַהֲבָה: "חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם" (מִיכָה ז, כ), שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ הַהֵיפֶךְ,
And generosity derives from love—"mercy to Abraham" (Micah 7:20)—which is the direct opposite,
וְאִם כֵּן אַדְּרַבָּה, הֵם עֵינֵיהֶם יָפוֹת וּבַעֲלֵי עַיִן טוֹבָה יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ:
so on the contrary, they [the brothers] have beautiful eyes and a better eye than he [Joseph].

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Yonah on Proverbs 23:26: ““My son, give Me your heart, and let your eyes keep My ways.” “To Me”: to fear and love Me. The heart is desire and longing. He therefore warns a person to give the whole heart to Him, blessed be He, for one is obliged to long and desire only for the service of God, and to make one’s worldly desires solely means of serving God. “Let your eyes keep My ways”: the commandments and good deeds.”

paragraphs.text: The Chanukah passage joins care over sight and thought with trust that Hashem will help complete the repair.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 20:6: “This is what is hinted at by placing “but there were snakes and scorpions in it” next to the first teaching about the Chanukah lamp. The essential point of the commandment is seeing, through which one merits the quality of “light sown for the righteous,” repairing the blemish of the covenant as mentioned above. This statement follows it so that a person will not rely upon the thought that everything has already been repaired. Rather, one should know that Chanukah is a preparation and initiation into the “light sown for the righteous,” through which one may merit the completeness of the repair during the days of Shovavim. The essential thing is to guard oneself in thought and sight. This is indicated by this month’s being created with the letter ayin: the preparation for repair through guarding the eyes. As it says, “Do not stray … after your eyes,” which Berakhot 12b explains as thoughts of transgression. Guarding the eyes saves one from such thoughts, as Avodah Zarah 28b says, “The vessels of the eye are attached to the chambers of the heart.” Every year, in these seasons, repair and clarification are brought about in the souls of Israel, with God’s help. When a person takes repair to heart, let him place his trust in God that he will be completely repaired, as is said of Joseph in Genesis Rabbah 89: “‘Happy is the man who makes the Lord his trust’—this is Joseph.””

When a person takes repair to heart, let him place his trust in God that he will be completely repaired, as is said of Joseph in Genesis Rabbah 89: “‘Happy is the man who makes the Lord his trust’—this is Joseph.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah uses the same connection between the eye and the heart, but stresses that a first illumination is preparation rather than proof that the entire task is finished. This develops the opening of the present siman, where both powers can become brokers for good. It also helps preserve the siman’s broader demand: guarding sight is essential, while a good eye ultimately includes a generous heart free of envy. The bodily guard and the heart’s positive direction belong together.

This develops the siman's demand that the repair of the eye reach the generous heart as well. The source describes that final disclosure; it does not authorize an observer now to presume the inward standing that only Hashem reveals.

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:23:1: “This is what they said in Bava Kamma 97a: The coin of Abraham our patriarch had an old man and an old woman on one side, and a young man and a maiden on the other. A coin is something with which one acquires all necessities. Likewise, love and fear are the parents that bring forth all holy qualities, corresponding to jealousy and desire on the side of impurity. Love is familiar in youth, unlike old age: “Desire fails.” As is known, Solomon said the Song of Songs in his youth—the intensity of love—and Ecclesiastes in his old age—the intensity of fear. sections.en: In Worldly Decency (Derekh Eretz), Even Gentiles Are Vigilant

p: [קצא] דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ גַּם הַגּוֹיִם זְהִירִים וְיוֹתֵר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי כִּבּוּד אָב וָאֵם זֶהוּ מִמִּדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
In worldly decency (derekh eretz), even gentiles are vigilant, and seemingly more so than Israel, for honoring parents is of the essence of derekh eretz,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין לא.): כֵּיוָן שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ "כַּבֵּד", הוֹדוּ אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לַדִּבְּרוֹת;
as stated in Kiddushin 31a: once they heard "Honor your father and your mother," the nations conceded to the commandments;
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סה) דְּעֵשָׂו נִזְהָר בּוֹ הַרְבֵּה, וְאָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: אֲנִי וְכוּלֵי וְלֹא הִגַּעְתִּי וְכוּלֵי.

and our Sages stated (Bereishit Rabbah 65) that Esau was exceedingly meticulous in it, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel remarking: I served my father, yet never reached even a fraction of Esau's honor to his father.
רַק בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין זֶה דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ כְּלָל, כִּי עִיקַּר הַדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הַיְינוּ הַהַכָּרָה בְּכָל עִנְיְנֵי הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
But in truth, that is not authentic derekh eretz at all, for true derekh eretz is the recognition across all worldly matters that everything is from the Blessed Name,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב.) עַל בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן: עֲשָׂאָן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּהִלְכוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן הַיְינוּ הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵכִין מָזוֹן לְכָל חָי.
as stated in Berakhot 22a regarding Grace after Meals, that Rabbi Yehudah categorized it like laws of derekh eretz, Grace being the recognition that Hashem prepares food for all living creatures.

וּ"בוּר" הוּא שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שָׂדֶה בּוּרָה, וְלֹא "שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרֲכוֹ ה'" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כז) דְּהַיְינוּ חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין, דְּהוּא מִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ זְרִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ רֵיקָנִין שֶׁבָּהּ מְלֵאִים מִצְווֹת וְהַכָּרָה בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם בֶּאֱמוּנָה שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;

And a boor (bur) is one deficient in derekh eretz, like an uncultivated field (sadeh burah), unlike the "field which Hashem has blessed" (Genesis 27:27)—the holy apple orchard, the attribute of Knesset Yisrael bearing the seed of Hashem, whose empty ones are filled with mitzvot and faith that all is from Hashem;
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "עַם הָאָרֶץ", שֶׁהוּא מִכְּלַל הָאָרֶץ הַיְדוּעָה וְעוֹסֵק בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ.
and this is called an am ha'aretz (person of the land), being part of the sacred land and engaged in holy derekh eretz.
אֲבָל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ דְּאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִצַּד הַהַכָּרָה דַּ"לה' הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ", אֵין זֶה דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ כְּלָל.
But the derekh eretz of the nations, not deriving from acknowledging that "the earth is Hashem's and the fullness thereof," is not derekh eretz at all.

וְנִרְאֶה דִּלְכָךְ בְּמַכַּת עָרוֹב נֶאֱמַר: "וְהִפְלֵיתִי" (שְׁמוֹת ח, יח), וְכֵן בְּדֶבֶר: "וְהִפְלָה" (שָׁם ט, ד), וּבִשְׁאָר מַכּוֹת לֹא נִזְכַּר כְּלָל, וּבְבָרָד נֶאֱמַר סְתָם שֶׁבְּגֹשֶׁן לֹא הָיָה, בְּלֹא "וְהִפְלָה".

And it seems that for this reason, regarding the plague of wild beasts (arov) Scripture says: "And I will set apart (ve-hifleiti)" (Exodus 8:18), and likewise in pestilence: "and Hashem shall sever (ve-hiflah)" (ibid. 9:4), whereas in other plagues it is omitted, and in hail it merely states that in Goshen there was none, without ve-hiflah.

דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר: עָרוֹב נֶגֶד "כַּבֵּד" בַּדִּבְּרוֹת שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַפְלֶה וּמְבָרֵר שֶׁאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים אֵינָן בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ כְּלָל כְּמוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
For arov corresponds to "Honor your father" among the Ten Commandments, which is derekh eretz, and Hashem severed and clarified that the gentiles possess no authentic derekh eretz like Israel.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קנא:): אֵין חַיָּה רָעָה וְכוּלֵי עַד שֶׁנִּדְמֶה כִּבְהֵמָה;
And they said in Shabbat 151b: a wild beast has no dominion over a man unless he appears to it like an animal;
וּמִי שֶׁהוּא בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ יֵשׁ לוֹ צוּרַת אָדָם, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בּוּר אֵינוֹ מִן הַיִּשּׁוּב וְנִדְמֶה כִּבְהֵמָה, עַל זֶה בָּא מַכַּת עָרוֹב.
and one who possesses true derekh eretz bears the divine form of man, whereas a boor belongs not to civilized humanity and resembles an animal, against which the plague of beasts came.
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ: "כִּי אֲנִי ה' בְּקֶרֶב הָאָרֶץ" (שְׁמוֹת ח, יח), שֶׁזֶּהוּ אֲמִיתַּת מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ – שֶׁבְּהַנְהָגַת הָאָרֶץ "אֲנִי ה'" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
Therefore regarding arov it is stated: "that I am Hashem in the midst of the earth" (Exodus 8:18), which is the essence of derekh eretz—that in the mundane affairs of earth, I am Hashem

[וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר "בְּקֶרֶב", כִּי בַּקְּרָבַיִם הוּא הַנְהָגַת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ; וְעוֹד, דְּעַל יְדֵי מַאֲכָלוֹת אֲסוּרוֹת נִדְמֶה לִבְהֵמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קכה עַמּוּד ב) עַל נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר, וְדָנִיֵּאל שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגָּאַל בְּפַת בַּג וְגוֹמֵר נִיצּוֹל מֵאֲרָיוֹת].

[and 'in the midst' (be-kerev) hints to the internal organs (keravayim) where worldly digestion takes place; furthermore, through forbidden foods one resembles a beast, as in Zohar II:125b on Nebuchadnezzar, while Daniel who refused defilement with the king's meat was saved from the lions].
וְדֶבֶר נֶגֶד "לֹא תִרְצַח", מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה
And pestilence (dever) corresponds to "You shall not murder," measure for measure
[וּשְׁחִין נֶגֶד "לֹא תִנְאָף", לְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ מְיַפִּין עַצְמָן, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְשִׂפַּח וְגוֹמֵר"].
[and boils (shechin) corresponds to "You shall not commit adultery," because they adorned their flesh for lust, matching "and Hashem will smite with a scab, etc."].

וְיָדוּעַ דְּ"לֹא תִרְצַח" וְ"לֹא תִנְאָף" שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים, וּמִצְרַיִם שְׁטוּפֵי זִמָּה, אֲבָל הֵם בִּכְלַל יִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם וּזְהִירִים מִ"לֹּא תִרְצַח", וְהָיָה גַּם בָּזֶה טַעֲנָה, לָכֵן אָמַר "וְהִפְלָה וְגוֹמֵר";

And it is known that "Do not murder" and "Do not commit adultery" are two opposites, and Egypt was steeped in licentiousness yet respected civil order avoiding murder; so there was room for a challenge, which is why Scripture stated "and Hashem shall sever";

וְזֶהוּ פֶּלֶא, כְּשֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִים בָּזֶה וְאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר לְעֵין אָדָם, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַמַּבְדִּיל מִצַּד הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת: שֶׁזֶּה נִזְהָר בִּשְׁבִיל כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם לְבַד, אֲבָל זֶה מִצַּד אַהֲבָתוֹ הָעוֹלָם וְחָפֵץ בְּיִשּׁוּב הָאָרֶץ, וְאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא הָאָרֶץ – אֵין זֶה קָרוּי בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ כְּלָל:

and this is a wondrous miracle (pela), where both appear equal to human eyes, yet the Blessed Name separates through the hidden realm: the Jew refrains solely for the honor of Heaven, while the gentile refrains out of civic attachment to worldly order, failing to recognize that Hashem created the earth—which is not termed derekh eretz at all.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 65:16: ““Rebecca took the fine garments of Esau, her elder son, that were with her in the house, and she dressed Jacob her younger son” (Genesis 27:15). “Rebecca took the fine [haḥamudot] garments of Esau, her elder son” – what he had coveted [sheḥamad] from Nimrod, and he killed him and took them. That is what is written: “The wicked covets the prey of the evil” (Proverbs 12:12). “That were with her in the house” – in them he would attend his father. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: I attended my father all my days, and I did not attend him one one-hundredth of what Esau attended his father. When I would attend my father, I attended him with dirty garments, but when I would go out on the road, I would go out with clean garments. But Esau, when he would attend his father, he would attend him only with royal garments. He said: ‘It is not in keeping with Father’s honor to attend him in anything other than royal garments.’ That is what is written: “That were with her in the house.” How many wives did he [Esau] have, and you say: “That were with her in the house”? It is because he [Esau] knew what their [his wives’] actions were. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: There was an incident involving a group of scoundrels in that Kefar Ḥatya, who were accustomed to eat and drink in the synagogue every Shabbat eve. When they finished eating they would take the bones and cast them on the scribe. One of them was dying; they said to him: ‘To whom do you wish to entrust your son?’ He said to them: ‘To the scribe.’ But, how many friends did he have, but he said: ‘To the scribe’? It is, rather, that he knew what their actions were, and that the scribe was much better than they were. So, how many wives did he have, and the verse says: “That were with her in the house”? It is because he knew what their actions were.”

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Yonah on Pirkei Avot 2:5:1: “He used to say: A boor does not fear sin, and an unlearned person is not pious. A boor is empty: he has neither Torah nor commandments nor proper conduct expressed in good character. In the Targum, “Let it not become desolate” is rendered “Let it not lie fallow.” It was unnecessary to say that a boor is not pious, since he does not even fear sin: because of his emptiness, he does not know how to guard against transgressions. But an unlearned person participates in society with worthy qualities and has some sound views. He knows how to take care, guards himself against wrongdoing, and can be righteous, doing and fulfilling what he is told he has been commanded.”

In the Targum, “Let it not become desolate” is rendered “Let it not lie fallow.” It was unnecessary to say that a boor is not pious, since he does not even fear sin: because of his emptiness, he does not know how to guard against transgressions. But an unlearned person participates in society with worthy qualities and has some sound views. He knows how to take care, guards himself against wrongdoing, and can be righteous, doing and fulfilling what he is told he has been commanded.”

paragraphs.text: Derech eretz as sustaining an inhabited world

rich.text: Derech eretz as sustaining an inhabited world

paragraphs.text: The term concerns constructive earthly life and has a limit distinct from indulgence.

rich.text: The term concerns constructive earthly life and has a limit distinct from indulgence.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Yisrael Kedoshim 4:2: “Derech eretz is what is needed for the settlement of the land and the world, for ‘He did not create it for emptiness, but formed it to be inhabited’ (Isaiah 45:18). Through it a person's household is settled. This is the meaning of derech eretz everywhere: engaging in the world's settlement, as Berakhot 35b says, ‘Conduct them according to derech eretz,’ and Kiddushin 40b says, ‘Someone who is not involved in derech eretz is not part of the settled world.’ Immersion in desires unnecessary for the world's settlement is the opposite of derech eretz. Avraham our father therefore chose the land of Israel: he saw them weeding and working, unlike those eating, drinking and behaving frivolously, as Bereishit Rabbah 39:8 says. He saw that they had the derech eretz preceding Torah (Vayikra Rabbah 9:3), and understood that this was the land prepared for Torah, for ‘Without derech eretz there is no Torah’ (Avot 3:17).”

It explains the barren-field image and why this conduct can prepare a person for Torah. The siman adds the decisive inward qualification: recognizing Hashem as the source of earthly life.

Explanation: Sod Yesharim develops the encounter between Rabbi Yannai and an unlearned guest into a responsibility of the scholar. The guest's lack of textual knowledge did not erase the Torah point expressed in his conduct. This clarifies why the present siman distinguishes an am haaretz belonging to the cultivated land from a barren field: the positive inward root must be recognized even where the person cannot himself name it.

sections.en: Through Bodily Lust, Fear of Heaven Departs, as Written Regarding the Immersion of One…

p: [קצב] עַל יְדֵי הַתַּאֲוָה מִסְתַּלֵּק הַיִּרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּטְבִילַת בַּעַל קֶרִי בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב.): מִשּׁוּם דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה צָרִיךְ בְּאֵימָה, בְּיִרְאָה וְכוּלֵי.
Through bodily lust, fear of Heaven departs, as stated regarding the immersion of one who experienced seminal emission in Berakhot 22a: because words of Torah require dread, awe, etc.
וְהַתִּיקּוּן לָזֶה – טְבִילָה בְּמַיִם, שֶׁרוֹמְזִים לְמִדַּת הַחֶסֶד וְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת מַהוּ תַּאֲוָתָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל? הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.

And the rectification for this is immersion in water, which alludes to the attribute of Chesed and the love of the Blessed Name, for in truth, what is the authentic desire of Israel? The Holy One, blessed be He.
כִּי הַתַּאֲוָה וְהָאַהֲבָה הֵם הִפּוּךְ הַיִּרְאָה, כִּי הֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים, רַק בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם מִתְיַיחֲדִים.
For desire and love are the opposite of awe, being two polar extremes, which unite solely in the service of the Blessed Name.

וְעַל זֶה רוֹמֵז בִּטְבִילָה, כִּי כָּל כַּוָּנָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁיּוֹצֵאת לַפּוֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הִיא מִתְחַזֶּקֶת, וְהַמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּמַיִם שֶׁמְּקַנְּחִים בֶּאֱמֶת הַלִּכְלוּךְ גַּם כֵּן, וְשׁוֹמֵר מִצְוַת חֲכָמִים לִטְבּוֹל,

And to this immersion alludes, for every intention of the heart actualized in physical deed is reinforced, the deed occurring in water which physically cleanses impurity, and by observing the Sages' ordinance to immerse,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם): גָּדֵר גָּדוֹל וְכוּלֵי, רֵיקָה וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁזֶּה גִּדֵּר בִּפְנֵי הַתַּאֲווֹת שֶׁעוֹצֵר תַּאֲוָתוֹ כְּשֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַיִם לִטְבּוֹל, וְנִמְצָא תַּאֲוָתוֹ רַק כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאָז הוּא אֶחָד עִם הַיִּרְאָה.

as stated there: a great fence, etc., which erected a barrier against lust, restraining desire when water was unavailable to immerse, so that his desire aligns solely with the divine will, uniting with awe.

וַחֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה סִדְּרוּ דִּינֵי טְבִילַת קֶרִי לְעִנְיַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּתְפִלָּה בְּיִחוּד, שֶׁבָּהֶם עִיקָּרֵי הַיִּרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ט:) עַל פָּסוּק "יִירָאוּךָ עִם שָׁמֶשׁ" (תְּהִלִּים עב, ה).
And our Sages formulated the laws of immersion specifically regarding the Shema and the Amidah, which embody the core of awe (Berakhot 9b on "They shall fear You with the sun").
וּבְמַרְגִּיל שֶׁהַתַּאֲוָה מִמֶּנּוּ, צָרִיךְ טְבִילָה, דְּהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן הִתְעוֹרְרוּת מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁהוּא נִכְנָס לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם וּמַמְשִׁיךְ וּמְשַׁעְבֵּד כֹּחוֹתָיו לְמַעְלָה.

And for one who willfully brought on the emission through his own desire, full immersion is required, which is an active awakening from himself, entering into the water to subordinate his faculties to Above.
וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מַיִם שֶׁכָּל גּוּפוֹ עוֹלֶה, כִּי הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב מְעוֹרֵר כָּל הַגּוּף עַד שֶׁכְּלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה גּוֹמְרִין.
Therefore forty se'ah of water are required so that his entire body is submerged, because desire in the heart stirs the entire body until the limbs of action execute it.
אֲבָל לְאֹנְסוֹ, שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁמִּלְּמַעְלָה הִכְנִיסוּ הַתַּאֲוָה בְּלִבּוֹ בְּשֵׁינָה שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ, דַּי גַּם כֵּן בִּנְפִילַת תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין שֶׁהַמַּיִם נוֹפְלִים עָלָיו,
But for an involuntary emission, where desire was seemingly cast into his heart from Above in sleep without his conscious knowledge, pouring nine kav of water upon him suffices,

דְּהַיְינוּ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא לְבַד, שֶׁעוֹלֶה בִּלְבָבוֹ אֵיזֶה אִתְעָרוּתָא לְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁפֶּכֶת עַל פְּנֵי כָּל חֲלַל הַלֵּב, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַעֲמִיק בָּהּ לִהְיוֹת כָּל גּוּפוֹ עוֹלֶה
representing an awakening from Above alone, where an awakening of love for Hashem surges in his heart pouring across the cardiac space, even if he does not immerse his entire body in it

[וְיְעוּיַּן שָׁם חִלּוּק בֵּין חוֹלֶה לְבָרִיא, דְּהַיְינוּ בֵּין תַּלְמִיד חָכָם לְעַם הָאָרֶץ, וּמִשָּׁם בְּאֵרָהּ דְּאֵין לְאֹנְסוֹ אֶלָּא בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ וְלֹא בְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם לִמְסַקְנָא דְּרָבָא].

[and examine there the distinction between the sick and the healthy, meaning between a Torah scholar and a commoner, where Rava's conclusion shows that the nine kav for an involuntary emission apply only to an am ha'aretz, not to a Torah scholar].
וּבִטְּלוּהָ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא דְּאָמַר: "הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ וְכוּלֵי" (יִרְמְיָה כג, כט), פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שׂוֹרְפִין כָּל תַּאֲווֹת רָעוֹת.
And they subsequently annulled Ezra's decree following Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira who declared: "Is not My word like as fire?" (Jeremiah 23:29), meaning words of Torah consume all evil desires.
וְגַם אָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (טז רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א): מַקִּישׁ אֹהָלִים לִנְחָלִים וְכוּלֵי, וְהֵם עַצְמָן דּוּגְמַת טְבִילָה:
And they also said in Berakhot 16a: tents of Torah are compared to flowing rivers, which themselves function like ritual immersion.

paragraphs.text: Desire used according to Hashem's will

rich.text: Desire used according to Hashem's will

paragraphs.text: Surrender of desire means being willing to refrain and then receiving Torah's direction for the same power.

rich.text: Surrender of desire means being willing to refrain and then receiving Torah's direction for the same power.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Soferim 17:1: “This is surrendering all desires to Hashem: even at the utmost force of desire, a person is ready to refrain if it is not according to Hashem's will. As the Midrash says (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7; Midrash Tehillim 2) concerning ‘fenced with roses’: after incurring many expenses and approaching his wife, she says, ‘I saw [blood] red as a rose’; he turns aside. What thorn pricked him? Only words of Torah, soft as a rose. This is the meaning of Shavuot's two loaves being leavened: offering to Hashem the leaven in the dough that holds one back, as Berakhot 17a says. Through this one merits receiving Torah, the seasoning for the inclination (Kiddushin 30b)—using it only according to Hashem's will. Then it is ‘very good,’ as Bereishit Rabbah teaches; and as Berakhot 34a says of leaven, a little is beneficial, while much is harmful.”

This is the meaning of Shavuot's two loaves being leavened: offering to Hashem the leaven in the dough that holds one back, as Berakhot 17a says. Through this one merits receiving Torah, the seasoning for the inclination (Kiddushin 30b)—using it only according to Hashem's will. Then it is ‘very good,’ as Bereishit Rabbah teaches; and as Berakhot 34a says of leaven, a little is beneficial, while much is harmful.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Divrei Soferim explains what it means to hand desire back to Hashem: even at its strongest, the person is willing to refrain when it conflicts with His will. Torah then directs the use of that power. This develops the siman's claim that desire ordered to Hashem's will can be united with awe rather than simply opposed to it.
