paragraphs.text: Torah purifies by encompassing the person

rich.text: Torah purifies by encompassing the person

paragraphs.text: The comparison to immersion concerns Torah becoming established throughout heart and mind.

rich.text: The comparison to immersion concerns Torah becoming established throughout heart and mind.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Shavuot 1:1: “For this reason the tents of Torah were compared to streams that raise a person from impurity to purity. Just as one immerses in water covering the whole body, so words of Torah become permanently established in heart and mind until the person's whole stature is immersed in the waters of knowledge, as the Rambam describes at the end of the laws of immersion pools. This is what the Zohar indicates by purification from the spring of the deep stream. Through the understanding of the heart, in which Torah becomes established, the source from the breadth of the river opens for the purification of the soul.”

Just as one immerses in water covering the whole body, so words of Torah become permanently established in heart and mind until the person's whole stature is immersed in the waters of knowledge, as the Rambam describes at the end of the laws of immersion pools. This is what the Zohar indicates by purification from the spring of the deep stream. Through the understanding of the heart, in which Torah becomes established, the source from the breadth of the river opens for the purification of the soul.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Peri Tzadik develops the tents-and-streams teaching with which this siman concludes. The water surrounds the whole body; correspondingly, Torah becomes continuously established in the heart and mind. This explains the positive content of Torah as purification and connects the outward immersion image to a sustained inward formation. It does not collapse the distinct practical categories discussed earlier in the siman.

sections.en: Even in Words of Torah Hearing Is Legally Equivalent to Speaking

p: [קצג] גַּם בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שׁוֹמֵעַ כְּעוֹנֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת בִּבְרָכוֹת (כ:) גַּבֵּי: כִּדְאַשְׁכְּחַן בְּסִינַי
Even in words of Torah hearing is legally equivalent to speaking, as Tosafot wrote in Berakhot 20b regarding "as we find at Sinai"
[וּמִיהוּ אֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי דִּבְסִינַי הָיָה דִּבּוּר מַמָּשׁ, דְּ"וַיְדַבֵּר ה' וְגוֹמֵר" הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי ה' מוֹצָאוֹת הַפֶּה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
[though I heard that at Sinai there was literal speech, "And Hashem spoke, etc." resounding through the five vocal organs of the mouth of Israel,
וְזֶה בָּרוּר וֶאֱמֶת דְּכָל נְבוּאָה הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי קוֹל הַנָּבִיא עַצְמוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם מה.) בְּקוֹלוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה,
and this is clear and true, that all prophecy manifests through the prophet's own voice, as in Berakhot 45a regarding the voice of Moses,
וְאָז הָיוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל מַדְרֵגַת נְבוּאָה שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ דְּבַר ה' כַּנּוֹדָע, וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרָם].
and then all Israel reached the level of prophecy hearing Hashem's word through their own speech].
וְצָרִיךְ לָזֶה אֵימָה וְיִרְאָה [דְּעַל זֶה הוּא צֹרֶךְ הַטְּבִילָה לְבַעַל קֶרִי] כְּמוֹ בַּמְדַבֵּר בְּעַצְמוֹ;
And for this, dread and awe are required [which is why a ba'al keri must immerse], just as for one who speaks himself;

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּמְהַרְהֵר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, הֲגַם דְּקַיְימָא לַן הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין צָרִיךְ אֵימָה וְיִרְאָה כָּל כָּךְ, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת דְּבַעַל קֶרִי מוּתָּר.

in contrast to meditating on Torah in thought alone, for even though we rule contemplation is like speech, one does not require such intense dread and awe, see Tosafot there that a ba'al keri may contemplate.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּהַיִּרְאָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁמָּא הוּא מְדַבֵּר מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי, וּבַלֵּב מוּתָּר הַכֹּל.
And that is because the fear in Torah speech is lest he utter what is unfitting, whereas within the heart everything is permitted.

וּמָצִינוּ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר: "אַשְׁרֵי תִּבְחַר וּתְקָרֵב יִשְׁכֹּן חֲצֵרֶיךָ" (תְּהִלִּים סה, ה) עַל אַהֲרֹן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג), וְהָיָה חוֹמֵד וּמִתְאַוֶּוה לְהַקְרִיב קָרְבָּנוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּבָר נֶאֱמַר: "וְהַזָּר הַקָּרֵב יוּמָת" (בַּמִּדְבָּר א, נא)

And we find King David, peace be upon him, said: "Happy is the man whom You choose and cause to approach, that he may dwell in Your courts" (Psalms 65:5) concerning Aaron (Bemidbar Rabbah 3), passionately coveting to offer sacrifices even though it had been commanded: "the commoner that draws near shall be put to death" (Numbers 1:51)
[וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּזָכָה לְמִלּוּי תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ בַּאֲכִילַת לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים שֶׁאָכַל לְפִקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ,
[and I heard that he merited the fulfillment of his longing through eating the Showbread which he ate to save his life,

וּדְבֵירוּרִין שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה עֻזִיָּה שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְהַקְטִיר, כִּי הַמְּלָכִים מֵעֻזִיָּה וְאֵילָךְ הֵם הַבֵּירוּרִים שֶׁל הַמְּלָכִים מִדָּוִד וְאֵילָךְ, כָּל אֶחָד מְבָרֵר הַמַּעֲלָלִים שֶׁל זֶה מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִתְכַּוֵּין.
and his soul-rectification was Uzziah who sought to burn incense, for the later kings rectified what earlier kings did unintentionally.

וְיוֹתָם שֶׁהָיָה בֵּירוּר שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נֶאֱמַר: "רַק לֹא בָא אֶל הֵיכַל ה'" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב כז, ב), שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ שׁוּם חִסָּרוֹן, כִּי כָּל מַעֲלָלֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים, וְזֶה עַצְמוֹ חִסָּרוֹן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חִסָּרוֹן, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ];

And Jotham who rectified Solomon, it is said: 'howbeit he entered not into the temple of Hashem' (II Chronicles 27:2), bearing no flaw, for all Solomon's deeds were holy of holies, which itself was the flaw of having no flaw, and this is not the place to elaborate];

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 38:1: “The meaning is this: Even matters that are clear in thought should be held in doubt when they come to expression through the tongue, which brings into actuality what is latent in the heart, for a person is liable to error. In one’s thoughts, however, one may consider even matters clear only to oneself. Concerning such a case: The heart does not disclose it to the mouth.”

And being part of the House of Israel, they were granted the additional houses of Priesthood and Royalty, which pass by inborn heredity: even a day-old infant of Aaron's seed is a Kohen, and even an unlearned priest stands and offers sacrifices upon the altar, while choice cannot grant this to the greatest non-priest: "and the common man that draws near shall be put to death" Numbers 1:51.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Ohr Zarua stresses that priestly service is determined by the particular covenant of the priesthood, even where another person is greater in learning. This clarifies why David’s longing for Aharon’s avodah does not by itself authorize performing it. The siman’s freedom of inner yearning must be held together with the actual boundaries of the action desired.

sections.en: There Are Four Ascending Stages in the Fear of Heaven Mentioned in Berakhot 22a…

p: [קצד] אַרְבַּע מַדְרֵגוֹת בְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם כַּנִּזְכָּר בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב.) לְעִנְיַן טְבִילַת קֶרִי: אֵימָה, וְיִרְאָה, וּרְתֶת, וְזֵיעָה.
There are four ascending stages in the fear of Heaven mentioned in Berakhot 22a regarding immersion: dread (eimah), awe (yirah), trembling (retet), and sweat (zei'ah).
שְׁתֵּי הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת בַּלֵּב: אֵימָה בַּהַתְחָלָה, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: עוֹנִים בְּאֵימָה וְאוֹמְרִים בְּיִרְאָה;
The first two reside in the heart: dread at the outset, as in: answering with dread and speaking with awe;
עֲנִיָּה בְּכָל מָקוֹם בְּקוֹל, וַאֲמִירָה בִּלְחִישָׁה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, פח עַמּוּד ב).
answering is everywhere aloud, whereas speaking is in a whisper (Zohar III:88b).
כִּי בְּהַתְחָלַת הַגָּעַת פַּחַד לָאָדָם הוּא צוֹעֵק בְּקוֹל עֲנוֹת, וְזֶה קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם דִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע;
For at the initial onset of fear, a person cries out aloud, which is the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven in the Shema;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַתְּפִלָּה בִּלְחִישָׁה שֶׁהוּא כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
and afterward the Amidah is in a whisper, as one standing before the King.
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם נִקְרָא יִרְאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת קצ"ב, וְהַתְּפִלָּה בְּיוֹתֵר כִּדְפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י בִּבְרָכוֹת (כה רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א).
And both are termed awe as noted in Section 192, and the Amidah even more so, as Rashi explains in Berakhot 25a.
וְהַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁמִּתְבּוֹנֵן בְּפַחַד ה' שֶׁבָּא לוֹ, אָז מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת הַיִּרְאָה עַד שֶׁכִּמְעַט אֵין יָכוֹל לְדַבֵּר מֵרוֹב הַפַּחַד.
That is, after contemplating the fear of Hashem that overtakes him, awe intensifies until he can scarcely articulate speech out of dread.
וּשְׁתֵּי אַחֲרוֹנוֹת בְּאֵבְרֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה: הַהַתְחָלָה רְתֶת, שֶׁאֵבָרִים רוֹעֲדִים;
And the latter two manifest in the physical limbs of action: the beginning is trembling (retet), where the bodily limbs shake;

וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁמִּתְבּוֹנֵן יוֹתֵר, אָז זֵיעַ, שֶׁהוּא מֵזִיעַ מֵרוֹב הַפַּחַד, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): מִזֵּיעָתָן שֶׁל חַיּוֹת נְהַר דִּינוּר יוֹצֵא עַל רֹאשׁ רְשָׁעִים בְּגֵיהִנָּם, עַיֵּין שָׁם.

and subsequently upon deeper contemplation, sweat (zei'ah) emerges out of fear, as in Chagigah 13b: from the sweat of the holy Chayot the river of fire issues upon the heads of the wicked in Gehenna, see there.
כִּי כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ דְּיִרְאָה עַד שֶׁמֵּזִיעַ, אָז נְהַר שֶׁל אֵשׁ דְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁלּוֹ שׂוֹרֵף כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתַּאֲווֹת רָעוֹת שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ,
For when one reaches such awe that he sweats, the river of fire of his fear of Heaven incinerates the root of evil desires in his heart,
שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא "רֹאשׁ רְשָׁעִים בְּגֵיהִנָּם", דְּעִיקָּרוֹ בַּתַּאֲווֹת כִּדְאִיתָא בְּעֵירוּבִין (יט.) שֶׁהַכֹּל יוֹרְדִין עַל עִסְקֵי הִנָּם וְכוּלֵי.
which is called "the head of the wicked in Gehenna," rooted in lust, as in Eruvin 19a that all descend there "on account of hinnam" (Rashi: forbidden relations).
וְלָכֵן אָמַר הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל כִּי הַזֵּיעָה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי עִסְקֵי הַמִּצְווֹת הוּא תִּיקּוּן לַקֶּרִי.
Therefore the holy Ari stated that the sweat produced through the physical toil of mitzvot is a rectification for nocturnal emission.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הַמַּזִּיקִים הֵן הֵם כֹּחוֹת הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁבֶּחָלָל הַשְּׂמָאלִי שֶׁבַּלֵּב, וְהֵן נִשְׂרָפִין עַל יְדֵי זֵיעָה זוֹ הַיּוֹצְאָה מֵחַיּוּת הַקְּדוּשָׁה שֶׁבָּאָדָם.
For the destructive forces (mazikin) are the powers of lust in the left cavity of the heart, and they are consumed by this sweat issuing from the holy vitality within man.
וּכְשֶׁהַזֵּיעָה בָּאָה לָאָדָם עַל יְדֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, וַדַּאי אֵין לְמַעְלָה הֵימֶנָּה, וְהוּא הֵיפֶךְ מַמָּשׁ לַקֶּרִי כִּדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם.
And when sweat comes to a person through fear of Heaven, there is certainly nothing higher, being the absolute opposite of seminal emission as stated in the Gemara.
רַק שֶׁזֶּה יָקָר וְקָשֶׁה, וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים קַל הוּא עַל יְדֵי פְּעֻלַּת אָדָם בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְווֹת בְּאֵבָרָיו.
But that is rare and difficult, whereas it is accessible through a person's physical labor in performing mitzvot with his limbs.
וְכָל פְּעֻלַּת מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְווֹת הֲרֵי זֶה קַבָּלַת עוֹל מִצְווֹת וְעוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.
And all physical execution of mitzvot constitutes the acceptance of the yoke of commandments, the yoke of Heaven, and fear of God.
וּבְיוֹתֵר בְּמִצְוַת מַצָּה, שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְהַתַּאֲוָה.
And especially in the mitzvah of matzah, which is the opposite of the leaven in the dough and bodily lust.
וְכָל מִצְוָה נוֹתֶנֶת קְדוּשָּׁה בָּאָדָם כְּפִי עִנְיָנָהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ".
And every mitzvah instills holiness in man according to its nature, as we bless: "Who has sanctified us with His commandments."

וּמַצָּה קְדוּשָׁה לְסִלּוּק הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה מֵהַלֵּב, דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קפג עַמּוּד ב): מֵיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָותָא, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי שַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק יד הֲלָכָה ג): כָּל חוֹלִי – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע.

And matzah possesses holiness to remove the leaven from the heart, which is why the Zohar (II:183b) calls it the "food of healing," matching the Yerushalmi (Shabbat 14:3): all sickness refers to the evil inclination.

paragraphs.text: Matzah establishes recognition before expansion
The initial discipline of matzah can carry recognition of Hashem into the fuller activities that follow.

rich.text: The initial discipline of matzah can carry recognition of Hashem into the fuller activities that follow.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 27:3: “‘This matzah that we eat—why? Because our ancestors' dough did not have time to become leavened.’ Matzah indicates a small degree of human action, through which it is still easy to recognize the source. Chametz indicates more human action, which can conceal the source, as when the mixing of a person's own understanding obscures recognition. At the beginning Israel were therefore commanded concerning matzah to establish recognition of the source in their hearts. The Zohar says that when Israel left Egypt they did not know the root and secret of faith. Hashem said: Let Israel taste this medicine; while they eat it, no other food should be shown to them. Once they ate matzah, the medicine for entering and knowing the secret of faith, Hashem said: From now on chametz is fitting for them and cannot harm them. This resembles the command to return every first portion to Hashem, such as terumah, tithes and challah. When a person recognizes the source at the beginning and accepts Hashem's kingship at the start of an outpouring, Hashem grants him the remainder to receive from the divine table. So Israel must clarify their recognition of the source during these first seven days through eating matzah. Through this they can recognize His light in every gift throughout the year, even when eating chametz.”

The smaller human intervention makes the source easier to recognize, and the first seven days establish a recognition meant to continue when chametz returns. This clarifies the siman's account of matzah opposing the heart's leaven: the aim is an enduring direction within human activity, not simply the disappearance of activity or appetite.

The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let Israel taste the remedy; until they eat this remedy, no other food shall be shown to them. Once they ate matzah, which is the remedy for entering and knowing the mystery of faith, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: From now on, leaven may be shown to them and they may eat it, for it cannot harm them. All the more so on Shavuot, when the higher bread is prepared, which is a remedy in every respect.”

sections.en: Fear Is the Attribute of Knesset Yisrael as Is Known

p: [קצה] יִרְאָה הִיא מִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע, וְהַיְינוּ כִּי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּעֲלֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם וְאַף עַם הָאָרֶץ.
Fear is the attribute of Knesset Yisrael as is known, meaning that all Israel possess fear of Heaven, even the common folk.
רַק הַבּוּר אֵין יְרֵא חֵטְא, שֶׁהוּא אֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַיְינוּ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.
Only a boor lacks fear of sin, because he lacks derekh eretz, whereas the derekh eretz of Israel is itself fear of Heaven.
וּלְכָךְ דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ קָדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: כָּל שֶׁיִּרְאָתוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ.
And therefore derekh eretz precedes the Torah, as stated: whoever's fear precedes his wisdom, his wisdom endures (Avot 3:9).
וְתוֹרָה הִיא מִדַּת "אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב" (מִיכָה ז, כ) – אֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ח).
And Torah is the attribute of "truth to Jacob" (Micah 7:20)—there is no truth other than Torah (Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah 3:8).
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כִּי יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב" (דְּבָרִים לג, ד), אֲפִילּוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ.
And all Israel are the seed of our father Jacob, having a portion in the Torah: "an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob" (Deuteronomy 33:4), even the unlearned.
כִּי בְּלָאו הָכִי, אִם אֵין חָכְמָה אֵין יִרְאָה.
For otherwise, if there is no wisdom there is no fear.
וְהֵם מִדַּת זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָזֶה בְּלֹא זֶה לְהוֹלָדַת הַוָּלָד.
And they represent the masculine and feminine dimensions, which cannot generate offspring without each other.
וְהַיִּרְאָה הִיא הַמּוֹלֶדֶת מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְווֹת, וְצָרִיךְ לָהּ הַחָכְמָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְהַזְרָעָה בַּיִּרְאָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא בַּחֲשַׁאי וּבְהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל אֵצֶל עַם הָאָרֶץ.
And awe gives birth to the performance of mitzvot, requiring wisdom to seed that awe, though in the unlearned this occurs in deep quiet concealment.
אֲבָל הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁתּוֹרָתָן אֻמָּנוּתָן, אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים (שַׁבָּת יא.) שֶׁאֵין מַפְסִיקִין לִתְפִלָּה;
But regarding scholars whose trade is Torah, the Sages stated (Shabbat 11a) that they do not interrupt their study for prayer;
הֲגַם דְּאִם אֵין יִרְאָה אֵין חָכְמָה, רַק יָדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, לט עַמּוּד ב) דִּבְמָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ דְּכַר וְנוּקְבָא לֵית שְׁבָחָא אֶלָּא לִדְכוּרָא, וְגַם הַנּוּקְבָא נִקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ.
for although without fear there is no wisdom, the Zohar (II:39b) teaches that where male and female unite, praise is ascribed to the male, the female being called by his name.
וְכֵן אֵצֶל הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַיִּרְאָה נִכְלֶלֶת בְּהַתּוֹרָה, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרַבִּי בִּבְרָכוֹת (יג:) שֶׁבְּעֵת לִמּוּדוֹ מַעֲבִיר יָדָיו עַל עֵינָיו
And so with the Torah scholar, awe is absorbed within the Torah, as with Rebbe in Berakhot 13b who placed his hands over his eyes during study

[כִּי עִיקַּר הַיִּרְאָה בַּעֲצִימַת הָעֵינַיִם מֵרְאוֹת בְּרָע; וְלָכֵן מַדְרֵגַת יִצְחָק הוּא דְּמַחֲוֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינַיְיהוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פט:), וּמִשּׁוּם "כִּי לֹא יִרְאַנִי וְגוֹמֵר" בְּעֵינֵי בָּשָׂר רַק בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׂכֶל, לְכָךְ מַעֲבִיר וְכוּלֵי],

[for the essence of awe is closing the eyes from seeing evil; hence Isaac points out the Holy One to their eyes (Shabbat 89b), and since 'man cannot see Me and live' with fleshly eyes but only with the intellect, he covered his eyes],
עַד שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה נִיכָּר קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם כְּלָל, שֶׁהָיְתָה מוּבְלַעַת תּוֹךְ הַתּוֹרָה.
so that his acceptance of the yoke of Heaven was not outwardly noticeable, being internalized within the Torah.
וְכֵן רַשְׁבִּ"י וַדַּאי הֲוָה מְהַדַּר אַשְׁמַעְתָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וַעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
And so Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai certainly reviewed teachings that contained the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven and the service of the heart, as one standing before the King.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל כָּלוּל בַּתּוֹרָה, כְּטַעַם "אֲנִי בִינָה" (מִשְׁלֵי ח, יד), שֶׁהוּא תְּשׁוּבָה כַּנּוֹדָע, וְזוֹ עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב הַיּוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה, דְּבִינָה לִבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע;
For in truth everything is included in Torah, reflecting "I am understanding" (Proverbs 8:14), which is repentance, the greatest service of the heart, Binah being the heart;
"לִי גְבוּרָה" – בִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר, זֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁכּוֹבֶשֶׁת תַּאֲווֹת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וְהַכֹּל בַּתּוֹרָה וְנִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הַדְּכוּרָא:
and "I have strength"—subduing the inclination through fear of Heaven, all incorporated in Torah and named after the male dimension.

paragraphs.text: Preparation of heart and received wisdom form a connected movement into action.

rich.text: Preparation of heart and received wisdom form a connected movement into action.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Soferim 17:1: “A person's principal power is the desire and yearning within him and his preparing himself to receive and fulfill the whole Torah. The rest comes from Hashem, Who completes it for him and gives wisdom. But He ‘gives only to the wise’: those who possess the beginning of wisdom, awe of Hashem, which is itself also called wisdom, as it says, ‘Behold, awe of Hashem is wisdom.’ This is preparing the heart not to do anything against Hashem's will. Then all Torah and wisdom is entrusted to him, to know Hashem's will and to have all his deeds and thoughts conform to Hashem's wisdom within him.”

The rest comes from Hashem, Who completes it for him and gives wisdom. But He ‘gives only to the wise’: those who possess the beginning of wisdom, awe of Hashem, which is itself also called wisdom, as it says, ‘Behold, awe of Hashem is wisdom.’ This is preparing the heart not to do anything against Hashem's will. Then all Torah and wisdom is entrusted to him, to know Hashem's will and to have all his deeds and thoughts conform to Hashem's wisdom within him.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Divrei Soferim identifies the first wisdom as awe itself: preparing the heart not to act against Hashem's will. Received Torah then tells the person how to direct deeds and thoughts. This explains the siman's reciprocal relation of awe and wisdom without treating either as a dispensable addition to the other.

sections.en: There Are Three Loves: the Love of the Holy One, the Love of the Torah, and the Love of Israel

p: [קצו] שָׁלֹשׁ אַהֲבוֹת יֵשׁ: אַהֲבַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְהַתּוֹרָה, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל; וְכֻלָּם חַד כִּידוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר, דְּהָא בְּלָא הָא לָא סַגִּי.
There are three loves: the love of the Holy One, the love of the Torah, and the love of Israel; and all are one as known in the Zohar, none functioning without the other.
וְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, כִּי אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד בְּלֹא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – הוּא אוֹהֵב צַוְותָּא וְחַבְרוּתָא, וְהוּא דּוֹר הַפְלָגָה שֶׁגַּם כֵּן אָהֲבוּ חַבְרוּתָא
And the love of the Blessed Name is the root, for love of Israel alone without Hashem is mere fondness for fellowship, exemplified by the Generation of the Dispersion who also loved fellowship
[וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּעַל זֶה תִּיקֵּן בֹּעַז שְׁאִילַת שָׁלוֹם בַּשֵּׁם, שֶׁהוּא אָהַב צַוְותָּא מְאֹד וּפָחַד שֶׁמָּא הוּא אַהֲבַת צַוְותָּא בְּזוּלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
[and I heard that for this reason Boaz instituted greeting with the divine Name, for he loved company and feared lest it be fellowship detached from Hashem,
וּלְכָךְ הָיָה פְּתִיחַת צַוְותָּא שֶׁלּוֹ וּשְׁאִילַת שָׁלוֹם שֶׁלּוֹ בַּשֵּׁם, לוֹמַר שֶׁרוֹצֶה רַק צַוְותָּא לִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם].
so he opened his greetings with the Name, expressing that he desired fellowship solely for the honor of Heaven].

וְאַהֲבַת תּוֹרָה בְּלֹא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – הַיְינוּ אַהֲבַת הַחָכְמָה בִּלְבַד, זֶהוּ דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, רטז עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי אָז מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, דְּהֵמָּה אָהֲבוּ תּוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה מְאֹד

And love of Torah without the Blessed Name is mere intellectual love of wisdom, exemplified by the Generation of the Flood who, as the Zohar states (III:216b), were fit to receive the Torah, possessing a great love of wisdom
[וְזֶה טַעַם "בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים אֶל בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם", דִּידוּעַ נוּקְבָא הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק וּדְכוּרָא הַמִּלּוּי,
[and this explains 'the sons of God [came] to the daughters of men,' for the female is longing and the male is fulfillment;

וּמַלְאָכִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם חָכְמָה וְהַשָּׂגָה רַק שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יֵצֶר הָרָע וּתְשׁוּקָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קלח עַמּוּד א) דְּגַם חֵשֶׁק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה צָרִיךְ יֵצֶר הָרָע,
and angels have wisdom but lack passion, as Midrash HaNe'elam states that even desire for Torah requires an inclination,
וְאָדָם יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵשֶׁק רַק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הַשָּׂגָה, וְאָז נִתְחַבְּרוּ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
while man has passion but lacks divine perception, and they united, and this is not the place to lengthen],
רַק בְּזוּלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מִזֶּה נִמְשַׁךְ זְנוּת.
only that detached from Hashem, it degenerated into unchastity.
וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אוֹהֲבִי, כְּבָר מִלֵּידָה מִבֶּטֶן קָבוּעַ בָּהֶם אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַכֶּתֶר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בִּתְפִיסַת אָדָם.
But within the children of Israel, the seed of Abraham who loved Me, love of the Blessed Name is embedded from birth as the root, corresponding to Keter which transcends human grasp.
וְחָכְמָה וּבִינָה הֵם אַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּבִינָה לִבָּא, וְשָׁם עִיקַּר אַהֲבַת חֲבֵירִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כֵּן לֵב הָאָדָם לָאָדָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כז, יט)
And Chokhmah and Binah are love of Torah and love of Israel, Binah being the heart where love of companions resides: "so the heart of man to man" (Proverbs 27:19)
[וְכָל מִדָּה קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה, וְאֵלּוּ הֵם ג' רִאשׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁבְּמִדַּת הַחֶסֶד, וְאַחַר כָּךְ ז' תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת הֵם הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתָם בַּכֹּחוֹת].
[and every attribute is a complete stature, these being the three upper sefirot of Chesed, whose seven lower sefirot expand into the faculties].

וְהֵם כֹּחוֹת נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה: כִּי חִבּוּר יִשְׂרָאֵל זֶה לָזֶה הוּא מִצַּד הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְחִבּוּרוֹ לַתּוֹרָה מִצַּד הָרוּחַ, וְלַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצַּד הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁמִּתַּחַת כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד;

And they correspond to Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah: the bond of Israel to each other is through Nefesh; connection to Torah is through Ruach; and to Hashem through Neshamah beneath the Throne of Glory;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ: "נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה", דְּשָׁם אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ קִלְקוּל, כִּי הוּא חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ.
therefore we say "the soul which You gave within me is pure," for there no flaw can reach, being an intrinsic part of God.

וְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין נִיזֶזֶת כְּלָל, וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה רֵישׁ פְּתִיחָתָא): "הַלְוַאי אוֹתִי עָזָבוּ וְאֶת תּוֹרָתִי וְכוּלֵי", דְּאוֹתוֹ כִּבְיָכוֹל אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לַעֲזוֹב, כְּעִנְיַן "בְּחֵמָה שְׁפוּכָה אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם" (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ, לג).

And the love of Hashem never moves, which is why the Midrash (Eichah Rabbah, Petichta 2) states: "Would that they had forsaken Me but kept My Torah"—for Him it is impossible for Israel to abandon, as in: "with poured out fury will I rule over you" (Ezekiel 20:33).

כִּי גַּם אִם מַגְדִּיל עֲבֵירוֹת לְהַכְעִיס, אֵין שׁוֹרֶשׁ אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד מִדַּת הַכֶּתֶר, שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה, שָׁם לֹא נִיתַּק כְּלָל, דְּ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.).
For even if one commits sins brazenly, the root of love of Hashem—corresponding to Keter, the hidden root of Thought—is never severed, for "even though he sinned, he remains Israel" (Sanhedrin 44a).

וְחוּרְבָּן רִאשׁוֹן הָיָה עַל "עָזְבָם אֶת תּוֹרָתִי" (יִרְמְיָה ט, יב); אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי אַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה, הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ וְכוּלֵי מֵבִיא לְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנֶּעְלֶמֶת שֶׁתָּבוֹא לִידֵי גִּלּוּי.
And the First Temple was destroyed over "their forsaking My Torah" (Jeremiah 9:12); yet through love of Torah, the light within it brings the hidden love of Hashem into manifest revelation.
וְחוּרְבָּן שֵׁנִי הָיָה עַל יְדֵי שִׂנְאַת חִנָּם (יוֹמָא ט:), דְּהַיְינוּ הֶעְדֵּר אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
And the Second Temple was destroyed through baseless hatred (Yoma 9b), which is the absence of love of Israel.
וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יד): דַּרְכָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם לוֹמַר: אַהֲבַת תּוֹרָה קוֹדֶמֶת וְכוּלֵי, וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹדֶמֶת.
And in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 14): It is the way of people to say love of Torah comes first, but I say love of Israel comes first.
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַכּוֹת כב:): כַּמָּה טִפְּשָׁאֵי אִינָשֵׁי דְּקָיְימֵי מִקַּמֵּי סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וְלֹא מִקַּמֵּי גַּבְרָא רַבָּא,
And this mirrors Makkot 22b: How foolish are people who stand before a Torah scroll but do not stand before a great sage!
דְּאֵצֶל בְּנֵי אָדָם סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה חֲשׁוּבָה, כִּי כָּךְ הוּא מִצַּד בְּנֵי אָדָם: אַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה צָרִיךְ לְהַקְדִּים לְהַכְנִיס בַּלֵּב,
for in human perception a Torah scroll is exalted, and from man's perspective love of Torah must first be instilled into the heart;
וְכֵן הָיָה מַתַּן תּוֹרָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּנִיסָה לָאָרֶץ, וְכֵן הָעֲזִיבָה כָּזֶה הַסֵּדֶר.
and so was the sequence: first the Giving of the Torah, and only afterward entry into the Land; and likewise the destruction followed this order.

אַךְ מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "רֵאשִׁית תְּבוּאָתֹה" (יִרְמְיָה ב, ג) – הַיְינוּ הַפְּרִי וְהַתְּבוּאָה שֶׁרָצָה לְהַכְנִיס בִּזְרִיעַת הָעוֹלָם הֵם נַפְשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהֵם כּוֹלְלִים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ,
But from Hashem's perspective, "the first-fruits of His increase" (Jeremiah 2:3)—the ultimate harvest He desired from sowing the cosmos—are the souls of Israel, which encompass the entire Torah,
רַק שֶׁאֶצְלָם הוּא סָתוּם וְהַתּוֹרָה הוּא פֵּירוּשׁ עַל זֶה.
only that within them it is concealed, and the Torah serves as the commentary upon it.
וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּת, אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹדֶמֶת, שֶׁהֵם הָעִיקָּר וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה;
And so for one who has attained spiritual perfection, love of Israel comes first, for they are the foundation and root of Torah;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוּא הַתּוֹרָה, לְפָרֵשׁ וּלְהָבִין הַמַּעֲמַקִּים הַגְּנוּזִים בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל:
and only subsequently is the Torah studied, to articulate and comprehend the profound depths hidden within every individual soul in Israel.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Machshavot Charutz 19:4: “as it is said: "but Esau I hated" (Malachi 1:3), being the polar opposite of the three aforementioned loves; as the Sages expounded on "since you have not hated blood" (Yechezkel 35:6): the blood of the Passover, the blood of circumcision, and the blood of man within his body. And the blood of the Paschal lamb awakens the love of the Blessed Name within the hearts of Israel like water reflecting face to face (Mishlei 27:19); because Hashem passed over and had compassion upon us, Pesach being the festival of love; and the blood of circumcision is the boundary separating Israel from the nations, all gentiles being uncircumcised (Nedarim 31b); this representing the love of Torah in the hearts of Israel who desired it and accepted it; whereas all the nations unto whom Hashem offered it refused to receive it (Avodah Zarah 2b);”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Machshavot Charutz explicitly returns to three loves and associates the blood of Pesach with Hashem’s compassion, and the covenant of milah with Israel’s willing reception of Torah. These concrete bonds help explain why the siman refuses to reduce love of Torah to intellectual taste or love of Israel to enjoyment of company. Their direction is toward the relationship Hashem establishes and the response it calls forth.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Berakhot 54a:1: “This was the matter with Boaz: by nature Boaz loved companionship, and he feared for himself that this might not be clarified as being for the sake of Heaven. He therefore instituted a restraint for himself: immediately upon seeing his fellow, his first words would be to inquire in God’s name—that they should mention and ask whether he had now, God forbid, departed from God’s name through any forgetfulness. This was to clarify his character, so that his companionship would be clearly intended for the sake of Heaven. After he devised this counsel, “they instituted” it: the Holy One, blessed be He, bestowed it and engraved it in the hearts of the children of Israel. This is why “they instituted” is plural.”

sections.en: There Are Three Ascending Levels in the Love of the Blessed Name

p: [קצז] שָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת בְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" (דְּבָרִים ו, ה) – הַיְינוּ כָּל הַתְּשׁוּקוֹת וַחֲמוּדוֹת שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
There are three ascending levels in the love of the Blessed Name: "with all your heart" (Deuteronomy 6:5)—meaning all the longings and desires within the heart,

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נד.): בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ, פֵּירוּשׁ: בֵּין בְּצָרְכֵי הַגּוּף בֵּין לְעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַבָּא, הַכֹּל לֹא יִהְיֶה לְאַהֲבַת עַצְמוֹ רַק לְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,

and our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Berakhot 54a): with both your inclinations, meaning whether in bodily necessities or in pursuits of the World to Come, none should be for self-love, but solely for the love of the Blessed Name,
וְזֶהוּ בִּכְלַל הַתְּשׁוּקוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ.
and this is encompassed within his desires.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ" – הַיְינוּ בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹ מְקֻשֶּׁרֶת בָּהֶם מַמָּשׁ,
And following that, "with all your soul"—meaning in matters with which his very life-force is intimately bound,
וּכְעִנְיַן "נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְדַבְּרוֹ" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה, ו) מִפְּנֵי גּוֹדֶל קִשּׁוּר הַתְּשׁוּקָה הַמַּגִּיעַ עַד כְּלוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ מַמָּשׁ.
in the manner of "my soul failed when he spoke" (Song of Songs 5:6), on account of the intense binding of longing that reaches literal expiration of the soul.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וַיִּקְרָא ה) עַל פָּסוּק "וְנֶפֶשׁ כִּי תַקְרִיב" (וַיִּקְרָא ב, א): דְּעָנִי – נַפְשׁוֹ הוּא מַקְרִיב, שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹ מְקֻשֶּׁרֶת בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר מוּעָט.
And as stated in Midrash Tanchuma (Vayikra 5) on the verse "And when any one (nefesh) offers a meal-offering": the poor man offers his very soul, for his soul is bound up in that meager possession.

וְכֵן נִקְרָא תְּפִלַּת הֶעָנִי "נֶפֶשׁ", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּחַנָּה: "וָאֶשְׁפֹּךְ אֶת נַפְשִׁי לִפְנֵי ה'" (שְׁמוּאֵל א א, טו), שֶׁתְּשׁוּקָתָהּ לְבֵן הָיָה כָּל נַפְשָׁהּ קְשׁוּרָה בִּתְשׁוּקָה זוֹ.

And so the prayer of the afflicted is termed nefesh, as written concerning Hannah: "and have poured out my soul before Hashem" (I Samuel 1:15), for in her yearning for a child her entire soul was bound up in that desire.
וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל נַפְשׁוֹ מְקֻשָּׁר בִּתְשׁוּקַת אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּעִנְיַן בְּמַעֲמַד הַר סִינַי: מִדִּבּוּר אֶחָד יָצְתָה נִשְׁמָתָם (שַׁבָּת פח:).
And a person must have his whole soul bound up in the desire for the love of the Blessed Name, as at the assembly at Mount Sinai: at each utterance their soul departed (Shabbat 88b).
וְזֶהוּ נִקְרָא דְּבֵיקוּת, כַּאֲשֶׁר מַמָּשׁ מָצוּי נַפְשׁוֹ קָשׁוּר וְדָבוּק בָּזֶה.
And this is termed cleaving (devekut), when his soul's reality is literally bound and affixed to this.
וְזֶהוּ תְּפִלִּין, שֶׁפֵּירוּשׁ דְּבֵקוּת, וְנִקְרָא חַיּוּתוֹ בִּבְרָכוֹת (כד.) עַל פָּסוּק "וְהָיוּ חַיֶּיךָ תְּלֻאִים לְךָ מִנֶּגֶד" (דְּבָרִים כח, סו);
And this is tefillin, which denotes cleaving and is called one's vitality in Berakhot 24a on the verse "and your life shall hang in doubt before you" (Deuteronomy 28:66);
כִּי הַדְּבֵיקוּת הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּמָּשׁ כָּל חַיּוּתוֹ תָּלוּי בָּזֶה.
for devekut means that literally his entire vitality is suspended upon this.
וּשְׁנֵי אֵלּוּ עֲדַיִן הוּא בְּיַד עֲבוֹדַת הָאָדָם וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג לָזֶה;
And these two levels are still within the grasp of human service and effort to attain;
וּלְכָךְ בְּפָרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ" (דְּבָרִים יא, יג) שֶׁאָמַר "וּלְעָבְדוֹ", נִזְכַּר רַק שְׁנֵי אֵלֶּה,
and therefore in the second paragraph of Shema where it says "and to serve Him," only these two are mentioned ("with all your heart and with all your soul"),
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן "בְּכָל מְאֹדְךָ" אֵינוֹ בְּיַד עֲבוֹדַת הָאָדָם, רַק מִסַּיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא,
whereas "with all your might (me'odekha)" is not solely within human effort, but depends on Heavenly assistance,
דְּפֵירוּשׁ: שֶׁבְּכָל רְכוּשׁוֹ וְקִנְיָנוֹ יִהְיֶה קָבוּעַ אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
which means: that within all his property and acquisitions the love of the Blessed Name shall be permanently established,
וְלֹא קָאֵי אַתְּשׁוּקָתוֹ וְחֶמְדָּתוֹ לִרְכּוּשׁ, שֶׁזֶּה בִּכְלַל "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ",
and it does not refer merely to his desire and passion for wealth, for that is already included in "with all your heart,"
רַק שֶׁבְּכָל הָרְכוּשׁ עַצְמוֹ.
but rather within the physical property itself.

כִּידוּעַ כִּי הָרְכוּשׁ שַׁיָּיךְ לָאָדָם, וְכָל כָּךְ יִהְיֶה הָאָדָם כֻּלּוֹ מְמוּלָּא מֵאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מַעֲמַקָּיו, עַד שֶׁמִּמֵּילָא גַּם בְּכָל קִנְיָנָיו שֶׁהֵם הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁלּוֹ, יִהְיוּ גַּם כֵּן מְמוּלָּאִים מֵאַהֲבָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,

For as is known, property is connected to a person, and the person should be so thoroughly filled with love of the Blessed Name in all his depths, that spontaneously all his possessions—which are extensions of him—will likewise be filled with His blessed love,
כְּעִנְיַן חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי פִּינְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר דִּמְחַמְּרָא אַנַּפְשַׁהּ לֶאֱכוֹל אִיסּוּר (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס).
like the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, which was so stringent upon itself as to refuse to eat untithed produce (Bereishit Rabbah 60:8).

וְזוֹ בְּבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים, וּמִסְּתָמָא הוּא הַדִּין בְּדוֹמְמִים, כְּעִנְיַן "אֶבֶן מִקִּיר תִּזְעָק" (חֲבַקּוּק ב, יא) לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כְּשֶׁיִּרְצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת אִיסּוּר, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים מִזְמוֹר עג).

And this was in an animal, and presumably the same applies to inanimate objects, in the spirit of "the stone shall cry out of the wall" (Habakkuk 2:11) in the future to come when one attempts to commit a transgression (Shocher Tov, Psalm 73).
וְזֶה עִנְיַן שְׁבִיתַת כֵּלָיו בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁאָז כֻּלּוֹ לַה' גַּם כָּל קִנְיָנָיו.
And this is the concept of the resting of one's vessels on the Sabbath day, wherein all is consecrated to Hashem, including all his possessions.

וּכְעִנְיַן צֹאן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה עג) שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא עֲדָרִים, דְּמִן הַשְׁתָּוַת הַמִּסְפָּר מְבוֹאָר דְּהֵן עַצְמָן שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל;

And like the flocks of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, concerning which our Sages stated (Bereishit Rabbah 73 end) that he possessed 600,000 flocks, where from the equivalence of the number it is evident that they correspond to the 600,000 souls of Israel;
וְאִם כֵּן בְּוַדַּאי אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קָבוּעַ גַּם בָּהֶם.
and if so, certainly the love of the Blessed Name was etched within them as well.

וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קסב סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דְּכַוָּנַת יַעֲקֹב בַּמַּקְלוֹת הוּא עִנְיַן הַתְּפִלִּין, דְּהַיְינוּ הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת וּדְבֵיקוּת מְצוּי נַפְשׁוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.

And they stated in the Zohar (Part I, 162a end) that Jacob's intention with the rods was the mystery of tefillin, namely the binding and cleaving of his soul's reality unto the Blessed Name as noted above.
וּמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב הוּא נֶגֶד "בְּכָל מְאֹדְךָ": לְקַשֵּׁר כָּל כָּךְ כָּל מְצוּי וְנַפְשׁוֹ עַד שֶׁגַּם הַקִּנְיָנִים הַשַּׁיָּיכִים לוֹ כֻּלָּן יִהְיוּ בִּכְלַל הַהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת זֶה;
And Jacob's attribute corresponds to "with all your might": to bind so thoroughly his entire being and soul, that even the possessions belonging to him are fully subsumed within this holy attachment;
וּלְכָךְ לֹא נֶאֱמַר זֶה בְּפָרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ" שֶׁהִיא בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים, דְּדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִיחִידִים שֶׁזָּכוּ בָּהּ,
and therefore this was not stated in the second paragraph of Shema which is phrased in the plural, for this level belongs only to rare individuals who merited it,
אֲבָל אִי אֶפְשָׁר מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ לָרַבִּים, אֶלָּא לֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיִּשְׁפּוֹךְ רוּחוֹ עַל כָּל בָּשָׂר,
as it is impossible for the masses, save in the future when He will pour out His spirit upon all flesh (Joel 3:1),

כְּעִנְיַן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלְטוּ שׂוֹנְאִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו, כִּי קִנְיָנָיו וּפְעֻלּוֹתָיו הַשַּׁיָּיכִים לוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ בְּדוֹמְמִים, קְבוּעָה בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִינָּתֵק כְּלָל.

like Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, whose handiwork enemies could never destroy, for within his possessions and actions, even inanimate ones, was fixed an enduring sanctity that could never be severed.
וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (צח:): אֵיתִיב בְּטוּלָּא דְּכוֹפִיתָא דַּחֲמָרֵיהּ.
And Rav Yosef stated in Sanhedrin 98b: "Let the Messiah come, and may I merit to sit in the shadow of the dung of his donkey."

וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ בְּכוֹרוֹת (ב.) דְּמוֹצִיא מִקְּדֻשָּׁתוֹ כְּשֶׁמּוֹכֵר הַחֲמוֹר לְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י וְתוֹסָפוֹת לְחַד פֵּירוּשׁ בְּזוּלַת הַמְּלָאכָה דְּשַׁבָּת.

And so they said at the beginning of Bekhorot 2a that one removes it from its sanctity when selling a donkey to an idolater, see Rashi and Tosafot according to one explanation, apart from labor on Shabbat.
וּלְיָחִיד הַזּוֹכֶה, גַּם בְּדוֹמְמִים כָּל קִנְיָנָיו הֵם כְּמוֹ תַּשְׁמִישֵׁי מִצְוָה וְקָדְשֵׁי שָׁמַיִם, וְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קָבוּעַ בָּהֶם שֶׁהֵם אוֹהֲבִים לְפַרְסֵם כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם,

And for a worthy individual, even among inanimate objects all his possessions are like instruments of mitzvot and holy celestial artifacts, and the love of the Blessed Name is embedded within them such that they yearn to publicize the honor of Heaven,

paragraphs.text: Gevurot Hashem 39:2: “This is what is written: “All the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you.” Rabbi Eliezer said: these are the tefillin on the head. The explanation is that tefillin show that Israel is set apart for the unique Name, since the tefillin mention the exodus from Egypt, when He brought them out through miracles; the unique Name specifically performs wonders. Therefore “they shall fear you,” because of His mighty and awesome deeds. Rabbi Eliezer specified the tefillin on the head because the tefillin on the arm express Israel’s attachment to the Holy One, blessed be He; therefore it says of them, “You shall bind them.” This is the difference between the tefillin of the hand and the head. Those of the hand express the connection and attachment Israel has to the Holy One, blessed be He. From this aspect there is no fear, but connection and attachment to Him, for where there is connection there is no fear. With those of the head, however, there is no binding of that kind; rather, His name is called upon them. In having His name called upon them He is distinct from them, being called “the God of Israel.” As their God He is distinct from them, and from this aspect there is fear, for it is fitting to fear the God of Israel, to whom might belongs. Understand this.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:77:1: “Possessions belong to a person: even after they are lost they must be returned when he has an identifying mark or recognition, indicating a relation, recognition and testimony that they are his. Everything exists through the word of Hashem that gives it life, and a person's life must have a relation to that life. There are four levels in the lower world—inanimate, growing, living and speaking—and the fifth is the higher beings. Correspondingly there are four elements—fire, air, water and earth—with heaven as the fifth substance; and four soul levels—nefesh, ruach, neshamah and the soul of the soul, chayah—with yechidah as the fifth. The human being includes the inanimate, growing, living and speaking levels, and the inanimate power corresponds to nefesh. Certainly there is a difference between the inanimate power in an inanimate object and that power within a person; nevertheless they have a connection and relation.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah explains the premise behind holiness extending into possessions: the divine word sustains both the person and the object, and the powers within the person correspond to levels of created life. It explicitly preserves the difference between them. This helps the reader understand the present siman's extension of love into possessions without mistaking that relation for an assertion that every object is already a human soul or that every owner has reached this exceptional degree of holiness.

paragraphs.text: The person's later acquisitions are described as connected to the life initially given to him.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 18:3: “Even when a person is born, all the possessions and expansions are already included in him. But because his life is then constricted in the smallness of the point, the possessions stand at a distance. After the person grows, Hashem gives desire and yearning within that point to draw in, gather and bring close all the possessions belonging to the point and included in it. Then the person and all his possessions are joined together, and he is called ‘a new creature.’”

rich.text: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 18:3

: “Even when a person is born, all the possessions and expansions are already included in him. But because his life is then constricted in the smallness of the point, the possessions stand at a distance. After the person grows, Hashem gives desire and yearning within that point to draw in, gather and bring close all the possessions belonging to the point and included in it. Then the person and all his possessions are joined together, and he is called ‘a new creature.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov describes possessions as included in the person's original point of life and later gathered into its expansion. This explains why the siman distinguishes a desire for property from holiness reaching the property itself. Its final degree of love still remains, as the siman expressly says, a gift requiring help from Heaven.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And like the flocks of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, concerning which our Sages stated (Bereishit Rabbah 73 end) that he possessed 600,000 flocks, where from the equivalence of the number it is evident that they correspond to the 600,000 souls of Israel;

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 91:1: “This is the secret of what is stated in Bereshit Rabbah, section 73, that Jacob had six hundred thousand flocks of sheep. His soul comprised the six hundred thousand souls of Israel, each comprising its particular generations. Portions of the light of his soul then spread into the sheep, a pure animal, for at that time he was still called Jacob, the level of an unlearned person, as stated at the end of the chapter “Elu Metziot.” Israel is also compared to sheep. They were his possession, from which he earned his livelihood, for a person’s principal vitality is hidden in that which sustains him: livelihood is the principal support of his life. This is why it was said, “Do not throw a clod into the well from which you drank”—one must not treat it contemptuously. This is not the place to elaborate.”

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And Jacob's attribute corresponds to "with all your might": to bind so thoroughly his entire being and soul, that even the possessions belonging to him are fully subsumed within this holy attachment;

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 254:1: “Likewise, “with all your might” is our father Jacob, of whom they said that he remained behind for small vessels, because his money was dearer to him than his body. In him there was the generosity of “all your might,” and in him this trait was clarified—not in someone who is naturally lavish and to whom money has no importance at all. Nevertheless, they said, “I praise the lazy,” for it is certainly still good, and such a person is called “idle and rewarded”; but he is not on the level of “with all.” “All” denotes that to which one’s soul is naturally bound, and which one subordinates to the love and service of the blessed God.”

paragraphs.text: Sotah 9a:13-14: “Rav Ḥinena bar Pappa expounded: What is the meaning of “Sing joyfully, righteous ones, in the Lord; praise is fitting for the upright”? Read not “praise is fitting,” but “a dwelling of praise.” This refers to Moses and David, whose enemies did not gain control of their handiwork. Of David it is written, “Her gates have sunk into the earth.” Of Moses, the Master said: When the First Temple was built, the Tent of Meeting was hidden away—its boards, clasps, bars, pillars, and sockets. Where? Rav Ḥisda said in Avimi’s name: in the subterranean passages of the Sanctuary.”

sections.en: Whoever Loves the Torah

p: [קצח] מִי שֶׁאוֹהֵב אֶת הַתּוֹרָה, הַתּוֹרָה אוֹהַבְתּוֹ גַּם כֵּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפָרָשַׁת "הֲלֹא חָכְמָה תִקְרָא" (מִשְׁלֵי ח, א): "אֲנִי אֹהֲבַי אֵהָב וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם, יז),
Whoever loves the Torah, the Torah loves him in return, as written in the passage "Does not wisdom call?" (Proverbs 8:1): "I love them that love me, etc." (ibid. 8:17),
וּמְגַלַּת לוֹ כָּל סְתָרֶיהָ וְרָזֵי הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ הֶחָשׁוּק לַחֲשׁוּקוֹ.
and she reveals to him all her secrets and mysteries, like a lover to her beloved.

וְכֵן הָאוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל, הֵן אוֹהֲבִין אוֹתוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּאַהֲרֹן בְּאָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק א, יב): "אוֹהֵב אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת", וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ: "וַיִּבְכּוּ אֹתוֹ... כֹּל בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כ, כט) כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן פֶּרֶק יב, הוּבָא בְּרַשִּׁ"י), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כַּמַּיִם הַפָּנִים לַפָּנִים כֵּן לֵב הָאָדָם לָאָדָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כז, יט),

And likewise, one who loves Israel, they love him in return, as stated of Aaron in Avot (1:12): "loving creatures," and therefore it was said of him: "and all the house of Israel wept for him" (Numbers 20:29; Avot DeRabbi Natan 12), and as written: "As in water face answers to face, so the heart of man to man" (Proverbs 27:19),
וּמְגַלִּין לוֹ כָּל רָזִין הַגְּנוּזִין בְּנַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and all secrets concealed within the souls of Israel are unveiled to him.
וְזֶה טַעַם: "וְנָשָׂא אַהֲרֹן אֶת שְׁמוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת כח, כט), כִּי הַשֵּׁם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ חַיּוּת נַפְשׁוֹ בִּמְקוֹרָהּ וּמְקוֹם אֲצִילוּתָהּ לְמַעְלָה מַּעְלָה.
And this is the reason for: "And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel, etc." (Exodus 28:29), for a name is the root vitality of the soul in its supernal source and emanation on high.
וּלְלֵב אַהֲרֹן הָאוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל גְּלוּיִים סוֹדוֹת כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת בְּשָׁרְשָׁן.
And to the heart of Aaron who loved Israel, the secrets of all souls in their root were open.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְגַּלִּין לוֹ כָּל חֲלָלֵי עָלְמָא שֶׁהָיוּ שׁוֹאֲלִין בְּאוּרִים וְתֻמִּים, וְהָאוֹתִיּוֹת בּוֹלְטִין,
And through this, all cosmic dimensions were revealed to him when inquiring of the Urim and Thummim, where the letters protruded,
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּלִיטָה בַּלֵּב לְהָאוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי שְׁמוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָדַעַת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּהַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם דָּבָר בְּעִתּוֹ בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר,

meaning that there is a protrusion and intuitive surge in the heart of one who loves Israel through the names of Israel, to know the will of Hashem in world governance, each matter in its season in every generation,
שֶׁעַל זֶה מוֹרִין נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּכָל דּוֹר
which the souls of Israel in each generation indicate
[הַכְּלוּלִין בִּמְקוֹרָן שְׁמוֹת הָאָבוֹת וּשְׁבָטִים הַחֲקוּקִים בְּצֵירוּף תֵּיבוֹת "שִׁבְטֵי יְשֻׁרוּן" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹמָא עג:),
[encompassed in their root within the names of the Patriarchs and Tribes inscribed along with the words 'the tribes of Jeshurun' (Yoma 73b),
שֶׁהֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת הַהַמְשָׁכָה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ כֹּחָן בְּזַרְעָן,
which are the letters of spiritual transmission to extend their power into their seed,
שֶׁעִיקַּר הַהַמְשָׁכָה עַל יְדֵי אוֹת הַטֵּי"ת כְּטַעַם "אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב" שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא בְּכֻלָּן;
the principal transmission being through the letter Tet, reflecting 'Say of the righteous that he is good (tov),' which letter was absent from their initial names;
וְכֵן אוֹת הַצַּדִּי"ק לֹא נִמְצָא אֶלָּא בָּאָבוֹת שֶׁהֵם הַתְחָלַת הַהַמְשָׁכָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
and likewise the letter Tzadik was found only among the Patriarchs (Yitzchak) who are the beginning of transmission, and this is not the place to elaborate].

paragraphs.text: Avot DeRabbi Natan 12:3: “LOVING PEACE. What does this mean? It teaches that a man should love [to foster] peace in Israel between man and man, just as Aaron loved [to foster] peace in Israel between man and man, as it is stated, The law of truth was in his mouth, and unrighteousness was not found in his lips; he walked with Me in peace and uprightness, and did turn many away from iniquity. R. Meir said: What is meant by and did turn many away from iniquity? Whenever Aaron walked along the road and met a wicked man, he would offer him greetings. On the following day when that man was about to commit a transgression, he would say, ‘Woe is me! How can I raise my eyes after doing that and look Aaron in the face? I should be ashamed before him, since he greeted me’. Consequently that man withholds himself from transgression. Similarly, when two men had quarrelled one with the other, Aaron would go and sit with one of them and say, ‘My son, see what your companion is doing! He beats his breast and tears his clothes, exclaiming, “Woe is me! how can I raise my eyes and look my companion in the face? I am ashamed before him since it is I who offended him” ’. Aaron would sit with him until he had removed all enmity from his heart. Then Aaron would go and sit with the other and say likewise, ‘My son, see what your companion is doing! He beats his breast and tears his clothes, exclaiming, “Woe is me! how can I raise my eyes and look my companion in the face? I am ashamed before him since it was I who offended him” ’. Aaron would sit with him until he had removed all enmity from his heart. Later when the two met, they embraced and kissed each other. Therefore it is stated, They wept for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.”

Aaron would sit with him until he had removed all enmity from his heart. Then Aaron would go and sit with the other and say likewise, ‘My son, see what your companion is doing! He beats his breast and tears his clothes, exclaiming, “Woe is me! how can I raise my eyes and look my companion in the face? I am ashamed before him since it was I who offended him” ’. Aaron would sit with him until he had removed all enmity from his heart. Later when the two met, they embraced and kissed each other. Therefore it is stated, They wept for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.”

items.h: From general Torah study to practical halakhah

p: וְהַתּוֹרָה הִיא לִמּוּד דֶּרֶךְ כְּלָל, אֲבָל בִּפְרָט בְּעִתּוֹ בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן וְנֶפֶשׁ וּמָקוֹם – זֶהוּ בִּבְנֵי יִשָּׂשכָר "יוֹדְעֵי בִינָה לַעִתִּים" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א יב, לג),

And the Torah instructs as a general blueprint; but specifically in its timely application in each moment, soul, and place—this belongs to the children of Issachar, "men that had understanding of the times" (I Chronicles 12:33),
שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ מִן הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁשָּׁם הוּא הָרַחֲמָנוּת וְהָאַהֲבָה לַבְּרִיּוֹת.
which issues from Binah in the heart where compassion and love for creatures reside.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַחָכְמָה הוּא אַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה, זֶהוּ בְּלֵוִי בְּיִחוּד שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
In contrast, Chokhmah is the love of Torah, belonging uniquely to Levi from whom Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, emerged,
וּבִכְלָל הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם הֵם הַשּׁוֹפְטִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּבָאתָ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט" (דְּבָרִים יז, ט) וּבְכָל מָקוֹם.
and in general the priests and Levites are the judges, as written: "and you shall come unto the priests the Levites, and unto the judge" (Deuteronomy 17:9), and elsewhere.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (כו.): צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנָן דְּמוֹרֵי – מִלֵּוִי אוֹ מִיִּשָּׂשכָר;
And they stated in Yoma 26a: a young Torah scholar who issues halakhic rulings stems either from Levi or from Issachar;
וְכֵן אִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עב): "רָאשֵׁיהֶם מָאתַיִם" – רָאשֵׁי סַנְהֶדְרָאוֹת;
and so in Bereishit Rabbah 72: "the heads of them were two hundred"—heads of Sanhedrin courts;
כִּי אֵין מְמַנִּין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין זָקֵן וְסָרִיס וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין לו:), דְּצָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן אַהֲבַת הַבְּרִיּוֹת כְּדֵי לֵידַע הַדָּבָר בְּעִתּוֹ,
for they do not appoint to the Sanhedrin an elderly man or a childless person (Sanhedrin 36b), because one also requires love of creatures to know the timely ruling,
וְזֶה זָכָה יִשָּׂשכָר עַל יְדֵי דִּמְרַצְיָא אַרְצוֹיֵי כִּדְאִיתָא בְּעֵירוּבִין (ק:), שֶׁזֶּהוּ תֹּקֶף הָאַהֲבָה לַבְּרִיּוֹת, וּבְכֹחַ זֶה נוֹלָד.
and this Issachar merited through Leah appeasing Jacob (Eruvin 100b), which was the pinnacle of loving outreach, and in that power he was born.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יְהוּדָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (י:), כִּי אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קָבוּעַ בּוֹ
In contrast, Judah was named after the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, as in Sotah 10b, for love of the Blessed Name was etched within him
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי: כִּי מִי שֶׁשּׂוֹנֵא הַנִּבְחָר מִשֵּׁבֶט יְהוּדָה נִקְרָא "שׂוֹנֵא ה'", וְכֵן נִקְרְאוּ שׂוֹנְאֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
[and as I heard: one who hates the chosen ruler from the tribe of Judah is called a hater of Hashem, as were the enemies of King David, peace be upon him;

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּשְׁאָר שְׁבָטִים, כָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַעֲלָתוֹ: מִשֵּׁבֶט יוֹסֵף, הַשּׂוֹנְאוֹ נִקְרָא "שׂוֹנֵא צַדִּיק", וּמִגָּד – "שׂוֹנֵא תָּם", וּמִלֵּוִי – "שׂוֹנֵא יִשְׂרָאֵל", כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי],
unlike other tribes where each is according to his quality: hating Joseph is hating a tzadik; Gad, hating an innocent; Levi, hating Israel; so I heard],
וְלָכֵן נִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל שְׁמוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צח).
and therefore all Israel are named after him as Jews (Yehudim, Bereishit Rabbah 98).
וְאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (יג.): כָּל הַכּוֹפֵר בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִקְרָא "יְהוּדִי",
And they stated in Megillah 13a: whoever denies idolatry is called a Yehudi;
לָכֵן אָמְרוּ שָׁם בְּיוֹמָא דְּגַם בּוֹ נֶאֱמַר: "יְהוּדָה מְחֹקְקִי" (תְּהִלִּים ס, ט), רַק דְּלָא מַסִּיק וְכוּלֵי.
therefore they said in Yoma that of him it is also said "Judah is my lawgiver" (Psalms 60:9), only that he does not conclude the halakhah.
דְּוַדַּאי הַמִּשְׁפָּט מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה: הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלֶּה לוֹ סְתָרָיו, אֶלָּא דְּזֶה אֵינוֹ אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא,
For certainly, measure for measure, the Blessed Name reveals His secrets to him, yet this does not establish normative halakhah,
פֵּירוּשׁ לְשׁוֹן "הֲלָכָה" הַיְינוּ מִלְּשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ לְכוּ בוֹ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ל, כא).
for "halakhah" (walking) derives from "this is the way, walk in it" (Isaiah 30:21).
וּלְעִנְיַן הַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם אָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (נט:): "לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא", וְאֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּבַת קוֹל;
And regarding the practical governance of the world they ruled in Bava Metzia 59b: "It is not in heaven," and we do not heed a heavenly voice;
(וְשָׁם פו.) נֶחְלְקוּ בִּמְתִיבְתָּא דִּרְקִיעָא: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹמֵר וְכוּלֵי,
and on 86a they disputed in the Heavenly Academy: the Holy One said pure, etc.,
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם נִקְרָא: חֻקָּה חָקַקְתִּי, גְּזֵירָה גָּזַרְתִּי וְכוּלֵי.
for the Written Torah from Heaven is titled: a statute I have enacted, a decree I have decreed.
וְכֵן הַבְּרִיאָה דְּהוּא מַעֲשֵׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְרָא "חֻקּוֹת שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ",
And so Creation, being the handiwork of the Holy One, is called "the ordinances of heaven and earth,"
וְכֵן "יְהוּדָה מְחֹקְקִי" נִתְגַּלּוּ לוֹ חוּקּוֹת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא;
and so to "Judah my lawgiver" were revealed the transcendent decrees of the Holy One;
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא, הוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת חֲגִיגָה (ב:) עַל דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: אֵין לְמֵדִין מִתְּקוֹעַ,
and as stated in the Tosefta, cited in Tosafot Chagigah 2b regarding David and King Solomon, peace be upon him: one does not derive halakhah from Tekoa,
שֶׁהוּא עָשָׂה שֶׁלֹּא כַּהֲלָכָה בְּלֹא שׁוּם טַעַם, רַק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרָצָה בְּכָךְ, וְסָמַךְ עַל מַה שֶּׁהוּא רוֹצֶה כָּךְ הוּא אֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאֵין בּוֹ עֲבֵירָה.
for Solomon acted outside standard halakhah without stated rationale, merely because he desired it, relying that what he desired reflected the true will of Hashem without sin.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם טַעַם, כִּי אֵין טַעַם לָרָצוֹן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר שָׁאֲלוּ עֵינַי לֹא אָצַלְתִּי מֵהֶם" (קֹהֶלֶת ב, י),
Even though there was no discursive reason, for the primal Will has no reason, as written: "And whatsoever my eyes desired I kept not from them" (Ecclesiastes 2:10),
אַף לְהָפֵר תּוֹרָה, הֲגַם שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע טַעַם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה'", רַק חֻקָּה,
even setting aside Torah law, although he possessed no reasoned justification of "It is time to work for Hashem," but acted from supra-rational decree,
וּכְהִלְכְתָא: הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי בְּלֹא טַעֲמָא, זֶה אֵינוֹ מַסְקָנָא וְהִלְכְתָא לְהַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם;
and like a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai without stated reason—this does not serve as normative law for worldly conduct;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): בִּקֵּשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לָדוּן בְּלֹא עֵדִים וְהַתְרָאָה,
and therefore they said (Rosh Hashanah 21b end): King Solomon, peace be upon him, sought to judge without witnesses and forewarning,
וּכְטַעַם "וַיֵּשֶׁב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא ה'" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, כג), וַהֲרֵי עַל כִּסֵּא ה' יוֹשֵׁב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא!
reflecting "And Solomon sat on the throne of Hashem" (I Chronicles 29:23)—and behold, upon the throne of Hashem sits the Holy One Himself!
רַק הָאַהֲבָה הוּא הַדְּבֵיקוּת בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר: וּמִי שֶׁאוֹהֵב הַתּוֹרָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל – דָּבוּק בָּהֶם;
Rather, love is cleaving to that entity: whoever loves Torah and Israel cleaves to them;
וּמִי שֶׁאוֹהֵב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁעַל זֶה יִסַּד שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּל סֵפֶר שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים, הֲרֵי דָּבוּק בּוֹ עַד כִּבְיָכוֹל "וְהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד":
and whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He—concerning which Solomon composed the Song of Songs—cleaves to Him until, as it were, "they become one flesh."

paragraphs.text: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 1:11: “In this the children of Issachar were praised: “Those who understood the times, to know what Israel should do.” They know at each time what is suitable for that time and the remedy beneficial to the dispositions of that generation; therefore they are fit to instruct Israel what to do. The tribe of Levi is likewise suited and chosen to know the action appropriate to each particular soul and generation. This comes through complete attachment to the blessed God, as stated in Sanhedrin: “The Lord was with him”—the law followed him everywhere. Reaching the practical legal conclusion, as stated there in Yoma, comes through God’s being with him continually, as it is written, “I have set the Lord before me always.” His heart’s entire purpose is only to be an agent of the Merciful One in His service, drawn after no worldly concern. Of this it is said, “He guards the feet of His faithful ones.” A ḥasid is one separated from every kind of worldly craving, as the Sages explained in Berakhot: the term denotes separation from the three principal worldly desires—envy, appetite, and honor—as the discerning reader will see there. Therefore the holy Zohar says that a ḥasid is called an angel of the Lord, and Torah is to be sought from his mouth: he is guarded from stumbling in practice and directed toward the truth.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 32:5-7: “But regarding one who is not his companion and is not close to him, Hillel the Elder said: “Be among the disciples of Aaron, loving peace … loving creatures and bringing them close to Torah.” That is, even those distant from God’s Torah and service, and therefore described simply as “creatures,” must be drawn with thick cords of love. With all this, perhaps one may bring them close to Torah and God’s service; if not, one has still not lost the reward of the commandment to love one’s fellows. Even those close to him whom he rebuked and who did not return from their sins, whom it is a commandment to hate, must also be loved. Both are true: hatred on account of the evil within them, and love on account of the hidden good within them—the divine spark within them that gives life to their divine soul. One must also awaken compassion in one’s heart for that soul, for it is in exile within the evil of the other side that overpowers it in the wicked. Compassion cancels hatred and awakens love, as is known from “Jacob, who redeemed Abraham.” [King David’s statement “I hate them with utmost hatred” referred only to the sectarians and heretics who have no portion in the God of Israel, as stated at the beginning of chapter 16 of Shabbat.]”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 72:5: ““Leah went out to meet him” – it teaches that she did not allow him to wash his feet. “And said: You will consort with me” – Rabbi Abahu said: The Holy One blessed be He saw that her intention was exclusively for the sake of Heaven, to produce tribes. That is why it was necessary for the verse to say: “God heeded Leah” (Genesis 30:17). “And said: You will consort with me” – Rabbi Levi said: Come and see how pleasing the mediation of mandrakes was before the One who spoke and the world came into being, as, by means of the mandrakes, two great tribes in Israel were produced – Issachar and Zebulun. Issachar sits and engages in Torah study, Zebulun sets out to the seas and comes and provides for Issachar’s mouth, and the Torah proliferates in Israel – “the mandrakes emitted fragrance” (Song of Songs 7:14). “Leah said: God has given me my reward, because I gave my maidservant to my husband. She called his name Issachar” (Genesis 30:18). “Leah said: God has given me my reward [sekhari]…She called his name Issachar.” Issachar was the ninth of the tribes, but he brought his offering second to the king. That is what is written: “On the second day, Netanel ben Tzuar, prince of Issachar, presented his offering” (Numbers 7:18). Why was that? It is because he was a Torah personality. That is what is written: “From the children of Issachar, possessors of understanding of the times” (I Chronicles 12:33). What is “of the times”? Rabbi Tanḥuma said: Of the propitious time for everything. Rabbi Tanḥuma said: Of intercalations. “Their leaders were two hundred, and all their brethren at their command” (I Chronicles 12:33) – Issachar would produce two hundred heads of the Sanhedrin, and all their brethren in accordance with them, and they all agreed to rule halakha in accordance with them, and he would answer them with halakha like a halakha transmitted to Moses at Sinai. From where did Issachar come to all this prominence? It was from Zebulun, who would engage in his commerce, and would feed Issachar, who was a Torah personality. That is what is written: “Zebulun will dwell at the shore of seas” (Genesis 49:13). When Moses came to bless the tribes, he had the blessing of Zebulun precede the blessing of Issachar: “Of Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your departure, and, Issachar, in your tents” (Deuteronomy 33:18) – Rejoice, Zebulun, in your departure from the fact that Issachar is in your tents. Some say: There is reward [yesh sakhar] in the tents of Zebulun.”

paragraphs.text: The example of Rabbi Meir explains how an unusually deep root of Torah can contribute decisively even when others cannot follow it to a practical conclusion.

rich.text: The example of Rabbi Meir explains how an unusually deep root of Torah can contribute decisively even when others cannot follow it to a practical conclusion.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 16:4: “The first banner, that of the camp of Judah, is the root of Oral Torah, as it says, “Judah is My lawgiver.” Although they said that he does not bring the discussion to its halakhic conclusion, the principal root of Oral Torah nevertheless comes from the tribe of Judah. His not bringing the discussion to its halakhic conclusion is because of its great depth, which others cannot fully fathom, as they said concerning Rabbi Meir. Nevertheless, an anonymous Mishnah follows Rabbi Meir, and he is called Rabbi Meir because he illuminates the sages’ eyes in halakhah.”

rich.text: : “The first banner, that of the camp of Judah, is the root of Oral Torah, as it says, “Judah is My lawgiver.” Although they said that he does not bring the discussion to its halakhic conclusion, the principal root of Oral Torah nevertheless comes from the tribe of Judah. His not bringing the discussion to its halakhic conclusion is because of its great depth, which others cannot fully fathom, as they said concerning Rabbi Meir. Nevertheless, an anonymous Mishnah follows Rabbi Meir, and he is called Rabbi Meir because he illuminates the sages’ eyes in halakhah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah compares Yehudah’s depth to Rabbi Meir: the inability to determine the final ruling from his discussion does not mean his Torah lacks illumination for the sages. This clarifies the distinction the present siman draws between an insight into divine decrees and the practical ‘way in which to walk.’ Both can be Torah, but they play different roles. Revealed depth does not dispense with the processes through which a ruling becomes authoritative in practice.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 17:1: “In every generation, no one tasted all the attractions of this world as King Solomon did, as stated in Ecclesiastes: “I made for myself … and whatever my eyes asked for,” as is known. Nor is there a heart clean of all kinds of desire like his, as the Sages said of the Song of Songs: it is the Holy of Holies. Wherever you find a boundary against forbidden sexuality and desire, there you find holiness. For holiness means separation from desires, being devoted only to the blessed God; these are opposites. Of one immersed in desires it is said, “One who separates himself seeks desire”—he is separated from the blessed God. In holiness, however, one is consecrated to Heaven, as the Sages explain betrothal as a term of consecration, whereby a woman belongs to her husband. Song comes from longing, hence the name “songs of love.” When his soul yearns for the blessed God and is lovesick for Him, his mouth opens to sing before Him. No songs awaken Israel’s love for their Father in Heaven and their union with Him as does the Song of Songs. This love is the opposite of love of this world. Therefore it is the Holy of Holies: wholly belonging to the blessed God, entirely separated from all worldly desires and having no connection with them at all. Such is the measure: the very heart that tastes darkness to its furthest limit and seeks God from there tastes light to its furthest limit, until it apprehends that there is no darkness, and “darkness does not darken … night shines as day.””

sections.en: The Discernment of Love Is Revealed Through the Three Things in Which Our Sages…

p: [קצט] הַכָּרַת הָאַהֲבָה הוּא בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין סה:) שֶׁאָדָם נִיכָּר.
The discernment of love is revealed through the three things in which our Sages stated (Eruvin 65b) a person is recognized:
"בְּכִיסוֹ" – נֶגֶד "בְּכָל מְאֹדְךָ", וְהוּא נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
"In his pocket (kiso)" corresponds to "with all your might (me'odekha)," representing our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת סא:): יֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁמָּמוֹנוֹ וְכוּלֵי, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: "בְּכָל מְאֹדְךָ".
as our Sages stated (Berakhot 61b): there is a person whose money is dearer to him than his body, therefore it is said: "with all your might."
וּבְחֻלִּין (צא.) לָמְדוּ מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּמָמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב מִגּוּפוֹ
And in Chullin 91a they derived from our father Jacob that his property was dearer than his body
[וְזֶה נֶגֶד אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא בְּמָמוֹנוֹ, וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל].
[and this corresponds to love of Israel which is expressed through one's wealth, Jacob being the lover of Israel].
וּ"בְכוֹסוֹ" – נֶגֶד "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יַיִן וְתִירוֹשׁ יִקַּח לֵב" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ד, יא).
And "in his cup (koso)" corresponds to "with all your heart," as written: "wine and new wine take away the heart" (Hosea 4:11).
וְנִסָּיוֹן הַלֵּב הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בִּלְתִּי מְיוּשָּׁב,
And the trial of the heart occurs when one's mind is unsettled,
וְאִם כְּבָר מְמוּלָּא כָּל חֲלָלוֹ מֵעֵבֶר לְעֵבֶר בְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת, גַּם כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס יַיִן יָצָא סוֹד ה' הַגָּנוּז בּוֹ.
and if his entire cardiac cavity is truly filled from end to end with love of the Blessed Name, even when wine enters, the divine secret concealed within him issues forth.

וְכָל עִנְיַן הַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת הוּא עַל יְדֵי קִיחַת הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מֵעִנְיַן אֲמַצְיָהוּ, וְכֵן מֵחִזְקִיָּהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "עֲזָבוֹ הָאֱלֹהִים לְנַסּוֹתוֹ" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב לב, לא).
And all trials proceed through the testing of the heart, as I heard regarding Amaziah and Hezekiah, of whom it is said: "God left him, to try him" (II Chronicles 32:31).
וּלְכָךְ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" נִתְנַסָּה בְּנִסְיוֹנוֹת;
Therefore our father Abraham, who embodies "with all your heart," was tried with ten trials;
וְהוּא עִיקָּרוֹ בְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ", כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:): רַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי.
and his essence lay in love of Hashem which is "with all your heart," as they taught (Sanhedrin 106b): the Merciful One desires the heart.
וּ"בְכַעֲסוֹ" – זֶה נוֹגֵעַ עַד הַנֶּפֶשׁ, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "טֹרֵף נַפְשׁוֹ בְּאַפּוֹ" (אִיּוֹב יח, ד), הוּא נֶגֶד "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ" – אֲפִילּוּ נוֹטֵל נַפְשְׁךָ,
And "in his anger (ka'aso)" touches the very soul, as in: "You who tear yourself (nafsho) in your anger" (Job 18:4), corresponding to "with all your soul"—even if He takes your soul,
דַּרְגָּא דְּיִצְחָק שֶׁמָּסַר נַפְשׁוֹ.
the rung of Isaac who surrendered his life.
וְהוּא עִיקָּרוֹ אַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה, כַּנּוֹדָע בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, פ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה;
And that is primarily the love of Torah, as known in the Zohar (Part III, 80b) that Torah issues from Gevurah;
וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי כָּל הַמְצָאוֹת וְחִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁל חָכְמָה מִסִּטְרָא דְּיִצְחָק.
and so I heard that all innovations of wisdom stem from the side of Isaac.
וּבַתּוֹרָה נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יט, יד) – שֶׁמֵּמִית עַצְמוֹ, וְהַיְינוּ "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ".
And regarding Torah it is said: "when a man dies in a tent" (Numbers 19:14)—that one slays himself over it, which is "with all your soul."
וְרוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן טָב בְּכָל סִטְרִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קפב עַמּוּד ב), וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַעֲנִית (ד.): דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּקָא מְרַתְּחָא,
And scholarly wrath is praiseworthy from all angles as written in Zohar II:182b, which aligns with Ta'anit 4a: it is the Torah that boils within him,
פֵּירוּשׁ: כְּשֶׁהַכַּעַס הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהַתּוֹרָה מַרְתִּיחָתוֹ, שֶׁעַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה רָאוּי לִכְעוֹס,
meaning when anger arises solely because the Torah stirs him, where by Torah law it is proper to be indignant,

כְּעִנְיַן הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁדָּנוּ נְפָשׁוֹת, וְאֵין מְמַנִּין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין זָקֵן וְכוּלֵי (סַנְהֶדְרִין לו:), שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ מְלֵאִים רַחֲמִים בֶּאֱמֶת וּמִשְׁתַּדְּלִים לִמְצוֹא זְכוּת עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה, וּרְתִיחָתָם רַק מִצַּד הֶכְרֵחַ הַתּוֹרָה

— like the Sanhedrin trying capital cases, where they appoint neither the aged nor the childless (Sanhedrin 36b), for they were full of true compassion seeking exoneration, their indignation emerging solely out of halakhic necessity—
זֶה נִקְרָא רוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן, הָאוֹהֲבֵי הַתּוֹרָה בֶּאֱמֶת, שֶׁגַּם בְּעֵת כַּעֲסוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה וְזוֹכֵר וּמִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּרַחֲמִים.
this is termed scholarly wrath of those who love Torah in truth, where even in anger it stems solely from the Torah and one remembers to exercise mercy.
וְהָעֲצִירָה בְּעֵת הַכַּעַס הוּא אַהֲבָה "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ", כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "עַזָּה כַמָּוֶת אַהֲבָה, קָשָׁה כִשְׁאוֹל קִנְאָה" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח, ו),
And self-restraint during anger is love "with all your soul," matching: "for love is strong as death, jealousy is cruel as the grave" (Song of Songs 8:6),
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁאַהֲבָה שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַקִּנְאָה הוּא קָשָׁה כַּמָּוֶת, וְהַמִּתְגַּבֵּר בְּאַהֲבָה כְּנֶגֶד – זֶהוּ "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ":
meaning that love counterbalancing jealousy is as demanding as death, and one who overcomes through love embodies "with all your soul."

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 7:3: “But our Sages of blessed memory said that they rise in their garments. Those garments, which will be created anew after decay, will certainly endure forever like the bodies. They surpass even the garments in the wilderness, of which the Sages said that they grew with the wearers, and of which it is written, “Your garment did not wear out upon you.” Thus some of one’s possessions also endure forever, as they become clothing for the body. This is through the Torah and its commandments, for many commandments—almost most of them—depend on a person’s money and possessions; through this, eternal life and permanence extend into them too. The body is the garment of the soul, and possessions are the garment of the body. The righteous, whose bodies have already been refined, cherish the garment, namely money: the coarser and more outward the garment, the more effort it needs. This is therefore more precious and beautiful to them, for there the effort is greater, and therefore the longing is greater.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 4:4: “Likewise, “They drank and became intoxicated with him” took place at a Shabbat meal. Bereishit Rabbah expounds “and prepare”: “Preparation” refers to Shabbat. On Shabbat the will of Atika, the Ancient One, is revealed: by day is the meal of Atika, and at the Friday-night meal the Holy Ancient One comes to dine with her [the Shekhinah]. Knowledge, which is the inwardness of the supernal crown, is revealed, and for this reason drinking is permitted then. This is why Joseph’s brothers drank at that time, although they had not drunk throughout the preceding twenty-two years, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah and the Talmud. Joseph shone the holiness of Shabbat into them; they felt the holiness of the Shabbat meal and drank. Joseph’s intention in giving them wine was to learn the depths of their hearts: were they bound to the root? This resembles the saying in Sanhedrin, “Increase their wine ... wine enters, the secret comes out.””
