paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Vayikra 6: “To this matter also belongs the case of Amaziah king of Judah. He struck ten thousand of Edom and hurled ten thousand from the top of the rock, so that they were shattered. Afterward he worshipped the gods of Edom and sent to Joash king of Israel: “Come, let us face one another.” The meaning is that Edom is the foremost husk, the most important of all the nations, as stated in Avodah Zarah: Edom enters immediately after Israel because of its importance. Immediately beyond this husk begins the name Israel. At present Israel has not been granted authority over them; that is only for the future, as explained in its place. Amaziah’s killing of the twenty thousand corresponds to the ten levels of the husk, for “God made this opposite that”: twenty thousand alludes to all ten levels from below upward and from above downward. He thought that since his power over them had become so great, whatever he now did would surely not turn his heart from God, nor would any evil have power to prevail over him, as will be in the future. He therefore tried worshipping the gods of Edom and sent Joash, “Come, let us face one another,” meaning: Although I have done something that appears evil, I am still more attached to the blessed God than you. But this was not the blessed God’s will. Therefore he was punished, and Joash king of Israel captured him. Nevertheless, it says there that Amaziah lived fifteen years after Joash’s death, hinting that in all fifteen levels found in Israel, Amaziah was greater than Joash, and his sin was only relative to the limits of human apprehension.”

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Shabbat 138b:1: ““The deep” signifies the things a person does in concealment while directing himself to the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, because in the depths of his heart he is attached to Him, even where his intellect and awareness do not reach. This is “By His knowledge the depths were split”: from the depths of the human heart, the Holy One, blessed be He, builds within a person’s heart the fulfillment of His will even in concealment, thereby clarifying that he is wholly attached to Him. This is the meaning of “by His knowledge”—not by human knowledge. Thus we find of Hezekiah king of Judah: “And so with the envoys of the princes of Babylon … God left him, to test him, to know all that was in his heart.” He concealed Himself from him and tested whether he would direct himself to God’s will even in concealment, as it is written, “I will surely hide My face on that day.””

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 7:10: “The Torah comes from the side of might, which is the mystery of restraint: one’s conduct is bounded by “Do this and do not do that.” Yet this restraint of Torah is entirely an expansion, for it is the root of Jacob’s inheritance without boundaries. Through this temporary restraint in this world, one grasps the tree of life and merits the abundance of Torah, whose measure is “longer than the earth and broader than the sea.” The restraint applies only to bodily activities and deeds. In apprehension, however—the principal wisdom of Torah, through contemplation in the mind and heart—one may expand without boundaries. “From the narrow place I called to God; He answered me with spaciousness”: the calling is the beginning of entry into Torah, which needs restraint and a narrow passage. Afterward, when the blessed God answers and helps him, he is in spaciousness.”

The anger of the Sages concerns words of Torah. The anger of the Sages is to give honor to Torah, and all of it is for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore it is said: ‘For Hashem your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God’ (Deuteronomy 4:24).’

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 6:2: “The root of the evil inclination is the fire of anger, as in “His fury burned within him”; it wishes to burn and consume everything. Corresponding to this in holiness is Oral Torah: much wisdom to repair much anger. It too is fire, as the Gemara says: “When a Torah scholar grows heated, Torah is what heats him, as it is written, ‘Are not My words like fire?’” It is a fire consuming the fire of the evil inclination, burning and consuming that inclination. paragraphs.text: Explanation: The Kislev passage explains what distinguishes two outwardly similar intensities: the inclination’s fire consumes indiscriminately, while Torah’s fire is directed against the inclination itself. This sharpens the test given here for the anger of a talmid chacham. The Sanhedrin’s search for merit and continuing compassion are not exceptions to holy zeal; they show that the heat remains governed by Torah rather than by personal aggression. Self-restraint therefore expresses love ‘with all your soul.’

sections.en: There Are Three Categories of Love

p: [ר] יֵשׁ שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינִים בְּאַהֲבָה: אַהֲבָה זוּטָא וְאַהֲבָה רַבָּה נִזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר פְּקוּדֵי (רנד עַמּוּד ב), וְאַהֲבָה רַבָּה וְאַהֲבַת עוֹלָם נִזְכָּר בְּנוּסַח בִּרְכַּת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בִּבְרָכוֹת (יא:).

There are three categories of love: Minor Love (Ahavah Zuta) and Great Love (Ahavah Rabbah) mentioned in Zohar Pekudei (254b); and Ahavah Rabbah and Eternal Love (Ahavat Olam) mentioned in the liturgy of the Shema blessings in Berakhot 11b.
וְהֵם בְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכֵן בְּאַהֲבָתָם לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי מִסְּתָמָא הֵם מַקְבִּילִים מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה.
And these apply to Hashem's love for Israel and Israel's love for Hashem, corresponding measure for measure.
פֵּירוּשׁ: "אַהֲבָה זוּטָא" הִיא הַנִּקְרֵאת בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "אַהֲבָה מְסֻתָּרֶת" (מִשְׁלֵי כז, ה), שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת בְּלִבּוֹ לִהְיוֹת בּוֹעֵר כְּרִשְׁפֵּי אֵשׁ,
Minor Love is termed in Scripture "hidden love" (Proverbs 27:5), which is not openly revealed in the heart to burn like flaming coals,
שֶׁהַתּוֹכַחַת מְגוּלָּה שֶׁמּוֹכִיחַ לְלִבּוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב וּמְיַסְּרָהּ עַל רִחוּקָהּ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה – טוֹבָה הֵימֶנָּה.
so that open rebuke where one rebukes his heart in outward anguish over being distant from Hashem—which is the attribute of fear—is better than it.
הֲגַם דְּאַהֲבָה גָּדוֹל מִיִּרְאָה, זֶהוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת וְהִתְלַהֲבוּת בַּלֵּב, וְנִקְרָא "אַהֲבָה רַבָּה".
Although love is greater than fear, that applies when love is likewise outwardly felt in fiery enthusiasm within the heart, termed Ahavah Rabbah.

אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּה רַק מַתְּנַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ, כְּמוֹ הַיִּרְאָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת שֶׁיָּכוֹל לָבוֹא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹכַחַת לְלִבּוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם לג:): הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם חוּץ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.

Except that this is a divine gift from Hashem and is not in human hands through effort alone, unlike manifest awe which can be attained through rebuking one's heart, as stated: "All is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven" (Berakhot 33b).
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רֹאשׁ הַמִּשְׁתַּדְּלִים זָכָה לְמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה שֶׁהוּא מַתְּנַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת;
And our father Abraham, leader of strivers, merited love which is truly Hashem's gift without human striving;
וְיִצְחָק, רֹאשׁ הַנּוֹלָדִים מְקוּדָּשִׁים מִלֵּידָה מִבֶּטֶן וְהֻבְטַח טֶרֶם לֵידָתוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה זֶרַע ה', זָכָה לְמִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁהוּא בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם.
while Isaac, foremost of those born sanctified from the womb, promised before birth to be God's seed, merited fear which depends upon human exertion.
כִּי כָּךְ מִדָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ: לְהַרְאוֹת לְכָל אֶחָד הַהֵיפֶךְ, לְמַעַן יֵדַע כִּי יַד ה' עָשְׂתָה כָּל אֵלֶּה.
For such is His divine way: to manifest within each the opposite, so that one recognizes that the hand of Hashem wrought all this.
וּבֶאֱמֶת כֻּלָּם כְּלוּלִים בַּכֹּל, רַק אֵצֶל יִצְחָק הָיְתָה מִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה מְסֻתֶּרֶת, וְהִיא אַהֲבָה זוּטָא, וְהַיִּרְאָה בְּתֹקֶף.
And in truth all are inter-included, only that with Isaac love was concealed—being Ahavah Zuta—while awe surged in power.

וּמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִיא מִדַּת "אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם", שֶׁהוּא הַמַּבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה, וּמִדַּת הָאֱמֶת וְקַיָּים לָעַד שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בִּיטּוּל וְהֶפְסֵק, כְּטַעַם (תַּעֲנִית ה:): יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לֹא מֵת.

And the attribute of our father Jacob is Ahavat Olam (Eternal Love), which traverses from end to end, the attribute of truth enduring forever without cessation, reflecting: "our father Jacob did not die" (Ta'anit 5b).
כִּי כָּל תֹּקֶף אַהֲבָה אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְשָׁעָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶעְלָם;
For intense love is often momentary and subsequently recedes;
וְגַם יֵשׁ חִלּוּק לָאָדָם: כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּשִׂמְחָה וְנִיחָא אָז גּוֹבֵר מִדַּת אַהֲבָה, וּבְצַעַר וְצָרָה – מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה;
and there is a distinction in man: when in joy and tranquility love surges, while in sorrow and distress awe dominates;
וּבֶאֱמֶת צָרִיךְ לְאַהֲבָה בֵּין בְּטִיבוּ בֵּין בְּעָקוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהַקְדָּמַת הַזֹּהַר (יב עַמּוּד א).
and in truth one must love both in prosperity and in adversity, as written in the Zohar's introduction (12a).

וְזֶה נִדְרַשׁ בִּבְרָכוֹת (נד.) מִ"בְּכָל מְאֹדְךָ", שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא הָיָה כּוֹלֵל שְׁתֵּי הַמִּדּוֹת בְּכָל זְמַן, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג): אֲנִי יָרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי וְשָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי.

And this is derived in Berakhot 54a from "with all your might," which corresponds to our father Jacob who integrated both traits at all times, as in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu: "I feared out of my joy, and rejoiced out of my fear."

וְלָכֵן אוֹמְרִים בְּעַרְבִית "אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם" נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁתִּיקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית, וְהוּא מִדָּתוֹ: לִהְיוֹת גַּם בָּעֶרֶב וְעֵת חֶשְׁכַּת הַצָּרוֹת הָאַהֲבָה בִּלְתִּי נִיתֶּקֶת.
Therefore we recite in the evening service Ahavat Olam facing Jacob who instituted Maariv, his trait being that even in the evening darkness of distress love remains unsevered.

וּבְשַׁחֲרִית – בֹּקֶר דְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁתִּיקֵּן תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית – "אַהֲבָה רַבָּה" כְּמִדָּתוֹ, כִּי בְּאוֹר הַיּוֹם הַמֵּאִיר וּבָא לְלִבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתְלַהֵב הַלֵּב בְּאַהֲבָה רַבָּה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה: אַהֲבָה רַבָּה אֲהַבְתָּנוּ וְכוּלֵי.

And in Shacharit—the morning of Abraham who instituted Shacharit—we recite Ahavah Rabbah reflecting his trait, for in the daylight shining into Jewish hearts the heart burns with intense love for Hashem, and measure for measure: "With a great love have You loved us, etc."

וְנוּסְחַת גַּם בְּשַׁחֲרִית "אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם", כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר כֵּן בִּבְרָכוֹת (יא:), כִּי אִם עַכְשָׁו בַּגָּלוּת צְרִיכִין לְעוֹרֵר מִדָּה זוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם גַּם בְּעָקוּ לְעוֹלָם גַּם בַּיּוֹם.
And the custom reciting Ahavat Olam in the morning as well (Berakhot 11b) reflects that in exile we must awaken this eternal love in adversity constantly, even by day.

וּמִדַּת אַהֲבָה רַבָּה נֶעְלֶמֶת, שֶׁאִלּוּ נִגְלֵית בְּלֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְעֻמָּתָם כֵּן, הָיָה מִתְקַיֵּים: "מַיִם רַבִּים לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְכַבּוֹת אֶת הָאַהֲבָה" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח, ז) – הֵם הָאֻמּוֹת – וְהָיוּ נוֹפְלִים תַּחַת יִשְׂרָאֵל.

And Ahavah Rabbah is concealed, for had it been openly revealed in the hearts of Israel, Hashem would correspond, fulfilling: "Many waters cannot quench love"—the nations—and they would fall beneath Israel.

רַק שֶׁאַהֲבָה זוֹ בְּהִתְלַהֲבוּת הָרָאוּי נֶעְלֶמֶת מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וּבָטַל אֵשׁ הַמַּעֲרָכָה שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הָיָה הַסַּיַּעְתָּא לִצְמוֹחַ אֵשׁ הִתְלַהֲבוּת לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, נִפְסַק זוֹ.
But this love in its proper blazing fervor has been concealed since the Temple was destroyed, and the Altar fire ceased from which assistance sprang to ignite fiery passion for Hashem.
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֶּאֱרַע לִפְעָמִים, אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דִּמְיוֹן וּבְהִתְגַּלּוּת הַלֵּב וְלֹא בְּמַעֲמַקָּיו.
And even if it occurs occasionally, it is often imagination in superficial emotion rather than in the depths of the heart.

וּכְעִנְיַן שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "לֹא בָאֵשׁ ה'" (מְלָכִים א יט, יב), כִּי צָרִיךְ לָזֶה מִבְחָן וּבֵירוּר עֲדַיִן אִם הוּא אֱמֶת גָּמוּר שֶׁאַהֲבָתוֹ עַזָּה כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת הַדְּבֵיקוּת, וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה ה' בְּקִרְבּוֹ מַמָּשׁ כְּמִשְׁפַּט הָאַהֲבָה בַּחֲשׁוּקִים:

And in the manner of "Hashem was not in the fire" (I Kings 19:12), one still requires testing to verify if it is absolute truth that his love is so fierce as to reach devekut, where Hashem abides within him literally like the love of devoted lovers.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 36:1: “There, at the upper root, it is called great love; all the levels and garments are called everlasting love, which is small love. Through their service in small love, Israel breaks through all the veils and recognizes His unity, saying, ‘Hear, Israel… Hashem is one.’ Israel therefore has a place in the light of His unity, so that even this verse, ‘Hear, Israel… Hashem is one,’ is called kingship on Israel's side. This is Rabbi Yose's reasoning in saying that ‘Hear, Israel…’ counts as kingship.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The terms need to be read in context. This siman distinguishes hidden love, revealed intensity and love's endurance through changing conditions. Sod Yesharim instead calls the revealed upper root great love and the clothed levels everlasting love or small love. Its measure is concealment and revelation. The shared names therefore do not justify treating the two classifications as an identical fixed hierarchy.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 42:1: “Fear is the root of the prohibitions, the level of Isaac, the mighty one who conquers his inclination. This is the whole root of his effort: to clarify “You shall have no other gods”—every kind of dross and the separation of evil from good, the outer boundary of the world that distinguishes it from what lies beyond. This is possible only for one whose conception and birth are in holiness, and in whose heart the root of “I am the Lord your God” is already fixed and enduring, a peg that cannot move. Nevertheless, afterward he still needs the warning “You shall have no other gods.” Even one who is an Israelite from birth, a believer descended from believers, can have evil prevail within him, God forbid, so strongly that it says to him, “Go, worship,” until it can even sever his root, God forbid—as with Esau, who is called an apostate Israelite in Kiddushin, yet became a nation of his own. All the effort of our father Isaac was directed toward this: to beget Jacob, whose offspring are complete, whose root cannot be severed in any way, for “even though he sinned, he is Israel.””

paragraphs.text: The union of love and awe is more stable than an alternation between youthful excitement and aged restraint.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:23:1: “Love is characteristic of youth, unlike old age, when ‘desire fails.’ As is known, Shlomo in his youth composed Shir HaShirim, the intensity of love, and in his old age Kohelet, the intensity of awe. Avraham, however, established something new in the circulating coin: on one coin, an old man and woman on one side, and a young man and maiden on the other, all united in a complete union—love and awe.”

rich.text: : “Love is characteristic of youth, unlike old age, when ‘desire fails.’ As is known, Shlomo in his youth composed Shir HaShirim, the intensity of love, and in his old age Kohelet, the intensity of awe. Avraham, however, established something new in the circulating coin: on one coin, an old man and woman on one side, and a young man and maiden on the other, all united in a complete union—love and awe.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah uses Avraham's coin to describe love and awe existing within one whole. The image helps explain the present siman's demand for love that remains even in darkness and distress: the purpose is not to eliminate awe, but to prevent either condition from excluding the other. It also preserves the distinction between a passing intensity of love and the union that continues through changing circumstances.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Introduction 22:200-201: “Therefore we learned: love, the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, is distinguished on two sides. There is one who loves Him because he has wealth, length of days, children around him, mastery over his enemies, and success in his ways; because of this he loves Him. If these circumstances were reversed and the Holy One, blessed be He, brought upon him a turn of harsh judgment, he would hate Him and not love Him at all. Therefore this love is not a love with a root. Love called complete is that which exists on both sides, in judgment as in goodness. His ways are set right so that he loves his Master, as we learned, even if He takes your soul from you. This is complete love on both sides. Thus the light of Creation came forth and afterward was hidden. When it was hidden, harsh judgment emerged, and both sides were included together, so that this love would be properly complete.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 13:11-14: “This love described in intermediate people during prayer, through the strengthening of the divine soul, is not called “service in truth” at all in comparison with the level of the righteous who serve God in His fullest truth, since it passes and departs after prayer; and it is written, “A truthful lip endures forever, but a lying tongue is only for a moment.” Nevertheless, in relation to the level of intermediate people it is called complete service in their fullest truth, each according to his own level among them. I also apply “A truthful lip endures forever” to their love during prayer, since their divine soul has the power to awaken this love again always, through its strengthening during prayer day after day, with the preparation suited to each soul’s standing and level. For truth is the attribute of Jacob, called “the middle bar that extends from end to end”—from the height of levels to the end of all ranks. Within every level it runs through the middle point, which is that level’s point and quality of truth. Truth is “an inheritance without boundaries,” without an upward limit, to the highest levels. All lower levels are as nothing compared with those above them [as is known to those versed in the hidden wisdom: the head and intellect of lower levels are below the heels and feet of higher ones, as our Sages said, “The feet of the living creatures correspond to them all”].”

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Numbers, Korach 1: “All this is not yet completely clarified, as we find written: “The Lord was not in the wind … the Lord was not in the earthquake.” Wind corresponds to the will found in a person of good deeds; earthquake is the fear within Torah, corresponding to the righteous person; and fire corresponds to the priest, whose service is in mighty love. Therefore it was first written, “The God who answers by fire—He is God; and all the people answered, ‘The proposal is good.’” They all agreed that the one able to act before the blessed God through service in mighty love is the one God chose. Yet afterward the blessed God showed Elijah the prophet that after all these things a person still needs God to agree and set His seal upon all of them. Thus it says, “After the fire, a still, thin voice”: voice is God’s seal upon wind, the will of one who performs good deeds—when they come from God, they are good; stillness is God’s seal upon earthquake; thinness is God’s seal upon fire. When God seals these things, so that the person does not incline in them toward his own interest, they are completely clarified. For even in such matters, when a person longs for love and fear, he may covet them as he covets worldly things. He needs the blessed God to affirm that his intention is truly for the sake of Heaven.”

sections.en: Surrendering One's Life (mesirut Nefesh) for the Love of Hashem Is Not Limited To…

p: [רא] מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ בִּשְׁבִיל אַהֲבַת ה' אֵינוֹ הַנֶּפֶשׁ לְבַד כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ, אֶלָּא גַּם הַנְּשָׁמָה,
Surrendering one's life (mesirut nefesh) for the love of Hashem is not limited to the bodily life (nefesh) alone, but includes the soul (neshamah),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר תְּרוּמָה (קסג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א) דְּ"בְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ" הַיְינוּ נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה
as written in Zohar Terumah (163a) that "with all your soul" encompasses Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah
[דִּלְשׁוֹן "כָּל" מַשְׁמָע לְפָחוֹת עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת כְּתוּבּוֹת (ח.).
[for the word 'all' (kol) denotes at least three things, as Tosafot write in Ketubot 8a.
וְכֵן "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" הֵם שְׁלֹשָׁה כִּתּוֹת שֶׁבַּלֵּב: קִנְאָה, וְתַאֲוָה, וְכָבוֹד, דְּהַיְינוּ שְׁנֵי הַחֲלָלִים שֶׁבַּלֵּב יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל וְחִבּוּרָם יַחַד.
And likewise 'with all your heart' encompasses the three drives: envy, lust, and honor—the right cavity, the left cavity, and their union.
וּ"בְכָל מְאֹדְךָ" אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר שָׁם דְּכַמָּה זִינִין אִינּוּן בְּמָמוֹן, פֵּירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי תְּרוּמוֹת סוֹף פֶּרֶק ח): לִבָּא בְּכִיסָא תַּלְיָא;
And 'with all your might,' the Zohar states there are many facets to wealth, as in Yerushalmi Terumot 8: the heart depends upon the pocket;
וּכְפִי הִתְחַלְּקוּת יִצְרֵי הַלֵּב כָּךְ הִתְחַלְּקוּת חֶמְדַּת הַמָּמוֹן: יֵשׁ שֶׁמָּמוֹנוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל קִנְאָה וְנִיצּוּחַ, וְיֵשׁ לְמִלּוּי תַּאֲוָה, וְיֵשׁ לְהַשִּׂיג כָּבוֹד עַל יָדוֹ],
and according to the drives of the heart is the pursuit of money: for rivalry, for physical lust, or to attain honor],
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "מְחֵנִי נָא מִסִּפְרְךָ אֲשֶׁר כָּתָבְתָּ" (שְׁמוֹת לב, לב) בִּשְׁבִיל אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and in the manner of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him: "blot me, I pray You, out of Your book which You have written" (Exodus 32:32) out of love for Israel.
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּקֵּשׁ לַעֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קז.) כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִתְחַלֵּל וְכוּלֵי, דְּהַיְינוּ בִּשְׁבִיל אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And King David, peace be upon him, sought to serve idols (Sanhedrin 107a) so that the Name of Heaven not be profaned, out of love for the Blessed Name.

וּמְקוֹשֵׁשׁ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם נִתְכַּוֵּין, הַיְינוּ בִּשְׁבִיל אַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הֲלָכָה זוֹ בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁל חִיּוּב מִיתָה לִמְחַלֵּל שַׁבָּת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קיט: בְּשֵׁם מִדְרָשׁ), הֲגַם דְּהוּא יֵעָנֵשׁ;

And the wood-gatherer (Mekoshesh) intended for the sake of Heaven out of love of the Torah, so that the halakhah of capital liability for desecrating the Sabbath would be clarified (Tosafot Bava Batra 119b citing a Midrash), even though he would be executed;

וְזָכָה גַּם כֵּן לְבָנוֹת שֶׁנִּתְלִין בּוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ נִדָּה לא סוֹף עַמּוּד א): חַכְמָנִיּוֹת, דַּרְשָׁנִיּוֹת, וְנִתְגַּלָּה גַּם כֵּן עַל יָדָם פָּרָשָׁה מְחוּדֶּשֶׁת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בִּנְחָלוֹת.
and he merited daughters who traced to him (Niddah 31a end)—wise, exegetical women—through whom a novel section of Torah on inheritances was revealed.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי: עִנְיַן הַיְרֻשָּׁה עִיקָּרוֹ יְרֻשַּׁת הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁל הָאָב לַבֵּן.
As I heard: the essence of inheritance is the transmission of the father's spiritual powers to the son.
וְיָדוּעַ נוּקְבָא הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק וְחִסָּרוֹן, וּדְכוּרָא – הַמִּלּוּי, וּלְכָךְ הַיְרֻשָּׁה לִדְכוּרָא;
And the female represents yearning and lack, while the male represents fulfillment, which is why inheritance normally passes to the male;
אַךְ כְּשֶׁאֵין לוֹ בֵּן, זֶהוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ מִלּוּי, רַק תֹּקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לְבַד שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִסִּטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא, אָז זֶה הַחֵלֶק גַּם הַבָּנוֹת יוֹרְשׁוֹת.
but when he has no son, it indicates he lacked fulfillment, possessing only intense desire from the female side, which the daughters then inherit.

וּמְקוֹשֵׁשׁ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ הַחֵשֶׁק לַתּוֹרָה כָּל כָּךְ, הֲגַם שֶׁלֹּא נִתְגַּלְּתָה הַהֲלָכָה אֶלָּא בְּמִיתָתוֹ, נִמְצָא לֹא זָכָה לְהַמִּלּוּי וְהָיָה לוֹ רַק הַחֵשֶׁק, לְכָךְ לֹא הָיָה לוֹ כִּי אִם בָּנוֹת,

And the Mekoshesh whose passion for Torah was so intense, yet whose halakhah was revealed only through his death, lacked personal fulfillment, retaining only the yearning; hence he had only daughters,
וְנִתְגַּלָּה עַל יָדָם פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ שֶׁהֵם יוֹרְשִׁים כֹּחוֹתָיו בְּמוֹתוֹ, שֶׁאָז הָיָה מִלּוּי חֶשְׁקוֹ, וְכֹחוֹתָיו הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק.
and through them this passage was revealed, inheriting his spiritual power at his death when his desire reached fulfillment.
וְכֵן הַמְטַיְּילִים בַּפַּרְדֵּ"ס יֵשׁ לָהֶם מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ בִּשְׁבִיל אַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי יְכוֹלִים לִטְעוֹת כֶּאֱלִישָׁע אַחֵר.
And so those who entered the Pardes practiced self-sacrifice for love of the Torah, being at risk of stumbling like Elisha Acher.
וּמִי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ שָׁלֵם בְּכָל שָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת הָאַהֲבָה, הֲרֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁנִּכְנַס בְּשָׁלוֹם וְיָצָא בְּשָׁלוֹם.
And he whose heart is complete across all three rungs of love merits like Rabbi Akiva, who entered in peace and departed in peace.

וְאַחֵר לֹא הָיָה שָׁלֵם בְּ"בְכָל לְבָבְךָ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה טו: רַשִּׁ"י דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "נוֹשְׁרִין"): טִינָא הָיְתָה בְּלִבּוֹ, שֶׁזֶּה נֶגֶד אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת קצ"ט – יָצָא לְתַרְבּוּת רָעָה.
And Acher was not whole in "with all your heart," as Rashi comments in Chagigah 15b that there was mud in his heart—counter to love of Hashem (Section 199)—and he fell into heresy.
וּבֶן עַזַּאי נַפְשׁוֹ חָשְׁקָה בַּתּוֹרָה, זֶהוּ נֶגֶד "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ" וְאַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה, רַק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה נָאֶה מְקַיֵּים כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (סג:);
And Ben Azzai's soul yearned for the Torah, corresponding to "with all your soul" and love of the Torah, only that he did not fulfill procreation (Yevamot 63b);

וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שָׁם קט.): כָּל הָאוֹמֵר אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה, אַף תּוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ, שֶׁזֶּה חִסָּרוֹן בְּאַהֲבַת הַתּוֹרָה כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַיֵּים, וְהוּא חִסָּרוֹן בְּאַהֲבָה דְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ, לָכֵן עָנְשׁוֹ בַּנֶּפֶשׁ וּבְמִיתָה.

and on this they said (ibid. 109b): whoever says he has nothing but Torah does not even possess Torah, for neglecting performance is a flaw in love of Torah and in "with all your soul," so his penalty was death.
וּמָצִינוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (י.) בְּחִזְקִיָּהוּ גַּם כֵּן: "מֵת תָּמוּת" עַל שֶׁלֹּא קִיֵּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה.
And we find in Berakhot 10a regarding Hezekiah likewise: "you shall die" for not engaging in procreation.
וּבַזֹּהַר פְּקוּדֵי (רנד עַמּוּד ב) דְּהוּא אִדְבַּק בְּעָפָר, וְיָדוּעַ דְּרַע שֶׁבִּיסוֹד הֶעָפָר הוּא הָעַצְלוּת בְּקִיּוּם הַמִּצְווֹת.
And in Zohar Pekudei (254b) that he cleaved to Earth, and it is known that the negative aspect of the element of Earth is sluggishness in fulfilling mitzvot.
וְאַחֵר אִדְבַּק בְּאֵשׁ, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הַכַּעַס נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב אֵשׁ, וְכֵן הַתַּאֲוָה בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין פא.): חֲזֵי דְּאַתְּ נוּרָא.
And Acher cleaved to Fire, whence anger is called fire in Scripture, and likewise lust (Kiddushin 81a): "see that you are fire."
וּבֶן זוֹמָא בְּרוּחַ, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ בָּא לֵיצָנוּת וְהִתְפָּאֲרוּת.
And Ben Zoma cleaved to Air/Wind, whence issue levity and self-aggrandizement.

וַהֲגַם דְּאֶצְלוֹ הָיָה הַכֹּל קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר בִּבְרָכוֹת (נח.): וּבָרָא כָּל אֵלּוּ לְשַׁמְּשֵׁנִי, וְהוּא לְשִׁיטָתוֹ (שָׁם ו:): כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לְצַוֶּות לָזֶה, וְכָךְ הוּא הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ;

And although with him everything was holy of holies, as in Berakhot 58a: "He created all these to serve me," following his view (ibid. 6b): "the entire world was created to accompany this one," which is absolute truth;
רַק לְפִי שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִסְמַךְ הָיָה זֶה לִקְצָת חִסָּרוֹן.
yet because he had not yet been ordained, this was accounted as a slight flaw.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּחֲגִיגָה (יד:): שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת בֶּן זוֹמָא: מַהוּ לְסָרוֹסֵי כַּלְבָּא, שֶׁהוּא אִם לֹא נִתְלוֹצֵץ מִבְּרִיָּה הַיּוֹתֵר פְּחוּתָה שֶׁבַּבְּרִיּוֹת, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
And as I heard on Chagigah 14b: they asked Ben Zoma whether one may castrate a dog, testing whether he mocked the lowliest creature, and this is not the place to elaborate.
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ עָלָיו: "פֶּן תִּשְׂבָּעֶנּוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי כה, טז), שֶׁקִּבֵּל יוֹתֵר מֵהָרָאוּי.
Therefore they applied to him: "lest you be filled therewith and vomit it" (Proverbs 25:16), having absorbed more than was fitting.

וּבֶאֱמֶת חָכְמָתוֹ מֻפְלֶגֶת מִכָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ, שֶׁמִּצַּד זֶה נִמְשַׁךְ הִתְפָּאֲרוּת נֶגֶד הַכֹּל כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּזְכַרְיָה: רָאָה עַצְמוֹ לְמַעְלָה וְכוּלֵי (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה י), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (נז:): בֶּן זוֹמָא יְצַפֶּה לְחָכְמָה, וּלְכָךְ עָנְשׁוֹ "נִפְגַּע", שֶׁהוּא הֶעְדֵּר הַחָכְמָה.

And in truth his wisdom was exalted above all, whence self-aggrandizement arose as with Zechariah (Kohelet Rabbah 10); and Berakhot 57b: one who sees Ben Zoma should anticipate wisdom; hence his penalty was being stricken in mind, which is the loss of wisdom.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהַפְּגָם בְּאַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַנִּפְגָּע וְיוֹצֵא מִדַּעַת הוּא מוּבְדָּל מֵאַהֲבַת רֵעִים, וְאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא קַמָּא פז.): חֵרֵשׁ, שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן פְּגִיעָתָן רָעָה וְכוּלֵי.
And because the flaw touched love of Israel, one who loses his mind is cut off from social companionship; and Bava Kamma 87a states: injury by a deaf-mute, idiot, or minor is calamitous.
אֲבָל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁנִּכְנַס בְּהֵיכַל אַהֲבָה, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּזֹּהַר, שֶׁהָיָה שָׁלֵם בְּכָל חֶלְקֵי הָאַהֲבָה – יָצָא בְּשָׁלוֹם:
But Rabbi Akiva who entered the Palace of Love (see Zohar there), being complete in all dimensions of love, departed in peace.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayera 57:4: “He did not look to any of this, but cast his life aside for love of Hashem. He surrendered himself in both worlds, agreeing that no continuation of himself should remain, solely for love of Hashem. His reward is therefore doubled and multiplied.”

rich.text: : “He did not look to any of this, but cast his life aside for love of Hashem. He surrendered himself in both worlds, agreeing that no continuation of himself should remain, solely for love of Hashem. His reward is therefore doubled and multiplied.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: In the preceding paragraph Beit Yaakov explains that Avraham's readiness to offer his only son seemed to leave him without reward or enduring continuation. The quoted conclusion therefore describes self-giving in two worlds, not bodily courage alone. This makes the opening of the present siman concrete: the attachment being yielded can include one's expectation of spiritual attainment and legacy. The illustration remains Avraham's response to a divine command.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Terumah 66:670: ““And with all your soul”: it could have said “with your soul.” What is “with all your soul”—why this “all”? Rather, it includes nefesh, ruaḥ, and neshamah. This is “with all your soul”: with everything bound to this soul. “And with all your might” is similar: there are several kinds of possessions, all differing from one another, and therefore it says “all.” Love of the Holy One, blessed be He, means handing all of this over to Him, loving Him with each and every one.”

This is “with all your soul”: with everything bound to this soul. “And with all your might” is similar: there are several kinds of possessions, all differing from one another, and therefore it says “all.” Love of the Holy One, blessed be He, means handing all of this over to Him, loving Him with each and every one.”

paragraphs.text: Context: The Zohar explicitly includes all three levels of soul and all varieties of possessions. The latter part also supplies the source Rav Tzadok cites a few phrases later.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: As I heard: the essence of inheritance is the transmission of the father's spiritual powers to the son.

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:140: “Whether a person is rich or poor depends on his mazal—that is, on the receptivity of his mazal and hidden root. How, then, does a poor son inherit a rich father when the father dies, if the son lacks the capacity to receive so much wealth? In truth, the father’s hevel de-garmei, the power of his mazal and hidden root, extends into the son himself, and the son becomes a vessel able to receive it. Therefore, in the chapter “HaPoalim,” concerning Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, they said, “The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life”: every son can attain his father’s level after his death if he wishes. This concerns the level of a righteous person; concerning the level of a Torah scholar, however, they said in Nedarim that scholars do not commonly bequeath it to their sons, for the three kinds of gifts correspond to the three hidden powers mentioned above.”

paragraphs.text: Yevamot 109b:4-6: “One who fixes himself in a matter of halakhah: it was taught that Rabbi Yosei says, “Whoever says that he has no Torah has no Torah.” That is obvious! Rather: “Whoever says that he has only Torah has only Torah.” This too is obvious! Rather, he does not have even Torah. Why? Rav Pappa said: Scripture says, “You shall learn and you shall do”—whoever participates in doing participates in learning; whoever does not participate in doing does not participate in learning. Alternatively, it is as you said at first: whoever says that he has only Torah has only Torah. This is needed where he teaches others and they go and act. One might have thought that he receives their reward; it teaches us otherwise.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Pekudei 51:666-670: “In this manner we learned: Four entered Pardes, and all were tested at this place, in these four elements. Each became attached to his place: one to the side of fire, one to water, one to air, and one to earth. All sank in their element as they entered, except for that perfect, pious one, who came from the right side, clung to the right, and ascended above. When he reached the place called the Palace of Love, he clung to it with the will of his heart. He said: This palace must be joined to the palace above through great love. Then he became complete in the mystery of faith; he ascended and properly completed lesser love with great love. Therefore he died in love, and his soul departed with the verse “You shall love.” Happy is his portion! All the others descended below, each one, and were punished in the element into which they descended. Elisha descended on the left side, which is fire; he descended into it and did not ascend, encountering the other side called “another god.” Repentance was withheld from him, and he was expelled because he clung to it; therefore he is called Aḥer, as we have explained. Ben Azzai descended into the element of earth; before reaching the burning of earth that extends to the other side, he sank in that earth and died. Of this it is written, “Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones.” Ben Zoma descended into the element of air and encountered another spirit reaching the side of impurity, called an evil affliction. It therefore struck him, and he did not become settled. None of them escaped punishment. Of this Solomon said, “There is a vanity that occurs upon the earth: there are righteous people to whom it happens according to the deeds of the wicked,” because these descended into these levels and were punished.”

Ben Azzai descended into the element of earth; before reaching the burning of earth that extends to the other side, he sank in that earth and died. Of this it is written, “Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones.” Ben Zoma descended into the element of air and encountered another spirit reaching the side of impurity, called an evil affliction. It therefore struck him, and he did not become settled. None of them escaped punishment. Of this Solomon said, “There is a vanity that occurs upon the earth: there are righteous people to whom it happens according to the deeds of the wicked,” because these descended into these levels and were punished.”

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Emor 4: ““In your land you shall not do this”: this means not to mock the creatures of the Holy One, blessed be He. The Gemara in Ḥagigah derives from this that castration is forbidden, and this signifies the prohibition against mockery. As stated there, they asked Ben Zoma: May one castrate a dog? He answered: “In your land you shall not do this”—do not do this to anything in your land. They also asked whether a virgin who became pregnant was permitted to a High Priest: should one be concerned about Shmuel’s case? He answered that Shmuel’s case was uncommon. They asked these questions because they saw that he had not descended in peace—as the Gemara says, he looked and was stricken—and understood that his apprehension was incomplete and that he had erred in something. Their first question tested whether he lightly regarded mocking God’s creatures. They asked about castrating a dog, the lowliest creature, to see whether nullifying its existence seemed trivial to him. He answered that it was forbidden: one must not mock it, for it is a creature of the blessed God. Then they asked whether his error lay in the opposite direction, attributing to created beings more power than they possess. This was the question about a pregnant virgin and the High Priest: the High Priest is the greatest of created beings, and perhaps he had overestimated the power of his existence. He answered that Shmuel’s case was uncommon: one should not ascribe to him greater existence than he possesses, or impose more stringency upon him than is fitting; since Shmuel’s case is uncommon, she is permitted to him. In truth, his principal error was apprehending a great distinction between the lower and upper waters, although only a hair’s breadth—the separating firmament—stands between them. Both are God’s creations, and one must receive them according to His will. This was the meaning of the lamb accompanying the omer, whose meal offering was doubled to two tenths, corresponding to the upper and lower waters, while the lamb alludes to the separating firmament. [Supplement:] As the Gemara says, he stated that only three fingerbreadths separate the lower and upper waters, and they said, “Ben Zoma is still outside.” This means that he apprehended a great separation between evil desire and good desire.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 2:261: “"His cup" corresponds to the perfection of Wisdom, for drunkenness removes Da'at, rendering a person like a simpleton (Eruvin 65a). Matching Avot (3:17): "Anyone whose wisdom exceeds his deeds... is uprooted," for excessive theory is not true wisdom, matching Proverbs (25:16): "If you find honey, eat only what is sufficient, lest you become sated and vomit it." For excess regurgitates even what was previously internalized, matching: "Give me neither poverty nor riches" (Proverbs 30:8)—meaning excessive intellectual wealth that detaches from reality uproots everything. So too with wine in Berakhot (57a): "There is one who drinks it and it is good for him, and one who drinks it and it is bad for him," for Torah is likened to wine (life for those on the right, poison for those on the left). In moderation, "wine and fragrance sharpen the mind" (Yoma 76b), adding wisdom; but in excess, it removes wisdom and uproots a person entirely. And perfection in Wisdom is that one does not become intoxicated, matching: "Who is wise? He who knows his place" and his true spiritual stature, never overreaching beyond his bounds.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Dover Tzedek uses the same warning about eating too much honey to explain wisdom pursued beyond one’s proper measure. It defines the wise person here as one who knows his place and level. This adds a needed distinction to the present siman: intensity of love is not the whole of spiritual readiness; wisdom also includes receiving an attainment in a form that one can sustain.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And in truth his wisdom was exalted above all, whence self-aggrandizement arose as with Zechariah (Kohelet Rabbah 10); and Berakhot 57b: one who sees Ben Zoma should anticipate wisdom; hence his penalty was being stricken in mind, which is the loss of wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Kohelet Rabbah 10:4:1: ““If the spirit of the ruler comes upon you, do not forsake your place, as in its abating he will pardon great sins” (Ecclesiastes 10:4). “If the spirit of the ruler comes upon you, do not forsake your place” – when dominion comes to you, do not forsake your attribute of humility, to teach you that anyone who forsakes his humility causes death to his world and sin to his generation. From whom do you learn this? From Zekharia, as it is stated: “The spirit of God clothed Zekharia….and he stood above the people” (II Chronicles 24:20). Did he, in fact, walk above the people? It is, rather, that he considered himself greater than all the people; son-in-law of the king, priest, prophet, and judge. He began speaking arrogantly to the people, and saying to them: “Why are you violating the mitzvot of the Lord so that you will not succeed?” (II Chronicles 24:20). Immediately, “they conspired against him and stoned him with stones at the command of the king [in the courtyard of the house of the Lord]” (II Chronicles 24:21). Rabbi Yudan asked Rabbi Aḥa: Where did they kill Zekharia, in the Israelite Courtyard or in the Women’s Courtyard? [Rabbi Aḥa] said to him: Neither in the Israelite Courtyard nor in the Women’s Courtyard, but rather in the Priests’ Courtyard. They did not treat his blood like the blood of a gazelle or the blood of a deer. Regarding the blood of a gazelle and a deer whose blood has been spilled, it is written: “You shall spill its blood and cover it with dirt” (Leviticus 17:13), but this righteous one [Zekharia], they did not treat his blood like the blood of a gazelle and not like the blood of a deer. Why [did God allow them to be wicked] to such an extent? It was “to arouse fury and to take vengeance” (Ezekiel 24:8). You find that when Nevuzaradan ascended to destroy Jerusalem, the Holy One blessed be He indicated to that blood that it should seethe. He said to it: This is the time that you will collect your debt. [Nevuzaradan] said to them: ‘What is the nature of this blood?’ They said to him: ‘It is the blood of bulls, rams, and sheep that we were sacrificing to the Holy One blessed be He.’ Immediately, he brought bulls, rams, and sheep and slaughtered many of them onto it, but it did not stop. He said to them: ‘If you tell me, fine. But if not, I will comb the flesh of these people with a comb of iron,’ but [at first] they did not say. Once he [again] said to them that [their explanation] was not [true], they said to him: ‘Why should we conceal it from you? We had a prophet, a priest, who would reprimand us in the name of Heaven. [He said to us]: Accept it, but we did not accept it from him. Rather, we rose against him and killed him.’ [Nevuzaradan] said to them: ‘I will assuage it.’ He then brought the Great Sanhedrin and slaughtered them onto it, but it did not rest. He slaughtered the lesser Sanhedrin onto it, but it did not rest. He brought young priests and slaughtered them onto it, but it did not rest. He slaughtered schoolchildren onto it, but it did not rest. He said to [the seething blood]: ‘Zekharia, I have eliminated the best of your people. Would you like all of them to be eliminated?’ Immediately, it rested. That wicked one contemplated repentance, and said: ‘One who eliminates a single Israelite soul, it is written in his regard: “Whoever sheds the blood of man, his blood will be spilled by man” (Genesis 9:6); this man who eliminated many souls, all the more so.’ At that moment, the Holy One blessed be He became filled with mercy, and He intimated to the blood, and it was absorbed in its place. Rabbi Yudan said: [The Israelites] performed seven transgressions [via one act] on that day: They killed a priest, a prophet, and a judge, they spilled innocent blood, they impurified the Temple Courtyard, and it was Shabbat and Yom Kippur. But Yaḥaziyel did not do so; rather, “Yaḥaziyel, son of Zekharia, son of Benaya, son of Yaḥaziyel, son of Matanya the Levite, from the sons of Asaf, the spirit of the Lord was upon him in the midst of the assembly” (II Chronicles 20:14). What is “in the midst of the assembly”? It is that he likened himself to the assembly. Another matter: “If the spirit of the ruler comes upon you,” is speaking of Noah. He entered the ark with permission and he emerged with permission. From where [is it derived] that he entered with permission? [It is from the verse:] “Come you and all your household to the ark” (Genesis 7:1). From where [is it derived] that he emerged with permission? [It is from the verse:] “Go out of the ark, you …” (Genesis 8:16). Another matter: “If the spirit of the ruler comes upon you,” is speaking of Joshua. Just as the Israelites crossed the Jordan with permission, so too they emerged only with permission. From where [is it derived that] they crossed with permission? As it is stated: “Pass through the midst of the camp…[in another three days you are crossing this Jordan]” (Joshua 1:11). They emerged with permission, as it is stated: “Joshua commanded the priests saying: Emerge from the Jordan” (Joshua 4:17). Another matter: “If the spirit of the ruler…” is speaking of David. Before he reigned, “David is the youngest” (I Samuel 17:14). When he reigned, “King David stood on his feet [and said: Hear me my brethren]” (I Chronicles 28:2). Another matter: “If the spirit of the ruler…” is speaking of Mordekhai. Before prominence came to him, “Mordekhai was sitting at the king’s gate” (Esther 2:19). When prominence came to him, “Mordekhai returned to the king’s gate” (Esther 6:12).”

From whom do you learn this? From Zekharia, as it is stated: “The spirit of God clothed Zekharia….and he stood above the people” (II Chronicles 24:20). Did he, in fact, walk above the people? It is, rather, that he considered himself greater than all the people; son-in-law of the king, priest, prophet, and judge. He began speaking arrogantly to the people, and saying to them: “Why are you violating the mitzvot of the Lord so that you will not succeed?” (II Chronicles 24:20). Immediately, “they conspired against him and stoned him with stones at the command of the king [in the courtyard of the house of the Lord]” (II Chronicles 24:21). Rabbi Yudan asked Rabbi Aḥa: Where did they kill Zekharia, in the Israelite Courtyard or in the Women’s Courtyard? [Rabbi Aḥa] said to him: Neither in the Israelite Courtyard nor in the Women’s Courtyard, but rather in the Priests’ Courtyard. They did not treat his blood like the blood of a gazelle or the blood of a deer. Regarding the blood of a gazelle and a deer whose blood has been spilled, it is written: “You shall spill its blood and cover it with dirt” (Leviticus 17:13), but this righteous one [Zekharia], they did not treat his blood like the blood of a gazelle and not like the blood of a deer. Why [did God allow them to be wicked] to such an extent? It was “to arouse fury and to take vengeance” (Ezekiel 24:8). You find that when Nevuzaradan ascended to destroy Jerusalem, the Holy One blessed be He indicated to that blood that it should seethe. He said to it: This is the time that you will collect your debt. [Nevuzaradan] said to them: ‘What is the nature of this blood?’ They said to him: ‘It is the blood of bulls, rams, and sheep that we were sacrificing to the Holy One blessed be He.’ Immediately, he brought bulls, rams, and sheep and slaughtered many of them onto it, but it did not stop. He said to them: ‘If you tell me, fine. But if not, I will comb the flesh of these people with a comb of iron,’ but [at first] they did not say. Once he [again] said to them that [their explanation] was not [true], they said to him: ‘Why should we conceal it from you? We had a prophet, a priest, who would reprimand us in the name of Heaven. [He said to us]: Accept it, but we did not accept it from him. Rather, we rose against him and killed him.’ [Nevuzaradan] said to them: ‘I will assuage it.’ He then brought the Great Sanhedrin and slaughtered them onto it, but it did not rest. He slaughtered the lesser Sanhedrin onto it, but it did not rest. He brought young priests and slaughtered them onto it, but it did not rest. He slaughtered schoolchildren onto it, but it did not rest. He said to [the seething blood]: ‘Zekharia, I have eliminated the best of your people. Would you like all of them to be eliminated?’ Immediately, it rested. That wicked one contemplated repentance, and said: ‘One who eliminates a single Israelite soul, it is written in his regard: “Whoever sheds the blood of man, his blood will be spilled by man” (Genesis 9:6); this man who eliminated many souls, all the more so.’ At that moment, the Holy One blessed be He became filled with mercy, and He intimated to the blood, and it was absorbed in its place. Rabbi Yudan said: [The Israelites] performed seven transgressions [via one act] on that day: They killed a priest, a prophet, and a judge, they spilled innocent blood, they impurified the Temple Courtyard, and it was Shabbat and Yom Kippur. But Yaḥaziyel did not do so; rather, “Yaḥaziyel, son of Zekharia, son of Benaya, son of Yaḥaziyel, son of Matanya the Levite, from the sons of Asaf, the spirit of the Lord was upon him in the midst of the assembly” (II Chronicles 20:14). What is “in the midst of the assembly”? It is that he likened himself to the assembly. Another matter: “If the spirit of the ruler comes upon you,” is speaking of Noah. He entered the ark with permission and he emerged with permission. From where [is it derived] that he entered with permission? [It is from the verse:] “Come you and all your household to the ark” (Genesis 7:1). From where [is it derived] that he emerged with permission? [It is from the verse:] “Go out of the ark, you …” (Genesis 8:16). Another matter: “If the spirit of the ruler comes upon you,” is speaking of Joshua. Just as the Israelites crossed the Jordan with permission, so too they emerged only with permission. From where [is it derived that] they crossed with permission? As it is stated: “Pass through the midst of the camp…[in another three days you are crossing this Jordan]” (Joshua 1:11). They emerged with permission, as it is stated: “Joshua commanded the priests saying: Emerge from the Jordan” (Joshua 4:17). Another matter: “If the spirit of the ruler…” is speaking of David. Before he reigned, “David is the youngest” (I Samuel 17:14). When he reigned, “King David stood on his feet [and said: Hear me my brethren]” (I Chronicles 28:2). Another matter: “If the spirit of the ruler…” is speaking of Mordekhai. Before prominence came to him, “Mordekhai was sitting at the king’s gate” (Esther 2:19). When prominence came to him, “Mordekhai returned to the king’s gate” (Esther 6:12).”

sections.en: In Youth, Passion and Love Surge within a Person, and That Is the Prime…

p: [רב] בַּיַּלְדוּת הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָאַהֲבָה גּוֹבֵר בָּאָדָם, וְאָז הַזְּמַן לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה.
In youth, passion and love surge within a person, and that is the prime time to utilize the attribute of love.
וְכֵן שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר בְּיַלְדוּתוֹ שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א וְזֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, לט עַמּוּד א).
And so King Solomon, peace be upon him, uttered in his youth the Song of Songs (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1; Zohar II:39a).
וְכֵן אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשַׁבָּת (פט:): "לֹא בְּסָבָא טַעְמָא וְלֹא בְּדַרְדְּקֵי עֵצָה"

— And likewise Abraham, who represents the beginning of the name of Israel, as I heard on the rabbinic dictum in Shabbat 89b: "neither in the elder is there reason, nor in the youth is there counsel"—
"דַּרְדְּקֵי" הוּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה הַהַתְחָלָה וְהַיַּלְדוּת, וְ"סָבָא" – יַעֲקֹב.
"youth" refers to our father Abraham who was the beginning and youth, while "elder" refers to Jacob.
וְכֵן מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹהֵב הָאָדָם בַּיַּלְדוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי נַעַר יִשְׂרָאֵל וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יא, א).
And so, measure for measure, the Blessed Name loves a person in his youth, as it is written: "When Israel was a youth, then I loved him" (Hosea 11:1).

וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָאָדָם חוֹשֵׁק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה, וְאָז זְמַן הַיִּרְאָה, דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, פ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב), וְכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ חָכְמָה.

And afterward a person yearns for words of Torah and wisdom, and then is the season of awe, for the Torah issues from the side of Gevurah (Zohar III:80b), and likewise the Blessed Name bestows wisdom upon him.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ זִקְנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דַּעְתָּן מִתְיַישֶּׁבֶת וּבָא לְדֵעָה שְׁלֵימָה וַאֲמִיתִּית הַקַּיֶּימֶת לָעַד, אָז הוּא זְמַן שִׂמְחָתוֹ וְתַעֲנוּגוֹ שֶׁמִּתְעַנֵּג עַל ה'.
And afterward, as elderly scholars age their minds settle (Shabbat 152a) and one arrives at complete and enduring truth; that is the era of his joy and holy delight wherein he delights upon Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ סֵדֶר שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת וְכֵן שְׁלֹשָׁה רְגָלִים כְּסִדְרָן.
And this is the order of the three Patriarchs, and likewise of the three pilgrimage festivals in their sequence.
וְכֵן שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עָשָׂה אַחַר כָּךְ סֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי מָלֵא חָכְמָה.
And so King Solomon, peace be upon him, composed subsequently the Book of Proverbs, filled with wisdom.

וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּהוּא כְּמוֹ פֵּירוּשׁ עַל הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁכָּל הַתַּרְיַ"ג מִצְווֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה – טַעְמָן וּרְמִיזָתָן בַּלֵּב כְּלָלָן שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּסֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי.

And I heard that it functions like a commentary upon the Torah: that all 613 practical commandments in the Torah—their reasons and inner allusions in the heart—were summarized by King Solomon in Proverbs.
וּבְזִקְנוּתוֹ – קֹהֶלֶת;
And in his old age he composed Ecclesiastes;

וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּלָכֵן קוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּסֻכּוֹת, לֹא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּהְבִּיל שִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִקַּח תֹּקֶף וְעִיקַּר הַשִּׂמְחָה הָאֲמִיתִּית עַל יְדֵי הַהַבְלָת כָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה: "רַק זֶה חֶלְקִי וְכוּלֵי", וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.

and I heard that for this reason we read it on Sukkot—not merely because it dismisses worldly joy as vanity, but because from it we derive the true strength of authentic spiritual joy, through nullifying all worldly pursuits: "only this is my portion, etc." (Ecclesiastes 2:10), and this is not the place to elaborate.

וְהַסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה הוּא מִצַּד הַשְּׁלֵימוּת הָרָאוּי, אֲבָל מִצַּד הַחֹמֶר וְשֶׁהָאָדָם בַּעַל חִסָּרוֹן וְצָרִיךְ לְהַגְדָּרָה – הַיִּרְאָה קוֹדֶמֶת, כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּכָל מָקוֹם הַסֵּדֶר "דְּחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ", דְּ"סוּר מֵרָע" וְאַחַר כָּךְ "עֲשֵׂה טוֹב" (תְּהִלִּים לד, טו).

And this sequence reflects the ideal spiritual trajectory; but from the side of the material body, where man is subject to deficiency and requires boundaries, fear must come first, as is known everywhere in the sequence of awe before love, "depart from evil" and only then "do good" (Psalms 34:15).
וּבַיַּלְדוּת שֶׁהַתַּאֲוָה גּוֹבֶרֶת מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן, צָרִיךְ לְיִרְאָה שֶׁהוּא הַמַּגְדֶּרֶת בִּפְנֵי הַתַּאֲוָה.
And in youth, when lust surges due to physical lack, one requires fear which sets a fence against desire.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה, צָרִיךְ לְהַגְבִּיר הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָאַהֲבָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא יָזוּז מִמֶּנּוּ.
And afterward, when engaging in Torah, one must intensify desire and love for words of Torah so that it never departs from him.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם כְּלוּלִים זֶה בָּזֶה, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֵינָם שְׁלֵימוּת הָאָדָם עֲדַיִן, כִּי אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה נִקְרָא "גַּדְפִין" בַּזֹּהַר, כִּי יַעֲקֹב גּוּפָא וְאַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה דְּרוֹעִין.

And in truth they are inter-included, and neither of them alone constitutes the final perfection of man, for love and fear are termed "wings" in the Zohar, Jacob being the torso while love and fear are the two arms.
כִּי עִיקַּר צוּרַת הָאָדָם הִיא הַדֵּעָה שְׁלֵימָה וְקַו הָאֶמְצָעִי, וְהוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם הָאָמוּר אַחַר אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה.
For the essential form of man is complete Da'at and the Central Column, which is fulfilling His will with a whole heart, articulated following love and fear.
רַק אֵלּוּ הֵם כֹּחוֹת הַשִּׁימּוּשׁ לְצוּרַת הָאָדָם.
Rather, these are the servant powers functioning for the form of man.
וּלְכָךְ צוּרַת יַעֲקֹב חֲקוּקָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא הַכּוֹלֵל הַכֹּל כַּנּוֹדָע.
Therefore the image of Jacob is engraved upon the Throne of Glory, corresponding to the Name Havayah which encompasses all, as is known.
כִּי זֶה כָּל הָאָדָם: לִהְיוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר אֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִי שׁוּם מָסָךְ וּמוֹנֵעַ;
For this is the whole duty of man: to be drawn after the absolute truth of the will of Hashem without any barrier or hindrance;
רַק שֶׁהַדֶּרֶךְ לְהַגִּיעַ לָזֶה הוּא עַל יְדֵי אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה הַקּוֹדְמִין:
only that the path to reach this is through the preceding love and fear.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1:10: “Rabbi Yonatan said: He wrote Song of Songs first, then Proverbs, and afterward Ecclesiastes. Rabbi Yonatan brought a proof from ordinary life: When a person is young, he speaks words of song; when he matures, words of parables; when he grows old, words of futility.”

rich.text: : “Rabbi Yonatan said: He wrote Song of Songs first, then Proverbs, and afterward Ecclesiastes. Rabbi Yonatan brought a proof from ordinary life: When a person is young, he speaks words of song; when he matures, words of parables; when he grows old, words of futility.”

paragraphs.text: Context: The Midrash records several opinions about the order of Solomon’s books. Rav Tzadok adopts Rabbi Yonatan’s account, which places Song of Songs in youth; it should not be presented as the only opinion in the passage.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And I heard that it functions like a commentary upon the Torah: that all 613 practical commandments in the Torah—their reasons and inner allusions in the heart—were summarized by King Solomon in Proverbs.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 6: “Moses our teacher embodied the wisdom of all Israel, and all his power lay in this: the mind and thought, with the blessed God always before him. Therefore the Torah speaks chiefly of actual deeds, so that action too should be as purified as thought. For this Moses made the Tabernacle, whose place was in the human form, in the depth of the heart, and which could be dismantled and carried elsewhere. Solomon’s wisdom, however, lay in actions; therefore he built the chosen House in a fixed place. The book of Proverbs that he composed speaks chiefly of the uprightness of the heart and thought, that they should be established as firmly as action.”

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Chayei Sara 3: ““Abraham was old, advanced in days, and God had blessed Abraham in everything.” It is written (Ecclesiastes 2:10), “This was my portion from all my labor.” The Gemara states (Sanhedrin 20b): Rav and Shmuel—one said, his staff; the other said, his pitcher. Certainly King Solomon, peace be upon him, was not lamenting, Heaven forbid, the loss of this world’s pleasures, for all of these counted as nothing to him. Rather, he took pride in himself and said that although it appeared that everything had been taken from him, the essence of all the life of this world nevertheless remained with him. These two things contain the essence of all the life of this world. This is what he meant by “This was my portion from all my labor.” One said, his staff: a staff alludes to life, meaning that the power of life remained with him. We find that a staff alludes to life, as it is written (Zechariah 8:4), “Each man with his staff in his hand.” The other said, his pitcher: his pitcher is a vessel for receiving, meaning that he was still ready and yearning for more. This was his delight, for this is the essential thing in the life of this world. This is the meaning of the verse, “Abraham was old, advanced in days”: he had reached the roots of life, and he was a vessel ready to receive and yearning for ever greater additions of life from God.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 40:12-14: “Just as a bird’s wings are not its essence, and its life does not depend on them at all—as we learned, “If its wings were removed, it is kosher”—its head and entire body are the principal thing, and its wings only serve the head and body by enabling flight. So, by analogy, Torah and commandments are the essence of the supernal union, through the revelation of the higher will disclosed by them; fear and love raise them to the place where the will, the blessed Infinite Light, and the union are revealed, namely Yetzirah and Beriah. [Gloss:] Or even into the ten holy sefirot of Asiyah, the place of practical commandments, and likewise Scripture. In Mishnah, however, the union and the blessed Infinite Light are revealed in Yetzirah, and in Talmud in Beriah. Through studying Scripture, the union and the Infinite Light extend from Atzilut to Asiyah; through Mishnah, only to Yetzirah; and through Talmud, only to Beriah—for all are in Atzilut. Kabbalah, however, does not extend from Atzilut into Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah at all, as stated in Peri Etz Ḥayyim. Although fear and love themselves are among the 613 commandments, they are nevertheless called “wings,” because the purpose of love is service from love. Love without service is “love in delights,” delighting in God as a foretaste of the World to Come and the receiving of reward; but it is written, “Today, to perform them,” and tomorrow to receive their reward.”

paragraphs.text: Connection together with awe
Joyful connection and reverent distinction must qualify each other.

rich.text: Joyful connection and reverent distinction must qualify each other.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Resisei Layla 24:1: “Mikdash means a place of holiness: it is the opposite of Mishkan, for holiness means distinction and separation, while dwelling means being present and joined, without separation, as it says, ‘Who dwells with them amid their impurities’ (Yoma 56b). Holiness, by contrast, separates from impurity. Yet we find Mishkan called Mikdash and Mikdash called Mishkan (beginning of Eruvin): all is one, and both are true together. The Holy One dwells within Israel and is also distinct from them. As Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah says (beginning of chapter 3), ‘I feared from within my joy and rejoiced from within my fear.’ Joy between companions proceeds from love and connection; awe proceeds from respect for someone greater and distinct. With Hashem both are together, and neither suffices without the other. Awe alone brings folly, as in ‘Is not your fear your folly?’ Joy alone brings levity. Of this the Sages said (Shabbat 31a), ‘Better that you had not brought it up,’ for Torah is called ‘rejoicing the heart,’ and through it one connects with Hashem.”

It uses the same combination of joy and awe and warns against either isolated extreme. This develops the siman's distinction between an ideal order and the practical balancing required by a person's present deficiencies.

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 4:8: “The soul of every living body is the form that God gave it. The additional knowledge found in the human soul is the form of a human being perfected in knowledge. Concerning this form the Torah says, “Let us make a human in Our image, according to Our likeness”: that he should possess a form that knows and apprehends intelligible things without material substance, like the angels, who are form without matter, so that he resembles them. This does not refer to the form visible to the eyes—the mouth, nose, jaws, and the other bodily features—which is called physical appearance. Nor is it the soul found in every living being, through which it eats, drinks, reproduces, perceives, and thinks. Rather, it is the knowledge that is the form of the soul; concerning the form of the soul Scripture says, “In Our image, according to Our likeness.” This form is often called nefesh or ruaḥ. Therefore one must be careful with these names to avoid error; each term must be understood from its context.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Shavuot 2: “The third stage is named when a person returns through his service to the first kindness. Although the Zohar says that Torah issues from the side of severity, this concerns the stage before he breaks through the concealment. Then Hashem's light and the concealment appear to him as opposites. Afterward he truly sees that all is through His kindness: the concealment too exists because Hashem abounds in kindness and wanted the person to have a share in the service he performs. He therefore concealed that kindness so there would be room for service. This is then called threefold Torah.”

The intervening severity had seemed to oppose the light, but the completed understanding sees why concealment allowed meaningful service. This clarifies the siman's final distinction: love and awe are necessary powers of service, while the complete human form is a settled direction toward Hashem's will that can hold them together.

sections.en: The Illusions and Idle Thoughts of Insignificance in the Mind and Heart of Every…

p: [רג] הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים שֶׁל בַּטָּלָה וְשֶׁל מַה בְּכָךְ שֶׁבְּמוֹחַ וְלֵב כָּל אֶחָד, הוּא מַמָּשׁ כְּחוֹלֵם חֲלוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּכֹחַ הַמְדַמֶּה.
The illusions and idle thoughts of insignificance in the mind and heart of every person are literally like one dreaming a dream, operating solely through the imaginative faculty (koach ha-medameh).

וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ: יוֹשֵׁב בָּטֵל כְּיָשֵׁן דָּמֵי, שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בְּמִיתָה (בְּרָכוֹת נז:) בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת, דְּמִיתָה הַיְינוּ מַעֲשֵׂה רֶשַׁע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם יח:): רְשָׁעִים בְּחַיֵּיהֶם וְכוּלֵי.

And therefore they said: one who sits idle is comparable to one asleep, which is one-sixtieth of death (Berakhot 57b) at that time, death denoting the action of wickedness, as stated (ibid. 18b): the wicked in their lifetime are called dead.
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי בְּכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ ו' קְצוֹת, דְּהַיְינוּ ו' מַדְרֵגוֹת וְכֹחוֹת לְכָל דָּבָר עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא לִגְמַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
And it is known that in every matter there are six extremities, meaning six levels and stages for everything until it emerges into the completion of action.
וְכָל אֶחָד קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה כָּלוּל מֵעֶשֶׂר, הֲרֵי שִׁשִּׁים;
And each of these is a complete stature composed of ten, totaling sixty;

וְהֲגַם דְּיֵשׁ מַדְרֵגָה שְׁבִיעִית שֶׁהוּא גְּמַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם בְּמַדְרֵגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה מִן הַשִּׁשִּׁית אֵין הַבְּחִירָה עוֹד בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לָצֵאת עוֹד לַפּוֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, כָּל שֶׁכְּבָר נִשְׁלְמוּ ו' הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת בִּכְלָלוּתָן.

and even though there is a seventh level which is the finalized act, nevertheless at the final phase of the sixth level free choice is no longer in his hands to prevent it from actualizing into deed, once the six stages in their totality are complete.
דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל, כְּשֶׁטִּפַּת הַזֶּרַע בְּפִי הַיְסוֹד אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא, אֲבָל בָּאֶמְצַע עֲדַיִן אֶפְשָׁר לְהַחֲזִיר בְּכֹחַ הַמּוֹשֵׁךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב יַעְבֵּ"ץ.
For example, when a seminal drop is at the orifice of Yesod it cannot be held back, but in the middle it can still be withdrawn through the retentive faculty, as the Yaavetz wrote.

וְהַתְחָלָתָן הוּא הַבַּטָּלָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִמַּדְרֵגָה אַחֲרוֹנָה דְּדַעַת, דְּהַיְינוּ קִשּׁוּר כָּל מִינֵי הִרְהוּרִים, מַחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁל בַּטָּלָה [וּבְהֵיפֶךְ לְטוֹבָה שֶׁל טוֹב], וְנִמְצָא הוּא אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים.
And their inception is idleness, issuing from the final tier of Da'at—the binding of all idle reflections, thoughts, and desires [and conversely toward the good]—which turns out to be one-sixtieth.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ: חֲלוֹם אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בִּנְבוּאָה (בְּרָכוֹת נז:), כִּי בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב, הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁהֵם חַבַּ"ד בְּהֶעְלֵמָן, לֹא מִצַּד גִּלּוּיָן לַפּוֹעַל, הֵם לַה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ עַל יְדֵי מוֹרָשָׁה מֵהָאָבוֹת שֶׁזִּכְּכוּם שְׁתֵּי כֹּחוֹת אֵלּוּ.

Nonetheless they taught: a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy (Berakhot 57b), for in the children of Israel, seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the hidden realms—Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at in their concealment—belong to Hashem our God through ancestral inheritance from the Patriarchs who refined these powers.
כִּי הַבָּנִים נִמְשָׁכִים מִמּוֹחַ הָאָב כַּנּוֹדָע, וְלָכֵן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא בְּמַעֲשֶׂה – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּחַבַּ"ד שֶׁבְּמוֹחוֹ.
For children are drawn from the father's brain as is known; therefore even though one sinned in deed, he remains Israel at his root in the Chabad of his mind.

וּלְכָךְ הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת בְּטֵלִים דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, מֵאַחַר שֶׁנּוֹבְעִים מֵחַבַּ"ד שֶׁבּוֹ, הֲרֵי יֵשׁ לָהֶם פִּתְרוֹן מַמָּשִׁי וַאֲמִיתִּי עַל הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁהֵן נוֹבְעִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּתְלַבְּשׁוּ בְּדִבְרֵי בַּטָּלָה.

And therefore the idle imaginations of a Jew, since they issue from the Chabad within him, possess a substantial and true interpretation reflecting their origin, only that they became clothed in idle matters.
וְזֶהוּ פִּרְקֵי דִּשְׁטוּתָא הַנִּזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, מז עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁמֵּהֶם יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמוֹד עַל דִּבְרֵי חָכְמָה.
And this is the "passages of folly" mentioned in Zohar III:47b, through which one can arrive at words of wisdom.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּעִנְיַן פִּתְרוֹן לַחֲלוֹם, כִּי גַּם כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה הוּא אֶחָד מִכֹּחוֹת שֶׁיִּסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּמּוֹחַ.
And this mirrors the interpretation of a dream, for the imaginative faculty is likewise one of the faculties that the Blessed Name established in the brain.

וְכָל עִיקָּרָהּ שֶׁל נְבוּאָה מִמֶּנּוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי, וְכֵן הוּא בְּמוֹרֶה נְבוּכִים, כִּי הַנְּבוּאָה חָלוּק מֵהַחָכְמָה וְכִדְאִיתָא בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יב.), וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַמְדַמֶּה, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן ו' מַדְרֵגוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר, וּבִכְלָלוּתָן ס'.

And the entirety of prophecy functions through it, as I heard and as found in the Guide for the Perplexed, for prophecy differs from wisdom (Bava Batra 12a), operating via the imaginative faculty, comprising six levels totaling sixty.

וְנִרְאֶה כִּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הוּא בִּידִיעַת בֵּירוּר שֶׁמַּחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ הַנּוֹפֶלֶת בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹ הוּא מֵאֲמִיתַּת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּדְבַר ה' הוּא שֶׁעוֹלֶה בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹ, וְלֹא כְּכָל דִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל תֹּהוּ וְשֶׁל הֶבֶל הָעוֹלִים לְכָל אֶחָד.

And it appears that these gradations lie in discerning with clarity that this thought arising in imagination stems from the authentic thought of Hashem and is the word of God rising in his imagination, and not like standard futile delusions.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא כְּפִי נִקְיוֹן הִרְהוּרָיו מִכָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא נוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ, שֶׁבָּזֶה הֵם כָּל הִרְהוּרֵי הָאָדָם מִדָּבָר שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְאַוָּה לָהֶן.
And this corresponds to the purity of his thoughts from personal bias, for all human musings stem from matters the soul craves.
וְיֵדַע שֶׁלֹּא הִכְנִיס הוּא הַהִרְהוּר בְּלִבּוֹ, וְהֵם ו' שֶׁהֵם ס' מַדְרֵגוֹת בְּנִקָּיוֹן כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁו' קְצוֹת יֵשׁ בַּמִּדּוֹת: תַּאֲוָה, וְכַעַס, וְגַאֲוָה, וְנִיצּוּחַ וְכוּלֵי;

And he should verify that he did not introduce the thought into his heart; and these are the six—totaling sixty—degrees of purity, matching the six extremities among traits: desire, anger, pride, rivalry, etc.;
וּכְפִי נִקְיוֹן הִרְהוּרָיו מִכָּל אֶחָד מִנְּגִיעוֹת אֵלּוּ, כָּךְ עוֹלֶה בְּמַעֲלוֹת מַדְרֵגַת נְבוּאָתוֹ.
and according to the cleansing of his thoughts from each of these biases, so does he ascend the rungs of prophecy.

וְהַחֲלוֹם שֶׁבְּעֵת הַשֵּׁינָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּיָדוֹ וּבְחִירָתוֹ לְנַקּוֹת הִרְהוּרָיו, וְכֵן הִרְהוּרֵי וְדִמְיוֹנוֹת כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל זְמַן שֶׁהֵם דּוּגְמַת חֲלוֹם, הֵם אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַמְדַמֶּה שֶׁהִיא נְבוּאָה.

And a dream during sleep—where it is not in his power to purify his thoughts—and likewise the musings of every Jew at all times which mirror a dream, are one-sixtieth of the true imaginative faculty which is prophecy.

כִּי גַּם בָּהֶם מְלוּבָּשׁ פִּתְרוֹן הָאֲמִיתִּי וּמְרוּמָּז חָכְמַת אֱמֶת הַנִּמְשָׁכוֹת מֵחַבַּ"ד שֶׁבְּמוֹחוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁמְּעוּרְבָּב בְּבַטָּלָה הַרְבֵּה, כְּעִנְיַן "אֵין חֲלוֹם בְּלֹא דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים" (בְּרָכוֹת נה.).

For within them is enclothed the true interpretation and allusions of wisdom drawn from the Chabad of his brain, only that it is mingled with much vanity: "no dream is without idle matters" (Berakhot 55a).
וּבְלִקּוּטֵי תּוֹרָה פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב בֵּיאֵר עִנְיַן הַחֲלוֹם: מוֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ מוֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And in Likkutei Torah (Vayeishev) the Ari explained the nature of a dream: expanded consciousness (Mochin de-Gadlut) concealed within constricted consciousness (Mochin de-Katnut), see there.

וְכֵן הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל הֶבֶל הֵם מוֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּתוֹ; וְאֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ אֱמֶת וְאֵינָהּ דִּמְיוֹן, הֲרֵי הַמּוֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת גָּנוּז תּוֹךְ מוֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת.

And so vain imaginings are his constricted consciousness; yet among Israel, where each possesses a root in Torah—concerning which Truth is written—expanded consciousness is hidden within the constricted consciousness.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִפְּנֵי הַקַּטְנוּת הַמְסַבְּבוֹ אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּלֹא דָּבָר בָּטֵל, אֲבָל יֵשׁ בּוֹ גַּם בָּר.
However, due to the surrounding constriction it cannot be without vanity, yet it also contains grain (bar).
וְהַמֵּבִין עַל זֶה לָדַעַת הַתּוֹכִיּוּת שֶׁבְּכָל הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת הוּא מִי שֶׁנָּקִי מִתַּאֲווֹת, כְּיוֹסֵף בְּתַאֲוַת נָשִׁים וְדָנִיֵּאל בְּתַאֲוַת אֲכִילָה – הֵם הָיוּ פּוֹתְרֵי חֲלוֹמוֹת;
And one who perceives the inner core within all imaginations is one cleansed of lusts, like Joseph regarding women and Daniel regarding food—they were interpreters of dreams;
דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הִרְהוּרֵי בַּטָּלָה הֵם בַּתַּאֲווֹת שֶׁבָּזֶה הַלֵּב חוֹשֵׁק לְהַרְהֵר.
for the root of all idle thoughts lies in desires wherein the heart longs to muse.
וּמִי שֶׁהוּא שָׁקוּעַ בַּדִּמְיוֹן אֵין יָכוֹל לְהַחֲלִיף וּלְהוֹצִיא הַדְּבַר אֱמֶת הַמְלוּבָּשׁ תּוֹךְ הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת; רַק מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁקוּעַ הוּא יוּכַל לְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב מִן הָרָע.
And one immersed in illusion cannot extract the element of truth enclothed within imaginations; only one who is not sunken can separate good from evil.

וְזֶה סוֹד הַעֲלָאַת מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת שֶׁבִּתְפִלָּה הַיָּדוּעַ בַּסְּפָרִים שֶׁאָמוּר לִגְדוֹלִים, הַיְינוּ לְשֶׁאֵין שְׁקוּעִים בְּתַאֲוָה, הֵם יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמוֹד עַל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמוֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת הַגְּנוּזִים בְּתוֹךְ מַחְשְׁבוֹת הֶבֶל שֶׁלּוֹ.

And this is the secret of elevating extraneous thoughts in prayer expounded in Hasidic works, designated for the spiritually great who are not immersed in lust, who can identify the Torah insight and expanded consciousness hidden within idle thoughts.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַעֲלֶה אוֹתָהּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה גַּם כֵּן מֵאַחַר שֶׁעַל יָדָהּ עָמַד;
And through this he elevates that alien thought as well, since through it he arrived at understanding;

עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁזֶּה מֵעֵין נְבוּאָה, דְּהַיְינוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד עָלָיו מִכֹּחַ הַחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא בְּכֹחַ הַשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, רַק עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַמְדַמֶּה שֶׁבּוֹ עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה זֶה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
perforce this partakes of prophecy—something one cannot fathom through intellectual wisdom alone, but grasps through the imaginative faculty as noted above.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 57b: ‘‘Five, six, and ten’ is a mnemonic. Five things are one sixtieth of something else. These are they: fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one sixtieth of Gehinnom. Honey is one sixtieth of the manna. Shabbat is one sixtieth of the World to Come. Sleep is one sixtieth of death. A dream is one sixtieth of prophecy.’

paragraphs.text: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 2 36:2: “You already know the actions of this imaginative faculty: recalling objects perceived by the senses, combining them, and the imitation natural to it. Its greatest and noblest activity occurs when the senses rest and cease their operations; then a measure of influence flows upon it in accordance with its preparedness. This is the cause of true dreams, and it is itself the cause of prophecy: the difference is one of more or less, not of kind. You know their statement that a dream is one sixtieth of prophecy. A numerical ratio does not apply to things differing in kind: it would be inappropriate to say that human perfection is so many times the perfection of a horse. They repeated this matter in Bereshit Rabbah, saying, “The fallen fruit of prophecy is a dream”—a marvelous comparison. Fallen fruit is the fruit itself, but it fell before attaining perfection and ripening. Likewise, the imaginative faculty’s action during sleep is its action during prophecy, though deficient and not brought to its full extent.”

rich.text: : “You already know the actions of this imaginative faculty: recalling objects perceived by the senses, combining them, and the imitation natural to it. Its greatest and noblest activity occurs when the senses rest and cease their operations; then a measure of influence flows upon it in accordance with its preparedness. This is the cause of true dreams, and it is itself the cause of prophecy: the difference is one of more or less, not of kind. You know their statement that a dream is one sixtieth of prophecy. A numerical ratio does not apply to things differing in kind: it would be inappropriate to say that human perfection is so many times the perfection of a horse. They repeated this matter in Bereshit Rabbah, saying, “The fallen fruit of prophecy is a dream”—a marvelous comparison. Fallen fruit is the fruit itself, but it fell before attaining perfection and ripening. Likewise, the imaginative faculty’s action during sleep is its action during prophecy, though deficient and not brought to its full extent.”

paragraphs.text: Likutei Torah, Vayeshev 25: “We shall now explain the dreams of Pharaoh, the chief cupbearer, and the chief baker. You know the Sages’ statement that Joseph rejoiced in these dreams because they pointed to him; their entire meaning concerns Joseph’s exile and the redemption from Egypt. Understand this as follows: the mystery of the dream is the three expanded intellectual powers, represented by three names Havayah, whose numerical value equals ḥet-lamed-mem, “dream.” This is when they descend within the three names Elohim in the throat, represented by the three officials. You know that sleep occurs entirely in a state of diminished consciousness. The dream then comes from the expanded consciousness remaining within the diminished consciousness, where it is concealed. Therefore the dream is concealed and is explained only through the interpreter—Joseph, who is the Yesod of Zeir Anpin. All the higher lights gather there.”
