sections.en: When a Person Prays for a Spiritual Virtue

p: [ריד] כְּשֶׁאָדָם מְבַקֵּשׁ עַל מַעֲלָה, יֵשׁ לוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה יוֹתֵר מִגְּבוּלוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שָׁוְא וּדְבַר כָּזָב הַרְחֵק מִמֶּנִּי" (מִשְׁלֵי ל, ח).
When a person prays for a spiritual virtue, he should pray that it not exceed his capacity, as it is written: "Remove far from me vanity and lies" (Proverbs 30:8).
פֵּירוּשׁ, "שָׁוְא" – דִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל תֹּהוּ, וְ"דָבָר" הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת קפ"ג מִגְּמָרָא דְּתַעֲנִית (י:);
Meaning, "vanity" (shav) denotes delusions of chaos, and "word" (davar) denotes words of Torah as noted above in Section 183 from Ta'anit 10b;
וַאֲפִילּוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, רַק שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִגְּבוּלוֹ, וַהֲרֵי זֶה כּוֹזֵב וּפוֹסֵק – הַרְחֵק.
and even words of Torah, if they are beyond his vessel so that they will prove false and cease—remove them far from me.
וְסִיֵּים עַל זֶה: "רֵאשׁ וָעֹשֶׁר [אַל תִּתֶּן לִי]... פֶּן אֶשְׂבַּע וְכִחַשְׁתִּי וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם, ח–ט),
And he concluded upon this: "Poverty and riches [give me not]... lest I be full and deny, etc." (ibid. 30:8–9),
שֶׁכְּשֶׁיַּעֲלֶה בְּמַדְרֵגוֹת שֶׁאֵינָם לְפִי עֵרֶךְ כְּלִי קִבּוּלוֹ, יָבוֹא לְגַאֲוָה וּלְשֶׁקֶר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
for if he ascends to spiritual rungs that do not match the capacity of his receptive vessel, he will arrive at pride and falsehood, Heaven forbid.
וְעַל זֶה בִּקֵּשׁ יַעְבֵּץ: "אִם בָּרֵךְ תְּבָרֲכֵנִי וְהִרְבִּיתָ אֶת גְּבוּלִי" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י) – הַגְּבוּל שֶׁלִּי תִּשְׁמוֹר שֶׁלֹּא לָצֵאת חוּץ מִגְּבוּל.
And concerning this Ya'betz prayed: "Oh that You would bless me indeed, and enlarge my border" (I Chronicles 4:10)—guard my boundary that I not spill beyond my proper border.
כִּי כָּל אֶחָד בַּעַל גְּבוּל, רַק שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ גְּבוּל תִּתֵּן בְּרָכָה וְרִבּוּי, כִּי וַדַּאי בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַגְדִּיל הַגְּבוּל וְהַכְּלִי קִבּוּל שֶׁל הָאָדָם.
For every person is bounded, yet within that boundary grant blessing and increase, for certainly it is in the hand of the Blessed Name to expand the border and the receptive vessel of a person.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּתְמוּרָה (טז.): "בָּרֵךְ" – בַּתּוֹרָה, "וְהִרְבִּיתָ" – בְּתַלְמִידִים,
And this is what our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Temurah 16a: "'Bless'—in Torah; 'and enlarge'—with disciples,"

כְּטַעַם (תַּעֲנִית ז.): "וּמִתַּלְמִידַי יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם", שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַתִּינוֹק מְמַשְׁמֵשׁ – מוֹצֵא, וּכְשֶׁנִּגְמַל גַּם הֶחָלָב נֶעְתַּק מִשָּׁדַיִם, רַק עַל יְדֵי הַתִּינוֹק מִתְרַבֶּה הֶחָלָב בָּאֵם.

in the spirit of Ta'anit 7a: "and from my disciples more than from all of them," for as long as the nursing infant suckles he finds milk, and when weaned the milk departs from the breasts, the milk multiplying in the mother solely through the infant.
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הִמְשִׁילוּ לָזֶה לִמּוּד הַתַּלְמִידִים בִּפְסָחִים (קיב.): יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁעֵגֶל וְכוּלֵי,
And our Sages compared the teaching of disciples to this in Pesachim 112a: "More than the calf wishes to suckle, the cow wishes to nurse,"
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַתַּלְמִידִים נִתְגַּדֵּל גְּבוּלוֹ לִהְיוֹת כְּלִי קִבּוּל יוֹתֵר לְקַבֵּל בְּרָכָה וְשֶׁפַע דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
for through disciples one's vessel is enlarged to become a greater receptacle to receive blessing and an outpouring of Torah from the Blessed Name.
כְּמוֹ לְעִנְיַן עֲשִׁירוּת כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים הַרְבֵּה
Just as in matters of wealth when one has many children
[וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ: "וְהִרְבִּיתָ אֶת גְּבוּלִי" – בְּבָנִים וּבָנוֹת, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה כְּלִי קִבּוּל גָּדוֹל לְעִנְיַן הָעֹשֶׁר],
[and so they expounded there: 'and enlarge my border'—with sons and daughters, through which he becomes a larger vessel for wealth],
וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת צָרִיךְ לַעֲשִׁירוּת יוֹתֵר, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶצְלוֹ עֲשִׁירוּת רַק לֶחֶם חֻקּוֹ.
and a family man requires greater resources, which for him is not superfluous luxury but his daily bread.
וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, לְכָךְ הִסְמִיךְ בַּקָּשַׁת הַתַּלְמִידִים לִבְרָכָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דְּלוּלֵי כֵן שֶׁמָּא אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְקַבֵּל כָּל כָּךְ בְּרָכָה.
And so too regarding Torah: therefore he juxtaposed the request for disciples to the blessing in Torah, for without them he could not contain so much blessing.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ: "וְהָיְתָה יָדְךָ עִמָּדִי" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י) – שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּכַּח וְיִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ,
And afterward: "and that Your hand might be with me" (I Chronicles 4:10)—that it not be forgotten and that it endure in his hand,
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי "יָדְךָ", פֵּירוּשׁ: דְּ"יָדְכָה" בְּהֵ"א נִדְרַשׁ יָד כֵּהָה (מְנָחוֹת לז.), אֲבָל "יָדְךָ" הַיְינוּ יָמִין,
and that is through "Your hand," for yadekhah, spelled with a final hei, is read as the weak hand (Menachot 37a), whereas yadekha without it is the right hand,
וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו.): בִּימִינוֹ זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי,
and they said in Berakhot 6a: by His right hand, this is the Torah,
שֶׁיְּמִין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַמַּשְׁפַּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְכַאֲשֶׁר תִּהְיֶה עִמָּדִי אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּשְׁכַּח שֶׁהֲרֵי מַשְׁפַּעַת תָּמִיד.
for the right hand of Hashem is what channels Torah, and when it is with me it is impossible to forget, since it bestows constantly.
וּלְפִי שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ עַל הַקִּיּוּם, עַל זֶה סָמַךְ תֵּיכֶף בַּקָּשַׁת הַחֲבֵירִים שֶׁהֵם הַמְּקַיְּימִים בְּיָדוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת קפ"ה.
And because he asked for permanence, he immediately followed with the request for colleagues who establish it in his hand, as noted in Section 185.

וְהִקְדִּים תַּלְמִיד לְחָבֵר, כִּי אָז הָיָה אַחַר פְּטִירַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא, וְנִתְמַנָּה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְפַרְנָס שֶׁעִסְקוֹ הַנְחָלַת הָאָרֶץ וְהִתְחִיל עֵסֶק אַחֵר.

And he preceded disciples before colleagues, for that occurred after the passing of Moses our teacher, see the Gemara there, when Joshua was appointed leader whose task was settling the Land, commencing a different focus.
רַק יַעְבֵּץ – הוּא עָתְנִיאֵל – לְבָבוֹ הָיָה רוֹעֵשׁ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא דְּהָיָה מְפוּלְפָּל יוֹתֵר מִיהוֹשֻׁעַ, רַק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ חֲבֵירִים וְלֹא תַלְמִידִים,
Only Ya'betz—who was Othniel—had a heart stormy for Torah, see the Gemara there that he was sharper in dialectic than Joshua, yet he had neither colleagues nor disciples,
וּבִקֵּשׁ תְּחִלָּה עַל הַבְּרָכָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיָה יְחִידִי בְּלֹא רַב וְחָבֵר וְתַלְמִיד.
and he prayed first for blessing in Torah since he was alone without master, colleague, or disciple.
וְתֵיכֶף לַבְּרָכָה הֻוצְרַךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל הַתַּלְמִידִים שֶׁעַל יָדָם הוּא כְּלִי מַחֲזִיק בְּרָכָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
And immediately following the blessing he had to pray for disciples through whom he becomes a vessel holding blessing.
וְאַחַר הַבְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל הַקִּיּוּם וְשֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכַּח, וְאָז בִּקֵּשׁ עַל הַחֲבֵירִים.
And after blessing one must pray for retention and not forgetting, and then he prayed for colleagues.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ, שֶׁלֹּא יִגְרוֹם אֵיזֶה חֵטְא, בִּקֵּשׁ: "וַעֲשִׂיתָ מֵרָעָה לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי" כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שָׁם, וּמִיָּד: "וַיָּבֵא [אֱלֹהִים אֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁאָל]" (שָׁם).
And afterward, that sin not disrupt it, he prayed: "and that You would keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me," and immediately: "and [God] granted [him that which he requested]."
וְהִנֵּה בְּרָכָה וְתַלְמִידִים וַחֲבֵירִים אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת מִיָּד כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ;
Now, blessing, disciples, and colleagues can manifest immediately;
אַךְ הַקִּיּוּם וְשֶׁלֹּא יִגְרוֹם הַחֵטְא, לִכְאוֹרָה זֶה אֵין נִתְוַודַּע רַק בְּקֵץ יָמָיו, שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁנִּתְקַיֵּים בּוֹ כָּל יָמָיו.
but retention and sin not causing failure are seemingly known only at the end of life when seeing it endured.

וְנִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב כַּאֲשֶׁר הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הֵם קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה לֹא יָזוּעַ עוֹד, וְשֶׁאֵין עֲבֵירָה מְכַבַּתּוֹ, כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּי לְפוֹצֵץ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,

Yet it appears that in this too there is a palpable sense in the heart when Torah is permanently anchored so that he will never budge, sin unable to extinguish it, having enough power to smash the inclination,
וְ"הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יט) וּמְסַלֶּקֶת הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁמָּא יִגְרוֹם הַחֵטְא, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא יִרְאָה גַּבֵּי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (בְּרָכוֹת ד.).
and "wisdom strengthens the wise" (Ecclesiastes 7:19), banishing the fear lest sin cause failure, which was termed fear regarding our father Jacob (Berakhot 4a).
וּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּקִיפוּת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, הוּא מְסוּלָּק מִכָּל מִינֵי יְרָאוֹת:
And whoever possesses steadfast fortitude from words of Torah is liberated from all manner of anxieties.

paragraphs.text: Passing the trial of lack does not remove the need to receive abundance with care.

rich.text: Passing the trial of lack does not remove the need to receive abundance with care.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 5: “When he returned from Egypt it therefore says, ‘Avram was very heavy.’ After he had been completely clarified in poverty through the first trial, ‘very heavy’ expresses a burden: he feared for himself because of wealth, like Shlomo's prayer, ‘Give me neither poverty nor wealth.’ Of Lot it does not say ‘heavy,’ only that Lot who went with Avram also possessed property. The expression indicates gladness, for he had no fear at all. Of Avraham, by contrast, it says ‘heavy’ because of his fear. Hence, ‘He went on his journeys … and Avram called there’: even now he was concerned about wealth. In this way he clarified himself in every circumstance.”

The expression indicates gladness, for he had no fear at all. Of Avraham, by contrast, it says ‘heavy’ because of his fear. Hence, ‘He went on his journeys … and Avram called there’: even now he was concerned about wealth. In this way he clarified himself in every circumstance.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach reads Avraham's wealth as a new burden of responsibility after the trial of poverty, using the same prayer from Proverbs cited here. Its material setting illustrates the siman's more general distinction: more of a gift is not automatically better unless the recipient can hold it properly. Asking for an enlarged vessel therefore accompanies asking for a greater Torah blessing.

paragraphs.text: Yaavetz asks for protection from interruption while already immersed in Torah, not only before beginning to learn.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 10:5: “We find this with Jabez: although he was emptied of all this world’s desires and constantly engaged in Torah, he prayed, “‘That it should not grieve me’—that the evil inclination should not overpower me and prevent my study,” as stated in Temurah 16a. Even while sitting in the study hall he feared that the evil inclination would confuse his mind. For this he needs help from the blessed God.”

rich.text: : “We find this with Jabez: although he was emptied of all this world’s desires and constantly engaged in Torah, he prayed, “‘That it should not grieve me’—that the evil inclination should not overpower me and prevent my study,” as stated in Temurah 16a. Even while sitting in the study hall he feared that the evil inclination would confuse his mind. For this he needs help from the blessed God.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Lech Lecha emphasizes that Yaavetz’s existing devotion did not make him independent of divine assistance. This helps explain why the present siman distinguishes a blessing in Torah from the further requests for retention, companions, and protection from sin. Receiving an insight and becoming a vessel in which it can endure are different needs. The prayer concerns the continuing life of Torah within the learner, including the ability to remain available for study and teaching.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 12:4: “This is called “flying in the air”: the person who fears has nothing clearly established upon which to rely. In every matter he fears and trembles, even in a deed that is clearly good, lest there be some blemish or deficiency. Thus he has no foundation on which his foot can take hold and find support. This is his fear preceding his wisdom, for “the beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem.” Afterward, through this, his wisdom endures, and “wisdom strengthens the wise person.” A “strong tower” is formed, into which “the righteous runs and is exalted.” Running means expansion without restraint, for “his heart is firm, trusting in Hashem,” and concerning this it says, “His heart is supported; he will not fear.””

sections.en: The Heart Is the Receptive Vessel

p: [רטו] הַלֵּב הוּא הַכְּלִי קִבּוּל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.) דְּיִרְאָה הוּא הָאוֹצָר, וּבְיוֹמָא (עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן" (מִשְׁלֵי יז, טז) דְּשָׁם הַיִּרְאָה.
The heart is the receptive vessel, as stated in Shabbat 31a that awe is the treasury, and in Yoma 72b on "and he has no heart" that there resides fear.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם הוּא הַגְדָּרַת חֶמְדַּת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בִּידֵי אָדָם,
That is, fear of Heaven is the bounding of the inclination's desires in the heart, which is in human hands,
וּכְפִי נִקְיוֹן הַלֵּב מִכָּל מִינֵי פְּסֹלֶת, כֵּן הוּא כְּלִי קִבּוּל יוֹתֵר לְטוֹבָה וּבְרָכָה.
and according to the cleansing of the heart from dross, so is it a greater vessel for goodness and blessing.
וְעִיקָּר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נָקִי מִגַּאֲוָה וְקִנְאָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר הַכְּלִי קִבּוּל שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא עַל יְדֵי רוֹב טוֹבָה לְגַאֲוָה הַמּוֹשֶׁכֶת אַחֲרֶיהָ קִנְאָה וְשִׂנְאָה וּשְׁאָר מִדּוֹת רָעוֹת.
And primarily it must be clean of pride and envy, which is the essence of the vessel, so that abundant goodness does not lead to pride that drags along envy, hatred, and evil traits.

וְלָכֵן כְּלִי מַחֲזִיק בְּרָכָה הוּא הַשָּׁלוֹם, וּבוֹ מְסַיֶּימֶת הַתְּפִלָּה, שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל טוֹבָה, וּבַסּוֹף מְבַקֵּשׁ עַל שָׁלוֹם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּלִי קִבּוּל לְרוֹב טוֹבָה.
Therefore the vessel holding blessing is peace (Uktzin 3:12), with which prayer concludes: petitioning for goodness, and concluding with peace so as to be a vessel for abundant good.
וְאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (מז:) וּבְתַעֲנִית (כג.) דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל רוֹב טוֹבָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה, וְהַיְינוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הוּסַר לֵב הָאֶבֶן.
And they said in Yevamot 47b and Ta'anit 23a that one cannot receive abundant goodness in this era, so long as the heart of stone is not removed.
וּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ בָּא לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם, וְיִסְתַּלֵּק הַקִּנְאָה וְהַשִּׂנְאָה וְגַאֲוָה מִלֵּב, אָז מְקַבֵּל כָּל אֶחָד רוֹב טוֹבָה בְּשֶׁפַע.
And in the future Elijah comes to make peace in the world, banishing envy, hatred, and pride from the heart, whereupon all receive goodness in abundance.
וְאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יד:): רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נִכְנַס בְּשָׁלוֹם וְיָצָא בְּשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאָחַז בָּהּ, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (טז.) "וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרוֹעֵי צֹאן",
And they said (Chagigah 14b): Rabbi Akiva entered in peace and emerged in peace, through holding fast to peace—as in Yevamot 16a: "not even to the shepherds of flocks"—
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְנַס וְיָצָא וְהִשִּׂיג חָכְמָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ, כִּדְאִיתָא (חֲגִיגָה טו:) דְּבִקְשׁוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לְדָחְפּוֹ, מַשְׁמָע שֶׁהָיָה לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ.
through which he entered and emerged, grasping wisdom above his level, where ministering angels sought to push him away (Chagigah 15b), showing it transcended his natural stature.

אֲבָל עַל בֶּן זוֹמָא אָמְרוּ: "אֱכֹל דַּיֶּךָּ פֶּן וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי כה, טז) כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"א מִמֶּנּוּ, וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"ו דִּשְׁבִירַת הַכֵּלִים שֶׁבִּקְּשׁוּ לְקַבֵּל אוֹר יוֹתֵר מִן הָרָאוּי וְהוּא גַּאֲוָה.

But of Ben Zoma they applied: "Eat so much as is sufficient for you, lest, etc." (Proverbs 25:16), as noted in Section 201, and in Section 206 regarding the Shattering of Vessels through seeking light beyond capacity, which is pride.
וּבַגְּמָרָא (שָׁם עַמּוּד א) אִיתָא טָעוּת בֶּן זוֹמָא בַּהֶבְדֵּל שֶׁבֵּין מַיִם עֶלְיוֹנִים לְמַיִם תַּחְתּוֹנִים, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And in Chagigah 15a Ben Zoma erred regarding the space between upper and lower waters, see there.

פֵּירוּשׁ, מַיִם עֶלְיוֹנִים וּמַיִם תַּחְתּוֹנִים יָדוּעַ דְּהֵם הַנִּקְרָא בַּזֹּהַר "מַיִין דְּכוּרִין" וּ"מַיִין נוּקְבִין", הַיְינוּ הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב וְהַמִּלּוּי מִלְּמַעְלָה עַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ.
Upper and lower waters are male waters (mayin dechurin) and female waters (mayin nukvin): the awakening from below through desire in the heart, and the supernal influx through wisdom in the mind.

וְהֵם תְּפִלָּה וְתוֹרָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת לב:): מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ? יַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה, וְ"עֵץ חַיִּים תַּאֲוָה בָאָה" (מִשְׁלֵי יג, יב), כִּי תוֹרָה הוּא מִלּוּי הַתַּאֲוָה וְהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבִּתְפִלָּה.
These are prayer and Torah (Berakhot 32b): what is his remedy? Let him engage in Torah, "and a tree of life is desire fulfilled" (Proverbs 13:12), Torah fulfilling the desire awakened in prayer.
בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן הָיוּ מְעוֹרָבִים, פֵּירוּשׁ כִּי יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן נֶגֶד מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאַהֲבָה, וְנִמְצָא הַחֵשֶׁק הוּא עַצְמוֹ הַמִּלּוּי.
On the first day they were mingled, corresponding to Abraham in love, where desire is itself fulfillment.

רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת בְּחֵשֶׁק הָאָדָם, אֲפִילּוּ לְתוֹרָה וְלִידִיעַת אֱלֹהוּת, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין הַלֵּב נָקִי, הַחֵשֶׁק הַטֶּבַע מִמֶּנּוּ גַּם כֵּן אֵין נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי, וְאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה תַּאֲוָה כְּכָל הַתַּאֲווֹת וּכְמוֹ שֶׁחוֹשְׁקִין לָדַעַת חָכְמָה וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
Yet in human longing, even for Torah and Godliness, so long as the heart is not pure, natural desire is not completely clean, possibly mixing with intellectual lust for wisdom.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "לֹא בָרוּחַ ה' וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א יט, יא), פֵּירוּשׁ: רָצוֹן וְהִתְלַהֲבוּת בְּאַהֲבָה וְרַעַשׁ בְּיִרְאָה – הַכֹּל עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ נָקִי וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְעוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ.
And as I heard on "Hashem was not in the wind, etc." (I Kings 19:11): fiery love and clamorous fear are not yet pure enough to be Hashem's dwelling.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁמַּגְדֶּרֶת הָאַהֲבָה וּמְצַמְצְמַתּוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא לִכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם.
And for this serves awe in the heart, bounding love and constricting it purely for the honor of Heaven.
וְהִתְכַּלְלוּתָם הוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָרוֹמֵז לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה וְצוּרַת אָדָם שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
And their synthesis is Jacob, alluding to the Name Havayah and the human form on the Chariot, representing ultimate perfection.

וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא נִשְׁלַם אֶלָּא אַחַר נִסָּיוֹן עֲשִׂירִי בָּעֲקֵידָה, שֶׁאָז אִתְכְּלִיל בְּמִדַּת יִצְחָק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קיט עַמּוּד ב), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא [אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה]" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כב, יב).
And Abraham was completed only after the tenth trial at the Akedah, integrating Isaac's awe (Zohar I:119b): "now I know that you fear [God]" (Genesis 22:12).
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "יַעֲקֹב אֲשֶׁר פָּדָה אֶת אַבְרָהָם" (יְשַׁעְיָה כט, כב), כִּי מִצַּד מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְכַּלְלוּת שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן כְּלוּלָה בְּאַבְרָהָם – נִיצּוֹל.
And this is: "Jacob who redeemed Abraham" (Isaiah 29:22), for through Jacob's synthesis, latent in Abraham, he was delivered.

דְּמִצַּד מִדָּתוֹ לְבַד, הֲרֵי בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן נֶאֱמַר: "וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ב), דְּעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ וְהַשְּׁבִירָה בָּא מִזֶּה: עַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָאַהֲבָה לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֹא יִרְאָה הַמְצַמְצֶמֶת.
For from his trait alone, the first day bore: "and the earth was unformed and void" (Genesis 1:2), the Shattering occurring through yearning for light without bounding awe.

וּלְכָךְ בְּיוֹם שֵׁנִי נַעֲשָׂה רָקִיעַ מַבְדִּיל בֵּין מַיִם לָמָיִם, שֶׁהַיִּרְאָה הוּא הַכָּרַת הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁאֵין חֶשְׁקוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת כְּמוֹ הַמַּיִם עֶלְיוֹנִים שֶׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ.
Therefore on the second day the firmament divided the waters, awe being the recognition of deficiency, human longing not equaling the upper waters of divine bestowal.
וְהַהֶבְדֵּל כִּמְלֹא נִימָא, וּפֵירֵשׁ בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן יט) שֶׁהוּא הַסּוֹד דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם.
And the separation was like a hairsbreadth, which Tikkun 19 explains as the secret of Torah.

פֵּירוּשׁ, דְּבֶאֱמֶת יָדוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פְּתוּחָה לְהַשְׁלִים תֵּיכֶף, רַק שֶׁיֵּשׁ הֶפְסֵק כִּמְלֹא נִימָא – רָקִיעַ הַמַּבְדִּיל וּמַעֲלִים, שֶׁיֵּדַע שֶׁיֵּשׁ סוֹד וְהֶעְלֵם וְשֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל הַכֹּל.
Hashem's hand is open to fulfill immediately, yet a hairsbreadth divider conceals, teaching that mystery exists and man cannot receive all.

וּבֶן זוֹמָא רָצָה לְקַבֵּל יוֹתֵר בְּתֹקֶף הָאַהֲבָה וְהַחֵשֶׁק, וּלְפִיכָךְ טָעָה לִלְמוֹד מִיּוֹם רִאשׁוֹן, וּבֶאֱמֶת אָז לֹא הָיָה הַבְדָּלָה כְּלָל, וּלְכָךְ "רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ב) – נוֹגֵעַ וְאֵינוֹ נוֹגֵעַ עַל יְדֵי הֶעְדֵּר הַהַבְדָּלָה, כִּי אָז הָיָה תֹּהוּ עֲדַיִן.

And Ben Zoma sought to receive beyond bounds through love and desire, erring by inferring from day one when no division existed, where "the spirit of God hovered"—touching and not touching—because chaos still reigned.

וְזֶהוּ "פֶּן וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה אַדְּרַבָּה נִפְגַּע וְיָצָא מֵחָכְמָה, לְפִי שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְהַשִּׂיג הַכֹּל וְשֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה סוֹד וְהֶעְלֵם כְּלָל לְפָנָיו; נִתְרַחֵק מִמֶּנּוּ עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה אֶצְבָּעוֹת וְנוֹגֵעַ וְאֵין נוֹגֵעַ.
And this was "lest you be filled," becoming stricken in mind because he sought to grasp everything without concealment; it receded to three fingerbreadths, touching and not touching.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.): אִי יִרְאַת ה' הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ וְכוּלֵי, מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ – שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא נִפְגָּע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
Therefore Shabbat 31a states: if the fear of Hashem is his storehouse, yes; if not, better he had not brought it up—lest he be stricken;
אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁבַּלֵּב הַמַּגְדֶּרֶת אוֹתוֹ, יוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג הַכֹּל, רַק שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מוּגְדָּר בְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם וּמְצוּמְצָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
but through fear of Heaven in the heart bounding him, he can attain all, provided he remains bounded in awe as noted above.

paragraphs.text: The heart’s preparation determines whether an increase of wisdom becomes a living attainment.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:146: “And so too all secular wisdom of the heathen nations is termed: "Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, seeing he has no heart?" which our Sages expounded in Yoma (72b) as referring to the fear of Heaven, which is the mystical secret of Knesset Yisrael, existing exclusively among Israel whose hearts follow their supernal wisdom, whereupon wisdom receives back from the heart and they gaze face-to-face, and then the divine flow shoots forth like an arrow, parallel to the rainbow granted to Noah after "the inclination of the heart is evil from his youth";”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Dover Tzedek develops the same verse “to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart” as a failure of living connection between mind and heart. The relationship is reciprocal: the heart follows wisdom, while wisdom also receives from the heart. This explains why the present siman treats yirah and peace as more than preliminary restrictions; they form the capacity by which greater wisdom can be received and expressed.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 33b:23-25: “Rabbi Chanina also said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven, as it is said, “And now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you, except to fear?” Is fear of Heaven a small matter? Did Rabbi Chanina not say in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: The Holy One, blessed be He, has in His storehouses only a treasury of the fear of Heaven, as it is said, “The fear of Hashem is His treasure”? Yes: in relation to Moshe it is a small matter. As Rabbi Chanina said: A parable of a person from whom a large vessel is requested: if he has it, it seems to him like a small vessel; if a small vessel is requested and he does not have it, it seems to him like a large vessel.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 14:2-5: “It is otherwise with a matter entrusted to the heart: that evil should truly be repulsive in the heart and hated with utter hatred—or even with a hatred that is not utter. This cannot be completely true except through the greatness and strength of love of Hashem, in the mode of “love in delights”: delighting in Hashem as a foretaste of the World to Come. Of this our Sages said, “May you see your world in your lifetime,” and so forth. Not everyone merits this, for it is akin to receiving a reward, as it is written, “I give your priesthood as a service of gift,” and so forth, as explained elsewhere. Therefore Job said, “You created righteous people,” and so forth. As stated in the Tikkunim, the souls of Israel have different grades and aspects: the pious, the mighty who overcome their inclination, masters of Torah, prophets, and righteous people, and so forth; see there. This explains the doubled language of the oath, “Be righteous, and do not be wicked.” At first this is puzzling: once a person is made to swear, “Be righteous,” why must he also swear not to be wicked? Rather, because not everyone merits becoming righteous, and a person does not have such complete freedom of choice in this—to delight truly in Hashem and to find evil truly repulsive—he is made to swear a second time, “Do not be wicked,” at least. In this, the power of choice and authority are given to everyone: to govern the desire in his heart and subdue his inclination, so as not to be wicked for even one hour throughout his life, both in “turning from evil” and in “doing good.” “There is no good but Torah”—meaning Torah study, which is equivalent to them all.”

paragraphs.text: Awe prepares the heart to receive love and wisdom

rich.text: Awe prepares the heart to receive love and wisdom

paragraphs.text: Even a longing for Torah can retain an unrefined personal motive. Awe sets the boundary that directs love toward Heaven, making the heart a vessel able to receive without grasping beyond its capacity.

rich.text: Even a longing for Torah can retain an unrefined personal motive. Awe sets the boundary that directs love toward Heaven, making the heart a vessel able to receive without grasping beyond its capacity.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 11:3: “In the blessing “Who bestows good kindnesses,” a person’s awakening below in the quality of kindness, Abraham our father’s quality, awakens kindness above, as the holy Zohar teaches (III, beginning of 92b). In this blessing we ask, “Subdue our inclination to serve You.” Likewise, in the blessing “With eternal love” we ask, “Unite our hearts to love and fear Your name”: may we have one heart for awe, emptying evil from the foolish heart. This blessing corresponds to love, Abraham our father’s quality, as it is said, “The offspring of Abraham, My beloved.” Our master and teacher Rabbi Ber, of blessed and holy memory, has already written that love comes from above, in the manner indicated by “For such is his way …”.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Peri Tzadik identifies a daily expression of the union sought here: the prayer “Unite our hearts to love and fear Your name.” Its account of asking God to subdue the inclination and empty evil from the heart translates Tzidkat HaTzadik’s relation between love, awe, and receptivity into the language of prayer.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayera 33:489-491: “Here one must consider: “God tested Avraham”—should it not say “Yitzchak”? Yitzchak was thirty-seven years old, and his father was not liable for his punishment: had Yitzchak said, “I do not want this,” his father would not have been punished on his account. Why, then, does it say “God tested Avraham,” and not “He tested Yitzchak”? Rather, it is indeed Avraham, who needed to be integrated with judgment, for previously Avraham had no judgment in him at all; now water was integrated with fire. Avraham was not complete until now, when he was crowned to perform judgment and establish it in its place. Throughout his life he had not been complete until now, when water was integrated with fire and fire with water. Therefore “God tested Avraham,” not Yitzchak: He summoned Avraham to become integrated with judgment. When he did this, fire entered water, and each was completed with the other. He performed judgment so that one would be integrated with the other. Then the evil inclination came to accuse Avraham, saying that he had not been properly completed until he performed judgment upon Yitzchak. For the evil inclination is “after these things,” and it came to accuse.”

sections.en: Each Day Contains Novel Insights of Torah

p: [רטז] בְּכָל יוֹם יֵשׁ חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
Each day contains novel insights of Torah, for the Blessed Name renews daily the work of Creation.
וּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה, וּמִסְּתָמָא גַּם הַחִדּוּשׁ הוּא עַל יְדֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה.
And Creation unfolded through the Torah (Bereishit Rabbah 1:1), so renewal likewise unfolds through novel Torah insights.

וּלְכָךְ אַחַר בִּרְכַּת יוֹצֵר הַמְּאוֹרוֹת, שֶׁהוּא הַהַכָּרָה בְּחִדּוּשׁ מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית בְּכָל יוֹם, תִּקְּנוּ בְּרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (יא:), שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ לֵידַע הַחִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית

Therefore after the blessing Yotzer HaMe'orot acknowledging daily cosmic renewal, they instituted the second blessing which functions like a blessing over Torah (Berakhot 11b), praying to know the Torah insights aligned with that day's cosmic renewal

[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי, כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָשָׂה סֵפֶר וְהוּא הָעוֹלָם, וּפֵירוּשׁ עַל אוֹתוֹ סֵפֶר וְהוּא הַתּוֹרָה, כִּי הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ מְפָרֵשׁ קִנְיָנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּנִּבְרָאִים].
[and as I heard: Hashem made a book which is the world, and a commentary upon it which is the Torah, explaining His acquisitions in creation].

וְאַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, שֶׁהוּא הַלִּמּוּד תּוֹרָה הַקָּבוּעַ בְּכָל יוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְנָחוֹת צט:) דִּבִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שַׁחֲרִית וְעַרְבִית קִיֵּים "לֹא יָמוּשׁ" (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ א, ח).
And happy is he who merits to grasp this in the Shema, the fixed daily Torah study, fulfilling "it shall not depart" through morning and evening Shema (Menachot 99b).

וּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע – דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, תְּפִלָּה – אֵינוֹ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרָכוֹת כא.), כִּי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּשִּׂיגוּ בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁהוּא מִצְוַת "לְדַבֵּר בָּם וְגוֹמֵר", עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה יַשִּׂיג הַחִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁל כָּל יוֹם.
Shema is Torah while prayer is not (Berakhot 21a), Hashem willing that through Shema—the mitzvah to speak of them—one grasp the daily insights through Torah speech.

וְכֵן רַשְׁבִּ"י וַחֲבֵירָיו שֶׁתּוֹרָתָן אֻמָּנוּתָן אֵין מַפְסִיקִין לִתְפִלָּה (שַׁבָּת יא.), כִּי הָיוּ יוֹדְעִים בְּכָל יוֹם חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה שֶׁמִּתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד כְּפִי הַחִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁבְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his colleagues whose trade was Torah did not interrupt for prayer (Shabbat 11a), knowing each day the insights renewed with Creation.
אֲבָל חֲכָמִים, שֶׁהֵם יָדְעוּ שֶׁלֹּא כָּל אֶחָד זוֹכֶה לְכָךְ, תִּקְּנוּ הַתְּפִלָּה לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיְּחָנֵּנוּ לִזְכּוֹת וּלְקַבֵּל הַשֶּׁפַע הַמְּחוּדָּשׁ שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם.
But the Sages, knowing not everyone merits this, instituted prayer to beseech Hashem to grant us that daily renewed influx.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן כב): לְבוּשִׁין דִּלְבַשׁ בְּצַפְרָא וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה תְּפִלָּה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ.
Therefore Tikkun 22 states: garments worn in the morning, etc., no prayer resembling another.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הַמִּלּוּי וְהַמְּבוּקָּשׁ לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ, כָּךְ הַבַּקָּשָׁה וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה שֶׁמְּקַבֶּלֶת כְּפִי הַמְּבוּקָּשׁ.
Just as the fulfillment differs, so the request and yearning adapt to what is sought.

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם הַתְּפִלָּה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים מִקּוֹדֶם: "אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח", וּכְפִי הַחִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם, כָּךְ הוּא פְּתִיחַת פִּיו בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ וּתְשׁוּקָתוֹ.
For prayer also stems from Hashem—"O Lord, open my lips"—opening his mouth according to that day's insights.
וּבְכָל יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הוּא זְמַן הָעֲבוֹדָה בְּעִיּוּן וִיגִיעָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה.
Weekdays are for toilsome labor in Torah and prayerful contemplation.

וּבָא שַׁבָּת בָּא מְנוּחָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קיט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב): בְּמָטוּתָא מִינַּיְיכוּ לָא תְּחַלְּלוּנִי; גַּם עַל יְדֵי לִמּוּד תּוֹרָה בִּיגִיעָה נִקְרָא חִלּוּל, כִּי אָז הוּא מְנוּחָה וּמֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּהֱנִין מִזִּיו מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם.

On Shabbat rest arrives (Shabbat 119b): "I beg of you, do not desecrate me"—even strenuous study is unfitting, for it is a day of rest like the World to Come, delighting in what Hashem directly bestows.
בַּלַּיְלָה הוּא חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין – פֵּירוּשׁ הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת נוּקְבָא כַּנּוֹדָע;
At night it is the Apple Field (Chakal Tapuchin)—yearning, the feminine attribute;

וּבַיּוֹם עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא הוּא מִדַּת אַיִן, פֵּירוּשׁ הֶעְדֵּר הַחֵשֶׁק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח (נב עַמּוּד ב) עַל "מַה תִּצְעַק אֵלָי" – בְּעַתִּיקָא תַּלְיָא, שֶׁהוּא הַשְׁפָּעָה בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגוֹת הַמּוּרְגָּשׁוֹת בְּחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וְחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב.

by day it is Atika Kadisha, the level of Ayin, beyond desire (Zohar Beshalach 52b on "Why do you cry to Me? It depends on Atika"), influencing the root of the soul above intellect and conscious desire.

וּבִסְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית שֶׁהוּא עִם הַיְצִיאָה, אָז זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הַמְּמַלֵּא לַחֵשֶׁק, וְהוּא אָז הַשֶּׁפַע הַיּוֹרֵד לְצוֹרֶךְ כָּל יְמֵי הַשָּׁבוּעַ גַּם כֵּן.
At the third meal as Shabbat departs, Ze'ir Anpin fulfills the desire, channeling the influx for the entire coming week.

וְתִקְּנוּ עַל זֶה שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת, כִּי הַמַּאֲכָל קִיּוּם הַחַיִּים, וְעַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילוֹת כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם נִכְנָסִים בַּלֵּב, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִסַּד הַמַּאֲכָל לְקִיּוּם חַיֵּי הָאָדָם, בְּוַדַּאי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ חַיּוּת הַמְחַיֶּה לוֹ.

And for this they instituted three meals, for food is the sustenance of life, and through eating in accordance with the will of Hashem it enters the heart; since Hashem, blessed be He, established food for the sustenance of human life, it surely has in it a vitalizing power that gives him life.
וְגַם בְּמַאֲכָל דְּחוֹל יֵשׁ שַׁיָּיכוּת, כִּדְאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (עא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): הַאי דְּלָא אֲמָרִי לָךְ מֵאוֹרְתָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אֲכַלִי בִּשְׂרָא דְּתוֹרָא.
Even weekday food has this impact (Bava Kamma 71b): "The reason I did not tell you this in the evening was because I had not yet eaten beef."

וְאָמְרוּ (מְכִילְתָּא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח): לֹא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא לְאוֹכְלֵי מָן, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהוּא לֶחֶם שֶׁמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹכְלִין, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ חַיּוּת רוּחָנִי עָצוּם מְאֹד, וְעַל יָדוֹ זוֹכֶה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה.
And the Mekhilta states the Torah was given only to eaters of the manna—bread of angels containing immense spiritual vitality, through which one merits much Torah.

וּמִסְּתָמָא כָּל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הָעוֹסְקִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לָהֶם, הֵם אוֹכְלֵי מָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: כָּל הַמְּקַבֵּל עוֹל תּוֹרָה מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּת וְעוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וּפַרְנָסָתוֹ הוּא דּוּגְמַת מָן, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ וַדַּאי אוֹתוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה לְהַכְנִיס בַּלֵּב חַיּוּת מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַשִּׂיג דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵאֲמִיתַּת חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ

And presumably all Torah scholars who engage in Torah, to whom the Torah was given, are eaters of manna, as stated: Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah, the yoke of the government and the yoke of worldly occupation are removed from him, and his livelihood is like manna; and it certainly contains that holiness to instill in the heart vitality from the truth of Hashem, blessed be He, by which he grasps the words of Torah from the truth of His wisdom, blessed be He

[וּמִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמָּן: "בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לֶחֶם יוֹמָיִם" (שְׁמוֹת טז, כט), נִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם לְעִנְיַן הַשְׁפָּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁפַע כָּפוּל, וְהוּא טְעִימָה מֵהַשְׁפָּעַת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם כֵּן לִטְעוֹם הַמַּאֲכָלוֹת דְּשַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת; וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח סא עַמּוּד ב, עַיֵּין שָׁם]:

[and from what is said of the manna, "on the sixth day, bread for two days" (Exodus 16:29), it appears that on Friday a double influx of Torah descends, tasting of Shabbat, just as one tastes Shabbat foods on Friday; and I subsequently found this in Zohar Beshalach 61b, see there].

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 49:2: “Rabbi Berekhiah, Rabbi Chiyya, and the Sages there said in Rabbi Yehuda’s name: There is no day on which the Holy One, blessed be He, does not introduce a new halakhah in the heavenly court. What is the scriptural basis? “Listen attentively to the thunder of His voice and the utterance that goes from His mouth.” “Utterance” means Torah, as it is said, “You shall meditate upon it day and night.” Even those halakhot were known to Abraham.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 119a:9-119b:1: “The Exilarch asked Rav Hamnuna: What does the verse mean, ‘And call Hashem’s holy day honored’? He answered: This is Yom Kippur, on which there is neither eating nor drinking. The Torah says: Honor it with clean clothing. As for ‘You shall honor it,’ Rav said: By eating earlier; Shmuel said: By eating later. The sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba asked Rav Pappa: For people like us, who have meat and wine every day, how should we make it different? He told them: If you usually eat early, eat later; if you usually eat late, eat earlier. In summer Rav Sheshet seated the scholars where the sun would reach them; in winter he seated them where the shade would reach them, so that they would get up promptly. Rabbi Zeira would seek out scholars studying in pairs and say to them, ‘Please do not profane Shabbat by neglecting its enjoyment.’”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Bechukotai 1:2: “Shabbat too is called a statute, as stated in the Mekhilta cited above: “A statute”—this is Shabbat. The Jerusalem Talmud states: Shabbatot were given only for eating and drinking, and so forth; another says: Shabbatot were given only for engaging in words of Torah. paragraphs.text: Zohar, Yitro 27:455-457: “Rabbi Elazar said to his father: How are these meals arranged? He said to him: Concerning Shabbat night it is written, “I shall cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth.” On that night the Queen and the entire field of apples are blessed, a person’s table is blessed, and an additional soul is given. On Shabbat day, at the second meal, it is written, “Then you shall delight above Hashem”—“above Hashem,” indeed. For at that time the Holy Ancient One is revealed, and all the worlds are in joy. We celebrate the completion and joy of the Ancient One, and the meal is certainly His. At the third meal of Shabbat it is written, “I shall feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father.” This is the meal of Zeir Anpin, who is in a state of completeness. All six days are blessed from that completeness. A person should rejoice at his meal and complete these meals, which are the meals of the complete faith of the holy seed of Israel, who belong to the supernal faith. For it is theirs, and not that of the nations who worship stars and constellations. Therefore it says, “Between Me and the children of Israel.””

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Toldot 8:1: “In truth, even physical eating and drinking give vitality to the human soul, yet the soul’s vitality comes only through words of Torah, as it is said, “For it is your life,” and it is written, “Choose life.” They said: “If this is so in the place of our life,” and so forth, “we too,” and so forth. That is, words of Torah are the place of our life, like water for fish. Necessarily, then, food and drink contain the vitality of words of Torah. This is the well-known interpretation of the verse, “Not by bread,” and so forth, “but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of Hashem,” and so forth: it means what proceeds from Hashem’s mouth within the bread.”

paragraphs.text: Receiving Torah’s renewal through the life carried by food

rich.text: Receiving Torah’s renewal through the life carried by food

paragraphs.text: The siman follows daily renewal in Creation, Torah, and prayer into the special reception of Shabbat. It then explains nourishment as a means by which spiritual vitality and Torah understanding enter the heart.

rich.text: The siman follows daily renewal in Creation, Torah, and prayer into the special reception of Shabbat. It then explains nourishment as a means by which spiritual vitality and Torah understanding enter the heart.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Et HaOchel 1:1: “Oil, which alludes to wisdom—the clear knowledge and recognition that “I am your God”—comes after proper eating, suitably directed toward God, to sustain one’s soul. Such eating then adds wisdom and knowledge of God. By contrast, gross eating like an animal dulls the heart and mind. This is like their saying in Bava Kamma: “The reason I did not tell you ... was that I had not eaten ox meat.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Et HaOchel adds the distinction between nourishment directed toward sustaining life for God and animal-like overeating. Its concluding image of oil as clear recognition specifies the effect of the former and the obstruction caused by the latter, clarifying why food’s influence on Torah understanding depends on its direction.

paragraphs.text: Manna as light made into nourishment

rich.text: Manna as light made into nourishment

paragraphs.text: The nourishment image includes a form in which divine illumination can be received by the creature.

rich.text: The nourishment image includes a form in which divine illumination can be received by the creature.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:79:12: “The Zohar therefore describes Netzach and Hod as garments of the Holy One. A garment covers and somewhat dims the strength of what is clothed, so that through it we can look upon what is clothed. They are also called the heavens that grind manna: the nourishment of the righteous, their delight in apprehending Hashem's radiance, as described in Berakhot. Thus Yoma calls manna the bread eaten by ministering angels, and Shemot Rabbah says that they are nourished by the radiance of the Shechinah. This delight occurs when the Shechinah is joined with her Beloved, and comes through the supporting powers that limit apprehension and grind it finely until it is fit as food and nourishment.”

A garment covers and somewhat dims the strength of what is clothed, so that through it we can look upon what is clothed. This delight occurs when the Shechinah is joined with her Beloved, and comes through the supporting powers that limit apprehension and grind it finely until it is fit as food and nourishment.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah explains why the Zohar describes powers of limitation as grinding manna. Their concealment does not merely obstruct the light; it makes the illumination approachable as nourishment. This illuminates the present siman's movement from heavenly life to Torah received through eating, while preserving the need for a suitable form of reception rather than identifying food with unbounded divine light without mediation.

sections.en: The Essence of Man Consists of the Thoughts

p: [ריז] עִיקַּר הָאָדָם הוּא הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים וּרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וָלֵב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ רוּחָנִיּוּת אָדָם; אֲבָל הַגּוּף הוּא גַּשְׁמִי וְנִקְרָא בְּשַׂר אָדָם.
The essence of man consists of the thoughts, musings, and desires within mind and heart, which constitute the spiritual person; the physical body is merely human flesh.

וּכְשֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ שְׁקוּעִים בַּהֲבָלִים, אָז נִקְרָא "אָדָם רָע", כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּדְמוּת אָדָם יוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכִּסֵּא וְהוּא מְקוֹר מַחְצַב הַנְּשָׁמוֹת, וְזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ אָדָם בְּלִיַּעַל – פֵּירוּשׁ קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה מִכָּל מִינֵי מַחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת לְרַע.

And when his thought and will are sunken in vanities, he is termed an "evil man"; for the human form sits upon the Throne as the source of souls, and opposite it stands the wicked man (adam beliya'al)—a stature composed of evil thoughts and desires.

וְכַנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הַזֹּהַר מִשְׁפָּטִים (צה עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת ח, ט), וְעַל זֶה מְבַקְּשִׁין: "חַלְּצֵנִי ה' מֵאָדָם רָע" (תְּהִלִּים קמ, ב).

And as known from Zohar Mishpatim 95b on "a time wherein one man has power over another to his own hurt" (Ecclesiastes 8:9), concerning which we pray: "Deliver me, Hashem, from the evil man" (Psalms 140:2).
כִּי בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מד.) הִמְשִׁילוּ חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהוּצֵי הַסּוֹבְבִים הָאָסָא.
For in Sanhedrin 44a they compared the sins of Israel to thorns surrounding a myrtle.

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאָדָם שֶׁעַל הַכִּסֵּא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, כו), רַק שֶׁהָאָדָם רָע מַלְבִּישָׁם וַאֲסוּרִים וּכְבוּשִׁים בּוֹ.
For the root of the Jewish soul derives from the Man upon the Throne—"in Our image, after Our likeness"—only that the evil man enclothes them, holding them captive.
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו.): וְקָיְימֵי עֲלַן וְכוּלֵי, כָּל חַד מִינַּן אַלְפָּא מִשְּׂמָאלֵיהּ וְרִבְבָתָא מִימִינֵיהּ.
And as in Berakhot 6a: they stand around us, a thousand at our left and ten thousand at our right.

"מִימִינוֹ" – פֵּירוּשׁ: תַּאֲווֹת וְחֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, זֶהוּ "רִבְבוֹת" לְשׁוֹן רִבּוּי, שֶׁהוּא בְּתוֹקֶף עָצוּם, כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁבְּלֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בְּטַעַם דִּמְצוֹרָע מִשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא הַזָּב.

"At his right"—the lusts of this world, designated as "ten thousand" (rivavah), multitude, surging with vast power, this being the primary inclination in Jewish hearts (as I heard, this is why a leper is expelled beyond the camp and not a zav).

"וּמִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ" – דְּהַיְינוּ גְּבוּרָה רָעָה בְּכַעַס וְקִנְאָה וְנִיצּוּחַ וַאֲבִיזְרַיְיהוּ, "אַלְפָּא" הוּא הַמִּסְפָּר הַיּוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ן עַל פָּסוּק "נָתַתִּי אֶלֶף כֶּסֶף" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ, טז).
"At his left"—corrupt Gevurah in anger, envy, and rivalry, designated as a "thousand," the highest named number (Ramban on Genesis 20:16).
וְהַיְינוּ דְּדָבָר שֶׁתַּחַת סוּג הַמִּסְפָּר וְהַגְּבוּל, רַק שֶׁהוּא בְּתוֹקֶף וְגוּזְמָא – נָקַט אֶלֶף; וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּסוּג הַמִּסְפָּר תּוֹפֵס רְבָבָה.
A bounded count taken to the extreme uses "thousand," while that transcending count takes "ten thousand."
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, דְּלָכֵן שָׂרִים עַד אֶלֶף, וְעַל הָרִבּוֹא הוּא מַדְרֵגַת מֶלֶךְ.
Thus officers extend to a thousand, while over ten thousand reigns a king.

וּלְפִי שֶׁיֵּצֶר הָרָע דְּתַאֲוָה הוּא "טוֹב מְאֹד", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קלח עַמּוּד א) שֶׁיִּשָּׁאֵר גַּם לֶעָתִיד רַק דְּאִתְלַבַּן, דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לָא אִשְׁתֲּכַח חֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, וּמִצַּד זֶה הוּא בִּלְתִּי גְּבוּל, לְכָךְ גַּם הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּתוֹ לְרַע הוּא בְּרִבּוּי.

And since the inclination for desire is "very good" (Midrash HaNe'elam, Zohar I:138a), remaining in the future refined—for without it love of Torah would vanish—being boundless, its spread in evil is likewise manifold.
וְכָל זֶה רַק מִצַּד וּמִיָּמִין שֶׁסּוֹבְבִים וּמַלְבִּישִׁים;
And all this merely surrounds and enclothes from the right and left;

וְ"אֵלֶיךָ" – פֵּירוּשׁ אֶל פְּנִימִיּוּתְךָ וּמַעֲמַקֵּי שָׁרְשְׁךָ – "לֹא יִגָּשׁ" (תְּהִלִּים צא, ז), דְּהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁאָר, וְ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.), רַק לָבוּשׁ תּוֹךְ הָאָדָם רָע.
but "unto you"—your inner core and deep root—"it shall not approach" (Psalms 91:7), the root enduring, for "even though he sinned, he remains Israel," merely clothed within the evil man.

וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַבַּקָּשָׁה: "חַלְּצֵנִי וְגוֹמֵר" – עַל הֶעָבָר, מַה שֶּׁכְּבָר נִשְׁתַּקַּע תּוֹךְ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת אֲשֶׁר לֹא לַה' הֵמָּה, וְנַעֲשׂוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מַלְבּוּשִׁים לְנִשְׁמָתוֹ: חַלְּצֵנִי וְהוֹצִיאֵנִי מֵהֶם.
And concerning this is the plea: "Deliver me, etc."—regarding the past, what was sunken in alien thoughts becoming garments for his soul: deliver me and extract me from them.
וְעַל לְהַבָּא: "מֵאִישׁ חֲמָסִים תִּנְצְרֵנִי" (שָׁם קמ, ב).
And regarding the future: "preserve me from the violent man" (ibid. 140:2).
פֵּירוּשׁ, "אָדָם" שֵׁם כְּלָלִי, וַחֲלוּקִים לְזָכָר וּנְקֵבָה "אִישׁ" וְ"אִשָּׁה";
"Adam" is a general term, dividing into male and female, ish and ishah;
וְיָדוּעַ דְּהַתַּאֲוָה וְהַחֵשֶׁק נוּקְבָא, וְהַכֹּחַ וּגְבוּרָה דְּכוּרָא, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִמְשָׁכִים בָּרָע רְצִיחָה וְכַעַס וַאֲבִיזְרַיְיהוּ.
and desire is female, while might is male, whence stem murder, anger, and their offshoots in evil.

וְזֶהוּ "אִישׁ חֲמָסִים", שֶׁהוּא בָּא לַעֲשׁוֹק הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁכְּבָר נֶחֶלְצָה מִמֶּנָּה כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁהִיא חֲלוּשָׁה, כְּטַעַם: אֵיזֶהוּ גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ, וּכְשֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כֹּחַ לִכְבּוֹשׁ הוּא חוֹמְסוֹ;
This is the "violent man" (ish chamasim) coming to rob the soul that was already extracted, seeing it weak, robbing it when strength to conquer fails;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּבָר בָּא לִיטָּהֵר וְנִטְהַר עַל הֶעָבָר כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ, הוּא מִשְׁתַּדֵּל לָשׁוּב לְעָשְׁקוֹ וּלְחוֹמְסוֹ לְחֶלְקוֹ בִּגְזֵילָה.
though he came to be purified and was cleansed of the past, the violent inclination strives to rob him again.

וְזֶה כֹּחַ הָאִישׁ, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַכַּעַס כַּיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל עַל פָּסוּק "טֹרֵף נַפְשׁוֹ בְּאַפּוֹ" (אִיּוֹב יח, ד), שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַכַּעַס הַנֶּפֶשׁ נִטְרֶפֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁהָאִישׁ חֲמָסִים הַמַּכְנִיס הַכַּעַס חוֹמְסָהּ,
And this is the male power operating through anger, as the Ari explained on "He tears his soul in his anger" (Job 18:4), the soul being torn and robbed by the violent man through anger,
וְאָז עַל יְדֵי זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ יֵשׁ שְׁלִיטָה לָרָע בּוֹ גַּם בְּכָל מִינֵי הִרְהוּרִים וַחֲמוּדוֹת.
giving evil subsequent dominion over him in lusts as well.

וְעַל זֶה מְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁיִּשְׁמְרֶנּוּ לְהַבָּא מִכַּעַס וְקִנְאָה וַאֲבִיזְרַיְיהוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נֶחְמָס, וּמִמֵּילָא יִהְיֶה שָׁמוּר גַּם כֵּן בְּתַאֲוָה שֶׁהִיא הַנּוּקְבָא שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ כֹּחַ הַחֲמוּסָה.
And concerning this he prays to be preserved from anger and envy so as not to be robbed, automatically remaining guarded in desire which lacks violent force on its own.

שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁכָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו שְׁקוּעִים בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵין שְׁלִיטָה לְהִרְהוּרֵי תַּאֲווֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם (סוֹף הִלְכוֹת אִיסּוּרֵי בִיאָה) דְּאֵין הִרְהוּרִין שׁוֹלְטִים אֶלָּא בְּלֵב פָּנוּי מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
For once his thoughts are immersed in Torah, lustful thoughts have no dominion, as Maimonides wrote (end of Issurei Biah) that lustful thoughts dominate only a heart vacant of Torah.

רַק שֶׁהַכַּעַס יָכוֹל לִגְבּוֹר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית ד.): הַאי צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנָן דְּרָתַח וְכוּלֵי, וּבָזֶה יֵשׁ שְׁלִיטָה לְאִישׁ חֲמָסִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לָבוֹא לְכַעַס גָּמוּר הָרַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
Yet anger can flare (Ta'anit 4a: "this young scholar who flares up"), giving the violent man dominion to bring about destructive wrath.

וְצָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּשְׁמְרֶנּוּ, וְזֶהוּ אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִטְהַר לְשֶׁעָבַר בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ "חַלְּצֵנִי וְגוֹמֵר", וְנֶחֱלַץ מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים הַשּׁוֹטְפִים וְעוֹבְרִים בְּמוֹחוֹ וְלִבּוֹ לְדַעְתּוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לְדַעְתּוֹ, וְנִתְיַיחֵד לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,

And he must pray to be preserved, following his purification over the past through "Deliver me," being rescued from turbulent thoughts passing through brain and heart consciously and unconsciously, consecrating himself to Hashem,
כְּטַעַם: אִם אַתְּ יָהֵיב עֵינָא וְלִבָּא לִי – אֲנָא יָדַע דְּאַתְּ דִּילִי (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה ה), שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר הָאָדָם;
in the spirit of: "If you give your eye and your heart to Me, I know that you are Mine" (Yerushalmi Berakhot 1:5), which constitutes the essence of man;
הָעַיִן רוֹמֵז עַל מַחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהִרְהוּרֵי הַמּוֹחַ שֶׁבָּאִים מִמֶּנּוּ.
the eye alluding to the thoughts of the brain that issue from it.
וְאָז עַל כָּל פָּנִים יֵשׁ לוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל לְהַבָּא מֵאִישׁ וְגוֹמֵר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
And then he must certainly pray for the future to be preserved from the violent man, as noted above.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Mishpatim 3:23-34: ‘This is a mystery higher than all the others. On the pillar that stands for weighing, within the blowing air, there is one balance on this side and another balance on that side. On this side are just scales, and on that side are deceitful scales. This balance is never at rest. Souls rise and descend, enter and return, and there are souls held captive when one man rules over another, as it is written: ‘At a time when one man ruled over another to his own harm’—to his own harm indeed.’

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Achrei Mot 3: “The land too will perceive the depth and have eyes to recognize who truly serves Hashem. No soul of Israel will consequently be lost, for in the depth of Israel's heart they are full of willingness and service. Although great concealment is sometimes found within Israel, it is in the garment; in the depth of the heart they are pure. The land will therefore understand that even when impurity and concealment appear within Israel, these concern the garment, while inwardly they are connected with the light of His will. This is ‘the land will not vomit you out’: no individual soul of Israel will be lost.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef describes the land acquiring eyes to recognize inward service rather than judging by the garment alone. This clarifies the distinction behind ‘rescue me from an evil man’: the obstructing configuration of thoughts is real, but it does not exhaust the soul's root. The enduring inward connection supplies the possibility of release; it does not make the work of removing the garment unnecessary.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Numbers, Nasso 4: “‘And they shall send out of the camp every leper, and every zav, and whoever is impure through a corpse’ (Numbers 5:2). The leper is anger, for tzara’at comes for the sin of evil speech (Arakhin 15b); the zav is the man of desire; and one impure through a corpse is sadness. Therefore the leper is sent out of all three camps, for the trait of anger has no share in Israel; and the zav is sent only from the camp of the Levites and the camp of the Shechinah, for the trait of desire does not befit Torah scholars.”

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar Ruach HaKodesh 15:4: “My teacher, of blessed memory, was more stringent about anger than about all the other transgressions, even when a person becomes angry for the sake of a mitzvah, as in the case of Moshe mentioned above. He gave this reason: all the other transgressions cause damage only in the particular limb affected by each transgression, but the trait of anger damages the entire soul and completely exchanges it. The matter is that when a person becomes angry, the holy soul departs from him entirely, and a soul from the side of the husk enters in its place. This is the secret of Scripture’s words, “He tears his soul in his anger,” and so forth: he actually tears his holy soul, makes it torn and unfit, and kills it at the time of his wrath and anger. This is explained in the Zohar, Tetzaveh, page 182b; see there how severely it describes anger, to the point of saying that one who speaks with an angry person is as though he speaks with idolatry itself; see there.”

sections.en: The Primary Root of the Evil Inclination Lies in Bodily Desire

p: [ריח] עִיקַּר הַיֵּצֶר הוּא בְּתַאֲוָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁרָאִינוּ בִּתְחִלַּת הַכְנָסַת הַיֵּצֶר לְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, וְלָכֵן הָיָה אִשָּׁה וְנוּקְבָא.

The primary root of the evil inclination lies in bodily desire, as we saw at the initial entry of the inclination into Adam the First, which is why it manifested through woman and the feminine dimension.
וְיֵצֶר דִּרְצִיחָה נוֹלָד מִכֹּחַ הַתַּאֲוָה וְנִתְחַדֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי קַיִן הַנּוֹלָד מֵהֶם, וּבָא לוֹ מִכֹּחַ חֶמְדָּתוֹ וְתַאֲוָתוֹ לִירַשׁ כָּל הָעוֹלָם.

And the inclination for murder was born out of the power of desire and was introduced into the world through Cain who was born of them, springing from his covetousness and lust to inherit the entire world.
אֲבָל בְּרִיאַת הַיֵּצֶר בָּאָדָם הוּא בְּתַאֲוָה, שֶׁזֶּה יֵשׁ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן טוֹב בַּחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא.
But the fundamental creation of the inclination in man is rooted in desire, for within this there also abides potential goodness in the holy yearning for Torah (chamidu de-orayta).
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: "בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע, בָּרָאתִי תוֹרָה תַּבְלִין" (קִדּוּשִׁין ל:), שֶׁהִיא מְתַבַּלְתּוֹ וְעוֹשָׂה אוֹתוֹ מַאֲכָל רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת בְּמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל;

And concerning this they said: "I created the evil inclination, I created the Torah as its seasoning/antidote" (Kiddushin 30b), for Torah seasons it and renders it a fitting food to dwell within the camp of Israel;
וּמִמֵּילָא מִתְפּוֹצֵץ גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִצְרָא דְּכַעַס וּרְצִיחָה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם תַּאֲוָה וְחֵשֶׁק רַק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
and automatically through this the inclination for anger and bloodshed is likewise shattered, since when one harbors no desire and passion except for words of Torah,
אֵינוֹ כּוֹעֵס אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מְרַתְּחָא לֵיהּ (תַּעֲנִית ד.), כְּעִנְיַן "מְשַׂנְאֶיךָ ה' אֶשְׂנָא" (תְּהִלִּים קלט, כא).
he becomes angry only where the Torah itself inflames him (Ta'anit 4a), in the manner of: "Do I not hate them, Hashem, that hate You?" (Psalms 139:21).
וְאָמַר: "וּרְבָבָה מִימִינֶךָ" (שָׁם צא, ז) – עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבַּיָּמִין, שֶׁמַּכְנִיס כָּל חֶשְׁקוֹ לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
And Scripture states: "and ten thousand at your right hand" (ibid. 91:7)—achieved through the Torah which is at the right, directing all his desire toward words of Torah.
אֲבָל בִּשְׂמֹאל לֹא אָמַר "מִשְּׂמֹאלְךָ", שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁימּוּשׁ בִּגְבוּרָתוֹ וְכַעֲסוֹ לְטוֹב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַצֵּחַ מִדַּת הַכַּעַס, דְּיוּכַל לָבוֹא גַּם כֵּן לִידֵי כַּעַס רָע;

But regarding the left it does not state "from your left," for through utilizing one's might and anger for good it is impossible to conquer the trait of anger, as it could still degenerate into evil wrath;

רַק הַנִּצּוּחַ גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְאַוֶּוה רַק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, מִמֵּילָא אֵינוֹ מִתְאַוֶּוה כְּלָל לְעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְאֵינוֹ כּוֹעֵס עֲלֵיהֶם וְלֹא מִתְקַנֵּא בָּהֶם רַק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,

rather its defeat is likewise achieved through Torah: when one desires solely words of Torah, he automatically desires nothing of worldly pursuits, feeling neither anger over them nor envy regarding them, except in words of Torah,
וְאִם כֵּן הַנִּצּוּחַ שֶׁלָּהּ הוּא בְּאִתְכַּפְיָא, וְשֶׁהַשְּׂמֹאל נֶעְלֶמֶת וּכְבוּשָׁה וְאֵינָהּ עוֹשָׂה פְּעֻלָּתָהּ.
so that the conquest of the left is through suppression (itkafya), the left remaining hidden and subdued without exerting its destructive force.
וּבִקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף, שֶׁהוּא טְבִיעַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהֵם כֹּחוֹת הַדִּמְיוֹן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"ה, נֶאֱמַר: "וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חוֹמָה מִימִינָם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָם" (שְׁמוֹת יד, כב),

And at the parting of the Red Sea, which was the drowning of Egypt representing the powers of illusion (Section 205), it is said: "and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left" (Exodus 14:22),
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח לְגִרְסַת יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי) עַל תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלִּין,
which our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Mekhilta, Beshalach, according to Yalkut Shimoni) as referring to Torah and tefillin,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם מְגִינִים עֲלֵיהֶם, שֶׁהֵם אֵין שְׁקוּעִים בְּדִמְיוֹנוֹת כְּמִצְרַיִם, כִּי כֹּחוֹת הַתַּאֲוָה שְׁקוּעִים בְּחֶמְדַּת הַתּוֹרָה.
meaning that these shield them so that they do not sink into illusions like the Egyptians, for their desires are channeled into the love of Torah.

וְהַנִּצּוּחַ בִּתְפִלִּין, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ו.): "וְיָרְאוּ מִמֶּךָּ" (דְּבָרִים כח, י) – אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם): "וּבִזְרוֹעַ עֻזּוֹ" (יְשַׁעְיָה סב, ח) – זֶה תְּפִלִּין,

And the victory over the left is through tefillin, as our Sages stated (Berakhot 6a): "'and they shall be afraid of you'—these are the tefillin of the head," and as stated: "'and by the arm of His strength'—this is the tefillin of the arm,"
שֶׁהִיא הַזְּרוֹעַ עֹז לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּכֹחַ שְׂמֹאלוֹ בִּרְצִיחָה וְכַעַס נֶגֶד הָאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים, לִשְׁפּוֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם הַזַּעַם.
which is the arm of strength to utilize the power of the left in holy wrath against the idolatrous nations, pouring out indignation upon them.
וְכָל דִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל קִנְאָה וְכַעַס שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיוּ תְּפִלִּין, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר קְשׁוּרִים וּדְבוּקִים בַּאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאֵינָם דִּמְיוֹן כּוֹזֵב מַה שֶּׁנֶּגֶד רְצוֹנוֹ.
And all their imaginings of jealousy and anger were like tefillin—meaning bound and cleaving unto the authentic will of the Blessed Name, not false illusions contrary to His will.

וּמִי שֶׁדָּבוּק לְגַמְרֵי, הוּא יָכוֹל לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ גַּם בְּמִדַּת הַשְּׂמֹאל וּבְרוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן, וְלִכְבּוֹשׁ יֵצֶר שֶׁל כַּעַס גַּם כֵּן בִּלְאִתְהַפְכָא, לִכְעוֹס רַק בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

And one who cleaves completely can also utilize the attribute of the left and scholarly indignation (rugza de-rabbanan), subduing the inclination of anger through transformation (ithapkha), becoming angry solely in accordance with Hashem's will.
רַק שֶׁזֶּה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קל.) דְּמִצְוַת תְּפִלִּין מְרוּפָּה בְּיָדֵינוּ, דִּצְרִיכִין גּוּף נָקִי,
Only that this is scarcely accessible in this world, as stated in Shabbat 130a that the mitzvah of tefillin is held weakly by us because it requires a pristine body,
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נָקִי מִכָּל מִינֵי חֶמְדָּה וּנְגִיעָה לְעַצְמוֹ כְּלָל אֲפִילּוּ כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה,
meaning that it be completely clean of any personal desire or selfish bias even by a hairsbreadth,
כְּעִנְיַן אֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹף סַנְהֶדְרִין קיג:) דְּקַפְּדָן הֲוָה, כִּי הָיָה מְרוּחָק מִתַּאֲווֹת גּוּפוֹ לְגַמְרֵי,
in the manner of Elijah of whom our Sages stated (end of Sanhedrin 113b) that he was zealous and exacting, because he was entirely detached from physical desires,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כז): הֲרֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא [הַיְינוּ בְּחֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּתַאֲוָה] וְחַי לְעוֹלָם.
as stated in Vayikra Rabbah 27: behold Elijah who did not sin [namely, in Adam's sin of lust] and lives forever.

וְהוּא יָבוֹא לִפְנֵי בִּיאַת הַמָּשִׁיחַ, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה כֹּחוֹ בְּלִבּוֹת כָּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת נְקִיִּים מִנְּגִיעָה לַגּוּף לְגַמְרֵי, וּלְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּמִדַּת הַכַּעַס וְהַנְּקָמָה נֶגֶד הָעַכּוּ"ם בִּזְרוֹעַ עֹז, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נוֹלָד בְּלִבָּם הִתְעוֹרְרוּת – זֶה נִקְרָא בִּיאַת אֵלִיָּהוּ.

And he will arrive before the coming of the Messiah, meaning that his spiritual power will be unveiled in the hearts of all Israel to be completely pure of bodily bias and to wield righteous anger and vengeance against the nations with an arm of strength; when this awakening is born in their hearts, that is termed the coming of Elijah.
וְכֵן הַיְחִידִים זוֹכִים לִפְרָקִים לְגוּף נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי, אָז זוֹכֶה לְמַדְרֵגַת גִּלּוּי אֵלִיָּהוּ לְפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ וְחָכְמָתוֹ, וְאָז יוּכַל לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּרוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן.
And so worthy individuals who merit at times a completely pristine body attain the disclosure of Elijah according to their spiritual level and wisdom, and can then utilize scholarly indignation.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהַסַּנְהֶדְרִין הָיוּ דָּנִין דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת וְלֹא הָיוּ אוֹכְלִין כָּל אוֹתוֹ יוֹם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין סג.), שֶׁהָיוּ צְרִיכִין לִהְיוֹת גּוּף נָקִי מִכָּל חֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
And just as the Sanhedrin when judging capital cases did not eat on that day (Sanhedrin 63a), for they needed to be a body cleansed of all worldly desires.
וְהוּא מְרוּפֶּה בְּיָדֵינוּ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת בִּקְבִיעוּת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁעֲדַיִן יֵשׁ עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ וְיֵצֶר הָרָע בָּעוֹלָם.
And this remains weakly held by us, since it cannot be attained continuously in this world where the counsel of the Serpent and the evil inclination still persist.
וְלָכֵן צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת הַשְּׂמֹאל נֶעְלֶמֶת וּלְהִשָּׁמֵר מִכַּעַס וְקַפְּדָנוּת לְגַמְרֵי, וּמִקִּנְאָה וְשִׂנְאָה וְתַחֲרוּת.
Therefore the left must remain concealed, and one must guard himself entirely from anger, strictness, envy, hatred, and strife.
"רַק בְּעֵינֶיךָ תַבִּיט [וְשִׁלֻּמַת רְשָׁעִים תִּרְאֶה]" (תְּהִלִּים צא, ח) הוּא כְּעִנְיַן "דּוֹם לַה' [וְהִתְחוֹלֵל לוֹ]" (שָׁם לז, ז) דְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּגִטִּין (ז.),
"Only with your eyes shall you behold [and see the recompense of the wicked]" (Psalms 91:8) is in the spirit of "Resign yourself unto Hashem [and wait patiently for Him]" (Psalms 37:7; Gittin 7a),
דְּעַל יְדֵי עֵינֵי הַשֵּׂכֶל וּשְׁקִידָתָם בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא הַנִּצּוּחַ מִמֵּילָא בְּלִי שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּנִיצּוּחַ כְּלָל:
for through the eyes of the intellect and diligent immersion in the study hall and words of Torah, victory arrives automatically without one needing to employ contentious triumph at all.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וְיֵצֶר דִּרְצִיחָה נוֹלָד מִכֹּחַ הַתַּאֲוָה וְנִתְחַדֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי קַיִן הַנּוֹלָד מֵהֶם, וּבָא לוֹ מִכֹּחַ חֶמְדָּתוֹ וְתַאֲוָתוֹ לִירַשׁ כָּל הָעוֹלָם.
footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And the inclination for murder was born out of the power of desire and was introduced into the world through Cain who was born of them, springing from his covetousness and lust to inherit the entire world.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 22:7: ““Cain said to Abel his brother, and when they were,” and so forth: What were they disputing? They said: Let us divide the world. One took the land and the other took the movable property. One said: The land on which you stand is mine. The other said: What you are wearing is mine. One said: Take it off! The other said: Fly away! As a result, “Cain rose against Abel his brother and killed him.” Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name: Both took land and both took movable property. What, then, were they disputing? One said: The Temple will be built in my territory; the other said: The Temple will be built in my territory. paragraphs.text: Learning through seeing another's failure
The teaching reached after a failure need not require the learner's own failure.

rich.text: The teaching reached after a failure need not require the learner's own failure.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Chagigah 2: “Although many words of Torah can be attained only through toil, patience and preceding failure—as Gittin 43a says, a person does not stand upon words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them—my holy grandfather explained that this too is only from the person's concealment. Because he distances himself from them, he needs toil, patience and a preceding failure. In truth, even the teachings reached only through failure do not require that he himself fail. By seeing others who wish to distance themselves from Torah fail, one can likewise reach and understand those teachings. He need not fail personally; seeing another's failure suffices, as it says (Psalms 91:8), ‘You shall see the recompense of the wicked.’”

Because he distances himself from them, he needs toil, patience and a preceding failure. In truth, even the teachings reached only through failure do not require that he himself fail. By seeing others who wish to distance themselves from Torah fail, one can likewise reach and understand those teachings. He need not fail personally; seeing another's failure suffices, as it says (Psalms 91:8), ‘You shall see the recompense of the wicked.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef directly explains the siman's closing verse about seeing the recompense of the wicked. A person can learn from another's failure instead of undergoing or choosing it himself. This supports the siman's ordinary instruction to remain in Torah and refrain from anger, while the earlier discussion of exceptional purity remains qualified.

sections.en: In Proportion to the Preeminence of Knowledge and Wisdom within a Person

p: [ריט] כְּפִי יִתְרוֹן הַדַּעַת וְהַחָכְמָה שֶׁבָּאָדָם, כָּךְ מִתְגַּבְּרִים לְעֻמָּתָן הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת בְּמוֹחוֹ וְלִבּוֹ, כְּעִנְיַן: "יוֹסִיף דַּעַת [יוֹסִיף מַכְאוֹב]" (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח).

In proportion to the preeminence of knowledge and wisdom within a person, so do illusions surge corresponding to them in his mind and heart, in the manner of: "he that increases knowledge [increases sorrow]" (Ecclesiastes 1:18).

וְכֵן עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע: עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּכְנַס בּוֹ דַּעַת טוֹב נִכְנַס גַּם כֵּן הַהֵיפֶךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סוֹטָה כא:): נִכְנְסָה חָכְמָה – נִכְנְסָה עַרְמוּמִיּוּת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֲנִי [חָכְמָה שָׁכַנְתִּי] עָרְמָה" (מִשְׁלֵי ח, יב).

And so with the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil: through good knowledge entering him, its opposite entered as well, as stated in Sotah 21b: once wisdom enters, cunning enters, as it is said: "I, [wisdom, dwell with] prudence/cunning" (Proverbs 8:12).
וְאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ע:): אֵין הַתִּינוֹק יוֹדֵעַ לִקְרוֹת "אַבָּא" וְ"אִמָּא" עַד שֶׁטּוֹעֵם דָּגָן, וְנִמְצָא אָז נִכְנַס בּוֹ דַּעַת וְחָכְמָה,
And they stated in Sanhedrin 70b: an infant does not know how to call "father" and "mother" until he tastes grain, showing that then knowledge and wisdom enter him;
וְאָז מַרְחִיקִין מִצּוֹאָתוֹ (סֻכָּה מב:), וּמְפוֹרָשׁ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת (פֶּרֶק ג הֲלָכָה ה) הַטַּעַם: שֶׁמַּחְשְׁבוֹתָיו רָעוֹת.
and then one must distance himself from his excrement (Sukkah 42b), the reason being explicitly stated in Yerushalmi Berakhot 3:5: because his thoughts become bad.
וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי, כִּי בִּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה שֶׁנִּכְנַס יֵצֶר טוֹב, שֶׁאָז הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִתְגַּבֵּר, וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב.): "כָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ [יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ]".

And so I heard, that at thirteen years when the good inclination enters, then the evil inclination intensifies, as they said (Sukkah 52a): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, [his inclination is greater than he]."
וּמִי שֶׁמִּתְגַּבֵּר וְכוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ לְגַמְרֵי, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "אֹיְבֵי אִישׁ אַנְשֵׁי בֵיתוֹ" (מִיכָה ז, ו).
And for one who overpowers and subdues his inclination completely, concerning him it is said: "a man's enemies are the men of his own house" (Micah 7:6).
שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע נִקְרָא "שׂוֹנֵא", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם) [וְכֵן בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נד) נִדְרַשׁ מִקְרָא זֶה אַיֵּצֶר],
For the evil inclination is called an "enemy," as stated there [and in Bereishit Rabbah 54 this verse is expounded upon the inclination],

וּמִי שֶׁכְּאִישׁ גְּבוּרָתוֹ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגְדּוֹ, אָז כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁלּוֹ מִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּאַנְשֵׁי בֵיתוֹ וּמְקוֹרָבָיו, שֶׁמִּכֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרוֹעֵשׁ בְּקִרְבָּם נִכְנָסִים לוֹ גַּם כֵּן דִּמְיוֹנוֹת תֹּהוּ;

and when a person has the manly strength to overcome it within himself, the power of his inclination disperses into the members of his household and associates, so that from the storming inclination within them, chaotic delusions enter him as well;
וּכְפִי גָדְלוֹ כָּךְ מִתְרַבִּים אַנְשֵׁי בֵיתוֹ: שָׂרֵי עֲשָׂרוֹת, וַחֲמִשִּׁים, וּמֵאוֹת, וַאֲלָפִים.
and according to his stature, so do the members of his house multiply: captains of tens, fifties, hundreds, and thousands.

וּמֶלֶךְ, שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדָיו, וְכָל מִינֵי יְצָרִים שֶׁבְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מוֹלִידִים דִּמְיוֹנוֹת בּוֹ, וְהוּא צָרִיךְ לְחַלְּצָם הַטּוֹב מֵהָרָע, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְקָנִים מִמֵּילָא אוֹתָם הָאֲנָשִׁים גַּם כֵּן.

And a king, whose servants are all Israel—all varieties of inclinations within every Jew generate delusions within him, and he must extract the good from the evil within them, whereby those individuals are automatically rectified as well.
וְעַל זֶה בִּקֵּשׁ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "מֵאֹיְבַי תְּחַכְּמֵנִי מִצְוֹתֶךָ [כִּי לְעוֹלָם הִיא לִי]" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, צח),
And concerning this King David, peace be upon him, pleaded: "You through Your commandments have made me wiser than my enemies, [for they are ever with me]" (Psalms 119:98),
כִּי לַעֲמוֹד עַל חָכְמַת הַמִּצְווֹת אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי הַתַּחְבּוּלוֹת אֵיךְ לְהִנָּצֵל מִיֵּצֶר מַחְשְׁבוֹת לִבּוֹ.
for to grasp the inner wisdom of the commandments is possible only through stratagems of how to be saved from the inclination of the thoughts of one's heart.
שֶׁהַתַּרְיַ"ג מִצְווֹת הֵם תַּרְיַ"ג עֵיטִין לָזֶה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, פב עַמּוּד ב), וְלָכֵן אָמַר לְמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת: יֵצֶר הָרָע יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיכֶם וְכוּלֵי (שַׁבָּת פט.),
For the 613 commandments are 613 spiritual counsels for this (Zohar II:82b), which is why Moses said to the ministering angels: "Is there an evil inclination among you, etc.?" (Shabbat 89a),
וְרַק עַל יְדֵי הַיֵּצֶר הַמִּתְגַּבֵּר, אָז סוֹמֵךְ עַל חָכְמַת וְעֵצוֹת הַמִּצְווֹת אֵיךְ הֵם מַצִּילוֹת אוֹתוֹ מִזֶּה.
and only through the surging inclination does one lean upon the wisdom and counsels of the commandments to see how they rescue him from it.

וְכֹהֲנִים רִבָּה בָּהֶן הַכָּתוּב מִצְווֹת יְתֵירוֹת, לְפִי שֶׁנִּבְדַּל אַהֲרֹן לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים, לְעֻמָּתוֹ גַּם כֵּן הַיֵּצֶר מוּבְדָּל מִיֵּצֶר מַחְשְׁבוֹת אֲחֵרִים, וְצָרִיךְ עֵצוֹת יְתֵירוֹת לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִמֶּנּוּ.

And for priests Scripture multiplied additional commandments, because Aaron was set apart to sanctify him as holy of holies; corresponding to him his inclination is distinct from the thoughts of others, requiring additional counsels to be guarded from it.

וּמִצְווֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ הֵם לְהִנָּצֵל מִיֵּצֶר הַכְּלָלִי דִּכְלָלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלָכֵן צָרִיךְ הַסֵּפֶר תּוֹרָה עַל לִבּוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין כא: וְעַיֵּין כֶּסֶף מִשְׁנֶה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג מֵהִלְכוֹת מְלָכִים),

And the commandments of the king are designed to deliver him from the collective inclination of all Israel, which is why he requires the Torah scroll upon his heart (Sanhedrin 21b; Kesef Mishneh, Hilkhot Melakhim 3:1),
פֵּירוּשׁ עַל דֶּרֶךְ תְּפִלִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת, שֶׁהַנָּחַת אוֹתוֹ כְּתָב מוֹעִיל לְהַכְנִיס בְּבֵיתוֹ וּבְחַדְרֵי מוֹחוֹ וּלְבָבוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת אוֹתָם דְּבָרִים הַכְּתוּבִים.
meaning in the manner of tefillin and mezuzot, where placing that holy script avails to instill within his house and the chambers of his mind and heart those very inscribed truths.

וּמִזֶּה הֵם סְגֻלּוֹת הַקְּמֵיעוֹת שֶׁכּוֹתְבִים אוֹתָם פְּסוּקִים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם רְפוּאַת וִישׁוּעַת אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לוֹ, וְנוֹשְׂאָהּ עָלָיו, וּמוֹעִיל לְהַכְנִיסָהּ בֶּאֱמֶת בְּקִרְבּוֹ

And from this principle derive the virtues of amulets, wherein they write verses speaking of the healing and salvation of that needed matter, which one wears, availing to instill that reality within him
[וְעַיֵּין לְעֵיל אוֹת צ"ח, וְשָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי כָּל פְּעֻלָּתָן עִנְיָנָם עַל דֶּרֶךְ קְצִיבַת הָעֵץ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רי"ב;
[and see above Section 98, and I heard that their entire efficacy reflects the casting of the wood in Section 212;
וּמַה שֶּׁמְּשַׁנִּים סֵדֶר צֵירוּף הָאוֹתִיּוֹת, בַּפָּשׁוּט הַטַּעַם מִשּׁוּם דְּאָסוּר לְהִתְרַפּאוֹת בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְגַם כְּדֵי לְהַעֲלִים כִּי דֶּרֶךְ הַנֵּס לָבוֹא בַּחֲשַׁאי],
and that they permute letter combinations is simply because it is forbidden to heal oneself directly with words of Torah, and also to conceal it, since miracles operate quietly],
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (יז.): הַנָּחַת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה – לוֹמַר: קִיֵּים זֶה וְכוּלֵי;
and along these lines they said in Bava Kamma 17a: placing a Torah scroll upon his bier means proclaiming: this one fulfilled, etc.;
וּבַחַיִּים מוֹעִיל לְהַכְנִיס בֶּאֱמֶת בַּלֵּב קִיּוּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בָּזֶה, וְהַיְינוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ שֶׁהוּא תַּבְלִין לִכְלָלוּת הַיֵּצֶר כֻּלּוֹ שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
and in life it avails to instill within the heart the fulfillment of all written therein, namely the entire Torah which serves as the seasoning against the collective inclination of the whole world.
וְסִיֵּים: "כִּי לְעוֹלָם הִיא לִי", לְפִי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (כא. לְרַב יוֹסֵף) דְּרַק בְּעִידָּנָא דְּעָסֵיק בְּמִצְוָה מַצְּלָא;
And he concluded: "for they are ever with me," because in Sotah 21a Rav Yosef states that only while actively engaged in a mitzvah does it protect;
רַק כְּשֶׁעוֹמֵד עַל הַחָכְמָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּמִּצְוָה, אָז נַעֲשָׂה מִן הַמִּצְוָה גַּם כֵּן תּוֹרָה, כִּי עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה עַל מְנָת לַעֲשׂוֹת הַיְינוּ הַלִּמּוּד לְהָבִין חָכְמַת הַמִּצְווֹת,
but when one grasps the wisdom within the mitzvah, the mitzvah itself becomes Torah, for the essence of learning in order to practice is understanding the wisdom of the mitzvot,
וּכְשֶׁמּוֹצִיא לַפּוֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה אָז הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַתּוֹרָה וְנִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב גַּם בְּעִידָּנָא דְּלָא עָסֵיק.
and when actualized in deed it attains the perfection of Torah, engraved in the heart even when not actively engaged.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁ"תְּחַכְּמֵנִי" – לָדַעַת כִּי לְעוֹלָם הִיא לִי, וְלֹא רַק בְּעִידָּנָא דְּעָסֵיק:

paragraphs.text: Understanding makes a mitzvah a lasting Torah acquisition

paragraphs.text: The enacted mitzvah can become inward Torah through attention to its details and meaning.

rich.text: The enacted mitzvah can become inward Torah through attention to its details and meaning.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 3:4: “When he is not engaged in it, the body's share in the mitzvah's holiness does not remain, because the body does not understand its root. But with a mitzvah related to a person—especially when he increases his care for its details and his understanding—Hashem illuminates for him an understanding of the mitzvah in Torah's light. The mitzvah's very substance becomes Torah for him; he understands its intention and sees that the garment and action of the mitzvah belong to this world. This is our prayer, ‘May He open our heart in His Torah’: it alludes to the Torah teachings and mitzvot particularly related to each person's essential root.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov develops the same distinction from Sotah with which this siman concludes. The person does not only perform a momentary act; attention to its particulars and meaning allows its Torah light to be grasped within him. This explains why the siman connects wisdom in the mitzvah with something that remains his beyond the moment of performance. The particular root described by Beit Yaakov deepens general observance rather than exempting the person from other mitzvot.
