sections.en: Words of Torah That Pass Through the Heart—meaning That the Heart Feels and Is…

p: [רכה] דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁעוֹבְרִים דֶּרֶךְ הַלֵּב – פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהַלֵּב מַרְגִּישׁ וּמִתְפַּעֵל בָּהֶם – הוּא נִקְרָא "עֵץ חַיִּים" וְסַמָּא דְּחַיֵּי.
Words of Torah that pass through the heart—meaning that the heart feels and is deeply moved by them—are termed a "tree of life" and an elixir of life.

כִּי הַלֵּב מְקוֹר הַחַיּוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כג), וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא מִתְפַּעֵל, הֲרֵי שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתוֹ מִתְפַּעֵל עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמוֹלִידָה חַיּוּת בָּאָדָם.

For the heart is the fountainhead of vitality, as it is written: "for out of it are the issues of life" (Proverbs 4:23), and when it is stirred, the very root of his vitality is moved by words of Torah, generating true life within man.

וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאַת חֶטְאוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ, כִּי הַיִּרְאָה בַּלֵּב כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן", וְיִרְאָה נוּקְבָא וְתוֹרַת אֱמֶת דְּכַר לְהַשְׁלִים וּלְשַׂמֵּחַ הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פִּקּוּדֵי [ה' יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב]" (תְּהִלִּים יט, ט), אַחַר הַיִּרְאָה הַמּוֹלֶדֶת לֵב נִשְׁבָּר וְעַצְבוּת.

And this is achieved through his fear of sin preceding his wisdom, for awe resides in the heart (Yoma 72b on "and he has no heart"), awe being the feminine vessel and the Torah of truth the male light that completes and gladdens the heart—"The statutes [of Hashem are right, rejoicing the heart]" (Psalms 19:9)—following the awe that engenders a broken heart and solemn gravity.

וְאָז הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִבְלָע בַּלֵּב וּמִתְקַיֶּימֶת, כִּי בַּלֵּב מְקוֹם רְתִיחַת הַדָּם, וְעַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק וְכִיסּוּפִין לִמְתִיקוּת הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְגַּבֵּר כֹּחַ הָאֵשׁ שֶׁבּוֹ, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית ד.): אוֹרַיְיתָא דְּקָא מְרַתְּחָא לֵיהּ.

And then words of Torah are absorbed into the heart and endure, for the heart is the furnace of the boiling blood, and through the intensity of desire and yearning for the sweetness of Torah the fiery force within it surges, in line with Ta'anit 4a: it is the Torah that boils within him.
וְיָדוּעַ כֹּחַ הַבִּישׁוּל לְהַבְלִיעַ, וְהַבָּלוּעַ אֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא עוֹד.
And known is the power of heat to absorb, and that which is absorbed does not leave.

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּצוֹנֵן וּקְרִירוּת, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר דֶּרֶךְ הַלֵּב, שֶׁהֲגַם שֶׁמֵּבִין חָכְמָה בְּמוֹחוֹ וּמַשִּׂיג עִנְיְנֵי אֱלֹהוּת וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אֵין הַלֵּב מִתְפַּעֵל עַל יְדֵי זֶה כְּלָל, כִּי הוּא כְּלוֹמֵד חָכְמָה חִיצוֹנִית שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לָזֶה, לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא קָדַם יִרְאַת חֵטְא שֶׁיִּתְבּוֹנֵן עַל חֶסְרוֹנוֹ וְצֹרֶךְ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְהַשְׁלִימוֹ – אָז אֵין חָכְמָתוֹ מִתְקַיֶּימֶת,

Not so in coldness and detachment, where study does not pass through the heart: even though he grasps wisdom in his brain and perceives concepts of Godliness and Torah, the heart remains wholly unmoved, as though learning an external science with which he has no personal stake, because fear of sin did not precede to make him reflect on his deficiency and his need for Torah to heal him—and then his wisdom does not endure,

כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּדוֹאֵג בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קו:) דְּשָׁכַח הַכֹּל, מִשּׁוּם דְּרַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִרְגָּשׁ בַּלֵּב, זֶהוּ הָעִיקָּר, שֶׁאָז יֵשׁ בּוֹ חַיּוּת וְהוּא נִבְלָע בּוֹ.

as stated of Doeg in Sanhedrin 106b who forgot everything, because the Merciful One desires the heart, that Torah be felt within the heart, which is essential, for then it possesses vitality and is absorbed within him.

וּבְלָאו הָכִי אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.): מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ, הַיְינוּ כִּי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב:), כִּי בְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם הַיֵּצֶר מִתְגַּבֵּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.), וְגַם זֶה נִקְרָא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, וּכְמוֹ דוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתֹפֶל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם.

And otherwise they said in Shabbat 31a: "Better had you not brought it up," for Heaven forbid it can become a potion of death (Yoma 72b), seeing that in a Torah scholar the inclination surges (Sukkah 52a), and even such an intellectual is called a scholar, like Doeg and Ahithophel who are called scholars throughout Chazal.

וּכְשֶׁאֵין לוֹ יִרְאַת חֵטְא לְהַגְבִּיר עַל הַיֵּצֶר, אָז יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כְּעִנְיַן אַחֵר שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה טו:): סִפְרֵי טוֹעִין וְכוּלֵי וְזֶמֶר יְוָנִי וְכוּלֵי, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁכָּל חָכְמָתוֹ הָיָה דּוּגְמַת לִמּוּד חָכְמָה חִיצוֹנִית בְּתוֹרַת חָכְמָה לְבַד, וְלֹא לְהַשְׁלָמַת הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר שֵׁם תּוֹרָה.

And when he lacks fear of sin to overcome the inclination, he can become like Acher of whom our Sages stated (Chagigah 15b): heretical books fell from his lap and Greek song did not cease from his mouth, meaning all his wisdom was studied like an external discipline for intellectual amusement alone, and not to heal deficiency which is the core meaning of Torah.
וּמִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא הָיָה נָקִי אַגַּב אִמֵּיהּ, כִּידוּעַ דְּאַבָּא וְאִמָּא הֵם מוֹחַ וְלֵב, וְהוּא חָכְמַת מוֹחוֹ מְרוּבָּה רַק דְּלֵב אָיִן, דְּהַיְינוּ אִמָּא.
And this was because he was tainted through his mother (ibid.), for as is known, Abba and Imma are brain and heart, and his cerebral wisdom was vast while he lacked heart, which is Imma.

וְכֵן בִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ מִסְּתָמָא זוֹכִין זֶה כָּל אֶחָד מֵאָב וָאֵם הַגַּשְׁמִיִּים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵדֻיּוֹת סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב מִשְׁנָה ט): הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ בְּחָכְמָה, וְאָב מַזְרִיעַ לוֹבֶן שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ מוֹחַ, וְאִשָּׁה אֹדֶם שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ בָּשָׂר וָדָם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ נִדָּה לא. לְגִרְסַת שְׁאֵלְתּוֹת), וְהַלֵּב בִּכְלָל.

And literally one derives these traits from his physical parents, as in Eduyot 2:9: a father endows his son with wisdom, the father contributing white whence the brain is formed, and the mother red whence flesh and blood derive (Niddah 31a; She'iltot), the heart being included therein.
וּמִזֶּה בָּא טֻמְאַת זִיבָה, כִּי תּוֹרָה נִמְשְׁלָה לְאִשָּׁה בִּיבָמוֹת (סג:), וְהַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא הָאִישׁ הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ בָּהּ.
And from this blemish arises the defilement of zivah (abnormal discharge), for the Torah is compared to a woman in Yevamot 63b, and the scholar is the man channeling influx into her.
וְקֶרִי יוֹצֵא מֵאֵבֶר חַי וְזִיבָה מֵאֵבֶר מֵת, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְפַּעֲלוּת הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב כְּלָל כַּנּוֹדָע.
Seminal emission issues from a living organ while zivah issues from a lifeless, limp organ, meaning without any emotional stirring of desire in the heart at all, as is known.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מח:): זָב – מֵרְחַבְעָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "הִתְאַמֵּץ לַעֲלוֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה" (מְלָכִים א יב, יח).
And this is what our Sages expounded (Sanhedrin 48b): one afflicted with zivah issued from Rehoboam, of whom it is said: "made speed to get him up to his chariot" (I Kings 12:18).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף" (שְׁמוֹת יג, יט), שֶׁהָעַצְמוּת שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הוּא: יִרְאַת חֶטְאוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ.
And as I heard regarding "And Moses took the bones (atzmot) of Joseph," that the essence (atzmut) of Joseph is: his fear of sin precedes his wisdom.
וְזֶה צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח בְּעֵת שֶׁרוֹאֶה שִׁינּוּי בְּהִתְנַהֲגוּת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵבִין, כְּהָךְ דְּ"וְלֹא נָחָם אֱלֹהִים דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ [פְּלִשְׁתִּים]" (שָׁם, יז).
And this one must seize when beholding an anomalous shift in divine direction that one cannot comprehend, as in "God led them not through the way of the land of [the Philistines]."
וּלְכָךְ יָרָבְעָם מָרַד בִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁטָּעַן עָלָיו שֶׁחָכְמָתוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְיִרְאַת חֶטְאוֹ, וְהוּא מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף.
Therefore Jeroboam rebelled against King Solomon, alleging that Solomon's wisdom preceded his fear of sin, Jeroboam descending from the seed of Joseph.

וְלָכֵן כְּשֶׁנִּצַּח לִמְלוֹךְ וְלִמְרוֹד בִּרְחַבְעָם, נֶאֱמַר בִּרְחַבְעָם: "הִתְאַמֵּץ וְגוֹמֵר", וְנַעֲשָׂה זָב, שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁהַדִּין עִמּוֹ וְשֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ עָלָיו טַעֲנָה לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא כֵן.
And therefore when he triumphed to reign and rebel against Rehoboam, it was said of Rehoboam: "made speed to mount his chariot," becoming a zav, confirming that the claim against him had substance.
וְטָהֳרַת הַזָּב הוּא בְּמַיִם חַיִּים, פֵּירוּשׁ עַל יְדֵי חֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב בְּחַיּוּת גָּמוּר לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
And the purification of a zav requires living waters (Leviticus 15:13), meaning through an ardent yearning in the heart filled with total vitality for words of Torah.

כִּי "הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יט), וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר כָּל כָּךְ לָבוֹא לְמַדְרֵגַת הַיִּרְאָה כְּמוֹ לְאַהֲבָה וְחֵשֶׁק עָצוּם לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה בַּלֵּב, גַּם זֶה מְזַכֵּךְ הַחָכְמָה לִהְיוֹת נִבְלָע בַּלֵּב וְלִהְיוֹת עֵץ חַיִּים, עַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב בְּחַיּוּת גָּמוּר, הַיְינוּ בִּדְבֵיקוּת בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ שֶׁנִּקְרָא חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹר הַחַיּוּת:

For "wisdom strengthens the wise" (Ecclesiastes 7:19), and while it is exceedingly difficult to attain the rung of fear, an intense love and burning desire for Torah in the heart likewise refines wisdom to be absorbed within the heart and become a tree of life, through the force of genuine emotional vitality, cleaving unto the Source of Life, blessed be His Name, Who is called the Life of the Worlds, the wellspring of all vitality.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 16:2: “Of this it says, “Those who hope for His kindness”: the repair comes through Oral Torah, which is “the Torah of kindness upon her tongue.” We have already said that specifically concerning Oral Torah they taught that it endures only in one whose mind is humble. Oral Torah is compared to liquids—the “wine of Oral Torah,” as explained in the fourteenth discourse—and it endures only in one whose mind is humble and whose heart is broken within him.”

rich.text: : “Of this it says, “Those who hope for His kindness”: the repair comes through Oral Torah, which is “the Torah of kindness upon her tongue.” We have already said that specifically concerning Oral Torah they taught that it endures only in one whose mind is humble. Oral Torah is compared to liquids—the “wine of Oral Torah,” as explained in the fourteenth discourse—and it endures only in one whose mind is humble and whose heart is broken within him.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah applies the image of liquid to Oral Torah and makes humility the condition for its endurance. This clarifies the present siman’s contrast between understanding an idea intellectually and having Torah pass through the heart. The broken heart is a receptive vessel, not the goal in isolation: it permits the Torah received there to become life, healing, and joy. That is why awe before wisdom can lead to a deeper and more lasting love of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Context: The Talmud explains “no heart” as the absence of fear of Heaven. This is the precise basis for Rav Tzadok’s statement that fear is in the heart and must precede wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Yosef's bones signify awe that anchors observance while the newly received good still needs clarification.

rich.text: Yosef's bones signify awe that anchors observance while the newly received good still needs clarification.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The Seventh Night of Pesach 24:1: “‘Moshe took Yosef's bones with him.’ My holy grandfather explained: When Moshe saw that Pharaoh accompanied Israel, he understood that they still had a connection to Egypt. The counsel was therefore to hold to the straightforward mitzvot. Yosef's bones allude to this counsel: his fear of sin preceded his wisdom. After Israel emptied Egypt and took all the good found there, their desire for those good things still required clarification through their service. As long as that clarification was unfinished, they still had a connection to Egypt.”

rich.text: Sod Yesharim, The Seventh Night of Pesach 24:1

: “‘Moshe took Yosef's bones with him.’ My holy grandfather explained: When Moshe saw that Pharaoh accompanied Israel, he understood that they still had a connection to Egypt. The counsel was therefore to hold to the straightforward mitzvot. Yosef's bones allude to this counsel: his fear of sin preceded his wisdom. After Israel emptied Egypt and took all the good found there, their desire for those good things still required clarification through their service. As long as that clarification was unfinished, they still had a connection to Egypt.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim expands the very received teaching cited here. Moshe recognizes an unresolved connection to Egypt and takes Yosef's bones as an image of holding to straightforward mitzvah observance before every reason has become clear. This explains why awe preceding wisdom is needed precisely when the route seems puzzling: the heart's attachment to the command keeps newly gained understanding from becoming detached knowledge.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 1: “It is taught in Avot, chapter 3, mishnah 11: Anyone whose fear of sin precedes his wisdom, his wisdom endures. The meaning is that sometimes God conceals His acts and hides His intention from human beings, and a person does not know God’s will in the matter. This was the situation here: Moses wondered why God had not led them by the way of the land of the Philistines. The counsel for this is that when a person sees God dealing with him in concealment, he should not multiply clever explanations, but engage in the plain practice of the commandments and include himself in the attributes of fear. This is “Moses took the bones of Joseph,” and so forth. For the way of a righteous person is to attribute the deficiency to himself when a doubtful matter comes before him. This is the significance of his taking Joseph’s bones: because he attributed the deficiency to himself, he began to enter the attribute of fear, which Joseph’s bones signify. Joseph the righteous had the attribute of fear, as explained concerning the verse, “Lest He burst forth like fire in the house of Joseph.” This is “Anyone whose fear of sin precedes his wisdom,” and it is the attribute of Joseph the righteous, of blessed memory.”

sections.en: Anyone Can Attain Intellectual Wisdom and Words of Torah Even If He Lacks Prior…

p: [רכו] כָּל אֶחָד יָכוֹל לְהַשִּׂיג חָכְמָה וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יִרְאַת חֵטְא הַקּוֹדֶמֶת וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר לְלִמּוּד וְהַשָּׂגַת הַתּוֹרָה בִּשְׁבִיל כְּבוֹד שְׁמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמַכִּיר שֶׁהוּא תּוֹרַת ה'.

Anyone can attain intellectual wisdom and words of Torah even if he lacks prior fear of sin and an awakening from below (itaruta de-letata) where one stirs himself to study for the glory of His blessed Name, recognizing it as Hashem's Torah.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוּכָן לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ תָּמִיד דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אַף בְּלֹא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְזֶהוּ "הַמְחַדֵּשׁ בְּטוּבוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית".

Nonetheless, the Blessed Name is constantly poised to bestow words of Torah even without an awakening from below, which is the meaning of "Who in His goodness renews each day continuously the work of Creation."

כְּמוֹ מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית שֶׁהָיָה בְּלֹא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא שֶׁהֲרֵי עֲדַיִן לֹא נִבְרָא אָדָם, כָּךְ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּטוּבוֹ לְבַד בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים מִקּוֹדֶם.
Just as the initial Work of Creation occurred without any awakening from below—since man was not yet created—so each day He renews it purely in His unprompted goodness without prior lower striving.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא בִּרְכַּת "יוֹצֵר אוֹר", לְהַשִּׂיג הַחִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד, וְזֶה נִקְרָא חָכְמַת מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
And for this the blessing Yotzer Ohr was instituted, to grasp the insights renewed each day, termed the wisdom of the Work of Creation.

אֲבָל מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלֶּה לְמִי שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר לוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז: הָאָבוֹת הֵן הֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה; כִּי מֶרְכֶּבֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַשָּׂם עָבִים רְכוּבוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קד, ג), "ה' רֹכֵב עַל עָב קַל" (יְשַׁעְיָה יט, א).

But the Work of the Chariot (Ma'aseh Merkavah) is what the Blessed Name reveals to one who actively awakens toward Him, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah 47: the Patriarchs are themselves the Chariot; for Hashem's riding upon lower beings occurs through their spiritual exertion: "Who makes the clouds His chariot" (Psalms 104:3), "Hashem rides upon a swift cloud" (Isaiah 19:1).

וְיָדוּעַ דְּהֶעָבִים הוּא אֵד הָעוֹלֶה מִן הָאָרֶץ לְקַבֵּל שֶׁפַע הַגְּשָׁמִים לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לָאָרֶץ, וְזֶהוּ הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא שֶׁל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים לְקַבֵּל שִׁפְעוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַל זֶה הוּא רְכוּבוֹ.

And it is known that clouds are the vapor rising from the earth to receive rain to water the land, which represents the awakening from below of mortals to receive His blessed influx—upon which He rides.
כִּי הַמֶּרְכָּבָה הוּא לְדֶרֶךְ וּלְהֲלִיכָה מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם.
For a chariot serves for travel and moving from place to place.

וּלְכָךְ יְחֶזְקֵאל בְּעֵת הַחוּרְבָּן רָאָה מֶרְכָּבָה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יְשַׁעְיָה רָאָה יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסְאוֹ בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, כִּי אָז שִׁפְעוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא.
Therefore Ezekiel at the destruction saw a moving Chariot, whereas Isaiah saw Him seated upon His Throne while the Temple stood, for then His influx was permanently anchored.

אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בְּמַדְרֵגַת "וָאֶהְיֶה מִתְהַלֵּךְ מֵאֹהֶל אֶל אֹהֶל" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א יז, ה), כְּמוֹ בַּחוּרְבָּן שֶׁנִּיטְּלָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד, וּקְבִיעוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִטַּלְטֵל מֵאֹהֶל אֶל אֹהֶל, כָּל אֶחָד בְּדוֹרוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עַד מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד גַּם כֵּן בְּשׁוֹפְטִים מִפַּרְנָס לְפַרְנָס וְאֵינוֹ בִּקְבִיעוּת – רְכוּבוֹ הוּא עַל הֶעָבִים: מִי שֶׁמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל וּמֵכִין עַצְמוֹ לְכָךְ, עָלָיו הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹכֵב וּמִתְהַלֵּךְ.

But when in the state of "I went from tent to tent" (I Chronicles 17:5)—as in the exile when Davidic kingship ceased and Hashem's presence moved from tent to tent in each generation, as under the Judges from leader to leader without fixed permanence—His riding is upon the clouds: upon whoever toils and prepares himself, the Blessed Name rides and journeys.

וְעַל זֶה הוּא בְּרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁלִּפְנֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, לְהַשִּׂיג הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה דְּחָכְמַת מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה, שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹפֵעַ לָנוּ בְּיִחוּד: "אֲשֶׁר בְּשֵׁם וְגוֹמֵר בָּטַחְנוּ, נָגִילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ", שֶׁאָנוּ מְחַכִּים וּמְצַפִּים לְךָ וּבְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא שֶׁלָּנוּ.

And for this the second blessing before Shema (Ahavah Rabbah) was instituted, to attain the Torah of the Work of the Chariot, which is what Hashem channels to us uniquely: "for we have trusted in Your holy Name; we will rejoice and be glad in Your salvation," waiting and yearning for You through our lower awakening.
וּ"בַעֲבוּר אֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְכוּלֵי" – שֶׁהֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא שֶׁלָּהֶם, תְּגַלֶּה בְּלִבֵּנוּ בִּינָה לְהָבִין וְכוּלֵי.
And "for the sake of our fathers, etc."—who are the Chariot through their awakening from below—reveal within our heart understanding to comprehend, etc.
וְיֵשׁ שָׁם שְׁמוֹנָה דְּבָרִים, וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּנֶגְדָּם רוֹמְזִים שְׁמוֹנָה בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְפוֹרָשִׁים בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
And there are eight verbs in that prayer, and I heard that corresponding to them are the eight garments of the High Priest, explained elsewhere.
וְהַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל הוּא הָעוֹבֵד וִיסוֹד הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא אַהֲרֹן "שׁוֹשְׁבִינָא דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, כ עַמּוּד א).
And the High Priest is the servant embodying the foundation of awakening from below, which is why Aaron is titled "the groomsman of the Matronita" (Zohar III:20a).

וְהַשְּׁמוֹנָה בְּגָדִים הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, שֶׁהוּא בִּקְבִיעוּת הַמָּקוֹם, דְּאָז יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא וְלֹא בְּמֶרְכָּבָה, רַק עַל יְדֵי הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא הַחַיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים נוֹשְׂאִים וְסוֹבְלִים הַכִּסֵּא כָּבוֹד, וְאָז הוּא עִיקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה בִּשְׁמוֹנָה מַדְרֵגוֹת דִּלְהָבִין וְכוּלֵי.

And the eight garments pertain to entering the Holy of Holies, the fixed place, where He sits upon a Throne and not a moving Chariot, the living creatures below bearing the Throne through the lower awakening, which is the core attainment in the eight rungs of "to understand, etc."
וְאָז נֶאֱמַר: "וַיֵּשֶׁב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא ה'" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, כג), שֶׁהָיָה דּוּגְמַת אָדָם הַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכִּסֵּא כִּבְיָכוֹל.
And then it was said: "And Solomon sat on the throne of Hashem" (I Chronicles 29:23), mirroring the likeness of a man sitting upon the Throne, as it were.
כִּי עֲבוֹדַת הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל הָיָה פּוֹעֵל שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ עֲבוֹדָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְהוּא מַדְרֵגַת הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁקּוֹדֵם לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל.
For the service of the High Priest effected a state requiring no further labor or lower awakening, which is the level of the king preceding the High Priest.
וְשַׁפִּיר מִצַּד קְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם הָיָה מִדַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁחָכְמָתוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְיִרְאָתוֹ.
And fittingly from the sanctity of the place, Solomon's trait was that his wisdom preceded his fear.
רַק יָרָבְעָם חָלַק גַּם אַקְּדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם, וְאָז רְחַבְעָם נָס בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה.
But Jeroboam contested the sanctity of the place, and then Rehoboam fled in his chariot.

וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מח:) דָּרְשׁוּ תֵּיבַת "מֶרְכָּבָה" אַזָּב, שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ "מֶרְכָּב" (וַיִּקְרָא טו, ט), [וְשֶׁמִּפְּנֵי חוּלְשָׁתוֹ אֵין יוֹשֵׁב אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ מֶרְכָּב].
And our Sages (Sanhedrin 48b) expounded the word "chariot" (merkavah) upon a zav, concerning whom it is written "saddle" (merkav), [who out of weakness cannot ride except on a saddle].

וְאִם כֵּן גַּם מֶרְכָּבָה דִּיחֶזְקֵאל וַדַּאי כִּבְיָכוֹל כֵּן, שֶׁהוּא שִׁפְעוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁאֵינוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הַלֵּב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בּוֹ חַיּוּת גָּמוּר, שֶׁהֲרֵי מֵחוּרְבָּן עִיקַּר הַשֶּׁפַע יוֹרֵד חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לַחִיצוֹנִים.

And if so, Ezekiel's Chariot was likewise so, reflecting divine influx not flowing directly through the heart with full vitality, since from the destruction onward the primary influx descended toward the external forces.
וְהַלֵּב הֵם יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהֵם קוֹלְטִים הַתַּמְצִית כַּנּוֹדָע.
And the heart is Israel, who absorb the holy essence.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (פב עַמּוּד א) שֶׁהוּא כְּמַאן דַּחֲמָא בָּתַר כּוֹתְלָא.
And this is what they said in Zohar Yitro 82a: that Ezekiel was like one looking from behind a wall.
כִּי "מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה" נִקְרָא מַה שֶּׁאֵין בּוֹ חַיּוּת גָּמוּר, רַק שֶׁמִּתּוֹכוֹ מֵבִין אִישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי הַקּוֹלְטוֹ בְּלִבּוֹ.
For the Work of the Chariot denotes that which lacks direct vitality, yet from within it the discerning Jew absorbs it into his heart.
וְנֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "מַרְאוֹת" (יְחֶזְקֵאל א, א), מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּישַׁעְיָה: "וָאֶרְאֶה וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, א).
And in Ezekiel it says "visions" (mar'ot), whereas in Isaiah it says "I saw the Lord" (va'er'eh).
וְגַם זֶה הָיָה בְּעֵת הַמַּסָּעוֹת כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה יג:),
And this occurred during the journeys of the Shechinah (Chagigah 13b),

וְרַק בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קָיְימָא סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא, פֵּירוּשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ לִלְבָנָה, וְהוּא הִשִּׂיג הַשֶּׁפַע הַבָּא עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁלֵימוּת גָּמוּר.
and only in the days of King Solomon did the moon stand in its full fullness—Israel being compared to the moon—and he attained the influx arriving through lower awakening in absolute perfection.

וְעַל זֶה חִבֵּר שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא מֵאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְהַשֶּׁפַע דִּלְעֵילָא, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יָדַיִם סוֹף פֶּרֶק ג) שֶׁהוּא קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים וְלֹא הָיָה כָּל הָעוֹלָם כְּדַאי וְכוּלֵי:

And concerning this he composed the Song of Songs, which is filled with lower awakening and supernal influx, of which our Sages stated (Yadayim 3:5) that it is the Holy of Holies, and the entire world was not worthy of the day it was given.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:65:1: “and see in Shemot Rabbah 15 and Tanchuma, Chayei Sarah 3 on the verse: “Who makes the clouds His chariot”: a king of flesh and blood rides a horse adorned with silver and gold, but the Holy One rides upon clouds. Silver and gold mean love and awe as is known, which are the primary foundation stones and the chariot for royal Rabbis, servants of Hashem, mortal kings; yet Hashem looks not upon these, but upon the ultimate culmination—the rung of Jacob, the choicest of Patriarchs, and as I wrote elsewhere, that light and darkness correspond to Abraham and Isaac, and the pillar of cloud to Jacob, and this is not the place to elaborate.”

Silver and gold mean love and awe as is known, which are the primary foundation stones and the chariot for royal Rabbis, servants of Hashem, mortal kings; yet Hashem looks not upon these, but upon the ultimate culmination—the rung of Jacob, the choicest of Patriarchs, and as I wrote elsewhere, that light and darkness correspond to Abraham and Isaac, and the pillar of cloud to Jacob, and this is not the place to elaborate.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah contrasts a king’s silver and gold adornment with Hashem’s chariot of clouds, relating the former to love and fear and the latter to Yaakov’s completed truth. This develops the cloud image used here: the decisive issue is not spiritual display or a forceful isolated middah, but the person’s capacity to become a truthful vehicle for the divine presence.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Pekudei 2: “Then the escort of the bride is needed: he must see that the person does not nullify himself completely, but remains alive in this world. Once a person sees that his service has a place with Hashem and that Hashem desires it, he must remain alive so that he can serve Hashem further. A complete nullification in which no life remains in this world is not Hashem's will.”

rich.text: : “Then the escort of the bride is needed: he must see that the person does not nullify himself completely, but remains alive in this world. paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the same description of Aharon as the escort of the bride: he safeguards the recipient's living capacity for continued service, alongside Moshe's disclosure of divine nearness. This gives substance to the siman's image of an awakening from below that carries divine presence. The eightfold correspondence here is conceptual: the actual Yom Kippur entry into the Holy of Holies is in four linen garments, specified in Leviticus 16:4, rather than the eight garments of the ordinary high-priestly service.

paragraphs.text: The symbolic eightfold account must be distinguished from the garments used for inward Yom Kippur service.

rich.text: The symbolic eightfold account must be distinguished from the garments used for inward Yom Kippur service.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 3:1: “This is also why the High Priest's service throughout the year was in golden garments: through his service he illuminated all the garments with the light of Hashem's will. But on Yom Kippur, when he enters the innermost place and Hashem reveals the light of His will explicitly without a garment, the High Priest does not stand before Hashem in such garments and expansion, but in linen garments, indicating that he then surrenders even the receiving vessel to Hashem. Thus the Sifrei says that bad, linen, is stated four times on Yom Kippur: one excludes the breastplate, one the ephod, one the robe, and one the forehead plate.”

rich.text: : “This is also why the High Priest's service throughout the year was in golden garments: through his service he illuminated all the garments with the light of Hashem's will. But on Yom Kippur, when he enters the innermost place and Hashem reveals the light of His will explicitly without a garment, the High Priest does not stand before Hashem in such garments and expansion, but in linen garments, indicating that he then surrenders even the receiving vessel to Hashem. Thus the Sifrei says that bad, linen, is stated four times on Yom Kippur: one excludes the breastplate, one the ephod, one the robe, and one the forehead plate.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim expressly distinguishes golden garments from linen at the inward Yom Kippur entry and lists the four additional garments excluded there. The siman's reference to eight garments belongs to its symbolic account of eight modes of understanding; it must not be read as a literal description of wearing all eight in the Holy of Holies. This distinction is also relevant to the later garment discussion in Siman 263.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And concerning this he composed the Song of Songs, which is filled with lower awakening and supernal influx, of which our Sages stated (Yadayim 3:5) that it is the Holy of Holies, and the entire world was not worthy of the day it was given.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Yadayim 3:5: ‘A book that has been erased but retains eighty-five letters, corresponding to the passage ‘When the Ark traveled,’ imparts impurity to the hands. A scroll with eighty-five letters written in it, corresponding to the passage ‘When the Ark traveled,’ imparts impurity to the hands. All the sacred Scriptures impart impurity to the hands. Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes impart impurity to the hands. Rabbi Yehuda says: Song of Songs imparts impurity to the hands, but Ecclesiastes is disputed. Rabbi Yosei says: Ecclesiastes does not impart impurity to the hands, but Song of Songs is disputed. Rabbi Shimon says: Ecclesiastes is among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said: I received a tradition from seventy-two elders, on the day they seated Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya in the academy, that Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes impart impurity to the hands. Rabbi Akiva said: Heaven forbid! No one in Israel disputed that Song of Songs imparts impurity to the hands, for the whole world is not worth as much as the day on which Song of Songs was given to Israel. All the Writings are holy, but Song of Songs is the holy of holies. If they disputed anything, they disputed only Ecclesiastes. Rabbi Yochanan ben Yehoshua, the son of Rabbi Akiva’s father-in-law, said: As Ben Azzai stated, so they disputed and so they decided.’

sections.en: All Israel Possess Complete Faith in the Blessed Name

p: [רכז] כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם אֱמוּנָה שְׁלֵימָה בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, בִּמְצִיאוּתוֹ וְאַחְדוּתוֹ וְהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (צז.) שֶׁהֵם מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים.
All Israel possess complete faith in the Blessed Name, in His existence, His unity, and His providence, as stated in Shabbat 97a: they are believers, children of believers.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "נֶפֶשׁ" דִּקְדוּשַׁת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
And this is termed the Nefesh of the sanctity of the children of Israel.

וְזָכָה יַתִּיר, יְהִיבִין לֵיהּ "רוּחַ" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, צד עַמּוּד ב), הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּזְדַּכֵּךְ הַלֵּב יוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ זֶה בַּלֵּב, וּבָא מִמַּדְרֵגַת אֱמוּנָה לְמַדְרֵגַת אֱמֶת, שֶׁהוּא הַדָּבָר הַבָּרוּר וְנִיכָּר לַלֵּב וְלֹא בֶּאֱמוּנָה לְבַד.

If he merits further, they grant him Ruach (Zohar II:94b), which occurs when the heart is refined until he feels this within his heart, advancing from the level of Faith (Emunah) to the level of Truth (Emet), which is clear and perceptible to the heart and not merely abstract belief.
וּכְשֶׁנִּזְדַּכֵּךְ יוֹתֵר, זוֹכֶה לְ"נְשָׁמָה" שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה לְהַחְכִּים בְּהַשָּׂגוֹת אֱלֹהוּת.
And when he refines himself further, he merits the Neshamah in the brain, which is from the side of Chokhmah, growing wise in perceptions of Godliness.

וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיג נְשָׁמָה קוֹדֶם לְרוּחַ, וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין זֶה חָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁשּׁוֹפֵעַ לוֹ עַל יְדֵי נִשְׁמָתוֹ כְּלָל, רַק כְּשֶׁזָּכָה קוֹדֶם לְרוּחַ הַחִיּוּנִי שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַרְגִּישׁ בַּאֲמִיתַּת אֱלֹהוּת.

And it is impossible to attain Neshamah prior to Ruach, and certainly it is not true divine wisdom channeling to him through his Neshamah, unless he first merited the vital Ruach in the heart, feeling the truth of Godliness.
כִּי "נְשָׁמָה" לְשׁוֹן נְשִׁימָה, מַה שֶּׁנּוֹשֵׁם הָרוּחַ בְּאַפָּיו, וְעִיקַּר הַחַיּוּת הָרוּחַ, רַק שֶׁצָּרִיךְ בְּכָל פַּעַם לִנְשִׁימַת רוּחַ חָדָשׁ.
For Neshamah shares the root of neshimah (breath), which breathes the spirit into his nostrils, the core vitality being the Ruach, only that it requires repeatedly the breathing in of fresh spirit.
וְזֶהוּ כֹּחַ הַנְּשָׁמָה: לִנְשׁוֹם רוּחַ ה' חָדָשׁ בַּלֵּב בְּכָל עֵת עַל יְדֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבְּמוֹחוֹ, שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג בְּכָל עֵת רוּחַ חַיּוּת חָדָשׁ.
And this is the power of the Neshamah: to breathe a fresh spirit of Hashem into the heart at every moment through innovations of wisdom in his mind, grasping continuously renewed vital spirit.
וְ"נֶפֶשׁ" הוּא כֹּחַ הָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ" (דְּבָרִים יב, כג).
And Nefesh is the basic human functional power, as it is written: "for the blood is the life (nefesh)" (Deuteronomy 12:23).
וְהוּא אַף בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ, הַכֹּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת וּלְדַבֵּר וְלַחְשׁוֹב מַה שֶּׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְפִי דַעְתּוֹ, מִצַּד אֱמוּנָתוֹ הַקְּבוּעָה בְּלִבּוֹ בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם.

And it exists even in the commoner: the strength to act, speak, and think in accordance with Hashem's will as he understands it, through the simple faith fixed in his heart in the living God and eternal King.
וְהָרוּחַ, כְּעִנְיַן "רוּחַ ה' דִּבֶּר בִּי" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כג, ב), הוּא לְלוֹמְדֵי תּוֹרָה מִצַּד דְּבַר ה' שֶׁבְּפִיהֶם, מוֹלִיד הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב לְהַכִּיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ אֱלוֹהַּ וּבוֹרֵא עוֹלָם.

And Ruach, in the spirit of "The spirit of Hashem spoke by me" (II Samuel 23:2), belongs to students of Torah through the word of Hashem upon their lips, generating a deep feeling in the heart that there is a God and Creator.

וְתַלְמִיד חָכָם הַמַּשִּׂיג חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא הוּא הַזּוֹכֶה לִנְשָׁמָה, שֶׁהוּא נְשִׁימַת טִפַּת חַיִּים חֲדָשָׁה בְּכָל עֵת וָרֶגַע מִמַּה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּטוּבוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית,
And the Torah scholar who innovates insights merits the Neshamah, which is breathing a fresh drop of life at every moment from what Hashem renews daily in His goodness,
הַיְינוּ רוּחַ הַחַיּוּת שֶׁל הַנִּבְרָאִים שֶׁהוּא מִכְּלַל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית, שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה מֵעוֹלַם הַבְּרִיאָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
namely the vital spirit of creations which is part of the Work of Creation, the Neshamah stemming from the World of Beriah as is known.
וְיֵשׁ עוֹד נְשָׁמָה לַנְּשָׁמָה (חַיָּה), וְהַיְינוּ כִּידוּעַ דִּבְכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת, וְהַתְחָלַת הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא מֵחָכְמָה, וְכֶתֶר הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן הַנֶּעְלָם.

And there is further a soul of the soul (Chayah), for as is known, in every dimension there are ten sefirot, where comprehension begins from Chokhmah, while Keter is the hidden root of the primal Will.

כִּי הָאָדָם מַחְכִּים וּמִתְבּוֹנֵן וְרוֹצֶה וּפוֹעֵל בַּמֶּה שֶׁהוּא רְצוֹנוֹ לְכָךְ, וְזֶה הָרָצוֹן קָדוּם לוֹ, הוּא קָבוּעַ וְנֶעְלָם בָּאָדָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּשָּׂג לוֹ מַה הוּא הַדָּבָר הַמּוֹלִיד בּוֹ מַחֲשָׁבָה וְרָצוֹן זֶה.

For a person acts, understands, and desires according to his primal inclination; and this Will precedes him, planted and concealed such that he cannot grasp what generates this thought and desire within him.

וְזֶהוּ הַכֶּתֶר שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵרֹאשׁ הָאָדָם, וְהוּא אוֹר מַקִּיף שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמַּקִּיף לְמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה יוֹתֵר, שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלֶה בִּלְבָבוֹ שׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה וְדִמְיוֹן הֶבֶל כְּלָל,
And this is Keter which hovers above man's head, the Surrounding Light (Ohr Makif) of Hashem encompassing one who merits, so that no alien thought or vain illusion enters his heart,
וְכָל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו וְהִרְהוּרָיו וּרְצוֹנוֹ בִּלְתִּי לַה' לְבַדּוֹ בִּידִיעָתוֹ וִידִיעַת תּוֹרָתוֹ, שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב:): אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי;
all his thoughts and desires being dedicated solely to Hashem and His Torah, concerning which they said (Sukkah 52b): "Were not the Holy One to help him, he could not overcome it";
וְעֵזֶר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הוּא הֶאָרַת הַכֶּתֶר, שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס בְּלִבּוֹ רַע כְּלָל, שֶׁזֶּה לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת כֹּחַ אָדָם.
and Hashem's help is the radiation of Keter preventing evil from entering his heart, which transcends human mortal capacity.
וְהֵם אַרְבַּע מַדְרֵגוֹת: אַחַת זָכוּ בָּהּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָבוֹת וּלְפִי שֶׁהֵם בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים, וְהַשָּׁלֹשׁ – כָּל אֶחָד עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ.
And these form four rungs: the first (Nefesh) all Israel merited through the Patriarchs as believers; while the other three (Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah) each attains through personal effort.
וְעַל אֵלּוּ שָׁלֹשׁ נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא בָרוּחַ ה'", "וְלֹא בָרַעַשׁ", "וְלֹא בָאֵשׁ" (מְלָכִים א יט, יא–יב).
And concerning these three it is said: "Hashem was not in the wind," "nor in the earthquake," "nor in the fire" (I Kings 19:11–12).

פֵּירוּשׁ, רַעַשׁ הוּא נוֹלָד מִנְּשִׁיבַת רוּחַ חָדָשׁ בְּכָל פַּעַם כַּנּוֹדָע, וְאֵשׁ הוּא הַשּׂוֹרֵף וּמְכַלֶּה הַכֹּל עַד שֶׁנִּתְבָּעֵר כָּל הָרַע מִקֶּרֶב לְבָבוֹ וְאֵין בּוֹ עוֹד שׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה הַנִּמְשָׁךְ מִסִּטְרָא דְּרָע כְּלָל, רַק כֻּלּוֹ כָּלִיל לַה'.
Earthquake is born of the blowing of a fresh spirit, and fire burns away all evil until his heart is purged of every alien thought, consecrated entirely to Hashem.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ בַּדְּבֵיקוּת הַגָּמוּר לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, שֶׁיִּקָּרֵא בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּבְקִרְבּוֹ קָדוֹשׁ מַמָּשׁ.
Nonetheless, he has not yet attained that absolute cleaving of the ultimate future, to be called by the Name of the Holy One, with the Holy One abiding literally within him.
כִּי יֵשׁ עוֹד מַדְרֵגָה חֲמִישִׁית הַנִּקְרֵאת "יְחִידָה", וְהוּא "קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה" (שָׁם, יב).
For there is yet a fifth level termed Yechidah, which is the "still small voice" (ibid. 19:12).
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי כֶּתֶר הוּא עֲדַיִן מִכְּלַל קוֹמַת אָדָם רַק שֶׁהוּא חוּץ לִתְפִיסָתוֹ, וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁבְּכֹחַ הָאָדָם בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ בְּנִצּוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר.
Meaning that Keter still belongs to the stature of man though beyond his grasp, representing what man achieves through effort with God helping him conquer his inclination.

וַעֲדַיִן יֵשׁ נִסְיוֹנוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי כִּי הַנִּסָּיוֹן הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְסַלֵּק הַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ וְסַיַּעְתָּא דִּילֵיהּ מִמֶּנּוּ, כִּדְאָמְרוּ בְּחִזְקִיָּהוּ: "עֲזָבוֹ הָאֱלֹהִים לְנַסּוֹתוֹ" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב לב, לא).
And trials still occur, a trial meaning when the Holy One withdraws His immediate assistance, as with Hezekiah: "God left him, to try him" (II Chronicles 32:31).
וְהוּא הַבֵּירוּר עַל זֹךְ לְבָבוֹ בְּסִלּוּק הַיֵּצֶר לְגַמְרֵי עַד שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לְסַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא כְּלָל, כִּי כְּבָר לִבּוֹ חָלָל בְּקִרְבּוֹ.
And this clarifies the purity of his heart in having removed the inclination so completely that he requires no external assistance, his heart being slain within him.
וְזֶהוּ חַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע הַנִּזְכָּר בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק ה) שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה הָאָבוֹת וְיִתְרוֹ וְיַעְבֵּץ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And this is a life without sorrow and without the evil inclination mentioned in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 5, which the Patriarchs, Jethro, and Ya'betz merited.
וְאָז הוּא מַשִּׂיג מַדְרֵגַת "יְחִידָה", שֶׁמִּתְאַחֵד עִם אֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא לֵב אֶחָד לַאֲבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם שֶׁכְּבָר הֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע.
And then he attains the level of Yechidah, unifying with the truth of the Blessed Name, having only one heart toward his Father in Heaven, having slain the evil inclination.

וְאָז הוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ עוֹד לְשׁוּם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַמְּכוּנֶּה בְּרוּחַ וְרַעַשׁ וָאֵשׁ, רַק קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה – הוּא מַדְרֵגַת נֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא:

And then it is a foretaste of the World to Come, needing no further striving symbolized by wind, earthquake, and fire; rather the still small voice is the state of delighting in the radiance of the Shechinah in the world to come.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 43:1: “In the order Hashem established in this world, in proportion to a person's surrender of himself to Hashem, Hashem returns to him a higher level. As the Zohar says (Mishpatim 94b), ‘When a person is born, he is given a soul from the side of the pure creature… If he merits more, he is given spirit.’ When this person can entrust his present level to Hashem, Hashem then trusts him with a higher level.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim cites the same progression from soul to spirit and explains that a person receives a further level by entrusting the present one to Hashem. This develops the relation between effort and gift in the siman without treating the numbered levels as achievements one can claim by intellect alone.

paragraphs.text: The still voice as Hashem’s seal upon human effort

rich.text: The still voice as Hashem’s seal upon human effort

paragraphs.text: The successive movements of spiritual effort culminate in a stillness that is not produced by effort alone.

rich.text: The successive movements of spiritual effort culminate in a stillness that is not produced by effort alone.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:38: “And in Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas 227b) it is explained that these parallel Elijah's vision of the "wind, earthquake, fire, and a still, small voice"; examine it there. The Nogah (translucent glow) represents this aforementioned root; Ezekiel beheld these forces in their chaotic fury during the Babylonian exile, as our Sages expounded: "a stormy wind came out of the north" to subdue the entire world under the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. Elijah, by contrast, beheld them in their rectified state, perceiving that the "still, small voice"—the Nogah surrounding it—is the very Glory of Hashem aligning with His sublime will. And I heard that the "still, small voice" is Hashem's divine seal impressed after human effort (metaphorized by wind, earthquake, and fire); during man's initial striving Hashem is not yet manifestly present, until the still, small voice seals it, revealing that Hashem was immanent within all those efforts in absolute truth; "Voice" is the seal of wind, "silence" is the seal of earthquake, and "thin/subtle" is the seal of fire; mirroring the construction of the Tabernacle, where human labor was categorized as wind, earthquake, and fire, without the Shechinah resting until Moses prayed "May the pleasantness of Hashem...", which was the still, small voice sealing their work with Divine grace; "Hashem our G-d be upon us" is the voice sealing the wind; "establish Thou the work of our hands upon us" is the silence sealing the earthquake; and "the work of our hands establish Thou it" is the subtle quietude sealing the fire, and this clarifies the concept somewhat.”

The Nogah (translucent glow) represents this aforementioned root; Ezekiel beheld these forces in their chaotic fury during the Babylonian exile, as our Sages expounded: "a stormy wind came out of the north" to subdue the entire world under the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. Elijah, by contrast, beheld them in their rectified state, perceiving that the "still, small voice"—the Nogah surrounding it—is the very Glory of Hashem aligning with His sublime will. And I heard that the "still, small voice" is Hashem's divine seal impressed after human effort (metaphorized by wind, earthquake, and fire); during man's initial striving Hashem is not yet manifestly present, until the still, small voice seals it, revealing that Hashem was immanent within all those efforts in absolute truth; "Voice" is the seal of wind, "silence" is the seal of earthquake, and "thin/subtle" is the seal of fire; mirroring the construction of the Tabernacle, where human labor was categorized as wind, earthquake, and fire, without the Shechinah resting until Moses prayed "May the pleasantness of Hashem...", which was the still, small voice sealing their work with Divine grace; "Hashem our G-d be upon us" is the voice sealing the wind; "establish Thou the work of our hands upon us" is the silence sealing the earthquake; and "the work of our hands establish Thou it" is the subtle quietude sealing the fire, and this clarifies the concept somewhat.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Dover Tzedek explicitly calls the still, thin voice Hashem’s seal after the wind, earthquake, and fire of human work. Its example is the completed Mishkan, whose labor awaited the revelation of the Shechinah. This explains why the present siman distinguishes even very refined effort from the final mode of union: the final seal confirms the work’s inner truth rather than simply adding another forceful human movement.

sections.en: The True Essence and Form of Man Are the Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah

p: [רכח] עִיקַּר צוּרַת הָאָדָם הוּא נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה שֶׁבּוֹ, וְהַגּוּף אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְבוּשׁ הָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (עו עַמּוּד א).
The true essence and form of man are the Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah within him, while the physical body is merely the outer garment of man, as written in Zohar Yitro 76a.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ ה' מַדְרֵגוֹת נַרַנְחַ"י כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ז, שֶׁזֶּהוּ דְּמוּת אָדָם הַשָּׁלֵם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, כו), שֶׁגַּם לְמַעְלָה הֵם ה' כֹּחוֹת וּפַרְצוּפִים עֶלְיוֹנִים כַּנּוֹדָע;

And just as there are five soul-levels—Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah (NaRaNChaY)—as mentioned above in Section 227, which constitute the stature of the perfected man of whom it is said: "in Our image, after Our likeness" (Genesis 1:26), corresponding Above to the five supernal powers and Partzufim as is known;
כָּךְ "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" חֵלֶק אָדָם רָע גַּם כֵּן בְּה' כֹּחוֹת, וְהֵם ג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת הַנִּזְכָּר בִּיחֶזְקֵאל (א, ד).
so, corresponding one opposite the other, the counterpart of the evil man likewise comprises five powers, manifest through the three completely impure husks (kelipot) mentioned in Ezekiel (1:4).

נֶפֶשׁ הַטְּמֵאָה – הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה עֲבֵירוֹת בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ, דִּבּוּרוֹ וּמַעֲשָׂיו, זֶה נִקְרָא "רוּחַ סְעָרָה" שֶׁבָּא מִן הַצָּפוֹן, הוּא הַצְּפוֹנִי שֶׁבֶּחָלָל הַשְּׂמָאלִי, וְסָעִיר כּוּלָּא עֵילָא וְתַתָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר וַיַּקְהֵל (רג עַמּוּד א).

The impure Nefesh—namely when one commits transgressions in thought, speech, and deed—is called the "stormy wind" coming from the north, which is the hidden evil inclination (tzafoni) residing in the left ventricle of the heart, storming and agitating above and below, as written in Zohar Vayakhel 203a.
כִּי עֶצֶם הָאָדָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּטוֹב, רַק שֶׁזֶּה סוֹעֵר בּוֹ וּמְעַרְבְּבוֹ עַד שֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ אַחֲרָיו.
For the intrinsic essence of a Jew derives from the side of good, only that this stormy wind rages within him and confuses him until he is drawn after it.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יג:): לִכְבּוֹשׁ כָּל הָעוֹלָם תַּחַת יַד נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר, הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הָרָע בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, אָז כֹּחַ נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר גּוֹבֵר עַל כָּל הָעוֹלָם;

And this is what they said in Chagigah 13b: to conquer the entire world under the hand of Nebuchadnezzar—meaning when evil surges in practical deed, the destructive force of Nebuchadnezzar prevails over the whole world;
כִּי נֶגֶד זֶה הֵם ד' מַלְכֻיּוֹת: בָּבֶל נֶגֶד רַע בְּמַעֲשֶׂה וּבְכֹחַ הַנֶּפֶשׁ.
for facing these forces are the four exilic kingdoms: Babylon corresponding to evil in physical deed and in the faculty of Nefesh.

וְ"עָנָן גָּדוֹל" – הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְגַּבֵּר עַד הַלֵּב, שֶׁכָּל הַרְגָּשׁוֹת הַלֵּב בַּחֲשָׁקוֹת וְכִיסּוּפִין רַק לְרַע, וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמַּחְשִׁיךְ וּמַאֲפִיל לְגַמְרֵי כֹּחַ רָצוֹן הַטּוֹב הַגָּנוּז בֶּחָלָל הַיְמָנִי דְּלֵב.

And a "great cloud"—this occurs when evil surges into the heart, such that all emotional longings and yearnings are directed solely toward evil, which happens when it completely darkens and obscures the latent will for good hidden in the right ventricle of the heart.
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בַּזֹּהַר: מַה בֵּין עֲנָנָא לַעֲנָנָא?
And see there in the Zohar: what is the difference between this cloud and a holy cloud?

הַיְינוּ דְּבֶאֱמֶת: "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים יח, יב), וַ"עֲבִים רְכוּבוֹ" (שָׁם קד, ג), דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת אֱמֶת הַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה רַק עַל יְדֵי הַאֲפָלָה קְצָת, וְעַל יְדֵי הַחֹשֶׁךְ הוּא מַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִסְתָּר בּוֹ,

That is, in truth: "He makes darkness His secret place" (Psalms 18:12) and "makes the clouds His chariot" (ibid. 104:3), for it is impossible to attain the rung of authentic, clear perception without a preliminary dimming, where through the darkness one recognizes that the Blessed Name is concealed within it,

כְּעִנְיַן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: כְּלוּם אֶפְשָׁר לְבִירָה בְּלֹא מַנְהִיג (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה לט), וּמִתּוֹךְ הַקֻּשְׁיָא עוֹמֵד עַל הַתֵּירוּץ, וּבְלֹא הַקֻּשְׁיָא וְהַחַשְׁכוּת אֵין עוֹמֵד כְּלָל.

in the manner of our father Abraham, peace be upon him: "Is it possible for a palace to exist without a governor?" (Bereishit Rabbah 39:1), where out of the perplexity one arrives at the resolution, and without the difficulty and obscurity one would never grasp it at all.
וְזֶה "עָנָן גָּדוֹל" שֶׁמַּחְשִׁיךְ לְגַמְרֵי וְאֵין מַנִּיחַ לְהִתְעוֹרֵר בְּקֻשְׁיָא וּתְמִיָהָה כְּלָל, עַד שֶׁגַּם אוֹר מוּעָט דֶּאֱמוּנַת הַלֵּב נֶעְלָם;
But this "great cloud" of impurity darkens so utterly that it allows no stirring of existential questioning or wonder to arise, until even the faint light of the heart's simple faith vanishes;
וְזֶהוּ מַלְכוּת פָּרַס שֶׁבִּקְּשׁוּ לְהַשְׁמִיד וְכוּלֵי, כִּי הַלֵּב מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים, וְכַאֲשֶׁר לֵב אָיִן, הֲרֵי זֶה מְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲרוֹג.

and this corresponds to the kingdom of Persia which sought to destroy, slay, and annihilate, for from the heart issue the springs of life, and when the heart is extinguished, it seeks total destruction.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה יב.): מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנֶּהֱנוּ וְכוּלֵי, הַהֲנָאָה הוּא הַהַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב.
And this is why they said in Megillah 12a: "Because they derived pleasure from the feast of that wicked one," for pleasure is the internal sensation in the heart.
רַק בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי" (תְּהִלִּים עג, כו; שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב).
Yet in truth they acted merely for outward appearance, for in genuine truth the Holy One is the heart of Israel, as it is said: "God is the rock of my heart" (Psalms 73:26; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2).
רַק הוּא עַל יְדֵי עָנָן גָּדוֹל הַמַּחְשִׁיךְ לְרֶגַע, וְכַאֲשֶׁר יָשֵׁב רוּחוֹ וְיִתְפַּזְּרוּ הָעֲנָנִים, יֵרָאֶה אוֹר בָּהִיר.
It was merely through a "great cloud" that darkened for a passing moment, and when His spirit blows and the clouds scatter, radiant light is revealed.

וּכְשֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם מִתְגַּבֵּר יוֹתֵר עַד הַמּוֹחַ, לְהַחְכִּים בְּכָל יוֹם בְּחָכְמוֹת חִיצוֹנִיּוֹת, תַּאֲווֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת לְרַע וּלְהַשְׁכִּיחַ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – זֶה נֶגֶד יָוָן, שֶׁנּוֹדָע מֵחָכְמַת יְוָנִית שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ חָכְמוֹת חִיצוֹנִיּוֹת,

And when, Heaven forbid, evil surges higher into the brain, scheming daily in alien philosophies, conceiving new lusts and perverse desires to cause the will of the Blessed Name to be forgotten—this corresponds to Greece, known for Greek wisdom which is the root of external disciplines,
וְלָכֵן מְנֻמֶּרֶת בִּגְזֵירוֹתֶיהָ וְכוּלֵי כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יג).
which is why Greece is compared to a spotted leopard in its variegated decrees, as our Sages taught (Vayikra Rabbah 13:5).
זֶהוּ "אֵשׁ מִתְלַקַּחַת", דְּ"מִתְלַקַּחַת" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמּוֹסֶפֶת בְּכָל רֶגַע הִתְלַהֲבוּת חָדָשׁ וְאֵין כָּבָה כְּלָל, וְזֶהוּ נַרַ"נ דְּרַע.

This is the "flashing fire" (esh mitlakachat), where mitlakachat denotes constantly igniting fresh intellectual fervor without ever subsiding, and these constitute the Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah of evil.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Yitro 11:126-136: ‘When Adam was created, what is written of him? ‘You clothe me with skin and flesh,’ and so forth (Job 10:11; Bereshit 20b). If so, what is the human being? If you say that he is nothing but skin, flesh, bones, and sinews, that is not so, for the human being is certainly none other than the soul. These things mentioned—skin and flesh, bones and sinews—are all only clothing. They are a person’s garments, but they are not the human being. When this human being departs, he strips off those garments he was wearing. The skin in which a person is clothed, and all those bones and sinews, are all in the mystery of supernal wisdom, corresponding to what is above. The skin corresponds to what is above, as the Master taught concerning those curtains, for it is written: ‘He stretches out the heavens like a curtain’ (Psalms 104:2), and ‘rams’ skins dyed red and tachash skins’ (Exodus 25:5). These are the garments above, which cover the garment that is the expanse of the heavens, the outer garment. The curtains are the inner garment, and this is the membrane that covers the flesh.’

p: וְ"נֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב" – יָדוּעַ דִּקְלִיפַּת נֹגַהּ הוּא נֶגֶד דְּבָרִים הַמּוּתָּרִים וְדִבְרֵי רְשׁוּת, וְזֶהוּ נְשָׁמָה לַנְּשָׁמָה (חַיָּה), וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם וְכֶתֶר דְּרַע, שֶׁנֶּגְדּוֹ אֱדוֹם כַּנּוֹדָע,

And "a brightness was about it" (ve-nogah lo saviv)—it is known that Kelipat Nogah corresponds to permitted, mundane matters, representing the Chayah (soul of the soul), the hidden root, and the Keter of evil, countered by Edom as is known,

דְּ"רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כד, כ), שֶׁהַהַתְחָלָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי דְּבַר הָרְשׁוּת, לִהְיוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ בְּתַאֲווֹת הָרְשׁוּת וְתַעֲנוּגִים הַמּוּתָּרִים רַק בְּלֹא שׁוּם סֶרֶךְ מִצְוָה, זֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּיֵצֶר הַמַּסִּית,

for "Amalek was the first of the nations" (Numbers 24:20), whose inception is through permissible things: being lured into permitted lusts and lawful pleasures devoid of any trace of a mitzvah, which is the foundational root of the inciting inclination,
וּמִן הַהֶיתֵּר בָּא לְאִיסּוּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ן רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים.
and from the permitted one slides into the forbidden, as the Ramban wrote at the beginning of Parashat Kedoshim.
וְזוֹ נִכְלֶלֶת פְּעָמִים בְּטוֹב וּפַעַם בְּג' קְלִיפּוֹת הָאֲסוּרוֹת;
And this Nogah is at times subsumed within good, and at times within the three totally forbidden husks;

פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁכָּל נַרַ"נ שֶׁלּוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה, הֲרֵי גַּם דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת שֶׁלּוֹ: שֻׁלְחָנוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְמִזְבֵּחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק ג דְּאָבוֹת), וּשְׁתִיָּיתָם יַיִן לִנְסָכִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹמָא עא.), וְשִׂיחַת חוּלִין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:), וְכֵן כָּל דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם.

meaning that for a Torah scholar whose Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah are sanctified, his permitted mundane actions are also holy: his table is comparable to an altar (Avot 3:3), his wine drinking to libations (Yoma 71a), and his casual speech to words of Torah (Sukkah 21b), and likewise all his permitted activities.
וּלְהֵיפֶךְ, בְּמִי שֶׁנַּרַ"נ שֶׁלּוֹ לְרַע יָרוּצוּ, כָּךְ כָּל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת, הָאֲכִילָה נוֹתֶנֶת כֹּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת רַע, הֲרֵי נִכְלָל בָּרָע וְכֵן הַכֹּל;
And conversely, in one whose faculties run after evil, so do all his permitted actions: his eating provides him strength to commit evil, becoming subsumed in the bad, and so with everything;

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayera 37:1: “‘When God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Avraham and sent Lot out of the overthrow.’ The relation between remembering Avraham and saving Lot is explained by the Zohar: Lot represents the inclination and Avraham the soul. The writings of the Ari identify Lot with the shell of nogah, a mixture of good and evil, as it says, ‘and brightness around it’—it is darkness, with light encamped around it. The soul chiefly comes to this world to clarify this shell and raise it to the highest levels. Nogah signifies all permitted worldly matters. Although these are entirely permitted, they nevertheless require clarification, as the Sages taught: Sanctify yourself within what is permitted to you.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov interprets Lot's rescue through the mixed category of nogah. Its conclusion precisely identifies the sphere at issue: worldly matters that are genuinely permitted, yet whose direction still needs clarification. This makes the siman's counsel against indiscriminate rejection intelligible while keeping its distinction between this mixed sphere and the three prohibited shells.

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Leviticus 19:2:2: “The matter is this: the Torah warned against forbidden sexual relationships and forbidden foods, while permitting intercourse between a man and his wife and the eating of meat and wine. A person driven by appetite could therefore find room to be immersed in sexual excess with his wife or his many wives, to be among wine drinkers and gluttonous meat eaters, and to speak as he pleases with every kind of vulgarity, since this prohibition was not specified in the Torah. He would then be a scoundrel with the Torah’s permission. Therefore, after detailing the prohibitions that it forbade entirely, Scripture came with a general command: that we should practice restraint regarding what is permitted.”

p: וּמַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה שֶׁבַּיֵּצֶר הוּא מִן הַצַּד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹרְאוֹ, הוּא כִּמְשַׁל הַזּוֹנָה הַמּוּזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קסג עַמּוּד א) שֶׁגַּם הוּא עוֹשֶׂה רְצוֹן קוֹנוֹ וּמְיוּחָד בַּאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

And the level of Yechidah within the inclination is from the perspective that the Blessed Name created it, akin to the parable of the harlot in Zohar II:163a who likewise fulfills the will of her master, unified within the ultimate truth of Hashem.
זֶהוּ "מִתּוֹכָהּ כְּעֵין הַחַשְׁמַל" (יְחֶזְקֵאל א, ד), שֶׁהוּא חַיּוֹת וְכוּלֵי (חֲגִיגָה יג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב), דְּמֵאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְדִבּוּרוֹ נִתְהַוָּה זֶה.

This is "from the midst thereof as the color of amber (chashmal)" (Ezekiel 1:4), which denotes speaking living creatures (Chagigah 13b), for from the true will and speech of the Blessed Name this was brought into being.
וְנִמְצָא דְּאֵין בְּרַע גָּמוּר רַק נַרַ"נ שֶׁמִּתְלַבְּשׁוֹת וְנִיכָּרוֹת בְּגוּפוֹ;
And it turns out that absolute evil applies only to Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah which enclothe and manifest within his physical body;

אֲבָל חַיָּה, יְחִידָה, שֶׁהֵם סָבִיב לוֹ לְאוֹר מַקִּיף, שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד דְּבֵיקוּתָן בְּשָׁרְשָׁן לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – בָּזֶה אֵין רַע כְּלָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּשָׁרְשָׁן מֵעַצְמִיּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

but Chayah and Yechidah, which encompass him as Surrounding Light from the side of their cleaving to their root in the Blessed Name—in this realm there is no evil whatsoever in Israel, their root deriving from the very essence of Hashem
[רַק בָּאֻמּוֹת שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אוֹר מַקִּיף כְּלָל, רַק הַגֵּרִים שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים לְאוֹר מַקִּיף דִּקְלִיפַּת נֹגַהּ כַּנּוֹדָע]:
[unlike the gentile nations who have no holy Surrounding Light at all, save for righteous converts who attain the Surrounding Light of Kelipat Nogah, as is known].

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Terumah 66:673-675: “Rather, it certainly performs its Master’s will. A king had an only son whom he loved greatly. Out of love, he commanded him not to approach an evil woman, for whoever approached her would be unworthy to enter the king’s palace. The son agreed lovingly to do his father’s will. Outside the king’s house there was a prostitute, beautiful in appearance. One day the king said: I wish to see my son’s devotion to me. He called the prostitute and said: Go and tempt my son, so that I may see his devotion to me. What did she do? She followed the king’s son and began embracing and kissing him and tempting him with many enticements. If the son is upright and obeys his father’s command, he rebukes her, does not heed her, and pushes her away. Then his father rejoices in his son, brings him within the curtain of his palace, and gives him gifts, presents, and great honor. Who brought all this honor to the son? Say: That prostitute. Does she deserve praise for this, or not? Certainly she deserves praise in every respect: first, because she performed the king’s command; second, because she brought the son all that good and all the king’s love for him. Therefore it is written, “Behold, it was very good”: “good” is the angel of life; “very” is the angel of death, which is indeed very good for one who obeys his Master’s commands. Come and see: Without this accuser, the righteous would not inherit the supernal treasures they are destined to inherit in the World to Come.”

paragraphs.text: Context: The king wills the test, while the son fulfills the king’s command by resisting the temptation. The woman serves the king through her assigned role. This distinction explains Rav Tzadok’s claim that, at the level of its divine origin, even the inclination serves its Creator. It does not turn yielding to the inclination into obedience to the command.

sections.en: The Commandments Are Divine Counsels for Man on How to Attain Spiritual Perfection

p: [רכט] הַמִּצְווֹת הֵם עֵצוֹת לָאָדָם אֵיךְ לִהְיוֹת שָׁלֵם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (פב עַמּוּד ב).
The commandments are divine counsels for man on how to attain spiritual perfection, as written in Zohar Yitro 82b.
וְהֵם עֵצוֹת לְהַשִּׂיג כָּל חֶלְקֵי נַרַנְחַ"י, לְכָל אֶחָד מִצְווֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת,
And they are counsels to attain all levels of NaRaNChaY, each level having designated mitzvot,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר שָׁם (פ עַמּוּד א) דְּה' קוֹלוֹת דְּהַר סִינַי הֵם נֶגֶד ה' דַּרְגִּין דִּיחֶזְקֵאל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ח, דְּהֵם נַרַנְחַ"י דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא.
as stated in the Zohar there (80a) that the five voices at Mount Sinai correspond to the five visions of Ezekiel (Section 228), which are the NaRaNChaY of the Other Side.

וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּקוֹלוֹת דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה הַיְינוּ מִפִּיּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּאֵין קוֹל בָּעוֹלָם זוּלַת מֵה' מוֹצָאוֹת הַפֶּה, וְנֶאֱמַר: "נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְדַבְּרוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה, ו), שֶׁכָּלְלוּ כָּל חֶלְקֵי נַפְשׁוֹתָם לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָז.

And I heard that the voices at the Giving of the Torah emerged from the mouths of the children of Israel, for there is no vocal sound in the world except through the five organs of speech, as said: "my soul failed when he spoke" (Song of Songs 5:6), uniting all faculties of their souls unto Hashem then.
וּמִצַּד כָּל כֹּחַ נֶפֶשׁ יָצָא קוֹל צְעָקָה מְיוּחֶדֶת לְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ, שֶׁהוּא מַכִּיר אֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמִתְיַיחֵד בּוֹ, שֶׁעַל זֶה הוּא כָּל מַתַּן תּוֹרָה.
And from each soul-faculty issued a unique cry corresponding to that faculty, recognizing the truth of the Blessed Name and unifying with Him, which was the entire purpose of the Giving of the Torah.
וּבְוַדַּאי יֵשׁ מִצְווֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת שֶׁהֵם עֵצוֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת לְכָל מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בָּהּ, אֵיךְ לְהִזְדַּכֵּךְ בָּהּ.
And certainly there are specific mitzvot serving as tailored counsels for every spiritual rung upon which one stands, teaching how to be refined therein.
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם דַּף צ' עַמּוּד א דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת הֵם חָמֵשׁ גּוֹ חָמֵשׁ, עַיֵּין שָׁם, וּבְרֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב דְּהֵם נֶגֶד ה' קָלִין הַנִּזְכָּרִים.
And see there (Zohar 90a) that the Ten Commandments are five within five, and at the top of 90b that they correspond to the aforementioned five voices.

וְהַיְינוּ "אָנֹכִי", דְּלֹא אָמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיוּוּי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד אֱמוּנָה פְּשׁוּטָה הַקְּבוּעָה בְּלֵב כָּל אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ עַל זֶה צִיוּוּי, דְּמִי שֶׁאֵין מַאֲמִין מַה יּוֹעִיל צִיוּוּי, רַק יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים.

That is, "I am Hashem" (Anokhi) is not formulated as a command, as I wrote elsewhere, corresponding to simple faith embedded in the heart of every Jew, over which a command is inapplicable—for what does a command help one who does not believe?—Israel being believers, children of believers.
וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תִרְצַח" – הוּא בְּהַרְחָקַת נֶפֶשׁ דִּמְסָאֲבוּ, שֶׁהוּא הִיפּוּךְ מַדְרֵגַת קְדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל, זֶהוּ בְּ"לֹא תִרְצַח".
And opposite it stands "You shall not murder," which is the distancing of the impure Nefesh, the antithesis of Israel's holiness.

כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי דִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרִים הֵם: רְצִיחָה וְנִיאוּף, הַיְינוּ כַּעַס וְתַאֲוָה, שֶׁנֶּגְדָּם מְצוֹרָע וְזָב, שֶׁהַמְּצוֹרָע נִשְׁתַּלַּח חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין זֶה מִכְּלַל נְפָשׁוֹת דְּסִטְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.

As I heard, the two primary inclinations are murder and adultery, wrath and lust, countered by the leper (metzora) and the zav; the leper is cast outside the camp of Israel, for wrath does not belong to the soul-realm of Israel at all.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יֵצֶר דְּתַאֲוָה זֶהוּ מִכְּלַל מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק שֶׁהֶעָנָן גָּדוֹל מַחְשִׁיךְ הַלֵּב, עַל זֶה הוּא "לֹא תִנְאָף".
In contrast, the inclination for desire is within the camp of Israel, only that the "great cloud" darkens the heart, countered by "You shall not commit adultery."
וְנֶגְדּוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה וְהִתְגַּבְּרוּת רוּחַ אֱלֹהִי נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ וְגוֹמֵר עַל פָּנַי", שֶׁהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב בַּאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא הֶאָרַת פָּנִים;
And opposite it in holiness and the surging of the divine Ruach it is said: "You shall have no other gods before My face," the heart's perception of Hashem being termed the shining of the Face;

וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה וְגוֹמֵר" נֶאֱמַר עַל מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַלֵּב כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם (פֶּרֶק א מֵהִלְכוֹת יְסוֹדֵי הַתּוֹרָה), הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְבוֹרָר בִּלְבָבְךָ אֲמִיתַּת כֹּחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ בְּכָל דָּבָר, עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלֶה בְּלִבְּךָ שָׁלְטָנוּת שׁוּם כֹּחַ אַחֵר.

and "You shall have no" refers to thought in the heart, as Maimonides wrote (Yesodei HaTorah 1:6), meaning that Hashem's omnipotence and providence be so clarified in your heart that no thought of any other sovereign power can enter.

וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּהַשְׁפָּעַת הַחָכְמָה, טִפָּה מְחוּדֶּשֶׁת לְהַחֲיוֹת הַלֵּב – זֶהוּ "לֹא תִשָּׂא אֶת שֵׁם ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ [לַשָּׁוְא]", זֶהוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת כא.) עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי שֵׁם ה' אֶקְרָא וְגוֹמֵר".

And afterward, in channeling wisdom as a fresh drop to enliven the heart, stands "You shall not take the Name of Hashem your God [in vain]"—which denotes words of Torah, as in Berakhot 21a on "When I call upon the Name of Hashem."
"לַשָּׁוְא" פֵּירוּשׁ לְחִנָּם, כְּעִנְיַן תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל דּוֹאֵג "מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ" (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:), רַק שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מוֹלִיד חַיּוּת חָדָשׁ.
"In vain" (lashav) means emptily, like the Torah of Doeg which was "from the lip outward" (Sanhedrin 106b), whereas it must continually generate fresh vitality.

וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תִגְנֹב", כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כב) בְּקַיִן: כְּגוֹנֵב דַּעַת הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, שֶׁהַמִּתְחַכֵּם בְּחָכְמַת דְּהַבְלֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּלְהַשְׁכִּיחַ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – זֶה נִקְרָא גַּנָּב הַמִּתְחַבֵּא מִבַּעַל הַבָּיִת.

And opposite it stands "You shall not steal," as expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 22) regarding Cain: like one deceiving the Supernal Knowledge, where one who acts clever in worldly vanities to cause Hashem to be forgotten is called a thief hiding from the Master of the house.

וּבִשְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ פָּסֵיק טַעֲמָא דְּאִסּוּר וְשָׁרֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, צג עַמּוּד ב), הַיְינוּ מִשּׁוּם דַּעֲדַיִן לֹא הִשִּׂיג לְאוֹר מַקִּיף לִהְיוֹת כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו וּמַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו בִּלְתִּי לַה' לְבַדּוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס הָרָע כְּלָל גַּם בִּדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁהוּא קְלִיפַּת נֹגַהּ,

And within these three commandments the distinction between forbidden and permitted still ceases and cuts across, as written in Zohar II:93b, because one has not yet attained Surrounding Light where all deeds and thoughts are solely for Hashem, preventing evil from intruding even in permitted matters of Kelipat Nogah,
דְּבָזֶה לָא פָּסֵיק טַעֲמָא כְּלָל כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עוֹד דְּבַר הָרְשׁוּת כְּלָל, רַק כֻּלּוֹ לַה'.
wherein that sharp distinction ceases because for him no purely secular realm exists, all being consecrated to Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Yitro 35:565-566: ““You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal.” The cantillation makes a pause after “not” in all three. Without the pause there would be no remedy, and it would be forbidden to take a life at all, even where a person had transgressed the Torah. Because there is a pause, there is a forbidden form and a permitted form. “You shall not commit adultery”: without the pause, even having children or rejoicing with one’s wife in the joy of a mitzvah would be forbidden. Because there is a pause, there is a forbidden form and a permitted form. “You shall not steal”: without the pause, it would be forbidden even to “steal” the mind of one’s teacher in Torah, or of a sage, in order to gain understanding from him; or for a judge deciding a case according to the claims to outwit the deceiver, and both litigants, in order to bring the judgment to light. Because there is a pause, there is a forbidden form and a permitted form.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Pasqa ta’ama refers here to a pause in the cantillation after lo, “not.” The Zohar reads this pause as distinguishing the prohibited act from a different, permitted application of the same general capacity: lawful judgment, marital intimacy, or discerning understanding. The murder example concerns the Torah’s judicial framework, not permission for private violence. Rav Tzadok uses the contrast of forbidden and permitted as an image of a spiritual stage in which ordinary permitted activity has not yet become wholly devoted to Hashem. The relevant passage is Zohar II 93b.

items.h: Shabbat and sanctifying the permitted

p: וְזֶהוּ "זָכוֹר" דְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ לַה', כָּל עִינּוּגִים שֶׁלּוֹ מִצְוָה גְּדוֹלָה, וְכָל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת, דְּהַיְינוּ דָּבָר שֶׁהַגּוּף עוֹשֶׂה לְצָרְכּוֹ וּלְהַנָאָתוֹ, וּמְדַבֵּר וּמְהַרְהֵר לַהֲנָאָתוֹ וְאֵין בּוֹ אִיסּוּר, הֲרֵי הֵם בְּשַׁבָּת מִצְוָה.

And this is "Remember" (Zakhor) of Shabbat which is entirely for Hashem, where all bodily pleasures are a great mitzvah, and all permitted acts—eating, speaking, and meditating for physical pleasure without sin—become a mitzvah on Shabbat.
שֶׁהֲרֵי אֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁשִּׂיחָה תַּעֲנוּג לוֹ, מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּשֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ (אֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן שז סָעִיף א) דְּהִיא מִכְּלַל עֹנֶג שַׁבָּת.
For even one for whom conversation is a pleasure, the Shulchan Arukh (Orach Chayim 307:1) rules that it is part of Sabbath delight.

וְזֶהוּ "מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי וְכוּלֵי" (שַׁבָּת י:), כִּי דָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן, רַק מֵעֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמִמַּתְּנָתוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ז.

And this is: "I have a precious gift in My treasury, and Shabbat is its name" (Shabbat 10b), for being entirely free from illusion is not in human hands alone, but comes as Hashem's gift (Section 227).

וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תַעֲנֶה [בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר]", כִּי לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נָקִי בָּזֶה דְּ"אִישׁ אֶת רָעַת רֵעֵהוּ אַל תַּחְשְׁבוּ בִּלְבַבְכֶם" (זְכַרְיָה ח, יז), דִּבְלָאו הָכִי לֹא יִמָּלֵט מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת שֶׁאֲחֵרִים מוֹלִידִים בּוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רי"ט.

And opposite it stands "You shall not bear [false witness against your neighbor]," for to attain this one must be clean of thinking evil against his fellow (Zechariah 8:17), without which he cannot escape alien thoughts that others induce in him (Section 219).
וּלְכָךְ בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בַּתְּחִלָּה: "וְכִפֶּר בַּעֲדוֹ... וּבְעַד בֵּיתוֹ" (וַיִּקְרָא טז, יא) הַקּוֹדֵם, שֶׁמּוֹלִידִים תֹּקֶף הִרְהוּרִים וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת בְּקִרְבּוֹ;
Therefore the High Priest atoned first for himself and his household who engender intense thoughts within him;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּעַד אֶחָיו הַמְקוֹרָבִים לוֹ גַּם כֵּן מוֹלִידִים יוֹתֵר;
and afterward for his fellow priests who are also close;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּעַד כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and afterward for all Israel.

וְאָז נִכְנַס לְקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְכָל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה [בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד]" (שָׁם, יז), פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ שׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה, שֶׁרוֹב הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת הוּא מִצַּד חִבּוּרוֹ לַנִּבְרָאִים דִּבְזֶה הוּא הִרְהוּרוֹ, וְאִלּוּ הָיָה לְבַדּוֹ בָּעוֹלָם, הוּא עִם הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ, הָיָה כָּל הִרְהוּרָיו בַּבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ לְבַד;

And then he entered the Holy of Holies, where "no man shall be [in the tent of meeting]" (ibid. 16:17)—meaning he must have no alien thought, for most foreign thoughts arise from connection to creatures, whereas were he alone in the world with the Creator, all his thoughts would be in the Creator alone;
כִּי הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת הוּא מִצַּד הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁעוֹבְרִים לְפָנָיו כַּיָּדוּעַ.
for delusions and alien thoughts arise from things passing before his eyes.

Gloss: People who take pleasure in recounting news and novel matters may recount them on Shabbat as on a weekday. But someone who does not take pleasure in them may not recount them so that his companion will enjoy them (Terumat HaDeshen, section 61).’
