items.h: Purified understanding and desire

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ "כַּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אִמָּךְ" (שְׁמוֹת כ, יב), כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי פֵּירוּשׁ: דְּאַבָּא וְאִימָּא יָדוּעַ דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא תִּדְחֶה שִׂכְלְךָ וּרְצוֹנְךָ גַּם כֵּן.
And afterward "Honor your father and your mother" (Exodus 20:12)—as I heard explained: Father and Mother represent brain and heart, meaning do not reject your own intellect and will either.

וְזֶהוּ אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר עָבַר כָּל ד' מַדְרֵגוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל וְהִשִּׂיג עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּשַׁבָּת, אָז הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְבוֹ לְנִסָּיוֹן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ז, לָדַעַת אִם בְּכֹחַ עַצְמוֹ לְהִנָּצֵל, וְזֶהוּ "כַּבֵּד".

And this applies after one has traversed all four preceding levels and attained Hashem's aid on Shabbat, whereupon the Holy One leaves him to trial (Section 227) to see if by his own power he remains preserved, which is "Honor."

וְאוּלַי יֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן מִן כִּיבּוּד הַבַּיִת שֶׁהוּא נִקָּיוֹן, וְגַם כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ "כַּבֵּד" הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּתַכְלִית הַהִדּוּר אַבָּא וְאִמָּא – שִׂכְלְךָ וּרְצוֹנְךָ, שֶׁהֵם הַמּוֹלִידִים אוֹתְךָ, פֵּירוּשׁ אֶת כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה שֶׁלְּךָ, יִהְיוּ מְנוּקִים, שֶׁמִּצַּד עַצְמָם יִהְיוּ כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמְיוּחָדִים.

And perhaps it also derives from sweeping (kibbud) the house, meaning cleansing; and literally "honor"—that your intellect and will, which give birth to your active powers, be so purified that of their own accord they align with Hashem's will.

וּבִפְשָׁטֵיהּ אָב וָאֵם גַּם כֵּן, כְּטַעַם (סַנְהֶדְרִין קד.): בְּרָא מְזַכֵּי אַבָּא, וְהַיְינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר מַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁמִּזְדַּכֵּךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ שָׁרְשׁוֹ הָעֶלְיוֹן, גַּם הַחֵטְא דִּתְחִלַּת בְּרִיאָתוֹ וְ"יֶחֱמַתְנִי אִמִּי" נִתְקָן, וְגַם אָב וָאֵם נִזְדַּכְּכוּ וְהוּא מְכַבְּדָם.

And literally with biological parents, in the spirit of "a son confers merit upon his father" (Sanhedrin 104a): when one reaches this rung, even the initial conception flaw of "in sin did my mother conceive me" is rectified, and parents are elevated through his honor.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין לא.): דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים הוֹדוּ לָזֶה, וְהַיְינוּ דְּהֵם אוֹמְרִים "כֹּחִי וְעֹצֶם יָדִי" וְשֶׁהַכֹּל בִּידֵי אָדָם וְלֹא בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, רַק בְּשֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם וּבִינָתוֹ;
And our Sages stated (Kiddushin 31a) that the gentiles conceded to this commandment, for they claim "my power and the might of my hand," believing all depends on human reason;
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מְצַפִּים לְעֶזְרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רַק לְבַסּוֹף הוּא "תּוֹרָתוֹ" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.) וְ"הָאָרֶץ נָתַן לִבְנֵי אָדָם", זֶהוּ מַדְרֵגָה חֲמִישִׁית דְּ"כַּבֵּד".
whereas Israel yearns for Hashem's help, yet ultimately it becomes "his own Torah" (Avodah Zarah 19a) and "the earth has He given to the children of men," which is the fifth rung of "Honor."

עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וְאָמְרוּ רַק עַם חָכָם וְנָבוֹן הַגּוֹי הַגָּדוֹל הַזֶּה" (דְּבָרִים ד, ו), שֶׁיּוֹדוּ עַל חָכְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד עַצְמָם, כְּעִנְיַן שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ, שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לָדוּן בְּלֹא עֵדִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא:), רַק כְּעִנְיַן מָשִׁיחַ דִּ"מוֹרַח וְדָאֵין" (סַנְהֶדְרִין צג:), שֶׁמַּעֲמִיד עַל חָכְמָתוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁכֵּן הוּא הָאֱמֶת גַּם בְּחָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,

Concerning this it is said: "and they shall say: Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people" (Deuteronomy 4:6), acknowledging Israel's inherent wisdom, like King Solomon who sought to judge without witnesses (Rosh Hashanah 21b), and like the Messiah who "judges by scent" (Sanhedrin 93b), his intellect and will reflecting the truth of divine wisdom,

לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיֵּשֶׁב [שְׁלֹמֹה] עַל כִּסֵּא ה'" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, כג), שֶׁהוּא דְּמוּת אָדָם שֶׁעַל הַכִּסֵּא, שֶׁזָּכָה לְמַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה, דְּהַיְינוּ נִקְרָא בִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
since it is said: "And [Solomon] sat on the throne of Hashem" (I Chronicles 29:23), mirroring the Man upon the Throne, having merited Yechidah and being called by God's Name.

וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תַחְמֹד", דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ הַחֵשֶׁק בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַחַשְׁמַל, דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא מַלְאָךְ קָדוֹשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא: שְׁמוֹ לָבָן, דְּאִתְלַבַּן וְכוּלֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קלז עַמּוּד ב), שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לַחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא.

And opposite it stands "You shall not covet"—attaining the inclination whose root is desire at the level of the Chashmal, as a holy angel, where in the future its name will be Lavan (pure white), transformed into the sweet longing for Torah (Midrash HaNe'elam, Zohar I:137b).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, צג עַמּוּד ב) דְּחָשֵׁיב פְּרָטִין בְּלֹא תַחְמֹד, דַּחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מוּתָּר;
And as written in Zohar II:93b enumerating details in "You shall not covet," that longing for Torah is permitted;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּיִזְדַּכֵּךְ הַיֵּצֶר לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ כְּלָל חֶמְדָּה חוּץ מֵחֶמְדָּה דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא.
meaning the inclination becomes so purified that he harbors no desire other than for Torah.
וְנִסְתַּלֵּק קֻשְׁיַת רַבִּי אַבְרָהָם בֶּן עֶזְרָא: אֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ לָאו עַל חֶמְדָּה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם?
And Ibn Ezra's famous query is resolved: how can the Torah prohibit coveting when desire seems beyond human control?
רַק הוּא אַחַר הַד' מַדְרֵגוֹת, אָז בֶּאֱמֶת לֹא יַעֲלֶה עַל לְבָבוֹ חֶמְדָּה.
For following the first four rungs, covetousness will truly never enter his heart.
וּבְיָדוֹ בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ בַּקּוֹדְמִים לְהַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה ה' שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּכֹחַ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ וּבְקוֹמַת אָדָם כְּלָל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ז.
And it is in his power through striving in the earlier rungs to reach this fifth level which transcends ordinary human capacity (Section 227).
וְזוֹ הַמַּדְרֵגָה כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְמַה שֶּׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, הוּא מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ וּבְכֹחוֹ וְעֹצֶם יָדוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
And this level, when one reaches that which requires no further effort, is the state where everything is credited as his own through his prior exertion and strength, as noted above.

paragraphs.text: The siman places honoring parents after Shabbos within a sequence of deeper spiritual refinement.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:22: ““Take for Me a threefold heifer” corresponds to honoring father and mother. Honoring father and mother is placed beside Shabbos to teach that if a person errs in the clarification of his handiwork, which is called Shabbos, its repair stands beside it: fulfilling the honoring of father and mother, so that he repairs the deficiency implanted in him from birth, from the root of father and mother. How does he repair it? Through the service he performs, he will perceive meaning even at this depth. This is what the sacrificial services signify: a person dedicates all his deeds to Hashem and afterward receives them from the table on high.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov likewise reads the adjacency of these commandments as repair reaching beyond one’s present acts toward what was received at birth. This helps explain Rav Tzadok’s extension of the commandment to the mind and heart from which a person’s actions are born. The developmental sequence is directed toward dedicating those actions to Hashem and then receiving them anew as a gift.

paragraphs.text: Context: Midrash HaNe’elam, Zohar I 137b, plays on Lavan and melubban: white and whitened. The preceding symbolic Lot represents the inclination while defiled, and Lavan represents its future purification. The continuation on I 138a explains why the force itself remains: it gives joy to Torah learning. Rav Tzadok joins these two statements when describing desire purified into longing for Torah. These are allegorical names for the inclination, rather than an endorsement of the biblical Lavan.

paragraphs.text: Ibn Ezra on Exodus 20:14:1: “So every understanding person should know that a beautiful wife or wealth will not come to a person through his own wisdom and knowledge, but according to what the Lord has allotted him. Kohelet says, “To a person who did not labor for it, he shall give it as his portion.” The sages said: Children, life, and sustenance depend not on merit but on mazal. For this reason the understanding person will neither desire nor covet. Once he knows that God has forbidden his fellow’s wife to him, she is further beyond his reach than a princess is in the villager’s eyes. He will therefore rejoice in his portion and will not set his heart on coveting and desiring what is not his, for he knows that what God did not wish to give him he cannot take by his strength, thoughts, or schemes. He will therefore trust his Creator to sustain him and do what is good in His eyes.”

sections.en: According to the Refinement of a Person's Spiritual Stature

p: [רל] כְּפִי זִיכּוּךְ מַעֲלַת הָאָדָם וּמַדְרֵגָתוֹ, זוֹכֶה לְהִתְמַנּוּת וּרְאָשׁוּת.
According to the refinement of a person's spiritual stature, he merits appointment and leadership.
וְהֵם ד' מַדְרֵגוֹת שָׂרִים שֶׁחָשַׁב יִתְרוֹ נֶגֶד ד' מַעֲלוֹת שֶׁזָּכַר:
And these are the four tiers of officers enumerated by Jethro (Exodus 18:21), corresponding to four virtues:
"אַנְשֵׁי חַיִל" – הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַגּוּף, וְגִבּוֹרִים לִכְבּוֹשׁ יִצְרָם בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה, דִּבּוּר וּמַעֲשֶׂה לִהְיוֹת לַה'.
"Able men" (anshei chayil)—pertaining to the Nefesh, physical strength, being mighty to conquer their inclination in thought, speech, and action for Hashem.
"וְיִרְאֵי אֱלֹהִים" – בַּלֵּב, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן", וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּלּוּת אֱלֹהוּת מוּרְגָּשׁ לַלֵּב.
"Such as fear God"—in the heart (Yoma 72b on "and he has no heart"), through the revelation of Godliness palpably felt within the heart.

"אַנְשֵׁי אֱמֶת" – אֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פְּתִיחַת אֵיכָה), וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַמְחַדְּשִׁים חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בְּכָל יוֹם נִקְרְאוּ אַנְשֵׁי אֱמֶת, שֶׁהֵם אֲנָשִׁים לָאֱמֶת.
"Men of truth"—there is no truth other than Torah (Midrash Rabbah, introduction to Eichah), and scholars who innovate Torah insights daily are called men of truth, being devoted men of Truth.

"וְשׂנְאֵי בָצַע" – פֵּירוּשׁ נְקִיִּים מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת, שֶׁכָּל דִּמְיוֹנוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַה שֶּׁחוּץ לַתּוֹרָה נִקְרָא בֶּצַע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַט [לִבִּי אֶל עֵדְוֹתֶיךָ] וְאַל אֶל בָּצַע" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, לו).

"Hating covetousness" (sonei vatza)—meaning cleansed of alien thoughts, for all worldly delusions outside of Torah are termed betza, as written: "Incline [my heart unto Your testimonies], and not to covetousness" (Psalms 119:36).
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכַר אַחַר כָּךְ רַק "אֲנָשִׁים חֲכָמִים" (דְּבָרִים א, טו), וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין ק:) דִּנְבוֹנִים לֹא אִשְׁתֲּכַח.
And Moses our teacher subsequently mentioned only "wise men" (Deuteronomy 1:15), in line with Eruvin 100b that "understanding men" could not be found.
וְיָדוּעַ בִּינָה לִבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַהַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב, וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְלֹא נָתַן ה' לָכֶם לֵב לָדַעַת וְגוֹמֵר עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" (שָׁם כט, ג), כִּי לֹא נִגְאֲלוּ אֶלָּא בִּזְכוּת הָאֱמוּנָה.
And Binah is the heart, emotional perception, and it is said: "Yet Hashem has not given you a heart to perceive... unto this day" (ibid. 29:3), for they were redeemed solely in the merit of faith.

פֵּירוּשׁ: הֲגַם דְּהָיוּ חֲכָמִים בַּתּוֹרָה דְּאִשְׁתֲּכַח, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין הַחָכְמָה לְהוֹסִיף הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב, הֲרֵי זֶה מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַנֶּפֶשׁ לְבַד, כִּי בְּכָל אֶחָד מֵהֶם כָּלוּל גַּם כֵּן נַרַנְחַ"י כַּנּוֹדָע.

That is, even though wise scholars were found, as long as wisdom does not infuse deep emotional perception into the heart, it remains confined to the Nefesh alone, each level containing all five soul-aspects.

וְהַחָכְמָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מוֹסֶפֶת חַיּוּת חָדָשׁ לַלֵּב בְּכָל עֵת, הוּא רַק מִצְוַת תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ עֲשִׂיַּת כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת שֶׁהוּא בַּנֶּפֶשׁ לְבַד, מִצַּד הָאֱמוּנָה הַתְּקוּעָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִשְׁמוֹעַ בְּקוֹל ה' וְלַעֲסוֹק בְּמִצְווֹתָיו וּבְתוֹרָתוֹ.

And wisdom that does not add fresh vitality to the heart at all times is merely the performance of the mitzvah of study like any practical deed within the Nefesh, stemming from rooted faith that one must obey Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ אַנְשֵׁי חַיִל לְבַד, לִכְבּוֹשׁ יִצְרָם.
And this is "able men" alone, conquering their inclination.

וְעָשָׂה מֵהֶם כָּל הַשָּׂרִים, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם מַדְרֵגַת הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל הַשָּׂרִים וְהוּא נֶגֶד מַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה, הֲרֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה דַּרְגָּא דְּנֶפֶשׁ לְבַד כַּנּוֹדָע בַּזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים.
And he appointed all the officers from them, for in truth even the king who transcends all officers, corresponding to Yechidah—King David was the level of Nefesh, as known throughout the Zohar.
רַק שֶׁהָיָה מַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה שֶׁבַּנֶּפֶשׁ, שֶׁהֲרֵי לִבּוֹ חָלָל בְּקִרְבּוֹ, שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע בְּתַעֲנִית;
Only that he attained the Yechidah of the Nefesh, having his heart slain within him, killing the inclination through fasting;

פֵּירוּשׁ: הֲרִיגָה בְּתַעֲנִית וְסִגּוּפִין זֶהוּ מִצַּד הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְכֹחַ הָעֲשִׂיָּה שֶׁבַּגּוּף, וְלֹא מִצַּד חָכְמָה וּבִינָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וָלֵב וְעַל יְדֵי הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת בְּגַדְלוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
meaning that slaying it through fasts and afflictions operates via the Nefesh and physical action, rather than through cerebral contemplation of Hashem's greatness.

items.h: The groups named in Nitzavim

p: וּבַזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (פב עַמּוּד א) דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת הֵם מְכֻוָּונוֹת נֶגֶד ה' דַּרְגִּין לִימִינָא וְה' לִשְׂמָאלָא הַנִּזְכָּר בְּפָרָשַׁת "אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים": "רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים כט, ט), מְבוֹאָרִים נֶגֶד ה' מַעֲלוֹת בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנִּזְכָּר:

And in Zohar Yitro 82a the Ten Commandments align with five rungs to the right and five to the left mentioned in Nitzavim: "your heads, etc." (Deuteronomy 29:9), reflecting the five levels of divine perception:
דְּכָל אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים;
all Israel are believers, children of believers;
וְשׁוֹטֵר הוּא מִצַּד הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב;
officers (shoter) reflect the feeling of the heart;
וְזָקֵן – שֶׁקָּנָה חָכְמָה;
elders (zaken)—one who acquired wisdom;
וְרָאשֵׁי שְׁבָטִים הַיְינוּ אֲלָפִים, שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד שׂוֹנְאֵי בָצַע;
heads of tribes are thousands, hating covetousness;
וְרָאשֵׁי כָּל הָעָם הוּא מַדְרֵגַת מֶלֶךְ נֶגֶד יְחִידָה, שֶׁמִּתְיַיחֵד לְגַמְרֵי בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and the heads of the people represent the king, Yechidah, unifying completely with Hashem.
וְלִשְׂמָאלָא הַיְינוּ בְּהַרְחָקַת הָרָע: "טַף" הוּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דַּעַת וְחֶמְדָּה דְּיֵצֶר כְּלָל;
And to the left, in distancing evil: "little ones" (taf) have neither knowledge nor base lust;

וְנָשִׁים – הֲגַם דְּנֶאֱמַר: "אִשָּׁה בְכָל אֵלֶּה לֹא מָצָאתִי" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כח), פֵּירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ הָאָדָם אֶחָד מֵאֶלֶף, דְּהַיְינוּ שַׂר הָאֶלֶף שֶׁהוּא שׂוֹנְאֵי בָצַע, לִהְיוֹת נָקִי מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת לְגַמְרֵי, כִּי זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּנָשִׁים

— and women—though it is said: "a woman among all those have I not found" (Ecclesiastes 7:28), meaning one in a thousand like the captain of a thousand who hates covetousness, pure of all alien thoughts, which is possible only through deep Torah study not mandated for women—

מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז.): הָנֵי נָשֵׁי בְּמַאי זָכְיָין? בְּאַקְרוֹיֵי וְכוּלֵי, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּכֹחָהּ לְהִתְבַּטֵּל לְגַבֵּי הַבַּעַל וְהַבֵּן וּמְבַטֶּלֶת רְצוֹנָהּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ט): אֵיזוֹ אִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁרָה? שֶׁעוֹשָׂה וְכוּלֵי.

nonetheless they said (Berakhot 17a): Whereby do women merit? By sending their sons and husbands to study, having the power to nullify their ego before them, as in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 9: "Who is a worthy woman? She who fulfills the will of her husband."

וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, לט עַמּוּד ב) דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה הַכֹּל נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הַדְּכוּרָא, כִּי הִיא בְּטֵלָה לְגַבֵּיהּ, וְעַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַבִּיטּוּל הֲרֵי בְּכֹחָהּ לְסַלֵּק עַצְמָהּ מִכֹּל וָכֹל.

Therefore Zohar II:39b states that wherever male and female unite all is called by the male name, for she nullifies herself, and through that self-nullification she removes herself from evil entirely.
וְזֶהוּ בִּיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר מִכָּל הַד' מַדְרֵגוֹת, הֲגַם שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַד הַמַּעֲלָה הַה', שֶׁזֶּהוּ הֲכָנָה לַחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, שֶׁזֶּהוּ רַק בְּטַף דְּיֵשׁ בּוֹ הֲכָנָה לָזֶה.
And this is the nullification of the inclination across all four rungs, even if not reaching the fifth which is preparation for the love of Torah, found in children who possess that future potential.
וְ"גֵרְךָ" – יָדוּעַ דְּהֵם מִקְּלִיפַּת נֹגַהּ, וּבְכֹחָם לִהְיוֹת נְקִיִּים מִן הָרָע עַצְמוֹ וְג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת;
And "your stranger" (gerkha)—known to stem from Kelipat Nogah, able to be clean of actual evil and the three impure husks;
אֲבָל לְזַכֵּךְ גַּם דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת וּלְבַטֵּל מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – זֶהוּ רַק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד,
but to refine permitted matters and nullify alien thoughts, which requires Hashem's unique aid, belongs to Israel alone,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת: "אוֹת הִוא בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם" (שְׁמוֹת לא, יג) לְבַד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר פָּרָשַׁת וַיַּקְהֵל (רג עַמּוּד א) דְּאַפֵּיק עֵרֶב רַב מִבֵּינַיְיהוּ בִּנְתִינַת שַׁבָּת.
as with Shabbat: "it is a sign between Me and you" alone, Zohar Vayakhel 203a stating that the mixed multitude was excluded through the giving of Shabbat.

וּ"מֵחֹטֵב [עֵצֶיךָ עַד שֹׁאֵב מֵימֶיךָ]" – הֵם הַנְּתִינִים שֶׁהֵם עֲבָדִים, דְּאִיתָא כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים דִּפְרוּצִים בַּעֲבֵירוֹת וַחֲשׁוּדִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מה:) וּבִפְסָחִים (צא סוֹף עַמּוּד א וְרֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) וּבְגִטִּין (סז:) וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת.

And "from the hewer [of your wood unto the drawer of your water]"—these are the Gibeonites (Netinim) who are slaves, frequently cited as prone to transgressions (Berakhot 45b; Pesachim 91a; Gittin 67b).
וְהַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר בְּנִצָּבִים לִפְנֵי ה' וּנְקִיִּים בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, וּכְאוֹתָם שֶׁנֶּחְשְׁבוּ בְּשֵׁם בְּסֵפֶר נְחֶמְיָה וְעֶזְרָא מִן הַנְּתִינִים וְעַבְדֵי שְׁלֹמֹה,
Yet Scripture speaks of those standing before Hashem, upright in action, like those enumerated by name in Nehemiah and Ezra among the Netinim and servants of Solomon,

וְאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה טז): יֵשׁ שֶׁשְּׁמוֹתֵיהֶם כְּעוּרִים וּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם נָאִים – עוֹלֵי גוֹלָה בְּנֵי סִיסְרָא וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם, וְהֵם מִן הַנְּתִינִים וּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם נָאִים.

of whom the Midrash (Bemidbar Rabbah 16) states: there are those whose names are ugly yet their deeds are beautiful—the returnees from exile, the children of Sisera, etc., who were Netinim of worthy deeds.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא יָצְאוּ גַּם מִג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת כֻּלָּם, דְּלָכֵן אֲסוּרִים לָבוֹא בַּקָּהָל.
Yet they were not freed from all three impure husks, which is why they are forbidden to marry into the congregation.
וְ"חֹטֵב עֵצֶיךָ" הַיְינוּ שֶׁנָּקִי בְּתַאֲוָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, רַק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, שֶׁהֲרֵי אָסוּר לְלַמֵּד עַבְדּוֹ תּוֹרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּתוּבּוֹת כח.).
And the "hewer of your wood" is clean of lust in the heart, but lacks wisdom in the brain, for it is forbidden to teach a slave Torah (Ketubot 28a).

וּמִצַּד שֶׁהוּא דְּכוּרָא וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ חָכְמָה, הוּא שׁוֹפֵעַ בּוֹ לְרַע, דְּלָכֵן אָסוּר לְלַמְּדוֹ תּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ לְאִשָּׁה (סוֹטָה כ.) שֶׁאֵין לָהּ דַּעַת, וְזֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ רַק שֶׁהַחָכְמָה אֵינָהּ מְבוֹרֶרֶת כְּלָל בְּעֶבֶד.

And being male he possesses intellect which would flow into corruption, which is why it is forbidden to teach him Torah, as with a woman (Sotah 20a), who lacks da'at. He does have it, but in a slave the wisdom is not clarified at all.
וְזֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֶבֶד: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ רֹאשׁ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ, רַק אֲדוֹנוֹ הוּא רֹאשׁוֹ, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בֶּן חוֹרִין יֵשׁ לוֹ רֹאשׁ.
And this is the essence of a slave: having no independent head, his master being his head, unlike a freeman who has a head.
וְהִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּת זֶה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִצַּד מַעֲלָתָם עָלָיו בְּתוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה, וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "חֹטֵב עֵצֶיךָ", דְּתוֹרָה נִקְרָא עֵץ הַחַיִּים וּבָזֶה הוּא שִׁימּוּשׁוֹ וְעַבְדוּתוֹ.
And his subjugation to Israel is due to their preeminence in Torah and wisdom, hence called "hewer of your wood," Torah being the Tree of Life wherein his service lies.
וְ"שֹׁאֵב מֵימֶיךָ" – יָדוּעַ דְּמַיִם רוֹמֵז לְחֵשֶׁק וְתַאֲווֹת, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁגַּם הַלֵּב אֵין נָקִי מֵחֶמְדַּת רָע, רַק שֶׁמּוּגְדָּר בְּמַעֲשֶׂה לְבַד;
And "drawer of your water"—water denoting desire, indicating that his heart is not cleansed of base desire, bounded in physical deed alone;

וְהִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּתוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד "מֵימֶיךָ", דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַחֲשָׁקוֹת שֶׁל הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי אֵין דּוֹמֶה לוֹ, דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב).
and his subjugation is relative to "your water," the desires of a Jew being incomparable, for the Holy One is the heart of Israel.

וְהוּא "שֹׁאֵב מֵימֶיךָ", הַיְינוּ רוֹצֶה וּמִשְׁתַּדֵּל שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִבּוֹ כֵּן, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָעַבְדוּת שֶׁהָעֶבֶד נִטְפָּל לָאָדוֹן, אֲבָל מִצִּידּוֹ אֵינוֹ כֵּן; וְ"חֹטֵב עֵצֶיךָ" מִשְׁתַּדֵּל לִהְיוֹת נִטְפָּל לְתוֹרָתְךָ וְחָכְמָתְךָ.
And he draws "your water," striving that his heart resemble theirs, which is the servant's subservience, though of himself he lacks it, while the wood-hewer attaches himself to your Torah and wisdom.
וְאֵלּוּ ה' מַדְרֵגוֹת אֵין מְמַנִּין מֵהֶם שׁוּם הִתְמַנּוּת וּרְאָשׁוּת, כִּי אֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם הִזְדַּכְּכוּת לְטוֹב גָּמוּר וּדְבֵיקוּת בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
And from these five lower rungs no leadership appointments are made, for they lack complete refinement and cleaving to Hashem;

רַק לִשְׂמָאלָא, הַיְינוּ בְּהַגְדָּרָה מֵרָע עַל כָּל פָּנִים עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּלָם לַטּוֹב, שֶׁבְּכֹחָם לְבַטֵּל עַצְמָם לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת מַהוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּלָל, רַק נִטְפָּל לַטּוֹב, כְּעֶבֶד לָאָדוֹן, וְאִשָּׁה לְבַעְלָהּ, וּבֵן לְאָבִיו, וְגֵר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכוּנֶּה, לִהְיוֹת נִטְפָּל וּבָטֵל לָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,

they stand on the left, bounding evil through self-nullification before the good, having the power to nullify their independent existence, serving as subordinates: slave to master, woman to husband, son to father, and convert to Israel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סִפְרֵי בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ סוֹף פִּסְקָא עח) שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁבֶט שֶׁיִּדְבַּק יוּכְלַל בּוֹ, וְהוּא הִתְכַּלְלוּת שְׂמָאלָא בִּימִינָא:
as stated in Sifrei Beha'alotekha (78) that to whichever tribe he attaches he is incorporated, which is the inclusion of the left within the right.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Nitzavim 5: “This is ‘your heads, your tribes … from your woodcutter to your water-drawer.’ A complete stature is counted here, from the greatest in Israel to the least. Where a complete stature is present, a person recognizes that every individual fulfills His will. This resembles the teaching that Yiftach in his generation is like Shmuel in his generation: one who proceeds in divine service recognizes that each fulfills the will and purpose Hashem seeks from him.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef interprets the same list used in this siman, from the leaders through the woodcutters and water-drawers. It emphasizes that the completed stature includes each member's particular service. This helps distinguish the present classification of spiritual capacities and appointments from the separate question of belonging to the covenantal whole; one member's role need not be identical to another's for both to participate in its completion.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 17a:14-15: “Rav said to Rabbi Hiyya: ‘Through what do women gain merit?’ Through having their children read in the synagogue, having their husbands study in the house of the Sages, and waiting for their husbands until they return from the house of the Sages. May your lips pour forth knowledge, your inner parts rejoice in uprightness, and your steps run to hear the words of the Ancient of Days.’”

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 16:10: ““These were the names of the men” (Numbers 13:16). What were their names? They were “Setur son of Mikhael…Naḥbi son of Vofsi…Geuel son of Makhi” (Numbers 13:13–15). There are people whose names are pleasant but their actions are repulsive; their names are repulsive but their actions are pleasant; their names are pleasant and their actions are pleasant; their names and their actions are repulsive. Whose names are pleasant but their actions are repulsive: This is Ishmael and Esau. Ishmael – God listens [shome’a el]; Esau – he performs [oseh] the will of his Maker [osehu]. Their names are repulsive but their actions are pleasant: These are those who ascended from the exile: “The children of Barkos, the children of Sisera, the children of Tamaḥ” (Ezra 2:53). paragraphs.text: Sifrei Bamidbar 78:3: ““To the place of which the Lord said, ‘I will give it to you’”—converts have no share in it. How, then, do I fulfill “In the tribe with which the convert resides”? If it does not refer to inheritance, apply it to atonement: if he is in the tribe of Judah, he receives atonement with the tribe of Judah; if in the tribe of Benjamin, with the tribe of Benjamin. Another interpretation: If it does not refer to inheritance, apply it to burial; converts are granted burial in the Land of Israel. “Come with us and we will do good to you”—is there a member of a person’s household to whom one does not do good? The matter follows all the more strongly: if one does good to a member of a person’s household, how much more to a member of the household of the One who spoke and the world came into being. “For the Lord has spoken good concerning Israel”—has no good been spoken concerning Israel until now? The Lord has always spoken good concerning Israel. The Omnipresent commanded Israel to do good to converts and to treat them with humility.”

sections.en: All Elevation and Authority Derive Through Words of Torah

p: [רלא] כָּל הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת וּשְׂרָרָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ח, טו).
All elevation and authority derive through words of Torah, as it is written: "By me kings reign" (Proverbs 8:15).
וְלָכֵן סָמוּךְ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה וּבְאוֹתָהּ פָּרָשָׁה נֶאֱמַר הִתְמַנּוּת הָרָאשִׁים.
And therefore adjacent to the Giving of the Torah, within that very portion, the appointment of the leaders was related.

וְהָיָה זֶה עַל יְדֵי יִתְרוֹ, דְּבֶאֱמֶת נֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית אֵין יָכוֹל לִסְבּוֹל הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת כְּלָל, אֲפִילּוּ מִן הַגָּדוֹל בְּחָכְמָה, לְפִי שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב" (דְּבָרִים לג, ד),

And this was introduced through Jethro, for in truth the Jewish soul cannot tolerate arrogance or lordly elevation at all, even from the greatest in wisdom, because all Israel possess a portion in the Torah: "an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob" (Deuteronomy 33:4),

כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר הַהוּא עַם הָאָרֶץ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשַׁת צַו פָּרָשָׁה ט), וְכַנּוֹדָע דְּכָל אֶחָד אֲחִיזָתוֹ בְּאוֹת מֵהַתּוֹרָה, וְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁחָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת פָּסוּל, וְאִם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁזֶּה צָרִיךְ לָזֶה, כָּךְ צָרִיךְ זֶה לָזֶה.

as that unlearned man challenged Rabbi Yannai in Vayikra Rabbah 9:3; and as is known, every Jew has a hold in a letter of the Torah, and a Torah scroll lacking a single letter is invalid, so just as this one needs that one, that one needs this one.
וְהֲגַם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל זֶה הַקָּטָן כְּלוּם.
And even though a great sage has a larger portion in Torah, he knows nothing of the unique portion belonging to the smallest individual.

וְזֶה טַעַם (תַּעֲנִית ז.): "וּמִתַּלְמִידַי יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם", כִּי רַב אֵין לָאָדָם רַק אֶחָד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.): כָּל הַלּוֹמֵד תּוֹרָה מֵרַב אֶחָד וְכוּלֵי, גְּמָרָא מֵרַב אֶחָד עָדִיף;

And this explains: "and from my disciples more than from all of them" (Ta'anit 7a), for a person has only one master, as it says (Avodah Zarah 19a): "Whoever learns Torah from one teacher, etc." For received teaching (gemara), one teacher is preferable;
וַאֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ יוֹתֵר, מִכָּל מָקוֹם חֲבֵירִים מְרוּבִּים יוֹתֵר כַּנּוֹדָע, וְתַלְמִידִים יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם דִּלְזֶה אֵין קֵץ,
and even if he has more, colleagues are far more numerous, and disciples most numerous of all without end,
וְהוּא קוֹלֵט כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּכָל אֶחָד שֶׁאֵין נִמְצָא בּוֹ, וְנִמְצָא לָמַד מֵהֶם יוֹתֵר לְרִבּוּיָם.
and he absorbs the Torah insights within each disciple that he lacked, learning more from them through their sheer number.
וְטַעֲנַת קֹרַח: "מַדּוּעַ תִּתְנַשְּׂאוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טז, ג) אֲמִיתִּית, דְּאֵין לְהִתְנַשְּׂאוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת.
And Korah's claim: "Why do you lift yourselves up, etc." (Numbers 16:3) was conceptually true in asserting that genuine arrogance is invalid.
וְהֲגַם דְּגַם הוּא בִּקֵּשׁ כְּהֻנָּה גְּדוֹלָה, וְאִם כֵּן סוֹתֵר דַּעַת עַצְמוֹ;
And although he also sought the High Priesthood, contradicting his own stance;

רַק כַּוָּנָתוֹ: וַדַּאי צָרִיךְ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְזֶה מְיוּחָד לִהְיוֹת שְׁלִיחָא דְּרַחֲמָנָא לִכְנוֹס לְקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מְיוּחָד לְקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה, וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מְיוּחָד לְאֵיזֶה דָּבָר וְאֵין לְהִתְנַשְּׂאוֹת עָלָיו.

yet his argument was: certainly a High Priest is needed as Heaven's emissary into the Holy of Holies, and Moses was designated to receive the Torah, but likewise every Jew is designated for a unique task and none should lord over another.
שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא צֹרֶךְ בַּתּוֹרָה, כָּךְ הוּא צֹרֶךְ;
For just as this one is necessary for the Torah, so is that one;

כֵּיוָן שֶׁבְּחֶסְרוֹן אוֹת אַחַת נִפְסָל, הָוֵי כְּמוֹ אֵבָרִים שֶׁבְּחֶסְרוֹנָן נִטְרַף, וְאֵין לְהִתְעַלּוֹת זֶה עַל זֶה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּה לְמַעְלָה וְזֶה לְמַטָּה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם זֶה צֹרֶךְ לְשִׁימּוּשׁ הַגּוּף כְּמוֹ זֶה.

since by lacking a single letter the scroll is invalid, they resemble bodily organs without which life fails, none boasting over another—even if one is higher and one lower, each is essential for the body.
וְזֶה טַעֲנַת אוֹתוֹ חוֹפֵר שִׁיחִין לְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בַּמִּדְרָשׁ, שֶׁגַּם הוּא עוֹסֵק בְּצָרְכֵי צִבּוּר;
And this was the argument of the well-digger to Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai in the Midrash, that he too served communal needs;
רַק הוּא הֱשִׁיבוֹ שֶׁאֵין זֶה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְשׁוֹן הוֹרָאָה לַאֲחֵרִים, וְהוּא אֵין יָכוֹל לְהוֹרוֹת לַאֲחֵרִים שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ לִשְׁאוֹל, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
but he replied that digging is not Torah, for Torah denotes halakhic instruction, and he could not instruct those coming to inquire.
וּמִצַּד זֶה הוּא הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם עַל עַם הָאָרֶץ, מִשּׁוּם דִּבְעַם הָאָרֶץ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלּוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל, וְהַגָּלוּי רַק מִצְווֹת, וְתַלְמוּד גָּדוֹל.
And from this stems the functional authority of a scholar over an unlearned person, because in the latter his Torah is deeply hidden, only mitzvot being manifest, and study is greater.
וְזֶה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר שֶׁהָיוּ דּוֹר דֵּעָה וְכֻלָּם קְדוֹשִׁים, וּבְתוֹכָם בִּפְנִימִיּוּתָם שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא קַו אֶמְצָעִי הַמַּבְרִיחַ בְּכָל קַצְוֵי הַבְּרִיאָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
And this did not apply to the Generation of the Wilderness who were a generation of knowledge, all holy, harboring within them the Name Havayah, the Central Column traversing all creation.
רַק עוֹנְשָׁם הָיוּ דִּבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא הִתְנַשְּׂאוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יב, ג).
Rather, they were punished because in truth [Moses and Aaron] did not exalt themselves, as it is written: "And the man Moses was very humble" (Numbers 12:3).
רַק הַגָּוֶון שֶׁל הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת זֶה צָרִיךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהֲרֵי הִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יְדֵי יִתְרוֹ,
But the outward appearance of hierarchy is necessary in this world, the Holy One having consented through Jethro,
דִּבְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֶחָד צָרִיךְ לַחֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁגָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ בְּחָכְמָה.
for in this world one needs his fellow who is greater in wisdom.

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Tefillin, Mezuzah and the Torah Scroll 10:1: “You thus learn that there are twenty defects, any one of which invalidates a Torah scroll. If any one of them occurs in it, it is like one of the books of the Torah used to teach children: it does not have the sanctity of a Torah scroll and may not be read publicly. They are: 1. It was written on the hide of an unclean animal. 2. It was written on the hide of a clean animal that was not processed. 3. The hide was processed without the intention that it be used for a Torah scroll. 4. It was written on the wrong writing surface: on the flesh side of whole hide, or on the hair side of parchment. 5. Part of it was written on whole hide and part on parchment. 6. It was written on the inner layer of split hide. 7. It was written without ruled lines. 8. It was written without lasting black ink. 9. It was written in other languages. 10. It was written by a heretic or a similarly disqualified person. 11. The divine names were written without the proper intention. 12. Even a single letter was omitted. 13. Even a single letter was added. 14. One letter touches another. 15. The form of a single letter was spoiled so that it cannot be read at all or resembles another letter, whether in the original writing, through a hole or tear, or through smearing. 16. The space between letters was increased or decreased so that one word appears as two words, or two words as one word. 17. The arrangement of the sections was changed. 18. The arrangement of the songs was changed. 19. Other portions of the text were written in the arrangement of a song. 20. The sheets were sewn with something other than sinews of a clean animal. The remaining requirements are for proper fulfillment, but their absence does not invalidate the scroll.”

paragraphs.text: Peace joins portions of Torah that no single learner possesses alone

rich.text: Peace joins portions of Torah that no single learner possesses alone

paragraphs.text: The good of peace is a joined completeness, distinct from the increased wisdom that a productive dispute may generate.

rich.text: The good of peace is a joined completeness, distinct from the increased wisdom that a productive dispute may generate.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Chalomot 2:1: “I dreamt that the plain meaning was this: sometimes there is contention of the kind described as “The rivalry of scholars increases wisdom” (Bava Batra 21a), and a dispute for the sake of Heaven that is beneficial and from which good things may grow [although Shemot Rabbah, chapter 30, says: “No good thing and no peace emerge from contention”; end of quotation]. But this particular good of peace [which is the joining of completeness and the vessel that holds blessing: an individual cannot be complete in everything; only through their unity is there a joining of all completeness. Shalom, “peace,” has the root shalem, “complete,” and the added letter vav indicates connection everywhere] cannot emerge from contention, even when it is good and for the sake of Heaven.”

But this particular good of peace [which is the joining of completeness and the vessel that holds blessing: an individual cannot be complete in everything; only through their unity is there a joining of all completeness. Shalom, “peace,” has the root shalem, “complete,” and the added letter vav indicates connection everywhere] cannot emerge from contention, even when it is good and for the sake of Heaven.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Divrei Chalomot distinguishes the good gained through rivalry in learning from the particular good called peace. Peace joins contributions that are individually incomplete. This illuminates the present siman’s insistence that even a great scholar lacks the smallest person’s unique portion of Torah. The need for teachers and functional authority in this world remains, but it gives no ground for contempt: no size of one person’s portion makes another’s portion dispensable.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 19a:19-19b:1: “Rav Chisda said to the Sages: I wish to tell you something, but I fear that you will leave me and go. Anyone who learns Torah from only one teacher never sees a sign of blessing. They left him and went before Rava. He said to them: This applies to reasoning; but for the received teaching, one teacher is preferable, so that the formulations will not conflict.”

paragraphs.text: Kohelet Rabbah 4:17:1: “Shimon Sikhna, a man of counsel, used to dig pits, channels, and caves in Jerusalem. He said to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Zakkai: “I am as great as you.” He asked him: “Why?” He replied: “Because I attend to the needs of the public, as you do.” He said: “If someone comes to you for judgment or a legal question, do you say to him, ‘Drink from this cistern, whose waters are clear and cool’? Or if a woman asks you about her menstrual status, do you say to her, ‘Immerse in this cistern, whose waters purify’?” He applied this verse to him: “Drawing near to listen is better than fools offering a sacrifice, for they do not know how to do evil.””

items.h: Hidden Torah and future revelation

p: וְרַק לֶעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר: "וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד... כִּי כֻלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי" (יִרְמְיָה לא, לג), אֲפִילּוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ יֵצֵא הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַגָּנוּז אֶצְלָם מִן הַהֶעְלֵם.
And only in the future is it said: "and they shall teach no more... for they shall all know Me" (Jeremiah 31:33), when even the unlearned will have their hidden Torah drawn out of concealment.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה יֵשׁ סוֹדוֹת וְסִתְרֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְגַלּוֹתָם שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹאוּ לִידֵי קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ מִפְּנֵי הַיֵּצֶר
For in this world there are mystical secrets of Torah that cannot be revealed lest people fall into levity through the inclination
[עַיֵּין בְּסֵפֶר בְּרִית מְנוּחָה כָּתַב כֵּן עַל מָאוֹר אֶחָד, דְּאִלּוּ יָדְעוּ תָּקְפּוֹ אֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא לִידֵי קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ, וְזֶהוּ טַעַם: אֵין דּוֹרְשִׁין וְכוּלֵי],
see Brit Menuchah writing regarding a certain light that were its power known, people might treat it lightly, which explains: we do not expound the Chariot, etc.,
וְכֵן יֵשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם נִסְתָּר מִטַּעַם זֶה, וְהֵם בִּלְבוּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ;
and so there are souls whose Torah is concealed for this reason, appearing in this world clothed as commoners;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיְּבוּטַּל יֵצֶר הָרָע יִתְגַּלֶּה הַכֹּל, וְ"לֹא יְלַמְּדוּ וְגוֹמֵר".
but when the inclination is abolished all will be revealed, and "they shall teach no more, etc."

וְרַק יִתְרוֹ שֶׁהָיָה גֵּר הִרְגִּישׁ דָּבָר זֶה, שֶׁגַּם לֶעָתִיד אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צח וְתַנְחוּמָא שָׁם) שֶׁמָּשִׁיחַ יְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה לַגּוֹיִם שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְנָהֲרוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה ב, ב), כִּי הֵם אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק מְיוּחָד בַּתּוֹרָה, מַה שֶּׁ[יֵּשׁ] לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.

And Jethro, being a convert, perceived this, for in the future too our Sages said (Bereishit Rabbah 98 and Tanchuma there) that the Messiah will teach Torah to gentiles who will convert: "and all nations shall flow unto it" (Isaiah 2:2), having no innate individual portion in Torah like Israel.
וּלְכָךְ אֶצְלָם שַׁפִּיר שַׁיָּיךְ עִנְיַן הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת.
Therefore among them hierarchy is fully applicable.
וְכֵן יֵשׁ עִנְיַן עֶבֶד בְּגוֹי, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: "עֲבָדַי הֵם וְכוּלֵי" (וַיִּקְרָא כה, מב), רַק עֶבֶד עִבְרִי לְשָׁעָה כְּעִנְיַן הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And so perpetual slavery exists for a gentile, but not for a Jew: "For they are My servants" (Leviticus 25:42), a Hebrew slave being temporary like worldly hierarchy,

וְגַם זֶה רַק בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲרָכִין כט.), שֶׁאָז גַּם גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נוֹהֵג (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם), שֶׁעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵר שֶׁבַע מִצְווֹת לְבַד גַּם הוּא קָרוּי גֵּר.
and even that only when the Jubilee applies (Arachin 29a), when a resident alien (ger toshav) also applies, a gentile observing seven Noahide laws being termed a ger.

לְעֻמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגַת עַבְדוּת וְשִׁעְבּוּד, וְגַם כֵּן קָרוּי יִשְׂרָאֵל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרְשׁוּת אָדוֹן עָלָיו, דְּזֶהוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם לב:) מִכִּבּוּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן דִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁהָיָה כִּבּוּשׁ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבַד, שֶׁלֹּא קִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כְּלָל.

Corresponding to this, in Israel there was a status of servitude where one remained a Jew despite a master's authority, lasting while all its inhabitants were upon the Land (Arachin 32b) from Joshua's conquest, which was a temporal conquest not sanctifying for the ultimate future.

אֲבָל מֵעֵת גָּלוּת רִאשׁוֹן דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים וּבָטְלָה כְּבִישָׁה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, אָז הֵחֵל צְמִיחַת גְּאוּלָּה וּכְבִישָׁה שְׁנִיָּה, כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי א, נא) וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת (פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד) דִּבְאוֹתוֹ יוֹם נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ.

But from the first exile of the Ten Tribes when the first conquest lapsed, the dawn of redemption and the second eternal conquest commenced (Eichah Rabbah 1:51; Yerushalmi Berakhot 2:4) when the Messiah was born.

וּמְכֻוָּון לְמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צד.): בִּקֵּשׁ לַעֲשׂוֹת חִזְקִיָּהוּ מָשִׁיחַ, דְּתֵיכֶף הִתְחִיל נְבִיעַת אוֹתוֹ אוֹר לָעוֹלָם, וְנִסְתַּלֵּק הָעַבְדוּת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְנִתְבַּטֵּל גַּם כֵּן קַבָּלַת גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב מֵאֻמּוֹת,
And this aligns with Sanhedrin 94a: He sought to make Hezekiah the Messiah, for that light began welling up, servitude departing from Israel and the acceptance of a resident alien lapsing,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בַּגְּמָרָא דְּגֵר עַמּוֹנִי בִּבְרָכוֹת (כח.), שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְבָּרֵר עִנְיַן יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר, אָז גַּם עִנְיַן הָעַכּוּ"ם מִתְבָּרֵר וְנִבְדָּל יוֹתֵר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
as in the Ammonite convert in Berakhot 28a: as Israel's distinct essence is clarified, the nations become separated from Israel.
וְלָכֵן אֵין נְקֻדַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל סוֹבֶלֶת שִׁעְבּוּד וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת כְּלָל, אֲפִילּוּ עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
Therefore the essential core of Israel cannot tolerate subjugation or lordly superiority at all, even through Torah.
וּלְכָךְ קָרֵי לַהּ הַזֹּהַר עַל יִתְרוֹ (סח סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): "מִלֵּי דִּהֶדְיוֹטָא", כִּי מַאֲמַר יִתְרוֹ לִהְיוֹת שָׂרִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָן זֶהוּ אֵינוֹ אֱמֶת גָּמוּר וּמִילֵּי דִּהֶדְיוֹט.
Therefore the Zohar (Yitro 68b) terms Jethro's counsel "common words" (milei de-hedyota), for establishing rulers over Israel themselves is not ultimate truth, but mundane perspective.

וְהֲגַם דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִסְכִּים וְנִכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא נִצְחִיִּית, זֶהוּ לְגַבֵּי הָאֻמּוֹת: הֵם יַשִּׂיגוּ לֶעָתִיד גַּם כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מַדְרֵגוֹת שָׂרֵי אֲלָפִים וְכוּלֵי כְּפִי מַעֲלָתָם בַּתּוֹרָה,
And though Hashem consented and inscribed it in the eternal Torah, that applies relative to the nations: they will perceive in Israel tiers of rulers according to Torah stature,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָאַחֵר מַרְגִּישׁ בְּהַבִּיטוֹ עַל אֵיזֶה אָדָם יִתְרוֹן בָּרֹאשׁ עַל הָרֶגֶל, אֲבָל הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ כָּךְ יַכְאִיב לוֹ כְּשֶׁיַּכּוּ הָרֶגֶל כְּמוֹ הָרֹאשׁ.
just as an onlooker beholding a man perceives the head higher than the foot, yet to the man himself an injury to the foot pains him just as much as to the head.
וְגַם לֶעָתִיד אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּפִי הַשָּׂגַת יִתְרוֹ וּשְׁאָר גֵּרִים.
And in the future this applies only according to the comprehension of Jethro and other converts.
רַק דְּ"מִלֵּי דִּהֶדְיוֹטָא" – מִלֵּי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִרְאֶה כֵּן הַגָּוֶון גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָן,
But "common words" means that in this world this outward appearance seems necessary even within Israel,
שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְבָּרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכָּל הָעַכּוּ"ם, צְרִיכִים לְהִתְנַהֵג כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בַּגָּוֶון לְעֵינֵי הַהֶדְיוֹטוֹת:
for as long as Israel has not been completely separated from all the nations, they must conduct themselves according to this external structure before the eyes of the common world.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Berakhot 27b:3: “The Rabbis taught: A student came before Rabbi Yehoshua and asked him, “Is the evening prayer optional or obligatory?” The evening prayer means crying out and calling to God over Israel’s suffering in exile. He asked “optional or obligatory”: is one obliged to pray because “in all their distress He is distressed,” or is it optional, since at present, before the true clarification is completed, nothing has yet been fully clarified, and therefore prayer is not obligatory? When an Ammonite convert came before them and it was ruled that he could enter the congregation, this was because the clarification was not yet complete. For converts are not accepted in the days of the Messiah; their present acceptance is because the clarification is unfinished and there are still holy sparks that must be gathered. Therefore, at present the ruling is that the evening prayer is optional; in the future, however, it will be obligatory, because the union will then be complete and their suffering will touch the Holy One, blessed be He.”

Therefore, at present the ruling is that the evening prayer is optional; in the future, however, it will be obligatory, because the union will then be complete and their suffering will touch the Holy One, blessed be He.”

sections.en: All Affairs of the World and All Created Beings Remind a Person That There…

p: [רלב] כָּל עִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם וְכָל הַנִּבְרָאִים מַזְכִּירִים לָאָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא,
All affairs of the world and all created beings remind a person that there is a Creator,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ו:): כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁיֵּדַע זֶה עַל יָדָהּ וְיַכִּיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא עוֹלָם;
as stated in Berakhot 6b: the entire world was created solely for the sake of this one, meaning so that through it he should know this and recognize that there is a Creator of the universe;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ קִנְיָנֶךָ" (תְּהִלִּים קד, כד), פֵּירוּשׁ לִקְנוֹת עַל יָדָם אוֹתְךָ.
and as I heard on "the earth is full of Your creations (kinyanecha)" (Psalms 104:24), meaning to acquire (liknot) You through them.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לָאָדָם בְּכָל יוֹם דְּבָרִים וְעִנְיָנִים שׁוֹנִים, אוּלַי עַל יָדָם יָבוֹא לִזְכִירָה בַּבּוֹרֵא.
And the Blessed Name orchestrates for a person daily various events and circumstances, so that perhaps through them he will come to remember the Creator.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַהַצָּלָה מִשִּׁכְחָה זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם, דְּלָכֵן לֹא נֶאֱמַר "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר" בִּלְשׁוֹן צִוּוּי, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַוּוֹת עַל הַיְדִיעָה דְּאָנֹכִי שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכַּח.

For in truth, being saved from forgetfulness is not within human power alone, which is why "I am, etc." was not stated as an imperative command, since it is impossible to command regarding the cognitive knowledge of "I am" that one not forget.
שֶׁצִּוּוּי הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁבְּיַד הָאָדָם לְקַיְּמוֹ, וּכְשֶׁשּׁוֹכֵחַ הֲרֵי הוּא שָׁכַח מִזֶּה וְשָׁכַח גַּם מֵהַמִּצְוָה;
For a command applies only to what is in human hands to execute, whereas when one forgets, he has forgotten the reality and forgotten the mitzvah as well;
רַק צָרִיךְ לְסַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא, וְהַסַּיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא הוּא עַל יְדֵי "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ וְגוֹמֵר".
rather one requires Heavenly assistance, and that Heavenly assistance comes through "You shall have no other gods, etc."

פֵּירוּשׁ, "אֱלֹהִים" – כֹּחַ וִיכֹלֶת בְּכָל מָקוֹם, וְהַיְינוּ בְּכָל שִׁימּוּשׁוֹ בְּכֹחוֹתָיו, בְּאֵיזֶה כֹּחַ מִכֹּחוֹת הַגּוּף: רְאִיָּה אוֹ שְׁמִיעָה אוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה אוֹ הִילוּךְ וְכַיּוֹצֵא, יַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה.

Meaning, elohim signifies power and ability everywhere, so that in all use of his faculties—in any bodily power: sight, hearing, physical action, walking, or the like—he must recognize that the Blessed Name is the One granting him this power.
וְזֶה טַעַם הַבְּרָכָה לִפְנֵי כָּל הֲנָאָה, וּבְלֹא בְּרָכָה – מָעַל (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרָכוֹת לה.);
And this is the reason for a blessing before every physical pleasure, where without a blessing one commits sacrilege (Berakhot 35a);
שֶׁהֲרֵי בֶּאֱמֶת קָדְשֵׁי שָׁמַיִם הוּא וְכֹחוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְלֹא הוּתַּר אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְשֶׁהוּא הַנּוֹתֵן.
for in truth it is consecrated to Heaven and constitutes Hashem's powers, becoming permitted only through recognizing that it is from Hashem and that He is the Giver.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם מ:): "לֹא עָבַרְתִּי מִמִּצְוֹתֶיךָ" – בִּבְרָכָה, "וְלֹא שָׁכַחְתִּי" – בְּהַזְכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם;
And this is what they expounded (ibid. 40b): "'I have not transgressed Your commandments'—in blessing; 'neither have I forgotten'—in mentioning the divine Name";
דִּשְׁנֵי אֵלֶּה "אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה" שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה בְּמִצְווֹת וַעֲבֵירוֹת.
for these two, "I am" and "You shall have no," are the root of the Torah in positive commandments and negative prohibitions.
וּסְתָם שִׁכְחָה הוּא שִׁכְחָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶהוּ בְּבִטּוּל "אָנֹכִי".
And standard forgetfulness is forgetting the Blessed Name, which is the neglect of "I am."

וּסְתָם עֲבֵירָה שֶׁבְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ הַיְינוּ שֶׁלּוֹקֵחַ הֲנָאָתוֹ וּצְרָכָיו וּמִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּכֹחוֹתָיו בִּלְעֲדֵי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּהַיְינוּ הֲשָׁבַת מִקּוֹדֶם לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁנָּתַן לוֹ הֲנָאָה זוֹ וְכֹחַ זֶה.

And standard transgression across the entire Torah means taking one's pleasures and needs and employing his faculties detached from Hashem's will, without first tracing back to Him that He granted this pleasure and faculty.
וְזֶהוּ כָּל עִנְיַן עֲבֵירָה וּרְמִיזוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הַשסָּ"ה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
And this is the inner core of sin and the esoteric allusions of all 365 negative prohibitions.
וְדָבָר זֶה בְּיַד הָאָדָם לִהְיוֹת בְּשֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה.
And this is within human power through passive restraint ("sit and do not do").
וְכַאֲשֶׁר מִתְעוֹרֵר לִפְעֻלָּה וְשִׁימּוּשׁ שֶׁהוּא הִתְעוֹרְרוּת גּוּפָנִי, אָז יִתְעוֹרֵר בְּנִשְׁמָתוֹ גַּם כֵּן לָדַעַת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרְרוֹ בְּכֹחַ זֶה,
And when one is stirred to action and use, which is a bodily awakening, let him also awaken in his soul to know that Hashem stirs him through this power,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָבוֹא לִהְיוֹת "אָנֹכִי" קָבוּעַ בַּלֵּב וְקַיָּימָא תָּמִיד, לֹא יָזוּז רֶגַע אֶחָד.
and through this "I am" will become permanently fixed in the heart, enduring continually without budging for a single moment.

וְזֶהוּ תַּקָּנַת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת עַל כָּל דִּבְרֵי הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף: בְּמָזוֹן, וּבִרְאִיָּה, וּבִשְׁמִיעָה כְּקוֹל תַּרְנְגוֹל, וּבִבְשׂוֹרוֹת טוֹבוֹת וּלְהֵיפֶךְ, וּבְמַלְבּוּשָׁיו וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
And this is the ordinance of our Sages in blessings over all bodily pleasures: food, sight, hearing like the rooster's crow, good tidings and their opposite, garments, and the like.
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הַשַּׁ"ס שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ,
And this is the opening of the Talmud (Tractate Berakhot), which is the root of the entire Torah,

כִּפְתִיחַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בְּ"אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה", שֶׁזֶּהוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ, וְאִידַּךְ פֵּירוּשָׁא זִיל גְּמוֹר: עֵצוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת בְּכָל זְמַן וּבְכָל מָקוֹם אֵיךְ לָבוֹא לִזְכִירָה זוֹ.

mirroring the opening of the Written Torah with "I am" and "You shall have no," which encapsulate the whole Torah, the rest being commentary—go and learn: various counsels for every time and place how to attain this remembrance.
אֲבָל הַמְּכֻוָּון בְּכֻלָּם הוּא יְדִיעַת הָאֱלֹהוּת, שֶׁלֹּא יָזוּז מִן הַלֵּב וְלֹא יִשְׁלוֹט בּוֹ הַשִּׁכְחָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם:
But the ultimate aim in all of them is the knowledge of Godliness, that it never depart from the heart and forgetfulness hold no dominion over it, Heaven forbid.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Machshavot Charutz 11:4: “Thus I received: the entire world is a book Hashem made. I recall that in my youth I saw [Me’or Einayim] by HaAdomi, citing a book attributed to Chanoch among the nations, and it seems to me that there was some trace of this there: that all the creatures of the world are forms of letters Hashem engraved in His world, which is His book. The Torah is the explanation He made and composed for that book. These are words of truth, for Torah is an offshoot of the letters of thought themselves, embodied and clothed in the forms of written letters, whereas the world is only a trace and indication. Through Torah one can understand the hints contained in that trace and indication in deeds, corresponding to what is in His thought. Nevertheless, all the deeds and creatures of the entire world form a complete book in which He engraved all the letters of thought in great concealment. No creature or created being fails to indicate a particular matter and meaning in His thought. “He did not create it for emptiness”; everything has a particular purpose, for His praise and to reveal the glory of Heaven. As Rabbi Baruch wrote on “the earth is full of Your acquisitions”: it means how to acquire and apprehend Him, blessed be He.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Machshavot Charutz describes the world as Hashem’s book and Torah as its explanation. This supplies an important qualification to the siman’s account of encounters that awaken remembrance: the world bears a concealed trace, while Torah teaches how that trace can be understood. Its reminders are therefore joined to learning and the disciplined practice of berachos, rather than arbitrary private interpretations of events. Title clarification: the book abbreviation M.E. refers to Me’or Einayim by Azariah de Rossi (HaAdomi). The supplied Hebrew expands it incorrectly as mitzvot aseh, positive commandments; the translation marks the corrected title in square brackets.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Pesach 30:1: “Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world is so that a person should derive from it instruction for serving the Lord, for He created everything for His glory. As was said in the name of the holy master of Peshischa, of blessed memory, concerning the name Shaddai, “who said to His world: Enough”: it is sufficient for learning to recognize the blessed God. When our father Abraham, of blessed memory, came and saw a palace ablaze, he wondered: Is it possible for the palace to have no governor? Until the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to him and said: “I am the owner of the palace,” as stated in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 39. He explained through this the verse “The earth is full of Your possessions”: the whole earth is filled with acquisitions through which a person may acquire knowledge of the blessed God and of what the blessed God wants from him. Everything that comes before a person’s eyes has been deliberately brought before him by particular providence, so that he should learn from it.”

rich.text: : “Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world is so that a person should derive from it instruction for serving the Lord, for He created everything for His glory. As was said in the name of the holy master of Peshischa, of blessed memory, concerning the name Shaddai, “who said to His world: Enough”: it is sufficient for learning to recognize the blessed God. When our father Abraham, of blessed memory, came and saw a palace ablaze, he wondered: Is it possible for the palace to have no governor? Until the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to him and said: “I am the owner of the palace,” as stated in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 39. He explained through this the verse “The earth is full of Your possessions”: the whole earth is filled with acquisitions through which a person may acquire knowledge of the blessed God and of what the blessed God wants from him. Everything that comes before a person’s eyes has been deliberately brought before him by particular providence, so that he should learn from it.”

sections.en: To Be Saved from Alien Thoughts and Musings Outside Hashem's Will All Day Long…

p: [רלג] לְהִנָּצֵל מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת וְהִרְהוּר שֶׁחוּץ מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל הַיּוֹם – זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁנָּקִי לְגַמְרֵי מִנְּגִיעָה לְגוּפוֹ.
To be saved from alien thoughts and musings outside Hashem's will all day long is impossible, except for one entirely cleansed of bodily self-interest.

וְהַיְינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר כְּבָר הֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע כְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וּמַאן דְּנָצַח בִּקְרָבָא יְהִיבִין לֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי צְלוֹתָא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר סוֹף תִּיקּוּן יג);
That is, when one has already slain his evil inclination like King David, where he who triumphs in battle is given the daughter of the King, which is prayer (Tikkunei Zohar 13);

כִּי מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת כָּל הַיּוֹם, לֹא יִמָּלֵט גַּם כֵּן מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת בִּתְפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קסד:) דְּעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה אֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל, וּמַשְׁמָע דְּעַל כָּל אָדָם קָאָמַר.

for one who is not clean of alien thoughts throughout the day will not escape alien thoughts during prayer either, as stated in Bava Batra 164b that from calculating expectation in prayer no man is saved, implying every person.

וְאָתָאן דִּבְרֵי הַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז:): "אֲנָא מִן יוֹמָא לָא כַּוְּונִית" כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהִמָּלֵט בְּכָל הַתְּפִלָּה כֻּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם נִצְנוּץ מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה.

And this brings us back to the Yerushalmi cited by Tosafot (Rosh Hashanah 16b): "In all my days I never achieved full concentration," according to its literal sense, that it was impossible to escape throughout the entire prayer from some spark of extraneous thought.

וּמַחְשֶׁבֶת "מַאן עָיֵיל קַמֵּי מַלְכָּא וְכוּלֵי" הוּא מַחְשֶׁבֶת כָּבוֹד, מִצַּד נְגִיעָה לְכָבוֹד נִכְנַס מַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ בְּיוֹמָא דְּבָעֵי כַּוָּנוֹת, שֶׁהֵכִין עַצְמוֹ כַּחֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים שׁוֹהִים וְכוּלֵי שֶׁיְּכַוְּונוּ וְכוּלֵי (בְּרָכוֹת ל:),

And the thought "who enters first before the king" was a thought of honor: from a subtle bias toward honor this thought entered on the day he sought deep concentration, having prepared like the early pious ones who waited an hour to direct their hearts (Berakhot 30b),

פֵּירוּשׁ יְיַשְּׁרוּ הַלֵּב שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ שׁוּם נְגִיעָה וְרָצוֹן זוּלַת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאוּלַי בְּשָׁעָה זוֹ יַעַזְרֵהוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְנַצֵּחַ בַּקְּרָב וּלְבַטֵּל הַיֵּצֶר מִקִּרְבּוֹ.
meaning to align the heart free of any personal motive other than Hashem's will, hoping that in that hour Hashem would help him conquer the battle and nullify the inclination from within him.
וּמַחְשֶׁבֶת מְנִית פַּרְחַיָּא וְדָמוֹסְיָא, שֶׁהוּא הִרְהוּרִים דִּרְכוּשׁוֹ, הוּא מִצַּד נְגִיעָה דְּתַאֲוַת מָמוֹן.
And the thought of counting chicks or building stones, reflecting musings over his property, stemmed from a subtle attachment to financial desire.
וּ"מַחֲזִיקְנָא טִיבוּתָא לְרֵישָׁא וְכוּלֵי", דְּמִצַּד הַקִּנְאָה בָּא מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה בְּעֵת "מוֹדִים" שֶׁהוּא הַהוֹדָאָה עַל חַסְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
And "I give thanks to my head that bows on its own"—for out of envy an alien thought enters during Modim, which is thanksgiving over Hashem's mercies;
וְהַמְקַנֵּא הֲרֵי חָסֵר וְאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל טוֹבוֹתָיו, אַדְּרַבָּה מִתְרָעֵם עַל שֶׁנּוֹתֵן טוֹבָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ.
and one who envies feels deficient and does not thank Hashem for His goodness, rather resenting that He bestows favor upon his fellow.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (טז.): שִׁדְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּלָא כָּרַע בְּמוֹדִים, דִּרְקַב עֲצָמוֹת קִנְאָה (מִשְׁלֵי יד, ל), וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ הוּא קִנְאָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נט:) רָאָה וְכוּלֵי וְנִתְקַנֵּא.

And this is why Bava Kamma 16a states: his spine becomes a serpent if he did not bow at Modim, for "envy is the rottenness of the bones" (Proverbs 14:30), the Serpent's root being envy, as in Sanhedrin 59b: he saw Adam and Eve and envied them.
וְכֵן הַאֲכָלַת חַוָּה לְאָדָם מִטַּעַם קִנְאָה.
And so Eve feeding Adam stemmed from envy.
וְיָדוּעַ דִּשְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ – קִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד – אֵין אָדָם כִּמְעַט שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי.
And it is known that of these three—envy, lust, and honor—there is almost no person completely clean.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל: "וּמִי יַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי קִנְאָה" (מִשְׁלֵי כז, ד);
And as I wrote above: "who can stand before envy?" (Proverbs 27:4);
וּבְתַאֲוָה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ): אֲפִילּוּ חֲסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים וְכוּלֵי;
and regarding desire our Sages stated (Midrash Rabbah, Tazria): even the most pious of the pious, etc.;
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בְּכָבוֹד שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל שְׁנֵיהֶם כַּנּוֹדָע, לְכָךְ אֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת.
and it goes without saying regarding honor which encompasses both as is known; therefore no man is saved from alien thoughts.

וּלְפִי שֶׁקִּנְאָה הוּא הַגָּרוּעַ מֵהַכֹּל וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ, שֶׁנֶּגְדּוֹ הַמְּצוֹרָע הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא עַל קִנְאָה שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַשִּׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲרָכִין טז. וּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת מְצוֹרָע), וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ) דְּנָחָשׁ הוּא מְצוֹרָע

— And because envy is the most destructive of all, the root of the Serpent countered by the leper banished outside the camp of Israel—leprosy stemming from envy that encompasses the seven sins enumerated in Arachin 16a and Vayikra Rabbah, the Serpent being a leper (Bereishit Rabbah 20)—
לְכָךְ אָמַר: מַחֲזִיקְנָא וְכוּלֵי, דְּהַגַּם דְּוַדַּאי אֵין אָדָם נָקִי מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ שֶׁהֲרֵי סוֹף אָדָם לָמוּת עַל זֶה,
therefore he said: I give thanks to my head, for although no man is immune to the counsel of the Serpent since all mortals ultimately die from it,
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם טִיבוּתֵיהּ לְרֵישֵׁיהּ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, כָּרַע מִנַּפְשֵׁיהּ, וְעַצְמוּת הַחַבַּ"ד שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁוֹ נְקִיִּים מִזֶּה.
nevertheless the gratitude to his head is that the root of the Jewish soul bows of its own accord, the essence of Chabad in his head remaining pristine.
רַק הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה הוּא לְבוּשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵעֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל, דְּהוּא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
The alien thought is merely an outer garment that does not belong to the intrinsic root of Israel at all, being outside the camp of Israel as noted above.

וְלָכֵן לֹא זָכַר מַהוּ אוֹתָן מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת, דְּמַה שֶּׁהֵם סִפְּרוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הוּא כְּדֵי לְהַעֲלוֹתָהּ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"ג בְּעִנְיַן הַחְלָצַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִן הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה, דִּבְוַדַּאי יֵשׁ רֶמֶז בָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן לְסוֹדוֹת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַגָּנוּז תּוֹךְ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה.

And therefore he did not articulate what those alien thoughts were, for when the Sages recounted an intrusive thought it was in order to elevate it (Section 203) by extracting the Torah insight within it, there being an allusion to Torah secrets hidden within the distraction.
כִּי הַלְּבוּשׁ הוּא כְּפִי הָרָאוּי לְאוֹתוֹ אָדָם, הַיְינוּ לִפְנִימִיּוּת הַחָכְמָה;
For the garment corresponds to that individual, to his internal wisdom;

מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַלְּבוּשׁ דְּקִנְאָה הוּא לְהַעֲלִימוֹ לְגַמְרֵי כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רי"ח, וְהַעֲלָאָתוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי אֲמִירַת "מַחֲזִיקְנָא וְכוּלֵי", דְּבֶאֱמֶת הָרֹאשׁ אֵינוֹ כֵּן כְּמוֹ הַלְּבוּשׁ, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת כָּךְ כְּלָל.

whereas the garment of envy must be suppressed entirely (Section 218), its elevation occurring through saying "I give thanks to my head," declaring that in truth the head does not resemble the garment and is not defined by it at all.

וְזֶהוּ הַתִּיקּוּן לַמְּצוֹרָע – שִׁילּוּחוֹ חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁיַּכִּיר שֶׁזּוֹ הַמִּדָּה אֵינָהּ מִמַּחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמִצַּד שֵׁם יַהֲדוּת שֶׁעָלָיו שֶׁזֶּהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ הוּא מְרוּחָק מִזֶּה לְגַמְרֵי, עַל יְדֵי הַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה זוֹ הִיא הַתִּיקּוּן וְהָרְפוּאָה לַקּוֹדֶם;

And this is the rectification of the leper—his expulsion outside the camp of Israel: through recognizing that this trait does not belong to the camp of Israel, and that by virtue of his Jewish identity which is his soul-root he is completely detached from it, through this clear recognition comes healing for the past;
כְּשֶׁהוּא מְדַבֵּק עַצְמוֹ בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשַׁת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָלָיו, מִמֵּילָא נִפְרָד מִן הָרָע וְנִרְפָּא גַּם אַלְּהַבָּא.
when he binds himself to the holy root of Israel upon him, he automatically separates from evil and is healed for the future.

דְּזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר מִשְׁפָּטִים (ק עַמּוּד א) דְּמַאן דְּלָא כָּרַע בְּמוֹדִים אֵינוֹ קָם בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, פֵּירוּשׁ דְּהוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע דְּקִנְאָה, וְהוּא מִי שֶׁהוּא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ:

For this reason Zohar Mishpatim 100a states that whoever does not bow at Modim will not rise at the resurrection of the dead, meaning he stems from the evil root of envy, being outside the camp of Israel in his soul's root.

paragraphs.text: Degrees of attachment and future completion

rich.text: Degrees of attachment and future completion

paragraphs.text: Unbroken attachment is distinguished from the enduring purity of the inner root.

rich.text: Unbroken attachment is distinguished from the enduring purity of the inner root.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Resisei Layla 10:2: “Prayer means connection and attachment. This is iyun tefillah, from which no person escapes: even Yaakov is not completely perfected in having every part equal and united without degrees of perfection and attachment. In the future, the Holy One will form a circle for the righteous, as stated at the end of Taanit 31a. A circle means that the level of circles will be revealed, where there are no degrees and everyone is equal in perfection. By contrast, Yaakov's stature is the upright form of a person, with degrees of head, end and extremities, as is known. One cannot escape—that is, attain complete perfection—for this power is not yet perfected until the coming of Mashiach, who will possess complete perfection. ‘As the leader, so the generation’ (Arakhin 17a): the entire generation will be completely perfected. They will then escape iyun tefillah as well, for there will be complete attachment, and consequently they will escape sinful thoughts and the dust of slander, which do not truly belong to the human person's own body.”

In the future, the Holy One will form a circle for the righteous, as stated at the end of Taanit 31a. A circle means that the level of circles will be revealed, where there are no degrees and everyone is equal in perfection. By contrast, Yaakov's stature is the upright form of a person, with degrees of head, end and extremities, as is known. One cannot escape—that is, attain complete perfection—for this power is not yet perfected until the coming of Mashiach, who will possess complete perfection. ‘As the leader, so the generation’ (Arakhin 17a): the entire generation will be completely perfected. They will then escape iyun tefillah as well, for there will be complete attachment, and consequently they will escape sinful thoughts and the dust of slander, which do not truly belong to the human person's own body.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Resisei Layla treats the same statement about unavoidable iyun tefillah as incomplete attachment. It distinguishes the soul's root from surrounding faults while reserving fully equal, uninterrupted attachment for the future. This explains why the siman can speak honestly about an intrusive thought without identifying that thought with the person's essential root.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Tzidkat HaTzadik 209:1: “It is difficult to understand such a statement about people of this greatness, particularly Rabbi Chiyya, of whom it is said that when he said ‘He causes the wind to blow,’ the wind blew. One may therefore interpret ‘I did not direct my heart’ to mean that he did not need to. Directing the heart applies to someone subject to imagination and thoughts, whose tongue speaks while his heart is elsewhere. He never needed this, for no other thing was in his thought: Hashem was before his eyes, and he always spoke as someone speaking before the King of kings. ‘One day I wanted to direct my heart’ means he then needed to because troubling thoughts had arisen; perhaps this was the occasion when Eliyahu disturbed them. Then he needed to direct his thoughts properly, but it did not help, since the disturbance had come from Heaven.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: In Siman 209 Rav Tzadok finds it difficult to attribute ordinary distraction to such great sages and suggests that ‘I did not direct my heart’ means they normally had no need for a separate act of concentration. Here he explicitly says the Yerushalmi can be understood in its plain sense: even their prayer could include a fleeting other thought. These are distinct interpretive proposals. The earlier explanation should not erase the qualification about a flicker of thought stated in the present siman.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Nitzavim 6: “This is ‘to bring you into the covenant of Hashem your God and its oath’: if your understanding is bound to Hashem, and in actual conduct you also accept the awe of punishment, you will consequently be bound to Hashem in action as well. Even without conscious direction you will be drawn after His will. As the Yerushalmi says: Let us acknowledge the goodness of the head, for when it reaches Modim it bows of itself.”

rich.text: : “This is ‘to bring you into the covenant of Hashem your God and its oath’: if your understanding is bound to Hashem, and in actual conduct you also accept the awe of punishment, you will consequently be bound to Hashem in action as well. Even without conscious direction you will be drawn after His will. As the Yerushalmi says: Let us acknowledge the goodness of the head, for when it reaches Modim it bows of itself.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef concludes its distinction between inward willingness and the body's training with the same Yerushalmi statement about the head bowing at Modim. The involuntary motion is thus not offered as a reason to dispense with service; it is the fruit of a bond carried into actual conduct. This clarifies why the present siman can recognize good in the head's response while still examining the other thoughts that accompanied the prayer.
