sections.en: Regarding Idle Thoughts No Explicit Prohibition Is Found in the Torah

p: [רלד] עַל מַחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת לֹא נִמְצָא שׁוּם אִיסּוּר מְפוֹרָשׁ;
Regarding idle thoughts no explicit prohibition is found in the Torah;
רַק "לֹא תָתוּרוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טו, לט) מוֹקְמִינַן בִּבְרָכוֹת (יב:) בְּהִרְהוּר עֲבֵירָה וְלֹא הִרְהוּר בָּטֵל לְבַד.
for "that you seek not, etc." (Numbers 15:39) is interpreted in Berakhot 12b as referring to thoughts of actual sin, and not mere idle thoughts alone.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין מ.) דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה, וְרַק בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
And our Sages stated (Kiddushin 40a) that an evil thought is not combined by the Holy One with action, except for thoughts of idolatry.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם וּבִבְחִירָתוֹ כְּלָל, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ז.
That is because this is not fully within human hands or free choice, as I wrote above in Section 227.
וְכֵן עַל מַעֲשִׂים בְּטֵלִים דִּרְשׁוּת.
And likewise regarding idle, permitted physical actions.
רַק עַל דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים יֵשׁ עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (יט:).
Only regarding idle speech is there a positive and negative commandment, as stated in Yoma 19b.
כִּי בְּדִבּוּר יֵשׁ מִצְוַת תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא תְּמִידִי: "לֹא יָמוּשׁ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ א, ח), וְיוּכַל לִהְיוֹת כָּל דִּבּוּרָיו תּוֹרָה;
For in speech exists the mitzvah of Torah study which is continuous: "it shall not depart, etc." (Joshua 1:8), and all of one's words can be Torah;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַעֲשֶׂה, אֵין כָּאן עֲשִׂיַּת מִצְוָה בִּתְמִידוּת, וְאָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יַפְעִיל.
whereas in physical deed there is no continuous performance of mitzvot, and a person possessing the faculty of action cannot avoid acting.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי גַּם כֵּן עַל הַדִּבּוּר עַל פָּסוּק "זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצֹרָע" (וַיִּקְרָא יד, ב), מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲרָכִין טו:) דְּתַקַּנְתֵּיהּ דְּבַעַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע יַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה,
And as I heard regarding speech on "This shall be the law of the leper" (Leviticus 14:2), based on Arachin 15b that the remedy for a slanderer is to engage in Torah:
לְפִי שֶׁהָאָדָם שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּכֹחַ הַדִּבּוּר אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲצוֹר עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יְדַבֵּר, רַק הָעֵצָה שֶׁיְּדַבֵּר, אֲבָל שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל דִּבּוּרָיו תּוֹרָה.
because man was created with the power of speech and cannot restrain himself from speaking, the remedy being that he speak, but ensure all his speech is Torah.
וְכָךְ מִי שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּכֹחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת יד.): סְתָם יָדַיִם עַסְקָנִיּוֹת;
And so one created with the power of action, matching Shabbat 14a: hands are naturally busy;
וְהֲגַם דְּזֶהוּ מִתְעַסֵּק בְּעָלְמָא דְּלָאו מְלָאכָה הוּא לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת כָּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּכַוָּנָה וְלָא מִקְרֵי מַעֲשֶׂה כְּלָל,
and even though aimless movement is not considered creative labor on Shabbat when unintentional,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן בְּכַוָּנָה; וְלִהְיוֹת הַכֹּל עֲבוֹדַת ה' וְכָל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַעֲשֵׂה מִצְוָה,
nevertheless purposeful action exists, and for all deeds to be purely for Heaven's sake is impossible when not directly a mitzvah,

רַק עַל יְדֵי סַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בְּחֻקֹּתַי) בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: וְהָיוּ רַגְלַי מוֹלִיכוֹת אוֹתִי לְבָתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת, שֶׁהָיָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו תַּכְלִיתָן לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
save through Heavenly assistance, as stated (Vayikra Rabbah, Bechukotai) of King David: my feet led me to synagogues and study halls, Hashem directing his actions ultimately for Heaven's sake.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַשְּׁמִירָה מִדְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים זוֹכֶה גַּם כֵּן לְהִנָּצֵל מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת וּמַעֲשֵׂה בְּטֵלוֹת.
And through guarding against idle speech one merits to be saved from idle thoughts and idle deeds as well.
וּלְהֵיפֶךְ: הַמַּרְבֶּה בִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בִּדְבָרִים אֲסוּרִים כְּלָשׁוֹן הָרָע וְכַדּוֹמֶה, לֹא יִמָּלֵט מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת כְּלָל.
Conversely: whoever indulges in idle speech, and all the more so in forbidden speech like slander, will not escape alien thoughts at all.

וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:) בְּדוֹאֵג: כָּל תּוֹרָתוֹ מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהַמּוֹחַ וְלֵב הָיָה מָלֵא מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים עַל יְדֵי הַלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע.
And our Sages said (Sanhedrin 106b) of Doeg: all his Torah was from the lip outward, meaning mind and heart were filled with alien thoughts through his slander.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְהַדִּבּוּר, וּמִי שֶׁחָפֵץ וּמִשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהִינָּקוֹת מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת, הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְסַיְּיעוֹ גַּם כֵּן לְהִנָּצֵל מִדְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים.
And in truth thought precedes speech, and whoever strives to be cleansed of alien thoughts, the Holy One helps him escape idle words as well.

רַק דּוֹאֵג שׂוֹנֵא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְרַתָּא דְּמַלְכָּא דָּא צְלוֹתָא, שֶׁזּוֹ מַדְרֵגָתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, מט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" (תְּהִלִּים קט, ד), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לְעוֹלָם שׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה;
Only that Doeg hated David who merited the King's daughter which is prayer, his unique level (Zohar III:49b on "and I am prayer"), having never had any alien thought;

וּבְוַדַּאי מִי שֶׁשּׂוֹנְאוֹ הֲרֵי שׂוֹנֵא לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר טוֹב, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ, דְּמָלֵא מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל דְּכָל תּוֹרָתוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וּמִזֶּה נִמְשַׁךְ לָשׁוֹן הָרָע וְגַם מַעֲשִׂים בְּטֵלִים.
and whoever hated him hated that holy virtue, being the exact opposite, full of alien thoughts, whence issued slander and idle deeds.
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר: "וְאֵת נֶפֶשׁ אֹיְבֶיךָ יְקַלְּעֶנָּה בְּתוֹךְ כַּף הַקָּלַע" (שְׁמוּאֵל א כה, כט).
Therefore it was said: "and the souls of your enemies, them shall He sling out, as out of the middle of a sling" (I Samuel 25:29).
וּבַזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח (נט עַמּוּד א) דְּהוּא עַל מַעֲשִׂים שֶׁאֵינָם לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהַיְינוּ מַעֲשִׂים בְּטֵלִים.
And in Zohar Beshalach 59a this refers to actions not for Hashem's service, meaning idle deeds.
וְזֶה "נֶפֶשׁ אֹיְבֶיךָ", פֵּירוּשׁ אוֹיְבֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחוֹ וְעִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁהוּא הֶעְדֵּר הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה, וְהֵם מַמָּשׁ הִיפּוּךְ זֶה.
And this is "the soul of your enemies"—the enemies of David's essential power of being free from alien thoughts, they being the antithesis.
וְנֶפֶשׁ הַיְינוּ דְּנוֹדַע כִּי יֵשׁ נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה: הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מִנֶּפֶשׁ, וְדִבּוּר מֵרוּחַ כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּתַרְגְּמִינַן: לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא, וּמַחֲשָׁבָה מִנְּשָׁמָה;
Action stems from Nefesh, speech from Ruach, as the Targum renders it, "a speaking spirit," and thought from Neshamah;
וִ"יקַלְּעֶנָּה" הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁיָּצָא לַפּוֹעַל גַּם בְּמַעֲשִׂים בְּטֵלִים.
and "He shall sling it" applies when it breaks forth into idle deeds as well.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם הַזֹּהַר עַל פָּסוּק "כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים וְכוּלֵי" (קֹהֶלֶת א, יד), שֶׁמִּמַּעֲשִׂים בְּטֵלִים נַעֲשָׂה הֶבֶל, פֵּירוּשׁ זֶהוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת;
And this is what the Zohar expounds on "all the works, etc." (Ecclesiastes 1:14), that from idle deeds vanity is formed—idle thoughts;

וּ"רְעוּת רוּחַ" – דְּהַשִּׁבָּרוֹן רַק לִדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָאִיסּוּר בְּיִחוּד כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, לְכָךְ בּוֹ הָעוֹנֶשׁ וְלֹא עַל מַחֲשָׁבָה וּמַעֲשֶׂה דְּאֵינוֹ בְּיָדוֹ, וְאָז "יְקַלְּעֶנָּה".

and "vexation of spirit" (re'ut ruach) denotes ruin regarding idle speech, which is an explicit prohibition, hence receiving punishment rather than thought and action which are beyond absolute control; then "He shall sling it."
וּמְפָרֵשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת (קנב:): זוֹמְמוֹת וְהוֹלְכוֹת, פֵּירוּשׁ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהוֹלְכוֹת, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמִּתְלַבְּשׁוֹת נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה דִּבְטָלָה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
And Shabbat 152b explains: they plot and wander, meaning wandering thoughts enclothed in the idle Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah:
הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הוּא גּוּף וְנֶפֶשׁ, וְדִבּוּר וּמַחֲשָׁבָה רוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה לְהַלְבִּישָׁהּ,
action being body and Nefesh, while speech and thought are Ruach and Neshamah to clothe it,
וּמַחְשָׁבוֹת וְהוֹלְכוֹת בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ כְּמוֹ בַּחַיִּים בְּאוֹתָם הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל קִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד, וּכְאִלּוּ פּוֹעֲלוֹת אוֹתָם הַפְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁל הֶבֶל.
and thoughts wander throughout the world just as in life in delusions of envy, lust, and honor, as though executing futile acts.

זֶהוּ פֵּירוּשׁ כַּף הַקֶּלַע, שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ "צְרוּרוֹת בִּצְרוֹר הַחַיִּים", שֶׁהוּא הִיפּוּךְ מַחְשְׁבוֹת הֶבֶל שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם חַיּוּת כְּלָל, וְאֵינוֹ דָּבָר קָבוּעַ וּמַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁקְּבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא, רַק הִשְׁתּוֹטְטוּת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר תִּפְנֶה, וְזֶהוּ "זוֹמְמוֹת וְהוֹלְכוֹת".

This is the definition of the Hollow of the Sling (Kaf HaKela), the antithesis of being bound in the Bundle of Life; for futile thoughts lack vitality and permanence, wandering aimlessly wherever they turn: "plotting and wandering."

אֲבָל מַחְשֶׁבֶת אֱמֶת קְבוּעָה כְּיָתֵד בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן, וְאֵינָהּ הוֹלֶכֶת וּמְשׁוֹטֶטֶת עַל פְּנֵי רַחֲבֵי הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, רַק צְרוּרָה וּקְשׁוּרָה בְּקֶשֶׁר הַחַיִּים, שֶׁלֹּא לַחְשׁוֹב וּלְהִתְבּוֹנֵן רַק בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁהֵם חַיֵּי עוֹלָם.
But a thought of Truth is fixed like a nail in a sure place, not wandering across mental expanses, but bound in the knot of Life, contemplating solely things of eternal life.
וְכֵן שְׂכָרוֹ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה וּפְעֻלָּתוֹ לְפָנָיו:
And so his reward is measure for measure, his deed before him.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 7:12: “Just as Yosef was placed in Egypt and in his mistress's house in order to refine him, so King David was placed in a generation full of harmful speech, as the Yerushalmi in Peah and Midrash Tehillim teach on ‘You will preserve them from this generation forever.’ His tongue, however, was filled with songs and praises.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Ohr Zarua places David's covenant of speech beside Yosef's trial of covenantal purity. The positive content matters: David's tongue was filled with songs and praise. This illustrates the present siman's counsel to redirect the power of speech toward Torah rather than imagine that a person must have no use for speech at all. The corrective occupation reaches the faculty through which the person is being tested.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Metzora 1: “This is the allusion in the verse “This shall be the teaching of the afflicted person.” “This” indicates, as a person might say: this very thing that initially seemed to have no connection with Torah will itself later become clarified as belonging to Torah. For tzaraat comes through the sin of harmful speech, and the defect is that a person’s spirit has no restraint, causing him to speak excessively. Its repair “on the day of his purification” does not follow the natural way. According to the natural way, he would need to restrain his spirit and reduce his power of speech. But concerning this it says, “This shall be”: he should not follow the natural way; instead he should see to it that the very power of speech which until now brought him to words contrary to Torah should now be used abundantly to speak words of Torah. Abundant talk of Torah is good.”

sections.en: One Who Strives to Be Saved from Alien Thoughts and Resolves in His Heart…

p: [רלה] הַמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל לְהִנָּצֵל מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת וְגָמַר בְּלִבּוֹ לִדְחוֹתָהּ, וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא נִזְכָּר מִיָּד מַדְחֶה וּמַכְנִיס בְּלִבּוֹ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת שֶׁל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ;
One who strives to be saved from alien thoughts and resolves in his heart to repel them, and whenever he remembers immediately repels them and introduces thoughts of Torah according to his strength;
רַק שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם הִיא תּוֹקַפְתּוֹ, וּבְעֵת שֶׁשָּׁקוּעַ בָּהּ נִשְׁכַּח מִמֶּנּוּ מַחְשֶׁבֶת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּרְצוֹנוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינוֹ בָּהּ, וּמִיָּד שֶׁנִּזְכָּר הוּא מַדְחֶה אוֹתָהּ

— yet nonetheless the intrusive thought overpowers him, and while immersed in it Torah thought is forgotten from him, though his authentic will is not in it, and the moment he remembers he casts it away—

הֲרֵי שִׁכְחָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מֵחֲמַת עַצְלוּת חָשׁוּב אֹנֶס, עַיֵּין בְּמָגֵן אַבְרָהָם (סִימָן קח סָעִיף קָטָן יא), וַהֲרֵי זֶה כְּחִשֵּׁב לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה וְנֶאֱנַס וְלֹא עֲשָׂאָהּ, מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאָהּ (בְּרָכוֹת ו.).

behold forgetfulness not born of negligence is legally deemed unavoidable coercion (ones, Magen Avraham 108:11), and he is like one who intended to perform a mitzvah and was prevented by circumstances, whom Scripture credits as though he performed it (Berakhot 6a).
וְהֲגַם דְּמַאן סָפֵין וּמַאן רָקֵיעַ [שָׁמַעְתִּי פֵּירוּשׁוֹ (בְּמוֹעֵד קָטָן כח.) טָהוֹר וָזַךְ כְּמוֹ הָרָקִיעַ, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר נָקִי מִנְּגִיעָה לְרָע] לָדַעַת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵחֲמַת עַצְלוּת,

And although "who is safin and who is raki'a?" (Moed Katan 28a) [I heard it explained: pure and clear as the firmament, meaning free of any leaning toward evil]—who can know that it is not from laziness—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם עַל עַצְלוּת זֶה חָשׁוּב אֹנֶס, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהוּא מְחַשֵּׁב וְרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת עָצֵל בִּדְחִיַּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת.
nonetheless even regarding that subtle sluggishness it is accounted coercion, since he genuinely desires not to be sluggish in repelling alien thoughts.

וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁלֹּא נִזְכַּר אִיסּוּר וַעֲבֵירָה מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת בְּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת, אִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ כְּחִשֵּׁב לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה וְלֹא עֲשָׂאָהּ דְּהוּא כַּעֲשָׂאָהּ, וּמִמֵּילָא יִהְיֶה הַמִּשְׁפָּט אַלְּהַבָּא שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יַעֲזוֹר לוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת לִהְיוֹת עוֹשֶׂה, דְּהַיְינוּ שָׁמוּר מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת, וְלֹא כְּאִלּוּ עָשָׂה בִּלְבַד.

And since no explicit prohibition is formulated against involuntary alien thoughts, the future ruling will be that the Holy One will help him actively succeed—becoming guarded from alien thoughts, and not merely credited as though he did.
וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שָׁמוּר בִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה.
Provided that he guards against idle speech, achieved through speaking words of Torah.
וְעִיקַּר אַזְהָרַת דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים מִ"וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם" (דְּבָרִים ו, ז) – וְלֹא בִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹמָא יט:);
And the primary prohibition of idle speech derives from "and you shall speak of them" (Deuteronomy 6:7)—and not in idle words (Yoma 19b);
וְכֹחַ לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה אֵינוֹ יוֹתֵר מִלָּאו הַנִּיתָּק לַעֲשֵׂה, שֶׁהָעֲשֵׂה תִּיקּוּן הַלָּאו.
and the force of a negative prohibition derived from a positive command is like a negative command linked to a positive one, where the positive command rectifies the negative.
וְכֵן בְּלָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה, כַּאֲשֶׁר מְקַיֵּים הָעֲשֵׂה דְּ"וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם" – תִּיקֵּן הַלָּאו דִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים, וְהוּא מוֹעִיל גַּם כֵּן לְעִנְיַן מַחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת.
And so when one fulfills the positive command "and you shall speak of them," he rectifies the negative prohibition of idle speech, which avails likewise to heal idle thoughts.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן" (מִשְׁלֵי י, לב), שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר מוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו דְּבָרִים הַמְּצוּדָּקִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ וְלִבּוֹ בַּל עִמּוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם יֵדְעוּן – מוֹדִיעִים וּמְלַמְּדִים רָצוֹן לַלֵּב, לִהְיוֹת רְצוֹן הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן.

And as I heard on "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable" (Proverbs 10:32): when one articulates righteous words with his lips, even if from the lip outward while his heart is not fully present, they inform and teach will to the heart, causing the heart's will to align with them in truth.
וְהָרָצוֹן מוֹלִיד מַחֲשָׁבָה, לִהְיוֹת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בָּזֶה לְבַד.
And will generates thought, focusing his thoughts on this alone.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין נד.): "חַיִּים הֵם לְמֹצְאֵיהֶם" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כב) – לְמוֹצִיאֵיהֶם בַּפֶּה,
And this is what they expounded (Eruvin 54a): "'they are life unto those that find them'—unto those who articulate them with the mouth,"

כִּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "עֵץ חַיִּים", הַיְינוּ בְּסוֹד הַוָּא"ו דְּשֵׁם שֶׁהוּא קַו הַמַּבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה, כַּאֲשֶׁר עוֹבֵר כָּל חֶלְקֵי נַרַ"נ שֶׁבְּגוּפוֹ: מוֹחַ וְלֵב וּכְלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, אָז נִקְרָא עֵץ חַיִּים.

for words of Torah are termed a "tree of life," the letter Vav of the divine Name traversing from end to end: passing through all parts of the soul within his body—brain, heart, and limbs of action—it is called a tree of life.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁמּוֹצִיא בַּפֶּה – זֶהוּ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, וְזֶה גּוֹרֵם רָצוֹן לַלֵּב וּמַחֲשָׁבָה לַמּוֹחַ, וְאָז הוּא חַיִּים וּמוֹלִיד חַיּוּת.
When spoken with the mouth it is an action, generating will in the heart and thought in the brain, bringing life and birthing vitality.
וּמִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִדְחֶה מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הַחַיּוּת, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"ג שֶׁהַבַּטָּלָה כְּשֵׁינָה – אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בְּמִיתָה.
And automatically alien thought is repelled, which is the antithesis of vitality (Section 203: idleness like sleep is one-sixtieth of death).
וְעַל יְדֵי הוֹצָאַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בַּפֶּה מוֹלִיד חַיּוּת, כִּדְמְתַרְגְּמִינַן: "לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" – לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ז), שֶׁעִיקַּר הַחַיּוּת עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר.
And uttering words of Torah with the mouth generates life, as Targum translates "a living soul" as "a speaking spirit" (Genesis 2:7), primary vitality coming through speech.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר מִתְעוֹרֵר רוּחַ הַחַיִּים, אָז מְקִיצוֹ מִתַּרְדֵּמַת הָאִוֶּולֶת שֶׁבָּזֶה נִמְשָׁל כַּבְּהֵמוֹת.
And when the spirit of life awakens, it rouses him from the slumber of folly wherein man resembles beasts.
שֶׁמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה הוּא מִצַּד נֶפֶשׁ הַבַּהֲמִית, וְהַדִּבּוּר הוּא עִיקַּר צוּרַת אָדָם וְיִתְרוֹנוֹ מִן הַבְּהֵמָה אִם הוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דְּאָז נִקְרָא דִּבּוּר
Alien thought stems from the animal soul, while speech is the form of man and his preeminence over beasts if it is in Torah, which alone is true speech

[דִּבְלָאו הָכִי לֹא נִקְרָא דִּבּוּר כְּלָל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בְּעִנְיַן הַנָּחָשׁ דְּלֹא נִזְכַּר בַּקְּלָלָה שֶׁנִּיטַּל הַדִּבּוּר מִמֶּנּוּ, לְפִי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא הָיָה לוֹ דִּבּוּר כְּלָל, דְּדִבּוּרוֹ לֹא נִקְרָא דִּבּוּר, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
[for otherwise it is not speech, as I heard regarding the Serpent whose curse did not mention losing speech because its speech was not true speech, and this is not the place to elaborate],
זֶה מְעוֹרֵר צוּרַת הָאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא לְהִשְׁתַּקַּע בְּנַפְשׁוֹ הַבַּהֲמִית.
and this awakens the human form not to sink into the animal soul.
וּבִלְבַד כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא מְדַבֵּר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּדֵי לְעוֹרֵר הַלֵּב וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה;
Provided that he speaks words of Torah in order to awaken heart and thought;

דִּכְשֶׁאֵין זֶה בִּרְצוֹנוֹ כְּלָל, הֲרֵי זֶה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רל"ד בְּדוֹאֵג שֶׁתּוֹרָתוֹ מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, כִּי לֹא הָיָה דַּעְתּוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ כְּלָל שֶׁתִּקָּבַע בְּלִבּוֹ וּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וּלְהוֹצִיא מַחְשֶׁבֶת הִיפּוּךְ כְּלָל.
for when this is not his desire at all, it is like Doeg (Section 234) whose Torah was from the lip outward, having no desire that it be fixed in his heart to drive out contrary thoughts.
וְזֶהוּ קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁאוֹמֵר פָּרָשַׁת "וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם", וְהַתְחָלָה: "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל" – שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע לָזֶה.
And this is the Shema where we recite "and you shall speak of them," opening with "Hear, O Israel"—that he listen to this.

וְכֵן נִקְרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע לְשׁוֹן קְרִיאָה, שֶׁקּוֹרֵא לְעַצְמוֹ שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע וִיקַבֵּל דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ, וְעַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת זֶה הוּא נִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב, וְיוּכַל אַחַר כָּךְ לִזְכּוֹת לִבְרַתָּא דְּמַלְכָּא צְלוֹתָא בְּכַוָּנַת הַלֵּב:

And it is called Kri'at Shema, an expression of calling, calling upon himself to hear and accept these words, through which awakening it is fixed in the heart, and he can subsequently merit the King's daughter—prayer—with sincere heart-intention.

paragraphs.text: Context: The exchange takes place as Rav Nachman approaches death; “him” refers to the Angel of Death. The last Aramaic expression is man rakia. That explanation is distinguished here from the ordinary meaning of the Talmudic exchange.

paragraphs.text: Speech joins the heart's life to actual action

paragraphs.text: Spoken Torah can affect inward will because speech belongs to both inward life and bodily action.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 15:108: “It therefore says, ‘The matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.’ The mouth includes and joins the two: moving the lips is an action, while its essential source is the living spirit within the heart. ‘A living soul’ is translated as ‘a speaking spirit,’ joining nefesh and ruach. ‘The lips of the righteous know desire’ means connection and attachment, and also teaching understanding to the will within the heart. Through spoken words it enters the heart as well, and afterward is carried into action.”

rich.text: : “It therefore says, ‘The matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.’ The mouth includes and joins the two: moving the lips is an action, while its essential source is the living spirit within the heart. ‘A living soul’ is translated as ‘a speaking spirit,’ joining nefesh and ruach. ‘The lips of the righteous know desire’ means connection and attachment, and also teaching understanding to the will within the heart. Through spoken words it enters the heart as well, and afterward is carried into action.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains why the lips have a distinctive role: their movement is an action, while their speech emerges from the heart's living spirit. The same verse about righteous lips is therefore read as teaching and joining the will. This gives the present siman's counsel a precise structure; the learner speaks in order that mind and heart also become involved, rather than treating an utterance without any intention to change as sufficient.

rich.text: Takanat HaShavin explains why the lips have a distinctive role: their movement is an action, while their speech emerges from the heart's living spirit. This gives the present siman's counsel a precise structure; the learner speaks in order that mind and heart also become involved, rather than treating an utterance without any intention to change as sufficient.

sections.en: It Is Completely Impossible for a Person to Remain Throughout the Entire Day Upon…

p: [רלו] אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם כְּלָל לַעֲמוֹד בְּכָל הַיּוֹם כֻּלּוֹ בְּמַדְרֵגָה אַחַת, תָּקוּעַ בִּדְבֵיקוּת כָּרָאוּי, וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי יִפֹּל לֹא יוּטָל" (תְּהִלִּים לז, כד), וְ"שֶׁבַע יִפּוֹל צַדִּיק וָקָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כד, טז).

It is completely impossible for a person to remain throughout the entire day upon one uniform level, firmly fixed in proper cleaving; concerning this it is said: "Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down" (Psalms 37:24), and: "For a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again" (Proverbs 24:16).

וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ה): שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה זָז מִפִּיךָ: "ה' [צְבָאוֹת עִמָּנוּ] מִשְׂגָּב לָנוּ [אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב סֶלָה]" (תְּהִלִּים מו, ח), וַחֲבֵירוֹ: "ה' [צְבָאוֹת אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם] בֹּטֵחַ בָּךְ" (שָׁם פד, יג), הַיְינוּ לְצוֹרֶךְ נְפִילוֹת הַלָּלוּ – לְהִתְחַזֵּק וְלִבְטוֹחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא יְשַׂגְּבֵהוּ.

And in Yerushalmi Berakhot (chapter 5): let not this verse depart from your mouth, "Hashem [of hosts is with us]; our refuge [is the God of Jacob, Selah]" (Psalms 46:8), and its companion, "Hashem [of hosts, happy is the man] that trusts in You" (ibid. 84:13)—intended for these falls, to strengthen oneself and trust in Hashem that He will lift him up.
וְעַל זֶה אוֹמְרִים בְּ"אַתָּה גִּבּוֹר": "סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים", שֶׁהֵן הֵן גְּבוּרוֹתָיו לְחַזֵּק לַכֹּל, שֶׁגַּם הַחַלָּשׁ יֹאמַר: גִּבּוֹר אָנִי.
And concerning this we recite in the blessing Atah Gibbor: "He supports the falling," for these are His divine powers of might, to strengthen everyone so that even the weak may declare: I am mighty.
וְלֹא תִּקְּנוּ עַל זֶה בַּקָּשָׁה, רַק בִּכְלַל הַזְכָּרַת שִׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם,
And they did not formulate an explicit petition over this, but included it within recounting the praise of the Omnipresent.
כִּי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּעֲנִית כה:): שְׁבָחוֹ שֶׁל צִבּוּר – אָמַר מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ נָשֵׁיב זִיקָא וְכוּלֵי,
For our Sages stated (Ta'anit 25b): the praise of the congregation—when he recited "He causes the wind to blow," the wind blew, etc.,
פֵּירוּשׁ כְּטַעַם: "טֶרֶם יִקְרָאוּ וַאֲנִי אֶעֱנֶה עוֹד הֵם מְדַבְּרִים וַאֲנִי אֶשְׁמָע" (יְשַׁעְיָה סה, כד);
in the spirit of: "before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear" (Isaiah 65:24);
קְרִיאָה נִקְרָא שֶׁקּוֹרֵא לַחֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲנֵהוּ, וְדִבּוּר הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ עֲנִיָּה, רַק מְדַבֵּר לְפָנָיו כְּמוֹ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
calling means one calls his fellow to answer him, while speaking denotes addressing him without requesting a response, like words of Torah.
וְכֵן סִפּוּר שְׁבָחָיו שֶׁל מָקוֹם, וְכַאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְפָּאֵר בְּשִׁבְחָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לוֹ, מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה זֶהוּ שְׁבָחָן שֶׁל צִבּוּר.
And so with recounting the praises of the Omnipresent: when Hashem glories in Israel's praise of Him, measure for measure, that is the praise of the congregation.

וְאָז הֵם דְּבָרִים הַפּוֹעֲלִים, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֶּׁבַח אֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ סִפּוּר דְּבָרִים לְבַד שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי "בִּדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ" (תְּהִלִּים לג, ו), וְדִבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה.

And then these words effect reality, the praise not being mere storytelling—which does not exist with Hashem—for "by the word of Hashem were the heavens made" (Psalms 33:6), Hashem's speech being equivalent to action.
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁשִּׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם הוּא שְׁבָחָן שֶׁל צִבּוּר, הַיְינוּ דְּדִבּוּרָן שֶׁל צִבּוּר כְּאִלּוּ הוּא דִּבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם, וְהַדִּבּוּר פּוֹעֵל יְשׁוּעוֹת.
And since the praise of the Omnipresent is the praise of the congregation, the speech of the congregation is like the speech of the Omnipresent, and speech effects salvations.
כִּי דִּבּוּר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ מִשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ רַק בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת, וּבְעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה הוּא בְּמַעֲשֶׂה.
For Hashem's speech is not from the lip outward, but reverberates across all worlds, manifesting in the World of Action as tangible deed.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא דִּבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְנִקְרָא דִּבּוּר, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי עַל "הָלוֹךְ וְדִבַּרְתָּ" דֶּאֱלִישָׁע וּבַגְּמָרָא תַּעֲנִית (י:).
And this is the power of the Torah which is Hashem's speech, termed speech (see the Yerushalmi on Elisha's "go and speak," and Ta'anit 10b).
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין סה:): אִי בָּעוּ צַדִּיקֵי בָּרוּ עָלְמָא, הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי עִסְקָם בַּתּוֹרָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
Therefore they said (Sanhedrin 65b): if the righteous desired, they could create a world—through engaging in the Torah of Creation.

וְזֶה כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חִיָּיא וּבָנָיו בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פה:) דְּאָמַר מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ נָשֵׁיב וְכוּלֵי, הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם דְּעָבֵיד לַתּוֹרָה דְּלָא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח, וּבְסֻכָּה (כ.) דְּנִשְׁתַּכְּחָה תּוֹרָה וְעָלוּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא וּבָנָיו וְיִסְּדוּהָ.

And this was the power of Rabbi Chiya and his sons in Bava Metzia 85b: reciting "He causes the wind to blow" and the wind blew, because he acted so that Torah not be forgotten, and in Sukkah 20a: Torah was forgotten, and Rabbi Chiya and his sons ascended and reestablished it.
וּמִצַּד דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ אֱמֶת, כֹּחַ דִּבּוּרוֹ לִהְיוֹת אֱמֶת, דְּהַיְינוּ מְבוֹרָר לָעַיִן וְלֹא אֱמוּנָה לְבַד.
And from Torah, of which Truth is written, the power of his speech is to be Truth—clarified to the eye and not mere faith.
וְהוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת וּמַבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה גַּם בְּעוֹלַם עֲשִׂיָּה בְּמַעֲשֶׂה מַמָּשׁ.
And this is Jacob's attribute, corresponding to the Name Havayah encompassing all worlds, traversing from end to end even in the World of Action in tangible deed.
וְעִיקַּר סְמִיכַת נוֹפְלִים מִמַּדְרֵגָתָן הוּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנּוֹתֶנֶת עֹז וְתוּשִׁיָּה.
And the essential supporting of those who have fallen from their spiritual level is through words of Torah which grant strength and wisdom.

וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּר שֶׁל אֱמֶת בְּהַכָּרַת מַעֲלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הֲגַם שֶׁהוּא מְרוּחָק מִמֶּנּוּ בְּתַכְלִית, שֶׁזֶּהוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְזֶה אֶפְשָׁר גַּם בְּעֵת הַנְּפִילָה וְהָרִחוּק, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִסְמָךְ.

Namely, through speaking truth in recognizing Hashem's greatness even when one feels utterly distant from Him; for Torah study does not demand standing directly before the King, being accessible even during a fall and distance, and through it he is supported.
אֲבָל תְּפִלָּה שֶׁהוּא כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, הַיְינוּ מְקוֹרָב, זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּעֵת נְפִילָה שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵינוֹ מְקוֹרָב;
But prayer, which requires standing before the King as one brought close, is impossible during a fall, for he is not close;
וְגַם אִי אֶפְשָׁר בִּתְפִלָּה לֶעָנִי מִפְּאַת שִׁבְרוּת לֵב, שֶׁגַּם לָזֶה צָרִיךְ חִזּוּק, וּבְעֵת נְפִילָה אַף זֶה אֵין לוֹ, רַק הַלֵּב מְטוּמְטָם כְּאֶבֶן לְגַמְרֵי.
and he cannot even muster the prayer of the poor out of a broken heart, for that too requires strength, while in a fall he lacks even this, the heart being stopped up like stone.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב:): מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, אִם אֶבֶן וְכוּלֵי הוּא מִתְפּוֹצֵץ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא נִסְמָךְ וְנִתְחַזֵּק לְהִתְעוֹרֵר לָקוּם מִנְּפִילָתוֹ.
And on this they said (Sukkah 52b): "drag him to the house of study; if he is stone, he will shatter"—for through words of Torah he is supported and strengthened to awaken and rise from his fall.

וְסִפּוּר שִׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם הַיְינוּ נֶגֶד דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא שִׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי שֵׁם ה' אֶקְרָא הָבוּ גֹדֶל לֵאלֹהֵינוּ" (דְּבָרִים לב, ג), וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת (כא.) עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;

And recounting the praise of the Omnipresent corresponds to Torah, which is entirely the praise of the Omnipresent: "When I proclaim the Name of Hashem, ascribe greatness unto our God" (Deuteronomy 32:3; Berakhot 21a);
וּפֵירוּשׁ "שֵׁם" הוּא הַשֶּׁבַח, כִּי שְׁמוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ מוֹרוֹת עַל כֹּחוֹתָיו.
and "Name" denotes praise, His Names signifying His powers.
וְכֵן "שֵׁם" הוּא הָרָצוֹן, וְכַנּוֹדָע כִּי "שְׁמוֹ" בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "רָצוֹן", כִּי כֹּחוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ הַיְינוּ מִדַּת רְצוֹנוֹ.
And "Name" (shem) is Will (ratzon), the numerical value of Shemo (346) equaling Ratzon (346), His powers being His Will.
וְכֵן הַתּוֹרָה רְצוֹנוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: שֶׁאָמַר וְנַעֲשָׂה רְצוֹנוֹ.
And the Torah is His Will, as in the rabbinic phrase: "Who spoke and His will was done."
וְכֵן כָּל שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת הַיְינוּ כָּךְ רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And so the first three blessings of the Amidah express what His Will is.
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים, וַדַּאי יִהְיֶה סוֹמְכָם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַנּוֹפֵל אֵין בּוֹ כֹּחַ וְדַעַת לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֶׁיְּעוֹרֵר רָצוֹן;
And since the Blessed Name wills to support the fallen, He will certainly support them, even though the fallen one lacks the strength and consciousness to plead for himself to awaken that Will;
אֲבָל אָנוּ אוֹמְרִים שֶׁכָּךְ הוּא רְצוֹנוֹ מֵעַצְמוֹ, מִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּר זֶה מִתְעוֹרֵר מִדַּת רְצוֹנוֹ הָעַצְמִי לָזֶה לִפְעוֹל,
but we declare that such is His inherent Will of His own accord, so through this speech His essential Will is stirred to act;

כֵּיוָן שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָזֶה הַנּוֹפֵל לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בִּתְפִלָּה, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וְאַבִּיט וְאֵין עֹזֵר וְגוֹמֵר וַתּוֹשַׁע לִי [זְרֹעִי וַחֲמָתִי הִיא סְמָכָתְנִי]" (יְשַׁעְיָה סג, ה):

since it is impossible for the fallen one to generate an awakening from below in prayer, concerning this Scripture proclaims: "And I looked, and there was none to help... and it brought salvation unto Me—[My own arm; and My fury, it upheld Me]" (Isaiah 63:5).

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:3: “Rabbenu Tam also mentions this in Sefer HaYashar: a person has times when he desires something and times when he recoils from it; see there. These are the familiar falls referred to by the verse, “A righteous person falls seven times and rises”: a person does not remain at his level without moving away from his service even for a moment. Since he was created with an inclination, if he remained that way it would be impossible to separate evil from good at all. This separation takes place through the power of repentance, and is accomplished through the sleep in between. Afterward he wakes from his sleep, returns, and regrets; through this, evil is gradually separated from good. The good remains by itself, while the evil passes away during the periods of sleep. Without sleep, however, separation is impossible; one could only make the evil good and transform it. This cannot be accomplished completely in this world, in which the evil inclination has already been created. Concerning this they said: “Very good”—this is sleep.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Cheshvan explains that the sukkah is supported even while it appears fallen, and that the fall can become the setting of ascent. This gives the present siman’s opening confidence a concrete image. The person need not first recover a full feeling of closeness before speaking truth about Hashem or turning to Torah. Those words are themselves a means of support through which the capacity to rise and pray can return.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And "Name" (shem) is Will (ratzon), the numerical value of Shemo (346) equaling Ratzon (346), His powers being His Will.

paragraphs.text: Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Toldot Adam, Beit Hashem 19: “But above, in the highest heights, at the root of the roots of the roots, before the revelation of emanation, “He” and “His name” are one essence. There the Great Name is related only to the will, insofar as He wills to bestow goodness so that the modes of being and the names may be apprehended. This will is the source of the modes of being and their names, and He and His name are one: there “He” is His name, and His name is “He.” This is hinted at in the word hu, “He,” whose initial letters signify “He and His name are one.” There the name Y-H-V-H is neither read nor written even in thought, even by Michael the great prince. When we speak there in the highest heights of His essence, we mean the mystery of the will: the concealment beyond the name Y-H-V-H, as stated. This will, in the supreme concealment beyond all concealments, is called “His name,” for shemo, “His name,” has the same numerical value as ratzon, “will.” This alludes to the profound concealment of Y-H-V-H, which amounts to the numerical value of shemo and ratzon. How? Y-H multiplied by Y-H, and V-H multiplied by V-H, amounts to shemo.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 8:1: “What Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote—that the Holy One, blessed be He, His being, His essence, and His knowledge are all truly one, a simple unity with no composition at all—applies in precisely the same way to all the attributes of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to all His holy names and the descriptions given to Him by the prophets and our Sages, of blessed memory, such as “gracious,” “merciful,” “kind,” and the like. The same applies to His being called “wise,” as it is written, “He too is wise,” and to His will: “The Lord desires those who fear Him,” “He desires kindness,” “He desires the repentance of the wicked and does not desire their death and their wickedness,” and “too pure of eyes to behold evil.” His will, His wisdom, His kindness, His compassion, and His other attributes add no plurality or composition, God forbid, to His being and essence. Rather, His essence and being, His will, His wisdom, His understanding and knowledge, His kindness and might, His compassion and beauty comprising His kindness and might, and likewise all His other holy attributes, are all a truly simple unity, which is His very essence and being.”

p: [רלז] עַל כָּל דָּבָר יֵשׁ עֵצוֹת עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת,
For every single matter there exist counsels by means of words of Torah and commandments,
וְיֵשׁ מִצְוֹת הַמּוֹעִילוֹת לְמִי שֶׁנִּפְסַק מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ,
and there are commandments that are efficacious for one who has fallen away from his spiritual level,
שֶׁגָּבְרוּ עָלָיו אֵיזֶה יָמִים מַחְשְׁבוֹת הֲבָלִים,
such that for several days vain and frivolous thoughts overwhelmed him,
וְנִיתַּק מִקְּבִיעוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בַּלֵּב
— and he became detached from the permanent fixture of words of Torah within the heart –
לַהֲחֲזִירוֹ לִקְבִיעוּתוֹ.
to restore him back to his established standing.
וּבְיִחוּד הוּא לָזֶה מִצְוַת שַׁבָּת,
And especially designated for this purpose is the commandment of Shabbat,
שֶׁבְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת יֵשׁ לוֹ לָקַחַת עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת מִצְוַת שַׁבָּת
for on the Sabbath day he is able to draw, through the sanctity of the commandment of Shabbat,
לַחֲזוֹר לִידָּבֵק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּלְמָאֵס הַבְלֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
to return and cleave unto words of Torah and to despise the vanities of this physical world.
וְעַל זֶה רוֹמֶזֶת מִצְוַת עֶבֶד עִבְרִי
And toward this alludes the commandment of the Hebrew servant,
"וּבַשְּׁבִעִת יֵצֵא לַחָפְשִׁי",
where 'in the seventh year he shall go out free' (Exodus 21:2),
רָצָה לוֹמַר: מִי שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּעְבֵּד לְיֵצֶר הָרָע.
meaning: one who became subjugated to the evil inclination.
וְהַגַּם דְּשָׁם בַּשָּׁנִים,
And although there the reckoning is in years,
יֵשׁ בַּיָּמִים,
here it is manifest within the days of the week;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי דִּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּאָלֶף־בֵּית אַתְוָון רַבְרְבִין וּזְעֵירִין,
just as I heard that just as there are large and small letters in the Hebrew alphabet,
כֵּן בַּזְּמַן – יָמִים וְשָׁנִים.
so too in the dimension of time are there days and years.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Mishpatim 2:2: “Rather, the explanation is that through observing Shabbat one merits awe and fear, as the Jerusalem Talmud says: “The awe of Shabbat rests upon an unlearned person.” Through awe he comes to repentance, as has often been explained from the Talmud: awe and repentance are one, for each depends on the other. This is “the lower Shabbat is awe, and awe rests within it,” as stated in the Zohar. This is the shofar, which signifies fear and awe, as it is said: “If a shofar is sounded in a city, will the people not tremble?””

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Behar 3: ““The land shall rest a Sabbath to the Lord.” The meaning of the sabbatical year is that it is a sign for Israel that “the earth and all that fills it belong to the Lord.” As stated in the holy Zohar, there are large letters and small letters. The small letters signify Shabbat, for Shabbat is a sign to Israel that the blessed God brings about everything and that nothing is accomplished through human actions. The large letters signify the sabbatical year: when seven years have passed, there must be an entire year in which it is shown that the earth belongs to the Lord, and that no person possesses the power of action; it belongs to the Lord alone.”

items.h: Judging the inclination

p: וּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ תְּחִלַּת מִשְׁפָּטִים,
And this scriptural portion opens Parashat Mishpatim,
דְּפֵירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (טו:):
whose meaning is in line with what is stated in Megillah (15b):
עַל "לְרוּחַ מִשְׁפָּט" – זֶה הַדָּן אֶת יִצְרוֹ.
on the verse 'for a spirit of judgment' (Isaiah 28:6) – this refers to one who judges his base inclination.
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי נִיצּוּחַ הַיְּצָרִים נִקְרָא מִלְחָמָה בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה,
The explanation being: conquering internal inclinations is titled 'warfare' in the words of our Sages of blessed memory,
וְהַדַּיָּין הַשּׁוֹפֵט בֵּינֵיהֶם
and the judge who adjudicates between them
צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נוֹגֵעַ לְכָאן וּלְכָאן,
must be entirely free of personal bias toward either this side or that,
וְעַל פִּיו יָקוּם דָּבָר וּשְׁנֵיהֶם צְרִיכִים לִשְׁמוֹעַ.
and upon his word shall every matter be established, with both parties bound to obey.
וְזֶה מִי שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ בְּיָדוֹ, שֶׁאוֹנוֹ בְּיָדוֹ,
And this characterizes one whose inclination is in his hand, whose strength is under his dominion,
שֶׁבְּכֹחוֹ לְסַלֵּק עַצְמוֹ מִנְּגִיעָה
who has the power to divest himself of personal vested interest
וְלִשְׁפּוֹט עַל כָּל דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יַעֲלֶה בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ לָדַעַת אִם טוֹב אִם רַע.
and to sit in clear judgment over every single thought that crosses his mind to discern whether it is good or evil.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַלִּימּוּד דְּמִשְׁפָּטִים,
And toward this applies the teaching of Mishpatim (civil ordinances),
וּבָזֶה נֶאֱמַר "אֲשֶׁר תָּשִׂים" – לְהָבִין הַטַּעַם.
and regarding this Scripture proclaims 'which you shall set before them' – to understand the underlying rationale.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 15b: ‘‘And for a spirit of judgment’—this is one who judges his own inclination. ‘And for one who sits in judgment’—this is one who renders a judgment that is true in its fullest sense. ‘And for strength’—this is one who overcomes his inclination. ‘Those who turn back battle’—those who debate in the battle of Torah. ‘At the gate’—(these are Torah scholars) who come early and stay late in synagogues and houses of study.’

p: פֵּירוּשׁ, דְּיֵשׁ חֻקִּים וּמִשְׁפָּטִים כַּנּוֹדָע,
The meaning is: there exist Chukkim (statutes) and Mishpatim (ordinances) as is well known,
וּבְוַדַּאי כָּךְ כֹּחַ פְּעֻלָּתָם בַּלֵּב.
and such assuredly is the manner of their operative impact within the heart.
אֵלּוּ לַחֲקוֹק חֻקֵּי חַיִּים, מַה שֶּׁלְּמַעְלָה מִשֵּׂכֶל הָאָדָם,
The former serve to engrave the statutes of transcendent life, which stand far above mortal intellect,
וְהַיְינוּ בְּעִנְיַן הַשָּׂגַת אֱלֹהוּת
namely in the realm of comprehending divinity,
וְכֵן בְּעִנְיַן נִיצּוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר
and likewise in the realm of conquering the base inclination,
מַה שֶּׁ"אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ" (קִידּוּשִׁין ל:).
wherein 'were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to assist him, he could not prevail over it' (Kiddushin 30b).
וְאֵלּוּ לָתֵת קְדוּשָּׁה בַּלֵּב,
And the latter serve to instill conscious holiness in the heart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ" –
as we say in the blessing: 'Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us' –
מַה שֶּׁהוּא מוּרְגָּשׁ בַּשֵּׂכֶל,
which is palpable to rational intellect,
וְכֵן בְּנִיצּוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר בְּכֹחַ אָדָם בְּרוּחַ מִשְׁפָּט.
and likewise in conquering the inclination through human mental faculty via the spirit of judgment.
וּבְכָל מִצְוָה עַצְמָהּ יֵשׁ חֻקִּים וּמִשְׁפָּטִים,
Moreover, within every single commandment itself there are aspects of both Chukkim and Mishpatim,
פֵּירוּשׁ: מַה שֶּׁמַּשְׂכִּיל מִמֶּנָּה וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא כְּמוֹ חֻקָּה,
meaning: that which one rationally understands of it, and that which remains an inscrutable decree,
וּלְכָךְ פְּעֻלָּתָן בִּשְׁתֵּיהֶם.
and therefore their inner efficacy functions through both channels.

p: וְזֶהוּ כְּלַל מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
And this embodies the entirety of the Giving of the Torah;
וְסָמַךְ לָהּ "אֵלֶּה הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים",
hence Scripture juxtaposed to it 'Now these are the ordinances',
אַחַר שֶׁנָּתַן תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין לַיֵּצֶר, וְהוּא הַסַּיַּיעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא,
for after He gave the Torah as an antidote to the inclination, which constitutes divine heavenly assistance,
בֵּיאַר הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים אֵיךְ לָדוּן יִצְרוֹ בְּשֵׂכֶל אָדָם,
He elaborated the ordinances showing how to adjudicate one's evil inclination using human intellect;
וְזֶהוּ "אֲשֶׁר תָּשִׂים" – לְהָבִין בַּשֵּׂכֶל.
and this is 'which you shall set before them' – to comprehend with the mind.
וְהֵם בְּקִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד,
Now, these base drives consist of envy, lust, and honor;
וּפָתַח בְּכָבוֹד,
and Scripture opened with honor,
דְּהַיְינוּ בְּהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת עַל זוּלָתוֹ,
which expresses itself through haughtiness over one's fellow,
וּבַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבַּהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת – כְּאָדוֹן עַל עַבְדּוֹ וַאֲמָתוֹ.
and in the most extreme manifestation of haughtiness – as a master ruling over his male and female servant.
יֵדַע שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת עַל נְקוּדָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית אֵין הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת כְּלָל
Let him know that in ultimate truth, over the quintessential Jewish core there can be no arrogance whatsoever,
כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רל"א.
as mentioned above in section 231.

rich.text: The seventh and the inward point of freedom

paragraphs.text: Outward concealment does not erase the inner point described by seventh-year release.

rich.text: Outward concealment does not erase the inner point described by seventh-year release.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 2:3: “As stated in the Zohar (Mishpatim 94): ‘If she is from the side of the Shekhinah, which is the seventh, certainly what is written? In the seventh he shall go free without payment.’ A soul from the side of a servant indicates concealment of the light, on account of which a little servitude is borne outwardly. But a soul from the side of the Shekhinah indicates the essential point of Israel, and that point does not bear any servitude at all. At the Exodus, that point's freedom was revealed without any concealment, for the light shone without an intervening screen. Concerning such illumination it says there, ‘But a soul from the side of the Shekhinah, which is the seventh—certainly what is written? In the seventh he shall go free without payment’: they went free from all four exiles.”

But a soul from the side of the Shekhinah indicates the essential point of Israel, and that point does not bear any servitude at all. At the Exodus, that point's freedom was revealed without any concealment, for the light shone without an intervening screen. Concerning such illumination it says there, ‘But a soul from the side of the Shekhinah, which is the seventh—certainly what is written? paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim reads ‘in the seventh he shall go free’ through the same inner point that cannot be enslaved. It distinguishes that point from the outward concealment in which servitude appears. This develops the siman's seventh-day and seventh-year correspondence; the source's Pesach setting is preserved rather than being presented as an identical account of every detail of Shabbat.

items.h: Freedom in the seventh year

p: וְזֶה נִקְרָא שְׁבִיעִית, שֶׁהוּא הַמֶּרְכָּז מֵהָעֲגֻלָּה,
And this is designated as the seventh, which constitutes the central axis of the circle;
וְשֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים הַיְינוּ מִצַּד חוֹחִים הַסּוֹבְבִים לַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
whereas the six years correspond to the thorns that encircle the rose, as is known.
כִּי הַמִּדּוֹת הֵם שֵׁשׁ קְצָווֹת,
For emotional attributes correspond to the six spatial dimensions;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִטַּמְטֵם הַלֵּב לְגַמְרֵי,
and when the heart becomes entirely blocked and desensitized,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי מְכִירַת פֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִידּוּשִׁין (כ.),
which occurs through illicitly trafficking in the produce of the Sabbatical year as stated in Kiddushin (20a),
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי טַעַם שְׁמִטָּה הוּא הַכָּרָה כִּי לַה' הָאָרֶץ,
meaning: because the reason of the Sabbatical year is the recognition that the earth is Hashem's,
וְזֶה נֶעְדַּר מִמֶּנּוּ הַכָּרָה זוֹ מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הַמַּשְׁכִּיחַ.
and this person became bereft of this recognition due to the inclination that induces forgetfulness.
וּבַפַּעַם הַשִּׁשִּׁית הוּא מוֹכֵר עַצְמוֹ, עַיֵּין שָׁם הַסֵּדֶר.
And upon the sixth progressive descent he sells his very self, see the sequence outlined there.
וְהַיְינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁתַּלֵּם בְּמַדְרֵגַת הָרַע בְּשֵׁשׁ קְצָווֹת,
And that is: when he has fully completed the descent of evil throughout all six dimensions,
אָז "שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים יַעֲבֹד",
then 'six years shall he serve';
אֲבָל בַּשְּׁבִיעִי, שֶׁהוּא סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה הַדָּבוּק בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה בְּהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
yet in the seventh, which is the culmination of action cleaving unto the primordial thought within the Root that derives from Hashem, blessed be He,
הוּא חָפְשִׁי.
he is free.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת "עֲבָדַי הֵם וְכוּלֵי" (וַיִּקְרָא כה, מב),
For in absolute truth, 'they are My servants, etc.' (Leviticus 25:42),
"וּבְחֵמָה שְׁפוּכָה אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם" (יְחֶזְקֵאל כ, לג),
and 'with fury poured out will I rule over you' (Ezekiel 20:33),
אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִצַּד הַכָּרַת הַלֵּב מִצַּד הַאֲפָלַת הַיֵּצֶר.
even when this does not stem from conscious recognition in the heart due to the clouding darkness of the inclination.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And this is designated as the seventh, which constitutes the central axis of the circle;

paragraphs.text: Derekh Chayyim 5:15:11: “The number seven signifies the level at which the physical and the nonphysical are joined. It is known that seven corresponds to the six extremities and the center, which is called the “Holy Palace” among them. This is known to those who understand: seven corresponds to the six extremities and the Holy Palace among them. The six extremities are especially related to the physical, for they possess extension, and extension belongs to a body. The center, however, has no extension at all, for extension does not apply to the center; it is therefore related to the nonphysical. This is why they called the center the “Holy Palace” within the six extremities: it is separate from the physical, and this is its holiness.”

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 20a:21: “He does not come to his senses until he borrows at interest, as it says, “If your brother becomes poor and his hand falters beside you,” and next to it, “Do not take from him interest.” He does not come to his senses until he sells himself, as it says, “If your brother becomes poor beside you and is sold to you.””

paragraphs.text: Context: The Talmud traces a progression of losses from trading in Sabbatical produce to selling oneself into servitude. The intervening stages include selling land, a house, and a daughter. The endpoint is necessary for Rav Tzadok’s explanation of how the Hebrew servant comes to his condition.

p: וְאָמְרוּ (שָׁם): "הַקּוֹנֶה עֶבֶד עִבְרִי כְּקוֹנֶה אָדוֹן לְעַצְמוֹ",
And they taught (there in Kiddushin 20a): 'He who acquires a Hebrew servant acquires a master for himself,'
כִּי הַקּוֹנֶה הוּא הַמִּתְנַשֵּׂא עָלָיו,
for the buyer who presumes superiority over him,
וַדַּאי הוּא בְּמִשְׁפָּט,
assuredly does so within strict justice,
כִּי זֶהוּ בְּהֵיפֶךְ מַכִּיר בַּאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי לוֹ הָאָרֶץ בְּכָל הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצָווֹת.
for he conversely recognizes the ultimate truth of Hashem, knowing that the earth is His throughout all six extremities.
וּלְכָךְ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים יַעַבְדֶנּוּ,
Therefore for six years shall he serve him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא עג:):
as stated in Bava Metzia (73b):
"הַהוּא דִּתְקֵיף אִינָשֵׁי דְּלָא מַעֲלֵי בְּגּוּהַרְקָא דִּילֵיהּ",
'There was a certain man who forced unworthy individuals into his retinue,'
שֶׁמִּצַּד יִתְרוֹנוֹ עַל דְּלָא מַעֲלֵי הוּא עוֹבֵד בּוֹ.
for on account of his spiritual superiority over the unworthy, he employs him in service.
וְכָל עִנְיַן הַפְּעֻלָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And the entire phenomenon of manual labor and servitude in physical affairs
הוּא מִצַּד שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם,
stems from the fact that they do not perform the will of the Omnipresent,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (לה:) עַל "וְאָסַפְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר":
as stated in Berakhot (35b) regarding 'and you shall gather your grain, etc.':
"וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁמְּלֶאכֶת אֲחֵרִים וְכוּלֵי".
'and what is more, their work is performed by others, etc.'

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וְאָמְרוּ (שָׁם):
footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And they taught (there in Kiddushin 20a): 'He who acquires a Hebrew servant acquires a master for himself,'

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 20a:14-15: “It was taught: “For it is good for him with you”—with you in food and with you in drink. You must not eat fine bread while he eats coarse bread, drink old wine while he drinks new wine, or sleep on soft bedding while he sleeps on straw. From here they said: Whoever acquires a Hebrew servant is as though he acquires a master for himself.”

paragraphs.text: Context: The saying follows the master’s obligation to provide comparable food, drink, and lodging. This context explains why Rav Tzadok calls the servant’s redemption and support a divine gift rather than unrestricted domination by the purchaser.

p: אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת יֵדַע שֶׁהוּא כְּקוֹנֶה אָדוֹן לְעַצְמוֹ,
Yet in truth he must know that he is like one who acquires a master for himself,
שֶׁגַּם הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת זוֹ אֵין רָאוּי עַל הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי.
for even this measure of haughtiness is unfitting toward any Jew.
וְהוּא כְּטַעַם "וּמִתַּלְמִידַי יוֹתֵר מִכּוּלָּם" (תַּעֲנִית ז.),
And this aligns with the principle 'and from my disciples more than from all of them' (Ta'anit 7a),
שֶׁוַּדַּאי עַל יְדֵי זֶה הָעַבְדוּת לְמִי שֶׁהוּא מַכִּיר בֶּאֱמֶת אֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for assuredly through this servitude unto someone who truly perceives the ultimate reality of Hashem, blessed be He,
פּוֹעֵל בַּעֶבֶד גַּם כֵּן,
an elevating effect is wrought within the servant as well;
כִּדְרָרְשׁוּ בְּחֻלִּין (ד:): "הָא לִדְבַר אֱמֶת כָּל מְשָׁרְתָיו וְכוּלֵי",
as they expounded in Chullin (4b): 'Behold, if one listens to truth, all his servants are righteous, etc.,'
עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ בֶּאֱמֶת לִהְיוֹת בַּשְּׁבִיעִי יוֹצֵא חָפְשִׁי וּמִשְׁתַּלֵּם.
until he truly arrives in the seventh year to go out free, having achieved completion.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְגַּדֵּל הָאָדוֹן, שֶׁהוּא רַבּוֹ שֶׁזִּכָּהוּ לְחֵלֶק עוֹלָם הַבָּא גַּם כֵּן,
And through this the master is elevated, being his mentor who enabled him to merit a portion in the World to Come as well,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָעֶבֶד אָדוֹן לוֹ
— and thereby the servant becomes an 'adon' unto him –
פֵּירוּשׁ: מַשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ וְהוּא מְקַבֵּל.
meaning: channeling divine influence to him while the master receives.

items.h: Shabbat remembrance and observance

p: וְכֵן הוּא יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי נֶגֶד שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
And so too is the seventh day set parallel to the six working days,
שֶׁעוֹסֵק בְּצָרְכֵי גּוּף בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
in which one is occupied with bodily needs in this physical world,
וּבַשְּׁבִיעִי יֵצֵא חָפְשִׁי לִמְנוּחָה וְעוֹנֶג דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and on the seventh he goes out free into rest and the spiritual delight of Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה'" (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יד).
as it is written: 'You shall delight upon Hashem' (Isaiah 58:14).
וּקְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת הִיא שֶׁפּוֹעֶלֶת.
And it is the sanctity of Shabbat that brings this about.
וּבְדִבְּרוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת נֶאֱמַר "זָכוֹר",
Now in the first Decalogue it is stated 'Remember' (Zakhor),
שֶׁדַּי בִּזְכִירָה לְבַד, שֶׁזּוֹכֵר שֶׁהַיּוֹם שַׁבָּת – בָּזֶה מְקַבֵּל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה.
for mere mindfulness alone suffices: in that he remembers that today is Shabbat, through this he receives the holiness.
וְדִבְּרוֹת אַחֲרוֹנוֹת שֶׁאַחַר הַחֵטְא נֶאֱמַר "שָׁמוֹר",
While in the second Decalogue following the sin of the Calf it is said 'Observe' (Shamor),
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַשְּׁמִירָה מֵעֲשִׂיַּת מְלָאכָה וְקִיּוּם הַלָּאו דְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה – עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא קַבָּלַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה.
meaning that through vigilant safeguarding against doing work and observing the negative prohibition, through this comes the absorption of sanctity.
וּשְׁנֵיהֶם בְּדִבּוּר אֶחָד נֶאֶמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כז.),
Yet both words were uttered in a single simultaneous utterance (Rosh Hashanah 27a),
דְּבֶאֱמֶת צָרִיךְ שְׁנֵיהֶם,
for in truth one requires both,
רַק הַחִלּוּק מִי שֶׁבּוֹלֵט יוֹתֵר,
the only variance being which aspect is more prominent,
וְשֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר קַבָּלַת:
and which constitutes the primary gateway of reception:
אִם עַל יְדֵי "סוּר מֵרָע" דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע,
whether through 'turning away from evil' of the base inclination,
אוֹ עַל יְדֵי "עֲשֵׂה טוֹב" וְקַבָּלַת קְדוּשַׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
or through 'doing good' and receiving the holiness of Hashem, blessed be He.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 16:1: “Hashem established this order: according to the person's work and self-limitation from below to above through six levels, Hashem illuminates corresponding levels from above to below, until ‘in the seventh he goes free, without payment.’ Further constriction is no longer needed. The person had limited himself at the last point, where there are no eyes and the world appears merely to follow its course, and introduced eyes there to recognize the governance of Heaven. Correspondingly, Hashem shows that this last and lowest point is the chief purpose and original intention of His will. This illumination is called ‘in the seventh he goes free, without payment.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim develops the same verse about the Hebrew servant's release. The movement through six stages culminates in recognizing divine kingship precisely where it had seemed absent. This explains the present siman's use of the seventh point as a return to freedom and Torah. The source's discussion of optional matzah after the first night is an analogy for that freedom; it does not make Shabbat observance optional.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Yitro 9:1: “The explanation is that in the first tablets it is written, “Remember.” The Zohar describes a place where there is no forgetting and forgetting does not abide. As the Midrash says, when Israel heard “I am,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts, and when they heard “You shall have no other,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. It was enough to remember verbally at the beginning of Shabbat, and throughout Shabbat one would be guarded by the holiness of Shabbat, which is fixed and established by the blessed God. In the second tablets, after the damage, it is written, “Guard”: guarding is required all day so that one does not cause damage, God forbid. As the Midrash on Psalms says: “What was created on the seventh day? Shabbat,” and so forth; “He found it entirely holiness and rest,” and so forth. “Afterward He saw that a person sins on it and incurs guilt against his life, and said, ‘This too is vanity.’” Since Scripture speaks of “those who desecrate it,” the evil inclination can enter and cause someone to desecrate Shabbat, God forbid. “Guard” is therefore required through awe, which involves human effort.”

sections.en: Sleep Also Is Good for Returning and Awakening

p: [רלח] הַשֵּׁינָה גַּם הִיא טוֹבָה לַחֲזוֹר וּלְהִתְעוֹרֵר
Sleep also is good for returning and awakening
אַחַר נְפִילַת הַמּוֹחִין בְּבִלְבּוּל מַחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת
after the falling of the mental faculties into the confusion of alien thoughts
וְהֶעְדֵּר מַחְשְׁבוֹת דִּקְדוּשָּׁה וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
and the absence of thoughts of holiness and words of Torah.
בְּעֵת הַשֵּׁינָה הוּא הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַמּוֹחִין,
At the time of sleep occurs the departure of the mental faculties,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ חוֹזֵר נְשָׁמָה חֲדָשָׁה,
and afterward a new soul returns,
כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים רֵישׁ מִזְמוֹר כה):
as our Rabbis of blessed memory stated (Shocher Tov, Psalms, beginning of Psalm 25):
וְיוּכַל לְהִתְחַזֵּק מֵחָדָשׁ לְהַעֲמִיד מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and he can strengthen himself anew to direct his thought in accordance with the will of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְנִשְׁכַּח כָּל מַה שֶּׁהָיָה בְּיוֹם אֶתְמוֹל.
with all that occurred on the preceding day being forgotten.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַבַּקָּשָׁה דִּבְרָכוֹת (טז:):
And regarding this is the supplication in Berakhot (16b):
"וְנַשְׁכִּים וְנִמְצָא יִחוּל וְגוֹמֵר",
'May we arise early and find the yearning of our heart directed toward Your fear, etc.,'
שֶׁפְּעָמִים מִיָּד בַּהַשְׁכָּמָה הוּא מוֹצֵא עַצְמוֹ בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה,
for sometimes, immediately upon awakening, one finds himself a new creation,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים דִּבְכָל יוֹם נַעֲשֶׂה בְּרִיָּה חֲדָשָׁה,
as the early authorities wrote that on each day a person is made into a new creation,
שֶׁעַל זֶה תִּקְּנוּ נְטִילַת יָדַיִם שַׁחֲרִית וּבִרְכַּת אֱלֹהַי נְשָׁמָה כַּמּוּבָא בְּבֵית יוֹסֵף.
concerning which they instituted the morning hand-washing and the blessing 'Elohai Neshamah,' as cited in the Beit Yosef.
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "הַמְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית",
And this mirrors what we say: 'Who renews daily and continuously the work of Creation,'
וְגַם הָאָדָם מִכְּלַל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית,
and man is likewise part of the work of Creation;
וְהַיְינוּ בְּקוּמוֹ מִשְּׁנָתוֹ יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת מִתְחַדֵּשׁ לְטוֹב.
meaning that upon arising from his sleep, he can be renewed for goodness.

paragraphs.text: Entrusting the night and receiving a renewed morning

rich.text: Entrusting the night and receiving a renewed morning

paragraphs.text: Sleep can interrupt a fixed pattern of thought and make a renewed beginning possible.

rich.text: Sleep can interrupt a fixed pattern of thought and make a renewed beginning possible.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Resisei Layla 3:1: “During sleep, it is possible for the soul to be exchanged, for our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded in Shocher Tov (Psalm 25) on the verse 'They are new every morning, etc.,' that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not exchange souls, inferring from this that an exchange is indeed possible, only that the Holy One, blessed be He, is trustworthy and does not switch deposits entrusted to Him. This applies to one who commits his soul into the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, saying 'Into Your hand I commit, etc.,' but for one who regards everything as chance and nature running its course, it can be exchanged. And they taught (Berakhot 57b): 'Sleep is one-sixtieth of death,' just as after death we maintain (Chagigah 15a): 'If a righteous person merits, he receives his portion and the portion of his peer in Gan Eden; if a wicked person is found guilty, etc.,' so too can it happen during sleep that an exchange occurs where the spark of goodness in the soul of the wicked is transferred to another who merits it, while the wicked person absorbs the evil in his counterpart. Concerning this they described the ways of the wicked who would arise early in the morning to pursue evil, etc., whereas conversely it is stated (Berakhot 16b): 'May we awaken and find the yearning of our heart directed toward You, etc.' And this explains what they stated (Sanhedrin 71b): 'Sleep for the wicked is beneficial for them in their way, and beneficial for the world.' The reverse is true for the righteous, for even though he absorbs that good, it is nonetheless deeply entwined with much evil from its original source and requires refinement and rectification; hence it is detrimental for them and detrimental for the world, since he absorbs that good from the creatures of the world during sleep. The remedy for both is the Bedtime Shema and one verse of divine mercy, 'Into Your hand I commit, etc.' (Berakhot 5a), for no evil emanates from Before Him, blessed be He, to any creature in the world, and therefore all will be for the good.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Resisei Layla uses the same Midrash about Hashem faithfully returning the soul and the same prayer to awaken with a heart turned toward Him. It places the night within an act of entrusting oneself to Hashem. This helps explain the siman’s “finding” a new heart: the beginning is received as help, and is then a basis for renewed effort rather than a claim to permanent attainment.

paragraphs.text: Beit Yosef, Orach Chayim 4:5:1: “If you ask: Why is the morning prayer different from the afternoon and evening prayers? It may be answered: Because in the morning we become like a new creation, as it is written, “New every morning; great is Your faithfulness.” We must thank Him, blessed be He, for creating us for His glory, to serve Him and bless His name. For this reason they instituted in the morning all those blessings that we recite each and every morning. We must therefore sanctify ourselves with His holiness and wash our hands from a vessel, like a priest who sanctifies his hands from the basin before his service. This concludes his words.”

p: וְזֶה טַעַם (מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין עא:) "שֵׁינָה לִרְשָׁעִים וְכוּלֵי",
And this is the reason for what is stated in Sanhedrin (71b): 'Sleep for the wicked is beneficial for them and beneficial for the world,' etc.,
וְהַהֵיפוּךְ לַצַּדִּיקִים,
while the reverse applies to the righteous;
דְּמִסְתַּלְּקִין הַמּוֹחִין וּמַחְשְׁבוֹת דִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁלָּהֶם כָּל הַיּוֹם,
because their mental faculties and holy thoughts of the entire day depart,
צָרִיךְ לְמָחָר חִיזּוּק חָדָשׁ וְהַתְחָלָה חֲדָשָׁה,
and on the morrow he requires fresh reinforcement and a new beginning,
וְכָל הַתְחָלוֹת קָשׁוֹת,
and all beginnings are difficult,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּיוֹמוֹ שֶׁהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה מְקוּשֶּׁרֶת וְהוֹלֶכֶת.
in contrast to the course of a single day when holy thought remains continuously linked.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה אָמַר דְּזֶהוּ רַק בִּשְׁינַת הַיּוֹם, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
Nevertheless, the holy Ari of blessed memory noted that this applies only to sleeping during the day, but this is not the place to elaborate.
וְהַהֵיפוּךְ מַחְשַׁבְתָּן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים זוֹמֶמֶת וְהוֹלֶכֶת כָּל הַיּוֹם,
Conversely, the thoughts of the wicked continuously devise schemes all day long,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְדָבְקָהּ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כִּמְעַט אִם לֹא בְּקֹשִׁי גָּדוֹל,
so that it is virtually impossible to attach them to words of Torah except with tremendous difficulty,
מֵחֲמַת תּוֹקֶף הִתְקַשְּׁרוּתָהּ בַּדְּבָרִים הַזָּרִים שֶׁחוֹשֵׁב,
owing to the intense bond forged with the alien matters he contemplates;
שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ מְקַשֵּׁר לִבּוֹ בָּזֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
for the evil inclination in his heart binds his heart to this, Heaven forbid.
וְעַל זֶה בִּיקֵּשׁ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא וְגוֹמֵר",
And concerning this King David, peace be upon him, pleaded: 'Create in me a clean heart, etc.,'
בְּרִיאָה חֲדָשָׁה,
denoting an entirely new creation,
הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁינָה,
namely by means of sleep,
שֶׁיַּשְׁכִּים וְיִמְצָא לִבּוֹ טָהוֹר מִכָּל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְנָקִי מֵהֶם.
that he awaken and find his heart purified and cleansed from all worldly lusts.

paragraphs.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Recitation of the Shema Before Retiring 1:3: “Sleep during the day is harmful for the righteous and beneficial for the wicked. This is what our Sages said: “Sleep for the wicked is beneficial to them and beneficial to the world.” The explanation is that, through his deeds, a righteous person may receive the souls of the righteous in ibbur when he sleeps at night. His soul returns to him and draws with it the souls of the righteous to assist him. When he sleeps during the day, those souls return and separate from him. In particular, at night a person deposits his soul in the care of Malkhut, and it returns pure, clear, and complete. During the day, however, the soul finds no resting place in which to be deposited, and therefore loses what it received at night. With the wicked, the opposite occurs: at night they are not taken into safekeeping beneath the wings of the Shekhinah, and their souls wander through the world and draw out souls of the wicked, which come with them in ibbur. If they sleep during the day, it is possible that, through a good deed those wicked people performed that day, these souls will separate from them when they sleep. Thus there are righteous people to whom the lot of the wicked comes, and wicked people to whom the lot of the righteous comes. However, for a person of great standing, like the earlier sages, it is possible that even if he sleeps during the day, he will gain as he does at night.”

p: וּמִטַּעַם הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה נִקְרָא דָּבָר זֶה
And in the kabbalistic tradition of the Ari of blessed memory, this phenomenon is termed
עִיבּוּר נִשְׁמַת אֵיזֶה צַדִּיק בִּשְׁנָתוֹ.
an impregnation (ibbur) of the soul of a righteous master during one's sleep.
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי וַדַּאי זֶהוּ סַיַּיעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא וְעֵזֶר אֱלֹהִי
The explanation being: this is assuredly heavenly assistance and divine aid
לִהְיוֹת "נַשְׁכִּים וְגוֹמֵר" בְּלֹא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא מִקּוֹדֶם.
to experience 'may we arise early, etc.' without prior awakening from below.
וְהַכֹּל הוּא בְּמִשְׁפָּט,
Yet everything operates within divine justice:
וַדַּאי הָיָה לוֹ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב וּמַחֲשָׁבָה טוֹבָה בְּיוֹם הַהוּא,
for he certainly initiated some good deed or worthy thought during that day,
שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאָדָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּלֹא זֶה,
as it is impossible for a Jewish person to be devoid of this,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת כָּרִמּוֹן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סוֹף חֲגִיגָה)
since even the sinners of Israel are as full of mitzvot as a pomegranate (as stated at the end of Chagigah),
וּמְלֵאִים חֲרָטָה בַּלֵּב גַּם כֵּן.
and are filled with heartfelt remorse as well.
רַק שֶׁשֶּׁפַע הָרָצוֹן דְּרַע וּדְהַבְלֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שׁוֹפֵעַ בַּלֵּב,
Except that the overwhelming tide of evil desires and worldly vanities pours into the heart,
עַד שֶׁלֹּא נוֹדָע וְנִיכָּר כְּלָל מְעַט הַטּוֹב,
until the modest spark of goodness is neither noticed nor discernible,
וְהוּא כִּמְעַט בְּלֹא אִתְעָרוּתָא שֶׁלּוֹ,
and it occurs almost without his conscious awakening,
רַק מִמֵּילָא מִכֹּחַ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ הַדָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
rather spontaneously through the inherent power of his soul's root cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He.
וּלְכָךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט לְעָזְרוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִמֵּילָא,
Therefore, justice dictates that he be aided likewise spontaneously,
בְּלֹא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ,
without the conventional sequence of lower arousal triggering supernal bestowal;
שֶׁכָּךְ הוּא הַסֵּדֶר: לִהְיוֹת מַיִין נוּקְבִין וְחֵשֶׁק הָאָדָם מִלְּמַטָּה,
for normal order requires the rising of feminine waters (Mayin Nukvin) and human yearning from below,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּנֶגְדּוֹ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ.
and only then does Hashem bestow divine influx correspondingly unto him.
אֲבָל בָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא מַשְׁכִּים וְנִמְצָא
— However, in this dynamic of awakening and finding—
כִּמְצִיאָה הַבָּאָה בְּהֶסַּח הַדַּעַת הַמּוֹצֵא,
it is like a lost object found through the finder's unawares,
וּבְלֹא דַּעַת בַּעַל אֲבֵידָה שֶׁזֶּה אָבַד וְהַלָּה מוֹצֵא.
and without the conscious knowledge of the loser that it fell or that the other found it.

p: וְהַיְינוּ כַּנּוֹדָע, דְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ מְיוּחָד בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
And that is, as known, because every Jewish soul possesses a unique faculty in holiness,
וּכְמִסְפַּר הַדּוֹרוֹת שֶׁעָבְרוּ כָּךְ הֵם מִסְפַּר כֹּחוֹת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה בָּעוֹלָם.
and corresponding to the number of past generations is the sum of holy forces and Torah teachings unveiled in the cosmos.
וּלְכָךְ בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר הַקְּדוּשָּׁה הוֹלֶכֶת וּמִתְגַּלֵּית יוֹתֵר,
Hence, in every single generation, holiness unfolds and is disclosed ever further,
הַגַּם דְּהַדּוֹרוֹת מִתְקַטְּנִים כַּנּוֹדָע,
even though the generations decline in spiritual stature as is known,
לְפִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְגַּלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּגְלוּ לַקּוֹדְמִים, כַּנּוֹדָע מִמְּשַׁל דְּנַנָּס עַל גַּבֵּי עֲנָק.
because matters previously revealed to the ancients remain available, as illustrated by the parable of a dwarf atop a giant.
וְזֶהוּ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִצַּד הַסְּפָרִים;
And this manifests within Torah literature through published works;
וּבְוַדַּאי גַּם כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּלְּמוּ, קְדוּשָּׁתָם כְּבָר גְּלוּיָה בָּעוֹלָם,
and certainly, all Jewish souls that reached spiritual completion have their holiness already present in the world,
פֵּירוּשׁ: בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
meaning: integrated within the hearts of the children of Israel.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לִיגִיעָה, וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּמִתְכַּוֵּין וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עוֹשֶׂה דָּבָר טוֹב וּמַחֲשָׁבָה טוֹבָה,
Whatever good deed or noble thought a person accomplishes without toil, deliberate intention, or personal striving,
הוּא מִצַּד שֶׁכְּבָר קָדַם אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת בָּעוֹלָם.
is because that specific holy force had already been unveiled in the universe by predecessors.
וְכָל דָּבָר וּפְעֻלָּה וּמַחֲשָׁבָה הוּא מִכֹּחַ מְיוּחָד וּדְבַר קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת,
And every distinct action and thought derives from a unique faculty and a particular point of holiness,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה חֲלוּקוֹת לְאַלְפֵי אֲלָפִים וְרִבּוֹא רְבָבוֹת כְּמִסְפַּר הַנְּפָשׁוֹת.
which branch into thousands of thousands and myriads of myriads corresponding to the census of souls.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 13:1: “As is known, whenever one person has experienced the clear illumination of a matter in its fullness, the gate of that light has already been opened in the world. It remains open afterward to everyone. This is the whole purpose of the succession of generations established by the blessed God, even though they become progressively smaller. For all the lights opened in each generation by outstanding individuals among the sages of Israel are never closed again. They remain open forever and become established teachings for all Israel. Therefore, although the later generations are smaller, they nevertheless possess the advantage of a dwarf upon a giant: all the gates opened by earlier generations already stand open before them, and they continue to bring forth new teaching and open other gates. Although they are very small, they nevertheless reach deeper places, for their souls have already passed through the gate that was opened for the earlier generations.”

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: and certainly, all Jewish souls that reached spiritual completion have their holiness already present in the world,

paragraphs.text: Poked Akarim 6:1: “For every generation that passes, its Torah and commandments remain and become fixed in the hearts of the children of Israel in the next generation. Were it otherwise, what purpose would the length of the exile serve, while the generations grow ever smaller? Where would there be hope of meriting the coming of the Messiah, speedily in our days, when the earlier generations, greater and better than these, did not merit it? Although the generations themselves grow smaller and are called the “footsteps of the Messiah,” because their souls are from the heels, nevertheless all the merits of all the earlier generations, and all the Torah and commandments they acquired in this world, remain fixed and firmly planted in the depths of the hearts of the last generation. From this perspective, each later generation possesses an advantage of preparedness and standing. The familiar comparison made concerning wisdom—a dwarf atop a giant—also applies to service, Torah, and commandments. From this perspective the generations continually ascend from level to level, through the additional merits and attainments renewed in every generation, which remain forever. Sins and deficiencies, however, are cleansed by death; they gradually pass away, and nothing of them remains. Only the good remains and becomes fixed in all hearts.”
