p: וּכְמוֹ מִדַּת אֱמֶת בַּיּוֹם בְּעֵת שֶׁנֵּיעוֹר
And just as the attribute of truth during the day when one is awake
הוּא הַכָּרָה הַבְּרוּרָה שֶׁרַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנְהֵג עוֹלָמוֹ בַּכֹּל מִכֹּל כֹּל
is the clear recognition that Hashem alone governs His world in all things completely,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְלָט מִמַּחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת;
and through this one is saved from alien thoughts;
כֵּן מִדַּת אֱמוּנָה בַּלַּיְלָה בְּעֵת שֵׁינָה וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַמּוֹחִין,
so too is the attribute of faith at night during sleep and the departure of the mental faculties,
מַאֲמִין בְּחֵי עוֹלָמִים
— wherein he believes in the 'Life of Worlds'—
פֵּירוּשׁ: מְקוֹר הַחַיּוּת שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָמִים,
meaning: the Source of vitality of all worlds,
אֲפִילּוּ עוֹלְמוֹת הַתֹּהוּ וְהַהֶבֶל, הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ,
that even the worlds of chaos and vanity derive from Him,
וְהוּא יִשְׁמְרֶנּוּ.
and He shall guard him.
וּבְוַדַּאי הֵם שֶׁאֵין מַקְפִּידִים בְּכָךְ אֵין צְרִיכִים לֶאֱמוּנָה זוֹ;
And certainly those who care nothing about this require no such faith;
אֲבָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּל יְגִיעָתָם כָּל יְמֵי חַיֵּיהֶם לִהְיוֹת דְּבוּקִים בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּבְתוֹרָתוֹ,
yet the children of Israel, whose entire toil all their life is to cleave to Hashem and His Torah,
צְרִיכִים בַּלַּיְלָה לֶאֱמוּנָה עַל הַפִּקָּדוֹן.
require faith at night regarding the entrusted deposit.

items.h: Two forms of redemption

p: וְסִיֵּים: "פָּדִיתָ וְגוֹמֵר",
And the verse concludes: 'You have redeemed me, Hashem, God of truth,'
כְּטַעַם "פּוֹדֶה ה' וְגוֹמֵר"
mirroring 'Hashem redeems the soul of His servants, etc.' (Psalms 34:23)
דִּמְסַיֵּים בּוֹ מִזְמוֹר "לְדָוִד בְּשַׁנּוֹתוֹ",
with which concludes the psalm 'Of David when he changed his behavior',
שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זֶה עַל עִנְיַן רְאִיַּת קֶרִי
— which I heard that King David, peace be upon him, composed regarding the experience of nocturnal emission—
דְּלָמָּה נִבְרָא זֶה,
as to why this was created;
וְנִתְבָּרֵר לוֹ אָז בְּשַׁנּוֹתוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ צוֹרֶךְ לִשְׁטוּת בָּעוֹלָם,
and it became clarified to him then in changing his behavior that there is a necessity for folly in the world,
וְכָךְ צוֹרֶךְ לְדָבָר זֶה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שְׁטוּת וָהֶבֶל.
and likewise a need for this phenomenon even though it appears as folly and vanity.
וְסִיֵּים "פּוֹדֶה",
And Scripture concludes 'redeems',
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּזֶה פִּדְיוֹן וְהַצָּלָה מִמִּיתָה כַּנּוֹדָע,
for there is within this a redemption and rescue from death as is known,
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת (נז:):
and as our Sages stated in Berakhot (57b):
דְּהוּא סִימָן יָפֶה לַחוֹלֶה.
that it is a favorable sign for a sick person.

p: וְזֶהוּ לְעִנְיַן דִּיעֲבַד, כְּשֶׁכְּבָר רָאָה קֶרִי – יִבְטַח בְּוַדַּאי הוּא לְטוֹבָה;
And this applies after the fact: when one has already experienced emission, let him trust that it is certainly for good;
אֲבָל לְכַתְּחִלָּה יְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטָרֵךְ לְפִדְיוֹן זֶה,
yet at the outset let him plead that he not require this form of redemption,
וּ"כְבָר פָּדִיתָ וְגוֹמֵר אֵל אֱמֶת",
and 'You have already redeemed me, O Hashem, God of truth',
פֵּירוּשׁ: בְּמִדַּת הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהָיִיתִי דָּבוּק בַּיּוֹם.
meaning: through the attribute of truth to which I cleaved during the day.
כִּי תַּאֲוָה נִקְרָא שֶׁקֶר,
For lust is called falsehood,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא פִּדְיוֹן עַל יְדֵי שֶׁקֶר;
and that is termed redemption through falsehood;
וְיֵשׁ פִּדְיוֹן עַל יְדֵי אֱמֶת וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
whereas there exists redemption through truth and words of Torah.
כִּי פִּדְיוֹן הוּא עַל יְדֵי נְתִינַת הַתְּמוּרָה,
For redemption is accomplished through giving a substitute exchange,
וְזֶה הוּא כְּעִנְיַן מִקְצָת נֶפֶשׁ כְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ.
and this operates akin to the principle of a part of a soul standing for the entire soul.
וְיֵשׁ כְּעִנְיַן: "וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם וְגוֹמֵר וּלְאֻמִּים תַּחַת נַפְשֶׁךָ" (יְשַׁעְיָה מג, ד),
And there is redemption in the spirit of: 'And I will give a man... and nations instead of your life' (Isaiah 43:4),
וְהוּא לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
and this belongs to a Torah scholar through words of Torah,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
which contains a potion of death unto idolatrous nations,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פט:):
and as stated in Shabbat (89b):
"הַר חוֹרֵב" – שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ חֻרְבָּה לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
'Mount Horeb'—from which ruin (churba) emerged unto the nations of the world.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא פִּדְיוֹן אֱמֶת,
And this is termed the redemption of truth,
שֶׁהֵם לִשְׁאוֹל וַאֲבַדּוֹן בֶּאֱמֶת לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד.
for they descend into the grave and perdition in absolute truth forever.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֵלּוּ דִּרְאִיַּת קֶרִי
— In contrast to those emissions of nocturnal seed—
סוֹף שֶׁיּוֹצִיא בִּלְעוֹ מִפִּיו,
where ultimately the destructive force must disgorge its swallowed prey,
וְהוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה, וְאִם כֵּן נִקְרָא פִּדְיוֹן שֶׁקֶר.
and it is merely temporary, and hence is called a redemption of falsehood.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 89a:7-89b:1: “One of the Sages said to Rav Kahana, ‘Have you heard why it is called Mount Sinai?’ He answered, ‘The mountain on which miracles were performed for Israel.’ ‘Then it should be called Mount Nissai!’ ‘Rather, the mountain on which a favorable sign was given to Israel.’ ‘Then it should be called Mount Simanai!’ He said to him, ‘Why do you not spend time with Rav Pappa and Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, who investigate aggadah? For Rav Chisda and Rabbah, son of Rav Huna, both said: Why is it called Mount Sinai? It is the mountain on which hatred toward the nations of the world descended.’ This is what Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said: It has five names. The wilderness of Tzin, because Israel were commanded there; the wilderness of Kadesh, because Israel were sanctified there; the wilderness of Kedemot, because the primordial Torah was given there; the wilderness of Paran, because Israel were fruitful and multiplied there; and the wilderness of Sinai, because hatred toward the nations of the world descended upon it. What, then, is its name? Its name is Chorev. This disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu, for Rabbi Abbahu said: Its name is Mount Sinai. Why is it called Mount Chorev? Because devastation for the nations of the world descended upon it.”

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה.):
And this is what our Sages said (Berakhot 5a):
בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁעַל מִטָּתוֹ "חֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת" לַהֲרוֹג הַמַּזִּיקִין.
concerning the Bedtime Shema: a 'two-edged sword' to slay the damaging spirits.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַמִּקְרָא מְסַיֵּים: "לַעֲשׂוֹת נְקָמָה בַגּוֹיִם וְגוֹמֵר",
And in truth the scriptural verse concludes: 'To execute vengeance upon the nations, etc.' (Psalms 149:7),
רַק דְּהַכֹּל אֶחָד:
only that both mean one and the same thing:
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הֲרִיגַת הַמַּזִּיקִין דְּמַחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים בְּקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם,
for through slaying the demons of alien thoughts and evil ruminations via accepting the yoke of Heaven,
מִמֵּילָא נַעֲשֶׂה הַפִּדְיוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ עַל יְדֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְעַל יְדֵי "לַעֲשׂוֹת וְגוֹמֵר",
automatically his redemption is effected through the nations and through 'to execute, etc.',
וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי מְסִירַת מִקְצָת נֶפֶשׁ לַמַּזִּיקִין חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
and not through surrendering a part of one's soul to the damaging forces, Heaven forbid.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 5a:4: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Anyone who recites Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a double-edged sword in his hand, as it is said: “The exaltations of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword is in their hand.” How does this refer to bedtime? Mar Zutra, or some say Rav Ashi, said: From the beginning of the passage, “Let the faithful rejoice in glory; let them sing upon their beds,” followed by “The exaltations of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword is in their hand.””

sections.en: Through Proper Sleep Without Bad and Alien Dreams and Ruminations

p: [רמד] עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁינָה הָרְאוּיָה בְּלֹא חֲלוֹמוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים וְזָרִים,
Through proper sleep without bad and alien dreams and ruminations,
הוּא יָכוֹל בְּקַל בַּהַשְׁכָּמָה לִמְצוֹא יִחוּל לְבָבוֹ לְיִרְאַת ה'.
one can easily upon awakening find the yearning of his heart directed to the fear of Hashem.
וּלְכָךְ מְסַיֶּימֶת בִּרְכַּת הַמַּפִּיל,
And therefore the blessing of HaMapil concludes,
שֶׁהוּא בַּקָּשָׁה לְהִנָּצֵל מֵחֲלוֹמוֹת רָעִים וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים,
which is a supplication to be delivered from bad dreams and bad ruminations,
מִטַּעַם: כִּי "אַתָּה הַמַּפִּיל וְגוֹמֵר"
from the reasoning: because 'You cause the bands of sleep to fall, etc.',
וּמִמְּךָ הוּא הַשֵּׁינָה וְאֵין לְךָ לִגְרוֹם לִי רַע.
and from You comes sleep, and it is not fitting that You cause me harm.
וּמְסַיֵּים: "הַמֵּאִיר לָעוֹלָם וְגוֹמֵר",
And it concludes: 'Who illuminates the world, etc.',
דְּאוֹר הַשַּׁחַר שֶׁמֵּאִיר לָעוֹלָם יִהְיֶה בִּכְבוֹדוֹ,
that the dawn light that shines upon the world be filled with His glory,
בְּהַכָּרַת כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם,
in the recognition of the glory of Heaven,
כְּטַעַם "כָּל פָּעַל לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ" – לְקִילּוּסוֹ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים מִזְמוֹר קמח).
mirroring 'all He made for His sake'—for His praise (Shocher Tov, Psalms 148).

paragraphs.text: The beginning and end of the blessing describe sleep as dependence on Hashem’s guarding light.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 3:4: “They therefore established the blessing over sleep to begin, “Who casts the bonds of sleep upon my eyes…”—He casts sleep so that one cannot see at all—and to conclude, “Who illuminates the entire world with His glory.” On the contrary, God illuminates a person through sleep, by surrounding one with an encompassing light and guarding one, as it is said, “For the Lord will be your confidence, and will guard your foot [from being caught].””

rich.text: : “They therefore established the blessing over sleep to begin, “Who casts the bonds of sleep upon my eyes…”—He casts sleep so that one cannot see at all—and to conclude, “Who illuminates the entire world with His glory.” On the contrary, God illuminates a person through sleep, by surrounding one with an encompassing light and guarding one, as it is said, “For the Lord will be your confidence, and will guard your foot [from being caught].””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kislev comments on the same transition in HaMapil that this siman explains: the eyes cease seeing, yet the blessing concludes with illumination. This clarifies why the siman prays for sleep that will make the morning’s recognition of Heaven easier. The desired light is not ordinary sight continuing uninterrupted through the night; it is the guarding and inward renewal received while conscious control is set aside.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 60b:3: “One who goes to sleep on his bed says from “Hear, Israel” until “And it shall be, if you listen,” and says: “Blessed … who casts the bonds of sleep upon my eyes and slumber upon my eyelids, and gives light to the pupil of the eye. May it be Your will, Hashem my God, to lay me down in peace. Grant me my portion in Your Torah; accustom me to a mitzvah, and do not accustom me to a transgression. Do not bring me to sin, iniquity, trial, or disgrace. Let the good inclination rule over me, and do not let the evil inclination rule over me. Save me from an evil occurrence and from evil illnesses. Let neither evil dreams nor evil thoughts terrify me. May my bed be whole before You. Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death. Blessed are You, Hashem, who illuminates the entire world with His glory.””

May it be Your will, Hashem my God, to lay me down in peace. Grant me my portion in Your Torah; accustom me to a mitzvah, and do not accustom me to a transgression. Do not bring me to sin, iniquity, trial, or disgrace. Let the good inclination rule over me, and do not let the evil inclination rule over me. Save me from an evil occurrence and from evil illnesses. p: וְזֶה טַעַם: "וְהָאֵרָה עֵינַי פֶּן אִישַׁן הַמָּוֶת" (תְּהִלִּים יג, ד),
And this is the meaning of: 'Enlighten my eyes lest I sleep the sleep of death' (Psalms 13:4),
פֵּירוּשׁ: כִּי שֵׁינָה אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בְּמִיתָה,
meaning: for sleep is one-sixtieth of death,
וְהַיְינוּ רוּחַ הַטֻּמְאָה שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי הִרְהוּרִים רָעִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and that refers to the spirit of impurity resulting from bad ruminations, as noted above.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא בִּשְׁנָתוֹ טוֹעֵם טַעַם טֻמְאַת הַמֵּת,
And through this one tastes in his sleep the taste of corpse-impurity,
וּבַבֹּקֶר אֵין הָעֵינַיִם מְאִירִים כָּל כָּךְ מֵעַצְמָם,
and in the morning the eyes do not shine so brightly on their own,
רַק עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
except through active exertion in words of Torah,
כִּי "שׁוּרְיָינָא דְּעֵינָא בְּלִבָּא תַּלְיָא" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כח:).
for 'the sinew of the eye depends upon the heart' (as stated in Avodah Zarah 28b).
וּלְזֶה מְבַקְּשִׁים לְהִנָּצֵל מֵחֲלוֹמוֹת רָעִים וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים וּלְהַאֲרַת עֵינַיִם,
And for this we plead to be saved from bad dreams and bad ruminations, and for the illumination of the eyes,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַשֵּׁינָה "טוֹב מְאֹד" כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט).
so that sleep may be 'very good' as our Rabbis of blessed memory taught (Bereishit Rabbah 9).
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי חֲלוֹם אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בִּנְבוּאָה,
And that is through a dream being one-sixtieth of prophecy,
כַּאֲשֶׁר הִרְהוּרָיו בַּלַּיְלָה גַּם כֵּן בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהִרְהֵר בַּיּוֹם,
when one's nighttime thoughts are likewise occupied with the words of Torah he pondered by day,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִדְבַּק בְּטוֹב יוֹתֵר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רל"ח.
and through this he cleaves to goodness all the more, as mentioned above in section 238.

paragraphs.text:
Bereshit Rabbah 9:6-7: “Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said: “And behold it was very good” – and behold sleep is good. Is sleep, then, very good? This is a rhetorical question. Did we not learn: Wine and sleep are beneficial for them [the wicked] and beneficial for the whole world? However, as a result of a person sleeping a bit, he can get up and toil extensively in the Torah.

Rabbi Naḥman bar Shmuel bar Naḥman said in the name of Rav Shmuel bar Naḥman: “Behold it was very good” – this is the good inclination; “and behold it was very good” – this is the evil inclination. Is the evil inclination, then, very good? This is a rhetorical question. Rather, were it not for the evil inclination, a man would never build a house, would never marry a wife, would never beget children, and would never engage in commerce. Likewise, Solomon says: “[And I have considered all toil and all excelling in work,] that it is each man’s envy of his counterpart” (Ecclesiastes 4:4).”

items.h: David and the struggle with the inclination

p: וְזֶה הָיָה טַעַם דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁלֹּא יָשַׁן שִׁשִּׁים נְשִׁימוֹת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סֻכָּה כו:),
And this was the reason that King David, peace be upon him, never slept sixty breaths (as stated in Sukkah 26b),
וְלֹא יָדַע טַעַם דְּמוֹתָא,
and never tasted the taste of death;
כִּי כָּל יְגִיעַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּל יָמָיו לְהִנָּצֵל מִמַּחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת,
for the entire toil of King David all his days was to be saved from alien thoughts,
שֶׁהָיָה מוּקָּף מֵהֶם מַמָּשׁ מִתּוֹלַדְתּוֹ
having been literally surrounded by them from his birth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is written: 'Behold, I was shaped in iniquity, etc.' (Psalms 51:7),
וְכַנּוֹדָע דְּהוּא נֶגֶד יְסוֹד הֶעָפָר
and as is known, he corresponds to the foundation of dust
וְזָכָה רַק לְחֵלֶק הַנֶּפֶשׁ כַּיָּדוּעַ,
and merited exclusively the soul-level of Nefesh as is known,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר וָאֵרָא (כז א);
and as written in Zohar, Va'era 27a;
וְשָׁם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחֵטְא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תֶחֱטָא",
and there lies the root of sin, as written: 'If a soul (nefesh) shall sin',
וְנֶאֱמַר: "הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ",
and it is stated: 'for the blood is the life (nefesh)',
וּ"בְּרֵישׁ כָּל מַרְעִין אֲנָא דָּם" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בָּבָא בַּתְרָא נח:),
and 'at the head of all illnesses I, the blood, stand' (as stated in Bava Batra 58b),
שֶׁבּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ חֳלִי הַנֶּפֶשׁ לְכָל מִינֵי תְּשׁוּקוֹת דְּתַאֲוָה וּרְצִיחָה.
wherein lies the root of the soul's malady for all manner of cravings of lust and bloodshed.
וְעַל זֶה הָיָה כָּל סִגּוּפָיו לַהֲרוֹג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בְּתַעֲנִית,
And toward this were all his mortifications directed: to slay the evil inclination through fasting,
מִפְּנֵי כֹּבֶד אֶבֶן שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ.
on account of the heavy stone within his heart.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 58b:2: “He saw that it was written: ‘At the head of all death am I, blood; at the head of all life am I, wine.’ But if so, when someone falls from a roof and dies, or falls from a palm tree and dies, was it blood that killed him? Moreover, if someone is about to die, can one give him wine to drink and he will live? Rather, this is what should be written: ‘At the head of all illnesses am I, blood; at the head of all remedies am I, wine.’ They wrote this: ‘However, the Jewish elders say: At the head of all illnesses am I, blood; at the head of all remedies am I, wine. Where there is no wine, medicines are needed.’”

p: וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נה:) שֶׁכָּל יָמָיו שֶׁל דָּוִד לֹא רָאָה חֲלוֹם טוֹב,
Therefore they stated (Berakhot 55b) that all the days of David he never saw a good dream;
כִּי הַגַּם שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע בֶּאֱמֶת,
for even though he truly slew the evil inclination,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא נִתְנַקָּה לְגַמְרֵי בְּיָמָיו.
nonetheless it was not entirely cleansed in his lifetime.
וְהוּא מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת ל.):
And this is what our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shabbat 30a):
"בְּחַיֶּיךָ אֵינִי מוֹדִיעַ, בְּחַיֵּי שְׁלֹמֹה בִּנְךָ אֲנִי מוֹדִיעַ".
'In your lifetime I will not make it known; in the lifetime of Solomon your son I will make it known.'
וְהַהוֹדָעָה הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא הַבֵּירוּר גָּמוּר שֶׁזֶּה נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי;
And making it known occurs when the absolute clarification is reached that it is utterly pure;
וְזֶה לֹא הָיָה בְּיָמָיו עֲדַיִן,
and this had not yet occurred in his days,
כִּי הַבֵּירוּר גָּמוּר הוּא עַל יְדֵי בִּנְיַן הַבַּיִת,
because the absolute clarification comes through the building of the Temple,
שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה שֶׁבָּאָדָם לְגַמְרֵי,
which is the perfection of the Nefesh, the faculty of practical action in man entirely,
לִמְצוֹא מָקוֹם לַה' שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה אוֹרָה יוֹצֵאת לָעוֹלָם (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ד דִּבְרָכוֹת הֲלָכָה ה),
to find a place for Hashem whence light goes forth to the world (Yerushalmi Berakhot 4:5),
וּבוֹ קָבוּעַ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא יָזוּז אֲפִילּוּ רֶגַע אֶחָד.
and in it the sanctity of Hashem is fixed so that it never moves even for a single moment.
וּבְוַדַּאי מִי שֶׁבָּנָה וּמָצָא מָקוֹם קָבוּעַ זֶה לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And certainly, he who built and found this permanent place for the sanctity of Hashem,
בְּוַדַּאי נִמְצָא זֶה קוֹדֶם בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ
assuredly had this exist beforehand within the midst of his heart:
קְבִיעוּת גָּמוּר לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא יָזוּז.
a total permanence for the sanctity of Hashem that never wavers.

p: וּכְשֶׁזָּכָה לְ"לִבִּי חָלָל בְּקִרְבִּי" (תְּהִלִּים קט, כב),
And when he merited 'my heart is slain within me' (Psalms 109:22),
אָז הֵחֵל רוּחַ ה' לְפַעֲמוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ בְּבִנְיַן הַבַּיִת,
then the spirit of Hashem began to stir him to seek the building of the House,
עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ מִפִּי ה' (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כב, ח): "לֹא תִבְנֶה וְגוֹמֵר כִּי דָמִים רַבִּים וְגוֹמֵר".
until He told him from the mouth of Hashem (I Chronicles 22:8): 'You shall not build... because much blood, etc.'
פֵּירוּשׁ: כָּל מִלְחֲמוֹתָיו הָיָה בְּנִיצּוּחַ הַיֵּצֶר;
The meaning is: all of his wars were in conquering the evil inclination;
כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁנִּצַּח לַיֵּצֶר, כָּךְ נִצַּח לָאֻמּוֹת, שֶׁהַכֹּל אֶחָד.
commensurate with how he vanquished the inclination, so he vanquished the nations, for all is one.
וְזֶהוּ בְּמִדַּת "אִתְכַּפְיָא",
And this belongs to the attribute of subjugation (itkafya),
וּבָזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת קְבִיעוּת גָּמוּר עֲדַיִן.
and through this it is impossible to attain complete permanence as yet.
הַגַּם שֶׁזָּכָה לְאִכַּפְיָא לְגַמְרֵי בַּהֲרִיגָה,
Even though he merited complete subjugation through slaying it,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּיוֹמָא (סט:)
nonetheless our Sages stated in Yoma (69b)
דַּהֲרִיגַת דְּיֵצֶר דְּתַאֲוָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַהֲרוֹג דְּצָרִיךְ לְקִיּוּם עוֹלָם,
that slaying the inclination of lust is impossible to kill because it is needed for the preservation of the world,
וּבְמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם (תּוֹלְדוֹת קלח א) אָמַר דְּצָרִיךְ לַחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא.
and in Midrash HaNe'elam (Toldot 138a) it states that it is needed for passion for the Torah.

Shall we plead for mercy to take away half of it? Heaven does not grant things by halves.’ They blinded its eyes and let it go. This helped in that it no longer incites a person toward his close female relatives.”

items.h: Solomon and the transformation of evil

p: אֲבָל בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "שָׁלוֹם יִהְיֶה לוֹ",
However, in the days of King Solomon, peace be upon him: 'peace shall be his',
כְּטַעַם: "אָז אֶהְפֹּךְ אֶל עַמִּים וְגוֹמֵר" (צְפַנְיָה ג, ט)
— mirroring: 'For then will I turn to the peoples, etc.' (Zephaniah 3:9)—
לְאִתְהַפְּכָא רַע לְטוֹב,
to transform (it'hapcha) evil into good,
שֶׁזֶּה כָּל עֵסֶק שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּל יָמָיו בְּעִנְיַן נָשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת,
which was the entire occupation of King Solomon all his days in the matter of foreign wives,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
as I have written elsewhere.
וּלְפִי שֶׁהַבָּנִים תַּעֲלוּמוֹת לֵב דְּאָב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי זֶה,
And since children represent the hidden mysteries of the father's heart, as I have heard this,
לָכֵן הָיָה אָז כְּשֶׁבָּנָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הוֹדָעָה עַל נִקְיוֹן לֵב דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן,
therefore, when Solomon built the Temple, it was also a revelation of the purity of King David's heart,
כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת שָׁם).
as our Rabbis of blessed memory stated (Shabbat ibid.).
וְנִקְרָא "חֲנֻכַּת הַבַּיִת לְדָוִד",
And the psalm is titled 'A Song at the Dedication of the House, of David' (Psalms 30:1),
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא מָצָא אוֹתוֹ הַמָּקוֹם בְּסוֹף יָמָיו
for in truth he found that place at the end of his days,
כְּשֶׁנִּצְטַנֵּן דָּמוֹ אָז מִפְּנֵי מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
when his blood was chilled on account of the Angel of Death,
כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ז, הוּבָא בְּרַשִּׁ"י רֵישׁ מְלָכִים א),
as our Rabbis taught (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah 7; cited in Rashi, I Kings 1:1),
שֶׁהוּא סִילּוּק הַיֵּצֶר מִכֹּל וָכֹל, וְהוּא הֵכִין הַכֹּל.
which is the total departure of the inclination, and he prepared everything.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 2:7: “(7) This is what they said (Shabbat 30a): “In the lifetime of your son Solomon I shall make it known,” and so forth. The clarification of King David’s excellence came through the opening of the gates, for that is David’s level (fear), as stated. Yet this announcement, which clarifies the repair of what came before (as I wrote above in section 1), occurred only in Solomon’s lifetime. Through his repentance, Solomon reached the Throne of Glory, for he sat upon Hashem’s throne. There there is no sin at all, in the sense of “Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil, for You are with me.” “You” is the recognition of the blessed God as present before oneself; “with me” means actually with me in the world of the Throne, called “et Hashem your God,” as stated. Then, even “when I walk” and do whatever I may do, Heaven forbid, there is no fear of evil, for it is written, “Evil shall not dwell with You,” and no evil thing descends from Heaven. Recognizing His presence means recognizing that “the whole earth is full of His glory”; consequently evil has no existence at all. This explains Solomon’s marrying foreign women, and also the expression applied to him in the Jerusalem Talmud (cited in Tosafot to the first chapter of Ḥagigah), “One does not learn from the one who fixed himself”: he fixed himself upon a matter of Torah, entering matters that appear like walking in the valley of the shadow of death. They even sought to count him among those who have no share in the World to Come (in the chapter Ḥelek). They were answered, “Should He repay it according to you?” This means: You suppose that he is with you, a human being of your measure. In fact he is “with Me” and upon My throne, and therefore he fears no evil at all. King Solomon was the first to attain this level of “for You are with me”; down to the lowest of all levels, whoever holds fast to it will fear no evil. Consequently, what came before is also repaired retroactively.”

p: וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אַדְּרַבָּה יָשַׁן הַרְבֵּה,
And King Solomon, peace be upon him, on the contrary, slept much,
וְעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר: "כֵּן יִתֵּן לִידִידוֹ שֵׁנָא" (תְּהִלִּים קכז, ב),
and regarding him it is said: 'So He gives His beloved sleep' (Psalms 127:2),
וְכִמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יב)
and as our Rabbis of blessed memory taught (Vayikra Rabbah 12)
שֶׁיָּשַׁן עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת וּמַפְתְּחוֹת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְכוּלֵי;
that he slept until four hours into the day and the keys of the Temple were under his head, etc.;
כִּי הוּא כְּמוֹ אִסְטְמָא לְפַרְזְלָא.
for it serves like quenching for hot iron (astema le-parzela).
דְּמִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּרְזֶל כַּנּוֹדָע,
For the attribute of King David is iron as is known,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר וָאֵרָא (כד ב) שֶׁהוּא מֵעָפָר
and as written in Zohar, Va'era 24b, that it comes from dust,
וּבוֹ תּוֹקֶף הַבֵּירוּרִים מִפְּסֹלֶת הֶעָפָר עַל יְדֵי הַהַכְנָסָה בָּאֵשׁ
and in it lies the intensity of clarifications from the dross of dust through casting it into fire
[דְּאַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה]
[of love and fear]
עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אִסְטְמָא, וְהוּא מִדַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
until it becomes hardened steel, and that is the attribute of King Solomon.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 2:4: “King Solomon attained all the wisdom of Solomon, lower wisdom, through one dream. “He was wiser than all men.” There is no way to attain this wisdom while awake. Such sleep is very good: it is the deep sleep of prophecy, in which he attains much in Torah and thereby rises and labors greatly in Torah.”

rich.text: : “King Solomon attained all the wisdom of Solomon, lower wisdom, through one dream. “He was wiser than all men.” There is no way to attain this wisdom while awake. Such sleep is very good: it is the deep sleep of prophecy, in which he attains much in Torah and thereby rises and labors greatly in Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kislev identifies Shlomo’s dream as the setting in which his distinctive wisdom was received, and relates that sleep to renewed labor in Torah. This develops the present siman’s contrast between David’s struggle and Shlomo’s settled stage. The sleep is valuable through what it receives and what it enables afterward. The example therefore explains a particular completed stage; it does not make every sleep equivalent to Shlomo’s prophetic reception.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 12:5: “Rabbi Yudan said: During all the seven years that Solomon built the Temple, he did not drink wine. Once he had built it and married Bitya daughter of Pharaoh, that night he drank wine. There were two dances there, one a celebration for the building of the Temple and one a celebration for the daughter of Pharaoh. The Holy One blessed be He said: ‘Whose [dance] shall I accept, of these or of those?’ At that moment, it entered His mind to destroy Jerusalem. That is what is written: “For this city has been a cause of My wrath [api] and of My anger [from the day that they built it until this day, to remove it from My presence]” (Jeremiah 32:31). Rabbi Hillel bar Hileni said: This is like one who passes a filthy place and wrinkles his nose. Rabbi Ḥonya said: Pharaoh’s daughter danced eighty kinds of dances that night. Solomon slept until four hours of the day, and the keys to the Temple were under his head. That is what we learned regarding the daily morning offering, that it was sacrificed at four hours. His mother entered and rebuked him. Some say that Yerovam ben Nevat entered and rebuked him. How was he able to do so? Rabbi Ḥagai in the name of Rabbi Yitzḥak: He stood and assembled one thousand from his tribe and entered and rebuked him. That is what is written: “As Ephraim spoke there was trembling [retet]” (Hosea 13:1); as Yerovam spoke [he aroused] the trembling of Solomon. The Holy One blessed be He said to him: ‘Why are you rebuking him? He is a prince in Israel! As you live, I will give you a taste of his authority and you will be unable to bear it.’ Immediately, when he entered the kingship, “he became guilty through the Baal and he died” (Hosea 13:1). The Rabbis say: Certainly, his mother rebuked him. She took her shoes and was slapping him with them this way and that, and she said to him: “What, my son [beri], and what, son of my womb?” (Proverbs 31:2). Rabbi Hoshaya said: “What, my son [beni]” is not written here, but rather, “what beri.” These are the commands and the prohibitions of the Torah, which is called bar, just as it says: “Yearn for bar” (Psalms 2:12), because all its matters are clear [barim]. “And what, son of my vows” (Proverbs 31:2) – she said to him: ‘My son, your father married many wives. When Natan the prophet came and said to him: “Behold, a son is born to you…for Solomon will be his name” (I Chronicles 22:9), each of them would say: ‘If I produce Solomon, I will sacrifice all the offerings in the Torah.’ Now, I have stood and my offerings are with me, and you are sleeping? “Do not give your strength to women, or your ways to that which destroys kings”’ (Proverbs 31:3). She said to him: ‘My son, the generation of the Flood was erased from the world because they were steeped in licentiousness.’ “It is not for kings, Lemoel” (Proverbs 31:4). Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Kingdom is not given to one who distances himself from the words of the Lord, but one who performs the word of God, he will be installed as king. “It is not for kings to drink wine” (Proverbs 31:4); let kings not drink wine, lest they forget and say like the one who said: “Who is God, that I should heed his voice?” (Exodus 5:2). “Or for princes: Where is [ei] strong drink?” (Proverbs 31:4). “O” is written; woe [oi], because of wine. “Lest he drink and forget what was legislated” (Proverbs 31:5). Anyone who drinks much wine will ultimately forget the two hundred and forty-eight limbs that are in him. That is what is written: “Lest he drink and forget what was legislated [meḥukak].” Meḥukak is written [without a vav], and they are two hundred and forty-eight. Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa said: The Holy One blessed be He said: ‘I had a great House and I destroyed it only due to wine.’ The Rabbis say: I had two princes and they died only due to wine, as Rabbi Yishmael taught: The two sons of Aaron died only because they entered intoxicated with wine…The Holy One blessed be He said: ‘Because in this world, wine is trouble for the world; in the future I will render it joy.’ That is what is written: “It will be on that day the mountains will drip with wine” (Joel 4:18).”

p: וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (סב:): "שֵׁינָה בְּעַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר כְּאִסְטְמָא לְפַרְזְלָא".
And they stated in Berakhot (62b): 'Sleep at dawn is like quenching unto iron.'
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּעִיקָּר כְּאוֹתוֹ הַפֵּירוּשׁ דְּרַשִּׁ"י שֶׁהוּא טוֹב,
And I heard that the primary interpretation follows Rashi, that it is beneficial,
כִּי בְּעַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר הוּא יִחוּד חַמָּה וּלְבָנָה,
because at dawn occurs the union of the sun and the moon,
דְּהַיְינוּ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ כַּנּוֹדָע;
namely the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, as is known;
וְאָז גְּמַר שֵׁינַת הַלַּיְלָה שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
and then is the culmination of night-sleep, which is the attribute of King David,
וְאוֹתָהּ רֶגַע הוּא מִדַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
and that exact moment is the attribute of King Solomon,
וְאָז הַשֵּׁינָה טוֹבָה כְּאִסְטְמָא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and then sleep is good like quenching steel as noted above.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (שָׁם נה סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) כִּי הַחֲלוֹמוֹת שֶׁסָּמוּךְ לְעַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר מִתְקַיְּימִים,
And so they said (ibid. 55b end) that dreams closest to dawn are fulfilled,
כִּי הֵם מִכְּלַל אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בִּנְבוּאָה,
because they belong to the category of one-sixtieth of prophecy,
שֶׁכְּבָר כָּלוּ דִּמְיוֹנוֹת וְהִרְהוּרֵי דְּיוֹמָא,
since daytime fantasies and ruminations have already ceased,
וְזֶה מִצַּד הַשֵּׁינָה הַטּוֹבָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and this stems from wholesome sleep as noted above.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 62b:1: “Shmuel said: Sleep at dawn is like istama for iron. Relieving oneself at dawn is like istama for iron.”

rich.text: : “Shmuel said: Sleep at dawn is like istama for iron. Relieving oneself at dawn is like istama for iron.”

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Berakhot 62b:1:2: ““Like istama for iron”—steel in the vernacular. As it benefits iron, so it benefits the body. “Relieving oneself” means going to the privy.”

rich.text: : ““Like istama for iron”—steel in the vernacular. As it benefits iron, so it benefits the body. “Relieving oneself” means going to the privy.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Rav Tzadok explicitly adopts the beneficial explanation of the comparison: dawn sleep perfects the body as steel strengthens or refines iron. The point is the beneficial image, which he relates to Solomon and the completion of the night’s spiritual work.

sections.en: Through the Sin of Youth in Wasting Seed and Nocturnal Emission

p: [רמה] עַל יְדֵי חַטַּאת נְעוּרִים בְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה וּרְאִיַּת קֶרִי,
Through the sin of youth in wasting seed and nocturnal emission,
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא תִּקֵּן כָּרָאוּי,
so long as one has not rectified it properly,
קָשֶׁה לְהִנָּצֵל מִמַּחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת הַמַּאֲפִיל אוֹר הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ.
it is difficult to be saved from alien thoughts that darken the light of the sun.
כִּי מֵאוֹתָן טִיפִּין, שֶׁהֵם חֶלְקֵי נֶפֶשׁ מַמָּשׁ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רמ"א וְרמ"ב,
For from those seminal drops, which are literal soul-parts as mentioned in sections 241 and 242,
וְכֵן קְרָאוּם רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּנִדָּה (יג.): "שׁוֹחֲטֵי הַיְלָדִים"
— and as our Sages of blessed memory called them in Niddah (13a): 'slaughterers of children'—
הֲרֵי זֶה כְּנַפְשׁוֹת הָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁמּוֹלִידִים מַחְשְׁבוֹת רָעוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רל"ט.
these are like the souls of the wicked that engender evil thoughts, as mentioned in section 239.
וְאֵלּוּ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם חֶלְקֵי נַפְשׁוֹ מַמָּשׁ וְהָיוּ רְאוּיִים לִהְיוֹת בָּנָיו,
And these, since they are literal parts of his own soul and were fit to be his children,
הֲרֵי סוֹבְבִים אוֹתוֹ וַאֲוִיר שֶׁלּוֹ מָלֵא מֵהֶם,
encircle him, and his surrounding atmosphere is full of them,
וְהָאֲוִיר מַכְנִיס מַחֲשָׁבָה לַלֵּב.
and the atmosphere introduces thought into the heart.
רַק שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַחֲשֶׁבֶת עֲבֵירָה,
Only that it is not a thought of an actual transgression,
רַק מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה וּבְטֵילָה לְגַמְרֵי
rather an alien and completely idle thought
אוֹ לְתַאֲווֹת הֶיתֵּר וּרְשׁוּת,
or toward permissible and mundane desires,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בִּפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים שַׁעַר קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁעַל הַמִּטָּה.
as is known from the Ari of blessed memory in Pri Etz Chayyim, Sha'ar Kriyat Shema She'al HaMitah.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Vaetchanan 3:2: “Even if a person has damaged and corrupted his three levels—mind, heart and organs of action, corresponding to nefesh, ruach and neshamah—within all seven holy qualities, the forty-nine gates in each, he still has hope of purification through repentance from the depth of the heart, the fiftieth gate within each. The Sages alluded to this in the disciple of Rabbi Meir who could purify the creeping creature: it symbolizes the three impure shells together. Even if a person has become impure through them all, Heaven forbid, he can nevertheless be purified through the fiftieth gate within each. This explains the hundred and fifty reasons: the three fiftieth gates, through which there is hope of purification from all three shells.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Peri Tzadik states the distinction between the three impure shells and mixed nogah, then expressly preserves hope for the person who has damaged mind, heart and action. This helps the reader follow the present siman's several levels of repair without treating a limitation on one form of restoration as the end of all purification. The source reads the teaching about purifying a creeping creature allegorically; it does not alter that creature's halakhic status.

paragraphs.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Bedtime Shema, chapter 5: “Concerning lying down with the recitation of Shema: Know that no transgressions in the entire Torah generate destructive beings as does the wasting of semen. The reason is that when someone commits other transgressions, destructive beings clothe themselves in them and become accusers; but the punishment of one who wastes semen is great. We shall explain a great, hidden, and exceedingly wondrous mystery for repairing a person’s soul, so that he may emerge clean and pure from this sin. Know that one who wastes semen impairs thought, since he makes use of no vessel; his punishment reaches the supernal da’at of Abba and Imma. Just as he acts as a male without a female, so too, as it were, above: the drop of that soul is drawn from the male but is not imparted into Malkhut. Instead, it goes outside into kelipat nogah. This is the scale that seizes souls, mentioned in the Elder’s discourse in Mishpatim. The lower “woman of harlotry” entices Eve through kelipat nogah; that soul is drawn to her, and the power of a destructive being from the woman of harlotry clothes itself in it, becoming a body for that soul. Thus the person who wastes semen causes the drops of his children’s souls to be clothed in bodies made from the woman of harlotry: he has turned holiness and goodness toward evil. The repair of this sin is to put to death those bodies made for the souls, so that the souls may escape to their place and ascend with him each night. These are the destructive beings that a person puts to death through the Shema he recites upon his bed. Understand this great mystery.”

p: כִּי הֵן אוֹתָן נְפָשׁוֹת הָעֲשׁוּקוֹת בְּטִיקְלָא
For they are those souls oppressed in the scale (tikla)
הַנִּזְכָּר בְּזֹהַר מִשְׁפָּטִים (צה ב)
mentioned in Zohar, Mishpatim 95b
[עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּסִטְרָא דְּרַע, וְיָדוּעַ בַּזֹּהַר בְּכָל מָקוֹם "רַע" הַיְינוּ עֲווֹן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה]
[see there on the side of evil; and it is known throughout the Zohar that 'ra' denotes the sin of wasting seed],
וּדְאוֹתָהּ טִיקְלָא הוּא קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and that scale is Kelipat Nogah, see there.
וְיָדוּעַ דִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ הוּא דְּבַר הָרְשׁוּת,
And it is known that Kelipat Nogah represents the realm of permissible choices,
וְאֵינוֹ מִג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת לְגַמְרֵי.
and is not of the three entirely impure husks.
וּבֶאֱמֶת בְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ לֹא נִזְכַּר לָאו עַל הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
And in truth, in the entire Torah an explicit negative prohibition against wasting seed is not mentioned,
רַק הָעוֹנֶשׁ דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל וְעֵר וְאוֹנָן,
only the punishment of the Generation of the Flood and of Er and Onan,
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד בִּיטּוּל פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וְ"לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ";
and that stems from neglecting procreation and 'He did not create it to be void' (Isaiah 45:18);
וְכֵן כָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (נט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) דְּהוּא בִּכְלַל מִצְוַת פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה.
and so Tosafot wrote in Sanhedrin (59b) that it is included in the mitzvah of procreation.
וְזֶה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ כָּל כָּךְ עַכְשָׁו,
And this does not apply so much nowadays,
דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִישָּׂא נָשִׁים הַרְבֵּה,
since one cannot marry many wives,
וּכְשֶׁאֵין מוֹנֵעַ מֵאִשְׁתּוֹ תַּפְקִידָתָהּ.
and provided he does not withhold from his wife her marital rights.
רַק שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטֻּמְאָה הוּא מִקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ,
Rather, the root of the impurity is from Kelipat Nogah,
וּלְכָךְ הוּא רַע בְּיוֹתֵר, דְּאַף תְּשׁוּבָה אֵין מוֹעִיל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים.
and therefore it is exceedingly severe, such that ordinary repentance does not avail as written many times in the Zohar.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Mishpatim 3:23-34: ‘There is a secret here: how souls are taken captive. This entire world is governed through the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. When the people of the world conduct themselves on the side of good, the balance stands and tips toward the side of good. When they conduct themselves on the side of evil, it tips toward that side. All the souls that were in the balance at that hour are seized and taken by it. But this is ‘to its own harm,’ for those souls subdue (another reading: ‘cover over’) everything they find from the evil side, and they destroy it. An illustration is the holy Ark, which was captured among the Philistines. They gained power over it—to their own harm. So too, these souls are taken captive by the Other Side to its own harm.’

p: וְהַגַּם דַּחֲמוּרָתוֹ מִכָּל עֲבֵירוֹת נִיחָא מִצַּד הַלְבָּשַׁת חֵלֶק הַנֶּפֶשׁ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רמ"ב,
And although its gravity beyond all sins is understandable due to enclothing a soul-part as in section 242,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַאי טַעְמָא רַע מֵעֲווֹן דַּעֲרָיוֹת,
nevertheless, what is the reason it is worse than the sin of forbidden unions (Arayot),
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּיצִיאַת זֶרַע וְחֵלֶק מִנֶּפֶשׁ, וְהֵם עֲבֵירוֹת חֲמוּרוֹת בְּיוֹתֵר?!
which also involves seminal discharge and a soul-part, and are far graver sins?!
דְּוַדַּאי בֶּאֱמֶת חֲמִירֵי מֵהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
For certainly they are in truth graver than wasting seed,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר חֲסִידִים (סִימָן קעו) דְּמוּטָב לְהוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה וְלֹא לַחְטוֹא בַּעֲרָיוֹת,
and as written in Sefer Chassidim (176) that it is better to waste seed than to sin in Arayot,
וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּדְרַבָּנָן, וַדַּאי דְּהוּא מִכְּלַל ג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת לְגַמְרֵי.
and even a rabbinic union is certainly of the three completely impure husks.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם תְּשׁוּבָה מוֹעֶלֶת,
And nonetheless repentance is effective,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (נט.) בְּבָא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ,
as stated in Bava Metzia (59a) concerning one who consorted with a married woman,
וְרַק בְּהוֹלִיד מַמְזֵר אָמְרוּ בַּחֲגִיגָה (ט.) דְּלֹא יָכוֹל לְתַקֵּן.
and only where he fathered a mamzer did they state in Chagigah (9a) that he cannot rectify it.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: and as written in Sefer Chassidim (176) that it is better to waste seed than to sin in Arayot,

But he requires atonement: let him sit in ice during the winter, or fast for forty days during the summer.’’

p: רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת זֶה יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּבְּרִיאָה בִּרְאִיַּת קֶרִי בַּלַּיְלָה,
Rather, in truth Hashem established this in creation through nocturnal emission at night,
שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ הֶכְרֵחַ וְצוֹרֶךְ הַבְּרִיאָה,
which is like an inevitable necessity and function of creation;
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר שָׁם: "לְרַע לוֹ",
and that is as written in the Zohar there: 'harmful to him',
וּמֵהֶם חֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and from them emerge the pious of the nations of the world, etc., see there.
וּלְכָךְ בְּעִקְּבוֹת מְשִׁיחָא עֲווֹן זֶה גּוֹבֵר,
And therefore in the footsteps of the Messiah this sin becomes pervasive,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה,
as written in Sefer Reishit Chokhmah,
כִּי זֶה הֲכָנָה לְ"אָז אֶהְפֹּךְ אֶל עַמִּים וְגוֹמֵר".
for this is preparation for 'For then will I turn to the peoples, etc.'
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹת אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ,
And the root of the souls of the nations stems from Kelipat Nogah,
וּמֵאַיִן יִתְהַפְּכוּ לְטוֹב?
and whence shall they be transformed to good?
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר יִקְלְטוּ מִנְּפָשׁוֹת אֵלּוּ דְּזֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה הָעֲשׁוּקוֹת בִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ.
Only when they absorb from these wasted souls oppressed within Kelipat Nogah.

rich.text: An involuntary occurrence does not prove a chosen thought

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin expressly distinguishes an involuntary event from deliberately bringing it about through thought.

rich.text: Takanat HaShavin expressly distinguishes an involuntary event from deliberately bringing it about through thought.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 15:41: “During those 130 years [Adam] spent fasting to return from his sin, he also produced spirits, demons and lilin through an involuntary seminal emission, as stated in Eruvin 18b. There he is called ‘a great pious person.’ Nevertheless, ‘even the most pious of the pious…’: his heart was not yet purified of bodily desire so as not to produce flesh, and through this he experienced impurity at night involuntarily. Although it was involuntary, he nevertheless produced spirits, demons and lilin and increased the power of the impure side, may the Merciful One protect us. Certainly it was not because he had entertained thoughts by day and violated ‘Guard yourself from every evil thing’—that one should not entertain thoughts, and so forth. Although the Torah had not yet been given to warn of this, they would not otherwise have called him ‘a great pious person.’ Nor would this have been called involuntary if he had brought it upon himself through his thoughts. Therefore he certainly guarded himself completely from every trace of such thought.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin discusses Adam's penitential years and insists that his involuntary occurrence did not follow a deliberate prior thought; otherwise the text would not call him a great pious person or describe it as involuntary. This is a necessary qualification when reading the siman's distinction between an occurrence built into bodily life and chosen wrongdoing. It does not erase the source's separate symbolic account of refinement.

p: וַחֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַיְינוּ גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב,
And 'pious of the nations' denotes a resident alien (ger toshav),
עַיֵּין רַמְבַּ״ם הִלְכוֹת מְלָכִים;
see Rambam, Laws of Kings;
וְאֵין גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲרָכִין כט.),
and a ger toshav applies only when the Jubilee year is observed (Arachin 29a),
דְּהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָרֶץ,
meaning when all Israel dwells in the Land,
שֶׁאָז שֶׁפַע דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל סָבָא לְמַעְלָה יוֹרֵד לָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה,
for then the supernal influx of Yisrael Saba descends to the Supernal Land,
כַּנּוֹדָע דִּלְמַעְלָה מְכֻוָּון כִּלְמַטָּה
as is known: above corresponds to below,
וּכְפִי מַה שֶּׁרוֹאִין לְמַטָּה כָּךְ הוּא מַמָּשׁ מְכֻוָּון לְמַעְלָה;
and according to what is seen below so is it precisely aligned above;
וְאָז הוּא סוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ נִכְלֶלֶת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
and then is the secret of Shabbat, wherein Kelipat Nogah is subsumed into holiness,
וּמְקַבְּלִין חֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לִהְיוֹת גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב.
and the pious of the nations are accepted to become resident aliens.
וְאָז הַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג, שֶׁהוּא תַּרְעָא דְּחֵירוּ לְעֶבֶד עִבְרִי
And then the Jubilee is observed, which is the gate of freedom (tara de-cheiru) for the Hebrew servant,
שֶׁנִּשְׁמָתוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה,
whose soul also stems from this root,
דְּלָכֵן נוֹפֵל עָלָיו שֵׁם עַבְדוּת שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת.
which is why the title of servitude applies to him, which otherwise belongs only to gentiles.
רַק הַיּוֹבֵל הוּא תִּיקּוּן הַכֹּל אַף לְאוֹתָן נְפָשׁוֹת,
Only that the Jubilee is the rectification of all, even for those souls;
אָז יוֹצֵא נְקוּדָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית לְחֵירוּת,
then the Jewish point goes out to freedom,
וְנִשְׁאָר רַק הַהַלְבָּשָׁה וְהָרְשִׁימוּ שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר מִמֶּנָּה בִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ.
and there remains only the enclothement and the imprint left from it in Kelipat Nogah.
כִּי כָּל אוֹר מוֹלִיד רְשִׁימוּ אַף אַחַר צֵאתוֹ כַּנּוֹדָע,
For every light produces an imprint even after its departure as is known;
מִזֶּה הֵם הַגֵּרֵי תּוֹשָׁב.
and from this originate the resident aliens.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 9:4: “Impurity at the fiftieth gate would mean that one could no longer return to one’s root, like a branch severed from the root. Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, feared this: perhaps they had sunk so deeply that they would not even believe, meaning that, Heaven forbid, they had been entirely uprooted from the good root inherited from their ancestors. For this the blessed God was angry with him: that he should suspect Israel’s offspring of such a thing—that the blessed God would allow them to sink so deeply. They are His portion and inheritance, believers descended from believers, and in this respect they cannot sink so far. Although “the wicked watches for the righteous and seeks to put him to death” completely, Heaven forbid, “Hashem will not abandon him into his hand.” The blessed God showed that, although they were immersed in such darkness, faith had nevertheless not perished or been cut off from their mouths and hearts. The essence of faith is to believe precisely this: wherever a person may be, the blessed God is nevertheless with him, for “I am Hashem who dwells with them amid their impurities.” Through this he can emerge from darkness and impurity, since, with the blessed God beside him, there is no evil at all. Rather, the blessed God wished that darkness should come first, and light afterward (Shabbat 77b).”

p: אֲבָל בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה אֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב,
However, nowadays we do not accept a resident alien,
כִּי קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ אֵין נִכְלֶלֶת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
because Kelipat Nogah is not subsumed into holiness,
רַק מְחוּבֶּרֶת אֶל ג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאִים לְגַמְרֵי.
being rather attached to the three completely impure husks.
וּבִזְמַן הַזֶּה: "חֶסֶד לְאֻמִּים חַטָּאת" (מִשְׁלֵי יד, לד),
And in this era: 'The kindness of the nations is sin' (Proverbs 14:34),
כְּטַעַם "לְרַע לוֹ" שֶׁהוּא חַטָּאת לָהֶם וְחִסָּרוֹן בֶּאֱמֶת,
mirroring 'harmful to him', which is sin to them and an actual deficiency,
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם יְנִיקָתָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מִצַּד זֶה,
yet nevertheless their sustenance in this world derives from this side,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (י:) עַל פָּסוּק "בִּיבֹשׁ קְצִירָהּ".
as stated in Bava Batra (10b) on the verse 'when its boughs are withered'.

Context: The first quotation follows the homiletic reading used in the Talmud and by Rav Tzadok, reading ḥesed as kindness. Other translations render that word as reproach. This reading explains Rav Tzadok’s discussion of the spiritual benefit that sustains the nations even when an act serves their own interest.

items.h: The bedtime Shema and the soul’s return

p: וְזֶה טַעַם: "חֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת בְּיָדָם וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is the meaning of: 'A two-edged sword in their hand, etc.',
שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
which the Ari of blessed memory explained
דִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁעַל הַמִּטָּה הוֹרֵג גּוּפוֹת הַמַּזִּיקִין,
that the Bedtime Shema slays the bodies of the damaging spirits;
פֵּירוּשׁ: מִן עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה,
meaning: from the World of Asiyah,
לְפִי שֶׁחָטָא בְּמַעֲשֶׂה נַעֲשִׂים רוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין
because by sinning in physical action, spirits, demons, and lilin are formed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (יח:),
as stated in Eruvin (18b),
רָצָה לוֹמַר: כֹּחוֹת מַזִּיקִין דְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה כַּנּוֹדָע כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
meaning: destructive forces of the World of Asiyah as known, as I wrote elsewhere,
וְהֵם מַלְבִּישִׁין לְהַנִּיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ וְנֶפֶשׁ
and they enclothe the holy spark and soul,
וְגַם לְהַחֵשֶׁק וְתַאֲוָה הַנּוֹבֵעַ מִקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ;
as well as the desire and lust flowing from Kelipat Nogah;
וְאוֹתוֹ הַגּוּף הוֹרֵג עַל יְדֵי קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם,
and that body one slays through accepting the yoke of Heaven,
שֶׁהוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ דִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ
which is the antithesis of Kelipat Nogah,
שֶׁעִיקַּר עִנְיָנָהּ פְּרִיקוּת עוֹל וּשְׁרִירוּת הַלֵּב.
whose core nature is casting off the yoke and stubbornness of the heart.

p: וְאָז אוֹתָן חֶלְקֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ מִתְחַבְּרִים בַּלַּיְלָה עִם נַפְשׁוֹ הָעוֹלָה לְמַעְלָה,
And then those soul-parts unite at night with his soul as it ascends upward,
כִּי בְּעֵת הַשֵּׁינָה מוּכָנִים בְּיוֹתֵר לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִמּוֹ בְּעֵת הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַמּוֹחִין,
for at the time of sleep they are most ready to unite with him upon the departure of the mental faculties,
וְגַם הֵם מְחוּבָּרִין עִם הַמּוֹחִין כִּי טִיפַּת זֶרַע יוֹצֵא מֵהַמּוֹחַ.
and they are likewise linked with the brain since the seminal drop issues from the brain.
וּמִצַּד הַגּוּף דְּרַע הוּא מוֹלִיד מַחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים;
And from the side of the evil body it engenders alien thoughts and evil ruminations;
וּמִצַּד הַקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע,
yet from the side of the Shema,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַשְׂבִּיעַ מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְ"לָן – אֵין מְבַשְּׂרִין וְכוּלֵי" (בְּרָכוֹת יד.),
which is sating oneself with words of Torah and 'sleeps—he is not visited by evil tidings, etc.' (Berakhot 14a),
וְהוֹרֵג הַגּוּף,
and slays the impure body,
וּבְהִתְחַבֵּר חֵלֶק נַפְשִׁי זֶה עִם נַפְשׁוֹ הָיוּ לַאֲחָדִים לִהְיוֹת מַעֲלִין בַּקֹּדֶשׁ,
and when this soul-part unites with his soul they become one to be elevated in holiness,
וְאָז חוֹטֵף אוֹתוֹ מִן הָאֻמּוֹת
and then he snatches it away from the nations
וְנִסְתַּלֵּק חֶסֶד לְאֻמִּים,
and the 'kindness of the nations' departs,
וְאָז "תִּשָּׁבַרְנָה",
and then 'they shall be broken',
וְזֶהוּ "לַעֲשׂוֹת נְקָמָה בַגּוֹיִם וְגוֹמֵר" עַל יְדֵי זֶה.
and this fulfills 'to execute vengeance upon the nations, etc.' through this.

items.h: The remaining desire and its sanctification

p: וּמִצַּד זֶה הַתִּיקּוּן קַל בְּיוֹתֵר מִכָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת קַל יוֹתֵר;
And from this aspect the rectification is easier than all other sins, for in truth it is lighter;
רַק לִהְיוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה מוֹעֶלֶת,
only that for repentance to avail,
דְּהַיְינוּ לָשׁוּב הַדָּבָר כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה
meaning to restore the matter just as it was
וְשֶׁיּוֹצִיא גַּם הַחֵשֶׁק וּמַחֲשָׁבָה דְּמוֹחַ וְלֵב הַמַּלְבִּישׁ לְאוֹתוֹ נִיצוֹץ שֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹב גָּמוּר
— and to extract also the desire and thought of mind and heart enclothing that spark to transform into complete good—
זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר,
this is impossible,
כִּי הוּא צוֹרֶךְ הָעוֹלָם וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ בְּתִיקּוּן בְּרִיּוֹתָיו דְּ"אָז אֶהְפֹּךְ וְגוֹמֵר",
for it is a necessity of the world, and Hashem desires the rectification of His creations in 'for then will I turn, etc.',
וְהוּא הַתְחָלָה לְבִיאַת מָשִׁיחַ דְּ"נָהֲרוּ אֵלָיו עַמִּים רַבִּים"
— and it is the prelude to the coming of the Messiah when 'many peoples shall stream unto him'—
זֶה עַל יְדֵי אוֹתָם חֶשְׁקוֹת שֶׁל קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ.
and this proceeds through those desires of Kelipat Nogah.
דְּהַגַּם דְּהוּא עוֹלֶה עִם נַפְשׁוֹ
For even though it ascends with his soul
וְנֶחְלָץ מִן הַגּוּף הַטָּמֵא דְּרוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין
and is extricated from the impure body of the spirits, demons, and lilin
שֶׁהוּא מִן ג' קְלִיפּוֹת טְמֵאוֹת
which derives from the three impure husks
שֶׁנֶּגְדָּן ג' מַדְרֵגוֹת דְּרוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר;
corresponding to which are the three levels of spirits, demons, and lilin as I wrote elsewhere;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַחֵשֶׁק דִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ נִשְׁאָר,
nonetheless, the desire of Kelipat Nogah remains,
רַק שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לִיבָּלַע עוֹד בְּשׁוּם פַּעַם תּוֹךְ ג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת לְגַמְרֵי כְּלָל,
only that it can never again be swallowed within the three completely impure husks at all,
כִּי כְּבָר הוֹצִיאוֹ מִכֹּחַ הָאָדָם רָע,
for he has already extracted it from the power of the evil man,
רַק עוֹמֵד בְּנוֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב
rather it stands in 'brightness round about him' (Ezekiel 1:27)
עַד עֵת שֶׁיְּבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח.
until the time when death is swallowed up forever.
וְאָז יְתוּקַּן חֵטְא זֶה לְגַמְרֵי כְּשֶׁיַּהֲפֹךְ אֶל הָעַמִּים
And then this sin will be completely rectified when He turns unto the peoples
וְיֵצְאוּ אוֹתָם חֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהֵם הָעֲשׁוּקִים
and those pious of the nations will emerge, who are the oppressed souls
הַנַּעֲשִׂים עַל יְדֵי הָעֲשִׁיקָה מִצַּד הַחֵשֶׁק.
produced through the oppression on the side of desire.

p: אֲבָל עֶצֶם הַנִּיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ וְכֹחַ נַפְשִׁי הוּא מִתְעַלֶּה וְנִכְלָל בְּנַפְשׁוֹ מִיָּד,
Yet the essential holy spark and soul-power ascends and is subsumed into his soul immediately,
כְּטַעַם: אֵין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי נוֹהֵג
mirroring the principle: the Hebrew servant does not apply
שֶׁהוּא נַעֲשָׂה מִנִּיצוֹץ הַנַּפְשִׁי כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
for it is formed from the soul-spark as mentioned above;
וְזֶה לֹא יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא,
and this will likewise not exist in the future to come,
כִּי הַנִּיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ אֵינוֹ מְשׁוּעְבָּד,
for the holy spark is not enslaved,
רַק הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁמִּצִּידּוֹ חֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
only the desire, from which derive the pious of the nations, as noted above.
וְהַגַּם דְּחֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת בְּיָדוֹ לַהֲרוֹג הָרַע הַגָּמוּר שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
And even though the two-edged sword is in his hand to slay the absolute evil formed by the deed
וְנִפְלַט הַחֶסֶד לְאֻמִּים;
and the 'kindness of the nations' is expelled;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁמִּצַּד קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ נִשְׁאָר כָּךְ כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא בִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ עַצְמָהּ,
nonetheless, the desire from Kelipat Nogah remains as it is in Kelipat Nogah itself,
רָצָה לוֹמַר: בְּהֶיתֵּר גָּמוּר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם תַּעֲרוֹבוֹת רַע
meaning: in complete permissibility containing no mixture of evil,
וְאֵין נִכְלָל בְּג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת לְעוֹלָם.
and is never included in the three impure husks.
רַק בְּשַׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא, אָז נִכְלָל בִּקְדוּשָּׁה כַּיָּדוּעַ,
Only on Shabbat, which is a foretaste of the World to Come, is it then subsumed into holiness as is known,
וְצָרִיךְ לָזֶה עֵצוֹת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁיַּכְנִיס הַחֵשֶׁק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
and one requires for this counsels from words of Torah to channel that desire into words of Torah,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה כָּל הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלּוֹ נִכְלָל בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
whereby all his desire is subsumed into holiness,
וְנַעֲשֶׂה מֵהֶם גַּם כֵּן "מַמְזֵר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר שָׁם.
and from them is also formed a 'mamzer who is a Torah scholar' as written in the Zohar there.
וְהַיְינוּ: "מִשְׁפָּחָה שֶׁנִּטְמְעָה – נִטְמְעָה" (קִדּוּשִׁין עא.),
And that is: 'A family that has become assimilate—remains assimilated' (Kiddushin 71a),
מִצַּד זֶה נִשְׁפָּע לְשָׁם נַפְשׁוֹת תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים,
and through this side, souls of Torah scholars are channeled thither,
וְאָז הוּא נִתְקָן לְגַמְרֵי גַּם בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה,
and then it is completely rectified even in the present era,
עַל יְדֵי הַפְלָטַת אוֹתוֹ חֵשֶׁק עִם הַנִּיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ בְּנֶפֶשׁ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
through expelling that desire together with the holy spark into the soul of a Jewish Torah scholar,
רַק שֶׁהוּא מִמִּשְׁפָּחָה פְּסוּלָה.
only that he stems from an illegitimate family.
וְאִם לֹא נִתְקַן, אָז הוּא נִשְׁפָּע בְּמַמְזֵר מְחוּדָּשׁ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי בִּיאָה אֲסוּרָה;
And if it was not rectified, it is then channeled into a newly born mamzer through a forbidden union;
וּכְשֶׁתִּיקֵּן, הוּא רַק בְּמִשְׁפָּחָה שֶׁנִּטְמְעָה,
yet when he rectifies it, it enters only an already assimilated family,
שֶׁזֶּה בֶּאֱמֶת תִּיקּוּן כָּל הַמִּשְׁפָּחָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
which is truly the rectification of that entire family, as I wrote elsewhere.

sections.en: The Root of All Alien Thoughts Is Haughtiness

p: [רמו] שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת כֻּלָּם הוּא הַגֵּיאוּת,
The root of all alien thoughts is haughtiness,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּמַחְשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת הוּא מִצַּד הַתֹּהוּ דִּמְלָכִין קַדְמָאִין דְּמִיתוּ,
as is known that alien thoughts derive from the Primordial Chaos (Tohu) of the early kings who died,
וְצָרִיךְ לְהַעֲלוֹת אוֹתָם נִיצוֹצִין.
and one must elevate those sparks.
וְהַשְּׁבִירָה הָיָה בִּשְׁבִיל גֵּיאוּת,
And the Shattering occurred on account of haughtiness,
וְלָכֵן הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ גַּם כֵּן לְכָל מִינֵי רַע כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"ו.
and therefore it is likewise the root of all forms of evil, as mentioned in section 206.
וְכָבוֹד הוּא קַו אֶמְצָעִי דְּרַע
And honor is the middle line of evil
שֶׁהוּא מַבְרִיחַ מִקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה וְעוֹלֶה עַד לַמּוֹחַ,
which extends from end to end and ascends up to the brain,
וּלְכָךְ הוּא עַד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה;
and therefore it reaches as far as idolatry;
דְּגִילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי קִנְאָה וְתַאֲוָה,
for sexual immorality and bloodshed stem from envy and lust,
וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עַל יְדֵי גֵּיאוּת כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה עַצְמוֹ אֱלוֹהַּ;
while idolatry arises from haughtiness so extreme that one makes oneself a god;
וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל כָּל חֲלוּקַּת כָּבוֹד לְאָדָם בִּבְרָכוֹת (יד.)
and so our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded on according honor to man in Berakhot (14a)
עַל שְׁאֵילַת שְׁלוֹם חֲבֵירוֹ קוֹדֶם הַתְּפִלָּה: "בַּמֶּה חֲשַׁבְתּוֹ לָזֶה? לֹא לֶאֱלוֹהַּ!".
concerning greeting one's fellow prior to prayer: 'Wherein have you esteemed him? Not as a god!'

p: וְכֵן יָדוּעַ מֵהַזֹּהַר גִּלְגּוּלֵי עֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּקִנְאָה וְתַאֲוָה,
And likewise it is known from the Zohar regarding the transmigrations of Esau and Ishmael that they are the root of envy and lust,
אַךְ בְּגִלְגּוּל שֵׁנִי עָשׂוּ עַצְמָם לֶאֱלוֹהַּ,
yet in a second transmigration they made themselves a god,
שֶׁהִגִּיעוּ לְקַו אֶמְצָעִי דְּכָבוֹד
having reached the middle line of honor
וְעָלוּ בוֹ מִקָּצֶה לְקָצֶה עַד תַּכְלִית בַּקָּשַׁת הַכָּבוֹד וְגֵיאוּת לִהְיוֹת אֱלוֹהַּ.
and ascended in it from end to end unto the ultimate pursuit of honor and haughtiness to be a god.
וְאֵינוֹ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מַמָּשׁ רַק בְּשִׁיתּוּף,
And it is not literal idolatry, but rather in partnership (shituf),
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם מִן הָרַע דִּקְצָווֹת.
because in truth they stem from the evil of the extreme branches.
וְכֵן כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת הוּא לְהַשְׁכִּיחַ מֵהַכָּרַת אֱלֹהוּת,
And so the entire root of alien thoughts is to cause one to forget the perception of divinity,
וְהוּא הַתְחָלַת "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" קוֹדֶם לוֹ "אָנֹכִי"
— and this is the threshold of 'You shall have no other gods' preceding 'I am Hashem'
הוּא הַיְדִיעָה בֶּאֱלוֹהַּ.
which is the knowledge of God.
וּמִזֶּה נִלְמוֹד עַל הַהֵיפֶךְ, כָּךְ הֵם גַּם כֵּן הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת.
And from this we deduce regarding the opposite: such are the holy gradations as well.
וְלָכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהָיָה בְּתַכְלִית הָעֲנָוָה,
Therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who stood at the absolute zenith of humility,
הָיָה נָקִי מִמַּחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת לְגַמְרֵי כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"ד.
was completely pristine from alien thoughts, as noted in section 204.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And likewise it is known from the Zohar regarding the transmigrations of Esau and Ishmael that they are the root of envy and lust,

paragraphs.text:
Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of The New Month, Chanukah, and Purim 3:29-30: “Esau came from the side of judgment, as the son of Isaac, but he drew sustenance from the first three sefirot. Therefore it is written: “Isaac loved Esau, for game was in his mouth.” This means that a holy spark was within him, in the first three sefirot. Because of that game, Isaac loved him, in the hope that he might be rectified through it.

Elsewhere, the name is written עשיו, because he was reincarnated as Yeshua, the disciple of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachiah; and because they pushed him away with both hands and punished him, as stated. For this reason Chushim son of Dan killed Esau: he cut off his head, and the head fell inside the cave and was buried there with Jacob. Because the holiness within him was in his head alone, he was therefore buried there.”

items.h: Holy pride and inward humility

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע וְהַתְחָלַת הַנְּפִילָה עַל יְדֵי גֵּיאוּת,
Nonetheless, just as the root of evil and the onset of the fall occur through haughtiness,
כָּךְ גַּם כֵּן הַתְחָלַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה הוּא עַל יְדֵי גֵּיאוּת;
so too the beginning of holiness occurs through holy pride;
שֶׁהֲרֵי זֶה הָיָה הַתְחָלַת בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָמוֹת,
for behold, this was the commencement of creating the worlds,
וּמֵעַצְמוּת אֱלֹהוּת נִשְׁפְּעָה מַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ.
and from the very divine Essence this thought was emanated.
וּבֶאֱמֶת אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ לְשׁוּם מַדְרֵגָה דִּקְדוּשָּׁה רַק עַל יְדֵי הַגֵּיאוּת
And in truth it is impossible to attain any spiritual rung in holiness except through pride,
שֶׁיִּתְגָּאֶה לִבּוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם בּוֹ יְדַבֵּר ה'.
such that his heart rises in noble boldness to say that Hashem might speak through him as well.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כה):
And on this they stated (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah 25):
חַיָּיב אָדָם לוֹמַר: מָתַי יַגִּיעוּ מַעֲשַׂי לְמַעֲשֵׂה אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב,
a person is obligated to say: 'When will my deeds reach the deeds of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?'
הַגַּם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת כֵּן,
even though it is impossible to equal them,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לוֹמַר מְחוּיָּב וְלַחְשׁוֹק לָזֶה.
nonetheless one is obligated to articulate it and yearn for this.
וּבְוַדַּאי מִי שֶׁהוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת, אֵיךְ יֹאמַר זֶה
And certainly, one who is in absolute, passive lowliness, how could he say this?
וְיִסְתַּפֵּק בְּמִיעוּט מַעֲשִׂים וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ.
and he would remain content with the meager deeds and Torah in his possession.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And on this they stated (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah 25):

paragraphs.text: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 25:1: “Blessed is the Omnipresent, blessed is He, who chose Israel from all His handiwork, acquired them as a complete possession, and called them children and servants to His name. Sometimes He speaks with them as one speaks with many, and sometimes He speaks with them as one speaks with an individual. Why all this? Because of the love with which He loves them and the joy He takes in them, He therefore speaks with them in the singular and the plural. Accordingly I would say: every individual in Israel is obligated to say, “When will my deeds reach the deeds of my ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?” For the ancestors acquired this world, the World to Come, and the days of the son of David only through their good deeds and Torah study.”

p: וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בִּיהוֹשָׁפָט: "וַיִּגְבַּהּ לִבּוֹ בְּדַרְכֵי ה'" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב יז, ו),
And regarding this it is said of Jehoshaphat: 'And his heart was lifted up in the ways of Hashem' (II Chronicles 17:6),
וְנֶאֱמַר זֶה רַק בּוֹ
and this is stated uniquely concerning him,
כִּי עָלָיו אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (כְּתוּבּוֹת קג:): "'יְרֵאֵי ה' יְכַבֵּד' –
because regarding him our Sages expounded (Ketubot 103b): ''He honors those who fear Hashem'—
שֶׁהָיָה מְכַבֵּד תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים",
this is Jehoshaphat who honored Torah scholars',
וְהָיָה מֵשִׂים הַכָּבוֹד לַמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי וּמְכַבֵּד אֲחֵרִים,
and he placed honor in its proper venue and honored others,
וְהָיָה מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּמִדַּת הַגֵּיאוּת בַּמָּקוֹם הָרָאוּי.
and utilized the attribute of pride in its appropriate sphere.
וְגַם בִּפְחוּתִים עַל יְדֵי הַגֵּיאוּת יִמָּנַע מִכַּמָּה מִינֵי עֲבֵירוֹת
And even among commoners, through personal pride one refrains from many sins
שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד כְּבוֹדוֹ,
that run counter to his personal dignity,
וַהֲרֵי זֶה טוֹב וּכְנִיסָה לִקְדוּשָּׁה;
and behold, this is good and an entry into holiness;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מוֹנֵעַ בִּשְׁבִיל הַגֵּיאוּת,
even though he holds back solely on account of pride,
הֲרֵי זֶה עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה כז:): "מְשַׁבֵּחַ אֲנִי אֶת הָעַצְלָנִים וְכוּלֵי",
this is in the manner of what they said (Sukkah 27b): 'I praise the indolent, etc.',
וְעַצְלוּת גַּם כֵּן גָּרוּעַ.
and indolence is likewise otherwise negative.

p: וְכֵן אוֹתוֹ גֵּיאוּת הֲרֵי נַעֲשֶׂה מֶרְכָּבָה לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
And so that pride becomes a vehicle for holiness,
וְהוּא מַלְבּוּשֵׁי גֵּיאוּת דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "ה' מָלָךְ גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ" (תְּהִלִּים צג, א).
and it represents the garments of majesty of Hashem, as it is said: 'Hashem reigns, He is robed in majesty'.
וְכֵן הָאָדָם הַדָּבֵק בְּמִדּוֹתָיו צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לְבוּשׁ דְּגֵיאוּת,
And so a person cleaving to His attributes must wear a garment of noble dignity,
וּבִפְנִימִיּוּת מַכִּיר שִׁפְלוּתוֹ,
while inwardly recognizing his own utter lowliness,
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם בַּלְּבוּשׁ יִהְיֶה כֵּן;
only that outwardly in his demeanor let it be thus;
כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּנוֹ: "הַנְהֵג נְשִׂיאוּתְךָ בְּרָמִים" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּתוּבּוֹת שָׁם),
as Rebbe commanded his son Rabban Gamliel: 'Conduct your leadership with loftiness' (Ketubot ibid.),
כִּי זֶה מוֹעִיל לְהַשָּׂגַת מַדְרֵגוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
for this assists in the attainment of spiritual levels as noted above.
וְכֵן בְּכָל אָדָם מוֹעִיל לְהַצָּלָה מֵרַע עַל כָּל פָּנִים,
And so too for every man it aids in rescue from evil at any rate,
כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בִּלְבוּשׁ דְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם וּמִשְׁתַּמְּעִין מִילּוֹהִי כְּצוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנָן,
when he appears in the dignified garb of a scholar and his words resonate as an accomplished student of the Rabbis,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה לֹא יוּכַל לַעֲשׂוֹת דְּבָרִים הַמְכוֹעָרִים לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם.
whereby through this he will be unable to commit deeds disgraceful to a Torah scholar.

paragraphs.text: Outward strength with inward humility
Rav Tzadok distinguishes destructive self-exaltation from the strength needed to enter avodas Hashem.

rich.text: Rav Tzadok distinguishes destructive self-exaltation from the strength needed to enter avodas Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Resisei Layla 14:1: “and 'before honor comes humility' (Proverbs 15:33), for the ultimate strength of Israel's light is designated as humility. Reflecting the nature of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who is the greatest in Israel, whose greatness lay in: 'And the man Moses was exceedingly humble, etc.' (Numbers 12:3). For exalted majesty (ge'ut) is the outward garment of Hashem, blessed be He, as it is written: 'Hashem reigns, He is robed in majesty' (Psalms 93:1); meaning: the World of Action and what is visible to the eyes of flesh and blood, this is termed the garment of Hashem, blessed be He, like a garment that conceals and shrouds the body. And from the perspective of this outer vestment, Hashem is described as 'exceedingly exalted,' for in this physical world, sovereignty and ruling power are termed grandeur, since being sovereign over all is viewed as lofty majesty and greatness. Yet according to ultimate truth, this is nothing other than lowliness, in the spirit of (Horayot 10b): 'Servitude am I conferring upon you,' for one who descends to exercise dominion over lowly, base subjects experiences lowering, becoming a head to foxes. And for the children of Israel, who recognize the inner truth (Megillah 31a): "Wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility," "I dwell with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit, etc." (Isaiah 57:15). And so they cling unto Him; the supreme force of their light is humility,”

And from the perspective of this outer vestment, Hashem is described as 'exceedingly exalted,' for in this physical world, sovereignty and ruling power are termed grandeur, since being sovereign over all is viewed as lofty majesty and greatness. Yet according to ultimate truth, this is nothing other than lowliness, in the spirit of (Horayot 10b): 'Servitude am I conferring upon you,' for one who descends to exercise dominion over lowly, base subjects experiences lowering, becoming a head to foxes. And for the children of Israel, who recognize the inner truth (Megillah 31a): "Wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility," "I dwell with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit, etc." (Isaiah 57:15). And so they cling unto Him; the supreme force of their light is humility,”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Resisei Layla explains the image of greatness as a garment, with leadership understood inwardly as service. This supplies a criterion for the difficult distinction in this siman. The useful outward bearing is a means of responsibility and service, while the inner recognition remains humble; self-exaltation that becomes an independent inner claim reproduces the very root of distraction the siman warns against.

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּזֶה הַגֵּיאוּת הַטּוֹב יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן רַע,
Nevertheless within this positive pride there also exists potential evil,
כְּמוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל: חַטַּאת נְעוּרִים הַמָּצוּי בִּנְעָרִים גַּם כֵּן
such as, by way of example, the sin of youth prevalent among young men as well
כַּאֲשֶׁר בּוֹשׁ לִהְיוֹת מָצוּי וְכוּלֵי כַּנּוֹדָע.
when one is ashamed to seek out illicit relations, as is known.
וּפְעָמִים מְעוֹרָב בַּעֲווֹן זֶה דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה גֵּיאוּת הַטּוֹבָה,
And sometimes there is intermingled in this sin of wasting seed a noble pride,
דְּבוֹשׁ לַעֲשׂוֹת אִיסּוּר גָּמוּר בְּעֶרְוָה וְנִדָּה,
in that he is ashamed to commit an absolute prohibition in forbidden unions or menstruation,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה.
and through this he succumbs to wasting seed.

items.h: The Hebrew servant and the correction of pride

p: וּמִזֶּה הוּא נֶפֶשׁ הָעֶבֶד עִבְרִי,
And from this stems the soul of the Hebrew servant;
כִּי בְּסָבָא דְּמִשְׁפָּטִים דָּרַשׁ פָּרָשַׁת אָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה
for in the Sava de-Mishpatim (Zohar II 95b) he expounds the passage of the Hebrew maidservant
עַל נְשָׁמוֹת הָעֲשׁוּקוֹת, דְּהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה
concerning the oppressed souls, that is, through wasting seed
כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רמ"ה.
as noted above in section 245.
וּבְוַדַּאי כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ הָאָמָה הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ זוֹ דְּזֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה
And certainly according to the literal sense, the maidservant represents the root of this soul of wasted seed
שֶׁהָאָב הִכְנִיסָהּ לִקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ.
which the father plunged into Kelipat Nogah.
וְלָכֵן הָאָב מוֹכֵר בִּתּוֹ וְהִיא נוּקְבָא,
And therefore the father sells his daughter, she being female,
כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נִדָּה לא.): "תָּלָה הַנְּקֵבוֹת בַּזְּכָרִים",
as our Rabbis taught (Niddah 31a): 'Scripture attributes female births to the male emissions',
דְּמִזֶּרַע הַזָּכָר הֵם נְקֵבוֹת.
for from the seed of the male originate females.
אֲבָל הָעֶבֶד עִבְרִי שֶׁמּוֹכֵר עַצְמוֹ אוֹ בֵּית דִּין בִּגְנֵיבָתוֹ,
However, the Hebrew servant who sells himself or whom the court sells for his theft,
זֶה הוּא מִצַּד הַגֵּיאוּת שֶׁבָּזֶה,
this stems from the pride involved in this,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ דְּכוּרָא,
which represents the masculine force,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי דְּגֵיאוּת וְכָבוֹד הוּא דְּכוּרָא
as I wrote that pride and honor are masculine
לְקִנְאָה וְתַאֲוָה שֶׁהוּא הָעִיקָּר בְּנוּקְבָא,
relative to envy and lust which predominate in the feminine,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן גֵּיאוּת וּמֶמְשָׁלָה בִּזְכָרִים.
whereas pride and dominion are in males.

p: וּבְוַדַּאי עוֹנֶשׁ הָעֶבֶד עִבְרִי עַל יְדֵי תּוֹקֶף הַגֵּיאוּת
And certainly the retribution of the Hebrew servant for excessive pride
בָּא מִשְׁפָּטוֹ: תּוֹקֶף הַשִּׁפְלוּת.
is visited in his judicial verdict: extreme lowliness.
וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ וַדַּאי מִגֵּיאוּת,
And his root is certainly from pride,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִן הָעֲשׁוּקִים,
and he is likewise from among the oppressed souls,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַגֵּיאוּת שֶׁבְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
namely through the pride linked with wasting seed,
כְּשֶׁהַהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה הָיָה עַל יְדֵי גֵּיאוּת.
when the wasting of seed was accompanied by pride.
וְאִם הוּא לְהִנָּצֵל מֵעֲבֵירָה חֲמוּרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
And if it was done to escape a graver sin as noted above,
אָז בַּשְּׁבִיעִית יֵצֵא חָפְשִׁי,
then in the seventh year he goes out free,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר שָׁם (קה ב) דְּנָחִית לְעָלְמָא דְּנוּקְבָא
— as written in the Zohar there (105b) that he descends to the feminine world—
פֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁבָּהּ הֶעְדֵּר הַגֵּיאוּת,
meaning: wherein pride is absent,
שֶׁהֲרֵי "וְהוּא יִמְשָׁל בָּךְ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, טז);
for 'and he shall rule over you' (Genesis 3:16);
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִתְנַקָּה מִגֵּיאוּת, אָז יֵצֵא לַחָפְשִׁי.
and once he is cleansed of haughtiness, he goes out free.
וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בּוֹ קְצָת גֵּיאוּת מִכָּל מָקוֹם
And he must retain some pride nonetheless
שֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת עֶבֶד.
so as not to remain a servant.

paragraphs.text:
Zohar, Mishpatim 3:218-221: “That old man began and said: “When you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh,” and so forth. This verse demonstrates all that has been said. Come and see: every male stands in his corresponding form in the male world, and every female stands in her corresponding form in the female world. As long as he is a servant of the Holy One, blessed be He, he cleaves to Him in those six primordial years. But if he uproots himself from His service, the Holy One, blessed be He, uproots him from those six years of the male world and hands him over to a human being, who is of six sides. He serves him for six years and is uprooted from the six years above (another reading adds: “primordial”).

Afterward he descends from there and is handed over to the female world. He did not wish to remain in the male; he descends and remains in the female. The female, which is the seventh, comes and takes him. From this point onward, he belongs to the female world.

If he does not wish to remain in her and in her redemption, he descends below, attaches himself below, and takes hold of the other side. From this point onward, he is uprooted from the male world and from the female world. He has taken hold among those servants who belong to the other side.

Now, since this is so, a blemish is required, and a mark of blemish must be made upon him, for every blemish belongs to the other side. From the Jubilee onward, he returns to reincarnation and comes back to the world as before (another reading: “If he becomes worthy and rectifies himself, he is broken”), and attaches himself to that female world, but no further. If he becomes worthy, he produces offspring in the female world. All this is the mystery of what is written: “Virgins after her, her companions, are brought to You.” Happy is he when he is rectified and becomes worthy of this.”
