p: אֲבָל אִם אָמַר "אָהַבְתִּי וְכוּלֵי"
However, if he declared 'I love my master... I will not go out free',
שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת עֶבֶד,
desiring to remain a servant,
וְהוּא שִׁפְלוּת רָעָה
this is a corrupted lowliness,
וְאֵין לוֹ אֲפִילּוּ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבַּגֵּיאוּת שֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת עֶבֶד;
and he lacks even the good within pride to refuse being a servant;
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי גֵּיאוּת שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא רַק צְבִיעוּת וְשֶׁקֶר גָּמוּר,
and that is because his pride is mere hypocrisy and total falsehood,
וּבִמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ וְאֵינוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בְּשִׁפְלוּת,
and in a place where it is unnecessary and contrary to Hashem's will he displays lowliness,
וְהוּא מַמָּשׁ בְּהֵיפֶךְ – יֵרָצַע.
which is entirely inverted—he shall have his ear pierced.
וּבַזֹּהַר שָׁם: דְּנִכְנָס בְּדַרְגָּא דְּעַבְדִין שֶׁלְּמַטָּה מִנּוּקְבָא.
And in the Zohar there: he descends into the rung of slaves beneath the Nukva.

p: וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ הַפְּשָׁט, הָרְצִיעָה וְנֶקֶב בָּאֹזֶן הָיָה סִימָן הָעֲבָדִים,
And according to the plain meaning, the piercing and hole in the ear was the mark of slaves,
וְהוּא כְּאִילּוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and it places him as though outside the camp of Israel, Heaven forbid.
כִּי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ שׁוֹרֶשׁ טוֹב,
For within Israel there resides a good root,
וְגַם מִי שֶׁשָּׁקוּעַ בְּרַע הוּא מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר
and even one immersed in evil is drawn through the external inclination
וּמִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ גַּם כֵּן בַּטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ;
and utilizes also the good within him;
רַק שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר הוּא מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּכָל דָּבָר רַק לְצַד הַטּוֹב,
except that the wholly righteous man uses every faculty solely for good,
וּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַנִּמְשָׁךְ אַחַר יִצְרוֹ.
while the transgressor in Israel is dragged after his inclination.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, לֶאֱחוֹז בִּשְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים רַק לְצַד הָרַע
— Nonetheless, grasping two opposites exclusively for the side of evil—
זֶהוּ חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל.
that is completely outside the camp of Israel.

items.h: Hearing at Sinai and release in the Jubilee

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִידּוּשִׁין כב:):
And this is what our Sages said (Kiddushin 22b):
"אֹזֶן שֶׁשָּׁמְעָה וְכוּלֵי",
'An ear that heard on Mount Sinai: For unto Me the children of Israel are servants, etc.'
דְּקָשֶׁה: אִם כֵּן בְּכָל עֲבֵירָה שֶׁעוֹבֵר יֵרָצַע,
For it is difficult: if so, upon every transgression a person violates let his ear be pierced!
וְגַם זֶה הָעֶבֶד יֵרָצַע מִיָּד בִּגְנֵיבָתוֹ אוֹ בִּתְחִלַּת מִכְרוֹ?!
And this servant too, let him be pierced immediately upon his theft or at the initial sale?!
גַּם שָׁמַעְתִּי מַקְשִׁים: אֹזֶן מַה חָטְאָה שֶׁשָּׁמְעָה,
I also heard commentators asking: wherein did the ear sin by hearing,
הֲרֵי בִּשְׁמִיעָה אֵין הַחֵטְא?!
since in the act of hearing there is no sin?!

p: רַק הַכַּוָּנָה: דַּהֲרֵי גַּם עֲבָדִים וְגֵרִים הָיוּ עַל הַר סִינַי מַזָּלַיְיהוּ
Rather the explanation is: even the spiritual counterparts of slaves and proselytes were present at Mount Sinai
כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת קמו.),
as our Rabbis of blessed memory taught (Shabbat 146a),
שֶׁהֲרֵי מְחוּיָּיבִים בְּמִצְווֹת;
for they are obligated in commandments;
רַק הָיָה הֶבְדֵּל בַּשְּׁמִיעָה,
only that there was a fundamental difference in their hearing;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ אָז בְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר: הָעֵרֶב רַב הָיוּ חוּץ לְעַמּוּד הֶעָנָן,
just as in that generation: the Mixed Multitude (Erev Rav) stood outside the Pillar of Cloud,
וּלְכָךְ אֵלּוּ סוּרָן רַע (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נט:)
and therefore their disposition was perverse (as stated in Bava Metzia 59b)
וּפְרוּצִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"ל מִכַּמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת),
and immoral (as I wrote above in section 230 from many sources),
כִּי הַשְּׁמִיעָה הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ מָסָךְ.
because their hearing passed through a barrier.
וּלְכָךְ הָרְצִיעָה שֶׁהוּא סִימַן הָעַבְדוּת יִהְיֶה בָּאֹזֶן,
Therefore the piercing which is the sign of servitude is placed specifically upon the ear,
לוֹמַר שֶׁשְּׁמִיעָתוֹ בְּהַר סִינַי הָיְתָה כַּעֲבָדִים וְלֹא כִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
to declare that his hearing at Mount Sinai was like that of slaves and not like the children of Israel,
וּלְכָךְ נִקְלְטָה אֶצְלוֹ כְּאֵצֶל עֲבָדִים.
and hence it was absorbed by him only as it was absorbed by slaves.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: as our Rabbis of blessed memory taught (Shabbat 146a),

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בַּיּוֹבֵל יוֹצֵא לְחֵירוּת,
Nevertheless, in the Jubilee year he goes out to freedom,
כִּי הַיּוֹבֵל הוּא סוֹד עוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע,
for the Jubilee represents the mystical secret of the World to Come as is known,
פֵּירוּשׁ: שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם
meaning: the transcendent hidden root of his soul which is not revealed in this world
[שֶׁאֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים מִזֶּה הוּא הַנְּשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה, שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים מֵעוֹלָם הַבָּא],
[one-sixtieth of which is the additional soul of Shabbat, which is one-sixtieth of the World to Come],
מִנַּפְשׁוֹ זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל לִהְיוֹת נִפְסָק מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
from which essential soul it is utterly impossible to be severed from the truth of Hashem, blessed be He;
וַאֲפִילּוּ נָפַל לְמָקוֹם שֶׁנָּפַל, לֹא נִיתַּק דִּיבּוּקוֹ מִשָּׁם,
and even if he fell to wherever he fell, his bond from that root was never cut,
שֶׁאָז חוֹזֵר לְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל גָּמוּר.
for then he returns to the status of an absolute Jew.

p: וְהַגַּם דְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי גָּמוּר אֵין נוֹהֵג בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה,
And although a literal Hebrew servant does not exist in the present era,
שֶׁאֵין גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נוֹהֵג
since the resident alien is not observed
לִהְיוֹת הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבְּתַאֲוָתוֹ אָז יוֹצֵא לַפּוֹעַל בְּנַפְשׁוֹת חֲסִידֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
such that the passion of his desire might then manifest in the souls of the pious of the nations,
גַּם הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת אֵין יוֹצְאִים לַפּוֹעַל בְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי וְאָמָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רמ"ה;
and holy sparks likewise do not manifest in a Hebrew servant and maidservant as noted in section 245;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, פּוֹעֲלִים וּמְשָׁרְתִים הֵם מֵעֵין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי,
nonetheless, day laborers and servants are a semblance of the Hebrew servant,
שֶׁהֲרֵי מִטַּעַם זֶה יְכוֹלִים לַחֲזוֹר בַּחֲצִי הַיּוֹם,
for it is on this account that they may withdraw even in the middle of the day,
וּבָהֶם הֵם גַּם כֵּן הַבֵּירוּרִים דְּנַפְשׁוֹת דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה בְּעֶבֶד וְאָמָה.
and within them occur likewise the spiritual clarifications of souls of wasted seed in servant and maid.

p: וְכַאֲשֶׁר הֵם מְתוּקָּנִים קְצָת,
And when they are partially rectified,
אָז הֵם מְשָׁרְתִים לְאָדָם גָּדוֹל,
they serve as attendants unto a great man,
עַד שֶׁנִּקְרָא "שִׁימּוּשָׁהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה" (בְּרָכוֹת ז:).
until it is termed 'attending the scholars of Torah' (Berakhot 7b).
וְאִם הוּא מְתַקֵּן בְּעַצְמוֹ וְקוֹלֵט אוֹתָם נִיצוֹצוֹת לְתוֹכוֹ,
And if he rectifies this within himself and re-absorbs those sparks into his being,
אָז זוֹכֶה לִהְיוֹת פַּרְנַס הַדּוֹר,
then he merits to become the leader (parnas) of the generation,
שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן עַבְדוּת בְּשִׁילְהֵי הוֹרָיוֹת (י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב).
which is likewise titled 'servitude' at the end of Horayot (10a).
וְזוֹכֶה גַּם כֵּן לִתְפִלָּה,
And he merits prayer as well,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת לד:): "עֶבֶד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ";
which is termed in the language of our Sages (Berakhot 34b): 'a servant before the King';
וְכֵן בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא מִשְׁפָּטִים (קטז ב) דָּרְשׁוּ "עֶבֶד עִבְרִי" עַל תְּפִלָּה.
and so in Ra'aya Meheimna, Mishpatim (116b) they expounded 'Hebrew servant' on prayer.
וְזֶה טַעַם: מַאן דְּנָצַח בִּקְרָבָא
And this explains: 'He who conquers in battle
[עַל יְדֵי חֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רמ"ה]
[through the two-edged sword as mentioned above in section 245]
יָהֲבִין וְכוּלֵי צְלוֹתָא
is given, etc., the crown of prayer'
(תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר סוֹף תִּקּוּן יג וְשִׁיּוּרֵי מִדְרָשִׁים).

sections.en: When Hashem, Blessed Be He, Shines His Face Upon a Person

p: [רמז] כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר פָּנָיו לָאָדָם,
When Hashem, blessed be He, shines His face upon a person,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁמֵּאִיר בְּלִבּוֹ אֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
meaning that He illuminates within his heart the absolute truth of Hashem, blessed be He,
אֵיךְ הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת "מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ"
how in truth 'the whole earth is full of His glory' (Isaiah 6:3)
וְאֶפֶס זוּלָתוֹ כְּלָל.
and there is absolute nothingness beside Him.
זֶה הוּא כְּבָר נוֹשָׁע בִּישׁוּעָה שְׁלֵימָה,
This person is already redeemed with complete salvation,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הָאֵר פָּנֶיךָ וְנִוָּשֵׁעָה" (תְּהִלִּים פ, ד).
and as it is written: 'Cause Your face to shine, and we shall be saved' (Psalms 80:4).
כִּי מְעַט מִן הָאוֹר דּוֹחֶה הַרְבֵּה מִן הַחֹשֶׁךְ,
For a little bit of light dispels much darkness,
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִכְנָס אוֹר בַּבַּיִת הֲרֵי הַחֹשֶׁךְ מִסְתַּלֵּק מִמֶּנּוּ.
and when light enters into a house, behold darkness departs from it.
וּבְשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב מִזְמוֹר פ'
And in Shocher Tov, Psalm 80:
אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא הֶאָרַת פָּנֶיךָ;
we have nothing other than the shining of Your face;
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ נֶאֱמַר: "יֵרָאֶה וְגוֹמֵר פְּנֵי הָאָדֹן"
and that is because regarding the Holy Temple it is said: 'Three times a year all your males shall appear before the face of the Lord' (Exodus 23:17),
הַיְינוּ רְאִיַּת פָּנִים מַמָּשׁ.
meaning literal, direct face-to-face vision.

paragraphs.text: The Temple's face-to-face vision and remembrance

rich.text: The Temple's face-to-face vision and remembrance

paragraphs.text: Temple vision is linked with remembrance and contrasted with the tower's forgetfulness.

rich.text: Temple vision is linked with remembrance and contrasted with the tower's forgetfulness.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Sichat Shedim 1:11: “The place of the tower causes forgetting, as the Sages said (Sanhedrin 109a), the opposite of the Temple's air, which increased the power of remembrance. For ascent to the Temple is called in Scripture seeing ‘the face of the Master, Hashem’ (Exodus 23:17). Concerning seeing King David, the Sages said (Eruvin 64b) on ‘goodly to look upon’ (I Samuel 16:12): whoever saw him remembered his learning. All the more so the Master's face. The holy Zohar (II 163b) says: who is ‘the face of the Master, Hashem’? Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, for in truth it is the same matter. In particular this is King David, whose quality is known to be called by the name Adnut [the sefirah of kingship]. As I have also written elsewhere, the Temple's holiness in the dimension of world corresponds exactly to King David's holiness in the dimension of souls. Seeing him and his atmosphere likewise brought remembrance, the opposite of seeing the tower.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sichat Shedim uses the same verse about seeing the Master's face and explains the Temple as a place that strengthens remembrance. Its comparison with David's presence develops the siman's relation between recognition and revealed presence without making its three degrees of apprehension interchangeable.

p: וְהַגַּם דִּבְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נֶאֱמַר: "וּפָנַי לֹא יֵרָאוּ" (שְׁמוֹת לג, כג),
And although concerning Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, it is stated: 'but My face shall not be seen' (Exodus 33:23),
לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ;
it was because he was outside the Land of Israel;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי דִּלְכָךְ בִּרְכַּת הַזָּן שֶׁתִּיקֵּן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מח:),
and as I heard, that for this reason the blessing of HaZan instituted by Moses as recorded in Berakhot (48b),
כֻּלָּהּ מְדַבֶּרֶת בִּלְשׁוֹן נִסְתָּר וְלֹא בְּנוֹכָח לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
is phrased entirely in the third person (hidden) and not in direct second-person address unto Hashem,
לְפִי שֶׁ"הַדָּר בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ דּוֹמֶה כְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֱלוֹהַּ" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּתוּבּוֹת קי:)
because 'one who dwells outside the Land of Israel is comparable to one who has no God' (Ketubot 110b)
וְאֵין מַכִּיר הַנּוֹכָח.
and cannot perceive the direct Presence.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא נִכְנַס לָאָרֶץ,
And Moses our teacher did not enter into the Land;
וְאֵין זֶה פְּגָם לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
yet this is no deficiency in Moses our teacher, Heaven forbid,
[וְעַיֵּין כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר],
[and see similarly in the Zohar],
כַּיָּדוּעַ מִג' מַדְרֵגוֹת אֲנִ"י, אַתָּ"ה, הוּ"א,
as is known from the three spiritual gradations: 'Ani' (I), 'Attah' (You), and 'Hu' (He),
דְּ"הוּא" מַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה
where 'Hu' is a vastly higher rung
שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג מָקוֹם יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר עָלָיו נוֹכָח
which perceives an exalted realm regarding which direct address does not apply
כִּי הוּא טָמִיר וְנֶעְלָם;
because it is concealed and transcendent;
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּעְלָא דִּמְטְרוֹנִיתָא הִשִּׂיג מַדְרֵגָה גְּדוֹלָה,
and Moses, being the 'husband of the Matronita', attained an exceedingly great rung,
וְלָכֵן לֹא נִכְנַס לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּהָיָה מַדְרֵגָתוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזֶּה.
and therefore did not enter Eretz Yisrael because his level surpassed it.

We refer to the blessed God in three modes: He, You, and I. “He” alludes to Atika, language of hiddenness and concealment—the intellect hidden from every thought. “You” alludes to Ze’ir Anpin, the name Havayah, through which we speak directly: “You, Hashem,” as is known (Zohar III 290a). “I” alludes to the Divine Presence, the field of apple trees, the souls of Israel, as it says, “I am Hashem who dwells among the children of Israel” (ibid. 223a). p: וְאָנוּ מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא מַדְרֵגָה תַּחְתּוֹנָה דְּהֶאָרַת פָּנִים
— And as for us, since the destruction of the Temple, we have only the lowest rung of the shining of the face—
פֵּירוּשׁ: זִיו שֶׁל הַפָּנִים,
meaning: the outer radiance of the Face,
וְהוּא הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁגָּלְתָה עִמָּהֶם,
which is the Shechinah that went into exile with them,
דַּרְגָּא דַּ"אֲנִי",
the spiritual level of 'Ani',
פֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁהוּא דָּר בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ;
meaning: that He dwells within his heart;
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַהַשָּׂגָה עַצְמוֹ הוּא הַדָּבָר הַמּוּשָּׂג,
namely that the perception itself is the very entity perceived,
כִּי הוּא מַשִּׂיג דְּלֵית אֲתַר פָּנוּי מִינֵיהּ
for he apprehends that no place is devoid of Him
וּ"מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ"
— and 'the whole earth is full of His glory'—
הַכָּבוֹד הוּא הַזִּיו,
this 'glory' being the outer radiance,
וְהַיְינוּ הַהַכָּרָה הַבּוֹלֶטֶת מִצַּד אֲדֹנוּתוֹ וּמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ שֶׁבַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה.
namely the manifest recognition stemming from His Mastership and Sovereignty that rules over all.
כְּמוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ, מִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאוּהוּ מַכִּירוֹ מִמִּדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ,
Like a king whom one who has never seen recognizes through his royal dominion,
כָּךְ הַכָּרַת הָאָדָם מִצַּד כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה,
so is man's recognition through the whole of creation;
כְּמוֹ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רָאָה בִּירָה דּוֹלֶקֶת וְכוּלֵי (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה לֶךְ לְךָ),
just as our father Abraham saw a palace illuminated, etc. (Bereishit Rabbah, Lech Lecha),
אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ז:):
our Sages of blessed memory taught (Berakhot 7b):
לֹא הָיָה אָדָם שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ "אָדוֹן" עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְכוּלֵי.
there was no person who addressed Him as 'Adon' (Master) until Abraham came, etc.
וְשֵׁם הָאֲדֹנוּת מוֹרֶה עַל הַכָּבוֹד וְהַזִּיו כַּנּוֹדָע.
And the divine Name of Adonut denotes glory and radiance, as is known.
וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי עַל: "הֵצִיץ עָלָיו בַּעַל הַבִּירָה וְכוּלֵי"
— And so I heard regarding 'the Master of the palace peeked out at him, etc.'—
לְשׁוֹן "עָלָיו" רָצָה לוֹמַר: שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ שֶׁאַתָּה בְּעַצְמְךָ גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלַל בַּעַל הַבִּירָה,
the phrasing 'at him' means: He said to him, 'You yourself are also included within the Master of the palace,'
כִּי הֲלֹא כָּל הָעוֹלָם רוֹאִים זֶה
for behold, the entire world observes this
וְאֵין לְבָבָם רוֹעֵשׁ כְּלָל לְהַשִּׂיג שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּעַל הַבִּירָה וּלְבַקְּשׁוֹ,
and their heart is not stirred at all to realize that there is a Master and to seek Him;
וְזֶה שֶׁאַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ, גַּם זֶה הוּא מִצִּדִּי
and that which you seek is likewise from My doing,
וּבְלִבְּךָ מְקוֹם שְׁכִינָתִי;
and in your heart is the resting place of My Shechinah';
וְזֶה טַעַם "אֲנִי".
and this is the essence of 'Ani'.

p: אֲבָל רְאִיַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ עַצְמוֹ הוּא הַשָּׂגַת "אַתָּה",
However, seeing the King Himself is the perception of 'Attah' (You),
דְּזֶהוּ תְּפִלָּה כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,
which is prayer, as one standing before the King,
שֶׁהוּא בִּמְקוֹם קָרְבָּנוֹת דְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ;
which stands in the place of the sacrifices of the Temple;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ל.):
and therefore our Sages taught (Berakhot 30a):
דִּיכַוֵּין לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים,
that he shall direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies,
שֶׁשָּׁם הוּא רְאִיַּת פָּנִים מַמָּשׁ.
for there is actual, direct face-to-face vision.
וְזֶהוּ לְמַאן דְּנָצַח בִּקְרָבָא
And this is given to one who conquers in battle
עַל יְדֵי הַחֶרֶב פִּיפִיּוֹת דִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע,
through the two-edged sword of the Shema,
שֶׁהוּא יִחוּד הַגָּמוּר עַכְשָׁו כְּעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם,
which is absolute unification now just as before the world was created,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְבַּטֵּל כָּל דָּבָר רַע וּמַחְשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת,
and through this every evil thing and alien thoughts are nullified,
וְאָז מַכִּיר הַנּוֹכָח שֶׁלֹּא מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה וְהַנִּבְרָאִים.
and then he perceives the immediate Presence not through the vantage point of creation and creatures.

p: וְהַתּוֹרָה הוּא הַשָּׂגַת "הוּא",
And the Torah represents the comprehension of 'Hu' (He),
דְּמַשִּׂיג אֲתַר יוֹתֵר נֶעְלָם
for one perceives an even more concealed realm
שֶׁאֵין תְּפִיסַת אָדָם בְּהַשָּׂגָתוֹ שׁוֹלֶטֶת כְּלָל.
wherein human comprehension holds no grasp whatsoever;
זֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא הַשָּׂגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
this is achieved through Torah which is the perception of Moses our teacher,
וְהִיא הַשָּׂגַת הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל בְּבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
and it is the perception of the High Priest in the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur,
שֶׁהִיא בְּסוֹד הַבִּינָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
which resides in the mystical realm of Binah as is known.
וְנֶאֱמַר: "שְׁלַח אוֹרְךָ וַאֲמִתְּךָ הֵמָּה יַנְחוּנִי, יְבִיאוּנִי אֶל הַר קָדְשְׁךָ וְאֶל מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֶיךָ; וְאָבוֹאָה אֶל מִזְבַּח אֱלֹהִים" (תְּהִלִּים מג, ג–ד),
And it is said: 'Send forth Your light and Your truth, let them lead me... then will I go unto the altar of God',
שֶׁהָאוֹר וְהַשָּׂגַת הַזִּיו דִּכְבוֹדוֹ מִצַּד הַנִּבְרָאִים
meaning that the light and comprehension of the radiance of His glory through created beings
הוּא "הַשַּׁעַר לַה', צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ" עַל יָדוֹ לְמַדְרֵגָה עֶלְיוֹנָה.
is 'the gate of Hashem, the righteous shall enter into it' (Psalms 118:20) by which to ascend to an exalted rung.

p: וְזֶה טַעַם הַפַּיְיטָן שֶׁיָּסַד לְפָרָשַׁת שְׁקָלִים "אוֹר פָּנֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי",
And this is the rationale of the liturgical poet who instituted for Parashat Shekalim 'the light of Your face, etc.',
כִּי הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת תַּכְלִית הַקֵּירוּב,
for sacrifices are the ultimate drawing near,
וְהַשְּׁקָלִים הוּא הֲכָנָה לַקָּרְבָּנוֹת,
and the Shekalim are the preparation for sacrifices,
וְהַשְׁמָעָה עַל הַשְּׁקָלִים הוּא הֲכָנָה לַשְּׁקָלִים.
and the public proclamation concerning Shekalim is the preparation for the Shekalim.
וְעַכְשָׁו אֵין לָנוּ שְׁקָלִים וְלֹא קָרְבָּנוֹת,
And nowadays we have neither Shekalim nor sacrifices,
רַק הַהַשְׁמָעָה עַל הַשְּׁקָלִים נִשְׁאַר מִתַּקָּנַת חֲכָמִים
only the proclamation concerning Shekalim has remained by rabbinic enactment
[מִשּׁוּם מְהֵרָה יִבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְיִצְטָרְכוּ לִשְׁקָלִים קוֹדֶם נִיסָן];
[because the Temple may be rebuilt speedily and they will need Shekalim before Nisan];
וְזֶה כְּטַעַם "אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא הֶאָרַת פָּנִים",
and this mirrors the principle 'we have nothing other than the shining of the face',
שֶׁהוּא הַכְּנִיסָה רִאשׁוֹנָה וַהֲכָנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה לְהִתְקָרְבוּת גְּמוּרָה.
which is the initial entry and primary preparation for complete closeness.
וּבְוַדַּאי הַכְרָזַת שְׁקָלִים מוֹלִיד הַרְגָּשַׁת אוֹר פְּנִימִי וְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לָזֶה בַּלֵּב
And assuredly the proclamation of Shekalim engenders a feeling of inner light and an awakening toward this in the heart
לָדַעַת אֶת ה' וְלֵיהָנוֹת מִזִּיווֹ.
to know Hashem and to delight in His divine radiance.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: And this is the rationale of the liturgical poet who instituted for Parashat Shekalim 'the light of Your face, etc.',

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Parshat Shekalim 5:1: ““Lift the light of Your face upon us, Master” is said in the Musaf prayer, in the liturgical poem within each blessing. Since these poems have been accepted throughout Israel, their words deserve interpretation. Even if their author and arranger did not intend a particular interpretation, it may still be true, as the Urim VeTummim writes concerning the Shulḥan Arukh and similar works accepted throughout Israel: their words may be interpreted even beyond their authors’ intention, because the spirit of Hashem spoke through them. “The light of Your face” indicates the light of Atika. At the Shabbat meal we say, “May its light rest within her,” and at the third meal there is the revelation of the forehead of Atika, as stated in the Idra. It is taught (Shabbat 151b), “‘The sun and the light’—the forehead and the nose.” Thus “the light of Your face” is Atika’s light “upon us,” above us like a crown upon the head. Each blessing likewise ends, “God, high and exalted,” indicating Atika, the intellect hidden from every thought. “High and exalted,” when applied to the blessed God, indicates what is without measure, beyond the grasp of all created beings, as explained many times.”

sections.en: The Essence of Man Is the Passionate Desire within the Heart

p: [רמח] עִיקַּר הָאָדָם הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב,
The essence of man is the passionate desire within the heart,
שֶׁבּוֹ הוּא יִתְרוֹנוֹ עַל הַמַּלְאָכִים,
in which lies his preeminence over the angels,
וְהוּא הַנִּקְרָא יֵצֶר: יֵצֶר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר רָע;
and it is what is termed yetzer: the good inclination and the evil inclination;
כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא מַגְבִּיר חֶשְׁקוֹ לְטוֹב הֲרֵי זֶה טוֹב, וְאִם לָאו וְכוּלֵי.
when he strengthens his desire for good, behold it is good, and if not, etc.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה נב.):
And our Sages of blessed memory stated (Sukkah 52a):
"כָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ",
'Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than he,'
כִּי גַּדְלוּת אֶחָד עַל חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא רַק כְּפִי גּוֹדֶל הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלּוֹ לְטוֹב,
for the greatness of one above his fellow corresponds solely to the magnitude of his desire for good,
דְּהַיְינוּ כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר;
which is the power of the yetzer;
כִּי יֵצֶר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר רָע אֶחָד זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה בִּשְׁנֵי חַלְלֵי הַלֵּב,
for the good yetzer and the evil yetzer stand parallel to each other in the two ventricles of the heart,
כְּפִי הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ בַּיָּמִין לְטוֹב כֵּן בַּשְּׂמֹאל לְרַע,
in proportion to the desire in his heart on the right for good, so is it on the left for evil,
וּלְכָךְ יֵצֶר הָרָע גַּם כֵּן גָּדוֹל.
and therefore his evil inclination is likewise great.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וְהוּא הַנִּקְרָא יֵצֶר: יֵצֶר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר רָע;
footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: and it is what is termed yetzer: the good inclination and the evil inclination;

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vayetzei 6:1: “Afterward the Men of the Great Assembly said: “On the contrary, this is the might of His might: He masters His inclination,” and so forth. The marginal gloss changes this to “His anger,” in accordance with the Ein Yaakov’s reading, because the phrase “masters His inclination” seemed difficult when applied to the blessed God. In truth, however, yetzer means desire, as it says, “Preserve this forever for the inclination of the thoughts of Your people’s heart.” He prayed that the desire with which they had offered willingly, wholeheartedly, should endure forever. When desire is directed toward good it is called the good inclination, and when directed oppositely it is called the evil inclination. Thus “masters His inclination” can apply to the blessed God: He has a desire to take vengeance and restrains that desire. Nevertheless, the expression “the might of His might” suggests that He restrains even His might, supporting the Ein Yaakov’s reading, “masters His anger.””

rich.text: : “Afterward the Men of the Great Assembly said: “On the contrary, this is the might of His might: He masters His inclination,” and so forth. The marginal gloss changes this to “His anger,” in accordance with the Ein Yaakov’s reading, because the phrase “masters His inclination” seemed difficult when applied to the blessed God. In truth, however, yetzer means desire, as it says, “Preserve this forever for the inclination of the thoughts of Your people’s heart.” He prayed that the desire with which they had offered willingly, wholeheartedly, should endure forever. When desire is directed toward good it is called the good inclination, and when directed oppositely it is called the evil inclination. Thus “masters His inclination” can apply to the blessed God: He has a desire to take vengeance and restrains that desire. Nevertheless, the expression “the might of His might” suggests that He restrains even His might, supporting the Ein Yaakov’s reading, “masters His anger.””

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְנָחוֹת כט:):
And this explains what our Sages taught (Menachot 29b):
עוֹלָם הַזֶּה נִבְרָא בְּהֵ"א וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּיוֹ"ד,
this world was created with the letter Hei, and the World to Come with the letter Yud;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דִּשְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת אֵלּוּ דְּשֵׁם מוֹרִים עַל חָכְמָה וּבִינָה,
for as is known, these two letters of the Name point to Chokhmah and Binah,
שֶׁהֵם מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא;
which are the brain and the heart;
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה "רַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי" (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:),
and in this world 'the Merciful One desires the heart' (Sanhedrin 106b),
וּמַעֲלַת הָאָדָם כְּפִי הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
and man's spiritual standing is measured according to the desire in the heart.
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁיִּשְׁחַט הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד מָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה,
However, in the World to Come when the evil inclination will be slaughtered and there will no longer be room for free choice,
אָז יִהְיֶה הַמַּעֲלָה כְּפִי יִתְרוֹן הַחָכְמָה וְהַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ.
then spiritual preeminence will be according to the superiority of wisdom and comprehension in the brain.

p: וְהָאָבוֹת נִקְרְאוּ "אֵיתָנִים" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יא.),
And the Patriarchs are designated 'Eitanim' (enduring/mighty; Rosh Hashanah 11a),
שָׁמַעְתִּי פֵּירוּשׁ: עַקְשָׁנִים,
and I heard the explanation: stubborn,
פֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק בּוֹעֵר כְּאֵשׁ
meaning: they possessed a fierce desire burning like fire
שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁקוֹט וְיָנוּחַ עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְמִלּוּיוֹ:
which would neither subside nor rest until reaching its complete fulfillment:
אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה
Abraham our father, peace be upon him, in the attribute of love,
עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית אַהֲבַת ה'
until he arrived at the ultimate love of Hashem,
שֶׁהוּא בְּהַרְחָקַת כָּל אַהֲבוֹת זוּלָתוֹ;
which entails distancing all loves other than Him;
עַד שֶׁהוֹלִיד יִצְחָק,
until he fathered Isaac,
שֶׁהוּא הָיָה תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לְיִרְאַת ה',
who possessed the fierce desire for the awe of Hashem,
שִׂנְאַת רַע וְכָל מִינֵי אַהֲבוֹת זָרוֹת וְחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָיוּ מְרוּחָקִים אֶצְלוֹ בְּתַכְלִית;
hatred of evil, such that all alien loves and worldly desires were distant from him in the absolute extreme;
עַד שֶׁהוֹלִיד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
until he fathered our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לִשְׁנֵיהֶם: אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְשִׂנְאַת רַע.
who possessed the fierce desire for both: love of Hashem and hatred of evil.

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim describes Avraham’s tests as the clarification of the full range of his powers, and states that an actual test requires an opposing impulse to overcome. This clarifies the present siman’s claim about the human advantage over angels. The power that makes willing service possible also makes struggle possible; what determines its direction is the work of bringing it into kedushah.

p: וְאֵין קוֹרִין אָבוֹת אֶלָּא לִשְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ (בְּרָכוֹת טז:),
And we call none 'Fathers' except these three (Berakhot 16b),
שֶׁהֵם כָּל כָּךְ נִגְבַּר חֶשְׁקָם כָּל אֶחָד לְמִדָּתוֹ בְּטוֹב
because their desire was so intensely fortified, each to his attribute in goodness,
עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִיתָהּ לִהְיוֹת כֻּלּוֹ כָּךְ.
until he reached its ultimate culmination to become entirely so.
כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר הַחֵשֶׁק בּוֹעֵר בָּאָדָם הוּא כְּלַהַב אֵשׁ,
For when desire burns within a person it is like a flame of fire,
עַד שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ עִם כָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו שְׁקוּעִים בָּזֶה,
until his entirety with all his faculties is immersed in this,
עַד שֶׁכָּל זַרְעָם אַחֲרֵיהֶם תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶם כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶם.
so that all their seed after them, their descendants, are like them.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָאָדָם יוֹלִיד אָדָם וּבְהֵמָה יוֹלִיד בְּהֵמָה וְכַיּוֹצֵא,
Just as man begets man and an animal begets an animal, etc.,
כָּךְ הֵם עֶצֶם גּוּפָם וְכָל כֹּחוֹתֵיהֶם הָיוּ מְשֻׁנֶּה מִפְּאַת רְתִיחָתָם
so their very bodily essence and faculties were transformed through their burning fervor
לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁחָשְׁקוּ עָלָיו לְהַגִּיעַ לוֹ;
toward that matter for which they yearned to attain;
וְהֵם מְיוּחָדִים בְּתוֹקֶף זֶה עַד קָצֶה
and they are uniquely distinguished in this intensity to the utmost limit
עַד שֶׁרְאוּיִים לְהִקָּרֵא אָבוֹת שֶׁכָּל זַרְעָם אַחֲרֵיהֶם כֵּן.
so as to be worthy of being called Fathers, whose offspring after them inherit this.

p: וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּיִחוּד נִקְרָא "אֵיתָן" בִּתְהִלִּים (פט, א וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טו.),
And Abraham our father in particular is titled 'Eitan' in Psalms (89:1; Bava Batra 15a),
כִּי תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק הוּא בְּאַהֲבָה
because the prime force of desire resides in love,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁרוֹאִין בְּאַהֲבוֹת זָרוֹת
just as we observe in worldly passions,
וְכֵן מִצַּד הַטּוֹב בְּאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and likewise on the side of good in the love of Hashem, blessed be He;
וְהוּא הַמַּתְחִיל, כִּי בָּזֶה הַתְחָלַת הַחֵשֶׁק.
and he is the initiator, for herein lies the beginning of desire.
וּבְשִׂנְאַת ה' – בָּזֶה הוּא מִדַּת הַכַּעַס
And in the zealous hatred on behalf of Hashem—this is the attribute of anger
שֶׁנִּקְרָא "אֵשׁ" בְּכָל מָקוֹם בַּכָּתוּב
which is termed 'fire' in every scriptural context
וְ"חָרוֹן" שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן לְשׁוֹן יוֹבֶשׁ הָאֵשׁ,
and 'charon' (wrath) which is also an expression of the parching dryness of fire,
כִּי הוּא בָּא מִכֹּחַ הָאֵשׁ
for it originates from the power of fire,
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לָזֶה עַקְשׁוּת וּתְקִיפוּת כֹּחַ כִּי הוּא עָצוּם מִמֵּילָא;
and requires no stubbornness and force, being intense spontaneously;
רַק שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּרַע,
only that this applies to evil,
אֲבָל בְּטוֹב, שִׂנְאַת רַע גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ מִצַּד הַכַּעַס חָלִילָה,
yet in goodness, hatred of evil likewise does not stem from anger, Heaven forbid,
רַק מִצַּד יִרְאַת ה' הַמְרַחֶקֶת זֶה, אֵין בּוֹ תּוֹקֶף כָּל כָּךְ.
rather from fear of Hashem which keeps it far away, and contains no such harsh turbulence.

p: וּשְׁנֵי אֵלּוּ הָיָה בְּחֶשְׁקָם נְטִיָּה לְאֵיזֶה צַד בְּיִחוּד;
And these two had in their desire a leaning toward a specific side;
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִדָּתוֹ חֵשֶׁק מְעוֹרְבָּב,
however, our father Jacob's attribute was a blended desire,
לֹא לְאֵיזֶה צַד וְדָבָר פְּרָטִי,
not leaning toward one specific polarized side,
רַק לִשְׁנֵי הַקְּצָווֹת יַחַד,
rather embracing both edges simultaneously,
וְהוּא הוֹלֵךְ בַּקַּו הָאֶמְצָעִי שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת
and he treads the Middle Path which is the attribute of Truth,
לִבְחוֹר בְּכָל דָּבָר הָאֱמֶת, אִם לְצַד זֶה אִם לָזֶה.
to choose in every matter the Truth, whether toward this side or that.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין סה:):
And our Sages of blessed memory stated (Eruvin 65b):
בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָדָם נִיכָּר;
in three things a person is recognized;
הַהַכָּרָה הוּא בְּהִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַחֵשֶׁק לְאֵיזֶה דָּבָר,
the recognition occurring when desire intensifies toward something,
אִם הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב שֶׁבַּחֲלַל יָמִין גּוֹבֵר לְהַטּוֹתוֹ לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
observing whether the good yetzer in the right ventricle prevails to turn him toward Hashem's will.
וּ"בְכִיסוֹ" וּ"בְכַעֲסוֹ" הֵם שְׁנֵי הַקְּצָווֹת
And 'in his purse' (kiso) and 'in his anger' (ka'aso) represent the two extremes
דְּתוֹקֶף הַחֶמְדָּה לְמָמוֹן
— of fierce desire for money—
דְּלָכֵן נִדְרַשׁ עַל זֶה "בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ",
which is why 'with all your might' (me'odekha) is expounded on this,
וּלְשׁוֹן "מְאֹד" מַשְׁמָע שֶׁהָאָדָם חוֹמֵד לָזֶה מְאֹד מְאֹד.
the word 'me'od' implying that man covets this exceedingly.
וּ"בְכוֹסוֹ" הוּא בֵּירוּר קַו הָאֶמְצָעִי,
And 'in his cup' (koso) is the clarification of the Middle Line,
כַּאֲשֶׁר הַדֵּעָה מְעוֹרְבֶּבֶת וְאֵין לוֹ נְטִיָּה לְשׁוּם צַד כְּלָל
when conscious reason is blurred and one has no calculated leaning to any side,
שֶׁיְּכַוֵּין אָז הָאֱמֶת,
such that he directs himself toward truth,
כִּדְאָמְרוּ (שָׁם עַמּוּד א):
as they said (there, 65a):
כָּל הַמִּתְפַּתֶּה בְּיֵינוֹ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִדַּעַת קוֹנוֹ.
whoever is appeased when drinking wine possesses something of the mind of his Creator.

sections.en: Desire Has the Power to Bring About That Very Thing for Which One Yearns…

p: [רמט] הַחֵשֶׁק יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ לִפְעוֹל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לוֹ הַרְבֵּה,
Desire has the power to bring about that very thing for which one yearns intensely,
אֲפִילּוּ הוּא רַע,
even if it is evil,
כְּעִנְיַן (מַכּוֹת י:): "בְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ וְכוּלֵי";
in the manner of (Makkot 10b): 'In the path a person wishes to walk he is led';
מִצַּד הָרָצוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ פּוֹעֵל אֲפִילּוּ כָּל חֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
by virtue of his desire he can actualize even all physical worldly pleasures,
אִם לֹא יִהְיֶה דָּבָר מְעַכֵּב שֶׁבַּמִּשְׁפָּט אֵין מַגִּיעַ לוֹ זֶה
unless there be an obstacle whereby divine justice dictates that this is unmerited
וּמוֹנְעִין מִמֶּנּוּ מֵה'.
and it is withheld from him by Hashem.
לוּלֵי זֶה, עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק הָיָה מַשִּׂיג כָּל מַה שֶּׁחוֹשֵׁק.
Were it not for this, through desire he would attain whatever he yearns for.

p: וּלְכָךְ שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דִּבְיָמָיו סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא וְלֹא הָיָה שׁוּם מוֹנֵעַ,
Therefore regarding King Solomon, in whose days the moon was full and there was no obstacle,
נֶאֱמַר: "כִּכְלוֹת וְגוֹמֵר כָּל חֵשֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹה וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א ט, א),
it is said: 'When Solomon had finished... all the desire of Solomon, etc.' (I Kings 9:1),
שֶׁכָּל חֶשְׁקוֹ הָיָה נִשְׁלָם וּמוּבָא לוֹ.
for his entire desire was completed and delivered unto him.
וְהוּא הָיָה בְּתוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק מִכָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים,
And he was endowed with the greatest intensity of desire among all creatures,
שֶׁעַל זֶה חִבֵּר שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים;
concerning which he composed the Song of Songs;
וּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הִתְגַּבְּרוּת כֹּחַ הַחֵשֶׁק כָּךְ הוּא מַשִּׂיג.
and commensurate with the fortified intensity of desire, so does one achieve.
כִּי הַחֵשֶׁק נִקְרָא סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּנוּקְבָא,
For desire is termed 'the end of action' which derives from the feminine aspect,
וּמִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן הוּא חוֹשֵׁק לְמִלּוּי,
and out of deficiency it yearns for fulfillment,
וְהוּא דָּבוּק בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה
and it cleaves unto the primordial thought
וְרֵאשִׁית מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַהַשְׁפָּעוֹת.
and the inception of Hashem's thought from which springs the root of all divine emanations.
וְכֵן מִסִּטְרָא דְּרַע כַּאֲשֶׁר אֵין דָּבָר מוֹנְעוֹ.
And so too on the side of evil, whenever nothing prevents it.

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach first describes silver as longing that acquires the gold of Torah. Its later reversal explains why the acquired Torah must itself kindle further longing as the person's natural energy changes. This develops the siman's account of a power impressed on possessions into a reciprocal process: the desire seeks wisdom, and the wisdom received can renew that desire. The siman's opening condition concerning divine judgment remains in force.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 20:7: “All wisdom on the human side, called “lower wisdom,” consists only in the desire to acquire wisdom. The blessed God “gives wisdom to the wise” (Daniel 2:21)—to someone who possesses the beginning of wisdom, which is desire. King Solomon’s great wisdom corresponded to his great desire, for in desire he attained the utmost perfection possible for the human species. Thus it says in I Kings (9:19), “And all Solomon’s desire that he wished (to build),” and so forth. This is Solomon’s essential quality: desire and seeking, which remain forever, as explained (and all his wisdom remains forever in the three books he composed). This is the beginning of wisdom in the heart, as stated in Berakhot 55a from the verse, “In the heart of every wise-hearted person I have placed wisdom” (Exodus 31:6). Wisdom itself is chiefly in the brain, but in the heart there is desire. Lower wisdom chiefly comes from the heart’s desire—that is, a heart possessing fear of Heaven, which is the essence of the Israelite heart. When fear of Heaven is absent, however, it says, “Why is there a price in a fool’s hand to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart?” (Proverbs 17:16). The Sages of blessed memory in Yoma 72b apply this even to those who engage in Torah without fear of Heaven, meaning within Israel.”

p: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל שִׁישַׁק מֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם
And as I heard regarding Shishak the king of Egypt,
נִקְרָא כֵּן לְשׁוֹן תְּשׁוּקָה
that he was named thus from the language of longing (teshukah),
מִצַּד עֹצֶם תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג רְכוּשׁ דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
on account of the enormity of his longing to seize the treasures of King Solomon;
מִצַּד זֶה עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ בִּימֵי רְחַבְעָם,
and through this he succeeded in the days of Rehoboam,
כְּשֶׁהָיָה קְצָת חֵטְא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט מְעַכַּבְתּוֹ.
when there was a slight sin in Israel such that the attribute of justice did not block him.
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ עַל זֶה (פְּסָחִים פז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב):
And our Sages of blessed memory said concerning this (Pesachim 87b):
כֶּסֶף מִצְרַיִם חָזַר לִמְקוֹמוֹ.
the silver of Egypt returned to its original place.
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי כָּל תּוֹקֶף מֶמְשֶׁלֶת אוּמָּה
The meaning being: the whole strength of a nation's dominion
הוּא כְּפִי תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּהֶם לְאֵיזֶה דָּבָר שֶׁבּוֹ יִחוּד כֹּחָם.
corresponds to the intensity of their desire for a particular thing wherein their strength is concentrated.
וְחֵשֶׁק מִצְרַיִם הָיָה לְחָכְמוֹת,
And Egypt's desire was for wisdoms,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קכה סוֹף עַמּוּד א בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם)
as written in the Zohar (I, 125a in Midrash HaNe'elam)
דְּלֹא הָיָה חָכְמָה כְּחָכְמָתָם;
that there was no wisdom like their wisdom;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ: הַדַּעַת הָיָה בַּגָּלוּת,
and therefore they stated: Da'at (Consciousness) was in exile,
דִּכְפִי תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לְרַע בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר מַאֲפִיל חֵשֶׁק הַטּוֹב.
for according to the force of evil desire in that matter, it obscures the good desire.
וְלָכֵן הָיוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדִים,
Therefore the children of Israel were slaves,
שֶׁהָעֶבֶד אֵין לוֹ הֲרָמַת רֹאשׁ שֶׁרְשׁוּת אַחֵר עָלָיו,
since a slave cannot lift his head, another authority being over him,
וְהָרֹאשׁ הוּא מְשׁוּעְבָּד,
and the head is subjugated,
דְּלָכֵן עֲבָדִים כְּנָשִׁים וַאֲסוּרִין בְּתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּתוּבּוֹת כח.).
which is why servants are like women and excluded from Torah study (Ketubot 28a).

Therefore it was taught: Some waters nurture wise people and some waters nurture fools; the waters that nurture the wise come from the drops of Eden. rich.text: : “With every drop that goes forth from Eden, a spirit of wisdom goes forth. Therefore it was taught: Some waters nurture wise people and some waters nurture fools; the waters that nurture the wise come from the drops of Eden. Rabbi Yosei said: The waters containing more of these drops are those of the first of the four rivers, as it is written: “The name of the first is Pishon.” The one distinguished above them all is Pishon, which flows into the land of Egypt; therefore Egypt’s wisdom exceeded that of the whole world.”

paragraphs.text: Context: This is Midrash HaNe’elam on Zohar I 125a. It supplies the specific description of Egypt’s exceptional wisdom. Rav Tzadok’s further explanation concerns Egypt’s intense desire for wisdom and the spiritual quality associated with its wealth.

p: וּבְוַדַּאי כָּל רְכוּשָׁם הָיוּ מוֹצִיאִים לְהַשִּׂיג חָכְמוֹת כְּפִי תּוֹקֶף חֶשְׁקָם,
And they certainly expended all their wealth to acquire wisdoms commensurate with their desire,
וְנִקְבַּע אוֹתוֹ חֵשֶׁק בָּרְכוּשׁ;
and that desire became embedded in the possessions;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּקִנְיָנֵי הָאָדָם יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת עִם הָאָדָם,
for as is known, a person's acquisitions possess an inner connection with him,
דְּלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים קיב.):
which is why they taught (Pesachim 112a):
הַנּוֹטֵל פְּרוּטָה מֵאִיּוֹב מִתְבָּרֵךְ,
whoever took a coin from Job was blessed,
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (שָׁם) בְּמִי שֶׁשָּׁעָה מְשַׂחֶקֶת וּמַצְלִיחַ,
and so they said (ibid.) regarding one whom fortune smiles upon and prospers,
כִּי הוּא קָבוּעַ גַּם בְּקִנְיָנָיו.
for his spiritual state is fixed within his acquisitions.
כִּי הַמָּמוֹן נִקְרָא "מְאֹד",
For wealth is termed 'me'od' (might/resources),
שֶׁבָּזֶה תּוֹקֶף חֵשֶׁק הָאָדָם;
in which lies the intensity of man's desire;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא מְשַׁעְבְּדוֹ לְדָבָר אַחֵר שֶׁחוֹשֵׁק עוֹד יוֹתֵר,
and when he subordinates it to another thing which he desires even more,
אָז נִקְבַּע גַּם בָּרְכוּשׁ,
then that desire is stamped also upon the property,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁזֶּה כָּל חֵשֶׁק הָאָדָם וְעִיקַּר קִנְיָנוֹ גַּם בּוֹ נִקְבַּע אוֹתוֹ חֵשֶׁק.
since this is his whole passion and acquisition, that desire is embedded in it as well.
שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן הֶקְדֵּשׁ לַשָּׁמַיִם וּמוּקְצֶה לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
This is the principle of consecration to Heaven and dedication to idolatry,
שֶׁחָל עַל הַחֵפֶץ הָעִנְיָן הַנִּקְבָּע עָלָיו שֶׁהוּא מוּכָן בְּדַעַת הָאָדָם,
where the designated status takes effect on the object because it was prepared in the person's mind,
זֶה מִצַּד קְדוּשָׁתוֹ וְזֶה מִצַּד הַהֵיפֶךְ.
this on the side of holiness, and that on the opposite side.
רַק לְפִי שֶׁכָּל כֹּחַ הָאָדָם הֲרֵי מוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ לֶאֱלוֹהַּ שֶׁלּוֹ,
Only because all of man's power is surrendered unto his deity,
הֲרֵי כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָאָדָם שְׁקוּעִים בָּזֶה,
behold, all human faculties are sunken in this;
כַּאֲשֶׁר קִנְיָנוֹ מִתְיַיחֵד לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר, הוּא חָל אוֹתָן כֹּחוֹת גַּם עַל הַקִּנְיָנִים;
and when his possession is designated for that matter, those faculties rest upon the possessions;
וְכֵן בְּכָל דָּבָר שֶׁתּוֹקֶף תְּשׁוּקַת הָאָדָם לוֹ וּמוֹצִיא מָמוֹנוֹ עַל זֶה.
and so in any matter for which man harbors intense yearning and spends his money.

p: וְזֶה טַעַם שֶׁקִּבֵּל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מַתָּנוֹת מִמִּצְרַיִם,
And this explains why Abraham our father received gifts from Egypt,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לִשְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו כִּשְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וְהָיוּ מְלַמְּדִין אוֹתוֹ חָכְמָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא),
whereby through this he merited his two kidneys acting like two rabbis teaching him wisdom (Bereishit Rabbah 61),
שֶׁקָּלַט הַחֵשֶׁק לְחָכְמָה שֶׁלָּהֶם, רַק שֶׁהוּא חָשַׁק לְחָכְמַת אֱמֶת.
for he absorbed their passion for wisdom, except that he yearned for true wisdom.
[וְכָךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קִבֵּל רוּחַ חָכְמָה וּבִינָה מִמִּצְרַיִם,
[And thus I heard: that Abraham received the spirit of wisdom and understanding from Egypt,
וְרוּחַ עֵצָה וּגְבוּרָה מֵאֲבִימֶלֶךְ;
and the spirit of counsel and might from Abimelech;
וְשֶׁזֶּה טַעַם שֶׁאָמְרוּ: מֵאֲבִימֶלֶךְ נִתְעַבְּרָה שָׂרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת),
and that this is the meaning of what they said: that from Abimelech Sarah conceived (Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot),
כִּי בְּעֵת שֶׁנִּיטַּל כֹּחַ הַהוֹלָדָה מֵאֲבִימֶלֶךְ, אָז נִיתַּן כֹּחוֹ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם].
for when the power of procreation was taken from Abimelech, his energy was given to Abraham].

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 4:10: “This is why he was informed here of the Egyptian exile and, at its end, “Afterward they will go out with great possessions.” “Great” indicates the qualities of Atika: being bound to the root. These are the great possessions they brought out of Egypt. Through the ten plagues they were clarified there in all ten qualities: in each plague Israel left one quality on the impure side, which also has ten corresponding qualities, and entered one quality in holiness. This resembles the holy Zohar’s expression, “Striking Egypt and healing Israel.””

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Lech Lecha explains the promised possessions through Israel’s movement from each impure quality into its holy counterpart. This develops the present siman’s claim that a people’s intense desire can become impressed upon its wealth. The possessions matter through the powers carried and redirected with them, especially the desire that becomes preparation for Torah’s wisdom. Their value cannot be reduced to an increase of property without that clarification.

paragraphs.text: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 6:3: “This is the meaning of the Torah’s descent into Egypt through the sins of the generations of the Flood and the dispersion, as is known from the writers of ancient history. The beginnings of all the sciences were in Egypt, through the ancient Egyptian sages; afterward (during the Babylonian exile and somewhat earlier) they were in the land of the Chaldeans, and then in Greece (in the days of Shimon the Righteous and the Oral Torah, as I wrote above in section 5). In the nation in which wisdom abounded, a great measure of the wisdom that the blessed God created and gave to humanity had spread. Only, because of their bad disposition, it turned toward evil for them. They were exceedingly wise in worldly sciences and also in the art of sorcery. The character of wisdom among the nations corresponds to the character of the wisdom the blessed God grants at that time to the one who imparts it within this world. Among Israel, they perceive in that wisdom its true point, which is called “Torah.” ”

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:137: “This follows what I heard concerning “Sarah conceived from Abimelech”: From where did Abraham obtain the strength to father a son? Only through Abimelech’s being restrained. At the very moment the power was taken from Abimelech, it was given to him, for sometimes this is the measure and judgment: one cannot receive an influence unless it is taken from another. Our father Abraham received the spirit of wisdom and understanding from Pharaoh, and the spirit of counsel and strength from Abimelech; but in him they operated through the spirit of knowledge and fear of Hashem, and he fathered Isaac. Likewise, from where did King David obtain strength? Only from overcoming Goliath. Then that strength was, of itself, joined to fear of Hashem in him, and he attained his own hidden root. But because he took it from the Philistine, he is called “Philistia.” (Nevertheless, this is a disparaging name, in the sense of “Through you he was driven out,” and so forth: punishment arises for this when accusation is made. He is therefore called this, because the power was not originally his but came from the Philistine, and from this side accusation could arise. For the same reason Isaac fathered Esau, from the side of Abimelech’s evil fear, as I wrote elsewhere.)”

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַבְטָחַת: "יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל" (בְּרֵאשִׁית טו, יד) וּבִזַּת הַיָּם,
And this is the promise: 'they shall go out with great substance' (Genesis 15:14) and the spoil of the Sea,
וְהוּא הֲכָנָה לְחָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה.
which served as a preparation for the wisdom of the Torah.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם שָׁרְשׁוֹ מִצַּד חָכְמַת חִיצוֹנוֹת;
Nevertheless its external root derived from external wisdom;
וּבִשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נֶאֱמַר: "וַתֵּרֶב חָכְמַת וְגוֹמֵר וּמִכָּל חָכְמַת מִצְרָיִם" (מְלָכִים א ה, י),
and concerning King Solomon it is said: 'And Solomon's wisdom excelled... all the wisdom of Egypt' (I Kings 5:10),
דְּהַיְינוּ בְּחָכְמַת חִיצוֹנוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם.
meaning in their external wisdom.
וְכָל חֵשֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹה הָיָה לְחָכְמָה,
And all the desire of Solomon was for wisdom,
שֶׁעַל זֶה בִּיקֵּשׁ בַּחֲלוֹם רַק זֶה.
concerning which he requested in the dream this alone.
וְכָךְ כֹּחוֹ קָבוּעַ בָּרְכוּשׁ,
And so his power was embedded in the possessions,
וּלְזֶה חָשַׁק שִׁישַׁק, וְחָזַר לִמְקוֹמוֹ;
and for this Shishak yearned, and it returned to its place;
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת חָכְמַת חִיצוֹנוֹת הוּא חֶלְקָם,
for truly external wisdom is their allotted portion,
רַק שֶׁהָיָה בִּשְׁאֵלָה לְשָׁעָה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
only that it was borrowed temporarily by the children of Israel
לְצוֹרֶךְ לִקְבּוֹעַ בְּלִבָּם עַל יְדֵי זֶה חָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
in order to establish thereby in their hearts the wisdom of Hashem,
וְעַד שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁחִבֵּר מִשְׁלֵי בְּבֵירוּר חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה,
and up until King Solomon who authored Mishlei in clarifying Torah wisdom;
וְאָז לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ עוֹד לְחָכְמַת חִיצוֹנוֹת,
and then they no longer needed external wisdom,
וְחָזַר כָּל אֶחָד לִמְקוֹמוֹ.
and each thing returned to its proper place.

sections.en: One Person's Victory Over Another Is Likewise Determined by the Magnitude of His Desire…

p: [רנ] הַנִּיצּוּחַ אָדָם לְאָדָם הוּא גַּם כֵּן כְּפִי גּוֹדֶל הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁל אָדָם בְּנִיצּוּחַ,
One person's victory over another is likewise determined by the magnitude of his desire for victory;
אִם מִתְגַּבֵּר מְאֹד אָז הוּא גּוֹבֵר,
if he intensifies it greatly, then he prevails,
אִם הֵם אַךְ שָׁוִים בְּמִדַּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט.
provided they are otherwise equal in the measure of justice.
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר: "וְכִי יָזִד אִישׁ עַל רֵעֵהוּ לְהָרְגוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת כא, יד),
Therefore it is stated: 'And if a man come willfully (yazid) upon his neighbor, to slay him, etc.' (Exodus 21:14),
וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר כֵּן בְּשׁוּם עֲבֵירָה דַּוְוקָא שֶׁיָּזִיד,
and this was not stated specifically regarding any other sin that he must act 'willfully',
דַּהֲרֵי עַל כָּרְחֲךָ עֲבֵירוֹת אֵין נִקְרָא אֶלָּא בְּמֵזִיד;
for perforce transgressions are designated as such only when intentional;
רַק פֵּירוּשׁ "יָזִיד" מִן "וַיָּזֶד יַעֲקֹב" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כה, כט),
rather, 'yazid' derives from 'and Jacob boiled (vayazed) pottage' (Genesis 25:29),
פֵּירוּשׁ: תּוֹקֶף הָרְתִיחָה וְהַחִמּוּם לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר;
meaning: the fierce boiling and heat toward that matter;
וְזֶה צָרִיךְ לַהֲרִיגַת אָדָם,
and this is necessary for slaying a human being,
שֶׁמִּתְגַּבֵּר נֶגְדּוֹ כָּל כָּךְ עַד לִטּוֹל נַפְשׁוֹ
where to overpower him so far as to take his life
צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה חֶשְׁקוֹ חָמוּם בְּיוֹתֵר.
his desire must be exceedingly inflamed.
וְכֵן "בַּדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר זָדוּ עֲלֵיהֶם" (שְׁמוֹת יח, יא)
And so too 'for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly (zadu) against them' (Exodus 18:11)
אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה יא.):
our Sages of blessed memory explained (Sotah 11a):
בִּקְדֵירָה שֶׁבִּשְּׁלוּ וְכוּלֵי,
in the pot wherein they cooked, etc.,
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן בַּהֲרִיגַת נְפָשׁוֹת,
which likewise involved the killing of souls,
וְתוֹקֶף חֶשְׁקָם לְהַשְׁלִיךְ נְפָשׁוֹת לַיְאוֹר שָׁב עַל רֹאשָׁם,
and the intensity of their desire to cast souls into the river recoiled onto their head,
כִּי הִצְמִיחוּ חֵשֶׁק זֶה גַּם כֵּן לְמַעְלָה
for they caused this fierce desire to ascend on High,
רַק שֶׁהָיָה עֲלֵיהֶם.
only that it turned against them.

p: וְזֶה כֹּחַ הָמָן,
And this was the power of Haman,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב):
concerning which our Sages stated (Megillah 13b end):
הִקְדִּים שִׁקְלֵיהֶם לִשְׁקָלָיו,
He caused their Shekalim to precede his shekalim;
נִרְאֶה שֶׁהָיָה אֵיזֶה כֹּחַ בִּשְׁקָלָיו
from which it appears that there was a potent force in his shekalim
עַד שֶׁהֻוצְרַךְ מִצְוַת שְׁקָלִים לְהָגֵן נֶגֶד זֶה בְּמִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה;
such that the mitzvah of Shekalim was required to shield against it measure for measure;
וּמָה טַעַם יֵשׁ בִּשְׁקָלָיו שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בּוֹ אֵיזֶה טַעֲנָה לְשֶׁיִּזְכֶּה
and what virtue could there be in his shekalim that it should give him claim to prevail,
שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לְמִצְוָה לְבַטֵּל זֶה,
such that a specific mitzvah would be needed to nullify it,
וְהָיָה לוֹ לוֹמַר רַק זְכוּת אֵיזֶה מִצְוָה שֶׁבִּיטֵּל כְּלָלוּת הַגְּזֵירָה?!
and the Talmud should merely have mentioned the general merit of any mitzvah that abolished the decree?!

Therefore He caused their shekels to precede his shekels.”

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 7:7: “On the side of wisdom, he certainly recognized that the world cannot exist without Israel. Therefore, in his wickedness he devised the statement, “I shall weigh ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who perform the work, to bring into the king’s treasuries” (Esther 3:9). This too means the King of kings. He was saying: Israel’s entire preciousness lies in their ability to surrender all their longings and desires to the blessed God; he too could do this, and could take their place. He was the first to think that he was Israel, as the Sages of blessed memory said (Numbers Rabbah 14:10), that the nations will eventually say, “We are Israel.” This began with him, as it says, “Whom would the king wish to honor (more than me)?” (Esther 6:6), meaning the King of kings. In his wisdom he recognized that his success came from the blessed God, who wished to exalt him and had agreed with him about destroying Israel, Heaven forbid. Since he knew that the whole world had been created only for their sake, he thought that the blessed God had certainly chosen him in their place—until he saw that “it was reversed” (Esther 9:1), and our handful of barley came and displaced his ten thousand talents of silver (Megillah 16a). The omer offering is called an “offering of jealousy,” like the offering of the suspected adulteress, as is known from the Zohar (II 148b): it tests the “woman of valor,” distinguishing her from the “woman of harlotry” who imitates the woman of valor. This follows “Better a meal of vegetables (with love there) than a fattened ox (with hatred in it)” (Proverbs 15:17), which the Sages expounded concerning Balaam’s offerings and his seven altars (Numbers 23:1). He too thought to build altars corresponding to all the righteous and the patriarchs who had built them, like Haman with his shekels, claiming the ability to offer and serve in place of them all, and still more. Thus Tanchuma at the beginning of Tzav (1) says that they would offer “thousands of rams … myriads of streams of oil” (Micah 6:7). But the distinction is that the righteous offered a pleasing fragrance, to bring satisfaction before Him, whereas Balaam offered in order thereby to create hatred between Israel and their Father in Heaven. His intent was only to harm. So too, Haman’s shekels were only a means of enabling him to destroy Israel, Heaven forbid.”

p: רַק כָּל כֹּחַ הָמָן הוּא מִצַּד תּוֹקֶף זְדוֹן חֶשְׁקוֹ לַהֲרוֹג אוּמָּה,
Rather, the whole strength of Haman stemmed from the fierce, boiling insolence of his desire to exterminate a nation,
וְזֶה כָּל כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק שֶׁנִּקְרָא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם",
and this is the entire power of Amalek who is termed 'first among the nations' (Numbers 24:20),
פֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁבּוֹ תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לְרַע עַד שֶׁדָּבוּק לְעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית.
meaning: within him resides the fiercest passion for evil such that he cleaves to the profound primal root.
וְזֶה טַעַם הַבְּכוֹרָה דְּעֵשָׂו שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק יוֹתֵר,
And this explains the birthright of Esau, who possessed a more ferocious desire,
וְקָנָה יַעֲקֹב בִּנְזִיד עֲדָשִׁים
— which Jacob acquired through a boiling pottage of lentils—
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי רְתִיחָתוֹ לְחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
meaning: because Esau's boiling fervor was toward physical worldly desires,
וְנָתַן לוֹ רְתִיחָה זוֹ,
and Jacob gave him this worldly fervor,
וְהוּא קָלַט הָרְתִיחָה הַטּוֹבָה מַה דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מְרַתַּחַת
while Jacob absorbed the holy boiling fervor through which the Torah inflames (Ta'anit 4a).
וְהוּא כְּטַעַם (חֲגִיגָה טו.):
And this reflects (Chagigah 15a):
זָכָה – נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ וְכוּלֵי, נִתְחַיֵּיב – נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ וְכוּלֵי;
if he merits, he takes his portion and the portion of his peer, etc.; if he is guilty, he takes his portion and his peer's portion, etc.;
כָּךְ חִילֵּף עִמּוֹ יַעֲקֹב,
so did Jacob exchange with him,
שֶׁנָּתַן לוֹ חֵלֶק רְתִיחָתוֹ שֶׁבְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְּהֵמָה
giving him his share of boiling passion in bestial pursuits,
וְקִבֵּל הַטּוֹב מִמֶּנּוּ
and receiving the good sparks from him
[כְּגוֹן נִשְׁמַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְכַדּוֹמֶה
[such as the souls of Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Meir, and the like,
שֶׁנִּתּוֹסְפוּ בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִקְלְטוּ בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב,
who were added to the children of Israel and absorbed into Jacob's seed,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי קְנִיָּה זוֹ],
and that was accomplished through this acquisition],
כִּי כָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ ב' חֲלָקִים בְּהֶכְרֵחַ: יֵצֶר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר רָע.
for everyone perforce possesses two components: the good yetzer and the evil yetzer.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 15a: ‘He said to him: Your teacher Rabbi Akiva did not say that. Rather: He created righteous people and He created wicked people; He created Gan Eden and He created Gehinnom. Each person has two shares, one in Gan Eden and one in Gehinnom. If a righteous person merits, he takes his own share and his fellow’s share in Gan Eden. If a wicked person incurs guilt, he takes his own share and his fellow’s share in Gehinnom.’

p: וּכְשֶׁרָאָהוּ יַעֲקֹב עָיֵיף מֵרְצִיחָה,
And when Jacob saw him exhausted from murder,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לָזֶה,
possessing an intense desire for it,
קָלַט כֹּחַ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁבּוֹ
Jacob absorbed the holy power latent within that trait
וְנִיתַּן לְזַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל וּלְיוֹסֵף בְּיִחוּד,
and it was bequeathed to the seed of Rachel and to Joseph in particular;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מַכּוֹת י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א):
as stated (Makkot 10a):
גִּלְעָד וּשְׁכֶם שְׁכִיחֵי רוֹצְחִים,
in Gilead and Shechem murderers were common,
וְהַיְינוּ שׁוֹגְגִים, דִּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ עָרֵי מִקְלָט;
meaning unintentional killers, which is why cities of refuge were needed;
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי אֶצְלָם יֵשׁ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבִּרְצִיחָה,
meaning: because with them resides the good dimension of zealous killing,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "שַׂעְרֵךְ כְּעֵדֶר הָעִזִּים שֶׁגָּלְשׁוּ מֵהַר גִּלְעָד" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ד, א),
just as I heard on 'Your hair is as a flock of goats that come down from Mount Gilead' (Song of Songs 4:1),
דְּ"שֵׂעָר" פֵּירוּשׁ: כַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה,
that 'hair' denotes anger and killing,
וּמֵהַר גִּלְעָד הוּא טוֹב.
and from Mount Gilead it is directed toward good.
וְשֶׁזֶּה טַעַם: "הַיְדַעְתֶּם כִּי לָנוּ רָמֹת גִּלְעָד" (מְלָכִים א כב, ג) דְּאַחְאָב,
And this was the intention of Ahab: 'Do you know that Ramoth-gilead is ours?' (I Kings 22:3),
שֶׁרָצָה לְבָרֵר עַל יְדֵי מִלְחָמָה זוֹ
where he sought to clarify through that battle
שֶׁרְצִיחָה שֶׁהָרַג נְבִיאֵי ה' בְּמִשְׁפָּט,
that his killing of the prophets of Hashem was justified,
כִּי לוֹ רְצִיחָה דִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
claiming that he possessed the zealous killing of holiness.

Explanation: Peri Tzadik distinguishes Moshe's slight lapse into anger from the particular zeal fitting to Pinchas. This is an important qualification beside the present account of Gilead and Ahab's attempt to vindicate his use of force: recognizing that severity can have a holy root does not by itself establish that a given act expresses it. The distinction is consistent with the siman's opening condition that desire's force remains subject to judgment.

p: וּלְכָךְ עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל בְּיַד זֶרַע רָחֵל
Therefore Amalek falls exclusively by the hand of the descendants of Rachel
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פְּסִיקְתָּא רַבָּתִי פָּרָשָׁה יג),
(as stated in Pesikta Rabbati 13),
שֶׁהֵם שֶׁקָּלְטוּ הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ;
for they are the ones who extracted the spark of good within that trait;
וְהוּא כְּלַל כָּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁבְּיַעֲקֹב,
and this comprises the entirety of the yetzer hara within Jacob,
שֶׁהוּא כְּלַל הַבְּרִיאָה,
who represents the totality of Creation,
וְתוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה מִזַּרְעוֹ עֲמָלֵק לְרֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם בְּחֶשְׁקוֹ.
and the intensity of desire from which Amalek emerged as 'first among the nations' in his fierce desire.

p: וְהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ תֵּיכֶף בְּרִפְיוֹן יָדַיִם דִּרְפִידִים מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And Amalek instantly senses any slackening of hands from Torah, as in Rephidim (Sanhedrin 106a);
מִיָּד "וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק" (שְׁמוֹת יז, ח):
immediately 'Then came Amalek' (Exodus 17:8):
כַּאֲשֶׁר נִתְרַפָּה מְעַט הַחֵשֶׁק הַטּוֹב אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ,
when the good desire slacks slightly among the children of Israel which stands opposite him,
תֵּיכֶף מַרְגִּישׁ וּבָא.
he instantly senses it and attacks.
וְכֵן אָז שֶׁהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַצֶּלֶם,
And so too then, when they bowed down to the idol of Nebuchadnezzar,
נֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ".
acting contrary to 'with all your soul'.
וְתוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק הוּא בְּ"בְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ, בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ, בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ",
And the peak of desire is manifest in 'with all your soul, with all your heart, and with all your might',
וְהֵם נִתְרַפּוּ מִ"בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ",
and they slackened in 'with all your soul',
מִיָּד הוּא נִתְגַּבֵּר בְּחֶשְׁקוֹ
immediately Haman was emboldened in his wicked desire
וּ"בְכָל מְאֹדוֹ" עַל יְדֵי הַשְּׁקָלִים,
and 'with all his might' through his shekalim,
שֶׁזֶּה תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק הֶעָצוּם בִּנְתִינַת רְכוּשׁ וּמְאֹד כָּל כָּךְ;
which demonstrates immense passion through giving up so much wealth and might;
עַל זֶה הָיָה יָכוֹל לְנַצֵּחַ עַל יְדֵי הַהַזְדָּה וְהַרְתָּחַת הַחֵשֶׁק כָּל כָּךְ.
and through this he might have prevailed by virtue of this inflamed, boiling desire.

p: רַק שֶׁהִקְדִּים שִׁקְלֵיהֶם
— Except that Hashem caused Israel's Shekalim to precede his—
שֶׁגַּם לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ תּוֹקֶף חֵשֶׁק כָּל כָּךְ
showing that the children of Israel likewise possess an equally fierce desire
בִּנְתִינַת רְכוּשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
in surrendering their possessions unto Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶה טַעַם: "אִם יִתֵּן אִישׁ אֶת כָּל הוֹן בֵּיתוֹ בָּאַהֲבָה וְגוֹמֵר" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח, ז),
And this is the meaning of: 'If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned' (Song of Songs 8:7),
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה וְשִׁיּוּרֵי מִדְרָשִׁים) עַל הָאֻמּוֹת;
which our Sages expounded upon the nations;
כִּי אֵין זְדוֹן הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּהֶם גַּם בִּנְתִינַת כָּל רְכוּשָׁם
for even the fierce boiling desire of the nations when tendering all their possessions—
שֶׁבָּזֶה בֵּירוּר חֶשְׁקָם,
which is the test of their desire,
כִּי הָרְכוּשׁ אֶצְלָם בְּיוֹתֵר הוּא כָּל חַיּוּתָם
— since property is their supreme vitality—
עִם כָּל זֶה, חֵשֶׁק וְאַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹד יוֹתֵר.
nonetheless, the desire and love of Israel for Hashem, blessed be He, surpasses it all the more.

p: [רנא] עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק הוּא כְּלִי קִבּוּל
Through passionate desire a person becomes a receptive vessel
לְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ.
for the indwelling of the divine presence of Hashem, blessed be He, within his heart.
וְזֶהוּ תְּרוּמַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן:
And this is the offering of the Tabernacle:
"מֵאֵת כָּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִדְּבֶנּוּ לִבּוֹ" (שְׁמוֹת כה, ב),
'From every man whose heart makes him willing' (Exodus 25:2),
דִּנְדִיבוּת הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
— for through the generosity of heart of the children of Israel—
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא בִּנְיַן הַמִּשְׁכָּן
by means of this is the construction of the Tabernacle accomplished,
דִּשְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים.
which brings the presence of Hashem to dwell in the lower realms.
וּבָזֶה הוּא כָּל חַד לְפוּם מַה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִבֵּיהּ,
And in this, each is according to what he measures in his heart (Zohar I 103b),
שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הַרְגָּשַׁת אֶחָד מִשְׁכַּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבּוֹ לַחֲבֵירוֹ;
for one person's perception of Hashem's tabernacle in his heart does not resemble his fellow's;
כִּי כְּפִי נְדִיבַת לְבָבוֹ בְּתִגְבּוֹרֶת חֶשְׁקוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג,
since according to the generosity of his heart in the surging force of his desire to comprehend,
כָּךְ הוּא שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
such is the dwelling of the presence of Hashem, blessed be He.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 7:4: “On Chanukah we light eight lamps. The eighth alludes to understanding in the heart, the source of the seven lights mentioned above: the heart’s longing and will to reach the illumination of Torah so that it spreads within the heart. The deepest yearning to attain Torah’s light was revealed in the days of the Greek decree, which sought to abolish Torah and commandments. Their hearts were greatly broken by this: it seemed that Heaven was preventing them because their Torah and commandments were not accepted before God, like a servant whose pitcher is poured back into his face. Through this they grew bitter and their hearts’ longing to study Torah in secret increased. Even those who could not hide themselves and study had an even greater cry and longing within their hearts to attain Torah’s light. Through this they merited the miracle of finding iron spits to make the menorah, the vessel receiving the light of the seven lamps. It corresponds to the will in the heart, through which a vessel is made to receive Torah’s illumination.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah describes both those able to learn in secret and those prevented from doing so, whose yearning nevertheless deepened. It relates the resulting menorah to the heart made ready to receive illumination. This gives a concrete example of the present siman’s opening: the willing heart is itself part of building a dwelling for the Shechinah. The siman then distinguishes this varied measure of positive reception from the equal foundation shared by all Israel.

paragraphs.text: Chanukah’s household dedication continues the Mishkan’s capacity to establish the Shechinah wherever Israel encamps.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 25:3: “The chief purpose in creating the world was that the Shekhinah should dwell primarily in the lower realm. On Shabbat He rose and sat upon His throne of glory: that is, He established His presence in the lower realm, and then held its dedication. The same applies to the dedication of the Mishkan and the Temple. Likewise, in the Hasmonean dedication they instituted that every Jew should dedicate a dwelling, for God dwells in the hearts of the children of Israel. This can be done “in those days, at this time.” It endures forever, even in exile and outside the Land of Israel. It commemorates the Mishkan’s dedication, which likewise took place in the wilderness, outside the Land. The Mishkan was not fixed in one location; wherever Israel encamped, they established its place, and there the divine presence dwelled.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah explains how the dwelling described in this siman is relevant beyond the original building of the Mishkan. Each person’s dedication of a house expresses the Shechinah’s dwelling in Jewish hearts, and this remains possible outside Eretz Yisrael and in exile. This preserves both dimensions of the siman: the divine purpose of dwelling below is shared, while the willing heart gives each person’s reception its particular measure and expression.

p: וְיֵשׁ עוֹד תְּרוּמַת הָאֲדָנִים וּדְקָרְבָּנוֹת,
And there is furthermore the offering of the sockets and of the communal sacrifices,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ: "הֶעָשִׁיר לֹא יַרְבֶּה וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת ל, טו),
concerning which it is said: 'The rich shall not give more, etc.' (Exodus 30:15),
שֶׁבֵּין הֶעָשִׁיר בְּדַעַת וּבְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב וְתִגְבּוֹרֶת הַחֵשֶׁק,
wherein both the one rich in understanding, emotional perception, and surging desire,
וּבֵין הֶעָנִי – שָׁוִים בַּחֲלָקִים;
and the poor man—are entirely equal in their shares;
כִּי הוּא "לְכַפֵּר עַל נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם" כִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בַּכָּתוּב,
because it is 'to make atonement for your souls,' as explicitly stated in Scripture,
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים (פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד):
and as our Sages of blessed memory stated in the Yerushalmi, Shekalim (2:4):
דִּלְכַפֵּר אַעֵגֶל;
that it comes to atone for the Golden Calf;
פֵּירוּשׁ: לְקַנֵּחַ לִכְלוּךְ דְּחֶשְׁקוֹת רָעוֹת מִן הַלֵּב.
meaning: to wipe away the filth of wicked desires from the heart.
וְכֵן בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת צִבּוּר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פִּינְחָס):
And so regarding communal offerings our Sages said (Midrash Rabbah, Pinchas):
"תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר מְכַפֵּר וְכוּלֵי";
'The morning continual offering atones, etc.';
וּבְעִנְיַן הַרְחָקָה מִן הָרַע כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁוִים,
and regarding distancing from evil all Israel are equal,
שֶׁכֻּלָּם יוּכְלוּ לִינָּקוֹת מִן הָרַע בְּתַכְלִית,
in that all are capable of being thoroughly cleansed from evil,
רַק חִלּוּק הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הוּא בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַטּוֹב.
the variance in spiritual levels applying only to the attainment of the good.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Ki Tisa 2: “The contribution for the sockets indicates what we find: all Israel have a share in the World to Come. After the clarification, all Israel will be equal, so this contribution was equal; no one has an advantage over another in this. The altar contribution indicates that Israel arose first in divine thought; there too all are equal. The Mishkan contribution indicates how each person breaks through concealment so that Hashem dwells with him. Between the first choice of Israel and their share in the World to Come, a person must clarify why Hashem chose him before his service and why He establishes Torah with him permanently. Therefore this contribution is according to the willing heart: according to the effort is the reward. To the extent that a person breaks through concealment, Hashem dwells with him permanently.”

The Mishkan contribution indicates how each person breaks through concealment so that Hashem dwells with him. Between the first choice of Israel and their share in the World to Come, a person must clarify why Hashem chose him before his service and why He establishes Torah with him permanently. Therefore this contribution is according to the willing heart: according to the effort is the reward. To the extent that a person breaks through concealment, Hashem dwells with him permanently.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef distinguishes the same three contributions. The sockets signify the equality reached after clarification, and the public offerings the common root before individual service. The freely given Mishkan contribution concerns the intervening work of breaking through concealment. This makes the siman's contrast precise: different intensity of longing describes the person's present reception without cancelling Israel's shared foundation or eventual equality.

p: וְגַם דְּמִצַּד הַנִּקָּיוֹן מֵהָרַע, בֶּאֱמֶת מַגִּיעִים לְמַדְרֵגָה דְּ"שָׁוֶה וּמַשְׁוֶה קָטָן וְגָדוֹל".
And furthermore, from the vantage point of cleansing from evil, one arrives in truth at the level of 'Who makes small and great equal'.
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּיֵשׁ עִגּוּלִים וְיֹשֶׁר,
For as is known, there exist Circles (Iggulim) and Linearity (Yosher),
וְחִלּוּק הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת מַעְלָה מַטָּה הוּא מִצַּד הַיֹּשֶׁר,
and the hierarchy of gradations of higher and lower derives from the side of Linearity,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּעִגּוּל – הַכֹּל שָׁוֶה.
whereas in a Circle—all points are equidistant and equal.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּהָרַע עוֹמֵד בֵּין עִגּוּלִים לְיֹשֶׁר;
And it is known that evil stands between Circles and Linearity;
וּלְעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיְּבוֹעַר הָרַע,
and in the future when evil is eradicated,
אָז "תִּשְׂמַח בְּתוּלָה בְּמָחוֹל" (יִרְמְיָה לא, יב),
then 'shall the maiden rejoice in the dance' (Jeremiah 31:12),
שֶׁהוּא הַמָּחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים מִצַּד הָעִגּוּלִים,
which is the circular dance for the righteous (Ta'anit 31a) stemming from Circles,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִגְלֶה אָז דְּהַכֹּל שָׁוִים.
wherein it will be revealed that all are equal.

p: וּלְפִי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה "אָנֹכִי" קוֹדֵם לְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
And because in this world 'I am' preceded 'You shall have no other gods',
דַּעֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְנַקּוּ מֵרַע לְגַמְרֵי,
in that people have not yet been thoroughly cleansed from evil,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה מַשִּׂיגִים קְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and nevertheless they perceive the holiness of Hashem, blessed be He,
וּלְכָךְ הוּא חָלוּק לְשִׁיעוּרִים.
therefore perception is divided into varied measures.
וּמֵאַחַר דִּנְקִיּוֹן הָרַע – כֹּחַ זֶה שָׁוֶה בֶּאֱמֶת בַּכֹּל,
And since the cleansing from evil is a capacity truly equal in all,
אַחַר שֶׁיִּגְמְרוּ פְּעֻלַּת אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ כָּרָאוּי בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
after they conclude the operation of that capacity properly in perfection,
אָז יִהְיֶה הַשָּׂגַת "אָנֹכִי", הַבָּא אַחַר "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ", גַּם כֵּן בְּהַשְׁתַּוּוּת.
then the perception of 'I am'—which follows 'You shall have no'—will likewise exist in equality.
וְזֶהוּ "הַשָּׁוֶה" בְּעַצְמוֹ – הוּא מִצַּד כֹּחַ דְּ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
And this is: 'He Who is equal' in Himself stems from the power of 'You shall have no',
וּ"מַשְׁוֶה" – מִצַּד "אָנֹכִי".
and 'Who equalizes' stems from 'I am'.
וְזֶהוּ בְּכֹחוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And this applies within the inner faculties of the children of Israel;
וְגַם בְּהַשְׁפָּעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא שָׁוֶה בֶּאֱמֶת,
and likewise within the divine influx of Hashem, it is truly equal,
מִצִּידּוֹ מוּכָן לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְכָל אֶחָד בְּשָׁוֶה.
from His side being prepared to bestow upon each person equally.
וְזֶה עִנְיָן בַּמָּן גַּם כֵּן: "לֹא הֶעְדִּיף הַמַּרְבֶּה וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת טז, יח),
And this is also the phenomenon of the manna: 'He that gathered much had nothing over, etc.' (Exodus 16:18),
מִצַּד נְתִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה שָׁוֶה;
for from the side of Hashem's giving it was uniform;
רַק הַחִלּוּק הָיָה בְּהַרְגָּשַׁת הַטְּעָמִים,
the only variation being in the sensation of flavors,
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד הָיָה טוֹעֵם כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁרוֹצֶה, כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא עה.),
in that each tasted according to what he desired, as our Sages stated (Yoma 75a);
בָּזֶה וַדַּאי הָיָה חִלּוּק כָּל אֶחָד אֵיזֶה טַעַם הָיָה מַרְגִּישׁ,
wherein there was certainly a difference regarding what flavor each experienced,
דִּבְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַטַּעַם אֵין הַשְׁתַּוּוּת.
for in the sensation of taste there is no uniformity.

p: וְכֵן נְתִינַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וּמִצְווֹת שָׁוֶה לַכֹּל,
And likewise the giving of the Written Torah and commandments is equal unto all,
רַק הַרְגָּשַׁת הַטְּעָמִים וְרָזֵי תּוֹרָה יֵשׁ חִלּוּקִים,
only that in the perception of the underlying reasons and secrets of the Torah there are differences,
וְהוּא הַנִּקְרָא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and this is what is termed the Oral Torah,
שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר לֶעָתִיד: "וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד וְגוֹמֵר" (יִרְמְיָה לא, לג),
concerning which it is said of the future: 'And they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, etc.' (Jeremiah 31:33),
כִּי הוּא גַּם כֵּן מַשְׁוֶה אֶת הַמְּקַבְּלִים,
because He will likewise equalize the recipients,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא שָׁוֶה מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ.
just as it is uniform in its own essence.

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן תְּרוּמַת אֲדָנִים,
And this is the meaning of the offering of the sockets (Adanim);
כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא הָעֲמִידָה לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
for the Written Torah serves as the foundational standing for the Oral Torah,
דְּלָכֵן פְּתִיחַת הַשַּׁ״ס: "תַּנָּא אַקְּרָא קָאֵי" (בְּרָכוֹת ב.),
which is why the Talmud opens: 'The Tanna bases himself upon the scriptural verse' (Berakhot 2a),
פֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁהַיְסוֹד הוּא הַמִּקְרָא,
meaning: the bedrock foundation is Scripture,
וְעַל זֶה הוּא עֲמִידַת הַמִּשְׁנָה.
and upon this rests the structure of the Mishnah.
וְזֶהוּ אֲדָנִים לַמִּשְׁכָּן גַּם כֵּן:
And such are the sockets of the Tabernacle as well:
הוּא הַיְסוֹד מִשֶּׁפַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִצַּד הַהַשְׁתַּוּוּת,
they are the foundation of Hashem's divine influx from the vantage point of equality,
כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְחַלֵּק עֲדַיִן לְהַשָּׂגַת לִבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
when it is not yet differentiated into the individualized perceptions of the hearts of Israel.
וְגַם זֶה הוּא מִצַּד הַכָּנַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּכְלָל בְּשָׁוֶה
And this likewise stems from the collective preparation of the children of Israel equally
בַּאֲמִירַת "נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע";
in their unified proclamation of 'we will do and we will hear';
בָּזֶה "הֶעָשִׁיר לֹא יַרְבֶּה וְגוֹמֵר",
in this 'the rich shall not give more, etc.',
שֶׁעַל זֶה נִבְנֶה גּוּף הַמִּשְׁכָּן
upon which is erected the main body of the Tabernacle
דִּשְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּפְרָטֵי לְבָבוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
embodying the dwelling of Hashem's presence within the individual hearts of Israel.
