p: וְגַם הַיְסוֹד הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַ"סוּר מֵרָע",
Moreover, the foundation is established through 'turning away from evil',
כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א, ג):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:3):
"יָצָא טִיפָּה שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת – נִכְנַס טִיפָּה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה".
'If a drop of mockery departs, a drop of Torah enters.'
וְעַל זֶה הוּא יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וִימֵי הַסְּפִירָה קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
And toward this were directed the Exodus from Egypt and the days of the Omer count prior to the Giving of the Torah,
הַגַּם דְּאֵינוֹ נִקָּיוֹן גָּמוּר שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר כְּלָל רוֹשֶׁם פְּסֹלֶת,
even though this was not an absolute purification leaving no lingering trace of dross;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ דִּבּוּר "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
for that was achieved by the divine utterance of 'You shall have no other gods',
שֶׁבְּעֵת הַדִּבּוּר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
wherein at the moment of the utterance of Hashem, blessed be He,
הָיָה בִּיטּוּל כֹּחַ הָרַע בֶּאֱמֶת בְּאוֹתוֹ רֶגַע.
there occurred the actual nullification of the power of evil at that very instant.
כִּי דִּבּוּר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַצְמוֹ פּוֹעֵל בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת,
For the speech of Hashem in itself acts throughout all worlds,
וּ"בִדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ" וְגוֹמֵר –
and 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made' (Psalms 33:6)—
גַּם בִּגְמַר מַעֲשֶׂה דְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה.
even down into the finished reality of the World of Action.
וְזֶה יִהְיֶה כֵּן לֶעָתִיד בִּגְמַר מַעֲשֶׂה דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
And so will it be in the future at the final completion of this world.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם, לַהֲכָנָה לְ"אָנֹכִי"
Nevertheless, as a preparation for 'I am',
צָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּכֹחַ אָדָם בְּ"סוּר מֵרָע",
one requires likewise human exertion through mortal power in 'turning away from evil',
שֶׁהוּא הֲכָנָה לַ"עֲשֵׂה טוֹב".
which is the indispensable preparation for 'doing good'.

sections.en: A Person Must Recognize That His Desire and Generosity of Heart Likewise Derive From…

p: [רנב] הָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לְהַכִּיר כִּי הַחֵשֶׁק וּנְדִיבוּת לֵב שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
A person must recognize that his desire and generosity of heart likewise derive from Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב): "הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל",
as stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): 'The Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel',
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּנִדְבַת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ:
and as King David, peace be upon him, proclaimed at the donation for the Temple:
"כִּי מִמְּךָ הַכֹּל וּמִיָּדְךָ וְגוֹמֵר", "וּלְךָ הַכֹּל" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, יד).
'For all things come from You, and from Your hand, etc.' 'and all is Yours' (I Chronicles 29:14, 16).
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַחֵשֶׁק הַהוּא נִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן תָּמִיד.
And through this realization, that desire becomes permanently fixed in the heart to endure always.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ: "שָׁמְרָה זֹּאת לְעוֹלָם וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם, יח),
And as he pleaded there afterward: 'Keep this forever, etc.' (ibid. 18),
דְּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהַכֹּל מִמְּךָ וְאַתָּה נִצְחִי וְאֵינְךָ מִשְׁתַּנֶּה,
for since everything is from You and You are eternal and immutable,
תּוּכַל לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן יֵצֶר לְבַב עַמְּךָ וְחֶשְׁקָם לְעוֹלָם.
You can preserve thus the inner inclination of Your people's heart and their desire forever.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Ki Tavo 1: “A person has the clearest recognition in the first produce, for there he recognizes explicitly that the entire power of growth comes from Hashem. The Torah therefore commanded, “You shall take from the first of all the fruit of the ground”: in the place where a person recognizes that Hashem has left him an opening to recognize “everything comes from You,” there he must return it to Hashem.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef applies the same verse “everything comes from You” to the first fruits, before possession and habit obscure the source of their growth. The gift is returned at the moment its dependence is clearest. This illuminates why the present siman begins by returning even the generous impulse to Hashem: that recognition is part of acquiring a lasting relation to the good, rather than merely surrendering ownership of it.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 14:1: “That is, there are two kinds of awakening of a person's intellect. One is the wisdom and intellect in the mind. This intellect belongs to him because he is human, for the nations, too, have intellect. There is also an awakening that comes from the understanding in the heart. This belongs to him specifically because he is a descendant of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, for the blessed God dwells within the hearts of the children of Israel. Among the nations of the world, by contrast, this heart is absent. Therefore, among the nations of the world an evil thought is joined to an action, but not among Israel. Between a thought in the mind and its actual realization in action stands the heart, where a person may reconsider. Among the nations of the world, however, the heart is filled with evil, and he will certainly not reconsider. Concerning this they said: “If there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it.” For the essence of Torah is in the heart, as in the words of our Sages: “I cannot learn the Torah in another person's heart.” Thus all the Torah is held in his heart. Similarly, our Sages say: “According to the heart of Rabbi so-and-so,” and many other such expressions. “He has not done so for any nation,” but only for the children of Israel, of whom it is said: “The Rock of my heart and my portion—God forever.” As our Sages said concerning the verse “My heart is awake,” the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel. Therefore they possess an awakening understanding in the heart. This, too, offers assurance: that he will awaken through the wisdom and understanding the blessed God has bestowed upon him. But “it is better to take refuge in the blessed God.””

And this explains 'that they take for Me an offering' (Exodus 25:2),
דְּפֵירֵשׁ בַּזֹּהַר (תְּרוּמָה קלד ב, קמ ב) דְּהוּא יִחוּד, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
which is explained in the Zohar (Terumah 134b, 140b) as signifying unification, see there.
פֵּירוּשׁ, דִּתְרוּמָה הוּא נְדִיבוּת הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
The explanation being: the offering (terumah) is the generosity of heart of Israel,
וְהוּא הַמְּכוּנֶה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל;
and it is what is designated as Knesset Yisrael (the Shechinah);
וְ"לִי תְּרוּמָה" פֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הוּא עַצְמוֹ הַתְּרוּמָה וְהַנְּדִיבוּת.
and 'for Me an offering' means: that the Holy One is Himself the offering and the generosity.
זֶהוּ יִחוּד דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ,
This is the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah;
פֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁגַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים – הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
meaning: that one recognizes that even all actions of the lower beings—all originate from Hashem.
דְּבֶאֱמֶת ה' אֶחָד יָחִיד וּמְיוּחָד בְּכָל עָלְמִין,
For in truth Hashem is One, Singular, and Unique throughout all worlds,
וְגַם בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל רַק הוּא הַמְּעוֹרֵר וְהַפּוֹעֵל.
and within the hearts of the children of Israel He alone is the Awakener and the Doer.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Terumah 13:151: ““From every man whose heart moves him willingly, you shall take My contribution.” Why “from every man”? Here is a mystery for those who know. Happy are the righteous, who know how to direct their heart’s desire toward the holy supernal King. Their desire is not for this world and its empty longing; they strive to attach themselves above, to draw their Master’s will toward them from above to below.”

p: וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה "וְיִקְחוּ" – שֶׁהֵם לוֹקְחִים זֶה בְּקִנְיָן,
And through this comes 'and they shall take'—that they acquire it as an absolute possession,
כִּלְשׁוֹן קִיחָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם;
in the sense of legal acquisition (kikha) everywhere;
דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה זֶה שֶׁלָּהֶם מַמָּשׁ,
meaning that this will belong genuinely to them,
דְּאוֹתוֹ נְדִיבוּת לֵבָב יִהְיֶה שַׁיָּיךְ לָהֶם וּבִרְשׁוּתָם,
such that that generosity of heart belongs to them and is under their domain,
כְּאָדָם הָעוֹשֶׂה בְּשֶׁלּוֹ בְּכָל עֵת שֶׁיִּרְצֶה,
like a man who does with his own property whenever he pleases,
דְּלִבּוֹ בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ לַחְשׁוֹק תָּמִיד לְכָךְ.
his heart being in his own control to yearn continually for this.
וּבְהַתְחָלַת הַקִּנְיָן מְדַבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹן נִסְתָּר "וְיִקְחוּ",
And at the commencement of acquisition Scripture speaks in the third person 'and they shall take',
כִּי אֵין הַנּוֹכָח דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא נִגְלֶה עֲדַיִן.
because the direct Presence of the Holy One is not yet manifest.
רַק אַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר "תִּקְחוּ"
Only afterward does He say 'you shall take' (in direct address)
וְגַם "תְּרוּמָתִי"
— and likewise 'My offering'—
פֵּירוּשׁ: שֶׁחֶשְׁקוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן בְּיָדָם,
meaning: that the desire of Hashem is likewise placed in their hands,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מוֹעֵד קָטָן טז:): "הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹזֵר וְצַדִּיק מְבַטֵּל",
in the manner of (Moed Katan 16b): 'The Holy One decrees and the righteous nullifies',
וּכְעִנְיַן "נִצְּחוּנִי בָּנַי" (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נט:),
and in the spirit of 'My children have triumphed over Me' (Bava Metzia 59b),
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.): "בִּתְחִלָּה תּוֹרַת ה' וּלְבַסּוֹף תּוֹרָתוֹ"
— concerning which they said (Avodah Zarah 19a): 'Initially it is the Torah of Hashem, and ultimately it is his own Torah'—
דְּהוּא בְּיָדוֹ;
for it is placed in his hand;
וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא חוֹשֵׁק, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חוֹשֵׁק גַּם כֵּן, וְהַכֹּל בְּיָדוֹ.
and whatever the tzaddik desires, Hashem desires as well, and all is in his hand.

items.h: The higher and lower unities

p: וְזֶה סוֹד יִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה וְיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה הַנִּזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר, וְעַיֵּין שָׁם (קלד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב).
And this is the mystery of the Higher Unity and Lower Unity mentioned in the Zohar, see there (134b).
דְּזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָד וְכוּלֵי" (פְּסָחִים נו.),
For this is what the brothers said: 'Just as there is in your heart only One, etc.' (Pesachim 56a),
דְּיִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה בְּלֵב יַעֲקֹב, וְיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה בְּלֵב בָּנָיו.
the Higher Unity being in Jacob's heart, and the Lower Unity in the hearts of his sons.
פֵּירוּשׁ: יִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה – דְּ"גַּם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ",
The explanation is: the Higher Unity affirms that 'all our works You have wrought for us',
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלָה וְהָרֵאשִׁית,
and this is the outset and the beginning;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל",
and concerning this Scripture states: 'Hear, O Israel',
דְּצָרִיךְ לָזֶה שְׁמִיעָה וְקַבָּלָה:
for this requires attentive hearing and acceptance:
אַתָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַשָּׂגַת אֱלֹהוּת
— you, Israel, who exerts yourself in striving to perceive divinity—
תֵּדַע דַּ"ה' אֶחָד", וְגַם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתְךָ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
know that 'Hashem is One', and your very exertion originates from Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Unity is apprehended as the one presence and as the kingship acknowledged by distinct creatures.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 2:228: “These are the two unifications, upper and lower, of ‘Shema’ and ‘Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever.’ The Zohar explains that Shema is actual unity: the whole earth is filled with His glory, and no place in any bodies or creatures is empty of Him. This is upper unity. ‘Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever’ is lower unity, at the level of His kingship: there is no king without a people, and there are distinct powers, but He is the master of them all, as the name Elokim indicates, and He is their lord and king.”

rich.text: : “These are the two unifications, upper and lower, of ‘Shema’ and ‘Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever.’ The Zohar explains that Shema is actual unity: the whole earth is filled with His glory, and no place in any bodies or creatures is empty of Him. This is upper unity. ‘Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever’ is lower unity, at the level of His kingship: there is no king without a people, and there are distinct powers, but He is the master of them all, as the name Elokim indicates, and He is their lord and king.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Dover Tzedek supplies a complementary definition of the terms used here. Upper unity recognizes that no place is empty of the divine presence; lower unity recognizes His kingship through the powers that appear distinct. The present siman applies these recognitions to the movement between received wisdom and the willing heart. Its later insistence on the actual limits of bodily action remains part of that account.

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ "בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד"
— And afterward, 'Blessed be the Name of the glory of His Kingdom forever and ever'—
הוּא כְּטַעַם אָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת לה:):
is in the spirit of their teaching (Berakhot 35b):
דִּלְאַחַר בְּרָכָה "הָאָרֶץ נָתַן לִבְנֵי אָדָם",
that following the blessing, 'the earth He gave to the children of men',
וּ"לְבַסּוֹף תּוֹרָתוֹ".
and 'ultimately it becomes his Torah'.
וְהַיִּחוּד לְהֵיפֶךְ:
And the unification proceeds in reverse:
דְּגַם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא שֶׁלּוֹ,
that Hashem, as it were, belongs to him,
דְּלֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ "אִמּוֹ" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נב).
for He did not cease cherishing Israel until He called her 'His mother' (Shemot Rabbah 52).
דְּאֵין בְּלִבֵּנוּ – שֶׁאָנוּ תּוֹלָדוֹת – כָּל מִינֵי חֶשְׁקוֹת
For within our hearts—we who are the offspring—arise all manner of desires
בִּפְרָטֵי פְּרָטוֹת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת כְּפִי חֲלוּקָּתָן.
across the individualized soul-facets according to their divisions.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 52:5: “Another matter, “they brought the Tabernacle” – that is what is written: “Emerge, daughters of Zion, and look at King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, and on the day of the rejoicing of his heart” (Song of Songs 3:11). When was this verse stated? On the day that the Tabernacle was set up, when there was great celebration in Israel because the Holy One blessed be He rested amongst them. “Daughters of Zion [tziyon]” – the children who are conspicuously [hametzuyanim] Mine, as acknowledged by the idolaters. Just as a signpost is pointed at with a finger, so, too, Israel is pointed at with a finger. That is, “the daughters of Zion.” “[Look] at King Solomon [Shlomo],” at the King of Whom [it may be said] that peace [hashalom] is His; that is the King of kings the Holy One blessed be He. “With the crown with which his mother crowned him,” this is the Tabernacle. Why did he call it a crown? Because just as a crown is beautifully designed, so, too, the Tabernacle was beautifully designed, as it is stated: “And the embroiderer in sky blue, purple, and scarlet wool, and in linen, and of the weaver, performers of all craftsmanship and devisers of designs” (Exodus 35:35). That is, “with the crown with which his mother crowned him.” Rabbi Yitzḥak said: I reviewed the entire Bible and I did not find that Batsheva crafted a crown for Solomon. Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai asked Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Yosei: ‘Did you, perhaps, hear from your father what is meant by [the phrase]: “With the crown with which his mother crowned him”?’ He said to him: ‘Yes; it is analogous to a king who had an only daughter and he loved her exceedingly. He called her: My daughter. He did not cease increasing his love for her until he called her: My sister, and until he called her: My mother. So, initially, the Holy One blessed be He called Israel a daughter, as it is stated: “Listen, daughter, and take note; incline your ear. Forget your people and your father’s house” (Psalms 45:11). He did not cease increasing His love for them until he called them: My sister, as it is stated: “Open for me, my sister, my love, my faultless dove, for my head is filled with dew, my locks, with drops of night” (Song of Songs 5:2). He did not cease increasing His love for them until he called them: My mother, as it is stated: “Pay attention to Me, My people, and listen to Me, My nation [uleumi]; for Torah will emerge from Me and My judgment I will lay down as a light for peoples”’ (Isaiah 51:4). Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai stood and kissed him on the head. “On the day of his wedding,” at Sinai; “and on the day of the rejoicing of his heart,” in Jerusalem. Alternatively, “on the day of his wedding,” at the sea; “and on the day of the rejoicing of his heart,” in the Tent of Meeting. Alternatively, “on the day of his wedding,” in the Tabernacle; “and on the day of the rejoicing of his heart,” in the Temple. Likewise, David said: “Beautiful in its view, joy of the entire world, is Mount Zion, the northern summit, the city of the great King.” (Psalms 48:3). “Beautiful in its view, joy of the entire world.” Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar said: There was an incident involving a certain merchant who went to Jerusalem to sell his merchandise. He went and sat there but did not sell [anything]. He said: ‘Is this [the city] of which they say it is the “joy of the entire world”?’ A short time later he sold all his merchandise. He said: “Beautiful in its view, joy of the entire world.” Rabbi Yoḥanan said: There was a dome of accounting outside of Jerusalem, and anyone who sought to take an accounting would go and take an accounting there, so that he would not take an accounting in Jerusalem and be distressed, for it is called “joy of the entire world.” Why is it the object of all this praise? Because it is “the city of the great King.” But when it was destroyed: “All joy is negated [arva], gladness of the land is exiled” (Isaiah 24:11). What is arva? It grew dark, just as it says: “It was evening [erev] and it was morning, one day” (Genesis 1:5). In this world, “the joy of the entire world” is suspended. But when the Holy One blessed be He will rebuild Jerusalem, He will restore all the joy to its midst, as it is stated: “For the Lord will comfort Zion; He will comfort all its ruins; He will render its wilderness like Eden and its desert like a garden of the Lord. Gladness and joy will be found in it, thanksgiving and the sound of music” (Isaiah 51:3).”

p: וְזֶהוּ: "מֵאֵת כָּל אִישׁ וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is 'from every man, etc.',
דְּגַם כֵּן מְדַבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹן נִסְתָּר;
which is likewise phrased in the third person;
וּלְמִי אָמַר "תִּקְחוּ"?
and to whom then does He say 'you shall take' (in the second person)?
וּבַזֹּהַר הִקְשָׁה זֶה גַּם כֵּן,
And in the Zohar this difficulty is raised as well,
דִּלְפִי הַתְחָלַת הַלָּשׁוֹן הָיָה לוֹ לוֹמַר "כָּל אִישׁ וְכוּלֵי יִקַּח",
that according to the opening phrasing Scripture should have said 'every man... shall take',
עַיֵּין שָׁם תֵּירוּצוֹ וּלְשׁוֹנוֹ (קל"ה רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א).
see the resolution and wording there (135a).
כַּוָּנָתוֹ: מִתּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁל כָּל פְּרָט,
His intention is: through the fierce desire of each individual,
כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַחֵשֶׁק
when it reaches the ultimate surging of longing
וְהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם עֲדַיִן
while it is yet in inward concealment,
וְנִקְרָא "תְּרוּמָתִי", דְּהוּא מִשֶּׁלִּי
— and is termed 'My offering', deriving from Me—
אֲנִי אוֹמֵר "תִּקְחוּ" בְּהַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכָח:
I declare 'you shall take' in direct address:
תּוּכְלוּ לִיקַּח בְּקִנְיָן
you are empowered to acquire it as a lasting possession,
שֶׁהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלִּי גַּם כֵּן שֶׁלָּכֶם.
such that My desire is likewise yours.
וְזֶה הַקְּבִיעוּת בַּלֵּב שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בֶּאֱמֶת אַחַר כָּךְ
And this is the permanent fixture within the heart that is truly established afterward,
אוֹתָן הַחֶשְׁקוֹת הַנּוֹלָדִים אַחַר כָּךְ
in those holy desires that are generated subsequently,
אַחַר שֶׁלִּבּוֹ קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא לַחְשׁוֹק רַק לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
after his heart is firmly anchored to yearn solely for Hashem's will.
הַחֶשְׁקוֹת הַנּוֹלָדִים אַחַר כָּךְ כָּל פְּרָטֵיהֶם
— Those subsequent desires in all their individualized expressions—
זֶה נִקְרָא יִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה דְּ"בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד",
this is termed the Lower Unity of Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto Le'olam Va'ed,
הַמּוֹלִיד אַחַר כָּךְ פָּרָשַׁת "וְאָהַבְתָּ" לְכָל פְּרָט נֶפֶשׁ.
which engenders afterward the section of 'And you shall love' for each individual soul.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ פָּרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ" בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים,
And subsequently follows the section of 'And it shall come to pass if you hearken' in the plural,
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב אַחַר כָּךְ: "וְזֹאת הַתְּרוּמָה אֲשֶׁר תִּקְחוּ מֵאִתָּם" (שְׁמוֹת כה, ג) בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים,
and this mirrors what is stated next: 'And this is the offering which you shall take from them' in the plural,
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בַּזֹּהַר (קל"ה א) הַתֵּירוּץ.
and see there in the Zohar (135a) the resolution.

items.h: From mind and heart to action

p: וּפֵירוּשׁ, כִּי "זֹאת" הוּא שֶׁמּוֹרֶה בְּאֶצְבַּע,
And the explanation is: 'zot' (this) implies pointing with a finger,
הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁיּוֹצֵא לִגְמַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
namely when a matter reaches practical completion.
כִּי יִחוּדָא עִילָּאָה בַּמּוֹחַ וְיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה בַּלֵּב;
For the Higher Unity is in the brain and the Lower Unity in the heart;
דְּהַחֵשֶׁק בַּלֵּב שֶׁחָפֵץ מְאֹד לָדַעַת אֶת ה' וְתוֹרָתוֹ,
for desire resides in the heart yearning deeply to know Hashem and His Torah,
וְהַשְׁפָּעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בַּמּוֹחַ
and Hashem's divine influx rests in the brain
שֶׁמִּתְבּוֹנֵן בּוֹ בְּחָכְמַת יְדִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
wherein one contemplates the wisdom of divine knowledge,
וְהַהַכָּרָה דְּהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלּוֹ גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— and the recognition that his desire is likewise from Hashem—
הֲרֵי מְיַיחֵד הַכֹּל לְהַמּוֹחַ.
behold, he unifies everything toward the brain.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה הַיְינוּ דְּגַם הַחָכְמָה הוּא תּוֹרָתוֹ,
And afterward the Lower Unity means that wisdom itself becomes his Torah,
שֶׁהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלּוֹ הוֹלִיד חָכְמָה זוֹ, וְהַכֹּל מִן הַלֵּב.
in that his heartfelt desire birthed this wisdom, and all flows from the heart.
וְאָז מִתְפַּשְּׁטִים הַכֹּחוֹת מִן הַלֵּב לְשֵׁשׁ קְצָווֹת,
And then these faculties expand outward from the heart into the six spatial directions,
שֶׁחָלוּק לִפְרָטֵי הַמִּדּוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת,
dividing into varied individual emotional traits,
וְהַכֹּל מְיוּחָד בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
with all unified in the will of Hashem, blessed be He,
וּרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ,
and our true desire is to perform His will,
וּמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ הַמִּתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת בָּנוּ הִיא הַפּוֹעֶלֶת.
and the attribute of His Sovereignty expanding within us is what operates.
וּכְשֶׁיּוֹצֵא לִגְמַר מַעֲשֶׂה,
And when it emerges into the finality of physical deed,
שֶׁהוּא הַנּוֹלָד מִמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְרָצוֹן דְּמוֹחַ וְלֵב,
which is born of thought and will in brain and heart,
בָּזֶה אֵין חִלּוּק בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת כְּלָל;
in this there is no differentiation among souls whatsoever;
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּגַם פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת כָּרִמּוֹן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סוֹף חֲגִיגָה).
for as is known, even the transgressors of Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate (Chagigah 27a).
דְּחִלּוּק מַדְרֵגוֹת רַק בְּמוֹחַ וְלֵב, חָכְמָה וְרָצוֹן;
For the variance in levels exists solely in brain and heart, in wisdom and will;
אֲבָל הַהַצְלָחָה בִּגְמַר מַעֲשֶׂה
— however, success in the completion of deed—
בָּזֶה אֵין מַדְרֵגוֹת,
in this there are no hierarchical ranks,
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
and all Israel possess a portion in the World to Come
מִצַּד גְּמַר מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמִצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים.
by virtue of the completed deeds of mitzvot and good works.

p: וְזֶהוּ פָּרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ" בְּעוֹל מִצְוֹת דְּהוּא מַעֲשֶׂה,
And this is why the passage of 'And it shall come to pass if you hearken' dealing with the yoke of mitzvot—which is action—
הוּא בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים, שָׁוֶה לַכֹּל.
is stated in the plural, being equal unto all.
וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "בְּכָל מְאֹדְכֶם",
And it does not state within it 'with all your might' (me'odkhem),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ נֶגֶד גְּמַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בִּנְתִינַת הָרְכוּשׁ בַּפּוֹעַל;
which corresponds to the completion of deed through surrendering possessions in actual fact;
זֶה שַׁיָּיךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא עֲדַיִן בְּמוֹחַ וְלֵב וְלֹא יָצָא לַפּוֹעַל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה,
for this applies when it is still in brain and heart and has not emerged into practical execution;
אָז צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַחֵשֶׁק וּנְדִיבוּת הַלֵּב בְּכָל מִינֵי מַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה
then the desire and generosity of heart must encompass every form of action and service that might arise,
וְשֶׁיְּצַוֶּוה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְיִרְאֶה שֶׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – הוּא מוּסְכָּם לְכָךְ.
such that whatever Hashem commands and whatever is seen to be His will—he is ready for it.

items.h: Boundless intention and bounded action

p: אֲבָל כְּשֶׁמּוֹצִיא לַפּוֹעַל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
However, when bringing the deed into physical execution,
וַדַּאי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה יֵשׁ לָהּ גְּבוּל וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת תָּמִיד,
surely the physical act has a boundary and cannot be performed continuously,
וְאָסוּר לְבַזְבֵּז כָּל מָמוֹנוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּתוּבּוֹת נ.),
and it is truly forbidden to squander all of one's money (Ketubot 50a),
וּלְמִצְוֹת "עַד שְׁלִישׁ בְּמִצְוָה" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בָּבָא קַמָּא ט:),
and for commandments 'up to a third for a mitzvah' (Bava Kamma 9b),
הַכֹּל בִּגְבוּל.
everything having a defined boundary.
לְכָךְ בְּפָרָשָׁה שְׁנִיָּה, דְּקָאֵי אַמִּצְוֹת וּלְעָבְדוֹ בַּפּוֹעַל, הוּא בִּגְבוּל.
Therefore in the second passage, which refers to mitzvot and actual service, it is bounded.
כִּי בְּמוֹחַ וָלֵב הוּא הַיִּחוּד עִילָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה
For in brain and heart resides the Higher and Lower Unity
דְּמִתְיַיחֵד בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא גְּבוּל.
which unites with the will of Hashem, blessed be He, which is limitless.
וְגַם בְּעֵת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַכַּוָּנָה דְּמוֹחַ וְלֵב,
And likewise during the physical deed, the inward intention of brain and heart—
דְּהַיְינוּ "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ" – הוּא בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת.
namely 'with all your heart and with all your soul'—is boundless in its reach.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: and it is truly forbidden to squander all of one's money (Ketubot 50a),

paragraphs.text: Ketubot 50a: ‘Rabbi Ila said: In Usha they enacted that one who gives generously should not give away more than a fifth. It was likewise taught: One who gives generously should not give away more than a fifth, lest he come to depend on other people. An incident occurred in which someone wished to give away more than a fifth, but his companion did not allow him. Who was that companion? Rabbi Yeshevav. Some say that Rabbi Yeshevav was the one who wished to give, and his companion did not allow him. Who was that companion? Rabbi Akiva.’

p: אֲבָל פְּעֻלַּת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה עַצְמָהּ
— However, the physical action itself—
זֶהוּ "הַנִּגְלֹת לָנוּ וּלְבָנֵינוּ" (דְּבָרִים כט, כח),
this represents 'the revealed things belonging to us and our children' (Deuteronomy 29:28),
שֶׁהוּא נַעֲשֶׂה עַל יְדֵי גּוּף הָאָדָם שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל גְּבוּל,
which is enacted through the body of man, which is finite and bounded,
וְלֹא שַׁיָּיךְ "בְּכָל", דְּהַיְינוּ בְּלֹא גְּבוּל.
and the term 'with all' (bekhol)—meaning without limit—does not apply to it.
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר: "וְזֹאת הַתְּרוּמָה", וְלֹא "תְּרוּמָתִי",
Therefore Scripture says: 'And this is the offering', and not 'My offering',
כִּי בְּפֹעַל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה נִרְאֶה שֶׁהוּא בִּידֵי אָדָם.
for in practical execution it appears to be in the hands of man.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא בְּהַכָּרַת הַנּוֹכָח מִצַּד הַכַּוָּנָה הַטּוֹבָה,
Nonetheless, it is accompanied by direct awareness of the Presence through pure intention,
וְנִקְבָּע בְּקִנְיָן הַצְלָחַת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
and the success of the deed becomes established as an enduring acquisition.
"מֵאִתָּם" – מֵאֵת הַמִּתְנַדְּבִים בְּלֵב טוֹב
'From them'—from those who give willingly with a good heart
וְהַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּיִחוּד
and conscious perception of Hashem in ultimate unity,
שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר עַל יְדֵי זֶה כְּשֶׁיּוֹצֵא אַחַר כָּךְ לַפּוֹעַל,
which clarifies that when it subsequently emerges into deed,
נִקְבָּע בְּקִנְיָן גַּם כֵּן הַצְלָחַת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
the success of the action is likewise secured as a lasting acquisition.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: this represents 'the revealed things belonging to us and our children' (Deuteronomy 29:28),

p: וְזֶהוּ לָרַבִּים,
And this applies to the multitude,
שֶׁכָּל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּשָׁוֶה יֵשׁ לָהֶם הַצְלָחַת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּקִנְיָן,
for all the seed of Israel possess equally the success of deed as a possession,
דִּ"מְלֵאִים מִצְוֹת כָּרִמּוֹן",
being 'full of mitzvot like a pomegranate',
וְ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.),
and 'even though he sinned, he remains Israel' (Sanhedrin 44a),
וְהַחֲטָאִים מְסוּדָּרִים וּבָאִים מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית (שַׁבָּת פט:),
and the sins are arranged and orchestrated from the six days of Creation (Shabbat 89b),
דְּהַיְינוּ הַצְלָחַת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה כְּפִי אֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which represents the true outcome of deeds according to the authentic will of Hashem.
לְפִי שֶׁיִּחוּדָא עִילָּאָה וְיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה דְּלֵב יַעֲקֹב וּבָנָיו
Because the Higher and Lower Unity of the heart of Jacob and his sons
קָבוּעַ בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
is permanently embedded within every single Jew,
דִּגְמִירֵי דְּלָא כָּלֶה שִׁבְטָא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קטו רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב),
for we have a tradition that a tribe never becomes extinct (Bava Batra 115b),
דְּהַיְינוּ לֵב בָּנָיו בְּיִחוּדָא תַּתָּאָה.
which is the heart of his sons in the Lower Unity;
וְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל קָבוּעַ בּוֹ יִחוּד דִּ"שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל" וּ"בָרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד",
and within every Jew is embedded the unity of 'Shema Yisrael' and 'Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto Le'olam Va'ed',
הַגַּם דְּהוּא אֵינוֹ מַרְגִּישׁ זֶה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת מוֹחוֹ וְלִבּוֹ כְּלָל;
even though he does not consciously sense this in the overt disclosure of his brain and heart at all;
הֲרֵי קַיְימָא לַן (בְּרָכוֹת יג.): "הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאָזְנוֹ – יָצָא",
for behold, the halakhah is established (Berakhot 13a): 'One who recites the Shema and did not make it audible to his own ear has fulfilled his obligation',
דְּהַיְינוּ הַגַּם שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַרְגִּישׁ זֶה.
which signifies: even though he does not consciously hear or feel this.

sections.en: Through the Generosity of Heart of the Children of Israel with Their Wealth (me'od)

p: [רנג] עַל יְדֵי נְדִיבוּת לֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּמְאֹדָם
Through the generosity of heart of the children of Israel with their wealth (me'od)
נִבְנֶה קְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם – מִשְׁכָּן וּמִקְדָּשׁ.
is constructed the sanctity of space—the Tabernacle and the Temple.
וְעַל יְדֵי נְדִיבוּת לְבָבָם בְּנַפְשָׁם,
And through the generosity of their heart with their vitality (nefesh),
דְּהַיְינוּ בְּכֹחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה שֶׁבַּגּוּף,
meaning within the active bodily faculties,
נִבְנֶה קְדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַן,
is constructed the sanctity of time,
כְּטַעַם (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג.): "מִי שֶׁטָּרַח בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת יֹאכַל בְּשַׁבָּת".
in the spirit of (Avodah Zarah 3a): 'He who toiled on the eve of Shabbat shall eat on Shabbat.'
וּכְפִי פְּעֻלַּת הָאָדָם בִּקְדוּשָּׁה בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
And according to a person's holy action during the six working days,
שֶׁהֵם יְמֵי הַפְּעֻלָּה בְּכֹחוֹתָיו,
which are the days of manual activity with his faculties,
כָּךְ הוּא מְקַבֵּל קְדוּשָּׁה בְּשַׁבָּת.
so does he receive sanctity on Shabbat.

Go and fulfill it.’’

p: וְכָךְ בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם:
And so too regarding the sanctity of space:
וַדַּאי כָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי נִדְבַת לְבָבוֹ בִּתְרוּמַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְנִדְבַת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
certainly each according to the willingness of his heart in the offering of the Tabernacle and Temple,
וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ בְּהַקְרָבַת הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת
— and so afterward in the bringing of the sacrifices—
כָּךְ הָיָה הַשָּׂגָתוֹ בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם.
such was his spiritual perception of the sanctity of space.
וְעַל יְדֵי נְדִיבוּת לִבּוֹ "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ",
And through the generosity of his heart in 'with all your heart',
דְּהַיְינוּ בִּכְפִיַּת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁבַּלֵּב
— meaning through subjugating the inclination within the heart—
עַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִים לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ.
through this one merits the sanctity of soul (the human dimension).
שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ זְמַן וּמָקוֹם מְקוּדָּשׁ,
For just as there exist sanctified time and sanctified space,
כָּךְ יֵשׁ נֶפֶשׁ נִבְחָר,
so is there a chosen soul,
כְּטַעַם (סַנְהֶדְרִין סה:): "מַה יּוֹם מִיּוֹמַיִם? מַה גְּבַר מִגֻּבְרִין?".
mirroring (Sanhedrin 65b): 'Why is this day different from any other? Why is this man different from any other?'
וְהוּא רֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר,
And this is the leader of the generation,
כִּי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד,
for all Israel are like one collective man,
וְהַנִּבְחָר הוּא בְּמַדְרֵגַת הָרֹאשׁ לַגּוּף.
and the chosen leader stands at the level of the head to the body.
וּכְפִי נִדְבַת לְבָבוֹ "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ", כָּךְ מֵאִיר בּוֹ קְדוּשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
And commensurate with the devotion of his heart in 'with all your heart', so radiates within him the sanctity of the soul,
כִּי בְּכָל הָאֵבָרִים מֵאִיר מִן הָרֹאשׁ.
for unto all limbs illumination spreads from the head.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: כָּךְ יֵשׁ נֶפֶשׁ נִבְחָר,
footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: so is there a chosen soul,

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 3: ““And behold, Hashem was stationed over him.” It is known that the blessed God’s principal revelation within the world comes through three: world, year, and soul. “World” is the place of the Temple, where His divinity is revealed. “Year” is the choicest of times, Shabbat, in which His divinity is revealed. “Soul” means that He reveals His Divine Presence upon souls from Israel. Here all three were complete: the place of the Temple, as it says, “This is none other than the house of God”; the choicest time, for this revelation certainly occurred on the holy Shabbat; and the soul, our father Jacob, the choicest of souls, in whom all the souls of Israel were included, as it says (Isaiah 29:23), “They shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob.””

p: וְיֵשׁ בַּגּוּף: מוֹחַ – וְהוּא כֹּחַ הַהַשְׂכָּלָה שֶׁבָּאָדָם;
And there exist within the body: the brain—which is the intellectual capacity in man;
וְלֵב – שֶׁבּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים;
and the heart—in which dwells the spirit of life;
וְכָבֵד – שֶׁבּוֹ כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁבּוֹ הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ.
and the liver—wherein lies the faculty of physical deed, wherein the blood is the life.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי כָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל מִג'.
And that is because each one is compounded of three.
וְכֵן בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם: עֶשֶׂר קְדוּשּׁוֹת (כֵּלִים פֶּרֶק א),
And so in the sanctity of space: there are ten degrees of sanctity (Kelim 1:6),
כִּי כָל דָּבָר כָּלוּל מֵעֶשֶׂר:
for every entity contains ten sefirotic levels:
וְג' רִאשׁוֹנוֹת הֵם כֹּחוֹת הַמְּקַבְּלִים;
the first three being the receptive faculties;
וְג' אֶמְצָעִיּוֹת – כֹּחוֹת הַגּוּף;
and the middle three—the faculties of the body;
וְד' תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת – כֹּחוֹת הַמּוּשְׁפָּעִים הַהַשְׁפָּעָה.
and the lower four—the faculties that channel the divine bestowal.
וְנֶגְדָּם: "נֶפֶשׁ" – הוּא שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ קַבָּלַת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה;
And facing them: 'Soul' (Nefesh)—is that in whose hand rests the receiving of the influx;
וּ"מָקוֹם" – הוּא הַמְּקַבֵּל הַהַשְׁפָּעָה;
and 'Space' (Makom)—is that which receives the influx;
וְהַ"זְּמַן" – הוּא אֶמְצָעִי וְהַגּוּף שֶׁבּוֹ עוֹבֶרֶת הַהַשְׁפָּעָה.
and 'Time' (Zman)—is the intermediary vessel and body through which the influx passes.

p: וּבַמָּקוֹם: יְרוּשָׁלַיִם הוּא קְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם;
And in space: Jerusalem embodies the sanctity of space;
וַעֲזָרוֹת – נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַן הַנִּבְנֶה עַל יְדֵי עֲבוֹדוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ;
and the Temple Courtyards correspond to the sanctity of time, built through the sacrificial services conducted therein;
וְקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים – נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
and the Holy of Holies corresponds to the sanctity of the soul,
וּבוֹ אֵין נִכְנָס אֶלָּא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, נֶפֶשׁ מְיוּחָד,
wherein none enters except the High Priest, a unique soul,
וּמְבַקֵּשׁ: "לָא יַעֲדֵי עָבֵיד שׁוּלְטָן מִדְּבֵית יְהוּדָה" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹמָא נג:) גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשַּׁת נֶפֶשׁ,
who prays: 'May rulership not depart from the house of Judah' (Yoma 53b), which likewise pertains to the sanctity of the soul,
וְנִבְנֶה עַל יְדֵי "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ",
and is constructed through 'with all your heart',
כְּטַעַם: "יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים" (בְּרָכוֹת ל.),
mirroring: 'He shall direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies' (Berakhot 30a),
שֶׁקְּדוּשָׁתוֹ בְּנוּיָה עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַׁת "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ".
for its sanctity is built through the holiness of 'with all your heart'.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 43:1: “The prayer that the rule of authority not depart from the house of Judah has this same intention. My holy father explained that he prayed to Hashem to attend continually and especially to the root. The tribe of Judah is the root of the life of all Israel; when the root is blessed, blessing will consequently not be lacking for the branches either.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim explains the precise prayer quoted here: Judah is the common root, so blessing the root sustains the branches. The surrounding discussion says that the Kohen Gadol's inward service must be followed by prayer that the light become perceptible in ordinary human life. This clarifies why the siman places the Kohen Gadol and the prayer for kingship together within the sanctity of a particular soul, whose service bears upon the whole people.

p: וְהַיְינוּ כִּי כָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל מִכָּל הַג':
And that is because each is compounded of all three:
בִּנְתִינַת הַמָּמוֹן שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הָרְכוּשׁ – הוּא "בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ";
in the giving of money which belongs to possessions—it is 'with all your might';
וְהַנְּתִינָה, הוּא כֹּחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה – הוּא "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ";
and the physical act of giving, being manual action—is 'with all your soul';
וְהַנְּדִיבוּת לֵב – הוּא "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ";
and the generosity of heart—is 'with all your heart';
וּמִכֹּחַ נְדִיבוּת לֵב הוּא קְדוּשַּׁת הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים.
and from the power of generosity of heart comes the sanctity of the Holy of Holies.
וְכֵן בַּזְּמַן: שַׁבָּת הוּא קְבִיעַ וְקַיָּימָא מִצַּד הַפְּעֻלָּה וּמַעֲשֵׂה הָאָדָם,
And so in time: Shabbat is inherently fixed and established through the action of man,
שֶׁזּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת קְבִיעַ וְקַיָּימָא,
which is indeed permanently fixed,
דַּאֲפִילּוּ פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִין מִצְוֹת, וּכְנִזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רנ"ב,
since even the sinners of Israel are full of mitzvot, as mentioned above in section 252,
וְהוּא הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ קְדוּשָּׁה בַּזְּמַנִּים וּבְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַחוֹל.
and it is what radiates sanctity into the appointed times and the six weekdays.
וְיוֹם טוֹב, שֶׁבּוֹ "יֵרָאֶה כָּל זְכוּרְךָ" בַּמָּקוֹם,
And Yom Tov, upon which 'all your males shall appear' in sacred space,
הוּא נֶגֶד "בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ",
corresponds to 'with all your might',
דְּוַדַּאי בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה מִצְוָה יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן צַד דִּ"בְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ"
for certainly in every performance of a mitzvah there is an aspect of 'with all your might'
וּרְכוּשׁ שֶׁמַּפְסִיד עַל יְדֵי כֵּן.
and financial expense one incurs thereby.
וְזֶה תָּלוּי כְּפִי נִדְבוֹת לֵב הָאָדָם וְכַוָּנָתוֹ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוָה,
And this depends upon the generosity of the person's heart and his intention in the mitzvah,
וְכַוָּנַת הַלֵּב הוּא "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ", שֶׁזֶּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי.
and heartfelt intention is 'with all your heart', which is why 'Israel sanctifies the seasons'.
וְנֶגְדּוֹ קְדוּשַּׁת רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ, שֶׁנִּבְנֶה עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין.
And corresponding to it is the holiness of Rosh Chodesh, built through the soul-sanctity of the Sanhedrin.
וְכֵן קְדוּשַּׁת חֲנֻכָּה וּפוּרִים שֶׁנִּבְנוּ עַל יְדֵי נְפָשׁוֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת,
And so the sanctity of Chanukah and Purim which were established through unique souls,
וּבָהֶם מֵאִיר קְדוּשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁמִּצַּד הַזְּמַן.
and within them shines the sanctity of soul from the aspect of time.

p: וּמִצַּד הַמָּמוֹן הַנִּתְלֶה בַּלֵּב הוּא יוֹם טוֹב,
And from the aspect of money bound up in the heart is Yom Tov,
שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת זְמַנּוֹ קָבוּעַ בַּתּוֹרָה,
whose date is truly designated in the Torah,
רַק שֶׁנִּתְלָה בִּקְבִיעוּת רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ הַתָּלוּי בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
yet is dependent upon the calendar sanctification of Rosh Chodesh established by Israel,
וּבָהֶם זוֹכִין לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם בְּיִחוּד
and through them one merits the sanctity of space in particular
[וְכָל אֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ חָלוּק גַּם כֵּן לְג' וּבִכְלָלָן עֶשֶׂר קְדוּשּׁוֹת, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
[and each of these is subdivided into three, totaling ten degrees of sanctity, but this is not the place to elaborate].
וּבַנְּפָשׁוֹת יֵשׁ מֶלֶךְ, וְהוּא נֶגֶד הַלֵּב כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה,
And among souls there is the King, who corresponds to the heart as written in Sefer Yetzirah,
שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ רוּחַ חַיִּים לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
from whom flows the spirit of life unto all Israel.
וְזֶה כָּל יְגִיעוֹת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּל יָמָיו,
And this was the lifelong toil of King David, peace be upon him,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ לֵב טָהוֹר,
that he possess a pure heart,
עַד שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ: "בְּרָא לִי וְגוֹמֵר" – יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן לְצוֹרֶךְ הַשְׁפָּעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
until he pleaded: 'Create in me a clean heart, etc.'—ex nihilo for the sake of channeling divine influence unto Israel.
וְהוּא נִבְנֶה עַל יְדֵי "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" שֶׁבַּלֵּב עַצְמוֹ
And it is built through 'with all your heart' in the heart itself,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר עַל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
which is not externally apparent upon manual action.

p: וּמִצַּד הַגְבָּרַת הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב עַד "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ" בִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ עַל רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— And from surging desire in the heart reaching 'with all your soul' in martyrdom for Hashem's will—
מִזֶּה נִבְנֶה קְדוּשַּׁת הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין וּמוּפְלָא שֶׁבְּבֵית דִּין,
from this is built the sanctity of the Sanhedrin and the chief sage of the Court,
וְהִיא נֶגֶד הַכָּבֵד וְהַדָּם הַדָּנִים דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
which corresponds to the liver and blood, judging capital cases
וְשׁוֹפְטִים עַל כֹּחוֹת הַפְּעֻלָּה שֶׁבִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and ruling over the faculties of practical action in Israel.
וּמְעַבְּרִים שָׁנִים וּחֳדָשִׁים
— And they intercalate leap years and declare new months—
הַיְינוּ שֶׁקְּדוּשַּׁת הַזְּמַן נִבְנֶה עַל יָדָם.
meaning that the sanctity of time is constructed through them.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַגְבָּרַת הַחֵשֶׁק עַד "בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ",
And through elevating desire up to 'with all your might',
לִהְיוֹתוֹ כָּל רְכוּשׁוֹ כְּלֹא חָשִׁיב בְּלִבּוֹ נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— such that all a person's wealth is deemed as nothing in his heart against Hashem's will—
נִבְנֶה קְדוּשַּׁת הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל,
is built the sanctity of the High Priest,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ (יוֹמָא יח.): "גַּדְּלֵהוּ מִשֶּׁל אֶחָיו" בְּעוֹשֶׁר,
concerning whom it is said (Yoma 18a): 'Make him greatest among his brethren' in wealth,
שֶׁהוּא שַׁיָּיךְ לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַמָּקוֹם בְּיִחוּד,
who is uniquely tied to the sanctity of space,
וְהוּא הַמּוֹחַ שֶׁבְּגוּף הַכְּנֵסִיָּה
and he represents the brain within the collective body of Israel
הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ הַשְׂכָּלָה לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
channeling divine wisdom unto all Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן יִשְׁמְרוּ דַעַת וְתוֹרָה יְבַקְשׁוּ מִפִּיהוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (מַלְאָכִי ב, ז).
as it is written: 'For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek Torah at his mouth, etc.' (Malachi 2:7).

p: וְהַגַּם שֶׁנֶּחְרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
And although the Temple was destroyed,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ ג' קְדוּשּׁוֹת אֵלּוּ בִּנְפָשׁוֹת מְיוּחָדוֹת,
nonetheless these three sanctities remain within unique souls,
רַק בְּהֶעְלֵם וְאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת מְיוּחָד.
only in hiddenness rather than in manifest disclosure.
וּכְפִי כִּשְׁרוֹן הַדּוֹר כָּךְ הֵם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת יוֹתֵר,
And according to the spiritual worthiness of the generation so are they more revealed,
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
and conversely so in decline, Heaven forbid.
וְכֵן כְּפִי כִּשְׁרוֹן כָּל אִישׁ פְּרָטִי בְּכֹחוֹת לִבּוֹ,
And so according to the worthiness of each individual in the faculties of his heart,
כָּךְ הוּא יוֹנֵק מֵאוֹתָהּ קְדוּשָּׁה.
so does he draw sustenance from that sanctity.

sections.en: A Person Must Offer Unto Hashem

p: [רנד] הָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לְנַדֵּב לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דָּבָר הֶחָבִיב לוֹ,
A person must offer unto Hashem, blessed be He, that which is precious to him,
שֶׁבּוֹ יִגְדּוֹר עַצְמוֹ לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
wherein he erects a boundary around himself for the will of Hashem.
וּמִי שֶׁהוּא מְמוּלָּא בְּכָל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת כְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְגוֹדְרָם,
And one who is filled with all manner of desires like Abraham and curbs them,
הוּא הַנִּקְרָא "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ";
he is the one termed serving 'with all your heart';
לֹא מִי שֶׁמְּקוֹרָר בְּטִבְעוֹ וְאֵינוֹ בַּעַל תַּאֲוָה,
not one who is naturally cold and devoid of passion,
אֵין זֶה עוֹבֵד "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְאַוֶּוה לְחֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
for he is not serving 'with all your heart' if he never covets worldly pleasures.

paragraphs.text: Eight Chapters 6:3: “The distinction is this: the evils that the philosophers call evils, concerning which they say that one who does not desire them is superior to one who desires them but restrains his inclination, are matters recognized by all people as evil: bloodshed, theft, robbery, fraud, harming someone who has done one no harm, repaying a benefactor with evil, dishonoring father and mother, and similar things. These are the commandments of which the Sages of blessed memory said, “Had they not been written, they would have deserved to be written” (Yoma 67b). Some of our later scholars, afflicted by the sickness of the theologians, call them “rational commandments.” There is no doubt that a soul that longs for any of these things and desires it is deficient. An excellent soul does not desire any of these evils at all, and is not distressed by refraining from them. The matters concerning which the Sages said that one who restrains his inclination is superior and receives a greater reward, however, are the laws received through revelation. This is true, because without the Torah they would not have been evils at all. Therefore they said that a person should allow his soul to desire them, with only the Torah preventing him from them. Consider their wisdom, peace be upon them, and the examples they gave. They did not say: “A person should not say, ‘I do not wish to kill a person; I do not wish to steal; I do not wish to lie,’ but rather, ‘I wish to, yet what can I do? My Father in Heaven has decreed against it.’” Instead, all their examples were revealed laws: meat with milk, wearing wool and linen together, and forbidden sexual unions. These commandments, and others like them, are what the blessed God calls “statutes.””

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 15:4-8: “Among the intermediate people there are also two levels: “one who serves God” and “one who has not served Him.” Nevertheless, the latter is not wicked: he has never committed even a minor transgression, has fulfilled every mitzvah he could fulfill, and has engaged in Torah study, which is equal to them all, without ceasing his review. Yet he does not wage any battle to overcome the inclination through Hashem’s light illuminating the divine soul in the brain, which rules the heart, as explained above. His inclination does not oppose him at all to distract him from Torah and service, and he has no need to fight it. For example, he may be diligent in study by his inborn nature, because of a predominance of “black bile”; he may have no struggle with desire for women because he is naturally cold, and likewise may naturally lack a feeling of pleasure in other worldly enjoyments. He therefore need not contemplate Hashem’s greatness so extensively in order to generate from his understanding a spirit of knowledge and fear of Hashem in his brain, to guard against violating prohibitions, and love of Hashem in his heart, to cling to Him through performing the mitzvot and Torah study, which is equal to them all. The hidden love in the heart of Israel as a whole, called “those who love His name,” is sufficient for him. He is therefore not called “one who serves” at all, for this hidden love is not his own action or labor, but our inheritance from our ancestors for all Israel, as will be explained below. Likewise, even someone who is not naturally diligent in study, but has trained himself to study with great diligence until habit becomes second nature, can suffice with this hidden love—unless he wishes to study beyond his usual measure.”

p: וְכֵן עַצְלָן בְּטִבְעוֹ וְאֵינוֹ פּוֹעֵל בְּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And likewise, one who is naturally indolent and inactive in physical affairs,
אֵין נִקְרָא "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ";
is not termed serving 'with all your soul';
רַק כְּמוֹ יִצְחָק, שֶׁהָיָה מִדָּתוֹ הַגְּבוּרָה בְּכֹחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה וּזְרִיזוּתוֹ,
rather like Isaac, whose attribute was Gevurah (Might) in practical action and zeal,
וְעָצַר זְרִיזוּתוֹ בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and restrained his zeal regarding the affairs of this world.
וְכֵן "בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ" הוּא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And likewise 'with all your might' corresponds to our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֻלִּין צא.): דְּנִשְׁתַּיֵּיר עַל פַּכִּין קְטַנִּים,
concerning whom they said (Chullin 91a): that he remained behind for small jugs,
דְּמָמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב מִגּוּפוֹ,
for his money was more precious to him than his body;
בּוֹ הָיָה הַנְּדִיבוּת דְּ"כָל מְאֹדְךָ",
within him resided the true dedication of 'all your might',
וּבוֹ הוּא בֵּירוּר מִדָּה זוֹ;
and through him this attribute is clarified;
וְלֹא מִי שֶׁבְּטִבְעוֹ וַתְּרָן וְאֵין מָמוֹן חָשׁוּב כְּלָל.
not one who is naturally indifferent to possessions, for whom wealth holds no value at all.

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה כז:): "מְשַׁבֵּחַ אֲנִי אֶת הָעַצְלָנִים וְכוּלֵי",
Nevertheless they said (Sukkah 27b): 'I praise the indolent, etc.',
דְּוַדַּאי מִכָּל מָקוֹם טוֹב,
for it is certainly good at any rate,
וְ"עָצֵל וְנִשְׂכָּר" קָרֵינַן לֵיהּ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פְּסָחִים נ:);
and we call him 'indolent and rewarded' (Pesachim 50b);
רַק שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּמַדְרֵגַת "בְּכָל וְגוֹמֵר".
only that he does not reach the spiritual level of 'with all, etc.'
"כָּל" נִקְרָא הַדָּבָר שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹ בְּתוֹלָדָה נִקְשֶׁרֶת בּוֹ,
'All' designates that specific matter to which his soul is bound by nature,
וְהוּא מְשַׁעְבְּדוֹ לְאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ.
and which he subordinates to the love of Hashem and His service.
וְכָל בֵּירוּרִין שֶׁל הָאָדָם הוּא בָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא מְקוּשָּׁר;
And all of a person's spiritual trials center on that to which he is bound,
בָּזֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְנַסּוֹ "לָדַעַת אֵת אֲשֶׁר בִּלְבָבוֹ".
in this the Holy One tests him 'to know what is in his heart' (Deuteronomy 8:2).

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 50b:4: “The Sages taught: Some are diligent and rewarded, and some are diligent and lose out. Some are idle and rewarded, and some are idle and lose out. Diligent and rewarded: one who works all week but does not work on Shabbat eve. Diligent and losing out: one who works all week and also works on Shabbat eve. Idle and rewarded: one who does not work all week and does not work on Shabbat eve. Idle and losing out: one who does not work all week but works on Shabbat eve. Rava said: Although the women of Mechoza do not work on Shabbat eve, it is because they are accustomed to luxury, for they do not work on the other days either. Nevertheless, we call them ‘idle and rewarded.’”

items.h: The trials of the Patriarchs

p: וְכָל נִסְיוֹנוֹת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And all the trials of Abraham our father, peace be upon him,
הֵם בְּעִנְיְנֵי חֶמְדּוֹת שֶׁל הָאָדָם:
were in the personal loves and desires of man:
אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו וְחַיָּיו וּמְזוֹנוֹתָיו.
his wife, his children, his life, and his sustenance.
וְנִסָּיוֹן יִצְחָק – בְּמַאֲמַר "גּוּר בָּאָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כו, ג),
And the trial of Isaac—was in the command 'Sojourn in this land, etc.' (Genesis 26:3),
שֶׁגַּם מִפְּנֵי זַלְעֲפוֹת רָעָב לֹא יִפְעַל שׁוּם פְּעֻלָּה,
that even before the famine he should initiate no human action,
הַגַּם שֶׁיָּדַע כְּשֶׁיֵּצֵא חוּץ לָאָרֶץ יִהְיֶה לוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל;
even though he knew that leaving the Land would provide food;
וְהוּא בְּטֶבַע תּוֹלַדְתּוֹ כֹּחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת
and he possessed by nature the power of action and exertion,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד עַמּוּד הָעֲבוֹדָה,
which corresponds to the Pillar of Divine Service,
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ: "וַיִּזְרַע יִצְחָק וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם, יב) – עֵסֶק הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
which is why it is said of him: 'And Isaac sowed, etc.' (ibid. 12)—active labor,
וְאָז נִמְנַע בִּדְבַר ה'.
and yet he restrained himself at the word of Hashem.

p: וְנִזְכַּר רַק נִסָּיוֹן זֶה,
And only this trial is highlighted,
כִּי עֶשֶׂר הוּא מִסְפַּר קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה כַּנּוֹדָע,
for ten is the measure of a complete spiritual stature as is known,
וּבְוַדַּאי לְכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ עֲשָׂרָה בֵּירוּרִים,
and certainly each of the Patriarchs underwent ten trials,
וְאֵצֶל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלָה, נִזְכְּרוּ כֻּלָּם.
and with Abraham, who is the beginning, all ten were recorded.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הָעִיקָּר הוּא הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַבֵּירוּר,
Yet in truth the primary test is the tenth, which is the culmination of clarification,
וְאִם לֹא עָמַד בּוֹ כְּאִלּוּ לֹא עָמַד בְּכֻלָּם (וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נו),
and had he not withstood it, it would be as though he withstood none of them (Bereishit Rabbah 56),
וְזֶה הוּא שֶׁנִּזְכַּר לְבַדּוֹ בְּיִצְחָק.
and this culminating trial alone was recorded regarding Isaac.

p: וּבוֹ, וְכֵן בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ בְּנִסָּיוֹן עֲשִׂירִי דַּעֲקֵידָה,
And in Isaac's trial, as in Abraham's tenth trial of the Binding,
הָיָה לָהֶם מַאֲמַר ה' בְּבֵירוּר שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה כָּךְ,
they received an explicit divine command directing them to act so,
וְהַנִּסָּיוֹן מַה שֶּׁשָּׁמַע לִדְבַר ה'.
the trial consisting of whether they would obey the word of Hashem.
הוּא לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מִטָּתָם שְׁלֵימָה, כִּי יָצָא פְּסֹלֶת וְסִיגִים,
This was because their bed was not completely pure, since dross emerged from them,
וּלְכָךְ אִלְמָלֵא דְּבַר ה' הַמְבוֹרָר
and therefore, were it not for the clear word of Hashem,
לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיַּעַמְדוּ בּוֹ מִצַּד הַפְּסֹלֶת,
it would have been impossible for them to withstand it on account of that dross,
שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַנְּטִיָּה שֶׁבָּהֶם לְצַד אֶחָד.
which was their natural leaning toward one extreme.
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דְּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
However, our father Jacob, whose bed was completely pure,
שֶׁהוּא קַו אֶמְצָעִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ נְטִיָּה
— being the Middle Line that possesses no one-sided bias—
כָּל נִסְיוֹנוֹתָיו הָיוּ בְּהֶעְלֵם;
all of his trials occurred in concealment without direct prophetic command;
וְנִסָּיוֹן הָעֲשִׂירִי שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה בְּלָבָן: "דְּמָה מַשְׂכֻּרְתֶּךָ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, טו),
and his tenth trial was with Laban: 'What shall your wages be?' (Genesis 29:15),
וְאָמַר "בְּרָחֵל וְגוֹמֵר", וְלֹא בִּיקֵּשׁ שְׂכַר מָמוֹן.
and he answered 'For Rachel, etc.', asking for no monetary reward.
הַגַּם דְּאֶצְלוֹ מָמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב מִגּוּפוֹ,
Even though his possessions were more precious to him than his body,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם חָשַׁק יוֹתֵר לְפַרְסֵם אֱמוּנַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
nonetheless he yearned even more to proclaim faith in Hashem
בְּאוּמָּה שְׁלֵימָה מֵחֲלָצָיו.
through an entire righteous nation issuing from his loins.
וְלָכֵן שָׁם קָנָה רְכוּשׁ גַּם כֵּן,
And therefore there he acquired vast wealth as well,
וְאֶצְלוֹ נִזְכַּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת רְכוּשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה,
and with him the active pursuit of wealth is detailed in the Torah,
שֶׁזּוֹ נֶגֶד מִדָּתוֹ "בְּכָל מְאֹדֶךָ".
this corresponding to his attribute of 'with all your might'.

p: וְהוּא אוֹחֵז בַּעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו
And he grasped the heel of Esau
לִקְלוֹט הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁבּוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"נ;
to absorb the holiness latent within him, as mentioned in section 250;
לָבָן נֶגְדּוֹ לְעוֹלָם וִיתֵּר מָמוֹן בִּקְנִיַּת הַבְּכוֹרָה,
Laban stood counter to him, and Jacob gave up money in buying the birthright,
וּבְוַדַּאי הָיָה זֶה אָז אֶצְלָם דָּבָר חָשׁוּב;
and this was certainly considered a matter of great importance among them;
וְכֵן בִּקְנִיַּת הַמְּעָרָה כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה לא),
and so too in the acquisition of the Cave of Machpelah (Shemot Rabbah 31),
וּבַמִּנְחָה שֶׁשָּׁלַח וְלֹא בָּטַח בְּמִלְחֶמֶת גּוּפוֹ לְבַד;
and in the tribute gift he sent to Esau, refusing to rely on bodily combat alone;
כִּי קִנְיַן קְדוּשָּׁה הוּא עַל יְדֵי נְתִינָה לוֹ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר,
for acquiring holiness is achieved through tendering something unto him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בִּקְנִיַּת בְּכוֹרָה.
just as occurred in the purchase of the birthright.
וְכָל עֲבוֹדוֹתָיו דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And all divine services of our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
הָיָה בְּעִנְיַן הַמָּמוֹן וּרְכוּשׁ וּ"בְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ".
centered on wealth, property, and 'with all your might'.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: and so too in the acquisition of the Cave of Machpelah (Shemot Rabbah 31),

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 31:17: “When Isaac died, Jacob and Esau came and divided everything. Jacob said: This wicked man and his sons will enter the Cave of Machpelah and have a share and a dwelling with the righteous buried there. At once he took all the money in his possession, made it into a heap, and said to Esau: My brother, would you prefer your share in this cave, or this silver and gold? … Esau took all that money and gave him his share. This is what Jacob said to Joseph: “In my grave that I dug for myself”—it does not say “purchased” but “dug”: I gave Esau a heap of dinars.”

paragraphs.text: Context: The play on kariti, “I dug,” and keri, “a heap,” explains Jacob’s purchase of Esau’s share in the burial cave. Although possessions were precious to Jacob, he gave them up for this holy acquisition. This is the portion of the long Midrash needed for Rav Tzadok’s argument.

items.h: David and unending repentance

p: וְנִסָּיוֹן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה בְּעִנְיַן הַחֵשֶׁק,
And the trial of King David, peace be upon him, was in the realm of desire,
שֶׁזֶּה מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת בְּתוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק,
which is the attribute of Malchut in the intensity of desire,
וְנִבְנֶה מֵחֶשְׁקוֹת דְּנוּקְבָא: בְּנוֹת לוֹט, וְתָמָר, וְרוּת.
built from the deep desires of the feminine: Lot's daughters, Tamar, and Ruth.
כִּי בְּנוּקְבָא תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מִלּוּי וּשְׂבִיעָה,
For within the feminine resides the intense desire that knows no satiety or exhaustion,
כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ד) עַל פָּסוּק "שְׁאוֹל וְעֹצֶר רָחַם" (מִשְׁלֵי ל, טז).
as our Sages stated (Vayikra Rabbah 4) on 'the grave and the barren womb' (Proverbs 30:16).
וְזֶה הֶבְדֵּל בֵּין מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאַהֲבָה דִּדְכוּרָא,
And this is the distinction between Abraham's attribute in masculine love,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ מִלּוּי,
which has fulfillment and containment,
וּלְכָךְ נִסְיוֹנוֹתָיו הָיוּ בְּהֶעְדֵּר הַדָּבָר שֶׁאוֹהֵב;
and therefore his trials lay in the deprivation of what he loved;
אֲבָל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא בְּחֵשֶׁק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה,
whereas King David embodied desire that has no satiety,
לְכָךְ נִסָּיוֹנוֹ בְּהַזְמָנַת חֵשֶׁק
therefore his trial lay in the sudden presentation of desire,
וְלֹא בְּהֶעְדֵּר הַמִּלּוּי שֶׁלּוֹ כְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
and not in the deprivation of its fulfillment like Abraham.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: For within the feminine resides the intense desire that knows no satiety or exhaustion,

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:115: “The fundamental power of deficiency in the world is called “woman” and “female,” as is known. The essence of deficiency seeks completion; only the power of completion’s hidden root descends into the world, and it seeks to be completed in perfection. This is called desire, the inclination of the human heart that longs for that one measure. Concerning this it says, “Three are never satisfied,” because that measure of the hidden root is expansive, and what is deficient wishes to be completed so that it too will be expansive like that measure. In truth this is impossible, because the nine measures that are existence from nothing are bounded and contracted, and from this comes their existence. Infinite expansion is nothingness, not a distinct existent, for a distinct existent is what is bounded. Nevertheless, it has no satiety, wishing to resemble its cause and source of influence. These are “the grave and the closed womb,” in the sense of “One who loves silver (will not be satisfied with silver).” The Sages of blessed memory expounded this in Leviticus Rabbah: “One who loves mitzvot (will not be satisfied with mitzvot).” It also bears its plain meaning regarding worldly desire, which is the grave.”

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 4:2: “Because the soul knows that all its exertion is for itself, it is never satisfied with mitzvot and good deeds. Rabbi Levi said: It is like a villager married to a king’s daughter: even if he feeds her all the delicacies in the world, he does not discharge his obligation, because she is a king’s daughter. So, whatever a person does for his soul does not discharge his obligation, because it comes from above. Three are ungrateful: the earth, the woman, and the soul. … Concerning the soul: “The soul is also not filled.””

paragraphs.text: Context: The Midrash connects the soul’s inability to be filled with its origin above, and places earth, woman, and soul together in a discussion of insatiability. Rav Tzadok develops the aspect of unending desire and its redirection toward God. The biblical phrase “Sheol and the closed womb” is quoted separately in the following note.

p: וְהוּא לֹא עָמַד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן,
And he did not withstand the trial (Sanhedrin 107a),
כִּי הוּא נֶגֶד מַדְרֵגַת "טוֹב מְאֹד" שֶׁבְּיֵצֶר הָרָע,
because he corresponds to the level of 'very good' within the evil inclination,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט) עָלָיו.
as our Sages expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 9) upon it.
כִּי זֶה דְּחֵשֶׁק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה – זֶהוּ תַּכְלִית תּוֹקֶף הַיֵּצֶר,
For this desire that knows no satiety—is the ultimate zenith of the inclination,
וְהוּא בְּנוּקְבָא שֶׁבָּהּ בְּיִחוּד הִתְגַּבְּרוּת,
and it resides in the feminine wherein it surges uniquely;
וְלֹא הָיָה שְׁלִיטַת הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ אֶלָּא בָּהּ וְלֹא בָּאָדָם, רַק עַל יָדָהּ;
and the serpent's seduction held dominion only over Eve and not over Adam, except through her;
כִּי הִיא הַתְחָלַת הַיֵּצֶר,
for she is the inception of the inclination,
הַיְינוּ מִדָּה זוֹ דְּחֵשֶׁק בְּלֹא שְׂבִיעָה,
namely this attribute of insatiable desire,
וּמִמֶּנָּה הוּא אַחַר כָּךְ הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בָּאָדָם.
and from her it subsequently expanded into man.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 107a:2: “Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: A person should never bring himself into a trial, for David king of Israel brought himself into a trial and failed. He said before Him: Master of the universe, why do they say “God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob,” but not “God of David”? He said: They were tried before Me, but you were not tried before Me. He said: Master of the universe, examine me and try me.”

p: וְהַתְחָלָה זוֹ הוּא גֶּדֶר "טוֹב מְאֹד"
And this inception is defined as 'very good'
כַּאֲשֶׁר מוֹשְׁכוֹ לְעִנְיַן חֶשְׁקוֹת דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
when one channels it toward desires for Hashem, blessed be He,
מַדְרֵגַת: "אוֹהֵב כֶּסֶף לֹא יִשְׂבַּע כֶּסֶף" (מַכּוֹת י.).
on the level of: 'He that loves Torah/silver shall not be satisfied with it' (Ecclesiastes 5:9; Makkot 10a).
וְהַנִּסָּיוֹן הוּא הַבֵּירוּר שֶׁכְּבָר הוּא מְבוֹרָר וּבְתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת,
And a trial serves as clarification that one is already refined and in complete perfection,
וְאִם כֵּן הוּא שְׂבִיעָה שֶׁכְּבָר שָׁלֵם;
and if so, it implies satiety, having achieved completeness;
אֲבָל זֶה אֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה וְהוּא חָסֵר לְעוֹלָם.
yet this desire knows no satiety and remains forever yearning.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:27: ““Am I not devoted?” A devoted person is separated from envy, desire and honor, which take a person out of the world. Corresponding to them are the three things on which the world stands. Torah repairs desire, as in “a tree of life is a desire fulfilled.” Desire—the condition of always wanting more than one has—was principally created for Torah, as the Sages interpreted “one who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver.” When a person places his desire in Torah, he is saved from worldly desires. Rambam writes that desire is found only in a heart empty of Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Dover Tzedek identifies the proper use of a desire that is never satisfied: increasing in Torah. This helps explain why the siman relates endless longing to teshuvah and to never considering oneself complete. The constructive direction is renewed attachment and growth; the cited paragraph does not make committing a transgression a method of acquiring that growth.

p: וּלְכָךְ הוּא הֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ מוֹעֵד קָטָן טז:),
Therefore David established the yoke of repentance (Moed Katan 16b),
כִּי לְהַשִּׂיג בְּכָל פַּעַם יוֹתֵר וְשֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת לְעוֹלָם עַל הַשְּׁלֵימוּת
for to attain ever greater heights each time and never rest in static perfection
הוּא רַק בְּדַרְגָּא דִּתְשׁוּבָה;
belongs solely to the spiritual plane of repentance;
וּלְכָךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲמוֹד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן וּבַבֵּירוּר,
and therefore it was impossible for him to withstand the static trial of completion,
דְּהַיְינוּ הַשְּׂבִיעָה, שֶׁזֶּה נֶגֶד מִדָּתוֹ,
namely satiety, which ran contrary to his intrinsic attribute,
וְאַדְּרַבָּה, מִדָּתוֹ הֶעְדֵּר הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
for on the contrary, his attribute was the perpetual absence of static completion.

And this is the meaning of his plea: 'That You may be justified when You speak' (Psalms 51:6),
כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קז.),
as our Sages of blessed memory explained (Sanhedrin 107a),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא חָטָא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הָרָאוּי נֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
namely that he fell so as not to remain in static perfection before Hashem,
רַק יִהְיֶה תָּמִיד מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק וְעֵינָיו צוֹפִיּוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּעֲזוֹר לוֹ,
but rather be constantly yearning with eyes gazing toward Hashem to help him;
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁזָּכָה בָּהּ.
and this is the attribute of Malchut (Sovereignty) which he merited.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 1: “Judah corresponds to the cupbearer, for David is called the King's entertainer, and David's songs are heard over the wine libation. In Judah's act with Tamar and the similar acts of his tribe, Hashem placed in them such a power of desire that they were unable to overcome it, as the Midrash explains that the angel appointed over desire compelled him. He is therefore not held guilty for what he could not overcome. This is the meaning of the King's entertainer: he allows himself to be overcome by Hashem. As David said, “So that You be justified in Your words”: whom does it befit to be justified, me or You?”

rich.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 1

: “Judah corresponds to the cupbearer, for David is called the King's entertainer, and David's songs are heard over the wine libation. In Judah's act with Tamar and the similar acts of his tribe, Hashem placed in them such a power of desire that they were unable to overcome it, as the Midrash explains that the angel appointed over desire compelled him. He is therefore not held guilty for what he could not overcome. This is the meaning of the King's entertainer: he allows himself to be overcome by Hashem. As David said, “So that You be justified in Your words”: whom does it befit to be justified, me or You?”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach discusses the same words, “so that You be justified,” through the contrast between Yosef and Judah. It first stresses that Yosef was given the power to overcome his desire and was therefore judged with exceptional rigor; only then does it discuss the distinct account of Judah. This provides context for Rav Tzadok's difficult conclusion about David. Both are particular expositions of these figures and their divine clarification, rather than a general instruction to choose sin or dispense with the restraint demanded at the siman's opening.

p: [רנה] בְּדָבָר שֶׁהָאָדָם חָסֵר בּוֹ וְצָרִיךְ תִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי הִתְנַהֲגוּת בַּהֵיפֶךְ,
In a matter where a person is deficient and requires rectification by means of behaving in the opposite extreme,
הוּא אֲפִילּוּ בְּעִנְיָן שֶׁהָיָה אֵצֶל אָדָם אַחֵר מִצְוָה,
this applies even in a situation that would be considered a mitzvah for someone else,
כִּדְשָׁמְעִינַן (סַנְהֶדְרִין כה:) בְּמַלְוֶה בְּרִבִּית
just as we learn (Sanhedrin 25b) regarding one who lends on interest
דַּאֲפִילּוּ לְעַכּוּ״ם לֹא,
that even to a gentile he may not lend on interest,
הֲגַם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִצְוָה דְּ"לַנָּכְרִי תַשִּׁיךְ",
even though there is a mitzvah that "to a foreigner you may lend on interest" (Deuteronomy 23:21),
כָּל שֶׁאֵין עֲבֵירָה בִּמְנִיעָתוֹ צָרִיךְ לִמְנוֹעַ.
as long as there is no active transgression in withholding it, he must withhold.
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם:
And likewise King David, peace be upon him, said:
"חַיֶּיךָ אֲנִי מַתְאִיבְךָ דָּבָר הַמּוּתָּר וְכוּלֵי"
“By your life, I make you long for a permitted thing, etc.”
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי סַנְהֶדְרִין פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ג)
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 2:3)
בְּפִילַגְשִׁים,
regarding concubines,
הֲגַם דְּיֵשׁ מִצְוָה לְהַרְנִין לֵב אַלְמָנָה,
even though there is a mitzvah to cause the widow’s heart to sing for joy,
רַק שֶׁאֵין שִׁעְבּוּד וְלָאו דְּ"עוֹנָתָהּ לֹא יִגְרָע" בְּפִילֶגֶשׁ.
only that there is no formal marital lien and negative prohibition of "her conjugal rights he shall not diminish" with a concubine.
וּתְשׁוּבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הָעֵגֶל,
And the repentance of Israel over the incident of the Golden Calf,
דְּהוּא בַּקָּשַׁת עֲבוֹדָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת בְּלֹא מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְהַרְגָּשַׁת רַב,
which was rooted in a longing for tangible divine service and exertion so as not to remain without Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, and the feeling of a master,
הַתְּשׁוּבָה הָיְתָה בִּנְטִיַּת אֹהֶל מֹשֶׁה חוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה
the repentance was expressed through the pitching of Moses' tent outside the camp
וְיִרְאָה מִגֶּשֶׁת אֵלָיו,
and their trembling fear of approaching him,
שֶׁהָיוּ מוֹנְעִים מֵרְאִיָּתוֹ
wherein they withheld themselves from seeing him,
הֲגַם דְּהוּא מִצְוָה בֶּאֱמֶת.
even though gazing upon one's teacher is truly a great mitzvah.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַקְדָּמַת רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה דְּמָרְדֳּכַי בְּבִגְתָן וָתֶרֶשׁ (בִּמְגִילָּה יג:),
And this explains the matter of anticipating the affliction with the cure through Mordechai regarding Bigthan and Teresh (Megillah 13b),
וּבְוַדַּאי הוּא רְפוּאָה פְּנִימִית לְמַכָּה פְּנִימִית.
and it is certainly an inward spiritual remedy for an inward spiritual wound.

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Human Dispositions 2:2: “What is their cure? A person prone to anger is told to train himself so that even if he is struck and cursed, he takes no notice at all. He should follow this course for a long time, until anger is uprooted from his heart. If he is haughty, he should conduct himself with great self-abasement: sit below everyone, wear worn-out rags that bring their wearer into contempt, and do similar things, until haughtiness is uprooted from him and he returns to the middle way, which is the good way. Once he returns to the middle way, he should follow it all his days. He should proceed along these lines with all the other character traits: if he has gone far toward one extreme, he should move far toward the other extreme and conduct himself that way for a long time, until he returns to the good way, which is the intermediate measure in every character trait.”

rich.text: : “Protective repentance, although he does not cite it from the Gemara, is explained in “This One Selects”: dice players do not play even without stakes; an interest lender does not lend even to a non-Jew; and pigeon racers do not do it even in the wilderness. See there.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin names the precise category used here: teshuvat ha-geder, repentance through a protective boundary, with the same examples of gambling and lending. This explains why the siman distinguishes this person from someone else for whom the act could be a mitzvah. Its explicit condition remains essential: the proposed abstention must not itself involve a transgression. The note concerns the extra boundary needed for repair, rather than a general cancellation of obligations.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 25b:5-6: “The rule concerning a lender at interest applies to both the lender and the borrower. When is their repentance recognized? When they tear up their loan documents and make a complete withdrawal from this practice, so that they no longer lend at interest even to a gentile. Those who fly pigeons are those who incite pigeons to fight one another. This was said not only of pigeons, but even of domesticated animals, wild animals, and birds. When is their repentance recognized? When they break the boards with which they urge the animals on and make a complete withdrawal from this practice, so that they do not do it even in the wilderness.”

paragraphs.text: Recognizing providence in Mordechai's rescue
A second account of the same rescue emphasizes recognition within concealment.

rich.text: A second account of the same rescue emphasizes recognition within concealment.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 5:2: “This is the reason for Mordechai's intention in rescuing him from Bigtan and Teresh (Esther 2:21–23). Even during this intense darkness of slumber he understood ‘all that had happened’ (4:1), the purpose of it all, and knew the matter through the holy spirit. He apprehended that Esther's root was the root of the congregation of Israel, and that her being seized by Achashverosh was no accident. It would have seemed more fitting to rescue her and seek Achashverosh's death. He did not do so because he understood that everything was truly under Hashem's providence.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Likkutei Maamarim asks the same question: why rescue Achashverosh when Esther needed deliverance? Here the answer emphasizes Mordechai's recognition that her situation belonged to divine providence even during concealment. This adds another aspect to the siman's analysis of correcting a personal motive; the two explanations are not presented as identical.

p: וּבֶאֱמֶת תָּמוּהַּ,
And in truth it is astounding:
לָמָּה גִּילָּה מָרְדֳּכַי?
why did Mordechai reveal the assassination plot?
וַהֲלֹא טוֹב יוֹתֵר שֶׁיֵּהָרֵג אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
Would it not have been far better had Ahasuerus been killed,
וְתִנָּצֵל אֶסְתֵּר מִבִּיאַת אִיסּוּר?
and Esther thereby rescued from forbidden relations?
הֲגַם דְּקַרְקַע עוֹלָם הִיא וְלֵיכָּא אִיסּוּר,
Even though she was merely passive (“earth of the world”) and committed no personal transgression,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם וַדַּאי מִצְוָה לְהַצִּילָהּ,
nonetheless it is certainly a mitzvah to rescue her,
וְעַכּוּ״ם לֹא מַעֲלִין וְלֹא מוֹרִידִין
and idolaters are neither brought up nor cast down into danger,
וְאֵין לְהַעֲלוֹתוֹ וּלְהַצִּילוֹ כְּלָל.
such that one ought not lift him up and save his life at all.
רַק שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי דִּקְלִיפַּת פָּרַס הוּא צָרוּת עַיִן,
Rather, it is because I heard that the spiritual shell (kelipah) of Persia is a begrudging, narrow eye,
וְדִלְכָכָן תִּקְּנוּ מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת בְּפוּרִים
and for this reason the Sages instituted the sending of portions on Purim,
שֶׁהוּא הַהֵיפוּךְ דְּצָרוּת עַיִן.
which is the absolute antithesis of a begrudging eye.
וְכֵן נִרְאֶה מִמַּה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כד.):
And so it appears from what is stated in Sanhedrin (24a):
"עֵילָם זָכְתָה לִלְמוֹד וְלֹא לְלַמֵּד".
“Elam (Persia) merited to learn, but not to teach.”
פֵּירוּשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "לִלְמוֹד וּלְלַמֵּד",
The explanation is as I heard concerning “to learn and to teach,”
דְּאֵיךְ מְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רַב?
how can a person pray to become a master over others?
רַק רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ טוֹבַת עַיִן
Rather, it means to say: that he should possess a generous, good eye
שֶׁאַחֵר יֵדַע גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁהוּא יוֹדֵעַ וְיִהְיֶה כְּמוֹתוֹ.
so that another will also know what he knows and become like him.
וְעֵילָם לֹא זָכָה לְלַמֵּד,
And Elam did not merit to teach,
שֶׁלֹּא זָכוּ לְטוֹבַת עַיִן כָּזֶה
because they did not merit such a generous eye
מִצַּד תּוֹקֶף הַצָּרוּת עַיִן שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵט בַּאֲוִיר אוֹתָהּ אוּמָּה
on account of the intense begrudging narrowness of eye that rules the spiritual atmosphere of that nation,
שֶׁנִּכְנַס גַּם לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁתַּחַת מֶמְשַׁלְתָּם,
which seeped even into the children of Israel dwelling under their dominion,
כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"ה.
as mentioned above in section 205.
