paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Megillah 7a:1: “Rabbi Yosef taught: “Sending portions, one to another”—two gifts to one person; “and gifts to the poor”—two gifts to two people. The distinction between sending portions and gifts to the poor is this. The Men of the Great Assembly established these two enactments after the miracle because Shushan the capital was in the province of Elam. Elam merited learning but did not merit teaching, as stated in Pesaḥim 87a: “We have a little sister, and she has no breasts”—this is Elam, which merited learning but not teaching, and so forth. This is because the root of the Persian kingdom and that nation’s character is narrowness of spirit, as explained in its place; therefore it did not merit teaching. But when the Men of the Great Assembly investigated where the decree had arisen at its root and recognized that it arose from narrowness of spirit, immediately upon their discovering the truth, salvation came and the decree was annulled. They therefore afterward instituted these two mitzvot, whose root is generosity. The mitzvah was divided in two. “Sending portions, one to another” means to righteous and upright people: two gifts, meaning that one should expand in generosity to give with both hands. For the poor and needy, however, one must give to anyone who extends a hand; the group includes people of different levels. Here one gift signifies the obligation, without that expansive giving. This also explains what is taught in Peah 4:1: even if ninety-nine say to distribute and one says to let them gather for themselves, one listens to the one who speaks according to the law. Since among the poor there are also those unworthy to receive directly from one’s hand, the mitzvah is to leave it for them to gather. The Men of the Great Assembly thus enacted this because they understood that the decree had grown from the beginning of narrowness of spirit. They recognized this, and immediately when it became clear to them the decree was annulled; afterward they established this enactment. Likewise, the root of the growth of evil decrees—may they not come upon Israel—is only the deficiency present in their hearts at that time. If we can reach its root, it can be annulled immediately, as it was in the days of the Men of the Great Assembly.”

paragraphs.text: Teaching as generosity of eye
The wish to teach is a wish that Torah's light reach another person.

rich.text: The wish to teach is a wish that Torah's light reach another person.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The Night of Shabbat Chol HaMoed Pesach 16:1: ““Your name is oil poured out”: words of Torah are always greatly generous and seek to give themselves to Israel's pure heart, as in “wine and milk without price.” This is the opposite of the other side, which is extremely narrow of eye. Though it too is called “free,” as the Zohar interprets the fish eaten in Egypt without blessing or the higher yoke, its wish to hide the light and leave creation in darkness is the greatest narrowness of eye. Torah, however, continually shines its light with great generosity.”

: ““Your name is oil poured out”: words of Torah are always greatly generous and seek to give themselves to Israel's pure heart, as in “wine and milk without price.” This is the opposite of the other side, which is extremely narrow of eye. Though it too is called “free,” as the Zohar interprets the fish eaten in Egypt without blessing or the higher yoke, its wish to hide the light and leave creation in darkness is the greatest narrowness of eye. Torah, however, continually shines its light with great generosity.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim distinguishes giving light from withholding it, even when both may outwardly be called “free.” This illuminates the siman's explanation of the request “to learn and teach”: the desired good is that another receive what one knows and be able to stand equally. It is this generosity, rather than the pursuit of the status of a teacher, that reverses narrowness of eye.

p: וְאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין (ד:): "אֵין הַסָּתָה בְּלֹא אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה",
And they stated in Chullin (4b): “There is no enticement without eating and drinking,”
וְזֶה טַעַם מִשְׁתֵּה אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ,
and this is the reason for the feast of Ahasuerus,
שֶׁהוּא הַסָּתָה לִהְיוֹת נִכְנָעִים תַּחְתָּיו.
that it was an enticement to make them submissive under him.
וְהַכְּנִיעוּת הוּא קַבָּלַת אַדְנוּתוֹ וּמֶמְשַׁלְתּוֹ,
And submissiveness entails accepting his mastery and sovereignty,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה מְקַבֵּל כֹּחוֹ עָלָיו
and through this one absorbs his spiritual force upon oneself
[וְכִדְשָׁמְעִינַן בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ח.):
[and as we learn in Avodah Zarah (8a):
"יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּטָהֳרָה עַל יְדֵי הַסְּעוּדָה"],
“Israel outside the Land of Israel serve idols in purity on account of the feast”].
וְתוֹקֶף כֹּחַ הָאוּמָּה בְּיוֹתֵר הוּא בַּמֶּלֶךְ,
And the apex of the nation’s force resides specifically within its king,
וְהַמְּקוֹרָבִים קוֹלְטִים כֹּחוֹ.
and those closest to him absorb his force.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יב סוֹף עַמּוּד א):
And our Sages of blessed memory taught (Megillah 12a end):
"כִּרְצוֹן אִישׁ וָאִישׁ – מָרְדֳּכַי וְהָמָן",
“According to the pleasure of every man—this refers to Mordechai and Haman,”
שֶׁהָיוּ שָׂרֵי מַשְׁקִים בַּסְּעוּדָה,
who served as chief cupbearers at the feast,
וַדַּאי קָלְטוּ מֵהַסָּתָה זוֹ בְּיוֹתֵר.
and they certainly absorbed the greatest impact of this enticement.
וְלָכֵן פְּתִיחַת הַמְּגִילָּה בַּסְּעוּדָה
Therefore the Megillah opens with the banquet,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה צְמִיחַת הַגְּזֵירָה
for out of this sprouted the decree of destruction,
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם): "שֶׁנֶּהֱנוּ וְכוּלֵי",
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (ibid.): “because they derived pleasure, etc.”
הֲגַם דְּמַסִּיק דְּהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַצֶּלֶם,
Even though the Gemara concludes that they had also bowed down to the image in Nebuchadnezzar's days,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֲרֵי לֹא נֶעֶנְשׁוּ אָז תֵּיכֶף,
nonetheless they were not punished immediately back then;
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם עָשׂוּ לִפְנִים,
perforce it is because in truth they acted only outwardly,
וַה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב אֵין חֵטְא,
and Hashem Who looks into the heart saw no actual sin,
רַק מִצִּידָּם דְּ"אָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם".
except from their mortal vantage where “man looks upon the eyes.”
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְנַהֲגִים בְּטוֹבַת עַיִן,
Only when they conduct themselves with a generous, good eye,
גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ טוֹבַת עַיִן כְּנֶגְדָּם
does Hashem, blessed be He, likewise have a generous eye toward them
לְהַשְׁפִּיעָם כְּמִדָּתוֹ דְּ"יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב".
to bestow upon them according to His divine measure of “looking into the heart.”
אֲבָל מִצַּד נֶהֱנוּ וְכוּלֵי,
However, from the standpoint of having derived illicit pleasure, etc.,
דְּהַיְינוּ הַסָּתַת כֹּחַ צָרוּת עַיִן,
which was the enticing power of the begrudging, narrow eye,
גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר: שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלִּי וְשֶׁלְּךָ שֶׁלְּךָ,
Hashem, blessed be He, likewise reacted with: “Mine is Mine and yours is yours,”
לִרְאוֹת לַעֵינַיִם.
judging them strictly according to external appearances.

p: וְעַל זֶה הָעוֹנֶשׁ בְּהָמָן גַּם כֵּן
And upon this the punishment manifested in Haman as well
עַל יְדֵי צָרוּת עֵינוֹ בְּמָרְדֳּכַי
through his narrow, begrudging eye toward Mordechai
שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהִשְׁתַּחֲווֹת לוֹ.
demanding that Mordechai bow down to him.
וְכֵן מָרְדֳּכַי דְּאִיקְנֵי בְּהָמָן
And so too Mordechai, who became jealous of Haman,
גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד צָרוּת עַיִן
was affected also from the trace of a narrow eye,
שֶׁזֶּה שֶׁהָיָה עַבְדּוֹ יַעֲלֶה כָּל כָּךְ.
that this one who was once his slave should rise so high.
הֲגַם דְּהָיָה גָּנוּז בָּזֶה צַד טוֹב גַּם כֵּן,
Even though there was concealed within it a holy motive as well,
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֶסְתֵּר, הוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת סַנְהֶדְרִין סא:)
as our Sages taught (Esther Rabbah, cited in Tosafot Sanhedrin 61b)
דְּצֶלֶם חָקוּק עַל לִבּוֹ
that an idolatrous image was engraved upon Haman’s heart
וְתִיקֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה שׁוֹרֶשׁ חֵטְא דְּהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַצֶּלֶם,
and through his refusal Mordechai rectified the root sin of their bowing to the image in Babylon,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ בּוֹ צָרוּת עַיִן.
nonetheless there was an element of narrowness of eye in it.
רַק בֶּאֱמֶת מָרְדֳּכַי כְּבָר הִרְגִּישׁ בַּדָּבָר וְרָצָה לְתַקֵּן.
Except that in truth Mordechai already sensed this nuance and desired to rectify it.
וְזֶהוּ הַקְדָּמַת רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה,
And this was the anticipation of the cure before the affliction,
שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ צָרַת עַיִן נֶגֶד אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ שֶׁלָּקַח אִשְׁתּוֹ
for he suspected that he harbored a begrudging eye toward Ahasuerus for taking his wife,
וְלֹא מִפְּנֵי הָאִיסּוּר הוּא רוֹצֶה בְּמִיתָתוֹ
and that it was not purely because of the prohibition that he desired the king's death,
רַק מִפְּנֵי צָרוּת עַיִן.
rather out of a begrudging eye.
וְהֲגַם דְּהָיָה מִצְוָה בְּמִיתָתוֹ,
And even though there would have been a mitzvah in Ahasuerus' death,
הוּא לְתַקֵּן הַצָּרוּת עַיִן,
he, in order to rectify that narrow eye,
אַדְּרַבָּה, נִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּהַצָּלָתוֹ
on the contrary, exerted himself to save his life,
לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ צָרוּת עַיִן נֶגְדּוֹ,
to prove that he harbored no begrudging eye toward him,
הֲגַם שֶׁהוּא גּוֹי וְרָשָׁע.
even though he was a gentile and a wicked person.
וּמִמֵּילָא הַצָּרוּת עַיִן שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ עַל הָמָן
Consequently, the fierce opposition he held afterward toward Haman
הוּא מִצַּד רִשְׁעוֹ וְכַהוֹגֶן,
was purely because of Haman's wickedness and completely righteous;
וְזֶהוּ הַקְדָּמַת רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה.
and this was the secret of anticipating the cure before the affliction.

sections.en: The Holy Spark Within Every Nation

p: [רנו] כָּל אוּמָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ רַע מְיוּחָד, כָּךְ יֵשׁ לָהּ גַּם כֵּן אֵיזֶה נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ מְיוּחָד שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה חַיּוּתָהּ,
Every nation, just as it possesses a particular evil, likewise possesses a specific holy spark from which its vitality derives,
כְּטַעַם "וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם", דִּלְוּלֵי כֵן כְּלֹא הָיָה.
mirroring the verse "And You give life to them all" (Nehemiah 9:6), for were it not so, it would be as nothing.
וְחַיּוּת דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וַדַּאי הוּא דָּבָר טוֹב,
And vitality from Hashem, blessed be He, is certainly something good,
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַגָּלוּת – לִקְלוֹט אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר טוֹב לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
and it is for this that exile exists—to absorb that good element into Israel.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר תְּרוּמָה (קנב עַמּוּד ב)
And as written in Zohar Terumah (152b)
דִּבְגָלוּת הַשֶּׁפַע הוֹלֵךְ לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְיִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹלְטִין תַּמְצִית.
that in exile the divine abundance flows to the nations of the world and Israel absorbs the distilled essence.
וּבְוַדַּאי הַשֶּׁפַע מֵאֵת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוֹלֵךְ לְמִינוֹ וּלְדָבָר טוֹב שֶׁנִּמְצָא בָּם,
And certainly the abundance from Hashem, blessed be He, is drawn to its own kind and toward the good element found within them,
וּמִצַּד זֶה הוּא הַשֶּׁפַע לָהֶם.
and from this aspect comes the abundance unto them.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל קוֹלְטִים הַתַּמְצִית, נִתְמַצֶּה לְתוֹכָם אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר טוֹב.
And when Israel absorbs the distilled essence, that good element is extracted and internalized within them.

paragraphs.text:
Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 2:1-7: “Here is the answer to the heretics, and the exposure of the root of the error of those who deny individual providence and the signs and wonders of the Torah. In their false imagination they mistakenly compare Hashem’s work—‘the Maker of heaven and earth’—to human work and craftsmanship. Once a vessel has left the craftsman’s hands, it no longer needs him: even when his hands have withdrawn from it and he goes away to the market, the vessel remains in precisely the form and shape it had when it left his hands. These foolish people imagine the making of heaven and earth in the same way.

But ‘their eyes are shut against seeing’ the great difference between human work and craftsmanship, which make something from something already existing—merely changing its form and shape from a piece of silver into a vessel—and the making of heaven and earth, which brings something into being from nothing.

This is a greater wonder than, for example, the splitting of the Red Sea. ‘Hashem drove the sea back with a strong east wind all that night, and the waters were divided’; they ‘stood like a heap’ and like a wall. Had Hashem stopped the wind for a moment, the water would have returned and flowed downward in its usual, natural way, and would certainly not have remained standing like a wall. This is so even though this nature of water was itself created and brought into being from nothing: a stone wall stands by itself without wind, but the nature of water is different.

All the more so with creation from nothing, which transcends nature and is an even greater wonder than the splitting of the Red Sea. If the Creator’s power were to withdraw from the created being, Heaven forbid, the created being would return to actual nothingness and nonexistence. Rather, the power of the maker must remain continually within what is made, giving it life and sustaining it. These are the letters of speech of the ten utterances through which the created beings were made.

Of this it is said, ‘You give life to them all.’ Read not merely ‘give life’ but ‘bring into being’—that is, bring something into being from nothing. ‘You’—atah—signifies the letters from alef to tav, while the hei signifies the five organs of speech, the source of the letters. These are the letters of speech of the ten utterances through which the created beings were made.

Although He has no bodily likeness, Scripture states explicitly, ‘Hashem spoke’ and ‘Hashem said.’ This is the revelation of the twenty-two supernal letters to the prophets. They are clothed in the prophets’ intellect and comprehension in the prophetic vision, and also in their thought and speech, as it is written: ‘The spirit of Hashem spoke through me, and His word was upon my tongue,’ and as the Ari, of blessed memory, explained in the Gate of Prophecy.

The letters are similarly clothed in created beings, as it is written: ‘By the word of Hashem the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.’ This, however, takes place through numerous and immense stages of descent, until the letters descend into physical action. By contrast, the prophets’ apprehension is in Atzilut as it is clothed in the World of Beriah.”

rich.text: Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 2:1-7

: “Here is the answer to the heretics, and the exposure of the root of the error of those who deny individual providence and the signs and wonders of the Torah. In their false imagination they mistakenly compare Hashem’s work—‘the Maker of heaven and earth’—to human work and craftsmanship. Once a vessel has left the craftsman’s hands, it no longer needs him: even when his hands have withdrawn from it and he goes away to the market, the vessel remains in precisely the form and shape it had when it left his hands. These foolish people imagine the making of heaven and earth in the same way.

But ‘their eyes are shut against seeing’ the great difference between human work and craftsmanship, which make something from something already existing—merely changing its form and shape from a piece of silver into a vessel—and the making of heaven and earth, which brings something into being from nothing.

This is a greater wonder than, for example, the splitting of the Red Sea. ‘Hashem drove the sea back with a strong east wind all that night, and the waters were divided’; they ‘stood like a heap’ and like a wall. Had Hashem stopped the wind for a moment, the water would have returned and flowed downward in its usual, natural way, and would certainly not have remained standing like a wall. This is so even though this nature of water was itself created and brought into being from nothing: a stone wall stands by itself without wind, but the nature of water is different.

All the more so with creation from nothing, which transcends nature and is an even greater wonder than the splitting of the Red Sea. If the Creator’s power were to withdraw from the created being, Heaven forbid, the created being would return to actual nothingness and nonexistence. Rather, the power of the maker must remain continually within what is made, giving it life and sustaining it. These are the letters of speech of the ten utterances through which the created beings were made.

Of this it is said, ‘You give life to them all.’ Read not merely ‘give life’ but ‘bring into being’—that is, bring something into being from nothing. ‘You’—atah—signifies the letters from alef to tav, while the hei signifies the five organs of speech, the source of the letters. These are the letters of speech of the ten utterances through which the created beings were made.

Although He has no bodily likeness, Scripture states explicitly, ‘Hashem spoke’ and ‘Hashem said.’ This is the revelation of the twenty-two supernal letters to the prophets. They are clothed in the prophets’ intellect and comprehension in the prophetic vision, and also in their thought and speech, as it is written: ‘The spirit of Hashem spoke through me, and His word was upon my tongue,’ and as the Ari, of blessed memory, explained in the Gate of Prophecy.

The letters are similarly clothed in created beings, as it is written: ‘By the word of Hashem the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.’ This, however, takes place through numerous and immense stages of descent, until the letters descend into physical action. By contrast, the prophets’ apprehension is in Atzilut as it is clothed in the World of Beriah.”

p: וְזֶה טַעַם לְקִיחַת אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ לְאֶסְתֵּר,
And this is the reason for Ahasuerus' taking of Esther,
שֶׁהָיְתָה צַדֶּקֶת גְּמוּרָה וּבַעֲלַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יד:),
who was completely righteous and possessed the Holy Spirit, as our Sages taught (Megillah 14b),
אֵיךְ נִפְגְּמָה פְּגָם גָּדוֹל כָּזֶה.
how she could be subjected to such a severe blemish.
וְהִיא רוֹמֶזֶת לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנּוֹדָע,
And she alludes to the Congregation of Israel, as is known,
וְאָז בַּגָּלוּת הַשֶּׁפַע יוֹרֵד לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל דֶּרֶךְ אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
and then in exile the divine influx descends to the Congregation of Israel through the nations of the world.
וְאָז לְצוֹרֶךְ בִּנְיַן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי שֶׁהָיָה הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַנְּבוּאָה,
And at that time, for the purpose of the construction of the Second Temple where prophecy departed,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּפִרְקֵי הֵיכָלוֹת (פֶּרֶק כז וּפֶרֶק כט)
yet it is nonetheless explicit in Pirkei Heikhalot (chapters 27 and 29)
כִּי עִיקַּר רָזֵי תּוֹרָה לֹא נִגְלָה אֶלָּא בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי,
that the primary secrets of the Torah were revealed only in the Second Temple era,
וְכַנּוֹדָע דְּאָז יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה מֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה.
and as is known, that was the founding of the Oral Torah by the Men of the Great Assembly.
וּבֶאֱמֶת "חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא",
And in truth, "a sage is superior to a prophet" (Bava Batra 12a);
עַיֵּין בָּרַמְבַּ״ן פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יב.) הַטַּעַם, דְּנוֹבֵעַ מִמָּקוֹם יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל,
see the Ramban in the first chapter of Bava Batra (12a) for the reason: that it flows from an even greater source,
וּבַזֹּהַר שְׁמוֹת (ו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) כִּי הוּא תְּמִידִי.
and in Zohar Shemot (6b end): because it is continuous.
רַק דְּהַנְּבוּאָה הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת מַאֲמַר ה' בְּבֵירוּר,
Except that prophecy is the manifest revelation of Hashem's word in clear perception,
וְהַשָּׂגָה דְּחָכְמָה הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם.
whereas the apprehension of wisdom is in concealment.

items.h: Modesty, Esther, and the Second Temple

p: וְזֶה טַעַם בִּנְיַן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי עַל יְדֵי מַלְכֵי פָּרַס,
And this explains the building of the Second Temple through the kings of Persia,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ח:): "בְּשַׁבָּת הַפַּרְסִיִּים צְנוּעִים וְכוּלֵי",
as stated in Berakhot (8b): "on Shabbat the Persians are modest, etc.,"
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם – מִדַּת הַצְּנִיעוּת;
for this was their holy spark—the attribute of modesty;
רַק דְּמַיְיתֵי עֲלָהּ תֵּיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ: "אֵלּוּ פַּרְסִיִּים הַמְקוּדָּשִׁים לְגֵיהִנָּם",
only that the Gemara immediately brings following this: "These Persians who are designated for Gehenna" (Berakhot 8b),
דְּאָסוּר לְסַפֵּר בְּשֶׁבַח עַכּוּ״ם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ.).
since it is forbidden to recount the praise of idolaters (as stated in Avodah Zarah 20a).
וּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם מַעֲלָתָם הִיא הַמְּבִיאָתַם לְגֵיהִנָּם,
And in truth, their very virtue is what brings them to Gehenna,
כִּי צְנִיעוּתָם הוּא כְּדֵי לְמַלֹּאות תַּאֲוָתָם בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת,
for their modesty is practiced in order to indulge their base desires with even greater intensity,
[וְגַם מִצַּד עַיִן הָרָע דִּצְרֵי עַיִן שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רנ"ה].
[and also on account of the evil eye of the begrudging narrow eye which they possessed, as mentioned above in section 255].
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ כֹּחוֹ יוֹתֵר שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָאוּמָּה (מְגִילָּה יג.):
And likewise they said concerning Ahasuerus—for a king's power is greatest, embodying the entire nation (Megillah 13a):
"מִגְּנוּתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע אַתָּה לָמֵד שִׁבְחוֹ וְכוּלֵי",
“From the disparagement of that wicked one you learn his praise, etc.,”
גַּם כֵּן בִּצְנִיעוּת,
also regarding modesty,
רַק שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִגְּנוּתוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דְּכַוָּנָתוֹ הַכֹּל לִגְנוּת.
except that in truth this is to his disparagement as noted above, for his entire intent was disgraceful.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לְגַבֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא טוֹב,
Nevertheless, in relation to Israel it yielded good,
וְזָכְתָה אֶסְתֵּר, כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם עַמּוּד ב): "בִּשְׂכַר צְנִיעוּת שֶׁהָיְתָה וְכוּלֵי",
and Esther merited, as our Sages taught (ibid. 13b): “In reward for the modesty that she maintained, etc.,”
וְהִיא קָלְטָה מִדַּת הַצְּנִיעוּת הַטּוֹבָה "הַצְנֵעַ לֶכֶת עִם אֱלֹהֶיךָ",
and she absorbed the holy attribute of modesty, "to walk humbly with your God" (Micah 6:8),
שֶׁגַּם הִיא מִמִּדָּה זוֹ – לִהְיוֹת בְּהֶעְלֵם וְלֹא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת.
which likewise stems from this trait—to abide in concealment and not in overt revelation.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 21:3: “This is also the hint in what is said in Berakhot 8b: “In three matters I love the Persians: they are modest in their eating, modest in the privy, and modest in another matter.” For this is the root of modesty. Yet close to it the Sages said, “‘I have commanded My consecrated ones’—these are the Persians, who are consecrated and prepared for Gehinnom.” Among Israel, this matter is holiness—restraining oneself in modesty—whereas among them it is only the outward appearance, and they are consecrated for Gehinnom. This was explained in discourse 14.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah places the praise of Persian modesty beside its criticism and distinguishes the outward form from its inward purpose. This clarifies the precise extraction described in the present siman: Esther receives the holy quality of concealed service, rather than adopting the intention in which that quality had been clothed. The siman’s later discussion of her concealed holiness depends on this distinction between the appearance of an act and the direction of the heart within it.

p: וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְלוֹט רַק מִצַּד אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וּמִכֹּחָם,
And it is impossible to absorb this except from the nations and through their power,
כִּי מִצַּד שֶׁיֵּשׁ רַע צָרִיךְ צְנִיעוּת,
because due to the presence of evil, modesty becomes necessary,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן אַחַר הַחֵטְא "נֶחְבָּאוּ",
as written concerning Adam the First who after the sin hid themselves (Genesis 3:8),
וּכְמַאֲמַר זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא לא) בְּלוּחוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת:
and as our Sages stated (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 31) regarding the second Tablets:
"אֵין לְךָ יָפֶה מִן הַצְּנִיעוּת", וְהַיְינוּ אַחַר הַחֵטְא.
“There is nothing more beautiful than modesty,” meaning specifically after the sin.
וְכֵן הָיָה בַּיִת שֵׁנִי נֶגֶד בַּיִת רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהָיָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת.
And so was the Second Temple in comparison to the First Temple which operated in open revelation.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הִיא קָלְטָה מִדַּת הַצְּנִיעוּת שֶׁבּוֹ, שֶׁהוּא כְּלָלוּת הָאוּמָּה,
And when she absorbed the trait of modesty within him, he being the embodiment of the entire nation,
אָז הָיָה יְשׁוּעָה בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת,
then salvation broke forth in overt manifestation,
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יא.):
as our Sages expounded (Megillah 11a):
"אֵימָתַי רָאוּ כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר? בִּימֵי מָרְדֳּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר".
“When did all the ends of the earth see, etc.? In the days of Mordechai and Esther.”
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דִּ"מְגִילָּה" – לְשׁוֹן הִתְגַּלּוּת,
And I heard that "Megillah" is an expression of revelation (hitgalut),
כִּי אָז נִתְגַּלָּה כִּי דֶּרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע גַּם כֵּן הוּא הַנְהָגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
for then it was revealed that the course of nature is likewise the sovereign guidance of Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּי אָז הָיָה יְשׁוּעָה בְּדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע וְנִגְלָה לַכֹּל דְּהוּא מִפְּעוּלוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
because salvation unfolded naturally and it became manifest to all that it was wrought by Hashem's actions.
וְזֶה רְאִיַּת כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ.
And this was the seeing of all the ends of the earth.
וִישׁוּעָה בְּדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע הַיְינוּ צְנִיעוּת וְהַלְבָּשָׁה, וְלֹא בְּנֵס מְגוּלֶּה.
And salvation through natural means embodies modesty and enclothement, rather than an overt miracle.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם זֶהוּ בֶּאֱמֶת הִתְגַּלּוּת יוֹתֵר גַּם לְאַפְסֵי אָרֶץ,
Nevertheless, this is in truth a greater revelation even to the ends of the earth,
דְּהַכָּרָה שֶׁגַּם דֶּרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַכָּרָה מְגוּלָּה יוֹתֵר.
for the realization that nature itself originates from Hashem is an even more profound disclosure.
וְכֵן חָכְמָה, הֲגַם דְּהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם, הוּא הַשָּׂגָה גְּדוֹלָה מִנְּבוּאָה.
Likewise wisdom, even though it operates in concealment, is a greater perception than prophecy.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Megillah 11a:1: “Rabbi Yochanan opened his exposition of this passage with “He remembered His kindness,” and “All the ends of the earth have seen.” When did all the ends of the earth see the salvation of our God? In the days of Mordechai and Esther. It is written, “You are the God who works wonders; You made Your might known among the peoples.” All the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel—such as the exodus from Egypt, the splitting of the sea, and all the wars that departed from the natural order—are called wonders. The language of seeing does not apply to them, because after the miracle the world remains as it was before. The language of hearing applies: what remains is the report heard by the ears that a wonder occurred in the world at that time. But in the miracle of Mordechai and Esther, the Holy One, blessed be He, showed that even all the natural processes operating in the world serve Israel’s good. This miracle appeared to follow the natural order, through his taking Esther, and the events involving Mordechai likewise appeared natural. Here the language of seeing applies, for this can be recognized by the eye at every time and moment.”

paragraphs.text:
Gevurot Hashem, Introduction to Gevurot Hashem 4-6: “There is a difference between wisdom and prophecy. The sage apprehends through his intellect, and because he apprehends through his intellect, he can apprehend the most hidden and concealed things. The prophet, however, is called a ‘visionary’ or a ‘seer’: seeing applies when someone sees a thing from outside. Every prophet must therefore have a connection to the matter concerning which he prophesies. He connects himself to those things and knows them through his prophecy.

The Sages therefore said, ‘A sage is greater than a prophet.’ The explanation is that prophecy resembles the sense of sight, which perceives its object from outside. Although prophecy does not come through the perception of a physical sense, nevertheless, just as a sense connects with its object, so the prophet’s power of prophecy—the imaginative faculty, or whatever faculty receives prophecy—connects with the thing about which he prophesies. For this reason the sage is greater: he apprehends and knows hidden matters and brings them forth from his own intellect. Because of this difference, the prophet is called a ‘visionary’ or a ‘seer,’ whereas the sage is not. It is therefore impossible for the matter of the World to Come and the soul’s continued existence to enter prophecy at all, since ‘seeing’ or ‘vision’ does not apply to them. This matter is separate from the human being; because it is completely separate from him, prophecy does not apply to it. We have already explained that prophecy requires an external connection with that about which one prophesies. The World to Come and the soul’s continued existence are therefore explained more fully through wisdom—for the sage apprehends hidden matters—than through prophecy. Thus ‘a sage is greater than a prophet,’ because he can apprehend something that cannot be apprehended through prophecy. The power of prophecy resembles the sense of sight, which receives its objects from outside. How, then, could the matter of the World to Come be written in the Torah, when it does not belong to the domain of prophecy? Anyone who knows the distinction between the sage and the prophet knows that this is impossible, for the prophets connected themselves with the things about which they prophesied.

The Sages therefore said: ‘All the prophets prophesied only concerning the days of the Messiah; but concerning the World to Come, “No eye has seen, O God, except You.”’ The explanation is that since prophecy requires seeing—an external connection with what is known through prophecy—the prophets could prophesy only concerning the days of the Messiah. The matter of the Messiah belongs to this world and is not completely separate from the human being, for it is in this world. But there is no prophecy concerning the World to Come, which is separate from this world, for no eye has seen it. The prophet prophesies only through seeing, as has been explained.”

items.h: Concealment and revelation in the Purim story

p: רַק עֵילָם זָכְתָה לִלְמוֹד וְלֹא לְלַמֵּד (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פְּסָחִים פז.),
Only that Elam merited to learn and not to teach (as stated in Pesachim 87a),
שֶׁהָיוּ בְּתַכְלִית הַצְּנִיעוּת הַמְצוּמְצֶמֶת בְּיוֹתֵר
because they held to the extreme of severely restricted modesty,
עַד שֶׁגַּם לְגַלּוֹת חָכְמָתָם לַאֲחֵרִים לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר, רַק לְעַצְמָם.
such that even revealing their wisdom to others was impossible, keeping it only to themselves.
וּמִצַּד זֶה הַתְחָלַת הַגְּזֵירָה עַל הִשְׁתַּחֲוָוֹת לַצֶּלֶם,
And from this root arose the initial decree on account of bowing down to the image,
הֲגַם דְּהֵם לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים וּבְהַצְנֵעַ עָבְדוּ ה' בְּכָל לְבָבָם,
for even though they acted outwardly for appearance only and served Hashem in privacy with all their heart,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם זֶה הָיָה בְּתַכְלִית הַהֶעְלֵם.
nonetheless it was sunken in ultimate concealment.
וְעַל זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר הָמָן,
And upon this Haman was stirred,
כִּי עֲמָלֵק הֵיפוּךְ הַצְּנִיעוּת, דְּלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים".
for Amalek is the antithesis of modesty, which is why it is said of him: "and he feared not God" (Deuteronomy 25:18).
כִּי מִצַּד הַיִּרְאָה הוּא הַצְּנִיעוּת,
For modesty stems from awe,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּנְדָרִים (כ.) דְּיִרְאָה הוּא בּוּשָׁה,
and as stated in Nedarim (20a) that awe is shame,
וְהַצְּנִיעוּת מִצַּד הַבּוּשָׁה,
and modesty derives from shame,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא "וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ".
as written concerning Adam the First before the sin: "and they were not ashamed" (Genesis 2:25).
וְהוּא "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם" שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה בְּתִיקּוּן חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
And Amalek is "the first of nations" who refuses the rectification of the sin of Adam the First,
רַק לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַחֵטְא כְּקוֹדֶם – בְּלֹא בּוּשָׁה.
desiring merely to remain after the sin as before—brazenly without shame.
וְהוּא מַבִּיט רַק עַל הַנִּגְלֶה,
And he gazes exclusively upon what is external,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵשָׂו (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה סה): "פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו וְכוּלֵי",
as stated concerning Esau (Bereishit Rabbah 65): "he spreads out his split hooves, etc.,"
וְהַנִּגְלֶה רַע.
and the outward appearance was evil.
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת "אִם יִסָּתֵר וְגוֹמֵר וַאֲנִי לֹא אֶרְאֶנּוּ",
Yet in truth: "Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him?" (Jeremiah 23:24),
וְאַחַר כָּךְ רָאוּ כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ הַפְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים.
and afterward all the ends of the earth witnessed their inward holiness, seeing that in truth they had acted only outwardly.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Purim 39:1: “The clarification that they had acted only outwardly became known to them after Hashem opened the deliverance. Before the deliverance, it seemed to them that they had become entirely estranged, Heaven forbid; such a clarification is possible only after the deliverance.”

rich.text: : “The clarification that they had acted only outwardly became known to them after Hashem opened the deliverance. Before the deliverance, it seemed to them that they had become entirely estranged, Heaven forbid; such a clarification is possible only after the deliverance.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim places an explicit limit on retrospective recognition: only after Hashem opened the deliverance did they know clearly that their outward act had not severed the inward bond. Beforehand, they feared that they had become estranged. This sharpens the siman's movement from hidden loyalty to visible rescue and guards against treating a person's advance assertion of a hidden good intention as the same thing as that later clarification.

p: וּלְכָךְ הַתְחָלַת הַגְּזֵירָה עַל יְדֵי צְנִיעוּת דְּאֶסְתֵּר,
Therefore the inception of the decree came about through Esther's modesty,
כִּי בְּוַדַּאי אִלּוּ הִגִּידָה מִיָּד עַל מָרְדֳּכַי מַה הוּא לָהּ,
for certainly had she immediately disclosed concerning Mordechai what he was to her,
לֹא הָיָה עַל לֵב הָמָן לִפְעוֹל כְּלוּם נֶגְדּוֹ.
it would never have entered Haman's heart to act against him.
וְהַהַצָּלָה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה בְּרָצוֹן,
And the salvation arrived through her entering unto the king willingly,
וְזֶה פְּרִיצוּת, הֵיפֶךְ צְנִיעוּת,
which appears as brazen forwardness, the antithesis of modesty,
וְכִמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים מִזְמוֹר כב) דְּכָעַס עַל זֶה אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ.
and as our Sages taught (Shocher Tov, Psalm 22) that Ahasuerus was angered by this.
רַק בֶּאֱמֶת בְּהַצְנֵעַ וּפְנִימִיּוּת הָיָה טוֹב וּקְדוּשָׁה,
Except that in truth, inwardly and in holy concealment it was goodness and sanctity,
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן צְנִיעוּת;
and that itself is true modesty;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה דַּיְיקָא כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ דִּצְנִיעוּת שֶׁבּוֹ נִקְלַט בָּהּ,
and specifically through this, the entire holy spark of modesty within him was absorbed into her,
שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק בְּרָצוֹן,
which is possible only through active willingness,
כְּאִילּוּ הוּא רוֹצֶה לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִמּוֹ,
as though one desires connection with him,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לִקְלוֹט מֵאַחַר שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִקְלוֹט מִמֶּנּוּ,
whereby one can extract the spark since he willfully engages to absorb it,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאוֹנֶס אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לִקְלוֹט כְּלָל.
whereas under absolute duress one absorbs nothing at all.
[וּבְוַדַּאי אָז נִתְעַבְּרָה מִדָּרְיָוֶשׁ שֶׁבָּנָה הַבַּיִת].
[And certainly at that very time she conceived Darius who rebuilt the Temple].
וְאָז הָיָה תַּכְלִית הַהַצְנֵעַ דְּ"אִם יִסָּתֵר וְגוֹמֵר",
And then was the ultimate expression of concealment of "Can any hide himself, etc.,"
לַעֲשׂוֹת מַעֲשֶׂה רָעָה כָּזוֹ וְלִהְיוֹת בּוֹ כַּוָּנָה קְדוֹשָׁה מְאֹד;
to perform an apparently reprehensible act yet harbor within it an intensely holy intention;
וְאָז נִתְקַיֵּים "וַאֲנִי לֹא אֶרְאֶנּוּ",
and then was fulfilled "that I shall not see him,"
וְ"רָאוּ כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר".
and "all the ends of the earth have seen, etc."

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim 22:19: “When did Esther say, “Do not be far from me, for trouble is near”? When Ahasuerus decreed destruction and killing, and Esther entered without permission. … When she entered the fourth enclosure, he began grinding and gnashing his teeth. He said: Alas for those who are lost and cannot be found! How much I desired and asked Vashti to enter before me, and she would not; yet this woman has entered like a harlot, without permission. … At that time Esther said, “Do not be far from me, for trouble is near.””

p: [רנז] כְּמוֹ שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּהֶם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים,
Just as the core root of the Congregation of Israel is their passionate longing for Hashem, blessed be He, as articulated throughout the Song of Songs,
כָּךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּהֶם לְחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
so too the root of all idolatrous nations is their lustful appetite for the worldly desires of this physical world.
וּבַזֹּהַר תְּרוּמָה (קמח עַמּוּד ב) דְּאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים מִתְתַּקְּנַת כְּגַוְונָא דְּאֵשֶׁת חַיִל,
And in Zohar Terumah (148b) it states that the adulterous woman is fashioned in the counterfeit semblance of the woman of valor,
כִּי הִיא אוֹת קוֹ״ף וְאֵשֶׁת חַיִל אוֹת הֵ״א, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
for she embodies the letter Kuf while the woman of valor embodies the letter Hei, see there.
וְשָׁם (קנב עַמּוּד א) דְּאוֹת קוֹ״ף שַׁרְיָא עַל גֵּיהִנָּם,
And there (152a) that the letter Kuf hovers over Gehenna,
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם (קנ עַמּוּד ב) דְּאֵשׁ דְּגֵיהִנָּם הוּא אֵשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְהוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and see there (150b) that the fire of Gehenna is the fire of the evil inclination and is identical with the Angel of Death, see there.
וּבְהַקְדָּמַת הַזֹּהַר דְּקוֹ״ף רֵי״שׁ אַתְוָון דְּשִׁקְרָא,
And in the Introduction of the Zohar (2b) that the letters Kuf and Reish are letters of falsehood,
פֵּירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קעח עַמּוּד ב) דְּהֵ״א דָּלֶ״ת הֲוַות,
the meaning being as written (Zohar Part II, 178b) that the letter Hei was originally a Dalet,
רַק בָּתַר דִּקְבִילַת עוּבָּרָא נַעֲשָׂה הֵ״א.
only that after receiving the embryo within it became a Hei.
וּבִפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים רֵישׁ שַׁעַר הַשַּׁבָּת דְּכֵן גַּם כֵּן אוֹת קוֹ״ף רֵי״שׁ הֲוַות וְכוּלֵי,
And in Pri Etz Chayim at the beginning of Sha'ar HaShabbat, that likewise the letter Kuf was originally a Reish, etc.,
פֵּירוּשׁ לְשׁוֹן דַּלּוּת וְרֵישׁ אֶחָד,
meaning an expression of poverty and destitution,
דְּמוֹרֶה עַל עֲנִיּוּת וְחִסָּרוֹן, דְּלֵית לָהּ מִגַּרְמָהּ וּמְבַקֶּשֶׁת הַשְׁלָמָה.
denoting impoverishment and lack, having nothing of its own and seeking completion.
רַק שֶׁזֶּה צוּרָתוֹ בְּקַוִּים יְשָׁרִים וְזֶה בַּעֲקַמְמוּמִיּוּת.
Except that one is formed with straight lines while the other is shaped with crookedness.
כִּי זֶה מִתְאַוֶּוה רַק לְהַשְׁפָּעַת קַו הַיּוֹשֶׁר דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For the holy side yearns purely for the influx of Hashem's Straight Line (Yosher),
וְכֵן הָעוּבָּר דִּקְבִילַת כֵּן בְּקַו הַיּוֹשֶׁר, וְזוֹ בַּעֲקַמְמוּמִיּוּת.
and likewise the embryo received by the Hei is straight, while the other receives through crooked distortion.

With every surge of heat with which they inflame themselves through the evil inclination, the fire of Gehinnom is kindled. paragraphs.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath, Introduction 1:15: “We have explained that, through our sins, the shell rules over Netzach, Hod, and Yesod; this is the shin of sheqer. What does the shell do afterward? It takes for itself the embryo of Malkhut, the vav within the holy heh. When the adulterous woman takes it, she becomes pregnant through it. At first she is in the mystery of resh, as is known: dalet belongs to holiness and resh to the shell. This resh takes the letter vav, the embryo within the heh of Malkhut, and joins it to her resh. Moreover, she extends it in the mystery of the leg of qof, so that it joins her in the mystery of the shell, a serpent coiled about the heel. She then becomes qof, for the shell is called an ape beside a human being. These are the letters shin and qof of sheqer. Afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, in His mercy takes it back from her, and she returns to being resh as at first and diminishes, as explained above.”

p: וְהִנֵּה בֶּאֱמֶת כָּל אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁקֶר אוֹתִיּוֹת הֵם בַּתּוֹרָה
Behold, in truth all the letters of sheker (falsehood) are holy letters in the Torah
וְכוּלָּם קוֹדֶשׁ וַדַּאי וּמֵאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and are certainly sacred and originate from Hashem's ultimate Truth.
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ "רָשׁ הוֹלֵךְ בְּתֻמּוֹ",
For in truth Scripture speaks of "a poor man who walks in his integrity" (Proverbs 19:1),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עא): "כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר רָשׁ וָדַל וְכוּלֵי – בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְדַבֵּר",
and our Sages expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 71): "Wherever 'rash' or 'dal' is mentioned, Scripture speaks of Israel,"
כִּי הַאי עָלְמָא נִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא.
for this physical realm is designated 'the World of Falsehood.'
כִּי שֶׁקֶר נִקְרָא דָּבָר לְפִי שָׁעָה כִּלְשׁוֹן כְּזָב, דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דָּבָר הַפּוֹסֵק.
For falsehood is termed anything that is transient, like the word kezav (deceit) denoting something that dries up and ceases.
וְכֵן כָּל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְשָׁעָה, וְ"לֹא בְמוֹתוֹ יִקַּח הַכֹּל".
And so all worldly delights are merely temporary, and "in his death he will take nothing" (Psalms 49:18).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא הֲכָנָה לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא וּפְרוֹזְדּוֹר לוֹ,
Nevertheless, it serves as a preparation and antechamber for the World to Come,
וּ"מִי שֶׁלֹּא טָרַח בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג.).
and "he who did not toil on the eve of Shabbat, etc." (Avodah Zarah 3a).
כַּיָּדוּעַ בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה דְּאוֹתִיּוֹת בּג״ד כפ״רת נֶגֶד שִׁבְעָה יָמִים,
As is known from Sefer Yetzirah, the letters Beged Kaperet correspond to the seven days of the week,
וְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בְּאוֹת רֵי״שׁ,
and the eve of Shabbat corresponds to the letter Reish,
וּבוֹ הוּא הַטּוֹרַח וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
and in it resides the physical toil and active spiritual exertion,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשִׁילְהֵי שַׁבָּת (קנו.): "מַאן דִּבְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת – חַזְרָן בְּמִצְווֹת".
as stated at the end of Shabbat (156a): "He who is born on Friday will be zealous in pursuit of mitzvot."

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 71:1: ““The Lord saw that Leah was unloved, and He opened her womb, and Rachel was barren” (Genesis 29:31). “The Lord saw that Leah was unloved…” “For the Lord hears the impoverished and does not despise His prisoners” (Psalms 69:34) – Rabbi Binyamin ben Levi said: The beginning of this verse does not correspond with its end, nor does its end correspond to its beginning. The verse should have said only: “For the Lord hears the impoverished and does not despise the prisoners” or: “For the Lord hears His impoverished and…His prisoners.” Rather: “For the Lord hears the impoverished” – this is Israel, as Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Every place that impoverished [dal], poor [ani], and indigent [evyon] is stated, the verse is speaking of Israel. “And does not despise His prisoners” – these are the barren women, who are prisoners in their homes, and forlorn. But when the Holy One blessed be He remembers them with children, they stand erect. Know that Leah was the unloved one of the household, but when the Holy One blessed be He remembered her, she stood erect. That is what is written: “The Lord saw that Leah was unloved.””

Falsehood is something that ceases, as in “its waters fail,” something without permanence. These are all the matters of this world, which appear in the imagination to endure, but do not truly do so, for they will pass away. The World to Come means stripping each thing of imagination to reach that thing’s truth: the underlying power of that power, which endures forever. This is eternal.”

paragraphs.text: Sefer Yetzirah 4:4-11: “Seven double letters, bet, gimel, dalet, kaf, peh, resh, and tav: He engraved them, hewed them, combined them, and formed through them planets in the world, days in the year, and gates in the living being. From them He engraved seven heavens, seven lands, and seven sabbaths; therefore He cherished the seventh beneath all the heavens. How? He made bet king over life, bound a crown to it, and formed through it Saturn in the world, the first day in the year, and the right eye in the living being. He made gimel king, bound a crown to it, and formed through it Jupiter in the world, the second day in the year, and the left eye in the living being. He made dalet king, bound a crown to it, and formed through it Mars in the world, the third day in the year, and the right ear in the living being. He made kaf king, bound a crown to it, and formed through it the sun in the world, the fourth day in the year, and the left ear in the living being. He made peh king, bound a crown to it, and formed through it Venus in the world, the fifth day in the year, and the right nostril in the living being. He made resh king, bound a crown to it, and formed through it Mercury in the world, the sixth day in the year, and the left nostril in the living being. He made tav king, bound a crown to it, and formed through it the moon in the world, Shabbat in the year, and the mouth in the living being.”

items.h: Human choice within divine foreknowledge

p: וּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַבְּחִירָה הוּא רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
And in truth the entire root of action and exertion, which stems from free choice, exists solely in this world.
דִּלְגַבֵּי אֲמִיתַּת יְדִיעוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין מָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה כְּלָל,
For relative to the ultimate foreknowledge of Hashem, blessed be He, there is no place for free choice or human exertion in deed at all,
וְהַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם אֲפִילּוּ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.
and everything is in the hands of Heaven, even the fear of Heaven.
רַק דִּבְהַאי עָלְמָא שֶׁהוּא עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא הַבְּחִירָה נִגְלֵית,
Only that in this world, which is the World of Falsehood, free choice is manifest,
דְּהַיְינוּ חוּץ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם,
namely, everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven,
וְזֶה אֱמֶת בִּשְׁעָתוֹ דְּהַיְינוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁכָּךְ רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and this is truth in its appointed hour—meaning within this world—for so Hashem willed it for this world.
וּלְכָךְ יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד יוֹם ו' דִּימֵי הַבִּנְיָן כַּנּוֹדָע,
Therefore Joseph the Righteous, who corresponds to the sixth day of the cosmic structure (Yesod),
דַּרְגָּא דִּילֵיהּ "יִרְאָתוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ה,
his spiritual level is "his fear of sin precedes his wisdom," as mentioned above in section 225,
וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּמַעֲשֵׂה אָדָם
and he represents the very root of human exertion and moral deeds
[מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכְּנֵסִיָּה, נֶגְדּוֹ יוֹם ג' שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּאוֹת הַדָּלֶ״ת].
[unlike our father Jacob, the root of the collective assembly, who corresponds to the third day created with the letter Dalet].
וְשִׁבְטוֹ נֶגֶד חוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר בְּחָדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה,
And his tribe corresponds to the month of Adar in the yearly cycle,
דְּלָכֵן יֵשׁ פְּעָמִים ב' אֲדָרִים כְּמוֹ פְּעָמִים שֵׁבֶט יוֹסֵף נֶחְלָק לִבְנַיִם.
which is why there are sometimes two Adars, just as the tribe of Joseph is divided into two.
וּמַזָּלוֹ דָּגִים שֶׁכֵּן נִתְבָּרַךְ "וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב",
And its astrological sign is Pisces (the fish), as he was blessed: "and let them multiply like fish" (Genesis 48:16),
וְהוּא נִבְרָא בְּאוֹת קוֹ״ף כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה,
and Adar was created through the letter Kuf, as written in Sefer Yetzirah,
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא אַחַר קַבָּלַת הָעוּבָּר,
which likewise operates from the perspective of this World of Falsehood after receiving the embryo,
דְּהַיְינוּ הַמִּילּוּי וְרִיבּוּי לִהְיוֹת שֵׁבֶט שָׁלֵם.
meaning the fullness and fruitful expansion to form a complete tribe.

paragraphs.text: Kedushat Levi, Exodus, Tetzaveh 8: “The month of Adar corresponds to Joseph, from whom two tribes emerged, Ephraim and Manasseh. Therefore Adar is the month that is intercalated, and there are sometimes two months of Adar. This is also why Adar’s sign is Pisces, the fish, which is the aspect of Joseph, as it is written: ‘May they multiply like fish in the midst of the earth’ (Genesis 48:16). It is known that Joseph’s descendants are compared to fish: just as the fish in the sea are covered, so are Joseph’s descendants—‘Joseph is a fruitful son, a fruitful son above the eye’ (Genesis 49:22).”

p: וּלְכָךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ יוֹסֵף בִּכְבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר בְּחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
Therefore Joseph's primary spiritual task is the conquering of the evil inclination regarding worldly desires.
וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף עָתִיד לֵיהָרֵג,
And Mashiach ben Yosef is destined to be slain,
כִּי בְּאוֹת הַקּוֹ״ף הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת,
because within the letter Kuf resides the Angel of Death,
כִּי הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז.),
for the evil inclination is itself the Angel of Death (as stated in Bava Batra 16a),
וּמִצַּד מִילּוּי תַּאֲוַות עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא הַמִּיתָה.
and from the indulgence of worldly desire comes death.
וְלִהְיוֹת בִּכְבִישָׁה גְּמוּרָה לְאַכְפַּיָּה לְגַמְרֵי – זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּתַאֲוָה,
And to achieve total subjugation by complete suppression—this is impossible regarding basic physical desire,
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּיוֹמָא (סט:);
as our Sages taught in Yoma (69b);
רַק הַנִּצּוּחַ עַל יְדֵי לְאִתְהַפְּכָא מִקּוֹ״ף לְהֵ״א,
rather, victory comes by transforming the Kuf into a Hei,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד חוֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן, שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לַמְּלָכִים,
which corresponds to the month of Nisan, the New Year for kings,
נֶגֶד יְהוּדָה וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד.
facing the attribute of Judah and Mashiach ben David.
כִּי לִהְיוֹת כֵּן רָשׁ וְשֶׁלֹּא יֵהָנֶה כְּלוּם מֵחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וַדַּאי הָיָה חַי;
For had one remained purely impoverished (like the letter Reish) deriving no physical pleasure whatever from worldly delight, he certainly would live;
רַק עַל יְדֵי הִתְהַוּוּת רֵי״שׁ לְקוֹ״ף,
only through the transformation of Reish into Kuf,
דְּהַיְינוּ קַבָּלַת עוּבָּר וַהֲנָאָה מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה – זֶהוּ מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת.
namely the reception of the embryo and drawing pleasure from this world—this is where the Angel of Death enters.
רַק בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם הַקּוֹ״ף מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת,
Yet in truth, the letter Kuf is likewise among the holy letters,
וְהַיְינוּ אַחַר הִתְגַּלּוּת הַהֵ״א, תּוֹקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and that is attained after the disclosure of the Hei, the sheer intensity of longing for Hashem, blessed be He;
אָז גַּם הֲנָאַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
then even the worldly enjoyment of the Jewish people is consecrated unto Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Adar and Nissan illustrate the mutual need of body and soul.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:38: “Within holiness this corresponds to Naftali, who joins all Israel, and Adar stands beside Nissan. In Israel, qof hints at “holy”: the body too has holiness through its connection with the soul, whose principal power is wisdom. Israel's souls derive from the letters of Torah. These are the six hundred thousand souls of the wilderness generation; the souls of other generations derive from the renewed Oral Torah of their own generation. The true reception of new life on the soul's side is therefore in the he of Nissan. The qof of bodily reception exists also among the nations, but Israel receives from Hashem, and bodily reception is never without spiritual reception. Both need one another, as the Sages' parable of body and soul explains regarding judgment, and likewise reward. The soul is the body's life, while the soul's manifestation in this world is through the body. So too Nissan comes in the spring through Adar's intercalation.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Likkutei Maamarim develops the same contrast between the letters qof and he through bodily and spiritual reception. It explains that the body can share in holiness through its bond with the soul, while the soul becomes manifest in this world through the body. This helps explain why the siman proceeds from suppressing desire to transforming permissible enjoyment for holiness. The two passages use different tribal associations in developing their particular arguments; the comparison concerns the reception and body/soul structure.

items.h: Adar, Nisan, and the transformation of desire

p: וְזֶה טַעַם הַכְלָלַת קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ בִּקְדוּשָׁה לִפְעָמִים כַּיָּדוּעַ,
And this explains why the shell of Nogah is sometimes subsumed into holiness, as is known,
דְּאֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים הוּא קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ,
for the wayward woman represents the shell of Nogah;
הֲגַם דִּלְפָנִים הוּא חֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
even though outwardly it looks like mundane pleasure,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ אֵין נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל דָּבוּק בְּחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּלָל,
nonetheless at the inner root no Jewish soul is attached to worldly desire at all,
וּמַה שֶּׁלּוֹקֵחַ מֵחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא רַק לְתַשְׁמִישׁ דִּקְדוּשָׁה.
and whatever he partakes of physical pleasure is solely for holy usage.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן גְּזֵירַת הָמָן בַּאֲדָר
And this is the secret of Haman's decree occurring in Adar
עַל שֶׁנֶּהֱנוּ מִסְּעוּדַת אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע וְנִדְבְּקוּ בְּאוֹת הַקּוֹ״ף.
because they partook of the banquet of that wicked king and attached themselves to the letter Kuf.
וּבוֹ מֵת מֹשֶׁה וְנוֹלַד,
And in Adar Moses died and was born;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל קְבוּרָתוֹ מוּל בֵּית פְּעוֹר, שֶׁהוּא הֵיפוּךְ תַּאֲוָה,
as I heard concerning his burial opposite Beit Peor, which embodies the absolute antithesis of lust,
וְהָיָה מ' יוֹם בְּלֹא אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה וּפֵירַשׁ מִן הָאִשָּׁה,
and he spent forty days without food and drink and separated from his wife,
שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ לְגַמְרֵי מֵחֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
having completely detached himself from all worldly pleasure.
רַק לֵידָתוֹ מֵעַמְרָם, שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת נה:) שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ,
Yet his physical birth stemmed from Amram, concerning whom the Sages stated (Shabbat 55b) that he died solely through the counsel of the serpent;
וּפֵירוּשׁ עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבַטֵּל לְגַמְרֵי.
and the meaning of the counsel of the serpent is the primal root of desire that cannot be wholly extinguished.
וּכְמוֹ בְּיִשַׁי בְּעִנְיַן אֲמָתוֹ שֶׁאָז נוֹלַד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And like Jesse regarding the incident of his maidservant from which King David, peace be upon him, was born, as the Sages taught
(מִדְרָשׁ, הוּבָא בְּעַשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת, מַאֲמַר חֲקוֹר דִּין חֵלֶק ג פֶּרֶק י),
(Midrash, cited in Asarah Maamarot, Maamar Chikur Din 3:10),
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ עִנְיַן תַּזְרִיעַ).
and concerning this Scripture states: "In iniquity was I brought forth" (Psalms 51:7; as expounded in Midrash Rabbah at the start of Tazria).
וְכֵן עַמְרָם חֲזָרַת לִיקּוּחִין ב',
So too Amram's remarriage to Yocheved,
דְּהֲגַם דִּגְזֵירָה עַל הַבָּנִים וְאֵינוֹ כְּדֵי לְהַעֲמִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת,
for since there was a decree drowning male children, and remarriage seemingly did not appear aimed at viable offspring,
נִרְאֶה כְּדֵי לְמַלֹּאות תַּאֲוָה לְבַד, זֶה נִקְרָא עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ,
it appeared as if engaged merely to satisfy bodily desire—which is termed the counsel of the serpent—
וְאָז נוֹלַד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
and at that moment Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was born.
וְזֶהוּ בַּאֲדָר, שֶׁהוּא הַנּוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה,
And this occurred in Adar, for he is the giver of the Torah,
וְעַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה הוּא תִּיקּוּן דְּכָל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן לְצוֹרֶךְ.
and through the Torah unfolds the rectification of all worldly desires to be utilized for holy purpose.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 7:2-7: “It is an intermediate level between the three entirely impure shells and the level of holiness. Therefore it is sometimes included in the three impure shells, as stated in Etz Chaim in the name of the Zohar; at other times it is included and rises into the level of holiness, when the good mixed within it is separated from the evil, prevails, rises, and is included in holiness. For example, someone eats rich ox meat and drinks fragrant wine to broaden his mind for God and His Torah—as Rava said, “Wine and fragrance,” and so forth—or to fulfill the mitzvah of delighting in Shabbat and the festivals. Then the vitality of the meat and wine that flowed from nogah is refined and rises to God like a burnt offering and a sacrifice. Likewise, someone says something humorous to clear his mind and gladden his heart for God, His Torah, and His service, which require joy, as Rava did for his students when he began with a humorous remark and the Sages became cheerful. But someone who gluttonously eats meat and drinks wine to satisfy the desire of his body and animal soul—the element of water among its four evil elements, from which desire comes—causes the vitality of the meat and wine within him to descend and become temporarily included in the complete evil of the three impure shells. His body temporarily becomes their garment and vehicle, until he repents and returns to serving God and studying His Torah. Since the meat was permitted and the wine kosher, they can return and rise with him when he returns to God’s service. This is the meaning of heter and mutar, “permitted”: it is not bound and held by the external forces so that it cannot return and rise to God. Nevertheless, a trace of it remains in the body, and therefore the body requires the affliction of the grave, as will be explained later.”

paragraphs.text: Asarah Maamarot, Maamar Chikur Din 3:10: “The aggadah relates that Jesse, his father, withdrew from his wife in his old age. We have no doubt that this was an act of piety: perhaps the Torah’s statement “An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter” means a male Moabite and even a female Moabite. For this law was uncertain in that generation until Yitra the Ishmaelite, Jesse’s son-in-law, sharpened and girded his sword like an Ishmaelite and planted it in the study hall to establish the law, “A male Moabite, but not a female Moabite,” from the court of Shmuel of Ramah. Jesse the righteous, to remove himself from doubt and fulfill “In the evening do not let your hand rest,” sought to come to his maidservant. It seems plausible to us that this was after he had freed her conditionally: If the Torah said a male Moabite but not a female Moabite, you are free; but if it meant a male Moabite and even a female Moabite, my words have no effect, for those of definite disqualified status are permitted to one another, as taught in the chapter Asarah Yuchasin. Although a mamzer may marry a female convert or freed maidservant, and the same applies to a male Moabite, since the community of converts and freed slaves is not called the congregation, he preferred that his children should be slaves whom he could immediately free, so that they would not inherit his disqualification. If their mother had been freed, the children would follow his disqualified status and be prohibited from entering the congregation forever. The faithful maidservant, knowing that the established law permits women from Ammon and Moab to enter the congregation, gave the identifying signs to Jesse’s wife, who was then hated by her husband because of her exalted level, as will be explained concerning Leah in chapter eighteen. From that event David was born.”

paragraphs.text: Sotah 12a:10-13: “It was taught: Amram was the leader of the generation. When he saw that Pharaoh the wicked had said, “Every son born you shall cast into the Nile,” he said: We are laboring in vain. He arose and divorced his wife, and everyone arose and divorced their wives. His daughter said to him: Father, your decree is harsher than Pharaoh’s. Pharaoh decreed only against the males, while you have decreed against both males and females. Pharaoh decreed only concerning this world, while you have decreed concerning both this world and the World to Come. Pharaoh is wicked, and it is uncertain whether his decree will be fulfilled; you are righteous, and your decree will certainly be fulfilled, as it is said, “You shall decree a matter and it shall be established for you.” He arose and took his wife back, and everyone arose and took their wives back. “He took”: should it not say “he took back”? Rav Yehuda bar Zevina said: He performed a marriage ceremony for her. He seated her in a bridal litter, Aaron and Miriam danced before her, and the ministering angels said, “The happy mother of children.””

p: וּלְכָךְ מַפַּלַת הָמָן בְּנִיסָן,
Therefore Haman's downfall occurred in Nisan,
דְּאַחַר הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹת הַהֵ״א, רָזָא דְּאֵשֶׁת חַיִל וְחֶשְׁקוּת דִּקְדוּשָׁה,
for after the revelation of the letter Hei, the mystery of the woman of valor and holy passion,
מִמֵּילָא נִתְגַּלָּה דְּהֵם לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים וְכוּלֵי.
it became automatically revealed that Israel had sinned only outwardly.
וְגַם אֲדָר נִתְקַן, דְּכָל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה פְּנִימִיּוּתָן אֵין כֵּן.
And Adar itself was rectified, disclosing that the inward reality of all their worldly delights was not corrupt.
וְזֶה טַעַם "וְנַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא",
And this is the meaning of "it was turned to the opposite" (Esther 9:1),
שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה שֶׁבְּאוֹתָן אִגְּרוֹת "לִהְיוֹת הַיְּהוּדִים עֲתִידִים",
wherein it was disclosed that within those very letters "that the Jews should be ready,"
פְּנִימִיּוּת הַכַּוָּנָה הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ, "אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁלְטוּ הֵמָּה וְכוּלֵי".
the inner intent was the reverse: "that they should have rule over them, etc."
כִּי כָּל כַּוָּנָתָם בֶּאֱמֶת לַעֲקוֹר חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, מִלִּבָּבָם,
For their entire true intent was to uproot worldly passions—the spiritual root of the nations—from their hearts,
וְאָז נִצְּחוּ לָאוּמּוֹת בִּ"לְאַכְפַּיָּא", וְזֶהוּ לַעֲמָלֵק;
and then they subdued the nations through suppression (itkafiya), which represents Amalek;
וּ"לְאִתְהַפְּכָא", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְרַבִּים מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִתְיַהֲדִים וְגוֹמֵר".
and through transformation (ithapkha), as it is written: "And many from the peoples of the land became Jews, etc." (Esther 8:17).
וְזֶה טַעַם שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה ו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): "מִסְמַךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִגְאוּלָּה עָדִיף",
And this explains why our Sages stated (Megillah 6b): "Juxtaposing redemption to redemption is preferable,"
כִּי כֵּן גְּאוּלַּת אֲדָר עַל יְדֵי נִיסָן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
because the redemption of Adar is fulfilled through Nisan as explained above.
וְכֵן בְּכָל זְמַן,
And likewise in all times,
כְּפִי נִצּוּחַ אִישׁ יְהוּדִי לְחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְתַאֲווֹת הַיֵּצֶר לְאַכְפַּיָּא וּלְאִתְהַפְּכָא,
according to the measure a Jewish man overcomes worldly delights and sensual appetites through suppression and transformation,
כָּךְ הוּא מְנַצֵּחַ וּמַשְׁפִּיל הָאוּמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים בְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר.
so does he conquer and humble the idolatrous nations in that generation.

sections.en: The Place of the Transgressor Within Israel

p: [רנח] כְּמוֹ שֶׁבִּכְלַל הָאוּמָּה יֵשׁ גַּם פּוֹשֵׁעַ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
Just as within the collective nation there exists also the transgressor of Israel,
וְכָל תַּעֲנִית שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מִפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינוֹ תַּעֲנִית כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (כְּרֵיתוֹת ו:) מֵחֶלְבְּנָה,
and any fast day that does not include the transgressors of Israel is not a valid fast, as the Sages deduced (Keritot 6b) from the galbanum spice,
כָּךְ בָּאָדָם עַצְמוֹ יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן חֵלֶק רַע מִשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבַּעִיסָה הַמְּכוּנֶּה פּוֹשֵׁעַ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
so too within an individual himself there is an evil portion from the leaven in the dough designated as 'transgressor of Israel,'
וְלִהְיוֹת בְּקֶשֶׁר אֶחָד עִמּוֹ,
and he must unite it in a singular bond,
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ז): "כְּשֵׁם שֶׁקִּילוּסוֹ עוֹלֶה מִן הַצַּדִּיקִים, כָּךְ עוֹלֶה מִן הָרְשָׁעִים".
as our Sages expounded (Shemot Rabbah 7): "Just as His praise ascends from the righteous, so does it ascend from the wicked."
וְזֶהוּ קִילּוּס יוֹתֵר כַּאֲשֶׁר צַד הָרֶשַׁע מְקַלֵּס גַּם כֵּן וּמַכִּיר גְּדוּלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And this constitutes an even greater praise—when the side of evil likewise offers praise and recognizes Hashem's greatness.
וְכֵן בָּאָדָם, כַּאֲשֶׁר גַּם מִצַּד הִשְׁתַּקְּעוּתוֹ בְּחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַכִּיר גְּדוּלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
So too within man: when even out of his immersion in physical pleasures he recognizes the greatness of Hashem,
כְּמוֹ בַּהֲנָאָה דַּאֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה עַל יְדֵי הַבְּרָכָה מִקּוֹדֶם,
such as enjoying eating and drinking by means of reciting the prior blessing,
וַאֲפִילּוּ אִם כְּעִנְיַן (מַה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרָכוֹת סג.): "גַּנָּבָא אַפּוּם מַחְתַּרְתָּא רַחֲמָנָא קָרֵי".
and even along the lines of (Berakhot 63a): "The thief at the mouth of the breach calls out to the Merciful One."
וּבַזֹּהַר תְּרוּמָה (קעד רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)
And in Zohar Terumah (beginning of 174a)
דְּ"אוֹדֶה בְּכָל לֵבָב" – הַיְינוּ גַּם בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע,
that "I will praise with all my heart" (Psalms 111:1) denotes serving Him with the evil inclination as well,
וְזֶהוּ "בְּסוֹד יְשָׁרִים וְעֵדָה",
and this is "in the council of the upright and in the assembly,"
פֵּירוּשׁ כֹּחוֹ, דְּצָרִיךְ עֵדָה שְׁלֵימָה מֵהַאי טַעְמָא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, כָּךְ בְּיָחִיד כֵּן.
meaning its spiritual force: that just as a whole community is required for this reason, so is it required within the individual.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 7:4: “Another interpretation: “Concerning Pharaoh king of Egypt” – Rabbi Levi said: This is analogous to a king who had an orchard and he planted non-fruit-bearing trees and fruit trees in it. His servants said to him: ‘What pleasure do you get from these non-fruit-bearing trees?’ He said to them: ‘Just as I need fruit trees, so too I need the non-fruit-bearing trees, as were it not for the non-fruit-bearing trees, with what would I make bathhouses and furnaces?’ That is why it says: “Concerning the children of Israel and concerning Pharaoh” – just as the praise of the Holy One blessed be He rises to Him from the Garden of Eden from the mouths of the righteous, so too it rises from Gehenna from the mouths of the wicked, as it is stated: “They pass through a valley of tears, they render it a place of springs” (Psalms 84:7). What is “they render it a place of springs”? They shed tears like springs until they cool Gehenna with their tears. The praise rises from there, as it is stated: “Blessings cover the early rain [moreh]” (Psalms 84:7). What do they say? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: You have said well, You have judged well, You have purified well, You have impurified well, You have condemned well, You have taught well, and You have ruled well. The Garden of Eden is destined to shout and say: Give me the righteous, I have no interest in the wicked, as it is stated: “I hate those who regard empty folly” (Psalms 31:7). Whom do I seek? Those who trusted in Your name, as it is stated: “But I trust in the Lord” (Psalms 31:7). Gehenna is destined to shout and say: I have no interest in the righteous. Whom do I seek? The wicked: “Empty folly,” those who engage in folly. The Holy One blessed be He says: ‘Give this one the righteous and this one the wicked,’ as it is stated: “The leech has two daughters” (Proverbs 30:15).”

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Eikev 19:1: ““Even when I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for You are with me.” The matter follows what they said in Berakhot 63a concerning “Know Him in all your ways, and He will straighten your paths”: Rava said, “Even in a matter of transgression.” The reading in Ein Yaakov adds: Rav Pappa said, “This is what people say: A thief at the mouth of the tunnel calls upon the Merciful One.” That is, although he commits an explicit transgression, violating “You shall not steal,” nevertheless, since he does not forget the blessed God and believes in Him at the time of the deed, calling upon the Merciful One, concerning this it is said, “He will straighten your paths”: God will straighten his paths, no outcast will remain cast out, and he will have a correction.”

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaZikhronot 1:10: “After commanding the poor person, Scripture says, “You shall keep the commandments,” and so forth, to warn about observing the commandments as a whole. For one who trusts in the Lord must join his trust with keeping His commandments, rather than act wickedly and trust that God will nevertheless treat him well. As Shmuel says in the chapter HaRo’eh, according to the reading of Ein Yaakov: “A thief at the mouth of the tunnel calls upon the Merciful One.” And in the first chapter of Yoma: “They were wicked, but they placed their trust in the Holy One, blessed be He.” This is not the quality of trust—to trust that, although one has sinned, the Holy One is with him—for this causes heedlessness about sinning. Even if he sees fortune smiling upon him, they said in Bava Kamma: “Whoever says that the Holy One, blessed be He, waives wrongdoing,” and so forth.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Terumah 88:883-884: ““I shall thank the Lord with all my heart”: with the good inclination and with the evil inclination that dwells within him. For one must thank the Holy One, blessed be He, for everything, with the good inclination and the evil inclination. From the side of the good inclination, good comes to a person, and one must bless the Holy One as “the Good who does good.” From the side of the evil inclination, accusation comes upon a person, and one must thank the Holy One [with the good inclination and the evil inclination] for whatever comes upon him, from this side and from that side. “In the council of the upright and the congregation”: “in the council of the upright” means those who know the mystery of the Holy One [another reading: the supernal holy angels], for they know all His mysteries and are His council. “And the congregation” means Israel when they gather in ten to thank the Holy One. Therefore one must thank the Holy One for good and for bad, and make it known before everyone. If you say: He already knows, so why must one publicize it? Through publicizing the miracle, the Holy One is honored in the world. Therefore it is written of the Holy One, “I shall be magnified and sanctified,” and so forth.”

p: וְאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת לד.): "שְׂאוֹר, רוּבּוֹ קָשֶׁה וּמִיעוּטוֹ יָפֶה",
And they taught (Berakhot 34a): "Leaven: too much is harmful, but a little is beneficial,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל יוֹתָם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב כז, ב): "רַק לֹא בָא אֶל הֵיכַל ה' וְגוֹמֵר",
and as I heard concerning Jotham of whom it is written (II Chronicles 27:2): "only he did not enter the temple of Hashem, etc.,"
שֶׁזֶּה נֶאֱמַר לְחִסָּרוֹן עָלָיו, לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ שׁוּם חִסָּרוֹן כְּלָל.
that this was stated as a critique against him, indicating that he had no human flaw whatever.
וּבֶאֱמֶת נֶאֱמַר: "יָקָר מֵחָכְמָה מִכָּבוֹד סִכְלוּת מְעָט",
And in truth Scripture declares: "A little folly is more precious than wisdom and honor" (Ecclesiastes 10:1),
דְּצָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּכָל אֶחָד סִכְלוּת מְעַט עַל כָּל פָּנִים, וְזֶהוּ הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
for each person must contain at least a measure of folly, and this constitutes true wholeness.
רַק שֶׁזֶּה טוֹב לָאָדָם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אוֹתוֹ הַסִּכְלוּת כַּמִּיעוּט הַיּוֹתֵר אֶפְשָׁרִי.
Only that it is good for man that this folly be kept to the smallest possible minimum.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר וַיַּקְהֵל (ר״ג עַמּוּד ב): "דְּנֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב וְלָא לְאַנְהָגָא בֵּיהּ קְלָנָא",
Therefore it is stated in Zohar Vayakhel (203b): "and a brightness (Nogah) was round about it, and one must not treat it with contempt,"
כִּי "יִתְרוֹן אֶרֶץ בַּכֹּל הוּא", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "אֲפִילּוּ וְכוּלֵי" (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כב).
for "the advantage of the earth is in all things" (Ecclesiastes 5:8), and the Sages expounded: "even creatures that appear useless, etc." (Vayikra Rabbah 22).
כִּי מִכָּל דָּבָר יֵשׁ יִתְרוֹן בֶּאֱמֶת,
For from everything there is indeed an ultimate advantage,

even from the side of evil through the praise and thanksgiving arising from the whole,

and through "All my bones shall declare: Hashem, who is like You" (Psalms 35:10), all becomes elevated.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Sefer Kedushat Shabbat 6:4: “Therefore they said it quietly and compared it to a king's daughter who smelled a dish's seasoning and would feel ashamed to ask for it. It is a disgrace to the congregation of Israel when its heart is not completely pure. Yet “a little foolishness is more precious than wisdom and honor,” and a little leaven is beneficial: His praise and the glory of His kingship rise still more when an impulse remains in the heart and, despite it, the heart recognizes His unity and that there is none besides Him.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Peri Tzadik explains the same images of a little leaven and a little foolishness through the quietly spoken declaration of lower unity. The added praise comes from recognizing Hashem while an opposing impulse remains, rather than from expanding that impulse. This fits the siman's own qualification that the remaining foolishness should be as little as possible, and its turn toward blessing over permissible enjoyment.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Writings, Proverbs 30:3: ““The semamit is grasped by the hands, yet it is in kings’ palaces.” Semamit signifies anger and sadness, from the word shemamah, desolation. “It is grasped by the hands” means that this deficiency can grow even in very great people, for “Who are the kings? The sages.” The sages, heads of Israel’s thousands, labor over this to perfect themselves so that no root of it remains in their hearts. This was the matter with Uzziah, who entered the innermost place to burn incense because he wished to perfect himself in this respect. As long as he knew that he had not attained completion in this, he understood that he had not attained completion in everything. Incense gladdens a person’s heart, as it is written, “Oil and incense gladden the heart.” This is what is said: “As he raged against the priests, the leprosy shone upon his forehead.” Because he recognized that he was not free of this fault, he judged himself to be in mortal danger and permitted himself to burn incense to attain the completion of his soul, for nothing stands in the way of saving life. Indeed, he truly succeeded, for afterward he attained completion. Scripture says of him, “The leprosy shone,” using the language of shining: only in outward appearance did it seem that he had acted improperly; in depth he attained completion through it. It is said of him, “He dwelt in the house of freedom”: he became free, for he was in a state of completion. But because he was among the priests, and the depth of his intention was hidden from them, he appeared to them as one profaning God’s name; according to their apprehension, he was afflicted with leprosy. This is what is said of his son Jotham: “He did what was upright in the eyes of the Lord, like everything his father Uzziah had done; only he did not enter the Lord’s sanctuary.” The word “only” limits, like all occurrences of akh and rak in the Torah: he did not reach that level. Had Uzziah burned the incense, he would immediately have entered the life of the World to Come.”

Rav Tzadok reads yakar homiletically as “precious”: the minimum element of ordinary human desire can itself have a necessary role, just as a little leaven is useful. This explains his positive use of the phrase “a little folly.”

paragraphs.text: Divrei Soferim 17:1: “This is the matter of the two loaves of Shavuot, which are brought as leaven: it is offering to the blessed God the obstructing leaven in the dough, as stated in Berakhot 17a. Through this one merits receiving the giving of the Torah, which is the remedy for the inclination—that is, using it only according to God’s will. Then it is “very good,” as our Sages say in Bereshit Rabbah, and as stated in Berakhot 34a concerning leaven: a little is beneficial, but much is harmful. This is the little folly that is more precious than wisdom and honor. Wisdom is apprehending the words of Torah themselves, while honor is what ultimately follows from it, for “the wise inherit honor.” The little folly brings all this through the feeling of deficiency: through it a person longs, desires, and waits for words of Torah to fill his lack. This is the principal human power: the yearning and longing one has, and the preparation to receive and do all the Torah. Everything else comes from God, who completes it for him. He gives wisdom, but “gives only to the wise”—those who have the beginning of wisdom, the fear of God, which is itself called wisdom, as it is written, “Behold, the fear of God is wisdom.” This is preparing the heart to do nothing contrary to God’s will. Then the whole Torah and wisdom are entrusted to him, to know God’s will and to make all his deeds and thoughts accord with the divine wisdom within him.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 4:6: “Mar Zutra said: ‘At a time of finding’ means finding a privy. In the West they said that Mar Zutra's interpretation is preferable to all the others: every pious person should pray for this. A privy indicates shame, meaning that a person should pray not to be put to shame. At the root, a deficiency is found in every person from birth. Hashem therefore created openings and cavities in a person, so that he should not become proud and imagine himself perfect in every respect. As the Talmud states (Bava Batra 75a), the Holy One said to Chiram king of Tyre, ‘I looked at you and created openings in the human person.’ This was said because he made himself a god. A person's openings indicate his lack of perfection: no person can be without deficiency, as it says (Ecclesiastes 7:20), ‘There is no righteous person on earth who does good and does not sin.’ This indicates deficiency at the root of each person's life. Therefore every person has surplus that is completely rejected and discharged: the excess of food and drink is not absorbed in his 248 limbs but is lost and rendered unfit. This indicates a deficiency present from birth; if there were only good in a person, from where would waste and surplus come? Every pious person should pray that this inherited deficiency be exceedingly fine and slight.”
