Its later examples concern carefully guarded people whose unintended speech is clarified. This supports the siman's express ‘smallest possible’ qualification, rather than suggesting that one should deliberately create a fault.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: for "the advantage of the earth is in all things" (Ecclesiastes 5:8), and the Sages expounded: "even creatures that appear useless, etc." (Vayikra Rabbah 22).

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 22:1: ““Any man from the house of Israel who will slaughter a bull, or a sheep, or a goat, in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp” (Leviticus 17:3). “Any man from the house of Israel who will slaughter a bull, or a sheep, or a goat” – that is what is written: “The advantage of land is in every way” (Ecclesiastes 5:8). Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda said: Even matters that you consider to be superfluous for the world are beneficial for the world; palm fiber to make rope; a thorn bush to fence a garden, “A king is subservient to a field” (Ecclesiastes 5:8); even if he is king and he rules from one end of the world to the other, “he is subservient to the field.” If the field produces, he will be successful; if the field does not produce, there is nothing. Therefore, “one who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver” (Ecclesiastes 5:9); one who loves money will not be satisfied with money, “nor one who loves abundance, with produce…” (Ecclesiastes 5:9), as anyone who avidly pursues money, but has no land, what benefit does he have? Rabbi Yishmael ben Rabbi Tanḥum and Rabbi Ḥanin son of Rabbi in the name of Rabbi Yirmeya: It is written: “They will disembark from their ships…they will stand on the ground” (Ezekiel 27:29). Do we not know that they would stand on the ground? Rather, one whose ship sinks at sea and he has land on the shore, he will recover. If he does not have land, you do not have any greater futility. Rabbi Neḥemya said: “The advantage of land is in every way” – even matters that you consider superfluous to the giving of the Torah, e.g., the halakhot of ritual fringes, phylacteries, and mezuza; they, too, are included in the giving of the Torah, as it is stated: “The Lord gave me the two tablets of stone inscribed with the finger of God and on them were all the matters [kekhol hadevarim]” (Deuteronomy 9:10). And it is written: “All the mitzva [hamitzva] that I [command you this day you shall take care to perform]” (Deuteronomy 8:1). Kol, kekhol; devarim, hadevarim; mitzva, hamitzva – [to teach that] Bible, Mishna, halakha, Talmud, addenda, aggadot, and even what a distinguished disciple is destined to say before his teacher, all these were stated to Moses from Sinai, as it is stated: “There is a matter regarding which one would say: See, this is new” (Ecclesiastes 1:10), his counterpart responds to him: “It has already been, in the ages [that were before us]” (Ecclesiastes 1:10). “A king is subservient to a field,” Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda says: “King,” this is an expert in Talmud; “is subservient to a field,” this is an expert in Mishna, as he arranges the halakha before him. Rabbi Neḥemya says: “King,” this is an expert in Mishna; “is subservient to a field,” this is an expert in Talmud, as he receives the halakha before him. Therefore, “one who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver,” – one who loves Torah will not be satisfied with Torah. “Nor one who loves abundance, [with produce]” as anyone who avidly pursues Torah, but does not have Talmud, what benefit does he have? Rabbi Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Aḥa: One who studied but does not teach, you have no greater futility than this.”

p: וּב' יְצָרִים הֵם: תַּאֲוָה, וְכַעַס דִּרְצִיחָה,
And there are two foundational inclinations: bodily lust, and the fury of bloodshed,
שֶׁהֵם דְּאָדָם וְחַוָּה מֵהַסָּתַת נָחָשׁ, וּדְקַיִן.
which originated with Adam and Eve from the incitement of the serpent, and with Cain.
וְזֶה דְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ הוּא בְּכָל אָדָם,
And this 'counsel of the serpent' resides within every human being,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא סט:): "דְּאִצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ עָלְמָא וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְבַטְּלוֹ".
and as our Sages taught (Yoma 69b): "the world requires it and it is impossible to abolish it."
וְזֶהוּ סִכְלוּת מְעָט הַהֶכְרֵחִי עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְקִיּוּם עוֹלָם.
And this is the indispensable 'little folly' required at minimum for the preservation of the world.
וְהוּא נֶגֶד אוֹת רֵי״שׁ הַמּוֹרֶה רֵישׁוּת,
And this corresponds to the letter Reish which denotes poverty (reishut),
כִּי "שָׁלֹשׁ הֵנָּה לֹא תִשְׂבַּעְנָה וְגוֹמֵר",
for "There are three things that are never satisfied, etc." (Proverbs 30:15),
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה נב:) בְּיִצְרָא דְּתַאֲוָה: "מַשְׂבִּיעוֹ רָעֵב".
as our Sages expounded (Sukkah 52b) regarding the inclination of lust: "feed it and it hungers."
וְעַל זֶה בִּיקֵּשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "רֵאשׁ וָעֹשֶׁר אַל תִּתֶּן לִי וְגוֹמֵר",
And concerning this King Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed: "Give me neither poverty nor riches, etc." (Proverbs 30:8),
שֶׁלֹּא לִרְדּוֹף בְּמוֹתָרוֹת תַּאֲוָה, דְּזֶה נִקְרָא רֵאשׁ,
meaning not to pursue the superfluities of lust, which is termed 'poverty,'
וְגַם שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲצוֹר תַּאֲוָתוֹ לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא עֹשֶׁר,
and also not to stifle physical desire entirely, which is termed 'riches,'
רַק צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּקַו אֶמְצָעִי,
rather one must walk the middle path,
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה מז.) עַל זֶה: "יֵצֶר שְׂמֹאל דּוֹחָה וְיָמִין מְקָרֶבֶת".
as our Sages expounded (Sotah 47a) upon this: "let the left push away and the right draw near."

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Numbers, Nasso 4: “‘They shall send from the camp every person afflicted with tzaraat, every person with a discharge, and everyone impure through contact with a corpse.’ A person afflicted with tzaraat represents anger, for tzaraat comes as punishment for evil speech. A person with a discharge represents one ruled by desire, and impurity through a corpse represents sadness. Therefore the person afflicted with tzaraat is sent out of all three camps, for the trait of anger has no share in Israel. The person with a discharge is sent out only from the Levite camp and the camp of the Divine Presence, for the trait of desire is unfitting for Torah scholars. The person impure through a corpse is sent out only from the camp of the Divine Presence, for the trait of sadness is sometimes found even among Torah scholars, as the Gemara says: ‘It is the Torah that makes him seethe’; this seething is sadness. He is therefore sent out only from the camp of the Divine Presence, for ‘strength and joy are in His place.’”

p: וְהַקּוֹ״ף נֶגֶד רְצִיחָה, שֶׁהוּא לְבָתַר דִּקְבִילַת עוּבָּרָא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רנ"ז,
And the letter Kuf corresponds to murder, which is after the reception of the embryo as noted above in section 257,
דְּהַיְינוּ הוֹלָדַת יֵצֶר הָרָע אַחֵר, כְּמוֹ קַיִן מֵאָדָם.
namely the birthing of an additional evil inclination, like Cain born from Adam.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר תְּרוּמָה (קסז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) דְּקַיִן נוֹלַד בְּאוֹת הַקּוֹ״ף
And as written in Zohar Terumah (167b end) that Cain was born under the letter Kuf
[וְהֶבֶל בְּהֵ״א, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
[and Abel under the letter Hei, see there.
וּמַחֲלוֹקְתָּם דּוּגְמַת מִמַּחֲלוֹקֶת יוֹסֵף וִיהוּדָה, "אֶפְרַיִם לֹא יְקַנֵּא אֶת יְהוּדָה וִיהוּדָה וְגוֹמֵר",
And their conflict mirrors the dispute of Joseph and Judah, "Ephraim shall not envy Judah and Judah, etc." (Isaiah 11:13),
שֶׁכֵּן קַיִן קִנֵּא בְּהֶבֶל.
for so Cain envied Abel.
דְּגַם יוֹסֵף וִיהוּדָה נֶגֶד ב' אוֹתִיּוֹת אֵלּוּ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רנ"ז,
For Joseph and Judah likewise correspond to these two letters as noted above in section 257,
וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת ר"נ דִּבְזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף שְׁכִיחַ רְצִיחָה].
and as mentioned above in section 250 that bloodshed is prevalent in the seed of Joseph].
וְזֶהוּ חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And this lies outside the camp of Israel;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם בּוֹ יֵשׁ צוֹרֶךְ,
yet nevertheless it too possesses a necessary purpose,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר שָׁם (קס עַמּוּד א) דִּבְאוֹת הַקּוֹ״ף הָיוּ יְרִיעוֹת עִזִּים בַּמִּשְׁכָּן,
as written in the Zohar there (160a) that with the letter Kuf were made the goat-hair curtains in the Mishkan,
בְּסוֹד "וְאֵת עֹרֹת גְּדָיֵי הָעִזִּים הִלְבִּישָׁה וְגוֹמֵר", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
in the mystery of "and she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, etc." (Genesis 27:16), see there,
שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵשָׂו – רְצִיחָה,
which in truth stems from the side of Esau—bloodshed,
רַק יֵשׁ צוֹרֶךְ לְהַלְבִּישׁ בּוֹ לְקַבֵּל בִּרְכוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
only that it is necessary to enclothe oneself in it to receive the blessings of this physical world.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Terumah 78:760-763: “The same pattern applies below. What is written below? “Adam knew his wife Eve, and she conceived and bore Cain.” Qof began to give birth within her, through Adam’s strength and assistance, after she had received impurity from that qof. Therefore it does not say here “he begot,” but “he knew,” “she conceived,” and “she bore,” and dross emerged within the female. “She continued to bear his brother Abel”: here too it does not say “he begot,” although he came from the male side. But the accuser grew weak and its strength was broken, for the letters had begun giving birth with qof. Once the dross was separated, the letters began to give birth through the mystery of the letters shin-tav: the rectification of male and female in agreement together. Then it is written, “He begot in his likeness, according to his image, and he called his name Seth”; it does not say “she called.” He called, not she: he called his name Seth, the rectification of male and female together in one accord. The letters then revolved again, returning to bring forth the alef of Adam and the letters at the place where his name ends. Which is it? Nun; afterward vav, not heh, for heh had already become pregnant with Abel [another reading: had already been born in Abel]. Therefore it took the following letter, vav, and concluded with the initial of Seth, shin, and he was called Enosh.”

p: וְהַיְינוּ כִּי יֵשׁ מִצְוָה "וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע וְגוֹמֵר" בְּחַיָּיבֵי מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין,
And this is because there is a commandment to "purge the evil from your midst" (Deuteronomy 17:7) regarding those liable to court execution,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סג) בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "אַדְמוֹנִי עִם יְפֵה עֵינַיִם – מִדַּעַת סַנְהֶדְרִין".
and as stated (Bereishit Rabbah 63) regarding King David: "Ruddy, with fine eyes—executing capital justice with the sanction of the Sanhedrin."
וְעַל זֶה בָּאָדָם עַצְמוֹ הוּא עִנְיַן "יַרְגִּיז יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע"
And concerning this within the individual himself is the counsel "let a person incite the good inclination against the evil inclination" (Berakhot 5a)
בְּרוֹגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן דְּטָב.
with the constructive anger of the Torah scholars.
וּכְמוֹ אַבַּיֵּי דִּמְכַפֵּין נַפְשֵׁיהּ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שַׁבָּת לג סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
And like Abaye who afflicted himself with fasting (Shabbat 33a end)
וְיוֹשֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית בִּדְמָצֵי לְצַעוֹרֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ (תַּעֲנִית יא רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב),
and fasting as much as he could endure (Ta'anit 11b),
זֶהוּ כִּרְצִיחָה וְאֵינוֹ "גּוֹמֵל נַפְשׁוֹ אִישׁ חָסֶד".
which resembles murder, seemingly failing to "reward his own soul like a merciful man" (Proverbs 11:17).
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא לְהַכְנָעַת הָרַע דְּתַאֲוָה, אֵינוֹ קָרוּי "עוֹכֵר שְׁאֵרוֹ אַכְזָרִי",
Only when undertaken to subdue the evil of lust, he is not termed "a cruel one who troubles his own flesh,"
כִּי אַדְּרַבָּה, הוּא מְרַחֵם עַל כָּל גּוּפוֹ.
for on the contrary, he shows ultimate mercy to his entire body.
וְכֵן כָּל חַיָּיבֵי מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין לו:): "אֵין מוֹשִׁיבִין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין זָקֵן וְסָרִיס וְכוּלֵי",
And likewise regarding judges of capital cases our Sages taught (Sanhedrin 36b): "We do not seat on the Sanhedrin an old man or a eunuch, etc.,"
כִּי הֵם בֶּאֱמֶת מְרַחֲמִים עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת,
because true judges are genuinely merciful toward creations,
רַק הַלְּבוּשׁ אַכְזָרִיּוּת;
only that the outer garment is harshness;
וְהוּא כִּסּוּי לַמִּשְׁכָּן דְּגִילּוּי אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and it serves as a protective covering for the Tabernacle of Hashem's light,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי הֶעְדֵּר תַּאֲוָה שֶׁהוּא הַמַּחְשִׁיךְ אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
which shines only through the negation of lust which darkens the divine light.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Tetzaveh 6:57-58: “If you say: What of the anger of the sages? The anger of the sages is good in every respect, for we have learned that Torah is fire, and Torah heats him, as it is written, “Is not My word like fire, declares the Lord?” The anger of the sages is in matters of Torah; the anger of the sages is to give honor to Torah, and it is all for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore it is said, “For the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.” But if it concerns other matters, this is not service of the Holy One. Among all the sins a person commits, none is actual idolatry like this, and one may not approach such a person. If you say: It was only momentary, and after it passed he returned—this is not so. Once he uprooted the holiness of his soul from himself and its place, that foreign god seizes the place, grows strong in him, and does not leave him, unless he purifies himself completely, uproots it forever, and afterward strives to sanctify himself and draw holiness upon himself. Then, if only he becomes sanctified! Rabbi Yosei said to him: He does indeed become sanctified. [Another reading: “Why? Has the foreign power not been expelled and the person sanctified?”]”

p: וּלְאוֹתוֹ סִכְלוּת מְעָט צָרִיךְ כִּסּוּי מֵהַרְגָּזַת יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע,
And for that minimal necessary folly one requires a covering from inciting the good inclination over the evil,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לְקַבֵּל בְּרָכוֹת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן,
and through this he is empowered to receive the blessings of this world as well,
שֶׁהוּא בְּאוֹת הַקּוֹ״ף, שֶׁהוּא הָעוּבָּר הָרוֹמֵז לְמִילּוּי תַּאֲוַות עוֹלָם הַזֶּה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רנ"ז.
which resides in the letter Kuf—the embryo signifying the fulfillment of worldly desires as noted in section 257.
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת בְּכֹחַ הַהַרְגָּזָה,
For through enclothing oneself in the power of holy anger,
וְשֶׁהוּא מוּכָן לִמְנוֹעַ מֵעַצְמוֹ חֶמְדָּה מַה שֶּׁזּוּלַת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and being prepared to withhold from himself any desire outside the will of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְלֹא לְקַבֵּל רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— and to receive nothing other than that which is Hashem's will—
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוּכָן לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ כָּל מִינֵי חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן.
through this Hashem is prepared to bestow upon him all varieties of worldly pleasures as well.

sections.en: Faith as the Root of Every Good Thing

p: [רנט] כְּמוֹ שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל דָּבָר טוֹב הוּא הָאֱמוּנָה, שֶׁבּוֹ פָּתְחָה הַתּוֹרָה "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר" שֶׁלֹּא בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיוּוּי,
Just as the root of every good thing is faith, with which the Torah opened at Sinai: "I am Hashem your God" (Exodus 20:2), not phrased as a command,
וְיָדוּעַ גַּם כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, ז עַמּוּד ב; יא עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "זֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַה' צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ",
and as is known from the Zohar (I 7b, 11b) on the verse "This is the gate of Hashem, the righteous shall enter into it" (Psalms 118:20),
דְּתַרְעָא הוּא מִדַּת הָאֱמוּנָה;
that this gateway is the attribute of Faith (Malchut);
כָּךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל דָּבָר רַע הוּא לֵיצָנוּת, שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ הָאֱמוּנָה, שֶׁהוּא מִתְלוֹצֵץ מִכָּל דָּבָר.
so too the root of every evil thing is mockery (leitzanut), the antithesis of faith, which scoffs at everything.
וְזֶה טַעַם "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק",
And this explains why "Amalek was the first of the nations" (Numbers 24:20),
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כז) עַל פָּסוּק "לֵץ תַּכֶּה" – זֶה עֲמָלֵק, "וּפֶתִי יַעְרִם" – זֶה יִתְרוֹ.
as expounded in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 27) on the verse "Smite a scorner" (Proverbs 19:25)—this is Amalek; "and the simple will become prudent"—this is Jethro.
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּפֶתִי הוּא הַמַּאֲמִין בַּכֹּל, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "פֶּתִי יַאֲמִין לְכָל דָּבָר",
And I heard that a 'peti' (simple one) is one who believes anything, as it is written: "The simple believes every word" (Proverbs 14:15),
וְיִתְרוֹ לֹא הִנִּיחַ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמְּכִילְתָּא) שֶׁהֶאֱמִין בַּכֹּל;
and Jethro left no idol unworshiped (Mekhilta) because he believed in everything;
וְלוֹ יֵשׁ תַּקָּנָה שֶׁיַּעֲרִים לְהַאֲמִין בַּה' אֱמֶת עַל יְדֵי הַכָּאַת הַלֵּץ, שֶׁהוּא שֶׁאֵין מַאֲמִין כְּלָל.
and for him there is remedy—that he become wise to believe in the true God through the smiting of the scorner who believes in nothing.
וְזֶה רֵאשִׁית וְהַתְחָלָה לְכָל כִּיתּוֹת הָרַע דְּגוֹיִם,
And this is the primary starting point for all factions of evil among the nations,
וּכְטַעַם "שְׂחוֹק וְקַלּוּת רֹאשׁ מַרְגִּילִין לְעֶרְוָה" (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג).
mirroring: "Laughter and levity habituate a person to immorality" (Avot 3:13).

paragraphs.text: Chanukah traces Amalek’s dismissal of revelation to pride that refuses to allow any reality beyond its own understanding.

rich.text: Chanukah traces Amalek’s dismissal of revelation to pride that refuses to allow any reality beyond its own understanding.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 2:1: “All the nations heard, ‘Peoples tremble’: after seeing open, explicit miracles they could not deny them. But Amalek, through mockery, dismissed everything and denied it. This comes from pride: in his eyes it is impossible that anything should be hidden from his intellect and above his apprehension. Through this he becomes a scoffer and denies everything by mockery. This is ‘Amalek is the first of the nations,’ the beginning of the husk, for the root of the serpent’s enticement was ‘You will be like God.’ This is the utmost pride, as said concerning Nebuchadnezzar and Hiram, and it is the root of the evil inclination.”

This is ‘Amalek is the first of the nations,’ the beginning of the husk, for the root of the serpent’s enticement was ‘You will be like God.’ This is the utmost pride, as said concerning Nebuchadnezzar and Hiram, and it is the root of the evil inclination.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The Chanukah passage explains the inward mechanism of the mockery called a root of evil here: it refuses the possibility that something can be true while exceeding the observer’s comprehension. This sharpens the siman’s distinction between Yisro’s misdirected readiness to believe and Amalek’s rejection of belief itself. The former can be corrected toward truth; the latter first blocks the receptivity through which correction could enter. Faith here is therefore joined to humility, rather than to indiscriminate acceptance.

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef places the same verse about Amalek and Yisro within an account of separating the good from the evil mixed with it. This clarifies why the siman can distinguish the simple person's misdirected belief from the scoffer's obstruction of belief: openness has something that can be redirected, but it still needs clarification toward truth. The surrounding incense discussion preserves the good capable of giving fragrance rather than identifying every existing mixture with its final condition.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 27:6: “Another matter, “Yitro…heard,” that is what is written: “Strike the cynic, and the naïf will become clever” (Proverbs 19:25). Likewise, it says: “With the punishment of a cynic, the naïf becomes wise” (Proverbs 21:11). Amalek and Yitro were consulted by Pharaoh. When Yitro saw that the Holy One blessed be He eliminated Amalek from this world and from the World to Come, he reconsidered and repented, as it is written above: “For I will expunge the memory of Amalek” (Exodus 17:14) and afterward: “Yitro heard.” He said: ‘I must go only to the God of Israel.’ From where do you derive that Amalek and the Midianites were enemies of Israel? As it is stated: The elders of Moav and the elders of Midian went” (Numbers 22:7). Likewise, “[Whenever Israel would sow,] the Midianites, Amalekites, and the people of the east [would come up against them. They would encamp against them and destroy the produce of the earth]” (Judges 6:3–4), and likewise, the wicked Bilam says: “He saw Amalek” (Numbers 24:20); that it did not change its ways. But when he saw that Yitro had repented, what did he say? “He saw the Kenite” (Numbers 24:21); this is analogous to a hunter who would hunt birds. He trapped the first. He came to trap the second. It went and sat on the statue of the king. The hunter stood bewildered by it. He said to it: ‘If I throw a rock at you, I will be liable to be executed. If I extend the reed, I am afraid that it might touch the king’s statue. I do not know what to say to you; rather, you fled to a fine place and were spared.’ So too, Bilam saw Yitro and Amalek in counsel. He stood [and looked] at Amalek and eradicated its name. He came to look at Yitro and found that he repented. He said to him: ‘You fled well.’ That is, “Mighty is your dwelling” (Numbers 24:21), like Abraham. That is, “strike the cynic,” this is Amalek; “and the naïf will become clever,” this is Yitro. “Rebuke the discerning” (Proverbs 19:25), this is Moses, whom Yitro admonished when he saw him sitting and judging Israel all day. He said to him: “Why are you sitting alone?” (Exodus 18:14). “You will wear away” (Exodus 18:18). He said to him: ‘Do not do it because it is my opinion, but rather, consult with the Holy One blessed be He,’ as it is stated: “Heed my voice, I will counsel you [and may God be with you]” (Exodus 18:19). What is written thereafter? “Moses heeded his father-in-law, and he performed everything that he had said” (Exodus 18:24).”

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Exodus, Yitro 3: ““Jethro heard.” In the Midrash: This is what is written, “Strike a scoffer and the naive person becomes discerning.” “Strike a scoffer”—this is Amalek; “the naive person becomes discerning”—this is Jethro. A scoffer is one who mocks something true, whereas a naive person believes everything. In truth, neither is good. Yet of the scoffer it says, “Strike,” because he will not come to recognize his deficiency and correct it, since he mocks every true matter and does not listen at all. The naive person, however, who is persuaded by anything, can receive the truth and come to correct the root of his deficiency. Therefore we were commanded to erase Amalek, for no good will emerge from him. Jethro, however, sought to know the ultimate good, but at first believed in the worship of stars and constellations and in vanities. Afterward, when he saw the exaltedness of God, he said, “Now I know that the Lord is great,” and converted.”

p: כִּי לֵיצָנוּת חָלוּק לִבְנַיִם:
For mockery is divided into two aspects:
בְּ"שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה" הַיְינוּ פְּרִיקַת עוֹל לֵילֵךְ בִּשְׁרִירוּת לִבּוֹ, זֶה נִקְרָא קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ,
in passive non-action ('sit and do not do'), it is the casting off of the yoke to walk in the arbitrariness of one's heart, which is called levity;
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בִּבְרָכוֹת ל:): "אֵין עוֹמְדִין לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֶלָּא בְּכֹבֶד רֹאשׁ",
and concerning this they taught (Berakhot 30b): "One may stand to pray only out of solemn gravity (koved rosh),"
דְּהַיְינוּ קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע הַקּוֹדֶמֶת,
namely the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven's sovereignty during the preceding Shema,
דְּעַל יְדֵי פְּרִיקַת עוֹל הוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ מִתְּפִלָּה הַנִּמְשֶׁכֶת מֵאֱמוּנָה.
for casting off the yoke is the antithesis of prayer which flows directly from faith.
דְּלָכֵן נִקְבַּע בַּשַּׁ״ס בִּתְחִלַּת סֵדֶר אֱמוּנוֹת,
Therefore prayer is codified in the Talmud at the beginning of the Order of Zera'im (Faith),
וְכַיָּדוּעַ דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּתְפִלָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (יח.): "כֵּיוָן שֶׁבָּא דָּוִד בָּאת תְּפִלָּה",
and as is known, King David, peace be upon him, represents the rung of prayer, as stated in Megillah (18a): "Once David came, prayer came,"
פֵּירוּשׁ דְּעַל יְדֵי בִּרְכַּת "אֶת צֶמַח דָּוִד" נִפְעָל תֵּיכֶף צְמִיחַת יְשׁוּעָה
meaning that through the blessing 'the sprout of David' there is immediately effected the flourishing of salvation
וְהַרְגָּשַׁת דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּלֵּב, וּבָאת גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁזּוֹ הִיא מַדְרֵגָתוֹ.
and the spiritual sensation of King David's rung in the heart, and there arrives likewise the rung of prayer which is his unique level.
וְזֶהוּ צְמִיחַת דָּוִד – לְהַצְמִיחַ כֹּחוֹ וּמִדָּתוֹ בַּלֵּב, וְהוּא הַתְּפִלָּה,
And this is the sprouting of David—to germinate his power and attribute within the heart, which is prayer,
וּמִדָּתוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִדַּת הָאֱמוּנָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
and his attribute is likewise the attribute of Faith, as is known.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 31a:10: “Reish Lakish said: What is meant by the verse, “The faithfulness of your times shall be a store of salvation, wisdom and knowledge”? “Faithfulness”—this is the Order of Seeds. “Your times”—this is the Order of Festivals. “A store”—this is the Order of Women. “Salvation”—this is the Order of Damages. “Wisdom”—this is the Order of Sacred Things. “And knowledge”—this is the Order of Purities. Even so, “Fear of the Lord is its treasure.””

p: וַעֲמָלֵק הוּא נֶגֶד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמִדַּת אֱמוּנָה,
And Amalek stands directly opposite King David and the attribute of faith,
כְּמוֹ עֵשָׂו נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִדַּת אֱמֶת.
just as Esau stands opposite our father Jacob and the attribute of truth.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּבֵית דָּוִד – דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה:
And just as there exist within the Davidic Dynasty both David and Solomon:
דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּכֹבֶד רֹאשׁ וּתְפִלָּה בְּיִחוּד,
King David is specifically the spiritual rung of solemnity and prayer,
וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ אֱמוּנָה דְּ"אָנֹכִי" עַד דְּלָא שַׁיָּיךְ בּוֹ מִצְוָה כְּלָל,
while King Solomon is the root of the absolute faith of "I am Hashem" where external commandment is not even applicable,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ "אָנֹכִי" דְּאֵינוֹ בִּלְשׁוֹן צִיוּוּי רַק שֶׁהוּא כָּךְ,
just as the foundation of "I am" is not phrased as a command but simply states reality;
וְלָכֵן אָמַר: "אֲנִי אַרְבֶּה וְלֹא אָסוּר וְכוּלֵי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין כא:).
and therefore Solomon said: "I will multiply and not turn aside, etc." (Sanhedrin 21b).
כָּךְ נֶגֶד זֶה בָּרַע:
So facing this in the realm of evil:
קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ, וּשְׂחוֹק שֶׁהוּא בְּ"קוּם וַעֲשֵׂה" – הוֹלֵלוּת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה,
are levity, and laughter which is in active commission ('arise and do')—namely practical frivolous madness,
כְּמוֹ: "כְּמִתְלַהְלֵהַּ וְגוֹמֵר הֲלֹא מְשַׂחֵק אָנִי" (מִשְׁלֵי כו, יח-יט),
as in: "Like a madman who throws firebrands... and says: Am I not joking?" (Proverbs 26:18-19);
"יוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם יִשְׂחָק, ה' יִלְעַג לָמוֹ".
"He who sits in heaven shall laugh, the Lord shall mock them" (Psalms 2:4).
וְנֶאֱמַר בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם "מְשַׂחֲקִים וְגוֹמֵר",
And it is written concerning David: "rejoicing/playing, etc." (II Samuel 6:5),
הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ הַלֵּצִים שֶׁעוֹשִׂים דְּבָרִים מְשׁוּנִּים;
referring to actions resembling those of jesters who do unusual things;
וּבִלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים: "מְשַׂחֵק בְּקֻבְיָא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין כד:) וּ"מְשַׂחֵק בַּתִּינֹקֶת" (נִדָּה יג:),
and in rabbinic phrasing: "one who plays with dice (gambles)" (Sanhedrin 24b) and "plays with an infant" (Niddah 13b),
פֵּירוּשׁ פְּעוּלָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ אֱמֶת וּלְתַכְלִית, רַק לִשְׂחוֹק בְּעָלְמָא.
meaning an act that lacks enduring truth and constructive purpose, engaged merely for frivolous diversion.
וְהֵיפֶךְ זֶה חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאָמַר: "לִשְׂחוֹק אָמַרְתִּי מְהוֹלָל וְגוֹמֵר",
And the reverse of this was the wisdom of Solomon who declared: "Of laughter I said: It is mad, etc." (Ecclesiastes 2:2),
כִּי כָּל חָכְמָתוֹ הוּא לְחַבֵּר אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה בְּיַחַד כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר תְּרוּמָה (קמה עַמּוּד א),
for his whole wisdom was to bind truth and faith together as written in Zohar Terumah (145a),
וְכָל פְּעוּלוֹתָיו דְּבַר אֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ וְלֹא לַעֲשׂוֹת לִפְנִים וְלִבּוֹ בַּל עִמּוֹ.
and all his deeds were authentic truth, never acting hypocritically for outward appearance while his heart remained detached.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Terumah 31:343-347: “Moses rose upward in his praise. His praise was to give praises and thanks to the supernal King, who rescued Israel and performed miracles and mighty deeds for them in Egypt and at the sea. But King David and Solomon his son sang in another manner. David labored to prepare the maidens and adorn them together with the Queen, so that the Queen and her maidens would appear in beauty. He therefore labored in their songs and praises until he had prepared and adorned all the maidens and the Queen. When Solomon came, he found the Queen adorned and her maidens in beauty. He labored to bring her to the bridegroom, brought the bridegroom into the bridal canopy with the Queen, and introduced words of love between them, to join them as one and bring both into one completeness, in complete affection. Thus Solomon rose in supernal praise above all people. Moses united the Queen in this world below, so that she would be in this world in complete union among those below. Solomon united the Queen in complete union above: first he brought the bridegroom into the bridal canopy; afterward he brought them both into this world and welcomed them in joy in the Temple he built. If you ask how Moses brought the Queen alone into this world, which appears to be separation: come and see. The Holy One, blessed be He, first united her with Moses, and she was Moses’ bride, as has been said. Once she was united with Moses, she descended into this world in its union and was established here as she had not been before. She was never in separation. But from the day Adam was created, no person introduced love, affection, and words of union above except King Solomon, who first established the union above and afterward welcomed them together into the house he prepared for them. Fortunate are David and Solomon his son, who established the union above. From the day the Holy One, blessed be He, told the moon, “Go and diminish yourself,” she was not united with the sun in complete union until King Solomon came.”

items.h: Haman’s accusation and the month of Adar

p: וַעֲמָלֵק כּוֹלֵל שְׁנֵיהֶם,
And Amalek embodies both forms of evil,
כִּי רֵאשִׁית הָרַע הוּא בְּסוֹף הַטּוֹב, כְּטַעַם "רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת",
for the beginning of evil borders the lowest edge of the good, as in "Her feet go down to death" (Proverbs 5:5),
הַיְינוּ דְּמִמְּקוֹם הַכְּנִיסָה לַטּוֹבָה שֶׁהוּא מִלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה,
meaning that from the entry-point into goodness which ascends from below to Above,
מִשָּׁם יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן הַתְחָלַת כְּנִיסָה לָרַע שֶׁהַתְחָלָתוֹ מִלְּמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה.
from there also starts the entry into evil which descends downward from Above.
וְהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית הַמַּרְגִּיל לְכָל מִינֵי רַע דְּכָל מִינֵי אוּמּוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ.
And he is the 'first' who habituates humanity to all forms of evil among the other nations later on.
וְזֶה כֹּחַ קִטְרוּג הָמָן עַל מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁלֹּא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים,
And this was the force of Haman's accusation over Israel's bowing to the Babylonian image—that they acted outwardly—
כִּי כָּל כֹּחוֹ הוּא בִּפְעוּלוֹת דְּלִפְנִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת.
for his entire demonic power resides in hypocritical external actions that lack internal truth.
וּבָחַר בְּחוֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר שֶׁנֶּגֶד הַקּוֹ״ף שֶׁבּוֹ נִבְרָא הַשְּׂחוֹק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה;
And he selected the month of Adar which corresponds to the letter Kuf through which laughter was created, as written in Sefer Yetzirah;
וּבֶאֱמֶת הָיָה הוּא לִשְׂחוֹק,
and in truth he himself was turned into a laughingstock,
וְרַק לִפְנִים כָּל גְּזֵירָה שֶׁלּוֹ, דִּבְאֶמֶת "נַהֲפוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי", וּכְכֹחַ חוֹדֶשׁ זֶה.
and his decree was purely superficial, for in internal reality "it was reversed to the opposite," according to the latent holy power of this month.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה יג:): "וְלֹא יָדַע כִּי בְּז' בַּאֲדָר מֵת וְכוּלֵי",
And this is what they taught (Megillah 13b): "and he did not know that on the seventh of Adar Moses died, etc.,"
פֵּירוּשׁ, דְּדַרְגָּא דְּדָוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה יָדַע דִּכְבָר נֶחְרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְנִפְסְקָה מַלְכוּתָן,
meaning that regarding the royal rung of David and Solomon, Haman knew that the Temple was destroyed and their dynasty suspended,
הֲרֵי נִפְסַק מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת וְאֵין לָנוּ שִׁיּוּר רַק הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת, דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
such that the manifest attribute of Malchut had ceased, leaving us only this Torah—the spiritual rung of Moses our teacher;
וּבְיָמָיו צָמַח עֲמָלֵק.
and during Moses' lifetime Amalek first emerged.

p: וּלְעוֹלָם צְמִיחוֹת הָרַע כְּנֶגֶד צְמִיחוֹת הַטּוֹב כַּנּוֹדָע;
And eternally the sproutings of evil mirror the sproutings of good, as is known;
וְעֵשָׂו, שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשֶּׁקֶר וַאֲחִיזָה בְּעָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא,
and Esau, who is the root of falsehood and attachment to this World of Falsehood,
בִּימֵי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ אֱמֶת וְהֵיפוּךְ עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַמָּשׁ.
emerged alongside our father Jacob who is the root of truth and the complete antithesis of worldly illusion.
רַק "יָדוֹ אֹחֶזֶת בַּעֲקֵב" וּבְסוֹף הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
Only that Jacob's "hand took hold on Esau's heel" (Genesis 25:26) and the extreme end of this world,
וְלָכֵן נִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד תֵּיכֶף בְּמִצְרַיִם, שֶׁהָעֶבֶד אֵין לוֹ הֲרָמַת רֹאשׁ כְּלָל וְהֵיפֶךְ חֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְגַמְרֵי.
wherefore his descendants were immediately enslaved in Egypt, for a slave has no proud standing at all and is wholly divorced from worldly luxury.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא גּוֹאֵל הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהִתְחִיל לְהוֹצִיא בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְחֵירוּת,
And Moses our teacher was the first redeemer who began to bring Israel out to freedom,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם תּוֹקֶף גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
so that they would possess strength and standing within this physical world as well,
רַק הַגְּמָר הוּא עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד,
yet the ultimate completion is through Mashiach ben David,
וְדָוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָיוּ מֵעֵין מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד.
and David and Solomon in this world who were a foretaste of Mashiach ben David.

items.h: Moses and inward truth

p: וְהַתְחָלַת זֶה בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הִתְחִיל גַּם כֵּן בְּיִחוּד אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה,
And the inception of this within Moses began likewise through the unification of truth and faith,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ בְּדַעַת – הַיְינוּ יְדִיעַת פְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁהַכֹּל אֱמֶת,
and this operated through his spiritual rung of Da'at—meaning the inward awareness that all is divine Truth,
כַּנּוֹדָע דְּ"מֹשֶׁה מִלְּגָאו, יַעֲקֹב מִלְּבָר" (תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן יג).
as is known: "Moses is internal, Jacob is external" (Tikkunei Zohar 13).
וּמִצַּד חִיצוֹנִיוּת הָאֱמֶת וַדַּאי אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא הִיפּוּכוֹ,
And from the perspective of external truth, it has no compatibility with this world which is its opposite;
וְאֵיךְ יִדְבַּק בַּשֶּׁקֶר?
for how could truth cling to falsehood?
אַךְ מִצַּד הַדַּעַת, הַפְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁל כָּל דָּבָר, וְיָדַע שֶׁהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא שֶׁקֶר,
However, from the perspective of Da'at, the inner core of everything, knowing that this physical world is illusory—
עַל יְדֵי יְדִיעָה זוֹ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת "אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ",
through this awareness that in ultimate truth "there is none else beside Him,"
וְהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמַּעֲלִים אֲמִיתָּתוֹ שֶׁקֶר,
and that this world which conceals His reality is mere falsehood—
מִמֵּילָא גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵינוֹ דָּבוּק בַּשֶּׁקֶר,
automatically even while dwelling within this world he does not cling to falsehood;
וְזֶהוּ פְּנִימִיּוּת הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהוּא גַּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
and this is the inward truth that permeates even this earthly realm.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Parshat Shekalim 1:2: “Therefore they said, “Jacob outwardly, Moses inwardly.” Jacob’s soul includes all the souls of Israel, since they are all his descendants and part of his soul; the totality of their souls is included in him. Moses our teacher belongs to the mystery of knowledge—as is known, this is why the wilderness generation is called the generation of knowledge, as the Midrash on Hukkat explains concerning Darda—for he includes all the souls in respect of knowledge, the inward dimension of the soul. As is known, when the ten sefirot are considered in their outward aspect, knowledge is not counted among them. It is counted only in their inward aspect, where the crown is not counted, since it is called “nothingness”: the skull and the place of the head-tefillin, above the brain and wisdom, the beginning of emergence from nothing into something. Inwardly, in what is accessible to a person, knowledge therefore fills the place of the crown. Rashi explains “and with knowledge” in Ki Tisa as divine inspiration: an apprehension above the wisdom in the brain and beyond its bounds. Thus Moses our teacher is the inward dimension of all the souls of Israel: the apprehension of knowledge that comes from the soul’s root and source in the letters of Torah. It is the knowledge within the souls of Israel in every generation.”

p: וּמִיתַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מוֹרָה כִּי בְּחוֹדֶשׁ זֶה כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲלִים פְּנִימִיּוּת הָאֱמֶת,
And the passing of Moses our teacher shows that in this month there rules the force that conceals the inner truth,
וְהַיְינוּ אוֹת הַקּוֹ״ף, שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר, שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַשְּׂחוֹק וְלֵיצָנוּת
— namely the letter Kuf, which is the root of the inclination, embodying the power of laughter and mockery—
דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא לִפְנִים וְאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת.
a matter that exists only for outward show and lacks substance.
וּבֶאֱמֶת אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ עַצְמוֹ הוּא הַמּוֹלִיד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
Yet in truth, that very same force is what gives birth to Moses our teacher,
עַל יְדֵי יְדִיעָה זוֹ שֶׁכָּל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְחֶמְדּוֹתָיו שְׂחוֹק וְלֵיצָנוּת.
through the deep realization that this entire world and its appetites are mere frivolity and mockery.
וּמִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה הָמָן וּגְזֵירוֹתָיו לִשְׂחוֹק וְלֵיצָנוּת וְאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת.
Consequently through this, Haman and his decrees were rendered into a joke and mockery, possessing no truth.
וְהוּא קָבַע גְּזֵירָתוֹ בְּי״ג, ז' יָמִים אַחַר ז' אֲדָר,
And he fixed his genocidal decree for the thirteenth of Adar, seven days after the seventh of Adar,
שֶׁחָשַׁב כִּי הַתְחָלַת כֹּחוֹ וְהַשְׁלָמַת כָּל דָּבָר בְּז' יָמִים שֶׁהֵם ז' יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן כַּנּוֹדָע,
for he calculated that the beginning of his power and the completion of every process occurs within seven days—which are the seven building days of Creation,
וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ חִיּוּב כְּלָיָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁהוּא עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה, מִצַּד הַמַּעֲשֶׂה דִּלְפָנִים.
and thus there would be an obligation of total annihilation, Heaven forbid, against Israel from the perspective of this world (the realm of Asiyah) on account of their outward deeds.
וּבֶאֱמֶת בּוֹ הַגִּלּוּי דְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה עוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִפְנִים
Yet in truth, on that day came the disclosure that all deeds of this world are merely outward show
[וְהוּא בְּז' אֲדָר גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד ז' יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן מֵהַתְחָלַת חוֹדֶשׁ זֶה שֶׁהוּא בְּכֹחַ עַד גְּמַר יְצִיאַת כֹּחַ זֶה לַפּוֹעַל דְּהַיְינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּחַ;

[and this on the seventh of Adar likewise corresponds to the seven building days from the beginning of the month when it is potential until the full emergence into actuality, which is the root of the power;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַיְצִיאָה מִן הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לַגְּמָר גַּם כֵּן ז' יָמִים, כִּי כָּל דָּבָר יְצִיאָה לַגְּמָר מִכֹּחַ לַפּוֹעַל צָרִיךְ ז' יָמִים כַּנּוֹדָע].
and afterward the transition from the root to full completion also requires seven days, for every actualization requires seven days, as is known].

items.h: From the Fast of Esther to Purim

p: וּלְכָךְ פּוּרִים בְּי״ד אַחַר גְּמַר הַז' יָמִים,
Therefore Purim is celebrated on the fourteenth, immediately following the completion of these seven days,
בְּהַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה דְּכָל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שְׂחוֹק
— in clear, vivid recognition that this entire physical world is vanity and sport—
זֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת נִבְדָּל מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
which is the exact spiritual level of Moses our teacher, who was truly detached from all worldly matters.
וְזֶה טַעַם תַּעֲנִית אֶסְתֵּר בְּי״ג,
And this explains the Fast of Esther on the thirteenth,
אַחַר כָּךְ הוּא פּוּרִים דְּ"חַיָּיב לִבְסוֹמֵי",
and immediately afterward arrives Purim where one is "obligated to become intoxicated,"
דַּרְגָּא דִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "תַּרְתִּי בְלִבִּי וְגוֹמֵר בַּיַּיִן וְגוֹמֵר",
which reflects the level of King Solomon: "I searched in my heart how to stimulate my flesh with wine, etc." (Ecclesiastes 2:3),
שֶׁעַל זֶה רִידְּתוֹ אִמּוֹ כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין ע:).
concerning which his mother chastised him, as our Sages expounded (Sanhedrin 70b).
וְ"עַד דְּלָא יָדַע" – הַיְינוּ הֶעְדֵּר הַדַּעַת דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And "until he knows not" signifies the transcendence of the conscious Da'at of Moses,
כִּי מַדְרֵגַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם בְּלֹא דַּעַת וְחָכְמָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּמִצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים;
for the ultimate rung of King Solomon is to remain cleaved to Hashem, blessed be He, even beyond intellect, wisdom, and active striving in commandments and good deeds;
וְכָל חָכְמָתוֹ הִשִּׂיג בַּחֲלוֹם, שֶׁהוּא בְּעֵת הִסְתַּלְּקוּת הַדַּעַת לְגַמְרֵי.
and all his profound wisdom he received in a dream (I Kings 3:5), which is precisely at the hour when conscious intellect has completely departed.

sections.en: Two Forms of Laughter and Their Rectification

p: [רס] ב' מִינֵי שְׂחוֹק הֵם:
There are two varieties of laughter:
הָאֶחָד – שֶׁשּׂוֹחֵק מֵאֵיזֶה בְּרִיָּה,
the first is when one laughs at some creature,
כְּעִנְיַן "שְׂחֹק לְרֵעֵהוּ אֶהְיֶה", וְזֶהוּ לֵיצָנוּת.
along the lines of "I am become as one that is a mockery to his neighbor" (Job 12:4), and this is scornful mockery.
וְצַד הַהֶיתֵּר שֶׁבּוֹ – לֵיצָנוּתָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
And the permitted dimension within it is the mockery of idolatry,
וְזֶה נִזְכַּר בְּמַסֶּכֶת מְגִילָּה (כה:)
and this is mentioned in Tractate Megillah (25b),
כִּי זֶה עִנְיַן יוֹם הַפּוּרִים,
for this is the very essence of the day of Purim,
שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן הַשְּׂחוֹק דַּאֲדָר,
which is the rectification of the laughter of Adar,
שֶׁלָּכֵן מִנְהַג יִשְׂרָאֵל לַעֲשׂוֹת בּוֹ מִינֵי שְׂחוֹק וְלֵיצָנוּת מֵהָמָן,
which is why the custom of Israel is to make types of laughter and jesting regarding Haman,
שֶׁהָיָה הוּא לִשְׂחוֹק תַּחַת שְׂחוֹק הַכְּסִיל שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לְפִי שָׁעָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
so that he was turned into a laughingstock in place of the laughter of the fool which he temporarily held over Israel.
וְלָאו דַּוְוקָא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
And it does not mean exclusively idolatry,
כִּי כָּל השס"ה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה הֵם עֲנָפִים מִ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
for all 365 negative prohibitions are branches extending from "You shall have no other gods",
וְכָל מִינֵי רַע נִקְרָא עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
and every kind of evil is termed idolatry.
וְאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין פא.):
And they said (Kiddushin 81a):
"רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִתְלוֹצֵץ בְּעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה",
“Rabbi Meir would mock transgressors,”
רַק דְּשָׁם אָמַר לוֹ: "אִי לָאו דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אַתְּ וְכוּלֵי",
except that there Satan said to him: “Were it not that you are Rabbi Meir, etc.,”
כִּי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ נָקִי גַּם כֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ,
for in a matter where the person himself is not completely clean,
אֵין לוֹ לְהִתְלוֹצֵץ מִן הָאַחֵר,
he must not mock another,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁגַּם הוּא עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ נָקִי מִזֶּה אָתֵי לְאַגְרוֹיֵי בֵּיהּ.
since he too is not yet cleansed from it and will come to incite the evil inclination against himself.
רַק מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גְּמוּרָה, דִּכְבָר בִּטְּלוּ לְיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
Only from actual idolatry, where the inclination for idolatry has already been eradicated from Israel,
מִזֶּה יוּכַל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לְהִתְלוֹצֵץ.
can every single Jew freely mock.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 13:1: “The month of Adar was formed through the letter qof, as Sefer Yetzirah says: “He made the letter qof reign over laughter…and through it formed fish in the world.” It appears to me that this means, “This Leviathan You formed to play with,” from which comes laughter above, as stated at the beginning of Avodah Zarah and in the chapter HaSefinah. Certainly the constellation Pisces in the heavens corresponds to Leviathan, chief of the fish of the sea. Adar in the year is the time when “we increase joy,” and laughter comes from it, for laughter is the opposite of weeping, as stated among the twenty-eight times in Ecclesiastes: one comes from sadness and mourning, and the other from abundant gladness and joy. It is an ancient custom to practice all kinds of play on Purim; see Sanhedrin concerning “like the Purim jumping” and Rashi there. The spleen in the person is the source of laughter, as stated in the chapter HaRo’eh. Both [laughter “with His creatures” and laughter “at His creatures”] are included, for these are two kinds of laughter: “with His creatures”—this is the play with Leviathan; and “at His creatures,” as stated in Avodah Zarah—this is the laughter of Purim at Haman’s downfall.”

rich.text: : “The month of Adar was formed through the letter qof, as Sefer Yetzirah says: “He made the letter qof reign over laughter…and through it formed fish in the world.” It appears to me that this means, “This Leviathan You formed to play with,” from which comes laughter above, as stated at the beginning of Avodah Zarah and in the chapter HaSefinah. Certainly the constellation Pisces in the heavens corresponds to Leviathan, chief of the fish of the sea. Adar in the year is the time when “we increase joy,” and laughter comes from it, for laughter is the opposite of weeping, as stated among the twenty-eight times in Ecclesiastes: one comes from sadness and mourning, and the other from abundant gladness and joy. It is an ancient custom to practice all kinds of play on Purim; see Sanhedrin concerning “like the Purim jumping” and Rashi there. The spleen in the person is the source of laughter, as stated in the chapter HaRo’eh. Both [laughter “with His creatures” and laughter “at His creatures”] are included, for these are two kinds of laughter: “with His creatures”—this is the play with Leviathan; and “at His creatures,” as stated in Avodah Zarah—this is the laughter of Purim at Haman’s downfall.”

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ג:)
Nevertheless, concerning the Holy One, blessed be He, they stated at the beginning of Avodah Zarah (3b)
דְּעַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו אֵינוֹ מְשַׂחֵק אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם.
that over His creatures He laughs only on that future Day.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (י:) דְּאָמַר: "מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי טוֹבְעִים וְכוּלֵי",
And that is like what is stated in Megillah (10b) where He said: “The work of My hands is drowning, etc.,”
וְהוּא אֵינוֹ שָׂשׂ אֲבָל אֲחֵרִים מֵשִׂישׂ.
and He does not rejoice, although He causes others to rejoice.
כִּי מִצִּידּוֹ קִילוּסוֹ עוֹלֶה מִן הָרְשָׁעִים,
For from His perspective His praise ascends even from the wicked,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵן גַּם כֵּן בְּרִיּוֹתָיו שֶׁהֲרֵי בּוֹרְאָן וּמְקַיְּימָן בְּכָל יוֹם,
since they too are His creatures whom He creates and sustains every day,
וְהִתְלוֹצְצוּת שַׁיָּיךְ רַק מִדָּבָר הַנִּבְדָּל מִמֶּנּוּ וְהוּא מוֹאֵס בּוֹ.
and mocking mockery applies only to something separate from oneself which one despises.
וְאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ זֶה,
And with Hashem, blessed be He, this is inapplicable,
כִּי אִם מוֹאֵס בּוֹ לֹא הָיָה לוֹ שׁוּם קִיּוּם כְּלָל.
for were He to utterly despise it, it would have no existence whatsoever.
רַק בְּאוֹתוֹ יוֹם, דְּאָז בֶּאֱמֶת יְבוֹעַר הָרַע מִן הָעוֹלָם
Only on that Day, when evil will truly be purged from the world
וִיסַלֵּק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חַיּוּתוֹ מֵהֶם בֶּאֱמֶת,
and the Holy One, blessed be He, will truly withdraw His vitality from them,
וְהֵם לֹא יַרְגִּישׁוּ בָּזֶה, "וְיֶהְגּוּ רִיק וְגוֹמֵר" –
while they will not perceive this, "and meditate a vain thing, etc.",
דָּבָר בָּטֵל וְרִיק, שֶׁיַּחְשְׁבוּ כְּמוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם קִיּוּם,
a futile and empty matter, imagining as in this world that they have enduring existence,
וּבֶאֱמֶת אָז הוּא זְמַן כִּלְיוֹן קִיּוּמָם לְגַמְרֵי
whereas in truth it is the time of the total annihilation of their existence
וְאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹצֶה בָּהֶם עוֹד וּמוֹאֵס בָּם
— and the Holy One desires them no longer and rejects them—
אָז יִהְיֶה הַשְּׂחוֹק לְפָנָיו עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו.
then will there be laughter before Him over His creatures.

paragraphs.text: Chanukah explains that Hashem wills the wicked to improve, even while those delivered from them can receive joy.

rich.text: Chanukah explains that Hashem wills the wicked to improve, even while those delivered from them can receive joy.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 19:2: “According to the Geonim’s reading, “the letter ayin with laughter”: our Sages indeed said that a person may not fill his mouth with laughter in this world. Rather, “with laughter” has the meaning we explained in the teaching, “He does not rejoice, but causes others to rejoice.” Although God does not rejoice in the downfall of the wicked—He would have wanted them not to perish, and their suffering to help them improve their ways—it nevertheless benefits Israel, whose blood was shed, by bringing them to joy. They attain this only when they attain an upright heart, without any inclination toward evil, as it says, “The upright, for joy.” At Chanukah they attained the light of Oral Torah; likewise, every Chanukah is a time to attain the shining of Oral Torah’s light in the heart. It is written, “The Lord’s precepts are upright, rejoicing the heart”: through the light of Oral Torah, one attains an upright heart and joy.”

They attain this only when they attain an upright heart, without any inclination toward evil, as it says, “The upright, for joy.” At Chanukah they attained the light of Oral Torah; likewise, every Chanukah is a time to attain the shining of Oral Torah’s light in the heart. paragraphs.text: Explanation: Chanukah develops the same distinction used in this siman—‘He does not rejoice, but causes others to rejoice’—by specifying the preferred outcome: that suffering lead to improved conduct rather than destruction. This explains why the siman bases Hashem’s relation to the wicked on His continuing creation and sustenance of them. Israel’s permitted joy is related to deliverance and an upright heart, not to a simple adoption of contempt for another created being.

items.h: Permitted playfulness and divine laughter

p: אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אֶצְלוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַשְּׂחוֹק עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו, עִם לִוְיָתָן, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
However, in this world, Hashem's laughter is with His creatures—with Leviathan, see there.
דְּיֵשׁ מִין הַב' דִּשְׂחוֹק, שֶׁהוּא הוֹלֵלוּת וּמַעֲשֵׂה נַעֲרוּת,
For there is the second kind of laughter, which is playful sport and youthful behavior,
כְּעִנְיַן "יָקוּמוּ נָא הַנְּעָרִים וִישַׂחֲקוּ לְפָנֵינוּ".
in the manner of "Let the young men now arise and play before us" (II Samuel 2:14).
וְצַד הַהֶיתֵּר שֶׁבּוֹ – לְצוֹרֶךְ מִצְוָה וּכְבוֹד שָׁמַיִם,
And the permitted dimension within it is for the sake of a mitzvah and the honor of Heaven,
וּכְעִנְיַן (שַׁבָּת ל:) "מִילְּתָא דִּבְדִיחוּתָא" וּבְדָחֵי רַבָּנָן קוֹדֶם הַלִּימּוּד,
and like the matter (Shabbat 30b) of a humorous joke with which he gladdened the Rabbis before study,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְרַחֵב הַלֵּב כַּאֲשֶׁר הַגּוּף בְּעַצְבוּת,
whereby the heart is broadened when the physical body is immersed in gloom,
וְצָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן לֵישֵׁב בְּאֵימְתָא בִּשְׁמַעְתָּא,
and he also needs to sit in reverent awe over the halakhic discourse,
וְאֵין יָכוֹל לִמְצוֹא בְּלִבּוֹ שִׂמְחָה אֲמִיתִּית
— and cannot immediately find authentic joy in his heart—
יוּכַל לְהַרְחִיב בִּשְׂחוֹק, שֶׁהוּא שִׂמְחָה מְדוּמֵּית לִפְנִים,
he can expand his mind through laughter, which is an imagined outward cheer,
הֲגַם שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת בַּלֵּב, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מוֹעִיל כְּלַפֵּי הַגּוּף שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ דִּמְיוֹן.
even though it is not yet genuinely felt in the heart, it nevertheless benefits the body which is governed by imagination.
כִּדְשָׁמְעִינַן בְּמַהֲרִי״ל כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא עַל רַבֵּינוּ תָּם,
As we find in the Maharil of a similar nature regarding Rabbeinu Tam,
שֶׁהָיָה מֵשִׂים לְפָנָיו תֵּל דִּנְרֵי זָהָב בְּעֵת לִימּוּד סוּגְיָא עֲמוּקָה לְהַרְחָבַת הַדַּעַת.
who would place before himself a heap of gold coins when studying a deep Talmudic topic to broaden the mind.
וְגַם "יְשַׂחֲקוּ" דְּאַבְנֵר כֵּן,
And the "let them play" of Abner was likewise so,
כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּהֵם רָאשֵׁי סַנְהֶדְרָאוֹת,
as is known that they were heads of Sanhedrin,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פב) דְּאַבְנֵר מִקְרָא דָּרַשׁ דְּ"מְלָכִים מֵחֲלָצֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר" וְהִמְלִיךְ אִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת,
and as stated (Bereishit Rabbah 82) that Abner expounded the verse "kings shall come out of your loins" and coronated Ish-bosheth,
וּמִלְחַמְתּוֹ הָיְתָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
— and his warfare was waged through words of Torah—
לְנַצֵּחַ עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהַהֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ בִּמְלוּכַת אִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת.
to triumph through Torah proof that the halakhah agreed with him regarding the reign of Ish-bosheth.
וּכְפִי חִידּוּשׁוֹ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כָּךְ נִיצּוּחוֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָה.
And commensurate with his novel Torah insight, such was his victory in battle.
וְכִדְשָׁמְעִינַן (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי שַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה ד) בְּי״ח דָּבָר,
Just as we learn (Yerushalmi Shabbat 1:4) regarding the eighteen decrees,
דְּתַלְמִידֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָיוּ הוֹרְגִים מִבֵּית הִלֵּל שֶׁהָיוּ נִלְחָמִים עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
that disciples of the House of Shammai slew those from the House of Hillel as they contended over words of Torah.
וְהַךְ "יְשַׂחֲקוּ" הוּא דּוּגְמַת מִילְּתָא דִּבְדִיחוּתָא קוֹדֶם הַלִּימּוּד.
And that "let them play" was in the manner of a light humorous warmup before intense study.
רַק אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֵּאָה פֶּרֶק א הֲלָכָה א וּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר)
Except our Sages taught (Yerushalmi Peah 1:1 and Midrash Rabbah, Parashat Emor)
דְּנֶעֱנַשׁ עַל שֶׁעָשָׂה דָּמָן וְכוּלֵי,
that Abner was punished for having treated their blood lightly, etc.,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת זֶה בְּדָמָן שֶׁל נְעָרִים.
for he should not have done this with the blood of young men.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 82:4: ““God said to him: I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply; a nation and an assembly of nations will be from you, and kings will emerge from your loins” (Genesis 35:11). “God said to him: I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply” – Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Yitzḥak: I used to say: Reuben was already out. Simeon was already out. Benjamin had already emerged from his loins and was still in his mother’s womb. Then I said: “A nation” – this is Benjamin; “and an assembly of nations” – this is Manasseh and Ephraim, as it is written: “His descendants will be a plenitude of the nations” (Genesis 48:19). Rabbi Berekhya, Rabbi Ḥelbo, and Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman: “And kings will emerge from your loins” – this is Yerovam and Yehu. The Rabbis say: Is it possible that Avner was a righteous man and he disputed that the kingdom [belonged to] the house of David? It is that he expounded a midrash, and crowned Ish Boshet. That is what is written: “And kings will emerge from your loins” – this is Saul and Ish Boshet. What did they see that led them to draw near and ostracize in the case of the concubine in Giva? It is, rather, that they read a verse and ostracized them, and read a verse and immediately welcomed them. They read a verse and ostracized them: “Ephraim and Manasseh will be like Reuben and Simeon for me” (Genesis 48:5). They read a verse and welcomed them: “A nation and an assembly of nations will be from you.””

paragraphs.text: Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1:47: “Why is it called “triple?” Because it kills three: The one who says it, the one who accepts it, and the one calumniated. And in the days of Saul, four were killed: Doeg who said it, Saul who accepted it, Aḥimelekh who was calumniated, and Abner. Why was Abner killed? Rebbi Joshua ben Levi, Rebbi Simeon ben Laqish, and the rabbis. Rebbi Joshua ben Levi said, because he made fun of the lives of his squires as it is said (2Sam. 2:14): “Let the squires get up and play before us, and Joab said, let them get up.” R. Simeon ben Laqish, because he prefaced his name before that of David; that is what is written (2Sam. 3:12) “Abner sent messengers to David the underling, saying: Whose is the land?” He wrote: From Abner to David. The rabbis say, because he did not let Shaul make peace with David. That is what is written (1Sam. 24:5): “My father, see, but see the corner of your coat in my hand!” He said to him, what do you want from the prattling of this one, it was torn off by thorns. But when they came to the circle, he said to him (1Sam. 26:14): “Can you answer, Abner?” About the corner, you said it was torn off by a thorn; were spear and pitcher cut off by a thorn? But some say, because he had it in his power to intervene for Nob, the city of priests, and he did not intervene.”

p: וְאֵצֶל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נֶאֱמַר גַּם כֵּן: "וְרָגַז וְשָׂחַק וְגוֹמֵר",
And concerning the Holy One, blessed be He, it is likewise said: "whether he is angry or laughs, etc." (Proverbs 29:9),
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קג.): "שָׂחַקְתִּי עִם אֲמַצְיָה",
and our Rabbis expounded (Sanhedrin 103a): “I laughed with Amaziah,”
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁנִּקְרָא שְׂחוֹק כִּי לֹא הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת,
meaning that it is called laughter because it was not in ultimate reality;
כִּי כָּל נִיצּוּחַ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְאוּמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי נִיצּוּחַ לְאוֹתוֹ כַּת הָרַע בַּעֲבוֹדָתָם שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
for any true victory of Israel over the pagan nations comes through conquering that category of evil within their inner service of the heart.
וְשָׁם אֵצֶל אֲמַצְיָה לֹא הָיָה נִיצּוּחוֹ לְכֹחַ הָרַע דֶּאֱדוֹם,
And there with Amaziah, his military victory was not a spiritual conquest of the evil force of Edom,
שֶׁהֲרֵי אַדְּרַבָּה, עָבַד אַחַר כָּךְ לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם,
for, on the contrary, he subsequently worshiped their gods,
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּתְדַּבֵּק בְּכֹחַ הָרַע שֶׁלָּהֶם עוֹד יוֹתֵר.
meaning that he became attached to their evil force even more.
וּמִסְּתָמָא לֹא נִצְּחוֹ כְּלָל,
And ostensibly he did not vanquish Edom spiritually at all,
רַק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שָׂחַק עִמּוֹ
— rather the Holy One laughed with him—
הַיְינוּ עָשָׂה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת, רַק כְּמוֹ לִשְׂחוֹק שֶׁנִּרְאֶה הַגָּוֶון כֵּן וְאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת.
namely He performed something not genuinely rooted, but merely like a sport where the external color appeared so while not being true.
וְהוּא חָשַׁב שֶׁהוּא נִיצּוּחַ אֲמִיתִּי לְכֹחַ הָרַע שֶׁבָּהֶם,
And Amaziah assumed that it was an authentic victory over their evil power,
וּלְכָךְ כְּשֶׁחָשַׁק לַעֲבוֹד לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם לֹא נִמְנַע,
and therefore when he desired to worship their gods he did not refrain,
כִּי חָשַׁב שֶׁוַּדַּאי הוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
because he thought it must surely be the will of Hashem,
שֶׁהוּא וַדַּאי נָקִי מֵחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּהֶם, דִּלְוּלֵי כֵן לֹא נִצְּחָם.
reasoning that he was certainly pure from their base lust, for otherwise he would not have defeated them.
וּלְכָךְ גָּעַר בַּנָּבִיא וְאָמַר לוֹ: "הֲלְיוֹעֵץ וְגוֹמֵר",
And therefore he rebuked the prophet, saying: "Have you been made counselor, etc.",
כִּי הַמֶּלֶךְ, מִצַּד כֹּחַ הַנִּיצּוּחַ שֶׁלּוֹ, וַדַּאי עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הוּא נָקִי בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ דְּרַע,
believing that the king, through his victorious strength, must perforce be clean of that evil force,
וְאֵינְךָ מֵבִין עָלָיו.
and that the prophet misunderstood him.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: "יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יָעַץ וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is what the prophet answered him: "I know that God has determined to destroy you, etc." (II Chronicles 25:16),
פֵּירוּשׁ: כְּבָר יָעַץ בְּמַה שֶּׁנִּצַּחְךָ עַל אֱדוֹם שֶׁהָיָה רַק לִשְׂחוֹק וְלֹא בֶּאֱמֶת.
meaning: God already decreed destruction by granting your victory over Edom, which was merely in jest and not genuine.

items.h: Leviathan and the education of children

p: וְזֶה טַעַם "מְשַׂחֵק עִם הַלִּוְיָתָן",
And this explains "playing with the Leviathan",
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר דְּלִוְיָתָן וְשׁוֹר הַבָּר הֵם יִצְרָא דְּתַאֲוָה וּדְרְצִיחָה
as I wrote elsewhere that the Leviathan and the Wild Ox embody the inclinations of lust and murder
שֶׁיִּשְׁחָטֵם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
which the Holy One will slaughter in the time to come, and this is not the place to elaborate.
וְלִוְיָתָן הוּא הַטִּיקְלָא הַנִּזְכָּר בְּסָבָא דְּמִשְׁפָּטִים (צה עַמּוּד ב; צו עַמּוּד ב)
And Leviathan corresponds to the celestial scale mentioned in Saba of Mishpatim (Zohar II 95b, 96b)
שֶׁחוֹטֶפֶת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת וְחָיְיכָא עִם יְנוֹקָא,
which seizes the souls and laughs with the child,
וְהוּא שְׂחוֹק הַכְּסִיל כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא לִשְׂחוֹק,
and this is the laughter of the fool, for in truth it is mere sport,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם עַל פָּסוּק "שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ" דַּיְיקָא.
as written there on the verse "man has power over man to his hurt" (Ecclesiastes 8:9).
וְשָׁם דְּנַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי עֲבֵירוֹת דִּבְנֵי אָדָם לְמַטָּה הִיא מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת.
And there, through the sins of mortals below, this force prevails.
וְזֶהוּ מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ דְּאֵין לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׂחוֹק (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שָׁם),
And this explains why since the Temple was destroyed the Holy One has no laughter (Avodah Zarah 3b),
כִּי שְׁכִינָה בַּגָּלוּת וִינִיקָתָן מִצַּד רַע דִּבְנֵי אָדָם.
because the Shechinah is in exile and the forces draw nourishment from the evil deeds of men.
אֲבָל בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים וְהַשֶּׁפַע יוֹרֵד לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
However, when the Temple stood and the divine abundance descended to the Congregation of Israel,
אָז הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְשַׂחֵק עִם לִוְיָתָן,
then the Holy One plays with the Leviathan,
כְּעִנְיַן "מְשַׂחֲקִין בַּתִּינֹקֶת" בְּנִדָּה (יג:),
in the manner of "playing with an infant" in Niddah (13b),
שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד יְסוֹד דְּקַטְנוּת הַיָּדוּעַ שֶׁנִּקְרָא נָחָשׁ דִּקְדוּשָׁה.
which stems from the realm of Katnut (immaturity) known as the holy snake.
כִּי כָּל שְׂחוֹק הוּא מַעֲשֵׂה קַטְנוּת,
For all play is an act of immaturity,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתּוֹסְפִין גֵּרִים כַּנּוֹדָע,
and through this converts are added as is known,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ דִּמְעַת הָעֲשׁוּקִים עַל יְדֵי הַטִּיקְלָא כִּדְאִיתָא בְּסָבָא שָׁם, וְהוּא "לְרַע לוֹ".
which is the tear of the oppressed through the scale as brought in Saba there, turning out "to his own hurt".

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:7: “These two inclinations are opposites, and each, when directed toward holiness, nullifies the other. In the chapter HaSefinah it says that this hunt of Leviathan is carried out through Gabriel, who represents holy powers of severity. For the inclination to bloodshed and anger will be nullified entirely, whereas the inclination of desire is also needed for the service of God. The Zohar says that it is called Laban because it will be whitened, and it will not be nullified. As our Sages said, “I will give you a heart of flesh”—a heart to produce flesh, rather than for one’s own pleasure. Its hunt will therefore be through the holy powers of severity, and the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, as stated there: without this, even the most pious of the pious…and so forth.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Mishpatim 3:27-29: “This is a supernal mystery beyond all others. At the beam on which the balances stand, within the blowing air, there is one scale on this side and another scale on that side. On this side are scales of justice, and on that side scales of deceit. This balance never rests: souls rise and descend, enter and return. Some souls are oppressed when one person rules over another, as it is written, “At a time when one person rules over another, to his harm”—certainly to his harm. But this soul, which came to the other side, to a stranger, and was oppressed by him, is “to his harm”: his—the stranger’s. She may not eat of the sacred offering until the Holy One, blessed be He, does with her what He does. Scripture therefore says, “If a priest’s daughter becomes married to a stranger”—so it is. Here is the mystery of how souls are oppressed. This world is entirely governed through the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. When the people of the world conduct themselves on the side of good, the balance stands and inclines toward good; when they conduct themselves on the side of evil, it inclines toward that side. All the souls that were in the balance at that time are oppressed and taken by it.”

We have seen in the books of the ancients that from them came the righteous among the nations, and those Torah scholars who are mamzerim and take precedence over an ignorant high priest, esteemed in the world though he enters the innermost sanctuary. The elder wept for a moment. The companions were astonished and said nothing.”

paragraphs.text:
Tanya, Part III; Iggeret HaTeshuvah 6:7-11: “It is written, ‘Jacob is the cord of His inheritance.’ By way of analogy, a cord has one end above and its other end below. If a person pulls the lower end, he also moves and draws the upper end after it, as far as it can be drawn.

Exactly so with the root and source of a person’s soul in the lower hei mentioned above: through his evil deeds and thoughts, he draws its influence down, as it were, into the chambers of the other side, from which his thoughts and deeds derive. Since he is the one who draws this influence to them, he takes the first share; this is sufficient for one who understands.

This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, meant by saying, ‘Neither the tranquility of the wicked, and so forth, is in our hands.’ ‘In our hands’ is precise: it means during the exile after the destruction of the Temple. This is the exile of the Divine Presence, as it were: to bestow influence upon the chambers of the other side, which His blessed soul abhors.

When a person repents properly, he removes from them the influence that he drew down through his deeds and thoughts, for through his repentance he restores the influence of the Divine Presence to its proper place.

This is the return of the lower hei from exile. As it is written, ‘Hashem your God will return with your captivity’—that is, together with your captivity. As our Sages, of blessed memory, said: ‘It does not say, “He will bring back,”’ and so forth.”

p: וְזֶה טַעַם "מְשַׂחֵק עִם לִוְיָתָן",
And this explains why He plays with Leviathan,
וְהָא וְהָא עָבֵיד – דִּמְלַמֵּד גַּם כֵּן לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
and He engages in both—for He likewise teaches schoolchildren,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא שֶׁפַע הַחָכְמָה לְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
for through this flows the abundance of wisdom to young children,
דְּקוֹדֶם י״ג שָׁנָה הוּא שְׁלִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
since prior to age thirteen the evil inclination holds sway,
וּמִצַּד זֶה הִיא "חָיְיכָא בִּינוֹקָא" וַדַּאי עַל יְדֵי מֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַיֵּצֶר בּוֹ בְּלִבּוֹ גַּם כֵּן.
and from this aspect it "laughs with the child," certainly through the inclination's dominion in his heart as well.
וְהַכְנָסַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בּוֹ הוּא עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר לְבַד,
And the instillment of Torah into him is facilitated through the power of the inclination alone,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּסִיתִין לְתִינוֹק לִלְמוֹד מִצַּד חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
just as one entices a child to learn by means of worldly treats
שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין לוֹ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר אוֹ מְפַתִּין לוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה דְּבַר כָּבוֹד וְחֶמְדָּה וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
giving him something or enticing him with honor, sweets, and the like.
וְזֶה שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי כֵּן לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא מִפְּעוּלַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת.
And that he comes through this to words of Torah is truly the working of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְגַם מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
And even after the destruction of the Temple,
הֲגַם דִּשְׁלִיטַת הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ הוּא מִצַּד מַעֲשֵׂה הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים,
even though man's dominion over man to his hurt stems from human deeds below,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַה שֶּׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִקְלָט גַּם כֵּן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן
— nevertheless, that through this Torah is absorbed by young schoolchildren—
כִּי הַשְּׂחוֹק הוּא בְּתִינוֹקוֹת
for playfulness belongs to children
וְעַל יְדֵי דְּבַר שְׂחוֹק הֵם קוֹלְטִים דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
— and through playful sport they absorb Torah—
דָּבָר זֶה הוּא עֵסֶק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
this matter is the direct engagement of Hashem,
כִּי הֲרֵי אֵינוֹ מֵאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא כְּמוֹ אֵצֶל הַגְּדוֹלִים,
for it does not derive from arousal below as with adults,
רַק מֵאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא לְבַד, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחַנֵּךְ לַנַּעַר עַל פִּי דַּרְכּוֹ.
but solely from supernal arousal Above, wherein Hashem educates the youth according to his way.
וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ הָעֵסֶק דִּשְׂחוֹק עִם לִוְיָתָן בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ עוֹד.
And this is identical to playing with the Leviathan when the Temple stood, and this is not the place to elaborate further.

paragraphs.text: Rambam on Mishnah Sanhedrin 10:1:8: “Imagine a young child brought to a teacher to learn Torah. This is a great good for him because of the perfection he will attain through it. Yet because of his few years and the weakness of his intellect, he does not understand the excellence of that good or the perfection he will attain through it. The teacher, whose understanding is more complete, must therefore encourage him to learn through things he loves at his young age. He says: “Read, and I will give you nuts or figs, or a little honey.” The child reads and makes an effort, not for the reading itself, whose excellence he does not know, but so that he will receive that food. Eating those delicacies is more precious in his eyes than reading, and undoubtedly much better. He therefore regards learning as toil and exertion, and works at it so that through this effort he will attain the goal he loves: a nut or a piece of honey.”

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Repentance 10:5: “Anyone who occupies himself with Torah in order to receive reward or to avoid punishment occupies himself with it not for its own sake. Anyone who occupies himself with it neither from fear nor to receive reward, but because of love for the Master of all the earth who commanded it, occupies himself with it for its own sake. The Sages said: A person should always occupy himself with Torah, even not for its own sake, because through doing so he comes to do so for its own sake. Therefore, when teaching children, women, and the unlearned generally, they are taught only to serve from fear and in order to receive reward, until their knowledge increases and they gain greater wisdom. Then this secret is revealed to them little by little, and they are gently accustomed to it until they grasp and understand it and serve Him from love.”

items.h: The limit on laughter in this world

p: וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת לא.):
And our Sages taught (Berakhot 31a):
"אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיְּמַלֵּא שְׂחוֹק פִּיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְכוּלֵי",
“It is forbidden for a person to fill his mouth with laughter in this world, etc.,”
פֵּירוּשׁ: מִילּוּי הַפֶּה נִקְרָא כְּשֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם כַּוָּנָה אַחֶרֶת וּמְשׁוּקָּע בָּזֶה,
the explanation being: filling the mouth means when he has no other intention and is entirely immersed in it,
כְּעִנְיַן "יִמָּלֵא פִי תְּהִלָּתֶךָ", שֶׁלָּמְדוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם נא.)
akin to "My mouth shall be filled with Your praise" (Psalms 71:8), which the Sages deduced (Berakhot 51a)
לְעִנְיַן בְּרָכָה כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּפִיו דְּבַר מַאֲכָל,
regarding a blessing when one has food in his mouth,
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר הַחוֹצֵץ מֵהֲנָאָה גּוּפָנִית.
namely that there is something separating from pure bodily pleasure.
וְכֵן בִּשְׂחוֹק בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת,
And so too with unrestrained laughter,
הֲגַם דְּאֵינוֹ עַל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו וְלֵיצָנוּת גָּמוּר,
even if it is not directed at people and not outright mockery,
כָּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה כַּוָּנָה לְמִצְוָה וְהַרְחָבַת לֵב דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
so long as it lacks intention for a mitzvah and mental relaxation for Torah study,
רַק כִּשְׂחוֹק וְהוֹלֵלוּת בְּעָלְמָא
— being mere empty sport and frivolity—
אָסוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁלִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
it is forbidden in this world where the evil inclination holds sway.
וְהוּא דַּרְגָּה לַשְּׂחוֹק הַב' דְּלֵיצָנוּת וְקַלּוּת רֹאשׁ וּפְרִיקַת עוֹל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
For it serves as a steppingstone to that other laughter of mockery, levity, and casting off the yoke, Heaven forbid,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְפַּנֶּה לִבּוֹ לְבַטָּלָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
for through this one's heart turns to vanity, Heaven forbid.
רַק "אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק וְגוֹמֵר",
Only "Then will our mouth be filled with laughter" (Psalms 126:2),
כִּי אָז לֹא יִהְיֶה בַּטָּלָה כְּלָל,
because then there will be no vanity at all,
כִּי כָּל דְּבַר בַּטָּלָה גַּם כֵּן קֹדֶשׁ לַה',
for even all idle matters will be holy unto Hashem,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "מְצִלּוֹת הַסּוּס וְגוֹמֵר",
as written "the bells of the horses shall be holy unto Hashem" (Zechariah 14:20),
וְהוּא הָאוֹהֵב זִמָּה כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים קיג:) גַּם כֵּן קֹדֶשׁ.
and the horse loves licentiousness, as our Sages taught (Pesachim 113b), yet it too will become holy.

At the time when ‘they will say among the nations: Hashem has done great things with these people.’ They said of Reish Lakish that he never filled his mouth with laughter in this world from the time he heard this teaching from Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher.’

paragraphs.text: Fixed holiness does not make the work of this world dispensable.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The Eighth Day of Pesach 11:1: “Through Israel's not relying on the assurance of the holiness fixed within them, but instead restraining themselves in the work of this world within the cycle of seven and submitting to Hashem like a horse to its rider, they will merit the day when even the horse's bells will be holy to Hashem. Hashem will then illuminate that Israel is kodesh to Hashem, without the letter vav.”

: “Through Israel's not relying on the assurance of the holiness fixed within them, but instead restraining themselves in the work of this world within the cycle of seven and submitting to Hashem like a horse to its rider, they will merit the day when even the horse's bells will be holy to Hashem. Hashem will then illuminate that Israel is kodesh to Hashem, without the letter vav.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim explains the same promise that even the horse's bells will be holy by first insisting that Israel not rely on an already fixed holiness. Present restraint and work prepare its disclosure. This makes the siman's concluding boundary precise: its future account of everything becoming holy is not a reason to erase the intention and discipline it requires of laughter in this world.

sections.en: The Holy One, Blessed Be He, His Glory Fills the Whole Earth

p: [רסא] הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ
The Holy One, blessed be He, His glory fills the whole earth,
וְלֵית אֲתַר פָּנוּי מִינֵּיהּ,
and there is no place devoid of Him,
רַק שֶׁהוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל, "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ".
only that He is in deep concealment, "He made darkness His secret place" (Psalms 18:12).
וְכַאֲשֶׁר מֵאִיר לְלֵב הָאָדָם הַכָּרָה זוֹ אֵיךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ,
And when this recognition shines into man's heart—how Hashem fills the whole earth with His glory—
זֶה נִקְרָא "הוֹצִיאָנוּ מֵאֲפֵלָה לְאוֹר גָּדוֹל" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בַּהַגָּדָה.
this is termed "He brought us forth from darkness to a great light," as recited in the Haggadah.
דִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁהוּא הוֹצָאָה מִן הַהֶעְלֵם הַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶל הַגִּילּוּי,
For the Exodus from Egypt, which is the extraction of the recognition of Hashem from concealment into revelation,
וְהוּא הֶאָרָה לְגַבֵּי הָאָדָם וְגַם לְגַבֵּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
is an illumination regarding man and likewise regarding Hashem,
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ל):
as our Sages taught (Bereishit Rabbah 30 end):
מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ שֶׁהָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְבוֹאוֹת אֲפֵלוֹת וּבָא אוֹהֲבוֹ וְהִדְלִיק אֶת הַנֵּר.
a parable of a king walking in dark alleys, and his beloved came and lit the lamp.
שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הֵאִיר לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
For Abraham our father, peace be upon him, illuminated before Hashem,
כִּי זֶה נִקְרָא שְׁכִינָה בַּגָּלוּת,
for this is termed the Shechinah in exile:
כַּאֲשֶׁר שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים הוּא בְּהֶעְלֵם עָצוּם וְאֵינוֹ בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת וּבְפִרְסוּם,
when His Presence among lower beings is in intense concealment, not in open revelation,
הֲרֵי זֶה כִּמְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְבוֹאוֹת אֲפֵלוֹת.
it is comparable to walking in dark alleys.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 30:10: ““Noah walked with God.” Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda said: This is analogous to a prince who had two sons, one older and one younger. He said to the younger, ‘Walk with me,’ and he said to the elder, ‘Come and walk before me.’ So too, of Abraham, whose strength was great, [God said,] “Walk before Me and be faultless” (Genesis 17:1). But Noah, whose strength was lesser, “Noah walked with God.” Rabbi Neḥemya said: This is analogous to a friend of the king who was sinking in thick mud. The king looked and saw him. He said to him: ‘Rather than sink in the mud, walk along with me.’ That is what is written: “Noah walked with God.” To what is Abraham comparable? To a friend of the king who saw the king walking in dark alleys. His friend peered and began illuminating for him through the window. The king peered and saw him. He said to him: ‘Rather than illuminating for me through the window, come and illuminate before me.’ So too, the Holy One blessed be He said to Abraham: ‘Rather than illuminating for Me from Mesopotamia and its environs, come and illuminate before Me in the Land of Israel!’ That is what is written: “He blessed Joseph, and said: The God before whom my fathers, [Abraham and Isaac], walked…” (Genesis 48:15). Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish, Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is analogous to a shepherd who is standing and looking at his flock. Reish Lakish said: It is analogous to a prince who is walking with the elders going before him. According to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, we are in need of His glory. According to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, He is in need of our glory.”
