p: וְאֵפוֹד עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
And the apron (ephod) atones for idolatry,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל מַעֲשִׂים רָעִים הַכְּלוּלִים בְּ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
which is the taproot of all evil deeds included in "You shall have no other gods",
וַעֲבוֹדָה הַיְינוּ מַעֲשֶׂה וְעוּבְדָא;
and 'service/worship' (avodah) signifies concrete physical action;
וּבַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרֵף מַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה לְמַעֲשֶׂה כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין מ.).
and regarding idolatry the Holy One joins evil thought to action, as the Sages taught (Kiddushin 40a).
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמַה דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה אֵינָהּ מִצְטָרֶפֶת,
And this implies that where normally evil thought is not joined to deed,
הַיְינוּ דְּבֶאֱמֶת "הַנִּסְתָּרֹת לַה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ" וְ"חֵלֶק ה' עַמּוֹ",
it is because in truth "the hidden things belong to Hashem our God" and "Hashem's portion is His people,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (יז.): "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ וְכוּלֵי וּמִי מְעַכֵּב וְכוּלֵי";
and as stated in Berakhot (17a): "It is revealed and known... and what hinders? The leaven in the dough";
אַךְ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דְּכוֹפֵר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בַּה',
but in idolatry where one denies Hashem, Heaven forbid,
מִמֵּילָא גַּם מַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה מִצְטָרֵף,
automatically evil thought also joins,
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְכַפֵּר רַק עַל יְדֵי מַחֲלָצוֹת,
and it cannot be atoned for except through translucent robes,
דְּהַיְינוּ גִּלּוּי הַסּוֹד דְּ"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.),
namely the disclosure of the secret that "even though he sinned, he remains Israel" (Sanhedrin 44a),
דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַתֵּק הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּלָל;
for it is impossible to sever the root at all;
הֲגַם שֶׁכּוֹפֵר בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
and even if he denies the root,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עֹמֶק פְּנִימִיּוּתוֹ הַנֶּעְלָם גַּם מִמֶּנּוּ הוּא לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
nevertheless the depth of his inwardness, hidden even from himself, remains consecrated unto Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ מִצַּד מַחֲלָצוֹת דְּמַעֲשֶׂה,
And this operates through the translucent robe of action,
כִּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עִיקָּרָהּ הֶעְלֵם מִצַּד הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה,
for idolatry is essentially concealment within action in the World of Asiyah,
וּמַעֲשֶׂה הוּא גַּשְׁמִיּוּת בְּיוֹתֵר
and deed is the coarsest physical realm,
עַד דִּבְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כִּמְעַט לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ מַעֲשֶׂה כְּלָל,
such that in words of Torah physical deed is hardly present at all,
זוּלַת מַעֲשֵׂה הַכְּתָב דְּהֻותַּר בַּדּוֹרוֹת אַחֲרוֹנִים מִשּׁוּם "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת וְגוֹמֵר" כַּנּוֹדָע,
save for the physical act of writing permitted in later generations because of "It is time to act for Hashem, etc." (Psalms 119:126),
פֵּירוּשׁ, שֶׁעֵת לְהַכְנִיס דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה גַּם כֵּן בְּמִצְוֹת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
meaning: it is time to instill words of Torah into physical deeds
לְתַקֵּן מַדְרֵגוֹת הַיּוֹתֵר תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת שֶׁל עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה מִשּׁוּם "הֵפֵרוּ תוֹרָתֶךָ".
in order to rectify the lowest rungs of the World of Action because "they have voided Your Torah."
וְעַל יְדֵי מַחֲלָצוֹת דְּמַעֲשֶׂה,
And through the translucent robe of action,
שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת דְּגַם בְּסוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתָּן וְאֵין נִיתָּק בְּשׁוּם עִנְיָן,
which is the disclosure that even at the end of action everything is truly from Hashem and never severed,
זֶהוּ תִּיקּוּן מַדְרֵיגוֹת הַיּוֹתֵר גְּרוּעוֹת בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הָעֲבֵירוֹת.
this constitutes the rectification of the basest rungs in sinful deeds.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 1:7: “But all this has no bearing on the thought that is the essence of the person: the wisdom within the brain, which is “the soul You placed within me is pure.” As is known concerning nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, the neshamah is in the brain and comes from God, as it is written, “He breathed into his nostrils,” and so forth. One who breathes forth does so from within: it is a portion of God, and therefore it is pure. Concerning this they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2 that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as it is written, “The rock of my heart and my portion,” and so forth. For the brain and heart are two companions, as explained; since He dwells within a person’s brain, which is called “my portion,” He is consequently also in his heart.”

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 17a: ‘After his prayer, Rabbi Alexandri would say: ‘May it be Your will, Hashem our God, that You place us in a corner of light and not in a corner of darkness. May our heart not ache, and may our eyes not grow dark.’ Some say that Rav Hamnuna prayed this, while Rabbi Alexandri, after praying, would say: ‘Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that our desire is to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven in the dough and subjection to kingdoms. May it be Your will to save us from their hands, so that we may return to carrying out the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.’’

p: וּמְעִיל, שֶׁהוּא מְכַסֶּה כָּל הַגּוּף נֶגֶד הַכְּתֹנֶת,
And the robe (me'il), which covers the whole body corresponding to the tunic,
הוּא עַל עַצְמִיּוּת כֹּחַ הַפּוֹעֵל שֶׁבַּנִּפְעָל,
operates upon the essential power of the operator embedded within the vessel,
וּמְגַלֶּה הַסּוֹד ה' שֶׁבְּעֶצֶם כֹּחַ הַנֶּפֶשׁ דְּחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ;
and reveals Hashem's secret within the soul's intrinsic divine portion;
זֶהוּ עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "חֵץ שָׁחוּט וְגוֹמֵר".
this atones for evil speech (lashon hara), which corresponds to bloodshed, as written: "Their tongue is a sharpened arrow, etc." (Jeremiah 9:7).
רַק דְּזֶה כְּבָר כְּרָתָן דָּוִד בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵרָכִין (טו:),
Only that David already cut them off through the Holy Spirit as stated in Arachin (15b),
וְצָרִיךְ לְדוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת דְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה.) שֶׁגַּם לָהֶן יֵשׁ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
requiring the exposition of the 'interpreters of subtle impressions' in Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 105a) that even they have a share in the World to Come
וּ"לִכְשֶׁיָּבוֹא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עָלַי וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and "when King David comes before me, etc.", see there.
וּפֵירוּשׁ "רְשׁוּמוֹת" הוּא הָרְשִׁימוּ דְּנֶפֶשׁ עַצְמָהּ הַנִּגְלֶה מִכֹּחַ הַפּוֹעֵל שֶׁבַּנִּפְעָל,
And the meaning of reshumot is the holy imprint of the soul revealed from the active power within the vessel,
וְדוֹרְשֵׁי הֵם הָעוֹמְדִים עַל גִּלּוּי וּמַחֲלָצוֹת סוֹד ה' שֶׁבּוֹ;
and its interpreters are those who grasp the disclosure and translucent robes of Hashem's secret within it;
הֵם מְבִינִים מִכֹּחַ גִּלּוּי עוֹמֶק שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית וּדְבוּקָה בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים
they understand through revealing the profound depth of the Jewish soul cleaving to the living God
שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שׁוּם נִיתּוּק כְּלָל בְּסוֹף הַכֹּל
that it suffers no permanent detachment at the end of all things,
כְּשֶׁיֵּעָדְרוּ כָּל מִינֵי לְבוּשִׁים דִּבְחִירָה שֶׁהֵם הַכֹּל לְבוּשֵׁי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
when all garments of mortal choice (which are garments of this world) fall away,
מִצַּד עַצְמִיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ דְּחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל
for from the perspective of the soul's essence as a divine portion from Above
שֶׁבְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִית מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הִיא מְקוּשֶּׁרֶת לְגַמְרֵי בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
each individual Jewish soul is bound wholly to Hashem.
וְזֶהוּ כַּפָּרָה עַל כְּרִיתַת הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן.
And this constitutes atonement even for the uprooting of the root, Heaven forbid.

If he is a Torah scholar, let him occupy himself with Torah. If he is unlearned, let him humble his mind, as it is said: ‘Perverseness in it brings a breaking of the spirit.’’

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:41: “The meaning of “those who expound traces” is that they can apprehend what has no full manifestation, only some trace. The teaching that certain people have no share in the World to Come concerns the revealed apprehension that the Sages of Israel had of the World to Come. In truth, however, its essence is something “no eye has seen.” What is attained is only an apprehension through wisdom, while it contains depths that none of the Sages of Israel in this world can apprehend at all. Concerning this it says, “No eye has seen, O God, besides You,” as stated in Berakhot 34b. From those depths, too, there are some traces revealed to those who truly seek them, enabling them to apprehend a hint, as one apprehends a trace of the thing itself. By apprehending this trace they said that these people, too, have a share in the World to Come, for in truth Israel’s root is never lost. All corruption comes from this world; even corruption affecting the World to Come occurs through this world, as in the analogy of the eve of Shabbat and Shabbat, or dry land and the sea, in Avodah Zarah 3a; see there. This is the entire apprehension of the World to Come available in this world: it is apprehended only through this world, insofar as this world prepares for it. In truth, however, there are further matters in the World to Come entirely concealed in this world, because there is no preparation for them except through a trace. That is, the preparation consists only of the holiness of the root, which existed in this world in utter concealment, like a trace alone. Those who expound traces apprehend the trace of holiness present even in the lowest person of Israel. Through this they apprehend the trace of a share in the World to Come belonging even to these people, because of some trace of holiness found in their root. As is known, every light and holiness that departs leaves a trace in its place, which the masters of Kabbalah call a reshimu. Likewise, Jewish holiness is present from birth, from the womb. Even if a person subsequently corrupts his deeds until, Heaven forbid, he is utterly rejected and the light departs entirely, so that he has no share in the World to Come, the trace nevertheless remains. Because of this trace, some holiness still remains within him, although it is not revealed; those who expound traces recognize it through their exposition.”

p: וְהִנֵּה עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אָדָם זוֹכֶה גַּם כֵּן לִלְבוּשֵׁי מַחֲלָצוֹת
And behold, through words of Torah a person likewise merits these translucent robes (machalatzot)
עַל יְדֵי מַחֲשָׁבָה דִּבּוּר וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
through holy thought, speech, and action in Torah study;
וּלְכָךְ גַּם "אֳהָלִים" מַעֲלִים מִכָּל טֻמְאָה וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרָכוֹת טז.),
wherefore "tents of Torah" elevate one from all impurity (Berakhot 16a),
וְגַם עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ יַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֵרָכִין שָׁם);
and for evil speech our Sages stated: "his remedy is to engage in Torah" (Arachin 15b);
וּבְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה זוֹכֶה גַּם כֵּן לְכָל בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
and through words of Torah one merits all vestments of the High Priest
לְבוּשִׁים לְכַפֵּר עַל נַפְשׁוֹ מִכָּל מִינֵי רַע לְגַמְרֵי כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
as protective garments to atone for his soul completely from all evil, as explained above.

sections.en: Mockery as the Entryway into Evil

p: [רסד] הַכְּנִיסָה לָרַע הוּא עַל יְדֵי לֵיצָנוּת,
The entryway into evil is through mockery,
כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּיוֹמָא (לח:):
as our Sages taught in Yoma (38b):
"הַבָּא לִיטַּמֵּא פּוֹתְחִין [לוֹ]", מִקְּרָא דְּ"אִם לַלֵּצִים הוּא יָלִיץ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, לד);
“To one who comes to defile himself, they open [for him],” derived from the verse: “If it concerns the scorners, he scoffs”;
מְבוֹאָר דְּלֵץ הוּא הַבִּיאָה וּכְנִיסָה לְכָל מִינֵי טֻמְאָה.
it is thus clear that the scorner represents the entry into all categories of impurity.
וְ"הוּא יָלִיץ" פֵּירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קפד עַמּוּד ב; וְחֵלֶק ג, צב עַמּוּד ב)
And "he scoffs" means as written in the Zohar (II 184b, III 92b)
דִּכְמוֹ שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר לְמַטָּה כָּךְ לְעוּמָּתוֹ לְמַעְלָה.
that as one stirs below, so corresponds Above.
וְהַלֵּץ – מִלְּמַעְלָה גַּם כֵּן מִתְלוֹצְצִים מִמֶּנּוּ,
And regarding the scorner—from Above they likewise mock him,
פֵּירוּשׁ מַרְאִים לוֹ כְּאִילּוּ יֵשׁ לְהִתְלוֹצֵץ בֶּאֱמֶת מֵאוֹתוֹ דָבָר.
meaning they make it appear to him as though there were legitimate reason to scoff at that sacred matter.
וְזֶהוּ "פּוֹתְחִין" – שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין לוֹ פֶּתַח לְהִתְלוֹצֵץ;
And this is "they open"—they provide him an opening to scoff;
וְזֶה בֶּאֱמֶת לֵיצָנוּת מִמֶּנּוּ,
and this is in truth mockery toward him,
כִּי הֲרֵי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין מָקוֹם כְּלָל לְהִתְלוֹצֵץ מֵאוֹתוֹ דָבָר.
for in truth there is no basis whatever to scoff at that matter.

paragraphs.text: The opening of the final siman treats mockery as a gateway into other forms of estrangement.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Machshavot Charutz 7:11: “but external wisdom found among the nations of the world, and there is that which is genuinely termed "wisdom" even in the language of Scripture, yet they absorb the dross from it, such being their root, and its dross is mockery of true sacred wisdom; and in all pagan idolatries that misled the masses, they demonstrated through their corrupted intellect that it supposedly held substance, yet all of it derived from cynicism toward the truth, forging a falsehood that mimics the truth. And this is likewise the nature of the idolatry of Ba'al Pe'or (Bamidbar 25:3); directly opposite which Moshe Rabbeinu was buried, he being the root of the Torah called by his name (Malachi 3:22), which is the exact antithesis of mockery, as written: "when a word of Torah enters, a word of scoffing departs" (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2);”

And this is likewise the nature of the idolatry of Ba'al Pe'or (Bamidbar 25:3); directly opposite which Moshe Rabbeinu was buried, he being the root of the Torah called by his name (Malachi 3:22), which is the exact antithesis of mockery, as written: "when a word of Torah enters, a word of scoffing departs" (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2);”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Machshavot Charutz describes the progression from mocking true wisdom to constructing a false appearance of truth. This explains why the present siman gives leitzanus a foundational role, rather than counting it as just another isolated bad habit. Once the mind dismisses the very standard by which it could be corrected, it becomes able to justify a substitute on its own terms.

p: וְהֵם מִד' כִּתּוֹת שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִים פְּנֵי שְׁכִינָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ סוֹטָה מב.),
And scorners are among the four groups that do not receive the Shechinah (Sotah 42a),
פֵּירוּשׁ, הַמְעַכְּבִים וּמְבַלְבְּלִים הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה בִּתְפִלָּה
meaning those forces that hinder and confuse thought in prayer
וּבְעֵת רְצוֹנוֹ לִדְבַּק בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת.
and in the hour when one desires to cleave to Him with extraneous thoughts.
וְהֵם ד' כֹּחוֹת שֶׁבַּלֵּב הַמְּכוּנִּים בַּזֹּהַר אַבָּא וְאִמָּא, דְּכַר וְנוּקְבָא כַּנּוֹדָע,
And they are four faculties in the heart designated in the Zohar as Abba, Imma, masculine, and feminine,
וְהֵם בָּרַע רָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת חַשְׁמַ״ל
and in evil their acronym spells Chashmal:
חֲנֵפִים, שַׁקְרָנִים, מְסַפְּרֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, לֵיצִים.
Flatterers, Liars, Slanderers, Scorners.
חֲנֵפִים הוּא הָאוֹמֵר לְרַע טוֹב
Flatterers (Chaneifim) are those who call evil good
[וּבִכְלָל גַּם כֵּן עַל עַצְמוֹ מַחֲנִיף וּמַחְשִׁיב עַצְמוֹ לְטוֹב].
[and included is one who flatters himself, considering himself righteous].
וְלֵיצִים הוּא הָרֵאשִׁית הָאוֹמֵר לְטוֹב רַע.
And scorners (Leitzim) represent the root-head who calls good evil.
וְ"רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק" שֶׁהוּא לֵץ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רנ"ט,
And "Amalek was the first of the nations" (Numbers 24:20), being a scorner as noted above in section 259,
הוּא הָרֹאשׁ לְז' עַמָּמִין,
he is the head of the seven Canaanite nations,
שֶׁהֵם ז' מִדּוֹת הַכּוֹלְלִים דְּכַר וְנוּקְבָא,
which are the seven emotional attributes encompassing masculine and feminine,
וְהוּא הָרֹאשׁ הַכּוֹלֵל תְּלָת מוֹחִין: חָכְמָה, בִּינָה, דַּעַת כַּנּוֹדָע.
and he is the head encompassing the three intellectual faculties: Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at.

p: וּלְכָךְ בּוֹ "תִּמְחֶה",
Therefore regarding him it is commanded "you shall blot out," (Deuteronomy 25:19)
כִּי בְּכָל מִדָּה רָעָה יֵשׁ בִּכְלָלוֹ טוֹב
for in every other evil trait there exists a latent good component
שֶׁהֲרֵי נִקְבַּע גַּם כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
since it is also embedded within Israel,
וּמִצַּד הַטּוֹב הֵם חֲסִידֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
and from the perspective of good they are the pious of the nations who have a share in the World to Come,
וְ"אָז אֶהְפֹּךְ אֶל עַמִּים שָׂפָה בְרוּרָה וְגוֹמֵר" (צְפַנְיָה ג, ט),
and "For then will I turn to the peoples a pure language, etc." (Zephaniah 3:9),
כִּי גַּם אוֹתָם כֹּחוֹת יִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ גַּם לֶעָתִיד.
for those forces will also remain in the future.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַטּוֹב שֶׁבְּלֵיצָנוּת הוּא לֵיצָנוּתָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
In contrast, the only goodness in mockery is the mockery of idolatry,
וְזֶהוּ רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
and this is relevant only in this world;
אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כְּשֶׁיִּתְבַּטֵּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מֵעוֹלָם
whereas in the World to Come when the evil inclination is abolished from the earth
[מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רְצִיחָה דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל,
[unlike murder, for example,
הֲגַם דְּ"בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח",
for even though "He will swallow up death forever" (Isaiah 25:8),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַתּוֹרָה נִצְחִיוּת
nonetheless the Torah is eternal,
שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ: "אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת", וְחַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין,
in which is written: "When a man dies" and capital executions of the court,
וְכִמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים סח.): "דְּהַנַּעַר בֶּן מֵאָה שָׁנָה יָמוּת"
— and as our Sages taught (Pesachim 68a): "'the youth of a hundred years shall die' —
הַיְינוּ בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעַכּוּ״ם יִהְיֶה גַּם אָז מִיתָה],
meaning among the gentile nations there will still be death],
וְאֵין מָקוֹם לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
and there will be no place for idolatry,
אֵין מָקוֹם לְלֵיצָנוּת כְּלָל,
there will be no place for mockery at all,
וְאֵין בּוֹ הַשְׁאָרָה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא כְּלָל וַהֲפִיכַת שָׂפָה בְּרוּרָה,
and it will leave no residue in the World to Come nor conversion to a pure tongue,
רַק "תִּמְחֶה".
only total obliteration.
וּכְמַאֲמַר זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְכִילְתָּא סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח) דְּאֵין מְקַבְּלִין גֵּר מֵעֲמָלֵק.
And as our Sages taught (Mekhilta, end of Beshalach) that no convert is accepted from Amalek.

items.h: The hidden root of evil

p: וְיָדוּעַ דְּהַתְחָלַת כְּנִיסַת כָּל דָּבָר מֵחָכְמָה,
And it is known that the initial entrance of everything is from Chokhmah,
שֶׁהוּא הַמּוּרְגָּשׁ וְנִקְרָא "יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן", וְהוּא הַנִּקְרָא אַבָּא כַּנּוֹדָע.
which is the perceivable emergence termed "existence from nothingness," called Abba.
אֲבָל כֶּתֶר הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם וּכְמוֹ מַקִּיף כַּנּוֹדָע,
However, Keter is the concealed root and acts as an encompassing light (makif),
וְהוּא בָּרַע כָּל מִינֵי מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת הַנִּכְנָסוֹת וּפוֹרְחוֹת מֵעַצְמָן לַמּוֹחַ וּמְבַלְבְּלִים.
and in evil this reflects all extraneous thoughts that enter and flit spontaneously into the brain, causing confusion.
וְשָׁרְשָׁן מִקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ שֶׁמִּכֹּחוֹ כָּל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת כַּנּוֹדָע,
And their root is in Kelipat Nogah from whose force stem all discretionary worldly matters,
וְזֶה עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ וּמַשְׁכָּא דְּחִוְיָא,
and this is the counsel of the serpent and the serpent's skin,
דְּיָדוּעַ דְּהוּא מִקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ
which is known to originate from Kelipat Nogah,
וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחֶמְדָּה הַגּוּפָנִית,
and is the root of bodily lust,
שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
which is impossible to rectify completely in this world,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי תִּיקּוּנָהּ הוּא בִּילּוּעַ הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח שֶׁהוּא מִכֹּחַ עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ.
for through its complete rectification comes the swallowing up of death forever, which derives from the serpent's counsel.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה לְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
Therefore they said in the Zohar (I 219b) that standard repentance is ineffective for emitting seed in vain,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵץ חַיִּים, שַׁעַר קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, דְּכָל טִיפַּת קֶרִי הוּא בִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as written in Etz Chayim, Sha'ar Kelipat Nogah, that every drop of nocturnal emission is bound to Kelipat Nogah, see there.
וּתְשׁוּבָה הוּא לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי, אִם כֵּן צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בִּילּוּעַ הַמָּוֶת.
And complete repentance rectifies totally; thus it requires the total eradication of death.

Explanation: Beit Yaakov identifies kelipas nogah with permitted matters that nevertheless require clarification, through the example of Lot’s rescue for Avraham’s sake. This helps explain why the final siman still speaks of repair after discussing the rejection of open evil. The remaining task concerns the direction and use of permitted powers, not a claim that everything permitted is already a transgression.

paragraphs.text:
Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 7:1-5: “The vital, animal soul in Israel that comes from the kelipah and is clothed in a person’s blood, as explained above; the souls of ritually pure domestic animals, wild animals, birds, and fish that may be eaten; the existence and vitality of all inanimate matter and all vegetation that may be consumed; and likewise the existence and vitality of every deed, word, and thought concerning this world that involves no prohibition—neither a root nor a branch of the 365 negative commandments or their biblical or rabbinic extensions—but is not for the sake of Heaven, and instead expresses the body’s will, desire, and appetite: all these belong to the same category. Even if something is actually necessary for the body’s existence and vitality, if one’s intention is not for the sake of Heaven, to serve Hashem with one’s body, these deeds, words, and thoughts are no better than the vital, animal soul itself. All of them alike receive and draw their vitality from the second level among the kelipot and the other side: the fourth kelipah, called kelipat nogah. In this world, called the World of Asiyah, it is almost entirely evil, with only a little good mixed into it. From it come the good traits of the animal soul in Israel, as explained above.

It is an intermediate condition between the three completely impure kelipot and the condition and level of holiness.

Therefore it is sometimes incorporated within the three impure kelipot, as stated in Etz Chayim, Gate 49, at the beginning of chapter 4, in the name of the Zohar. At other times it is incorporated within and ascends to the condition and level of holiness: namely, when the good mixed into it is separated from the evil, prevails, and ascends to become incorporated within holiness.

For example, someone eats rich beef and drinks fragrant wine to broaden his mind for Hashem and His Torah, as Rava said, ‘Wine and fragrance,’ and so forth; or he does so to fulfill the commandment of delighting in Shabbat and the festivals. The vitality of the meat and wine, which had flowed from kelipat nogah, is then refined and ascends to Hashem like a burnt offering and sacrifice.

The same applies to someone who says something humorous to open his mind and gladden his heart for Hashem, His Torah, and His service, which must be undertaken joyfully. This is what Rava did for his students: he first said something humorous before them, and the Sages were cheered.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 6:85: “Therefore the Zohar says that repentance does not avail: this means availing completely, according to the full measure of repentance in which deliberate sins become merits, the past is entirely repaired and even becomes a merit. If this were attained here, the guard of the tree of life would be removed and the person could eat and live forever; this is not Hashem's will in this world. The guards prevent a repair and complete return extending to living forever. Nevertheless, “nothing stands in the way of repentance,” and repentance concerning the holy covenant brings a person from death to length of days and years.”

If this were attained here, the guard of the tree of life would be removed and the person could eat and live forever; this is not Hashem's will in this world. The guards prevent a repair and complete return extending to living forever. Nevertheless, “nothing stands in the way of repentance,” and repentance concerning the holy covenant brings a person from death to length of days and years.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains this very qualification of the Zohar. It defines the negation as complete repair that would remove the guard of the tree of life and allow endless bodily life, then explicitly states that nothing stands in the way of repentance. Reading it beside the final siman prevents “repentance does not help” from being detached from the immediately stated meaning of total repair. The siman itself ends by placing that final root repair in divine aid.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 15:39: “In any event, the understanding shared by them all—that the Zohar’s statement “he has no repentance” concerns forgiveness of the sin and atonement themselves—is certainly astonishing and strange, and everything they wrote to explain it is strained and remote. All the more so is the plain sense that he has no repentance at all certainly impossible: the prohibition of a married woman is unquestionably more severe, as is also explained in Sefer Chasidim, cited by Chelkat Mechokek and Beit Shmuel and mentioned above. Concerning David’s act with Bathsheba, which involved a married woman, they said at the end of Avodah Zarah 4b that he was not suited to it, but it occurred to teach repentance: if an individual sins, and so forth; see there. Thus even the more severe sin involving a married woman admits repentance, and certainly this does. But according to what I explained above concerning the repentance prescribed by the Rokeach and the Ari—that these practices do not prevent atonement but are a gift, each person according to his level—it seems clear to me that the Zohar, too, intends the acceptance achieved through a gift: that one be accepted completely, to ascend and appear before God at lofty levels, like an entirely righteous guardian of the covenant who never sinned. This applies to all transgressions: through complete repentance from love, deliberate sins become merits, and through them he shall live. That is, after the appropriate repentance and the bringing of the gift, he again becomes close and a member of the household as before, with even greater strength, since the sins themselves enter the reckoning of commandments. Concerning this, the Zohar said that for this transgression repentance does not make it into merits or restore one entirely to the former state, even after all the gifts. The Rokeach and the Ari spoke according to their levels: each person’s repentance is effective for the level he apprehended it could achieve. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s level of apprehension, and what he revealed to his companions, was higher than all of them, as is known from what he said about himself in the holy Zohar and about his entire generation: that there would be no generation like that one, and that such a revelation would not occur again until the coming of Mashiach. In accordance with the level they apprehended, they said that repentance for this sin does not enable one to attain so lofty a level, which can be reached only by an entirely righteous guardian of the covenant who never blemished it.”

paragraphs.text: Sefer Etz Chaim 49:3:1: “All the drops of the “plagues of human beings” go there, into the shells of nogah, the female aspect of nogah, and it becomes good and evil; understand this. Concerning this it is said, “I too shall walk with you in the fury of keri,” for fury is the female aspect of nogah. Remember this: in the shell of each of the four worlds there are iniquity, destroyer, anger, and fury, which are Chokhmah, Binah, Zeir Anpin, and the female aspect of nogah. They are not equal, in the manner explained above concerning Samael and Lilith. Wherever keri is found, it belongs to nogah; remember this. See Terumah, page 130. The good within this nogah is the eleven ingredients of the incense. Galbanum is the female aspect of Zeir Anpin of nogah, and therefore its smell is bad, because its evil adheres to it. The shell of nogah is nourished by the smoke of the offerings, for the animal soul within a person and within kosher animals comes from there.”

p: וְהִנֵּה הַכֹּהֵן הוּא נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁקָּבַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִהְיוֹת נוֹשֵׂא עֲוֹן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם.
And behold, the priest is a soul established by Hashem to bear the iniquity of Israel to atone for them.
וּח' בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הֵם תִּיקּוּן ח' מַדְרֵיגוֹת בָּרַע,
And the eight garments of the High Priest rectify eight rungs of evil,
וְהַט' הוּא גּוּף הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל עַצְמוֹ הַמְלוּבָּשׁ בָּהֶם,
and the ninth is the very body of the High Priest enclothed in them,
הוּא מְכַפֵּר עַל מַדְרֵגָה ט' שֶׁהוּא לֵיצָנוּת,
atoning for the ninth level which is mockery,
כִּי כֹּהֵן דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר עוֹבֵד הוּא הֵיפֶךְ לֵיצָנוּת,
for a priest (kohen), meaning a servant, is the antithesis of mockery,
כִּי מִצַּד לֵיצָנוּת אֵין מָקוֹם לַעֲבוֹדָה כְּלָל.
since from the stance of mockery there is no place for service at all.
וּלְכָךְ יִתְרוֹ כֹּהֵן מִדְיָן הוּא הֵיפֶךְ דַּעֲמָלֵק,
Therefore Jethro, priest of Midian, is the opposite of Amalek,
רַק שֶׁהוּא פֶּתִי כִּי עָבַד לְאֵל זָר "וַיַּאֲמִין לְכָל דָּבָר".
only that he was a simpleton (peti) worshiping foreign deities, "believing every word."
אֲבָל צָרִיךְ לְהַאֲמִין בְּ"אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר" וּלְעָבְדוֹ.
Rather, one must believe in "I am Hashem" and serve Him.
וּמִצַּד גּוּף כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
And through the body of the High Priest whose title is High Priest,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ כֻּלּוֹ כָּךְ – שׁוֹרֶשׁ דַּעֲבוֹדָה
— meaning his entire root is completely service —
בָּזֶה הוּא מְתַקֵּן וּמְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל מִינֵי רַע דְּלֵיצָנוּת שֶׁבִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
in this he rectifies and atones for every form of evil mockery within the Jewish people.

items.h: The crown of priesthood and the incense

p: וְתִיקּוּן הָעֲשִׂירִי הוּא כֶּתֶר כְּהֻנָּה שֶׁבְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה,
And the tenth rectification is the "crown of priesthood" in rabbinic teachings,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר מִדַּת הַכֶּתֶר וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם לְתַקֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּרַע.
meaning the attribute of Keter and the concealed root, rectifying the hidden root of evil.
וְכֶתֶר כְּהֻנָּה הוּא הַזֵּיר דְּמִזְבַּח מִקְטַר קְטֹרֶת כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא עב:).
And the crown of priesthood is the rim of the Incense Altar as our Sages taught (Yoma 72b).
וּלְכָךְ פָּרָשַׁת מִזְבַּח מִקְטַר קְטֹרֶת כְּתוּבָה בְּסוֹף פָּרָשַׁת תְּצַוֶּה
Therefore the section of the Incense Altar is placed at the end of Parashat Tetzaveh,
אַחַר צִיוּוּי עֲשִׂיַּת בִּגְדֵי כְּהֻנָּה וְאַחַר קִידּוּשׁ וּמְשִׁיחַת גּוּף הַכֹּהֲנִים,
after the command to make the priestly garments and after the sanctification and anointing of the priests' bodies,
וְלֹא בְּפָרָשַׁת תְּרוּמָה דְּשָׁם מְקוֹמוֹ.
and not in Parashat Terumah where it would seem naturally to belong.
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהַכֶּתֶר חוּץ לַגּוּף וּמַקִּיף,
Only because the crown is outside the body and encompasses it,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַוּוֹת עָלָיו אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן זָכַר מִקּוֹדֶם ח' לְבוּשִׁים וְהַט' הַגּוּף הַמְלוּבָּשׁ בָּהֶם,
it could not be commanded until first mentioning the eight garments and ninth the body enclothed in them,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָיָה הַכֶּתֶר הוּא עַל מִזְבַּח הַקְּטֹרֶת,
and thereafter the crown placed upon the Incense Altar,
דְּיָדוּעַ בְּעֵץ חַיִּים שָׁם דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן לְתִיקּוּן קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
which is known from Etz Chayim to serve likewise as the rectification of Kelipat Nogah, see there.

p: וְלָכֵן הוּא עוֹצֵר הַמַּגֵּפָה וְהַמִּיתָה,
Therefore the incense halts the plague and death,
וְהַיְינוּ כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת מג:) דְּרֵיחַ הַנְּשָׁמָה נֶהֱנֵית מִמֶּנּוּ.
aligning with the Sages' teaching (Berakhot 43b) that the soul derives delight from scent.
כִּי הַנְּשָׁמָה בָּאַף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נְשָׁמָה בְּאַפּוֹ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ב, כב),
For the soul is in the nose, as written: "breath is in his nostrils" (Isaiah 2:22),
כִּי ה' חוּשִׁים נֶגֶד ה' כֹּחוֹת: נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה, חַיָּה, יְחִידָה.
for the five senses correspond to the five levels: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah.
מִשּׁוּשׁ בַּנֶּפֶשׁ,
Touch resides in the Nefesh;
וְטַעַם בַּחֵךְ וְגָרוֹן נֶגֶד הַלֵּב שֶׁבּוֹ כֹּחַ הַרְגָּשַׁת הַטַּעַם וְהוּא מִשְׁכַּן הָרוּחַ,
taste in palate and throat corresponds to the heart holding the sensation of taste, being the seat of the Ruach;
וְרֵיחַ בַּמּוֹחַ שֶׁמּוֹשֵׁךְ הָרֵיחָנִי דֶּרֶךְ הָאַף.
and scent reaches the brain which draws the fragrance through the nose.
וְאֵלּוּ ג' נִכְנָסִים לַגּוּף, כִּי אֵלּוּ ג' כֹּחוֹת נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה מְלוּבָּשִׁים בַּגּוּף.
And these three enter inside the body, for Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah are internal garments within the body.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רְאִיָּה וּשְׁמִיעָה הוּא חוּץ לַגּוּף
In contrast, sight and hearing operate from outside the body,
וְהוּא נֶגֶד חַיָּה וִיחִידָה שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן מַקִּיפִים כַּנּוֹדָע.
corresponding to Chayah and Yechidah which are transcendent encompassing lights (makifim).

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: aligning with the Sages' teaching (Berakhot 43b) that the soul derives delight from scent.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 43b: ‘Rav Yehudah said: One who goes out in the days of Nisan and sees trees blossoming says: ‘Blessed is He who has left nothing lacking in His world and has created in it good creatures and good trees for people to enjoy.’ Rav Zutra bar Toviyah said in Rav’s name: From where do we know that a blessing is recited over a fragrance? It is stated: ‘Let every soul praise Yah.’ What is something from which the soul derives pleasure, but the body does not? You must say: It is fragrance.’

paragraphs.text: Ibn Ezra on Exodus 23:25:2: “The human body belongs to the lower world, and the higher soul is bound to it. There are intermediaries between the soul and the body: two powers, generally called ruach and nefesh in the holy tongue. The neshamah is wisdom, and its dwelling is in the brain of the head. From it comes the power of all the senses and voluntary movement. The ruach is in the heart, and in it is human life. It seeks dominion, to overcome whatever opposes it, and it possesses anger. Thus Solomon said, “Do not be hasty in your spirit to become angry,” and, “A fool gives vent to all his spirit.” The nefesh is in the liver, and it desires to eat, as it is written, “For your nefesh desires”; sexual desire also comes from it.”

paragraphs.text: Sefer Etz Chaim 5:1:4: “Concerning the five internal aspects—nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, and yechidah—and the two encompassing aspects, chayah and yechidah: one must know that even among the five internal aspects each has an encompassing aspect, as with the souls of Nadav, Avihu, and Elijah, of blessed memory. But these two encompassing aspects are different, comprehensive ones, apart from the five encompassing aspects within the internal aspects. A sign of this is that among these internal encompassing aspects there are more than five: an encompassing light, an encompassing light around that encompassing light, and an encompassing light around the two encompassing lights, as mentioned in the section on the Priestly Blessing in the Idra Rabba. Thus all these are distinct from those two comprehensive ones.”

p: וְנוֹדַע דְּנֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה, חַיָּה, יְחִידָה הֵם נֶגֶד ה' פַּרְצוּפִין,
And it is known that the five soul-levels correspond to the five Supernal Partzufim,
וּנְשָׁמָתִין אִתְגְּזָרוּן מִבְּרִיאָה
and souls are hewn from the World of Beriah
דְּתַמָּן אִימָּא עִילָּאָה מְקַנֶּנֶת
where the Supernal Mother (Binah) nests,
שֶׁהִיא תַּרְעָא דְּחֵירוּ בְּסוֹד הַיּוֹבֵל כַּנּוֹדָע.
which is the Gate of Freedom in the mystical secret of the Jubilee.
וְסוֹד כָּל הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת בִּכְלָל אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא הָרֵיחַ,
And the mystical secret of all sacrifices is nothing other than scent,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיָּרַח ה' אֶת רֵיחַ וְגוֹמֵר",
as written: "And Hashem smelled the sweet savor, etc." (Genesis 8:21),
וְצָרִיךְ לִזְבּוֹחַ הַזֶּבַח לְשֵׁם רֵיחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זְבָחִים מו:).
and one must slaughter the offering with intent for the sweet savor (Zevachim 46b).
כִּי הֲנָאַת הָרֵיחַ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן "בְּצַלְמֵנוּ",
For Hashem's pleasure in scent, which reflects "in our image," (Genesis 1:26)
הַיְינוּ בְּכֹחַ הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ תַּרְעָא דְּחֵירוּ וְכַפָּרָה עַל כָּל מִינֵי רַע.
resides in the power channeling the Gate of Freedom and atonement over every evil.
רַק שֶׁהַהַעֲלָאָה מִצַּד אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא אֵינוֹ רֵיחָנִי;
Only that the initial elevation through arousal from below is not itself sweet fragrance;
וְהַקְּטֹרֶת הִיא הַעֲלָאַת רֵיחָנִי לְהַעֲלוֹת רֵיחַ,
yet the incense raises fragrance to generate sweet aroma,
וְהַיְינוּ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא מִכֹּחַ הַנְּשָׁמָה
which is arousal from below driven by the pure soul,
שֶׁאוֹמְרִים "נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה הִיא" בֶּאֱמֶת מִצִּידָּהּ.
concerning which we proclaim: "the soul which You gave within me is pure," truly from its side.
כִּי מִשְׁכַּן הָרַע רַק בַּלֵּב וְלֹא בַּמּוֹחַ,
For the seat of evil is only in the heart and not in the brain,
רַק הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת הַמְסַבְּבִים הֵם רַק כְּעִנְיַן רֵיחַ רַע הַנִּכְנָס לַמּוֹחַ.
and extraneous thoughts that swirl are merely like a foul odor wafting into the mind.
וְזֶה הַעֲלָאַת הַקְּטֹרֶת
— And this is the elevating function of the incense —
כָּל מִינֵי רֵיחוֹת טוֹבוֹת בְּצֵירוּף הַחֶלְבְּנָה שֶׁרֵיחָהּ רַע גַּם כֵּן
all types of pleasant fragrances bound together with the foul-smelling galbanum
לְרֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
to form a sweet savor unto Hashem, blessed be He.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הִיא קִישּׁוּרָא דְּכוּלָּא,
And through this occurs the supreme binding of all things,
שֶׁמִּתְקַשְּׁרִים כָּל מִינֵי מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת לִקְדוּשָּׁה.
wherein all foreign thoughts become bound into holiness.
וְזֶהוּ הַעֲלָאַת קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ וַעֲצִירַת הַמִּיתָה.
And this is the elevation of Kelipat Nogah and the halting of death.
וּלְכָךְ שָׁם הוּא כֶּתֶר כְּהֻנָּה,
Therefore there resides the crown of priesthood,
מַדְרֵגַת הַכֶּתֶר דְּכַפָּרַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל חַטֹּאתָם,
the high level of Keter atoning for Israel across all their sins,
גַּם מִכִּתְרִין דִּמְסָאֲבוּתָא וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע דְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ.
even purifying them from the crowns of defilement and the taproot of evil from the serpent's counsel.
וְדָבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד אָדָם כְּלָל,
And this matter is not within human power at all,
רַק עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
only the supernatural assistance of Hashem;
לְכָךְ אֵין הַכֶּתֶר בְּרֹאשׁ הַכֹּהֵן,
therefore this crown is not placed upon the priest's head,
רַק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ מִקְטַר קְטֹרֶת.
but rests upon the Incense Altar.

For the supernal Mother nests in the Throne with the three upper sefirot. The central pillar encompasses six sefirot, which nest in Metatron. The lower Mother nests in the Ofan, concerning which it is said, “Behold, one wheel on the earth.””

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayechi 41:420: “Come and see: incense binds bonds and holds together above and below. This removes death, accusation, and wrath, so that they cannot rule in the world, as it is written, “Moses said to Aaron: Take the firepan, place fire upon it from the altar, put incense on it, and bring it quickly,” and so forth. After this it is written, “And (Aaron) ran,” and so forth, “and made atonement for the people”; and it is written, “He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.” For none of the evil sides or accusers can stand before incense. Therefore it is the mystery of everything (another reading: the joy of everything) and the binding of everything.”

p: סְלִיק סֵפֶר צִדְקַת הַצַּדִּיק מִכְּתַב יַד קֹדֶשׁ בְּסִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא.
Completed is the book Tzidkat HaTzaddik from the holy manuscript, with Heaven's assistance.
וַיַּעַן יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר:
And Yisrael responded and said:
"אוֹדֶה אֶת ה' שֶׁזָּכִיתִי לִהְיוֹת נִטְפָּל לַקֹּדֶשׁ,
“I give thanks unto Hashem that I merited to be an assistant to the holy,
וְצִיַּינְתִּי אֶת הַמַּרְאֵה מְקוֹמוֹת בְּהַסֵּפֶר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַזֶּה,
and I annotated the cross-references throughout this holy book,
אֲשֶׁר רַבֵּינוּ הַגָּאוֹן הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שָׁנָה לָשׁוֹן קְצָרָה.
which our master, the holy Gaon of blessed memory, taught with concise phrasing.
וּמוֹדָעָה דְּבָרֵינוּ,
And let our notice be known:
אֲשֶׁר הַמּוּקָּפִים בִּשְׁנֵי חֶצְאֵי מְרוּבָּעִים כָּזֶה []
that which is enclosed in square brackets like this []
הֵם מֵהַעְתֵּק גּוּף כְּתַב יַד קֹדֶשׁ,
is transcribed from the actual holy manuscript itself,
וְהַמּוּקָּפִים בִּשְׁנֵי חֶצְאֵי עִגּוּלִים כָּזֶה ()
while that which is enclosed in parentheses like this ()
הוּא מַה שֶּׁצִּיַּינְתִּי בְּעֶזְרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ".
is what I have annotated with the help of Heaven.”

A matching signed epilogue distinguishes editorial source references from the underlying manuscript.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Chalomot, Epilogue 1: “The booklet Divrei Chalomot is completed, with Heaven's help. Yisrael said: I shall bless at the completion, for Hashem enabled me to mark the references in the book Resisei Layla and the booklet Divrei Chalomot. They are enclosed in two round halves, thus: (). May Hashem help us so that our master's words, may the memory of the righteous and holy be a blessing for life in the world to come, enter our hearts to love and revere Hashem, and so that our children and children's children engage in Torah and fear of Hashem all their days. Yisrael, son of my father, our teacher and master, the pious rabbi Yosef Yozel, of blessed memory for life in the world to come, of Lublin.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: This paragraph is the annotator Yisrael's notice, following the book's closing colophon. Here he distinguishes square-bracketed matter copied from the manuscript from round-parenthesized references he supplied. The Divrei Chalomot epilogue bears the same signature and explicitly uses round parentheses for his references in that work and Resisei Layla. It confirms that convention; it does not extend the square-bracket rule beyond what this notice actually says.
